description: QMCO reported adjusted EBITDA of $8 million, far above the preview’s $1.5 million guidance midpoint and $5.5 million above the guidance range’s high end. This was a much stronger profitability result than expected.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was a positive $8 million, $5.5 million above the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: $1.5M ± $1M.”

description: Instead of the expected non-GAAP loss, QMCO reported $4 million of non-GAAP net income, or $0.18 per share. That is a substantial reversal from the preview’s expected loss per share.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income was $4 million ($0.18 per share), the first positive non-GAAP adjusted net income since 2023.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: ($0.15) ± $0.10”; consensus was “($0.17)” and Northland’s estimate was “($0.14).”

description: Revenue came in at $80.8 million, above both the $75 million guidance midpoint and roughly $75 million consensus. The preview characterized revenue as a low-differentiation variable centered on guidance, so the size of the beat was better than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue was $80.8 million … exceeding guidance of $75 million (+/- $2 million).”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus sits exactly on the guidance midpoint”; revenue guidance was “$75.0M ± $2M.”

description: GAAP gross margin reached 39.3%, above the preview’s roughly 38% margin implied by guidance and above its 37% validation threshold. The preview identified margin recovery as the key debate, so this was a stronger recovery than its central expectation.
fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin reached 39.3%, up 360 basis points sequentially and nearly 400 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview calculated “~38% gross margin” implied by guidance, described a base range of “36.5–38%,” and said “gross margin ≥37% validates the FY27 recovery path.”

description: Q2 revenue guidance is approximately $82 million, above the preview’s roughly $78 million reference point and the base-case range of $78–81 million. It meets the preview’s bull-case threshold rather than its base-case expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance is approximately $82 million (+/- $2 million).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a Q2 guide below ~$78M puts $313M at risk,” gave a base-case Q2 guide of “$78–81M,” and listed “Q2 guide ≥$82M” in the bull scenario.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported backlog was significantly higher than the prior quarter’s $45 million, rather than remaining roughly flat in the preview’s base case. That signals stronger demand, but alongside the continuing tape-drive constraint it also means orders are still not converting fully into shipments.
fact_evidence: “A significantly higher backlog (prior quarter was $45 million).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “backlog roughly flat at $40–48M”; it also said that revenue in line with backlog up would mean “demand is real but shipping is still broken.”

description: Despite the stronger Q2 revenue outlook, QMCO guided adjusted EBITDA down to $6 million, citing higher R&D hiring and sales commissions. The preview did not provide a Q2 EBITDA estimate or flag those costs, so this is an unanticipated near-term profitability headwind.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA is guided down to $6 million due to higher R&D hiring and sales commissions.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: QMCO reported a $155.3 million GAAP net loss, driven by $157.7 million in one-time non-cash debt-related charges, including a $129.7 million loss from the convertible-note fair-value change. The preview focused on non-GAAP EPS and did not flag these large GAAP charges, so the GAAP result was unexpectedly distorted by debt accounting.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $155.3 million ($7.06 per share), driven by $157.7 million in one-time non-cash debt-related charges including a $129.7 million loss on convertible note fair value change.”

description: The preview noted that management expected China service to run at or near capacity through peak season, but gave no quantified Q3 earnings outlook. Matson now guides Q3 Ocean Transportation operating income to be about 45% above Q3 2025, with both rates and volume contributing.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 Ocean Transportation operating income is guided to be approximately 45% higher than the $147.4 million posted in Q3 2025, driven by both higher rates and volume.”
expectation_evidence: “CEO Matt Cox: China service expected to run ‘at or near capacity through peak season’”; the preview also flagged Q3/peak-season commentary on rates and capacity utilization.

description: The preview anticipated updated full-year guidance but did not state an expected increase. Matson raised its outlook to consolidated operating income above 2025’s $499.8 million.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting consolidated operating income to exceed the $499.8 million achieved in 2025.”

description: The preview gave no Q4 operating-income outlook. Matson now expects Q4 Ocean Transportation operating income to be modestly below Q4 2025, as last year’s elevated post-trade-agreement demand normalizes.
fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 Ocean Transportation operating income is expected to be modestly lower than the $136 million in Q4 2025, reflecting a normalization versus last year's elevated post-trade-agreement demand.”

description: The preview did not flag a fuel-cost recovery issue. Matson reported that it had undercollected fuel costs by a low-teens millions amount because of the Iran conflict, although it expects to recover the shortfall by year-end.
fact_evidence: “The company had undercollected fuel costs across all trade lanes by a low-teens millions of dollars amount at quarter-end due to the Iran conflict, but expects full recovery by year-end.”

description: The preview did not mention SSAT. The joint venture’s Q2 contribution fell year over year, and Matson expects its full-year contribution to be below 2025’s level.
fact_evidence: “The SSAT joint venture contributed $4.8 million in Q2, down $2.5 million year-over-year, with full-year 2026 contribution expected below the $32.5 million achieved in 2025.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview highlighted China-service strength but did not describe this change in cargo mix. Southeast Asia now makes up 20%–25% of weekly China-service volume, with slightly lower all-in rates and higher operating costs than China-direct cargo.
fact_evidence: “Southeast Asia cargo now represents 20% to 25% of weekly China service volume, up significantly from early 2025, though at slightly lower all-in rates and higher operating costs than China-direct cargo.”

description: The preview estimated F1 segment revenue at about $705 million, down 42% year over year; the call reported a 15% decline despite the race-count disruption. That is a substantially smaller revenue drop than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: F1's race count fell 44% year over year in Q2, driving a 15% revenue decline.
expectation_evidence: “F1 segment revenue | ~$705M | vs $1,226M (−42%).”

description: The preview expected disrupted-race costs and pro-rata team payments to cushion the OIBDA decline relative to revenue. Instead, the reported adjusted OIBDA decline was twice the reported revenue decline, indicating weaker cost protection than that expectation suggested.
fact_evidence: F1's race-count decline drove a 15% revenue decline and a 30% adjusted OIBDA decline.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. OIBDA should decline far less than revenue in percentage terms.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported that U.S. F1 hours watched on Apple TV were up 13% season-to-date and that the audience was younger and more female. The preview anticipated the Apple TV revenue step-up, but did not flag this viewership or audience-mix improvement.
fact_evidence: “Total hours watched up 13% season-to-date,” with F1 attracting “a younger and more female audience.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix was extended through 2037, and 2026 ticket sales had already reached the comparable end-of-September 2025 level by the end of July. The preview did not anticipate this extension or the strong advance-sales update.
fact_evidence: “The Las Vegas Grand Prix was extended 10 years through 2037,” and 2026 ticket sales had reached end-of-September 2025 levels “as of end-July on a like-for-like basis.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: MotoGP secured agreements with all manufacturers and teams through 2031 alongside new regulations beginning in 2027. The preview wanted evidence of progress on MotoGP's growth path, but did not anticipate this long-dated framework.
fact_evidence: MotoGP “secured agreements with all manufacturers and teams through 2031” alongside “new technical regulations beginning in 2027.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage rose to 3.4x from 3.0x at Q1, rather than improving immediately, though management attributed the increase to F1 calendar timing and still expected full-year leverage improvement. The preview had flagged the weak cash-generation quarter as a risk to the deleveraging path.
fact_evidence: Net leverage was 3.4x, “a slight uptick driven by F1 calendar timing.”
expectation_evidence: “A quarter with 5 races is a weak cash-generation quarter — watch whether the de-levering path slips.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: House 44 is planned to expand from 9 locations in 2026 to 30 in 2027, while the Paddock Club was sold out for the rest of the season and 2028 allocations were complete. The preview had raised the possibility of hospitality weakness, not this level of demand and planned expansion.
fact_evidence: House 44 is to expand “from 9 locations in 2026 to 30 locations in 2027”; the Paddock Club was “sold out for the rest of the season” and “2028 allocations complete.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether “hospitality/Paddock Club falls harder than the race count” as a bear-case risk.

description: PLBY reported $31.2 million of revenue, above the preview’s $29.69 million consensus and its $28.8–$29.6 million estimate. That is a clear, roughly 5% beat against the preview’s expectation of only modest growth.
fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue grew approximately 10.9% year over year to $31.2 million, up from $28.1 million.
expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $29.69M; my Q2 2026E total revenue: $28.8 – 29.6M.

description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $7 million, well above the preview’s $5.0–$5.5 million estimate and its $5 million minimum bar, even after more than $700,000 of litigation expense. The preview’s bull case began at $6.5 million, which the reported result also exceeded.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to approximately $7 million (22% margin) versus $3.5 million a year ago, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA, though it included over $700,000 of litigation expenses.
expectation_evidence: Adj. EBITDA: $5.0 – 5.5M; the buy-side bar here is Adjusted EBITDA ≥ $5M. Bull scenario: $6.5M+.

description: Honey Birdette revenue reached $19.5 million, above the preview’s $18.0–$18.5 million estimate despite the expected seasonal softness. The seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit brick-and-mortar comp growth and +13% retail comps, however, were in line with the preview’s key comp expectation.
fact_evidence: Honey Birdette net revenue grew 18% year over year to $19.5 million, with total comparable stores up 15% (retail comps +13%, online +16%) and every region positive, marking its seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit brick-and-mortar comp growth.
expectation_evidence: Direct-to-Consumer (Honey Birdette): $18.0 – 18.5M; Q2 is seasonally softer (AU winter). A seventh straight double-digit comp quarter holds the story together.

description: Licensing returned to growth rather than merely stabilizing: revenue rose about 2% to $11.2 million despite a China transition-related step-down. With the $5 million Biborg minimum, the reported total implies roughly $6.2 million from other licensing, just above the preview’s approximately $5.9 million ex-Byborg threshold.
fact_evidence: Licensing revenue rose about 2% to $11.2 million, held back by a couple-hundred-thousand-dollar quarterly step-down in China during the UTG owner-operator transition, while the Biborg partnership contributed $5 million of digital licensing revenue at the contractual minimum.
expectation_evidence: If ex-Byborg licensing is ~$5.9M or better, the 'higher-quality, higher-rate' story is intact. The base scenario expected licensing flat-to-down slightly ex-Byborg.

description: PLBY reported roughly $200,000 of positive net income, slightly better than the preview’s expectation of approximately break-even to a small GAAP loss. The preview did not set a meaningful positive-income expectation.
fact_evidence: The company reached break-even net income (~$200,000) versus a net loss of $7.7 million (8 cents per share) in Q2 2025.
expectation_evidence: EPS (GAAP): ~$(0.00) to $(0.003); my GAAP EPS estimate: $(0.02) – $(0.00).

description: The company disclosed an agreement to repurchase nearly 15% of its shares at $1.05, below both the stated $1.75 conversion price and the current trading level. The preview did not anticipate a buyback; the low price is favorable to remaining shareholders, though using cash for repurchases is notable alongside the company’s substantial debt.
fact_evidence: Playboy agreed to repurchase approximately 16.6 million shares (nearly 15% of shares outstanding) at a fixed price of $1.05 (roughly $17 million total), below the $1.75 conversion price and current trading level, paid in installments ($2 million paid, $3 million due by August 31st).

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: PLBY quantified a substantial pool of future licensing revenue that the preview did not flag: more than $320 million is contracted but not yet recognized. This adds visibility beyond the preview’s discussion of the known Biborg minimum guarantee.
fact_evidence: The company reported over $320 million of contracted but not-yet-recognized future licensing revenue.

description: The second paid-voting contest with Honey Birdette drew nearly 50,000 contestants and generated about 2.5 times the revenue of the first, with the revenue expected in Q3. The preview did not anticipate this new near-term revenue contribution.
fact_evidence: Its second paid-voting contest with Honey Birdette drew nearly 50,000 contestants generating about 2.5 times the revenue of the first, with those economics landing in Q3.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Playboy.com’s subscription offering completed its first full quarter with roughly 2 million unique visitors, July was its strongest month, and initial content sponsorship revenue is expected in Q3. The preview did not identify these web audience and monetization milestones as expectations to watch.
fact_evidence: The newly launched Playboy.com subscription completed its first full quarter with roughly 2 million site unique visitors, July was its strongest month yet, and first sponsorship deals for content are expected to begin showing revenue in Q3.

description: AIT’s Q4 organic sales growth was 9.7%, far above the preview’s expected 4.0%–5.5% range, with June growth still above 10% despite tougher comparisons.
fact_evidence: “Q4 organic sales grew 10% (9.7%), the strongest in more than 3 years” and June organic sales were “up over 10% year-over-year despite tougher comparisons.”
expectation_evidence: “Organic daily sales” guidance: “+4.0% to +5.5%.”

description: Q4 EPS reached $3.17, well above the $2.92 consensus and above the preview’s already upper-half-of-guidance expectation. That result came despite higher LIFO expense, tax rate, and net interest expense.
fact_evidence: “Q4 EPS reached a record $3.17, up 13.2% from $2.80 a year ago, despite higher LIFO expense, tax rate, and net interest expense.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS” consensus: “$2.92”; the preview said consensus “sits in the upper half” of the $2.85–$2.96 implied Q4 guidance band.

description: Q4 EBITDA margin reached 13.1%, beating the guided 12.6%–12.8% range rather than merely landing within it, even as the preview highlighted higher LIFO and moderating pricing as margin risks.
fact_evidence: “EBITDA margin expanded 64 basis points to 13.1%, exceeding guidance of 12.6%-12.8%,” with incremental margins “over 19% (22%+ excluding LIFO).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q4 guidance called for “12.6–12.8%” EBITDA margin and warned that higher LIFO and moderating price contribution would test the margin step-up.

description: Engineered Solutions organic growth was 12.9%, substantially above the preview’s 7.1% sales-growth consensus, led by automation sales growth above 20%.
fact_evidence: “Engineered Solutions led with 12.9% organic growth, including automation organic sales up over 20% (strongest in 4 years).”
expectation_evidence: “Engineered Solutions sales” consensus implied “+7.1%” growth.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Within Engineered Solutions, flow control lagged because process-market MRO activity was softer; the preview focused on the segment’s growth and orders but did not anticipate this specific weakness.
fact_evidence: “Flow control lagged due to softer process-market MRO activity.”

description: Service Center organic sales accelerated to 7.9%, above the preview’s 4.7% sales-growth consensus, while EBITDA rose 16.3% and margin expanded 91 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Service Center segment organic sales accelerated to 7.9% growth from 4% last quarter, with EBITDA up 16.3% and margin expanding 91 basis points to 14.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “Service Center sales” consensus implied “+4.7%” growth; “Service Center op. income” consensus implied “+7.4%.”

description: FY2027 EPS guidance has a $11.90 midpoint, modestly above the $11.69 consensus, whereas the preview’s base case was an in-line midpoint of about $11.70. The high end also reaches $12.15.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for EPS of $11.65-$12.15.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2027 EPS consensus at “~$11.69” and its base case as “$11.30–$12.10 (midpoint ~$11.70, in line).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: July Engineered Solutions orders rose in the mid-20s percent, materially stronger than the preview’s key operational threshold of another quarter of double-digit order growth. Q1 organic growth guidance and quarter-to-date trends were also constructive.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 organic sales are projected to grow 6%-8% year-over-year, with quarter-to-date trending at approximately 7% and July orders in Engineered Solutions up in the mid-20s percent.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “a third consecutive quarter of double-digit organic order growth” and flagged July commentary as a key read-through for FY2027.

description: Management raised its five-year targets substantially, lifting the sales objective from $5.5 billion to $7 billion and the EBITDA-margin objective from 13% to 14%; the preview did not anticipate a target increase.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its 5-year intermediate targets, lifting the sales objective to $7 billion from $5.5 billion and the EBITDA margin objective to 14% from 13%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: AIT ended FY2026 with just 0.2x net leverage and nearly $2 billion of deployment capacity, an unexpectedly strong balance-sheet position that gives it substantial capital-allocation flexibility.
fact_evidence: “The company generated $461 million of free cash flow in fiscal 2026, ended with net leverage of just 0.2x EBITDA and nearly $2 billion of deployment capacity.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $1.96, above the preview’s $1.81 consensus and the $1.85–$1.95 base-case range. That is a stronger beat than the preview’s expected slight-to-clear beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $1.96.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | Q3 FY26 Consensus: $1.81”; the base case expected “$1.85–1.95.”

description: Gross margin reached 35.5%, above the preview’s 34.0–34.5% base case. The 240-basis-point expansion was stronger than expected, and management said further expansion is expected in Q4.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 240 basis points to 35.5%”; “with further expansion expected in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s “Base case 34.0–34.5%” and catalyst checklist called for “Gross margin ≥34.0%.”

description: Management raised the plant-consolidation savings target from $15 million to at least $20 million, taking the total Project Apollo annualized target to at least $25 million—above the preview’s $20 million total target.
fact_evidence: “Management raised the plant consolidation component of Project Apollo from $15 million to at least $20 million, lifting the total program's annualized savings target to at least $25 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$20M annualized target,” including “~$15M plant,” and said a raised Apollo target would be a catalyst.

description: Frozen beverage sales declined 5.8%, worse than the preview’s modeled 2–4% decline, although the $106.7 million result was within its $106–110 million range. Beverage volume grew 5.9%, below the preview’s watch case of high-single- to low-double-digit beverage growth, as lower service and machine sales offset volume.
fact_evidence: “Frozen beverage sales fell 5.8% to $106.7 million as 5.9% beverage volume growth was more than offset by lower service and machine sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case forecast FBev “−2 to −4%” and its catalyst checklist cited “~$106–110M”; it also said to watch for “beverage sales up high-single/low-double digits.”

description: Freight and fuel costs weighed more heavily than the preview’s estimate suggested: the call cited roughly $4.7 million in net cost pressure and about $5 million of higher freight and fuel costs before surcharge offsets. The preview had sized a roughly $3.5 million H2 headwind if fuel held.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “hurt by roughly $4.7 million in net freight and fuel cost pressures”; distribution expenses rose to “11.6% of sales from 9.8%,” reflecting “roughly $5 million in higher freight and fuel costs before surcharge offsets.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management sized a “~$3.5M H2 headwind if fuel holds.”

description: Retail sales grew 1.7% instead of declining the 6–8% modeled in the preview; growth would have been 4.8% excluding higher slotting fees. However, retail operating income fell $3.5 million, tempering the stronger sales result. Several brands also posted strong growth: Dogsters retail sales rose over 30%, Luigi’s over 20%, and Dippin’ Dots more than 100% in tracked channels.
fact_evidence: “Retail segment sales rose 1.7% to $64.9 million but would have grown 4.8% excluding a $2 million increase in slotting fees, though retail operating income fell $3.5 million.” Dogsters grew “over 30%,” Luigi’s “over 20%,” and Dippin’ Dots “more than 100% in tracked channels.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case forecast “Retail −6 to −8%.”

description: The company returned $120 million year-to-date, above the preview’s estimate of about $95 million returned in FY26 to date, and continued both dividends and buybacks during the quarter.
fact_evidence: “The company returned $25 million to shareholders in the quarter ($15 million dividends, $10 million buybacks) and $120 million year-to-date.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$95M returned in FY26 to date” and noted that pausing repurchases to fund a deal “would be poorly received.”

description: Management said it expects bakery sales to return to organic growth in fiscal 2027. The preview discussed the planned reduction in the bakery headwind for Q4, but did not forecast a return to organic growth in FY27.
fact_evidence: “A return to organic growth [is] expected in fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said planned volume reductions were expected to ease from “~3.5% in Q3” to “~2.5% in Q4,” but gave no FY27 organic-growth outlook.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management expects to collect about $17 million in insurance proceeds in August from the Holly Ridge plant-fire settlement, a positive cash inflow not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Expects to collect about $17 million in insurance proceeds in August from the Holly Ridge plant fire settlement.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $67.4 million, below the preview’s roughly $70 million estimate, despite the stronger-than-expected adjusted EPS result.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined 6.4% to $67.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted EBITDA ~$70M (my est.).”

description: The preview estimated a quarterly loss of about $60–70 million, but Eve reported a $34 million net loss. The unusually low $29 million of R&D—well below the roughly $55 million in prior quarters—helped narrow the loss, though management expects R&D to return to about $50 million per quarter.
fact_evidence: “Net loss was $34 million in Q2 2026”; “Q2 2026 R&D fell to $29 million (versus roughly $55 million in prior quarters) due to better-than-expected supplier agreements, but is expected to return to around $50 million per quarter going forward.”
expectation_evidence: “EVEX is a pre-revenue eVTOL developer that will report ~$0 revenue and a ~$60–70M quarterly loss.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview worried that Q2 cash use could put first-half burn near $135 million and annualized consumption at or above the top of guidance. First-half burn was instead $118 million, and full-year consumption is expected near the midpoint of the $225–275 million range.
fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 total cash burn was $118 million (Q2 burn of $49 million), with full-year cash consumption expected near the midpoint of the $225-275 million guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “A repeat [of Q1’s $68.6M] in Q2 puts H1 at ~$135M, annualizing to $270M+ — at or above the top of guidance.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview estimated total liquidity of about $510–525 million, while Eve reported $531 million and said it believes that funding is sufficient through 2028 without new funding. The liquidity figure is somewhat above the preview range, although the through-2028 funding statement itself was anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Eve ended Q2 2026 with $403 million in cash and total liquidity of $531 million (including $128 million in undrawn credit facilities), which management believes is sufficient to fund operations through 2028 without new funding.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash + investments should land near $375–390M … with total liquidity ~$510–525M”; “funded through 2028” was flagged for confirmation.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected roughly 90–130 cumulative test flights by Q2, but Eve reported 66. Test-point validation was ahead of the preview’s Q1 baseline, at 150 versus about 130, so the flight-count shortfall was not matched by a shortfall in validated points.
fact_evidence: “The engineering prototype has completed 66 flights logging 2 hours 46 minutes of airtime and validated 150 test points.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch the flight count disclosed for Q2”; the base case anticipated “flight count ~90–130 with transition progress framed as the win.” The preview cited “130 performance points validated” at Q1 exit.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Full transition moved from Q3 to Q4 2026, pushing the next major flight-test milestone later. Eve said another 30–40 flights are needed before the lifters can be powered off at 90 knots.
fact_evidence: “Full transition flights slipped from Q3 into Q4 2026, requiring an estimated 30-40 more flights to complete before lifters are powered off at 90 knots.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “dated path to full transition / wing-borne cruise” and said a specific quarter would be bullish.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview cited mid-2027 for the first conforming prototype flight; Eve now plans the first crewed conforming prototype flight in the second half of 2027. The overall 2028 certification and entry-into-service target remains unchanged.
fact_evidence: “The first crewed conforming prototype flight is planned for the second half of 2027, with certification and entry into service targeted for 2028 (requiring roughly 12 months of post-first-flight testing).”
expectation_evidence: “Guide: first conforming prototype assembly complete late 2026, first flight mid-2027.”

description: Eve disclosed a roughly $100 million capex plan across 2026–2028 for modular production capacity, a spending commitment the preview did not discuss. It supports production readiness but adds a meaningful future cash requirement.
fact_evidence: “Capex is planned at approximately $20 million in 2026, rising to around $50 million in 2027 and $30-40 million in 2028 (about $100 million total) for modular production capacity.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Eve said European EASA certification is expected 12–15 months after ANAC and FAA approval, adding a specific follow-on timeline for Europe that the preview did not address. This suggests European approval would lag the initial ANAC/FAA approvals.
fact_evidence: “European (EASA) certification expected 12-15 months after ANAC and FAA approval.”

description: Q2 revenue of $670 million beat the preview’s $646 million consensus and the company’s $641–649 million preliminary range. The preview raised the possibility that the beat reflected delayed exits; management instead attributed the main upside to a one-time private-cloud revenue-recognition item that pulls revenue forward from future periods, including the second half of 2026.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total GAAP revenue was $670 million,” beating expectations primarily due to “a one-time revenue recognition timing item in private cloud that pulls forward revenue from future periods including 2H 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $646M” consensus; preliminary range “$641–649M.” The preview also said the beat might mean low-margin exits “ran slower than planned.”

description: Private-cloud revenue was $263 million, well above the preview’s $242–246 million preliminary range. But the upside came from an embedded lease accounted for as a hardware sale rather than more volume, and management left full-year guidance unchanged.
fact_evidence: “Private cloud revenue was $263 million … exceeding the $242-246 million guidance,” but the upside “came from an embedded lease treated like a hardware sale rather than volume growth, so full-year guidance is unchanged.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Private Cloud preliminary revenue of “$242–246M.”

description: Public-cloud revenue also finished above its preliminary range, at about $407 million versus the preview’s $399–403 million, although it was still down 2% year over year.
fact_evidence: “Public cloud revenue was $407 million, down 2% YoY.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Public Cloud preliminary revenue of “$399–403M.”

description: The non-GAAP loss per share was $0.08, a penny narrower than the preview’s approximate $0.09-loss consensus, even though the loss widened from $0.06 a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP loss per share widened to $0.08 from $0.06 a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP EPS consensus as “~$(0.09).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Rackspace moved beyond the preview’s unresolved question about whether an AMD agreement would be signed and how many megawatts would be committed: it announced a definitive 30-megawatt agreement, with 15 megawatts targeted cumulatively by the end of 2027.
fact_evidence: The company “entered a definitive agreement with AMD to deploy 30 megawatts of AMD-based compute in phases from late 2026 through 2028, targeting 15 MW cumulative by end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Rackspace had been “targeting a near-term definitive agreement” and urged investors to watch for “signed vs. still MOU” and “committed megawatts.”

description: The preview highlighted the expected roughly $75 million initial AI deployment capex but treated its financing as an open dilution question. Management said financing is planned largely through asset-backed and OEM/equipment facilities secured by the hardware.
fact_evidence: The first approximately 2 MW deployment “requires approximately $75 million in capital expenditures, with financing planned largely through asset-backed and OEM/equipment facilities collateralized by the hardware.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$75M initial deployment capex” and called the funding mix a question, saying “ATM shares issued to date and funding plan” and whether GPU capex gets “debt, ATM, or vendor financing” were key issues.

description: Despite Q2 negative free cash flow and the preview’s emphasis on cash burn, management maintained full-year free-cash-flow guidance of $50–70 million and said generation should accelerate in the second half.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $48 million” in Q2, while the company “maintains full-year free cash flow guidance of $50-70 million, expecting generation to accelerate in the second half.”

description: The company repurchased $11.2 million of senior notes during the quarter, an additional capital-allocation action not anticipated in the preview. It reduces debt, but the call facts also show limited cash and negative quarterly free cash flow.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $11.2 million in senior notes during the quarter” and ended the quarter with “$111 million in cash and $202 million in total liquidity.”

description: Q2 product revenue of $25.1 million was a strong sequential rebound and beat the preview’s lower $22.9 million consensus, but it remained below the higher $27.8 million estimate. The result was also well above the preview’s implied guidance floor of more than $19.9 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net product revenue reached $25.1 million” and reflected “a meaningful quarter-over-quarter rebound from Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$22.9M” and “$27.8M,” and said the implied guidance floor was “>$19.9M.”

description: The company secured about $90 million in non-dilutive funding, sharply exceeding the preview’s expected quarter-end cash of $145–150 million and easing the anticipated financing pressure. The resulting $201.4 million pro forma cash balance is expected to fund operations into the second half of 2027.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $90 million in non-dilutive funding” included a “$50 million initial draw” from royalty financing and a “$15 million Copiktra sales milestone”; pro forma Q2 cash was “$201.4 million,” expected to fund operations “into the second half of 2027 without needing additional capital.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 cash near “$145–150M,” described the funding clock as loud, and flagged a financing as a key question.

description: Quarterly operating expenses came in above the preview’s watch range: the preview expected SG&A to remain around $22 million and said total opex above roughly $66–68 million would pressure the runway narrative. The call cited $27.4 million of SG&A and $41.3 million of R&D, or $68.7 million combined.
fact_evidence: “R&D expenses rose to $41.3 million” and “SG&A held roughly flat at $27.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited SG&A guided “flat ~$22M” and warned that “anything meaningfully above ~$66–68M” in total opex would pressure runway.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The comprehensive VS-7375 data update is now expected in October, later than the preview’s H1 2026 timing for a safety/efficacy update. The call did specify a broad update across pancreatic, lung, and colorectal cohorts, with an early look at durability.
fact_evidence: “A comprehensive VS-7375 data update is expected in October,” including response rates across three cohorts and “an early look at durability.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for the TARGET-D 101 “safety/efficacy update guided for H1 2026,” while also noting meaningful data sets could come in H2.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: VS-7375 received FDA Fast Track designation for non-small cell lung cancer, an indication-specific regulatory milestone the preview did not anticipate. The preview had referred to Fast Track for pancreatic cancer instead.
fact_evidence: VS-7375 “received FDA fast-track designation for non-small cell lung cancer.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “FDA Fast Track in 1L and ≥2L pancreatic.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The company reported that all three VS-7375 dose-expansion cohorts had completed target enrollment, a concrete enrollment milestone not flagged in the preview.
fact_evidence: “VS-7375 completed target enrollment in all three dose-expansion cohorts.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management provided a specific response-rate and durability guidepost for accelerated approval—about a 30% overall response rate with at least six months of durability. The preview discussed upcoming data but did not give this threshold, adding a new numerical benchmark for the program.
fact_evidence: Management cited a “~30% overall response rate with at least six months durability” as the guidepost for FDA accelerated approval across the three lead indications.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management reported considerable inbound strategic interest and progress toward a partnership, but did not announce a deal. The new funding also means the company does not feel pressure to rush into a partnership or equity financing at the current stock price.
fact_evidence: Management said it was “advancing a partnership” and had “considerable inbound strategic interest,” while the new funding removes pressure to rush into a partnership or equity financing.
expectation_evidence: The preview called a partnership announcement “not expected,” while identifying partnership activity as a “live, underappreciated catalyst.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview identified copper as the least-visible metal and highlighted the need for confidence in volume guidance. On the call, Royal Gold said copper and other metals were trending around or above the top of guidance, with the new Antamina royalty contributing $26 million in the first half.
fact_evidence: “Copper and other metals are trending around or above the top end of guidance ranges,” driven largely by the Antamina NPI royalty, which generated “$26 million in the first half versus $16-17 million annually in 2023-2024.”
expectation_evidence: “Copper looks like the line with the least visibility.”

description: The preview expected Royal Gold to reduce its Hod Maden stake, but the call also described a favorable exchange for additional royalty interests and a remaining base CapEx commitment of roughly $65 million after the Q2 funding. That gives more detail on the reduced ownership and future funding exposure than the preview provided.
fact_evidence: Royal Gold reduced its Hod Maden equity interest “from 30% to 15% in exchange for additional royalty interests,” with its remaining base CapEx commitment “reduced to roughly $65 million after funding $70 million in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Hod Maden resolution — the 30%→15% stake reduction was promised ‘in the near term’”; the preview also cited “$120M of Hod Maden and Warintza funding.”

description: The preview said Relief Canyon obligations had been settled but did not anticipate an acceleration of stream ounces. The call reported that advanced delivery added about $22 million of Q2 revenue and delivered 1,175 more ounces this year than originally scheduled.
fact_evidence: “The advanced delivery of Relief Canyon stream ounces added approximately $22 million in incremental revenue this quarter, delivering 1,175 more ounces this year than originally scheduled.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Relief Canyon obligations settled” among the pre-disclosed cash items.

description: The preview discussed buybacks and debt reduction but did not flag a dividend increase. The call reported a dividend at an annual rate of $1.90 per share, 6% higher than last year.
fact_evidence: Royal Gold “paid $40 million in dividends at an annual rate of $1.90 per share (6% higher than last year).”

description: Chemours reported that Q2 adjusted EBITDA exceeded expectations, helped by stronger operations, improved APM product mix, lower corporate costs, and Titanium Technologies pricing strength. That outperformance contrasts with the preview’s $220–250 million Q2 EBITDA guidance range as the expected benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeded expectations due to stronger operations, improved APM product mix, lower corporate costs and pricing strength in Titanium Technologies.”
expectation_evidence: “Consolidated Adj. EBITDA $220–250M.”

description: The full-year outlook was reset lower: adjusted EBITDA guidance is now $775–825 million rather than the preview’s $800–900 million range, and sales growth is now 1–5% rather than 3–5%. This weakens the expected H2 contribution that the preview identified as the central issue.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for net sales growth of 1-5% over 2025 and adjusted EBITDA of $775-825 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 unchanged: sales +3–5%, Adj. EBITDA $800–900M.”

description: TSS is expected to face a pronounced sequential slowdown in Q3, with sales down mid-teens to 20% and EBITDA of $125–140 million. The preview highlighted TSS as the key swing factor and softer residential HVAC demand, but did not flag this scale or duration of aftermarket destocking, which is expected to persist through Q1 2027.
fact_evidence: “TSS Q3 net sales are guided to decline sequentially by mid-teens to 20% with adjusted EBITDA of $125-140 million”; aftermarket destocking headwinds are “expected to persist through Q1 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is peak cooling season and TSS carries ~90% of guided segment EBITDA”; “Watch whether the $210–225M TSS guide holds.”

description: Q2 sales came in slightly below expectations because residential AC demand was softer, while the preview’s consensus revenue estimates sat at or near the top of the company’s guided sequential range. The direction was weaker than expected, though the reported shortfall was described as slight.
fact_evidence: “Net sales came in slightly below expectations on softer residential AC demand.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $1.67B” (Zacks) and “$1.66B” (Investing.com); “Consensus revenue sits at/near the top of the guided sequential range.”

description: The company raised its full-year free-cash-flow-conversion outlook to above 25%, compared with the preview’s expectation of more than 20%; Q2 conversion was already above 40%.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 free cash flow conversion guided above 25% and Q2 already above 40%.”
expectation_evidence: “FCF conversion >20%.”

description: Chemours repaid nearly $270 million of its 2028 euro term loan—$103 million more than it had previously communicated—but now describes its year-end leverage target as approximately 3.8x. That repayment is stronger than the preview’s stated deleveraging setup, while the target is a little less ambitious than the preview’s expectation of below 3.8x.
fact_evidence: “Chemours repaid nearly $270 million of its 2028 euro term loan in Q2, $103 million more than previously communicated, and targets net leverage of approximately 3.8x adjusted EBITDA by year-end 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Deleveraging. 4.9x → <3.8x by year-end requires both the H2 EBITDA ramp and cash conversion.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Chemours reported a 70% year-over-year increase in product trials and initial nominal sales of two-phase liquid-cooling products. The preview had identified cooling-product commercialization as a watch item, but these early trial and sales milestones were not part of its stated expectations.
fact_evidence: “Product trials increased 70% year-over-year and Chemours recorded initial nominal sales of two-phase liquid cooling products for sampling.”
expectation_evidence: “APM: post-outage run-rate, semiconductor/data-center order conversion, Opteon 2P50 two-phase immersion cooling commercialization (2CRSi JDA).”

description: The preview centered on a quantified FY2027 revenue and adjusted operating-income outlook, but the reported outlook specifies revenue per enrollment, margins, and expense ratios without giving an overall revenue or adjusted operating-income range. That leaves the main forecast question the preview highlighted unanswered in the reported facts.
fact_evidence: Management guided FY2027 revenue per enrollment to be flat to up slightly, gross margins flattish, and CapEx/SG&A ratios roughly flat.
expectation_evidence: “FY2027 revenue and adjusted OI guidance — the whole ballgame”; the preview also said that guidance being deferred would be “the single worst outcome.”

description: Stride reported FY2026 gross margin of 37.8%, above the preview’s 37.0–37.4% target for exiting the year, even though margin was down 140 basis points year over year. The reported level was modestly better than the preview’s stated target.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell 140 basis points to 37.8% due to platform investments.”
expectation_evidence: “Management targeted 37.0–37.4% exiting FY26.”

description: The preview said buybacks were conspicuously absent from recent commentary and identified a new buyback signal as a potential positive. Stride had already repurchased about $189 million in FY2026, retained $311 million under its authorization, extended that authorization, and the new CEO expressed intent to pursue opportunistic repurchases.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately $189 million of stock in FY2026, with $311 million remaining under an authorization now extended to October 31, 2027”; the new CEO “signaled intent to pursue opportunistic buybacks.”
expectation_evidence: “A buyback authorization at $78 would be the cleanest signal of board confidence and is conspicuously absent from recent commentary.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Enrollment signals were not uniformly strong: applications were slightly behind last year, contrary to the preview’s report that application volumes had been strong relative to historic levels. Conversion and reregistration were ahead, but management also warned that Q1 count-date comparisons will be tougher because year-end carryover was lower.
fact_evidence: “Applications are tracking slightly behind last year, but conversion rates and reregistration activity are running ahead of the prior year”; Q1 comparisons “will be tougher due to lower year-end carryover from moderated FY2026 in-year enrollment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had described application volumes as “strong relative to historic levels” and identified whether applications converted as a key question.

description: The preview called for a quantified account of Roscoe’s enrollment loss and recapture. The reported facts say affected Texas families are being redistributed to other programs but give no recapture count or percentage, leaving that key issue unquantified.
fact_evidence: “Roscoe Independent School District declined to renew its Lone Star Online Academy contract citing performance issues, and Stride is redistributing affected Texas families to other programs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “Quantified Lone Star Online Academy hit” as a key metric and asked “How much did they recapture?”; it said anything above ~40% recaptured would be a positive surprise.

description: Management explicitly said the CEO change was intended to accelerate growth, not prompted by a disappointing fall enrollment outlook. That addresses a concern raised by the preview, though it does not resolve the mixed enrollment indicators.
fact_evidence: “Management stated the transition was driven by a desire to accelerate growth rather than any disappointing fall enrollment outlook.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified fall enrollment and the new CEO’s agenda as the central event questions and noted the possibility of a new-CEO reset after the leadership change.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview expected quarter-end cash of roughly $125–135 million, with at least $130 million as the watch-point; cash instead fell to $105.3 million. About $39 million of the decline was tied to TSA obligations, which management said should diminish into 2027.
fact_evidence: “Cash, cash equivalents and investments fell to $105.3 million at end of Q2 from $167 million at Q1, with about $39 million of the decline due to TSA obligations expected to diminish into 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 exit cash at roughly $125–135M”; the ranked cash metric called for “≥$130M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview cited casdozokitug first-line HCC data as guided for mid-2026 and looked for disclosure on the call or a hard near-term date. Management instead said only about half of the 72-patient study had undergone three scans, pushing initial data availability to Q4 2026.
fact_evidence: “The casdozokitug first-line HCC triplet study is 72 patients, but only about 50% have had 3 scans, pushing initial data availability to Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the study as guided for “mid-2026” and said the bar was “Data disclosed on the call, or a hard date (‘Q3’, named medical meeting).”

description: The preview expected FY2026 revenue consensus of $73.02 million, while management gave a full-year 2026 revenue range of $57–62 million. That is materially below the consensus figure the preview said depended partly on non-product revenue.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $57-62 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY2026 revenue: $73.02M” and said consensus required “~$16–20M of embedded non-product revenue.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview looked for tagmokitug initial data around mid-2026; management now projects formal disclosure of mature head-and-neck data in October. The call also characterized the available head-and-neck data as immature and uncleaned, so the fuller readout is later and less ready than the preview’s timing suggested.
fact_evidence: “Formal disclosure of mature head and neck squamous cell carcinoma tagmokitug data is projected for October 2026”; early data “remains immature and uncleaned.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said tagmokitug initial data had been guided for “mid-2026” and listed “Any efficacy signal + confirmation ESCC/CRC hold 2H26” as the bar.

description: The preview described a roughly $45 million quarterly cost base; Q2 R&D and SG&A together were $42.4 million, and management guided to $170–175 million of combined full-year OpEx. That points to lower costs than the preview’s run-rate assumption.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D from continuing operations fell to $21.4 million from $26.3 million year-over-year, and SG&A dropped to $21.0 million from $26.0 million”; “Full-year 2026 combined OpEx is guided to $170-175 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview characterized the loss as a function of “a stable ~$45M quarterly cost base.”

description: The preview discussed the $75 million aggregate UDENYCA sales milestones as one possible source of non-product revenue embedded in FY2026 consensus. The $37.5 million Q2 earn-out was not achieved, although it remains eligible in Q3; the preview did not specify Q2 attainment as certain.
fact_evidence: “A $37.5 million UDENYCA milestone earn-out was not achieved in Q2 based on buyer-reported results, but remains eligible for achievement in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 consensus implied non-product revenue from “BD upfront, license, or the Intas milestone.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview did not flag that the tagmokitug head-and-neck and colorectal cohorts might already be fully enrolled. Management reported that both cohorts, along with the CADILYZE study, were fully enrolled, reducing enrollment uncertainty even though the tagmokitug data are still pending.
fact_evidence: “Three studies are now fully enrolled: the CADILYZE first-line HCC study, and the tagmokitug head and neck squamous cell and colorectal cancer cohorts.”

description: Q1 revenue was $30.6 million, about 19% above the $25.67 million consensus estimate. The preview’s expected range was $24–27 million, so the result also cleared its base case and landed in its bull scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 total revenues rose 175% year-over-year to $30.6 million from $11.1 million,” driven primarily by a “$19.4 million increase” from newly acquired revenue streams.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $25.67M”; the preview’s base scenario expected “$24–27M.”

description: The direct operating margin came in at 35%, below the preview’s 40% expected level and its warning threshold of roughly 38%. The preview attributed margin pressure to lower-margin media services, while the call specified that the new ad-tech stream carries an average 79% revenue-share expense paid to supply partners.
fact_evidence: “Direct operating margin fell to 35% from 57% a year earlier,” largely because the new advertising technology revenue stream carried an “average 79% revenue-share expense paid to supply partners.”
expectation_evidence: “Direct operating margin ≥40%”; the preview said “Below ~38% signals the acquired revenue is lower-quality than modeled.”

description: The net loss attributable to common stockholders widened to $5.8 million, worse than the preview’s implied loss of about $3.3 million from consensus EPS. The preview flagged that a loss materially worse than $0.14 per share would put more pressure on the rest of the fiscal year.
fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common stockholders widened to $5.8 million from $3.6 million,” driven by higher SG&A, depreciation and amortization, earnout fair-value adjustments, and interest costs following the acquisitions.
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | -$0.14”; “Implied net loss | ~-$3.3M.”

description: Management identified more than $13 million in annual cost reductions, above the preview’s expected $7.5 million cost program. The preview expected the remaining $5.5 million of that program by September; the call also described $5.5 million more from product streamlining, with cuts expected to be materially complete by September 30.
fact_evidence: “Over $13 million in annual cost reductions,” including “$8.3 million already cut” and “$5.5 million more from product streamlining,” with cuts expected materially complete by September 30.
expectation_evidence: “The remaining $5.5M was due by end of Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Technology now accounts for more than 60% of consolidated revenue, exceeding the preview’s cited target of more than 50% technology-based revenue and making technology the company’s largest revenue source.
fact_evidence: “Technology now represents more than 60% of consolidated revenue, positioning it as the company's largest and most recurring revenue source.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “targets >50% technology-based.”

description: Management gave the new audio ad-tech product a roughly $12 million annual run-rate target by fiscal year-end, a concrete target not anticipated in the preview. The preview mentioned VAUDIO only as a possible incremental catalyst.
fact_evidence: The new “‘audio’ ad-tech product targeting CTV is guided to a roughly $12 million annual run rate by fiscal year-end,” targeting 5%–7% of the $3 billion annual podcast ad spend.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Liquidity remained tight and the working-capital deficit was larger than the preview’s stated $12.2 million, although cash was above the preview’s FY26 exit balance and operating cash flow improved substantially. The call also specified that $18 million of deferred consideration is payable in equity.
fact_evidence: “Liquidity remains tight with only $4.3 million cash, a $12.5 million revolver, and negative $18.9 million net working capital (including $18 million of deferred consideration payable in equity), though operating cash flow improved by more than $13 million year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave “$3.4M cash” and working capital of “-$12.2M (though $12.2M of that is IndiCue deferred consideration settleable in equity).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed low all-in costs and low box-office breakevens for the upcoming theatrical slate, details the preview did not provide. Each of the three releases carries under-$5 million in all-in costs and a box-office breakeven below $10 million.
fact_evidence: The three upcoming theatrical releases “each carry under-$5 million all-in costs with sub-$10 million box office breakevens.”

description: Digital revenue grew 60.8%, far ahead of the preview’s roughly 11% growth estimate, and rose to 19% of gross revenue from 14% a year earlier. This was a much stronger digital contribution than expected.
fact_evidence: “Blended digital revenue surged 60.8% in Q2 and 76.4% for the first six months, lifting digital to 19% of gross revenue versus 14% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Digital revenue … My Base Est. … ~$5.0M … ~+11%.”

description: Operating income was $623,000, well above the preview’s estimate of a $1.1 million operating loss. The reported result was about $1.7 million better than that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Operating income dropped to just $623,000.”
expectation_evidence: “Operating income … My Base Est. … −$1.1M.”

description: Traditional revenue was weaker across the board: local, national, and nontraditional each declined by double digits. The preview focused on the total-revenue outlook and expected digital growth, but did not anticipate this degree of broad weakness in traditional lines.
fact_evidence: “Traditional revenue lines all posted double-digit declines in Q2, with local down 11.2%, national down 25%, and nontraditional down 16.4% year-over-year.”

description: Station operating income was $3 million, below the preview’s $3.4 million estimate, while station operating expense rose 5.4% rather than the modeled 2.3%. Hiring nine sales and digital campaign managers added roughly $357,000 of quarterly expense.
fact_evidence: “Station operating income fell to $3 million”; “Station operating expense rose 5.4% in Q2 (3.9% excluding noncash tower rent)”; hiring “9 sales managers and digital campaign managers” added “roughly $357,000 in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Station operating expense … My Base Est. … $22.7M … +2.3%”; “At −7.5% revenue and +2% opex, Q2 SOI goes to ~$3.4M.”

description: Saga’s Q3 revenue was pacing down mid-single digits, or mid-to-high single digits excluding political, rather than reaching the preview’s better-than-4%-down marker for a materially improved H2 narrative. The reported October pacing of up mid-single digits provides a more positive counterpoint.
fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is pacing down mid-single digits (down mid-to-high single digits excluding political), though monthly trends improved with October pacing up mid-single digits.”
expectation_evidence: “A Q3 pacing better than −4% would materially change the H2 narrative.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview identified $2.5 million or more in updated political bookings as a de-risking outcome; the call reported $1.1 million sold for the rest of the year. That leaves the reported forward sales figure short of that marker, despite political revenue being higher in Q2.
fact_evidence: “Gross political revenue reached $450,000 in Q2 versus $50,000 a year ago, with an additional $1.1 million sold for the rest of the year.”
expectation_evidence: “An updated booked figure of $2.5M+ would de-risk H2; a figure still near $1.4M would suggest a weak midterm cycle.”

description: Management lowered its full-year corporate G&A outlook to $11.8–$12 million from $12.3 million, rather than holding the roughly flat $12.3 million level used in the preview’s assumptions.
fact_evidence: “Corporate G&A to fall to $11.8-$12 million from $12.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Corporate G&A held at guided $12.3M/yr flat.”

description: Saga repaid its full $5 million revolver and terminated the credit agreement, reducing cash and short-term investments to $22.9 million. The preview described the $5 million debt and $27.8 million of cash but did not anticipate the repayment and facility termination; the move reduces debt but also cash and borrowing flexibility.
fact_evidence: “The company terminated its credit agreement after repaying the full $5 million revolver, reducing cash and short-term investments to $22.9 million as of August 10 from $27.8 million at June 30.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash + short-term investments: … $27.8M (5/4/26). Long-term debt only $5.0M.”

description: Saga reported selling six noncore properties for more than $4 million since Q4 2025, including a Sarasota house and a Portland tower site. These additional asset monetizations were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company has monetized noncore assets, selling 6 properties for over $4 million since Q4 2025 (including a $1.7 million Sarasota house and a $1 million Portland tower site).”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Karyopharm said FDA feedback supports using week-24 SVR35 as the basis for the myelofibrosis sNDA: the agency indicated SVR35 appears to qualify as a reasonably likely surrogate for overall survival. That is more supportive than the preview’s central concern about the missed symptom-score co-primary and its request for FDA clarity on the endpoint risk.
fact_evidence: “The FDA provided written feedback indicating that SVR35 appears to qualify as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for overall survival, supporting the planned sNDA submission based on week 24 SVR35 data.”
expectation_evidence: “SENTRY hit SVR35 decisively … but missed on total symptom score, the second co-primary. The label risk from that miss is now the central bull-case variable.”

description: The reported $33.4 million of Q2 revenue exceeded the preview’s $32.19 million consensus estimate, although it was below the preview’s optimistic $34–37 million bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue declined to $33.4 million from $37.9 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 Consensus” total revenue: “$32.19M.”

description: U.S. Xpovio revenue was $30.8 million, above the preview’s estimate of about $29 million and higher than the roughly flat year-over-year trend it expected. This was a stronger commercial result than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “U.S. Xpovio net product revenue grew to $30.8 million from $29.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “US XPOVIO net product rev.”: “~$29M”; the preview described the business as “roughly flat YoY.”

description: Karyopharm reaffirmed its $130–150 million full-year revenue guidance rather than trimming it to $130–140 million, as the preview expected. The retained upper end is a more favorable outlook than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $130-150 million.”
expectation_evidence: “A trim to $130–140M is expected and largely discounted.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The call made the September term-loan payment risk more immediate: paying the $15.8 million installment without new financing or a waiver would breach the minimum-liquidity covenant and trigger a default. The preview noted the deferred September 10 payment and covenant but did not state this explicit consequence.
fact_evidence: “A $15.8 million principal payment is due September 10, 2026” and paying it “without additional financing or a waiver would breach the $10 million minimum liquidity covenant and trigger an event of default.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted the June installment was deferred to “Sept 10, 2026” and identified the “Min. liquidity $10M through Oct 10, 2026” covenant, but did not spell out that making the payment without financing or a waiver would trigger default.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management gave a specific potential scale for the myelofibrosis opportunity—up to about $1 billion in peak annual U.S. revenue, based on roughly 4,000 newly treated frontline patients per year. The preview discussed the sNDA as a catalyst but did not include this market or revenue estimate.
fact_evidence: “Management estimates Selinexor plus ruxolitinib could generate up to approximately $1 billion in peak annual U.S. revenue, targeting roughly 4,000 newly treated frontline patients annually among about 20,000 U.S. myelofibrosis patients.”

expectation_evidence: The preview listed GSV consensus of “~$0.97–1.00B” and implied year-over-year performance of “~flat to -3%.”

fact_evidence: “Upwork plans to boost marketing spend by an incremental $5-10 million in the back half after cost per new contract start improved 22% quarter over quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to confirm that “go-to-market wasn't damaged by a 24% headcount cut.”

description: The company reported a new $150 million revolving credit facility to repay its August 2026 convertible notes. The preview identified the converts as a capital-allocation issue but did not anticipate this refinancing facility.
fact_evidence: “[The company] secur[ed] a new $150 million revolving credit facility to repay August 2026 convertible notes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$361.0M converts” and said to watch “buyback pace against $256.1M remaining and only $12.9M of Q1 FCF, plus $361M of converts.”

fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were $50.8 million as of June 30, 2026,” excluding “the net proceeds from the July 2026 royalty financing.”

description: Watts raised FY2026 organic sales growth guidance to 8%–11%, well above the prior 2%–6% range and the preview’s expected buy-side range of 4%–7%. Reported sales growth guidance also rose to 14%–17% from 8%–12%.
fact_evidence: Management raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 8%-11%, a more than 5-point increase to the prior midpoint, and reported sales growth guidance to 14%-17%.
expectation_evidence: Full-year FY2026 guidance ... organic +2% to +6%; reported sales +8% to +12%. The preview also says buy-side wants +4–7%.

fact_evidence: Q2 2026 organic sales rose 12% to a record $763 million (up 19% reported), driven by data center growth, favorable pricing, and pull-forward demand.
expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $725.8–726.0M; organic sales growth: ~+6% (guide midpoint). Company guidance for Q2: organic sales +4% to +8%.

expectation_evidence: Company guidance for Q2 ... adjusted operating margin 20.0%–20.6%; consensus implied ~20.3% and a 130 bps year-over-year decline.

fact_evidence: Data center sales more than tripled year-over-year and represented 8% of total sales in the first half of 2026, up from just 3% of sales in the prior full year. Full-year data center sales are now expected to reach mid- to high single digits as a percentage of company sales.
expectation_evidence: The preview highlights data center revenue growth and the “high double-digit for the year” reaffirmation, and says the Street wants a dollar figure or revenue %.

expectation_evidence: Management is pointing at a >$1B addressable market.

expectation_evidence: The preview flags “order-timing lumpiness” as something to watch in data center commentary.

fact_evidence: APMEA organic sales grew 31% led by China data center demand.
expectation_evidence: APMEA Q2 estimate: ~$45M; “Saudi Cast contribution; conflict headwind concentrated here.”

expectation_evidence: The preview says the ≥90% conversion target requires a large H2 catch-up and that “a second weak FCF quarter would be a real negative.”

expectation_evidence: The preview says “Residential remains soft” and calls for watching whether the core is decelerating underneath data center growth.

expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus $149.75M”; “My estimate: $150.5M.”
