description: WRAP reported $2.1 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $1.7–1.9 million estimate and its roughly $2.0 million whisper. The 103% year-over-year increase also exceeded the preview’s modeled 75–85% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue increased 103% year-over-year to $2.1 million from $1.0 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q2'26E (my base) $1.7–1.9M”; “Revenue vs. ~$1.8M (my base) / ~$2.0M whisper.”

description: Gross margin was approximately 75%, far above the preview’s 58–63% estimate and opposite its expectation of year-over-year compression. The preview had identified services mix as central to margin recovery, but the reported margin expanded even though subscription revenue was still ahead rather than realized.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit rose 217% to $1.5 million with gross margin expanding to approximately 75% from approximately 48% a year earlier”; subscription revenue is “still ahead of the company rather than realized.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … Q2'26E (my base) 58–63% (down Y/Y)”; “the entire margin-recovery thesis rests on services mix rising.”

description: The $2.3 million net loss was substantially narrower than the preview’s modeled $4.3–4.8 million loss. The year-over-year improvement is less pronounced after accounting for the prior-year warrant charge, but the reported loss still beat the preview estimate by a wide margin.
fact_evidence: “Net loss improved 39% to $2.3 million from $3.7 million, though the prior year included a $0.9 million non-recurring noncash warrant fair-value loss.”
expectation_evidence: “Net loss … Q2'26E (my base) $(4.3)–(4.8)M.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management identified a larger potential customer pool for BolaWrap than the preview described: the ATF classification was said to open access to more than 1.2 million licensed private security officers. The preview discussed the ruling mainly as easing agency procurement, not this private-security opportunity.
fact_evidence: The July ATF determination classified BolaWrap 150 as a restraint/rescue tool, “unlocking access to the private security market of over 1.2 million licensed security officers—larger than the entire U.S. law enforcement population.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the ruling’s “practical effect” was that “federal/agency procurement collapses from a weapons-appropriation path to a standard non-lethal/safety-equipment line.”

description: Management pointed to 11 active reopened DOJ grant programs that could fund BolaWrap and related offerings, an additional funding route not identified in the preview. The programs may help the company’s mostly small and midsized department customers, though no dollar amount or resulting orders were given.
fact_evidence: “Management identified 11 active reopened DOJ grant programs that could fund BolaWrap, body cameras, de-escalation training, and virtual training for its predominantly small and midsized department customers.”

description: The company said Chile business is excluded from its 2026 growth forecast because of a Chilean government funding gap. The preview discussed the 100% growth target and the risk of order timing, but did not flag this specific funding constraint.
fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed roughly 100% revenue growth for 2026, “with Chile business excluded from the forecast due to a Chilean government funding gap.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the target implied “~$10.4M for FY26” and highlighted that it required a step-change in H2; it did not mention Chile funding.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Liabilities fell to $2.0 million from $3.9 million after WRAP terminated its former office lease, a balance-sheet improvement the preview did not discuss. Cash at $4.8 million was within the preview’s $4.5–5.5 million estimate, so the surprise is the liability reduction rather than the cash balance.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents grew to $4.8 million at June 30, 2026 from $3.5 million at year-end 2025, while total liabilities fell to $2.0 million from $3.9 million after terminating the former office lease.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash (period end) … Q2'26E (my base) $4.5–5.5M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $2.1 million, well above the preview’s $1.4 million estimate. Adjusted net income was also $838,000, rather than the expected near-break-even to small loss.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA rose 63% year-over-year to $2.1 million from $1.3 million,” and “adjusted net income” was $838,000 ($0.04 per share).
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 base estimate was “Adjusted EBITDA $1.4M”; its EPS estimate was “$(0.01) – $0.00.”

description: SPAR returned to GAAP profitability, reporting $0.02 per diluted share instead of the preview’s expected small loss to break-even. The preview had expected GAAP EPS of $(0.01) to $0.00.
fact_evidence: “SPAR Group returned to profitability in Q2 2026 for the first time since Q1 2025,” with GAAP net income of $409,000, or $0.02 per diluted share.

description: Quarterly revenue was $36.9 million, above the preview’s $34.5 million base estimate, even though revenue still declined year over year. The preview had modeled a 10.7% decline; the reported decline was 4.5%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net revenues declined 4.5% year-over-year to $36.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 base was “$34.5M (–10.7% YoY).”

description: Full-year gross-margin guidance was raised by one percentage point at both ends, to 21.5%–23.5%, from the previously stated 20.5%–22.5% range. This was a more favorable outlook than the preview’s cited company guidance.
fact_evidence: The company maintained full-year gross-margin guidance of “21.5%–23.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed company FY2026 gross-margin guidance of “20.5%–22.5%.”

description: Quarterly SG&A was higher than the preview expected: $6.8 million versus a $6.3 million estimate and a stated buy-side benchmark of no more than $6.5 million. The $543,000 of one-time costs partly explains the gap, but does not eliminate it.
fact_evidence: “SG&A fell to $6.8 million from $7.9 million year-over-year, including $543,000 in one-time costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 base estimate was “SG&A ~$6.3M,” and its buy-side benchmark was “SG&A ≤ $6.5M.”

description: Despite the quarterly SG&A coming in above estimate, the full-year SG&A range was cut substantially, to $21–24 million from the previously stated $25.5–26.5 million. Management also pointed to an underlying annual run rate of roughly $20 million.
fact_evidence: The company maintained full-year SG&A guidance of “$21–24 million,” while management guided underlying run-rate SG&A toward “roughly $20 million annually.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY2026 SG&A guidance of “$25.5–26.5M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash flow deteriorated rather than normalizing: SPAR used $8.7 million in cash in the quarter, compared with $3.9 million used in Q1. The preview specifically flagged cash flow as a risk to watch and said Q2 needed to show working-capital normalization.
fact_evidence: “Net cash used by operating activities was $8.7 million for the quarter,” reflecting working-capital timing tied to merchandising-business growth.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 operating cash flow of “–$3.9M” and said “Q2 must show working-capital normalization.”

description: SPAR disclosed a new ongoing technology agreement with ReposiTrak costing $151,500 per month to re-platform its technology and develop a scan-based trading proposition. The preview focused on whether the partnership was generating revenue, not on this recurring cost commitment.
fact_evidence: “SPAR entered an IT agreement with Repositrak costing $151,500 per month to re-platform its technology and develop a scan-based trading proposition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the ReposiTrak partnership was “generating revenue yet” and discussed the share issuance and ownership stake.

description: The call disclosed ongoing legal matters involving Robert Brown, which were not specifically anticipated in the preview’s discussion of board and governance tensions. Management characterized the matters as non-material.
fact_evidence: The company disclosed “ongoing legal matters involving Robert Brown that management deemed non-material.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed governance concerns, the board reset, and founder Robert G. Brown’s public pressure on the board, but did not mention ongoing legal matters.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview treated a clean FDA review as a bull case and flagged an additional-information request or clock stop as a key risk. Management reported that the FDA sent an additional information letter in July and requires an SIR alignment meeting before the data package can be resubmitted, although the company still targets authorization later in 2026.
fact_evidence: “Since the March FDA submission, the company roughly tripled its collected study samples and received an additional information letter in July, requiring an SIR alignment meeting before resubmitting its data package.” Management continues to target authorization “later in 2026,” while cautioning that government review timing is not fully within its control.
expectation_evidence: The preview said a clean “on track, no AI request” would be a bull-case outcome, and that “any commentary on Additional Information (AI) requests, clock stops, or a shifted timeline” was the largest swing factor.

description: Management raised its expected second-half cash burn to about $8 million per quarter, rather than the roughly $6 million per quarter the preview said was the prior expectation. The increase reflects regulatory, registry, and commercial-launch costs.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its second-half cash burn guidance to approximately $8 million per quarter, up from a prior expectation of roughly $6 million per quarter, due to regulatory, registry, and commercial launch costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided H2 burn “back toward ~$6M/quarter” and highlighted reaffirmation of “~$6M/qtr H2 burn” as a key item to watch.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The call introduced a $2 billion estimate for the kidney-testing opportunity, with potential to grow through more frequent surveillance, therapy monitoring, and additional organ indications. The preview discussed reimbursement and the transplant revenue ramp but gave no comparable TAM estimate.
fact_evidence: “The company estimates a $2 billion total addressable market based on a conservative 2 tests per year per kidney patient, which grows further with higher surveillance frequency, therapy monitoring, and expanded organ indications.”

description: The preview implied roughly 7–8% same-park revenue growth, based on the fresh $914 million revenue estimate and the expected divestiture-related reduction. The call reported same-park net revenue growth of only 2%, to about $864 million, despite 44 fewer operating days.
fact_evidence: “Same-park basis, Q2 2026 attendance rose 4% … and net revenue increased 2% to approximately $864 million, despite 44 fewer operating days.”
expectation_evidence: “Flat reported revenue on a portfolio ~$65–75M smaller in Q2 revenue terms implies ~7–8% same-park revenue growth”; Guggenheim revenue estimate: “$914M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin fell short of the preview’s bar: same-park adjusted EBITDA was $249 million, versus the preview’s $288 million estimate, while the implied same-park margin was about 29% rather than the preview’s roughly 31.5% estimate and expectation of more than 30%.
fact_evidence: “Same-park adjusted EBITDA increased 7% to $249 million in Q2 2026, with margins expanding roughly 120 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: Guggenheim adjusted EBITDA estimate: “$288M”; the preview estimated “$288M on $914M” revenue, or “31.5%,” and said “if EBITDA margin does not print north of 30%” the cost thesis would be in question.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Per-capita spending declined slightly rather than reaching the preview’s expected roughly 4% increase. Higher average prices on single-day and combined pass/membership products did not prevent the overall per-capita result from being weighed down by pass mix.
fact_evidence: “Both single-day and combined pass/membership products [were] yielding higher average prices, while per capita spending declined less than 1% due to pass mix effects.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “per cap ~$65 (+4%)” and flagged admissions yield as a key debate, noting that “admissions per cap” was +3% in Q1.

description: The divested parks removed more year-ago revenue than the preview’s estimated portfolio headwind: $86 million rather than roughly $65–75 million. That made the reported revenue comparison more exposed to the portfolio change than the preview had modeled.
fact_evidence: “The sale of 7 noncore parks removed approximately $86 million of Q2 2025 revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a portfolio “~$65–75M smaller in Q2 revenue terms.”

description: Management gave a constructive quarterly EBITDA outlook despite the preview’s emphasis on uncertainty around the July update: it expects year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth in both Q3 and Q4, with the larger opportunity in Q4. The preview anticipated demand and trading commentary, but not this specific growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management expects adjusted EBITDA to grow year-over-year in both Q3 and Q4 2026, with the larger growth opportunity weighted toward Q4 from Halloween and Holiday in the Park events.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said there was “no formal FY2026 guidance” and that management had chosen to guide on “demand trends, per-caps, cost discipline and liquidity instead.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Q3 operating calendar provides a larger tailwind than the preview discussed: the company plans 66 more operating days than a year earlier. This is a favorable, unanticipated offset to the July holiday timing and wildfire disruptions, though the call did not quantify its financial effect.
fact_evidence: “The company plans 2,133 operating days in Q3 2026, 66 more than the prior year, primarily due to Labor Day timing adding an extra week of summer operations.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Despite the preview’s concern about a weak or merely flat July, management cited a strong attendance day on days not affected by air quality: the company recorded its highest summer attendance day in five years. This is a limited positive datapoint, not a quantified July trend.
fact_evidence: “The company still delivered its highest summer attendance day in five years on unaffected days.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “July flat-to-slightly-up” was the base case and described a “hot start to July and air quality issues from Canadian wildfires” as an existing concern.

description: MEC reported Q2 sales of $163 million, above the preview’s $150.6 million consensus and the company’s $145–155 million guide. That is a clear upside surprise, though organic growth was 9.2% excluding AccuFab.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 net sales rose 23.2% year-over-year to $163 million, with organic sales up 9.2% excluding the AccuFab acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales (consensus) $150.6M”; “Company Q2 guide (sales) $145–155M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was negative despite the preview expecting a positive quarter, and MEC cut full-year free cash flow guidance from $25–35 million to $7–15 million. This is a substantial deterioration from the cash outlook investors were given.
fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was a use of $6.6 million versus $12.5 million provided a year earlier, prompting the company to lower full-year free cash flow guidance to $7-15 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … FCF $25–35M”; “Q2 FCF positive — Q1 was −$6.9M against a $25–35M FY target.”

description: MEC raised its full-year sales outlook to $620–650 million, above the prior $590–620 million range the preview expected it to reaffirm. The higher outlook is positive, although the company did not raise its adjusted EBITDA range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 net sales guidance was raised to $620-650 million while adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained at $52-60 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guidance … sales $590–620M, adj. EBITDA $52–60M”; “Reaffirmation of $590–620M / $52–60M is the base case.”

description: The preview expected launch costs to roll off after Q2 as the margin recovery progressed. Instead, the full-year outlook still includes $5–6 million of launch costs plus $2–3 million of outsourcing costs, with equipment lead times delaying the move of work in-house.
fact_evidence: “Full-year outlook includes $5-6 million of launch-related costs and $2-3 million of outsourcing costs, with new equipment carrying four-to-six-month lead times before work moves in-house.”
expectation_evidence: “The bridge management offers is real — launch costs roll off ($1.2M in Q1, similar guided for Q2)”; the preview also expected the H2 margin step-up to be supported by launch costs rolling off.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage was 2.9x, worse than the preview’s estimated 2.6–2.8x after the offering and above its 2.8x checkpoint. The offering reduced debt, but the reported leverage did not reach the expected post-offering level.
fact_evidence: “Net debt rose to $134.7 million from $71.8 million a year ago, pushing the bank covenant net leverage ratio to 2.9x versus a long-term target of 2.5x.”
expectation_evidence: “Applying ~$93.9M of net proceeds implies roughly $125–130M net debt and ~2.6–2.8x”; “Net leverage ≤ 2.8x — the clearest available positive.”

description: MEC disclosed a substantial capacity expansion plan: about $50 million of incremental investment over two years, plus a possible $25–30 million Southeast facility, to expand beyond its prior $850 million revenue capacity. The preview noted capacity conversion and a possible greenfield as watch items, but did not anticipate this scale of investment.
fact_evidence: “The company plans ~$50 million of incremental investment over two years (plus a potential $25-30 million new Southeast facility) to lift revenue capacity beyond the prior $850 million level, targeting 15%+ IRR and 2-3 year payback.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guidance … capex $15–20M”; “Secondary: capacity conversion pace … any commentary on an eastern-seaboard greenfield.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed that a single new post-acquisition customer awarded MEC more than $55 million this year. The preview discussed pipeline and quarterly award expectations but did not flag a customer award of this size.
fact_evidence: “One new post-acquisition customer alone awarding over $55 million this year.”

description: Purple reported Q2 revenue of $98.3 million, below the preview’s roughly $102.5–$103.9 million expectation. The shortfall was driven primarily by wholesale weakness.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue declined 6.5% year-over-year to $98.3 million from $105.1 million, driven primarily by wholesale weakness.”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: ~$103.9M”; the alternate feed was “~$102.5M.”

description: Purple cut its FY2026 revenue guidance to $420–$440 million from $465–$485 million, a substantial reduction where the preview described reaffirmation as the base case. It maintained adjusted EBITDA guidance despite the revenue cut.
fact_evidence: “The company lowered fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $420–$440 million while maintaining its adjusted EBITDA outlook, trimming the top of its prior range due to wholesale softness.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “FY2026 guidance action” was “reaffirm / trim / withdraw,” and that the base case was “FY guide reaffirmed.”

description: Wholesale revenue fell 19.1%, contrary to the preview’s expectation that the channel would inflect and help carry the second half. Even excluding $5.3 million in incremental customer payments, wholesale was down about 8%.
fact_evidence: “Wholesale revenue fell 19.1% to $37.4 million, though excluding $5.3 million in incremental customer payments (co-op marketing and related-party transactions) the decline was approximately 8%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said wholesale “needs to inflect to carry H2” and noted Q1’s “early traction.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $2.1 million, above the preview’s roughly breakeven threshold and its base-case range of a $2 million loss to $1 million of profit.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved $4.4 million year-over-year to a positive $2.1 million, versus a $2.4 million loss in the prior-year period.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 EBITDA above roughly breakeven keeps the guide credible”; the base case projected “−$2 to +$1M.”

description: Gross margin reached 45.2%, well above the preview’s roughly 38% watch level and its expectation that margins would return toward 40%. A $5.3 million tariff refund and sourcing-driven tariff mitigation helped produce the unusually strong result.
fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin rose about 470 basis points to 45.2%, helped by a $5.3 million tariff refund (100% of applied amount) and sourcing-driven tariff mitigation.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the EBITDA bridge above is impossible without margin back toward 40%” and flagged “Gross margin vs. ~38%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The early customer response to Purple’s mid-June price increases was worse than management expected, raising a demand concern not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Management took an 8–10% price increase across mattresses and pillows in mid-June to offset input inflation, but noted early consumer demand reaction was more negative than expected, with elasticity not fully readable until after Labor Day.”
expectation_evidence: “Early consumer demand reaction was more negative than expected.”

description: The GAAP loss was much smaller than the preview’s roughly $8 million implied loss: Purple reported a $3.2 million loss and a $0.74 per-share loss, versus the preview’s post-split consensus estimate of a $1.84 per-share loss.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed by $14.1 million to $3.2 million, or a loss of $0.74 per share versus $4.01 last year.”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS: −$1.84 post-split” and “Implied GAAP net loss: ~$8M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Showroom comparable-store sales were up 18%, a strong acceleration from the 7% Q1 comps cited in the preview, rather than merely another positive quarter.
fact_evidence: “Showroom revenue jumped 16.6% to $18.4 million with comparable-store sales up 18%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive comps.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “+7% comps in Q1” and said a “fourth consecutive positive quarter matters for the narrative.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $1.16, below the preview’s current consensus of $1.22, rather than meeting the roughly $1.25 working estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was essentially flat at $1.16 versus $1.17.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Adj. EPS $1.22”; “Working center of gravity: Adj. EPS ~$1.25.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $54.2 million, below the preview’s roughly $56 million level needed to keep the full-year bridge credible, although it fell within the preview’s $54–57 million base-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA declined to $54.2 million from $56.2 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EBITDA needs to land at roughly $56M+ to keep the range credible without a back-half hockey stick.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Applebee’s comps were negative 1.8%, a reversal from the preview’s expectation of continued momentum and its base case of positive comps. The preview had highlighted Applebee’s traffic as a risk, but the reported comp was weaker than its expected range.
fact_evidence: “Applebee's posted negative 1.8% comp sales (hurt by a tough April comparison against last year's Sizzlin' Skillets).”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Applebee’s as having “momentum” and gave a base case of “Applebee's +0.5–1.5%”; its bull case expected “+2.5–4%.”

description: Full-year guidance was maintained, but management said results were trending toward the lower end of the range. The preview expected the range to be maintained, while specifically warning that low-end language would effectively amount to a cut.
fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was maintained but management signaled results are trending toward the lower end of the range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Buy-side expects ‘maintained’” and that “anything like ‘toward the low end’ is functionally a cut”; its base case also anticipated “maintained-but-hedged guidance.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half adjusted free cash flow was only $3.7 million, down from $48.7 million a year earlier, rather than showing the sharp recovery the preview said investors needed to see after Q1’s negative $3.0 million. That leaves the preview’s concern about cash generation and the buyback funding more acute.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow collapsed to $3.7 million for the first six months of 2026 from $48.7 million a year earlier,” driven by “higher capex, marketing timing, and compensation/interest payments.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Adj. FCF recovery + Q2 buyback disclosure” and said “If Q2 FCF doesn't recover sharply, the buyback runway—and the entire EPS bridge—comes into question.”

description: Applebee’s commodity inflation was much higher than IHOP’s, adding a specific cost headwind not quantified in the preview: Applebee’s costs rose 8.2%, versus 1.6% at IHOP, with mid-single-digit full-year inflation still expected at Applebee’s.
fact_evidence: “Applebee's commodity costs rose 8.2% (driven by beef and lapping favorable contracts) versus just 1.6% at IHOP, with full-year guidance of mid-single-digit and low-single-digit inflation respectively.”

description: The Q2 buyback was slower than the Q1 pace the preview highlighted: the company bought back $7 million of shares in Q2 versus $22 million in Q1. The new $100 million authorization and $29 million of year-to-date repurchases provide continued capacity, so the signal is mixed rather than a halt to buybacks.
fact_evidence: “The company returned $9 million to shareholders in Q2 ($7 million buybacks, $2 million dividends) and repurchased $29 million year-to-date—about 7% of shares outstanding—under a new $100 million authorization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “retired roughly 5% of shares outstanding in Q1 alone ($22M of buyback)” and flagged “Q2 buyback disclosure” as a key metric.

description: Management said the 136 company-owned restaurants are tracking near breakeven EBITDA, with AUVs in the low $2 millions versus about $3 million for the system, and is beginning to consider refranchising them. That raises a portfolio-quality and refranchising question beyond the preview’s stated roughly three-year timeline for refranchising acquired units.
fact_evidence: “The company owns 136 restaurants (about 4% of the system) tracking near breakeven EBITDA, with AUVs in the low $2 millions versus a system average near $3 million, and management is beginning to consider refranchising.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “refranchising timeline on the acquired units (management indicated ~3 years).”

description: Longeveron reported a Q2 net loss of $6.1 million, above the preview’s $4.4–4.9 million estimate. The loss was therefore materially wider than expected.
fact_evidence: “Net loss widened 22% to $6.1 million for Q2 2026 versus $5.0 million in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Net loss … $4.4–4.9M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash at June 30 was $10.1 million, below the preview’s $11.0–11.5 million estimate. The shortfall was roughly $0.9–1.4 million.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were $10.1 million as of June 30, 2026.”

description: G&A rose to $3.2 million, well above the preview’s roughly $2.6 million estimate. The increase was attributed mainly to higher legal and personnel costs.
fact_evidence: “G&A expenses rose 23% to $3.2 million, driven mainly by a $0.4 million increase in legal spend and $0.2 million in personnel costs.”
expectation_evidence: “G&A … ~$2.6M”; the preview expected “asset-light” cuts to show.

description: R&D was $3.2 million, above the preview’s $2.2–2.6 million estimate, despite the preview expecting database-lock costs to be offset by trial wind-down.
fact_evidence: “R&D expenses rose 7% to $3.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “R&D … $2.2–2.6M”; “ELPIS II database lock costs offset by wind-down.”

description: Revenue was about $0.3 million, below the preview’s roughly $0.35 million estimate. Management attributed the decline to the absence of contract manufacturing revenue.
fact_evidence: “Quarterly revenue declined 10% (about $29,000) to $0.3 million due to the absence of contract manufacturing revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Q2’26E ~$0.35M”; the preview described the base as “Bahamas Registry + contract mfg.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: ELPIS-2 topline is now expected in mid-September rather than the preview’s August expectation, a modest delay. Management attributed it to MRI and last-patient-visit scheduling, not unresolved FDA statistical-analysis-plan issues.
fact_evidence: “Top-line data … in mid-September 2026”; database lock is planned for “August 31st,” with the delay attributed to “MRI and last-patient-visit scheduling rather than any unresolved FDA statistical analysis plan issues.”
expectation_evidence: The trial was “guided to ‘August 2026’ topline”; the preview said “any language other than August/early September is a negative.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management described an “auction” among major potential HLHS partners, suggesting stronger partnering interest than the preview’s watch for progress or a possible term sheet. Any deal remains contingent on positive ELPIS-2 data.
fact_evidence: “Management is pursuing an ‘auction’ among major potential partners for HLHS commercialization contingent on positive ELPIS-2 data.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “partnering progress” and noted that “a term sheet would change the financing calculus.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management said it may still pursue BLA or pivotal status even if the RVEF primary endpoint misses significance, relying on exploratory event-based outcomes. That is more optimistic than the preview’s warning that a clean RVEF result alone would not be sufficient and that transplant-free survival or MACE signal mattered.
fact_evidence: “Even if the RVEF primary endpoint misses statistical significance, management believes it can still pursue BLA/pivotal status using exploratory endpoints like all-cause mortality and transplant-free survival,” and said it had “sufficient blinded data to demonstrate significance on event-based outcomes.”
expectation_evidence: “Even a clean RVEF result is not sufficient — FDA has said RVEF cannot demonstrate efficacy and no longer treats ELPIS II as pivotal”; a primary-endpoint headline without “a transplant-free survival or MACE signal” should be sold, not bought.

description: The call identified a second possible priority review voucher tied to the planned pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy program; the preview’s bull-case discussion centered on a voucher from HLHS.
fact_evidence: “A second potential voucher [is] tied to the planned pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy program.”
