fact_evidence: “The company reduced gross impressions sequentially by 2% while increasing monetized impressions by 4%, signaling an intentional strategy expected to lift monetization rates in future quarters.”
expectation_evidence: “Secondary: … take-rate/ad-spend-on-platform commentary.”

description: PubMatic announced that CFO Steve Pantelick will retire, a leadership change the preview did not flag. His continued service as CFO into Q1 2027 and advisory role through July 1 provide a transition period, while Megan Ramm is set to join as Global Chief Revenue Officer.
fact_evidence: “CFO Steve Pantelick announced his retirement, remaining CFO into Q1 2027 and then advisory through July 1, with a new Global Chief Revenue Officer, Megan Ramm, joining August 10.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The reported cash balance of $137.5 million with no debt was above the preview’s estimate of approximately $102 million in net cash. The preview did not specify an expected quarter-end cash balance, so the comparison is indicative rather than a precise forecast miss.
fact_evidence: “ended with $137.5 million in cash and zero debt.”
expectation_evidence: “Net cash: ~$102M.”

description: Arrow's Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $5.45, above the preview's $5.00–$5.25 working whisper and well above the $4.45 consensus. The earnings beat was larger than the preview's already-elevated expectation.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS surged 124% year-over-year to $5.45, above the guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “My working whisper is ~$9.9–10.1B revenue and ~$5.00–5.25 non-GAAP EPS.”

description: Q3 guidance fell short of the preview's $10 billion-plus revenue and $5.00-plus EPS bar: revenue guidance has a $9.9 billion midpoint, while EPS guidance has a $4.93 midpoint and implies a sequential decline from Q2. ECS is guided to only 2% year-over-year growth, although management attributed that to lapping a large partner addition.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $9.6-$10.2 billion” and “non-GAAP EPS of $4.83-$5.03, implying a sequential earnings decline from Q2's $5.45.” ECS Q3 guidance is “$2.1-$2.3 billion (up only 2% YoY)” and “reflects lapping a large partner addition from last year rather than a change in business trajectory.”
expectation_evidence: “Arrow needs to guide Q3 to at least ~$10B revenue and ~$5.00+ non-GAAP EPS to keep pace with that read-across.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Memory's share of Global Components revenue was described as low double digits, above the preview's mid-single-digit estimate. Price inflation also contributed roughly one-third of sequential Components growth, so the upside was volume-led but had more memory and pricing exposure than the preview's baseline suggested.
fact_evidence: “Memory now represents a low double-digit percentage of Global Components segment revenue”; price inflation contributed “roughly one-third of sequential Global Components growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Memory only a mid-single-digit percentage of revenue.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: ECS disclosed a $27 million charge tied to underperforming multiyear contracts with a strategic partner, reducing ECS operating margin by 100 basis points year over year; management expects additional, smaller charges in the second half. The preview did not flag these contract costs.
fact_evidence: “ECS took a $27 million charge on underperforming multiyear contracts with a strategic partner, cutting ECS operating margins by 100 basis points year-over-year, with additional but smaller charges expected in the second half.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The reported supplier relationship departure was less damaging than the reported figure implied: management said it affected roughly $700 million of revenue, not $1.4 billion, and would not affect ECS revenue, margin, or profit because alternatives were available.
fact_evidence: The departure “impacted roughly $700 million in revenue (not $1.4 billion as reported) but is expected to have no impact on ECS revenue, margin, or profit due to alternative solutions.”
expectation_evidence: “not $1.4 billion as reported.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog and ordering indicators were stronger and extended further out than the preview's expectation of backlog building into Q3–Q4: ECS backlog was up more than 75% to an all-time high, book-to-bill remained above parity in all three regions, and backlog was building into the first half of 2027.
fact_evidence: “ECS backlog grew over 75% year-over-year to an all-time high”; “book-to-bill ratios remain above parity in all three regions, and backlog is building into the first half of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Backlog building into Q3–Q4” and the preview asked whether “extending lead times are pulling double-ordering into the backlog.”

description: Global Components held a 5.4% operating margin, modestly above the preview's roughly 5.0% expected trough and its 5.3% threshold for a bullish outcome. Management also expects margins to remain around 5% in Q3.
fact_evidence: Global Components had “operating margins of 5.4%” and management “expects to sustain around 5% margins in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything holding ≥5.3% is a bull outcome” and the preview described “~5.0% expected trough.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash generation and deleveraging were reassuring against the preview's concern about a possible cash burn: Arrow reported more than $1 billion in year-to-date operating cash flow and reduced gross debt to $2.2 billion, with adjusted leverage down to 1.75x.
fact_evidence: “The company generated over $1 billion in year-to-date operating cash flow, reduced gross debt by ~$650 million YoY to $2.2 billion, and improved adjusted leverage by over a full turn to 1.75x.”
expectation_evidence: “If Arrow posts a large cash burn, the ‘earnings power’ narrative gets a real challenge.”

description: Share repurchases increased from the $25 million reported in Q1 to $43 million in Q2, a step-up in capital returns that the preview specifically watched for.
fact_evidence: Arrow was “repurchasing $43 million in shares.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch whether buybacks step up from the token $25M pace.”

description: BKTI reported Q2 revenue of $23.4 million, above the preview’s $22.6 million consensus and $22.7 million model, making the quarter’s growth stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 10.6% year-over-year to $23.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 consensus” revenue of “$22.6M”; the preview’s model estimated “$22.7M.”

description: Gross margin reached 51.9%, beating the preview’s 51.0% estimate by nearly a percentage point, with the BKR 9000 and favorable mix supporting the expansion.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 445 basis points to 51.9%,” driven by “favorable product mix and adoption of the higher-margin BKR 9000.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s model estimated gross margin of “51.0%.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.4%, below the preview’s roughly 20% estimate, indicating somewhat weaker operating profitability than modeled even as revenue and gross margin beat expectations.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 19.4% from 20.9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~$4.6M (20%)” in adjusted EBITDA and described its base case as having “SG&A ~$7.5M.”

description: Adjusted EPS of $1.01 edged above the preview’s $0.98 model, landing near the top of its stated base-case range despite declining year over year.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EPS fell to $1.01 from $1.30 in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled non-GAAP adjusted EPS of “$0.98” and gave a base-case range of “$0.92–1.02.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The BKR 9500’s FCC approval is now expected in early 2027, later than the preview’s stated H2 2026 approval timing, although customer deliveries remain anticipated in H1 2027.
fact_evidence: The radio “was submitted for FCC testing, with approval expected in early 2027 and customer deliveries anticipated in the first half of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the company was “Guided to H2'26 approval, H1'27 shipments” and flagged an FCC slip as a risk.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: BKTI disclosed purchase orders for more than 200 BKR 9500 units before customers had seen the radio, an early demand signal the preview did not anticipate or quantify.
fact_evidence: “The new BKR 9500 in-vehicle multiband radio has drawn purchase orders exceeding 200 units sight unseen.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Trailing 12-month after-tax free cash flow reached $19 million, up 49% and outpacing revenue growth, adding a stronger cash-generation result than the preview’s Q1-focused cash and FCF discussion anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month after-tax free cash flow reached $19 million, up 49% year-over-year and outpacing revenue growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$4.1M FCF in Q1 (+44% YoY)” and listed cash, FCF, and buyback activity as a metric to watch, but gave no Q2 or trailing-12-month FCF estimate.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call added a January 2027 target for general release of BKR Play, a tethering solution not mentioned in the preview, providing an additional product launch on the roadmap.
fact_evidence: “The BKR Play tethering solution is targeted for general release in January 2027.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: BKTI described the Tango Tango agreement as extending InteropONE to more than 1,500 agencies and 35,000-plus active users and creating a recurring licensing-fee pathway; the preview had identified licensing economics as an open question, though no fee amount was reported.
fact_evidence: “A licensing agreement with Tango Tango extends InteropONE technology to over 1,500 public safety agencies and 35,000+ active users, creating a recurring licensing fee pathway.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said this was the “first chance for management to quantify royalty/licensing revenue” and that “any recurring-software disclosure” could matter.

description: Coeur’s revenue was above $1.1 billion, but below the preview’s $1.19–$1.24 billion consensus range. The record result therefore still represented a top-line miss of roughly 7–11% versus expectations.
fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue exceeding $1.1 billion”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: New Afton’s ramp to 16,000 tonnes per day slipped from the expected end-of-Q2 timing to early Q4, a roughly three-month delay. That pushes out part of the operating contribution investors were looking for from the acquired assets.
fact_evidence: “New Afton’s ramp to 16,000 tonnes per day was pushed roughly three months to early Q4 (from end of Q2)”
expectation_evidence: “This is the first clean quarter of the ‘new’ Coeur — the first full three months consolidating New Gold’s Rainy River and New Afton mines”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The Rainy River acquisition-accounting inventory charge was a sizable drag on Q2 earnings and costs, with another charge still expected in Q3. The preview flagged PPA as a key cost issue, but the reported $140 million charge and its $834-per-ounce consolidated CAS impact were substantial.
fact_evidence: “A $140 million (~$0.10 per share) noncash charge from acquisition accounting on Rainy River stockpile inventory hit Q2 EBITDA, net income and CAS, with a remaining $38 million expected in Q3”; “inflated consolidated Q2 CAS by $834 per ounce out of $2,442 total”
expectation_evidence: “What matters: does management disclose an ex-PPA cost bridge, and does the PPA drag persist at ~$689/oz or step down?”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow reached $388 million, up from the preview’s cited Q1 figure of $267 million, despite the preview’s concern that a lower-price quarter and full capex load would test cash conversion. The Canadian assets alone contributed about $175 million while still ramping.
fact_evidence: “Record quarterly free cash flow reached $388 million … up 45% versus the prior quarter, with the Canadian assets contributing 45% (~$175 million) despite being in ramp-up mode”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 was $267M against capex guidance of $437–526M … FCF conversion in a lower-price quarter with a full capex load is the durability test.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash rose to $1.1 billion from the preview’s cited $843 million, crossing $1 billion for the first time and taking total liquidity above $2 billion. This was a stronger balance-sheet outcome than the preview’s already-net-cash setup suggested.
fact_evidence: “Ending cash balance surpassed $1 billion for the first time ($1.1 billion at June 30), doubling from year-end 2025, with total liquidity over $2 billion”
expectation_evidence: “Cash $843M, total debt $761M, net leverage (0.1x) — a net cash position”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Rainy River underground mining accelerated: July rates were about 3,300 tonnes per day versus 2,300 in Q2, with a target of 5,000 by year-end and underground grades roughly three times open-pit grades. That provides a more concrete and favorable ramp signal than the preview’s general expectation that Rainy River’s grade profile could support the second half.
fact_evidence: “Rainy River underground mining rates jumped over 40% from 2,300 tpd in Q2 to ~3,300 tpd in July, targeting 5,000 tpd by year-end, with underground grades roughly 3x higher than open pit grades”
expectation_evidence: “There is a real second-half story (Rochester ramp, Wharf, Rainy River grade profile, full New Gold contribution).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Rochester reported record crushing and had 97% of throughput running through all three crushing stages, with the Phase 2a leach-pad expansion completed. That is a stronger operating update than the preview’s description of Rochester as a chronic underperformer, and supports the anticipated second-half production ramp.
fact_evidence: “Rochester achieved a record 6.8 million metric tons crushed (up 15% quarter-over-quarter) with 97% running through all three crushing stages, positioning it for a strong second-half silver production spike as the Phase 2a leach pad expansion completed”
expectation_evidence: “Rochester. The chronic underperformer”; “The FY guide’s H2 ramp leans on Rochester.”

description: Coeur deployed $110 million on buybacks, about 45% of Q2 free cash flow, and also paid its first dividend in 30 years and reduced debt by $39 million. Buyback execution was a key open question; the amount was meaningful but below the preview’s $150 million-plus bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Coeur began actively repurchasing shares under its expanded $750 million buyback program, deploying about 45% of Q2 free cash flow via $110 million of buybacks, its first dividend in 30 years ($0.02), and $39 million of debt reduction”
expectation_evidence: “How many dollars of buyback were actually executed in Q2”; bull case: “$150M+ of buyback executed”; “The $750M buyback authorization and the new $0.02 semi-annual dividend were announced with Q1.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The UK Ebstrocel filing had not reached submission as the preview’s expected early-Q3 window arrived; management now expects to submit by the end of Q3 or early Q4 2026. That pushes the filing later than the preview’s near-term expectation, even though management said the MHRA alignment had de-risked the path.
fact_evidence: “expects to submit the Ebstracell marketing authorization application to the UK MHRA… by end of Q3 or early Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “guided ‘early Q3 2026’ on the Q1 call”; the preview asked whether the MAA was “filed, or slipping?”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The US BLA timing is now Q1 2027, later than the preview’s expected Q4 2026 filing. The preview had already noted the EU filing’s move to 2027, so the clearly new timing gap is the US submission.
fact_evidence: “a US BLA in Q1 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 PR said… FDA BLA in Q4 2026”; the preview asked for “Reconfirmation of FDA BLA in Q4 2026.”

description: Q2 results were substantially better than the preview’s modeled loss: net loss was about $1.3 million versus an estimated $5.2–5.9 million, and R&D was a benefit rather than the expected $3.4–4.2 million expense. The swing was driven mainly by additional Australian rebates and management said rebates are not expected to recur at this level over the next 12 months, limiting how much of the improvement represents a repeatable cost reduction.
fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common stockholders fell to approximately $1.3 million”; “R&D expenses swung to a benefit of roughly $0.8 million… driven mainly by recognition of additional Australian R&D rebates that are not expected to recur at that level over the next 12 months.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss: $5.2–5.9M” and “R&D expense: $3.4–4.2M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and runway came in better than the preview’s base expectation: June cash was $18.4 million, followed by a $4.2 million rebate, and management said resources should last into Q2 2027 rather than only through Q1 2027. The extension is tempered by management’s plan to use the ATM in small increments through 2027.
fact_evidence: “$18.4 million in cash as of June 30, 2026,” an “additional $4.2 million Australian R&D tax rebate subsequently,” and resources expected “to fund operations into Q2 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “$16–18M” cash at June 30 and described prior runway guidance as “through Q1 2027”; it identified extension past Q1 2027 as a bull-case outcome.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management supplied concrete commercial assumptions for Ebstracell that the preview did not include: annual pricing of £400,000–£500,000 per child and a target of about 100 UK patients within two years of approval. These are new company projections, rather than reported sales or an established market expectation.
fact_evidence: “priced Ebstracell at an expected £400,000-£500,000 per child per year” and “projects reaching roughly 100 UK patients within two years of approval.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management specified that the confirmatory open-label Phase 3 trial would take 18 months, with data around mid-2028. The preview focused on the filing and the XPro trial plan, and did not flag this Ebstracell confirmatory-trial timetable; it adds a defined, relatively distant data milestone.
fact_evidence: “The confirmatory open-label Phase 3 trial will enroll roughly 40-45 patients… run 18 months, and produce data around mid-2028.”

description: Management introduced the potential value of a US rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, saying it could be worth $150–200 million and that proceeds would fund platform expansion. The preview did not discuss this potential source of value, which is contingent on US accelerated approval and voucher issuance.
fact_evidence: “A US accelerated approval would carry a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher,” recently sold for “$150-200 million” in the secondary market, with proceeds “earmarked to fund platform expansion.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million, well above the preview’s roughly $21.5 million estimate and the prior-year $22.5 million level management had been expected to come in below. This was a stronger profit result than the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 7% to $24 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA: ‘slightly lower than prior year’ → below $22.5M”; the model estimated “~$21.5M.”

description: Revenue of $149 million exceeded both the preview’s $146 million model and its cited $143.88 million consensus. The result was stronger than the expected roughly 12%–13% growth pace.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 15% to $149 million,” with “Q2 organic (ex-ArrowEye) growth of 12%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s model was “$146.0” million, with “+12.5%” YoY; cited consensus was “$143.88M.”

description: Gross margin reached 32.5%, materially above the preview’s roughly 29.5% estimate. More than $3 million of tariff refunds contributed about 160 basis points, making part of the margin upside a one-time benefit rather than evidence of an equivalent recurring improvement.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA benefited from “more than $3 million in tariff refunds that boosted gross margin ~160 basis points to 32.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled gross margin at “~29.5%” and flagged tariff refund recognition as uncertain and a “non-recurring optical boost.”

description: The company raised full-year revenue growth guidance from high single digits to high single digits/low double digits. That is an upward revision beyond the previously affirmed high-single-digit outlook, though it is consistent with the preview’s upside scenario.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue growth guidance to high single digits/low double digits.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was “high single-digit revenue growth” and described the bull case as guidance raised “to low-double-digit.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half free cash flow was far stronger than the preview’s expectation of conversion similar to 2025, and the company raised its full-year outlook to $45–$50 million. Management cautioned that the first-half level was not repeatable because some of the improvement was timing-related.
fact_evidence: “First half free cash flow was a record $36 million versus just $1 million a year earlier”; guidance rose to “$45-$50 million,” but management cautioned “this level won't repeat” because some benefit was timing-related.
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was for “FCF conversion similar to 2025.”

description: Integrated PayTech’s underlying growth remained weaker than the preview’s modeled Q2 inflection: the segment grew only 4% in Q2 and low single digits in the first half, versus an estimated roughly 10% Q2 increase. The roughly 20% full-year target therefore depends on a steep second-half acceleration, even with TRISM included.
fact_evidence: Integrated PayTech “grew only low single digits (4% in Q2) in the first half, implying steep second-half acceleration.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Integrated PayTech at “~$16.5” million and “~+10%” YoY for Q2, and said it needed “a visible inflection.”

description: Prepaid weakness was described as likely to continue into late 2026, rather than being only a short-lived order-timing issue. That is weaker than the preview’s expectation of full-year growth and its view that a decline could still be explained by timing.
fact_evidence: “Prepaid Solutions remains soft and is expected to stay choppy into late 2026 due to tough prior-year comparisons and uneven ordering.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “guided to full-year growth” and warned that a further decline could reframe the weakness from “timing” to “structural.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage ended at 2.7x, better than the preview’s roughly 2.9x estimate, and the company subsequently redeemed $26.5 million of Senior Notes. This is a stronger deleveraging outcome than the preview’s expected gradual improvement.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to 2.7x from 3.6x a year earlier,” and CPI “redeemed $26.5 million of Senior Notes in mid-July.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated net leverage at “~2.9x” and noted that net leverage was “just under 3.0x” in Q1.

description: Zoetis cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $9.12–$9.32 billion and adjusted diluted EPS to $6.15–$6.25, far below the preview’s existing ranges of $9.68–$9.96 billion and $6.85–$7.00. The preview treated a reaffirmation as the base case and a further cut as the bear case.
fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $9.12–$9.32 billion” and “adjusted diluted EPS of $6.15–$6.25.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance action. Reaffirm, narrow, or cut”; “Reaffirm = base case”; existing guidance was “Revenue $9.680–9.960B” and “Adj. diluted EPS $6.85–7.00.”

description: The Companion Animal portfolio fell 6%, much worse than the preview’s roughly 0.9% expected decline, while U.S. Companion Animal fell 11% versus an expected 3.5% decline. U.S. revenue overall was also weaker than the preview’s expected 2.2% decline, falling 7%.
fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue declined 7%” and “U.S. Companion Animal fell 11% as the total Companion Animal portfolio declined 6%.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus showed “Companion Animal” at “−0.9%,” “U.S. Companion Animal” at “−3.5%,” and “U.S. total” at “−2.2%.”

description: Dermatology suffered a sharp decline, with global revenue down 16% and U.S. revenue down 18%; U.S. in-clinic share fell about 5 points sequentially and 10 points year over year. The preview identified the new competitor as a major risk, but the reported revenue and share losses show the pressure was pronounced.
fact_evidence: “Key Dermatology revenue dropped 16% globally to $395 million (U.S. Dermatology down 18% to $251 million)” amid “intensified competition from a new U.S. entrant in Q2”; U.S. in-clinic share fell “5 points sequentially and 10 points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Apoquel/Cytopoint faced “Merck’s Numelvi oral JAK, launched Feb 2026,” and described the franchise as “the largest unquantified risk in the model.”

description: Zoetis’s full-year price outlook deteriorated from the preview’s 1–2% realization target to a range of 0% to -2%. The company attributed the change to Dermatology gross-to-net investments and price cuts on Cerenia and Convenia amid generic competition.
fact_evidence: “Full-year price realization is now expected between 0% and -2%, driven by gross-to-net investments in Dermatology and price cuts on Cerenia and Convenia amid generic competition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY price guidance was cut from 2–3% to 1–2%” and flagged whether pricing would hold around the “revised 1–2% target.”

description: Livestock growth was stronger than expected in Q2: global revenue grew 11% versus the preview’s 6.4% estimate, and U.S. Livestock grew 23% versus 6.2% expected. However, management said the pace would moderate in the second half as some current gains were temporary.
fact_evidence: “Livestock grew 11% globally to $731 million, with U.S. Livestock up 23% to $222 million,” but management expects “second-half growth to moderate to mid-single digits as screwworm-driven and supply-timing gains are transitory.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus expected “Livestock” growth of “+6.4%” and “U.S. Livestock” growth of “+6.2%”; the preview said livestock would “carry the quarter.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.87, a small beat against the preview’s $1.84–$1.86 estimate range, even though adjusted net income fell 2% and missed company expectations. Repurchases of more than $550 million—above the historical quarterly average—helped support EPS growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income down 2% to $781 million, falling short of company expectations”; the company repurchased “over $550 million of shares in the quarter—above its historical quarterly average—helping lift adjusted diluted EPS 4% year-over-year to $1.87.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave a published EPS band of “$1.84–$1.86” and noted that buybacks had “added ~3 points to Q1 adjusted EPS growth.”

description: The CFO is departing, and the incoming CFO will also take on COO responsibilities in a newly created role. The preview did not flag an executive transition or this change in the role’s scope.
fact_evidence: “CFO Wetteny Joseph is departing after five years, with Jay Saccaro … joining August 17 in a newly created EVP CFO and COO role overseeing finance, manufacturing, and supply.”

description: Q2 revenue was approximately $2.5 billion and essentially matched the preview’s $2.49 billion estimate, but the reported result was flat year over year rather than the roughly 1.3% growth implied by consensus.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $2.5 billion, flat on a reported basis but down 1% organically.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue at “$2.49B” versus approximately “$2.458B” a year earlier, or “+1.3%.”

description: Q2 revenue was $214 million, above the roughly $211–212 million implied by consensus and management’s prior “about 14%” growth outlook. The resulting 15% year-over-year growth was a modest beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $214 million, up 15% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 revenue” consensus was “$211.24M”; management said “Overall growth in Q2 should be similar to Q1 at about 14%” (approximately $212M).

description: ATEC raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to approximately $140 million from $134 million, rather than simply delivering on the previously maintained $134 million target. The increase also lifts the stated margin target from 15% to 16%.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $140 million (16% margin) from $134 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “~$134M / 15% margin” and noted management had “held $134M adj. EBITDA.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Revenue per case weakened more than the preview’s outlook suggested: it fell 2.7% year over year, and management cut full-year revenue-per-case guidance from flattish to a low-single-digit decline. Biologics weakness accounted for about three-quarters of the Q2 shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Revenue per case declined approximately 2.7% year-over-year”; “Full-year revenue-per-case guidance was cut from flattish to a low-single-digit decline,” with “about three-quarters of the Q2 shortfall attributed to biologics.”
expectation_evidence: The call described the prior outlook as “flattish” before saying it was cut to a low-single-digit decline.

description: Gross margin reached 72.5%, up 260 basis points year over year, with the call attributing the improvement to inventory efficiency, cost reductions, and product mix. The preview noted Q1 gross margin of 71.6% but did not flag this degree of further improvement as an expectation.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 72.5%, up 260 basis points year-over-year, driven by inventory efficiency, cost reductions, and product mix.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ATEC reported that implant revenue at established EOS Insight accounts rose about 32% within six months of going live, a positive account-level adoption signal not anticipated in the preview. Overall EOS revenue, however, was essentially flat year over year.
fact_evidence: “Established EOS Insight accounts showed implant revenue rising approximately 32% within six months of going live.”

description: Net product revenue of $15.4M slightly exceeded the $15.22M consensus and the preview’s ~$15.0M implied estimate, but came in about $0.6M below the preview’s assumed ~$16M buy-side bar.
fact_evidence: “Net product revenue grew 45% quarter-over-quarter to $15.4 million in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. $15.22M” consensus; “Assume the buy-side bar is ~$16M.”

description: Although Q2 gross-to-net was 29.6%, better than the preview’s cited Q1 level of about 32%, management said GTNs would rise to the low-to-mid 30% range and could reach the mid-to-high 30s if a new PBM contract is signed. That outlook is less favorable than the preview’s expectation that gross-to-net would hold or show only modest erosion.
fact_evidence: “Gross-to-net was 29.6% in Q2, but management guided GTNs will rise to the low-to-mid 30% range, potentially mid-to-high 30s if a new PBM contract is signed.”
expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires both seasonality and price stability”; base case: “modest price erosion.”

description: SG&A rose 31% to $27.7M rather than flattening as the preview’s operating-leverage bull case anticipated. Management attributed much of the increase to a $5.3M one-time, non-recurring sales milestone, which limits how much of the increase appears ongoing.
fact_evidence: “SG&A rose 31% to $27.7 million largely due to a $5.3 million one-time non-recurring sales milestone.”
expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires SG&A to flatten”; “Flat-to-down SG&A on +40% revenue is the operating-leverage proof point.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $5.7M, better than the preview’s base-case range of negative $6M to negative $7M, while still delivering the expected first sequential improvement.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $5.7 million in Q2 (from negative $8.0 million in Q1).”
expectation_evidence: Base case: “Adj. EBITDA –$6.0M to –$7.0M”; the preview also called the “first sequential adjusted-EBITDA improvement” the signal management had promised.

description: The preview emphasized roughly 84% gross margin, but the call disclosed a $0.9M write-off of out-of-spec API inventory and said stepped-up inventory would keep unit costs above the expected normalized level for another 12–15 months. The eventual normalized cost is expected to be about $1,000 per unit, so the call also supplied a longer-term cost target that the preview had not specified.
fact_evidence: “COGS included a $0.9 million write-off of out-of-spec API inventory,” and normalized per-unit cost is expected to reach “~$1,000” once stepped-up inventory is consumed over “the next 12-15 months.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “the ~84% gross margin” as the basis for operating leverage.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company disclosed a restatement of Q1 2026 financials related to fair-value accounting for convertible debt under a subordination agreement, which the preview did not anticipate. Management said it does not change cash, revenue, expenses, operating loss, or adjusted EBITDA, so the surprise is in the accounting restatement rather than the operating results.
fact_evidence: “The company disclosed a restatement of Q1 2026 financials tied to fair value accounting of convertible debt under a subordination agreement,” but it “does not affect cash, revenue, expenses, operating loss, or adjusted EBITDA.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Zepi’s Q1 2027 launch timing matched the preview’s early-2027 expectation, but Zegalyze was slated for Q3 2027 rather than the preview’s mid-2027 timing, pushing the second launch later.
fact_evidence: “Zepi (impetigo) in Q1 2027 and Zegalyze (head lice) in Q3 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “XEPI early 2027 / XEGLYZE mid-2027 timing.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The Phase 2 AD trial’s top-line readout is now expected in Q3 2027, later than the preview’s secondary-reported mid-2027 timing. Management also expects enrollment to finish in early 2027.
fact_evidence: “enrollment completion expected early 2027 and top-line data in Q3 2027”
expectation_evidence: “Secondary reporting points to topline in mid-2027”; the preview also said to listen for whether management “repeats or refines a data date.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The planned HS study is a Phase 1b trial, not the Phase 2 initiation the preview expected to be reaffirmed for later in 2026. The stated plan is a small, up-to-25-patient, uncontrolled study.
fact_evidence: “plans to initiate a Phase 1b HS trial (up to 25 patients, no placebo, 200mg BID for 12 weeks)”
expectation_evidence: “HS and asthma Phase 2 initiations — guided ‘later this year’”; the preview’s checklist asks whether “HS + asthma Phase 2 starts [are] reaffirmed for 2H26.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The PTCL interim futility analysis is now projected for Q1 2027, and the interim will not disclose safety or efficacy results. The preview focused on Phase 3 enrollment progress and did not flag either this timing or the limited interim disclosure.
fact_evidence: “The Phase 3 PTCL trial's interim futility analysis is now projected for Q1 2027 (versus prior expectations)”; “no safety/efficacy data to be publicly disclosed at the interim.”
expectation_evidence: “An enrollment-complete or enrollment-ahead-of-plan comment would be a genuine upside surprise”; the preview does not state an interim-analysis date.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Corvus reported $215.2 million in cash and marketable securities, below the preview’s $219–224 million estimate. The runway remains into Q2 2028, as expected, so the cash-balance shortfall did not come with a shorter stated runway.
fact_evidence: “ended Q2 2026 with $215.2 million in cash and marketable securities”; the balance includes “$189.4 million in net proceeds from a Q1 follow-on offering” and funds operations “into Q2 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash & marketable securities (6/30) … $219–224M”; “Runway … Reaffirm ‘into Q2 2028.’”

description: Corvus committed $5 million to Angel Pharmaceuticals’ financing, a cash investment not anticipated in the preview. The investment supports the existing collaboration, but also directs company cash to its partner.
fact_evidence: “Corvus invested $5 million in Angel Pharmaceuticals' $13.5 million financing and remains Angel's largest shareholder.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Angel’s upcoming China data and noted “Nothing has been announced” on business development, but did not anticipate an investment in Angel.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management described a prolonged benefit after soquelitinib dosing ends, without the rebound it contrasted with dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and STAT6 agents. The preview covered the previously reported day-56 AD efficacy but did not anticipate this durability claim.
fact_evidence: “Soquelitinib showed prolonged treatment benefit beyond dosing without disease rebound, contrasting with rebound seen in dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and STAT6 agents, attributed to enhanced T regulatory cell function.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Cohort 4 discussion gave day-56 response rates and described the study’s 56-day dosing, but did not mention post-dosing benefit or rebound.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Angel’s Chinese AD-trial data can be used in Corvus’s FDA filings, giving the partner-generated results a stated regulatory use beyond the China trial. The preview anticipated Angel data but did not mention this use.
fact_evidence: “its data is usable in Corvus's FDA filings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Angel’s China trial as “A second, independent readout on soquelitinib before the pivotal AD data,” without mentioning use in FDA filings.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The asthma Phase 2 is planned to include both T2 and non-T2 patients; the preview expected an asthma Phase 2 start but did not specify this broader population. Management said non-T2 patients represent about 40–50% of asthma patients.
fact_evidence: “a Phase 2 asthma trial enrolling both T2 and non-T2 patients (the latter representing ~40-50% of asthma patients) before year-end 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “HS and asthma Phase 2 initiations — guided ‘later this year’”; no asthma patient subgroups were specified.

description: R&D expense was $16 million, above the preview’s $13–15 million estimate, while the $18 million net loss was also slightly wider than its $15–17 million model. The preview explicitly framed R&D above $15 million and a wider loss as evidence of trial execution, so the expense overrun is favorable in that context.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D expenses rose to $16 million”; “Net loss widened to $18 million in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “R&D expense … $13.0–15.0M”; “Net loss … $15–17M”; the preview says “R&D >$15M” is confirmation and that a wider-than-consensus loss “is a sign of trial execution, not deterioration.”

description: Cummins raised its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 10%–13% from 8%–11%, rather than merely narrowing the range toward its upper half as the preview’s base case anticipated. It also increased the midpoint of EBITDA-margin guidance to 18.25%.
fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 10%-13% (from 8%-11%) and increased the midpoint of EBITDA guidance to 18%-18.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “Base ... FY guide narrowed to the upper half rather than raised”; the preview also said the Street needed a guidance raise, not just a beat.

description: Q2 EBITDA margin was 17.5%, well below the preview’s implied 18.5%–19.1% range, and fell from 18.4% a year earlier. The preview expected a year-over-year margin increase, not a decline.
fact_evidence: “Record EBITDA of $1.7 billion, though EBITDA margin declined to 17.5% from 18.4% a year ago due to tariffs and higher variable compensation.”
expectation_evidence: “Implied EBITDA ... ~$1.73–1.78B, 18.5–19.1% margin”; the preview described this as “+30–60 bps.”

description: Q2 diluted EPS of $6.73 missed the $7.33 consensus estimate, despite being above the year-ago result. The $0.21-per-share unfavorable discrete tax items explain part, but not all, of the gap.
fact_evidence: “Net earnings were $932 million, or $6.73 per diluted share, up from $6.43 a year ago, despite $29 million ($0.21 per share) in unfavorable discrete tax items.”

description: Power Systems revenue reached $2.3 billion, substantially above the preview’s $2.10 billion estimate and its expected 11.2% year-over-year growth. Its 24.5% margin, however, was essentially in line with the 24.7% estimate rather than the preview’s greater-than-27% upside-surprise threshold.
fact_evidence: “Power Systems was the standout segment with record revenues of $2.3 billion (up 19%) and EBITDA margin expanding to 24.5% from 22.8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Power Systems $2.10B” revenue, “+11.2%”; “consensus 24.7%” margin, with “any print above ~27%” described as a clean upside surprise.

description: Demand in China was much stronger than the preview specifically laid out: China revenue including joint ventures rose 30%, while power-generation equipment sales there rose 88% on accelerating data-center demand.
fact_evidence: “China revenues including joint ventures rose 30% year-over-year to $2.3 billion, with power generation equipment sales up 88% on accelerating data center demand.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Cummins disclosed a multiyear hyperscaler agreement that provides visibility into several gigawatts of future backup-power genset demand, a concrete large-customer commitment not specified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Cummins signed a multiyear agreement with a global hyperscaler securing visibility into several gigawatts of future backup power genset demand.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New 95-liter diesel genset orders are booking into the second half of 2028, extending well beyond the preview’s expectation that orders would spill into the first half of 2027. Management also said demand is still growing rather than plateauing.
fact_evidence: “Diesel genset lead times have extended, with new 95-liter orders now booking into the second half of 2028, and demand continues to grow rather than plateau.”
expectation_evidence: “2026 build slots effectively sold out and orders spilling into 1H27 on EPA-2027 pre-buy.”

description: Higher incentive compensation tied to record earnings weighed on Q2 margins across segments, an added cost headwind not identified in the preview. Management expects it to ease by about $25 million per quarter in H2 and reset roughly $200 million lower going into 2027.
fact_evidence: “Higher incentive compensation tied to record earnings weighed on Q2 margins across segments but is expected to be ~$25 million lower per quarter in H2 and reset roughly $200 million lower going into 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview set an implied Q2 EBITDA margin expectation of “18.5–19.1%” and discussed tariffs and MY2027 launch costs, but did not identify higher incentive compensation as a margin headwind.

description: Q2 revenue was $181 million, well above the preview’s $161–165 million base case and management’s steer of only slightly above Q1’s $160.8 million. Core organic growth was nearly 8%, making this a substantial upside to the expected quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $181 million,” with “core organic growth of nearly 8%.”
expectation_evidence: “My base case” revenue was “$161–165M”; management had steered to revenue “slightly above Q1 levels” (Q1 was $160.8M).

description: Adjusted gross margin fell to 20.3%, below the preview’s 21.5% guide-floor threshold and the 21.5–22.0% full-year margin outlook cited in the preview. The reported pressures included currency-driven material costs, MirrorEye transition inventory costs, and lower Smart2 tachograph sales.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross profit margin declined 277 basis points year-over-year to 20.3%,” pressured by “currency-driven material costs,” “inventory-related costs from the shift to factory-built MirrorEye,” and “lower Smart2 tachograph sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for adjusted gross margin to “Hold ≥21.5% (guide floor)” and listed FY adjusted gross margin guidance of “21.5–22.0%.”

description: Management said Q3 and Q4 revenue should each be modestly lower than Q2 due to seasonality, rather than following the preview’s expectation of heavier Q3/Q4 revenue after a modest Q2. The full-year revenue and EBITDA ranges were nevertheless reaffirmed.
fact_evidence: “Both Q3 and Q4 revenue [are] expected to be modestly lower than Q2 due to seasonality.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s revenue arithmetic described a “Modest Q2, heavier Q3/Q4” and said Q2–Q4 would average “$161–170M/qtr.”

description: SG&A showed stronger operating leverage than the preview specifically anticipated: expense rose by less than $400,000 despite a $24 million year-over-year increase in revenue, lowering SG&A to 14.3% of sales. This is an additional positive efficiency result beyond the headline revenue growth.
fact_evidence: “SG&A expense fell 182 basis points to 14.3% of sales, rising less than $400,000 despite a $24 million year-over-year revenue increase.”

description: Stone Ridge Brazil’s adjusted operating margin reached 11.2%, above the preview’s expectation to sustain roughly 9% or better. The call attributed part of the result to a temporary competitive supply dislocation, so the outperformance may not be fully durable.
fact_evidence: “Stone Ridge Brazil delivered record sales of $20.5 million” and “adjusted operating margin of 11.2%, aided partly by a temporary competitive supply dislocation.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified Brazil as the portfolio’s best-margin business at “9.5%” and said to watch whether it could “Sustain ~9%+ margin.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: IHS sharply raised its 2026 weighted-average OEM end-market growth forecast while cutting its 2027 forecast, citing orders moving into 2026. The preview highlighted improving near-term end-market data, but did not anticipate this pronounced year-to-year timing shift.
fact_evidence: “IHS raised its 2026 weighted-average OEM end-market growth forecast to 5.5% (up from 1.8% in May) while trimming 2027 growth to 5.4% (from 10%), primarily reflecting a timing shift of orders into 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said recent end-market data had “moved in Stoneridge’s favor,” citing June North American Class 8 orders “+230% YoY” and EU H1 heavy truck registrations “+11.1%”; it did not cite the IHS forecast revisions or a 2026-to-2027 timing shift.

description: Q3 revenue guidance was far below the preview’s roughly $82M placeholder and $80–86M base-case range: the $68M midpoint excludes about $17M of product revenue delayed by Chinese supply-chain disruptions. The preview did not anticipate the recent Chinese scrutiny of dual-use optics components that is driving the delay.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $63-73 million (midpoint $68 million) excludes approximately $17 million of product revenue delayed due to Chinese supply chain disruptions”; China’s increased scrutiny on dual-use optics components is a recent development “over the past few weeks.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue guide vs. ~$82M sell-side placeholder”; the Base scenario expects “$80–86M,” and a guide “≤$78M” is the bear trigger.

description: Management expects JLWS to begin contributing in Q3 and ramp significantly in 2027, and says it should more than offset the anticipated HELSI-2 decline. That gives a firmer replacement-program outlook than the preview’s unresolved concern that consensus implied a 2H26 revenue decline and its question of whether JLWS dollars would arrive on schedule.
fact_evidence: “JLWS will begin contributing revenue in the current quarter, ramp significantly in 2027, and management expects it to more than offset the anticipated decline of the HELSI-2 program.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says FY26 consensus implied “a ~6% sequential-half decline” and asks whether “the first guided quarter” can “embed JLWS revenue”; it also identifies JLWS timing as a key uncertainty.

description: Q3 product gross margin is guided to 34–40%, below Q2’s 41.2% and with a low end below the preview’s expected Q2 margin range. The stated reasons are reduced volumes and fixed-cost absorption.
fact_evidence: “Q3 product gross margin guided lower at 34-40% due to reduced volumes and fixed cost absorption.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gives a Q2 product gross-margin expectation of “~39%” consensus and a company range of “37–41%,” but does not provide a Q3 margin forecast.

description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1–7M signals a substantial sequential step-down from Q2’s $10.7M, with management attributing it to lower expected volumes; the preview did not flag a Q3 EBITDA outlook this low.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million in Q2… with Q3 guidance of just $1-7 million reflecting lower expected volumes.”

description: Q2 revenue exceeded consensus by about $4.4M, with product revenue also slightly above the preview’s approximate estimate. The reported 34% total growth and 45% product growth were stronger than the preview’s implied year-over-year growth estimates.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue hit a record $83 million, up 34% year-over-year, with record products revenue of $59 million growing 45% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$78.59M”; product revenue was estimated at “~$58M,” with implied growth of “+27.4%” overall and “~+35%” for products.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash flow was much stronger than the preview’s Q1 reference point, and the company repaid its credit-line borrowing while retaining substantial cash and investments. This contrasts with the preview’s concern that the Longmont buildout and JLWS investment could increase cash burn.
fact_evidence: “The company generated a record $20.7 million in operating cash flow and ended Q2 with $330.8 million in total cash and investments, having repaid the $20 million drawn on its credit line.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cites “+$9.7M operating cash flow in Q1” and says capex is going up, with “Negative FCF” considered acceptable if framed as JLWS capacity.

description: Harrow retained its $350–365M FY26 revenue and $80–100M adjusted EBITDA guidance, despite saying first-half revenue was lighter than expected. That leaves roughly $250M of revenue to deliver in H2, weighted toward Q4—more demanding than the preview’s estimated $230–245M H2 requirement, even as retaining the guide is better than the preview’s base-case expectation of a trim.
fact_evidence: Management reiterated full-year guidance of $350–365 million in revenue and $80–100 million in adjusted EBITDA; first-half revenue was approximately $115 million and management described an approximately $250 million second-half ramp weighted toward Q4.
expectation_evidence: “Base ... FY revenue guide trimmed to low end (~$340–355M) and/or EBITDA guide cut”; the preview also said H2 “must deliver $230–245M.”

description: Q2 revenue was essentially at the preview’s consensus range but came in $0.3M below the company’s $71M guidance floor. Management also said the first half was lighter than expected, largely because of Vevye and AIHESO revenue timing.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $70.7 million”; management said first-half revenue was “lighter than expected largely due to Vevye and AIHESO revenue timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited consensus estimates of “$70.99M / $70.35M” and “$71M – $81M” company guidance, noting that a sub-$71M result would be a formal guidance miss.

description: Vevye revenue and demand indicators came in stronger than the preview’s implied quarterly bar: revenue was $29.4M versus the preview’s rough $26–27M quarterly estimate, while prescriptions continued to grow sequentially rather than showing the feared demand break after the pricing change.
fact_evidence: “Vevye delivered record quarterly revenue of $29.4 million”; prescriptions were up 21% sequentially, the prescriber base was up 15%, and branded dry-eye market share reached 14.6% versus 7.8% a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview said more than $100M in FY Vevye revenue required roughly “$26–27M/quarter,” and warned that a sharp TRx deceleration would suggest the ASP gain came at the expense of volume.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AIHESO demand was much stronger than the preview’s expectation of a somewhat muted quarter: units reached a record and rose 44% sequentially. The expected 20–25% net price improvement is also now effective, while management said the product has less than 2% addressable-market penetration.
fact_evidence: AIHESO reached record quarterly unit demand of 65,477, up 44% sequentially and 34% year over year; net pricing improved about 25% effective July 1, gross margins exceeded 90%, and penetration is estimated below 2%.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had pre-warned Q2 would be “somewhat muted” and described a “20–25% net price improvement in H2.”

description: Q2 gross margin was 71%, above the preview’s 66–68% estimate, and management expects it to move back toward the high 70s in H2. This is a better starting point for the recovery than the preview’s modeled quarter implied.
fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin was 71% in Q2” and is expected to trend back toward the high 70s in the second half as AIHESO’s revenue cycle normalizes and product mix improves.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 gross margin at “~66–68%E” and said anything below roughly 64% would signal pricing actions were not flowing through.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Tervaia deal came with additional economics and operating costs not detailed in the preview: management expects more than $30M in 2027 revenue and exclusivity through 2034, but also roughly $20M of annualized SG&A once integrated. Integration costs may weigh on early quarters, though management said they will not reduce 2026 earnings.
fact_evidence: The acquisition is for $30 million upfront funded from cash, with self-funded contingent milestones; management expects more than $30 million in 2027 revenue, accretive economics and assumed exclusivity through 2034, alongside roughly $20 million in annualized SG&A once fully integrated. Early integration costs are not expected to pull down 2026 earnings.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the announced deal had a “$30M TYRVAYA upfront,” was cash-funded, and was expected to be “accretive shortly after close.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management provided a new GMELT regulatory timeline that the preview did not discuss: a pre-NDA FDA meeting is scheduled for early Q4, with an NDA targeted for H1 2027 and potential approval and launch in 2028.
fact_evidence: GMELT secured a pre-NDA FDA meeting for early Q4; NDA submission is targeted for the first half of 2027, potential approval for the first half of 2028, and commercial launch later that year.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Relmada had not filed the NDV-01 IND or started RESCUE by the time of the call, despite the prior mid-2026 target. Management attributed the slip mainly to Piramal’s GMP production schedule and said manufacturing execution remained; enrollment can start after the 30-day IND review.
fact_evidence: The mid-2026 IND timeline slipped primarily due to delays getting on Piramal’s GMP production schedule; management characterized development activities as complete with only manufacturing execution remaining. Patient enrollment can begin shortly after the 30-day IND review period.
expectation_evidence: Management guided at Q1 to “IND filing and Phase 3 RESCUE initiation in ‘mid-2026’”; the preview called whether the program had “actually started” the key issue.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The expected year-end 2026 initial three-month response-data disclosure may move to first-half 2027. Management said it preferred a more meaningful six-month readout from 15–20 patients over early three-month results.
fact_evidence: Management indicated the previously guided year-end three-month complete response data disclosure may be pushed to first-half 2027, favoring a more meaningful six-month readout with 15-20 patients over early three-month results.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “initial 3-month response data from the 2L BCG-unresponsive study by year-end 2026” and identified reaffirmation of that timing as a key metric.

description: Q2 R&D expense was well below the preview’s estimate, rather than stepping up to reflect Phase 3 startup spending. The $8.4 million result was below even the preview’s $10–16 million range and its stated expectation that a move to $12 million or more would corroborate that spend had started.
fact_evidence: R&D expense was $8.4 million in Q2 2026, driven by higher NDV-01 and sepranolone study costs plus increased manufacturing and drug storage costs.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 R&D at “$12.5M (range $10–16M)” and said “a move to $12M+ corroborates that spend has started.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Sepranolone also missed the expected mid-2026 initiation timing: the company now plans to file its IND by year-end, with the Phase 2 study to begin only after clearance.
fact_evidence: The company plans to file an IND for sepranolone by year-end 2026, with the Phase 2 study to initiate upon IND clearance.
expectation_evidence: The preview said sepranolone Phase 2b was “also guided mid-2026” and flagged initiation status as a key metric.

description: The quarterly loss was materially smaller than expected: Relmada reported a $12.9 million net loss and a $0.11 per-share loss, versus the preview’s roughly $20.1 million loss and $0.19 estimated loss per share, as well as the cited $0.21 consensus loss per share. The lower per-share loss partly reflects a larger share count.
fact_evidence: Q2 2026 net loss was $12.9 million ($0.11 per share), compared with $9.9 million ($0.30 per share) a year earlier; the lower per-share loss reflected a larger share count.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss … ~$20.1M” and “EPS … -$0.19,” and listed Q2 EPS consensus of “-$0.21.”

description: G&A expense came in below the preview’s estimate and range, declining year over year rather than landing near the anticipated $10 million.
fact_evidence: G&A expense declined to $6.6 million from $7.4 million year-over-year, primarily on lower stock-based and employee compensation.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 G&A at “$10.0M (range $9–12M).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview’s base case expected quarter-end cash of $1–2 million, but DRCT ended Q2 with only $0.5 million. Cash plus receivables also fell to $3.2 million from $3.9 million at year-end, leaving liquidity weaker than the preview’s base case implied.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with just $500,000 in cash and cash equivalents,” and “Total cash plus accounts receivable was only $3.2 million as of June 30, 2026, down from $3.9 million at the end of 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The base case projected “cash $1–2M funded by facility draws.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview treated a second covenant breach as a bear-case risk, while DRCT reported that it was not in compliance with certain financial covenants and had requested a lender waiver. The breach and ongoing waiver discussions are worse than the preview’s base case of no new covenant breach.
fact_evidence: “Direct Digital was not in compliance with certain financial covenants under its credit facility and has requested a waiver from its lender, with discussions ongoing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “second consecutive breach requiring a Thirteenth Amendment” was a bear-case condition; its base case assumed “no refi news” and a going-concern reiteration.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: DRCT reported new AI search, GEO, and web-infrastructure offerings, along with an approximately 80% retention rate for clients representing about 80% of first-half revenue. The preview looked for quantified Ignition+ traction but did not anticipate these specific product launches or this retention disclosure.
fact_evidence: “The company launched new AI search, GEO, and web infrastructure technology offerings” and reported “approximately 80% client retention among clients representing about 80% of first-half revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Ignition+ had “strong initial interest” but had “never put a number on it,” and that “any disclosed customer count or bookings figure would be new information.”

description: Fortune Brands cut FY26 EPS guidance excluding tariff benefits to $2.70–$3.00 from $3.00–$3.30, about $0.30 lower at the midpoint, rather than reaffirming the prior range. Management attributed roughly $0.20 of the reduction to incremental investments and $0.10 to service-related volume loss.
fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year EPS guidance excluding tariff benefits to $2.70-$3.00 (from a prior $3.00-$3.30), roughly $0.30 lower at the midpoint, with about $0.20 from incremental investments and $0.10 from service-related volume loss.”

expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) | Consensus | $0.02.” The preview’s base scenario also assumed “no land sale.”

fact_evidence: “The BLA remains under review with a PDUFA target action date of August 22, 2026, though the FDA has agreed to extend that date upon receiving a planned BLA amendment.”
expectation_evidence: “The August 22 PDUFA for deramiocel — nine days after the call — is the entire equity.”

description: Rather than continuing to pursue the preview’s cardiomyopathy-focused approval path, Capricor plans to amend the BLA for a refined indication focused on upper-limb skeletal-muscle function. fact_evidence: “Capricor plans to submit a BLA amendment including 24-month open-label extension data from HOPE-3 to pursue a refined indication focused on upper limb skeletal muscle function rather than cardiomyopathy.”
expectation_evidence: The preview centered on the August 22 PDUFA and described the advisory committee vote as being on “substantial evidence of effectiveness in DMD cardiomyopathy”; it noted that “the panel's upper-limb discussion was reportedly directionally supportive.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: A statistical-model correction weakened the all-patient left-ventricular-ejection-fraction result from the earlier 2.4-point, p=0.04 result to 1.8 points, p=0.09. The cardiomyopathy subgroup result remained significant, but results lower in the testing hierarchy are now only nominally significant.
fact_evidence: “A statistical model correction reverted the key secondary endpoint (LV ejection fraction in all patients) from a 2.4-point difference (p=0.04) at top line to a weaker 1.8-point difference (p=0.09) as published in The Lancet”; the subgroup result was unchanged at 2.8 points with p=0.02, while lower endpoints are “now only nominally significant.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FDA briefing document reported that HOPE-3 “failed its prespecified primary and secondary endpoints,” but did not flag this subsequent model correction or its specific effect on the published result.

description: Q2 loss was worse than the preview’s estimates: net loss was about $40.7 million and EPS was $(0.70), versus an estimated net loss of about $35 million and EPS of $(0.60), with consensus EPS at $(0.58)–$(0.59). Higher operating expenses accompanied the miss.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss widened to approximately $40.7 million ($0.70 per share) … with operating expenses rising to $42.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS … $(0.58) – $(0.59)”; “My Estimate” was $(0.60), and “Net loss” was estimated at “~$35M.”

The preview had identified a spending pause as a possible response to regulatory uncertainty, but not as its base case.
fact_evidence: “The company is slowing commercial readiness spending and pacing capital deployment until it gains greater regulatory clarity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked, “Are they still spending into launch?” and described the base case as “no new information”; it listed commercial spend “paused” in the bear scenario.

description: Capricor withdrew its preliminary-injunction motion against NS Pharma and said rescission of the U.S. distribution agreement will instead proceed through arbitration expected this fall. The preview identified the litigation as important, but had looked for an injunction ruling, settlement, or reversion of rights rather than this stated route and timing.
fact_evidence: “Capricor withdrew its preliminary injunction motion against NS Pharma and will pursue rescission of the U.S. distribution agreement through arbitration expected to begin this fall.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “any settlement, injunction ruling, or reversion of U.S. rights” would be a catalyst and listed “hearing dates, settlement posture, or reversion of U.S. commercial rights” to watch.

fact_evidence: “All non-deramocel pipeline work is on hold.”

fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $158-162 million,” including its 40% share of Propelis adjusted EBITDA.
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance (adj. EBITDA, incl. 40% Propelis) | ≥ $180M”; the preview expected a reaffirmation, possibly with hedges.

description: Industrial Technology adjusted EBITDA was a $5.4 million loss, well below the preview’s estimate of a $1 million loss to breakeven. Two anticipated engineering orders were lost, others were delayed, and another order’s scope was reduced, leading to a restructuring and strategic review.
fact_evidence: Industrial technology “swung to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $5.4 million versus a $9 million profit”; the engineering/OBRA business “lost two anticipated orders,” saw others delayed, and had an order scope immediately reduced, prompting a “$10 million annual cost-reduction restructuring and a strategic review.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Industrial Tech adjusted EBITDA at “~$(1)M to $0M” and said it “must inflect positive.”

fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net loss of $23.7 million (-$0.75 per share), compared to net income of $15.4 million ($0.49 per share) a year ago,” largely reflecting “the absence of a prior-year SGK divestiture gain and weaker industrial technology results.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed expected GAAP EPS as “low positive / near breakeven.”

fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q3 sales fell to $246 million from $349 million,” driven by “roughly $85 million of divestiture impact” and partly offset by “$4.4 million from the Dodge acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave “Revenue | $264.5M” consensus and a “~$257M” base estimate.

expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Propelis 40% contribution” at “~$9.9M” and did not flag a SAP-related synergy delay.

expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Memorialization at “~$210M / ~$44M” and highlighted the need to watch price versus volume and input-cost commentary.

fact_evidence: “CEO Joe Bartolese announced his intention to retire once a successor is hired.”

fact_evidence: The company announced “planned $5 million corporate cost reductions for next year.”

fact_evidence: “Management guided to a 20% non-GAAP operating margin in Q4 2026, up sharply from 13.7% in Q2, and raised full-year operating income guidance to $129-133 million.”

expectation_evidence: “A refinancing announcement — or the conspicuous absence of a plan — is a real catalyst and is not in most models.”

fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for ARR declining further to approximately $812 million, with core solutions roughly flat sequentially and the decline coming from noncore offerings.”

fact_evidence: “The company announced a restructuring impacting approximately 12% of its workforce, incurring $10-11 million in charges, to refocus resources on core platform solutions.”

fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow guidance was maintained at approximately $130 million (~15.5% margin), with management expecting free cash flow to improve in 2027 despite a lower ARR base.”

expectation_evidence: The preview identified “European TB $10–15M in FY26” as the expected outlook.

expectation_evidence: The preview said the Q2 guide midpoint “implies EI of only ~$26–28M.”
