description: The preview's earnings bridge implied Q3 EPS of about $1.90. Onto guided to approximately $2.28, well above that implied level.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for … EPS of approximately $2.28.”

description: The preview cited an approximately 25% full-year growth target for Advanced Nodes. The call reported 50% sequential growth in Q2 to about $120M and raised the full-year growth outlook to above 35%, with both memory and logic contributing.
fact_evidence: “Advanced nodes revenue grew 50% sequentially to approximately $120 million, with memory … up ~60% and logic up over 40%, and full-year growth expected to exceed 35%.”
expectation_evidence: “Advanced Nodes — $80M in Q1 vs. ~25% FY growth target.”

description: The preview highlighted limited Q1 cash and a prospective $710M Rigaku outlay as reasons to scrutinize post-deal liquidity. The call reported nearly $1.9B in cash alongside a new $1.5B 0% convertible offering, a materially larger cash position than the preview's cited starting point.
fact_evidence: “The company completed a $1.5 billion 0% convertible debt offering (net ~$1.2 billion) … [and] holds nearly $1.9 billion in cash.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “cash & marketable securities $654.2M” at Q1 and said the “$710M Rigaku outlay lands in H2 against a $654.2M pre-raise cash balance.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed a single-OSAT Dragonfly order exceeding $200M, with most deliveries in 2027. The preview expected a Dragonfly ramp but did not anticipate an order of this size or its extended delivery visibility.
fact_evidence: “The company secured over $200 million in Dragonfly orders from a single OSAT partner, with the majority to be delivered in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Dragonfly G5 as “<5–10% of Q1 revenue” and said management had indicated units would “nearly double each quarter”; it did not cite a large single-partner order.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview did not flag a record backlog above $1.1B or that a substantial portion was already associated with 2027 deliveries. That adds stronger forward visibility than the preview's general H2 ramp discussion anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Backlog surpassed a record $1.1 billion, with roughly 30-40% tied to 2027 deliveries, signaling strong customer visibility into next year.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The call introduced silicon photonics as a future growth opportunity with a projected $500M market by 2030; the preview did not identify this opportunity.
fact_evidence: Management identified “silicon photonics ($500M SAM by 2030) … as [a] future growth driver.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview characterized free cash flow as a significant pressure point, citing a cut in expected FY26 conversion to 30% and KUBRA’s capex needs and debt interest. Instead, Q2 free cash flow was $27.4 million, with 75% conversion (81% adjusted), a notably strong quarter against that concern, though it does not establish full-year conversion.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $27.4 million (75% conversion), up 21% year-over-year, with adjusted free cash flow conversion of 81%.”
expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow conversion — cut from 45% to 30% for FY26. A real, underappreciated negative: KUBRA is more capex-intensive and the new debt carries heavy cash interest.”

description: Business payments grew faster than the preview’s Q1-based expectation: reported growth accelerated from 18% to 32%, and normalized growth rose from 16% to 19%. The reported rate includes political media contributions, but the normalized rate also accelerated.
fact_evidence: “Business payments revenue accelerated to 32% reported growth (19% normalized excluding political media).”
expectation_evidence: “Business Payments momentum. The genuine bright spot: +18% reported / +16% normalized in Q1.” The preview warned, “If this decelerates, the growth story loses its last clean leg.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s roughly $38 million estimate at $36.3 million, even though adjusted EPS matched consensus. The roughly 36% EBITDA margin was also below the preview’s approximate 37% estimate; management attributed the margin pressure almost entirely to KUBRA’s lower-margin mix, as the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA grew 14% year-over-year to $36.3 million”; adjusted EBITDA margin was “~36%,” with declines attributed “almost entirely to CUBRA's lower-margin mix.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 adj. EBITDA estimate: ~$38M (~37% margin).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The AP supplier network grew, but more slowly than the preview’s cited pace: it reached over 731,000 vendors, up 65% year-over-year, versus the preview’s expectation of 70% growth. This contrasts with the acceleration in business payments revenue.
fact_evidence: “The AP supplier network reaching over 731,000 vendors, up 65% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Supplier network +70% YoY to 665,000 vendors.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Reported pro forma synergized net leverage was about 3.7x, slightly below the preview’s 4.0x net leverage figure at close. The measures are not stated on exactly the same basis, so the apparent improvement is modest rather than conclusive evidence of faster deleveraging.
fact_evidence: “Pro forma synergized net leverage stood at approximately 3.7x, with a target of below 3x within 18 months.”
expectation_evidence: “4.0x net at close, targeting <3.0x within 18 months.”

description: Revenue of $498 million was above the preview’s working estimate of about $475 million, though it was below the preview’s cited alternative estimate of $508.7 million. The revenue result therefore looks better against the working estimate, but the preview’s flagged consensus discrepancy makes the beat less definitive.
fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue rose to $498 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “I use ~$475M as the working consensus,” while also citing “$508.7M (Chartmill).”

description: Stimulation Services’ margin reached only 9%, below the preview’s key test of clearing roughly 11–12%. The segment’s EBITDA rose sequentially, but the margin result fell short of the price-capture improvement the preview said was central to the Q2 thesis.
fact_evidence: Stimulation Services revenue grew to $430 million with EBITDA rising to $39 million, a 9% margin.
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If Stim margin doesn't clear ~11–12% in Q2, either the price increases didn't stick or they were given back in white space,” and listed “Stimulation margin ≥11%” as a catalyst.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow remained negative at $8 million, rather than reaching the preview’s roughly breakeven base-case expectation. The outflow did improve substantially from Q1, but year-to-date free cash outflow was still roughly $40 million.
fact_evidence: Free cash flow was negative $8 million in Q2, improving from negative $25 million in Q1, with year-to-date free cash outflow of roughly $40 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “FCF ~breakeven” and flagged Q2 free cash flow as a key item to watch.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Liquidity was about $72 million, materially below the preview’s $108 million figure following the refinancing. ABL borrowings also rose to $162 million from $116 million quarter-over-quarter, leaving liquidity tighter than the preview’s setup suggested.
fact_evidence: The new $300 million ABL replaced the prior $275 million facility, but total liquidity remained tight at approximately $72 million; ABL borrowings rose to $162 million from $116 million quarter-over-quarter.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “total liquidity $108M” and said the new ABL “materially de-risks the near term.”

description: The CEO is resigning effective August 7, and Executive Chairman Matt Wilks will take over as CEO while retaining the chairman role. The preview did not flag an imminent leadership change.
fact_evidence: CEO Ladd Wilks is resigning effective August 7th to take a board seat, with Executive Chairman Matt Wilks assuming the CEO role while retaining his chairman title.

description: Flotek delivered a sharp sequential increase in both revenue and EBITDA, with revenue rising from $72 million to $102 million and EBITDA from $11 million to $19 million. The preview gave Q1 figures and identified Flotek as a secondary watch item, but did not forecast a Q2 result of this strength.
fact_evidence: Flotek revenue jumped to $102 million from $72 million and EBITDA rose to $19 million from $11 million.

description: Adjusted EBITDA of $69 million was just below the preview’s $72 million buy-side whisper, although it remained within the preview’s broader $68–78 million base-case range. This is a modest shortfall against the more demanding expectation, not a miss against the stated base range.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was $69 million, a 14% margin.
expectation_evidence: The preview described the buy-side whisper as “EBITDA ≥ $72M” and gave a base-case range of “$68–78M.”

description: Q2 revenue was $392.4 million, well above the preview’s $360.2–360.7 million consensus and the company’s $355–365 million guidance. The roughly 9% beat versus the guidance midpoint was substantially larger than the preview’s bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue reached a record $392.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus $360.2M (Zacks) / $360.7M”; “Q2 FY26 Guidance $355–365M.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $540–560 million was far above the preview’s approximately $410 million consensus and its $425 million-or-higher momentum threshold. The midpoint is about one-third above consensus, well beyond the preview’s bullish scenario of at least $445 million.
fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $540-560 million, representing approximately 40% sequential growth at the midpoint, led by Scorpio-X Series volume production.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 ~$410M”; “a guide starting with a ‘4’ and midpoint ≥$425M”; bull scenario “≥$445M.”

description: Scorpio is expected to become Astera’s largest product line in Q3—one quarter earlier than the preview’s year-end 2026 expectation—and Scorpio-X is expected to exceed Scorpio-P revenue. That indicates a faster product-line transition than the preview’s anticipated Q3 Scorpio share test.
fact_evidence: “Scorpio is expected to become the company's largest product line by revenue in Q3, one quarter ahead of prior expectations, with Scorpio-X surpassing Scorpio-P revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Management says it becomes the largest product line by end-2026”; the preview said the buy-side test was Scorpio “approaching ~25% or more of revenue this quarter.”

description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.80, above the preview’s $0.69 consensus and $0.68–0.70 guidance. It even reached the lower end of the preview’s explicitly bullish $0.80–0.84 scenario.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.80 in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $0.68–0.70” guidance and “$0.69” consensus; bull scenario “$0.80–0.84.”

description: Q2 operating margin reached 39.1%, versus the preview’s roughly 36% expectation, and management guided to approximately 43% in Q3. The reported margin improvement and further expected operating leverage were stronger than the preview’s implied Q2 path.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 39.1% in Q2 (up 290 bps) and is guided to approximately 43% in Q3 (up 400 bps), reflecting significant operating leverage.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin ~36% implied.”

description: Q2 gross margin was 73.7%, above the approximately 73% guidance and the preview’s 73.5% threshold for defusing the margin concern. However, Q3 guidance of approximately 72% is below that Q2 level and points to further mix-related pressure, matching a risk the preview had highlighted.
fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 73.7% (above 73% guidance), but Q3 gross margin is guided lower to approximately 72% due to increased switch/module mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Guidance ~73%”; “If reported GM lands ≥73.5% ... the margin scare defuses”; “If Q3 is guided to ~72% or below, the ‘Scorpio scales, margins fade’ bear case gets its evidence.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: PCIe 6 products across AI fabric and signal conditioning rose to more than half of Q2 revenue, compared with roughly one-third in Q1. The preview had flagged PCIe Gen 6 as just over one-third of Q1 revenue to watch, so the reported mix indicates a much faster shift toward these products than that baseline suggested.
fact_evidence: “PCIe 6 products across AI fabric and signal conditioning represented more than 50% of total revenue in Q2, up from roughly one-third in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “PCIe Gen 6 mix (>1/3 of revenue in Q1) and signal conditioning (>1/3 of Q1 revenue) — is the legacy Aries/Taurus base still growing, or is Scorpio cannibalizing the mix?”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management described a future Scorpio-X content opportunity well beyond $1,000 per XPU, targeting multiple thousands of dollars of total content per XPU. The preview already cited a $1,000-plus content target, so the materially higher multiple-thousands ambition is incremental upside.
fact_evidence: “Management sees Scorpio-X content opportunity growing well beyond $1,000 per XPU in future generations, targeting total content of multiple thousands of dollars per XPU.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “$1,000+ of content per accelerator” target.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Astera reported more than 10 customers engaged on Scorpio-X, with additional customers expected to reach production by late 2025 or early 2026. That is more quantified customer breadth and an earlier ramp outlook than the preview’s expectation of initial shipments to multiple hyperscalers and additional Scorpio-P customers toward the end of 2026.
fact_evidence: “The company has over 10 customers engaged on Scorpio-X, with additional customers expected to ramp to production by late 2025 or early 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Scorpio X initial shipments to multiple hyperscalers” and Scorpio-P moving “to at least two additional major hyperscalers toward the end of 2026.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Astera closed a new Leo memory-controller design win at a U.S. hyperscaler and expects volume CXL shipments to two U.S. hyperscalers in 2027. The preview mentioned Leo/CXL activity with Microsoft in private beta, but did not anticipate this additional win or the two-hyperscaler shipment outlook.
fact_evidence: “A new Leo memory controller design win was closed at a U.S. hyperscaler, with volume CXL shipments to two U.S. hyperscalers expected in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “Leo/CXL with Microsoft Azure M-series in private beta.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $9.41, well above the preview’s $7.40 working consensus midpoint and the listed $7.68 Zacks estimate, though just below the preview’s $9.50–10.50 bull case. The reported result exceeded the preview’s consensus-based expectation by roughly 27%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted earnings were $3.8 billion, with adjusted EPS of $9.41 and reported EPS of $9.55.”
expectation_evidence: “I use $7.40 as the working consensus midpoint below”; consensus adjusted EPS “$7.68.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Phillips 66 reached its existing $17 billion debt target ahead of schedule, expects net debt below $16 billion by year-end, and introduced a lower net-debt target of approximately $13.5–14 billion. The preview anticipated a $17 billion target only by year-end 2027 and did not anticipate the new lower target.
fact_evidence: “Expects net debt below $16 billion by year-end, and plans to hit its $17 billion debt target ahead of the 2027 schedule”; “signaled a new net debt target of approximately $13.5 billion to $14 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Debt walk toward $19B by YE2026 (then $17B YE2027).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Refining captured 98% of its market indicator in Q2, a strong result against the preview’s concern that Phillips 66 might fail to capture the unusually strong refining environment. The preview did not state a specific Q2 capture-rate estimate.
fact_evidence: “Refining captured 98% of its market indicator in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “If PSX's realized margin prints below ~$18–20/bbl, the market will read it as a capture-rate failure”; the preview also cited capture-rate concerns versus peers.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Rodeo Renewable Fuels ran at a record 106% utilization, while RD prices and RINs roughly doubled versus 2025 amid the Iran conflict. The preview discussed Middle East disruption as a chemicals headwind but did not anticipate this combination of strong renewable-fuels utilization and pricing.
fact_evidence: “Rodeo Renewable Fuels ran above nameplate at record 106% utilization, with RD prices and RINs roughly doubling versus 2025 due to the Iran conflict.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The quarter included a one-time $100 million tariff-refund benefit that the preview did not flag, adding a discrete positive to results.
fact_evidence: “A one-time $100 million tariff-refund benefit.”

description: Refining operating cost was $5.57 per barrel, already close to the $5.50 target set for 2027; management attributed the progress to more than 200 initiatives it described as structural and permanent. The preview identified the target but did not anticipate how close costs would already be or emphasize the permanence of the savings.
fact_evidence: “Refining Q2 operating cost of $5.57/barrel is closing in on the annualized $5.50/barrel target for 2027, supported by over 200 cost-reduction initiatives that management describes as structural and permanent.”
expectation_evidence: “Secondary: refining opex/bbl (Q1 $6.21, targeting $5.50 by 2027).”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management quantified substantial refining capacity outages in Asia, the Middle East, and Russia, and disclosed that each $1 widening in the WTI/WCS spread adds about $140 million to annual EBITDA. The preview discussed Iran-related crack strength but did not provide these outage totals or the quantified spread sensitivity.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 7 million barrels/day of Asian/Middle East refining and 1.4 million b/d of Russian capacity is offline”; “every $1 widening in the WTI/WCS spread adds about $140 million to annual EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “the same Hormuz-region disruption that inflated refining cracks” was affecting the industry, but did not quantify offline capacity or WTI/WCS sensitivity.

description: Kingstone reported diluted EPS of $1.05, above the preview’s $0.95 consensus and the $0.90–$1.00 base-case range. The beat was solid but not as large as the preview’s bull-case $1.10–$1.20.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS of $1.05, up 35% year over year.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $0.95”; base case: “EPS $0.90–$1.00.”

description: The reported GAAP net combined ratio was 70.2%, materially better than the preview’s 75–77% base-case combined-ratio scenario. This is a GAAP net ratio, so it is not directly comparable to the preview’s separate 74–76% underlying combined-ratio guide.
fact_evidence: “The GAAP net combined ratio improved 1.3 points to 70.2%.”
expectation_evidence: Base case: “Combined Ratio 75–77%”; the preview also said to watch the “Underlying combined ratio vs. the 74–76% guide.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The underlying loss ratio rose to 43.1%, contrary to the preview’s expectation that the Select mix could push the non-cat loss ratio into the mid-30s. This indicates weaker underlying loss performance than the preview’s favorable operating thesis anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The underlying loss ratio rose to 43.1% from 38.7% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch whether Select mix keeps pushing the non-cat loss ratio into the mid-30s.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The quarter had a negative 0.8% catastrophe loss ratio, better than the preview’s already-low expectation of roughly 1–3 points. The June storms did not produce the cat load that the preview’s base case allowed for.
fact_evidence: “The quarter benefited from a negative 0.8% catastrophe loss ratio.”
expectation_evidence: “Cat loss ratio vs. ~1–3 pt whisper”; base case assumed a “Modest June cat load (2–4 pts).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Kingstone recorded $1.6 million of favorable prior-year reserve development, rather than the adverse development the preview identified as a possible downside scenario.
fact_evidence: “$1.6 million (2.7 points) of favorable prior-year reserve development.”
expectation_evidence: The bear case included “adverse PY development” as a possible driver.

description: Management reaffirmed the full-year guidance range rather than narrowing it toward the upper half, which the preview said investors were looking for. The unchanged $2.20–$2.90 EPS range also remains below the preview’s roughly $2.54 FY26 EPS consensus at its low end.
fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance,” including “EPS of $2.20-$2.90.”
expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm at this point reads as conservative-to-disappointing”; the bull trigger was “guidance narrowed to the upper half ($2.55–$2.90).”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management warned that the market is softening and becoming more competitive, particularly in Dwelling Fire, and expects New York growth to moderate in the second half. The preview expected continued growth and focused on whether it would remain strong, but did not anticipate this explicit market-softening warning.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged a softening, increasingly competitive market—most visible in Dwelling Fire—and expects New York growth to moderate in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said growth “continued into the second quarter” at “slightly higher” premium growth and asked whether organic growth could remain “mid-to-high-teens.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Diluted book value per share was $8.69, above the preview’s estimate of current BVPS of about $7.91. That is a substantially higher reported book value than the preview carried into the release.
fact_evidence: “Diluted book value per share rose 35% year over year to $8.69.”
expectation_evidence: “Current BVPS ~$7.91.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The new reinsurance placement did more than the preview’s expected roughly 15% cost reduction: it cut risk-adjusted core catastrophe excess-of-loss cost by over 15%, increased total catastrophe protection to $500 million, and added wildfire coverage.
fact_evidence: “The July 1 reinsurance placement increased total catastrophe protection 14% to $500 million, added wildfire coverage, and cut core cat excess-of-loss risk-adjusted cost by over 15%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a “15%-cheaper reinsurance tower.”

description: Kingstone disclosed that it had repurchased about 19,500 shares at an average price of $14.98. The preview identified Q2 buyback execution as incremental and worth watching, but the disclosed purchase was modest in scale.
fact_evidence: “Repurchased ~19,500 shares at an average $14.98.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any buyback execution in Q2 is incremental” and asked whether any authorization had been used at prices well below $20.80.

description: i3 Verticals reported Q3 revenue of $53.1 million, below the $54.99 million consensus, with total growth of just 2% and organic revenue down 2%. The preview expected roughly 6% growth and viewed flat organic revenue as the key threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue rose only 2% to $53.1 million from $51.9 million, while organic revenue declined 2%.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $54.99M” and “Implied Y/Y +6.0%”; the preview also said, “If organic stays at zero for a third straight quarter” it would weaken the growth narrative.

description: The company cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $216–221 million, below the prior $221–229 million range, and lowered adjusted EPS guidance to $1.08–1.12 from $1.09–1.15. This was a second revenue-guidance reduction in the fiscal year, rather than the expected reaffirmation.
fact_evidence: “Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $216-221 million and adjusted EPS to $1.08-1.12,” including “a $6.5 million revenue reduction” attributed mostly to professional services and the rest to decelerating transaction revenue.
expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm at $221–229M / $61–65M / $1.09–1.15 is the buy-side expectation”; the preview called a second outright cut “the bear trigger.”

description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $13.3 million, well below the preview’s roughly $15.4 million model, and its 25% margin fell short of the roughly 27–28% run rate the preview said was needed. The expected margin step-up had not yet appeared in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 5% to $13.3 million with margin improving to 25% from 24.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~ $15.4M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~28.0% (modeled)”; and “Q3 is the first quarter where that has to actually show up in reported numbers.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ARR reached $174.1 million and grew 8%, below the preview’s modeled $179–182 million and 11–13% growth. That missed the preview’s roughly 10% minimum for the recurring-growth thesis.
fact_evidence: “Annualized recurring revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $174.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “ARR ~$179–182M (modeled),” “+11–13%,” and “below ~10% breaks the ‘recurring engine intact’ thesis.”

description: Maintenance revenue fell 13% because of the timing of SaaS conversions, a steeper current decline than the preview anticipated. Management expects the decline to normalize to about 3.5% going forward, limiting the duration of the shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Maintenance revenue dropped 13% due to timing of SaaS conversions, expected to normalize to about a 3.5% decline going forward.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A $9.9 million unrealized gain on a minority equity investment was recorded in other income, an unanticipated gain that increased reported income but was not a recurring operating result.
fact_evidence: “Results included a $9.9 million unrealized gain on a minority equity investment recorded in other income.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: High commercial-card usage drove elevated interchange rates that reduced the payments net take rate by more than $1 million. Management described it as a data issue expected to be fixed with its processor in Q4, but it was an unanticipated near-term hit.
fact_evidence: “Elevated interchange rates from high commercial card usage cut over $1 million from the payments net take rate,” and management expects “to fix” the issue “with its processor in Q4.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Debt was $114.3 million and cash only $2.6 million, compared with the preview’s March balance-sheet figures of $81 million of debt and $7.1 million of cash. The company also had $285.7 million of revolver capacity, below the preview’s $319 million figure.
fact_evidence: “Debt stood at $114.3 million with $285.7 million of remaining revolver capacity and only $2.6 million cash.”
expectation_evidence: “Debt $81M, cash $7.1M at March 31” and “$319M of revolver capacity.”

description: The company lowered FY2027 revenue growth guidance to mid-single digits from previously guided high-single-digit growth, a weaker outlook than the prior expectation embedded in its guidance.
fact_evidence: “FY2027 revenue growth guidance was lowered to mid-single digits from previously guided high single-digit growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Previously guided high single-digit growth.”

description: The share count had fallen from over 34 million to under 28 million due to buybacks, indicating repurchases had been carried out rather than merely remaining a possible capital-allocation action.
fact_evidence: “Buybacks reduced adjusted weighted average shares from over 34 million to under 28 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “both acquisitions and buybacks” and that “an announced or executed repurchase” was a key capital-allocation signal to watch.

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.25, slightly above the $0.24 consensus, even though EBITDA and revenue missed expectations.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS from continuing operations rose 8.5% to $0.25 from $0.23.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. Diluted EPS $0.24 (range $0.23–$0.24).”

description: Professional services declined by $1.8 million, a smaller drag than the preview’s expected $2–3 million year-over-year decline. The weakness was still concentrated in utilities.
fact_evidence: Revenue was “hurt by a $1.8 million drop in professional services concentrated in the utilities market.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “budget another $2–3M y/y drag in Q3” from professional services.

description: Paymentus reported Q2 revenue of $360.7 million, above the $345.4 million consensus estimate and even above the top of its $340–350 million guidance range. The result exceeded consensus by about 4.4%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $360.7 million, up 28.8% year-over-year, exceeding the top end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $345.4M”; “Q2 FY2026: revenue $340–350M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $48.8 million, well above the previewed Q2 guidance range of $38–40 million. That is more than 20% above the range’s upper end.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 54% year-over-year to $48.8 million, achieving a record margin of 41.3% and a 740 basis point improvement over the prior year.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026: … adjusted EBITDA $38–40M.”

description: The company raised its full-year outlook above the already-raised guidance cited in the preview, especially for adjusted EBITDA: the new midpoint is about 6.8% higher than the previous midpoint. The revenue midpoint also rose, by about 1.3%.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.443-1.458 billion … and adjusted EBITDA of $175-185 million (raised ~6.8% at midpoint).”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 (raised): revenue $1.425–1.440B; adjusted EBITDA $165–172M”; the preview also calls a raise “the likely swing factor.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.25 exceeded the preview’s cited estimates of $0.16–$0.20, including the highest estimate by $0.05. The preview did not confirm the prior-year comparison, but the call reported growth from $0.15.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income rose 66.7% to $32.4 million, or $0.25 per share.”

description: Oportun reported adjusted EBITDA of $49 million, $10 million above the top of its $34–39 million guidance range. The preview expected Q2 EBITDA near the $37 million midpoint, so this was a substantial beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $49 million, up 56% year-over-year and well above the $34-39 million guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA — Company Guide (May 7, 2026): $34–39M (mid $37M)”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.42 versus the preview’s $0.33 consensus, a much larger result than the expected modest year-over-year increase. The preview also noted a roughly $0.32 effective whisper, widening the gap further.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $0.42 (up 35% YoY).”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.33”; the preview also said “the effective whisper is roughly $0.32.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Oportun’s annualized net charge-off rate was 12.0%, better than the 12.2% guidance midpoint, and management lowered its full-year forecast to 11.7% from 11.9% ±50 basis points. The preview expected an approximately 12.2% Q2 result and highlighted the need to reaffirm an H2 “11 handle”; the Q2 result and lower full-year outlook improved on that setup.
fact_evidence: “The annualized net charge-off rate improved 65 basis points sequentially to 12%, beating guidance, with Q3 guided to 11% and full-year revised down to 11.7%.”
expectation_evidence: “Annualized NCO rate — Company Guide: 12.2% ±15bps”; the preview also described FY NCO guidance as “11.9% ±50bps” and said to watch for an “11 handle” in H2.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Delinquencies reached 4.0%, below the preview’s expected 4.1%–4.2% range. That was a modest but clear improvement on the anticipated credit metric.
fact_evidence: “The 30-plus day delinquency rate fell to 4.0%, below the 4.1-4.2% expectation.”
expectation_evidence: “30+ day delinquency — 4.1%–4.2%.”

description: Q2 revenue was $233 million, about $1 million above the company’s guidance ceiling and above the preview’s consensus range of roughly $231 million. The preview characterized Q2 as tightly guided and largely de-risked, so the beat was positive but small.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $233 million, roughly flat year-over-year but $1 million above the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus: $230.7M–$231.2M | Company Guide: $227–232M”; the preview said “Q2 itself is largely de-risked.”

description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by 6% at the midpoint, to $168 million, rather than merely maintaining the prior $150–165 million range. Adjusted net income and EPS guidance remained unchanged, with management citing fair-value headwinds despite lower interest expense.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised 6% at the midpoint to $168 million (13% growth), while adjusted net income ($74-82 million) and adjusted EPS ($1.50-1.65) guidance were maintained as fair value headwinds offset lower interest expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$150–165M” and described FY adjusted EPS guidance of “$1.50–1.65,” with the key question whether management would “reiterate, narrow, or cut” it.

description: Interest expense fell 30% year over year, and Oportun improved its full-year reduction target to at least 15% from 10%. The preview already identified funding costs as running ahead of plan, but the larger revised savings target was stronger than the stated plan; the reported Q2 decline also included a noncash recognition change.
fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell 30% year-over-year to $42 million, aided by a ~$7 million noncash change in interest expense recognition, and full-year interest expense is now guided to decline at least 15% versus the prior 10% guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the FY target as “≥10% reduction” and said interest expense was “the one line item consistently running ahead of plan.”

description: ATI reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $284 million, $29 million above the high end of its $245–$255 million guidance and well above the roughly $250 million implied consensus estimate. The quarter was its strongest EBITDA result since 2007.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $284 million” and was “$29 million above the high end of prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$250M (implied)” and company guidance of “$245–$255M.”

description: Revenue reached $1.3 billion, above the preview’s $1.22 billion consensus estimate, while growing 11% year over year. That is a clear reversal of the preview’s concern that ATI had repeatedly missed revenue estimates.
fact_evidence: “Revenue up 11% to $1.3 billion.”
expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: “$1,220M”; the preview also said ATI had “missed revenue repeatedly over two years.”

description: ATI’s full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint rose to $1.160 billion, above both the prior $1.010–$1.060 billion guidance range and the preview’s stated bar of a raise to roughly $1.05–$1.09 billion.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year guidance across all metrics: adjusted EBITDA midpoint to $1.160 billion (35% growth).”
expectation_evidence: Prior FY26 guidance was “$1,010–$1,060M”; the preview said the bar was “a raise to roughly $1.05–$1.09B.”

description: The full-year adjusted EPS midpoint increased to $5.04, substantially above the prior guidance range of $4.20–$4.48 and the preview’s bull-case range of about $4.40–$4.60.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS midpoint to $5.04 (56% growth).”
expectation_evidence: Preview estimates listed FY26 adjusted EPS of “$4.20–$4.48”; its bull case cited FY EPS of “~$4.40–$4.60.”

description: ATI raised its full-year free-cash-flow midpoint to $575 million, above the previous $465–$525 million guidance range. The preview had highlighted the back-half-loaded FCF target as something to monitor, but the updated midpoint is higher than that range.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow midpoint to $575 million (51% growth).”
expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted FCF guidance was “$465–$525M.”

description: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 22.6%, versus the preview’s roughly 20.5% expectation. The margin increase was therefore stronger than the preview’s already positive year-over-year margin outlook implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 440 basis points year-over-year to 22.6%.”
expectation_evidence: Preview consensus implied an “Adj. EBITDA margin ~20.5%” and “+~200bps.”

description: AA&S margins were much stronger than the preview’s expected move toward 19%: the reported margin was 23.7%, or 22% excluding the asset-sale gain, and management now expects sustained mid-20% margins. This also turns the segment’s prior-year margin decline into a substantial expansion.
fact_evidence: “AA&S segment margins expanded 930 basis points to an all-time high of 23.7% (22% excluding a $10 million asset sale gain, versus 14% a year ago), with management now guiding to sustained mid-20% margins.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for AA&S margin “pushing toward 19%+.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog increased to $4.4 billion, up 7% sequentially from the $4.1 billion Q1 record. That exceeds the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly flat to 5% growth and its bull-case threshold of more than $4.3 billion.
fact_evidence: “Record backlog reached $4.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 backlog of “$4.1B,” a base case of “~flat to +5%,” and a bull threshold of “backlog >$4.3B.”

description: Defense revenue grew 36% to an all-time high, and management raised its full-year defense growth expectation to the high teens. That is stronger than the preview’s mid-teens reference for full-year defense growth.
fact_evidence: “Defense revenue grew 36% year-over-year to an all-time high,” prompting management to raise full-year defense growth expectations to “high teens.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the existing FY defense guide as “mid-teens.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: ATI disclosed that approximately $30–40 million of HPMC revenue shifted from the first half into the second half because qualifications at the new Mexico facility and EB2 titanium furnace took longer. The revenue is delayed rather than described as lost, and carries high incremental margins, but the timing shift was not flagged in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $30-40 million of HPMC revenue at 40-50% incremental margins shifted from the first half into the second half due to qualification timing at the new Mexico facility and EB2 titanium furnace.”

description: Management raised full-year consolidated incremental margin guidance from 40% to 50%, a sizeable improvement in the expected profitability of incremental revenue that the preview did not specify.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year consolidated incremental margin guidance from 40% to 50%.”

description: Management’s implied Q4 EBITDA of about $335 million corresponds to an annualized exit rate of roughly $1.35 billion, above the newly raised $1.16 billion full-year EBITDA midpoint. This points to a stronger year-end run rate than the preview discussed.
fact_evidence: “Implied Q4 EBITDA of ~$335 million translates to a ~$1.350 billion annualized exit rate.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Jet-engine revenue grew 13% year over year, with high-teens full-year growth expected, and ATI reported lead times reaching 20 months for premium titanium and over 24 months for isothermal forgings. Those lead times extend well beyond the preview’s general expectation of one-year-plus lead times for differentiated materials.
fact_evidence: “Jet engine revenue grew 13% year-over-year (high-teens full-year growth expected)” and lead times were “20 months on premium titanium, and over 24 months on isothermal forgings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “1yr+ lead times on differentiated titanium/nickel.”

description: The preview looked for Q3 revenue of roughly $290–320 million, with anything below $280 million putting the full-year math at risk. AOI instead guided to $255–290 million, a notably weaker range whose midpoint is $272.5 million.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $255-290 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 guided $290–320M” in the base case; “Anything with a 2-handle below $280M breaks the FY math.”

description: The preview's central expectation was that AOI would defend full-year revenue above $1.1 billion. Management instead reaffirmed revenue of “around” $1.1 billion, a softer formulation, while saying production capacity and supply chain cap results below estimated demand.
fact_evidence: “AOI reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue of around $1.1 billion,” capped by capacity and supply chain.
expectation_evidence: “Management defends a FY26 guide (>$1.1B revenue)” and the base case expected “FY reiterated at >$1.1B.”

description: The preview flagged equity issuance as a financing risk, but AOI did raise substantial equity: it raised $538.8 million net through its at-the-market offering. That is a significant dilution event relative to the preview's expectation of a reaffirmation without a raise.
fact_evidence: “Raised $538.8 million net under its new at-the-market equity offering.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for equity/convert issuance language — a raise on this print would be poorly received.”

description: The preview's margin math implied roughly 37% gross margin in 2H to support its expected full-year operating income. Management's stated Q4 target was only about 32–33%, below that implied level, even though it expects a longer-term return to roughly 40%.
fact_evidence: “Expecting Q4 to reach roughly 32-33% as 1.6T mix increases” and targeting a long-term return to “~40%.”
expectation_evidence: “2H gross margin near 37%” was implied by the preview's full-year operating income math.

description: The preview discussed laser and MOCVD constraints, but did not flag a shortage of memory that would prevent customers from sourcing 100G switches. AOI expects that issue to cut Q3 100G revenue by $20–25 million and persist into late 2026 or early 2027.
fact_evidence: “A Q3 decline of $20-25 million in 100G revenue” due to customers' inability to source 100G switches; the memory shortage is expected to persist “until late 2026 or early 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Supply chain / laser constraint” and MOCVD backlog, but did not identify a memory shortage disrupting customers' 100G switches.

description: The preview expected Q2 CATV revenue of $75–80 million and questioned whether the business would hold up as data center revenue scaled. CATV reached $80.6 million and AOI guided to $100–110 million for Q3, indicating continued growth rather than merely holding steady.
fact_evidence: “CATV revenue hit a record $80.6 million” and Q3 guidance was “$100-110 million.”
expectation_evidence: “CATV rev” Q2 guide was “$75–80M”; the preview asked “whether it holds as data center scales.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview did not anticipate a specific DOCSIS 4.0 customer win. Mediacom selected AOI as its primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades, a new positive indication for the CATV business.
fact_evidence: “Mediacom selected AOI as primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected Q2 manufacturing capacity of about 150,000 units per month. AOI said it was already approaching 200,000, and also gave a new target of more than 930,000 units per month by the end of 2027.
fact_evidence: “Monthly manufacturing capacity is approaching 200,000 units” and targets are “over 650,000 units/month by end of 2026 and over 930,000 units/month by end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Capacity exited Q1 at ~100k units/month with a Q2 target of 150k/month, >650k/month by YE26.”

description: AOI reported $565.5 million in Q2 capital investments, including $280 million in equipment prepayments. The preview noted rising capex and the need to expand capacity, but its stated Q1 capex was $68.7 million and it did not anticipate investment at this scale in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Made $565.5 million in Q2 capital investments (including $280 million in equipment prepayments).”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 capex was $68.7M and rising.”

description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was expected at $0.02–$0.03, but AOI reported $0.06 per diluted share and returned to non-GAAP profitability. The beat was partly aided by foreign tax benefits and government subsidies, so the reported result was stronger but included benefits the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “Net income of $5.5 million or $0.06 per diluted share,” beating guidance, “aided by foreign tax benefits and government subsidies.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus was “$0.02–0.03”; Q2 guidance was “$(0.03) – $0.03.”

description: The preview expected an 800G ramp in Q2 and meaningful later-year growth, but did not anticipate management guiding to roughly fivefold sequential growth in Q3. Q2 800G revenue was already $12.8 million, more than doubling sequentially.
fact_evidence: “800G revenue reached $12.8 million,” more than doubling sequentially, with management guiding for “roughly 5x sequential growth in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 800G to become the largest data-center line and cited roughly 4x sequential unit growth, but gave no comparable Q3 revenue-growth outlook.

description: Revenue was $29.8 million, about $3.7 million below the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $33.5 million and below its $32.5 million lower bear-case threshold. Instead of the expected 7.7% year-over-year growth, revenue declined from $31.12 million a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $29.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~ $33.5M (derived, not published)” and “Q2 revenue vs. ~$33.5M derived / ~$33M whisper”; the preview described sub-$32.5M as a bear outcome.

description: Diluted EPS was $0.01, well below the preview’s $0.04 MarketBeat consensus and $0.06 Zacks estimate. The preview considered $0.02–$0.04 a plausible base range, so the reported result also came in below that anticipated range.
fact_evidence: “Net income fell to $1 million ($0.01 per diluted share) from $0.05 per diluted share a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) Consensus: $0.04 (range $0.02–$0.06)” and “My base case is Q2 GAAP EPS of $0.02–0.04.”

description: Selling and marketing reached 34% of sales, versus the preview’s expected gross margin/opex setup that already allowed for rising expenses, and management said this elevated spending rate will continue. The preview did not anticipate this degree of ongoing S&M intensity.
fact_evidence: “Selling and marketing expense jumped to 34% of net sales from 26.4% a year ago,” and management indicated the elevated run rate “will continue” with investment in retail rollout, brand campaigns, and China expansion.
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “opex up again on pharma R&D” and flagged that “S&M, R&D (NB4168), and G&A” were guided higher, but did not forecast S&M at 34% of sales or that this rate would persist.

description: Ingredient revenue was only $5.4 million, and management expects it to decline year over year amid NMN and NAD competition and lower Life Extension purchases. That is worse than the preview’s hoped-for stabilization in the B2B and ingredient lines.
fact_evidence: “The ingredient business generated only $5.4 million ($4.9M food-grade, $0.4M pharma-grade) and is expected to decline year-over-year due to competitive pressure from NMN and NAD, partly reflecting lower purchases from Life Extension.”
expectation_evidence: “These are the lines that caused the Q1 shortfall — they need to stop getting worse.”

description: Gross margin held at 64.8%, above the preview’s expected 63.5–64.0% and contrary to its anticipated 100–150 basis-point year-over-year decline. The actual margin was nearly flat against the prior-year 65.0%.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin held roughly stable at 64.8% versus 65% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~63.5–64.0%” and “−100 to −150bp.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management disclosed that NB4168’s Ataxia-Telangiectasia indication alone could support a $200–400 million NPV, with a potentially transferable priority review voucher recently valued at $150–180 million. The preview discussed the pharmaceutical pivot as a potential option but did not anticipate these quantified value estimates.
fact_evidence: “Management estimates the lead pharmaceutical candidate NB4168's Ataxia-Telangiectasia indication alone could support a net present value of $200-400 million, plus a potential transferable priority review voucher recently valued at $150-180 million.”

description: The expected NB4168 development commitment was quantified at only about $30 million over four years through approval, with first-in-human studies expected next year and the company expected to remain cash-flow positive. This addresses the preview’s concern about an unquantified R&D step-up or possible need for outside funding more favorably than it anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Total drug development spending for NB4168 from now through approval is projected at only about $30 million spread over four years, with first-in-human studies expected next year, keeping the company cash-flow positive.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for a “quantified FY R&D dollar commitment” and whether spending was funded from net cash, warning that “a raise hint” would be a downside catalyst.

description: China cross-border revenue through May had already exceeded all of 2025, and the company had received Mainland China approval for topical/skincare products while dietary-ingredient approval remained pending. The preview did not flag this degree of China traction or the topical-product approval.
fact_evidence: “China cross-border revenue through May 2026 already exceeded the full-year 2025 total (which was under $1 million), and the company recently received topical/skincare product approval in Mainland China though dietary ingredient approval remains pending.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: NanoClouds sold out its limited 3,000–4,000-unit run, leading to a broader relaunch planned for October/November; management also disclosed discussions with two large global skincare companies about potentially exclusive Niagen deals. These commercialization developments were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The branded skincare product NanoClouds sold out its limited run of 3,000-4,000 units with strong new-to-brand and repeat purchases, prompting a broader relaunch in October/November, while two large global skincare companies are in discussions about potentially exclusive Niagen deals.”

description: Management described 2026 as an investment year and positioned it as a springboard for accelerated growth in 2027. That emphasizes a later growth payoff rather than the near-term H2 acceleration the preview said was needed to support the full-year growth outlook.
fact_evidence: Management framed “2026 as an investment year and a springboard for accelerated growth in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide required “a sharp H2 acceleration” and that H2 needed to grow “+11–14% after an H1 of ~+6%.”

description: A temporary Amazon marketplace listing issue in June reduced reported e-commerce growth from an estimated 19% absent the issue to 14%, although the issue has since been resolved. The preview had not anticipated this disruption; the reported growth still met its healthy-growth benchmark.
fact_evidence: “E-commerce revenue grew 14% to $20.5 million, but the company estimates growth would have been 19% absent a temporary Amazon marketplace listing issue in June that has since been resolved.”

description: LMAT missed the Q2 sales expectation: sales were about $1.1 million below guidance, whose midpoint was essentially the $71.47 million consensus. The shortfall was attributed in equal thirds to a stronger U.S. dollar, Middle East war-related export delays, and cardiac allograft supply constraints.
fact_evidence: “The company missed its Q2 sales guidance by $1.1 million,” attributed “in equal thirds to a stronger U.S. dollar, Middle East war-related export delays (~$400,000 of orders blocked), and cardiac allograft supply constraints.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 sales consensus was “$71.47M”; guidance was “$70.5 – $72.5M (mid $71.5M).”

description: Q2 earnings fell short of the preview’s $0.81 EPS expectation: fully diluted EPS was $0.74. Operating income was also below the preview’s $21.6 million expectation, at $20.4 million, with a 29% operating margin versus the expected 30%.
fact_evidence: “Operating income reached a record $20.4 million (up 26%) for a 29% operating margin,” and “fully diluted EPS grew 23% to $0.74.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 diluted EPS consensus was “$0.81”; expected operating income was “$21.6M” and operating margin “30%.”

description: The full-year outlook was cut rather than raised: revenue guidance is now $276.3 million and organic growth 11%, below the previous $277–283 million range and 12% organic-growth outlook. Full-year EPS guidance of $2.89 is also below the previous $2.93–$3.08 range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was updated to $276.3 million,” with “organic growth cut from 12% to 11% reflecting Q2 results, export weakness, and RFA supply constraints.” Full-year fully diluted EPS guidance is “$2.89.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance of “Sales $277–283M (mid $280M, +12% organic); EPS $2.93–$3.08 (mid $3.00).” It also said the buy side wanted the sales line lifted.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Cardiac allograft supply is limiting growth despite strong recent results, and the company is shifting tissue processing to address the constraint. This adds a specific supply bottleneck to the preview’s discussion of RestoreFlow momentum and expected Q2 activity.
fact_evidence: “Cardiac allograft (RFA) revenue grew 17% in Q2 and cardiac allografts specifically rose 39% quarter-on-quarter, but growth is slowing due to supply constraints being addressed by moving tissue processing to Burlington, Massachusetts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “RestoreFlow allografts (+25% in Q1; Germany implants were to begin in Q2, Irish approval H2).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The headline organic growth masked a sharp catheter decline: catheters fell 11% because of recall-driven overstocking in the prior year, while organic growth excluding catheters was 12%, with 5% unit growth. The preview’s unit-growth debate centered on whether volume could reach 4%, so the stronger ex-catheter volume was offset by an unflagged product-specific drag.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 organic sales grew 10% (7% price, 3% units), but excluding catheters organic growth was 12% (7% price, 5% units), as catheters fell 11% due to year-earlier recall-driven overstocking.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “units ≥4%” as the key watch item and described a base case of “~7% price / 3% unit.”

description: International Artegraft sales are ahead of the preview’s pace: Q2 international sales rose to $2.8 million, above the roughly $2.5 million needed to stay on the preview’s $10 million full-year target. The company now expects $11 million of international sales for 2026.
fact_evidence: “International Artegraft sales rising from $2.1 million in Q1 to $2.8 million in Q2 and full-year 2026 international sales expected at $11 million versus $4 million in 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the business “needs ~$2.5M+ in Q2 to stay on plan” for a “$10M FY2026 target.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The FDA indicated that a clinical trial is likely needed for the Artegraft Quick Stick indication, pushing any timeline out by years and leaving LMAT unsure whether it will pursue the indication. The preview did not flag this regulatory hurdle.
fact_evidence: “The FDA indicated a clinical trial is likely required for the Artegraft Quick Stick indication, pushing the timeline to years and leaving the company uncertain whether to proceed.”

description: The preview highlighted warehouse and tissue-transfer costs as a possible gross-margin drag, but management reported European gross-margin gains of 5–9 percentage points year over year from its relocalization strategy, alongside plans to open about seven new or larger warehouses across 2026–2027.
fact_evidence: The company is opening “about 7 new or larger warehouses across 2026/2027 as part of a ‘relocalization’ strategy driving European gross margin gains of 5-9 full points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 gross margin was guided “down 60 bps sequentially from 72.7% on the Irish warehouse standup and tissue-processing transfers,” and warned that sub-72% would validate concerns about margin expansion being capped.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected NRR around 108–110% in its base case and warned that a result below 105% would signal broader franchise weakness. OPRX reported NRR of 90%, alongside sequential declines in average revenue per top-20 pharma customer and revenue per FTE.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention rate fell to 90%, average revenue per top-20 pharma manufacturer was $2.7 million, and revenue per FTE was $750,000, all showing sequential declines.”
expectation_evidence: “Base ... NRR ~108–110%”; “Below ~105% signals a franchise problem, not a client problem.”

description: The preview expected the disrupted major client might contribute to Q3–Q4 buying acceleration if its situation improved. Instead, a large customer generated no revenue in Q2, and the revenue decline was concentrated in a small number of large customers.
fact_evidence: “The decline [in revenue was] concentrated in a small number of large customers including one that generated no revenue this quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Possible Q3–Q4 buying acceleration”; “If this client has deteriorated further, the guide breaks.”

description: Management held the annual revenue guide, as expected, but said Q4 alone is expected to provide 35–40% of full-year revenue. That makes the forecast notably dependent on a very large Q4 contribution, beyond the preview’s general expectation of a strong second half.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $95-100 million in revenue ... with Q4 expected to represent 35-40% of full-year revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “The guide requires $55–60M in H2”; management had framed the requirement as “nearly 60% in H2.”

description: The preview treated roughly 67% gross margin as the reference point, while management raised its full-year margin outlook to the high-60% to low-70% range. Favorable mix and the wind-down of low-margin managed services are expected to support the improvement.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin guidance was raised, with full-year 2026 gross margins now expected in the high-60% to low-70% range.”
expectation_evidence: “At 5.9x EBITDA on a 67% gross margin...”

description: Q2 revenue was slightly above the preview’s $20.20 million consensus estimate, despite a year-over-year decline of 30%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue was $20.5 million ... but exceeded consensus expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus Revenue: $20.20M.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS came in above the preview’s $0.11 consensus estimate. GAAP EPS, by contrast, was close to the preview’s approximate $(0.05) estimate.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income ... $0.16 per diluted share”; “net loss ... $0.04 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $0.11”; “GAAP EPS ~$(0.05).”

description: Adjusted EBITDA appears to have exceeded the preview’s estimated range based on the $4.9 million figure, although the CFO also cited $4.1 million, which falls within that range. The reported decline from the prior year included $1.7 million of severance expense.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million (or $4.1 million per CFO remarks) ... impacted by $1.7 million in severance expense.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.): ~$3.5–4.5M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected DSP contribution later in 2026. The DeepIntent DSP integration went live during the week of the call, an earlier operational milestone, and management described access to programmatic channels as a potential way to double the business over two years.
fact_evidence: “The DeepIntent DSP integration went live during the week of the call”; management said programmatic channels account for 60% of buys in its space and DSP access could be “a potential driver to double the business over two years.”
expectation_evidence: “Contribution expected late 2026.”

description: The AI-enabled DAAP and software offerings posted specific growth rates that the preview had not quantified: more than 30% for DAAP and 25% for AI-enabled software. This provides evidence of growth in the recurring-subscription shift beyond the preview’s general description of these products as future drivers.
fact_evidence: “The AI-enabled Dynamic Audience Activation Platform (DAAP) grew over 30% year-over-year and AI-enabled software offerings grew 25%.”

description: OPRX paid down debt faster than the preview’s discussion of refinancing and interest savings suggested: it made an extra roughly $5 million principal payment in Q2 and paid another $3 million after quarter-end. Management also described debt paydown as a capital-allocation priority.

expectation_evidence: The preview says a Q3 guide of “$(70)–(80)M confirms” sequential improvement, while “anything at or beyond $(85)M” would imply stickier burn.
