description: Adjusted operating income and EPS both beat the company’s Q1 outlook: operating income was $52 million versus a $30–$40 million range, and EPS was $0.05 versus $0.00–$0.02 guidance. EPS also exceeded the preview’s $0.02 consensus.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income of $52 million significantly exceeded the company's outlook range of $30 million to $40 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.05 also beat guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income… $30–40M”; “Adj. diluted EPS… $0.00–$0.02”; consensus EPS “$0.02.”

description: Management reversed the expected increase in marketing investment: it now expects marketing to fall as a share of revenue and in absolute dollars, rather than adding the incremental marketing spend embedded in the preview’s discussion of the full-year plan.
fact_evidence: “Management now expects marketing spend to decline as a percentage of revenue (toward the low end of the 10%-11% range) and in absolute dollars, reversing prior guidance for higher marketing investment.”
expectation_evidence: The FY27 guide “embeds… ~$30M of incremental marketing”; the base case expected marketing spend “weighted to the back half.”

description: The Q2 EPS outlook was below UBS’s previewed $0.03–$0.05 expectation: Under Armour guided to an adjusted loss of $0.01–$0.03 per share. The preview had warned that a Q2 guide below $0.03 would imply a more back-loaded year.
fact_evidence: “For Q2, the company guided to… an adjusted diluted loss per share of $0.01 to $0.03.”
expectation_evidence: “UBS preview… Q2 guide of $0.03–$0.05”; “A Q2 guide below $0.03 implies an even more back-loaded year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Traffic weakened sharply from mid-to-late May, particularly in North America and APAC, and China faced additional stock-outs and aggressive discounting by licensees. This added a specific deterioration in recent demand and China conditions to the preview’s concerns about stabilization and the order book.
fact_evidence: “Traffic deteriorated sharply from mid-to-late May forward, particularly in North America and Asia Pacific, with China further hurt by stock-outs and aggressive discounting by licensees.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the fall/holiday order book “the forward signal” and flagged North America as “the swing factor.”

description: DTC weakness extended beyond the preview’s reference to prior-year e-commerce declines: e-commerce fell 12%, owned stores fell 3%, and DTC overall fell 6%.
fact_evidence: “DTC revenue fell 6% (e-commerce down 12%, owned stores down 3%).”
expectation_evidence: “eCommerce -7% in FY26; owned stores +1%. Deliberate discount restraint has cost e-comm volume — has that annualized?”

description: Footwear declined 8%, less than the double-digit decline contemplated in the preview’s bear case and an improvement on the prior-year declines highlighted there.
fact_evidence: “Footwear revenue declined 8%.”
expectation_evidence: The bear case described “footwear still down double digits”; the preview cited declines of “-11% in FY26” and “-14% in Q1 FY26.”

description: Under Armour announced another planned 25% SKU reduction over the next 18 months, beyond the 25% reduction the preview said was already complete, targeting roughly 40% cumulative reduction by FY28.
fact_evidence: “Targeting an additional 25% SKU reduction over the next 18 months, building on a prior 25% cut, for a cumulative reduction of roughly 40% by the end of fiscal 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “~25% SKU reduction is complete.”

description: APAC revenue fell 7% (10% in constant currency), diverging from the preview’s expectation of low-single-digit growth for EMEA/APAC in the full year; EMEA and Latin America instead grew 12% and 8%, respectively.
fact_evidence: “APAC down 7% (10% constant currency), while EMEA rose 12% and Latin America rose 8%.”
expectation_evidence: “International… EMEA/APAC LSD growth (FY).”

description: Vanda's Q2 net loss was $62.5 million, far worse than the preview's estimate of about $36 million implied by consensus EPS and its own estimated EPS loss of roughly $0.76. The call attributed the higher loss to R&D and SG&A spending on clinical programs and commercial launches.
fact_evidence: “Vanda posted a Q2 2026 net loss of $62.5 million,” driven by “higher R&D and SG&A tied to clinical programs and commercial launches.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS of −$0.60 implies a net loss near $36M”; the preview's estimate was “≈ −$0.76.”

description: Hetlios sales were only $5.6 million versus the preview's $14.5 million estimate. Generic competition and a shipment timing issue explain much of the gap, although the preview had already expected generic erosion.
fact_evidence: “Hetlios net product sales fell 66% year-over-year to $5.6 million” due to generic competition and a shipment timing issue that “pushed roughly $7 million of revenue into Q3 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Hetlios at “$14.5M” and noted generic erosion, with management warning the decline was “potentially significant.”

description: Nereus recognized just $1 million in sales, below the preview's $2.5 million estimate. The call also revealed that most initial wholesaler stocking was constrained over demand and return uncertainties, a further indication that the launch's early sales were limited.
fact_evidence: “Nereus generated only $1 million in recognized net product sales”; “$12.6 million of the $15.2 million initial wholesaler stocking was constrained due to demand and return uncertainties.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “NEREUS … $2.5M” for Q2 and said “~$0–1M turns the guide into a liability.”

description: The $150–170 million 2026 product-sales target was described as combined FNAPT and Basanti, whereas the preview presented that range as the Fanapt guide and noted that Basanti had no separate forecast. Including Basanti in the same range makes the target less supportive of Fanapt sales alone, though the combined range still implies growth.
fact_evidence: “Combined FNAPT and Basanti 2026 net product sales are guided at $150–170 million,” implying roughly 36% growth versus 2025 FNAPT revenue, with Basanti launch expected in the second half.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “FY2026 guide” for “Fanapt” as “$150–170M” and said management “did not separately forecast BYSANTI revenue.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview modeled cash and securities of about $155 million at quarter-end; Vanda reported $170 million. Management also said existing funding should last through at least the end of 2027, addressing the preview's central concern about funding the launch cycle and 2027 runway.
fact_evidence: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were “$170 million as of June 30, 2026,” and management guided to funding “through at least end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + securities (EOQ) … ≈ $155M” and described funding the launch cycle before Fanapt's November 2027 loss of exclusivity as the central question.

description: Management gave a specific outlook for operating expenses to start declining by year-end 2026 and fall more substantially in 2027 as Phase 3 programs and commercial supply build-out conclude. The preview raised opex as a key issue but did not anticipate this expense-reduction timing.
fact_evidence: “Operating expenses [are expected] to begin decreasing by end of 2026 and more substantially in 2027” as Phase 3 programs and commercial supply build-out conclude.
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “Opex trajectory” and asked whether there would be “any sign of a ceiling,” but gave no expense-reduction timing.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The Hetlios jet-lag disorder application is moving to a formal FDA administrative hearing culminating in December 2026, with a favorable judge recommendation only hoped for in early 2027. This regulatory process and uncertainty were not raised in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The Hetlios jet-lag disorder application is proceeding to a formal FDA administrative hearing culminating in December 2026,” with a favorable judge recommendation hoped for in early 2027.

description: FNAPT sales came in modestly above the preview's estimate, at $36 million versus $35 million, with prescriptions also up strongly year over year.
fact_evidence: “FNAPT net product sales grew 23% year-over-year to $36 million,” with total prescriptions up 31% and new-to-brand prescriptions up 32%.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Fanapt at “$35.0M.”

description: Q4 revenue guidance of $415–425 million was well above the preview’s $375–390 million level it said might be needed to satisfy marginal buyers, and far above the $360–365 million implied by FY26 consensus. Management also forecast 35% sequential Data Center growth and 20% I&D growth, pointing to broader strength than a Data Center-only ramp.
fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 guidance calls for revenue of $415-425 million” and implies “about 35% sequential Data Center growth and 20% I&D growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Assume $375–390M is what's needed to satisfy the marginal buyer”; FY26 consensus “implies Q4 of roughly $360–365M.”

description: The quarter beat the preview’s consensus and the company’s prior guidance: revenue was $342.2 million versus $335.1 million consensus and a $331–339 million guide, while adjusted EPS was $1.40 versus $1.34 consensus and a $1.31–1.37 guide.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue was $342.2 million” and “adjusted EPS of $1.40.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$335.1M”; company guide was “$331–339M.” Consensus EPS was “$1.34”; company guide was “$1.31–$1.37.”

description: Data Center revenue came in above the preview’s build, and the FY26 growth trajectory moved above the preview’s roughly 70% bull-case trigger. The preview estimated about $132.6 million for the quarter and described a raise toward ~70% as a potential catalyst; reported revenue was $137.6 million and the company is trending toward roughly 74% full-year growth.
fact_evidence: “Data Center revenue reached a record $137.6 million” and is “trending toward roughly 74% full-year growth in FY26.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 Data Center revenue at “~$132.6M” and said to watch for “a third raise toward ~70%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings strengthened further rather than merely sustaining the preview’s already-record Q2 level: book-to-bill reached 1.6:1 versus 1.5:1 at Q2, with the highest quarterly bookings in company history.
fact_evidence: “Q3 book-to-bill ratio hit a record 1.6:1 with the highest quarterly bookings in company history.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 book-to-bill of “1.5:1” and said “≥1.3x sustains the upgrade cycle.”

description: Management gave a stronger FY27 Data Center growth frame than the preview’s >40% watch threshold: Data Center is trending toward 50% year-over-year growth.
fact_evidence: Annualizing Q4 guidance implies “Data Center trending toward 50% year-over-year growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said that “any qualitative FY27 Data Center framing (>40% growth?) sets the 2027 bar.”

description: Management set out a steep operating-margin trajectory—approximately 37% in Q4 and a target of breaching 40% in FY27—which the preview had not forecast, despite discussing operating leverage.
fact_evidence: Adjusted operating margin was “31.5%,” with Q4 “guided to approximately 37%” and a “target of breaching 40% in FY27.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The company raised its 2027 serviceable addressable market estimate to approximately $15 billion, with Data Center and I&D each representing about $6 billion. The preview did not flag a higher market-size estimate.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2027 SAM estimate to approximately $15 billion” and said it was “up 20-30% from 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management described a broader base of large customers than the preview had discussed: customers contributing more than $10 million grew from about 8 two years ago to over 20, while the top 10 end-customers remain under 40% of revenue.
fact_evidence: “Customers above $10 million in revenue grew from about 8 two years ago to over 20 today”; “top 10 end-customers remain under 40% of total revenue.”

description: The call disclosed a $61 million investment in IQE and a $41 million noncash GAAP gain associated with it, which was excluded from non-GAAP results. This investment and one-off accounting gain were not discussed in the preview.
fact_evidence: The company “made a $61 million investment in IQE that generated a $41 million noncash GAAP gain excluded from non-GAAP results.”

description: Adjusted EPS was about $1.44, inferred from the reported $0.21 increase to $1.23 a year earlier, well above the preview’s $1.26 consensus. The company said trailing-four-quarter repurchases of about $650 million helped drive the 17% year-over-year growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 17% ($0.21) year-over-year,” aided by “approximately $650 million in share repurchases” over the trailing four quarters.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS **$1.26**” for Q2 consensus.

description: Adjusted operating margin reached 11.3%, above the preview’s roughly 10.9% guide-implied expectation. Every business unit also expanded margins, rather than the preview’s key concern being whether pressure in weaker businesses would ease.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 100 basis points to 11.3%” and “every business unit expanded margins.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. op. margin ~10.9% (guide-implied)”; the preview also flagged “BES trajectory + PDS loss” as a key issue.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was $492 million, substantially above the preview’s $250 million checkpoint for validating the full-year cash-flow bridge after only $13 million in Q1.
fact_evidence: “Generated $492 million of free cash flow during the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “FCF >$250M in the quarter confirming the FY bridge”; the preview noted Q1 FCF was “only $13M.”

description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EPS range to $5.05–$5.30 from $5.00–$5.20, lifting the top end above the preview’s $5.18 Street estimate. The increase was primarily due to first-half buybacks, rather than an improvement to the sales, margin, or FCF outlook.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.05-$5.30 (from $5.00-$5.20) primarily due to first-half buybacks,” while sales, margin, and FCF guidance were maintained.
expectation_evidence: “Street FY26 sits at $14.18B / $5.18 EPS”; the preview called for a possible guide “to ~$5.05–5.20” in its base case.

description: The Board added $1 billion to the buyback authorization, bringing the total to $1.35 billion through 2029. The preview discussed buybacks as dependent on cash generation but did not anticipate this larger authorization.
fact_evidence: “The Board approved a $1 billion increase to the buyback authorization,” bringing total authorization to “$1.35 billion” through 2029.
expectation_evidence: The preview said FCF “gates the buyback” and noted recent repurchases, but did not forecast an authorization increase.

description: The effective full-year margin midpoint was described as 10.6% after incremental second-half industrial R&D spending, below the preview’s 10.8% midpoint expectation. The spending supports data-center product readiness, but is a near-term margin cost.
fact_evidence: “Increasing second-half industrial R&D spending by an incremental $10-15 million,” lowering the midpoint to “10.6% (from 10.8% excluding it),” to accelerate data-center product readiness.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. op. margin 10.7–10.9%”; the preview also framed the expected margin around “~10.9%.”

description: The battery business is now expected to weigh about 170 basis points on full-year sales growth, around 20 basis points more than the preview’s estimate. The underlying pressures—lack of North American incentives and weaker European demand—were already anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The battery business is expected to be a roughly 170 basis point headwind to full-year sales growth” due to “lack of North American incentives and weaker European demand.”
expectation_evidence: “BES is a ~$210M / ~150bp headwind to FY growth on weak NA EV incentives and European demand.”

description: Management’s China production outlook of down 4–7% extends below the preview’s expected down 4% to down 1.5% range. With China representing about 20% of global sales, this is a weaker regional outlook than the preview’s market assumption.
fact_evidence: “China represents about 20% of global sales,” and management guides “regional production to China down 4-7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s market assumption was “China −4% to −1.5%.”

description: Sales were roughly flat year over year, better than the preview’s 1.5% decline expectation, and slightly above the $3.58 billion consensus. The difference was modest, with the reported amount only just over $3.6 billion.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales exceeded $3.6 billion, roughly flat year-over-year,” with organic sales up 0.5%.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue **$3.58B**” consensus and “−1.5%” year over year.

description: Thryv cut FY2026 SaaS adjusted EBITDA guidance to $42–44 million from $70–75 million, far below the preview’s expected range. Management attributed the reduction to first-half underinvestment in sales headcount and marketing.
fact_evidence: “Thryv lowered its full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $453-457 million and SaaS adjusted EBITDA guidance to $42-44 million, reflecting first-half underinvestment in sales headcount and marketing.”
expectation_evidence: “SaaS adj. EBITDA $70–75M”

description: FY2026 SaaS revenue guidance was lowered to $453–457 million, below the preview’s expected $463–471 million range. This is a clear downward revision, though smaller than the cut to SaaS adjusted EBITDA guidance.
fact_evidence: “Thryv lowered its full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $453-457 million”
expectation_evidence: “SaaS revenue $463–471M”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Seasoned net revenue retention was 90%, below the preview’s 92–93% base-case expectation, while SaaS subscribers ended at 95,000 versus the 96,000 figure highlighted in the preview. This points to somewhat greater customer attrition than expected, though the NRR result was at—not below—the preview’s cited 90% concern threshold.
fact_evidence: “Seasoned net revenue retention was 90%, reflecting attrition of smaller, lower-spend clients”; “ending the quarter with 95,000 SaaS subscribers.”
expectation_evidence: “NRR ~92–93%” and “SaaS client count (96,000)”; the preview also said “NRR below ~90%” would signal uncontrolled churn.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Reported leverage was 2.5x, materially above the preview’s cited 1.6–1.7x, even though ending net debt of $241 million was below the preview’s $258.6 million snapshot. The leverage figure therefore came in worse than the preview’s stated expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with net debt of $241 million and a 2.5x leverage ratio.”
expectation_evidence: “Net debt $258.6M ... leverage ~1.6–1.7x.”

description: Thryv announced an approximately $25 million restructuring charge, split between workforce reductions and vendor spend, with roughly $60 million in expected run-rate savings. The preview discussed the need for cost actions in a possible bull case but did not anticipate this specific charge-and-savings plan.
fact_evidence: “The company announced a restructuring charge of approximately $25 million (split evenly between workforce reductions and vendor spend) expected to yield roughly $60 million in run-rate savings.”

description: Thryv raised the low end of its FY2026 Marketing Services revenue guidance to $161 million from the preview’s $157 million low end, a modestly better outlook for the legacy business.
fact_evidence: “raising the low end of marketing services revenue guidance to $161-163 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Marketing Services revenue $157–163M”

description: Thryv’s reported adjusted EBITDA for Q2 SaaS was $13.6 million, above the preview’s expected $12–13 million range, including a result above its high end.
fact_evidence: “Q2 SaaS revenue was $114.5 million with adjusted gross margin of 66.6% and adjusted EBITDA of $13.6 million (12% margin).”
expectation_evidence: “SaaS adj. EBITDA ... $12–13M (~10.4–11.3% mgn)”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Thryv was reclassified by the JICs as a software company, a new external validation of its transformation that the preview did not specifically anticipate.
fact_evidence: “SaaS now represents 76% of Thryv's total revenue, and the company was reclassified by the JICs as a software company, validating its transformation to a pure-play SaaS business.”

description: Thryv announced strategic partnerships with Wix and Ooma and integrations with Breezy and Jobber to broaden distribution. These specific ecosystem relationships were not part of the preview’s stated expectations.
fact_evidence: “The company entered strategic partnerships with Wix and Ooma and launched integrations with Breezy and Jobber to expand distribution into new customer ecosystems.”

description: Revenue grew 48% year over year, well above the preview’s roughly 31–32% consensus growth estimate. That is a much larger top-line beat than the preview’s base case implied.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 48% versus Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue consensus is tight and reliable (~$20.3–20.7B)” and the consensus table showed implied YoY growth of “+31%” to “+32%.”

description: Even including $3.30 per share of acquired IPR&D charges, non-GAAP EPS was $8.38. Adding back that stated charge implies $11.68 before the charge, above the preview’s $8.84 ex-large-IPR&D consensus and its $9.10–9.40 base case.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $8.38 (including $3.30 of acquired IPR&D charges).”
expectation_evidence: “EPS — ex-large IPR&D” consensus was “$8.84”; the preview’s “Working base case” was “non-GAAP EPS $9.10–9.40 ex-IPR&D.”

description: Gross margin reached 86.3%, 2.9 percentage points above the preview’s 83.4% consensus. The margin result was substantially stronger than expected despite the preview’s concern about capacity scaling and lower-priced mix.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose 1.3 points to 86.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin” consensus was “83.4%.”

description: Mounjaro and Zepbound together generated $14.9 billion, above the preview’s base-case combined estimate of about $13.6 billion and even above its bull-case threshold of more than $14.1 billion. Their $6.3 billion contribution to year-over-year growth also shows these products drove a particularly strong quarter.
fact_evidence: “Mounjaro and Zepbound combined for $14.9 billion in revenue and contributed $6.3 billion of year-over-year growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Q2 ~$9.2B / ~$4.4B” for Mounjaro and Zepbound; its bull case called for “Mounjaro >$9.5B, Zepbound >$4.6B.”

description: Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance to $85–87 billion, putting the new floor at the top of the preview’s expected $83–85 billion base-case band and the top end above it. The preview expected a raise, but this was stronger than its base case.
fact_evidence: “Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance to $85–$87 billion (up $3 billion at the low end and $2 billion at the high end).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the guide to be raised to the “$83–85B” band; its bull case was “$84–86B.”

description: The underlying full-year EPS outlook increased by $2.78 at the midpoint before the IPR&D charge, as the preview expected an upward revision. But after the $3.03 per-share charge impact, the stated $35.50–36.50 range has a lower high end than the existing $35.50–37.00 range, so the reported range did not deliver the anticipated upward reset.
fact_evidence: “[Lilly] lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to $35.50–$36.50, a $2.78 midpoint increase before the $3.03 IPR&D charge impact.”
expectation_evidence: The existing guidance was “$35.50B – $37.00” and the preview’s base case expected the “EPS band narrowed upward.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: U.S. net price declined only 3% on the reported measure, better than the preview’s low-to-mid-teens full-year erosion concern. The decline was 9% excluding favorable rebate and discount estimate adjustments, which narrows the apparent outperformance.
fact_evidence: “U.S. net price declined 3% (or 9% excluding favorable rebate/discount estimate adjustments).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to “low-to-mid-teens price erosion for FY26” and noted Q1 U.S. price decline of “~7–10%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Foundayo’s reported launch indicators were stronger than the preview’s concern about scripts declining for three straight weeks: prescribers rose from about 8,000 to 36,000, it reached roughly one in four U.S. new starts, and management said volume doubled in late July versus a month earlier. The call facts do not provide quarterly revenue, so the preview’s revenue estimate cannot be assessed here.
fact_evidence: “Orforglipron (Foundayo) prescribers grew from about 8,000 to 36,000, U.S. new starts reached roughly 1 in 4, and management cited volume doubling in the last week of July versus a month earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Foundayo scripts were “down for three straight weeks” after peaking in week 10 and asked whether management would “reaffirm the launch trajectory, or reset it.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Medicare bridge launch matched the preview’s expected July 1 timing and $50 monthly price, but the call added evidence of a sizable coverage expansion and early uptake: 20 million eligible seniors, a 35% increase in U.S. obesity-medicine coverage, and most early users being new patients.
fact_evidence: “The Medicare GLP-1 bridge program launched July 1 [and] gives 20 million eligible seniors obesity coverage at $50 per month, expanding U.S. obesity-medicine coverage by 35%, with early uptake skewing ~80% injectable and 60%-70% new patients.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “July 1 Medicare GLP-1 Bridge at $50/mo” and said guidance commentary on its impact would matter, but did not give these coverage or uptake figures.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call reported positive results in three Phase III retatrutide trials, including high-dose weight loss approaching bariatric-surgery levels and a large reduction in osteoarthritis knee pain. The preview mentioned possible early-2027 filing color, but did not anticipate these trial results.
fact_evidence: “Retatrutide posted positive results in three Phase III Triumph trials (with high-dose weight loss approaching bariatric-surgery levels and ~75% osteoarthritis knee-pain reduction).”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Lilly reported that selpercatinib cut recurrence or death risk by 83% in adjuvant RET-positive lung cancer. The preview did not identify this readout as an expectation or debate.
fact_evidence: “Selpercatinib reduced risk of recurrence or death by 83% versus placebo in adjuvant RET-positive lung cancer.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Lilly also reported a substantial pirtobrutinib benefit in previously treated CLL, including among patients previously treated with a BTK inhibitor. This result was not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Pirtobrutinib cut progression or death by 45% (68% after prior BTK inhibitor) in previously treated CLL.”

description: Q2 revenue was $1.12B, above the $1.08B consensus and the company’s $1.07–1.08B guide. It reached the preview’s upper whisper range, so the beat was against consensus rather than beyond the most optimistic preview case.
fact_evidence: Q2 revenue reached $1.12 billion, up 36% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, with a record quarter-over-quarter revenue addition of $115 million.
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was $1.08B; the preview’s functional buy-side whisper was closer to $1.10–1.12B, with a $95–110M sequential add.

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.135–1.145B fell short of the preview’s $1.16B-or-higher bull-case threshold and implies a sharp slowdown from Q2’s 36% growth to 28–29%.
fact_evidence: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.135–$1.145 billion implies decelerating growth of 28–29% year-over-year, notably below the 36% posted in Q2.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q3 guide ≥$1.16B” in its key metric ranking and listed “Q3 guide ≥$1.16B” among the bull-case conditions.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management disclosed that its largest customer will reduce usage beginning in Q3, a concrete instance of the optimization risk the preview warned about. The customer’s nine-figure renewal and management’s statement that the reduction was fully derisked in Q3 and full-year guidance partly offset the concern.
fact_evidence: Management disclosed a usage reduction from its largest customer beginning in Q3, which they fully derisked in both Q3 and full-year 2026 guidance despite the customer signing a 9-figure renewal.
expectation_evidence: The preview said any “renegotiation, in-housing, or optimization language” would be a multi-turn de-rate and identified largest-customer concentration commentary as a key debate.

description: Full-year revenue guidance rose to $4.45–4.47B, above the preview’s roughly $4.42B buy-side bar. The preview’s bull case anticipated $4.45B or more, so the increase cleared the central bar but landed at the bull-case level; full-year EPS guidance also rose above the previously stated range.
fact_evidence: The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $4.45–$4.47 billion (30% growth) with non-GAAP EPS of $2.50–$2.54.
expectation_evidence: The preview set a functional buy-side bar of “≥$4.42B” and a bull case of “FY26 guide to $4.45B+”; it listed the then-current full-year revenue guide as $4.30–4.34B and EPS as $2.36–2.44.

description: Q2 operating margin reached 23%, above the preview’s expected 21–22% range. This was a modestly better profitability result than the preview’s operating-income estimate implied.
fact_evidence: Q2 operating margin improved to 23% from 20% a year ago.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated non-GAAP operating income of about $230M, or a 21–22% margin, and listed Q2 company guidance of 21–22%.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free-cash-flow margin was 25%, below the preview’s expectation of at least 27%, although free cash flow was still $279M.
fact_evidence: Free cash flow was $279 million at a 25% margin.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s “good looks like” threshold for FCF margin was “≥27%.”

description: Gross margin slipped to 79.6%, below the preview’s preferred 80%-or-higher level and slightly below its base-case range, though it remained above the preview’s sub-79.5% bear threshold.

fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 2026 with $110.2 million in cash and marketable securities, which is expected to fund operations only into early 2027.

fact_evidence: Management is positioning sabirnetug's IgG2 antibody format and oligomer selectivity as differentiating safety advantages over IgG1 competitors Kisunla and Leqembi by potentially reducing ARIA risk.

description: Sempra’s Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.16, well above the preview’s $1.00–$1.05 estimates and its roughly $1.01 consensus. The result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case range of $1.08–$1.15.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16 ($762 million)”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.01” (Zacks); “$1.00” (alt. compiler); KeyCorp “$1.05”; bull case “$1.08–$1.15.”

expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Sempra Texas at “~$295M” versus “$208M” in Q2'25, and said the catch-up timing could swing quarterly EPS by “±$0.05–$0.10.”

expectation_evidence: The preview called for watching “for a formal capital plan raise or a pre-announcement of one” and described a hard number on Texas capex above the existing plan as a potential catalyst.

description: Oncor’s system already has about 8 GW of the 44 GW batch-zero load connected and ramping toward full use. The preview discussed a large Texas load queue, but did not identify this much demand as already connected and actively ramping.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 8 gigawatts of the 44 GW batch zero load is already connected to Oncor's system and ramping toward full utilization.”

description: BRINSUPRI revenue reached $309.2 million, above the preview’s $285 million script-derived estimate and the $290–300 million buy-side chatter. Sequential growth was 49%, stronger than the preview’s modeled 38%.
fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI generated $309.2 million in revenue in its third full quarter of launch, up 49% sequentially.”

description: Management raised 2026 BRINSUPRI guidance to $1.25–1.4 billion, well above the preview’s stated de facto bar of at least $1.10 billion. This was a substantially larger raise than the preview’s base case of a soft “$1.0B+” indication.

description: Q2 added about 7,000 BRINSUPRI patients, above the preview’s 6,300 organic-start comparison, and management said all additions came from organic demand after the ready-and-waiting cohort was exhausted. fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI added approximately 7,000 new patients in Q2, beating the prior expectation of 6,300, with all coming from organic demand as ready-and-waiting patients are exhausted.”

expectation_evidence: The preview cited “BMO initiated Outperform, $192 PT on July 21, 2026, modeling $9.2B peak BRINSUPRI sales.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Gas utilities grew 15% sequentially to an 11-quarter high. The preview identified gas utility as a source of resilience but did not forecast growth of this size or a new multi-quarter high.
fact_evidence: “Gas utilities grew 15% sequentially to an 11-quarter high.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described gas utility as “the counter-cyclical ballast against upstream softness” and flagged gas utility demand as a metric to watch.

description: EHC raised its full-year 2026 revenue, EBITDA, and EPS ranges instead of merely narrowing guidance to the upper half as the preview treated as the base case. The new EPS midpoint is $6.135, up from $6.00, though it remains below the preview’s $6.15 bull-trigger threshold.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance” to net revenue of $6.41B-$6.49B, adjusted EBITDA of $1.365B-$1.395B, and adjusted EPS of $6.02-$6.25.
expectation_evidence: “A narrow-to-upper-half is the base case and is roughly neutral.” The preview also said “an EPS guidance raise” was needed for the bull case.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The 89% success rate in adjudicated MA admit-and-appeal cases was a strong initial result, and management plans to scale certain high-success diagnoses. The preview anticipated pilot data might arrive and discussed scaling as a potential outcome, but gave no expected success rate.
fact_evidence: The pilot “has admitted 298 patients through July, with 128 of 144 adjudicated cases won (89% success rate),” and management “plans to scale certain high-success diagnoses in coming quarters.”
expectation_evidence: “Any quantified approval-rate improvement plus a commitment to scale beyond nine hospitals is a 2027 estimate-raiser.”

description: Q2 revenue growth and discharge growth ran ahead of the preview’s estimates: revenue grew 9.6% versus the implied 7.7%, while discharges grew 5.6% versus the derived 4.3% estimate. The reported facts do not specify same-store discharge growth, so they do not resolve that specific debate in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 9.6% year-over-year, driven by 5.6% discharge growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue growth of “+7.7%” and total discharges of “+4.3%.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company cut its expected 2026 provider-tax benefit to adjusted EBITDA by about half, from roughly $21 million to $10 million. Retroactive Florida Medicaid adjustments also reduced Q2 year-over-year results, an adverse item not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Net provider tax benefit to 2026 adjusted EBITDA” is now expected to be “about $10 million, down from the prior ~$21 million estimate,” including “an $11.5 million year-over-year decrease in Q2.”

description: EHC raised its full-year SWB-per-FTE growth guidance to 3.5%-4%, indicating more wage growth than the preview’s labor-leverage case suggested. The increased career-ladder participation supports retention, but it also raises the cost outlook.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 SWB per FTE growth guidance was raised to 3.5%-4% due to increased participation in career ladder programs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said salaries and wages per FTE had run “+3.7% in Q1” and identified “clinical-ladder wage inflation” as an offset to the labor story.

description: The Board increased the quarterly dividend and expanded the buyback authorization, adding to shareholder returns beyond the preview’s stated $0.19 dividend and Q1 repurchase pace.
fact_evidence: The Board “increased the quarterly dividend to $0.21 per share and raised the stock repurchase authorization to $1 billion,” with “$145.8 million of shares repurchased year-to-date.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “$0.19 quarterly dividend” and “$71.6M repurchased in Q1,” and said buyback pace mattered for EPS.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: EHC reported higher Q2 occupancy and record census milestones, rather than the capacity constraint remaining at the prior-year occupancy level described in the preview. Average daily census exceeded 9,000 for the first time in two quarters.
fact_evidence: “Q2 occupancy reached 77.4%, up 290 basis points year-over-year,” and the company had its “first two quarters ever with average daily census above 9,000.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 occupancy as “78.7% flat Y/Y” and framed capacity-constrained volume as the key debate.

description: Beyond the 2026 opening cadence discussed in the preview, management disclosed a substantial post-2026 pipeline and a set of newly accessible North Carolina markets. The preview did not anticipate these specific expansion opportunities.
fact_evidence: EHC has “a post-2026 pipeline of 13 hospitals with 606 beds,” plus “15 prioritized North Carolina markets following CON repeal effective October 1.”

description: Q3 revenue was $718 million, below the preview’s $726.1 million consensus and its +2.5% implied growth rate; reported growth was 1.3%.
fact_evidence: “Q3 total revenue rose 1.3% to $718 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $726.1M”; implied year-over-year growth “+2.5%.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Adjusted EBITDA was well below the preview’s estimated $115–120 million at $96 million, but the gap reflected a nonroutine $16 million self-insurance adjustment and a $4 million fuel headwind. Excluding those items, EBITDA was $116 million at a 16.2% margin, within the expected range; management said the claims charge should not recur.
fact_evidence: “Reported adjusted EBITDA was $96 million (13.3% margin), but excluding a $16 million self-insurance adjustment and $4 million fuel headwind, EBITDA would have been $116 million at a 16.2% margin”; the charge was “largely tied to adverse development of 2023-and-prior claims,” with “over 85%” closed and “it should not recur.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived, no clean published consensus) | ~$115–120M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~15.8–16.5%.”

description: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was cut sharply to $70–80 million from $100–115 million, with fuel and self-insurance impacts cited as the reasons. The preview treated the existing range as the base case and flagged a trim as a downside scenario.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow guidance was cut to $70-$80 million from the prior $100-$115 million due to fuel and self-insurance impacts.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … adjusted FCF … $100–115M”; the base case expected the “FY FCF guide” to be reaffirmed, while the bear case said it could be “trimmed.”

description: Management guided to 3%–6% Land growth in Q4, a forward growth range not specified in the preview, while identifying ancillary revenue as the key swing variable. Full-year Land growth guidance remained 2%–3%.
fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year Land revenue guidance of 2%-3% growth and guides Q4 Land growth of 3%-6%, with ancillary being the key swing variable.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company reported stronger selling momentum than the preview discussed: it had added 200 net sellers since the end of 2024 and new contract sales were up about 20% year-to-date. The expansion carried costs of $4 million in Q3 and $16 million year-to-date.
fact_evidence: “The company added a net 200 sellers since end of 2024 (toward a 500 target), lifting new contract sales ~20% year-to-date,” with sales investments costing “$4 million (60 bps) in Q3 and $16 million (80 bps) year-to-date.”

description: Q2 revenue less ancillary services reached $164 million, above both the $154.3 million consensus and the guidance range’s $159.4 million high end. Travel and hospitality strength helped drive the beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue less ancillary services reached $164 million, up over 28% on a spot basis and 27% FX-neutral, beating the midpoint of guidance largely on Travel/hospitality strength.”
expectation_evidence: “RLA (Revenue Less Ancillary Services) $154.3M” consensus; Q2 guidance was “$151.7M–$159.4M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million at a 14.6% margin, above the preview’s roughly $21 million estimate and well above the 13.75% guide-midpoint margin. The preview identified 14.5% or more as a clear beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million with a 14.6% margin, expanding ~160 bps year-over-year and coming in above the upper end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est., not consensus) ~$21M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~13.75%”; “≥14.5% is a clear beat.”

description: Management raised FY2026 FX-neutral revenue growth guidance to 21%–27% from 18%–24%. Both ends of the range moved up by three percentage points, rather than the reaffirmation the preview treated as its base case.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 21%-27% FX-neutral revenue growth.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (raised at Q1): 18–24% FX-neutral RLA growth”; the base case expected “FY26 18–24% reaffirmed.”

description: The company’s FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin-expansion outlook also improved, to 200–400 bps and about 23% at the midpoint, from the preview’s 175–375 bps and roughly 22.8% midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … ~200-400 bps of EBITDA margin expansion (reaching ~23% at midpoint).”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin +175–375 bps to ~22.8% at midpoint.”

description: Adjusted gross margin fell about 450 bps in Q2, worse than the preview’s estimated 250–400 bps decline. The full-year decline is now expected to be closer to 350 bps, also worse than the preview’s 200–300 bps outlook.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell ~450 bps year-over-year to 56.6% … with full-year margin decline now expected closer to 350 bps reported.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 math … implies … −250 to −400 bps Y/Y”; “FY26 guide is for −200 to −300 bps compression.”

description: U.K. visa conditions became an explicit drag: management incorporated higher rejection rates and expects U.K. revenue growth to decelerate below the company’s overall growth rate by year-end. The preview highlighted U.K. issuance as a risk but hoped for no new U.K. caveat.
fact_evidence: “Management held its U.S. student visa assumption at a 30% decline and baked in higher U.K. visa rejection rates, expecting U.K. revenue to decelerate and exit the year below overall company growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Truist's July downgrade was specifically about worsening UK issuance”; the preview’s bogey was “no new UK caveat,” and it said silence on the U.K. issue would be negative.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Payment volume grew much faster than the preview’s expected 25%–30% TPV growth, but it also outpaced revenue growth—43% versus 27% FX-neutral RLA growth. The preview specifically warned that TPV outrunning revenue could signal take-rate compression, so the volume strength came with that concern.
fact_evidence: “Transaction payment volume” grew 43%; “total revenue less ancillary services” grew 27% FX-neutral.
expectation_evidence: “TPV +25–30%, revenue growing at or above it”; “If TPV outruns revenue in Q2, take rate is compressing.”

description: Travel and hospitality strength was a notable contributor to the Q2 revenue beat, whereas the preview treated travel cross-sell conversion as something to watch rather than an established growth driver.
fact_evidence: Q2 revenue beat guidance “largely on Travel/hospitality strength.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “evidence of that cross-sell converting” in Travel / Sertifi and noted “$2.5B of capturable volume inside existing US hospitality clients.”

description: Management upgraded full-year GAAP net income to more than $50 million, or fourfold growth, an outlook the preview did not provide and which contrasts with its warning that GAAP earnings could remain thin or negative in the seasonally weak Q2.
fact_evidence: Management “upgraded GAAP net income to grow fourfold to over $50 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the seasonally weakest quarter and GAAP could still print thin or negative.”

description: The company set a new long-term target of $1 billion in annual organic revenue at a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, and said it expects to reach about 25% margin by 2027. The preview did not discuss these targets.
fact_evidence: “The company set a multiyear target of $1 billion in annual organic revenue with 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, and expects to reach ~25% EBITDA margin by 2027 when transformation investment peaks.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Three new U.S. SFS deals carried twice the ARR value of the same quarter a year earlier, a stronger deal-value signal than the preview’s focus on the number and geographic mix of client additions.
fact_evidence: “Its three new U.S. SFS deals carried double the ARR value of the same quarter in 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Client adds: ~200/qtr, ~5,100 total globally”; the preview’s client-add bogey was “≥200 adds, with 60%+ of education adds from non-Big-4.”

description: Q2 net product revenue was $13.5 million, well above the preview’s $7.10 million consensus and $9.5 million estimate, driven by Tonmaya sales of about $11 million versus roughly $4 million implied in the preview. This was a much larger sales beat than the preview’s already-bullish Tonmaya estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total net product revenue reached $13.5 million in Q2 2026 ($11M Tonmaya plus $2.5M migraine products)” and “Tonmaya generated approximately $11 million in net sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” My Q2'26E: “$9.5M”; Q2'26 consensus: “$7.10M.” The preview also estimated “TONMYA net revenue” at “$6.3M” and said consensus was “~$4.0M (implied).”

description: Migraine-product sales were $2.5 million, below the preview’s roughly $3.1 million consensus expectation and $3.2 million estimate. The Tonmaya beat therefore more than offset a shortfall in the legacy migraine products.
fact_evidence: Q2 net product revenue comprised “$11M Tonmaya plus $2.5M migraine products.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Zembrace/Tosymra” at “$3.2M” and listed consensus at “~$3.1M.”

description: SG&A rose to $36 million, exceeding the preview’s $31 million estimate by $5 million. The preview anticipated launch and sales-force ramp costs, but the reported expense was still materially higher than its estimate.
fact_evidence: “SG&A expenses surged to $36 million (from $16.2M) year-over-year, reflecting launch investment and pipeline prioritization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “SG&A” at “$31M” and noted the “pre-ramp of +50 reps.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Q2 gross-to-net was helped by favorable channel mix and lower copay buy-downs, rather than the erosion the preview had allowed for. However, management expects gross-to-net to keep fluctuating around Q1/Q2 levels through the rest of 2026 before stabilizing.
fact_evidence: “The Q2 gross-to-net benefited from favorable channel mix and lower copay buy-downs”; management expects “continued fluctuations at similar Q1/Q2 levels through Q3 and Q4 before stabilizing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said it “haircut for gross-to-net erosion (copay support, Medicaid rebates, bridge/free goods)” and flagged that “a drop toward $400–450” net per script would indicate volume bought with discounts and free goods.

description: R&D expense was $19.4 million, slightly above the preview’s $18 million estimate. The increase reflects launch and pipeline prioritization, but exceeded the expected spend.
fact_evidence: “R&D expenses rose to $19.4 million (from $10.8M) year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D” at “$18M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The planned addition of 50 sales representatives is now expected to be fully deployed by September, later than the preview’s target of mid-third quarter. The expansion itself was anticipated, but the stated completion timing is somewhat later.
fact_evidence: The company is “adding 50 reps (bringing the field force to roughly 150) fully deployed by September.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “+50 targeted ‘by mid-third quarter 2026’ to reach ~150” and described the confirmation as a key item to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Refill prescriptions rose 207% quarter over quarter while new-patient prescriptions rose 36%, providing a notably strong refill signal on the durability question the preview highlighted. Total prescriptions were around the preview’s expected level, so the surprise is in the reported refill growth rather than the overall script count.
fact_evidence: “Tonmaya prescriptions totaled 12,592 in Q2, up 100% quarter-over-quarter, with new patient prescriptions up 36% and refills up 207%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “prescriber breadth and refill rate” a key metric and said “Refill persistence is the durability test for a fibromyalgia product — new patient adds without refills is a leaky bucket.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call provided an additional development update on TNX-4800: its Lyme-prevention Phase 2 study has FDA-aligned minutes, is expected to begin enrolling in Q1 2027, and could be pivotal if positive. The preview did not discuss this program or study timeline.
fact_evidence: The “TNX-4800 Lyme prevention Phase 2 adaptive field study (~3,300 participants) has FDA-aligned minutes,” is “expected to begin enrolling in Q1 2027,” and “could serve as a pivotal registrational study if positive.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview focused on Ovaprene enrollment and the prior positive DSMB review but did not flag a change to the FDA protocol requirements. The FDA approved removing the 250-completer expectation, while still strongly recommending at least 250 completers for adequate safety characterization—a regulatory relaxation with a continuing safety-data caveat.
fact_evidence: The FDA approved Daré's protocol amendment removing the 250-completer expectation for the Ovaprene Phase III trial, though it continued to strongly recommend a minimum of 250 completers for adequate safety characterization.

description: The preview did not discuss DARE-HPV, but Daré reported that its approximately 100-woman Phase II study had started with ARPA-H funding and that a second $1 million NIAID tranche brought total project funding to $2 million. This adds a funded clinical program and non-dilutive support not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: The DARE-HPV Phase II study (~100 women) was initiated with ARPA-H funding, and the company secured a second $1 million NIAID tranche bringing total project funding to $2 million, with top-line results expected in 2027.

description: The preview estimated a Q2 net loss of about $3.3 million. The reported loss was about $3 million, a modestly narrower loss than expected, with nondilutive funding offsets contributing to the result.
fact_evidence: Net loss improved to approximately $3 million in Q2 2026 from approximately $4 million in the prior-year period, aided by nondilutive funding offsets.
expectation_evidence: “Net loss n/a” for consensus; “My Estimate: ~$3.3M.”

description: The preview did not identify a 2027 commercialization plan for DARE to RECLAIM. Daré now targets commercial availability of its menopause ring through 503B compounding beginning in 2027, adding a prospective product to its stated 2026–27 commercial lineup.
fact_evidence: DARE to RECLAIM estradiol/progesterone intravaginal ring for menopause is targeted for commercial availability via 503B compounding beginning in 2027, positioning Daré for a diversified multiproduct revenue profile across 2026-2027.

description: Mattel’s constant-currency sales grew 9%, above the preview’s expected 6%–8% growth. The quarter was stronger on revenue than the preview’s roughly $1.08–$1.10 billion sales estimate implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales grew 10% as reported and 9% in constant currency.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales … +6% to +8%”; base case: “$1,085M (+6.5%)” against consensus of “$1,080M.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.01, below the preview’s $0.03–$0.05 consensus range. That was a weaker earnings result despite the better-than-expected sales growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.01 from $0.21.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.03 (Zacks) · $0.04 (AAII, 12 analysts) · $0.05 (alt. compiler)”; base case: “$0.04.”

description: North America gross billings grew 12%, ahead of the preview’s estimate of about 7%. This was a stronger result in the region the preview highlighted as a key test against an easy comparison.
fact_evidence: “North America gross billings up 12%.”
expectation_evidence: “North America ~$545M (+7%)”; the preview also said, “If Mattel’s NA doesn’t grow against a −16% comp, that’s a company-specific problem.”

description: Hot Wheels grew 12%, modestly ahead of the preview’s 10% forecast for Vehicles. Mattel also said the brand is approaching $2 billion in annual revenue.
fact_evidence: “Hot Wheels grew 12% in the quarter” and “is approaching $2 billion in annual revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Vehicles gross billings growth of “+10%” and noted “Hot Wheels ran +13% cc in Q1.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Masters of the Universe showed stronger commercial momentum than the preview’s concern about muted performance around the film suggested: gross billings more than tripled year-to-date, and the film was a major streaming hit despite the preview’s negative box-office framing.
fact_evidence: “Masters of the Universe gross billings more than tripled year-to-date” and the film became “the #1 movie on Prime Video globally and the most-watched movie across U.S. streaming in its first week.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Goldman cited “muted performance” around the MOTU release and described the film as “a confirmed bomb,” citing its box office.

description: Management gave a constructive 2027 outlook, including Barbie returning to growth, which was not covered in the preview’s expectations. This added a positive longer-term message while management characterized 2026 as an investment year.
fact_evidence: Management guided to 2027 delivering “mid- to high-single-digit top-line growth, strong double-digit bottom-line growth, and Barbie returning to growth.”

description: Mattel said it would delay most of the planned $40 million in digital performance marketing until UNO Wild’s commercial launch in early 2027. The preview discussed strategic-investment ROI but did not anticipate this timing change; management said it would not affect 2026 guidance.
fact_evidence: “Management is delaying the majority of $40 million in digital performance marketing spend to coincide with UNO Wild's commercial launch in early 2027, with no impact to 2026 guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “ROI on the ~$150M strategic-investment program” and said management would be pressed on the program’s performance, but did not mention delaying this spend.

description: Nutex reported Q2 revenue of $210.8 million, about 2.9% below the preview’s working consensus of roughly $217 million. The reported decline was attributed to unusually strong IDR-driven revenue realization in the year-ago quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell 13.6% to $210.8 million” due to “unusually strong IDR-driven revenue realization in the 2025 comparison period.”
expectation_evidence: “Working consensus” revenue: “~$217M.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $90 million, well above the preview’s warning that a result below roughly $60 million would signal a structural margin problem. This points to substantially stronger quarterly profitability than that downside threshold implied, despite the revenue miss.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 25.7% to $90 million.”
expectation_evidence: “A print below ~$60M with revenue in line means the margin problem is structural, not timing.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Same-hospital visits grew 6.3%, a much stronger result than the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly flat same-hospital activity. Total visits also grew 9.6%, above the preview’s +5% threshold used in its bull scenario.
fact_evidence: “Hospital visits grew 9.6% to 49,962 in Q2 2026 with same-hospital visits up 6.3%.”
expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “same-hospital flat”; the bull scenario cited “visits +5%+.”

description: A renegotiated Halo MD contract shifted arbitration fees to pay-on-collected terms retroactive to 2024, contributing $38.4 million to lower facility operating costs. The company also expects total contract services costs to be 25%–30% lower going forward, a specific cost reduction not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: The contract change “contribut[ed] about $38.4 million to a $49.6 million decrease in facility operating costs” and is expected to lower “total contract services costs an expected 25%-30% going forward.”

description: The final federal IDR rule reduced CMS administrative fees from $115 to $15 per party, generating another $4.3 million of quarterly savings. The preview focused on arbitration-cost normalization but did not anticipate this additional regulatory fee reduction.
fact_evidence: “The final federal IDR rule cut CMS administrative fees from $115 to $15 per party,” contributing “about $4.3 million in cost savings for the quarter.”

description: Net revenue per visit settled around $4,000–$4,200 and management expects it to stay there, rather than retaining the prior-year quarter’s unusually high $5,185 level. That suggests a lower ongoing revenue-per-visit level than the headline comparison alone might suggest.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue per visit normalized to roughly $4,000-$4,200,” down from “$5,185 in Q2 2025,” and management “expects this level to persist.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said 50%–60% of claims continue to be submitted through IDR, with high award and collection rates. That is reassuring against the preview’s flagged concern that IDR submissions were declining, though it does not indicate that submission rates have increased.
fact_evidence: The company “continues submitting 50%-60% of claims through IDR, winning over 85% of award determinations with an average collection rate over 80%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged that “submissions are declining, ‘possibly due to better initial payments by payers,’” and asked for an update on IDR submission rates.

description: YETI reported adjusted EPS of $0.67, far above the preview’s $0.52–$0.54 consensus range, which implied an approximately 18%–21% year-over-year decline. Instead, adjusted EPS grew 2%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 2% to $0.67 in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.52–$0.54” and “–18% to –21%.”

description: Q2 gross margin reached 59.5%, well above the preview’s estimated 54%–55% and reversing the expected year-over-year decline. The preview identified gross margin as the central risk and said a result of at least 55.5% would de-risk the H2 bridge.
fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin expanded 170 bps to 59.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin ~54–55%” and “A Q2 adj. GM ≥55.5% de-risks the H2 bridge.”

description: The company raised full-year gross-margin guidance by 100 bps to 57.5%–58%, a substantial improvement over the preview’s existing 56.5%–57.0% range and its expectation of a 60-bps year-over-year decline.
fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin guidance was raised 100 basis points to 57.5%–58%, implying a 40 bps year-over-year increase versus a prior expected 60 bps decline.”
expectation_evidence: “FY adj. GM guided 56.5–57.0%” and the preview describes a “~60 bps decline” versus the prior year.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: YETI quantified an IEEPA tariff refund benefit of $8.2 million, or 170 bps of Q2 gross margin. The preview called refund quantification un-modeled upside, so this was a favorable one-off contribution not included in the expected margin picture.
fact_evidence: “Including an $8.2 million (170 bps) benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds.”
expectation_evidence: “Any quantification of YETI's refund receivable is un-modeled upside” and “IEEPA tariff refund quantification — pure un-guided upside.”

description: The full-year adjusted EPS range rose to $2.94–$3.00 from $2.83–$2.89, exceeding the preview’s existing guidance and delivering the raise the preview said investors were looking for. The new upper end also reaches the preview’s bull-case threshold of above $2.95.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $2.94–$3.00 … from prior $2.83–$2.89.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus expects at least a reaffirm of … $2.83–$2.89 EPS”; the preview says the buy-side was “positioned for a raise, not a reaffirm” and its bull case calls for “EPS >$2.95.”

description: YETI raised full-year adjusted operating-margin guidance to approximately 14.9%, up 30 bps, rather than keeping the approximately 14.6% outlook cited in the preview. The company also expects second-half margins to rise about 280 bps year over year, supporting the margin recovery that the preview said the guide depended on.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted operating margin guidance was raised to approximately 14.9% (up 30 bps) … with second-half margins up roughly 280 bps year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin ~14.6%”; the preview says the FY guide “rests on H2 margin recapture.”

description: U.S. Drinkware was flat, rather than extending the U.S. growth streak the preview viewed as evidence of an inflection. Management said three SKUs were dragging 2026 U.S. Drinkware growth by about 600 bps, though it expects that drag to lap by year-end.
fact_evidence: “Drinkware grew only 2% … with U.S. Drinkware flat”; management flagged “a roughly 600 basis point drag on 2026 U.S. Drinkware growth from just 3 SKUs, expected to fully lap by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 was the second straight quarter of category growth and the called-out ‘U.S. inflection’”; the preview says a third consecutive quarter of growth would “confirm the inflection thesis.”

description: Adjusted SG&A rose 19% and deleveraged 410 bps, a notable cost and margin headwind not highlighted in the preview’s margin discussion. Management attributed much of it to a brand campaign shifting from last year’s Q4 into this Q2, plus higher incentive compensation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A rose 19% and deleveraged 410 bps to 45.4% of sales, largely due to the brand campaign shifting from Q4 last year into Q2 this year plus higher incentive comp.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s margin discussion focuses on tariff effects, capacity, and lower product costs; it does not flag a Q2 SG&A deleverage of this size.

description: YETI repurchased $130 million of shares in Q2 alone, more than the roughly $100 million of buybacks the preview said was embedded in the full-year outlook. The call also reported more than $600 million of buybacks since 2024, with about $370 million still authorized.
fact_evidence: “Repurchased 2.8 million shares for $130 million in Q2,” with “total buybacks since 2024 to over $600 million” and “roughly $370 million remaining on authorization.”
expectation_evidence: “~$100M of buybacks embedded against a $500M authorization.”
