description: Q2 diluted EPS of $3.30 exceeded the preview’s $3.00–$3.05 estimate and the $3.20 ceiling of the company’s guidance range. The preview expected a beat, but the reported result was materially above its estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net earnings were $232 million or $3.30 per diluted share,” “exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “My estimate: … EPS ~ $3.00–3.05”; company guidance was “$2.90 ± $0.30.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.35 billion at the midpoint is well above the preview’s roughly $1.26 billion base expectation and above its $1.30 billion bull-case threshold. This signals a stronger next-quarter revenue outlook than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $1.35 billion (±$40M),” with continued sequential and accelerating year-over-year growth.
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Q3 Rev Guide ~$1.26B”; the bull case expected “≥$1.30B.”

description: Q3 EPS guidance of $3.58 at the midpoint is above the preview’s roughly $3.25 Q3 estimate. The preview therefore understated the earnings level implied by the company’s outlook.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for … EPS of $3.58 (±$0.31).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY26 build assumed “Q3E ~$3.25.”

description: The semiconductor outlook is stronger than the preview’s caution around a Q3 figure below roughly $590 million: management said Q3 implies semiconductor year-over-year growth above 50%, far ahead of estimated WFE growth. That points to acceleration rather than the deceleration the preview identified as a risk.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance implies semi YoY growth accelerating to over 50%, well ahead of estimated WFE growth of 25-30%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If Q3 semi guides below ~$590M, the buy-side reads deceleration”; it also highlighted a “Q3 semi guide vs. a ~$600M whisper.”

description: Electronics & Packaging revenue reached $381 million, substantially above the preview’s $350 million guide and its $360 million bull-case marker. The reported chemistry-equipment demand and visibility through 2027 also extend beyond the preview’s near-term durability discussion.
fact_evidence: “Electronics & Packaging revenue rose to $381 million (up 44% YoY),” with “chemistry equipment demand described as the strongest ever and visibility now extending through 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 Electronics & Packaging guidance of “$350M ± $15M,” and its bull case called for “E&P >$360M.”

description: Specialty Industrial revenue of $313 million came in above the preview’s $300 million guide and its $310 million upper end. The segment’s highest level since 2023 and growth driven by datacom and defense were additional strength versus the preview’s expectation of only a slight uptick.
fact_evidence: “Specialty Industrial revenue grew to $313 million (up 14% YoY), the highest since 2023, driven by datacom and defense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 Specialty Industrial guidance of “$300M ± $10M” and described the expected trend as a “slight uptick.”

description: The margin outlook fell short of the preview’s hoped-for inflection: Q3 gross margin is guided at 47%, not 48%, and factory ramp costs are expected to weigh on results. Q2’s 47.6% headline margin also included about 100 basis points of discrete benefits, making it less evidence of durable margin expansion than the preview’s bull case sought.
fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin is guided to 47% (±100bps), down from Q2's reported 47.6% which included roughly 100bps of discrete benefits mainly from tariff/duty refunds,” with “50-80bps of quarterly headwind expected from factory ramp costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “Q3 guide of 48%” was the margin-inflection datapoint bulls wanted; its bull case called for “GM 47.5%+ with 48% Q3 guide.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management raised the scale of the capacity plans beyond the preview’s general references to Malaysia and China expansion: Penang can now support WFE of $200–$250 billion, and Guangzhou chemistry-equipment capacity is being doubled. The higher supported WFE range is a more expansive capacity signal than the preview’s $170–$180 billion 2027 WFE framing.
fact_evidence: “The company is doubling capacity at its Guangzhou chemistry equipment factory (online Q3 2027)” and “reconfigured plans so that filling out its Penang facility can support WFE in the $200-250 billion range, an increase from prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “the Malaysia supercenter and China capacity expansion ramp” and noted management had floated “$170–180B WFE for 2027.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Chemistry’s AI-related revenue share is now 15–20%, above the 10% figure cited as prior guidance, and chemistry-equipment revenue this year is expected to significantly exceed its prior peak. These are stronger AI exposure and chemistry-demand indicators than the preview quantified.
fact_evidence: “AI-related applications now represent 15-20% of chemistry revenue, up from 5% in 2024 and 10% in prior guidance,” while chemistry-equipment revenue “this year will significantly exceed the prior peak of roughly $200 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed chemistry equipment and AI-related advanced-PCB demand, but did not anticipate a 15–20% AI share or chemistry-equipment revenue exceeding the prior peak.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Leverage reached 3.0x, better than the preview’s expectation of roughly 3.2x and its sub-3.3x bull-case marker. The $100 million prepayment itself was anticipated, but the lower leverage and plans for further Q3 and Q4 prepayments were stronger than the preview’s base expectation.
fact_evidence: “Leverage declined to 3x trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion (down a full turn YoY),” with “a $100 million term loan prepayment made this week and additional prepayments planned for Q3 and Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected leverage to move “toward ~3.2x” and said “Sub-3.3x plus a fresh term loan paydown” was the bull case.

description: The preview framed Sandersville’s roughly $2 billion buildout as a major funding gap and wanted an explicit answer on equity issuance. Management said the project’s equity portion is fully funded, no equity raises are planned for the project, and the investment-grade tenant supports favorable-rate financing without credit wrappers or equity backstops—meaningfully more reassuring, although no completed financing facility was reported.
fact_evidence: “The equity portion already fully funded and no equity raises planned for the project”; the tenant is “high investment-grade” and enables financing “without credit wrappers or equity backstops at favorable rates.”
expectation_evidence: “The gap is real and the market knows it. What I want: a named structure (project finance / ABS against the investment-grade lease, JV capital, or a construction facility), an indicative cost of capital, and an explicit statement on equity issuance.”

description: Revenue was $138 million, above the preview’s own $128–133 million estimate, even though it was slightly below the cited $139.4 million consensus. That makes the quarter less weak than the preview’s model implied, but not a clear consensus beat.
fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue was $138 million.”
expectation_evidence: “I model $128–133M, roughly 5–7% light”; the preview also cites “Revenue $139.4M” as consensus.

description: Gross margin declined to 38% as power prices rose, a further deterioration from the 40% Q2 level cited in the preview. The preview flagged mining unit economics as a key debate, but did not explicitly forecast another margin decline.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declining to 38% from 40% as power prices rose $0.01.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin fell to ~40% in Q2 FY26 from 47% in Q1”; the preview said to “watch marginal cost to mine and whether power costs are being absorbed by curtailment credits.”

description: Calumet reported $175 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes, well above the preview’s $115–125 million base estimate. The result came despite three planned turnarounds at Princeton, Cotton Valley and Montana Renewables.
fact_evidence: “Calumet delivered $175 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes in Q2 2026, despite absorbing three planned turnarounds at Princeton, Cotton Valley and Montana Renewables.”
expectation_evidence: “my base build $115–125M”; the preview also said “Anything under ~$95M breaks the recovery narrative.”

description: Specialty Products & Solutions adjusted EBITDA reached $161.7 million, far above the preview’s $85–95 million estimate. The preview expected the March price increases to flow through, but the reported result also reflected more than 20 realized increases and record specialty production.
fact_evidence: “Specialty Products & Solutions adjusted EBITDA more than doubled year-over-year to $161.7 million, driven by over 20 realized specialty price increases and a record specialty production quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “SPS segment | $85–95M (est.)”; “20+ price increases implemented in March should flow through in Q2.”

description: Montana Renewables generated only $17 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes, below the preview’s $28–38 million estimate. It was offline all of April and half of May, foregoing roughly $40 million of margin, although management estimated a normalized quarterly run rate near $60 million.
fact_evidence: “Montana Renewables generated only $17 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes due to being offline all of April and half of May, foregoing roughly $40 million of margin, implying a normalized quarterly run rate near $60 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Montana/Renewables | $28–38M (est.)”; the preview expected Q2 to capture “only ~2 of 3 months” after MaxSAF 150 came online in early May.

description: Performance Brands EBITDA was $6.3 million, well below the preview’s $14–16 million estimate. The call cited a $7 million LIFO headwind, which the preview had not flagged.
fact_evidence: “taking a $7 million LIFO headwind in Performance Brands, whose EBITDA fell to $6.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Performance Brands | $14–16M (est.).”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management described a new, capital-efficient way to expand SAF capacity by reusing a refinery reactor for SAF polishing, enabling up to 200 million gallons at 17,000 bpd by 2028 for a fraction of the originally expected capital. The preview focused on the MaxSAF 150 ramp and DOE funding for MaxSAF 300, not this expansion approach or capacity.
fact_evidence: “A novel, capital-efficient expansion repurposing a second reactor from the fossil refinery into a patent-pending SAF polishing service will enable up to 200 million gallons of SAF at 17,000 bpd throughput by 2028 for a fraction of the originally expected capital.”

description: Calumet said renewable index margins were about $2.60 per gallon and rising, and expected Montana Renewables’ Q3 earnings to be meaningfully higher with a full quarter of production. The preview anticipated a MaxSAF ramp but did not give this Q3 earnings outlook or margin level.
fact_evidence: “Renewable index margins are approximately $2.60 per gallon and rising, with management expecting Q3 Montana Renewables earnings to be meaningfully higher from a full quarter of production.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch: SAF gallons produced,” the “realized $1–2/gal SAF premium over RD,” and MaxSAF 150’s “4–5x SAF volume increase on a run-rate basis.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management said more than 10% of global paraffinic base oil capacity was offline and expected the resulting tight market to persist through 2026. The preview discussed specialty margin recovery and price increases but did not anticipate this supply disruption or its expected duration.
fact_evidence: “Over 10% of global paraffinic base oil capacity (roughly 700,000 bpd market) is offline due to the Iranian and Russia-Ukraine wars, creating a structurally imbalanced, tight market that management expects to persist through 2026.”

description: Management said delaying the reactor reconfiguration until winter would let Montana Renewables capture more than $50 million of unexpected EBITDA during peak asphalt season. The trade-off is a planned roughly two-week fossil-side downtime early in winter, neither of which was anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Delaying the reactor reconfiguration to winter allows CMR to capture over $50 million of unexpected EBITDA during peak asphalt season before the tie-in”; the planned tie-in includes “a ~2-week fossil-side downtime.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Restricted group leverage was already below 4x, with management expecting it to fall below 3x next quarter, aided by a $115 million repurchase that terminates the CMR truck rack sale-leaseback. The preview flagged deleveraging to watch, but did not anticipate that leverage milestone or the additional transaction.
fact_evidence: “Restricted group leverage fell below 4x and management expects to surpass 3x next quarter, aided by calling $100 million of 2028 notes and a $115 million repurchase terminating the CMR truck rack sale leaseback.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch FCF, the deleveraging trajectory, and DOE $1.44B facility draws against MaxSAF 300.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company generated more than $90 million of cash flow from operations despite a $70 million working-capital build. The preview flagged the prior quarter’s working-capital squeeze and said to watch cash generation, but did not set an expectation for this level of cash flow alongside another build.
fact_evidence: “The company generated over $90 million of cash flow from operations despite a $70 million working capital build,” including crude inventory, receivables and MRL; fuel hedges offset about $20 million.
expectation_evidence: “Q1 saw a $100M+ working-capital squeeze”; “Watch FCF, the deleveraging trajectory.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview's base case expected the post-offering runway to extend into the first half of 2028, but REGENXBIO said the strengthened balance sheet extends runway only into Q4 2027. That is shorter than the preview's central expectation, although it still covers the anticipated RGX-202 PDUFA date and wet AMD readouts.
fact_evidence: The company said its pro forma cash position of over $310 million extends its cash runway into Q4 2027, covering the expected RGX-202 PDUFA date and top-line wet AMD data readouts.
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected runway "into first half of 2028"; the preview also said the key distinction was "the gap between 'into 2028' and 'into mid-2027.'"

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call added a sizable commercial opportunity and launch-readiness detail for CERAVEC that the preview did not discuss: management estimated a roughly $10 billion wet AMD market at launch and said more than 500 surgeons had been trained on the delivery procedure. These are favorable new details, but the preview supplied no benchmark for either claim.
fact_evidence: Management estimated the wet AMD market could reach approximately $10 billion at launch and said over 500 surgeons globally have been trained on the CERAVEC subretinal delivery procedure.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed royalty sources and potential product scale that the preview did not address: royalties continue in about 20 ex-U.S. countries after the U.S. Zolgensma patent expired, and worldwide royalties apply to an Abecma follow-on product that management said could reach up to $2 billion in sales. The U.S. patent expiry is a negative, while the continuing and potential royalties are positive.
fact_evidence: The U.S. patent on Zolgensma has expired, but royalties continue in about 20 ex-U.S. countries; the company also has worldwide coverage on Abecma/Novartis's follow-on product, which management noted could reach up to $2 billion in sales.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call provided a specific plan for an ex-U.S. randomized RGX-202 study that the preview did not mention: about 100 patients, 2-to-1 active-to-placebo randomization, planned crossover, and a start in the first half of 2027. The preview gave no expectation against which to judge the study's size or design.
fact_evidence: The new ex-U.S. Affinity Rise trial will enroll approximately 100 patients at 2-to-1 active-to-placebo randomization with a planned crossover and is set to initiate in the first half of 2027.

description: Revenue was slightly above the preview’s $376.2–$376.3 million consensus, at $377.4 million; reported 8% growth also edged the preview’s 7.7% implied growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $377.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$376.2–376.3 million”; “Implied YoY revenue growth | +7.7%.”

description: Adjusted EPS of $1.73 modestly exceeded the preview’s estimate range of roughly $1.69–$1.70.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 16.1% to $1.73.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | ~$1.70 (one source: $1.69).”

description: The company reported a 13% Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin and said full-year margin should land toward the high end of its 12%–13% range, a stronger outlook than the preview’s expectation that margin stay above 12%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13% in Q2, with management guiding full-year margin toward the higher end of its 12%-13% range.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to stay above 12%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Home health was still contracting in Q2, down 2.8% same-store, despite the preview’s note that management expected a return to growth in the second half. The decline narrowed from Q1’s 6.6%, and new admissions rose 9.8%, so the results showed improvement but not yet the expected growth inflection.
fact_evidence: “Home health same-store revenue declined 2.8% but improved from a 6.6% first-quarter drop, with same-store new admissions up 9.8% following new leadership hires.”
expectation_evidence: “Home health segment declined but was expected to return to growth in 2H 2026”; “Q2 results will be an early read on whether that inflection is materializing.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The tax rate reached 26.9%, and management now expects it to remain in the upper-20% range, above the preview’s mid-20% expectation; management attributed the change to the Work Opportunity Tax Credit program’s expiration.
fact_evidence: “The tax rate rose to 26.9% and is expected to stay in the upper-20% range due to expiration of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit program at the end of 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Effective tax rate mid-20% range.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A Medicare Cap accrual of just over $3 million, primarily in Ohio, unexpectedly pressured hospice margins. Management said it expects no additional cap expense and sees possible mitigation for the rest of the year.
fact_evidence: “A Medicare Cap accrual of just over $3 million, primarily in the Ohio market, pressured hospice margins, though management expects no additional cap expense and potential mitigation for the rest of the year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Personal Care’s fill rate improved to 84%–85%, with management attributing the improvement to faster-than-expected caregiver-app adoption in Texas—an operational improvement not flagged in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The consolidated fill rate improved to 84%-85% from the lower 80s, driven by faster-than-expected caregiver app adoption in Texas.”
expectation_evidence: “Faster-than-expected caregiver app adoption in Texas.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash flow rose to $40 million, but the call tied roughly $20 million of first-half working-capital benefit to the increase and said it is not expected to persist; the preview did not flag this cash-flow boost or its temporary nature.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged to $40 million from $22.5 million a year earlier, aided by roughly $20 million in first-half working capital benefits that are not expected to persist.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company reduced bank debt by $30 million sequentially and reported substantial cash and revolver availability, leaving it positioned for larger acquisitions. The preview flagged M&A as an issue to watch but did not anticipate this improvement in acquisition capacity.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced bank debt to $64.3 million (down $30 million sequentially) with ~$100 million cash and $577.8 million in revolver availability, positioning it for larger acquisitions.”
expectation_evidence: “M&A/acquisition update — Addus closed the HomeCourt Home Care (Indiana) acquisition in Q1 FY2026 and had a second Indiana deal pending; watch for confirmation of closing and integration commentary.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management said the Medicaid 80/20 provision could potentially be eliminated by year-end, a new potentially favorable policy outlook not mentioned in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Management expects the Medicaid 80/20 provision to potentially be eliminated by year-end.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Aethlon said its current cash resources are sufficient to fund operations for at least the next 12 months, a more reassuring statement than the preview’s base expectation that the prior going-concern language would be retained. The preview had identified softened or removed language as an upside case.
fact_evidence: “Management states current cash resources are sufficient to fund operations for at least the next 12 months.”
expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects: retained” [going-concern language]; the preview also said the language “could plausibly be softened or removed” in its bull case.

description: Operating expenses were approximately $1.6 million, below the preview’s $1.85 million estimate and even below its $1.70 million low end. The preview expected expenses near the prior-year level, while Aethlon reported an 11.9% year-over-year decline.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated operating expenses fell 11.9% to approximately $1.6 million, down from $1.8 million in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Total opex” of “$1.85M” with a “range $1.70–2.10M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Aethlon gave a concrete window for completing all Cohort 3 treatments and follow-up—by the end of calendar 2026 or early 2027—and said only two more participants are needed. The preview expected enrollment to be ongoing and did not expect a dated completion or analysis window.
fact_evidence: “Only 2 additional participants needed to complete the trial”; management aims to complete treatments and the “8-week follow-up measurement period by the end of calendar 2026 or early 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side expected “Cohort 3 enrollment ongoing,” with “no date” for the readout; it called for a date for the independent statistician’s dose-response analysis.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The Cohort 2 biomarker changes were described as more consistent across participants and lasting up to eight weeks, compared with changes in only two of three Cohort 1 participants that lasted two to three weeks. The preview had noted that Cohort 2 replicated the direction of Cohort 1’s biomarker results, but did not flag this greater consistency and persistence.
fact_evidence: “Cohort 2 ... showed biomarker signals that were more consistent across participants and persisted longer—up to the 8-week mark—compared with cohort 1 ... changes in only 2 of 3 participants lasting 2-3 weeks.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Cohort 2 replicated Cohort 1 biomarker direction,” including tumor-derived EVs, miRNA, and immune-cell measures.

description: Same-station revenue fell 9.6%, worse than the preview’s -6% to -8% base case and beyond its stated -9% bear-case threshold. That indicates the top-line decline was more severe than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell approximately 9.6% on a same-station basis to about $44.1 million from $49.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “-6% to -8% same-station”; it said “worse than -9% breaks the ‘stabilizing’ narrative.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached about $5.3 million, well above the preview’s $2.5–3.5 million base case. Cost benefits therefore appeared sooner or were stronger than the preview allowed for.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to approximately $5.3 million from $4.7 million in Q2 2025 and reversed a negative $0.4 million in Q1 2026, reflecting early cost-cut benefits.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted EBITDA … $2.5–3.5M (cost cuts partially offset revenue decline).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The debt restructuring produced a $91.8 million GAAP gain, exceeding the preview’s expected $70–85 million range. The accounting gain was larger than anticipated, though the preview already expected a substantial gain.
fact_evidence: The restructuring “produced a $91.8 million GAAP gain on debt restructuring.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “a book gain on extinguishment in the ~$70–85M range.”

description: The May expense program is expected to save about $10.5 million annually, above the roughly $7 million in annualized reductions the preview described. That points to a larger cost-savings opportunity than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The May expense reduction program is expected to generate about $10.5 million in annualized run-rate savings, with roughly $5 million benefiting 2026 and full impact realized in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$2M annualized from an early-retirement offering plus ~$5M of further annualized reductions.”

description: Same-station digital revenue grew about 7%, below the preview’s expectation of high-teens growth. Owned-and-operated digital still grew, but its 10% Q2 increase also fell short of the preview’s high-teens digital growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “Overall same-station digital revenue rose roughly 7%”; “Owned-and-operated digital revenue … grew about 10% in Q2 and 18% in the first half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview forecast “high-teens” same-station digital growth and estimated digital revenue of “$11.5–12.5M.”

description: Local direct revenue grew 9%, while national revenue excluding political fell 21% and local agency revenue fell 12%. Local direct demand held up better than the preview’s key debate implied, but weakness in national and agency channels was consistent with its identified downside risk.
fact_evidence: “Same-station local direct revenue grew approximately 9% year-over-year, while national revenue (ex-political) fell about 21% and local agency revenue declined about 12%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required “late-cycle local direct demand holding up” and identified “national/agency weakness” in its bear case.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management described Q4 pacing as very strong even though only minimal political revenue had been booked, suggesting strength beyond a political-advertising lift. The preview expected a midterm political tailwind but did not anticipate this strong Q4 pacing with little political already booked.
fact_evidence: Management “characterized Q4 pacing as very strong with only minimal political revenue booked.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “2026 is a midterm year; political should be a Q3/Q4 tailwind.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: More than 25% of the full-year political budget was already booked or tracking, giving a concrete progress measure for the expected midterm tailwind that the preview had not quantified.
fact_evidence: “Beasley has booked more than 25% of its full-year political budget tracking with the 2024 presidential cycle.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any quantification is the most useful forward datapoint on the call,” but gave no expected booking level.

description: The company agreed to sell two stations for $8 million and plans to use the proceeds to reduce debt, with no expected EBITDA impact. The preview discussed debt and capital structure but did not anticipate this asset sale.
fact_evidence: “The company agreed on July 31 to sell two radio stations in Charlotte and Las Vegas to EMF for $8 million, expected to close in 60-90 days, with proceeds reducing debt and no expected EBITDA impact.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company said its ‘Summer of Influence’ and ‘America 250’ programs had generated nearly $6 million in closed business, an unanticipated commercial update that adds evidence of enterprise-level sales activity.
fact_evidence: “Its enterprise ‘Summer of Influence’ and ‘America 250’ programs have generated nearly $6 million in closed business.”

description: Elanco’s Q2 revenue was $1.368 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.31 billion consensus and above the company’s $1.325 billion guidance ceiling. Organic constant-currency growth was 8%, versus the 4–6% guided range.
fact_evidence: “8% organic constant currency revenue growth in Q2,” with “total revenue of $1.368 billion,” and the company “outperforming the high end of guidance for revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$1.31B”; Q2 company guidance was “$1,300–1,325M (+4–6% OCC).”

description: Adjusted EPS of $0.34 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.27 consensus estimate and the company’s $0.25–$0.28 guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 31% year-over-year to $0.34,” exceeding expectations.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $0.27 (Zacks); $0.28 at some feeds”; company guidance was “$0.25–$0.28.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $288 million, well above the preview’s roughly $250 million consensus and the company’s $260 million guidance ceiling.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $288 million,” exceeding expectations.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$250M”; company guidance was “$240–260M.”

description: Elanco raised its full-year outlook across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS, rather than merely reiterating the existing ranges. The new EPS midpoint of $1.13 also exceeds the preview’s cited buy-side expectation of roughly $1.08–$1.10.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year guidance to 6-7% organic constant currency growth (from 5-7%), adjusted EBITDA of $1.01-1.035 billion … and adjusted EPS of $1.10-1.16.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY guidance of “Revenue $5,010–5,085M (+5–7% OCC),” “Adj. EBITDA $975M–1.005B,” and “Adj. EPS $1.03–1.09”; it said the buy-side expected the EPS midpoint “to move to ~$1.08–1.10.”

description: The gross-margin rebound was stronger than the preview’s roughly 57% consensus and its expectation that margins be only flat-to-up year over year. Elanco also raised its full-year gross-margin expansion outlook.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 80 basis points to 58.1% in Q2,” and “full-year gross margin expansion guidance [was] raised to 50 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: The preview put Q2 adjusted gross margin consensus at “~57%” and said it “needs to be flat-to-up” year over year.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Zenrelia’s commercial progress exceeded the preview’s cited clinic-penetration and market-share markers: penetration is now above 60% of U.S. clinics and share gains reached 9 points year over year.
fact_evidence: Zenrelia is “penetrating ~18,000 U.S. clinics (>60% of the base)” and “improving U.S. JAK market share by 9 points year-over-year,” with an “over-80% reorder rate.”

description: Park’s Q2 RevPAR rose nearly 7% excluding Royal Palm, well above the preview’s roughly 1.5% company-guidance midpoint and even its +5% bull case. Growth also accelerated to over 11% in June, and July RevPAR was up 8.5%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 RevPAR increased nearly 7% year-over-year excluding Royal Palm,” with monthly growth accelerating from “~4% in April to 5% in May and over 11% in June,” and “July RevPAR up 8.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 RevPAR as “~+1.5%, including ~100bps of Miami drag”; its bull scenario was “+5.0%.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA and adjusted FFO both came in well above the preview’s estimates: EBITDA was $204 million versus about $185 million, and FFO was $0.70 per share versus an estimated $0.60–$0.62.
fact_evidence: “Q2 hotel adjusted EBITDA rose nearly 9% to $204 million” and “adjusted FFO was $0.70 per share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted EBITDA ~$185M” and “Adjusted FFO/share ~ $0.60–0.62 (est.).”

description: Park raised its full-year RevPAR guidance midpoint by about 225 basis points, more than twice the preview’s 100-basis-point threshold for a meaningful raise. The new 3%–4.5% range also exceeds the preview’s bull-case range of 2.5%–4.0%.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 RevPAR guidance by ~225 bps at the midpoint to a new range of 3% to 4.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a raise of “less than ~100bps at the midpoint” would be negative and set its bull case at “FY RevPAR to 2.5%–4.0%.”

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA and FFO guidance were raised more than the preview’s base case anticipated: EBITDA midpoint increased by about $25 million, versus an expected $5–$10 million increase, and FFO guidance rose by $0.13 per share.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was increased by ~$25 million at the midpoint to $617–$637 million, and adjusted FFO guidance rose ~$0.13 to $1.90–$2.00 per share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “EBITDA mid +$5–10M”; it listed prior FY guidance of “Adj. EBITDA $587–617M” and “Adj. FFO/sh $1.74–1.90.”

description: Hawaii performed much better than the preview’s uncertain setup suggested: Hilton Hawaiian Village RevPAR was up nearly 12% and EBITDA increased over 13%, despite the preview noting HHV had been only +1% in Q1 and flagging Hawaii as a key debate.
fact_evidence: “Hilton Hawaiian Village RevPAR up nearly 12% and EBITDA up over 13%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “HHV was only +1%” in Q1 and described Hawaii as “genuinely mixed,” with “any progress” on the HHV index a key disclosure.

description: The non-core hotel sale program advanced far beyond the preview’s concern that only $31 million had closed year-to-date and the program might not finish in 2026: Park has sold 10 of 19 identified hotels for nearly $200 million, leaving less than 5% of portfolio value in non-core assets.
fact_evidence: “Since its 2025 exit plan, Park has sold 10 of 19 identified non-core hotels for nearly $200 million at ~12.5x EBITDA, with remaining non-core assets now less than 5% of portfolio value.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Only $31M of the planned pipeline has closed year-to-date” and noted Barclays’ view that “the program won’t finish in 2026.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The reopened Royal Palm showed much stronger balance-of-year pricing than the preview’s delayed-ramp concern implied: group ADRs were up 21% and transient ADRs up 53% versus pre-renovation. The July 22 reopening itself was expected, but these pricing figures were not.
fact_evidence: “The $100M+ Royal Palm South Beach redevelopment reopened July 22” and balance-of-year “group and transient ADRs up 21% and 53% versus pre-renovation.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the reopening was “pushed into Q4/2027” for the ramp and described “a ramp pushed into Q4/2027.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Forward group demand was strong beyond the preview’s Q2 focus: full-year group pace was nearly 6% higher, Q3 pace was over 15% higher, and 2027 core group pace was over 6% higher.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 group pace is up nearly 6%, Q3 group pace is up over 15%, and 2027 core group pace is up over 6%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Leverage improved rather than remaining above the preview’s 6.3x concern: net debt-to-EBITDA was 6.1x, down about 0.2x from the prior quarter. Park also gave a specific plan to repay the $1.27 billion Hilton Hawaiian Village mortgage in September.
fact_evidence: “Net debt was ~$3.7 billion (6.1x net debt-to-EBITDA, down ~0.2x from prior quarter) with $2.6 billion liquidity,” and Park plans to “fully repay the $1.27 billion Hilton Hawaiian Village mortgage in September.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “6.31x net debt / TTM comparable EBITDA” and described leverage as a concern, with its bear case including “leverage above 6.3x.”

description: Hotel EBITDA margin expanded 80 basis points to nearly 32%, a stronger result than the preview’s margin discussion—which highlighted Host’s 60-basis-point expansion and Park’s need to control costs—would suggest.
fact_evidence: Q2 hotel adjusted EBITDA was $204 million “with margin of nearly 32% (up 80 bps).”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Host expanded 60bps on rate-led growth” and said Park’s opex guidance was “+2.4%–3.4% against ~5% wage growth, offset by lower insurance premiums.”

description: July net sales grew about 18% year over year, well ahead of the preview’s roughly 10% Q3-to-date reference point and above its low-teens bull-case signal. This marked a clear acceleration from Q2’s 12% growth.
fact_evidence: “July net sales increasing approximately 18% year-over-year, a 6-point acceleration from Q2's growth rate.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything below ~+10% Q3-to-date breaks the reacceleration story”; the bull case called for Q3-to-date growth in the “low-teens.”

description: Gross margin reached 56.6%, above the previewed 54.1%–54.6% guide. Even excluding roughly 160 basis points from tariff refunds, underlying gross margin rose about 90 basis points year over year, exceeding the preview’s expected flat-to-50-basis-point improvement.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 56.6%, but excluding roughly 160 basis points of tariff refund benefit, underlying gross margin rose about 90 basis points year-over-year on AI-driven markdown recalibration.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | 54.1–54.6% (co. guide) | ... flat to +50bps.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Tariff refunds delivered an unmodeled benefit, including 6 cents per share and $5.6 million of adjusted EBITDA. That helped lift reported EPS to 26 cents versus the 22-cent estimate, but backing out the EPS benefit implies 20 cents, below consensus; the preview had identified refunds as a possible one-time upside excluded from guidance.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS rose to 26 cents ... including a 6-cent benefit from IEPA tariff refunds,” and adjusted EBITDA was $27 million “including a $5.6 million tariff refund benefit.”
expectation_evidence: “Tariff refunds filed April 20 with 60–90 day timing were explicitly excluded from guidance — a possible unmodeled one-time benefit.”

description: Management disclosed that it plans to invest about two points of adjusted EBITDA margin in 2026, including 150 basis points in marketing and 50 basis points in G&A. The preview anticipated substantial marketing spend and watched for cost overruns, but did not flag an investment of this stated size, which pressures near-term profitability.
fact_evidence: “Management is investing approximately two points of adjusted EBITDA margin in 2026 (about 150 bps in marketing and 50 bps in G&A) to seed long-term initiatives, pressuring near-term profitability.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited marketing at “~15.7% of sales (FY 15.3–15.8%)” and warned that “marketing above 15.8%” could indicate that growth was being bought.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Active-customer growth accelerated to 11%, above the preview’s expected 8% range, and the company exceeded 3 million trailing 12-month active customers. The quarterly increase of 115,000 was also described as the highest in four years.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month active customers accelerated to 11% growth year-over-year, surpassing the 3 million milestone with a 115,000 quarterly increase—the highest quarterly growth in four years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Active customers (TTM) ~2.95–3.00M” and said sustaining “≥8% active growth” was important.

description: International sales grew 16%, above the preview’s watchpoint of roughly 15%, while the Middle East rebounded to strong double-digit growth despite the expected continued slowdown. The international mix also reached a record high.
fact_evidence: “International sales grew 16% year-over-year and reached nearly 23% of total net sales—the highest mix ever—with the Middle East rebounding to strong double-digit growth despite a weak start.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the Middle East slowdown “persisted into Q2” and asked whether international sales would “decelerate below ~15%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow was negative $11 million and inventory rose 25% year over year, a working-capital and inventory build that the preview did not identify as an expected Q2 issue.
fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was negative $11 million on unfavorable working capital and inventory rose 25% year-over-year.”

description: The company repurchased nearly 500,000 Class A shares for about $10 million, more than 1% of the Class A stock. The preview discussed the company’s cash position but did not flag a repurchase as an expected capital-allocation action.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased nearly 500,000 Class A shares at an average price of $19.98 (about $10 million, over 1% of Class A stock).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Cardi B Grow Good venture showed strong repeat purchasing and social-media traction, and its gross margins are accretive. The preview noted prior sellouts and expected more inventory, but the call said inventory constraints still limited sales.
fact_evidence: “The Cardi B Grow Good beauty joint venture sold out within hours across its first drops, achieved a repeat purchase rate approaching 40%, generated 670,000 Instagram followers, and carries gross margins accretive to the business, though inventory constraints limited sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted GrowGood had “sold out in under an hour, gated on inventory” and that management had flagged “a big wave of inventory coming.”

description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $0.35, well above the preview’s $0.21 estimate. The 67% gap was much larger than the preview’s expected 11% year-over-year increase.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rising to $0.35 from $0.19 a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.21”; implied y/y “+11%.”

description: Q4 total segment EBITDA reached $423 million, substantially above the preview’s estimated $355–365 million range.
fact_evidence: “Total segment EBITDA surged 31% to $423 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total Segment EBITDA ~$355–365M (est., not a published print).”

description: Q4 revenue was $2.3 billion, about 4% above the preview’s $2.21 billion estimate, rather than merely matching the roughly 5% year-over-year growth expected.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue rose 11% to $2.3 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $2.21B”; implied y/y “+5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Digital-only subscription net adds were about 194,000, far above the preview’s self-set expectation of notably higher adds and its warning that anything below 60,000 could be a soft miss.
fact_evidence: “Digital-only subscriptions up 9% to nearly 6.3 million and the highest sequential net adds (~194,000) in over two years.”
expectation_evidence: Management guided to “notably higher” Q4 net adds; “Sub-60k would read as a soft miss.”

description: Digital Real Estate Services delivered especially strong growth, with revenue up 19% and EBITDA up 46%; realtor.com revenue grew 13% despite the preview’s concerns about housing and rate headwinds and its warning that forward commentary was a risk.
fact_evidence: “Digital Real Estate Services delivered standout Q4 results with revenue up 19% to $553 million and EBITDA up 46% to $222 million, as realtor.com posted its seventh straight quarter of revenue growth (+13%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview described realtor.com as “the clearest bear vector,” citing falling existing home sales and higher mortgage rates, and said “the forward commentary is where this bites.”

description: FY2026 revenue and EBITDA finished above the preview’s derived expectations: revenue was $9 billion versus about $8.90 billion, and EBITDA exceeded $1.6 billion versus an estimated $1.55–1.60 billion range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue grew 7% to $9 billion and total segment EBITDA rose 15% to over $1.6 billion.”
expectation_evidence: Derived FY2026 revenue of “~$8.90B, +5.3%” and total segment EBITDA of “~$1.55–1.60B.”

description: The Meta AI licensing deal was already signed, but it was contributing to Q4 results across Dow Jones and News Media, rather than remaining mostly a future-facing narrative as the preview suggested.
fact_evidence: “The Meta AI licensing deal is now contributing to Q4 results across both Dow Jones and News Media, with more deals in the pipeline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview characterized AI licensing as “narrative >> numbers this quarter” and said the Meta and OpenAI deals were signed.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Dow Jones raised the WSJ digital subscription full price for new customers from $39.99 to $44.99, a pricing action the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “The WSJ digital subscription full price [was raised] from $39.99 to $44.99 for new customers.”

description: Peloton guided to FY27 revenue of $2.3–2.4 billion, down 3.9% at the midpoint, rather than the roughly flat revenue the preview said the Street expected. Management also framed FY27 as a transition year, with new-category launches not expected to drive acceleration until fall 2027.
fact_evidence: “FY27 revenue guidance of $2.3-2.4 billion implies a 3.9% year-over-year decline at the midpoint,” with acceleration from new-category launches “starting fall of calendar 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Street: roughly flat revenue (~$2.43B)” and UBS “models revenue −1%.” The preview also said to watch for a date for the revenue inflection.

description: FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance was below the preview’s $504 million consensus midpoint: the company’s $435–525 million range has a $480 million midpoint. The top of the range is near consensus, but the midpoint is about 5% lower.
fact_evidence: “FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $435-525 million reflects a 7% increase at the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$504M” for FY27; the preview’s base scenario expected “$495–520M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q4 net churn reached 2.2%, materially above the preview’s 1.4% level for reopening the bear case. Management attributed about half of the increase to a since-reverted payment reactivation algorithm change and half to lingering price-increase effects; FY27 churn is expected roughly flat.
fact_evidence: “Q4 net churn rose 37 basis points year-over-year to 2.2%,” with roughly half attributed to a “one-time payment reactivation algorithm change” and half to “lingering price-increase effects”; “full-year FY27 churn is expected roughly flat.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 churn was 1.2%; anything ≥1.4% reopens the bear case.”

description: FY27 gross margin guidance of about 54% was higher than the preview’s roughly 52.5% full-year guide assumption, by about 150 basis points.
fact_evidence: “FY27 gross margin is expected around 54%, up roughly 140 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “FY gross margin guide of ~52.5% requires a meaningful Q4 step-up.”

description: Q4 revenue was $608 million, above the $597 million consensus and $6 million above the high end of the implied company range. The beat was modest, but it exceeded the preview’s upper implied-guide threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue of $608 million beat the high end of implied guidance by $6 million.”
expectation_evidence: Q4 revenue consensus was “$597.0M” and company implied guidance was “$581.6–601.6M.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Peloton recorded a $23.8 million Q4 legal contingency accrual for a patent-infringement jury verdict, an unanticipated charge. Management said it does not expect a material ongoing royalty impact.
fact_evidence: “The company booked a $23.8 million legal contingency accrual in Q4 tied to a jury verdict over third-party media player patent infringement,” though it “does not expect material go-forward royalty impact.”

description: Peloton reported its first full fiscal year of positive net income and operating income, an annual profitability milestone the preview did not specifically anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Its first full fiscal year of positive net income ($63 million) and positive operating income ($161 million).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Peloton IQ engagement and interest were stronger than the preview’s unquantified discussion of IQ as a possible conversion driver: it engaged more than half of monthly active users in Q4 and ranked as the top feature of interest among prospective customers.
fact_evidence: “Peloton IQ engaged more than 50% of monthly active users in Q4 and is now the #1 feature of interest among prospective customers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case required “Peloton IQ converting existing members at higher attach.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The number of members owning multiple connected-fitness products reached 316,000, up 20,000 year over year, and these members churn at lower rates. The preview identified higher attach as a possible driver but did not give an expected ownership figure or churn comparison.
fact_evidence: “316,000 members now own multiple connected fitness products (up 20,000 YoY) and churn at lower rates.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case cited “Cross Training Series and Peloton IQ converting existing members at higher attach.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.52 versus the preview's $0.36 consensus, but $0.17 per share came from tariff refunds; excluding that benefit, EPS was about $0.35, slightly below consensus and down year over year. The headline beat was therefore large, but the underlying result did not beat expectations.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was flat year-over-year at $0.52, including a $0.17 per share benefit from $44 million in tariff refunds, meaning underlying EPS declined absent the refund.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.36.”

description: Management said Q3 revenue would decline sequentially and Q3 earnings would be below Q2 levels excluding the tariff-refund benefit, with investment benefits not visible until Q4. That pushes visible benefits later than the preview's expectation that tariff mitigation would land in Q2–Q3 and transformation benefits would accelerate in H2.
fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 2026 revenue to decline sequentially on seasonality and Q3 earnings to fall below Q2 levels (excluding the $0.17 tariff benefit), with investment benefits expected to become visible starting in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly told the Street that tariff mitigation lands in Q2–Q3 and that transformation benefits accelerate in H2.”

description: Revenue of $898 million beat both preview estimates, but the constant-currency decline was 6.3%, slightly worse than the preview's roughly 4%–6% range. The reported decline of 4.1% was flattered by currency; adjusting for Byte and the planned dealer inventory reduction, the constant-currency decline was 3.6%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $898 million, down 4.1% as reported and 6.3% on a constant currency basis, or a 3.6% constant currency decline when adjusting for Byte and an ~$8 million planned dealer inventory reduction.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales $883.9M” and an alternative estimate of “~$893M”; the preview also described the base case as “cc still −4 to −6%” and warned that FX could make reported revenue beat while constant-currency results remained weak.

description: The underlying OIS picture remained weak: implants declined mid-single digits and SureSmile ortho fell double digits on U.S. weakness. That fell short of the preview's highlighted possibility that core implants could stabilize, although the 5.7% OIS decline excluding Byte was close to the preview's roughly 6% bull-case decline.
fact_evidence: “OIS revenue fell 13.2% as reported (5.7% excluding Byte), with SureSmile ortho revenue of $40 million declining double digits driven by U.S. weakness, while implants (IPS) of $157 million declined mid-single digits.”
expectation_evidence: “Core implant stabilization is the most under-appreciated potential positive”; the preview's bull case also required the OIS decline to halve to “~−6%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash from operations more than doubled to $99 million, a stronger cash-flow result than the preview's concern about another weak cash quarter suggested. The improvement was partly supported by tariff refunds and working-capital management, so it does not by itself establish a comparable improvement in free cash flow.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow more than doubled to $99 million from $48 million a year earlier, aided by tariff refunds and improved working capital management.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 FCF was −$12M” and “A second consecutive negative-FCF quarter puts capital-allocation questions … into the Q&A.”

description: The company restarted share repurchases, buying 1.3 million shares for about $12 million, its first buyback since Q3 2024. The preview raised buyback pace as a capital-allocation question amid cash-flow concerns, but did not anticipate a resumption.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 1.3 million shares for approximately $12 million at an average price below $10 per share, marking its first buyback since Q3 2024.”

description: CTS showed a pronounced regional split: Americas revenue was down nearly 10% constant currency as customers deferred CAD/CAM capital spending, while APAC grew at a double-digit rate, including in milling systems. The preview did not flag this segment or regional pattern.
fact_evidence: “CTS Americas was down nearly 10% constant currency driven by CAD/CAM CapEx deferrals, while APAC posted double-digit growth including double-digit growth in milling systems.”

description: The preview expected FY26 guidance to be reaffirmed at $730–750 million of revenue and $91–93 million of adjusted EBITDA, while noting that a raise was possible. Management raised the ranges to $740–755 million and $92–95 million.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $740-$755 million in revenue and $92-$95 million in adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (reaffirmed May 5, 2026): FY26 revenue $730–750M, adj. EBITDA $91–93M”; the preview said investors wanted “a narrow to the top half ... or an outright raise.”

description: Adjusted EPS came in above the preview’s $0.25 anchor and the top of its $0.23–$0.27 analyst range. GAAP EPS also exceeded the preview’s derived estimate of about $0.14–$0.16.
fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS was $0.23 and non-GAAP EPS was $0.28.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (ex-special items) $0.25 (range $0.23–$0.27, 3 analysts)” and “GAAP diluted EPS ~$0.14–$0.16 (my est.).”

description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s roughly $25.0 million estimate, and the reported margin was slightly above the preview’s 13.2% base-case scenario.
fact_evidence: “Record second-quarter adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million, up 7% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 30 basis points to 13.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$25.0M (my est., no published consensus)”; the base scenario projected “$25.0M (13.2%).”

description: Revenue was above the preview’s $189.2 million consensus estimate, delivering 4.2% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s expected 2.0%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 4.2% year-over-year to $193 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $189.2M” and “Y/Y +2.0%.”

description: Aerospace & Defense grew only 13.2%, below the preview’s expectation that growth markets stay comfortably above roughly 20%. Infrastructure and Power Generation did clear that bar, but A&D fell short of the stated threshold.
fact_evidence: “Aerospace & Defense up 13.2% ($3.2 million).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said A&D, Infrastructure, and Power Generation “must stay comfortably north of ~20% to offset O&G.”

description: Operating income rose much faster than revenue, with management reporting nearly 60% conversion of incremental revenue into operating income and calling that rate sustainable. The preview expected margin expansion but did not forecast this degree of operating leverage or management’s sustainability claim.
fact_evidence: “Operating income increased 53.6% to $12.9 million, converting nearly 60% of incremental revenue into operating income, a rate management called sustainable and slightly higher on a full-year basis.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called margin momentum “the strongest part of the story” and said margins “need[]” to expand, but gave no operating-income conversion estimate.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management disclosed plans to nearly triple in-lab testing capacity by the end of 2027, backed by visible customer demand. The preview discussed recent lab expansions but did not anticipate this larger capacity buildout.
fact_evidence: “The company is investing to nearly triple its in-lab testing capacity by the end of 2027, supported by visible customer demand, with new investments typically taking 9-12 months to come online.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted the Los Angeles aerospace lab expansion and a similar Houston expansion, but did not mention a plan to nearly triple total in-lab testing capacity.

description: Cisco’s FY27 revenue guide of $72.2–73.4 billion implies roughly 15% growth at the midpoint, well above the preview’s estimate of about 9.5% growth and $68.7–69.0 billion. This was a substantially stronger outlook than expected.
fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance calls for revenue of $72.2-$73.4 billion (roughly 15% growth at midpoint).”
expectation_evidence: “Street models ~9.5% FY27 revenue growth (≈$68.7–69.0B).”

description: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $5.05–5.11 was above the preview’s roughly $4.80 consensus and above Evercore’s expected $4.80–5.00 range. The earnings outlook therefore exceeded even the preview’s cited upper-end expectation.
fact_evidence: “non-GAAP EPS of $5.05-$5.11.”
expectation_evidence: “Street models … ~$4.80 EPS”; “Evercore ISI expects management to guide $4.80–5.00 EPS.”

description: Q4 revenue of $17.3 billion exceeded the roughly $16.83 billion consensus and the preview’s inferred $17.0–17.2 billion whisper range. The revenue beat was stronger than the preview’s already-above-consensus expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached a record $17.3 billion, up 18% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue … $16.82–16.85B”; “Inferred whisper … revenue ~$17.0B.”

description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 beat both the $1.17 consensus and the preview’s inferred $1.19–1.20 whisper range, and exceeded the high end of company guidance. The beat was larger than the preview’s expected narrow, roughly 2% pattern.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 up 23%, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $1.17”; “Inferred whisper … EPS ~$1.19–1.20”; Cisco had beaten “by a narrow, consistent ~2%.”

description: Security revenue grew 14% in Q4, far above the preview’s expected 4.7% growth and breaking from the recent flat trend. Management said unusually large, longer-duration on-prem Splunk deals benefited the quarter, which qualifies the strength but does not erase the sizable beat.
fact_evidence: “Security revenue grew 14% in Q4 … though management noted the quarter benefited from unusually large on-prem Splunk deals with longer duration.”
expectation_evidence: “Security … +4.7%”; “Security was flat Y/Y in Q3 and has missed repeatedly.”

description: Cisco set its FY27 AI infrastructure revenue target at $7.5 billion, above the preview’s expected $6.5–7 billion range. That implies a stronger AI revenue outlook than investors were led to expect.
fact_evidence: “Guiding to $7.5 billion in AI infrastructure revenue for FY27 versus $4 billion in FY26.”
expectation_evidence: “Morgan Stanley expects an FY27 AI revenue target of $6.5–7B.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: FY26 hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders totaled $9.3 billion, slightly surpassing the preview’s $9 billion target. The preview’s implied Q4 requirement was about $3.7 billion, so the result indicates a modest overachievement rather than a major step-up.
fact_evidence: “AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers totaled $9.3 billion in FY26.”
expectation_evidence: “Cisco raised the FY26 hyperscaler AI order target to $9B”; “implying ~$3.7B needed in Q4.”

description: Non-GAAP gross margin was 66.3%, about 40 basis points above the preview’s roughly 65.9% model despite the year-over-year decline. The preview had expected margin pressure from AI mix, but the reported margin level was better than modeled.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin fell 210 basis points year-over-year to 66.3%, driven by higher hardware mix and memory costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP GM (implied) ~65.9%”; “Street models ~65.9% in Q4.”

description: The FY27 core business excluding AI is implied to grow about 10%, a stronger outlook for non-AI demand than the preview’s concern that growth outside AI was only around 4%.
fact_evidence: “The core business ex-AI [is] implied to grow about 10%.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue growth of ~7% collapses to roughly 4% ex-AI”; campus/traditional networking saturation was described as “the core bear argument.”

description: Cisco guided to roughly 35% FY27 operating margin, above the preview’s cited expectation of about 34%. This suggests the much stronger growth outlook is not accompanied by the degree of operating-margin pressure the preview contemplated.
fact_evidence: Management guided to “~35% operating margin.”
expectation_evidence: “Evercore ISI expects management to guide … on ~34% EBIT margin.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Cisco reported three new hyperscaler design wins in Q4 and visibility to multiple additional AI design wins over the next six months. The preview focused on orders, revenue conversion, and the AI target, but did not anticipate this specific expansion of the design-win pipeline.
fact_evidence: “The company secured three new hyperscaler design wins in Q4 … with line of sight to multiple additional AI design wins over the next six months.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Networking product orders grew 40%, with campus networking orders up 20%, giving stronger evidence of continuing campus demand than the preview’s question of whether the refresh cycle would merely sustain. This was a positive demand signal beyond the preview’s stated concern about traditional networking saturation.
fact_evidence: “Networking product orders grew 40% in Q4 marking the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with Campus Networking orders up 20%.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the campus refresh cycle (a Q3 strength) sustains”; “Campus/traditional networking saturation is the core bear argument.”

description: FY26 revenue of $63.3 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $4.33 both exceeded the company’s full-year guide ranges of $62.8–63.0 billion and $4.27–4.29. Full-year operating margin also expanded 40 basis points to 34.8%.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 revenue was a record $63.3 billion … with non-GAAP EPS of $4.33 … and operating margin improving 40 basis points to 34.8%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 full-year guide: revenue $62.8–63.0B; non-GAAP EPS $4.27–4.29.”

description: Harmony reported diluted EPS of $1.28, well above the preview’s working expectation of about $1.05–$1.10. The preview identified Q2 expenses as the key uncertainty, but the reported EPS was roughly 16%–22% above that bar.
fact_evidence: “Net income more than doubled to $75.4 million ($1.28 per diluted share)” in Q2 2026.
expectation_evidence: “A fair working bar is ~$1.05–1.10.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: WAKIX added about 450 patients, described as its highest Q2 increase in brand history. The preview expected demand-led sequential growth to be confirmed, but did not anticipate a record Q2 patient gain.
fact_evidence: WAKIX “added approximately 450 patients in Q2” and this was “the highest Q2 increase in the brand's history.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “demand-led QoQ growth confirmed”; the preview also said to watch whether the sequential jump reflected “demand/new patient starts” rather than gross-to-net or channel effects.

description: Cost of product sold rose to 24.2% of revenue, above the preview’s estimate based on Q1’s 20.7% ratio. Management attributed the increase primarily to new royalties under the Novitium license, making product costs less favorable than the preview’s build assumed.
fact_evidence: “Cost of product sold rose to 24.2% of net revenue from 19% a year ago, primarily due to new royalties tied to the Novitium license agreement signed in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview applied Q1 margins to Q2 revenue and estimated “COGS ~$54M”; Q1 COGS was listed as “20.7%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The reported WAKIX protection date was March 2030 including pediatric exclusivity, shorter than the preview’s stated July 2030 protection with pediatric exclusivity. That leaves a shorter stated protection period than investors were led to expect.
fact_evidence: “WAKIX exclusivity is protected to March 2030 including pediatric exclusivity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “July 2030 with pediatric exclusivity.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The BP-205 SAD readout included a notably detailed favorable profile: once-daily-supportive half-life, high orexin-2 selectivity, a wide projected margin over the maximum predicted efficacy dose, and no serious adverse events in the volunteers studied. The preview expected the data as a credibility checkpoint but did not specify or set expectations for these characteristics.
fact_evidence: BP-205 showed a “~25-hour half-life supporting once-daily dosing,” “over 600-fold selectivity for orexin-2 over orexin-1 receptors,” a “projected 140-fold margin over the maximum predicted efficacy dose,” and no serious cardiovascular, hepatic, or visual adverse events across 72 volunteers.
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “BP-205 Phase 1 SAD PK/safety data” as “the credibility test for Harmony's own orexin answer.”

description: McDonald’s adjusted EPS was $3.38, above the preview’s $3.32–$3.34 consensus range. The reported 5% constant-currency growth was stronger than the roughly 4.1% growth implied by the preview’s comparison.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $3.38, up 5% in constant currency, including a $0.03 foreign currency benefit.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The U.S. exit rate remained weak: management said same-store sales were slightly negative in July, rather than describing an improving trend or a July acceleration. That adds evidence of continued pressure entering Q3, though the preview had identified the exit rate as uncertain.
fact_evidence: “U.S. same-store sales were slightly negative in July, signaling weak momentum entering Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “If management frames May/June as sequentially improving and quantifies a July acceleration, the quarter gets forgiven”; the preview also identified the “June and July exit rate” as a key metric to watch.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said the launch of the under-$3 EDAP menu coincided with pulling back digital offers and removing Buy One Add One for $1, a “bad trade” that accounted for about two-thirds of U.S. traffic underperformance. The preview worried that value offers might not restore traffic, but did not anticipate this specific promotional trade-off.
fact_evidence: “About two-thirds of the U.S. traffic underperformance” came from a “‘bad trade’” in which the EDAP menu launched while digital offers were pulled back and Buy One Add One for $1 was removed.
expectation_evidence: “If comps are positive on price/mix alone with traffic down mid-single digits, the value strategy is not working as advertised.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Only 60% to 65% of the U.S. system followed the recommended EDAP pricing architecture, and management said inconsistent execution contributed to lower incrementality. The preview discussed the value menu’s potential traffic and margin effects but did not flag this limited franchisee execution as a risk.
fact_evidence: “Only about 60% to 65% of the U.S. system executed the recommended EDAP pricing architecture, contributing to inconsistent results and lower incrementality.”
expectation_evidence: “The $3 menu (launched April) and $4 breakfast deal are margin-dilutive by construction; franchisee P&L commentary matters as much as the corporate line.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The June FIFA marketing campaign underdelivered against expectations, accounting for about one-third of U.S. underperformance. That contrasts with the preview’s potential upside case that World Cup-related marketing and the value menu could drive traffic.
fact_evidence: “The remaining one-third of U.S. underperformance was tied to the June FIFA marketing campaign underdelivering versus expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “World Cup cups + $3 menu drive real traffic.”

description: McDonald’s reduced its expected 2026 forex tailwind to about $0.15 from the preview’s $0.20–$0.30 framework. That is a meaningful reduction in the expected currency support to full-year results.
fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year 2026 forex tailwind estimate to about $0.15, down from a prior range of $0.20 to $0.30.”
expectation_evidence: “A $0.20–0.30 FY EPS FX tailwind.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The 50,000-restaurant target moved from the end of 2027 to 2028, with management citing pressured consumers and higher cumulative development costs. The preview expected about 2,600 openings in 2026 but did not anticipate this delay to the longer-term target.
fact_evidence: “McDonald’s pushed its 50,000-restaurant target from end of 2027 to 2028, citing pressured consumers and cumulative inflation on development costs.”
expectation_evidence: “The only standing framework is FY26 operating margin in the mid-to-high 40% range, ~2,600 openings (~2,100 net new).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The beverage platform was already exceeding expectations, with more than half of its traffic after lunch and average checks on those orders about 50% above the full-day average. The preview had called for beverage datapoints as proof of the platform’s potential but did not anticipate these strong reported usage and check figures.
fact_evidence: “The new beverage platform is exceeding expectations, with more than half of traffic coming after lunch and average checks on those orders running about 50% above the full-day average.”
expectation_evidence: “Beverage platform datapoints. McCafé Refreshers, crafted sodas, energy entry, plus Germany/Canada platforms. Any hard mix or attach-rate numbers would be the first real proof point.”

description: McDonald’s announced an immediate change in U.S. leadership, with Sky Anderson replacing Joe Erlinger, who is leaving after more than two decades. The announcement came alongside Q2 declines in customer satisfaction and service times—operating and leadership developments not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Sky Anderson was named U.S. President effective immediately, replacing Joe Erlinger who is leaving after over two decades, amid Q2 declines in customer satisfaction and service times.”

description: Cibus reported Q2 revenue of about $1 million, well below the preview’s $1.70 million consensus estimate and $1.8 million model. The shortfall was roughly 40% versus consensus.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue of approximately $1 million”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue Q2 2026E: $1.70M”; the preview’s model was “$1.8M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Cibus pushed its Latin American rice commercial launch from the preview’s 2027 target to 2028. That is a further delay to a major anticipated rice opportunity.
fact_evidence: “Delayed rice commercial launch guidance in Latin America from late 2027 to 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Ecuador/Colombia launch is targeted 2027.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash was slightly below the preview’s roughly $21 million estimate, and management described runway only into early Q1 2027, earlier than the prior late-Q1 wording. This points to financing needs sooner than the preview’s already-cautious runway expectation.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were $20.4 million as of June 30, 2026, projected to fund operations only into early Q1 2027, signaling potential near-term financing needs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled cash of “~$21M” and said Q1 had indicated runway “into late in the first quarter of 2027.”

description: Net loss was worse than the preview’s $20.6 million model, and GAAP loss per share of $0.29 was also below the $0.26 loss consensus. The per-share miss was less severe against the preview’s own $0.27 model.
fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $22.1 million ($0.29 per share).”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Net loss $(20.6)M” and “EPS $(0.27),” and listed GAAP EPS consensus of “–$0.26.”

description: The company’s stated exit-2026 net cash usage run rate target was about $35 million, above the preview’s approximately $30 million annual burn target. Although cash usage declined, the stated target implies a higher burn level than investors were watching for.
fact_evidence: “Quarterly cash usage fell approximately 19% sequentially and 31% year-over-year, with the company targeting a net cash usage run rate of about $35 million exiting 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to a “stated ~$30M/yr burn target” and said cash usage “must trend to ~$7.5M/qtr to hit the $30M/yr target.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Cibus expanded the Interoc rice framework from two traits to five, adding breadth to the opportunity beyond the preview’s description of the existing two-trait framework. A definitive commercial agreement is still being pursued, so the expansion is progress but not a conversion to a signed deal.
fact_evidence: “Expanded its Interoc framework from two rice traits to five in August, shifting toward a multi-trait pipeline model as it works toward a definitive commercial agreement.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the January LOI as non-binding and focused on the “LOI → definitive” step; it characterized the base case as Interoc “still ‘negotiating in good faith.’”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: In addition to the EU decision already highlighted in the preview, Cibus cited favorable edited-crop determinations across several other jurisdictions. The preview had identified the EU rule as the known regulatory tailwind but did not anticipate these additional determinations.
fact_evidence: “Regulatory tailwinds strengthened as the EU finalized rules in June treating most non-GMO edited crops as conventional, while Ecuador, Peru, USDA APHIS, and the FDA granted favorable determinations across three continents.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the June EU decision and said “No dates or dollars have been attached”; it asked whether a named EU seed partner would emerge.

description: Non-cash royalty liability interest expense was $9.5 million, slightly above the preview’s $9.3 million estimate. The preview already expected this to be the largest single item in net loss, so the difference was limited.
fact_evidence: “A large non-cash royalty liability interest expense of $9.5 million (up from $8.7 million) remains the primary driver of the gap between operating loss and net loss.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Royalty liability interest (non-cash) $(9.3)M” and described it as “the largest single item in net loss.”

description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $8.91, well above the preview’s reconstructed $7.24 consensus and the $6.78–$7.46 guidance-implied range. The call noted that the year-over-year comparison is affected by an unusually low prior-year tax provision, but the reported quarter still substantially exceeded the preview’s benchmarks.
fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS of $8.91 grew only 6.1% due to a much lower prior-year tax provision.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | ~$7.24”; guidance-implied range “$6.78 – $7.46.”
