description: Full-year adjusted EPS reached $29.83, above both the preview’s $28.16 Street estimate and its $27.70–$28.38 guidance range. The preview had highlighted ARKA-related interest expense as a headwind, but EPS rose 12.7% despite $120 million of additional interest and tax expense.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS rose 12.7% to $29.83 despite $120 million in additional interest and tax expense.”
expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted diluted EPS: guidance “$27.70 – $28.38”; Street “$28.16.” The preview also noted “a full year of ARKA interest expense … is a real EPS drag.”

description: Q4 EBITDA margin was 13%, far above the preview’s roughly 11.5% consensus and 11.4%–11.7% implied range, despite the warning that Q4 would be softer than Q3. About 30 basis points came from a UK divestiture gain, but the reported margin still cleared the expected range substantially.
fact_evidence: “Fourth quarter … EBITDA margin of 13%, up 150 basis points, though about 30 basis points came from a UK divestiture gain.”
expectation_evidence: “EBITDA margin | ~11.5%”; guidance-implied range “11.4% – 11.7%.” The preview said management had pre-warned Q4 margin would be “softer than Q3.”

description: FY26 EBITDA margin was 12.3%, above the preview’s 11.8%–11.9% full-year guidance. This was a favorable full-year margin outcome in addition to the stronger-than-expected Q4 margin.
fact_evidence: “CACI delivered fiscal '26 … EBITDA margin of 12.3%.”
expectation_evidence: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance: “11.8% – 11.9%.”

description: FY27 revenue guidance has a $10.75 billion midpoint, modestly above the preview’s $10.67 billion Street estimate. The range also includes about $500 million of acquired revenue, so the headline growth rate includes a material acquisition contribution.
fact_evidence: “For fiscal '27, CACI guided revenue of $10.65-$10.85 billion (11.3%-13.4% growth including ~$500 million acquired revenue).”
expectation_evidence: FY27 Street revenue: “$10.67B (+11.8%).”

description: The FY27 EBITDA margin outlook in the high-12% range is above the preview’s FY26 margin baseline of 11.8%–11.9% and indicates margin expansion rather than a flat or dilutive outcome. The preview specifically identified the ARKA mix and margin bridge as an issue to assess.
fact_evidence: “For fiscal '27, CACI guided … EBITDA margins in the high 12% range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “FY27 EBITDA margin guide vs. FY26's 11.8–11.9%” and said “flat-to-down implies dilution.”

description: FY27 free cash flow guidance of at least $900 million is a strong step-up from the preview’s FY26 floor of $725 million, with management indicating roughly 22% per-share growth. However, the FY27 figure includes substantial tax-related cash benefits, including a Section 174 benefit that was larger than previously discussed.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of at least $900 million (~22% per-share growth)”; FY27 FCF “includes a delayed $40 million tax refund and a $115 million cash benefit from Section 174 R&D tax credit changes, which was larger than previously discussed due to the ARKA acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 FCF guidance as “≥ $725M” and said the FY27 FCF guide and deleveraging path were a key swing factor, but gave no FY27 FCF estimate.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: CACI accelerated its deleveraging timeline: it reduced pro forma leverage to 3.7x in one quarter and now expects to reach the low 3s by June 2027, a quarter earlier than previously communicated. The preview expected a return to the low 3s within six quarters, so the earlier timing is favorable.
fact_evidence: “Reduced pro forma leverage to 3.7x, a full turn reduction in one quarter, and now expects to reach the low 3s by June 2027, a quarter earlier than originally communicated.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management projected “4.2x net debt/EBITDA returning to ‘low threes’ within six quarters.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: FY26 book-to-bill was 1.1x, avoiding the sub-1.0x Q4 outcome the preview identified as a genuine negative signal. CACI also won more than $10 billion in awards, broadly meeting the preview’s focus on a strong year-end award quarter.
fact_evidence: “CACI won more than $10 billion in awards in fiscal '26 (book-to-bill of 1.1x).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a sub-1.0x Q4 book-to-bill would be a genuine negative signal into FY27” and tracked FY26 total awards against FY25’s “$10B.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Funded backlog grew 29% year over year, faster than the 19% growth cited in the preview’s Q3 snapshot, while total backlog grew only 2%. The funded backlog result is stronger than the prior update, but the modest total-backlog growth is a weaker headline than the preview’s latest 6% total-backlog growth figure.
fact_evidence: “Funded backlog grew 29% year-over-year while total backlog of over $32 billion grew only 2%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q3 “backlog $33.4B (+6%), funded backlog +19% (+10% organic).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bids under evaluation rose from $4 billion to nearly $11 billion, with about 75% new business. The preview anticipated $22 billion of bids to be submitted over the next two quarters, but did not flag this sharp increase in the current evaluation pipeline.
fact_evidence: “Bids under evaluation surged from $4 billion to nearly $11 billion (about 75% new business).”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$22B of bids planned across the next two quarters, ~75% new business,” but did not give an expectation for bids already under evaluation.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: CACI disclosed a separate $500 million Domestic Shield counter-drone award and export approval for most of its counter-UAS systems already delivered to 17 countries. The preview watched counter-UAS deployment and international expansion but did not anticipate these specific award and export developments.
fact_evidence: “CACI received a separate $500 million Domestic Shield counter-drone award, holds export approval for the majority of its counter-UAS systems already delivered to 17 countries.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “counter-UAS deployment detail” and “international expansion” as strategic items to watch, without quantifying an award or export approval.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The value of CACI’s OTA awards in FY26 exceeded the combined value from FY24 and FY25, an acceleration not anticipated in the preview’s strategic discussion.
fact_evidence: “Its OTA award value in fiscal '26 exceeded the combined value of fiscal '24 and '25.”

description: Revenue was $0.9 million, below the preview’s $1.1–1.4 million base case, although it rebounded from Q1’s $0.16 million. Management said deferred offshore projects contributed to the shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $0.9 million,” up $0.7 million sequentially but down $1.2 million year-over-year, “reflecting deferred offshore projects.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” revenue: “$1.1–1.4M”; the preview also said revenue of “≥ ~$1.0M” was the minimum threshold to validate the seasonal rebound.

description: The GAAP net loss widened to $11.1 million, worse than the preview’s $7.5–9.0 million modeled range. The excess loss was driven mostly by non-cash debt-extinguishment losses.
fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $11.1 million” from $9.3 million in Q1 and $7.4 million a year earlier, “driven mostly by non-cash losses on debt extinguishment.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” GAAP net loss: “($7.5–9.0M).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash was $2 million, below the preview’s expected $3–5 million and indicating greater liquidity pressure than modeled.
fact_evidence: “Cash fell sharply to $2 million at the end of Q2 2026 from $7.6 million at year-end 2025, signaling significant liquidity pressure.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash (period end)” Q2'26 base case: “$3–5M.”

description: Adjusted net loss was $7 million, slightly worse than the preview’s $5.8–6.6 million range, despite improving from $7.4 million a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net loss improved slightly to $7 million versus $7.4 million in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” adjusted net loss: “($5.8–6.6M).”

description: Operating expenses were $6.9 million, above the preview’s $5.5–5.9 million model, even though they declined year-over-year. The decrease was not enough to meet the modeled expense level.
fact_evidence: “Operating expenses declined $1.6 million year-over-year to $6.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” operating expenses: “$5.5–5.9M.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management said cautious operator spending at $55–60 oil prices would push several anticipated Gulf projects into 2027 and beyond, extending project delays beyond the quarter’s revenue shortfall.
fact_evidence: Management expects “operators' cautious spending at $55-$60 oil prices to push several anticipated Gulf projects into 2027 and beyond.”
expectation_evidence: The preview framed Q2 as the test of the seasonal-rebound story and modeled a partial revenue rebound; it did not flag several Gulf projects being pushed into 2027 or later.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: ToolKITT was formally released to energy and defense fleet operators, a product milestone, but management expects recurring, predictable revenue only starting in 2027. That falls short of the preview’s hoped-for first named licensing customer with dollars attached in the near term.
fact_evidence: “Nauticus formally released its Toolkit software for ROVs to energy and defense fleet operators,” and expects recurring, predictable revenue “starting in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a first named licensing customer with dollars attached” and described product news to date as “pre-revenue positioning.”

description: Management described a shift to acting as the primary international contractor, using fixed-price contracts and vessels of opportunity instead of long-term charter commitments. This was a new strategic approach not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: The company is “shifting to a primary contractor model internationally using fixed-price contracts and vessels of opportunity to capture autonomy-driven margins while avoiding long-term charter commitments.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management said a reverse stock split was not required to maintain the Nasdaq listing because the share price had recovered, easing a shareholder concern the preview highlighted amid the company’s recent reverse splits.
fact_evidence: Management stated “a reverse stock split is not required to maintain its NASDAQ listing given recent share price recovery.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “two reverse splits in eight months” and described the stock’s recovery off its late-July low, but did not say another split was unnecessary.

description: AMTM guided FY27 revenue growth of only 0–1%, well below the roughly 8% growth sell-side models cited in the preview. The outlook also assumes a 3% NASA headwind rather than the previously guided ~1%, with the intentional exit of low-margin programs adding another ~1% offset; the margin-accretive nature of these headwinds makes the picture mixed rather than wholly negative.
fact_evidence: “The company now expects NASA's workforce insourcing directive to reduce FY27 revenue by 3%, up from the ~1% impact guided on the prior quarter's call”; “FY27 to only 0-1% total revenue growth” as the NASA headwind and “~1% intentional exit of low-margin base operations programs largely offset mid-single-digit growth in the remaining portfolio.”
expectation_evidence: “Sell-side is modeling ~8% revenue growth” for FY27; the preview also described NASA as a “known ~1% FY27 revenue headwind.”

description: Q3 revenue was slightly below the $3.572 billion consensus, despite the preview describing the revenue bar as fair. The reported $3.5 billion included only about 1% normalized growth, with procurement delays and lower low-margin material volume cited as factors.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue reached $3.5 billion with only ~1% normalized growth, coming in slightly below expectations due to procurement delays and lower low-margin material volume.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $3.572B” consensus; “the bar on revenue is fair.”

description: Profitability substantially outperformed the preview’s estimates: adjusted EPS was $0.67 versus $0.611 consensus, while adjusted EBITDA was $290 million versus an estimated ~$279 million. The 8.3% margin also exceeded the preview’s estimated 7.8–7.9% range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% year-over-year to $290 million with record quarterly margins of 8.3%, a 60 basis point improvement, while adjusted diluted EPS grew 20% year-over-year to $0.67.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.611”; “Adj. EBITDA *(est.)* ~$279M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin *(est.)* ~7.8–7.9%.”

description: The company cut FY26 revenue guidance instead of reaffirming the range expected in the preview. The new $13.8–13.95 billion range is below the prior $13.95–14.3 billion range, with awards under protest and lower materials volume cited.
fact_evidence: “FY26 revenue guidance was lowered to $13.8-13.95 billion (citing ~$175 million from awards under protest and lower materials volume).”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 11, 2026): Revenue $13,950–14,300M”; the preview’s base case expected the “full FY26 range reaffirmed.”

description: Despite the revenue reduction, AMTM raised its FY26 adjusted EBITDA and EPS guidance, rather than merely maintaining the prior ranges. The new EPS range is $2.40–2.50 versus $2.25–2.45, and EBITDA guidance is $1.115–1.14 billion versus $1.10–1.14 billion.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $1.115-1.14 billion and adjusted EPS guidance increased to $2.40-2.50.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $1,100–1,140M” and “Adj. diluted EPS $2.25–2.45”; the preview expected the full FY26 range to be reaffirmed in its base case.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: AMTM disclosed concrete lifetime economics for the Savannah River project, whereas the preview’s base case anticipated progress without disclosed terms. The project is expected to generate over $1 billion in revenue, with potential additional economic interest in commercial operations, tokens, and electrons.
fact_evidence: “The DOE-selected Savannah River AI data center and nuclear project is expected to generate over $1 billion in revenue over its life”; there may be “additional economic interest in commercial operations, tokens, and electrons.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was SRS “progressing, no terms disclosed” and called for details on “revenue recognition timing” and project economics.

description: AMTM announced new nuclear partnerships that were not anticipated in the preview, expanding its position beyond the Savannah River project. The arrangements include a global delivery role with Rolls-Royce and a long-term alliance with Westinghouse.
fact_evidence: “The company signed strategic partnerships expanding its nuclear position, including as global delivery partner to Rolls-Royce (SMR wins in Sweden, U.K., and Czech Republic) and a long-term alliance with Westinghouse covering the AP1000 and AP300 platforms.”

description: AMTM reached 3x net leverage a quarter earlier than the preview’s year-end target, and reported substantial debt repayment during the quarter and over the trailing 12 months.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage was reduced to 3x at quarter end—one quarter earlier than the Capital Markets Day target—supported by $125 million in debt repayments during the quarter and nearly $700 million over the trailing 12 months.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management was “on track” for below 3x, or “high-2x,” leverage “by fiscal year-end.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management disclosed that 92% of anticipated FY27 revenue is already covered by existing or follow-on work, providing a specific level of revenue visibility that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 92% of anticipated FY27 revenue is already covered by existing or follow-on work.”

description: eHealth reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $21.8 million, below the preview’s base-case range of a $12 million–$16 million loss and even worse than its bear-case threshold of a $20 million loss. The operating loss was therefore materially worse than the preview’s expected range for the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss of $21.8 million (widening from a $14.1 million loss a year ago).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Adj. EBITDA: $(12)M to $(16)M”; its bear case cited “$(20)M or worse.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Medicare submissions fell 44%, worse than the preview’s watchpoint of a decline no worse than about 35%. That deeper contraction makes the volume pullback look less favorable than the preview’s hoped-for disciplined reduction.
fact_evidence: “Medicare submissions declined 44%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “submissions decline no worse than ~–35%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Unit economics weakened: MA-equivalent acquisition cost per approved member rose 16%, while Medicare Advantage LTV declined 1%. The preview was looking for LTV:CAC to hold at or above 1.3x, so these results point in the opposite direction from the expected resilience.
fact_evidence: “Total acquisition cost per MA-equivalent approved member rose 16%,” including “a 42% increase in customer care/enrollment cost per member”; “Medicare Advantage LTV declined 1%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “LTV:CAC holding ≥1.3x” and flagged LTV:CAC as a key metric.

description: The revised full-year net adjustment revenue range is $16 million–$20 million, compared with the preview’s cited $8 million–$20 million range. Although the top end is unchanged, the floor has doubled, a better outlook at the low end than the preview indicated.
fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year 2026 net adjustment revenue outlook to $16 million–$20 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited the FY26 range as “Net adjustment revenue: $8–20M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 ancillary cross-sell rates doubled year over year, and management offered a mature Medicare cross-sell target of roughly 0.5. The preview expected a first read on attach but did not anticipate this reported growth rate or the stated long-term target.
fact_evidence: “Ancillary product cross-sell rates doubled year-over-year in Q2,” and management sees “a mature Medicare cross-sell rate of roughly 0.5 as a realistic long-term target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 as “the first full quarter” for the lifetime advisory and ancillary attach read, but said “any disclosed attach rate is a new datapoint”; it gave no expected rate.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Medicare Supplement and Part D LTV rose substantially even as MA LTV slipped: Supplement was up 16% and Part D was up 52%. The preview focused on MA LTV and overall LTV:CAC and did not forecast these product-specific gains.
fact_evidence: “Medicare Supplement LTV rose 16% and Medicare Part D LTV rose 52%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half operating cash flow remained positive at $30.8 million, so the company had not yet recorded the meaningful first-half burn the preview inferred from its full-year cash-flow guidance. Q2 itself was negative $5 million, but that was far less negative than the year-earlier quarter.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow for the first six months was $30.8 million, with Q2 operating cash flow at negative $5 million, a substantial improvement from negative $41.2 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 OCF range “implies meaningful H1/H2 burn ahead.”

description: Management said Q3 marketing spend would be cut even more than the 45% year-over-year reduction in Q2, implying steeper enrollment and revenue declines. The preview anticipated a weak, back-end-loaded year but did not specifically anticipate an even deeper Q3 marketing cut.
fact_evidence: “Q3 marketing spend will be cut even more than the 45% year-over-year reduction seen in Q2, implying steeper enrollment and revenue declines, with the majority of the annual marketing budget deployed in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described 2026 as an “intentional bridge year” and said Q2–Q4 guidance was “extraordinarily back-end-loaded”; it also identified further carrier marketing pullback into AEP as a bear-case risk.

description: Q2 revenue was $481 million, far above the preview’s $402.3 million consensus and $405–415 million estimate. The result also exceeded the preview’s $425 million bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $481 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2'26 Consensus $402.3M”; “My Estimate $405–415M”; bull scenario: “Revenue | ≥$425M.”

description: Royalty revenue reached $308 million, above the preview’s roughly $280 million consensus and its $278–288 million estimate. This was a stronger result than the preview’s already favorable partner read-throughs suggested.
fact_evidence: “Royalty revenue of $308 million (up 50% YoY).”
expectation_evidence: “Royalty revenue | ~$280M (implied)”; “My Estimate $278–288M”; the preview said partner data supported royalties “at or above the high end” of that range.

description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $2.28, well above the $1.79 consensus and $1.80–1.88 estimate. That also greatly surpassed the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.95.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.28.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $1.79”; “My Estimate $1.80–1.88”; bull scenario: “Non-GAAP EPS | ≥$1.95.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $328.8 million with a margin above 65%, far above the preview’s $245–260 million estimate. This also substantially outpaced the preview’s concern that the remaining quarters required a steep EBITDA step-up.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose 46% to $328.8 million with a margin above 65%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$245M (implied)”; “My Estimate $245–260M”; the preview said the low end of full-year guidance required “~$302M/quarter for the remaining three quarters.”

description: Management raised full-year guidance beyond the level the preview expected: revenue is now $1.835–1.91 billion, royalties $1.22–1.245 billion, and EPS $8.65–9.00. The preview expected a raise to roughly $1.78–1.83 billion in revenue and an EPS floor of at least $8.00, while the prior guide was $1.710–1.810 billion revenue, $1.130–1.170 billion royalties, and $7.75–8.25 EPS.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to total revenue of $1.835-1.91 billion … royalty revenue of $1.22-1.245 billion … and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $8.65-9.00.”
expectation_evidence: “Buy-side is positioned for a raise to roughly $1.78–1.83B revenue and an $8.00+ EPS floor”; prior guidance: “Revenue $1.710–1.810B … Royalty $1.130–1.170B … Non-GAAP EPS $7.75–8.25.”

description: The preview identified four 2026 agreements and expected the Incyte upfront to land in Q3; the call reported five agreements in 2026 and $35.5 million in upfront collaboration revenue, split roughly evenly between ENHANZE and Hypercon. The reported upfront total and deal count point to more collaboration activity than the preview had identified, though the call facts do not specify which agreements contributed the upfronts.
fact_evidence: “Halozyme signed five new collaboration and licensing agreements in 2026 (four in Q2, one in July), contributing $35.5 million in upfront collaboration revenue split roughly evenly between ENHANZE and Hypercon.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Vertex, Oruka, GSK, and Incyte as deals signed in 2026, and said: “Watch for the Incyte upfront landing in Q3 rather than Q2.”

description: Royalties from the newer Opdivo SC, Ocrevus SC, and Rybrevant SC launches grew approximately 80% quarter-over-quarter, expanding the diversified royalty base to six products. The preview highlighted individual partner read-throughs but did not anticipate or quantify this combined contribution from newer launches.
fact_evidence: “Newer launch products (Opdivo SC, Ocrevus SC, Rybrevant SC) grew royalty contributions approximately 80% quarter-over-quarter, expanding the diversified royalty base to six products.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Opdivo Qvantig and Ocrevus Zunovo ramps, but gave no combined royalty-growth expectation for these newer launches.

description: Halozyme reported repurchasing $332.8 million of shares in Q2, a large portion of the $400 million full-year target already completed in one quarter. The preview flagged buyback pace as important but did not forecast this level of execution.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $332.8 million of shares in Q2 against a $400 million full-year buyback target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “$400M targeted for 2026” and that “Q2 pace tells you how management reads its own valuation,” without stating an expected quarterly amount.

description: Halozyme expanded ENHANZE into ADCs and nucleic acids and estimated that at least 100 commercial and development products could benefit. The preview discussed adding ENHANZE development programs but did not anticipate this expansion into new modality areas or the stated potential reach.
fact_evidence: “The company expanded ENHANZE into two new modality areas—ADCs and nucleic acids—via GSK and an undisclosed partner, estimating at least 100 commercial and development products could benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said nine ENHANZE products in development were “going to 13 by YE26,” but did not mention ADCs, nucleic acids, or a potential 100-product reach.

description: The call gave a specific long-term Hypercon outlook: its first two products are projected to launch in 2030–2031, with about $1 billion in royalty revenue by the mid-2030s from five to seven launches. The preview highlighted Hypercon commercialization but provided no comparable launch schedule or revenue target.
fact_evidence: “Hypercon is projected to launch its first two products in the 2030-2031 timeframe and reach approximately $1 billion in royalty revenue by the mid-2030s from an assumed five to seven launches.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Hypercon/Surf Bio commercialization” but did not state launch dates or a royalty-revenue target.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview mentioned wildfire season as a watch item but did not anticipate a Spokane-area event that left about 7,300 electric and 5,300 gas customers without service. A key transmission line has been restored and reduced the risk of capacity-related outages, though additional line and distribution damage still needs assessment.
fact_evidence: “Multiple wildfires near Spokane have left roughly 7,300 of Avista's 429,000 electric customers and about 5,300 of its 386,000 natural gas customers without service”; crews “repaired and energized a key transmission line,” though “a few transmission lines and significant distribution damage remain to be assessed.”
expectation_evidence: “Wildfire season and resiliency spend” was listed as something to watch.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Despite the fires, management said Avista facilities did not start them and estimated the infrastructure damage was far below the scale that would require securitization. Because the damaged assets are long-lived, management also expects minimal regulatory lag and may seek cost recovery from the UTC.
fact_evidence: Avista said its facilities “were not involved in starting any” of the fires; the monetary impact was “nowhere near the scale that would require securitization”; management expects “minimal regulatory lag impact” and may file a UTC cost-recovery petition.

description: The preview highlighted the possibility of resuming negotiations on the 500 MW data-center project. Instead, Avista removed it from its capital plan and paused the MOU while it works through internal processes and customer-affordability protections; management said it will proceed only if existing-customer reliability is maintained and current customers receive a net benefit.
fact_evidence: Avista “removed the 500-megawatt data center project from its capital plan and paused the MOU”; management “will not proceed with a new large data center customer unless existing customer reliability is maintained and there is a net benefit for current customers.”
expectation_evidence: “Any update on resuming negotiations is the main strategic swing factor.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: A settlement in the Washington rate case now appears difficult because of a fundamental disagreement over the four-year plan term, rather than being merely an open procedural question. Management expects a September 17–18 hearing and a mid-December commission order; it also said public counsel's return-level and power-supply-adjustment positions are the main disagreements, while staff is relatively close to Avista.
fact_evidence: Management said a settlement would be “difficult due to fundamental disagreement over the 4-year plan term”; the hearing is set for September 17–18 and the commission order is expected mid-December. Public counsel's main disagreements are the return level and power supply adjustment, while staff's position is “relatively close to the company's.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch for settlement or procedural commentary.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The nonregulated segment had a strong quarter driven by ERock going public, an investment-mark gain the preview did not anticipate specifically. Management also warned that an expected gain next quarter will likely reverse at ERock's current stock price, adding near-term earnings volatility.
fact_evidence: “The nonregulated segment delivered a strong quarter driven by an EIP investment (ERock) that went public,” but an “expected gain next quarter will likely reverse given the current ERock stock price.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the prior-year clean-tech fund losses made the comparison easy “if non-utility marks don't repeat,” and identified investment marks as the main source of headline-EPS noise.

description: Hertz reported $2.4 billion of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $2.28 billion consensus and its $2.26–$2.30 billion base case. The beat was achieved with a 1% smaller fleet, making revenue stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $2.4 billion, achieved with a 1% smaller fleet and beating both consensus and prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $2.28B” consensus; the derived base case was “$2.26–2.30B.”

description: Q2 adjusted corporate EBITDA came in just above the top of the pre-announced $50–$80 million range. That is a small upside surprise rather than the broadly expected in-range result.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted corporate EBITDA reached $81 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted Corporate EBITDA of $50–80M” was pre-announced; the scenario analysis also put the base case at “$55–75M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: RPD growth reached 9%, above the preview’s approximately 6.5% build. The stronger pricing result exceeded the expected acceleration in an already-strong metric.
fact_evidence: “RPD increased 9%,” with “U.S. airport RPD up 12%.”
expectation_evidence: The derived operating build assumed “RPD ~$59.3 (+6.5%, ‘accelerating above Q1’s +5.5%).’”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Utilization was 79%, materially below the preview’s 82–84% base case. The reported 80-basis-point year-over-year improvement did not prevent utilization from missing that expected level.
fact_evidence: “Total fleet utilization improved 80 basis points to 79%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s utilization base case was “82–84%.”

description: Q3 EBITDA guidance of $275–$325 million is above the preview’s modeled $250–$300 million range. The outlook therefore points to a stronger next quarter than the preview’s base case expected.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects adjusted corporate EBITDA of $275-$325 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview scenario analysis modeled “Q3 $250–300M.”

description: Q3 net DPU guidance of $285–$295 is below the preview’s expected $290–$305 range, suggesting a somewhat better unit-cost trajectory than anticipated. The range also keeps Q3 DPU below $300, which the preview identified as a positive surprise threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects … net DPU of $285-$295.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 DPU guided $290–305”; it also said “any number starting with a ‘2’ is a positive shock.”

description: The reported full-year EBITDA range of $225–$275 million is stronger than the preview’s modeled outcome of roughly $35–$250 million and its expectation that guidance might be cut to around a 1–3% margin. The range’s lower end is still not an unambiguous confirmation of the original 3–6% margin framing.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for adjusted corporate EBITDA of $225-$275 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a realistic H2 implied FY26 EBITDA of “roughly $35–250M,” and its base case expected the margin guide to be “cut/narrowed to ~1–3%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Pro forma liquidity after the financing was only slightly above $1 billion, well short of the preview’s roughly $1.35 billion expectation. Separately, the year-end liquidity outlook was reduced from about $1.5 billion to $1.0–$1.4 billion after excluding ATM proceeds.
fact_evidence: The company had “$984 million in liquidity” at Q2 end; after the notes and greenshoe, pro forma liquidity was “slightly above $1 billion.” Full-year guidance gave “year-end liquidity of $1.0-$1.4 billion (lowered from ~$1.5 billion after removing ATM proceeds).”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Q2-end liquidity vs. ~$1.0B + $350M” and flagged “Q2-end liquidity vs. ~$1.35B pro forma”; it also cited year-end guidance of “>$1.5B.”

description: The call disclosed that Oro is expected to generate more than $600 million in revenue this year and gave a later-this-year launch window for its Lucid/Nuro AV partnership. The preview identified Oro as an important potential value driver and sought economic details, but did not anticipate these specific disclosures.
fact_evidence: “The Oro mobility platform … is expected to generate more than $600 million in revenue this year,” with an AV partnership “launching in the San Francisco Bay Area later this year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said that “any disclosed economics, contracted volume, or separate-capitalization commentary” on Oro would be a meaningful vector.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Hertz said RPU reached $1,542, surpassing its $1,500 North Star target. This is a positive target overrun that was not quantified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “RPU rose 8% to $1,542, surpassing the $1,500 North Star target.”
expectation_evidence: The call identified a “$1,500 North Star target.”

description: The company reaffirmed its roughly $1 billion 2027 EBITDA target, as the preview expected, but also stated that it expects its first full year of positive net income and free cash flow in 2027—an additional favorable outlook not specified in the preview.
fact_evidence: Hertz was “reaffirming the ~$1 billion EBITDA target and first full-year net income and free-cash-flow positivity for 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview treated the “2027 $1B EBITDA target” as a key question and said dropping it would be a bear signal; it did not give an expectation for 2027 net income or free cash flow.

description: WLDN reported net revenue of $117 million, about 14% above the $102.27 million consensus estimate, while contract revenue reached $231 million. The preview expected only about $180–190 million of contract revenue and modeled net revenue growth of 7.7%, versus the reported 23% growth.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue up 23% to $117 million” and “contract revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $231 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenue… $102.27M”; “Contract revenue (est.): ~$180–190M”; implied net revenue growth of “+7.7%.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $33 million, well above the preview’s derived estimate of about $23–25 million, and the 28.2% margin on net revenue substantially exceeded the roughly 24% Q2 run rate the preview said was needed. The reported margin was also the highest in WLDN’s history.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 51% to a record $33 million, achieving a record 28.2% adjusted EBITDA margin on net revenue—the highest quarterly margin in company history.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived) ~$23–25M”; “Q2 needs ~24%” adjusted EBITDA margin.

description: Adjusted EPS reached $2.07, far above the $1.30 consensus estimate and the preview’s expectation of a year-over-year decline. The $5.3 million tax benefit aided the reported EPS, although pre-tax income also rose 88%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 38% to $2.07, aided by a $5.3 million tax benefit that pushed pre-tax income up 88% to $19.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $1.30” and implied year-over-year change of “-13.3%.”

description: WLDN raised its full-year 2026 guidance rather than merely reaffirming the prior range the preview considered sufficient. The revised ranges are higher by $5 million at both ends for net revenue, $3 million at the low end and $2 million at the high end for adjusted EBITDA, and $0.10 for adjusted EPS.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net revenue of $415–430 million, adjusted EBITDA of $103–107 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $5.00–5.15.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “clean reaffirm of $410–425M / $100–105M / $4.90–5.05” could be sufficient and identified guidance action as the key metric.

description: WLDN reported a 150-basis-point decline in gross margin, despite the unexpectedly high adjusted EBITDA margin. The preview highlighted Q1 gross-margin improvement but did not anticipate a Q2 decline attributed to a change in project mix.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 150 basis points in Q2 due to a mix shift toward performance engineering and commercial projects carrying heavier equipment and subcontractor loads.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 delivered 40.7% gross margin (vs 37.8% LY)” and focused on Q2 EBITDA margin, without flagging an expected gross-margin decline.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: WLDN disclosed $110 million of new LADWP work plus two other sizable contract wins, totaling $212 million in awards. The preview discussed the existing LADWP contract and prior wins, but did not anticipate this new set of awards.
fact_evidence: “Notable new contract wins since the last call include a $110 million LADWP solar streetlight expansion (half already authorized), a $53 million City College of New York plant upgrade, and a $49 million five-year SoCalREN contract.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$214M of wins… at Q1, plus the $31M Encina cogeneration award” and said the market wanted “named or quantified new bookings.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: WLDN reported net debt of 0.3x trailing EBITDA, below the 0.6x leverage level the preview cited after the Burton acquisition. This leaves the company with less leverage than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The balance sheet carries only $33 million net debt (0.3x trailing EBITDA) with $165 million in total liquidity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the Burton transaction took leverage “to 0.6x net debt / TTM EBITDA.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: WLDN cited $34 million of deferred tax assets, above the $28 million cushion described in the preview, and said they survive the 179D provision’s sunset. That is a larger stated tax asset cushion than investors were told to expect.
fact_evidence: “Targeting over 70% conversion of adjusted EBITDA to free cash flow, aided by $34 million in deferred tax assets that survive the June 2025 sunset of the 179D provision.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$28M of deferred tax assets expected to offset liabilities well into 2027 and beyond.”

description: The preview expected servicing to return to profitability or at least improve as runoff eased. Instead, servicing adjusted pretax income fell more than 60% year over year, with MSR runoff nearly 80% higher than a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Servicing adjusted pretax income declined over 60% year-over-year as lower interest rates drove MSR runoff up nearly 80% versus the prior year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Servicing back to +$25M” in its bull case and said the base case had “Servicing profitable but subdued”; it also expected runoff to improve as rates rose.

description: Management pointed to an adjusted pretax ROE operating level around 9%, below the preview’s 10% low end, and directed investors to the low end of the range. The preview said a result materially below its roughly $20 million adjusted pretax-income threshold would put the guidance at risk, although its base case already allowed for a low-end posture.
fact_evidence: “The company lowered expectations, guiding to the low end of its full-year 2026 adjusted pretax ROE range of 10% to 15%, currently operating around the 9% range.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ≥ ~$20M adjusted pretax income for the low end of guidance to remain credible”; the base case anticipated guidance “reaffirmed but explicitly ‘low end.’”

description: The preview highlighted pressure on origination margins and hedge effectiveness, but reported origination adjusted pretax income grew more than threefold year over year on record funded volume. The call attributed the volume chiefly to B2B correspondent and co-issue, though it did not provide margin figures to show whether the preview’s margin concerns eased.
fact_evidence: “Origination adjusted pretax income grew over 3x year-over-year on record funded volume of $15.5 billion (up 64% YoY), driven primarily by the B2B correspondent and co-issue channel.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Originations margin, not volume” was the key issue, describing “hedge effectiveness and loan sale margins” as pressured.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Servicing portfolio growth was stronger than the preview’s H1 subservicing target: first-half subservicing additions exceeded $28 billion, while total servicing UPB also grew faster than the industry despite planned transfers and client sales. This supports the growth-engine thesis more strongly than the preview’s target alone implied.
fact_evidence: “First-half subservicing additions of $35 billion exceeded guidance”; “Total servicing UPB grew 10% year-over-year versus industry growth of 3%, with servicing additions net of runoff of $76 billion despite planned Rithm transfers and client MSR sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Subservicing additions vs. the $28B H1 target” as a key metric and said Q1 had delivered $28B of total servicing additions.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview anticipated a GAAP gain from the reverse-mortgage sale, while the reported quarter included a net loss and about $33 million of pretax costs tied collectively to the reverse asset sale, legacy subservicing transfer, and unfavorable fair-value adjustments. The call also reported a $12 million unfavorable reverse-MSR fair-value swing, rather than a clearly favorable quarter-end effect from the exit.
fact_evidence: “Onity reported a Q2 2026 net loss that included approximately $33 million of pretax costs from the Finance of America reverse asset sale, legacy subservicing transfer to Rithm, and unfavorable market-driven asset fair value adjustments”; the reverse portfolio had “a $12 million net unfavorable fair value swing in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FAR sale closed inside the quarter and that “Any book gain lands in GAAP but should be excluded from adjusted.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview emphasized rising rates and the risk of weaker refinance activity, but Onity reported better refinance recapture and rapid growth in home-equity lending. These call metrics were not specifically anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Refinance recapture rate improved to 51%, up 3 percentage points year-over-year, exceeding the ICE industry average, with home equity product volume doubling and second lien volume more than doubling (over $70 million funded) year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described rising rates as potentially having “crushed refi volume” and framed the quarter as a possible “worst-of-both-worlds crossover.”

description: KULR reported Q2 revenue of $2.1 million, far below the preview’s $5.5 million estimate and the cited $8.5–9.0 million consensus range. Revenue also fell from both Q1 and the year-earlier quarter, rather than coming in roughly flat to modestly higher sequentially.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $2.1 million, down significantly from both the prior year and Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … My estimate: $5.5M”; “Consensus … ~$8.5–9.0M”; and the base case expected “sequential revenue roughly flat-to-up modestly.”

description: Instead of holding gross margin in the preview’s expected 25–28% range, KULR reported a gross loss. That is a major reversal from the preview’s key test of whether Q1’s 29% margin could be sustained.
fact_evidence: “The quarter produced a gross loss, missing management's expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My estimate: 25–28%”; the preview called for margin to “hold mid-to-high 20s” in the base case.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management said supply-chain bottlenecks and long lead times delayed planned Q2 battery shipments, whereas the preview expected a modest sequential revenue increase and described the Q3 production ramp as on track. Management expects the delayed shipments to recover in the second half, but that recovery was not yet reflected in Q2.
fact_evidence: “New program supply chain bottlenecks and long lead times delayed planned Q2 battery shipments, which management expects to recover in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “sequential revenue roughly flat-to-up modestly” and the ramp to be “on track for Q3”; the preview said any line-start slip would directly affect the second-half revenue ramp.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: KULR disclosed that it had secured a defense drone battery opportunity exceeding $5 million, alongside Q2 orders from two new customers using new battery configurations. The preview identified defense and UAV programs as possible catalysts, but did not anticipate this specific opportunity or its stated size.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was driven principally by two large orders from new customers involving new battery configurations, and the company secured a defense drone battery opportunity exceeding $5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said defense/UAV programs might “convert to shipped revenue” in its bull case, but gave no expectation of a secured opportunity exceeding $5 million.

description: The Board authorized management to sell any or all remaining Bitcoin, indicating a move toward full divestment rather than merely using some Bitcoin to repay the Coinbase facility. The preview treated the longer-term treasury policy as unresolved and asked whether Bitcoin would remain a funding reserve or strategic holding.
fact_evidence: “The Board authorized management to sell any and all remaining Bitcoin holdings, signaling a full divestment of the crypto treasury to focus on the operating business.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the treasury was “now a funding reserve to be drawn down, or still a strategic hold” and said a clear “no new BTC purchases with cash” reaffirmation would remove an overhang.

description: Qualys raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $732–738 million, above the preview’s expected base-case raise to roughly $726–729 million and even above its bull-case threshold of $729 million. The increase is positive, though the gap is modest relative to the forecast.
fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $732–738 million from prior $721–727 million.
expectation_evidence: “FY26 raised to ~$726–729M” in the base case; the bull case called for “FY26 revenue raised to $729M+.”

description: Q2 revenue came in above both the roughly $178.7 million consensus and the preview’s estimate of a normal Qualys beat at about $180.5–182 million. At $182.2 million, it reached the preview’s bull-case revenue level.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $182.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “~$178.7M,” and said a “normal” quarter produces “~$180.5–182M”; its bull case was “$182M+.”

description: Q2 EPS of $1.98 exceeded the preview’s functional buy-side bar of roughly $1.88–1.95, although it was just below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $2.00. This was a modest positive surprise rather than an outsized beat.
fact_evidence: “EPS was $1.98.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Treat the functional buy-side bar as ~$1.88–$1.95”; its bull case was “$2.00+.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
