description: iGaming share stabilized after several quarters of losses, rather than continuing the slippage the preview identified as a key concern. Management credited the Lightning Link and Flex Spins launches.
fact_evidence: “iGaming share stabilized after several quarters of losses, aided by the Lightning Link and Flex Spins launches.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s key metrics included “iGaming/iCasino share” and noted, “DB flagged slippage.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Combos already account for nearly 20% of Predictions volume, an adoption milestone that took years to reach in Sportsbook. The preview did not call out this level of product mix or adoption.
fact_evidence: “Combos already represent nearly 20% of Predictions volume, a milestone that took years to reach in Sportsbook.”

description: RCAT reported Q2 revenue of $20.2 million, below the preview’s $22.3 million Zacks estimate and $22.65 million broader Street estimate. The result was also below the preview’s $21–24 million base-case range, despite strong year-over-year growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $20.2 million” and was “up approximately 30% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$22.3M (Zacks) / $22.65M (broader street)”; the base scenario projected “$21–24M.”

description: Gross margin was 16.1%, below the preview’s expected range of roughly 18–22% and below the 18% level the preview said was needed to keep the year-end margin path credible. Management nevertheless continued to target 30% gross margin by year-end.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 16.1% in Q2”; management “targets 30% gross margin by the end of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~18–22%” and said “Anything below ~18% and the year-end 30% target is functionally withdrawn.”

description: Operating expenses were about $41.9 million, substantially above the preview’s expectation of roughly $30 million or more. R&D alone was $14.2 million, roughly double sequentially, pointing to heavier spending and losses than the preview’s operating-cost assumptions implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 operating expenses totaled approximately $41.9 million, including R&D of $14.2 million (roughly double sequentially).”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 “Opex” at “~$30M+” and discussed an operating-loss model assuming opex “near $29–30M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Blue Ops generated its first revenue from Variant 7 and moved the vessel into mass production, whereas the preview expected USV revenue in Q2 to be “likely near zero.” Management also said fewer than 10 boats could make the division profitable if Q4 internal targets are met.
fact_evidence: “Blue Ops moved its Variant 7 uncrewed surface vessel into mass production and received first revenue”; management said “fewer than 10 boats would make the division profitable if Q4 internal targets are met.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 USV revenue was “likely near zero” and called the segment the “newest, least-proven” part of the annual revenue bridge.

description: The Drone Dominance Program now has a stated potential to contribute $14–28 million in Q3 revenue, adding a specific near-term revenue opportunity the preview did not quantify. The preview noted Gauntlet II as a future catalyst but said it would not fix the H2 revenue bridge.
fact_evidence: “The Drone Dominance Program could contribute $14 million to $28 million in Q3 revenue alone,” and the company “advanced to Gauntlet II.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Gauntlet II as a “future catalyst” and said it “doesn't fix H2 revenue”; it gave no Q3 revenue estimate for the program.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended June at $325.6 million, above the preview’s expected quarter-end range of $290–310 million. That leaves the company with more liquidity than anticipated, though the facts do not identify how much of the difference came from operating cash flow.
fact_evidence: “The company holds $325.6 million in cash as of June 30, 2026,” with working capital of “about $396.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “should end near $290–310M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory including prepaid inventory rose to about $84.8 million from $30.4 million at year-end, a substantial build not specifically forecast in the preview. Management said $50–80 million of Black Widows and Hellcats could ship immediately if orders materialize, making the build both a working-capital exposure and potential near-term delivery capacity.
fact_evidence: “Inventory including prepaid inventory grew to about $84.8 million from $30.4 million at year-end,” and “$50–80 million of Black Widows and Hellcats could ship immediately if orders materialize.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The customer mix was less dependent on the Army than the preview’s discussion of the Black Widow pipeline and Army contract timing might suggest: Army represented roughly 50% of first-half revenue, while Japan and Europe’s NSPA were the second- and third-largest customers. Revenue nevertheless remained concentrated in the Teal/Black Widow line.
fact_evidence: “Army dependence fell to roughly 50% of first-half revenue from 73% in 2025, with Japan and Europe's NSPA now the #2 and #3 customers”; revenue “remains concentrated in the Teal/Black Widow drone line.”

description: The preview expected new-issue and advisory revenue to hold near or above Q1’s $45.7 million. It reached $54 million, driven primarily by SPAC M&A and IPO transactions.
fact_evidence: “Investment banking and new issue revenue reached $54 million,” up from $45.7 million in the prior quarter, “driven primarily by SPAC M&A and SPAC IPO transactions.”
expectation_evidence: “New issue & advisory holds near or above the $45.7M Q1 run-rate”; the line to watch was new issue and advisory “vs. $45.7M (Q1 26).”

description: The preview’s base case expected adjusted pre-tax income per diluted share below Q2 2025’s $0.94. Adjusted pretax income instead rose to $10.1 million; using the reported 7.4 million fully diluted shares as an approximate denominator implies about $1.36 per share, although the call facts do not report that per-share figure directly.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted pretax income surged to $10.1 million,” more than doubling from $4 million in the prior quarter. The call also reported 7.4 million fully diluted shares outstanding on an as-if-converted basis.
expectation_evidence: “Base: ... adjusted pre-tax per diluted share below the $0.94 of Q2 2025.”

description: The preview flagged affiliate losses as a risk but cited a Q1 loss of $527,000; the reported loss from equity method affiliates widened to $3 million before a credit reduced the net loss to $900,000. That was a larger drag than the preview’s scenario of a small principal-transactions impact from the BRR mark suggested.
fact_evidence: “Loss from equity method affiliates widened to $3 million,” largely from Columbus Circle Capital II; a “$2.1 million offsetting credit reduced the net loss to $900,000” tied to forfeited placement units.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed equity-method affiliates as a line to watch, citing “$(527)K Q1 loss,” and described its base case as having “a small principal-transactions drag from the BRR mark.”

description: Revenue of $365.4 million exceeded the preview’s highest cited consensus estimate of $361.8 million, though it was within the preview’s base-case range of $360–366 million. The beat over the top of the published consensus range was small.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 31.3% year-over-year to $365.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus … $353.3M … $360.1M … $361.8M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA of $54.7 million came in above the preview’s roughly $50 million consensus and its $50–52 million base-case range. This was a meaningful beat relative to the expected level.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 30% to $54.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$50M”; the base case anticipated “EBITDA ~$50–52M.”

description: Diluted EPS of $0.19 topped the preview’s highest cited consensus estimate of $0.18, a modest beat.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS grew to $0.19 from $0.16.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS … $0.17 (Zacks) / $0.18 (StockStory, GAAP) / $0.14 (GuruFocus).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: After the post-quarter food-safety concerns, same-restaurant sales recovered sequentially each week to mid-single-digit growth. That recovery was better than the preview’s base case of Q3-to-date traffic being down mid-single digits, although the preview had anticipated sequential improvement.
fact_evidence: “Same-restaurant sales dipped to flat-to-positive amid cyclospora food safety concerns after quarter-end but have since recovered sequentially each week to mid-single digits.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “Q3 QTD down mid-single-digit traffic” with “sequential improvement cited.”

description: Restaurant-level margin was 25.7%, just below the preview’s base-case range of 25.8%–26.3%. It did clear the preview’s 25.5% watch threshold, so the shortfall from the base case was small.
fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level profit was $93.8 million (25.7% of revenue), down 60 basis points from 26.3% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “RLP ~25.8–26.3%”; the checklist watched for “RLP margin ≥25.5%.”

description: Management flagged additional back-half margin pressures from fuel surcharges and the premarinated chicken rollout, and called out a roughly 300-basis-point typical Q3-to-Q4 seasonal margin decline. The preview discussed salmon, energy, and wage costs but did not anticipate these specific pressures or the seasonal decline.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged margin headwinds in the back half from fuel surcharges and the premarinated chicken rollout, plus roughly 300 basis points of typical Q3-to-Q4 seasonal margin decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “salmon … ~100bp headwind through Q4,” “energy 20–40bp,” and wage investment as margin considerations.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: CAVA opened 17 net new restaurants, slightly below the preview’s estimate of roughly 18–19 for the quarter. The gap was small, and full-year opening guidance was unchanged.
fact_evidence: “The company opened 17 net new restaurants, ending the quarter with 476 locations.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a “fairly ratable” cadence implying “~18–19 openings, ~477 units.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New-restaurant productivity exceeded 100% as expected, but the 2024 cohort’s double-digit same-restaurant sales and status as the portfolio’s highest-performing vintage were not anticipated. Systemwide AUV also reached $3.1 million versus the preview’s expectation of about $3.0 million.
fact_evidence: “New restaurant productivity remained above 100% across all geographies and formats, with the 2024 cohort delivering double-digit same-restaurant sales as the highest-performing vintage in the portfolio, lifting systemwide AUV to $3.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “new-class productivity >100% and AUV holding ~$3.0M.”

description: The Multi-Platform Group produced $59 million of adjusted EBITDA, down from $96 million a year earlier, and its implied margin was about 11%. That fell well short of the preview’s 15% recovery threshold and points to weaker profitability than expected, even though the decline was attributed largely to non-cash co-marketing expenses.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA dropped sharply to $59 million from $96 million, largely due to non-cash co-marketing expenses”; revenue was $536 million.
expectation_evidence: “Multiplatform margin compression from 14%-ish to 9.5% is the underappreciated problem”; “Sub-15% would signal the cost programs aren't landing where they need to.”

description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance has a $200 million midpoint, below the roughly $230 million the preview said was needed to keep the $800 million full-year target on track with a normal Q4 skew. The full-year target was reaffirmed, but this Q3 range leaves the H2 bridge more demanding.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $180-220 million”; full-year guidance was reaffirmed at $800 million.
expectation_evidence: “To keep $800M alive with a normal Q4 skew, Q3 needs to guide to roughly $230M+”; the base scenario anticipated Q3 guidance of “$205–225M.”

description: Multi-Platform Group revenue declined 1.6%, missing the preview’s approximately flat Q2 expectation. The shortfall was modest, but it adds to the segment’s weaker-than-expected performance.
fact_evidence: “The Multi-Platform Group's revenue fell 1.6% to $536 million (below approximately flat guidance).”
expectation_evidence: “Multiplatform Group ~Flat” for Q2.

description: Consolidated revenue of $977 million was above the preview’s roughly $969 million consensus and its approximately $972 million bottom-up estimate. The beat was modest, while growth excluding political revenue was 3.5%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $977 million, up 4.7% year-over-year (up 3.5% excluding political).”
expectation_evidence: “Consolidated revenue | ~$969M (+3.8% cons.)”; the bottom-up estimate was “~$972M (+4.1%).”

description: Digital Audio Group revenue grew 12.4%, ahead of the preview’s approximately 10% growth estimate. This was a modest upside to an already strong expected result.
fact_evidence: “The Digital Audio Group generated $364 million in revenue (up 12.4%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview derived Digital Audio Group revenue of “~$357M” from management’s guidance of “~+10%.”

description: Management described a potentially presidential-cycle-sized midterm political year, but the reported update did not provide the quantified Q3/Q4 political bookings or pacing the preview identified as needed to support the H2 ramp. The outlook therefore remained more aspirational than the concrete de-risking detail the preview sought.
fact_evidence: “The company expects a robust midterm political year potentially rivaling a presidential cycle.”
expectation_evidence: “Political dollars must show up as booked revenue with specific Q3/Q4 pacing, not aspiration”; “hand-waving would not” materially de-risk the H2 bridge.

description: Instead of raising or maintaining adjusted EPS guidance, Maximus cut its FY26 midpoint by about $0.35 to $8.05 after a customer-directed pause in VA MDE performance incentives. The pause is assumed to last through at least December 31, with no incentives expected in Q1 FY27.
fact_evidence: “A customer-directed pause in VA MDE performance incentives, effective July 1, 2026, cut full-year diluted EPS guidance by roughly $0.35, lowering the midpoint to $8.05 from $8.40”; the pause is assumed to continue through at least December 31, 2026, with no incentives expected in Q1 fiscal 2027.
expectation_evidence: The preview called a third EPS-guidance raise “the single cleanest bull signal” and said a maintain “would be read as the margin story stalling out”; it listed FY26 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $8.25–$8.55.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow guidance was cut despite the preview already highlighting the risk from weak first-half cash generation. Q3 free cash flow was an outflow and DSO reached 98 days, above the preview’s stated 78-day level to watch at quarter-end.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was reduced to $425-475 million,” and Q3 had “a free cash flow outflow of $137 million with DSO elevated at 98 days due to a major federal customer's administrative delays.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the $450–500M guide required $520–570M of second-half cash flow and that “DSO ≥78 days would put the $450–500M guide in question”; it also anticipated Q3 FCF “may still be unimpressive.”

description: The quarter’s adjusted EBITDA margin substantially exceeded the preview estimate, and the call attributed the improvement to efficiency gains rather than unusually high volumes. This is stronger than the already-expected margin improvement.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 15.0% from 14.7%, driven by efficiency gains rather than surge volumes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin at “~14.2–14.4% (est.).”

description: Management said a roughly 13% Q4 EBITDA margin is a reasonable near-term run rate, a weaker near-term earnings profile than the preview’s expectation that Q4 revenue and earnings would run a little higher sequentially.
fact_evidence: Management “flagged the ~13% Q4 EBITDA margin as a reasonable near-term run rate.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had indicated “Q4 revenue and earnings should run ‘a little higher sequentially’ than Q3.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Awarded-but-unsigned contracts rose sharply even though book-to-bill remained weak, providing a more constructive awards signal than the preview’s prior-quarter figure suggested. These wins are longer-term recompetes, so they do not remove the low book-to-bill concern.
fact_evidence: “Awarded-but-unsigned contracts stepped up significantly to $1.35 billion, driven by longer-term recompete wins,” while trailing-12-month book-to-bill was about 0.5x.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$322M awarded-but-unsigned” and framed sub-1.0x book-to-bill as a growth-credibility concern.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Collections from the delayed federal customer had already accelerated after quarter-end, giving more immediate support to the expected year-end DSO improvement than the preview’s account of elevated collections risk suggested.
fact_evidence: “Collections from the delayed federal customer accelerated with about $245 million received since June 30,” supporting expectations that DSO will finish the fiscal year below 70 days.
expectation_evidence: The preview said DSO would “stay elevated through June 30” and only drop below 70 days by fiscal year-end, with the FCF guide relying on Q4 collections.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage rose from the preview’s 1.8x figure to 2.0x after Maximus raised $325 million in Term Loan B. It remains within the company’s stated target range, but the higher leverage was not part of the preview’s setup.
fact_evidence: “Total debt rose to $1.65 billion with a net leverage ratio of 2.0x (up from 1.8x), still within the stated 2x-3x target range, after raising $325 million in Term Loan B.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net leverage | 1.8x net debt/EBITDA.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call gave new evidence of AI adoption and operational benefit: most new bids and rebids now have explicit AI requirements, and AI process improvements were associated with a measurable margin gain across five contracts. The preview expected AI-related efficiency gains broadly, but did not anticipate these specific figures.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 75-80% of new bids and rebids now include explicit AI requirements,” and AI-based process improvements across five contracts “delivered a 3.5% operating margin improvement for that group.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “AI/automation margin capture” and technology-driven margin improvement, but did not give a bid-coverage or contract-level result expectation.

description: Auryxia revenue was $25.5 million, below the preview’s $30 million estimate and just below its stated $26 million downside threshold for a more severe erosion signal.
fact_evidence: “Auryxia revenue dropped to $25.5 million from $47.2 million due to generic competition.”
expectation_evidence: “Auryxia net product rev … $30.0M”; the preview said “below $26M reframes FY2026 down materially.”

description: Total revenue was $49.1 million, about $2.9 million below the roughly $52.0 million consensus estimate, despite Vafseo coming in above the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total revenues fell to $49.1 million in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … ~$52.0M” consensus; the base case was “~$52.0M.”

description: The preview expected a net loss of about $10 million, while the reported loss was $8.9 million, a modestly better result. This included a $1.9 million commercial reorganization expense that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “The company swung to a net loss of $8.9 million … including a $1.9 million commercial reorganization expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Net loss / EPS … $(10.0)M / $(0.04).”

description: Vafseo revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s estimate: $21.3 million versus $20.5 million, or about 4% higher.
fact_evidence: “Vafseo net product revenue reached $21.3 million in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Vafseo net product rev … $20.5M” in the segment build; the preview also watched for revenue of “~$20M+.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash was higher than the preview’s expected range, at $155.5 million versus an estimated $143–148 million. The stated two-year runway, however, assumes the planned term-loan refinancing.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were approximately $155.5 million … which management believes funds operations for at least two years assuming a planned refinancing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 cash at “~$143–148M” and said management had committed to “>2 years” of cash runway.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: First-refill adherence reached about 89%, above the preview’s roughly 86% figure.
fact_evidence: “First-refill adherence has reached about 89%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “first-refill adherence (~86%).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: About one-quarter of previously discontinued QD patients had restarted therapy, a positive retention or reactivation result the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 25% of previously discontinued QD patients have restarted therapy.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: DaVita had not yet produced a meaningful adoption inflection, even though it represents 200,000 patients. The rollout of a three-times-weekly protocol and management’s expectation for growth into 2027 temper the near-term disappointment.
fact_evidence: “DaVita, representing 200,000 patients, has not yet shown a meaningful adoption inflection” but rolled out a dosing protocol in early June, with management expecting growth into 2027.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Vafseo’s Q1 inflection needed to prove structural and highlighted the need for updates on “large dialysis organizations (DaVita, Fresenius)” and post-TDAPA contracting.

description: Teradata reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.69, far above the preview’s $0.55–$0.56 consensus and the $0.57 top of its guidance. The call attributed the beat primarily to higher recurring revenue.
fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.69, beating the top end of guidance by $0.12, driven primarily by higher recurring revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | Q2'26 Consensus: ~$0.55–0.56”; company guide: “$0.53–$0.57.”

description: Recurring revenue grew 3% to $363 million, well above the preview’s expectation of roughly flat growth and the company’s guidance range. The beat was partly timing-driven, and management said revenue recognition shifted into the first half under ASC 606, alongside guiding to a Q3 recurring-revenue decline.
fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue grew 3% year-over-year to $363 million, marking the third consecutive quarter of positive growth and coming in 3 points above the high end of guidance due to timing of on-premise revenue recognition”; Q3 recurring revenue was guided to “decline 4% to 2% year-over-year,” reflecting revenue recognition shifted into the first half under ASC 606.
expectation_evidence: “So a print of ‘recurring roughly flat y/y’ is expected, not a disappointment.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Cloud ARR grew only 8% as reported, below the preview’s 12%–13% growth bogey and its $710–$720 million expected range. This fell short of the preview’s most closely watched growth metric.
fact_evidence: “Cloud ARR grew 8% as reported (9% in constant currency), coming in below the low-double-digit cloud growth target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Public cloud ARR: ~$710–720M” and “12% to 13% y/y”; its catalyst checklist highlighted “Public cloud ARR ≥$710M with a ≥$25M sequential add.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Total ARR grew 1% as reported, below the preview’s roughly 2%–3% implied Q2 growth bogey, although constant-currency growth was 2%. The company nevertheless reaffirmed its full-year ARR outlook.
fact_evidence: “Total ARR grew only 1% as reported (2% in constant currency).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 total ARR needed to be “~$1.52–1.535B” to keep the FY26 outlook credible and described the implied growth as “+2% to +3%.”

description: Teradata raised FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.65–$2.73, above the preview’s cited prior range of $2.55–$2.65. The upper end moved up by $0.08.
fact_evidence: “Teradata raised its FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.65-$2.73.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FY26 non-GAAP EPS of $2.55–2.65” and described a raise “above $2.65” as a bull-case outcome.

description: Adjusted free cash flow guidance rose to $330–$350 million from the $320–$340 million range the preview expected. Q2 cash generation was also stronger than the preview’s back-loaded setup suggested.
fact_evidence: “[Teradata] increased its adjusted free cash flow range to $330-$350 million”; “Adjusted free cash flow was $127 million in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 adjusted FCF guidance of “$320–340M” and noted “Q1 adjusted FCF was only $31M, so 2H is heavily back-loaded.”

description: Consulting services revenue fell 24% to $39 million, a steeper decline than the 14% Q1 decline cited in the preview and weaker than its identified stabilization upside. Management pointed to improving bookings and backlog, but the reported revenue decline remained pronounced.
fact_evidence: “Consulting services revenue fell 24% year-over-year to $39 million,” while management cited “improving bookings and a growing project backlog.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported consulting “Down 14% y/y in Q1'26” and said “Stabilization here is a quiet upside lever; continued double-digit decline caps the total-revenue line.”

description: ECPG raised full-year EPS guidance from $13.00 to a $13–$14 range. The $13.50 midpoint meets the preview’s bullish threshold, though the lower end is below the $13.50+ level it identified as the clearest positive signal.
fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $13-$14 per share.
expectation_evidence: The preview said a raise to “$13.50+” would be bullish, while its base case was “reaffirmed at $13.00 or nudged to $13.25.”

description: Q2 GAAP EPS of $2.81 beat the $2.67 consensus but fell short of the preview’s $3.05 base estimate and guidance-implied run rate. The gap came with an unanticipated $30.5 million pretax refinancing charge that reduced EPS by $1 per share.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP net income was $64 million, or $2.81 per share,” including “a $30.5 million pretax refinancing charge that reduced EPS by $1 per share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$2.67” Q2 EPS consensus and a “$3.05” base estimate, and said consensus was “~10-14% below the company's own guidance-implied run rate.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Portfolio purchases substantially exceeded the preview’s expected $350–$380 million range: ECPG bought $444 million, including a record $372 million in the U.S. That U.S. amount also exceeded the preview’s $340 million bull-case marker.
fact_evidence: “Global portfolio purchases totaled $444 million, with a record $372 million in the U.S., representing 84% of purchasing dollars amid favorable U.S. market conditions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$350–380M” in global purchases and said U.S. purchases of “$340M” or more would fit its bull case.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Changes in recoveries were $71 million, above the preview’s roughly $45 million base-case expectation and its $60 million bull-case marker. Most was collections already above forecast, rather than future-period revaluation, making the result more cash-driven than the preview’s key quality-of-earnings debate feared.
fact_evidence: “Changes in recoveries totaled $71 million, including $53 million of collections above forecast (incremental cash) and $18 million in raised future recovery expectations, driven by strong 2024-2025 vintage performance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected changes in recoveries to be “moderate to ~$45M”; its bull case specified “$60M+.” It also emphasized distinguishing “cash collections vs. changes in expected recoveries.”

description: The full-year collections outlook moved above the preview’s existing approximately $2.8 billion guide, with the new range extending to $2.85 billion on reported operational overperformance.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 collections guidance was raised to $2.8-$2.85 billion, reflecting operational overperformance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed current FY2026 collections guidance as “~$2.8B.”

description: The refinancing produced expected annualized interest savings of roughly $15 million, a positive outcome against the preview’s concern that interest expense could step up after debt issuance.
fact_evidence: ECPG refinanced $1 billion of debt by issuing “$750 million of 2032 high-yield notes and EUR 325 million of 2033 floating rate notes,” and expects “roughly $15 million in annualized interest savings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch the interest expense line against the ~$300M FY guide” and flagged that “interest expense steps up post-$325M issuance” as a bear-case risk.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ARR grew 6%—about 7% excluding FX—well below the preview’s roughly 9% expectation. Dollar-based net revenue retention also came in at 102.4% (about 104% excluding FX), below the 105% Q1 baseline, with management citing fewer user adds under unlimited-user pricing.
fact_evidence: “ARR grew 6% (approximately 7% excluding a 1-point FX headwind) to $719 million,” and dollar-based net revenue retention “was 102.4% (about 104% normalizing for FX), pressured by lower user adds from the shift to unlimited-user platform pricing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said ARR of “~$725–735M (≥9% growth) keeps the story intact” and identified a drop in NRR to “103–104%” as a concern.

description: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin reached 23.3%, above both the 21.5%–22.5% company guide and the preview’s roughly 22% expectation. This was a stronger margin result than the preview’s anticipated Q2 level.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 23.3% from 22.1% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 non-GAAP operating margin guidance of “21.5%–22.5%” and Street consensus of “~22%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: About $8 million of deals expected to close in Q2 slipped beyond quarter-end, reflecting longer mega-enterprise sales cycles. Half had closed by the call, but the delays were an unanticipated source of near-term timing risk.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $8 million of deals expected to close in Q2 slipped past quarter-end, of which half had already closed by the earnings call,” due to mega-enterprise sales cycles extended by “roughly 40-45 days.”

description: Management provided a stronger forward growth outlook than the preview discussed: platform conversion and Agentic adoption are expected to add at least 2 points of revenue growth next year, with double-digit growth exiting 2026 and further acceleration in 2027.
fact_evidence: Management expects “platform conversion and Agentic adoption to add at least 2 points of incremental revenue growth next year,” supporting “an exit from 2026 at double-digit growth with further acceleration in 2027.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Verity Prepare had already contributed more than $20 million of platform ACV, with over 80% of platform upsell interest tied to Verity and customer count nearly quadrupling quarter over quarter. That is concrete monetization and commercial traction beyond the preview’s Q1 baseline of essentially no disclosed revenue contribution.
fact_evidence: “Verity Prepare has contributed to more than $20 million of platform ACV to date,” over 80% of platform upsell interest is tied to Verity, and Verity customer count “grew nearly fourfold quarter-over-quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 had “essentially no disclosed revenue contribution” and that the market wanted “pricing model, attach rate, and whether any FY26 ARR is being underwritten to it.”

description: The company expanded its buyback authorization by $100 million and said roughly 100% of free cash flow would go to repurchases. The preview flagged strategic and capital-allocation tone as a watch item but did not anticipate this specific scale of buyback commitment.
fact_evidence: BlackLine repurchased 1.2 million shares for $38 million; the Board approved an additional “$100 million buyback increase,” bringing remaining capacity to “approximately $280 million,” with “~100% of free cash flow earmarked for repurchases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Strategic/M&A tone” as a catalyst checklist item and mentioned “aggressive buyback framing” as a possible development, but gave no expected buyback amount or FCF allocation.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: RPO and current RPO growth were each about 1 percentage point below the prior-year rates cited in the preview, while their six-point growth gap did not widen. Larger deal sizes and a higher multiyear renewal mix add a positive booking-quality signal, but the reported growth rates were slightly softer.
fact_evidence: “RPO grew 17%” and “current RPO grew 11%,” driven by “24% larger average deal sizes” and multiyear commitments rising to “56% of the renewal book from 45% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 RPO/cRPO growth of “+18% / +12%” and said to watch whether the gap widened further from those rates.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported broad AI availability and usage—roughly 90% of eligible customers enabled and 77% actively using AI, with feature actions up more than 220% sequentially. The preview cautioned that usage metrics alone were not the commercial evidence investors wanted, so this is notable adoption data but does not itself establish monetization.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 90% of eligible customers (about 3,500) are AI-enabled and 77% (about 3,000) are actively using AI,” with nearly 13 million feature actions in the quarter, “up over 220% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said that for Verity, “what matters now is pricing model, attach rate, and whether any FY26 ARR is being underwritten to it—not usage vanity metrics.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company announced several major new customer wins after quarter-end, including Vodafone, Royal Dutch Shell, and two of the six largest U.S. banks. These enterprise wins were not anticipated in the preview, though the facts do not provide a net customer-count result.
fact_evidence: New customer wins included “Vodafone, Royal Dutch Shell, and two of the top six largest U.S. banks signed post-quarter.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview estimated post-raise non-funding debt-to-equity at roughly 1.7x; management reported it at 1.2x after the raise, with the quarter-end ratio at 5.6x. The resulting leverage position is better than the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “The non-funding debt-to-equity ratio dropped from a spiked 5.6x at quarter-end to 1.2x post-capital raise.”
expectation_evidence: “Applying $1.65B to debt paydown against ~$6.0B of implied non-funding debt takes the ratio from 6.13x to roughly 1.7x pro forma.”

description: The preview said the warrant count and strikes were undisclosed and framed a modest package as part of its bull case. The call disclosed 330 million warrants split between $2 and $6 strikes: a substantial potential overhang, though the strikes are above the current stock price and limit near-term dilution.
fact_evidence: “330 million total warrants, split evenly between $2 and $6 strike prices, with an average around $4—well above the current stock price—limiting near-term dilution.”
expectation_evidence: “Warrant count and strike. Unquantified equity overhang”; the bull case called for “modest warrant package (<5% fully diluted).”

description: The call disclosed litigation against Two Harbors and CrossCountry following the failed Two Harbors transaction, a complication the preview did not identify. Management declined to provide details.
fact_evidence: “The failed Two Harbors transaction has led to litigation against Two Harbors and CrossCountry, though management declined to detail specifics.”

description: The call quantified a roughly $100 million reduction in interest expense from paying down MSR lines, offset by about $165 million in new preferred coupon payments. That means the preferred’s gross coupon burden is partly offset by debt-cost savings, a net effect the preview had not quantified.
fact_evidence: “Interest expense will decline roughly $100 million from paying down MSR lines, but net cost is slightly higher due to about $165 million in new preferred coupon payments.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated the preferred coupon at “$165–198M annually” and said proceeds would “Repay existing debt and MSR financing facilities,” but did not quantify the resulting interest savings.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management highlighted capacity to originate $250–$300 billion annually against roughly $40 billion in Q2, and said UWM could benefit sharply if rates fall. This capacity-based upside was not part of the preview’s operating discussion.
fact_evidence: “UWM's origination platform can handle $250-$300 billion annually (vs. $40 billion in Q2), positioning it to benefit sharply if rates fall.”

description: The call flagged elevated servicing costs this year because UWM is running both in-house and Cenlar operations. The preview discussed servicing income but did not flag this operating-cost headwind.
fact_evidence: “Servicing costs are elevated this year from running both in-house and Cenlar operations.”

description: OUT's Q2 revenue grew 14%, above the preview's 10.7% consensus growth estimate. The preview described that revenue bar as low and well telegraphed, but the reported growth exceeded it by 3.3 percentage points.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenues rose 14% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus implied “+10.7%” year over year; the preview also said revenue was “a low-bar, well-telegraphed number.”

description: Adjusted OIBDA reached $160 million, above the preview's estimated $146–152 million range. Its 29% growth also implies a margin of roughly 30.5% on Q2 revenue, above the preview's roughly 29% base case and its 28.5% warning threshold.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated OIBDA [was] up 29% to $160 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted OIBDA” at “~$146–152M” and said “Anything under ~28.5% signals the incremental margin story is fading”; its base case was “~29%.”

description: The FY26 AFFO outlook moved beyond the preview's expected mid-teens guide and its base-case estimate of about $400–405 million: management now expects low-20s growth over 2025. That is a stronger revision than the preview's central expectation, and at least around its bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to low-20s percent growth over 2025's reported AFFO of $338 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the existing guide was “mid-teens,” built a base case “near $400–405M, ~+19%,” and identified a raise “toward ~$400M” as the key catalyst.

description: The World Cup contribution was quantified as substantial, with over $35 million of Q2 revenue and over $50 million overall; about half was incremental to normal business. The preview expected the promised disclosure but had no dollar estimate, and Q3 guidance also includes a $16 million World Cup benefit, indicating some contribution continues beyond Q2.
fact_evidence: “The FIFA World Cup generated over $35 million of revenue in Q2 (over $50 million overall), with roughly half considered incremental to normal business”; Q3 guidance “includ[es] a $16 million World Cup benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had deferred the figures and that “Tonight is that event,” and asked “whether Q3 carries residual benefit or Q2 was the peak.”

description: Transit growth slightly exceeded the roughly 30% expected, while New York MTA growth accelerated to 48%. Transit adjusted OIBDA improved by about $26 million to $33 million, providing stronger evidence of the above-MAG cash flow-through the preview was watching.
fact_evidence: “Transit growth was led by New York MTA revenue surging 48% during the quarter, while transit adjusted OIBDA improved by about $26 million to $33 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Transit revenue growth vs. ~+30% guide,” noted MTA grew “+26% in Q1,” and said to watch the “above-MAG flow-through.”

description: Billboard growth was stronger than the preview's mid-single-digit clean-growth expectation: reported growth was 8%, or 9.4% excluding the exited low-margin LA contract. Digital billboard growth was also over 21% excluding that contract, versus 17.6% reported.
fact_evidence: “Billboard growth would have [been] 9.4%” excluding the exited LA contract, and “digital billboard revenue over 21% versus reported 17.6%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to look for “mid-single-digit clean” billboard growth and listed “Billboard clean organic ≥ +5% ex-condemnation” as a catalyst.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Billboard yield rose to $3,344 per month, with 12% year-over-year growth—above the preview's reference points of more than $2,900 and Q1 growth of 11%.
fact_evidence: “Billboard yield rose 12% year-over-year to $3,344 per month.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “yield holding above the Q1 +11% / >$2,900/month/display” and listed “yield >$2,900/mo” in its catalyst checklist.

description: Combined digital revenue grew over 23% and reached about 37% of total revenue, while programmatic and automated sales grew nearly 50%. The preview did not flag this level of digital mix or programmatic growth.
fact_evidence: “Combined digital revenue grew over 23% and represented about 37% of total revenues (up from 34%), with programmatic and automated sales up nearly 50% to 20% of digital revenue.”

description: The board raised the quarterly dividend from $0.30 to $0.33 per share, a 10% increase. The preview identified a dividend increase as a possible capital-allocation surprise, but did not predict its size.
fact_evidence: “The Board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.33 per share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “a dividend raise or first buyback authorization” a “live, under-priced surprise” and listed “dividend above $0.30” as a catalyst.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage was about 4.0x, below the preview's 4.3x figure and the preview's possible catalyst threshold of leverage below 4.3x.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage stood at about 4x (bottom of the 4-5x target).”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “4.3x net leverage” and listed “leverage <4.3x” as a potential catalyst.

description: Management expects SG&A to grow faster than revenue for the rest of 2026 as it accelerates investment in programmatic sales, data analytics, and a Chief Data Officer. That near-term cost pressure was not anticipated in the preview, which emphasized incremental-margin expansion.
fact_evidence: “SG&A growth is expected to outpace revenue growth for the rest of 2026 due to accelerated investments in programmatic sales, data analytics, and a newly hired Chief Data Officer, aiming to boost 2027 revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted that “Q1 expanded ~690bps Y/Y” and watched whether “the incremental margin story” was fading, without anticipating SG&A growth outpacing revenue.

description: OUT replaced $650 million of 5% notes due 2027 with $500 million of 6% notes due 2034. The longer maturity extends the debt timeline, but the new notes carry a higher coupon; the preview did not discuss this refinancing.
fact_evidence: “The company refinanced $650 million of 5% 2027 notes with $500 million of 6% notes due 2034.”

description: Reported AFFO rose 45% to $121 million, much stronger than the preview's roughly 10% year-over-year AFFO-per-share expectation. The reported figure is total AFFO while the preview's estimate is per share, so the measures are not directly comparable.
fact_evidence: “AFFO [was] up 45% to $121 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “AFFO/share” consensus of “~$0.56” versus “$0.51” a year earlier, or “+10%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Policies in force ended at 484,000, below the preview’s 505,000–515,000 base-case range and short of the 500,000 threshold it expected to be crossed. Management also said full-year PIF will likely be roughly flat with 2025 if competition persists, rather than signaling continued growth.
fact_evidence: “Policies in force grew 6% year-over-year to 484,000 but declined sequentially,” and management guided full-year 2026 PIF to be “roughly flat versus 2025's ~482,000 if the competitive environment persists.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “500K threshold gets crossed this quarter almost mechanically” and gave a base-case Q2 PIF estimate of “~505-515K.”

description: The net loss and LAE ratio was 66%, well above the preview’s expectation that Q2 would be near the low end of the 60–65% full-year range, around 60–62%. That makes the loss-ratio contribution to the quarter weaker than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The net loss and LAE ratio held broadly flat at 66%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided the loss ratio to “60-65% for 2026, with Q2/Q3 at the low end (~60-62%).”

description: The 92.1% combined ratio beat the preview’s 94–95% consensus estimate, but the reported result was supported by a 26% expense ratio that management said is not sustainable—not by the lower loss ratio the preview identified as the key test of earnings quality. Management pointed investors to roughly 29% as a normalized expense ratio.
fact_evidence: The net combined ratio improved to “92.1%,” driven mainly by a “lower net expense ratio of 26%”; management said that level “is not sustainable” and cited Q1/Q4’s “~29% level” as normalized.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated a “~94-95%” combined ratio and said a sub-92% ratio “driven by current-accident-period results” would be genuinely bullish.

description: Revenue came in slightly below the preview’s consensus estimate, despite year-over-year growth being close to the preview’s implied rate.
fact_evidence: “Revenue increased just 2% year-over-year to $389 million.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “~$392.5M,” implying “+2.5%” year-over-year.

description: Root bought back more than $20 million of shares during the quarter, exceeding the preview’s concern that zero repurchases would be a negative signal about management’s view of the setup.
fact_evidence: “Root repurchased over $20 million of shares under its $75 million authorization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “zero repurchase activity in the quarter would be a loud negative signal.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A $4.4 million impairment on private equity investments reduced reported net investment income to $5 million, versus roughly $10 million of underlying portfolio income. The preview did not flag this charge.
fact_evidence: “Root recorded a $4.4 million full impairment on private equity investments (only $600K original cash cost), reducing reported net investment income to $5 million versus ~$10 million underlying portfolio income.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said Root’s rates are roughly 3% overpriced and expects to make modest rate decreases. The preview discussed industry rate softening, but did not anticipate this company-specific pricing position or planned decreases.
fact_evidence: “Average premiums fell year-over-year with management estimating rates are roughly 3% (low single digits) overpriced, signaling planned modest rate decreases ahead.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Root launched in New Jersey, taking its footprint to 37 states covering over 80% of the U.S. population, and set a target for a near-national footprint by the end of 2027. This expansion target was not covered in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company launched New Jersey to reach 37 states covering over 80% of the U.S. population, targeting a near-national footprint by end of 2027.”

description: Management disclosed plans for about $10 million of second-half R&D spending to test new upper-funnel acquisition channels ahead of a Q4 pricing-model launch. The preview anticipated continued restraint in direct marketing but did not identify this R&D program.
fact_evidence: Root “plans ~$10 million in H2 R&D spend to test new upper-funnel acquisition channels ahead of a Q4 pricing model launch.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to expect “more of what you saw in Q1”—“restraint” in direct marketing spend.

description: Hyliion reported Q2 revenue of $4.9 million, more than double the $2.4 million consensus estimate and well above the preview’s roughly $3.0 million buy-side whisper. The revenue beat was substantially larger than the preview’s base case of a modest beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $4.9 million,” up from $1.5 million a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” revenue of “$2.40M”; the preview also said the “buy-side whisper is realistically ~$3.0M” and described the base case as a “modest revenue beat.”

description: Hyliion raised its 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $15 million from $10 million, a 50% increase. The preview identified a raise as the clearest upside trigger, but its base case expected the $10 million guide to be reaffirmed.
fact_evidence: “Hyliion raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by 50%, from $10 million to approximately $15 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance as “~$10M revenue” and said the base case was “FY26 $10M ... reaffirmed”; it also identified whether guidance was “raised, or merely reaffirmed” as a key catalyst.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The $41.7 million Navy award was already known, but the call said most of its work is expected in 2027 and 2028. That points to a slower near-term contribution than the preview’s discussion of a 2H26 contract start and possible early mobilization suggested.
fact_evidence: The $41.7 million Navy contract was awarded, with “most work expected to be performed in 2027 and 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the $10 million annual guide left “~$4.8M for a second half that contains ... the start of a $41.7M contract” and described “early mobilization on the new $41.7M award” in its bull case.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The expected 200-kilowatt commercialization timing moved from year-end 2026 to 2027. This is a delay to a milestone the preview described as central to the investment case.
fact_evidence: “200-kilowatt commercialization now pushed into 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had stated “we should be at that 200 kilowatts of power rating by the year-end,” targeted year-end commercialization, and called the timing “the whole ballgame.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The quarter-end cash balance exceeded the preview’s on-track estimate, and the year-end cash outlook improved substantially: Hyliion now expects $115–$120 million rather than about $100 million. This indicates a better cash trajectory than the preview’s assumed roughly $50 million of 2026 net cash use.
fact_evidence: Hyliion ended Q2 with “$132.4 million in cash and investments” and expects to finish 2026 with “$115-$120 million, a ~$20 million improvement over prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + investments” at “~$126M” for June 30 and listed prior year-end guidance of “~$100M”; it said the FY plan required “~$50M net cash use.”

description: Q2 net loss was somewhat worse than the preview’s estimated $12–$13 million loss, despite the large revenue beat. The miss was modest rather than a major deterioration.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss was $13.9 million,” compared with $13.4 million in Q2 2025.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss ~$12–13M (est.).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Hyliion disclosed that its existing 30-printer fleet could support up to 15 megawatts of annual Carnot core capacity, and gave a capital and revenue estimate per megawatt. The preview said management had not provided 2027–28 capacity and treated an initial capacity or unit-economics framework as new information.
fact_evidence: The “existing fleet of 30 printers is now estimated capable of producing up to 15 megawatts per year”; about “$1.5 million in printer investment” can support 1 megawatt of annual capacity, representing “roughly $2.5-$3 million of annual revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “explicitly declined to give 2027–28 production capacity” and that “any first framing of 2027 units, ASP per core, or target gross margin is a genuine new datapoint.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Hyliion identified a possible additive-manufacturing improvement that could raise print speed and throughput by as much as three times. This is a new potential production upside, although it remains under validation.
fact_evidence: Management identified additive manufacturing improvements it believes could “increase print speed and throughput by up to three times,” though “this is still being validated.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $37.4 million, above the preview’s modeled $34–35 million. That is a clear beat against the expected bar.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 29% year-over-year to $37.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$34–35M (modeled — not a widely published Street line).”

description: Privia raised its 2026 guidance across collections, revenue, care margin, platform contribution, and EBITDA. The preview expected an EBITDA guide raise, but the broad set of increases is favorable versus that expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 guidance across practice collections, GAAP revenue, care margin, platform contribution and EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy-side expects the high end taken to at least ~$155M”; the base scenario anticipated guidance “nudged to $150–158M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Attributed lives reached 1.64 million, above the prior guidance ceiling of 1.625 million and above the preview’s modeled Q2 level of 1.60–1.62 million. The preview flagged a second lives raise as a key debate, and the reported level exceeds that modeled range.
fact_evidence: “Attributed lives now above the high end of prior guidance”; the company serves “over 1.64 million attributed lives.”
expectation_evidence: “Attributed lives: ~1.60–1.62M”; the preview asked whether there would be “a second raise” and said standing pat would read as decelerating momentum.

description: Despite the guidance raises, the updated outlook implies only roughly 3% year-over-year practice collections growth in the second half, versus 13.4% growth in the first half. Management attributed the implied slowdown to conservative guidance rather than specific headwinds, but the outlook is more subdued than the strong first-half run rate.
fact_evidence: “The implied second-half practice collections growth decelerates to roughly 3% year-over-year versus 13% in the first half,” which management attributed to “conservative guidance rather than specific headwinds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 had delivered “+25.8%” collections growth and that the FY26 guide implied “only ~13% growth”; it framed the debate around the size of the guidance raise.

description: The company expects 70%–80% of full-year adjusted EBITDA to convert to free cash flow, below the preview’s roughly 80% conversion expectation at the low end of the range.
fact_evidence: “Expects 70% to 80% of full-year adjusted EBITDA to convert to free cash flow as a full cash taxpayer.”
expectation_evidence: The existing guidance was described as “~80% of adj. EBITDA converting to FCF,” and the preview said H1 FCF tracking toward the 80% target mattered.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: CMS may delay final 2025 MSSP reconciliation until November, creating an atypical year-end cash-flow pattern. Management expects minimal accrual impact and no problem receiving the cash, which limits the downside but does not remove the timing surprise.
fact_evidence: “CMS may delay final MSSP reconciliation results for performance year 2025 until November, creating an atypical year-end cash flow dynamic,” while management expects “minimal impact on accruals and no issues receiving the cash.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Implemented providers ended Q2 at 5,644, slightly below the preview’s modeled range of 5,660–5,700; the company also left implemented-provider guidance unchanged while raising its other guidance.
fact_evidence: “Privia ended Q2 with over 5,644 implemented providers”; “implemented provider guidance was left unchanged.”
expectation_evidence: “Implemented providers: ~5,660–5,700 (modeled).”

description: PAYC reported Q2 revenue of $531 million, well above the preview’s $512.3 million consensus, and said growth was broad-based rather than driven by one-off factors. This was a substantial top-line beat against the expected 6% growth pace.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $531 million, up 10% year-over-year,” with “broad-based strength with no one-off factors.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $512.3M” and “Implied YoY | +5.9%.”

description: Recurring and other revenue was $505 million, materially above the $485.7 million consensus, with 11% growth versus the preview’s 6.7% expectation. That also came in well above the preview’s warning that growth with a 5-handle would threaten the annual recurring-revenue outlook.
fact_evidence: “Recurring and other revenue of $505 million, up 11%.”
expectation_evidence: “Recurring & other revenue | $485.7M” and “+6.7%”; the preview said “Anything with a 5-handle puts the FY +7–8% recurring guide in jeopardy.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $235 million, above the preview’s estimated $213–218 million, and its 44.2% margin substantially exceeded the estimated 41.5–42.5% range. This was especially strong against the preview’s expectation that Q2 would be the seasonally weakest margin quarter.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $235 million in Q2, expanding margins by 320 basis points year-over-year to 44.2%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$213–218M est.” and “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~41.5–42.5% est.” The preview also described Q2 as “seasonally the weakest margin quarter.”

description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.78, above the preview’s comparable $2.28 consensus and also above its $2.35–2.45 realistic-whisper range. This reversed the preview’s concern that absolute non-GAAP earnings might decline despite the buyback-driven increase in EPS.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income was $128 million ($2.78 per diluted share).”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $2.28”; the preview called “$2.35–2.45” the realistic whisper and expected “a mid-single-digit YoY decline in absolute non-GAAP earnings.”

description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance above its prior range: the new $2.197–$2.212 billion range is entirely above the previous $2.175–$2.195 billion range. The midpoint rose by about $20 million, a modest increase relative to the prior midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.197–$2.212 billion (7%–8% growth).”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $2.175–2.195B (+6–7%).” The preview said the market was watching for a raise rather than a reaffirmation.

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance rose to $1.007–$1.022 billion, with even the new low end above the old $950–970 million range. The new midpoint implies a record 46% margin, a much larger improvement than the preview’s approximately 44% midpoint expectation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.007–$1.022 billion, implying a record 46% margin at the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $950–970M (~44% midpoint).”

description: PAYC now expects 2026 free cash flow to exceed $650 million, supported by sustainable process and labor efficiencies that bring free-cash-flow margins closer to EBITDA margins. The preview did not identify a free-cash-flow outlook as an expectation or key debate.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow is now expected to exceed $650 million in 2026,” driven by “sustainable process and labor efficiencies bringing free cash flow margins closer to EBITDA margins.”

description: Management disclosed that the prior data-center investment for proprietary AI models is generating roughly $100 million in R&D savings this year plus more than $30 million in avoided third-party fees. The preview discussed AI-driven automation and margin efficiency, but did not anticipate or quantify savings of this scale.
fact_evidence: “Last year's $100 million+ investment in data centers to host proprietary AI models is generating roughly $100 million in R&D savings this year plus $30 million+ in avoided third-party fees.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 margin expansion reflected “automation and process efficiencies,” but gave no expectation of these specific savings.

description: The annual interest-on-client-funds outlook increased to approximately $105 million, modestly above the preview’s $103 million assumption. The reported average daily client-funds balance was $2.9 billion, up 9% year over year, although the preview had cited a Q1 balance of about $3.1 billion.
fact_evidence: “Guidance assumes no rate changes for the rest of the year, with interest on funds held for clients of approximately $105 million and average daily client funds of $2.9 billion (up 9%).”
expectation_evidence: “Interest on client funds | ~$25–27M est.” for the quarter and “FY26 … interest on client funds ~ $103M.”

description: PAYC reported that first-half repurchases reached approximately 11 million shares and reduced shares outstanding by 20%, returning about $1.4 billion. The preview knew of 8.4 million shares retired in Q1 and expected further Q2 buybacks, but did not anticipate this reported first-half scale.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 11 million shares in the first half of 2026, reducing shares outstanding by 20% and returning roughly $1.4 billion to stockholders.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “8.4M shares … retired … in Q1” and listed as a key question “How much of the $2B authorization was used in Q2.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones

fact_evidence: “The DoJ closed its criminal investigation into Black Diamond's avalanche transceiver reporting on June 4, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described an “unresolved DOJ criminal investigation” with “grand jury subpoenas and two former executives named as targets.”

description: Q2 revenue was $14.5 million, above the preview’s $12.9 million consensus and $13.1 million estimate; U.S. revenue of $12.6 million also exceeded the preview’s roughly $10.6 million model. The quarter grew about 120% year over year, versus the preview’s roughly 95–103% base-case growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew approximately 120% year-over-year to $14.5 million, with U.S. revenue up more than 150% to $12.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $12.9M” consensus and “My Estimate $13.1M”; the model build estimated “US ~$10.6M.”

description: Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $62–66 million rather than reaffirming $60–64 million as the preview’s base case expected. The higher range is a modest positive versus that expectation, though its midpoint is close to the preview’s $62.2 million FY consensus.
fact_evidence: “Raised full year 2026 global net revenue guidance to $62-66 million from $60-64 million.”
expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm at $60–64M is table stakes”; base case: “FY guide reaffirmed at $60–64M.”

description: Q2 gross margin reached 59%, above the preview’s 56–57% expectation, and management raised full-year margin guidance to 58–61% from 55–58%. This was stronger than the preview’s concern that lower-margin Europe mix could cause margin deceleration.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 59% in Q2… the strongest organic margin in company history,” prompting a full-year guidance increase “to 58-61% from 55-58%.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin estimate: “57%”; the preview’s base case expected “GM 56–57%,” and the existing FY guide was “55–58%.”

description: The loss was worse than expected despite the revenue beat: GAAP EPS was $(0.63) versus the preview’s $(0.55) consensus and $(0.56) estimate. The call attributed the wider loss to SG&A of $32.9 million after commercialization moved in-house from Ascensia.
fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $36.7 million ($0.63 per share) from $14.5 million ($0.36 per share) a year ago, driven by SG&A rising to $32.9 million from $9.7 million after bringing commercialization in-house from Ascensia.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) $(0.55)” consensus and “My Estimate $(0.56)”; the preview also estimated SG&A of “$30.5M.”

description: The European transition did not close in Q2 as the preview expected, and outside-U.S. revenue was only $1.9 million versus the preview’s roughly $2.5 million model. Management attributed the weakness to delayed European tender updates following a later-than-planned Ascensia transition, while saying the shortfall would shift into Q3 and Q4 and Europe would remain about 20% of full-year revenue.
fact_evidence: “Outside-U.S. revenue grew only about 12% to $1.9 million due to delayed European tender updates from the later-than-planned Ascensia transition,” with the shortfall “shifting into Q3 and Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the transition was “guided to close in Q2 2026” and its model estimated “OUS ~$2.5M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Eon Care network was already above 90 nurses and handling about 40% of U.S. insertions, with management expecting it to exceed half by year-end. The preview did not flag this network’s progress as a key metric; the call said the provider count was ahead of the company’s 100-by-year-end goal.
fact_evidence: “The Eon Care network added 28 providers to exceed 90 nurses (ahead of its 100 by year-end goal), now performs about 40% of all U.S. Eversense insertions, and is expected to exceed half by year-end.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call disclosed animal testing with 100% Bluetooth success within 8 feet for Freedom, a technical result not anticipated in the preview. Freedom’s first-in-human study remains planned for later this year, broadly matching the preview’s timing expectation.
fact_evidence: “Freedom's first in-human study is planned for later this year, supported by animal data showing 100% Bluetooth success within 8 feet.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: KVH ended the quarter with approximately 10,700 subscribing vessels, above the preview’s expected range of 10,300–10,600. The more than 1,000 net additions also show strong conversion to subscribers despite terminal shipments falling from Q1’s record.
fact_evidence: “The company added over 1,000 net subscribing vessels in the quarter, ending with approximately 10,700, an 11% sequential increase.”
expectation_evidence: “Look for ~10,300–10,600 vessels.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Ending cash was $57.7 million, above the preview’s estimated $50–54 million. Cash fell only $1.4 million, with the decline primarily attributed to stock repurchases.
fact_evidence: “The ending cash balance fell $1.4 million to $57.7 million, primarily due to $2.3 million in stock repurchases.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash … Q2’26E … ~$50–54” and “Cash at 6/30 is the tell on how much of that $45M remains to be funded.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: KVH said its GEO/VSAT bandwidth commitments predominantly expire at the end of 2026, with only a small commitment remaining in 2027. The preview focused on LEO-related margin pressure and VSAT churn but did not flag this near-term reduction in legacy bandwidth exposure.
fact_evidence: “The company's GEO/VSAT bandwidth commitments predominantly expire at the end of 2026, with only a small remaining commitment in 2027, de-risking future margin exposure as LEO grows.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: LEO connectivity reached 55% of airtime revenue, above the preview’s expectation that the mix would cross roughly 50%. Management also described Starlink as its fastest-growing segment.
fact_evidence: “LEO connectivity now accounts for 55% of airtime revenue, with growth driven by Starlink, which management called their fastest-growing segment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “LEO mix crossing ~50% of airtime.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The land-based Starlink initiative had grown to approximately 1,600 sites, adding roughly 500 in the quarter and broadening recurring revenue beyond maritime. The preview discussed other expansion and commercial traction but did not anticipate this scale of land-based activity.
fact_evidence: “The land-based Starlink initiative grew to approximately 1,600 sites, an increase of roughly 500 during the quarter, broadening the recurring revenue base beyond maritime.”

description: Managed IT and cybersecurity services began converting from pilots into recurring revenue, providing concrete monetization progress beyond the preview’s general watch for commercial traction. KVH also launched multi-network plans and put Link streaming into beta, developments the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “New multi-network service plans (spanning Starlink, OneWeb, and VSAT) launched this quarter, while Link streaming entered beta trials and managed IT/cybersecurity services began converting from pilots into recurring revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “managed IT / CommBox commercial traction” as a narrative watch and mentioned the “vessel-based managed IT launch.”

description: KVH said it expects to complete and conclude the full $15 million buyback authorization within the current month. The preview did not discuss this accelerated completion timing.
fact_evidence: “The full $15 million buyback authorization is expected to be completed and concluded within the current month.”

description: Q2 consolidated EPS was reported at $2.19, well above the preview’s $1.27 adjusted-EPS consensus and the company’s previously stated adjusted-EPS floor of $1.25. The supplied call facts do not specify whether the $2.19 uses the same adjusted basis, so the comparison is not strictly like-for-like.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated EPS of $2.19” on Q2 pretax income of $64.5 million.
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS **$1.27**”; company guidance was “Adj. EPS **≥ $1.25**.”

description: Management assumed Q3 fuel of $3.80 per gallon and Q4 fuel of $3.70, substantially below the preview’s fuel-risk framing around Q2’s roughly $4.20 realized price and its bear case of Q3 fuel at $4.50 or higher. Alongside those assumptions, management guided to full-year 2026 EPS above $6.
fact_evidence: “Guided full-year 2026 consolidated EPS of greater than $6,” assuming “fuel of $3.80/gallon in Q3 and $3.70/gallon in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 fuel the “single largest swing factor,” noted Q2 realized “~$4.20/gal,” and described a bear case with “Q3 fuel guided ≥$4.50.”

description: Despite the lower-than-feared fuel assumptions, the company guided to a Q3 loss of about $0.50 per share and only a 2% operating margin at the midpoint. The preview emphasized the Q3 guide but did not provide a numerical Q3 EPS forecast, so the loss is a newly disclosed weak outlook rather than a miss against a stated consensus estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for a consolidated loss of approximately $0.50 per share and a 2% operating margin at the midpoint.”

description: The preview already flagged elevated unit costs, citing Q1 CASM ex-fuel growth of 7.1%, but the call indicated a sharper near-term increase: legacy Allegiant nonfuel unit costs are expected up 9–10%, and consolidated nonfuel CASM ex-cargo up 10–12% in Q3, its year-over-year peak.
fact_evidence: “Legacy Allegiant nonfuel unit costs expected up 9-10% and consolidated nonfuel CASM ex-cargo up 10-12% in Q3, marking the peak year-over-year CASM ex increase.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 CASM ex-fuel was “8.64¢, +7.1% YoY — already running hot” and flagged CASM ex-fuel as a key item to watch.

description: The company announced a $275 million pilot retention bonus payable from cash in the coming weeks, with management expecting net leverage to reach its peak after the payment. The preview discussed liquidity and leverage but did not anticipate this large cash outlay.
fact_evidence: “Pay a pilot retention bonus of approximately $275 million (including payroll taxes) from cash on hand,” expected “to push net leverage to its peak from the current 2.6x pro forma level.”

description: The preview’s FY aircraft CapEx guide was $570–590 million, but management raised full-year 2026 CapEx to about $850 million and expects roughly 20 additional MAX aircraft in 2027. The higher investment plan is a substantial step-up from the preview’s stated baseline.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 CapEx raised to approximately $850 million”; the MAX fleet is expected to grow by “~20 aircraft in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY aircraft capex guide **$570–590M**.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Sun Country faced elevated junior-pilot attrition in Minneapolis–St. Paul because the largest Twin Cities carrier was hiring more pilots, leading to a temporary reduction in off-peak MSP capacity in the second half. The preview did not flag this staffing and capacity issue.
fact_evidence: “Sun Country experienced elevated junior pilot attrition in Minneapolis-St. Paul driven by increased hiring at the largest Twin Cities carrier, prompting a temporary reduction of off-peak MSP capacity in the back half of the year.”

description: The preview said investors wanted a quantified first-year synergy tranche, but management only reiterated confidence in at least $140 million of run-rate synergies by 2029. The long-term target matched the preview; the lack of a first-year amount left the requested near-term detail undisclosed.
fact_evidence: “Reiterated confidence in at least $140 million in run-rate Sun Country synergies by 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for a “quantified first-year tranche” and that investors wanted “a number and a bridge, not a reaffirmation.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The new Expedia partnership was already live across the company and generating bookings, with more than half from net-new customers—an early customer-acquisition result the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “The newly launched Expedia partnership went 100% live on July 10 and already accounts for approximately 3% of bookings, with more than half coming from net-new customers.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Cobrand card remuneration grew 24% year over year, and management set a goal of doubling its share of revenue from 5% to 10%. The preview did not flag this revenue stream or the stated growth target.
fact_evidence: “Cobrand card remuneration rose 24% year-over-year toward a goal of doubling from 5% to 10% of revenue.”

description: Q2 revenue was $321 million, about 3.7% above the preview’s roughly $309.4–$309.7 million consensus, with growth of 8% in constant currency versus the preview’s implied 5.2%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 9.2% to $321 million (8% constant currency).”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenues: $309.4M – $309.7M”; “Implied Y/Y: +5.2%.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $166 million, above the preview’s modeled $158–$161 million. The 51.6% margin, however, was in line with the preview’s model.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to $166 million with margins expanding 36 basis points to 51.6%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: *not published* — model ~$158–161M”; the model table estimated “~$160M (51.6%).”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.26, above the preview’s approximately $0.24 estimate. The company also raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted EPS range by $0.02, while leaving the upper end unchanged.
