fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 30% year-over-year to $0.26, and the company raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $0.95-$1.01 from $0.93-$1.01.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: ~$0.24 ($0.2389)”; the preview listed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of “$0.93–1.01.”

description: The full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised rather than reaffirmed: both ranges increased by 25 basis points. The preview considered a raise constructive, but its base case was reaffirmation.
fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 outlook,” with constant-currency revenue growth of 5.25% to 6.75% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 5.75% to 7.25%, “a 25 basis point increase to both from prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance verb: ‘reaffirm’ vs. ‘raise/narrow up’”; the preview’s base case was “FY reaffirmed,” while its bull case expected “FY guide raised or narrowed to upper half.”

description: Nordion’s 16.7% constant-currency growth was far above the preview’s low-single-digit expectation and its roughly $43 million model. The strength was partly timing-related: second-half shipments shifted into Q2, leaving tougher comparisons later in the year.
fact_evidence: “Nordion posted 16.7% constant currency revenue growth,” but “first-half revenue exceeded the guided 40%-45% of full-year range as second-half shipments shifted into Q2, implying tougher second-half comparisons.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Nordion’s FY guide as “low-to-mid single digits cc” and modeled Q2 revenue of “$43M” with “+1.4%” year-over-year growth.

description: Nelson Labs returned to growth more strongly than the preview’s expectation of a slight return to growth: constant-currency revenue rose 5.4%. Its 32.4% margin was around the preview’s modeled 32.2%, and the year-over-year margin decline was anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Nelson Labs exceeded expectations with 5.4% constant currency revenue growth and improved segment margin 438 basis points sequentially to 32.4%, though margins declined year-over-year due to higher costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a “slight return to growth” in Q2 and modeled a 32.2% segment margin; it also warned that a decent quarter would “likely show segment margin down Y/Y against 34.2%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage reached 3.0x, better than the preview’s starting point of 3.2x and the expected deleveraging path, putting the company at the upper end of its long-term target range.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage ratio improved to 3x, reaching the company's long-term target range of 2-3x, with roughly $950 million of liquidity and nothing drawn on the revolver.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 net leverage was “3.2x” and described Q2 as a chance for “a clean cash quarter to keep the 3.2x → deleveraging narrative alive.”

description: Borrowing costs fell more than the preview’s interest-cost discussion implied, and the interest expense outlook narrowed to a lower ceiling. Repricing the term loan by 100 basis points in under a year helped drive the improvement.
fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell over $6 million to $34 million after repricing lowered borrowing costs on the $1.4 billion term loan by 100 basis points in under a year,” and the outlook narrowed to “$135-$142 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited annual interest expense of “~$135–145M/yr guided.”

description: The company raised the low end of its capital expenditure range and restarted a previously paused greenfield project, rather than keeping the investment plan at the preview’s stated range. Management also said capex should step down meaningfully in 2027.
fact_evidence: “A new X-ray facility begins generating revenue in Q3 and a previously paused second greenfield project is now fully underway,” with full-year CapEx guidance of “$200-$225 million” and “a meaningful step down expected in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed capex guidance of “$175–225M” and noted that capacity/emissions-control capex was proceeding “regardless of regulatory uncertainty.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The New Mexico EO litigation was resolved for an immaterial amount, a case outcome not discussed in the preview. Other EO matters remain outstanding, with a Georgia appellate ruling awaited and the California trial expected in 2027.
fact_evidence: “Management resolved the New Mexico EO litigation in July for an immaterial amount, awaits a spring/summer appellate ruling in Georgia, and expects the California trial in January or April 2027.”

description: Ouster reported $55 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $51.6–51.9 million consensus and the $52.5 million top of company guidance. That is a clear beat, though it was also within the preview’s bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 revenue of $55 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus: $51.6–51.9M”; company guidance “$49.5–52.5M”; the preview’s bull case was “$54–56M.”

description: The 49% GAAP gross margin looks substantially better than expected, but a one-time refund added roughly 1,000 basis points; normalized margin was only in the high-30s, below the preview’s 42–44% buy-side expectation. The headline beat therefore masks weaker underlying margin than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin was 49%, but included a one-time refund benefit of roughly 1,000 basis points, meaning normalized gross margin was in the high-30s”; management reaffirmed a “35%-40% long-term range.”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP gross margin: ~42–44% (buy-side).”

description: Q3 guidance has a $56 million midpoint, within the preview’s $55–58 million buy-side anchor, but its $54.5 million low end falls below that range. Management also said upside flexibility is limited because output is constrained to protect backlog, making the outlook less open-ended than the midpoint alone suggests.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance is $54.5 million to $57.5 million” and “limited upside flexibility since output is constrained to protect backlog.”
expectation_evidence: The Q3 buy-side anchor was “$55–58M”; the preview also called for a guide “≥$56M” as a catalyst threshold.

description: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $4 million, better than the preview’s expected loss of roughly $5–7 million.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $4 million, a roughly $1 million improvement versus Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~–$5 to –$7M (buy-side).”

description: Operating expenses rose about 10% year over year, faster than the preview’s expected opex-growth framework of less than 5–8%.
fact_evidence: “GAAP operating expenses rose about 10% year-over-year to $47 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described “reaffirmation of the … <5–8% opex growth framework.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Rev8 had meaningful commercial validation, including multiple million-dollar-plus Fortune 500 orders and a statewide Utah DOT deployment, but contributed only minor prototype sales in Q2 and production volumes are not expected until the end of Q3. That gives investors sizable orders, but not the near-term realized revenue the preview said the market needed to see.
fact_evidence: “Rev8 contributed only minor prototype sales in Q2, with production volumes expected by the end of Q3”; it “already secured multiple million-dollar-plus orders from Fortune 500 customers, plus a Utah DOT order covering several hundred intersections statewide.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the market now needed “dollars, not logos” and described “design wins with no revenue attached” as the disappointment case.

description: The company ended Q2 with substantially more cash than the preview’s Q1-based liquidity estimate implied, but also disclosed a further $98 million of ATM proceeds and about 72 million shares outstanding—more dilution than the preview’s modeled July offering alone. Management’s statement that no more capital is expected to be needed is consistent with the preview’s expectation that the financing removed near-term funding risk.
fact_evidence: “Ouster ended Q2 with $263 million in cash and no debt (including ~$98 million from ATM),” raised “an additional ~$191 million net in a July 6 stock offering,” and had “~72 million shares outstanding.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$175M including short-term investments” at Q1 and an expected “~$191.9M net” July raise, with “3.62M shares,” producing “roughly $360M+” pro forma liquidity.

description: Strata raised 2026 revenue guidance to $285–295 million from $260–275 million, putting even the new low end above the preview’s cited $275.8 million consensus. It also raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33–35 million from $29–33 million, a stronger increase than the preview’s bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Strata raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $285-295 million from $260-275 million previously, and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33-35 million from $29-33 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue consensus of ~$273–276M sits at or above the top end of management's own $260–275M guide”; the bull case anticipated a raise to “~$270–285M / EBITDA $31–34M.”

description: Q2 revenue was $72.5 million, above the preview’s $68–70 million management-framework range and roughly $69.5 million base case. Gross profit of $15.2 million also exceeded the preview’s approximately $14.6 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew 60.7% year-over-year to $72.5 million”; “gross profit [was] up 68.9% to $15.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue (mgmt framework) | ~$68–70M”; the model lists Q2 revenue of “~$69.5” and gross profit of “~$14.6.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $7.9 million with a 10.9% margin, above the preview’s roughly $7.0 million and 10.1% base case. The result also cleared the preview’s $7.0 million catalyst threshold.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.9 million in Q2 2026 from $6.4 million in Q1, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 140 basis points to 10.9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “~$7.0M (10.1%)” and its catalyst checklist called for “Adj. EBITDA ≥ $7.0M.”

description: Clinical revenue reached $24.3 million, well above the preview’s $21.2 million estimate. Growth was 15.1% sequentially even excluding acquisitions, while transplant clinical revenue grew 23.8%.
fact_evidence: “Clinical revenue rose 22.6% sequentially to $24.3 million (15.1% excluding Q2 acquisitions), led by 23.8% growth in transplant clinical revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 model estimated Clinical revenue at “~21.2”; it also flagged clinical momentum and transplant growth as key metrics to watch.

description: Logistics gross margin fell to 18.4%, below the preview’s roughly 20% expectation and management’s prior outlook for margins to remain in the 20% range. Management now expects only 18.5–20% in the second half and a return to 20% in 2027.
fact_evidence: “Logistics gross margin fell to 18.4% in Q2 2026 versus 19.3% in Q1 and a 20% expectation, with management guiding to 18.5-20% for the second half and a return to 20% in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 Logistics gross margin at “~20.0%” and said management had guided margins to “remain in the 20% range” for the rest of 2026.

description: Logistics faces an unanticipated customer-related revenue headwind: one nonexclusive customer cut flying for an organ type, with the full impact expected in Q3. Strata now expects Q3 Logistics revenue to fall high single digits sequentially, rather than the preview’s roughly flat sequential estimate, before recovering by Q4.
fact_evidence: “Logistics faces a roughly 3% revenue headwind from one nonexclusive customer that reduced flying for one organ type starting in June, expected to fully hit in Q3 before recovering by Q4”; Q3 Logistics revenue is expected “to decline high single digits sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said its framework implied “Logistics roughly flat sequentially at ~$48M” and highlighted Logistics organic revenue as a key question.

description: Strata completed three clinical bolt-on acquisitions year-to-date, adding over $20 million of revenue and $6.3 million of projected annualized adjusted EBITDA at mid-single-digit multiples. That is more concrete and greater realized acquisition contribution than the preview’s description of an active pipeline capable of adding low-single-digit millions of adjusted EBITDA annually.
fact_evidence: “The company completed three bolt-on clinical acquisitions year-to-date at mid-single-digit multiples, adding over $20 million of revenue and $6.3 million of projected annualized adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described an “active tuck-in M&A pipeline” capable of “low single digit millions of adjusted EBITDA annually.”

description: Management expects higher-margin Clinical to rise to roughly 40% of revenue and nearly 50% of gross profit in the second half. The preview anticipated Clinical growth, but did not indicate this degree of expected mix shift.
fact_evidence: “The business mix is shifting toward higher-margin clinical, expected to reach roughly 40% of revenue and nearly 50% of gross profit in the second half, up from 30% and 35% respectively in Q1 2026.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The call indicated that a $17.5 million performance earn-out is expected to be received in full by year-end, adding near-term certainty and timing detail not specified in the preview’s discussion of earn-out payments extending through March 2027.
fact_evidence: “The company anticipates a $17.5 million performance earn-out to be received in full by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “up to $45M in Joby earnout payments through March 2027,” without specifying this $17.5 million amount or a full receipt by year-end.

description: CareCloud’s adjusted EBITDA was $5.9 million, below the preview’s $6.8–7.0 million base case and below its $6.8 million credibility threshold. The company nevertheless reaffirmed its full-year EBITDA range, leaving a steeper second-half ramp than the preview already viewed as demanding.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $5.9 million.” Management “reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance” of $29–31 million adjusted EBITDA, implying a materially stronger second half.
expectation_evidence: “My base case has Q2 at $6.8–7.0M”; “Adjusted EBITDA ≥ ~$6.8M” was the catalyst threshold, and “Anything with a ‘5-handle’ makes the full-year EBITDA guide arithmetically very hard.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: R&D expense more than doubled because CareCloud began expensing AI development instead of capitalizing it. The preview wanted hard AI monetization metrics but did not anticipate this near-term earnings pressure from the accounting treatment of development costs.
fact_evidence: “R&D expense more than doubled as the company shifted AI development to current expense rather than capitalizing it, pressuring near-term earnings.”
expectation_evidence: “The bar is now customers, ARR, or pricing disclosure — not another TAM slide.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: CareCloud reported $13.4 million of cash, well above the $3.4 million Q1-end balance that framed the preview’s liquidity concern. However, net working capital was only $695,000, so the reported cash improvement came alongside a still-thin working-capital position.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with about $13.4 million in cash and net working capital of only $695,000.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash was $3.4M at Q1-end” and the preview flagged liquidity, cash balance, and FCF as items to watch.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The recurring technology-enabled business solutions mix reached about 75% of revenue, versus 69% a year earlier, and totaled $24 million. That is a favorable mix update against the preview’s concern about whether organic growth could hold up, although the call facts do not separate acquisition-driven growth from organic growth.
fact_evidence: “Recurring technology-enabled business solutions rose to approximately 75% of revenue this quarter, up from 69% a year ago, reaching $24 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “whether that services erosion stabilizes determines whether H2 organic growth exists” and flagged “organic growth disclosure” as important.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: CareCloud added that Empower’s president had historically referred business now representing about 10% of CareCloud’s annualized revenue. The preview expected Empower to be immaterial near term and identified cross-selling as a possible catalyst, but did not give this scale for the existing referral relationship.
fact_evidence: “Empower's president Mitchell Brey has historically referred business now representing approximately 10% of CareCloud's annualized revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Closed May 22, 2026; management said not material to FY2026. Any framing of it as a growth driver should be discounted; the compliance SaaS launch is a 2H26 event.”

description: Gross margin reached 73.6%, well above the preview’s 66–69% estimate and the prior record, rather than merely holding around the expected range.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached a company record of 73.6%, improving 510 basis points sequentially and 810 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My estimate: 66–69%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The cash position was slightly below the preview’s estimate, but the more notable difference was management’s warning that $5.1 million would fund operations for only at least nine months—shorter than the preview’s base-case expectation of runway into Q3 2027.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $5.1 million in cash, which management expects to fund operations for only at least the next 9 months”; Q2 cash usage was “approximately $1.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash (6/30/26) … My estimate: $5.2–5.5M”; the base case expected “runway into Q3 2027 reaffirmed.”

description: Momentum continued after quarter-end: July e-commerce and subscription revenue both set new monthly records, an additional positive update beyond the preview’s focus on the Q2 print and pre-announced growth.
fact_evidence: “July results showed continued momentum with record e-commerce revenue of $245,000 (up 19% from June) and record subscription revenue of $52,000 (up 22% from June).”

description: Total revenue was $218 million, below the preview’s $221.9–$224.5 million consensus range and its $223 million base model. The shortfall was modest, but the headline print missed expectations.
fact_evidence: “Total net product revenue reached $218 million in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $221.9M – $224.5M”; “My Q2'26 build… Total revenue $223M.”

description: SG&A jumped to $208.1 million, well above the preview’s $193 million model and its expectation that spending at or below roughly $195 million would validate the guide. Management expects SG&A to plateau at this higher level for the rest of the year, rather than at the lower level investors were modeling.
fact_evidence: “SG&A surging to $208.1 million from $130.3 million a year earlier”; management “guided that SG&A should plateau at the Q2 level of ~$208 million for the rest of the year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “SG&A $193M,” said “Anything at or below ~$195M validates the guide,” and flagged “$205M+” as breaking the operating-leverage story.

description: SYMBRAVO revenue was far below the preview’s $6 million estimate: sales were $2.3 million, with gross-to-net discounts rising into the high 80% range rather than remaining in the expected high-70% range. Demand nevertheless increased sequentially, so the revenue miss came alongside worse-than-expected discounting.
fact_evidence: “SYMBRAVO net sales fell to $2.3 million… as gross-to-net discounts deviated into the high 80% range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “SYMBRAVO $6M” and said discounts were “elevated in the high-70% range.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Auvelity prescriptions reached about 266,000, above the preview’s watchpoint of the mid-240,000s or better. The strong prescription growth contrasts with Auvelity sales of $180.3 million, slightly below the preview’s $183 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total prescriptions of ~266,000 (up 34% YoY)”; Auvelity sales were “$180.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for sequential TRx acceleration into the mid-240Ks or better” and modeled “AUVELITY $183M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The early Alzheimer’s agitation launch showed a quantified acceleration among older patients: new-to-brand prescriptions for patients 65 and older rose 126% versus the prior quarter’s comparable eight-week period. The preview expected qualitative launch color and sought quantified ADA metrics, but had no comparable growth expectation.
fact_evidence: “In the first 8 weeks of the Alzheimer's disease agitation launch, new-to-brand prescriptions among patients 65 and older rose 126% versus the same period in the prior quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to expect management to discuss launch activity and listed “first quantified ADA launch metrics” as a catalyst to watch.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at about $320 million, above the preview’s expected $255–$270 million range. Management also reiterated that the balance should fund operations into cash-flow positivity without additional financing.
fact_evidence: “Axsome ended the quarter with ~$320 million in cash, which management expects is sufficient to fund operations into cash flow positivity without additional financing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “cash ~$255–270M” and said a balance near or below ~$250 million could revive dilution concerns.

description: R&D expense was $46.2 million, below the preview’s $58 million model. That is a meaningful underspend relative to expectations, even though management expects R&D to rise going forward.
fact_evidence: “R&D declined to $46.2 million”; management guided that “R&D rises” after Q2.
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “R&D $58M.”

description: Management described a goal of roughly one NDA filing per year through 2030, adding a specific filing cadence to the pipeline outlook that the preview did not set out.
fact_evidence: The pipeline was described as “targeting roughly one NDA filing per year through 2030.”

description: Q2 revenue was $4.3 million, well below the preview’s $5.2 million company guide and $4.85 million consensus, and it declined 2% year over year rather than delivering the expected return to growth. Sequential growth was only 3%, versus the roughly 15%–24% implied by the preview’s estimates and guide.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $4.3 million, down 2% year-over-year but up 3% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue: ~$5.2M” and “Revenue $4.85M”; the preview also says a $5.2M quarter would mark “first year-over-year revenue growth in years.”

description: The anticipated Q2 non-GAAP net loss was about $0.42 million, but the reported loss was $0.989 million—more than twice the preview’s base estimate. The preview’s modeled Q2 opex was also slightly below the reported $4.4 million.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net loss narrowed to $989,000”; “Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 26% year-over-year to $4.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Non-GAAP net loss” of “-$0.42M” and modeled non-GAAP opex of “~$4.28M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The new carrier deployment expected by the end of Q2 had not launched by quarter-end; management instead expected two customer launches by the end of August. The timing is later than anticipated, although both customers had fully executed contracts.
fact_evidence: “Management expects to launch two new customers by month-end”—one SafePath OS device deployment and one SafePath Connect deployment in Europe—“both with fully executed contracts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says the Q1-signed carrier’s “delivery [was] expected by end of Q2” and identifies whether it “actually went into revenue” as a key issue.

description: Management expects non-GAAP operating expenses to rise by as much as 6% sequentially in Q3 to add engineering headcount. That is a shift away from the cost-reduction trajectory the preview was looking to confirm, though the added spending is intended to support the pipeline.
fact_evidence: “Management guided to a sequential increase of up to 6% in Q3 to add engineering headcount to support the pipeline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says to “confirm the 8%–11% sequential decline” in non-GAAP opex and asks whether cuts have gone so deep that they impair delivery.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash at quarter-end was higher than the preview’s roughly $2.0 million estimate, at $2.8 million. That is a favorable balance-sheet difference, although the reported amount remains limited.
fact_evidence: “The company held only $2.8 million in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Cash (period end) … ~$2.0M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management disclosed a significant multi-year extension with an existing Tier 1 customer that was close to signing and expected to drive revenue growth beginning in Q3. The preview highlighted customer concentration risk but did not anticipate this specific extension.
fact_evidence: “A significant multi-year contract extension with an existing Tier 1 customer is within days of signing and is expected to generate revenue growth beginning in Q3 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flags that three customers represented “~99% of the business” and says any hint of “churn or renegotiation” at the largest account is a key risk.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The SafePath SDK/API opportunity had advanced beyond general positioning: management described one contract as near signing, alongside additional opportunities and a growing senior-focused pipeline. The preview specifically left open whether the offering would convert into pipeline or remain positioning.
fact_evidence: “New SafePath SDK/API offerings targeting carrier ‘super apps’ reaching tens of millions of subscribers are described as a high-margin future growth driver, with one contract near signing and additional opportunities including a growing senior-focused pipeline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says to look for whether the SDK/API expansion “has produced pipeline conversion or is still positioning.”

description: UHAL.B earned $0.63 per share, below the preview’s roughly $0.80 base estimate and down from $0.73 a year earlier, rather than delivering the preview’s expected year-over-year growth. The preview cautioned that reported EPS consensus was unreliable, so the comparison is to its own estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings fell to $123 million ($0.63 per nonvoting share) from $142 million ($0.73 per share) a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (UHAL.B) ~ $0.80” and “Δ YoY +10%”; the preview also said to “Treat the EPS consensus as unusable.”

description: Moving and storage costs rose sharply, cutting EBITDA margin by just over 1.5%; freight and shipping costs alone were up about $22.5 million. Management expects that freight pressure to persist through the rest of the fiscal year, whereas the preview flagged U-Box freight headwinds but did not anticipate this scale or duration of the cost drag.
fact_evidence: “Moving and storage operating expenses rose $55 million, cutting EBITDA margin by just over 1.5%,” including “~$22.5 million in higher freight and shipping costs”; freight pressure is “expected to peak in July and remain a headwind through the rest of the fiscal year.”
expectation_evidence: “U-Box. Transactions and box counts up, but revenue per transaction is falling on shorter moves, freight headwinds, and competitive intensity. … Watch for margin, not just volume.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Disposal results were far better than the preview’s expected roughly $15 million of losses: UHAL instead reported a $1.9 million gain. Management cautioned that the strong resale market may be temporary and could lead the company to hold retired units longer.
fact_evidence: “Losses on disposal of retired rental equipment improved by $24 million year-over-year, resulting in a $1.9 million gain”; management said the strong Q1 resale market “appears temporary” and may prompt holding units longer.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “disposal losses ~$15M,” and its disposal watchpoint said “Watch for losses under ~$15M.”

description: Equipment depreciation still increased $13.5 million for the quarter, above the preview’s flat-year-over-year base expectation, so the inflection was not yet fully visible in the quarterly figure. However, only $800,000 of the increase came after April, and management expects no further per-unit increases next year, tempering the shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Fleet depreciation increased $13.5 million for the quarter, but only $800,000 came after April”; management said the cargo van depreciation-driven headwinds are subsiding and “no further per-unit increases” are expected next year.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed depreciation “~flat YoY” and said “Q1 depreciation growth must be near zero or negative YoY.”

description: Equipment rental revenue grew by $29 million, a little below the preview’s $1.095 billion estimate (about $37 million above the prior-year figure). Growth across both In-Town and one-way markets and July tracking in line with Q1 were constructive, but the result did not reach the preview’s growth estimate or management’s 4.5–5% target.
fact_evidence: “Equipment rental revenues rose $29 million year-over-year with transaction and revenue growth across both In-Town and one-way markets, and July revenue tracked in line with Q1 results.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated equipment rental of “$1,095M” versus $1,058M a year earlier and said management was targeting “4.5–5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The dealer and location rollout was further along than the preview’s stated one-third progress toward the independent-dealer goal: UHAL reported being roughly halfway to its goal of net-gaining 3,000 dealers, alongside 75 net new company-operated locations.
fact_evidence: “The company added 75 net new company-operated locations and over 1,100 net independent dealers year-over-year, reaching roughly halfway toward its goal of net-gaining 3,000 independent dealers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said dealer expansion should show up in Q1 and described the company as “only one-third of the way to the dealer expansion goal.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: New storage customer rates rose about 2.5% while departing customer rates fell just under 2%, creating a positive spread that management described as unusual versus industry peers. That is more favorable pricing behavior than the preview’s concern about compressed street rates and the rate-versus-occupancy tradeoff suggested.
fact_evidence: “New customer storage rental rates rose about 2.5% year-over-year while departing customer rates fell just under 2%, an unusual positive spread versus industry peers seeing move-in rates below move-out rates.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “street rates” as “compressed” and said to watch “whether [revenue per occupied sq ft] decelerates as the rate-vs-occupancy tradeoff bites.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Dropbox added about 96,000 net new paying users sequentially, versus the preview’s expectation of roughly 10,000–14,000 additions and about 18.10 million users. It was also the third consecutive quarter of user growth, a much stronger confirmation of the recovery than the preview’s expected second positive quarter.
fact_evidence: “Dropbox added approximately 96,000 net new paying users sequentially to reach 18.9 million,” marking its “third consecutive quarter of paying user growth” and “strongest gain in about three years.”
expectation_evidence: “Paying users ~18.10M (unguided)” and “Q1 broke a multi-quarter decline with ~+10–14K net adds”; “A second consecutive positive quarter converts ‘stabilization’ into a trend.”

description: Q2 revenue was $631.5 million, above the $625.6 million consensus and the $627 million high end of company guidance that the preview treated as the functional whisper. The beat was modest, and constant-currency growth was only 0.1%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose 0.9% year-over-year to $631.5 million,” with growth of 1.7% excluding Form Swift and 0.1% on a constant-currency basis.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $625.6M” consensus; company guide “$624–627M”; “the high end of guide ($627M) as the whisper.”

description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 39.7%, above the 38.5% guide and the preview’s expected range of about 38.5%–39%. The year-over-year decline was about 180 basis points, less than the roughly 300-basis-point compression implied by the preview’s guide comparison.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 39.7%, beating guidance of 38.5%,” though it declined “roughly 180 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin ~38.5–39%”; company guide “~38.5%”; the guide “implies ~300bp of YoY compression.”

description: Dropbox raised full-year revenue guidance by $13.5 million to $2.513–$2.523 billion, putting the range above the preview’s $2.51 billion consensus and its stated $2.515 billion raise threshold. However, the increase came with only about 80 basis points of growth excluding Form Swift and was aided by a $31 million currency tailwind, so the underlying outlook remained weak.
fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was raised by $13.5 million to $2.513-$2.523 billion,” implying “only about 80 basis points” of growth excluding Form Swift and “aided by a $31 million currency tailwind.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide/consensus: Revenue $2.497–2.512B (cons. $2.51B)”; a raise “below ~$2.515B is a non-event”; the bull case calls for a raise “to ≥$2.515B.”

description: The company raised its full-year non-GAAP operating margin outlook by 50 basis points to 40.0%–40.5%, above the preview’s expected 39.5%–40.0% range.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating margin guidance by 50 basis points to 40.0%-40.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide/consensus: … non-GAAP op. margin 39.5–40%.”

description: Full-year unlevered free cash flow guidance rose by $15 million to at least $1.070 billion, above the preview’s expected floor of $1.055 billion.
fact_evidence: The company “lifted unlevered free cash flow guidance by $15 million to at or above $1.070 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide/consensus: … unlevered FCF ≥$1.055B.”

description: Gross margin fell only about 60 basis points year over year to 81.6%, a narrower decline than the 180-basis-point fall the preview cited for Q1. But management said AI compute costs would create further pressure in the second half, tempering the improvement in the margin trend.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined about 60 basis points year-over-year to 81.6% due to compute costs from AI rollout,” with “further back-half pressure partially offset by infrastructure efficiencies.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin fell 180bp YoY to 81.1%” in Q1; “The tension: is margin compression an investment cycle or structural? GM trajectory is the tell.”

description: Dropbox authorized a new $900 million share repurchase program and bought back about $315 million of shares in Q2. The new authorization was not anticipated in the preview, which highlighted concern about the pace and per-share economics of buybacks at higher prices.
fact_evidence: “The company announced a new $900 million share repurchase authorization and repurchased approximately 12.6 million shares for about $315 million in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation at 34% higher prices. Q1 retired 14.3M shares for ~$367M … Watch pace, and any commentary on leverage — the debt-funded buyback is the standing bear objection.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Simple SKU was the largest contributor to net new paying-user growth, and Teams returned to positive license growth for the first time since 2024. The preview discussed self-serve changes and Teams as possible growth drivers but did not forecast these specific results.
fact_evidence: “The ‘Simple’ SKU was the largest contributor to net new paying user growth, while Teams turned to positive license growth for the first time since 2024.”
expectation_evidence: The bull-case discussion says to watch for “Teams/self-serve pricing-and-packaging changes cited as the driver of net adds.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Integrations with Claude and ChatGPT had already attracted more than 150,000 connected users despite minimal dedicated investment. This added a concrete early usage signal for the AI ecosystem, although the facts provided do not establish AI monetization.
fact_evidence: “Integrations with tools like Claude and ChatGPT have already attracted over 150,000 connected users despite minimal dedicated investment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said there was “still no disclosed revenue contribution” from Dash and identified pricing, packaging, attach rates, or a named enterprise SKU as the major potential upside.

description: Q2 revenue was $72.8M, about 8% below the $79.4M consensus; Revuforj at $55M was below the $61–62M consensus-implied level and drove the shortfall. It was, however, close to the preview’s own $73M estimate and $55.5M Revuforj estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue was $72.8 million”; “Revuforj net revenue was $55 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus total revenue of ~$79.4M therefore implies Revuforj net revenue of ~$61–62M”; the preview’s own estimates were “$73.0M” total revenue and “$55.5M” Revuforj.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New Revuforj patient starts fell sequentially to 250, rather than growing with the NPM1 ramp the preview anticipated. Total prescriptions still rose 15% quarter over quarter, and management called the start decline a temporary anomaly.
fact_evidence: “Total Revuforj prescriptions were approximately 1,500 (up 15% QoQ), but new patient starts declined sequentially to 250, which management characterized as a temporary anomaly.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 was ~330 starts. NPM1 label came Oct 24, 2025 plus NCCN inclusion; that cohort should still be in steep ramp”; the preview’s base case expected starts to grow.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at $575M, far above the preview’s expected $305–315M, after Syndax raised $244M net from convertible notes. Management also said it remained fully funded through profitability, consistent with the preview’s runway expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $575 million in cash including $244 million net from June's $250 million 2.25% convertible notes offering, and maintains full funding through profitability.”
expectation_evidence: “Expect ~$305–315M”; the preview also said cash above $305M and reaffirmed funding through profitability would address the financing concern.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call added two Q4 pipeline events beyond the preview’s named IPF and frontline chronic GVHD readouts: a NUP98 relapsed/refractory publication and updated frontline AML trial data. These broadened the set of anticipated fourth-quarter updates, though no results were reported.
fact_evidence: “Multiple fourth-quarter catalysts are pending, including … NUP98 relapsed/refractory publication, and updated frontline AML trial data.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist named “IPF topline and frontline cGVHD” as the two 2H narrative offsets.

description: Getty reported Q2 revenue of $229.1 million, down 2.5%, versus the preview’s roughly $235 million and flat-year-over-year expectation. Revenue recognition timing added about 50 basis points, so the underlying result was weaker still.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 2.5% to $229.1 million (down 4.1% currency-neutral), with results aided by roughly 50 basis points from revenue recognition timing.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$235M … | Implied Y/Y ~0%”; “Revenue vs. consensus is the third-most important thing in this release.”

description: Getty declined to provide any earnings guidance while evaluating its capital structure, rather than reaffirming the FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges. This also left the preview’s expected H2 margin normalization unconfirmed.
fact_evidence: “The company declined to provide any earnings guidance due to the ongoing capital structure evaluation, signaling uncertainty around its financial outlook.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guide | $948–988M (reaffirmed at Q1)”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide | $279–295M”; “CFO Jennifer Leyden said margins ‘normalize to approximately 30%’ in H2.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $62.3 million, below the preview’s $64–66 million estimate, and its 27.2% margin was below the expected 27.5–28%. The decline and margin compression reflected lower revenue and higher cost of revenue.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 8.4% to $62.3 million with margin compressing to 27.2% from 28.9%, reflecting lower revenue and higher cost of revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$64–66M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~27.5–28%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Annual subscriber trends were worse than the preview’s already-negative figures: active annual subscribers were 240,000 rather than 258,000, and retention was 88.4% rather than 90%. Getty attributed the deterioration to the free-trial exit and traffic headwinds, including weaker iStock search-engine and affiliate traffic that hurt new-customer acquisition.
fact_evidence: “Annual subscription revenue retention fell to 88.4% … and active annual subscribers dropped to 240,000 from 321,000”; “iStock continued to suffer from search-engine and affiliate traffic declines hurting new customer acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: “Active annual subscribers fell to 258K from 318K Y/Y; annual subscription retention slipped to 90% LTM from 92.7%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Getty ended Q2 with only $51.6 million of cash, down $45 million from Q1, and then drew another $30 million on its revolver in July, taking the $150 million facility to its limit. That left no remaining revolver capacity, a worse liquidity position than the preview’s pro forma estimate based on the $120 million April draw.
fact_evidence: “Getty ended Q2 with only $51.6 million of balance sheet cash (down $45 million from Q1)”; “drew an additional $30 million on its revolver, maxing out the $150 million facility to bolster liquidity.”
expectation_evidence: “Pro forma for redemption and the $120M April revolver draw, gross debt is roughly $1.48B and net debt ~$1.38–1.40B”; “What matters is the cash balance and undrawn revolver capacity exiting Q2.”

description: The agency business fell 13%, a steep contraction amid secular pressure and customers producing more content internally with AI. The preview discussed AI exposure in Creative, but did not anticipate or quantify this agency decline.
fact_evidence: “The agency business declined 13% amid secular headwinds and AI-driven internal content production.”
expectation_evidence: “Creative is the structurally AI-exposed segment.”

description: Despite the subscriber-base concerns highlighted in the preview, annual subscription revenue grew 7.1% and reached 58.8% of total revenue; Premium Access grew 5.5% and its customer revenue retention was near 100%. This points to resilience in subscription revenue even as subscriber counts and overall retention weakened.
fact_evidence: “Annual subscription revenue grew 7.1% to 58.8% of total revenue, with Premium Access (over 40% of revenue) growing 5.5% and Premium Access customer revenue retention near 100%.”
expectation_evidence: “Subscriber base erosion” was ranked as a key metric to watch, with the preview noting falling active annual subscribers and retention.

description: ACV’s adjusted EBITDA was $21 million, above the preview’s $18–20 million guidance range, and EBITDA per unit reached a record, up 11% year over year. That was a stronger result than expected against a preview that anticipated Q2 margin compression.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $21 million exceeded the high end of guidance,” and “adjusted EBITDA per unit hitting a record, up 11% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 guidance itself embeds YoY margin compression ($18–20M vs $18.6M in Q2'25)” and “Adj. EBITDA: $18–20M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Rather than showing a clear unit-growth inflection, ACV cited a 600-basis-point drag on unit growth from a buyer-seller price dislocation and a 300–350-basis-point conversion-rate contraction as macro pressure affected June and July. This is a headwind to the go-to-market-driven acceleration the preview was watching for, though the facts do not state the final unit-growth rate.
fact_evidence: “A 600 basis point drag on unit growth resulted from a price dislocation between sellers and buyers, driving a 300-350 basis point conversion rate contraction as macro headwinds pressured June and July.”
expectation_evidence: “The single question the market will answer tonight: did the go-to-market spend buy units?” and “Below +3% is a red flag; above +6% resets the narrative.”

description: Revenue was $214 million, below the preview’s cited consensus estimates of about $215.5 million and $219.2 million, and its +10% growth was below the preview’s implied +11% to +13%. It nevertheless landed within company guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $214 million, up 10% year-over-year, landing within guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “~$215.5M” and “$219.2M” consensus; implied year-over-year growth of “+11% to +13%.”

description: ACV said full-year operating-expense growth would be about 6%, below the preview’s roughly 8% expectation, while still absorbing about $10 million of go-to-market investment. This implies more expense restraint and margin expansion than the preview’s baseline assumed.
fact_evidence: “Full-year OPEX growth is guided to ~6% … enabling ~100 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion even while absorbing ~$10 million of go-to-market investment.”
expectation_evidence: “non-GAAP opex growth ~8%” and “$11M of incremental go-to-market spend.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: ViPR had reached commercial availability, with more than half of the top 50 dealer groups in active conversations and management targeting 500 to potentially 1,000 units in 2027. The preview focused on 2026 deployments and did not anticipate this stated 2027 scale target.
fact_evidence: “ViPR launched commercial availability with over 50% of the top 50 dealer groups in active conversations, 100+ units being built in 2026, and management targeting 500 to potentially 1,000 units in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1: 18 deployed, ~75 backlog, 60–70 more planned in 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Five regions where ACV had added field capacity delivered mid-teens unit growth, including one region above 30%. That is evidence of productivity from the field expansion the preview said needed to start working, even as the overall unit-growth picture faced conversion pressure.
fact_evidence: “Five emerging regions where the company leaned into field capacity delivered mid-teens unit growth (one exceeding 30%).”
expectation_evidence: “Requires the field-expansion hires … to be productive within one quarter.”

description: The preview did not flag CFO Bill Zerella’s departure or Tim Fox’s succession as a Q2 development. The facts give no reason for the transition, so its implications are unclear.
fact_evidence: “CFO Bill Zerella is departing and being succeeded by Tim Fox.”

description: LENSAR reported Q2 revenue of $16.5 million, above the preview’s $14.65–$15.00 million consensus range and its $14.4 million base estimate. The roughly 10%–15% gap was a clear upside surprise.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $16.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $15.00M | $14.65M | $14.4M”; “I sit ~2–4% below the revenue consensus.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $3.6 million, far ahead of the preview’s expectation of a $0.3 million loss. This was a substantial positive gap, not merely a return to break-even.
fact_evidence: “The company delivered its strongest adjusted EBITDA to date at $3.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | … | ‑$0.3M.”

description: LENSAR swung to $3.5 million of GAAP net income, while the preview expected a GAAP loss based on consensus EPS of about negative $0.17 to negative $0.21. That reversal was a sizeable upside surprise, although the preview cautioned that GAAP EPS could be misleading.
fact_evidence: “Swung to GAAP net income of $3.5 million versus a net loss of $1.8 million in Q2 2025.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Worldwide procedure volume reached 58,682, well above the preview’s estimate of about 54,500 and the 54,000-plus level it identified as a key threshold. The actual result also showed much stronger year-over-year growth than the preview’s concern about low-single-digit growth suggested.
fact_evidence: “Procedure volume reached 58,682, up 13% year-over-year and 8% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Procedures (WW) … ~54,500”; “procedure growth reaccelerating above ~5%”; “procedures ≥54,000.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: U.S. procedure share rose to 24.1%, above the preview’s 23.4% Q1 reference and its stated watchpoint of share above 23.4%. The gain was a positive development against the preview’s concern that share had been flat.
fact_evidence: “U.S. procedure market share increased to 24.1% from 23.4% in Q1 and 21.4% in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “U.S. procedure market share was 23.4% at Q1, flat vs. Dec 31”; “U.S. share >23.4%.”

description: Gross margin was well above the preview’s 46%–49% guided band and 48% base estimate. Even excluding the $1.1 million tariff refund, margin was about 52%, so the upside was not solely the refund.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose to approximately 59% (52% excluding a $1.1 million tariff refund benefit).”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My Base Estimate | 48%”; “Gross margin vs. the 46–49% guided band.”

description: Management warned that Q3 is historically the weakest quarter for cataract procedures because of holidays and summer vacations. The preview did not flag this seasonal caution, adding a near-term headwind to the otherwise strong procedure results.
fact_evidence: “Q3 is historically the seasonally weakest quarter for cataract procedures due to holidays and summer vacations.”

description: Management said it plans to modestly increase commercial spending and make its first-ever direct appearance at ESCRS to expand in Europe. The preview discussed rebuilding after the merger but did not anticipate this specific commercial investment or event presence.
fact_evidence: “Management plans to modestly increase commercial spending, including a first-ever direct presence at ESCRS in Q3 to expand in Europe.”

description: Q2 revenue was $4.4 million, well below the preview’s roughly $7.0 million consensus and its $5.4 million base estimate. It also declined 12% year over year, rather than the preview’s base case of 9% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 12% year-over-year to $4.4 million from $5.0 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “~$7.0M” and a “Q2 FY26E (base)” total of “~$5.4M” with “+9% y/y.”

description: LiqTech cut its full-year 2026 revenue range to $20–23 million from $23–27 million, rather than reaffirming the range the preview identified as the primary swing factor. The company attributed the cut to a major Water for Energy project delay after the customer restarted its internal approval process.
fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $20-23 million after a major Water for Energy project was delayed due to a customer's organizational change that restarted its internal approval process.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “reaffirmed $23–27M twice” and framed the key question as “reaffirm, trim, or cut.”

description: Commercial Pool did achieve a record quarter, but its $1.5 million revenue was below the preview’s $1.8 million segment estimate. It met the preview’s roughly $1.5 million credibility threshold, while falling short of the modeled ramp.
fact_evidence: “Commercial Pool achieved record quarterly revenue of $1.5 million, nearly doubling from $0.8 million in both Q2 2025 and Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Commercial Pool at “$1.8M” for Q2, and said a result “under ~$1.5M” would break credibility on order-book conversion.

description: Gross margin was only 8.4%, far below the preview’s base expectation of 20% and even below its 15% level flagged as undermining the unit-economics story. The reported explanation—unfavorable mix and low utilization—also points to weaker fixed-cost absorption than expected.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 8.4% from 9.8% a year earlier, remaining below the level needed to fully absorb fixed production costs, reflecting unfavorable product mix and lower manufacturing utilization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed “20%” gross margin, said “>20% is on-track,” and warned that “<15% on a record pool quarter undermines the entire unit-economics story.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.6 million, substantially worse than the preview’s base estimate of negative $0.85 million and slightly worse than its negative $1.55 million bear case. The preview had no published consensus for this measure, so the gap is against its scenario estimates.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to negative $1.6 million from negative $1.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated adjusted EBITDA of “$(0.85)M” and its bear scenario “$(1.55)M.”

description: Marine revenue was $0.7 million, below the preview’s $1.0 million estimate despite year-over-year growth. The four-system China EGR order was already anticipated, so the surprise is the weaker quarterly revenue contribution.
fact_evidence: “Marine revenue rose to $0.7 million from $0.4 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment build estimated Marine revenue at “$1.0M” for Q2.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash including restricted cash reached $15.7 million, above the preview’s estimated $12–13 million pro forma balance, and the company repaid senior promissory notes and original issue discount notes. The cash comparison is approximate because the reported figure includes restricted cash.
fact_evidence: “A June underwritten public offering generated approximately $18 million in net proceeds, boosting cash including restricted cash to $15.7 million from $2.7 million at the end of Q1, and enabled repayment of senior promissory notes and original issue discount notes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$12–13M cash” after the offering and expected “~$4.1M” of senior-debt repayment.

description: Gran Tierra entered an agreement to sell all of its Colombia and Ecuador oil businesses, a transaction the preview did not anticipate. The sale requires special stockholder approval, and management gave no details, so its implications remain uncertain.
fact_evidence: “entered a definitive share purchase agreement to sell all of its Colombia and Ecuador oil businesses”; the transaction requires “special stockholder approval,” and management declined to discuss details.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was about $6 million, well below the preview’s expected $25–35 million. The preview expected a strongly positive quarter, while reported capex was also higher than modeled.
fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was approximately $6 million,” compared with $2.7 million in Q2 2025; capex rose to $54 million from $45 million in the prior quarter.
expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow … Q2/26E: +$25 to +$35M”; the scenario table also expected “FCF … +$25–35M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Production averaged about 41,500 barrels per day, below the preview’s 43,000–44,000 estimate. The reported shortfall reflected Canadian dispositions and temporary artificial-lift failures at Acordionero and Cohembí.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 average working interest production was approximately 41,500 barrels per day, down 9% sequentially and 12% year-over-year,” reflecting “Canadian dispositions and temporary artificial lift system failures at Acordionero and Cohembí.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 production … 43.0–44.0 Mboe/d”; the model used “Production … Q2/26E: 43,500.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $85 million, below the preview’s $90–100 million estimate, though above the preview’s stated threshold for a more severe hedge-related shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $85 million,” from $74 million in the prior quarter and $77 million in Q2 2025.
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … $90–100M”; the preview said “Below $85M = the hedge book is worse than modeled.”

description: Net income was $25 million, below the preview’s expected $40–80 million profit. The preview attributed its anticipated larger profit mainly to an unrealized derivative reversal; the call instead cited stronger commodity prices and lower operating costs as drivers of the reported turnaround.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $25 million,” versus a $119 million loss in the prior quarter, “driven by stronger commodity prices and lower operating costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Net income … +$40 to +$80M”; the preview said the gain was “Driven by unrealized derivative reversal, not operations.”

description: Capex reached $54 million, above the preview’s $38–45 million estimate. The call said spending was elevated because the capital program was weighted toward the first half.
fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures rising to $54 million from $45 million in the prior quarter due to a first-half-weighted capital program.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net debt was $479 million, essentially flat with Q1’s $481 million and above the preview’s roughly $450 million base-scenario expectation. The modest reduction was less deleveraging than that scenario anticipated.
fact_evidence: “$127 million cash, $606 million total gross debt, and $479 million net debt,” plus $53 million of undrawn credit facilities.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net debt (Q1): $481M” and its base scenario expected “net debt to ~$450M.”

description: The company bought back an additional $50 million face value of its 9.75% notes after quarter-end at a 10% discount. The preview anticipated further discounted note repurchases but did not suggest a buyback of this size.
fact_evidence: It “bought back an additional $50 million face value at a 10% discount after quarter-end”; it had also repurchased $6 million face value during the first half at a 12% discount.
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for further open-market note repurchases” and listed “incremental note buybacks” in its bull scenario.

description: The $123 million Suroriente capital carry commitment was completed, with the post-carry period beginning July 18 and expected to improve the block’s economics and cash generation. The preview did not flag this milestone.
fact_evidence: “completed its $123 million capital carry commitment in Suroriente,” with “the post-carry period beginning July 18 and expected to improve economics and cash generation on the block.”

description: The lodgepole sale removed $13 million of asset retirement obligations while generating $9 million and shedding about 850 barrels per day of production; the company characterized the result as a net benefit. This disposition was not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The lodgepole disposition sold a 54% working interest for $9 million while removing $13 million in asset retirement obligations and roughly 850 barrels per day of production, resulting in a net benefit to the company.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: New resource reports assigned Canadian assets about 6.5 million barrels of 2C contingent resources and 67 million barrels of combined unrisked best-estimate prospective resources, with drilling planned for 2027. The preview did not discuss these resource estimates or plans.
fact_evidence: “New McDaniel resource reports assigned Canadian assets approximately 6.5 million barrels of 2C contingent resources and about 67 million barrels of combined unrisked best-estimate prospective resources across Dawson Clearwater and Mount Head, with drilling planned for 2027.”

description: Political advertising was $147 million, at the top of the preview’s $120–150 million base case, but management said pacing was running ahead of expectations and that internal targets had been raised multiple times. That forward-pacing commentary was stronger than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Q2 political advertising reached $147 million” and management indicated “internal political targets have been raised multiple times with pacing running ahead of expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “My base case is $120–150M combined”; the preview also said “Q3/Q4 pacing commentary” mattered.

description: Nexstar repaid $409 million of debt in Q2, more than the roughly $332 million of paydowns the preview cited through April 30 and post-quarter. The faster repayment is a positive difference in the deleveraging cadence.
fact_evidence: “The company repaid $409 million of debt in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “quarterly debt paydown ($182M through April 30 plus $150M post-quarter)”

description: Although the preview expected management to maintain its no-guidance posture, the call gave a Q3 nonpolitical advertising outlook: a mid-single-digit decline, slightly better than Q2. The decline remains weak, but the modest improvement and added forward detail were not expected.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 nonpolitical advertising is guided to decline mid-single digits but slightly better than Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Management gave no forward guidance on the Q1 call, citing litigation constraints. Expect the same posture.”

description: Distribution performance was split: legacy Nexstar distribution revenue rose 3.1%, but TEGNA distribution revenue declined while it remained on its own contracts. That TEGNA weakness contrasts with the preview’s expectation that renewal-rate gains would push combined distribution revenue ahead of subscriber erosion; the call facts do not provide a combined growth figure to measure the overall result.
fact_evidence: “TEGNA distribution revenue declined year-over-year because it continues operating under its own contracts rather than Nexstar's, whereas legacy Nexstar distribution revenue rose 3.1% ($23 million).”
expectation_evidence: “2026 carries a heavy retrans renewal cycle that should push rate ahead of the ~6–8% subscriber erosion”; “Anything below ~+1% YoY pro-forma is a problem.”

description: Management added a specific full-year CW loss outlook—losses are expected to improve by more than 30%—beyond the preview’s focus on the Q4 profitability target. This gives a more favorable quantified view of the path toward profitability.
fact_evidence: “The CW remains on track for profitability in Q4 2026 with full-year losses expected to improve by more than 30%.”
expectation_evidence: “CW is still guided to Q4 2026 profitability — a reiteration matters.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The call highlighted a planned Nielsen local-measurement change that could significantly boost local ad impressions, an incremental potential advertising benefit the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “A planned August 31 Nielsen local measurement change lowering the viewing threshold from 5 minutes to 1 minute could significantly boost local ad impressions.”

description: Revenue was $372 million versus preview consensus of about $300–302 million, and diluted EPS was $1.51 versus $0.53 expected. The large beat was substantially driven by the European ERC increase.
fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to PRA rose to $58 million, or $1.51 per diluted share,” with the European ERC increase “driving total revenues up 29% to $372 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $300.0M (MarketBeat) / $301.6M (Investing.com)” and “Diluted EPS: $0.53.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Cash collections reached $559 million, below the preview’s modeled $570–585 million and up 4% year over year, below the preview’s +6% threshold for maintaining the growth narrative. The company nevertheless said collections were 4% above its own expectations.
fact_evidence: “Cash collections grew 4% year-over-year to $559 million” and “total collections came in 4% above the company's expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash collections (~$570–585M base)” and “anything under +6% Y/Y breaks the two-year compounding narrative.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: PRA increased European ERC by $349 million after a portfolio review, an unanticipated upward revision that management said reflects repeated overperformance. It expects about $260 million of additional portfolio income over the remaining cash curves, although the near-term annualized contribution is about $25 million and the 2026 net income effect is nominal.
fact_evidence: “The company increased its European ERC by $349 million” following “26 consecutive quarters of overperformance,” and expects “approximately $260 million of additional portfolio income” over the remaining life of the cash curves, with “only nominal net income impact in 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “ERC: ~$8.6–8.8B modeled” and the preview identified changes in expected recoveries as a swing factor, but gave no expectation of a European ERC write-up.

description: Beyond the legal-cost moderation already anticipated, PRA announced a second wave of cost reductions expected to produce about $20 million of annualized net savings, bringing the two waves to roughly $35 million annually.
fact_evidence: “A second wave of cost reductions eliminated 100 U.S. corporate/overhead roles and 35 offshore roles,” expected to generate “about $20 million in annualized net savings,” with combined savings of “approximately $35 million annualized.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed expected moderation in legal collection cost growth, but did not anticipate a second wave of workforce reductions or these savings.

description: The Board authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million, a larger formal authorization than the preview’s reference point of only $10 million repurchased in Q1 and its call for a possible step-up in buybacks.
fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million,” after “$10 million repurchased in the quarter and $40 million over the past 12 months.”
expectation_evidence: “Only $10M repurchased in Q1” and “any step-up in buyback authorization or pace is an outsized catalyst.”

description: PRA refinanced its $730 million European credit facility and extended its maturity by five years, leaving no debt maturities until February 2028; this refinancing and maturity extension were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company refinanced its $730 million European credit facility extending maturity by 5 years with no debt maturities until February 2028.”

description: OXY reported adjusted EPS of $2.40, well above the preview’s $1.84–$1.88 cluster and even its $2.10–$2.25 bull case. The preview expected a strong windfall quarter, but the reported result exceeded its high-end scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q2 delivered adjusted EPS of $2.40”
expectation_evidence: “Working range | $1.66 – $1.96 (cluster $1.84–$1.88)” and the bull scenario projected “Adj. EPS $2.10–2.25.”

description: Midstream and marketing earnings were far above the preview’s $350–550 million Q2 guidance range: OXY reported about $960 million, more than twice the range’s midpoint, and raised full-year segment guidance by $300 million.
fact_evidence: “Midstream and marketing set a record with ~$960 million in adjusted earnings, more than double guidance midpoint, prompting a $300 million increase to full-year segment guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Company guidance for Q2 ... midstream & marketing pre-tax income $350–550M”; the preview also flagged this segment as a potential upside surprise.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: OXY’s debt ended at $11.8 billion, above the preview’s expected $10.5–11.5 billion range. The $1.5 billion reduction was substantial, but left debt slightly higher than the preview’s anticipated range.
fact_evidence: “Occidental reduced principal debt by $1.5 billion to $11.8 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “That could put principal debt at $10.5–11.5B.”

description: OXY announced a further 8% quarterly dividend increase, taking the dividend to $0.28 per share. The preview listed the existing $0.26 dividend and emphasized uncertainty about a formal capital-return framework, but did not anticipate another dividend hike.
fact_evidence: “The Board approved an 8% increase to the quarterly dividend to $0.28 per share, enabled by structural interest savings.”
expectation_evidence: “Dividend | $0.26/qtr (raised 8% after Q4'25).”

description: OXY laid out a new plan to add more than $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030 versus 2025, with about half of the improvement expected in 2026–27. The preview focused on the Q2 windfall and near-term capital-return choices, not this longer-term cash-flow roadmap.
fact_evidence: “Oxy laid out a plan to add over $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030 versus 2025”; “roughly $2 billion (about 50%) ... will be captured between 2026 and 2027.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: OXY reported Q2 production at the top of its guided range, 23,000 BOE/day above the midpoint despite Middle East disruptions. The preview’s base case was about 1.405–1.420 million BOE/day, so the result was stronger than that central expectation, though within the stated guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 production averaged 1.43 million BOE/day, exceeding the guidance midpoint by 23,000 BOE/day, driven by Permian and Gulf of America strength offsetting Middle East disruptions.”
expectation_evidence: “Company guidance for Q2 ... total production 1,390–1,430 Mboed”; the base scenario expected “Production ~1,405–1,420.”

description: OXY provided a 2027 starting point of $5.9 billion in capital spending, implying roughly flat production versus 2026, while about $400 million of Stratos LCV capital rolls off beginning next year. The preview gave 2026 capital guidance but no 2027 spending or production outlook.
fact_evidence: “2027 capital spending starting point is $5.9 billion (~$5.0-5.1 billion sustaining) implying roughly flat production versus 2026, while Stratos LCV capital of ~$400 million rolls off beginning next year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 capex guidance of “$5.5–5.9B” but did not provide a 2027 outlook.

description: RPID reported a $12.9 million net loss, versus the preview’s roughly $12.0 million consensus estimate and $11.9 million estimate. That was a worse loss than expected, although the preview had warned that a bottom-line miss was a key risk.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $12.9 million from $11.9 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Net loss | ~$12.0M” and “My estimate | –$11.9M.”

description: The company’s funding plan appears more conditional and smaller than the preview’s $25 million of undrawn Trinity capacity: management is relying on a $10 million tranche later this year, a *potential* $10 million tranche in mid-2027, and warrant exercises. The preview explicitly questioned whether the remaining facility was gated, but the call facts do not establish access to the full $25 million.
fact_evidence: “Management is relying on a $10 million debt tranche from Trinity Capital later this year, a potential second $10 million tranche in mid-2027, and warrant exercises to fund a path to positive cash flow by end of 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “$25M undrawn under the Trinity Capital facility” and “Key call question: what conditions gate the remaining $25M?”

description: Recurring revenue growth slowed to 14%, and consumables growth was over 20%—below the preview’s 25%+ benchmark for evidence of durable installed-base growth. Consumables still set quarterly records, but the reported pace was weaker than the preview’s hoped-for confirmation.
fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue rose 14% to $5 million while consumable revenue grew over 20% and hit new quarterly records.”
expectation_evidence: “A second consecutive 25%+ consumables quarter is the strongest evidence” and “Consumables/recurring growth ≥25%.”

description: MilliporeSigma’s contribution is expected to build meaningfully in the second half and into 2027, but the partnership will not fully meet its calendar-year commitment. That leaves a timing shortfall even as management describes improving contribution ahead.
fact_evidence: “The MilliporeSigma partnership contributed to first-half placements and is expected to increase meaningfully in the second half and into 2027, though it will not fully deliver on its calendar-year commitment.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: RPID ended the quarter with about $20 million in cash and short-term investments, well above the preview’s roughly $14 million estimate. The higher balance indicates less cash depletion than the preview’s base case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only about $20 million in cash and short-term investments.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash & investments (EOQ) | ~$14M.”

description: Management set explicit longer-term targets that the preview had not anticipated: average annual revenue growth above 20% and gross margin above 50% exiting 2028, with 2027 gross margin expected to exceed the 2026 exit rate. These targets extend the outlook beyond the preview’s focus on the FY26 and Q4 margin bridge.
fact_evidence: “Management set long-term targets of greater than 20% average annual revenue growth and 50%+ gross margin exiting 2028, with 2027 gross margin expected to exceed the 2026 exit rate.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company raised its full-year validation target to at least 27 systems, above the preview’s cited target of at least 25. This improves the expected validation pace, while the full-year revenue and placement guidance remained unchanged.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year validation guidance to at least 27 systems while reaffirming full-year revenue guidance of $37–41 million and 30–38 system placements.”
expectation_evidence: “Validations are the other tell: 5 completed in Q1 against a ≥25 FY target.”

description: Management announced a new efficiency program expected to reduce expenses and cash usage by about $1 million for the rest of 2026 and roughly $3 million annually from 2027. The preview discussed the need for opex discipline but did not flag this specific additional savings program.
fact_evidence: “A newly executed efficiency program is expected to cut expenses and cash usage by roughly $1 million for the rest of 2026 and about $3 million annually beginning in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Clean run-rate needs ~$12.5M/quarter to stay inside the guide.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 TTV was about $169 million, far below the preview’s $350–550 million base-case range and below its roughly $400 million threshold for keeping the ramp plausible. Bakkt nevertheless kept its $2.5 billion full-year target unchanged, leaving about $2.1 billion to be achieved in the second half.
fact_evidence: “Second quarter total transacting volume (TTV) was approximately $169 million, with first-half TTV of approximately $410 million, meaning the company must achieve roughly $2.1 billion in the second half to hit its unchanged full-year target of ~$2.5 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “TTV $350–550M — directionally up but back-end-loaded”; “A Q2 TTV below ~$400M makes the $2.5B exit rate arithmetically implausible and should force a reset.”

description: GAAP EPS was $1.94, dramatically above the preview’s $0.03 consensus, although the preview anticipated that positive EPS could come from non-cash strategic-asset marks. The reported profit was largely driven by the Transchem warrant fair-value remeasurement rather than operating performance, so the source of the gain was expected but its reported size was not.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP net income of $80.8 million with diluted EPS of $1.94, though this was largely driven by the Transchem warrant fair value re-measurement rather than operating performance.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS +$0.03”; “Any positive EPS this quarter will almost certainly come from non-cash mark-to-market gains on the Bakkt Global strategic holdings.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and restricted cash ended the quarter at $50.7 million, down from the $82.6 million cash balance the preview cited at March 31.
