fact_evidence: “The Big Crispy chicken sandwich drove sales from 20 sandwiches per restaurant per day pre-launch to 55 by the end of Q4, a 175% increase that continues to build.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the sandwich was “at +161% vs. pre-launch sales after two weeks” and described Q4 as the first full read on “whether that's incremental traffic or mix cannibalization.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Chili’s average annual unit volumes reached $5 million, up from just over $4.5 million, while restaurants were still operating at only 80% of historical guest capacity. The preview discussed reimages and unit-growth economics but did not anticipate or quantify this AUV and capacity update.
fact_evidence: “Chili's average annual unit volumes rose from just over $4.5 million to $5 million year-over-year, with restaurants still operating at only 80% of historical guest capacity.”

description: Brinker said the Maggiano’s turnaround was slower than planned and FY27 guidance assumes flat revenues and profits. The preview highlighted the risk of further deterioration and the possibility of stabilization, but did not forecast a flat FY27 outlook.
fact_evidence: “Maggiano's turnaround has been slower than planned… with fiscal '27 guidance assuming flat revenues and flat profits year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any sign of stabilization is a quiet margin tailwind; further deterioration invites strategic-review questions.”

description: The company raised its total share-repurchase authorization to $750 million, which was not specifically anticipated in the preview. The reported $100 million of Q4 repurchases and nearly $400 million for the year add context, but the larger authorization is the distinct new capital-allocation update.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $100 million of stock in Q4 (nearly $400 million for the year), raised total buyback authorization to $750 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$108M repurchased in Q3” and discussed the planned bond call, but gave no expectation for a higher repurchase authorization.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 adjusted free cash flow was $1.7 billion, below the preview’s estimated $1.8–$2.0 billion. That is a modest shortfall against the preview estimate, although the call did not explain the gap.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 generated $1.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: “I estimate Q2 FCF of ~$1.8–2.0B.”

description: Q2 capital spending was $1.3 billion, above the preview’s modeled $1.15–$1.25 billion. It was still 2.4% below the company-guidance midpoint, so the miss against the preview estimate was limited rather than a company-guidance overrun.
fact_evidence: “Q2 capital of $1.3 billion coming in 2.4% below the guidance midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “I model ~$1.15–1.25B” for Q2 capex.

description: Devon completed its full $1.25 billion 2026 debt-reduction target by July, earlier than the preview’s expectation of completing that amount over the year. The amount was expected; the early completion was the positive difference.
fact_evidence: “The company completed its full $1.25 billion 2026 debt reduction target,” including “the remaining $750 million term loan in July.”
expectation_evidence: “$1.25B of 2026 debt retirement.”

description: Management reaffirmed the $1 billion annual synergy target for year-end 2027, as expected, but added that more than 350 initiatives have been identified to support it. That supplies more execution detail than the preview’s base case, which expected no new synergy number or detail.
fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed at least $1 billion in annual synergy targets by year-end 2027, now backed by more than 350 identified initiatives.”
expectation_evidence: “Base — ‘on track,’ reaffirmed FY ranges, no new numbers”; the preview also described the target as “$1.0B run-rate by YE2027.”

description: Devon disclosed a New Mexico federal lease sale adding 400 Delaware locations, an acquisition the preview did not flag. Management framed the $6.5 million headline cost per location as about $4 million per premium location after adjusting for the lower royalty burden; the added inventory is positive, while the upfront price makes the news mixed.
fact_evidence: “The New Mexico federal lease sale added 400 top-tier Delaware locations at a headline $6.5 million per location,” which management said “equates to an effective ~$4 million per premium location after accounting for the lower 12.5% royalty burden.”

description: The call offered stronger and more specific operating-efficiency evidence than the preview anticipated: Delaware drilling costs were already $800 per foot before most synergies, and second-half capital efficiency was described as 24% better than the peer average. The preview watched unit costs and spending discipline but did not anticipate these benchmarks.
fact_evidence: “Delaware D&C costs are already at $800 per foot on a 9-12 month trailing basis before most synergies are captured”; “second-half capital efficiency is claimed to be 24% better than the peer average on a 20:1 basis.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Unit costs vs. FY guide” and said “G&A is where synergies show up first,” but gave no expectation for these Delaware D&C or peer-efficiency benchmarks.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Devon disclosed encouraging results from surfactant trials and the scale of its automated gas-lift program, neither of which the preview anticipated. The reported well uplift and existing deployment suggest operational upside, although the call did not quantify the resulting financial impact.
fact_evidence: “90% of tested wells” had “material uplift exceeding 15% at 180 days,” prompting expansion to “more than 50 wells this year”; AI-enabled closed-loop gas lift “autonomously optimizes 1,000 wells with over 2,000 more targeted in the Permian.”

description: The preview estimated Q2 revenue at about $31.95 million; ARS reported $33.7 million, about 5% above that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue was $33.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $31.95M (6 analysts)”

description: The preview’s cost build assumed roughly $8 million of COGS and a Q1-like gross margin near 72%. Q2 gross margin was about 62%, with short-dated product reserves, manufacturing inefficiencies, and ex-U.S. launch costs cited as pressures.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin was about 62% in Q2 and over 64% year-to-date, pressured by reserves for short-dated product, manufacturing inefficiencies, and ex-US launch costs, but expected to improve in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “My EPS build: revenue $32M, COGS ~$8M (Q1 gross margin ~72%).”

description: The preview estimated Q2 SG&A at about $70 million, while reported SG&A was roughly $77.6 million. That was a material cost overrun against the preview’s quarterly expense build, separate from the weaker gross margin.
fact_evidence: “Total operating expenses were $95.1 million, including $12.8 million in cost of goods sold and roughly $77.6 million in SG&A.”
expectation_evidence: “My EPS build: revenue $32M, COGS ~$8M, SG&A ~$70M, R&D ~$5M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview modeled Q2 cash near $155–160 million; ARS ended the quarter with $143.8 million, roughly $11–16 million below that estimate. The company nevertheless continued to project cash-flow break-even by the end of 2027, as the preview expected.
fact_evidence: “ARS ended Q2 with $143.8 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments and projects reaching cash flow break-even by the end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 burn of ~$40–45M puts cash near ~$155–160M at 6/30/26”; the preview also flagged “the 2027 breakeven reaffirmation.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected the CSU Phase 2b interim readout in Q4 2026. Management pushed it to Q1 2027 because patients need time to log three separate flare episodes.
fact_evidence: “The CSU Phase 2b interim data readout has been delayed from end of 2026 to Q1 2027 due to the time required for patients to log three separate flare episodes.”
expectation_evidence: “CSU Phase 2b interim, Q4 2026.”

description: The preview anticipated a soft or absent formal guide and emphasized cost discipline generally. Instead, ARS gave a specific H2 cash-based SG&A and R&D range of $100–110 million and said cash-based SG&A would fall more than 40% from H1, with the trend continuing through 2027.
fact_evidence: “The company guided second-half 2026 cash-based SG&A and R&D expenses to $100-110 million, driven by a more than 40% reduction in cash-based SG&A from the first half, with the trend expected to continue through 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “soft/no formal FY guide”; the preview described the bull case as “deeper opex cuts extend runway.”

description: The preview estimated Q2 U.S. net product revenue of about $27–29 million. ARS reported $26.2 million, slightly below that estimate, though within the preview’s $26–29 million base-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 U.S. net product revenue was $26.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026E … neffy U.S. net product … ~$27–29M (my est.)”; the base scenario gave “neffy U.S. | $26–29M.”

description: The preview focused on whether the company would make cost and strategic changes, but did not anticipate a specific move away from broad direct-to-consumer TV advertising. ARS said it was shifting toward lower-cost, targeted provider-focused channels such as social media and search; the savings goal is positive, while the effectiveness of the new approach is not yet established.
fact_evidence: “The company is pivoting away from broad direct-to-consumer TV advertising toward lower-cost, targeted provider-focused channels like social media and search to improve SG&A efficiency.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the call would outline “updated strategic priorities” and highlighted cost discipline and sales-force sizing, but did not identify this advertising shift.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview did not provide a specific market-share expectation. ARS reported that total U.S. NEPI share reached 5%, double the prior-year quarter, and that share in the targeted sales-force universe rose to 8% from 4%, compared with roughly 1% in non-targeted areas.
fact_evidence: “Total U.S. NEPI market share reaching 5%, doubling from 2.5% in the prior-year quarter”; “Within the field sales targeted universe, NEPI market share rose to 8% from 4% a year ago, versus roughly 1% share in non-targeted areas.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview did not forecast a prescriber count. ARS said unique NEPI prescribers exceeded 16,000 in Q2, more than tripling from the year-earlier quarter, a concrete sign of adoption beyond the revenue estimates in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Unique NEPI prescribers exceeded 16,000 in Q2, representing more than a three-fold increase versus the same period last year.”

description: Heritage earned $2.05 per diluted share, well above the preview’s functional whisper of $1.40–$1.50 and even above its bull-case range of $1.70–$1.85.
fact_evidence: Heritage reported Q2 net income of $61.7 million, or $2.05 diluted EPS.
expectation_evidence: “Treat $1.40–$1.50 as the functional whisper”; the bull scenario projected “$1.70–$1.85.”

description: Underwriting results were much stronger than the preview’s already favorable base case: the combined ratio was 64.9% versus an estimate of about 74.6%, and the net loss ratio was 30.4% versus about 40%.
fact_evidence: “The combined ratio improved to 64.9% from 72.9%, and the net loss ratio improved to 30.4% from 38.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The base case projected a “~74.6%” combined ratio and “~40%” net loss ratio; even the bull case projected a 68–71% combined ratio.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Favorable prior-period reserve development was substantially larger than the preview’s bull-case assumption, adding to the unusually strong quarter’s underwriting result.
fact_evidence: Heritage reported “$23.4 million of favorable prior period reserve development (versus $2.3 million a year earlier).”
expectation_evidence: The bull case assumed “favorable PYD >$8M”; the base case assumed “minimal PYD.”

description: Premium momentum did not turn as the preview hoped: gross premiums written fell 5.5% rather than reaching the expected roughly $400 million or turning positive, while premiums in force also remained down. Net premiums earned were below the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Gross premiums written fell 5.5% to $380.4 million,” premiums in force “declined 1.4% to $1.41 billion,” and net premiums earned were $201.1 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross premiums written at “~$400M,” said a positive print would validate the growth-inflection thesis, and estimated net premiums earned at “~$205M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Heritage disclosed plans for Florida rate reductions of 3%–5%, while the preview had identified how much of the reinsurance savings might be passed through to policyholders as an unresolved issue. Management expects other states’ increases to roughly match claims inflation and keep margins flat.
fact_evidence: “Management expects Florida rate reductions in the 3%-5% range driven by lower reinsurance costs, while other states should see modest rate increases roughly matching claims inflation to keep margins flat.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said it was unknown “how much drops to the bottom line vs. gets passed to policyholders in rate filings.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Book value per share finished above the preview’s estimate, at $19.09 rather than about $18.40.
fact_evidence: “Book value per share rose to $19.09.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 book value per share at “~$18.40.”

description: Tandem’s implied U.S. sales were about $180 million ($255 million worldwide less $75 million international), above the preview’s roughly $175 million expectation and at its $180 million bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: Worldwide Q2 sales were $255 million and international sales were $75 million, implying about $180 million of U.S. sales.
expectation_evidence: The preview lists U.S. sales of “~$175M” and says “If US comes in at $178M+, the PayGo drag is proving smaller than feared”; its bull case uses “US Rev | $180M+.”

description: Gross margin reached 57%, above the preview’s 55–56% consensus range and its 56% threshold for de-risking the full-year margin ramp.
fact_evidence: Gross margin reached 57%, improving 5 percentage points year-over-year and 2 points sequentially.
expectation_evidence: The preview gives “Gross margin … ~55–56%” consensus and says “A Q2 print ≥56% de-risks that.”

description: International sales were $75 million, below the preview’s roughly $80 million expectation, even though international pump shipments grew 19%. The company cited distributor inventory buyback headwinds.
fact_evidence: International sales rose 7% to $75 million, with approximately $3 million of distributor inventory buyback headwinds; shipments grew 19%.
expectation_evidence: The preview lists international sales at “~$80M” and “+13.5%” year-over-year, and flags distributor destocking as a risk.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Pharmacy adoption was ahead of the preview’s stated penetration checkpoints: pharmacy shipments and sales each reached about 10% of the U.S. total, above the preview’s >8% sales checkpoint and its sub-5% Q1 pump-order baseline.
fact_evidence: In the first full PAYGO quarter, pharmacy pump shipments and pharmacy sales each reached approximately 10% of the U.S. total.
expectation_evidence: The preview gives Q1 baselines of “6% of US sales” and “<5% of pump orders via pharmacy,” and lists “pharmacy % of US sales >8%” as a catalyst checkpoint.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Formulary coverage reached about 45%, improving from the preview’s roughly 40% baseline but short of its >50% checkpoint. Coverage across the top three PBMs is in place, but the preview’s numerical milestone was not yet reached.
fact_evidence: Formulary coverage was approximately 45%, already approaching the high end of the company’s target range for the year, with contracts in place across the top three PBMs.
expectation_evidence: The preview gives a Q1 baseline of “~40% formulary coverage” and says to watch whether coverage “crosses 50%”; its catalyst checklist says “Pharmacy coverage >50%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: International direct-channel sales more than doubled to about 13% of international revenue, showing substantial channel progress despite the distributor transition and buyback headwind the preview expected to weigh on near-term results.
fact_evidence: Direct-channel sales more than doubled to approximately 13% of international revenue, despite approximately $3 million of distributor inventory buyback headwinds.
expectation_evidence: The preview says the “distributor→direct in Europe” transition depresses reported revenue near-term and flags distributor destocking as a risk.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Net favorable pricing contributed more than half of sales growth despite an approximately $8 million initial pharmacy-pump headwind, a better offset to the transition drag than the preview’s discussion of near-term revenue pressure implied.
fact_evidence: The initial pharmacy pump headwind was approximately $8 million in Q2, but net favorable pricing still drove more than half of total sales growth.
expectation_evidence: The preview says the PayGo pharmacy transition depresses reported revenue near-term and asks whether its headwind scales with adoption; it gives no pricing contribution estimate.

description: Stock-based compensation fell materially and the full-year expectation was reduced to about $65 million from about $80 million, helping operating margin improve by 8 points to negative 5%. This cost reduction was not part of the preview’s stated margin expectations.
fact_evidence: Stock-based compensation fell to $16 million, or 6% of sales versus 11%, and full-year expectations were lowered to approximately $65 million from approximately $80 million, helping drive an 8-point improvement in operating margin to negative 5%.

description: The preview derived a Q3 revenue guide midpoint of about $33.9 million, but Blend guided to $31.5–33.5 million, a midpoint of $32.5 million. Management cited weaker macro conditions, making the outlook meaningfully softer than the preview’s bar.
fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 revenue of $31.5-33.5 million (negative 4% to positive 2% year-over-year)”; the guide reflects “a weaker macro.”
expectation_evidence: “Derived bar for the Q3 guide: ... implying a Q3 revenue guide midpoint of ~$33.9M (+3% Y/Y).”

description: Q2 non-GAAP operating income was $7 million, above both the preview’s roughly $6 million consensus and the top of Blend’s $5.5–6.5 million guide. That was a stronger profitability result than expected even though revenue was only modestly above consensus.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $7 million exceeded the top of its $5.5-6.5 million guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income | ~$6.0M (guide mid)” and “OI above $6.5M on in-line revenue ... [would] prove[] the 80% gross margin is structural.”

description: Q2 revenue of $33.8 million beat the preview’s $33.08 million consensus, although it remained within Blend’s guidance range rather than reaching the preview’s bull-case threshold. The beat was positive but relatively small.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $33.8 million, up 7% year-over-year and near the high end of the $32-34 million guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $33.08M” consensus; the preview’s bull case was “$34.3M+.”

description: Blend now expects Q4 funded loan volume to fall 10–15% year over year to 180,000–190,000 loans. The preview noted a large-customer roll-off risk and cited a market-growth forecast, but did not anticipate a contraction of this size in Q4 volume.
fact_evidence: “Q4 funded loan volume is expected to decline approximately 10-15% year-over-year to 180,000-190,000 loans,” reflecting “a projected 11% market contraction and the final roll-off of a previously disclosed large customer.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited management’s anchor of “Fannie Mae's ~19% Y/Y market volume growth forecast” and said to watch for confirmation that the large-customer “volume roll-off” was contained.

description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 78.3%, below the roughly 80% level the preview treated as structural. The year-over-year improvement was positive, but the reported margin did not reach that expected level.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 78.3% from 76.1% a year earlier despite growing Autopilot model costs.”
expectation_evidence: “OI above $6.5M on in-line revenue proves the 80% gross margin is structural.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Autopilot had six paying contracts, including Onity, and had processed more than 45,000 loans, ahead of the preview’s reference to five commercial customers and 25,500-plus loans. Blend also disclosed quantified early customer gains in pull-through, cycle time, and task automation, beyond the preview’s general expectation of faster, higher-converting loans.
fact_evidence: “Autopilot became commercially available July 1st, has processed over 45,000 cumulative loans since February, activated 65+ lenders, and already signed six paying contracts including major servicer Onity.” Early data showed “10-15% improvement in pull-through rates, 2-4 days of cycle time improvement, and automation of roughly 4.5 hours” of tasks per loan.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “first five commercial customers” and “25,500+ loans” processed, and said Autopilot loans “moved faster and converted at higher rates”; it wanted “a dollar number or a paying-customer count.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company reported more churn notices, with some customers moving to lower-cost or free point solutions. The preview did not flag this competitive pressure, though management characterized the revenue impact as manageable.
fact_evidence: “The company reported an uptick in churn notices this quarter, with customers moving to lower-cost or free point solutions, estimated to have a manageable low-single-digit impact on annual revenue.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Engineering throughput rose 3.6 times since January with roughly unchanged headcount, materially exceeding the 1.5-times level reported in May. The preview did not anticipate this internal productivity disclosure.
fact_evidence: “The engineering team increased its throughput (pull requests) 3.6x since January 2026 with roughly the same headcount, up from 1.5x in May,” with management “targeting 10x by year-end.”

description: Q2 revenue was $12.9 million, below the preview’s $14.45 million consensus anchor and roughly $15.0 million model, while the net loss widened to $6.2 million, or $0.32 per share, versus the modeled $4.0 million loss and consensus loss of $0.17 per share. A customer-directed hold pushed treatment revenue into the second half even though related personnel and operating costs had already been incurred in Q2.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue fell to $12.9 million” and “net loss widening to $6.2 million (-$0.32 per share)”; the primary driver was “a customer-directed hold on waste processing that pushed treatment revenue into the second half while related personnel and operating costs were already incurred in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview used “$14.45M” as the revenue anchor and modeled “~$15.0M” revenue and a “~−$4.0M / −$0.20” net loss/EPS.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The going-concern qualification remained in the 10-Q despite the preview expecting the May offering to support its removal. Cash ended at $20.5 million, slightly above the preview’s $18–20 million estimate, but the company still cited reliance on non-guaranteed government-directed waste shipments.
fact_evidence: The company “disclosed a going concern qualification in its 10-Q due to reliance on non-guaranteed government-directed waste shipments”; it ended the quarter with “$20.5 million cash and only $2.1 million total debt.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the offering “should support removal” of the going-concern paragraph and described removal as “likely but not certain”; it modeled “$18–20M” of cash at June 30.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call supplied a much larger prospective grouting scale than the preview’s discussion of 4.2 million gallons per year by October 2027: DOE’s target is 9 million gallons per year by 2030, and Perma-Fix is expanding its permit from 1.2 million to over 9–10 million gallons annually. The upgrades are expected to be operational by Q2/Q3 2027.
fact_evidence: “The company is expanding its grouting permit from 1.2 million to over 9-10 million gallons annually to serve DOE's target of 9 million gallons per year by 2030, with upgrades expected operational by Q2/Q3 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted maintaining “100,800 gallons/week” and a “4.2M gallons/year by October 2027 target,” and noted the existing 1.2M-gallon annual permit.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described DOE’s dual glass-plus-grout strategy as potentially delivering up to 300% more throughput while reducing treatment and disposal costs from roughly $1,200 per gallon to under $50 per gallon versus vitrification. The preview did not anticipate this scale of throughput or cost advantage.
fact_evidence: “DOE's dual glass-plus-grout strategy is projected to deliver up to 300% more throughput while cutting treatment and disposal costs from roughly $1,200 per gallon to under $50 per gallon versus vitrification.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call gave a specific DOE feedstock schedule: roughly 60,000 gallons per month could be available for grouting as early as Q4 2026, rising to about 130,000 gallons per month by 2028. The preview emphasized that no company volume was guaranteed and sought quantified task-order color, but did not include this schedule.
fact_evidence: “DOE estimates roughly 60,000 gallons per month will be available for grouting as early as Q4 2026 (about 720,000 gallons in 2027), rising to approximately 130,000 gallons per month by 2028,” within the existing permit.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “No revenue is guaranteed” and identified first task-order timing and PESI’s expected share as key questions; it called quantified 2027 Hanford revenue framing a potential bull trigger.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Perma-Fix Northwest’s location gives it a specific logistical advantage among the three master subcontract holders: it is about one mile from Hanford and can grout near the point of generation instead of requiring long-haul, out-of-state transport of liquid tank waste. The preview noted the three-awardee competition but not this advantage.
fact_evidence: “Perma-Fix Northwest is the only one of three master subcontract holders located near Hanford (about one mile away), allowing grouting near the point of generation without long-haul transport of liquid tank waste out of state.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the $4.367B ceiling was “shared across three awardees” and highlighted the need for task-order timing and PESI’s expected share.

description: Solid Power reported Q2 revenue of negative $300,000 versus the preview’s approximately $1.55 million estimate. The shortfall included a $1.2 million non-cash reversal of Q1 revenue after assumptions about SK On milestone payments changed.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was negative $300,000, hurt by a $1.2 million reversal of Q1 revenue tied to changed assumptions on SK ON milestone payments,” and the adjustment was “non-cash with no associated cost reversals.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$1.55M (MarketBeat, 7/28/26)”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview focused on evaluation feedback from Samsung SDI and BMW, but the update was that the Phase 1 agreement expires at the end of September and continuation is still under discussion. That leaves the next framework unresolved rather than reporting evaluation progress.
fact_evidence: “The Phase 1 Joint Evaluation Agreement with Samsung SDI and BMW is set to expire at the end of September,” and Solid Power is “in discussions to continue collaboration on a new framework.”
expectation_evidence: “Samsung SDI received electrolyte samples under the joint evaluation agreement with BMW — watch for evaluation feedback.”

description: The preview described Solid Power as evaluating partners for a commercial-scale facility, while management now expects to announce a South Korea electrolyte-production joint venture by year-end, with one prospective partner already discussing a draft term sheet. This is a step toward a concrete partnership, though no agreement is yet final.
fact_evidence: “The company expects to announce a joint venture for commercial-scale electrolyte production in South Korea by the end of the year,” with “one of three prospective partners already in draft term sheet discussions.”
expectation_evidence: “Management is evaluating partners for a 500-metric-ton electrolyte facility, with demand focus in Korea rather than North America.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview emphasized Korean demand and did not flag US customer interest, but management reported growing interest from humanoid-robotics companies and new interest from defense and aerospace. The opportunity remains early, with management noting that domestic cell manufacturing at scale is not yet available.
fact_evidence: “Management noted growing US customer interest from humanoid robotics companies plus new interest from defense and aerospace,” while “no domestic cell manufacturing at scale” exists yet.
expectation_evidence: “Demand focus in Korea rather than North America.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $2.36, above the preview’s published $2.10–$2.20 consensus range and slightly above its $2.25–$2.35 whisper estimate. The beat was larger versus published consensus than versus the preview’s higher whisper bar.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS was $2.36, versus $1.76 a year ago.
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS” consensus: “$2.10 – $2.20”; the preview also says the whisper was “likely closer to $2.25–2.35.”

description: Management raised full-year adjusted net income guidance, as expected, but the increase was smaller than the preview’s central expectation: the low end rose to $270 million while the high end stayed at $280 million, rather than reaching the preview’s expected $272–$286 million range.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted net income guidance for the third time to $270-$280 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called a raise to “~$272–286M” the base case and said a 9th raise was expected.

description: The crop outlook moved well beyond the preview’s cited expectation of roughly 35% full-year growth: management raised the premium outlook from about $320 million to more than $400 million after Q2 crop premiums nearly doubled.
fact_evidence: “Crop franchise nearly doubled with gross written premium up 96% year-over-year,” prompting a raised outlook “to over $400 million (up from ~$320 million).”
expectation_evidence: “Crop GWP +82% in Q1 with FY guidance raised to +35% growth.”

description: The adjusted combined ratio came in at 76.7%, above the preview’s watch level of 76% and just outside its 74–76% base-case range, although it remained below the preview’s greater-than-78% bear-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted combined ratio of 76.7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch: does adjusted CR hold ≤76%?” and gave a base case of “74–76%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Commercial earthquake pricing was weaker than the already-negative rate trend in the preview: average rate decreases exceeded 20%, and some new business was priced below technical levels.
fact_evidence: “Commercial Earthquake, now 36% of the earthquake book, saw average rate decreases exceeding 20% (over 20% on large layered/shared business), with some new business priced below technical levels.”

fact_evidence: “Supply chain constraints on memory, CPU and GPU components delayed shipments, leaving a portion of booked orders unrecognized as revenue and pushed into future quarters.”

fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$4.5 million in deferred revenue (up $0.6 million from year-end 2025).”

fact_evidence: “Revenue from related party NewtekOne declined as it cut IT spending, a headwind partially offset by growth from new non-related-party customers.”

description: Adjusted EPS was a much larger loss than expected: Enviri reported a $0.63 adjusted loss per share versus the preview’s roughly $0.30 loss estimate (and $0.31 consensus).
fact_evidence: “The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.63.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: ~$−0.30”; consensus “−$0.31.”

fact_evidence: “Total reported Q2 revenue was $187 million, reflecting a negative $136 million adjustment from exiting the two rail contracts (previously booked at zero margin), though underlying revenue grew year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $310–320M”; consensus revenue “$311.3M.”

fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose over 20% year-over-year to $34 million (up 22%), exceeding company expectations and driven primarily by Harsco Environmental”; Harsco Environmental adjusted EBITDA “rose 15% to $46 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$29–32M”; HE Adj. EBITDA “$38–40M.”

fact_evidence: “Enviri ended the quarter with net debt of approximately $290 million and a net leverage ratio of 1.9x, counting only $100 million of its roughly $400 million cash balance in the covenant calculation.”

fact_evidence: The contracts “consumed roughly $40 million of cash in 2025 and were expected to consume a similar amount in 2026,” and Enviri “exited” them, “significantly derisking the rail business.”

fact_evidence: “Restructuring actions eliminating approximately 300 positions are expected to deliver over $15 million in annual margin uplift on a full run-rate basis once completed.”

description: Management set an additional longer-term target of meaningful earnings and cash-flow growth beginning in 2027. The preview centered on 2026 guidance and did not identify this 2027 outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management [is] targeting meaningful earnings and cash flow growth beginning in 2027.”

expectation_evidence: “RCC is also the largest commercial prize and the most crowded competitively.”

fact_evidence: “The cash runway funds the IPF-related chronic cough program through potential FDA approval, but explicitly excludes commercial launch costs and any Phase III RCC trial.”
expectation_evidence: “The market is watching whether the April raise really was the last one before approval.”

fact_evidence: “Management indicated the LAKE trial could be upsized by up to 50% following the SSRE, but framed any increase as a routine statistical exercise rather than a negative signal.”

fact_evidence: “Trevi submitted an FDA meeting request for its non-IPF-ILD chronic cough program and expects to learn within the month whether the meeting is granted, with alignment anticipated in 2H 2026.”

fact_evidence: “The company targets a treatment-resistant RCC population of approximately 1 million U.S. patients, pursuing specialty pricing rather than the broad market to avoid cannibalizing IPF/ILD revenue.”

fact_evidence: “Management stated it will not hold OCEAN-2 top-line data (expected 2H 2027) until OCEAN-1 reads out (1H 2028), and expects OCEAN-1 to be largely enrolled by the time OCEAN-2 reports.”

fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin (excluding prior-year tariff refunds) surged to 18.6% from 12.9% a year ago, and diluted EPS rose to $0.15 from $0.04.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. EBITDA margin” at “~13.5%” and “EPS (GAAP diluted)” at “$0.07.”

fact_evidence: “CEO Ryan Lance will retire effective September 1 after 14 years, with CFO/Strategy head Andy O'Brien becoming President and CEO and Konnie Haynes-Welsh joining as the new CFO.”

expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $14.1 billion” and “+1.8%.”

expectation_evidence: “Prepared Foods: Branded portfolio momentum, innovation, and distribution expansion expected to support growth.”

fact_evidence: “Management raised the Prepared Foods full-year operating income guidance midpoint to a range of $1.3-$1.35 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Prepared Foods: Branded portfolio momentum, innovation, and distribution expansion expected to support growth.”

fact_evidence: “About three-quarters of chicken operating income now runs on a demand-committed model rather than commodity spot markets.”
expectation_evidence: “Chicken: Expected to stay the primary earnings engine — steady demand plus gains in live production, yield, and labor productivity.”

The preview discussed Chicken productivity gains generally but did not anticipate this specific initiative or its expected contribution.

expectation_evidence: The preview expected Chicken gains in “live production, yield, and labor productivity.”

expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Elevated debt levels and questions around dividend sustainability” as a valuation risk.

fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $257.5 million, up 6.6% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue relatively flat sequentially” → ~$244.7M”; estimate “$244–246M.”

expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … $150–153M”; “Above $153M de-risks the year.”

expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guide … reaffirm expected”; “FY26 Adj. EBITDA guide … Reaffirm”; catalyst: “FY26 Adj. EBITDA guide reaffirmed at $605–615M.”

expectation_evidence: Base case: “FCF … $25–40M”; catalyst checklist: “Q2 FCF ≥$30M.”

fact_evidence: “Prompting a $5 million raise to full-year free cash flow guidance to $5–$15 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF guide … $0–$10M”; “Reaffirm — the fragile line.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said “3%–5% growth for the second half” as “ACV bookings convert (6–12 month lag).”

fact_evidence: “The TPA vertical was the largest contributor to Q2 bookings and is expected to represent about 30% of total new bookings this year, second only to the payer segment.”

fact_evidence: “2028 PPL spark spreads up 28% and West Hub sparks up 27% versus July 2025 Investor Day pricing.”

fact_evidence: “The PPL zone's power price discount to PJM West Hub widened from a historical ~$9/MWh to ~$20/MWh due to transmission outages, with each $1 of basis improvement translating to roughly $1 of adjusted free cash flow per share.”

fact_evidence: “As the AWS campus ramps to full build-out between 2028 and 2030, long-term contracted margin is projected to rise from 10% to 35%, with potential to reach 60% if an additional ~2 gigawatts of contracts are executed.”
expectation_evidence: “On the Q1 call management flagged 1+ GW of long-term PPA opportunities” and “a signed contract is the single largest upside catalyst available tonight.”

expectation_evidence: “Treat $0.30–$0.33 as the live band”; the bull case listed “$0.34+.”

expectation_evidence: “FY26 AFFO guidance action. Maintained = base case.” The preview gave existing guidance of “$1.20–$1.30.”

fact_evidence: “The gap between physical and economic occupancy narrowed 240 basis points to 860 basis points, which management views as a healthier, more sustainable long-term level.”

fact_evidence: “Interest expense of $155-$160 million.”
expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 guidance listed “interest expense $170–180M.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said POWER2 enrollment was “paused,” expected a “decision by year-end” in its base case, and described a restart as the bull case.

fact_evidence: Relutrigine is “carrying a new PDUFA date of December 27, 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave relutrigine’s PDUFA date as “Dec 27, 2026.”

expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D expense” at “$74–78M” and “G&A expense” at “$32–36M.”

description: KMB unveiled a proprietary alternative natural-fiber program, including acquired land and a pilot facility beginning construction, that was not part of the preview’s discussion. The company says it is intended to improve margins and reduce forest-fiber cost volatility, with investment already included in results and outlook.
fact_evidence: “Kimberly-Clark unveiled a proprietary alternative natural fiber program (with land already acquired and a pilot facility breaking ground) aimed at improving margins and reducing forest fiber cost volatility, with investments already embedded in current results and outlook.”

description: Q2 sales were $152.5 million, well above both the roughly $129 million implied by management’s flat-sequential guide and the $136.6 million consensus. Instead of staying near Q1’s level, sales rose 18.6% sequentially, making the year-over-year decline smaller than the preview’s 29% consensus decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $152.5 million,” up “18.6% sequentially from Q1's $128 million,” exceeding the company's prior expectation of flat sequential revenue; sales were down 21% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue ($136.6M) sits ~6% above management's own ‘flat sequentially’ guide (~$129M)”; the consensus table projected revenue down 29% year-over-year.

description: Gross margin recovered much more sharply than the preview’s flat-or-slightly-better guide and 23% base case suggested: it reached 27.1%, above even the preview’s 24%+ recovery threshold. EBITDA margin also improved substantially sequentially, although it remained below the year-ago level.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved approximately 420 basis points sequentially to 27.1% from 22.9%,” driven by Wisconsin operational improvements. EBITDA margin improved 670 basis points sequentially to 16.9%, versus 17.8% a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided gross margin “flat or slightly better” for Q2, set a 23.0% base case, and said “24%+” would give the recovery narrative its first real datapoint.

description: Diluted EPS of $0.73 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.32 consensus estimate. It was still below the preview’s roughly $0.95 adjusted prior-year comparison, but the year-over-year decline was much less severe than the preview’s clean-comp estimate of about 66%.
fact_evidence: “Net income was $16.9 million ($0.73 per diluted share), down from $51.2 million ($2.22) a year ago,” with the prior-year result including a “$29.2 million ($1.27 per share) tax benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 diluted EPS consensus of “$0.32” and estimated prior-year “clean” operating EPS of “~$0.95,” implying a roughly 66% decline.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash generation was much stronger than the preview’s expectation of a working-capital build ahead of the second-half ramp: operating cash flow reached $56.6 million and the company used cash to reduce debt by about $38.8 million during the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged to $56.6 million in Q2” versus $20.2 million a year earlier, enabling “a total debt reduction of approximately $38.8 million”; quarter-end cash was $70.1 million and total debt about $72.6 million, down from $103.4 million at March 31.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$95M drawn against $45.1M cash” and said “A working-capital build ahead of the H2 ramp is expected and fine.”

description: Adjusted EPS was expected to be about $1.06, but Innospec reported $1.27—roughly 20% above consensus, despite being essentially flat year over year.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS essentially flat at $1.27 versus $1.26 a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.06.”

description: Revenue was expected to be about $462.35 million, but came in at $491.4 million, about 6% above consensus.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenues rose 12% year-over-year to $491.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $462.35M.”

description: Oilfield Services substantially outperformed the preview’s estimates: revenue was $115.4 million versus $105 million expected, and operating income was $8.7 million versus $6.5 million expected. The preview anticipated only a gradual improvement and management’s cautious stance.
fact_evidence: “Oilfield Services was the standout with revenue up 14% to $115.4 million and operating income up 40% to $8.7 million,” with gross margin up 2.7 points to 32.3%.
expectation_evidence: “Oilfield Services” Q2’26E “Rev / OI” of “$105M / $6.5M”; management was described as “cautiously optimistic.”

description: Performance Chemicals beat the preview’s model, with revenue of $190.3 million versus $178 million expected and operating income of $16.4 million versus $15.5 million expected. Price/mix and currency more than offset a 2% volume decline.
fact_evidence: “Performance Chemicals revenue grew 9% to $190.3 million, with an 8% positive price/mix and 3% favorable currency offsetting a 2% volume decline, driving 15% operating income growth to $16.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: Performance Chemicals Q2’26E “Rev / OI” of “$178M / $15.5M.”

description: Fuel Specialties revenue exceeded the $180 million estimate, reaching $185.7 million on 7% volume growth. That stronger top line came with the expected margin pressure, however, and operating-income growth was limited to 3%.
fact_evidence: “Fuel Specialties revenue rose 12% to $185.7 million on 7% volume growth, but gross margin fell 1.5 points to 36.6% on weaker sales mix, limiting operating income growth to just 3%.”
expectation_evidence: Fuel Specialties Q2’26E revenue of “$180M”; the preview also flagged “some gross margin compression” and operating income “a little lighter than Q1.”

description: Management said Fuel Specialties margins would likely face further sequential pressure in Q3 before potentially stabilizing, indicating that the raw-material pricing lag is likely to persist into Q3 rather than clearly reverse sooner.
fact_evidence: “Fuel Specialties margins will likely face further sequential pressure in Q3 due to the pricing lag against cost inflation before potentially stabilizing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified whether the raw-material lag “reverses in Q3 or extends” as the key question, and asked whether pricing had “caught up” or the lag would “persist into H2.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview described the North Carolina plants as repaired, but management said repairs were only about 60% complete and expected to finish by the end of Q4. The eventual efficiency gains are meaningful—more than 10% additional capacity next year without extra CapEx—but arrive later than the preview’s recovery framing suggested.
fact_evidence: “The North Carolina Performance Chemicals plant repairs are about 60% complete, expected to finish by end of Q4, with efficiency gains projected to add north of 10% capacity for next year without additional CapEx.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the “NC plants” as “repaired” and said the backlog was “largely worked through.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Oilfield demand and expansion prospects sounded stronger than the preview’s cautious framing: existing DRA capacity was nearly sold out, management was discussing another expansion, and it cited strong Middle East demand tied to East-West pipeline shipments.
fact_evidence: “DRA capacity added is nearly sold out with strong Middle East demand tied to East-West pipeline shipments, and management is discussing a further DRA expansion,” alongside new technologies and potential Mexico opportunities within roughly six months.
expectation_evidence: The preview said DRA capacity was “maxed out in Q2 and Q4,” described management as “cautiously optimistic,” and cited heavy-crude opportunities in Argentina, Venezuela, and Mexico.

description: Adjusted EBITDA fell short of the preview’s modeled range: $50.1 million versus an estimate of roughly $52–54 million, even as revenue and adjusted EPS beat consensus.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA edged up only modestly to $50.1 million from $49.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est.): ~$52–54M.”

description: The preview’s base case put Q2 gross margin at 9–12%, but KSCP reported about 7% ($0.7 million). Gross margin was positive for a second consecutive quarter, but it came in below that expectation.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin turned positive at $0.7 million (~7% of revenue), the second consecutive positive gross margin quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Gross Margin 9–12%”; the preview also said to watch whether Q1’s 7.7% margin was “a trend or a one-quarter artifact.”

fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $14.1 million ($0.79 per share) ... though loss per share improved due to a larger share count.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 EPS | ~-$0.60 (derived, not published)” and “Base: ... -$0.60 to -$0.70.”

fact_evidence: “The new K7 autonomous security robot passed its Alpha Prototype gate review and remains on track for initial deployments in Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided to K7 limited release by late summer 2026.”

fact_evidence: “Net expense included roughly $1 million tied to fair value changes in contingent consideration (earn-out) from the recent acquisition.”

expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $0.99M (GuruFocus) / $1.03M (MarketBeat).”

expectation_evidence: “Gates Foundation / CEPI program milestones — the credible non-dilutive channel.”

description: The preview had flagged an approximately 80% productivity gain in transferrin, but the call added a potential cost benefit: management expects the pilot result to reduce costs by roughly 40%.
fact_evidence: “The animal-free recombinant human transferrin program achieved an approximately 80% productivity increase in its pilot run, expected to reduce costs by roughly 40%.”
expectation_evidence: “~80% productivity gain in recombinant human transferrin.”

description: Q1 revenue was about $3.6 billion, below the preview’s $3.661 billion consensus and its $3.65–$3.70 billion base case. The 3% constant-currency decline was within the preview’s expected range, so the miss was modest.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue was $3.6 billion, down 3% year-over-year on both a reported and constant currency basis.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $3.661B”; “My base case: revenue $3.66–3.70B (CC ~−3.5%).”

description: The adjusted pretax loss was less severe than the preview’s roughly $50 million base-case loss, and the $152 million workforce rebalancing charge was below the roughly $200 million charge the preview expected. The preview still expected Q1 to be the year’s earnings low point, so this was a modestly better trough than modeled.
fact_evidence: “The company reported an adjusted pretax loss of $37 million, primarily driven by $152 million of workforce rebalancing charges that impacted adjusted pretax income margin by more than 4 points.”
expectation_evidence: “My base case: … adjusted PTI ≈ −$50M”; “Q1 is also the quarter management pre-announced as the earnings and cash-flow trough of FY27, absorbing a ~$200M workforce rebalancing charge.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q1 signings of $3.9 billion beat the preview’s $3.0–$3.3 billion base case and exceeded its $3.5 billion bull-case threshold. TTM signings were $14.2 billion, although still below the preview’s cited $18.3 billion year-ago level.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month signings totaled $14.2 billion with $3.9 billion signed in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “Base: … signings ~$3.0–3.3B”; “Bull … Q1 signings >$3.5B”; “anything under ~$3.0B makes the back-half revenue ramp implausible.”

fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 revenue of $234 million…landing within prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Base…Revenue $238–246M”; consensus revenue was “$231.6M (Zacks) / ~$232M (LSEG).”

description: Q2 gross margins beat the preview’s expected guided step-down: non-GAAP margin was 41.5%, above the 38–40% guide, and GAAP margin was 36.1%, above the 33–35% guide. The beat was partly aided by a nonrecurring tariff refund, with an inventory reserve offsetting some of it.
fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin of 41.5% and GAAP gross margin of 36.1% both exceeded guidance, aided by a nonrecurring tariff refund offset by an inventory reserve on the new light launch vehicle.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided down sequentially: GAAP 38.2% → 33–35%, non-GAAP 43.0% → 38–40%.”

description: Rocket Lab’s Q3 margin outlook is lower than its Q2 reported margins, with management citing unfavorable Space Systems mix. The preview discussed Q2 margin compression but did not give a Q3 margin forecast.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for…GAAP 29–31%, non-GAAP 35–37%…due to unfavorable Space Systems mix.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 backlog ended at $2.36 billion, above the preview’s roughly $2.2 billion expectation, despite the preview noting that two large awards would land in Q3 backlog. Rocket Lab also reported over $1 billion of new contracts across Q2 and post-quarter, including the $266 million Space Force award.
fact_evidence: “The company signed over $1 billion in new contracts across launch and Space Systems during Q2 and post-quarter, including a record $266 million Space Force contract”; “ended Q2 with $2.36 billion total backlog.”
expectation_evidence: “Backlog…~$2.2B”; “Q2 backlog holding roughly flat near $2.2B while burning ~$232M of revenue is a good outcome”; the $266M RSLP award was expected to land in Q3 backlog.

expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “the Neutron ‘Q4 2026’ language survives intact” and described the base case as “Neutron ‘Q4, tracking.’”

description: The pending Iridium acquisition is a major strategic development not anticipated in the preview: it would add a 66-satellite constellation and about $870 million in annual revenue, with management citing significant free cash flow. The deal is expected to close in mid-2027.
fact_evidence: “The pending Iridium acquisition, expected to close mid-2027, adds a 66-satellite constellation with 2.5 million subscribers and roughly $870 million in annual revenue, providing significant free cash flow.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management disclosed Neutron pricing of $50–55 million per launch and said it is not offering significant early discounts, with potential pricing upside in a supply-constrained market. The preview discussed launch pricing for Electron but did not anticipate this Neutron pricing commentary.
fact_evidence: “Neutron is being sold at a $50-55 million ASP with no significant early discounting, and management sees more upside than downside to launch pricing given a supply-constrained market.”

fact_evidence: “Free cash flow deteriorated to a use of $110.1 million in Q2 (from $77.4 million in Q1), driven by Neutron tail production and Mynaric supply chain replenishment, with cash flow positivity expected 18-24 months after Neutron's first successful launch.”

fact_evidence: “The company raised $1.08 billion through its now-terminated at-the-market equity program, ending Q2 with roughly $2.4 billion in cash and equivalents to fund M&A and growth initiatives.”

fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $22.2 million”; management said results came in “well below analyst expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “My base estimate: revenue $25M”; the preview said “$24–26M = on plan” and “<$22M = no recovery.” Published consensus was “$30M.”

expectation_evidence: The preview quoted management saying traffic volatility “has subsided” and asked whether that was “reaffirmed or walked back”; it also described Q2–Q4 as seasonally stronger.

expectation_evidence: “My base estimate: … adjusted EBITDA ~$6M”; the preview said Q1 one-time costs were “largely limited to the first quarter.”

description: Arena reported a $200,000 net loss rather than the return to profitability anticipated in the preview’s base case. The much higher year-ago net income included a one-time discontinued-operations gain, which the preview had explicitly cautioned investors to disregard.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a net loss of $200,000 in Q2 2026”; Q2 2025 net income included “a $96.2 million gain from discontinued operations.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “EPS ~$0.02–0.04” and described a “Return to profitability.” It also said the Q2’25 one-time benefit should not be treated as a meaningful comparison.

fact_evidence: Arena “refinanced and extended its debt facility by three years with its existing lender at the same interest rate, avoiding dilution and removing near-term refinancing risk.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called a signed refinancing a “balance-sheet re-rating event” and its checklist looked for a “completed facility with a commercial bank at lower cost.”

description: Arena made an unpreviewed cash-funded acquisition of InfoSentience, an AI content-generation firm, and said it expects the deal to contribute immediately to cash flow and profit through existing B2B contracts.
fact_evidence: The company “acquired InfoSentience, an AI content-generation firm, entirely with cash on hand” and “expects it to be immediately accretive to cash flow and profit via existing B2B contracts.”

description: Arena announced a rebrand to Pradium AI and a repositioning from traditional publishing toward an asset-light AI technology company, a strategic shift not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Arena is rebranding to Pradium AI, repositioning from a traditional publisher to an asset-light AI technology company empowering creators.”

fact_evidence: Cutter Studios targets “about 1,000 video-first creators,” converting long-form videos into “5-10 derivative articles each at roughly one-third the efficacy of handwritten articles but with comparable or better monetization rates.”

expectation_evidence: “EPS (Class A, diluted) Consensus: $0.08”; the preview’s base case modeled “~$0.05 EPS.”

expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$106–108M (my model, no published cons.)” and “~flat” year over year.
