fact_evidence: “Print segment revenue declined 4.3% to $235.9 million but EBITDA margins expanded to the mid-30s (up ~110 bps)”; “the Safeguard exit added roughly 80 bps to enterprise margins.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch whether core decline stays inside 4–6% and whether the 32%+ Print EBITDA margin holds.”

description: The reported Celero combination places Deluxe among the top 10 nonbank merchant acquirers, a positioning milestone not identified in the preview’s description of the deal’s expected scale.
fact_evidence: “[Celero] bring[s] combined processing volume to over $70 billion annually across more than 210,000 merchants and moving Deluxe into the top 10 nonbank merchant acquirers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a combined “~$70B annual gross transaction volume” and listed the acquisition as adding “+55,000 merchants,” but did not anticipate Deluxe entering the top 10.

description: Q2 revenue exceeded both cited consensus estimates, although it remained within the preview’s $490–$500 million base-case range. Comparable-adjusted growth was positive rather than the reported decline suggesting a weaker underlying quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $499.3 million, down 4.2% on a reported basis but up 2.6% on a comparable adjusted basis.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited revenue consensus of “$491.45M” and “$486.3M,” and described its base case as “$490–500M” with “revenue in line to slightly light.”

description: Q4 revenue was $196.3 million, above the preview’s $184.7 million consensus and above its $175–185 million base-case range. The preview’s bull case began at $195 million, but the reported result cleared that threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenues rose 27% year-over-year to $196.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue | Consensus | $184.7M”; the base case was “$175–185M” and the bull case “$195M+.”

description: Q4 adjusted operating income was $18.6 million, well above the preview’s $5–10 million base case and close to its $20 million bull-case threshold. This was a stronger recovery than the preview’s central case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income swing[ing] to $18.6 million from a $1.3 million loss in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q4 AOI +$5M to +$10M”; its bull case expected “+$20M or better.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Theater bookings were weaker than the preview’s description of a contracted, largely de-risked FY27 calendar would suggest: MSGE was only about 60% toward its theater booking goal, with theaters pacing behind for both the September and December quarters. Garden bookings were much further along, at roughly 90%.
fact_evidence: “The company is roughly 90% toward its Garden bookings goal but only ~60% toward its theater goal, with theaters pacing behind for both the September and December quarters.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the “FY27 calendar” as “contracted and largely de-risked” and highlighted “Joe Hisaishi (7 nights, theater).”

description: Full-year revenue was about $1.061 billion, derived from the reported $1 billion-plus full year and the $196.3 million Q4 result, versus the preview’s $1.03 billion consensus. That is a modest beat, while reported 13% growth also exceeded the preview’s expected 9.4% growth.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 full-year revenues exceeded $1 billion (up 13%).” Q4 revenue was reported as “$196.3 million.”

description: Full-year adjusted operating income was $262 million, above the preview’s roughly $250 million base-case estimate, though below its roughly $265 million bull-case figure. The 18% increase was also stronger than the base case’s implied growth of about 12%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income of $262 million (up 18%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY26 AOI ~$250M (+12%)”; its bull case expected “FY26 AOI ~$265M (+19%).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Christmas Spectacular reported a record season—over 1.2 million tickets sold and the highest attendance in 25 years—whereas the preview discussed the upcoming 230-show season but did not anticipate a record attendance result for the season just completed.
fact_evidence: “The Christmas Spectacular set a record with over 1.2 million tickets sold across 215 performances (highest attendance in 25 years) generating approximately $195 million in revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “a 230-show Christmas Spectacular (+7% shows)” for FY27, but gave no expectation for attendance or revenue in the completed season.

description: ESAB cut its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $5.40–$5.50 from the prior $5.70–$5.90 range, even as it raised EBITDA guidance. Management said the new EPS range includes a $15 million drag from transitory price-cost neutrality tied to logistics and commodity inflation.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance is $5.40–$5.50,” incorporating “an assumed $15 million drag from transitory price-cost neutrality from logistics and commodity inflation.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the standing FY26 adjusted EPS guide was “$5.70–5.90” and called for watching whether “core ex-Eddyfi” was held as guidance was recast.

description: Q2 core organic growth was 2.5%, a clear improvement on the preview’s near-flat to slightly negative base case and above the flat level it identified as the key threshold for keeping the full-year organic-growth bridge credible.
fact_evidence: “Core organic growth of 2.5%,” driven by “double-digit growth in automation and equipment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Organic ~flat to −1%” and it said “Anything worse than flat organic” would make the full-year bridge implausible.

description: Q2 sales of $766 million exceeded the preview’s $747.3–$750.1 million consensus range by about 2–3%. The reported 13% year-over-year increase included only 2.5% core organic growth, so the headline beat was not all organic.
fact_evidence: “Record Q2 total sales of $766 million, up 13% year-over-year, with core organic growth of 2.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview put revenue consensus at “$747.3M – $750.1M.”

description: ESAB raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $615–$625 million from the prior $575–$595 million range. The increase is positive, though it comes with the acquired business and offsets, rather than the preview’s clearest bull case of retaining the core outlook and adding the acquisition on top.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance” to adjusted EBITDA of “$615–625 million”; DFI’s incremental contribution was “approaching $50 million,” including a $35 million net raise and $15 million of offsetting headwinds and investments.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior core adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$575–595M” and described the bull outcome as “core FY guide held, Eddyfi added on top (EBITDA → ~$625M+).”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The Middle East business was down roughly 10–11%, while logistics costs had tripled due to the conflict. The preview had already flagged the region’s conflict-related drag, but the reported contraction and cost escalation show a substantial ongoing impact; management said rebuilding could restore prior growth rates.
fact_evidence: The Middle East, “representing 7–8%” of the business, was “down double digits (~10–11%)” with logistics costs “tripling due to conflict”; rebuild efforts could restore prior “~20% growth rates.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the Middle East was “≈ 7% of sales,” noted an Iran-related regional drag, and highlighted whether management described the impact as “persisting” rather than “easing.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management disclosed a cross-selling funnel with DFI approaching $450 million, but said conversion would take time and materialize mainly in 2027 and beyond. This adds a sizable opportunity not quantified in the preview, while indicating that it is not an immediate revenue driver.
fact_evidence: “DFI’s cross-selling funnel with ESAB is approaching $450 million,” but conversion is expected “to take time and materialize mainly in 2027 and beyond.”

description: LVLU revenue was $67.8 million, down 17% year over year, versus the preview’s $76 million estimate and expected 6.8% decline. The company attributed the sharper drop to 17% fewer orders and higher return rates.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue declined 17% year-over-year to $67.8 million, driven by a 17% drop in total orders placed and higher return rates.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 FY2026 estimate: $76.0M (-6.8% YoY)”; the preview also said “worse than -12% kills” the recovery story.

description: Gross margin reached 48.6%, far above the preview’s 45.8% estimate. Lower markdown sales and higher-margin mix helped drive the expansion, despite the preview’s concern that clearance markdowns could pressure margins.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 330 basis points to 48.6%, the company's highest Q2 gross margin since 2021, aided by higher-margin sales mix and freight cost savings”; “Total markdown sales fell 38%,” including a “65% decline in casual apparel markdowns.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 FY2026 estimate: 45.8% (+50 bps)”; the bear scenario cited “casual/footwear clearance markdowns hit GM.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company reported that units transacted per new casual-apparel and footwear launch rose 28% year over year and 29% sequentially, even as it cut launches 48% year over year. The preview anticipated the assortment reset and fewer launches, but did not anticipate this improvement in productivity per launch.
fact_evidence: “Casual apparel and footwear new product launches were cut 48% year-over-year, while units transacted per new launch rose 28% versus Q2 2025 and 29% sequentially.”

description: LVLU secured a $4.5 million equity line of credit, with an option for an additional $5.5 million. The preview focused on liquidity and the ABL but did not anticipate this financing; it adds potential funding while also creating possible equity dilution.
fact_evidence: “Secured new financing including a $4.5 million equity line of credit with an option for an additional $5.5 million.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million matched UBS’s published estimate of about $93 million, but came in below the preview’s $95–105 million buy-side whisper. The shortfall versus the whisper was small.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Whisper: I'd put the buy-side bar at $95–105M adjusted EBITDA”; the preview also cited UBS’s “~$93M” mark.

description: Diluted EPS of $0.83 was well above the preview’s stated consensus range of $0.52–$0.65, exceeding even its high estimate by $0.18.
fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to Green Plains was $67.1 million or $0.83 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted): $0.52”; the preview also gave an “EPS (alt.)” range of “$0.54 / $0.65.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Green Plains had not monetized any of its 2026 45Z credits by the end of Q2, rather than providing the cash-conversion confirmation the preview identified as important. Management said it was waiting for a partner that could provide stable, predictable cash flows.
fact_evidence: “The company has not yet monetized any of its 2026 45Z credits, opting to stay patient to secure a partner offering stable, predictable cash flows.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “confirmation that credits are converting to cash on schedule” and said “EBITDA-to-cash lag is a real risk to the story.”

description: The Q3 margin outlook was more resilient than the preview’s concern that board crush would soften entering Q3: margins were said to be only slightly below Q2’s historically high levels, with the favorable structure expected to last into early Q4.
fact_evidence: “Q3 crush margins are only slightly below Q2's historically high levels, with the favorable margin structure expected to carry into early Q4 before seasonal declines.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “board crush [appears] to have softened from Q2 into Q3” and flagged Q3 crush commentary as a key debate.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 operating cash flow and the ending cash balance were strong despite the preview’s concern about a lag between recognized 45Z EBITDA and cash collection. The reported $87 million of operating cash flow included a separate final $41 million payment for 2025 credits, so it does not establish that 2026 credits were monetized.
fact_evidence: “Green Plains generated nearly $87 million of operating cash flow and ended June with over $243 million in cash”; it also received “a final $41 million cash payment for its 2025 45Z credits during Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “EBITDA-to-cash lag is a real risk to the story” and highlighted the timing of 45Z cash conversion; it cited Q1 cash of “$183.1M” including restricted cash.

description: The carbon platform generated nearly $59 million of net EBITDA, above the preview’s $45–55 million base-case range for net 45Z recognized value and close to its $60 million bull-case threshold. This was a modestly stronger credit contribution than the base case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The carbon platform contributed nearly $59 million of net EBITDA in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s operating scenarios used “net 45Z recognized” of “base $45–55M” and “bull ≥$60M.”

description: Revenue was expected to be roughly flat to slightly down at $142.9–$143.4 million, but SGC reported $148 million, up 3% year over year. That was about $5 million above the consensus range.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenue rose 3% year-over-year to $148 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $142.9M (MarketBeat) / $143.4M (Zacks)” with “Implied Y/Y” of “-0.5% to -0.8%.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was expected at $0.09–$0.10, with even the preview’s discounted whisper only $0.12–$0.13; reported adjusted EPS was $0.21. This was a substantial upside gap, although GAAP EPS was $0.08 after the trade-name impairment.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS more than doubled to $0.21”; “GAAP net income was $1.2 million or $0.08 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.10 (MarketBeat) / $0.09 (Zacks)” and “A naive whisper is $0.12–$0.13.”

description: Branded Products revenue was expected to land roughly flat at $92–$93 million, with the preview warning that Q1’s pull-forward could weigh on Q2. Instead, the segment grew 6% to $98 million.
fact_evidence: “Branded Products, the largest segment, grew revenue 6% to $98 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus of ~$143M total effectively assumes BP lands flat, ~$92–93M”; the preview also said “Q1 2026 pulled revenue forward out of this quarter.”

description: Healthcare Apparel revenue was expected to grow 3–5%, but instead fell 4%. The decline was a clear miss against the preview’s segment outlook.
fact_evidence: “Healthcare Apparel revenue fell 4% to $27 million.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “HA +3–5% but margin-pressured.”

description: Healthcare Apparel’s gross margin fell to 32.9%, with a $2.6 million inventory write-down weighing on the quarter. The preview anticipated margin pressure but did not flag a write-down or a decline of this reported size.
fact_evidence: “Healthcare Apparel revenue fell 4% to $27 million with gross margin down 260 basis points to 32.9%, hurt by a $2.6 million noncash inventory write-down partially offset by a $1.8 million net tariff refund benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Healthcare Apparel mix shift toward lower-margin customers” and expected the segment to be “margin-pressured.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: SGC recognized a $2.6 million noncash trade-name impairment in Healthcare Apparel, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.13 per share. The preview did not anticipate this charge, which helps explain why GAAP EPS of $0.08 was far below adjusted EPS of $0.21.
fact_evidence: “A pretax noncash trade name impairment of $2.6 million ($2 million net of tax, or $0.13 per diluted share) was recognized in the Healthcare Apparel segment.”

description: Contact Centers revenue declined 4%, a milder decline than the preview’s expected 5–8% drop; it also improved sequentially for a second consecutive quarter. However, its gross margin fell 170 basis points to 50.9% as onboarding investments weighed on results.
fact_evidence: “Contact Centers revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $23 million but improved sequentially for the second consecutive quarter, with gross margin down 170 basis points to 50.9% due to onboarding investments.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “CC -5% to -8%”; the preview also said segment gross margin was “~52–53%.”

description: Management said Healthcare Apparel margin pressure would continue through the rest of 2026 under the assortment transition, with improvement anticipated in 2027. The preview identified ongoing pressure as a risk, but did not spell out this duration before improvement.
fact_evidence: “Management expects continued Healthcare Apparel margin pressure through the balance of 2026 during its assortment transition under new leadership, with improvements anticipated in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Healthcare Apparel mix shift toward lower-margin customers” and asked “whether Healthcare Apparel mix has stabilized.”

description: Management signaled that a Contact Center acquisition or a Philippines call-center startup is likely this year. The preview anticipated M&A commentary broadly but did not identify either of these specific expansion paths.
fact_evidence: Management “signaled a Contact Center acquisition or Philippines call center startup is likely this year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had positioned SGC “as a participant” in industry consolidation and listed “M&A commentary” as a narrative item to watch.

description: Revenue was expected at about $9.33–$9.54 million, with even the preview’s bull case at $12.5–$14.5 million. Satellogic reported $15.9 million, roughly 67% above consensus and above the bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 259% year-over-year to $15.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $9.33M (Zacks) / $9.54M (Benzinga)”; bull case: “$12.5–14.5M.”

description: The preview expected an adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $3.5–$4.5 million, with even its bull case calling for a loss of $1.5 million or better. Satellogic instead reported positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.8 million and its first positive quarterly operating income.
fact_evidence: “The company achieved its first-ever positive quarterly operating income (~$300,000) and positive adjusted EBITDA ($2.8 million) in Q2 2026”; operating expenses “rose only 46%” while revenue grew 259%.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~–$3.5M to –$4.5M”; bull case: “EBITDA –$1.5M or better.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview modeled a large noncash fair-value gain because the stock had fallen, estimating a possible $40–$90 million gain. Instead, Satellogic reported a $19.7 million noncash fair-value charge and a $20 million GAAP net loss.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $20 million for the quarter, primarily due to a $19.7 million noncash fair value charge tied to stock price movements.”
expectation_evidence: “The stock fell roughly 40–45% between March 31 and June 30, which should drive a large non-cash gain … plausibly $40–90M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview expected a roughly 70/30 Data and Analytics/Space Systems revenue mix and flagged Space Systems at 35% or less as a quality test. Actual revenue was 45% Data and Analytics and 55% Space Systems, so the much larger-than-expected quarter was more weighted toward lumpy satellite deliveries than the preview’s preferred mix.
fact_evidence: “Data and Analytics revenue reached $7.1 million (45% of Q2 revenue)”; “Space Systems contributed $8.8 million (55% of Q2 revenue).”
expectation_evidence: Base case: “a roughly 70/30 D&A/Space Systems split”; catalyst: “Revenue ≥ $9.33M and Space Systems ≤ 35% of the total.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected Merlin’s first launch in October 2026 and full deployment in H1 2027. The October launch remains on track, but the call put full service in the second half of 2027, later than the preview’s stated deployment timetable.
fact_evidence: “The Merlin constellation's first satellite is fully integrated and on track for an October 2026 launch, with full service expected in the second half of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “First launch targeted October 2026, full deployment H1 2027.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview anticipated that the previously signed defense monitoring contract would push RPO higher, but did not anticipate the pilot converting into a full-scale program in under six months. The reported conversion and program value add a stronger signal of rapid pipeline conversion than the preview described.
fact_evidence: “A key defense pilot converted into a full-scale program valued at over $18 million in under 6 months, signaling faster-than-expected pipeline conversion amid a nearly $1 billion Space Systems pipeline.”
expectation_evidence: “The $18M+ one-year international defense monitoring contract signed in May should push [RPO] materially higher.”

description: The company reduced secured convertible debt by $12 million through an equity conversion, a capital-structure change the preview did not anticipate. Lower debt is favorable, while the equity conversion also means dilution.
fact_evidence: “Reduced secured convertible debt from $30 million to $18 million via a $12 million equity conversion.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview’s working assumption was roughly 55–65 of 70 patients enrolled, but Talphera reported 75% enrollment, or about 53 patients. That is below the expected range, although all sites are now active and management said enrollment remains on track.
fact_evidence: “Talphera reached 75% enrollment in the registrational NEPHRO CRRT study with all clinical sites now activated,” and “remains on track to complete enrollment later in 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Enrollment number or LPO timing vs. the market’s assumption of ‘roughly 55–65 of 70 enrolled.’”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected management to reiterate a second-half 2026 topline. Instead, enrollment is expected to finish later in 2026 and topline data to follow roughly four to five weeks afterward, pointing to a possible early-2027 readout rather than a clear 2H26 result.
fact_evidence: Management said enrollment is expected to complete “later in 2026,” with “top-line data expected roughly four to five weeks after enrollment completion.”
expectation_evidence: “Reiteration (or not) of 2H26 topline”; the preview said the buy-side was listening for “‘second half of 2026’ topline reiterated verbatim.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview did not anticipate a larger estimated U.S. CRRT market: Talphera’s updated research put 2027 annual procedures at about 200,000, up 21% from its prior estimate of 165,000.
fact_evidence: “Updated market research raised the estimated 2027 annual U.S. CRRT procedures to approximately 200,000, a 21% increase from the prior estimate of 165,000.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview did not flag new guideline support for Nefamostat. The 2026 KDIGO guideline now references it as an acceptable regional anticoagulant alternative to citrate for the first time, although final publication is still pending.
fact_evidence: “The 2026 KDIGO clinical practice guideline … now references Nefamostat as an acceptable regional anticoagulant alternative to citrate for the first time.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Talphera reported an additional potential source of market access not anticipated in the preview: about three-quarters of U.S. institutions lack citrate, which management said could leave a large potential market for Nefamostat from launch.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 75% of U.S. institutions do not have citrate available,” and citrate “is not FDA approved for CRRT and carries usage complexities, creating a large potential market for Nefamostat out of the gate.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview did not describe Talphera’s specific commercial rollout plan. Management said CRRT procedures are concentrated in about 70 U.S. institutions, supporting a targeted rollout with account managers and educators rather than a traditional sales force.
fact_evidence: “About 70 U.S. institutions [represent] over 50% of CRRT procedures,” supporting “a targeted commercial rollout using account managers and educators rather than a traditional sales force.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview mentioned partnering only as possible upside optionality; the call disclosed a specific post-readout negotiation right held by CoreMedix. This creates a concrete strategic-partner pathway, but no partnership was announced.
fact_evidence: “CoreMedix holds a right of first negotiation for 60 days post data readout, and its CEO Joe Tedisco sits on Talphera’s board, representing a potential strategic partnership consideration.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “commentary on PMA module pre-work, or on partnering/commercialization” as “upside optionality.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview did not anticipate disclosure of blinded-study dosing results. Talphera said most patients reached therapeutic range at the starting dose within about half an hour and that the independent safety committee recommended continuing without changes, a favorable interim signal.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 80-85% of patients reached therapeutic range at the starting dose within about half an hour,” most were titrated to “20-25 mg/hour, well below the 50 mg maximum,” and the committee “recommended continuing without changes.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.40, well above the preview’s $0.29 consensus and $0.30–$0.32 estimate. The preview expected adjusted EPS to decline year over year, whereas the reported figure was up $0.02 per share.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $25.3 million or $0.40 per diluted share, up only $0.02 per share year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.29” consensus; “$0.30–0.32” estimate; the preview also described the consensus as “–19.4%” year over year.

description: Revenue of $543.7 million exceeded both the $526.2 million consensus and the preview’s $528–$532 million estimate, as well as the stated consensus range high of $539.5 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 16.9% year-over-year to $543.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $526.2M” consensus and “$528–532M” estimate; consensus range “$479.3–539.5M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA guidance was held at $473–$483 million even though the preview said a raise was the key question and that buyers expected one; the preview specifically warned that a hold could signal disappointment. The reported $30 million revenue-guidance increase was mostly fuel recovery fees, not a corresponding increase to EBITDA guidance.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $473-$483 million”; revenue guidance rose by $30 million, “majority fuel recovery fees.”
expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects a raise given the Q1 outperformance”; “A hold after explicitly deferring the decision last quarter reads as a negative signal.”

description: The adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 22.7%, down 80 basis points, well below the preview’s roughly 23.3% estimate and its expectation that fuel would dilute margin by about 30 basis points. Resource Solutions added an unexpected 70-basis-point drag, despite the preview anticipating that recovering OCC prices could become a modest tailwind.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin declined 80 basis points to 22.7%, hurt by 40 bps from fuel and 70 bps from Resource Solutions.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin … ~23.3%”; the preview modeled fuel “dilut[ing] optics ~30bps” and said the OCC year-over-year comparison would turn into a “modest tailwind.”

description: GAAP net income guidance was lowered again, from the existing $4–$10 million range to $0–$6 million, while the preview listed the $4–$10 million range as the standing guide. The company attributed the new reduction to higher amortization and taxes.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net income guidance lowered to $0-$6 million on higher amortization and taxes.”
expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance listed “Net Income (GAAP) $4–10M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Landfill volumes surged 8.4%, including a sharp increase in third-party tons. That was a strong positive datapoint against the preview’s central volume debate, which framed Q2 around whether solid-waste volumes would remain weak or improve only to around –1.0% to –1.5%.
fact_evidence: “Landfill volumes surged 8.4% (86,000 tons) year-over-year, with third-party volume up 62,000 tons and internalized volume up 24,000 tons.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the quarter that proves or breaks that claim”; the preview’s base case expected “Volume –1.0 to –1.5%.”

description: Five acquisitions had been completed year to date, representing about $165 million of annualized revenue—more than the preview’s expectation of four deals totaling about $150 million.
fact_evidence: “Five acquisitions completed year-to-date represent approximately $165 million of annualized revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Four deals closed YTD (~$150M annualized revenue).”

description: NCM announced a definitive $275 million acquisition of Captivate, a digital elevator and lobby advertising operator—an unanticipated expansion beyond its cinema network. Captivate reported $64 million of 2025 revenue and $19.3 million of adjusted EBITDA, and NCM expects at least $3.5 million in annual run-rate cost synergies; the deal will be debt-financed and bring net leverage to about 3.9x at close.
fact_evidence: NCM signed a definitive agreement to acquire Captivate for an enterprise value of $275 million, approximately 10x pro forma EBITDA including synergies. Captivate generated approximately $64 million revenue and $19.3 million adjusted EBITDA in 2025; management expects at least $3.5 million of annual run-rate cost synergies. The acquisition will be financed with $275 million of new committed term debt, resulting in net leverage of approximately 3.9x at close.

description: NCM provided no forward guidance because the Captivate transaction is pending, despite the preview identifying Q3 guidance as the key issue and deriving a roughly $68–71 million Q3 revenue bar. Investors therefore did not get the expected read on the second half or whether the FY revenue model remained achievable.
fact_evidence: No forward guidance was provided due to the pending transaction.
expectation_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue/OIBDA guidance. This is the whole ballgame”; “implying a Q3 guide of roughly $68–71M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Attendance growth greatly exceeded the preview’s estimate, but the extra moviegoers did not translate into commensurate advertising yield gains. The preview expected attendance growth of 5.9%, while NCM reported approximately 19.3% growth and said lower-yielding horror films and FIFA-related budget shifts limited yield.
fact_evidence: “Network attendance grew approximately 19.3% year-over-year, but strong turnout from lower-yielding R-rated horror films (Backrooms, Obsession) plus a FIFA World Cup budget shift limited advertising yield gains.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus attendance: “122.15M” versus “115.30M,” or “+5.9%” year over year.
