description: The preview expected Balloon Museum rent to have commenced and called for confirmation of the start date and early attendance. The call facts instead place Balloon Museum among non-income-producing space still opening within the next 18 months and provide no attendance or rent-start confirmation.
fact_evidence: The company has “over 194,000 square feet of non-income-producing space opening within 18 months,” including “Balloon Museum,” with incremental EBITDA “yet to materialize.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the museum “opened July 15, 2026” and that “Three weeks of operating data will exist by the call”; it identified rent commencement and early attendance as key items to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: SEG substantially reduced available seaport leasing space, from roughly 150,000–200,000 square feet to under 50,000 square feet. This is progress beyond the preview’s focus on the roughly 20,000-square-foot One Seaport Plaza vacancy, although management cautioned that the remaining smaller spaces may take longer to lease.
fact_evidence: “Available seaport leasing space fell from roughly 150,000-200,000 square feet to under 50,000 square feet,” while “remaining smaller footprints are expected to take longer to lease.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted One Seaport Plaza as “~20,000 sf, the last material vacancy” and said a signed anchor there would effectively complete lease-up.

description: The company had cut trailing 12-month G&A by more than 20% over nine months, even though the preview said management had warned that the pace of reductions would moderate. That indicates stronger cost reduction over the period than that expectation suggested.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month G&A was reduced more than 20% over nine months to under $27 million from $34 million in Q3 2025”; management is “targeting further cuts as legacy contracts expire.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “management warned the pace of reduction moderates from here.”

description: Remaining capital expenditures were estimated at $50–70 million over the next two years, below the preview’s $70–90 million estimate for remaining capex through 2028.
fact_evidence: SEG “expects $50-70 million in remaining capital expenditures over the next two years to reach 2028 stabilization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$70–90M of remaining capex through 2028.”

description: Sadie’s Garden Bar grew revenue 125% year over year in its first full quarter under company management, a strong operating result not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the hospitality segment.
fact_evidence: “Sadie's Garden Bar grew revenue 125% year-over-year in its first full quarter under company management.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled hospitality at $9.8 million versus $15.2 million a year earlier, attributing the expected decline to the Tin Building closure, but did not flag this growth at Sadie’s.

description: GEN’s Q1 revenue was $1.34 billion, above the preview’s $1.300–$1.312 billion consensus range and the $1.325 billion top of company guidance. Revenue growth of 11% also exceeded the preview’s 8–10% pro forma growth guide; bookings grew 11% as well.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 bookings and revenue both grew 11% year-over-year to $1.28 billion and $1.34 billion respectively, the fastest revenue growth rate since Gen was created.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company Guide … $1.300–1.325B | Street Consensus ~$1.300B … / $1.312B …”; “management guided Q1 to ‘+8–10% pro forma.’”

description: Non-GAAP EPS reached $0.71, above both the preview’s $0.69 consensus and the $0.68–$0.70 guided range. That was a stronger result than the preview’s base case of $0.69–$0.70.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $0.71, up 19% year-over-year and beating the guided range of $0.68-$0.70.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Street Consensus $0.69 …”; “Base … Non-GAAP EPS $0.69–0.70.”

description: Rather than maintaining FY27 guidance as the preview’s base case anticipated, GEN raised its revenue and EPS ranges. The new midpoints are $5.425 billion in revenue and $2.92 EPS, versus prior midpoints of $5.375 billion and $2.90.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance to 9%-11% revenue growth (to $5.375-$5.475 billion) and 14%-18% non-GAAP EPS growth (to $2.87-$2.97), up from prior guidance of 8%-10% revenue and mid-teens EPS.”
expectation_evidence: “Base … FY27 maintained”; “With Street pinned to the $2.90 midpoint, maintaining FY27 is a de facto disappointment.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Cyber Safety did not reaccelerate to the 6–8% bookings growth the preview said to watch for: bookings and revenue each grew 4%, below that target and below the segment’s 5% bookings exit rate. This contrasts with the much faster growth in Trust-Based Solutions.
fact_evidence: “Cyber Safety bookings and revenue each grew only mid-single digits (4%), while Trust-Based Solution bookings grew 25% and revenue grew 24%, showing the growth is concentrated in the Trust segment.”
expectation_evidence: “Exited FY26 at only +5% bookings … Watch for mid-single-digit → 6–8%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Engine’s annual network inquiries exceeded the preview’s roughly $400 million reference point, reaching more than $425 million; the marketplace also surpassed a $0.5 billion annual revenue run rate. The preview discussed Engine expansion but did not give an expected revenue run rate.
fact_evidence: “The Engine embedded marketplace surpassed a $0.5 billion annual revenue run rate with over 30 new partnerships added and total network inquiries exceeding $425 million annually.”
expectation_evidence: “Engine ~400M annual inquiries”; the preview also noted “Engine expansion” as part of the expected H2 contribution.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: MoneyLion connected accounts exceeded the preview’s 107 million figure, reaching more than 110 million. The call also reported that 35% of the paid base engages with financial wellness, for which the preview gave no specific benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Connected financial accounts grew to over 110 million from 75 million at MoneyLion's acquisition, with 35% of the paid base now engaging with financial wellness.”
expectation_evidence: “connected accounts 107M (+36%).”

description: Instead of revising its full-year sales outlook downward, Heron withdrew its $173–183 million net product sales guidance altogether. The preview expected a cut, with its base case at $155–168 million.
fact_evidence: The company withdrew its full-year 2026 guidance of $173–183 million in net product sales, citing generic uncertainty, spending cuts, and strategic review.
expectation_evidence: “I assign ~70% probability to a guidance cut on this print”; base case: “FY guide cut to $155–168M.”

description: Heron also withdrew its $10–20 million adjusted EBITDA guidance rather than providing a lower or revised target. The preview identified withdrawal of this guidance as a bearish possibility, but its base case anticipated a reduction toward breakeven.
fact_evidence: The company withdrew its full-year 2026 guidance of $10–20 million in adjusted EBITDA, citing generic uncertainty, spending cuts, and strategic review.
expectation_evidence: The preview's base case anticipated “adj. EBITDA guide cut toward breakeven”; it also called withdrawal of this guide “the bear trigger.”

description: Heron disclosed a strategic-alternatives process with no timetable and no assurance of a transaction. The preview named this kind of review as a bear-case signal, but it was not part of its base-case outlook.
fact_evidence: Management is exploring strategic alternatives with no set timetable and no assurance a transaction will result; the process is also reflected in the amended credit agreement.
expectation_evidence: The preview said a bear-case signal would be management “evaluating strategic alternatives” or capital-structure options.

description: The Hercules amendment requires up to $17.5 million of principal reduction, including $13.5 million paid immediately, and could leave cash at about $24.3 million after a further payment. The preview flagged Hercules covenant status and possible amendments as issues to watch, but did not anticipate this size of cash outflow.
fact_evidence: The company agreed to a principal reduction of up to $17.5 million ($13.5 million paid at execution plus a potential further $4 million by September 15); pro forma cash falls to roughly $28.5 million and then about $24.3 million, from $42.7 million at quarter-end.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “cash vs. the $44.8M base” and “Hercules covenant compliance” as balance-sheet issues to watch, and noted “any amendment, waiver, or forward-looking covenant caution.”

description: Heron paused its planned second-half Salesforce expansion and tightened spending after the court decision. The preview focused on whether Zynrelef could sustain growth, but did not anticipate this specific commercial pullback.
fact_evidence: The company paused its planned second-half Salesforce expansion and tightened spending following the June court decision.
expectation_evidence: The preview called Zynrelef “the only genuine growth asset” and said it “needs >$11.5M to keep the acute-care story intact.”

description: Zynrelef sales were $11.1 million, slightly below the preview's $11.5 million threshold, and average daily unit growth was 19% year over year rather than the 22% demand growth cited in the preview. The sales shortfall was modest, though the preview also expected strong growth.
fact_evidence: Zynrelef net sales were $11.1 million, up 9% sequentially and 35% year-over-year, with average daily units growing 19% year-over-year but below internal targets.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Zynrelef “needs >$11.5M to keep the acute-care story intact” and cited “demand units +22% YoY.”

description: Aponvy reached $4.2 million in sales, above the preview's $3.9 million base-case build, and its share of the surgical NK1 segment rose to 23%.
fact_evidence: Aponvy net sales reached $4.2 million, up 74% year-over-year, capturing 23% of the surgical NK1 segment, up two points sequentially.
expectation_evidence: The preview's base-case build estimated Aponvy at “$3.9M.”

description: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at $9.43–9.45 billion and described a bull case of $9.65 billion or more. Amgen reported revenue above $10 billion, a substantially larger beat than either the consensus or the preview’s bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Total revenues exceeded $10 billion in Q2 2026, a 10% year-over-year increase.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $9.43–9.45B”; bull scenario: “Revenue | $9.65B+.”

description: The preview said a raise was important and framed a narrow-and-raise as the guide to watch. Amgen raised both full-year guidance ranges, with the revenue range moving to $38.2–39.4 billion and the EPS range to $22.30–23.50; the revenue midpoint is above the preview’s $37.8 billion consensus, while the new EPS midpoint is roughly in line with its consensus.
fact_evidence: “Amgen raised full-year 2026 guidance to total revenues of $38.2 billion to $39.4 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $22.30 to $23.50.”
expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “$37.1B – $38.5B” revenue and “$21.70 – $23.10” non-GAAP EPS; consensus was “~$37.8B” revenue and “~$22.90” EPS. The preview called a “narrow-and-raise” the action to watch.

description: Repatha exceeded the preview’s $904.4 million estimate by about 5%, and its reported 37% growth was also above the preview’s roughly 30% growth expectation. The preview’s bull case had identified sales above $950 million as upside.
fact_evidence: “Repatha delivered $953 million in sales growing 37% year-over-year, with new-to-brand prescriptions growing more than 50% in the U.S.”
expectation_evidence: “Repatha — total | $904.4M | +29.9%”; bull scenario: “Repatha >$950M.”

description: The preview expected margins to hold around 45–46%. Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 48%, above that expectation, although full-year margin guidance remained roughly 45–46% of product sales.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 48%”; full-year operating margin was guided to “roughly 45%-46% of product sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected non-GAAP operating margin of “~45–46%” and said the base case was that “margins hold ~45–46%.”

description: The preview highlighted UPLIZNA’s 188% Q1 growth and warned that deceleration in a growth driver could weaken the growth-portfolio thesis. UPLIZNA still grew rapidly, but its reported Q2 year-over-year growth rate was 90%, well below that highlighted Q1 rate.
fact_evidence: “UPLIZNA sales surged 90% year-over-year to $335 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 UPLIZNA sales growth of “+188%” and said “Any one of these decelerating undermines the ‘new portfolio outruns the cliff’ thesis.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview focused on MariTide’s planned Phase III readouts and dosing cohorts but did not anticipate that Amgen would discontinue a separate Phase I obesity asset. Ending development of AMG 513 removes that program from the obesity pipeline.
fact_evidence: “Amgen discontinued development of AMG 513, a Phase I obesity asset.”

description: The call disclosed that a Q3 business-development transaction will bring a $100 million upfront R&D payment and a meaningful sequential increase in operating expenses, an expense item and near-term cost increase not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “A Q3 business development transaction will trigger a $100 million upfront R&D payment, contributing to an expected meaningful sequential increase in Q3 operating expenses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed cyber remediation, legal costs, and the MariTide R&D ramp as potential cost pressures, but did not mention this transaction or its payment.

description: The preview did not flag a CFO transition. The call reported that Peter Griffith is departing and Thomas Dittrich is taking over, an unanticipated management change.
fact_evidence: “CFO Peter Griffith departs as Thomas Dittrich takes over.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Amgen reported that MariTide is being advanced across nine ongoing and three planned Phase III studies, with a target of as few as four to six doses per year. The preview expected Phase III progress and early-2027 readouts, but did not anticipate this breadth of studies or the stated dosing target.
fact_evidence: “Advancing MariTide through 9 ongoing and 3 planned Phase III studies targeting as few as 4-6 doses per year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described two Phase III studies reading out “early 2027” and advised watching for maintenance-dosing information; it gave no expectation of nine ongoing and three planned studies or a four-to-six-dose annual target.

description: The preview modeled Q2 retail adjusted EBITDAR at about $505–515 million and expected a roughly 33.5% margin amid the Aurora disruption and new-property costs. PENN reported $517.2 million at a 34.4% margin, above the estimate range and the anticipated margin softness.
fact_evidence: “Retail segment achieved record quarterly revenues of $1.5 billion and adjusted EBITDAR of $517.2 million,” with “margins of 34.4%.”
expectation_evidence: “Retail adj. EBITDAR ~$505–515M”; the base case expected “~$500–515M, margin ~33.5%,” while the preview said the Aurora closure and opening-period costs “argue for a soft optical margin.”

description: The preview’s existing retail guidance midpoint was $5.795 billion of revenue and $1.93 billion of adjusted EBITDAR, with a raise viewed as a possible catalyst. PENN raised the 2026 midpoints to $5.87 billion and $1.963 billion, respectively.
fact_evidence: “PENN raised its full-year 2026 retail guidance to $5.87 billion revenue and $1.963 billion adjusted EBITDAR at the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: The guidance in force was “Retail revenue | $5.73B–$5.86B” and “Retail adj. EBITDAR | $1.88B–$1.98B”; the preview said “any FY guidance revision” was worth watching and called a second consecutive retail raise a catalyst.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview described the year-end lease-adjusted net leverage outlook as 5.3x–5.7x. Management now says PENN is deleveraging faster than expected and is targeting leverage below 5x.
fact_evidence: PENN’s 2026 outlook includes “faster-than-expected deleveraging”; management is “targeting lease-adjusted net leverage below 5x.”
expectation_evidence: “YE lease-adj. net leverage | 5.3x–5.7x (>1 turn improvement).”

description: The preview expected Interactive revenue of about $355–375 million, based on roughly $1.6 billion of full-year guidance. Q2 revenue was $349.4 million, and PENN cut its 2026 Interactive revenue guidance to $1.57 billion.
fact_evidence: “The Interactive segment posted revenues of $349.4 million”; PENN “lowered its 2026 Interactive revenue guidance to $1.57 billion from $1.6 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Interactive revenue | ~$355–375M”; full-year guidance was “Interactive revenue | ~$1.6B (incl. ~$820M tax gross-up).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview knew Aurora had opened but identified the prior riverboat shutdown as a Q2 retail drag and sought early ramp data. The new Aurora roughly doubled admissions, slot volumes, table volumes, and non-gaming revenue versus the prior year; rated guests staying at the hotel had 21% higher daily worth, and 20% of guests were new to the property.
fact_evidence: Hollywood Casino Aurora “roughly doubled admissions, slot volumes, table volumes and non-gaming revenue versus prior year,” with “rated guests generating 21% higher daily worth when staying at the hotel and 20% of guests being new to the property.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “a ~2-week shutdown of the legacy riverboat in late May/early June — a known drag on Q2 retail” and said to watch for “Early Aurora / Columbus ramp data points.”

description: The preview noted Columbus’s hotel tower opening but gave no expectation of an immediate record or the share of hotel revenue coming from outer-market guests. In July, its first full month with the tower, Hollywood Columbus set an all-time net revenue record, with outer-market guests generating 85% of hotel cash revenue.
fact_evidence: “Hollywood Columbus set an all-time net revenue record in July, its first full month with the new hotel tower, with outer-market guests accounting for 85% of hotel cash revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview stated that the “203-room, ~$100M hotel tower opened June 12” and flagged early Columbus ramp data as something to watch.

description: The preview expected total 2026 CapEx of $420 million, including $200 million of project CapEx. PENN reduced project CapEx to $180 million and total CapEx to $400 million, and said the $31 million retail EBITDA guidance increase flows fully into improved cash flow.
fact_evidence: “PENN reduced 2026 project CapEx to $180 million from $200 million (total CapEx cut to $400 million), and the $31 million retail EBITDA guidance increase flows fully into improved cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: “Capex | $420M ($200M project / $220M maintenance).”

description: The preview discussed leverage and buybacks but did not anticipate the specific debt transactions PENN reported. The company extended major debt maturities and repaid $106.7 million of convertible notes, eliminating 4.5 million potentially dilutive shares.
fact_evidence: PENN “refinanc[ed] its $1 billion revolver and Term Loan A to 2031, extend[ed] Term Loan B to 2033, and repay[ed] $106.7 million of convertible notes to eliminate 4.5 million potentially dilutive shares.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview said investors wanted to see sports-betting hold nearer 9.0% after 8.4% the prior quarter. Instead, PENN said customer-friendly sports outcomes reduced quarterly hold by roughly $3 million, indicating an adverse outcome rather than the anticipated hold improvement.
fact_evidence: “Customer-friendly sports outcomes creating roughly a $3 million hold impact for the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Street is looking for hold nearer ~9.0% vs. 8.4% last quarter.”

description: The preview described M&A as something PENN might pursue opportunistically. Management instead emphasized a high bar: a deal must outperform returns from deleveraging, buybacks, and internal growth projects, while also saying the 2027 consensus implies a nearly 20% free cash flow yield that makes buybacks attractive.
fact_evidence: Management cited “a nearly 20% free cash flow yield on 2027 consensus making buybacks attractive, and a high bar for M&A that must beat returns on deleveraging, buybacks, and internal growth projects.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said PENN had “said it would act opportunistically” on M&A and listed buyback pace and capital return as items to watch.

description: Q2 loss per share was $0.33, better than the preview’s $0.44 loss consensus and its base-case range of $0.40–$0.50. The loss also improved 32% sequentially, although net loss was still 6% worse year over year.
fact_evidence: “Net loss was $3.97 million in Q2 2026, a 32% sequential improvement from $5.83 million but a 6% worse result year-over-year, with loss per share improving to $0.33 from $0.71 a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” EPS: “$(0.44)”; the base scenario also projected EPS of “$(0.40)–$(0.50).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 operating cash outflow fell to $3.4 million, below the preview’s $5 million level of concern and sharply down from Q1. This was a better quarterly cash-burn result than the preview’s key risk framing implied, though cash burn and going-concern concerns remain.
fact_evidence: “Net cash used in operating activities improved 58% sequentially to $3.4 million in Q2 2026 from $8.2 million in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything above ~$5M undermines the ‘cash-flow positive in 2026’ claim outright”; management had said Q1 working-capital use would “not repeat at the same magnitude.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: NEXUS was already generating meaningful sales soon after launch: it reached $1 million in cumulative sales in about 10 weeks, with another $1.5 million in orders in July. The preview expected a first disclosed contribution but said NEXUS had not contributed meaningfully in Q1 and did not anticipate this scale or pace.
fact_evidence: “The new NEXUS tonneau cover reached $1 million in cumulative sales within about 10 weeks of its April 13 production launch and generated approximately $1.5 million in sales orders in July alone.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “first disclosed revenue contribution from SOLIS, COR (UL/CSA certified April), and NEXUS” and that “none contributed meaningfully in Q1.”

description: Management put a sizable gap between current revenue and operating cash-flow breakeven: at a 35% margin, it says roughly $12.9 million in quarterly revenue is needed to cover the current cost structure, versus Q2 sales of $5.2 million. That makes the preview’s 2026 cash-flow-positive expectation look more demanding than the preview’s already difficult H2 revenue math alone suggested.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit covered only about 32% of the quarter's recurring cash operating requirements, with roughly $12.9 million in quarterly revenue at 35% margins needed to fully cover the current cost structure absent expense cuts.”
expectation_evidence: Company-guided FY2026 included “operational cash-flow positive during 2026”; the preview described the low end of revenue guidance as requiring “~$26.6M in H2.”

description: The cash-flow-positive goal remained for 2026, but management would not give a calendar target for sustained breakeven and described only a possible momentary positive quarter in Q3. That is less definite than the preview’s expectation of operational cash-flow positivity during 2026.
fact_evidence: “Management believes it may reach momentary operating cash flow positivity in Q3 2026 but declined to provide a specific calendar target for sustained breakeven, which it still aims to achieve in 2026.”
expectation_evidence: Company guidance, “reaffirmed May 13, 2026,” was “operational cash-flow positive during 2026.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory had increased by $2.5 million from year-end and included $4.6 million of finished goods, even as the preview expected inventory to convert to revenue and reduce working-capital use. Management’s identification of inventory as its largest internal liquidity source also underscores reliance on selling down stock to fund operations.
fact_evidence: “Inventory stood at $12.1 million (up $2.5 million from year-end), including $6.6 million raw materials, $4.6 million (roughly 6,800 covers) finished goods, and $845,000 work-in-progress, which management targets as its largest internal liquidity source.”
expectation_evidence: Management said Q1 working-capital use would “not repeat at the same magnitude as inventory converts to revenue.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Worksport reported two distributor additions, including Meyer as its first multinational partner, and discussions with three more major distributors. The preview expected distribution activation but did not flag a first multinational partner or this specific pipeline.
fact_evidence: “The company added two distributors in Q2, including its first multinational partner Meyer Distributing, is in talks with three additional major distributors.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “distribution activation” and said to watch for a hard number of dealer locations, with a target of 1,500+ by year-end.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: AetherLux certification is expected in fall 2026, with product available 45–60 days afterward, bringing a product milestone forward relative to the preview’s framing of Terravis/AetherLux as a 2027+ story.
fact_evidence: “The company added two distributors in Q2 … and expects AetherLux heat pump certification in fall 2026 with product available 45-60 days thereafter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Terravis/AetherLux “a 2027+ story” and said “no 2026 revenue is projected.”

description: The preview's base case was EPS of $1.88–$1.92, with a ~$1.90 whisper, but TXRH reported $1.85. That was slightly above the $1.83 consensus cited in the preview, yet below its higher expected bar.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS declined 0.7% to $1.85.”
expectation_evidence: “My base estimate: revenue ~$1.69B, EPS ~$1.90”; the base scenario gave EPS of “$1.88–1.92.” The preview also cited consensus EPS of “$1.83.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comps were strong but came in a little below the preview's 6.5% base and buy-side expectation. They also eased from 6.7% in May to 5.7% in June, though the preview's implied-consensus comp estimate was lower, at about 5%.
fact_evidence: “Comparable sales rose 6.2%”; monthly comps were “6.2%, 6.7% and 5.7% for April, May and June.”
expectation_evidence: The preview's base case was “+6.5%” comps and said the buy side expected “comps 6.5%+”; it also said published consensus implied roughly “5.0%.”

description: TXRH cut full-year commodity inflation guidance to about 5%, a larger cut than the preview's bull-case range of 5–6% and a contrast with its base case of holding at 6–7%. The preview expected Q2 to be the peak; management also described a sharp Q3 easing before inflation rises again in Q4.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 commodity inflation guidance was lowered from 6%-7% to approximately 5%,” with Q3 inflation “just 2%-3% (versus 7% in Q2)” before returning to “about 5% in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide was “currently 6–7%,” with a “second cut to 5–6%” as the bull catalyst; its base case was that management “reiterates 6–7%” and calls Q2 the peak.

description: Restaurant margin was better than the preview's expected range despite still declining year over year: 16.4% versus the preview's 16.0–16.3% estimate, with a 66-basis-point decline rather than the expected 80–110 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Restaurant margin as a percentage of sales fell 66 basis points to 16.4%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~16.0–16.3%” margin and expected a decline of “−80 to −110bps.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The average check rose 3.2%, below the 3.6% menu pricing the preview cited, suggesting some check or mix dilution even as traffic grew. Traffic was up 3%, below the prior-quarter 4.5% figure discussed in the preview, though the preview did not give a specific Q2 traffic forecast.
fact_evidence: Comps were driven by “3% traffic growth and a 3.2% higher average check.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “3.6% menu pricing” and flagged “mix erosion” if check underperformed that pricing; it described Q1 as “+4.5% traffic / +2.6% check.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management announced a 1% menu price increase for the start of Q4, resolving the preview's open question in favor of additional pricing rather than relying only on the existing carryover. That supports margin defense, though the preview also noted the possible traffic-confidence trade-off.
fact_evidence: “The company will implement a 1% menu price increase at the start of Q4, bringing effective pricing to 2.9% in both Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said pricing was “currently 1.9% carryover ‘plus any additional’” and flagged the “Q4 pricing decision” as an important unknown.

description: Management newly quantified a holiday-calendar headwind to Q4 same-store sales, which the preview did not flag: shifted Halloween and Christmas calendars are expected to reduce comps by about 75 basis points.
fact_evidence: Management “flagged an estimated ~75 basis point negative impact to Q4 same-store sales from Halloween and Christmas holiday calendar shifts.”

description: Labor costs improved by 40 basis points even though traffic grew 3%, with labor hours up only 0.8%. The preview did not identify this labor leverage, while wage inflation guidance remained at 3–4%.
fact_evidence: “Labor costs improved 40 basis points to 32.5% of sales as labor hours grew only 0.8% against 3% traffic growth,” while “wage inflation of 3.9%” kept the “3%-4% full-year guidance intact.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Weekly sales reached a company record, exceeding $175,000 for the first time in TXRH's 33-year history. The preview discussed revenue and comps expectations but did not anticipate this sales-per-week milestone.
fact_evidence: “Q2 average weekly sales exceeded $175,000 for the first time in the company's 33-year history,” including over $183,000 at company-operated Texas Roadhouse, over $129,000 at Bubba's 33, and over $76,000 at Jaggers.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: To-go sales exceeded $25,000 per week and dining-room mix turned positive during the quarter. The preview did not forecast these channel-mix developments.
fact_evidence: “To-go sales reached over $25,000 per week, representing 14.3% of total weekly sales while dining room mix turned positive during the quarter.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Contract momentum was far stronger than the preview’s recent weekly data suggested: Opendoor said it was signing over 500 purchase contracts a week, reached roughly 700 in the latest week, and had 6,908 acquisition contracts. That points to a much stronger forward pipeline than the preview’s report of weekly contracts up 12% in mid-July.
fact_evidence: “signing over 500 purchase contracts weekly,” hitting “a multi-year high of roughly 700 last week,” with acquisition contracts “reaching 6,908.”
expectation_evidence: “Weekly contract data showed +12% in the week ended July 18”; the preview warned that if contracts stalled, Q3/Q4 revenue could re-accelerate downward.

description: The Q3 outlook combines stronger growth language with a lower contribution-margin forecast: revenue is guided up at least 20% year over year and contribution profit more than doubles, but margin is expected to fall to 4%-4.5%. The margin decline is less severe than Opendoor’s historical seasonal pattern, but it does not match the preview’s preference for Q3 growth with contribution margin held.
fact_evidence: “For Q3, the company guided to revenue up at least 20% year-over-year, contribution profit more than doubling year-over-year, and contribution margin of ~4%-4.5%, reflecting seasonal decline better than its historical 470 bps Q2-to-Q3 average.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side wanted “sequential growth and CM held,” and described the base case as Q3 revenue “roughly flat-to-up modestly.”

description: Q2 contribution margin and contribution profit came in a little below the preview’s midpoint expectations: margin was 5.8% versus about 6%, and contribution profit was $51 million versus about $54 million. The margin was still within Opendoor’s 5%-7% guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Contribution margin climbed to 5.8%” and contribution profit was “$51 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed contribution margin consensus at “~6% (guide midpoint)” and contribution profit at “~$54M.”

description: Opendoor described substantial operating-productivity improvements that were not quantified in the preview: per-acquisition operations expense fell to $3,000 from $8,400 a year earlier, while project managers and underwriters are handling many more homes. These gains reinforce a leaner cost structure than the preview’s profitability discussion captured.
fact_evidence: “home project managers now handling ~10 renovations each (up from 3, targeting 20), underwriters doing 50+ per day (up from 20), and per-acquisition operations expense falling to $3,000 from $8,400 a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted fixed OpEx of “$33M, −$6M Y/Y” and estimated a roughly “$63M below-the-line bridge,” but did not anticipate these productivity figures or the per-acquisition expense decline.

description: The company said it built inventory largely with nonrecourse asset-backed financing, rather than the preview’s stated expectation that inventory growth would be funded from its cash balance. This is a meaningful difference in how the expansion was financed.
fact_evidence: “grew inventory by over $700 million funded largely by nonrecourse asset-backed facilities.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Growth funded from the $999M cash balance with no equity raise.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Mortgage attach appears to be gaining traction quickly, with more than half of scheduled Colorado closings and nearly one in five in Texas financed through Opendoor just six weeks after launch. However, the stated plan to reach 35-40 states by year-end is later than the preview’s target of 20-plus states by Q3.
fact_evidence: “over half of scheduled closes in Colorado and nearly 1 in 5 in Texas (just 6 weeks post-launch) are financed through Opendoor, with plans to be licensed in 35-40 states by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “20+ states targeted by Q3” and listed mortgage expansion and attach rates as items to watch.

description: Marketing spend dropped sharply to $5 million, from $19 million in Q1, taking marketing from 1.6% to 0.3% of acquisition GMV. The preview did not forecast a cut of this size, so the lower spend is an unexpected cost reduction, though its effect on future acquisition momentum is not specified.
fact_evidence: “Marketing spend fell dramatically to just $5 million in Q2 (from $19 million in Q1), lowering marketing as a percent of acquisition GMV from 1.6% under Opendoor 1.0 to 0.3%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed fixed OpEx and profitability but did not give an expected Q2 marketing-spend level.

description: Ibsrela came in well below the preview’s $95–100 million build at $86.2 million, and Ardelyx cut its 2026 Ibsrela outlook from $410–430 million to $350–370 million. Management attributed slower new-patient starts to stricter prior authorizations and step edits, which are delaying rather than blocking prescriptions.
fact_evidence: “Ibsrela Q2 revenue was $86.2 million”; management “lowered full-year 2026 Ibsrela guidance to $350-$370 million”; “Payers implemented more stringent prior authorizations and step edits that slowed new patient starts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s build estimated “IBSRELA $95–100M” and said current FY guidance was “$410–430M IBSRELA.”

description: Xphozah revenue of $31.9 million substantially exceeded the preview’s $24–26 million estimate, and Ardelyx kept its 2026 outlook at $110–120 million despite the preview identifying that range as vulnerable to a cut.
fact_evidence: “Xphozah revenue was $31.9 million (up 27% YoY), driven by strong demand”; the company “reiterated full-year 2026 Xphozah guidance of $110-$120 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “XPHOZAH $24–26M” for Q2 and called it “where the cut risk sits,” with a trim identified as the most likely messy-print outcome.

description: Ardelyx withdrew its $750 million long-term Xphozah revenue guidance rather than framing the 2027 opportunity as an upside case. Management cited uncertainty around the end of TDAPA, a proposed phosphorus QIP measure, and competing binders in development.
fact_evidence: “The company pulled its $750 million long-term Xphozah revenue guidance,” citing “uncertainty from the end of the TDAPA period, a proposed phosphorus QIP quality measure, and competitive binders in development.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “2027 XPHOZAH framing post-TDAPA cliff” as an “under-owned upside” and said management’s framing of the opportunity was a “free option.”

description: The company lowered its 2026 operating-expense outlook to below $500 million, better than the preview’s expectation of roughly $520 million. This is a more favorable cost outlook even though SG&A and R&D were higher year over year in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Revising 2026 OPEX guidance to below $500 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 opex was “guided to ~$520M” and flagged spending above that level as a bear trigger.

description: Ardelyx drew $50 million from its SLR arrangement, a financing step not identified in the preview, which had highlighted the cash balance and undrawn facility. The draw supported a higher reported cash balance, but also means more borrowing rather than an improvement funded solely by operations.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $281.8 million in cash and equivalents and drew down $50 million from its SLR arrangement.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Cash fell $26.6M in Q1 to $238.1M against $234M of debt” and noted “$100M undrawn.”

description: Free-cash-flow guidance was cut by about $200 million to $150–$200 million, rather than being held at the preview’s expected $350–$400 million. That is roughly a 50% reduction at the midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was cut by roughly $200 million… now expected at $150-$200 million for the year versus a prior forecast of $350-$400 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Management called it AP-timing ‘noise’ reversing in Q2–Q3 and held FY FCF.”

description: Gross margin was 4.9%, below the preview’s 6.0%–6.5% estimate, and Energy margin was slightly negative rather than the modeled 2%–4%. The reported margin damage was therefore worse than expected.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin collapsed to 4.9% in Q2 from 12.3% a year earlier”; renewables overruns pushed “Energy segment margins slightly negative versus 10.8% prior year.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin (my est.) ~6.0–6.5%”; Energy segment “Q2 2026E GM 2–4%.”

description: The expected Energy margin recovery is arriving more slowly: management guided to 6%–8% in Q3 and 8%–10% in Q4, rather than the preview’s expectation that Q3 would gravitate toward normal and Q4 would reach 10%–12%.
fact_evidence: “Energy segment gross margins are guided to 6%-8% in Q3 and 8%-10% in Q4, before returning to the normal 10%-12% range in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 ‘gravitating back toward normal,’ Q4 reaching the 10–12% target.”

description: Revenue came in slightly below consensus: just under $1.7 billion versus the preview’s $1.734 billion estimate. The gap was modest, and the Energy decline was broadly in line with the preview’s modeled decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was just under $1.7 billion, down 10.7% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $1.734B.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The renewables close-out had slightly less progress completed than the preview’s near-term expectation: two projects were complete, while three were still expected to reach substantial completion in Q3. The final project remained on a year-end completion path.
fact_evidence: “Six renewables projects drove the margin pressure, with two now complete, three expected to reach substantial completion in Q3, and the final project…by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: “Three complete ‘within the next month,’ one in Q3, one in Q4 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog and awards exceeded the preview’s expected range: backlog reached nearly $13.9 billion versus an expected $12.5–$13.0 billion, with more than $3.9 billion in new awards. Natural-gas generation contributed about $1.4 billion of bookings, supporting a stated revenue ramp to $800 million–$1 billion in 2027.
fact_evidence: “Record total backlog of nearly $13.9 billion, up ~$2.2 billion sequentially,” with “more than $3.9 billion in new awards”; natural-gas generation contributed “approximately $1.4 billion of new bookings” and is expected to grow from “$500-$600 million in 2026 to $800 million-$1 billion in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Backlog should print ~$12.5–13.0B”; the company had flagged “~$2.0B of Q2 Energy awards” and the gas funnel was “$7.1B, with ~$800M of verbal awards described as imminent.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Pain Crest was described as performing better than expected, adding about $200 million of acquired backlog and securing another $250 million of bookings in the quarter. The preview noted the acquisition and its data-center contribution but did not anticipate these backlog and booking figures.
fact_evidence: “The Pain Crest acquisition is exceeding expectations, adding ~$200 million of acquired backlog plus $250 million of new bookings in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Utilities includes ~1 stub quarter of PayneCrest Electric ($399.5M, closed May 1; ~$112M annualized hyperscaler data-center revenue).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Leverage rose to 1.6x net debt-to-EBITDA and is expected to approach just under 2x in Q3 before improving. The preview highlighted cash and liquidity risk but did not anticipate this leverage trajectory.
fact_evidence: “Net debt-to-EBITDA rose to 1.6x following the Pain Crest acquisition and lower Q2 EBITDA,” with a Q3 increase “toward just under 2x.”

description: Revenue growth was 28% year over year, below the preview’s $371.1 million consensus estimate: applying 28% growth to the preview’s $282.3 million prior-year revenue implies roughly $361 million. That also falls just below the preview’s $364 million low end of its revenue bridge.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total omnichannel revenue increased 28% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $371.1M”; the preview’s revenue bridge estimated “Total revenue” of $364M–$392M.

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was a substantially larger loss than expected: –$0.53 versus consensus of about –$0.33 and the preview’s –$0.30 to –$0.35 base-case range. Management attributed the decline to acquisition integration costs.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.53 (a $0.31 decline), reflecting acquisition integration costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “–$0.33 (range –$0.33 to –$0.34)”; the base scenario expected “–$0.30 to –$0.35.”

description: The company broke the year-over-year adjusted EBITDA improvement streak the preview viewed as a key test: adjusted EBITDA worsened by $4 million from Q2 2025, despite the preview’s expectation that a seventh consecutive year-over-year improvement was a possible outcome. The $12 million loss itself was within the preview’s estimated range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $12 million (a $4 million decline versus Q2 2025).”
expectation_evidence: The preview called a “seventh consecutive improvement with TBHC consolidated” the “single most bullish outcome” and said the bear case would “break[]” the streak; its estimate was “–$10M to –$14M.”

description: Gross margin was stronger than the preview’s guided range: Q2 margin reached 26.8%, above the 24–26% band, with the acquired business’s mix helping rather than dragging on margin. Management also forecast Q3 margin near 30%, materially above that band.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 310 basis points to 26.8%, aided by favorable mix shift” from the merger; Q3 margins are expected to improve “close to or potentially touching 30%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited company guidance of “24–26%” and flagged gross margin “vs. the 24–26% guided band” as a key metric.

description: The base e-commerce business returned to year-over-year growth for a second quarter in a row, reversing a 19-quarter run of declines. That is a more encouraging underlying-business trend than the preview’s concern that legacy organic growth might slow to roughly flat–3%.
fact_evidence: “The base e-commerce business grew year-over-year for a second consecutive quarter, reversing 19 straight quarters of revenue decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the revenue estimate implied legacy organic growth of “roughly flat–3%” and warned that growth built on fewer customers could be fragile.

description: The company disclosed a planned rebrand and exchange/ticker change that the preview did not anticipate: the parent will become Neighborhood Intelligence and move from the NYSE to NASDAQ under NXH.
fact_evidence: “The parent company will rebrand as Neighborhood Intelligence and begin trading on NASDAQ under ticker NXH effective August 17, transitioning from the NYSE.”

description: Management disclosed a pending acquisition pipeline valued at over $2.5 billion, a scale not discussed in the preview’s review of announced and contemplated deals. The growth opportunity is accompanied by additional deal-execution and funding uncertainty.
fact_evidence: Management described “total pending acquisitions valued at over $2.5 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the Container Store, F9 Brands, and Fathom transactions and estimated “~30%+ potential dilution from announced/LOI deals,” but did not cite a pending-acquisition total of this size.

description: Avient reported Q2 organic sales growth of 4.3%, well above the preview’s expectation that organic growth could remain flat to negative. Growth was still mostly price-led—about 75% price and 25% volume—rather than the volume-driven inflection the preview emphasized.
fact_evidence: “Organic sales grew 4.3% year-over-year, composed of roughly 25% volume and 75% price.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said organic sales “could still be ~flat-to-negative” and highlighted “Organic sales growth ex-FX vs. ~+1% whisper” as a key catalyst.

description: Avient raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS and EBITDA ranges instead of simply reaffirming the prior outlook: EPS guidance moved to $3.10–$3.25 from $2.93–$3.17, and EBITDA guidance to $575M–$603M from $555M–$585M. The new EPS range also exceeds the preview’s bullish scenario, which called for narrowing to $3.05–$3.17.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to adjusted EBITDA of $575M-$603M [and] adjusted EPS of $3.10-$3.25.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 guidance of “$2.93–$3.17” EPS and “$555–585M” EBITDA, and said a simple reaffirm was the base case while the bullish outcome was “$3.05–$3.17.”

description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.96, substantially above the preview’s anticipated $0.90–$0.91 result, not merely a small beat of the $0.89 consensus. The call attributed the beat primarily to volume growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS came in at $0.96, beating expectations by $0.09, driven primarily by volume growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “$0.90–0.91 is the expected beat,” with consensus and company guidance both at $0.89.

description: Specialty Engineered Materials EBITDA rose 20% and its margin expanded 310 basis points, overcoming the preview’s highlighted risk of continued SEM margin pressure. About 100 basis points of the expansion came from lapping prior-year maintenance expense, so not all of the improvement was underlying.
fact_evidence: “Specialty Engineered Materials adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $76 million with margins up 310 basis points, though about 100 bps came from lapping ~$3M of prior-year maintenance expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged SEM as “the one to check” after its margin “contracted 160bp y/y last Q2,” and included SEM margin compression in its bear case.

description: Asia delivered unusually strong growth that the preview did not identify as an expected driver: organic sales rose 18% year over year and 20% sequentially, led by electronics, high-performance computing, and functional additives.
fact_evidence: “Asia was a standout with organic sales up 18% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, driven by electronics, high-performance computing, and functional additives.”

description: Management described a larger data-center and electronics business and a stronger growth trajectory than the preview’s stated tracking level: related business is near $100M today, including about $60M in electronics, and is expected to double over two to three years.
fact_evidence: “A directly addressable data center/electronics opportunity of roughly $2 billion, with current related business near $100 million (electronics ~$60M) and expectations to double over the next 2-3 years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said electronics/HPC was “tracking >$40M FY26 sales, +$10M incremental.”

description: Avient lowered its 2026 capex guidance to $120M–$130M from $140M because of project timing, a change not anticipated in the preview. The call attributes the reduction to timing rather than a stated cancellation or permanent cost saving, so its shareholder implication is unclear.
fact_evidence: “Capex guidance was lowered to $120M-$130M from $140M due to project timing.”

description: Radian reported adjusted operating EPS of $1.14, well below the preview’s $1.38 consensus and the $1.36–$1.44 base-case range. The revenue result was stronger, but it did not offset the sizeable earnings miss.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS $1.38”; the base case expected “$1.36–1.44.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Specialty’s Q2 combined ratio was 98%, worse than the preview’s 85–90% base case and above its 95% bear-case threshold. The preview identified storm losses and reserve strengthening as risks, but the reported roughly $30 million reserve charge included Middle East conflict claims and updated inflation assumptions.
fact_evidence: “Radian took roughly $30 million in reserves in the Specialty segment for expected and potential Middle East conflict claims plus updated inflation assumptions, pushing the Q2 specialty combined ratio to 98% (versus mid-to-high 80s excluding the item).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Specialty CR 85–90%”; it described “north of 95%” as a bear-case outcome.

description: Management said a low-90s Specialty combined ratio now better reflects the softening market, above the mid-80s to high-80s historical levels cited for Inigo and above the preview’s 85–90% base-case range. This signals a less favorable expected run-rate beyond the quarter’s reserve charge.
fact_evidence: “A specialty combined ratio in the low 90s is now more reflective of the softening market environment, up from the mid-80s to high-80s seen historically for Inigo.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Specialty CR 85–90%” in its base case and described Q1’s 85.3% as the key reference point.

description: Revenue reached $575 million, above the preview’s $537–$557 million estimate range and its $540–$565 million base case. The preview cautioned that revenue estimates were unreliable because analysts used different definitions, so the beat is less definitive than the EPS miss.
fact_evidence: “Total revenues grew 93% year-over-year to $575 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue estimates of “$556.5M” and “$537.2M,” and a base-case range of “$540–565M.”

description: Radian raised expected 2026 dividends from Radian Guaranty to at least $650 million, above the preview’s expectation of at least $600 million. This is a higher expected capital return to the holding company than the preview described.
fact_evidence: “Increasing expected 2026 dividends from Radian Guaranty to at least $650 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Radian Guaranty is committed to ≥$600M of dividends to the holdco in 2026.”

description: The company had repurchased $176 million year-to-date and moved full-year buyback guidance toward the upper end of the $200–$250 million range. The preview expected the program to remain on pace and noted $115 million deployed through April, but did not expect a move toward the top of the range.
fact_evidence: “Radian repurchased $176 million (5 million shares) year-to-date and raised full-year buyback guidance toward the upper end of the $200-$250 million range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$115M (3.3M shares) already deployed through April” and described the base case as “buyback on pace.”

description: Radian reduced holding-company leverage to 19% after repaying $75 million of its revolver draw, reaching below the preview’s sub-20% year-end target earlier than that target implied. Another $75 million is still expected to be repaid in 2026.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced holding company leverage to 19% by repaying $75 million of its revolver draw (with $75 million remaining to be repaid in 2026).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said debt/capital was 20.2% with a target “below 20% by year-end.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The PMIERs cushion was $1.5 billion, below the $1.6 billion cushion cited in the preview. The difference is modest, but the reported cushion was smaller than the stated reference level.
fact_evidence: “Maintained a $1.5 billion PMIERs cushion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “PMIERs cushion $1.6B (41%).”

description: Book value per share was $36, below the preview’s approximate $37 expectation. The company still reported 8.5% year-over-year growth, but the reported level was lower than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Grew book value per share 8.5% year-over-year to $36.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “BVPS ~$37.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Mortgage defaults were better than the preview’s expected normalization: new defaults fell quarter-over-quarter and the default rate was 2.47%, below the preview’s 2.50–2.60% base-case range. This contrasts with the expected upward drift in defaults.
fact_evidence: “New defaults declined 9% quarter-over-quarter to 12,400” and “the default rate fell to 2.47%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected a mortgage default rate of “2.50–2.60%” and said Radian’s rate “should drift similarly” to MGIC’s increase.

description: Q1 revenue was $166 million, about 10.8% above the $149.8 million consensus, and management said it exceeded company expectations. This was a materially stronger result than the preview’s expected double-digit growth bar.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue reached $166 million, up 27% year-over-year, exceeding company expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $149.8M Zacks consensus, +14.4% YoY”; the preview said the bar was to “sustain double-digit growth.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.19 beat the preview’s $0.14 consensus by about 36%. The preview also cited a lower analyst estimate of $0.10, which the reported result exceeded by more.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income more than tripled to $24.1 million ($0.19 per share) from $7 million ($0.06) a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: $0.14 Zacks consensus”; “Craig Hallum ... is below consensus at $0.10 for the quarter.”

description: Instead of merely reiterating FY2027 guidance, Digital Turbine raised both ranges: revenue by $20 million at each end and adjusted EBITDA by $10 million at each end. That was a clear upside to the preview’s stated likely outcome.
fact_evidence: “Management raised FY2027 guidance to revenue of $650-670 million (from $630-650 million) and adjusted EBITDA of $145-155 million (from $135-145 million).”
expectation_evidence: “The bar: ... at least reiterate FY27 guidance”; “reiteration vs. raise is likely the key swing factor.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: On-Device Solutions accelerated to 15% year-over-year growth from 5% in the prior quarter, despite the preview highlighting soft U.S. device volumes. International ODS was especially strong, with nearly 80% growth and more than 40% RPD expansion.
fact_evidence: “On-device solutions revenue rose 15% year-over-year to $110 million, with international ODS growing nearly 80% driven by both higher device volumes and 40%+ RPD expansion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged On-Device Solutions growth of “+5% in Q4” amid “soft U.S. device volumes,” while highlighting international carrier expansion and revenue-per-device trends.

description: Adjusted EBITDA rose 69% and its margin expanded about 640 basis points to 25.6%, a strong increase in profitability alongside revenue growth. The preview did not provide a quarterly EBITDA estimate, so the scale of the margin improvement was not quantified in its expectations.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 69% year-over-year to $42.5 million, with margin expanding roughly 640 basis points to 25.6%.”

description: Gross margin improved 210 basis points year over year to 49.4%, while cash operating expenses rose only 7% against 27% revenue growth. That indicates stronger operating leverage than the preview’s open-ended question about the gross-margin trajectory had specified.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 49.4% from 47.3% a year earlier on favorable AGP-weighted mix, while cash operating expenses rose only 7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “AI monetization ... and gross-margin trajectory” as issues to watch but gave no margin estimate.

fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved dramatically from over five turns a year ago to 2.5 turns, and a post-quarter leverage threshold triggered a 50 basis point reduction on the largest loan tranche.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the ~$354M debt load / deleveraging” as a key issue to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported a sharp productivity gain: revenue per employee rose from about $800,000 to over $1 million, attributed to AI-driven automation and operating leverage. The preview discussed AI monetization but did not anticipate or quantify this workforce-productivity measure.
fact_evidence: “Revenue per employee rose from about $800,000 a year ago to over $1 million, reflecting AI-driven automation and operating leverage.”
expectation_evidence: The preview raised “AI monetization (DTiQ, Ignite Graph)” as a topic to watch but did not mention revenue per employee or an automation productivity target.

fact_evidence: “record Q2 2026 free cash flow of $751 million, up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter”
expectation_evidence: “$600–670M is the bogey”; “Anything above $650M is a genuinely new record”

description: Management raised full-year oil production guidance to 199,000 barrels per day, above the preview’s 190,000–195,000 range and contrary to its base case of reaffirmed guidance. Most of the production increase was attributed to higher working interest rather than acquired volumes.
fact_evidence: “raised full-year 2026 oil production guidance to 199,000 barrels per day”; “only 1,000 bbl/d of the 6,500 bbl/d production increase came from acquired volumes … with the majority from higher working interest”
expectation_evidence: “190–195 MBbl/d oil”; base case: “FY guidance reaffirmed with H2 flexibility language intact”

description: Permian Resources disclosed about $1.05 billion of year-to-date Delaware acquisitions, exceeding the preview’s stated $600–800 million historical sweet spot. The transactions added about 55,000 net acres and 330 high-NRI drilling locations, including a $520 million Ward County bolt-on.
fact_evidence: “acquired ~55,000 net acres … for ~$1.05 billion across roughly 190 separate transactions, adding ~330 high-NRI drilling locations”; “largest deal was a … Ward County bolt-on for $520 million”
expectation_evidence: “targeting their historical $600–800M sweet spot”; “any confirmed bolt-on in the $600–800M range”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position

fact_evidence: “Leverage stood at approximately 0.5x at the end of Q2 and is expected to remain around 0.5x at year-end, giving the company an investment-grade balance sheet while funding acquisitions.”
expectation_evidence: “Leverage 0.8x”

description: Gas curtailments were substantial, at about 20% quarter over quarter, but the company still reported positive realized gas pricing and more than $75 million of incremental gas revenue from curtailments, firm transportation, and hedging. fact_evidence: “curtailed natural gas production by ~20% quarter-over-quarter amid WAHA prices averaging negative $3.14 per Mcf”; “still realized $0.38 per Mcf and captured over $75 million of incremental gas revenue through curtailments, firm transportation, and hedging.”
expectation_evidence: “Expect total BOE/d to look soft … even if oil beats”; “Gas/NGL volume disclosure and curtailment quantification”

description: The call described a $100 million CapEx increase, including $25 million of Ward County takeover costs, whereas the preview’s base case expected the existing CapEx range to be reaffirmed.
