description: MetLife announced a new $3 billion repurchase authorization, a larger-than-expected capital-return step given the preview described a refresh as plausible but noted about $1.1 billion remained on the existing authorization.
fact_evidence: “The company announced a new $3 billion share repurchase authorization,” repurchased “~$700 million of shares in Q2 plus ~$225 million in July,” and returned “over $2.4 billion to shareholders year-to-date through July.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “fresh authorization on the print is a plausible, and underappreciated, offset” and noted “~$1.1B authorization remaining.”

description: Asia adjusted earnings grew 21% (25% in constant currency), above the preview’s 14.1% consensus estimate and despite the preview’s warning that growth could moderate. Sales also rose 17% in constant currency, including nearly 90% A&H growth in Japan from a new medical product.
fact_evidence: “Asia adjusted earnings rose 21% (25% constant currency) to $420 million, with sales up 17% constant currency led by Korea and nearly 90% A&H growth in Japan from a new medical product.”
expectation_evidence: Asia adjusted earnings consensus was “+14.1%.” The preview noted management had pre-warned of “some moderation in year-over-year growth rates.”

description: RIS adjusted earnings grew only 2%, well below the preview’s 10.3% consensus growth estimate. The reported total investment spread was 97 basis points, below the stated 100–120 bps guidance range, with weak private equity returns cited as a factor; core spread excluding VII reached 100 bps, as the preview expected.
fact_evidence: “RIS adjusted earnings were $377 million, up only 2%, as total investment spread of 97 basis points fell below the 100-120 bps guidance range due to weak private equity returns,” while “core spread ex-VII was 100 bps, up 5 bps sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: RIS adjusted earnings consensus was “+10.3%.” The preview expected core spread ex-VII to print “≥100bps” after “modest improvement in 2Q.”

description: Management said the full-year direct expense ratio should beat the 12.1% target, a better outlook than the preview’s scorecard framing, especially given that the quarter’s ratio absorbed a roughly 50-basis-point PineBridge acquisition drag.
fact_evidence: “The direct expense ratio was 12.1%, absorbing a ~50 basis point drag from the PineBridge acquisition, and management expects to beat its 12.1% full-year 2026 target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “the FY direct expense ratio target” of 12.1% as a scorecard metric, without anticipating an expectation to beat it.

description: MetLife’s full-year adjusted earnings outlook for MetLife Investment Management was toward the low end of its $240–280 million range. The preview did not flag this segment outlook, so it provides no clear prior benchmark beyond the stated range.
fact_evidence: MetLife Investment Management “expects full-year adjusted earnings toward the low end of its $240-280 million guidance range.”

description: Latin America reported record quarterly adjusted earnings and said it was on track to reach $1 billion in annual earnings, a positive earnings trajectory not covered by the preview’s segment earnings estimates, which listed no Latin America earnings consensus.
fact_evidence: “Latin America posted record quarterly adjusted earnings of $268 million (up 15%, 4% constant currency) and is on track to reach $1 billion in annual earnings, roughly double pre-pandemic levels.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Latin America revenue growth expectations but no adjusted earnings estimate.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 21%, up from 13% in Q1, and contribution margin rose to 55% from 50%, with all-time-high contribution profit. The preview expected a margin rebound but said the annual guide implied steep H2 acceleration toward 21%; reaching that margin already in Q2 was an earlier, sharper inflection than that outlook suggested.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $77 million… with a 21% margin, up sharply from a 13% EBITDA margin in Q1”; “Total contribution margin improved to 55% (from 50% in Q1)”; “all-time high contribution profit of $193 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY guide implies steep H2 acceleration toward the 21% target”; CFO said Q1 contribution margin should be “the low point for the year.”

description: The preview cited follow-through on $4B+ of committed capital YTD as a funding watchpoint; the call reported partnerships expected to add up to $10.8B in incremental capacity and loans held on the balance sheet at a nearly two-year low. That is materially more capacity, alongside less balance-sheet exposure, than the preview’s stated marker suggested.
fact_evidence: “Loans held on the balance sheet fell to 5.9% of total outstanding principal, the lowest in nearly two years,” with partnerships “expected to add up to $10.8 billion in incremental capacity year-to-date.”
expectation_evidence: “Follow-through on $4B+ of committed capital YTD” and funding durability and balance sheet were listed as key things to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: July origination growth was 34% year-over-year, slower than Q2’s 50%, as UMI rose about 9% during the quarter and reached 1.5, the top of its guidance range. The preview highlighted volume and macro conditions but did not anticipate this specific near-term slowdown.
fact_evidence: “July origination growth slowed to 34% year-over-year from 50% in Q2,” reflecting a “modest headwind from UMI rising ~9% over the course of the quarter”; UMI rose to 1.5, the top of the 1.4–1.5 range.

description: Reported GAAP diluted EPS was $0.16, below the preview’s alternative GAAP-based consensus estimate of $0.1931, a shortfall of about 17%. The preview cautioned that this estimate appeared to be GAAP and was not directly comparable to the $0.58 adjusted EPS consensus.
fact_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS of $0.16.”
expectation_evidence: “A second aggregation cites $0.1931 EPS / $352.29M revenue”; “the EPS basis appears to be GAAP rather than non-GAAP, so the two EPS figures are not directly comparable.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Auto and Home grew rapidly, and together accounted for about 14% of originations. The preview expected attention on newer products, especially Auto and HELOC, but did not suggest this scale of combined mix or report Home’s growth rate.
fact_evidence: “Auto originations grew 264% year-over-year and 62% sequentially while Home grew 139% year-over-year,” with Auto and Home “comprising about 14% of total originations versus 1% in Q4 2021.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “New products: auto… HELOC… and the Cashline revolving-credit launch,” but gave no Q2 growth or mix estimate for Auto and Home.

description: Upstart said it sunset its Auto Refinance business this quarter, a product withdrawal not anticipated in the preview. Management framed the decision as capital discipline, so the news is mixed rather than an unambiguously negative operating development.
fact_evidence: “The company sunset its Auto Refinance business this quarter for capital discipline.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported that the underwriting model was 2.74 times as accurate as traditional credit scoring and that the last 12 loan vintages exceeded Treasuries by about 660 basis points. These specific model and vintage results went beyond the preview’s broad focus on consumer credit commentary and funding durability.
fact_evidence: “Its underwriting model reached 2.74x the accuracy of traditional credit scoring, and the last 12 loan vintages exceeded Treasuries by ~660 basis points.”

description: AFG reported core operating EPS of $2.82, well above the preview’s $2.32–$2.37 consensus range. That is a sizable beat, although the preview warned that the Charleston sale could make headline EPS timing-sensitive.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 core net operating earnings of $2.82 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS: ~$2.32”; “AAII shows a slightly higher $2.37 next-quarter consensus.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Alternative investment returns were exceptionally strong: the reported 7.1% return helped lift P&C net investment income to a second-quarter record. The preview flagged alternatives as a source of earnings volatility but did not forecast a return level.
fact_evidence: “P&C net investment income rose 23% year-over-year to a second-quarter record,” with “alternative investment returns jumping to 7.1% versus just 1.2% in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Returns on private equity and real estate partnerships have been the main source of quarter-to-quarter earnings variance.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Net written premium growth was 6% in Q2, faster than the preview’s 3–5% full-year growth target and up from 3% in Q1. That is a stronger quarterly growth pace, though the facts do not say management raised its full-year outlook.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross and net written premiums grew 7% and 6% respectively.”
expectation_evidence: “Management's full-year 2026 targets are 3–5% net written premium growth”; Q1 net written premiums were “+3% YoY.”

description: The Specialty Financial Group grew premiums 10%, with lender-placed property benefiting as a 12-month quota-share drag rolled off. The preview did not identify this segment or the quota-share change as a driver to watch.
fact_evidence: “The Specialty Financial Group grew gross and net written premiums 10% led by lender-placed property (following the roll-off of a 12-month quota share drag), despite renewal pricing declining less than 1%.”

description: Commercial auto liability produced a small underwriting profit for a second consecutive quarter, despite the preview’s concern about specialty-casualty pricing pressure. Management still said more rate is needed to reach targeted returns, so the improvement did not resolve the adequacy concern.
fact_evidence: “Commercial auto liability posted a small underwriting profit for the second consecutive quarter,” while “management indicated more rate is needed to reach targeted returns”; commercial auto liability rates were “up 15%.”
expectation_evidence: “Sustained sub-92% prints plus renewal pricing commentary in specialty casualty (social-inflation-exposed lines) will drive the reaction.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Workers’ compensation pricing was declining, including in California, which AFG said was underperforming; the segment nevertheless grew mid-single digits. The preview did not specifically flag this pricing or California exposure.
fact_evidence: “Workers' comp pricing declined about 2% in Q2 and 3% through six months, with California (14% of the comp book) underperforming, yet the segment still grew mid-single digits.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Favorable prior-year reserve development contributed 3.4 points to the Specialty P&C combined ratio, versus 0.7 points in the prior-year quarter. The preview flagged reserve development as a key uncertainty but did not provide an expected contribution.
fact_evidence: “3.4 points of favorable prior-year reserve development (up from 0.7 points).”
expectation_evidence: “Catastrophe losses and reserve development” were listed as items to watch.

description: Catastrophe losses contributed just 1.8 points to the Specialty P&C combined ratio. The preview identified catastrophe losses as a key issue but gave no expected level for the quarter.
fact_evidence: The combined ratio was aided by “lower catastrophe losses of 1.8 points.”
expectation_evidence: “Catastrophe losses and reserve development” were listed as items to watch.

description: Energizer lowered its full-year outlook to the low end of its range, cutting expected back-half organic growth from roughly 4% to flat-to-up 1%. That is weaker than the preview’s expectation that management would retain high-end guidance and deliver an organic-growth inflection.
fact_evidence: Management lowered its full-year outlook to the low end of its range and cut expected back-half organic growth from roughly 4% to flat-to-up 1%.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management was guiding to the “high end” of FY26 EPS and EBITDA ranges, and described Q3 as the promised “inflection” quarter for organic net sales.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The battery category weakened more than expected: trends were 200 to 300 basis points below prior expectations, and management now expects the category to be weaker than flat for the rest of the year. The preview was looking for a growth inflection and a possible normalization in battery momentum.
fact_evidence: Category trends softened by roughly 200 to 300 basis points relative to prior expectations; management expects the category to be weaker than the previously anticipated flat trend for the balance of the year.
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 the “inflection point for organic net sales” and said to watch for “Batteries & Lights momentum” and the gap between consumption and shipments to close.

description: The implied Q4 EPS step-up was less ambitious than the preview’s guidance math suggested. Management’s approximately 25% adjusted EPS growth guidance implies about $1.31 against the preview’s Q4 FY25 base of $1.05, below the preview’s implied Q4 range of roughly $1.45–$1.50.
fact_evidence: Management guided to approximately 25% adjusted EPS growth at the midpoint in the fourth quarter.
expectation_evidence: The preview calculated “Implied Q4 ≈ $1.45–$1.50” and described this as a “+38–43% y/y step-up.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Energizer reported U.S. value and volume growth and global share gains even as the battery category declined. That is better relative performance than the preview’s concern that retailer inventory tightness was limiting sell-in and that global battery trends lagged the U.S.
fact_evidence: In the U.S., Energizer grew value 1.8% and volume 5% against a declining category, and gained both volume and value share globally.
expectation_evidence: The preview said U.S. retailer inventory tightness had been “capping sell-in” and that “global battery trends trail the U.S. by ‘a quarter or two.’”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Some IEEPA tariff-refund cash had arrived, contrary to the preview’s statement that none had been received. The $11 million collected is a partial conversion of the receivable; $53 million remains booked and is expected to support cash generation into FY2027.
fact_evidence: The company had collected about $11 million of IEEPA tariffs, with a remaining $53 million booked expected to be a meaningful source of cash generation into fiscal 2027.
expectation_evidence: The preview stated, “no cash has been received on the $64.3M IEEPA refund,” and called the process and timing open.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Q3 promotional activity created a pricing headwind, a pressure the preview did not specifically flag. Management said pricing should be neutral to slightly positive in Q4 and cautioned investors not to extrapolate Q3 pricing trends.
fact_evidence: Q3 experienced a pricing headwind due to increased promotional activity; management expects pricing to be neutral to slightly positive in Q4 and cautioned against extrapolating Q3 trends.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said retailer destocking was not expected to be an additional meaningful headwind, easing a concern raised by the preview about inventory constraints and the consumption-to-shipment gap.
fact_evidence: The projected category weakness was described as split roughly between volume erosion and promotional/price pressure, with retailer destocking not expected to be an additional meaningful headwind.
expectation_evidence: The preview said U.S. retailer inventory tightness had been “capping sell-in” and urged investors to watch for the gap between consumption and shipments to close.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management characterized battery-category weakness as near-term consumer caution and value-seeking, rather than a structural shift to battery-free technologies. The preview did not raise this structural-substitution concern, so the explanation is a reassuring new detail rather than a reversal of an explicit forecast.
fact_evidence: Management described the weakness as near-term consumer caution and value-seeking behavior rather than a structural shift toward battery-free technologies, citing healthy device usage and change-out frequency.

description: Energizer said Project Momentum is being completed this year, with facility-exit and severance cash costs expected to decline significantly and CapEx expected to fall by roughly $30 million, or 1% of net sales. The preview emphasized cash-flow restoration but did not anticipate these specific cost and CapEx reductions.
fact_evidence: Project Momentum is being completed this year; related cash costs for facility exits and severance are expected to decline significantly, and CapEx is expected to fall by roughly 1% of net sales or $30 million going forward.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management was working to “return to the historical cash flow profile” and listed FY26 FCF guidance of “>10% of net sales.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Grove’s customer funnel weakened more than the preview’s base case anticipated: active customers were 509,000, below the preview’s 535,000–550,000 base range and its 530,000 downside threshold, while DTC orders were 489,000 versus the preview’s 510,000 watch level. That is a sharper deterioration than the preview’s expected decline with deceleration.
fact_evidence: “Active customers fell 23.3% year-over-year to 509,000 and DTC total orders declined 23.6% to 489,000.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “535–550K” active customers; it said “Anything below ~530K breaks the trough narrative” and flagged orders “≥510K.”

description: Gross margin fell to 53.6%, below the preview’s 54.5% catalyst threshold and its warning that a drop below roughly 54% would weaken the margin story. The reported causes were one-time inventory disposals and the non-recurrence of a prior-year reserved-inventory sell-through.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 190 basis points to 53.6% due to one-time inventory disposals and the non-recurrence of a prior-year reserved inventory sell-through.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Adj. EBITDA ≥$0.5M with gross margin held ≥54.5%” and said “If GM slips below ~54% to buy volume, the margin story weakens.”

description: The CFO’s departure was not anticipated in the preview: Tom Siragusa is leaving on August 16 to pursue another opportunity, and the company is searching for a successor. The significance for shareholders is unclear from the information provided.
fact_evidence: “CFO Tom Siragusa is departing the company on August 16 to pursue a new opportunity, with a successor search underway.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash generation improved unexpectedly relative to the liquidity concern highlighted in the preview: operating cash flow was positive $1.3 million and cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash rose to $11.4 million from $10.4 million. The preview cited negative Q1 operating cash flow and emphasized liquidity risks, but did not forecast Q2 cash flow.
fact_evidence: “Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash rose to $11.4 million from $10.4 million, supported by $1.3 million of positive operating cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “OCF was −$0.7M in Q1” and flagged liquidity commentary as a key watch item.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: DSA bookings were far stronger than the preview’s roughly 1.00–1.05x book-to-bill expectation: reported net book-to-bill was 1.9x, with net bookings of $701 million and backlog rising to $1.97 billion. Management’s context suggests a roughly 1.2x figure on a different basis, but the reported level still substantially exceeded the preview’s threshold.
fact_evidence: “DSA net bookings grew 12.6% sequentially to $701 million with a net book-to-bill of 1.9x (management context suggests ~1.2x)”; backlog rose to “$1.97 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “A second straight quarter ≥1.0x with backlog holding ≥$1.9B validates the 2027 setup”; the base scenario expected “book-to-bill 1.00–1.05x, backlog ~$1.90B.”

description: Revenue returned to slight organic growth rather than the decline the preview expected. The 0.1% increase also beat the prior outlook for a low-single-digit decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue returned to organic growth of 0.1% year-over-year,” beating “the prior outlook of a low single-digit decline.”
expectation_evidence: Preview estimated “Organic revenue growth: ~−1% to −2%.”

description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS exceeded consensus and management’s sequential-growth floor by a meaningful amount: $3.02 was above the preview’s $2.72–$2.74 consensus and the $2.68 implied by at least 30% sequential growth. Management said more than half the beat was operational, with the rest from nonoperating items.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $3.02 rose 47% sequentially, well above the prior outlook of at least 30% growth, though over half the beat was operational with the remainder from nonoperating items.”
expectation_evidence: Preview consensus was “$2.72 (Zacks) / $2.74 (street)” and noted management’s “at least 30%” sequential-growth outlook, implying “≥$2.68.”

description: The company raised its full-year organic revenue outlook to flat-to-1% growth, an improvement over the prior negative-growth range. The preview discussed a possible guidance raise but identified reaffirming the prior organic range as a scenario, so the stronger organic outlook was better than that baseline.
fact_evidence: “Lifted organic revenue growth to flat-to-1%, a 150 bps improvement.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Reaffirm (organic −0.5% to −1.5%)” as a possible FY26 guidance outcome.

description: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin came in above the preview’s estimated range, at 20.5%. The sequential improvement was also substantial, though divestitures helped lift Manufacturing segment margin.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin improved 420 basis points sequentially to 20.5%, aided by divestitures that pushed the Manufacturing segment margin to 37.8%.”
expectation_evidence: Preview estimated Q2 non-GAAP operating margin at “~19–20%.”

description: Free cash flow guidance was raised rather than left at the prior range. The preview’s guidance checklist used the prior $375–$400 million range as the reaffirmation case.
fact_evidence: “Raised free cash flow guidance to $400-$420 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FCF $375–400M” among the figures that could be reaffirmed.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The full-year tax-rate outlook rose about 100 basis points, creating an approximately $0.20 EPS headwind, while a deferred compensation plan gain of about $0.19 nearly offsets it. Neither item was flagged in the preview, making the underlying earnings offsets a new detail rather than a major net change to the outlook.
fact_evidence: “The full-year tax rate outlook rose ~100 bps to 23%-24%, creating a ~$0.20 EPS headwind that essentially offsets a $0.19 deferred compensation plan gain, with a Mauritius tax legislation change still pending.”

description: Q2 buybacks were $100 million, below the preview’s bullish signal of maintaining a pace above $200 million per quarter. The preview presented that pace conditionally as a bull-case signal, not as its base expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $100 million of shares at ~$174 in Q2 (bringing year-to-date buybacks to $300 million).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull-case commentary signal was “buyback pace maintained above $200M/qtr.”

description: Valvoline reported $162 million of EBITDA, well above the preview’s roughly $154 million consensus and its roughly $155–156 million base estimate. The 29.8% margin also topped the preview’s roughly 29% expectation.
fact_evidence: “EBITDA rose 25% to $162 million with margin expanding 30 basis points to 29.8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$154M”; the preview’s base case expected “~$155M / ~29% margin.”

description: Net sales reached $545 million, above the preview’s roughly $532 million published consensus and its roughly $535 million estimate. The 24% increase also exceeded the preview’s expected 21–22% growth.
fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 24% year-over-year to $545 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenues … $531.7M”; the preview’s Q3 estimate was “~$535M” and implied growth was “+22%.”

description: EPS was $0.57, above both the preview’s stale $0.50 consensus and its roughly $0.51–$0.52 base expectation. However, the full-year EPS outlook was only narrowed to $1.70–$1.75, short of the preview’s expected $1.72–$1.78 base-case range and its stated $1.80-plus catalyst threshold.
fact_evidence: “EPS grew 21% to $0.57”; full-year guidance was narrowed “to … $1.70-$1.75.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS … $0.50”; base case: “FY EPS guide nudged to $1.72–1.78”; the preview said “you need roughly $1.80+” and that “anything less than ~$1.80 is a non-event.”

description: The full-year same-store-sales outlook was raised to 7.5%–8%, above the preview’s suggested marker of roughly 6.5%–7.5% for a meaningful guidance increase. The sales midpoint also rose by $25 million, broadly in line with the preview’s expected upward revision.
fact_evidence: “Full-year system-wide same-store sales guidance was raised to 7.5%-8%, and the sales midpoint was lifted by $25 million to a range of $2.05-$2.1 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a revision “to something like 6.5–7.5% is the marker for a genuine raise” and expected revenue to be “narrowed upward toward ~$2.03–2.07B.”

description: Management now expects only about 50 basis points of full-year EBITDA margin compression, compared with the previously planned 100 basis points. That is a better margin outlook than the preview’s discussion of the planned dilution and cost pressures implied.
fact_evidence: “Now expects only about 50 basis points of full-year EBITDA margin compression versus the previously planned 100 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had sized Oil Changers dilution at “less than 100 bps” of full-year EBITDA margin and flagged lubricant-cost pressure as a live risk.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The expected cost pressure proved more severe and persistent than the preview specified: finished-lubricant costs are expected to be roughly 60% above March levels, adding $5–$7 per oil change, and the elevated environment may continue for 4–6 months after the Strait reopens.
fact_evidence: “Finished lubricant costs [are expected] to be roughly 60% above March levels, translating to a $5-$7 increase per oil change”; management expects the environment to persist “at least 4 to 6 months after the Strait fully reopens.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Middle East conflict risk to lubricant costs” and said costs had remained “a headwind through the June quarter,” but did not indicate increases of this scale or duration.

description: Management forecast 300–400 basis points of Q4 margin compression, driven almost entirely by product-cost increases. The preview recognized base-oil risk but did not anticipate this specific degree of near-term margin pressure.
fact_evidence: “Q4 is expected to see 300-400 basis points of margin compression driven almost entirely by product cost increases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted lubricant-cost risk and expected a measured outlook on the second half, but gave no 300–400 basis-point Q4 compression expectation.

description: Year-to-date free cash flow and deleveraging were stronger than the preview’s benchmarks, and management is targeting a restart of share repurchases. The preview had flagged a buyback signal as a potential catalyst around 2.9–3.0x leverage, while reported leverage was already down to 2.8x.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow reached $112 million (up ~$93 million), operating cash flow improved $105 million to $285 million, and net leverage declined ~10% sequentially to 2.8x as the company targets restarting share repurchases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FCF … $45M YTD (up ~$57M YoY),” leverage of “~2.9x,” and said language about resuming buybacks at “~2.9–3.0x leverage” would be an unpriced positive.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The sales comp matched the preview’s roughly 8% whisper, but its mix was more ticket-dependent than expected: more than three-quarters came from ticket, versus the preview’s roughly two-thirds expectation. That leaves less contribution from transactions than the preview identified as the more bullish outcome.
fact_evidence: “System-wide same-store sales grew 8%, with ticket driving more than three-quarters of the comp.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the Q2 mix as “~two-thirds of comp came from ticket” and said “a shift toward transaction growth would be the genuinely bullish tell”; its bull case required transaction growth to expand to “~40%+ of the comp.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Twelve Breeze stores had been converted to the Valvoline Instant Oil Change brand, with performance slightly ahead of expectations—an integration update the preview had identified as an area to watch but had not expected to be ahead of plan.
fact_evidence: “12 Breeze stores have been converted to the Valvoline Instant Oil Change brand with performance slightly ahead of expectations.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for watching “Oil Changers service-menu conversion” and the “equipment/training rollout,” without forecasting that converted stores would outperform expectations.

description: AIG reported adjusted EPS of $2.00, above the preview’s $1.92–$1.95 bogey based on the published consensus estimates. The result was nevertheless at the preview’s stated $2.00–$2.05 whisper range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted after-tax income was $1.1 billion, or $2.00 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “I'd treat $1.92–$1.95 as the real bogey and a whisper near $2.00–$2.05.”

description: The calendar-year combined ratio was 89.0%, better than the preview’s 90.1% consensus estimate and better than the deterioration implied by that estimate. This was a clearer headline underwriting result than the preview’s consensus setup suggested.
fact_evidence: “The calendar year combined ratio improved 30 basis points to 89.0%.”
expectation_evidence: “GI combined ratio | 90.1% | 89.3% | +80 bps (worse).”

description: Underlying accident-year performance was weaker than the preview’s roughly 87% expectation: AIG’s adjusted accident-year combined ratio was 88.1%. That missed the preview’s key underlying-margin threshold even though it improved year over year.
fact_evidence: “The accident year combined ratio (adjusted) improved 30 basis points to 88.1%.”
expectation_evidence: “AYCR ~87%” in the base case; the preview also said “Anything ≤87%” would validate its margin thesis.

description: International Commercial’s calendar combined ratio came in at 91.3%, far worse than the preview’s 87.6% estimate. The call attributed the deterioration in part to $75 million of losses tied to the Middle East conflict, an event the preview had not anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Catastrophe charges totaled $210 million, including $75 million in net losses tied to the Middle East conflict that pushed International Commercial's calendar year combined ratio to 91.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Int'l Commercial CR | 87.6% | 85.9% | +170 bps.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: AIG recorded $74 million of strengthening in U.S. excess casualty reserves, including accident years 2016 and 2023. The preview specifically identified U.S. casualty reserve strengthening as a key gap risk, so this was a negative development against the expected favorable reserve-release backdrop.
fact_evidence: “Prior year development was $145 million favorable, led by $177 million of favorable U.S. workers' compensation, but was partially offset by $74 million of strengthening in U.S. excess casualty (accident years 2016 and 2023).”
expectation_evidence: “A genuine gap risk if AIG strengthens” reserves; the preview also said to watch for “reserve-strengthening in US casualty.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: North America retail casualty pricing was stronger than the market backdrop in the preview: AIG reported 10% increases, including 14% in excess casualty, versus the preview’s 7% U.S. casualty market-rate figure. That suggests better pricing momentum in these lines than the market-level expectation implied.
fact_evidence: “North America retail casualty up 10% (excess casualty up 14%).”
expectation_evidence: “US casualty +7% (decelerating from +9% in Q1).”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Global energy pricing fell 15%, and management said those rates were inadequate. That was materially weaker than the preview’s already-soft global commercial pricing backdrop of –6%.
fact_evidence: “Global energy pricing down 15%, which management flagged as inadequate.”
expectation_evidence: “Global commercial rates –6%.”

description: Buybacks were $641 million, below the preview’s $700 million–$1.0 billion base-case quarterly range and well below its $1.0–$1.5 billion acceleration scenario. Total shareholder returns were higher at $904 million after including dividends, but the repurchase pace itself fell short of the preview’s baseline.
fact_evidence: “The company returned $904 million to shareholders ($641 million in buybacks and $263 million in dividends).”
expectation_evidence: “Buyback ~$0.7–1.0B” in the base case; the preview also described “an acceleration toward $1.0–1.5B of quarterly buyback.”

description: Solventum raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $7.10–$7.20, well above the preview’s $6.58 consensus and the prior $6.40–$6.60 range. The increase is less operationally strong than the headline suggests: management attributed much of it to an approximately $100 million one-time tariff refund recognized in Q2.
fact_evidence: “Full-year EPS guidance was raised significantly to $7.10-$7.20 from the prior $6.40-$6.60 range, largely reflecting a one-time tariff refund of approximately $100 million recognized in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EPS: $6.58”; the preview said a formal raise to “$6.60–$6.70 is required to clear the bar.”

description: The FY2026 operating-margin range rose to 22.2%–22.7% from 21%–21.5%, a larger improvement than the preview’s stated target. About 120 basis points of the new range comes from the tariff refund, so part of the increase is a one-time benefit.
fact_evidence: “Full-year operating margin guidance was raised to 22.2%-22.7% from 21%-21.5%, though this includes about 120 basis points from the tariff refund benefit.”

description: The company tightened its full-year organic-sales outlook upward to 2.5%–3.0%, rather than maintaining the prior 2.0%–3.0% range; excluding SKU exits, the range is 3.5%–4.0%. Management also said the high end reaches the low end of its 2028 long-range-plan targets.
fact_evidence: “Organic sales growth guidance was tightened upward to 2.5%-3% (or 3.5%-4% excluding SKU exits), with management noting the high end already reaches the low end of the 2028 long-range plan targets.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 organic sales growth (co. guide) +2.0% to +3.0%.”

description: Although reported Q2 EPS was $2.55, removing the ERP-order contribution and tariff-refund benefit leaves normalized EPS of $1.73—below the preview’s $1.91 adjusted-EPS consensus. Management nevertheless said the normalized result beat expectations, making the comparison mixed.
fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS was $2.55, but excluding a $0.34 advanced-order contribution and a $0.48 tariff refund benefit, normalized EPS was $1.73, which management said beat expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS” consensus: “$1.91.”

description: Solventum disclosed that it is advancing a separation of Health Information Systems to become a pure-play MedTech company focused on MedSurg and Dental. The preview discussed HIS performance but did not flag a separation of the business.
fact_evidence: “The company announced it is advancing the separation of its Health Information Systems (HIS) business … to become a pure-play MedTech company focused on MedSurg and Dental.”

description: Buybacks accelerated sharply from the pace the preview highlighted as slow: Solventum repurchased nearly 4 million shares for $288 million in Q2, after buying only $67 million in Q1.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased nearly 4 million shares for $288 million in Q2 (4.8 million shares for $355 million year-to-date) as it accelerated its $1 billion buyback program.”
expectation_evidence: “Only $67M of the $1B authorization executed in Q1”; the preview said a slow repurchase pace could invite questions.

description: Acera’s growth was especially strong: it increased roughly 48% year over year to $32 million in sales and had gross margins above 80%, with continued double-digit growth expected. The preview called for visible acceleration involving Acera but did not anticipate this reported growth rate.
fact_evidence: “The Acera acquisition continued to outperform, growing roughly 48% year-over-year to $32 million in reported sales with gross margins above 80%, and management expects continued double-digit growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said MedSurg “needs visible acceleration from V.A.C. Peel and Place NPWT and Acera integration.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The Q2 free-cash-flow figure was $144 million, and management expected meaningful improvement only starting in Q4. That leaves the preview’s roughly $200 million full-year target dependent on a substantial second-half recovery, with the meaningful improvement apparently weighted late in the year.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of only $144 million in Q2 expected to improve meaningfully starting Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 FCF at “~$200M” and said “SOLV needs a very large H2.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Progress on the separation transition was ahead of the preview’s concern that most transition-service agreements would run into 2027: nearly 70% of the agreements had been exited, with a target of 90% by year-end 2026. The call also reported roughly 950 of 1,200 systems migrated.
fact_evidence: “The 3M separation is nearing completion with nearly 70% of ~200 transition service agreements exited (targeting 90% by year-end 2026) and roughly 950 of 1,200 systems migrated.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “majority of TSAs run into 2027” and that 75% of 1,200+ applications had been migrated as of Q1.

description: Q2 revenue was $5.6 million, about 7% below the preview’s published consensus of roughly $6.0 million. However, it landed at the top of the preview’s $5.4–$5.6 million realistic-whisper range, which the preview said was the more relevant low-confidence anchor.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $5.6 million” and was “essentially flat versus Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | ~$6.00M”; the preview also said “the relevant ‘whisper’ is roughly $5.4–5.6M.”

description: Gross margin fell to 73%, below the preview’s expected 74–76% range and below the 74% Q1 level the preview called the trough. The preview warned that another sequential decline would break management’s margin-recovery story.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross margin compressed to 73% of revenue from 76% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “GM 74–76%,” and the preview said “74% in Q1 was the trough” and “a second sequential decline breaks that story.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $0.6 million, below the preview’s base expectation of $0.65–$0.75 million. The result also came in below the preview’s $0.70 million point estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $0.6 million (11% of revenue) in Q2 2026 from $0.8 million (15%) in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Adj. EBITDA $0.65–0.75M (13%)”; the preview’s estimate was “$0.70M (13%).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ARR per subscription customer rose 15% year over year, essentially matching the preview’s expected 14.9%, but slipped about $100 sequentially. That breaks the upward streak the preview identified as an important operating signal.
fact_evidence: “Average ARR per subscription customer rose 15% year-over-year to $12,718,” but “declined roughly $100 sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed ARR per subscriber at “$12,803” and said it “has risen in seven of the last eight quarters — a break in that streak would be a real negative.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Recurring revenue remained about 60% of the total, since non-subscription revenue was still about 40%. The preview had identified progress from roughly 60% toward about 65% as an important measure of the business transition.
fact_evidence: “Non-subscription revenue still represents about 40% of total revenue,” with the company “targeting 80% recurring by next year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said ARR was “~60% in Q1” and described progress “toward ~65%” as the re-rating metric.

description: The call provided no first-revenue disclosure for Social Monitoring, ACCESS Verified, or MCP, despite the preview identifying Q2 contributions as a key test. Instead, the reported product update was a plan for a content-studio add-on, with no current revenue contribution specified.
fact_evidence: Management is “planning new product add-ons—including a content studio priced at an incremental $200-$300/month”; no first-revenue figures for the named products were provided in the supplied call facts.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Social Monitoring, ACCESS Verified, and MCP were “all guided to start contributing in Q2” and called “First revenue disclosure” the swing factor.

description: Management outlined a concrete second-half cost-saving plan to reduce cost of revenue by about $150,000 and target gross margins in the high-70% range. That offered a specific recovery path even though Q2 margin fell below the preview’s expectations.
fact_evidence: “Cost savings initiatives are expected to reduce cost of revenue by approximately $150,000 (125-150 basis points) in the second half, aiming to restore gross margins to the high-70% range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected margins to “recover as volume and subscription revenue grow,” but warned that “a second sequential decline breaks that story.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported 124% net revenue retention and 24% year-over-year customer growth, including growth driven by private-company e-commerce initiatives. The preview did not provide expectations for either metric, so these were additional positive operating signals rather than results that can be measured against a stated forecast.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention reached 124%” and “total customer count rose 24% year-over-year and 6% sequentially, driven largely by private company e-commerce initiatives.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management offered a new positive view that the PR industry could return to double-digit growth in 2027, citing a Gartner report and more new-business incorporations. The preview discussed the ongoing revenue decline but did not flag this industry-growth outlook.
fact_evidence: Management “expects the PR industry to return to double-digit growth in 2027, citing a Gartner report and a 14% rise in new business incorporations.”

description: GAAP loss per share was $0.09, worse than the preview’s derived consensus estimate of a $0.03 loss, though better than the preview’s own $0.12 loss estimate. The preview cautioned that the consensus figure was derived and unreliable, so the result was mixed against its conflicting expectations.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $354,000 ($0.09 per share) from $239,000 ($0.06).”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 GAAP EPS consensus as “~$(0.03) (derived)” and its own estimate as “$(0.12),” while warning that Q2 EPS was “not reliably published.”

description: LIND reported $199 million of revenue, about 7.7% above the preview’s $184.72 million consensus estimate; year-over-year growth was 19% rather than the roughly 10% expected.
fact_evidence: “Total company revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $199 million.”

description: The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $830–$860 million from $800–$850 million. The preview identified a guidance increase as a key swing factor, and the new range is above the prior range at both ends.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $830-$860 million (from $800-$850 million).”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance — after H1 momentum, a raise above $800–850M revenue / $130–140M adjusted EBITDA is likely the key swing factor.”

description: The quarterly loss was much smaller than expected: EPS was a loss of $0.02 versus the preview’s expected loss of $0.09.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss narrowed to $1.4 million (-$0.02 per share) from -$0.18 per share a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS: loss of $0.09.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA guidance stayed at $130–$140 million even though the preview said an increase above that range was likely to be a key swing factor. The revenue range was raised, but the EBITDA range was not.
fact_evidence: The company “reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA guidance of $130-$140 million.”
expectation_evidence: “A raise above $800–850M revenue / $130–140M adjusted EBITDA is likely the key swing factor.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 occupancy reached 91%, but it did not hold the 93% record level from Q1. It nevertheless remained above the company’s 90% target and was the highest second-quarter occupancy in a decade.
fact_evidence: “Occupancy reached 91%, up 5 points from 86% a year ago,” and was “the highest second-quarter occupancy in 10 years” and the “second consecutive quarter above the 90% target.”
expectation_evidence: “Occupancy and net yield — whether the record 93% Q1 occupancy and +7% yield trends held into the seasonally lighter Q2.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Net yield growth continued, but at 4.3% it was below the +7% Q1 growth rate the preview highlighted as a trend to watch. The yield itself reached another record, including despite a 12% capacity increase.
fact_evidence: “Net yield increased 4.3% to a record $1,294 per available guest night, the sixth consecutive quarter of record net yields, achieved despite a 12% capacity increase.”
expectation_evidence: “Occupancy and net yield — whether the record 93% Q1 occupancy and +7% yield trends held into the seasonally lighter Q2.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings for the newly launched 2028 deployment generated twice the revenue of the prior year’s launch period, a strong advance-booking result beyond the preview’s discussion of 2026 and 2027 bookings.
fact_evidence: “The newly launched 2028 deployment generated twice the revenue of the prior year's launch period”; 2027 bookings also “continue to pace ahead of 2026 in both segments.”

description: Fuel costs rose sharply despite lower consumption: expense increased 64% year over year while fuel consumption fell by more than 3% amid 12% capacity growth. The preview did not flag this cost pressure; management said it is modeling about $100-per-barrel oil for the rest of the year.
fact_evidence: “Fuel costs rose $2.7 million or 64% year-over-year to 5.3% of Lindblad revenue,” while “fuel consumption was cut more than 3% amid a 12% capacity increase,” and management was “modeling ~$100/barrel oil for the rest of the year.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Management said GAAP net income would have been positive without accelerated depreciation tied to retiring two ships in Q4. That specific charge was not anticipated in the preview and helps explain why the quarter remained loss-making despite the much smaller-than-expected EPS loss.
fact_evidence: The quarter “would have been positive GAAP net income excluding accelerated depreciation from retiring two ships in Q4.”

description: Management disclosed that second-half 2026 capacity will be roughly flat—up mid-single digits in Q3 and down mid-single digits in Q4. The preview did not set an expectation for this capacity pattern, so the growth profile is new guidance rather than a clear beat or miss.
fact_evidence: “Second-half 2026 capacity will be roughly flat (up mid-single digits in Q3, down mid-single digits in Q4).”

description: Management said it expects 2027 net-yield growth to shift from being occupancy-driven to pricing-driven. The preview discussed 2027 bookings but did not anticipate this change in the expected source of yield growth.
fact_evidence: “Management expects 2027 net yield growth to shift from occupancy-driven to pricing-driven.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS was $1.34, above the preview’s $1.21 estimate and $1.12 consensus; the preview expected a beat, but the reported beat was substantially larger.
fact_evidence: “Fully diluted non-GAAP EPS was $1.34, up 55.8% year-over-year, marking a quarterly record.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS” consensus was “$1.12”; “My Estimate” was “$1.21.”

description: Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $4.95–$5.05, above the preview’s expected raise to $4.85–$4.95.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $4.95-$5.05 (from $4.70-$4.80).”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected to “Raise to $4.85–4.95” and said the EPS guide should be raised to at least a “$4.85 low end.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 35.4%, well above the preview’s roughly 33% estimate and 33% threshold, showing more operating leverage than expected.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 740 basis points to 35.4%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~33.0%” adjusted EBITDA margin and set “≥ 33.0%” as the catalyst bar.

description: Nevro revenue appears to have fallen to about $71 million, below the preview’s roughly $80 million trough expectation, and management now expects trial volumes to recover only late in Q4, with a top-line recovery by year-end.
fact_evidence: Nevro revenue “declined 14.3% year-over-year and fell $1.7 million sequentially”; management expects trial volumes to return to historical levels “late in Q4” and drive a recovery “by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Nevro at “~$80M (trough)” and highlighted a “2H recovery,” with a catalyst bar of “≥ $80M with 2H recovery reaffirmed.”

description: The company reaffirmed its $3.18–$3.22 billion revenue guide instead of making the raise the preview expected, leaving implied second-half growth at roughly 2%–5%.
fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed revenue guidance of “$3.18-$3.22 billion,” implying second-half growth of roughly “2%-5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a raise to “$3.20–3.24B” and called for a revenue-guide raise to at least a “$3.22B low end.”

description: U.S. Spine grew 7%, well short of the preview’s anticipated fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit U.S. Spine growth.
fact_evidence: Revenue growth was driven by “7% U.S. Spine growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called a “fourth quarter of double-digit growth” the cleanest bull confirmation and described the expected result as “fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit U.S. Spine growth.”

description: Enabling Technologies revenue was $26.1 million, below the preview’s already cautious $32 million estimate, although the preview had anticipated a decline from the rental and leasing mix shift.
fact_evidence: Enabling Technologies revenue “fell 25.8% to $26.1 million due to a shift toward flexible capital acquisition models.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Enabling Technologies at “$32M” and said revenue would “look soft on the rental shift.”

description: The base business excluding Nevro grew 9%, a little below the preview’s roughly 9.9% estimate and its 10% catalyst bar, though it exceeded the growth implied by consensus.
fact_evidence: Revenue grew “9% excluding Nevro.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated ex-Nevro growth of “+9.9%” and set a catalyst bar of “≥ +10%”; it also said consensus implied about “+8.6%.”

description: Nevro’s stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 22.4%, up sharply from 11.8% in Q1 and turning positive versus a year earlier, despite the weaker revenue and slower recovery timing.
fact_evidence: Nevro’s stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margin “swung to positive 22.4% from negative 1.4% a year earlier” and improved “from 11.8% in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Nevro’s “11.8% in Q1” standalone EBITDA margin and flagged the risk that “Nevro is dilutive”; it did not anticipate a 22.4% margin.

description: Trauma revenue rose 31% year over year and 18% sequentially, a strong segment result not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Trauma revenue grew 31% year-over-year and 18% sequentially,” aided by restored PRECICE supply and new OUS market activation.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Management lowered the full-year non-GAAP tax-rate range to 23%–24% from 24%–25%, an unanticipated reduction that supports earnings.
fact_evidence: “The non-GAAP tax rate guidance was lowered to 23%-24% from 24%-25%.”

description: Q2 competitive sales hiring was unusually strong: hires were double Q1’s level and the second-highest onboarding in eight quarters, a growth investment the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “Competitive sales hires in Q2 were double the Q1 level, representing the second-highest onboarding in eight quarters.”

description: Q2 revenue was $296.8 million, well below the preview’s $321–330 million consensus range and even below its $315 million bear-case cutoff. Management attributed the year-over-year decline partly to operating five fewer stores after consolidations.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue declined slightly to $296.8 million from $299.9 million, primarily due to operating five fewer stores following consolidation efforts.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue **$329.9M** (high read) / **$321.0M** (low read)”; the bear case was “<$315M.”

description: Same-store revenue grew just 3%, a sharp deceleration from Q1’s 13.1% and below the preview’s watchpoint that low-single-digit growth would suggest Q1’s strength might have been a pull-forward. The call did not provide a same-store unit-growth rate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 same-store revenue reached $291.7 million (reported as $291.5M in Josh's section), a 3% increase over the prior year period.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 same-store powersports revenue was “+13.1%” and warned that “a deceleration to low single digits reframes Q1 as a tax-refund pull-forward.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $20.5 million, above the preview’s modeled $17–19 million range. This was a stronger result than the preview’s base-case expectation, despite the revenue miss.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.2% year-over-year to $20.5 million in Q2 2026, up from $17.2 million in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: *No published consensus* — my framework bar: **$17–19M**”; the base case was also “$17–19M.”

description: Adjusted SG&A improved to 74.1% of gross profit, substantially better than the preview’s already-positive threshold of below roughly 82%. Expense dollars also declined year over year.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A improved to 74.1% of gross profit (down from 77.4%), reflecting cost discipline with expenses of $62.8 million versus $64.9 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “SG&A below ~82% of gross profit in the peak quarter would be a clear positive.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New retail unit sales rose only 1.8%, well short of the preview’s modeled 8–12% unit growth, although new-unit margins improved to 14.8% from 13.2%. The margin improvement was favorable, but the reported volume gain was modest.
fact_evidence: “New retail unit sales grew 1.8% to 10,807 units with margins improving to 14.8% (from 13.2%).”
expectation_evidence: The base-case scenario anticipated “Units +8–12%”; the preview also identified the margin split as a key item to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Pre-owned retail units fell 6.8% and their margins slipped to 18% from 18.8%, a weak result against the preview’s expectation of unit growth and its focus on whether retail volume could translate into better per-unit economics.
fact_evidence: “Pre-owned retail units fell 6.8% to 4,924 with margins declining to 18% (from 18.8%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “Units +8–12%” and said to “watch new vs. pre-owned margin split separately.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said current-quarter same-store sales were already down by a low-single-digit percentage year over year. That adds a near-term warning beyond the reported quarter, whereas the preview focused on Q2 and described the industry backdrop as supportive but mixed.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged that current-quarter same-store sales are down slightly in the low single digits year-over-year amid market volatility, signaling potential softening after a strong first half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the industry read-through as “Supportive but not uniformly so” and listed Q2 same-store performance as a key watchpoint; it did not flag current-quarter sales as down.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Six-month adjusted free cash flow was $20.8 million, far above the prior-year $2.9 million, but operating activities still used $28.2 million of cash over the same six months. Because the preview was looking for Q2 free cash flow to turn positive and the call supplied a six-month adjusted figure rather than a Q2 figure, the result does not establish that the expected quarterly cash harvest occurred.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow for the first six months surged to $20.8 million from $2.9 million in the prior-year period, though operating activities showed a cash outflow of $28.2 million for the six months.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the harvest quarter — Q1's -$28.2M should reverse. If FCF is still negative in the seasonal peak, the ‘increased free cash flow in 2026’ commitment breaks.”

description: Refinancing sounded closer to completion than the preview’s cautious base case of refinancing merely ‘advancing’: management expected to provide more details in coming weeks. However, no completed refinancing or terms were reported.
fact_evidence: “Refinancing efforts are nearing completion with more details expected in coming weeks.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described refi as “‘advancing’”; it warned that “‘still in progress’ for a third straight quarter is a slow negative.”

description: Management explicitly made refinancing a prerequisite to pursuing accretive tuck-in and new-market acquisitions. The preview emphasized refinancing as a catalyst but did not say it was gating the company’s acquisition plans.
fact_evidence: Management identified refinancing as “the key prerequisite before pursuing accretive tuck-in and new-market acquisitions.”

description: Q2 revenue was $156 million, above the preview’s $153 million estimate and the roughly $147–149 million consensus range. It also cleared the preview’s suggested buy-side whisper of $155 million or more.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached a record $156 million.”
expectation_evidence: “My Est. [total revenue]: $153M”; consensus “~$147.4M – $149.0M”; functional buy-side whisper “revenue at or above the $155M high end.”

description: Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $580–600 million from $550–580 million. The new midpoint is $590 million, reaching the preview’s bullish threshold rather than leaving the full-year range unchanged.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to total revenue of $580-$600 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue guide: $550M – $580M”; “If revenue is raised toward $590M+, the guide was stale.”

description: The Q3 revenue outlook has a $145 million midpoint, below the preview’s roughly $150 million consensus benchmark. The preview identified a Q3 guide below $150 million as a downside scenario and specifically warned that a guide starting with a 14 would confirm a step-down.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for total revenue of $140-$150 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 guide vs. ~$150M consensus”; the bear scenario included “Q3 guide <$150M,” and the preview said “A Q3 guide starting with a 14 confirms the hardware step-down is real.”

description: Services revenue was $93 million, below the preview’s $95 million estimate, and its 19% growth rate fell short of the preview’s 20%-plus watchpoint. That is a modest miss on a metric the preview called central to the thesis.
fact_evidence: “Service revenue of $93 million (60% of total) growing 19%.”
expectation_evidence: “Subs & services rev: $95M”; “Watch for … services growth ≥ 20%”; a print in the high teens “would break the central pillar of the thesis.”

description: Reported EPS of $0.28 topped the preview’s $0.24 estimate, but $0.07 came from an $8 million tariff refund. Excluding that benefit, EPS was $0.21—above the $0.20 published consensus, but below the preview’s $0.24 estimate and its suggested $0.24-plus whisper.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $0.28 … but included a $0.07 benefit from an $8 million tariff refund; pro forma EPS excluding the refund was $0.21, still ahead of guidance and consensus.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: $0.20” consensus; “My Est.: $0.24”; functional buy-side whisper “EPS $0.24+.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Paid-account additions were roughly 298,000, about 48,000 above the preview’s 250,000 benchmark and well above its 230,000 downside threshold. The quarter therefore showed stronger account growth than the preview’s adequate-case expectation.
fact_evidence: “Arlo added roughly 298,000 paid accounts in the quarter, bringing total paid accounts to 6.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “≥250K is fine; <230K is the bear tell.”

description: Lifetime value per paid account rose about 15% year over year to $967, with renewals better than forecast. The preview did not identify LTV or renewal performance as a quantified expectation to watch.
fact_evidence: “Lifetime value per paid account rose about 15% year-over-year to $967, supported by higher ARPU, lower churn, and better-than-forecast subscription renewals.”
expectation_evidence: “Better-than-forecast subscription renewals.”

description: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance increased to $0.90–1.00 from $0.75–0.85. The new range is above the preview’s $0.81 consensus and its base-case expectation of roughly $0.85–0.90.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … non-GAAP EPS of $0.90-$1.00.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 non-GAAP EPS: $0.75 – $0.85 (consensus $0.81)”; base case expected “FY EPS to ~$0.85–0.90.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Arlo said it will launch Arlo Secure 7 in September with advanced AI threat-assessment features and a higher-priced subscription tier expected to lift ARPU and ARR. The preview did not anticipate this product or subscription-tier announcement.
fact_evidence: “Arlo will launch Arlo Secure 7 in September, introducing advanced AI threat-assessment features and a new higher-priced subscription tier expected to lift ARPU and ARR.”
