expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side needs “≥$2.4B gross subs”; its base case was “PW subs $2.2–2.5B.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Company-wide inflows were especially strong: nearly $40 billion over the trailing 12 months, the best 12-month period ever, with quarterly inflows of $10 billion. The preview highlighted flow risks and thresholds but did not anticipate this record company-wide inflow figure.
fact_evidence: “Gross inflows totaled $10 billion for the quarter and nearly $40 billion over the trailing 12 months, the best 12-month period ever, split evenly between managed accounts and commingled funds.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: SPRING returned 23% net in the first half of the calendar year, a stronger update than the preview’s cited +11% YTD through April and potentially reassuring on the portfolio-mark concern it flagged.
fact_evidence: “SPRING delivered 23% net returns in the first half of the calendar year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited SPRING as “+11% YTD through April” and flagged AI/software marks as a potential narrative resetter.

description: Management reported a $116 million GAAP net loss attributable to StepStone, or $1.41 per share, due to the fair-value change in the Private Wealth profits interest buy-in. The preview discussed GAAP revenue volatility but did not flag a loss of this size tied to this item.
fact_evidence: “A GAAP net loss attributable to the company of $116 million or $1.41 per share, driven by the change in fair value of the Private Wealth profits interest buy-in.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that GAAP revenue “includes unrealized carried interest” and that a GAAP ‘beat’ or ‘miss’ headline was “close to meaningless,” but gave no expectation for a profits-interest-related GAAP loss.

description: The dividend rose 18% to $0.33 per share from the $0.28 quarterly base the preview described, a larger payout than that stated base expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its quarterly dividend by 18% from $0.28 to $0.33 per share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “base is $0.28/qtr” and described the remainder of the trailing dividend as supplemental and carry-dependent.

description: Repurchases had reached $30 million of the $100 million authorization, with more than 710,000 shares bought at an average $41.87. That is a more substantial pace than the preview’s concern that only $9 million had been executed in March and that a passive buyback could signal a lack of conviction.
fact_evidence: “Repurchased $30 million of its $100 million authorization, buying over 710,000 shares at an average price of $41.87.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “only $9M executed in March” and warned that “a passive buyback will be read as a lack of conviction.”

description: Management plans to buy in the Private Wealth profits interest as soon as contractually able, with up to 75% funded in equity and the balance in cash. The equity mix includes shares tradable immediately and shares locked up over three years; this transaction and funding structure were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company plans to buy in the Private Wealth profits interest as soon as contractually able, funding up to 75% in equity (30% tradable immediately, remainder locked up over 3 years) with the balance in cash while maintaining its A+ investment-grade rating.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management flagged a $1.5 billion managed-account expiration next quarter, creating a specific near-term flow risk not identified in the preview’s flow discussion.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged a $1.5 billion managed account expiration next quarter.”

description: The commingled fee rate is expected to remain relatively flat because PE secondaries funds carry a lower fee structure, with growth resuming only once those funds are fully raised. This is a less favorable fee-growth timing detail than the preview’s emphasis on UFEC activation turning on fees and the possibility of pulled-forward flagship activation.
fact_evidence: “A lower fee structure on PE secondaries funds will keep the commingled fee rate relatively flat before resuming growth once fully raised.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said activation of flagged undeployed capital “turns on management fees,” and its bull case included “UFEC activations pulled forward.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: More than 70% of net accrued carry was tied to programs older than five years and described as ready to harvest, a favorable maturity profile beyond the preview’s estimate of the carry balance and its general focus on whether carry would convert into realizations.
fact_evidence: “Net accrued carry reached $935 million, up 19% year-over-year, with over 70% tied to programs older than five years and ready to harvest.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated net accrued carry at “~$936M” and said to watch whether accrued carry was “still building or starting to convert.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management warned that SPRING’s public positions could add performance volatility as lockups expire and positions are exited; the SpaceX holding had already fallen from its peak to a mid-teens share of NAV. The preview flagged software and venture marks as a possible issue but did not anticipate this specific position-level volatility and exit commentary.
fact_evidence: “The SpaceX position in SPRING has declined from its peak to a mid-teens percentage of NAV, and management expects public positions to introduce performance volatility as lockups expire and positions are exited.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “AI/software mark commentary” and noted SPRING’s venture/growth exposure, but gave no specific expectation about SpaceX or lockup-related volatility.

description: Chegg reported Q2 revenue of $51.8 million, above the preview’s $49.8 million consensus and the company’s $49–50 million guide, as well as the preview’s $50 million-plus functional whisper. The beat was real but relatively modest.
fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue was $51.8 million, exceeding company expectations.
expectation_evidence: Total net revenue: $49.8M consensus; company guide $49–50M. The functional whisper is revenue $50M+.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA came in well above the expected $5–6 million guide and the preview’s $6 million-plus whisper, at $9.1 million and a 17% margin. This was a substantial beat against the expected range.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA for Q2 was $9.1 million (17% margin).
expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA: company guide $5–6M (~11% margin); the functional whisper is adjusted EBITDA ≥$6M.

description: Chegg is pivoting toward an employability platform for internships and jobs, which the preview did not identify as the company’s strategic direction. More than 10,000 students have used the beta, but rollout is just beginning and continues through 2027, so the opportunity is not yet proven.
fact_evidence: The company is pivoting strategically toward an 'employability' platform to help students find internships and jobs, targeting what management believes is a larger TAM than its academic business. More than 10,000 students have used the beta; rollout begins in Q3 and continues through 2027.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Chegg is ending separate revenue guidance for Academic Services and Skilling as the businesses integrate. That removes visibility into the segment trends the preview treated as central, including Skilling’s growth and the pace of Academic Services’ decline.
fact_evidence: The company is discontinuing separate revenue guidance for Academic Services and Skilling, instead guiding on total revenue and adjusted EBITDA as the businesses integrate.
expectation_evidence: The preview gave a Chegg Skilling revenue guide of $17.5–18.0M and an implied Academic Services range of about $31.5–32.5M; it identified Skilling growth and the Academic Services decay slope as key metrics to watch.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash generation and liquidity were stronger than the preview’s runway framing suggested: Q2 free cash flow was $6.4 million despite $14.4 million of severance payments, and quarter-end cash and investments were $72.3 million. After the expected $33.9 million debt repayment, that implies about $38.4 million of cash, above the preview’s rough $30–35 million post-repayment estimate.
fact_evidence: Free cash flow was $6.4 million in Q2 and $9.5 million in the first half, despite $14.4 million in severance payments from prior restructuring. The company ended the quarter with $72.3 million in cash and investments.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated roughly $30–35M of post-repayment cash against the business’s quarterly EBITDA needs.

description: Chegg repurchased $1.7 million of stock in Q2, a capital-allocation action the preview did not anticipate while emphasizing the upcoming convertible repayment and cash runway. The amount was small, and the call also noted that $120.7 million remained on the buyback authorization.
fact_evidence: Chegg repurchased $1.7 million of stock in Q2 and has $120.7 million remaining on its buyback authorization.

description: Q2 continuing-operations sales were $66.7 million, above the preview model’s $62–65 million range. The preview warned that published consensus was unreliable, so this is a modest beat against its own model rather than a clean consensus comparison.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales from continuing operations were roughly flat year-over-year at $66.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$62–65M” in the preview’s model.

description: The company raised full-year potash production guidance to 290–300,000 tons from the previously stated 270–285,000 tons, exceeding the preview’s expectation that production was tracking toward the upper end of the old range. Management said the increase reflected sustainable recovery and throughput improvements, not tons pulled forward from 2027.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year production guidance for…potash (to 290-300,000 tons)…driven by sustainable mill recovery and throughput improvements rather than pulling tons forward from 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year potash production guide 270–285k tons, tracking ‘upper end’ as of May.”

description: Management also raised full-year Trio production guidance to 295–305,000 tons. The preview did not provide a full-year Trio production expectation or anticipate this increase.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year production guidance for…Trio (to 295-305,000 tons).”

description: Trio’s cost of goods sold per ton reached its lowest level since Q4 2019, providing a stronger indication of durable cost improvement than the preview’s base case of roughly $230 per ton. The preview had identified a rebound toward $240 or more as a risk and sub-$230 as the more favorable outcome.
fact_evidence: “Trio delivered its lowest cost of goods sold per ton since Q4 2019.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Trio COGS ~$230” in its base case and said a move “back toward $240+” could signal Q1’s performance was not structural.

description: Q3 Trio pricing guidance of $400–410 per ton was above the $390–400 level the preview used as its comparison point for Q3/H2 pricing. Management also said Trio pricing was expected to trend up on low-chloride and sulfate value.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance…Trio sales of 30-40,000 tons at $400-410 per ton, with Trio pricing expected to trend up on low-chloride and sulfate value.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist compared Q3 pricing with “$390–400 Trio” and said buyers wanted “flat-to-up.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The $5 million Pecos Water Rights accrual was an unanticipated charge that reduced reported continuing-operations net income and diluted EPS. The preview’s EPS estimates focused on adjusted EPS and did not flag this accrual.
fact_evidence: “Net income from continuing operations improved to $2.4 million ($0.18 per diluted share), including a $5 million accrual related to the Pecos Water Rights matter.”

description: Although the $50 million authorization was already known, the preview looked for Q2 buyback execution as a read on capital allocation. Management instead said buybacks were expected to begin in Q3, meaning the anticipated Q2 execution had not begun.
fact_evidence: “Buybacks expected to begin in Q3 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked “How many shares were retired in Q2” and said “> $15M executed” would be a strong signal; it also identified “near-zero” execution as a concern.

description: Full-year capital expenditure guidance moved to approximately $40 million, at the low end of the preview’s $40–50 million expectation. The reduction reflected deferral of the AMAX project and lower Wendover Primary Pond 8 costs.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance was reduced to approximately $40 million, reflecting deferral of the AMAX project and reduced costs for Wendover's primary pond 8.”
expectation_evidence: “Capex guide $40–50M including Wendover Primary Pond 8.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash was $185 million, above the preview’s approximate $170 million cash expectation based on the South Ranch proceeds. The company also reported no revolver borrowings and $149.8 million of revolver availability.
fact_evidence: “Ending the quarter with $185 million cash, no revolver borrowings, and $149.8 million of revolver availability.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash was $99.3M at 3/31 plus $70M South Ranch proceeds (closed April 1) ≈ $170M.”

description: Veeco reported Q2 revenue of $193 million, above the $180.1 million consensus and the $190 million top of its guidance range. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.33 beat the $0.26 consensus and $0.32 guidance ceiling, while non-GAAP operating income of $23 million was also well above the preview’s $1–10 million guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $193 million with non-GAAP operating income of $23 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.33, exceeding guidance and Street expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” was $180.1M revenue and $0.26 non-GAAP EPS; Q2 guidance was $170M–$190M revenue, $0.20–$0.32 EPS, and $1M–$10M operating income.

description: Veeco raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $780–810 million from $740–800 million. That is better than the preview’s expected range, including a higher low end.
fact_evidence: “Veeco raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $780-810 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reiterated 5/5/26): Revenue $740M–$800M.”

description: Despite raising revenue guidance, Veeco cut FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.36–1.61 from $1.50–1.85. Management attributed the reduction to growth investments, which add about $10 million of operating expenses and reduce full-year gross margin by roughly 75 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Lowered non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.36-1.61 due to growth investments”; the investments “will add approximately $10 million of incremental operating expenses and reduce full-year 2026 gross margin by roughly 75 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reiterated 5/5/26): ... Non-GAAP EPS $1.50–$1.85”; the preview said the key issue was whether the range was “reaffirmed / narrowed to lower half / cut.”

description: Veeco’s Q3 revenue outlook has a $210 million midpoint, above the preview’s $200 million threshold to keep the FY outlook intact and at the level it said would validate the upper half of expectations. The preview’s base case was a $195–205 million midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $200-220 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Needs ≥$200M midpoint to keep FY intact; ≥$210M to validate the upper half”; base case: “$195–205M mid.”

description: Q3 EPS guidance of $0.35–0.49 is below the preview’s estimated $0.55–0.72 quarterly EPS run rate needed in H2 to meet the original FY2026 EPS range. The annual EPS outlook was cut as well, but the Q3 range itself falls short of that earlier required run rate.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance ... diluted EPS of $0.35-0.49.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated an “Implied H2 run-rate/qtr” of “~$0.55 – $0.72” to meet the FY2026 guide.

description: Veeco guided Q3 gross margin to 41–42%, above the preview’s expectation that management would need to move gross margin toward 40% or higher in H2. This contrasts with the separately disclosed full-year margin reduction from growth investments.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects ... gross margin of 41-42%.”
expectation_evidence: “Management needs to walk the Street to 40%+ in H2”; the preview also said the H2 EPS ramp required gross margin to move “toward 40%+.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Veeco disclosed $200 million of Q2 orders for advanced-packaging wet-processing and lithography systems, primarily for 2027 delivery. The preview watched for order acceleration and a possible same-day order announcement, but did not anticipate this specific order amount or advanced-packaging demand.
fact_evidence: “The company secured $200 million in advanced packaging orders for wet processing and lithography systems during Q2, primarily for delivery in 2027.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Veeco plans to more than double advanced-packaging and silicon-photonics capacity during 2027, using internal production and Southeast Asian outsourcing partners. The preview discussed the opportunity and order book but did not flag a capacity expansion of this scale.
fact_evidence: “The company plans to more than double advanced packaging and silicon photonics capacity during 2027 through internal production and Southeast Asian outsourcing partners.”

description: Veeco said compound-semiconductor revenue is expected to approximately double in 2026 versus 2025, an end-market outlook not specified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Compound semiconductor revenue is expected to approximately double in 2026 versus 2025.”

description: Spire reported an adjusted continuing-operations loss of $0.26 per share, slightly worse than the preview’s $0.24 loss consensus. The gap was $0.02 per share.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted Q3 FY2026 loss from continuing operations improved to $0.26 per share ($15 million).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The divestitures produced a substantial after-tax sale gain and reported discontinued-operations earnings, an accounting boost the preview did not quantify even though it discussed the asset sales. This was separate from the adjusted continuing-operations loss.
fact_evidence: “Spire recorded $253.8 million in earnings from discontinued operations, including an after-tax gain on sale of $254.6 million from divesting Spire Marketing and Spire Storage.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Spire disclosed FFO-to-debt of 13% during the transition year, below the 14%–15% target, and said it expects to reach that target by the end of 2028. The preview flagged the target but did not specify a current 13% level or that timeline.
fact_evidence: “FFO-to-debt currently stands at 13% during the transition year, with a 14%-15% target expected to be reached by end of 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch bridge balance, FFO/debt against the lowered 14–15% target.”

description: O&M expense rose by about $4 million, primarily because of higher bad debt, a cost pressure the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “O&M expense rose about $4 million primarily due to higher bad debt.”

description: Corporate/other losses widened to $12 million from $3 million, with higher corporate and interest costs contributing. The preview anticipated higher interest expense from Tennessee, but did not flag the wider corporate/other loss.
fact_evidence: “Corporate/other losses widened to $12 million from $3 million on higher corporate and interest costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Interest expense stepped up hard — Q2 net interest was $62.6M, +38.2% y/y, before Tennessee debt was fully carried.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Ahead of the Alabama RSE hearings, intervenors recommended 8%–9% ROEs, below both the company’s requested 10.5% and 10.75% adjusting-point ROEs and the current 9.9% allowed ROE. This introduced a specific downside to the rate-setting debate that the preview did not describe.
fact_evidence: “Alabama RSE renewal hearings on August 6-7 will decide requested adjusting-point ROEs of 10.5% for Spire Alabama and 10.75% for Spire Gulf, with intervenors recommending 8%-9% versus the current 9.9% allowed.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Spire Tennessee filed its first annual review mechanism, seeking a $14 million revenue increase and new rates effective October 1, 2026. The preview focused on Tennessee’s first-full-quarter economics and financing costs but did not identify this rate filing.
fact_evidence: “Spire Tennessee filed its first annual review mechanism seeking a $14 million revenue increase based on a 9.8% ROE and $1.5 billion rate base, with new rates expected effective October 1, 2026.”

description: PSEG reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.86, well above the preview’s roughly $0.79–$0.80 consensus range (and the $0.83 alternate estimate).
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating earnings of $0.86 per share,” compared with $0.77 in Q2 2025.
expectation_evidence: “Consensus looks for non-GAAP EPS of roughly $0.79–$0.80”; alternate estimates were $0.794 and $0.83.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: PSE&G plans to file a base-rate update by year-end 2026, advancing the filing from the previously required 2029 deadline. The preview mentioned favorable distribution-rate trends but did not flag this much earlier filing.
fact_evidence: “PSE&G plans to file to update base rates by year-end 2026, pulling forward from the previously required 2029 deadline,” citing regulatory lag and distribution rate-base additions.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “favorable electric/gas base distribution rates” but gave no expectation of an accelerated rate case.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: PSEG disclosed that a PJM transmission cost-allocation change will provide customer benefits of about $33 million through 2026 and an expected annual benefit of about $65 million thereafter; the preview did not identify this benefit.
fact_evidence: The change effective June 1, 2026 “will deliver roughly $33 million in customer benefit through year-end 2026” and an “expected prospective annual benefit of approximately $65 million.”

description: PSEG identified a prospective earnings headwind from the potential loss of the RTO transmission incentive, beginning in 2027, which the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “Potential elimination of the 50 basis point RTO transmission incentive represents an annual headwind of about $40 million net income (roughly $0.08 per share) effective January 2027,” with no 2026 impact.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: PSEG said it can fund its five-year capital program without new equity issuance or asset sales, an important funding assurance not covered in the preview.
fact_evidence: The “$24 billion to $28 billion five-year capital investment program” can be funded “without issuing new equity or selling assets.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: PSEG Nuclear cleared 3,600 MW in the latest PJM capacity auction at the $325/MW-day collar ceiling, below the prior $333 and far below the stated uncapped price of $555. The preview did not discuss the auction outcome.
fact_evidence: PSEG Nuclear cleared “approximately 3,600 megawatts” at “$325 per megawatt day (the collar ceiling),” versus the prior $333 and an uncapped price that “would have been $555.”

description: PSEG said higher realized prices and generation more than offset the absence of expired zero-emission certificates, a favorable nuclear earnings offset not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The absence of expired zero emission certificates was more than offset by higher realized prices and generation”; nuclear generation was 7.8 TWh at a 92% capacity factor.

description: PSE&G disclosed a planned residential gas-bill reduction and a $166 million customer refund. The preview had highlighted affordability pressure, but did not anticipate these specific customer-relief actions; no earnings effect was stated.
fact_evidence: PSE&G “filed to lower residential gas bills by more than 5% beginning October 1” and is refunding “roughly $166 million of zero emission certificates over 12 months to customers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Affordability pressure on New Jersey bills remains a political overhang.”

description: Ziff Davis’s adjusted diluted EPS was $1.03, well above the preview’s $0.807 consensus. The company attributed the growth primarily to buybacks, so the per-share result beat expectations even though the underlying revenue and EBITDA were roughly on plan.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 13.2% year-over-year to $1.03, driven primarily by the significant share count reduction from buyback activity.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.807”

description: Technology & Shopping improved much more than the preview’s base case: revenue declined 5%, versus the preview’s expected decline of roughly 9–11%, and adjusted EBITDA grew more than 8%.
fact_evidence: “Tech & Shopping revenue declined 5% year-over-year, a marked improvement from the 13% drop in Q1 and 18% drop in Q4, while its adjusted EBITDA rose more than 8%.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “T&S ~−9 to −11%”; the preview also said “Better than −8% is a genuine positive surprise.”

description: Buybacks were substantial: Ziff Davis spent more than $200 million in the first seven months of 2026 and reduced shares outstanding by nearly 11%, including $121.5 million of repurchases in Q2. That is more aggressive than the preview’s base case of buybacks continuing at the existing pace, though it had identified a large capital return as a possible bull-case outcome.
fact_evidence: “The company deployed over $200 million to buy back 4.5 million shares in the first seven months of 2026, reducing shares outstanding by nearly 11%, and repurchased $121.5 million of stock during Q2 alone.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “buyback continues at existing pace, no new authorization”; the bull case called for a “large capital return announced.”

description: Health and Wellness weakened despite the preview noting that MedPage bookings were improving: revenue fell nearly 5% and adjusted EBITDA dropped nearly 10%. Management also cited pharma clients cutting HCP advertising and shifting to lower-cost AI platforms.
fact_evidence: “Health and Wellness revenues fell nearly 5% and adjusted EBITDA dropped nearly 10% as large pharma clients reduced HCP advertising spend at MedPage and shifted to lower-cost AI-based platforms.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q1 baseline showed Health & Wellness revenue “+0.2%” and stated “MedPage bookings improving.”

description: The outlook did not reaffirm the H2 revenue growth thesis the preview highlighted: management instead expects revenue to keep declining in Q3 and Q4, although the decline should ease in Q4. Q3 margins are expected to improve modestly, while Q4 margins are expected to be slightly lower year over year.
fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to decline low-to-mid single digits year-over-year with modest margin improvement, and expects Q4 to show a lower rate of revenue decline with adjusted EBITDA margin slightly down year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “H2 revenue growth reaffirmation” as a key metric and cited the prior outlook for “YoY growth in H2” in Technology & Shopping.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management disclosed a notable internal AI productivity gain that the preview had not anticipated: the share of code authored by AI roughly doubled in one quarter, enabling more code output with fewer engineers, with an ambitious target for year-end.
fact_evidence: “The share of code authored by AI roughly doubled in one quarter, enabling 24% more code shipped in Q2 versus Q1 on lower engineering headcount, with a target of nearly all code being AI-authored by end of 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CPSS’s Q2 originations were far above the preview’s ~$600–640 million estimate: the company reported $758 million, up 75% year over year. The preview said anything below $560 million would suggest March’s run rate had not held, but reported volume substantially exceeded even the estimate’s upper end.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 loan originations surged to $758 million, up 75% from $433 million in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “New contract purchases … ~ $600–640M”; “Anything under $560M says March was a pull-forward.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Credit losses were materially better than the preview’s expected range: net charge-offs were 7.28%, below the preview’s 8.5–8.9% base case and below its ~8.5% thesis-intact threshold. This was also a year-over-year improvement rather than the modest deterioration the base case allowed for.
fact_evidence: “Net charge-offs declined to 7.28% from 7.45%” year over year.
expectation_evidence: “Base … NCO … 8.5–8.9%”; “NCOs at or below ~8.5% with the bad vintages shrinking = thesis intact.”

description: Revenue exceeded the preview’s estimate by $4.4 million, or about 4%, and grew 11% year over year versus the preview’s modeled 6.6% growth. The revenue beat was positive but smaller than the originations outperformance.
fact_evidence: “Revenue increased 11% to $121.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue … My Q2'26 Base Est. ~ $117M (+6.6% YoY).”

description: The preview worried that the expanded sales force could weigh on expenses before volume arrived, but reported expense trends showed leverage instead: core operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue and the expense-to-managed-portfolio ratio improved.
fact_evidence: “Core operating expenses grew only 3% over six months while revenue grew 8%, improving the expense-to-managed-portfolio ratio to 4.6% from 4.9%.”
expectation_evidence: “If Q2 opex runs above ~$110M without a commensurate origination beat, the market will read the growth as bought rather than earned.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Recoveries improved further rather than reversing: the reported 33.3% rate was above the preview’s Q1 reference of 31.1%. The stronger recovery rate also accompanied the better-than-expected net charge-off result.
fact_evidence: “Recovery rates rose to 33.3% from 30.4% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Recoveries improved to 31.1% from 27.7% in Q1. If that reverses, gross charge-offs flow straight through.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The growth was not accompanied by a higher approval rate: applications rose sharply while approvals stayed near 51%. That addresses the preview’s concern that rapid dealer and sales-force expansion might be buying growth through looser credit.
fact_evidence: “Applications received climbed 42% to 1.1 million, while the approval rate held steady at roughly 51%, indicating growth was achieved without loosening credit standards.”
expectation_evidence: “The bear” case required that “the growth is real but is being bought with looser credit”; the preview also called for evidence that dealer and rep expansion converted.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Delinquency improved year over year but rose from Q1’s 11.58% to 12.16%, so the leading indicator did not continue its prior sequential improvement. The increase was not paired with rising charge-offs, however, and the year-over-year rate remained better.
fact_evidence: “Total delinquency over 30 days improved to 12.16% from 13.14% a year earlier.” The preview reported Q1 at 11.58%.

description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin fell short of the preview’s expected profitability recovery: EBITDA was $42.6M versus an estimated $44–47M, and the 10.4% margin was below the roughly 11.0% estimate and the preview’s 10.5–11% validation threshold.

expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$44–47M (est., not formally polled)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin: ~11.0% (est.).” The preview said the margin “Needs to be ≥10.5–11% to validate the guide.”

description: Infrastructure Solutions margin moved in the opposite direction from the recovery the preview was looking for: it compressed 130 basis points, with management citing a mix shift toward lower-margin mobile paving equipment.
fact_evidence: “Infrastructure Solutions net sales grew 11.6% to $228.3 million but margin compressed 130 basis points due to an unfavorable mix shift toward lower-margin mobile paving equipment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “a return toward 17–18%” and said a recovery to “17%+” would signal the thesis was intact.

description: Q2 sales slightly exceeded the published consensus estimate: $408.1M was $2.6M, or about 0.6%, above the $405.5M estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 23.6% year-over-year to $408.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $405.5M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported that July was among Astec’s strongest booking months for asphalt plants and parts, a constructive update against the preview’s concern that customers might defer orders around the highway-funding deadline.
fact_evidence: Management noted “July was among its strongest bookings months for asphalt plants and parts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “customer order deferral risk” and said that an admission of customers “deferring ahead of reauthorization” would be a concern.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The call gave new, mixed detail on highway funding: the proposed Build America 250 Act would raise core highway funding and the guaranteed formula-funded share, but management said only a continuing resolution appeared likely near-term. The preview had flagged reauthorization timing as uncertain but did not anticipate these proposal details.
fact_evidence: “The proposed Build America 250 Act carries a smaller $580 billion headline but raises core highway funding ~7% ($351B to $376B) and lifts guaranteed formula-funded share from 87% to 90%, though only a continuing resolution appears likely near-term.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the “Surface Transportation Bill” expiration on September 30, 2026, and called for a read on reauthorization timing and customer order deferral risk.

description: Underlying earnings fell well short of the preview’s realistic bar: adjusted EPS was $0.15 versus an estimated $0.40–$0.50, and adjusted EBITDA was $3.4 million versus the preview’s $5.5 million estimate. The weakness came despite the preview’s expectation of a partial recovery as the quarter progressed.
fact_evidence: “Excluding the bargain purchase gain, adjusted net income from continuing operations dropped to $0.9 million ($0.15/diluted share) from $3.5 million ($0.57) a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA fell approximately 49% to $3.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Assume the real buy-side bar is materially lower — roughly $64–67M revenue and $0.40–0.50 adj. EPS.” The preview’s estimates were “adj. EPS $0.42” and “adj. EBITDA $5.5M.”

description: Sales were weaker than the preview’s realistic estimate, falling 11.9% year over year rather than landing around $64–67 million. Shipments declined across truck mirrors, returnable transport packaging, and latch/handle assemblies, so the expected RTP inflection was not evident in the reported results.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales from continuing operations fell 11.9% year-over-year to $61.8 million from $70.2 million,” driven by lower shipments of truck mirror assemblies, returnable transport packaging, and latch/handle assemblies.
expectation_evidence: “Assume the real buy-side bar is materially lower — roughly $64–67M revenue.” The preview also flagged “RTP volume inflection” and noted program launches management had flagged for Q2–Q3.

description: Gross margin was 20.8%, below the preview’s 21.5% estimate, and the below-margin Big 3 contract runoff was still weighing on the quarter rather than being largely behind the company by quarter-end. Tariff costs also remained a headwind, although margin improved sequentially.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 20.8% ($12.8M) from 23.3% ($16.4M) year-over-year due to lower volume, the below-margin Big 3 contract runoff, and ~$1.9 million of China tariff costs, though it improved roughly 60 basis points sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “gross margin 21.5%” and said management’s damage was “largely behind us by the end of the second quarter.” It described 21.5–23% as needed for the bull case.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog far exceeded the preview’s roughly flat base-case expectation: it reached $126.2 million, up 45% year over year, versus an anticipated $80–84 million. About $19 million came from the newly acquired aerospace businesses, but legacy business also contributed to the increase.
fact_evidence: “Backlog surged 45% year-over-year to $126.2 million from $87.1 million, with roughly $19 million from the new aerospace book and the balance from legacy business.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “backlog roughly flat $80–84M”; its bull case called for backlog above $88 million.

description: Eastern completed a $7.85 million acquisition of Crown Precision and Sun Gear, entering aerospace and defense manufacturing—an actual deal rather than merely the possible tuck-in M&A mentioned in the preview. The businesses contributed $1.7 million of sales for one month and are expected to generate about $20 million in annual revenue, but currently have near-breakeven gross margins and are expected to weigh about 120 basis points on overall margin near term.
fact_evidence: “The company acquired California-based Crown Precision and Sun Gear for $7.85 million, funded by borrowings, marking its entry into aerospace and defense precision manufacturing effective June 1.” The businesses “contributed $1.7 million in sales during the one month of ownership,” are expected to run at “roughly $20 million in combined annual revenue,” and “currently operate near breakeven gross margins”; the acquisition is expected to weigh “~120 basis points on overall gross margin near-term.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “tuck-in M&A” among possible strategic/capital-allocation news, but did not anticipate this acquisition or its near-term margin effects.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The reported $5.6 million of GAAP net income included a $6.5 million noncash bargain-purchase gain, making the headline profit much stronger than the underlying adjusted result. The preview’s earnings bar was based on adjusted EPS, so this accounting gain was not part of the expected operating performance.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net income from continuing operations rose to $5.6 million ($0.94/diluted share) from $2.0 million ($0.33) a year ago, but this was inflated by a $6.5 million one-time noncash bargain purchase gain from the acquisitions.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company borrowed to fund the acquisition rather than showing the deleveraging the preview highlighted: long-term debt was $41.7 million and revolver availability was $59 million, versus the preview’s cited $33 million of debt and $67 million of availability. Cash generation was notably stronger, however, with first-half operating cash flow of $12 million.
fact_evidence: The acquisition was “funded by borrowings.” The company ended the quarter with “$15.1 million cash, $41.7 million long-term debt, and $59 million available under its $100 million revolving credit facility”; cash from operations was “$12 million in the first six months versus $1.9 million a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Deleveraging and cash,” citing “LT debt ~$33M” and “$67M available on the $100M Citizens revolver,” and said Schroeder called deleveraging “a clear priority.”

description: ADTRAN's gross margin was 40.7%, below the preview's base-case expectation of roughly 41–42% and well below the 42–43% level it identified as a healthier outcome. Management attributed the decline to supply constraints that limited shipments of higher-margin products.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 40.7%, down from 43% in Q1 2026 and 41.4% a year ago, driven by supply constraints limiting shipments of higher-margin products.”
expectation_evidence: “If GM held near 42–43%, this is an opex/absorption story that self-corrects; if GM printed 40% or below, memory/freight is structural.” The base scenario also expected “GM ~41–42%.”

description: The preview treated the delayed project as potentially recapturable in H2, but management said it did not expect a Q3 rebound in the delayed customer's Access & Aggregation orders. That makes near-term recovery less likely than the preview's base-case H2 framing suggested, though it does not establish that the project is lost.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $275-295 million and non-GAAP operating margin of 1.5-5.5%, with no expected rebound in the delayed customer's Access & Aggregation orders.”
expectation_evidence: “‘Delay’ implies H2 recapture. Watch for an explicit dollar quantification and a re-booking timeline.” The base scenario expected the project to be “expected to recover in H2.”

description: Enterprise, government and cloud revenue grew 47% year over year, while hyperscaler revenue surged 97%. The preview anticipated hyperscaler momentum but did not quantify growth of this scale.
fact_evidence: “Revenue from enterprise, government and cloud customers grew 47% year-over-year and 19% sequentially, reaching 25% of total company revenue.” “Hyperscaler revenue surged 97% year-over-year, driven by data center interconnect.”
expectation_evidence: “Optical / hyperscaler momentum” was identified as an offsetting bull leg, with the preview watching for “backlog commentary on hyperscalers”; no growth rate was given.

description: Management disclosed that reaching its 10% operating-margin target requires roughly $310–320 million of revenue at 42–43% gross margin. The preview highlighted the margin collapse and Q3 margin bridge but did not provide this revenue hurdle, which shows the target depends on materially higher revenue and gross margin than the Q3 guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Management estimates reaching its 10% operating margin target requires revenue of roughly $310-320 million at 42-43% gross margin.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: ADTRAN generated positive Q2 free cash flow despite the preview's concern about cash burn, although cash still declined during the quarter. The cash-flow result was better than the preview's bear-case scenario of continued cash burn, but the lower cash balance tempers the improvement.
fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $8.7 million and operating cash flow was $25.9 million, while cash declined to $79.2 million from $88.3 million at March 31, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview's bear scenario included “cash burn continues,” and it flagged “Free cash flow, inventory, and the new facility” as key items to watch.

description: The refinancing was already known to have closed, but the call added that it reduced borrowing costs by 200 basis points and extended the facility's maturity to 2031—favorable financing details the preview did not specify.
fact_evidence: “The company completed a refinancing of its credit facility led by JPMorgan, reducing borrowing costs by 200 basis points and extending maturity to 2031.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said ADTRAN had closed a “$350M JPMorgan-led senior secured facility” and listed its interest spread and covenants, but did not state the 200-basis-point reduction or 2031 maturity.

description: Ironwood reported Q2 LINZESS U.S. net sales of $582.3 million, far above the preview’s estimate of about $288 million. The reported figure is more than double the expected level.
fact_evidence: “LINZESS delivered Q2 2026 U.S. net sales of $582.3 million, up 14% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026E” LINZESS U.S. net sales: “$288M”; the preview also cited a guidance-implied bar of “~$288–292M.”

description: The company raised its full-year LINZESS sales outlook to $1.15–1.2 billion, above the preview’s cited prior guidance range of $1.125–1.175 billion. This is a positive, though relatively modest, increase to the outlook.
fact_evidence: “Ironwood raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting LINZESS U.S. net sales of $1.15-1.2 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether FY26 guidance of “$1.125–1.175B is reaffirmed, raised, or narrowed,” and its base case assumed “FY guidance maintained not raised.”

description: Ironwood raised full-year revenue guidance to $460–485 million, while the preview cited prior guidance of $450–475 million and described maintaining guidance as its base case. The new range is also above the cited $460.1 million FY consensus at the midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $460-485 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance math of “$450–475M” and FY26 revenue consensus of “$460.1M”; its base case expected “FY guidance maintained not raised.”

description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to greater than $310 million, above the preview’s cited prior guide of more than $300 million. The increase is positive, though below the preview’s bull-case threshold of more than $325 million.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance to greater than $310 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “>300M of guided FY26 adjusted EBITDA” and its bull scenario called for EBITDA “to >$325M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 LINZESS prescription demand grew 4%, one percentage point below the preview’s 5% reference for demand. The company nevertheless raised its full-year demand-growth expectation from low-single-digit to mid-single-digit.
fact_evidence: “LINZESS TRx volume grew 4% year-over-year in Q2 and 5% year-to-date, prompting a raise in full-year demand growth expectations from low-single-digit to mid-single-digit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified demand growth “vs. +5%” as a key metric and described its base case as “demand ~4–5%.”

description: Q2 total revenue was $113 million, slightly below the preview’s $114.8 million consensus and its own $115 million estimate. The shortfall was small relative to the preview’s stated $114–123 million reasonable Q2 band.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 delivered … $113 million in total revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed total revenue consensus of “$114.8M,” a company-model estimate of “$115M,” and a “honest Q2 revenue band at $114–123M.”

description: Q2 GAAP net income was $51.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $46 million estimate. The preview cautioned that EPS comparisons were unreliable, so this is a modest upside versus its own net-income model rather than a clean consensus beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 delivered $51.3 million in GAAP net income.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 model estimated “~$46M” in GAAP net income and warned that EPS estimates mixed GAAP and adjusted conventions.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The STARS-EXTEND update provided encouraging long-term patient outcomes that the preview did not discuss: more than one in five patients had achieved enteral autonomy, and roughly 90% of STARS patients rolled over into the extension study.
fact_evidence: “In the STARS-EXTEND long-term extension study, more than 1 in 5 patients achieved enteral autonomy as of January, with roughly 90% of STARS patients rolling over into the extension.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call disclosed that the original STARS trial’s delivered dose was 3.5 mg rather than the intended 5 mg, and that STARS II will use the 3.5 mg dose with a redesigned delivery kit to prevent dosing errors. The preview did not flag this prior dosing issue or the resulting trial-design detail.
fact_evidence: “STARS II uses a 3.5 mg dose to match the actual delivered dose in the original STARS trial (intended to be 5 mg), with an improved delivery kit developed after root cause analysis to prevent prior dosing errors.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: GENK delivered much stronger CPG progress than the preview’s still-unproven, forward-looking framing suggested: management reported 341% sequential revenue growth, more than $2 million of June sales, and placement in nearly 2,000 retail doors. It raised the next-12-month run-rate target to $35–$40 million from the prior $20 million-plus target, excluding a prepared-meals opportunity that buyers say could double frozen-product sales.
fact_evidence: “The CPG division's revenue grew 341% sequentially from Q1,” June was “the biggest month at over $2 million in revenue,” products were in “nearly 2,000 retail doors nationwide,” and management raised the forward 12-month CPG run rate to “$35 million-$40 million” from the “prior $20 million+ run rate target.” The guidance excludes fresh prepared/cooked meals, which buyers indicate could generate double the sales of frozen products.
expectation_evidence: The preview said CPG projections were “promised ‘by end of Q2 2026’” and that “First hard numbers on revenue, margin, and door count matter more than the restaurant P&L.” It described the three-year framing as “$100M+ revenue at high-teens EBITDA margin — completely unproven.”

description: GENK disclosed a nonbinding offer to sell its U.S. restaurant operations and related leases for approximately $100 million while retaining all of its CPG business—an unexpected potential separation of the restaurant and CPG businesses. The letter is nonbinding, so the transaction is not assured.
fact_evidence: GEN received a “nonbinding letter of intent” from a nationwide restaurant operator to acquire “only its U.S. restaurant operations and related leases” at approximately “$100 million,” while GEN retains “100% of its CPG business.”

description: Management reaffirmed the $215–$225 million FY2026 revenue range rather than trimming it to the low end, as the preview’s base case expected. That is a better outcome than the preview’s central forecast, though reaffirmation was also identified as a possible outcome.
fact_evidence: “GEN reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $215 million-$225 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “FY guide trimmed to low end”; it also framed “$215–225M reaffirmed vs. cut” as the guidance decision to watch.

description: Q2 revenue was slightly above the preview’s own $54.5 million estimate and above Q1, returning to year-over-year growth, although it still missed the $57.2 million consensus that the preview expected it to miss. This is a modest improvement over the preview’s base forecast, not a consensus beat.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose just 1.2% year-over-year to $55.7 million,” after a 6% decline in Q1.
expectation_evidence: The preview gave “Consensus of $57.2M revenue” but said “My base” was “$54.5M,” with a likely range of “$54–55.5M”; it also forecast $53–55M after applying the prior-year seasonal step-down to Q1 revenue.

description: Restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margin recovered to 11.3%, above the preview’s 10.5% estimate and its 10% credibility threshold for the H2 margin target. However, it remained below the preview’s roughly 13% consensus-implied margin, so the comparison is mixed.
fact_evidence: Restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA was “$6.3 million (11.3% of revenue)” versus 7.4% in Q1 and 7.9% in Q4 2025.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “10.5%,” and it said Q2 “needs to print 10%+” for the H2 guide to be credible; its consensus-implied margin was “~13%.”

description: The expected Q2 easing in food-cost pressure did not appear: COGS rose to 39.1% of revenue rather than recapturing costs from Q1. Most of the reported food-cost increase was tied to the new CPG business, with the remainder attributed to commodity inflation.
fact_evidence: “Cost of goods sold jumped over 5 percentage points to 39.1% of revenue”; 81% of the $3.2 million food-cost increase was attributable to CPG and the rest to commodity inflation.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management reported commodity pressure had “eased considerably” during Q2 and identified “a 200–300bps COGS recapture” as the most likely source of upside.

description: The company’s stated development pace was more restrained than the preview’s cited guidance of 5–7 new restaurants: GEN expects development to remain near maintenance levels while completing its fifth and final restaurant transfer in Q3.
fact_evidence: GEN expects to “complete its fifth and final restaurant transfer in Q3 while keeping development near maintenance levels.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “5–7 new restaurants” for FY26.

description: The reported Class A loss per share was worse than both the preview’s base estimate and consensus, despite the preview’s warning that this metric was a low-signal measure for GENK.
fact_evidence: Net loss widened to “$4.6 million (negative $0.14 per share)” from a $1.7 million net loss a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed EPS consensus of “$(0.08)” and its own estimate of “$(0.11).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The CPG inventory build required a substantial line-of-credit draw and raised total debt to $24 million. The preview expected borrowing to fund CPG, but did not quantify a draw of this size.
fact_evidence: “Total debt rose to $24 million from $14.6 million at year-end,” driven by an “$11 million net line-of-credit draw to fund CPG inventory build.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “expects to draw on credit to fund CPG,” and highlighted Q1-end cash of $4.4 million and $4.5 million drawn on the revolver.

description: Adjusted operating EPS was $8.89, far above the $6.51 consensus estimate. Even subtracting the $0.83-per-share benefit from onetime/other items leaves about $8.06 per share.
fact_evidence: RGA reported $8.89 per share after tax; onetime/other items contributed $0.83 per share.
expectation_evidence: Adjusted operating EPS consensus: $6.51.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A material $71 million of onetime/other items boosted the quarter, although management said they were nonrecurring and expected to net closer to zero over time. The preview cautioned that some revenue lines were lumpy, but did not anticipate this specific earnings benefit.
fact_evidence: “Onetime/other items contributed a material $71 million ($0.83 per share) benefit this quarter,” and management characterized it as “nonrecurring” and expected it “to net closer to zero over time.”

description: TTM adjusted operating ROE rose to 18.4%, above the preview’s 16.2% starting point and even the preview’s bull-case threshold of 16.5%. The 13%–15% target was not reported as having been reset.
fact_evidence: TTM adjusted operating ROE was 18.4%, “tracking above the 13%-15% intermediate-term target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said ROE was “Running 16.2% at Q1” and its bull case specified “TTM ROE ≥16.5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: In-force deployment was only $158 million in Q2 and nearly $500 million year to date, leaving RGA below the pace needed for roughly $1.5 billion annually. That fell well short of the preview’s bull-case Q2 deployment threshold, though the preview already expected deployment to remain below the annual pace in its base case.
fact_evidence: RGA deployed “$158 million this quarter” and “nearly $500 million year-to-date,” below the roughly $1.5 billion annual deployment pace previously discussed.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 deployment of $338 million against an annual need of about $1.5 billion, said the buy-side wanted to see Q2 deployment and pipeline conversion, and set “Q2 deployment ≥$600M” as a bull-case condition.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Variable investment income was substantially ahead of plan: the Q2 annualized return was 15%, and the year-to-date return was 11%, both above the 7% planned return for 2026. Management said this increased confidence in meeting or exceeding the target.
fact_evidence: Variable investment income delivered a “15% annualized return in Q2 and 11% year-to-date,” “well above the 7% planned return for 2026,” raising confidence of meeting or exceeding the target.
expectation_evidence: “7% planned return for 2026.”

description: Economic claims were favorable rather than roughly neutral, despite the preview noting that two consecutive favorable quarters raised the chance of mean reversion. The favorable experience included a $14 million current-period earnings benefit.
fact_evidence: Economic claims were “$31 million favorable to expectations,” with a “$14 million current-period earnings benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described an “implicit neutral bar” for claims and said two consecutive favorable quarters raised “the odds of mean reversion.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The cumulative pool of favorable economic claims not yet fully reflected in earnings was $375 million, $32 million above the $343 million cited in the preview.
fact_evidence: Cumulative economic claims favorability since 2023 totaled “$375 million not yet fully reflected in earnings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$343M cumulative unrecognized favorable economic claims” since 2023.

description: Buybacks did not accelerate: RGA repurchased $50 million of shares, the same amount as in Q1, despite the preview flagging acceleration toward the stated payout target as a key issue. The $111 million total shareholder return also included $61 million of dividends.
fact_evidence: RGA returned $111 million to shareholders, including “$50 million buybacks and $61 million dividends.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Buyback acceleration toward the 20–30% payout target” and noted that “$50M/quarter is light.”

description: RGA announced a 5.4% dividend increase for Q3, an increase not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of capital returns.
fact_evidence: RGA “announced a 5.4% dividend increase for Q3.”

description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $2.96, well above the preview’s $2.31 consensus, and FY26 adjusted EPS reached $4.57 versus the preview’s $3.75–$4.00 full-year guide. Record Q4 operating and EBITDA margins accompanied the earnings beat, largely because of favorable raw-material timing.
fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS reached a record $2.96” and “Q4 adjusted EBITDA and operating margins hit records of 46.8% and 41.5%”; FY26 adjusted EPS was $4.57. The margin results were “driven largely by ~$252 million favorable timing of raw material pricing versus cost.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $2.31”; the preview’s FY26 guide reconciliation showed “$3.75–4.00.”

description: FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.15–$5.15 has a $4.65 midpoint, below the roughly $5.40–$5.50 NTM EPS embedded in published estimates. The range also implies little growth from FY26’s $4.57 despite the very strong Q4 result.
fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance projects…adjusted EPS of $4.15–$5.15 (midpoint $4.65, roughly flat versus FY26's $4.57).”
expectation_evidence: “The 6.6x forward multiple implies NTM consensus EPS near $5.40–$5.50”; the preview also called FY27 guidance the “entire trade.”

description: The FY27 free-cash-flow outlook is weaker than the preview’s base case: management expects free cash flow of only about 20% of adjusted net income, rather than the preview’s 60–80% base-case conversion. The FY26 cash result itself was close to the preview’s expected roughly negative $90 million.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 free operating cash flow was negative $79 million” and “FY27 free cash flow expected at only ~20% of adjusted net income.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY27 FOCF conversion 60–80%”; it estimated FY26 FOCF at “roughly -$90M for the year.”

description: Management gave a concrete FY27 Q4 EBITDA margin reference point of only the mid-teens for a “clean” FY28 starting base, underscoring how far normalized margins could sit below Q4’s record 46.8%. The preview anticipated normalization in FY27 H2 and asked for a clean underlying margin, but did not forecast this specific mid-teens endpoint.
fact_evidence: “Management guided to a Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin in the mid-teens as a ‘clean’ jump-off point for modeling FY28, implying normalized earnings materially below the reported peak levels.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the timing benefit would be “normalizing in H2” and called for “a clean, ex-timing underlying margin for Q4.”

description: Higher debt is expected to add about $0.25 of EPS expense in FY27, an earnings headwind the preview did not identify in its guidance framework.
fact_evidence: “The company expects a ~$0.25 EPS headwind from higher interest expense in FY27 due to increased debt.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The energy outlook improved sharply: Q4 energy sales surged, and the FY27 U.S. land-rig outlook shifted from a decline to growth. The preview had noted strong prior-quarter energy growth but did not anticipate this upward revision to the rig outlook.
fact_evidence: “The energy end market surged in Q4 (up 101% overall, +135% in infrastructure), and U.S. land rig count outlook was revised upward from a mid-single-digit decline to high-single-digit growth for FY27.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q3 “Energy +28%” and flagged whether volume growth was durable, but did not give a more positive FY27 rig-count outlook.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The end of Bolivia’s preferential exchange program created an additional currency headwind that was not flagged in the preview.
fact_evidence: “A 23% Bolivia FX headwind after the government ended its preferential exchange program.”

description: Inspire’s Q2 revenue declined 7.6% year over year, a smaller drop than the preview’s expected 9%–11% decline and above its $194.72 million consensus estimate. Revenue was $200.6 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 7.6% year-over-year to $200.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 revenue was guided to a “9%–11% year-over-year decline” and cited consensus revenue of “$194.72 million.”

description: The company raised the lower end of its 2026 revenue outlook by $10 million while keeping the upper end unchanged, to $835 million–$875 million from $825 million–$875 million. The preview had flagged the existing range as the full-year outlook to watch.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was revised to $835 million-$875 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year revenue guidance of “$825M–$875M.”

description: Inspire raised its adjusted profitability outlook: adjusted operating margin is now 4%–6% rather than 2%–4%, and adjusted diluted EPS is $1.05–$1.45 rather than $0.75–$1.25.
fact_evidence: The company “narrowed profitability guidance to adjusted operating margin of 4-6%” and “adjusted diluted EPS of $1.05-$1.45.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave full-year adjusted operating margin guidance of “2%–4%” and adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$0.75–$1.25.”

description: At the same time, the GAAP diluted EPS outlook was cut below the preview’s expected range and now includes a loss: the range moved from $0.07–$0.62 to -$0.42–$0.17.
fact_evidence: The company guided diluted EPS to “-$0.42 to $0.17.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed GAAP diluted EPS guidance of “$0.07–$0.62.”
