description: Q3 revenue guidance was high-single-digit growth, above the preview’s expectation of mid-single-digit-or-better growth and above management’s historic mid-single-digit guidance.
fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 to high single-digit revenue growth—above its historic mid-single-digit guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side wanted “mid-single-digit-or-better revenue growth.”

description: Alongside the stronger Q3 revenue outlook, management expected gross margin at the low end of the 29.5–30.5% range. That is a cautious margin signal against a preview that emphasized holding margin within the range and warned that margin trajectory was central to the debate.
fact_evidence: Q3 gross margin was “expected at the low end of the 29.5%-30.5% range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called gross margin versus “the 29.5–30.5% guide” the key debate and described the base case as “GM ~30%.”

description: Perigold and the specialty brands substantially outgrew the core mass-market business, a brand-level growth result the preview did not set expectations for. Perigold’s scale and customer spending were also disclosed, adding evidence of a sizable higher-end business.
fact_evidence: “Specialty retail brands grew nearly 20% and Perigold grew more than 35% in Q2, both meaningfully outpacing the core mass Wayfair business”; Perigold had “just over $400 million in annual sales” and “near 400,000” active customers.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The 2026 store opening count was three, below the preview’s expectation of more than three, but Wayfair also disclosed five leases for 2027 and favorable store economics: over half of store customers were new, with supplier-owned inventory keeping capital needs low.
fact_evidence: “3 large-format stores opening in 2026 and 5 leases signed for 2027”; “over 50% of store customers are new to the file” and “inventory is supplier-owned, keeping combined CapEx in the low single-digit percentage of revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “more than 3” stores in 2026 and said “Any store-level economics would be new information.”

description: Rather than further convertible repurchases, Wayfair issued a $400 million high-yield note to redeem 2028 converts. The transaction moves the company away from convertible debt, but the preview had specifically identified additional convert repurchases as a possible catalyst; the Fitch upgrade and lower stock-based compensation were additional favorable disclosures.
fact_evidence: “The company completed its shift away from convertible debt by issuing a $400 million high-yield note to redeem 2028 converts”; it “earned a 2-notch Fitch upgrade” and cut trailing-12-month stock-based compensation “~40% versus two years ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “further convertible repurchases (~$300M principal retired in Q1)” as a narrative wildcard.

description: North and Central America operating earnings declined 2.4%, rather than growing around 8% as the preview’s $225 million estimate implied. The reported low-single-digit volume growth did not prevent Millersburg start-up costs and capacity constraints from weighing on the segment.
fact_evidence: “North and Central America segment operating earnings declined 2.4% year-over-year,” as “roughly $5 million in Millersburg start-up costs and capacity constraints offset low-single-digit volume growth.”
expectation_evidence: “NCA comparable op. earnings $225M” versus “$208M” a year earlier; the preview said consensus implied “+8%.”

description: EMEA operating earnings rose just 6.6%, well short of the preview’s $161.2 million estimate, which implied roughly 25% growth from the cited $129 million prior-year base. Benepack’s contribution was largely offset by the divested Saudi Arabian business.
fact_evidence: “EMEA volumes grew mid-single digits with segment operating earnings up 6.6%, though Benepack contributions were largely offset by the divested Saudi Arabian business.”
expectation_evidence: “EMEA comparable op. earnings $161.2M” versus “$129M” a year earlier; the preview’s dollar figures imply roughly 25% growth.

description: South America operating earnings surged 64%, far above the preview’s $53 million estimate versus $51 million a year earlier, which implied only about 4% growth. World Cup-driven customer demand helped produce the outsized result against a flattish regional market.
fact_evidence: “South America was the standout region with mid-teens volume growth and a 64% surge in segment operating earnings, aided by World Cup-driven customer demand against a flattish regional market.”
expectation_evidence: “S. America comparable op. earnings $53M” versus “$51M” a year earlier, or “+4%.”

description: Comparable EPS growth was 14.4%, above the roughly 10% growth implied by the $0.99 consensus estimate against the $0.90 year-ago result. The call did not provide the Q2 EPS dollar amount, so the precise beat versus consensus cannot be established from these facts.
fact_evidence: “Comparable diluted EPS grew 14.4% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Comparable diluted EPS” consensus was “$0.99” versus “$0.90” a year earlier, implying “+10%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Global can-volume growth was 4.3%, ahead of the preview’s 3%-or-better threshold for validating the full-year build. Growth across all three regions also extended the volume-growth streak to six consecutive quarters.
fact_evidence: “Global shipped beverage can volumes increased 4.3% year-over-year in Q2 2026 with growth across all three regions, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of volume growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs +3% or better to validate the full-year build.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: South American volume growth reached the mid-teens, below the preview’s estimate of about 20.4% and its expectation of a roughly 20% Q2 snapback. The segment still delivered strong growth, but the recovery was less pronounced than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “South America” had “mid-teens volume growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated South America volume growth at “+20.4%” and said the “South America” segment was expected to deliver “the +20% snapback.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: North and Central America volume growth was low-single-digit, better than the preview’s 0.8% estimate, even though segment earnings fell. This was a modest volume upside in a region the preview described as capacity-constrained.
fact_evidence: Capacity constraints “offset low-single-digit volume growth” in North and Central America.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated NCA volume growth at “+0.8%.”

description: Ball said it expected to return about $800 million to shareholders in 2026, including at least $600 million of buybacks, but had completed only about $100 million of repurchases in the first half. That is well below the preview’s roughly $150 million-per-quarter pace and leaves a substantial amount to execute in the second half.
fact_evidence: “Ball plans to return approximately $800 million to shareholders in 2026, including at least $600 million in buybacks and roughly $200 million in dividends, with only ~$100 million of repurchases completed in the first half.”
expectation_evidence: “≥$600M repurchase / $800M total returns implies roughly $150M/quarter of buyback”; the preview said an H1 run rate below that “raises questions about capital deployment priorities.”

description: Millersburg start-up costs are expected to total about $35 million for 2026, with roughly $30 million in the second half. The preview flagged the plant ramp and FCF trajectory, but did not anticipate this specific expense burden or its concentration in the back half.
fact_evidence: “Full-year Millersburg start-up costs are expected to total approximately $35 million, with roughly $30 million landing in the second half and no start-up costs anticipated in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the Millersburg, Oregon plant ramps in 2H26” and highlighted “FCF and capex commentary against >$900M / capex ≈ D&A” as a key watchpoint, but gave no start-up-cost estimate.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call placed Millersburg’s full ramp and delivery of full value in 2027, later than the preview’s description of the plant ramping in the second half of 2026. Commercial production had begun, but the full contribution was not expected until the following year.
fact_evidence: “The Millersburg, Oregon plant began producing commercial cans last month” and is “expected to reach full ramp and deliver full value in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the Millersburg, Oregon plant ramps in 2H26.”

description: The expected South American full-year volume outlook was at the low end of the 4%-6% range, rather than a stronger position within the range suggested by the preview’s emphasis on the recovery. This is a cautious forward signal alongside the weaker-than-expected Q2 volume recovery.
fact_evidence: Management expected South America to be “at the low ends of their respective 1%-3% and 4%-6% ranges.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said South America was guided to “4–6% with April volumes already running +20%” and identified the Q2 “+20% snapback” as an important test.

description: Interest expense guidance was around $310 million, below the preview’s approximately $320 million expectation. This is a modest favorable change to the full-year outlook.
fact_evidence: Ball reaffirmed “interest expense around $310 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the FY2026 guidance as “interest expense ~$320M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Broadridge finished FY26 closed sales at $305 million, above the preview’s $240–290 million guide, with a record $158 million in Q4. The $470 million backlog and year-end pipeline growth also made the sales result stronger than a simple recovery to the expected range.
fact_evidence: “Q4 closed sales hit a record $158 million, lifting full-year closed sales to $305 million and the closed sales backlog to $470 million (up $40 million year-over-year)”; “year-end sales pipeline was up more than one-third from a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 closed sales landing inside $240–290M”; the preview also said Q4 closed sales of “$93–143M” were implied by the guide.

description: FY27 recurring revenue guidance starts at 6%, below the preview’s 7% mental anchor, although the 6%–8% range includes 7% and matches the preview’s stated base-case range. The low end therefore leaves more room for growth below the level the preview said investors needed to defend the compounder narrative.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 guidance calls for 6%-8% recurring revenue growth.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy side needs ≥7% recurring”; the preview also said “Anything with a 5- or 6-handle on recurring validates the bear case,” while its base case anticipated “FY27 recurring 6–8% cc.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The year-end sales mix showed strong adoption of platform-enabled and next-generation products: they rose more than 50% and made up nearly 40% of closed sales. The preview anticipated pipeline conversion as an important test, but did not forecast this degree of contribution from newer products.
fact_evidence: “Platform-enabled and next-generation products [were] rising over 50% and accounting for nearly 40% of closed sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 is the proof quarter” for the claim that larger, complex deals were timing rather than demand weakness; the preview called for evidence the pipeline was converting.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Broadridge gave concrete, rapidly growing tokenized-repo activity rather than only the general tokenization proof points the preview was looking for: DLR processed $360 billion in daily volume in June, three times May’s level, with nearly 20 institutions onboarding and further growth expected.
fact_evidence: “The DLR tokenized repo platform processed $360 billion in daily volume in June (3x the prior May), with nearly 20 institutions onboarding and management guiding to 50% further growth by December.”
expectation_evidence: “Explicit management framing on AI and tokenization” was a key watch item; “tokenization expanding the opportunity. Reiteration with proof points matters more than any EPS line.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported position-growth metrics strengthened versus the Q3 figures highlighted in the preview: equity position growth reached 17% (14% revenue-generating) versus the prior 11% equity growth, and fund growth was 7% versus 6%. That provides a stronger near-term data point against the disintermediation concern.
fact_evidence: “Q4 equity position growth was 17% with 14% revenue-generating position growth, while fund positions grew 7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q3 “equity record growth +11%, fund/ETF positions +6%” and said these were “the hard-data rebuttal to disintermediation fears; any crack here is disproportionately damaging.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: A proposed SEC e-delivery rule introduced a new medium-term trade-off not raised in the preview: management expects no FY27 impact, but sees a possible modest recurring-revenue headwind over two to three years, partly offset by new solutions, alongside a reported-margin benefit from lower low-margin distribution revenue.
fact_evidence: “The SEC's proposed e-delivery rule is expected to have no impact in fiscal '27 but may create a modest recurring revenue headwind over 2-3 years (offset by new solutions) while boosting reported margins by reducing low-margin distribution revenues.”

description: Broadridge disclosed $25 million of expected AI-driven productivity gains in FY27, presenting AI as a source of operating efficiency as well as a risk discussed in the preview. Because the company plans to reinvest the gains in growth initiatives, this is not a direct increase to expected earnings.
fact_evidence: “The company embedded $25 million in expected AI-driven productivity gains in fiscal '27, primarily in the technology organization, which it plans to reinvest to fund growth initiatives.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “AI-disintermediation” as a longer-dated fear and called for explicit management framing on AI; it did not anticipate quantified productivity gains.

description: Broadridge returned more than $9 per share in FY26, including record buybacks and a 12% dividend increase, and expanded its buyback authorization to $1.5 billion. The preview identified an enlarged authorization as a possible confidence signal, but did not specify this scale of total returns or the dividend increase.
fact_evidence: “Broadridge returned over $9 per share to shareholders in fiscal '26 via a record $600 million in buybacks and $443 million in dividends, and raised the dividend 12% to $4.36 while increasing buyback authorization to $1.5 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “An enlarged repurchase authorization at these levels would be a credible confidence signal.”

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $275–$295 million, from $315–$335 million, despite the preview focusing on whether the company would avoid another cut. The new outlook implies an adjusted EBITDA margin of only about 12%.
fact_evidence: “adjusted EBITDA is now guided to $275-$295 million with a margin of only about 12%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance hold or cut again — the release explicitly includes an updated FY2026 outlook; a third cut this fiscal year would confirm the bear case.” The preview also cited the then-current $315–$335 million guide.

description: Q3 adjusted gross margin fell to 27.7% from 35.1% a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA margins were below guidance. The preview flagged the margin trajectory as a key debate, but the reported shortfall and the 180-basis-point inventory charge added to the cost pressure.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin collapsed to 27.7% from 35.1% a year ago,” driven by “protein and freight inflation, tariffs, and an excess bottled shake inventory charge that alone was a 180 basis point headwind”; adjusted EBITDA margins “came in below guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin trajectory — whether the Q2 collapse (27.0%) was the trough; tariff, whey-protein and freight cost commentary.”

description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be only about 10%, with promotions, costs ahead of pricing, and bottle inventory weighing on results. The preview discussed margin pressure generally but did not indicate a margin outlook this weak for Q4.
fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be only about 10%,” reflecting “heavy seasonal promotions, commodity/freight inflation ahead of pricing, and a ~100 bp bottle-inventory headwind.”

description: The company raised its full-year net sales outlook to $2.335–$2.375 billion, or 1–3% growth, from $2.325–$2.365 billion, or flat-to-2% growth. That was better than the preview’s concern that the company might cut guidance again.
fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales guidance was raised to $2.335-$2.375 billion (1-3% growth) from prior flat-to-2%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance hold or cut again” and “a third cut this fiscal year would confirm the bear case.”

description: Q3 net sales grew 4% year over year, above the preview’s 1.6% growth consensus. Both Premier Protein and Dymatize also exceeded expectations.
fact_evidence: “Q3 net sales rose 4% year-over-year, with both Premier Protein and Dymatize exceeding expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $556.0M … +1.6% YoY.”

description: Excess bottled-shake inventory created a substantial, newly disclosed cost and required further discounting: the full-year outlook includes $28 million of unfavorable inventory impacts, with additional Q4 promotional markdowns. The preview flagged retailer inventory and destocking risk, but not this specific excess bottle inventory and associated charges.
fact_evidence: “The full-year outlook includes $28 million of unfavorable inventory-related impacts ($21 million already recorded)”; Premier required a “$10 million reserve (2% of total inventory) plus additional Q4 promotional markdowns.”
expectation_evidence: “Retailer inventory/weeks-of-supply — destocking triggered the 2025 downdrafts and is central to the pending securities class action.”

description: Dymatize sales surged 27%, including 6% volume growth and 21% favorable price/mix, and exceeded expectations. That is a sharp recovery from the 1.9% sales decline reported for Q2, although the company cautioned that Q4 faces a tough comparison.
fact_evidence: “Dymatize net sales surged 27% on 6% volume growth and 21% favorable price/mix from earlier inflation-driven price increases, though it faces a tough Q4 comparison.”
expectation_evidence: “Dymatize exceeding expectations.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company announced a double-digit price increase on Premier shakes and further powder pricing for Q1 FY2027, but expects volume elasticity to be slightly greater than 1—suggesting volume pressure could outweigh the price increase. The preview highlighted the tension between pricing, promotions, and consumer sensitivity but did not anticipate this specific price action or elasticity estimate.
fact_evidence: “A double-digit price increase on Premier shakes plus additional powder pricing effective Q1 fiscal 2027,” with “expected volume elasticity slightly greater than 1.”
expectation_evidence: “Price/mix vs. volume — can promotion be dialed back without losing Premier Protein shelf space” and the preview cited “price-sensitive consumers.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A sizable Q4 legal settlement payment is expected to push net leverage from 3.2x at quarter-end to approximately 4x by fiscal year-end. The preview mentioned a pending securities class action but did not anticipate a settlement payment or this leverage increase.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage stood at 3.2x at quarter-end but is expected to rise to approximately 4x by fiscal year-end due to a sizable legal settlement payment in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “Retailer inventory/weeks-of-supply — destocking triggered the 2025 downdrafts and is central to the pending securities class action.”

description: A June organizational realignment incurred a $5 million charge but is expected to produce $10–$12 million in annualized operating expense savings, mostly in fiscal 2027. The preview identified a possible new-CEO strategic reset but did not forecast this specific restructuring charge or savings plan.
fact_evidence: “A June organizational realignment incurred a $5 million charge and is expected to generate $10-$12 million in annualized operating expense savings, mostly realized in fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “New CEO's strategic reset — Axelrod … may rebase expectations.”

description: Revenue was expected at $19.31 billion, with even the preview’s bull case set at $19.8 billion or more; Caterpillar reported a record $20.5 billion, its first quarter above $20 billion. That is a substantially stronger top-line result than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales and revenues reached a record $20.5 billion, up 24% year-over-year,” and this was “the first time Caterpillar surpassed $20 billion in a single quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $19.31B”; the bull scenario was “Revenue | ≥$19.8B.”

description: Adjusted EPS was expected at $6.25, with the preview’s inferred buy-side bar at $6.45–$6.60 and its bull case at $6.75 or more. The reported $8.17 was well above all of those benchmarks.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted profit per share rose 73% to $8.17, exceeding company expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: $6.25”; the preview described the functional buy-side bar as “$6.45–$6.60 EPS” and the bull case as “≥$6.75.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog was expected to grow by only $1–3 billion in the base case, while the preview’s bull case called for $5 billion or more of sequential growth. Instead, backlog rose $9 billion to a record $72 billion, with contributions from all three primary segments.
fact_evidence: “Backlog grew sequentially by $9 billion to a record $72 billion,” up “approximately 92% versus Q2 last year,” with “all three primary segments contributing.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “backlog $64–66B (+$1–3B q/q),” while the bull case anticipated “Backlog ≥$67–68B (+$5B q/q).”

description: The consolidated adjusted operating margin was expected to be about 19.1%; the reported 21.9% was materially higher. The result included $392 million of IEEPA tariff recoveries, an important contributor the preview had not identified.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating profit margin was 21.9%, a 430 basis point increase over the prior year, boosted by $392 million in IEEPA tariff recoveries.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin | ~19.1% | 17.6% | +150bps.”

description: The full-year sales-growth outlook was raised from low double-digit growth to mid- to high-teens growth, a larger upgrade than the preview’s example of a raise to low-teens growth.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 sales and revenues growth outlook to mid- to high-teens, up from prior guidance, driven by demand across all three primary segments.”
expectation_evidence: The standing guide was “low double-digit” sales growth; the preview said an explicit raise “to ‘low-teens’ growth” would be a bull trigger.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Power-generation sales to users surged 72% on data-center demand, far stronger than the preview’s expectation that growth would hold around 35–40%. This is a pronounced acceleration in the demand metric the preview identified as central to the Power & Energy outlook.
fact_evidence: “Sales to users in power generation surged 72% on data center demand.”
expectation_evidence: The bull scenario expected “power gen still +35–40%”; the preview also said Q1 power-generation sales were “+41% y/y” and that sustaining that growth rate mattered.

description: Construction Industries sales growth substantially exceeded the preview’s directional estimate, and its reported margin was also above the displayed estimate. The $400 million dealer-inventory increase is a qualification, but sales to users grew for a sixth consecutive quarter, so the result was not just dealer restocking.
fact_evidence: “Construction Industries sales jumped 35% to $8.3 billion with a 23.3% margin, aided by a $400 million dealer inventory increase and sixth consecutive quarter of sales-to-users growth.”
expectation_evidence: The segment table showed Construction Industries sales of “$7.24B,” “+18.0%,” and an operating-margin estimate of “22.4%.” The preview also said to watch whether CI was being “flattered by dealer restocking versus end-user demand.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Power & Energy orders were being taken as far out as 2030, extending beyond the preview’s reference to orders well into 2028 and its request for quantified forward-order visibility. That provides stronger evidence of demand duration than the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: Caterpillar was “taking Power and Energy orders as far out as 2030.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 orders were “well into 2028” and called for “Explicit 2027 order commentary / data-center regulatory response,” including quantified new power-generation bookings.

description: Caterpillar is restarting production of its 10-megawatt gas reciprocating-engine platform, adding about 1.5 gigawatts of capacity with shipments due to begin in Q4. The preview discussed capacity investment generally but did not anticipate this specific restart or near-term shipment timing.
fact_evidence: “The company is restarting production of its 10-megawatt gas reciprocating engine platform, bringing about 1.5 gigawatts of capacity online with shipments beginning in Q4.”

description: Full-year tariff costs were guided to the low end of the preview’s $2.2–$2.4 billion range. This is a favorable reduction in expected costs, although the facts do not provide the actual Q2 tariff cost needed to compare with the preview’s roughly $700 million quarterly guide.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 tariff costs are now expected to be around $2.2 billion (low end of the prior range), while Q3 tariff costs are estimated at roughly $600 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “the FY $2.2–$2.4B range” and said “Another trim is a clean, high-quality margin beat.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company reported record MP&E free cash flow of $5.1 billion and returned $2.2 billion to shareholders, including an 8% dividend increase. The preview flagged cash flow and capacity spending as issues to watch but gave no Q2 cash-flow or shareholder-return expectation.
fact_evidence: “Caterpillar generated record MP&E free cash flow of $5.1 billion and returned $2.2 billion to shareholders via $1.5 billion buybacks and dividends, including an 8% dividend increase.”

description: Q2 revenue was $93.3 million, about $4.8 million below the preview’s $98.1 million consensus. That was a miss even though revenue grew 1% year over year, rather than showing the roughly 6% reported decline implied by the preview.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew just 1% year-over-year to $93.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$98.1M … vs. $104.6M in Q2 2025 — an implied ~6% reported decline.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.08, below the preview’s $0.10 consensus. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was also lower than the preview’s cited range, at $0.31–$0.36 rather than $0.35–$0.41.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS held flat at $0.08; full-year adjusted diluted EPS is guided to $0.31-$0.36.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.10”; FY2026 guidance was “$0.35–0.41.”

description: The company reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance at $367–$382 million, below the preview’s cited $395–$405 million range. The preview expected confirmation of that range, although it also noted a 0–4% growth target excluding the divested business.
fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of 0% to 4% growth ($367 million to $382 million).”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … revenue $395–405M”; the preview also asked whether “the $395–405M revenue … ranges are reiterated.”

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to 29%–31%, rather than holding at the preview’s cited 30%–32% range. Management attributed the reduction to divestiture-related stranded costs, not weaker underlying performance.
fact_evidence: “Full-year EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to 29%-31% from the prior 30%-32%, attributed to divestiture-related stranded costs rather than underlying performance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin 30–32%”; the preview asked whether the range would be reiterated.

description: Bookings momentum was stronger than the preview’s cautious setup suggested: normalized trailing-12-month bookings growth accelerated to 7% exiting the first half, from 0.8% at the end of 2025, and pipeline grew 27% year over year. The preview had highlighted weak Q1 bookings and sought evidence of a second-half bookings-to-revenue recovery.
fact_evidence: “Normalized for the Chemaxon acquisition, trailing 12-month bookings growth accelerated to 7% exiting the first half, up sharply from 0.8% exiting 2025, and sales pipeline grew 27% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Total bookings fell 2%” in Q1 and said to watch for “second-half bookings-to-revenue conversion commentary.”

description: The company disclosed a May workforce reduction of about 5% and said combined operational actions should produce roughly $13 million of run-rate savings, more than the previously identified plan. The preview did not flag this expanded savings program.
fact_evidence: “A May reduction in force cut approximately 5% of the global workforce, and combined operational actions are expected to yield roughly $13 million in run-rate savings, an increase over the prior identified plan.”

description: Alongside completing a $100 million buyback, the Board authorized a new $50 million repurchase program, a capital-allocation action the preview did not discuss.
fact_evidence: “The company completed a $100 million buyback (including $17.4 million repurchased in Q2), and the Board authorized a new $50 million share repurchase program.”
