description: The preview identified a pending Breakthrough Therapy request as a potential catalyst, including a grant in its bull case. The FDA declined BTD for the cVM program based on the initial 12-week data package, although management said this does not change the development path.
fact_evidence: “The FDA declined to grant Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the cutaneous venous malformation (cVM) program based on the initial 12-week data package, though management says this does not alter the development path.”
expectation_evidence: “Phase 3 start guided 2H26 with a Breakthrough Therapy request pending”; the bull case included “TOIVA Ph3 dosing + BTD granted for CVM.”

description: The preview framed FY26 cash burn at about $80 million and warned that a higher burn could reopen financing concerns. Management raised planned 2026 cash spend to approximately $85–95 million, citing expanded commercial and medical affairs investment, while saying the existing cash supports operations through potential approval and a standalone launch.
fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 cash spend guidance to approximately $85-95 million due to expanded commercial and medical affairs investments”; the company said its cash funds operations “through potential approval and a standalone launch.”
expectation_evidence: “Prior framing was ~$80M FY26 burn”; the preview said burn above that level could imply a 2027 equity raise.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview focused on the more than 30,000 diagnosed U.S. MLM patients and the MLM opportunity. Management described a potential expansion of QTORIN rapamycin’s addressable U.S. population to more than 300,000 across multiple mTOR-driven indications, with cVM approval targeted for 2029 and angiokeratomas for 2031.
fact_evidence: “The pipeline-in-a-product strategy could expand QTORIN rapamycin's addressable U.S. population from over 30,000 MLM patients to over 300,000 across multiple mTOR-driven indications,” with cVM targeted for 2029 and angiokeratomas for 2031.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “>30,000 diagnosed U.S. mLM patients” and a “$1B+ peak U.S. sales” claim, and discussed pipeline expansion without quantifying a population above 300,000.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview flagged pricing and payer framing as items to watch but gave no specific favorable expectation. Management cited orphan-drug pricing of $100,000–$200,000 per patient per year for MLM and payer research indicating strong coverage support with no expected step-throughs of unapproved therapies.
fact_evidence: “Orphan drug pricing of $100,000-$200,000 per patient per year for MLM,” with “strong coverage support and no expected step-throughs of unapproved therapies.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for: ... payer/pricing framing.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview discussed commercial hiring and patient identification but did not report physician-demand survey findings. Management said more than 80% of surveyed physicians would consider QTORIN as first-line therapy across all four indications, and 96% would incorporate it for angiokeratomas.
fact_evidence: “More than 80% of surveyed physicians said they would consider the QTORIN candidate as first-line therapy across all four indications, and 96% said they would incorporate QTORIN rapamycin into their practice for angiokeratomas.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “patient-identification progress” and commercial buildout, but stated no expectation for physician survey results.

description: The preview anticipated DSAP pitavastatin entering Phase II, but did not mention a third product candidate. Management also said the company expects to announce a third product candidate later this year, adding a pipeline disclosure beyond the preview’s specific expectations.
fact_evidence: “Expects to announce a fourth indication (QTORIN pitavastatin for DSAP entering Phase II in Q4 2026) and a third product candidate later this year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “QTORIN pitavastatin (DSAP) Ph2 initiation 2H26” and said two new indications were promised for 2H26; it did not mention a third product candidate.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management introduced a plan to pursue FDA Platform Designation after the first approval to expedite future programs, a regulatory strategy not discussed in the preview. The potential benefit is prospective rather than a near-term change to the stated timelines.
fact_evidence: “Plans to pursue FDA Platform Designation after its first approval to expedite future programs.”

description: Enpro raised its 2026 outlook further than the preview’s bull case: sales growth is now 14%-16%, adjusted EBITDA $330-$340 million, and adjusted EPS $9.30-$9.80. The preview’s bull case contemplated roughly $325-$338 million of EBITDA and $9.20-$9.70 of EPS, while its current baseline guidance was lower still.
fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 guidance,” with total sales growth of 14%-16% (up from 10%-14%), adjusted EBITDA of $330-$340 million (up from $315-$330 million), and adjusted diluted EPS of $9.30-$9.80 (up from $8.85-$9.50).
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario expected a raise to “~$9.20–9.70 EPS / $325–338M EBITDA”; its current guidance was 10%-14% sales growth, $315-$330 million EBITDA, and $8.85-$9.50 EPS.

description: Q2 sales were well above both published consensus and the preview’s higher buy-side estimate: $338.8 million versus consensus of about $323 million and a suggested buy-side bar near $328 million. The 17.6% reported growth also exceeded the preview’s roughly 12% consensus growth expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales rose 17.6% year-over-year to $338.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$322.9M – $323.7M”; the preview said the buy-side bar sat closer to “~$328M revenue.”

description: Q2 adjusted EPS substantially exceeded expectations, reaching $2.50 versus $2.30 consensus and even above the preview’s estimated $2.35-$2.40 buy-side bar.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS reached $2.50 in Q2, up 23.2% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus of “$2.30” and estimated a buy-side bar of “$2.35–2.40 EPS.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA also beat the preview’s derived estimate, and the margin was slightly above its projected range: $86.9 million versus roughly $80-$82 million expected, at 25.6% versus a derived 24.9%-25.4%.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “$86.9 million” and the margin was “25.6%,” up 90 basis points.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s derived estimates were “~$80–82M” of adjusted EBITDA and a “~24.9% – 25.4%” adjusted EBITDA margin.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Enpro recorded an unanticipated roughly $60 million environmental reserve for legacy Arizona uranium mines. The long delay before meaningful cash outflows limits the near-term cash impact, but the reserve build is a sizeable unexpected charge and long-duration remediation obligation.
fact_evidence: The company recorded a “roughly $60 million environmental reserve build” tied to legacy uranium mines in Arizona; no meaningful cash outflows are expected for about 3 years and remediation could span up to 10 years.

description: The company raised 2026 capital expenditure expectations from about $50 million to $60-$65 million, pulling AST cleaning-capacity investments forward. The preview discussed the AST ramp but did not anticipate this higher spending plan.
fact_evidence: “Raised 2026 capital expenditure expectations to $60-$65 million (up from ~$50 million),” pulling forward AST cleaning capacity investments in Arizona, Milpitas, California, and Taiwan.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage came down to 1.6x, below the preview’s cited 1.9x level, after $80 million of revolving debt repayment. That is better deleveraging than the preview’s starting point implied.
fact_evidence: Enpro “reduced net leverage to 1.6x” after repaying “$80 million in revolving debt” and generated “over $60 million in year-to-date free cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “net leverage (1.9x)” as a metric to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said AST visibility now extends through 2027, adding a longer-dated visibility signal beyond the preview’s focus on the near-term H2 ramp and whether management would quantify orders or backlog. The preview did not anticipate visibility extending that far.
fact_evidence: Management said “visibility [is] now extending through 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview focused on the H2 ramp and said to watch “whether management quantifies backlog/order growth again.”

description: Revenue was $130 million, about 6% above the preview’s $122.1 million consensus estimate and above its $118–125 million base-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $130 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $122.1M”; the base case projected “Revenue $118–125M.”

description: The company lifted the low end of both FY26 guidance ranges: GOV’s floor rose from $2.2 billion to $2.3 billion, and adjusted EBITDA’s floor rose from $30 million to $34 million. The upper ends were unchanged.
fact_evidence: “The company raised or set full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to Marketplace GOV of $2.3 billion to $2.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $34 million to $40 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 Marketplace GOV $2.2–2.6B, Adj. EBITDA $30–40M — reaffirmed at Q1.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: World Cup volume was exceptionally concentrated: the call compared its transaction volume with the entire Taylor Swift Eras Tour, while noting that the World Cup volume came in one quarter. The preview anticipated a World Cup boost but warned that falling resale prices could mean weak sell-through.
fact_evidence: “The World Cup generated transaction volume comparable to the entire Taylor Swift Eras Tour but concentrated in a single quarter rather than spread across two years”; it also drove “a mid-teens percentage of Q2 GOV.”
expectation_evidence: “The FIFA World Cup ... falls across Q2 and Q3”; the preview asked “how much GOV came from World Cup” and cautioned that pricing was “in free fall” with “possibly weak sell-through.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: World Cup orders had a greater than 99.7% successful fulfillment rate, a customer-experience result the preview did not identify as an expected outcome or key metric.
fact_evidence: “Vivid Seats maintained a greater than 99.7% successful fulfillment rate for World Cup orders,” contrasting its experience with “publicized fulfillment problems at a competitor.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Outside the World Cup, industry volumes were softer, with theater weakness attributed to rising competition and soft Las Vegas leisure travel among lower-end consumers. The preview discussed competitive pressure generally but did not flag these specific demand headwinds.
fact_evidence: “Industry volumes outside the World Cup were softer in Q2, with theater weakness driven by rising competitive intensity and soft Las Vegas leisure travel among lower-end consumers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a “crowded” competitive set and said “other competitors remain aggressive,” but did not identify theater and lower-end Las Vegas travel as specific Q2 pressures.

description: The revolving credit facility was renewed with maturity extended through August 2029, a concrete financing extension not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of stalled recapitalization talks and ongoing lender negotiations.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $137 million in cash and renewed its revolving credit facility with an extended maturity through August 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said talks with the ad hoc group “ended” and that “negotiations with other lenders continue”; it focused on possible recapitalization terms rather than a revolver renewal and maturity extension.

description: IDEXX reported Q2 EPS of $4.27 versus the preview’s $3.95 consensus, a substantial beat. The reported EPS included $0.14 per share from share-based compensation activity and $0.06 from favorable FX, so those factors account for part of the gap.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS reached $4.27” and included “a $0.14 per share benefit from share-based compensation activity and $0.06 from favorable foreign exchange.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS | $3.95” consensus; the preview also cautions to “Confirm which basis the $3.95 consensus is struck on before calling a beat or miss.”

description: Revenue growth was approximately 10% reported, above the roughly 8.3% growth implied by the preview’s $1.20B consensus against Q2’25 revenue. That is a meaningful, though not enormous, beat against the stated bar.
fact_evidence: “Revenue grew approximately 10% as reported and 9% organically.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.20B” consensus versus “$1,109M” in Q2’25, with “Implied Y/Y” growth of “+8.3%.”

description: CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue grew more than 10% organically, ahead of the roughly 9% guide-implied pace and the preview’s 9.5–10% buy-side whisper. The growth premium over declining clinical visits also showed the utilization-and-price offset remained strong.
fact_evidence: “Over 10% organic growth in CAG Diagnostics recurring revenues” and an “approximately 1,100 basis point CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growth premium over clinical visits.”
expectation_evidence: “Guide implies ~9% for the balance of the year. Buy-side whisper is ~9.5–10%”; the preview called “10%+” the “bull trigger.”

description: The full-year outlook moved up, especially for EPS: the EPS midpoint increased by $0.14, while the revenue midpoint rose only about $5M and the range remained broad. The EPS raise was stronger than the preview’s base case of a largely intact midpoint, although smaller than its bull-case raise.
fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 EPS outlook to $14.69-$14.94,” an “increase of $0.14 at midpoint,” and “lifted revenue guidance to $4,700M-$4,745M.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “raise, narrow-to-midpoint, or reaffirm” was in play and its base case expected the “midpoint largely intact”; its bull case projected EPS of “~$14.70–15.05” and revenue of “~$4,720–4,780M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Premium placements accelerated inVue Dx placements to 1,602 in Q2, bringing first-half placements to 2,700 and keeping the 5,500 full-year goal on pace. That addressed the preview’s concern that Q1’s 1,099 placements would require visible acceleration.
fact_evidence: “Premium instrument placements totaled 5,265 units including 1,602 inVue Dx analyzers,” with “2,700 placed in the first half” and the company “on pace for its full-year goal of 5,500.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1’s “1,099” inVue Dx placements “requires visible acceleration” toward the “5,500 inVue Dx FY target.”

description: Comparable operating margin expanded 110 basis points and gross margin reached 64%, despite the preview’s warning that the prior-year Q2 margin was a tough comparison and that H2 needed to carry the annual margin target. Favorable product costs and easing inflation helped deliver the expansion.
fact_evidence: “Comparable operating margin expanded 110 basis points with gross margins reaching 64%, up ~120 basis points, aided by favorable product costs and eased inflationary pressures.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 was 31.8% reported … vs. 32.1–32.5% FY guide, so H2 must carry the load” and that “Q2’25 ran ~33.6%, a tough comp.”

description: Global Reference Lab revenue grew more than 10% organically—the first double-digit growth since early 2023—and Cancer Dx had passed 10,000 clinics, with some orders coming from competitive-lab practices. The preview did not set a specific Reference Lab or Cancer Dx expectation, so this was an unanticipated positive development in the material provided.
fact_evidence: “Global Reference Lab revenues rose over 10% organically, the first double-digit growth since early 2023,” with IDEXX Cancer Dx “surpassing 10,000 global clinics” and “20% of its orders coming from competitive-lab practices.”

description: XMTR raised its FY2026 revenue growth outlook to 33%-34%, above the preview’s expected raise to at least 30% and even above its 31%-33% bull scenario. This was a stronger full-year outlook than the preview’s stated bar.
fact_evidence: The company raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 33%-34% from prior 27%-28%.
expectation_evidence: “A raise to ≥30% growth” was what the long side needed; the bull scenario called for “31–33%.”

description: Marketplace gross margin came in below the preview’s 36%-37% estimate and its stated 36%+ threshold. At 34.7%, it was flat sequentially rather than showing the near-term expansion the preview looked for.
fact_evidence: Marketplace gross margin was 34.7% (flat sequentially, up ~100 bps in first half).
expectation_evidence: “Marketplace gross margin: ~36–37%” and “Need 36%+ here.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Large-customer account growth modestly exceeded the preview’s derived estimate: XMTR reported 2,039 accounts spending at least $50,000, versus an expected 1,950-2,000. The 175 quarterly net additions were also a record, and enterprise revenue from larger customers grew over 40%.
fact_evidence: Accounts spending at least $50,000 in the trailing 12 months grew 23% year-over-year to 2,039, with a record 175 quarterly net adds, and enterprise revenue from larger customers grew over 40%.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “$50k+ LTM accounts” at “~1,950–2,000” and described “in-line buyer adds” as the base case.

description: Supplier services revenue was weaker than the preview’s roughly flat to slightly lower expectation. At $13.9 million versus about $15 million a year earlier, it declined more than the preview’s estimated 0%-3%.
fact_evidence: Services revenue was $13.9 million.
expectation_evidence: Supplier services were estimated at “~$14–15M” and “roughly flat”; the table showed “~flat to -3%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The cash balance was higher than the preview’s pro-forma estimate. XMTR ended the quarter with $517 million in cash and marketable securities, versus the preview’s expectation of roughly $430 million or more.
fact_evidence: Cash and marketable securities ended Q2 at $517 million, boosted by a $248 million follow-on offering and $50 million Siemens investment.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$430M+ cash pro-forma” after the equity raise and asked investors to confirm the actual cash figure.

description: Operating spending was more restrained than the preview’s downside risk of the company spending the revenue upside. Non-GAAP operating expenses grew less than half as fast as revenue, while marketplace advertising fell to a record-low share of marketplace revenue.
fact_evidence: Marketplace advertising spend fell to a record low 3.4% of marketplace revenue, down 220 basis points year-over-year, and total non-GAAP operating expenses grew only 19%, less than half the revenue growth rate.
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “a print at the low end of guide despite a revenue beat = they are spending the beat”; its bear scenario also cited “opex absorbs upside.”

description: Q2 revenue was $329.5 million, below the $339.2 million consensus and the company’s prior $335–345 million guidance range. The preview’s buy-side “whisper” was even higher at $345–355 million; the reported shortfall was attributed mainly to Machine Clothing equipment downtime and delayed defense tooling shipments.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $329.5 million… though it modestly trailed forecast primarily due to Machine Clothing equipment downtime and delayed defense tooling shipments.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $339.2M”; company guidance was “$335–345M”; the preview said the buy-side whisper was “likely $345–355M revenue.”

description: Engineered Composites revenue reached a record, but at $150.8 million it fell short of the preview’s $155–160 million expectation. This was a smaller-than-expected result despite strong year-over-year growth and program ramps.
fact_evidence: “Engineered Composites posted record quarterly revenue of $150.8 million, up 16% from $130.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 scenario expected “AEC ~$156–160M” in the base case, and its consensus table listed “Engineered Composites rev” at “$155–160M.”

description: Engineered Composites’ adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 13.3%, above the preview’s base-case range of 12–13% and back above the roughly 13% threshold the preview identified as validating the growth story. It was still below the preview’s 13.5% bull-case marker.
fact_evidence: “Engineered Composites adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $20 million (13.3% of sales) from $11.1 million (8.5%) a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected AEC at “12–13% margin”; it said a print “back above ~13%” would validate the re-rating, while its bull case specified “AEC ≥$162M with EBITDA margin back ≥13.5%.”

description: Machine Clothing revenue was $178.7 million, below the preview’s expected $180–185 million step-up. The company also now expects full-year Machine Clothing revenue to be slightly down versus 2025 because of weaker Americas demand, a weaker outlook than the preview’s expectation of full recovery from the equipment failure by year-end.
fact_evidence: “Machine Clothing revenue declined to $178.7 million… and full-year Machine Clothing revenue is now guided to be slightly down versus 2025 due to weaker Americas demand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 guidance of “Machine Clothing rev” at “$180–185M” and said management “expects full recovery ‘by end of year.’”

description: The Q3 revenue outlook of $320–330 million is below the preview’s base-case expectation of a roughly flat sequential guide and its bull-case threshold of at least $350 million. The range points to a lower revenue quarter than the preview’s expected trajectory.
fact_evidence: “The company guided Q3 2026 revenue to $320–$330 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “Q3 guided roughly flat sequentially”; its bull case called for “Q3 guide ≥$350M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow was a $14.5 million use rather than the positive Q2 cash flow the preview expected. The company attributed the outflow to inventory built for the Engineered Composites ramp and European seasonal shutdowns.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was a net use of $14.5 million versus a $17.8 million inflow last year, driven by inventory build to support Engineered Composites ramp and European seasonal shutdowns.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 should turn positive” after Q1 free cash flow of -$3.6 million.

description: The Salt Lake City strategic review advanced to eight finalists, with a decision expected in the coming weeks. The preview had identified a signed deal or named bidder and timeline as the upside catalyst, while its base case anticipated the process would remain ongoing without much to report.
fact_evidence: “The strategic review of the Salt Lake City (Sikorsky) site has advanced to 8 final candidates from multiple indications of interest, with a decision expected in the coming weeks.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “a signed deal — or even a named bidder and timeline” the largest discrete catalyst and said the base case was “Structures ‘process ongoing, too early to comment.’”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management described a more intensive and longer LEAP production ramp than the preview specified: 24/7 operations across three sites this summer, continuing until the ramp settles in late 2027, with Airbus potentially targeting 75 aircraft per month in 2028. This adds a concrete production trajectory to the preview’s broader expectation of LEAP-driven growth.
fact_evidence: “LEAP production is moving to 24/7 operations across three sites this summer and is expected to continue ramping until settling in late 2027, with Airbus targeting 75 aircraft per month potentially in 2028.”

description: Zebra’s sales exceeded $1.5 billion and beat the high end of its Q2 guidance, rather than landing near the preview’s $1.498 billion consensus. Organic growth was 9.2%, above the preview’s 5–6% base expectation and its 4–7% estimate if Elo contributed a similar amount as in Q1.
fact_evidence: Q2 sales exceeded $1.5 billion, growing 20.4% total and 9.2% organically year-over-year, beating the high end of guidance.
expectation_evidence: Consensus sales of $1,498M; the base scenario expected $1.50–1.51B and organic growth of 5–6%. The preview also said that if Elo contributed a similar ~10 points as in Q1, guidance implied organic growth of only ~4–7%.

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $6.35 was far above the preview’s $4.35 consensus and the company’s $4.20–$4.50 outlook. The preview’s bull case was only $4.55 or higher.
fact_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS reached $6.35, a 76% year-over-year increase, significantly exceeding the top end of the outlook.
expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP diluted EPS consensus was $4.35, against company guidance of $4.20–$4.50; the bull scenario was at least $4.55.

description: Zebra raised its full-year outlook substantially: sales growth is now 14%–16% versus the prior 10%–14%, and EPS is $20.75–$21.25 versus $18.30–$18.70. The new 23.5%–24% EBITDA margin expectation is also well above the preview’s approximately 22% outlook.
fact_evidence: The company raised full-year 2026 sales growth guidance to 14%-16%, full-year EPS guidance to $20.75-$21.25, and expects EBITDA margin at 23.5%-24%.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 guide: sales +10–14%, adjusted EBITDA margin ~22%, and non-GAAP EPS $18.30–$18.70.

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 27.7%, far above the preview’s roughly 22% estimate, rather than showing the anticipated Q2 margin trough. The result included a $73 million IPA tariff recovery that was not in prior guidance.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 7.1 points to 27.7%, boosted by a $73 million IPA tariff recovery that was not included in prior guidance.
expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was estimated at ~22% (derived), and the preview described Q2 as the trough quarter for margin.

description: Despite the preview’s concern that escalating memory costs could pressure Q2 margins, Zebra said it fully offset the approximately $120 million memory cost headwind. The expected pricing offset rose from $60 million to $90 million on strong Q2 price realization.
fact_evidence: The company fully mitigated the approximately $120 million memory cost headwind, raising the pricing-driven offset expectation from $60 million to $90 million due to strong Q2 price realization.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged sequential escalation in memory costs into Q2 and asked whether pricing actions were realized or still planned.

description: Connected Frontline’s 7.5% organic growth exceeded the preview’s 4–7% implied range if Elo contributed a similar amount as in Q1. The segment grew nearly 26% overall, led by mobile computing.
fact_evidence: The Connected Frontline segment grew nearly 26% (7.5% organic) led by mobile computing.
expectation_evidence: The preview said that if Elo contributed a similar ~10 points as in Q1, the guide implied organic growth of only ~4–7%; Q1 Connected Frontline growth was +20.6% (+3.8% organic).

description: Elo Touch grew above management’s expectations, and Zebra identified about $10 million in synergies—additional positive acquisition commentary beyond the preview’s assumption that Elo would contribute a similar amount as in Q1.
fact_evidence: The Elo Touch acquisition delivered above-expectation growth with about $10 million in identified synergies.
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If Elo contributes a similar ~10pts in Q2” as in Q1, it would carry much of the headline growth.

description: Free cash flow guidance increased to at least $1 billion, above the preview’s already-positive expectation of at least $900 million.
fact_evidence: Free cash flow guidance was raised to at least $1 billion, reflecting roughly 100% conversion.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 free cash flow guidance was ≥$900M (~100% conversion).

description: Bruker’s $838.5 million of Q2 revenue fell short of the $853.6 million consensus and the preview’s higher $865–875 million whisper range. Organic growth was positive at 2.8% (3.4% excluding tariff refunds), but remained below the preview’s whisper threshold of at least 4%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 5.2% to $838.5 million with organic growth of 2.8% (3.4% excluding tariff refunds).”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue of “$853.6M”; the preview’s whisper was “~$865–875M revenue with organic growth ≥+4%.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.49 substantially exceeded both the $0.38 consensus and the preview’s $0.41–0.43 whisper. The size of the beat was especially notable given that revenue was below consensus.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 53% year-over-year to $0.49 from $0.32, beating on margins and EPS despite top-line results coming in at the low end of expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” non-GAAP diluted EPS of “$0.38”; the preview’s whisper was “~$0.41–0.43 EPS.”

description: Reported non-GAAP operating margin reached 14.1%, above the preview’s roughly 13% expectation. However, tariff refunds contributed about 200 basis points, implying that margin without that contribution was roughly 12.1%, below the preview’s benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 510 basis points to 14.1%”; net U.S. tariff refunds contributed “roughly 200 basis points to operating margin.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~13%” Q2 non-GAAP operating margin and said “a sub-13% Q2 margin makes the full-year bridge back-end loaded and fragile.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Unexpected U.S. tariff refunds provided a meaningful one-time boost to the quarter’s earnings and margin, contributing about $0.06 to EPS as well as roughly 200 basis points to operating margin.
fact_evidence: “Net U.S. tariff refunds contributed about $0.06 to EPS and roughly 200 basis points to operating margin.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said tariff headwinds were easing as the quarter lapped the Q2'25 tariff introduction, but did not anticipate refunds of this size.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Scientific Instruments’ semi bookings growth was far stronger than the preview’s 20%+ run-rate hurdle: the segment reported greater than 50% growth in semi, alongside 10% organic bookings growth overall.
fact_evidence: “The Scientific Instruments segment posted 10% organic bookings growth ... led by greater than 50% growth in semi.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “third consecutive 20%+ quarter” in semiconductor metrology bookings and said a deceleration to “high-teens” would be concerning.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Scientific Instruments also reported greater than 20% bookings growth in biopharma, a stronger positive end-market signal than the preview’s discussion of clinical microbiology placements and a still-early broader recovery had established.
fact_evidence: Scientific Instruments bookings were “led by ... greater than 20% growth in biopharma.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described biopharma as still in the “early innings of an organic recovery” and noted clinical microbiology placements “ran 40% ahead of plan,” but did not forecast this bookings growth.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The strong semiconductor metrology demand is not converting quickly into revenue: 9–24 month lead times are delaying revenue realization despite strong first-half orders and revenue growth.
fact_evidence: Semiconductor metrology had “first-half organic order growth over 30% and revenue growth over 15%,” but “9-24 month lead times” are “delaying revenue conversion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview emphasized the semi-metrology order run-rate and capacity ramp, but did not flag these long lead times as a constraint on converting demand to revenue.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Bruker reported a GAAP loss per share despite strong non-GAAP EPS, because it recorded a $135 million noncash goodwill impairment for underperforming automation and spatial biology businesses.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP diluted loss per share of $0.41, driven by a $135 million noncash goodwill impairment tied to its underperforming automation and spatial biology businesses.”

description: Management reiterated the $2.10–$2.15 full-year EPS range rather than raising it, despite the preview’s expectation that the company might lift guidance or at least move to the high end. The reported revenue range was also reduced to $3.54–$3.57 billion after the assumed FX tailwind was cut.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at $2.10-$2.15 non-GAAP EPS ... with organic revenue growth of 1-2%, though the FX tailwind was cut from 1.5% to 0.5%, lowering reported revenue guidance to $3.54-$3.57 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted “$2.20+” or “at minimum, a move to the high end,” and carried revenue guidance of “$3.57–$3.60B” with an FX contribution of “~+1.5%.”

description: The near-term outlook includes a weaker Q3 than the preview had specified: about $20 million of semiconductor revenue shifts into Q4, leaving Q3 organic revenue roughly flat to slightly up and sequential margins and EPS lower.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $20 million of Q3 revenue is shifting to Q4 due to semiconductor customer delivery timing, leaving Q3 organic revenue roughly flat to slightly up with sequentially lower margins and EPS.”

description: Management described a very strong Q4, with revenue around $1 billion and roughly two-thirds already in backlog, supporting meaningful year-over-year gains in organic growth, margin, and EPS. That is a more specific and constructive outlook than the preview’s general expectation of a back-end-weighted recovery.
fact_evidence: Management expects “a very strong Q4 with revenue around $1 billion (of which roughly two-thirds is already in backlog) driving meaningful year-over-year gains in organic growth, margin, and EPS.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described margin expansion as “second-half weighted” in its base case and said management had called Q2 “the highest organic growth quarter of the year.”

description: Bruker expects another $20 million of savings in 2027 from its new four-group structure, beyond the $140 million annualized 2026 savings program already in the preview. Management also set out a longer-term target of double-digit EPS growth and EBIT margins moving back toward 20%.
fact_evidence: “A new four-group operating structure [is] expected to add $20 million more in 2027, supporting a target of double-digit EPS growth and margins moving back toward 20% EBIT.”
expectation_evidence: The preview already expected “~$140M annualized” savings in 2026 and said benefits would “extend into 2027,” but did not specify an additional $20 million or the stated longer-term targets.

description: Entegris reported Q2 revenue of $883 million, up 11% year over year, versus the preview’s $839.9 million consensus and the company’s $845 million guidance high end. The result was well above both expectations.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $883 million, exceeding guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Zacks, 7/31/26) $839.9M”; company Q2 guidance was “$815M – $845M.”

description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.93, above the preview’s $0.83 consensus and the $0.84 guidance high end. This was a substantially larger result than the preview’s high-end-of-guide setup implied.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.93.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Zacks, 7/31/26) $0.83”; company Q2 guidance was “$0.76 – $0.84.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance midpoint was $920 million, well above the roughly $871 million level implied by management’s prior indication and the preview’s key watchpoint. Rather than merely delivering the expected roughly 5% sequential increase, the midpoint implies substantially stronger growth.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies ~14% year-over-year revenue growth ($905M-$935M).”
expectation_evidence: Management had pre-committed to “approximately 5% [sequential growth] from the midpoint of the second quarter’s guidance range” — “i.e. ~$871M”; the preview said anything below “~$865M reads as a walk-back.”

description: Q3 gross-margin guidance of 47.5%–48.5% is above the Q2 guidance range and points to a much higher margin level than the preview’s base case of flat-to-slightly-up. The midpoint is also above the preview’s 47.5% bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin of 47.5%-48.5% (over 400bps year-over-year expansion).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Q3 gross margin “flat-to-slightly-up”; its bull case called for “GM ≥47.5%.”

description: Entegris expects Q4 revenue to grow about 4% sequentially from the Q3 midpoint, implying mid-teens year-over-year growth, versus the preview’s $917 million Q4 consensus estimate and roughly 11% year-over-year growth. Both MS and APS are also expected to grow more than 10%.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue is expected to grow ~4% sequentially from the Q3 midpoint, representing mid-teens year-over-year growth, with both MS and APS segments growing more than 10%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$917M in Q4,” “+11% YoY and +5% sequential”; it also said “APS reacceleration is the cleanest evidence the capex cycle is flowing through.”

description: Q2 adjusted gross margin reached 47.6%, 35 basis points above the top of the preview’s expected range; adjusted EBITDA margin was also 28.4%, above the preview’s 28.0% guidance ceiling. Margins therefore came in stronger than the already-improving outlook.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached 47.6%, its highest level since early 2022, improving 70 basis points sequentially”; adjusted EBITDA margin was “28.4%.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 gross-margin guidance was “46.25% – 47.25%”; adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$220M – $236M (27.0–28.0%).”

description: CapEx-related revenue was up 15% year over year in Q2, indicating an earlier and stronger inflection than the preview’s description of Q1 CapEx-related revenue being down modestly and improving through the second half.
fact_evidence: “Unit-driven revenues up 10% and CapEx-related revenue up 15%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 CapEx-driven revenue was down modestly YoY” and that “CapEx-driven revenue improves through 2H.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow was $120 million, below the preview’s expectation of roughly $140 million or more per quarter to support the deleveraging plan. This was a weaker cash-flow result than expected despite the strong earnings report.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $120 million (14% of sales).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the path from 3.6x leverage to about 3.0x by year-end “requires continued ~$140M+ quarterly FCF.”

description: Despite Q2 free cash flow below the preview’s expected pace, Entegris repaid $200 million of debt, reduced net leverage to 3.4x, and now expects year-end leverage in the high 2x range. That is ahead of the preview’s roughly 3.0x year-end target.
fact_evidence: “$200 million of debt repayment and reducing net leverage to 3.4x, with management now expecting to end the year in the high 2x range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “Target ~3.0x by YE26” and said the path from 3.6x to “~3.0x by YE26” required continued quarterly FCF.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management raised its 2026 MSI growth forecast to 7%–8%, above its initial mid-single-digit assumption. The preview did not anticipate this upward revision to the market-growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its 2026 MSI growth forecast to 7%-8% from an initial mid-single-digit assumption.”
expectation_evidence: “From an initial mid-single-digit assumption.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management cited more than 20 major leading-edge capacity expansions but said fab-construction benefits will accrue mostly in 2027. The project pipeline adds a longer-term growth indicator, while the timing is later than the preview’s anticipated improvement in CapEx-driven revenue through the second half of 2026.
fact_evidence: “Tracking over 20 major leading-edge capacity expansions globally (8-10 advanced logic, 7-8 advanced memory, 6-8 advanced packaging), with fab construction benefits mostly accruing to 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “promised CapEx-driven revenue improves through 2H” and described fab-construction forecasts improving “from low-single-digit to high-single-digit growth.”

description: Molybdenum precursor demand grew more than 20% in Q2 and is expected to roughly double in 2026 as NAND scales to 300-plus layers. The preview did not flag this product-specific growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “Molybdenum precursor demand grew over 20% year-over-year in Q2 and is expected to roughly double in 2026 versus 2025, driven by NAND scaling to 300-plus layers.”

description: Entegris exited its U.S. life sciences fluid management business and announced another facility closure, extending its rationalization of dilutive operations. The preview mentioned possible portfolio actions only as a governance-related topic and did not anticipate these specific moves.
fact_evidence: “Exited its U.S. life sciences fluid management business (less than $20 million annual revenue, dilutive margins) and announced closure of its Logan, Utah facility, its third dilutive facility rationalization since late 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “tone and strategic framing (M&A appetite, portfolio actions) may shift,” but did not identify an expected exit or facility closure.

description: Ingredion’s $1.85 billion of Q2 net sales exceeded the preview’s $1.81 billion consensus, and rose 1% rather than falling 1.4% year over year as consensus implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 1% to $1.85 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $1.81B”; implied YoY “−1.4%.”

description: Adjusted operating income fell 5%, a milder decline than the preview’s expected high-single-digit drop and its implied $246–252 million range; the reported result was $258 million.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income fell 5% to $258 million.”
expectation_evidence: The May outlook was “adjusted operating income down high-single-digits”; the preview translated that to “Down-HSD off $273M ≈ $246–252M.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The expected Q2 relief from tapioca costs did not arrive: route prices were up more than 40% since the start of the year, leaving near-term margin pressure for roughly another 1 to 1.5 quarters.
fact_evidence: “Tapioca route prices are up more than 40% since the start of the year” and create “near-term margin pressure until price pass-throughs catch up over roughly 1 to 1.5 quarters.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 was “the first quarter where” the prior tapioca-cost margin pressure “should reverse.”

description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was reaffirmed at $10.30–$10.90, below the preview’s expected range of $10.45–$11.15.
fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $10.30 to $10.90.”
expectation_evidence: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was “$10.45–$11.15.”

description: Full-year adjusted operating income is now expected to decline by mid-single digits, worse than the preview’s expected flat-to-down-low-single-digit outlook; the call attributed the revision to the Pakistan stake sale.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted operating income was revised to down mid-single digits after the sale of its majority stake in the Pakistan business.”
expectation_evidence: FY2026 adjusted operating income was expected to be “flat to down LSD.”

description: Food and Industrial Ingredients U.S./Canada now has a steep full-year outlook, with operating income guided down 20% to 25%; the preview instead framed the key question as whether the segment would recover sequentially from its Q1 trough.
fact_evidence: “Food and Industrial Ingredients U.S./Canada net sales declined 7% and operating income fell to $58 million” and “full-year segment operating income [is] now guided down 20% to 25%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for watching “F&II—U.S./Canada operating income recovering sequentially off $34M” and described sequential operating improvements at Argo as central to the outlook.

description: The full-year operating-cash-flow range was lowered to $700–$800 million from the preview’s $725–$825 million, despite the preview already flagging cash flow as a metric to track.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date cash from operations was $123 million after $231 million of working capital investment, with full-year operating cash flow now guided to $700-$800 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 operating cash flow guidance of “$725–825M.”

description: Capex is now guided at $450–$490 million, above the preview’s $400–$440 million range, with the increase tied to funding Argo reliability.
fact_evidence: “Capex raised to $450-$490 million to fund Argo reliability.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 capex guidance of “$400–440M.”

description: Texture & Healthful Solutions produced its second-highest quarterly operating income ever, alongside 5% sales growth and 7% volume growth—stronger evidence of performance than the preview’s general description of the segment as a franchise bright spot.
fact_evidence: “Texture & Healthful Solutions delivered its second-highest quarterly operating income ever, with net sales up 5% driven by 7% sales volume growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview characterized T&HS as “the franchise bright spot” and focused on whether it would deliver a ninth consecutive quarter of volume growth.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management disclosed an unexpected potential industry tailwind: a competitor plans to close a facility representing about 5% of U.S. industry capacity in 2027, which it expects to affect contracting dynamics.
fact_evidence: “A competitor's announced closure of a facility representing about 5% of U.S. industry capacity in 2027 is expected to meaningfully impact industry contracting dynamics going forward.”

description: The preview modeled diluted EPS of $0.13 and cited consensus of $0.105; InfuSystem reported $0.15. The EPS beat was expected in direction, but the reported result was higher than the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: Net income increased to $3.2 million ($0.15 per diluted share) from $2.6 million ($0.12 per diluted share) a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 FY26E” diluted EPS was “$0.13”; consensus diluted EPS was “$0.105.”

description: The preview expected Wound Care to reach roughly $2.5 million in its base case and flagged deceleration as a risk. Instead, revenue surged 154%, increasing by $2.1 million, a much stronger growth outcome than the preview’s base case implied.
fact_evidence: “Wound Care revenue surged 154% ($2.1 million), driven mainly by compression devices for lymphedema.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “wound care ~$2.5M” and said to watch whether growth was decelerating; it identified “$2.4M+” as the watch level.

description: Revenue was above the preview’s working consensus of $36.35 million, though below the alternate $37.08 million estimate. The $36.9 million result was also at the top of the preview’s implied range for results consistent with the company’s growth guide.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $36.9 million,” up 2.6% GAAP and 7.5% pro forma.
expectation_evidence: The preview used “$36.35M” as working consensus, listed an alternate “$37.08M,” and said 6–8% pro-forma growth implied “$36.3M–$36.9M” for Q2.

description: Device Solutions revenue fell 16.1%, a steeper reported decline than the preview’s estimate of a 9% decline. The preview had anticipated the GE-related revenue reduction, but modeled a smaller reported contraction.
fact_evidence: Device Solutions had “a 16.1% revenue decline in that segment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Device Solutions at “−9% Y/Y reported; ~+4% ex-GE.”

description: Patient Services gross margin fell to 61.8%, below the prior-year 64.2% and the Q1 level the preview highlighted as a potential pressure point. The reported reasons included mix from lower-margin Wound Care and higher pump maintenance costs.
fact_evidence: Patient Services gross margin “declined to 61.8% from 64.2% due to a larger mix of lower-margin Wound Care revenue and higher pump maintenance costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged Patient Services gross margin, noting it was “64.8% in Q1,” and asked “whether that pressure is contained.”

description: The company returned $4.4 million through buybacks, a stronger deployment than the preview’s expectation of limited in-quarter activity after the new authorization opened July 1.
fact_evidence: The company returned “$4.4 million to shareholders via buybacks.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “only ~1 month of the new program falls inside this reporting quarter” and said the disclosure to watch was “post-quarter commentary, not the Q2 cash flow statement.”

description: The preview put Q2 adjusted EPS consensus at about $1.80, but NRG reported $1.49. EPS also fell from $1.73 a year earlier despite higher EBITDA, as acquisition-related interest expense and D&A weighed on results.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 34% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, but adjusted EPS declined to $1.49 from $1.73 as acquisition-related interest expense and D&A offset higher EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | Consensus | ~$1.80”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview identified an anchor hyperscaler contract as a key possible catalyst, but NRG reported that it had aligned on principal commercial terms for a 1.2 GW Texas project, with potential to expand to 2.4 GW. The agreement was not described as fully executed, but it advances the anticipated opportunity with a specific project scale and timing.
fact_evidence: “NRG aligned on principal commercial terms with an investment-grade global cloud and AI hyperscaler for a 1.2 gigawatt Bring Your Own Power project in Texas, with potential to expand to 2.4 gigawatts”; commercial operations are “targeted” for late 2029.
expectation_evidence: “The awaited catalyst is the anchor hyperscaler deal tied to the 5.4 GW GE Vernova/Kiewit JV”; the preview also described the contract as a “live and unscheduled catalyst.”

description: Although NRG kept its 2026 guidance range unchanged, management said it expects to track below the midpoint. The preview treated a plain reaffirm as a scenario in which the low end remained live, but did not anticipate this explicit below-midpoint indication.
fact_evidence: “NRG reaffirmed its 2026 guidance but expects to track below the midpoint due to softer Texas load and power prices, Winter Storm Fern supply costs, and $70 million of incremental RGGI costs.”
expectation_evidence: “A plain reaffirm reads as ‘low end still live’”; the base scenario anticipated a “plain reaffirm.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The hyperscaler project came with substantial economics not quantified in the preview: $3.2 billion of investment is expected to produce $500 million of annual adjusted EBITDA and $375 million of annual free cash flow before growth, at an approximately 6x build multiple and a 12%–15% pretax un-levered IRR.
fact_evidence: “The 1.2 gigawatt project requires $3.2 billion of investment (~$2,700/KW) and is expected to generate $500 million of annual adjusted EBITDA and $375 million of annual free cash flow before growth once fully operational, implying a build multiple of approximately 6x”; it “targets a 12%-15% pretax un-levered IRR.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The project’s contracted cash flows appear more insulated from data-center utilization than the preview had specified: 95% of free cash flow is supported by availability-based capacity payments, with costs recovered separately and an investment-grade parent guarantee.
fact_evidence: “The commercial structure supports 95% of the project's free cash flow via availability-based Capacity Payments independent of data center utilization, with fuel and operating costs recovered separately and backed by an investment-grade parent guarantee.”

description: NRG disclosed $70 million of incremental costs from Virginia rejoining RGGI, an added headwind not called out in the preview and one of the reasons management expects to track below the guidance midpoint.
fact_evidence: “$70 million of incremental RGGI costs from Virginia rejoining the program.”

description: NRG said the project will slow debt reduction and push the target of 3x leverage out by a year, from 2028 to 2029. The preview highlighted the leverage trajectory as a key watch item but did not anticipate this specific delay.
fact_evidence: “The project spend does not change guidance but reduces planned net debt reduction, extending the timeline to reach the 3x leverage target from 2028 to 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net leverage trajectory toward ~3x within 24–36 months post-LS Power” and said any softening on the “~3x leverage timeline” would be a bear signal.

description: NRG added a longer-term growth illustration beyond the preview’s discussion of the contracting pipeline: it cited $1.2 billion of contracted free cash flow opportunity by 2030 alongside a base business expected to deliver 14%-plus adjusted EPS CAGR through 2030.
fact_evidence: “The 1.2 gigawatt project represents only the first tranche of 5.4 gigawatts of secured turbine and EPC capacity through 2032, plus ~2 gigawatts of PJM uprate opportunities, supporting an illustrative $1.2 billion contracted free cash flow opportunity by 2030 on top of a base business expected to deliver 14%-plus adjusted EPS CAGR through 2030.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the “5.4 GW GE Vernova/Kiewit JV” and “up to 2 GW of uprates/conversions,” but did not give this contracted free-cash-flow opportunity or EPS growth outlook.

description: The preview said investors wanted guidance narrowed toward the upper half or raised, and that a plain reaffirmation would be a mild disappointment. Pediatrix instead reaffirmed its $280–300 million FY26 adjusted EBITDA outlook without an upward action.
fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook of $280 to $300 million in adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “A second plain reaffirm is a mild disappointment. The buy-side wants a narrow to the upper half ($290–300M) at minimum.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview’s base case called for same-unit growth of 2.5%–3.5% and saw flat-to-positive volumes as part of the upside case. Instead, same-unit growth was 2% as patient service volumes fell 2% and NICU days fell 3%, including a decline in neonatology.
fact_evidence: “Same unit patient service volumes fell 2% with NICU days down 3%, primarily in neonatology”; consolidated revenue growth included “2% same unit growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Base: … Same-unit +2.5–3.5%; volumes −1% to flat”; the preview also said Q2 had “NICU days +6%” in the prior-year quarter and that “Anything above +3% total same-unit is a genuine beat.”

description: Consolidated revenue growth was 4%, above the preview’s roughly 1.8%–2.1% consensus growth estimate, although the outperformance came partly from non-same-unit activity from recent acquisitions rather than stronger same-unit growth.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue grew 4%, driven by 2% same unit growth plus non-same unit activity from recent acquisitions.”
expectation_evidence: Preview consensus for net revenue was “$477.3M – $478.5M” versus Q2 FY25 actual of “$468.8M,” or “+1.8% to +2.1%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview expected payer mix to remain stable and was focused on avoiding the deterioration reported by peers. Instead, payer mix improved substantially both year over year and sequentially, with management still reporting no signs of peer-like deterioration.
fact_evidence: “Payer mix improved 135 basis points year over year and 120 basis points versus Q1 2026, with management reporting no signs of the payer mix deterioration seen by peers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 payer mix had been pre-announced as “stable and unchanged” and that Pediatrix “had not seen the adverse mix shifts reported elsewhere in healthcare.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Pricing held at 4%, the high end of the preview’s expected 3%–4% range and the specific outcome it identified as an upside surprise. The call attributed it partly to strong RCM collections, but said that tailwind should dissipate in the second half, as the preview had anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Same unit pricing rose 4%, driven by strong RCM cash collections, favorable payer mix, and increased patient acuity, though RCM collections tailwind is expected to dissipate in the second half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “If pricing holds near 4% in Q2, that is the upside surprise”; the base case expected “pricing ~3–4% with modest RCM fade.”

description: The preview flagged a potential step-up in repurchases as an upside lever. Pediatrix bought back just under 2 million shares in Q2, roughly twice the 1 million shares repurchased in Q1, and reported 7 million shares repurchased since August 2025.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased just under 2 million shares in the quarter, bringing total buybacks since August 2025 to 7 million shares.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “any step-up in buyback” would be an “underappreciated upside lever,” and cited Q1 repurchases of “$21.5M/1.0M shares.”

description: The call disclosed that 2026 G&A is expected at the higher end of the $230–240 million range because of one-time executive transition costs. The preview had focused on practice compensation as a margin risk but did not flag these transition costs.
fact_evidence: “G&A expense is expected to land at the higher end of a $230 to $240 million range for 2026, elevated by one-time executive transition costs that should step down in the second half.”

description: Despite the preview’s concern about higher variable practice incentive compensation as a 2026 margin headwind, management said salary increases were holding to 3%–3.5%, below the mid-single-digit growth seen historically.
fact_evidence: “Salary increases have remained in a tight 3% to 3.5% band, down from mid-single-digit growth historically.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “higher variable practice incentive compensation as a 2026 margin headwind.”

description: PRKS reported Q2 revenue of $483.3 million, about 2% below the preview’s roughly $493–494 million consensus and down year over year, rather than the modest growth consensus implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $483.3 million, down 1.4% year-over-year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Attendance fell despite the preview’s emphasis on an easier weather comparison and forward indicators that suggested attendance growth. Easter timing and lower international visitation were cited as drags.
fact_evidence: “A 2.9% attendance decline of approximately 179,000 guests due to the Easter calendar shift and lower international visitation.”
expectation_evidence: “Attendance vs. the weak weather comp — Q2 2025 was weather-depressed; failure to grow attendance against that comp would undercut the ‘forward indicators’ narrative.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA and net income declined, contrary to the growth implied by consensus EPS and the preview’s expectation of an easier comparison. The preview did not provide a Q2 EBITDA estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell $10.8 million to $195.5 million and net income dropped to $63.3 million from $80.1 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS: $1.69 … Year-ago Q2 2025 GAAP EPS was $1.45, so consensus implies ~17% y/y growth”; the preview also noted the “easier weather comp this year.”

description: July revenue was already down about 2%, with management citing several weather and air-quality disruptions. That is a negative update against the preview’s focus on the 2026 revenue and EBITDA growth commitment, although the call facts do not state a revised full-year outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management provided a preliminary view that July revenue was down approximately 2%, hurt by wildfires, air quality issues, excessive heat and rain.”
expectation_evidence: “July trading update / 2026 EBITDA-growth reiteration — after four straight misses, credibility of the full-year growth commitment is the swing factor”; the preview also quoted management’s commitment to “growth in revenue and Adjusted EBITDA in 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The paid pass base was down 1% from June 2025, despite the preview’s report that season-pass sales had been pacing 12% ahead through April. Deferred revenue was modestly higher, but the pass-base figure points to a weaker conversion or retention outcome than that earlier pacing suggested.
fact_evidence: “Deferred revenue rose about 2% year-over-year to $211.9 million, while the paid pass base was down 1% versus June 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Season-pass sales pacing ~12% ahead of 2025 through April 30.”

description: PRKS disclosed credible third parties interested in buying some or most of its real estate, with offers valued very favorably against its public equity value. The preview did not flag a potential real-estate transaction.
fact_evidence: “Management is engaged with multiple credible third parties interested in acquiring some or most of its real estate, with valuations offered that compare very favorably to the company's public equity market value.”

description: The company said it was on pace for a $50 million gross cost-savings target for 2026, above the roughly $30 million annualized savings initiatives referenced in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Remains on pace for its $50 million gross cost savings target for 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Progress on the ~$30M annualized cost-savings initiatives referenced in Q1 disclosures.”

description: PRKS raised its growth/ROI capital-expenditure budget to $75–85 million, in addition to $180–190 million of core CapEx. The preview did not anticipate a higher investment budget.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 growth/ROI CapEx budget to $75-85 million (from prior levels) alongside $180-190 million in core CapEx.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: PRKS introduced Sony Pictures horror IP into Howl-O-Scream, and early booking sales were running ahead of last year. Neither the new offering nor the early booking comparison appeared in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Introduced new Sony Pictures horror IP into Howl-O-Scream with early booking sales running ahead of last year.”

description: STRL reported 90% Q2 revenue growth, above the preview’s consensus growth estimates of 74% from Zacks and 66.5% from FactSet. The growth rate exceeded the higher estimate by 16 percentage points.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 90% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Zacks Consensus … YoY growth implied +74%”; “FactSet … YoY growth implied +66.5%.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $5.80, above both preview estimates of $5.20 and $5.01. The result also represented 116% year-over-year growth, versus the preview’s estimate of 93.3% growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 116% from $2.69 to $5.80.”
expectation_evidence: “Zacks Consensus … EPS est. $5.20 … YoY growth implied +93.3%”; “FactSet … EPS est. $5.01.”

description: Management raised full-year guidance across revenue, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA. The new midpoints—$4.075 billion, $20.00, and $903.5 million—are respectively about 9%, 7%, and 5% above the prior guidance midpoints.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $4.0-$4.15 billion, adjusted diluted EPS of $19.70-$20.30, and adjusted EBITDA of $891-$916 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Management's own raised guidance midpoint of ~$18.73 (range $18.40–$19.05)” and “revenue of $3.70B–$3.80B, adjusted diluted EPS of $18.40–$19.05, adjusted EBITDA of $843M–$873M.”

description: E-Infrastructure revenue grew 192% in the quarter, far above the preview’s cited expectation that the segment would grow at rates approaching 60% or higher during 2026. The preview’s figure was a full-year outlook, so the periods are not directly comparable, but the quarterly growth rate was much higher.
fact_evidence: “E-Infrastructure revenue grew 192%.”
expectation_evidence: “E-Infrastructure momentum: segment guided to grow ‘at rates approaching 60% or higher during 2026.’”

description: Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, with its margin expanding 150 basis points to 22%. That was a favorable outcome on the margin trajectory the preview identified as a key issue to watch.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled with margins expanding 150 basis points to 22%.”
expectation_evidence: “Margin trajectory — gross margin hit a Q1 record of 23.5%; whether vertical-integration/mix benefits persist.”

description: Management cautioned that award timing could lead to softer Q3 orders and a sequential backlog decline, before stronger awards in Q4 2026 and early 2027. The preview flagged backlog expansion as something to watch but did not anticipate this near-term timing risk.

description: Q2 sales were about $1.26 billion, roughly 2% above the $1.233 billion consensus, and grew 7.5% rather than the 5.2% implied by consensus. Organic growth was 4.4%, driven by pricing and volume across both segments.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total sales rose 7.5% year-over-year to $1.26 billion, with organic revenue growth of 4.4% driven by higher pricing and volume across both segments.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A $0.08-per-share benefit from $8 million of IEEPA tariff refunds contributed to Q2 adjusted EPS. The preview discussed tariff costs and pricing but did not anticipate a refund benefit in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased nearly 30% year-over-year to $1.83, including an $0.08 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds ($8 million).”
expectation_evidence: “~$20M of tariff cost ate the pricing benefit”; “Price covers tariffs roughly one-for-one.”

description: Industrial Motion posted record sales of $454 million, up 14.6%, and a 23.3% EBITDA margin. The preview expected growth above Q1’s 12% and identified margins above 22% as a bull-case outcome; the reported segment result exceeded both markers.
fact_evidence: “Industrial Motion posted record quarterly sales of $454 million (up 14.6%) with EBITDA margins of 23.3%, up 500 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “IM revenue growth should exceed Q1's +12%”; bull scenario: “IM >22% on full-quarter Bijur.”

description: The preview expected the belts divestiture to raise Industrial Motion’s margin but did not quantify the effect. Management said the transaction should improve pro forma Industrial Motion EBITDA margins by more than 200 basis points.
fact_evidence: “The pending belts divestiture, expected to close in Q3, is projected to structurally improve Industrial Motion EBITDA margins by more than 200 basis points on a pro forma basis.”
expectation_evidence: “The belts divestiture closes in Q3, removing revenue and EPS while raising margin.”

description: The company raised its full-year organic revenue growth outlook to 3.5% at the midpoint, up 1.5 percentage points. The preview cited full-year revenue guidance of about 5% but did not anticipate this increase in the organic-growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “Full-year organic revenue guidance was raised to 3.5% at the midpoint (up 1.5 points).”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~+5% at midpoint.”

description: Second-half guidance includes a $0.10-per-share headwind, mostly for strategic investment and added aerospace and defense headcount. The preview instead identified a $0.10 inflation contingency and suggested it might be released in the bull case, so the reported use of that amount for investment was a different and less favorable earnings bridge.
fact_evidence: “Management embedded a $0.10 EPS headwind in second-half guidance, mostly tied to strategic investments in aerospace and defense operations to add operative headcount amid a growing backlog with book-to-bill well above 1.”
expectation_evidence: “The $0.10 inflation contingency embedded in guidance is released” in the bull case.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported a growing aerospace and defense backlog with book-to-bill well above 1, providing a stronger demand signal than the preview could confirm when it asked whether backlog had grown again.
fact_evidence: “A growing backlog with book-to-bill well above 1.”
expectation_evidence: “What matters is whether backlog again grew sequentially and YoY (off-highway, aerospace, rail, wind led in Q1).”

description: The company raised its quarterly dividend by 3%, repurchased about 155,000 shares, and returned $45 million to shareholders. The preview said a buyback announcement alongside the belts divestiture would be a positive surprise; the call also reported a dividend increase.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its quarterly dividend by 3%, repurchased about 155,000 shares, returned $45 million to shareholders, and ended the quarter with net leverage at 2x.”
expectation_evidence: “A buyback announcement alongside [the belts divestiture] would be a positive surprise.”

description: Automation and robotics grew mid-teens, while strategic verticals collectively delivered high-single-digit organic growth. The preview discussed selected end-market questions but did not anticipate this reported strength across these activities.
fact_evidence: “Automation and robotics grew mid-teens year-over-year while strategic verticals collectively delivered high-single-digit organic growth.”

description: Westlake’s $3.3 billion of Q2 net sales came in above the preview’s $3.244–3.25 billion consensus range, despite the preview expecting the company to miss revenue consensus again. It also exceeded the preview’s $3.05–3.10 billion working estimate.
fact_evidence: “Westlake reported Q2 2026 net sales of $3.3 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Revenue $3.244–3.25B”; the preview also modeled “~$3.05–3.10B revenue” and said Westlake had missed revenue consensus in all eight prior quarters.

description: PEM EBITDA was far stronger than the preview’s $230–290 million estimate: it reached $416 million, with a sharp sequential recovery as average sales prices rose and North American natural gas and ethane costs fell.
fact_evidence: “The PEM segment's EBITDA jumped to $416 million,” up $380 million sequentially, “driven by a 21% sequential rise in average sales price and lower North American natural gas and ethane costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled PEM at “$230–290M adj. EBITDA” and said “Anything above ~$250M validates the price-increase realization story.”

description: HIP’s Q2 revenue and EBITDA both beat the preview’s model: revenue was $1.3 billion rather than $1.10–1.15 billion, and EBITDA was $276 million rather than $225–240 million. The 22% margin was also above the preview’s modeled ~20%, although it was down from 24% a year earlier amid lower prices and freight and raw-material inflation.
fact_evidence: “HIP revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $1.3 billion,” while EBITDA was “$276 million”; EBITDA margin was 22%, versus 24% a year ago.
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “$1.10–1.15B sales, ~20% adj. EBITDA margin → ~$225–240M.”

description: The preview did not flag an Epoxy turnaround, but Westlake said the business—previously losing more than $100 million annually—was profitable in Q2 2026.
fact_evidence: “The formerly loss-making Epoxy business turned around from annual losses exceeding $100 million to profitability in Q2 2026.”

description: Management identified a Q3 pipe-volume headwind the preview had not anticipated: some customers pulled Q3 demand into Q2 to secure supply amid the Middle East conflict.
fact_evidence: “Some Q3 pipe demand was pulled forward into Q2 as customers secured supply amid the Middle East conflict, implying a modest headwind to Q3 pipe volumes.”

description: Westlake returned about $100 million to shareholders, including $30 million of buybacks. The preview highlighted balance-sheet and leverage concerns and expected $500 million of note repayment, but did not flag buybacks or this additional shareholder return.
fact_evidence: “The company retired $500 million of 2026 notes and returned about $100 million to shareholders (dividends plus $30 million of buybacks).”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Free cash flow and the balance sheet” as a key metric and said “$500M was called for Q2 repayment.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Accel’s first Chicago locations are expected to open within weeks, much earlier than the preview’s base case of late 2026 or Q1 2027. The company has already been approved for 17 of 39 establishment licenses.
fact_evidence: “approved for 17 of 39 (approximately 44%) of Chicago establishment licenses” and “expects the first Chicago locations to begin operating within weeks.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected Chicago to be reiterated at “late 2026 / Q1 2027”; the preview also noted an earlier “late 2026 or the first quarter of 2027” timeline.

description: Revenue was about 3% above the preview’s $356.5–356.7 million estimate, with growth of 10% rather than the expected 6.1%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to a record $368 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $356.5–356.7M” and “+6.1%.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $59 million, above the preview’s derived $55–56 million estimate, and the implied margin was about 16.0%, recovering above the expected 15.5–15.7% range. This is a stronger recovery than the base case’s expected margin stabilization.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 11% to a record $59 million” on revenue of $368 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA: ~$55–56M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~15.5%”; its base case expected the margin to “stabilize but doesn't expand.”

description: Diluted EPS was $0.15, below the preview’s $0.18 GAAP estimate despite nearly doubled net income. The call cited a $2.5 million noncash warehouse-equipment disposal charge and a $5 million noncash mark-to-market loss on earn-out shares, neither of which reduced adjusted EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS came in at $0.15”; net income was “$13 million from $7 million”; reported income included “a ~$2.5 million charge to dispose of legacy warehouse equipment and a $5 million mark-to-market loss on Class A-2 earn-out shares,” neither affecting adjusted EBITDA.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s consensus table gave “GAAP diluted EPS: $0.18.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Illinois hold-per-day increased 9% to $992 even as location and terminal counts declined modestly, a stronger hold result than the preview’s concern about possible hold-per-day deceleration. However, Illinois distributed gaming revenue growth excluding Fairmount was 6%, below the 8.3% growth cited for Q1.
fact_evidence: “Illinois distributed gaming revenue (excluding Fairmount Park) grew 6% year-over-year with average location hold-per-day up 9% to $992,” despite modest declines in location and terminal counts.
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for any hold-per-day deceleration” and cited Illinois growth of “+8.3% in Q1.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Nebraska and Georgia sustained very high growth and, according to management, became meaningful contributors to earnings growth rather than remaining only revenue-growth stories. That is better than the preview’s identified risk that their growth could normalize toward 20%.
fact_evidence: “Nebraska and Georgia posted revenue growth of 55% and 47% respectively, and are now meaningful contributors to earnings growth rather than just revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “Any sign of these normalizing to +20% resets the growth narrative.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Nevada’s rapid expansion came with a sharp decline in blended hold-per-day: revenue rose 17%, but hold-per-day fell 15.8% as locations and terminals expanded by more than 50%. The preview had flagged the need to distinguish unit growth from hold, but did not anticipate this degree of hold dilution or the 6–12 month upgrade transition.
fact_evidence: “Nevada revenue grew 17% year-over-year with locations and terminals up 54% and 53%, but blended hold-per-day fell 15.8%” due to rapid convenience-store expansion; a “6- to 12-month upgrade transition” is underway.
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Distinguish price/hold from unit adds — unit-driven growth is lower quality.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Reported operating cash flow was only $20 million, or 34% of EBITDA, which tempers the preview’s expectation that lower capex would produce a meaningful free-cash-flow inflection. Management said conversion would have been $37 million, or 63%, excluding a $17 million green tax credit purchase that shifts cash into Q3.
