expectation_evidence: The preview estimated SG&A of “6.4” million and described it as “flat” year over year.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The active selling pipeline reached $140 million, far above the preview’s reference point of roughly $24–25 million for Q1 and its expectation that the pipeline would hold above $24 million. The reported pipeline was also up about 33% sequentially.
fact_evidence: “The active selling project pipeline reached a record $140 million, up approximately 33% sequentially, boosted by Midwest's addition and legacy momentum.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 pipeline of “$24–25M” and set the bar at “Pipeline holds >$24M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company converted 17 commercial opportunities, below the preview’s bar of at least 25 wins. However, the 26% conversion rate was above the cited industry benchmark, making the reported conversion picture mixed rather than uniformly weak.
fact_evidence: “The company converted 17 commercial opportunities across 13 customers worth approximately $5.8 million in annualized revenue at a 26% conversion rate, above the industry benchmark of 10%-15%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 bar was “wins ≥25”; it also cited Q1 conversion of 22%.

description: Management said to expect moderate gross-margin contraction in Q4, whereas the preview’s model required substantial margin recovery in the second half to support its low-20s full-year margin framing. The call facts do not say whether management reaffirmed or changed a full-year margin target.
fact_evidence: “Management guided investors to expect moderate gross margin contraction in Q4 due to seasonal patterns and custom manufacturing program turnover, consistent with 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said H2 needed “~25%” gross margin to average “low 20s” for FY revenue, and flagged whether management would reaffirm “FY26 ‘low 20s’ gross margin language.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended at $28.1 million, below the preview’s roughly $32 million estimate. The reported uses included the acquisition, $6.9 million of repurchases, and $7.7 million used by operations; total liquidity remained about $46 million with no revolver borrowings.
fact_evidence: “Cash fell about $29.5 million from year-end to $28.1 million, driven by the Midwest acquisition, $6.9 million in share repurchases, and $7.7 million used by operations, leaving roughly $46 million total liquidity with no revolver borrowings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated ending cash of “~32” million.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The cash conversion cycle lengthened by 12 days to 75 days, and management set an initial improvement target rather than reporting that working-capital efficiency had already improved. The preview did not flag this metric or set an expectation for it.
fact_evidence: “The cash conversion cycle increased 12 days to 75 days,” with an initial target of a “5-day improvement worth roughly $1 million-$1.5 million in cash,” aiming toward 70 days.

description: Zeta reported $443 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $433–440 million whisper range and $23 million, or 5%, above company guidance. The result was stronger than the base case, though below the preview’s $445 million low end for its bull scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $443 million” and “beat[] guidance by $23 million (5%).”
expectation_evidence: “Derived whisper: $433–440M revenue” and the bull scenario projected “$445–455M.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $92 million, about $5.5 million above the preview’s roughly $86.5 million expectation. The 20.7% margin itself was within the previewed 20.4–20.8% guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million” and came in “$5 million above the guidance midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$86.5M” and company guidance of “$86.2–86.9M (20.4–20.8%).”

description: The FY revenue midpoint rose by $33 million to $1.818 billion—an increase larger than the roughly $22.5 million Q2 beat against the guidance midpoint. That exceeds the preview’s explicitly cautious “flow-through” case, even though the new midpoint is within its $1.80–1.82 billion base-case range and below its $1.83 billion bull threshold.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint was raised $33 million to $1.818 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Raising FY by exactly the Q2 beat (a ‘flow-through’ raise) is management signaling caution on H2”; the base case was “FY to ~$1.80–1.82B.”

description: FY free-cash-flow guidance increased to $255 million, materially above the roughly $235 million level the preview expected. The $20 million raise was not just a continuation of the preview’s expected Q2 margin performance.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow [guidance] raised $20 million to $255 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY guidance implied “$234.5–235.5M FCF.”

description: FY adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised by $8 million to $405 million. The preview focused on Q2 EBITDA and expected margin progression, but did not anticipate or quantify this full-year guidance increase.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance [was] raised $8 million to $405 million.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Superscale customer and ARPU growth both came in at 17%, below the preview’s expectation that the two measures would continue compounding at about 20%. ARPU still increased to $1.8 million, so this was a modest shortfall from the anticipated pace rather than a decline.
fact_evidence: “Superscale customers grew 17% year-over-year to 197 and superscale ARPU rose 17% to $1.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the two legs were “compounding ~20%” and flagged “super-scaled ARPU growth ≥20%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Sales pipeline growth was unusually strong: total pipeline was up more than 60%, and pipeline creation per seller more than doubled, while quota-carrying headcount grew only 11%. The preview did not flag this sales-productivity acceleration.
fact_evidence: “Total sales pipeline was up more than 60% year-over-year and over $100 million higher than 90 days ago, with per-seller pipeline creation up more than 100%, while quota-carrying headcount rose only 11%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Expansion activity was strong across several measures: more customers adopted multiple use cases, cross-sell and upsell wins increased, and average contract values on won deals rose sharply. These operating results were not part of the preview’s stated expectations.
fact_evidence: “Customers using more than one use case grew 90% year-over-year, cross-sell/upsell deals won rose 43%, and average contract values on deals won increased more than 40%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AI adopters showed substantially higher retention: the 20% of customers that comprehensively adopted the tools generated about 70% of revenue, with year-to-date net revenue retention 400 basis points above the company average. The preview discussed AI partnerships and product monetization but did not anticipate these adoption and retention figures.
fact_evidence: “The 20% of customers who comprehensively adopted AI tools account for roughly 70% of revenue” and have “year-to-date net revenue retention 400 basis points above the company average.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company reported early Palantir-sourced commercial traction, with two of two such deals closed, and said the OpenAI, Palantir, and Snowflake partnerships are largely excluded from guidance. The preview looked for a named joint enterprise client; the supplied call facts report closed Palantir-sourced deals but do not identify a named joint client.
fact_evidence: “Newly announced partnerships with OpenAI, Palantir, and Snowflake are largely excluded from guidance, with Palantir-sourced deals achieving a 100% hit rate (two of two closed).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “first joint enterprise client” was expected this quarter and that a “named signed logo is the single biggest upside surprise available.”

description: AI costs were kept below 1% of revenue while unit AI costs fell nearly 40%, a favorable cost-efficiency detail the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Total AI costs kept under 1% of revenue as unit AI costs fell nearly 40%.”

description: FY GAAP EPS guidance rose to a $0.10 midpoint, above the previous $0.02–0.04 range, with potential additional upside from a one-time tax benefit excluded. The preview expected positive FY GAAP income but did not anticipate this higher guidance level or the excluded potential benefit.
fact_evidence: “Full-year GAAP EPS guidance was raised to a $0.10 midpoint, well above the prior $0.02-$0.04 range, excluding potential additional upside from a onetime tax benefit later this year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY26 is guided to positive GAAP net income.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview treated the DHA relationship as unresolved and said there was no public confirmation of a new direct contract. Amwell reported that DHA had issued an intent to award it a sole-source direct contract, though negotiations remain ongoing and the final agreement and scope are not settled.
fact_evidence: “The Defense Health Agency issued an intent to award a sole-source direct contract to Amwell (one of five distinct vendors),” expected to be a “three-to-five year agreement”; negotiations are ongoing, with “potential for expanded, higher-revenue services.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said it found “no public Amwell announcement confirming the new direct contract” and described the renewal as “unresolved.” Its bull case was a direct contract signed with behavioral-health expansion; its base case was a transition expected shortly without a signed direct contract.

description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was about $1 million, substantially better than the roughly $3 million consensus loss and the company’s prior guide midpoint of a $3 million loss. The result was also much closer to break-even than the preview’s expected range suggested.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to approximately $1 million, the closest to break-even in company history.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 adjusted EBITDA consensus of “~−$3M (guide midpoint)” and company guidance of “−$4M to −$2M.”

description: Revenue of $52 million exceeded the preview’s $49.9 million consensus estimate, although it remained within the company’s prior $48–52 million guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $52 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus of “$49.9M” and company guidance of “$48–52M.”

description: Subscription revenue was $25.7 million and rose 3.2% sequentially, beating the preview’s roughly $24.5 million threshold for evidence that the decline was bottoming. It was still down sharply year over year, but the sequential direction was better than the preview’s base-case expectation of a modest sequential decline.
fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue at $25.7 million (down 36.5% YoY but up 3.2% sequentially).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a sequential print “at or above ~$24.5M” would be the best evidence the reset was bottoming, while its base scenario anticipated subscription “down modestly Q/Q.”

description: AMG visit revenue grew only 7.4% year over year, well below the preview’s estimated 25% growth. Flat visit volume meant the increase came from higher revenue per visit rather than visit growth.
fact_evidence: “AMG visit revenue rose 7.4% YoY to $24.4 million on flat visit volume (~315,000), driven by revenue per visit increasing ~6% to $77.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated AMG visit revenue growth of “+25%” and flagged it as a growth engine, while warning to watch for payer volume seasonality or rate pressure.

description: Amwell raised the low end of its 2026 revenue guidance by $5 million, from $195 million to $200 million, rather than leaving the range unchanged as the preview’s base case anticipated. The upper end remained $205 million.
fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $200 million-$205 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY2026 guidance of “$195–205M” and said its base case was “FY $195–205M reaffirmed unchanged.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The Q2-end balance sheet was stronger than the preview’s latest figures: cash and marketable securities were $196 million with no debt, versus the preview’s Q1 figures of $179 million and about $4 million of debt.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $196 million in cash and marketable securities and zero debt.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported “$179M cash/investments, ~$4M debt” as of the last reported Q1 balance sheet.

description: Management gave a specific longer-term gross-margin outlook that the preview had not flagged: roughly 1,000 basis points of improvement by Q4 2027, attributed to a shift toward subscription revenue. Current gross margin was 53%, down slightly year over year but up sequentially.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 53% (down ~50 bps YoY but up ~200 bps sequentially), with management projecting roughly 1,000 basis points of margin improvement by Q4 2027 driven by subscription mix shift.”

description: Management disclosed plans to divest non-core assets and consolidate around a single platform, a strategic action not discussed in the preview. The facts provided do not specify the assets, timing, or financial effects.
fact_evidence: Management is “planning to divest non-core assets and consolidate around a single platform.”

description: Atomera reported Q2 revenue of $158,000, versus the preview’s roughly $75,000 consensus and $50,000–$100,000 company guide. That is more than twice consensus and above the guide’s high end, with revenue primarily from wafer delivery fees to its large IDM customer.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was only $158,000, consisting primarily of wafer delivery fees to Atomera's large IDM customer.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$75K (co. guide $50K–$100K)”

description: The quarterly loss was worse than expected: non-GAAP loss was $0.17 per share versus the preview’s $0.13 loss estimate, and GAAP loss was $0.17 per share versus its $0.15 model. The non-GAAP shortfall was about four cents per share.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $6.3 million ($0.17 per share) … while non-GAAP loss grew to $5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP) | –$0.13”; “EPS (GAAP) | … –$0.15”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Atomera cleared a significant manufacturability milestone with one of its two active GAA customers, a step beyond the preview’s expectation that both customers would still be progressing toward results. The path to license talks remains conditional, however: they could begin as early as late 2026 or slip roughly nine months if more testing is needed.
fact_evidence: “Atomera cleared a significant manufacturability milestone with one of two active gate-all-around customers,” with license negotiations potentially beginning “as early as late 2026” or slipping “roughly 9 months” if additional test rounds are required.
expectation_evidence: “Both GAA customers still ‘progressing,’ results still ~1–2 quarters out”; the preview also described a roughly six-month timeline to full electrical results.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Atomera introduced a NAND flash opportunity that the preview did not identify: management said it could more than double MST’s total addressable market because NAND ships more wafers annually than DRAM. This is a substantial potential expansion, though the reported fact is an opportunity rather than a commercial agreement.
fact_evidence: “The company opened an entirely new market opportunity in NAND flash memory,” which “could more than double MST's total addressable market since NAND ships more wafers annually than DRAM.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The GaN-on-silicon RF results were more specific and technically striking than the preview’s expectation of merely encouraging GaN commentary: the breakthrough showed roughly 1,000x better linearity at the benchmark drive level and 2–3 orders of magnitude improvement across the full power range. The results also point toward integrated RF front ends and a possible power-amplifier market, but no commercialization partner or revenue model is reported in the facts.
fact_evidence: “Linearity roughly 1,000x better than the GaN-on-silicon reference at benchmark drive level, with 2-3 orders of magnitude improvement across the full power range”; the results “approach trap-rich RF-SOI performance on a low-cost silicon substrate” and could support power amplifiers.
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “encouraging GaN language, no counterparty” and called for a “named partner, foundry engagement, or a wafer-product revenue model with timing.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: AI-driven movement toward vertical/3D memory architectures prompted Atomera to develop a new 4F2 DRAM value proposition, which multiple customers validated and an IEEE conference accepted. The preview mentioned memory as a potential wafer-product path but did not anticipate this specific DRAM repositioning or validation.
fact_evidence: “AI-driven demand pushed manufacturers toward vertical/3D architectures,” prompting a “new 4F2 DRAM value proposition validated with multiple customers and accepted for an IEEE conference in September.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and short-term investments ended Q2 at $38.4 million, above the preview’s estimated $36–$37 million exit balance. The preview modeled $4.5–$5.0 million of quarterly burn, while management reported $3.9 million of cash used in operations.
fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and short-term investments declined to $38.4 million … from $41.1 million at March 31, with $3.9 million of cash used in operations during Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash + ST investments … ~$36–37M exiting Q2”; the preview estimated “~$4.5–5.0M” cash burn per quarter.

description: FY2026 non-GAAP operating expense guidance moved to the high end of the $18.25–$18.75 million range, above the preview’s $18.5 million reaffirmed figure. The increase is modest, but management also warned of significant structural cost increases in 2027 from tool leases, metrology, and fabrication, a cost risk the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating expense guidance to the high end of its $18.25-$18.75 million range” and warned of “significant structural cost increases from tool leases, metrology and fabrication that will hit more heavily in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP opex | $18.5M FY26 reaffirmed”; the preview also expected “Opex reaffirmed.”

description: Atomera did not win the PowerAmerica GaN power program, an unanticipated setback. Its stated value was only about $300,000, limiting the size of the direct financial impact.
fact_evidence: “Atomera did not win the PowerAmerica GaN power program (worth only ~$300,000).”

description: The preview highlighted possible STMicroelectronics re-engagement as a key catalyst, but the call produced no new update on that relationship. That leaves the potential re-engagement unconfirmed rather than delivering the formal progress the preview identified as a positive outcome.
fact_evidence: “No new updates on its STMicroelectronics relationship.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “STMicroelectronics re-engagement” as a key metric and said “Formal re-engagement on a new product line” would look good.

description: AMD guided Q3 revenue to about $13 billion, above the preview’s roughly $12.5 billion consensus and at the preview’s bull-case threshold. That is a meaningful upward guide rather than the merely modest beat in the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $13 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3'26 revenue guide” consensus was “$12.5–12.53B”; the preview’s bull case was “≥$13.0B.”

description: Data Center revenue of $6.7 billion exceeded the preview’s roughly $6.5 billion published consensus, but fell just short of the $6.75 billion buy-side bar the preview said was needed for a genuine beat. The result therefore beat consensus without clearing the higher whisper threshold.
fact_evidence: “Data center segment revenue grew 107% year-over-year to a record $6.7 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$6.5B” consensus and said “the buy-side needs a $6.75B+ handle on Data Center for the print to read as a genuine beat.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview identified September as the expected timing for initial Helios shipments, but AMD described the platform as entering production this quarter with shipments ramping through Q4 and into 2027. That did not confirm the expected September shipment timing and points to a later ramp.
fact_evidence: “Helios rack-scale platform is entering production this quarter with initial shipments ramping through Q4 into 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Helios was “in full production with initial shipments guided for September, ramping through Q4.”

description: AMD said total Data Center revenue in FY2027 will more than double, with AI growth potentially well over 100%. The preview highlighted a more-than-70% server CPU growth outlook but did not anticipate this stronger total-segment and AI-growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “AMD guided full-year 2027 server CPU revenue to grow more than 70% year-over-year and total data center segment revenue to more than double, with management hinting actual data center AI growth could be ‘well over 100%.’”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management raised its long-term market estimates for both AI accelerators and server CPUs, introducing substantially larger market opportunities than the preview had quantified. The preview did not provide prior TAM figures to compare with the new estimates.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its market outlook, now expecting the data center AI accelerator TAM to reach ~$1.4 trillion by 2030 (over 45% annual growth) and the server CPU TAM to reach ~$220 billion (over 50% annual growth).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said customer demand for Helios is ahead of its initial forecasts, an upside demand signal the preview did not identify as an expectation.
fact_evidence: “Management said customer demand is tracking ahead of initial forecasts.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: AMD said it is planning for a softer PC market in the second half, adding a demand-related headwind beyond the component-cost concerns the preview flagged for PC and Gaming.
fact_evidence: “Management is planning for a softer PC market in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “higher component costs hitting PC/Gaming in H2'26” and said to watch for an H2 margin caveat.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Embedded revenue was within the preview’s expected range, but AMD also said it is tracking toward more than $18 billion in new design wins for the year, a forward-looking metric the preview did not discuss.
fact_evidence: “Embedded revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $977 million … with the company tracking toward more than $18 billion in new design wins for the year.”

description: Q2 revenue was about $651 million, above the preview’s $624–630 million consensus range and even its $645 million bull-case threshold. The roughly 10% sequential increase also exceeded management’s previously indicated ~5% sequential lift.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $651 million” and “rising 10% sequentially from Q1.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “~$624–630M”; the preview said management’s sequential steer was “~5% sequential lift” to “~$622M,” and its bull scenario was “$645M+.”

description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.62, above the preview’s coherent consensus estimate of about $2.46 and contrary to the preview’s expectation of a year-over-year decline. It was also slightly above the prior-year $2.61.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.62 versus $2.61 in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP EPS consensus at “~$2.46” and described it as “~ -6%” year over year.

description: Operating margin reached 12.5%, above the preview’s estimated 10–11% and the 10.5–11.5% base case. The preview identified the required margin recovery from Q1 as a key risk, so this was a stronger Q2 recovery than expected.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 12.5%,” compared with 6.6% in Q1 2026.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~10–11%” operating margin and gave a base case of “10.5–11.5%”; it said Q2–Q4 needed to average “~12.3%.”

description: Clinical Diagnostics returned to growth and rose 8.3% on a currency-neutral basis, substantially stronger than the preview’s bull-case operational assumption of roughly flat Clinical Diagnostics currency-neutral sales. This stands out against the preview’s concern about the Middle East drag on the segment.
fact_evidence: “The Clinical Diagnostics segment returned to growth with sales of $399 million,” up “8.3% currency-neutral.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said its bull case required “Clinical Diagnostics CN back to roughly flat” and highlighted the Middle East as a significant revenue and margin headwind.

description: The company announced a restructuring with quantified annual savings, margin benefits, and a sizable one-time cost. A named program was anticipated, but the call supplied specific targets: $30–35 million of annualized net savings, 40–50 basis points of 2027 operating-margin expansion, and about $90 million of one-time cost.
fact_evidence: The restructuring is expected to deliver “$30-$35 million in annualized net cost savings” and “roughly 40-50 bps of operating margin expansion in 2027,” with a “~$90 million one-time cost.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “formal restructuring announcement would be read as credible” and asked whether management would provide a “named cost/restructuring program.”

description: Digital PCR grew 6% currency-neutral and instrument revenue rose more than 20%, but consumables declined slightly and pull-through remained below expectations. That leaves the overall growth story intact while revealing weaker consumable demand than expected.
fact_evidence: “Digital PCR (ddPCR) revenue grew 6% currency-neutral with instrument revenue up more than 20%, though consumables revenue declined slightly year-over-year with pull-through still below expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Pull-through still below expectations.”

description: China, about 6% of revenue, declined in the high teens and is expected to create a further $4 million headwind for the rest of the year. The preview did not flag this China-specific weakness or quantified future drag.
fact_evidence: “China, representing about 6% of total revenue, declined in the high teens due to order timing and life science softness, creating an estimated $4 million headwind for the remainder of the year.”

description: Management confirmed active, constructive engagement with Elliott and broad alignment on execution, capital allocation, and closing the value gap. The preview’s base case anticipated no strategic news; however, the call announced no specific Sartorius monetization action, only that the stake is monetizable at the right time and price.
fact_evidence: Management confirmed “active, constructive engagement” with Elliott, citing “broad alignment” on priorities, and reiterated the Sartorius stake is “monetizable at the right time and price.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case specified “no strategic news”; it also said Elliott had not published specific demands or a public letter.

description: Revenue was $156.3M, about 7% below the $167.8M consensus and below the preview’s $166M base estimate. The decline was steeper than the preview’s base-case expectation, though within its bear-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue declined approximately 9% year-over-year to $156.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $167.8M” consensus; preview base case: “Revenue $166M.” Its bear scenario was “$154–158M (–8 to –10%).”

description: Product revenue fell to $71.3M, down 22% year-over-year—substantially weaker than the preview’s roughly $80M base estimate and expectation of a 10–13% decline. The reported pressure came from lower volumes, promotional pricing, and a lower-priced machine mix.
fact_evidence: “Product revenue fell 22% year-over-year to $71.3 million due to lower volumes, promotional pricing, and a lower-priced machine mix.”
expectation_evidence: Preview base case: “Products $80M (–12%).” It also described the base case as “Products –10 to –13%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Despite the weak product revenue, global cutting-machine sellout and sell-in units both grew double digits, rather than showing the feared stalled transition. The preview identified Q2 as the first clean sell-through quarter for Joy 2 and Explore 5 and warned that the bundle transition could stall.
fact_evidence: “Global cutting machine sellout units and sell-in units both grew double digits, aided by an earlier Prime Day and the new Joy 2 and Explore 5 bundles.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 was “the first clean sell-through quarter” and described a bear case where “Bundle-only transition stalls at retail.”

description: The reported 19-cent EPS and 30.3% operating margin were far above the preview’s 6–7-cent buy-side EPS bar and 10.6% base-case operating margin, but the headline results were inflated by unexpected one-time benefits. Even excluding those items, operating income was about $23M and operating margin 14.7%, above the preview’s $17.5M and 10.6% estimates.
fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $39.1 million (19 cents per diluted share)”; gross margin was “inflated by $17.9 million in IEPA tariff refunds and a $6.4 million royalty settlement reserve release”; excluding one-time items, “operating income would have been about $23 million versus the reported $47.4 million, and operating margin 14.7% versus the reported 30.3%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview put the realistic buy-side EPS bar at “$0.06–0.07, not $0.04”; its base estimate was “Op. income $17.5M (10.6%) · EPS $0.06.” It expected gross margin around “57.0%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Paid subscribers were just over 3.1M, ahead of the preview’s 3.05–3.08M watch range, and platform revenue of $85M was essentially in line with the $85.5M base estimate. Subscriber growth therefore held up better than the preview’s concern about seasonal softness and a possible sequential decline.
fact_evidence: “Platform revenue grew just over 5% to $85 million,” with paid subscribers increasing “93,000 (over 3%) year-over-year to just over 3.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited paid subscribers of “3.05–3.08M” as the key range and a base-case Platform estimate of “$85.5M (+6%).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at $286M, above the preview’s roughly $250M balance-sheet reference, and the company was debt-free despite the preview listing about $11M of debt. The preview had also highlighted the prior decline in cash, while the call reported $50.4M of quarterly operating cash flow and a $19M inventory reduction.
fact_evidence: “The company generated $50.4 million in cash from operations,” ended the quarter “with $286 million in cash,” “remained debt-free,” and “reduced inventory by $19 million to $106 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “~$250M cash, ~$11M debt” and noted cash had fallen from “~$298M (Q2'25) to $236.5M (Q1'26).”

description: The preview identified a buyback upsize as a likely capital-return lever and called it a possible positive surprise, but the call reported $7.5M of repurchases and $21.6M still available under the existing authorization, without reporting an upsize. The regular $0.10 semiannual dividend, by contrast, was consistent with the preview’s expectation of no special dividend.
fact_evidence: “Cricut repurchased 1.7 million shares for $7.5 million (leaving $21.6 million of the $50 million authorization), paid a $0.10 semiannual dividend.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a buyback upsize is the more likely capital-return lever” and listed a buyback upsize as an “underappreciated positive surprise”; it also said “a second consecutive year without a special is now the base case.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $12.12, $0.08 below the preview’s $12.20 consensus. The reported result therefore fell slightly short of the expected headline, despite adjusted EPS being reported up 21% year over year.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $12.12 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS: $12.20”; the preview says this consensus tracks adjusted EPS.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Core market share recovered to 4.9% for the first two months of Q2 from 4.5% in the first two months of Q1, although it remained below the year-ago 5.3%. The preview highlighted share loss as a key issue but did not anticipate this rebound.
fact_evidence: “Core segment market share … was 4.9% for the first two months of the quarter, down from 5.3% a year ago but recovered from a Q4 2024 low of 4.4%.”
expectation_evidence: “Market share fell to 4.5% (Jan–Feb 2026) from 5.2% a year earlier”; the preview called the volume and market-share trajectory a key question.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The 2025 vintage underperformed modestly but remained within 10 basis points of its initial forecast, and the 2022 vintage was stable. That is a contained vintage update amid the preview’s focus on credit deterioration and forecast revisions, though the preview gave no specific expected performance for these vintages.
fact_evidence: “The 2025 loan vintage experienced modest underperformance during the quarter but remains within 10 basis points of its initial forecast, while the 2022 vintage stayed stable through the first half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged forecast revisions and vintage performance as swing factors, and noted record subprime delinquencies; it did not state a specific expected result for the 2025 or 2022 vintages.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The provision forecast change was $82 million even though the decline in forecasted net cash flows was $39 million; the gap was attributed mainly to prepayments continuing to run slower than forecast for several quarters. The preview discussed forecast revisions and their effect on provisions, but did not anticipate this specific gap or its persistent prepayment explanation.
fact_evidence: “The provision forecast change was $82 million versus a $39 million undiscounted cash flow decline, with the roughly $43 million gap driven mainly by prepayments continuing to come in slower than forecast for several consecutive quarters.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said forecast revisions drive provision and asked whether the mild Q1 revision would hold or move toward the larger revisions seen in 2024–25; it gave no expected provision-to-cash-flow gap.

description: Compass reported $4.3 billion of Q2 revenue, above the $4.0–$4.2 billion guidance range and the preview’s $4.06–$4.11 billion consensus band. Pro forma growth of 14.3% also far exceeded the preview’s +4–6% organic-growth base case.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $4.3 billion,” up “14.3% year-over-year on a pro forma basis” and “exceeding the high end of guidance of $4.0-$4.2 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 revenue consensus of “$4.06–4.11B” and said “Q2 organic revenue growth of +4–6% would be a reasonable base case.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded even the top of the previewed guidance range, despite the preview identifying synergy capture as the central test of the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA hit a record $363 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$310–350M” and consensus of “~$330M (guide mid),” with the key metric ranked against “$310–350M.”

description: Compass actioned its $300 million year-1 synergy target five months ahead of plan and raised its 2026 actioned-synergy expectation to $330 million. That is ahead of the preview’s $300 million actioned baseline, though short of its $200 million FY realized-synergy target at roughly $150 million realized through the P&L.
fact_evidence: “Compass actioned its entire $300 million year-1 cost synergy target five months ahead of plan and now expects to action $330 million in 2026, with ~$150 million realized through the P&L.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$200M realized / $300M actioned” and said the Q2 guide assumed “~$40M of P&L synergies” in the quarter, “of $200M FY realized target.” It also identified a third raise above $325 million actioned as a potential upside catalyst.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was substantially better than the preview’s near-breakeven expectation, adding to cash rather than merely avoiding a cash burn.
fact_evidence: Cash on hand rose “$210 million quarter-over-quarter to $694 million, driven by $180 million of free cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 free cash flow to be “~breakeven” and cited management’s outlook of “close to breakeven or slightly negative.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Leverage improved sharply during the quarter, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA falling by nearly a full turn; management also expects the ratio to reach the 2s by year-end.
fact_evidence: “Net debt to adjusted EBITDA improved by roughly one turn quarter-over-quarter to 3.3x from 4.2x in Q1, with management expecting the ratio to reach the 2s by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the debt burden and deleveraging path, citing “$3.14B” of long-term debt and saying the path depended on FY26 free cash flow being positive, but did not forecast this quarter’s leverage improvement.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Compass’s GTV outperformance widened substantially: growth was about 16% against a market up 6%, roughly 1,000 basis points of outperformance and an acceleration from Q1’s roughly 600 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Brokerage GTV grew ~16% year-over-year versus a market up 6%, reflecting roughly 1,000 basis points of outperformance, an acceleration from ~600 basis points in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 pro forma GTV growth of “+7.3%” versus a market up “+1.5%” and described continued share gains as a key proof point.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Agent retention improved to 95.5% despite the preview’s focus on post-merger attrition and the technology migration as a major integration risk.
fact_evidence: “Total agent retention improved to 95.5% from 94.1% in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “94% retention” as the Q1 baseline and said post-merger attrition was “the core integration risk,” warning that “any sequential agent decline is a red flag.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call described especially strong Bay Area performance in the standalone Compass brand, including a high-end sales indicator not highlighted in the preview’s broader discussion of luxury demand.
fact_evidence: “Bay Area revenue in the Compass standalone brand rose 19% year-over-year in both July and August,” and “140 San Francisco homes [closed] $1M+ above asking in H1 versus just eight a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said luxury holding up was a condition for its bull case, but did not forecast this Bay Area growth or the increase in San Francisco homes closing more than $1 million above asking.

description: Management quantified a much larger earnings scenario if the housing market recovers: $2.5 billion of adjusted EBITDA at 6 million home sales, alongside tax protection from NOLs. The preview had discussed the $1 billion flat-market scenario, but not this higher-volume case or the NOL tax shield.
fact_evidence: “The scenario analysis projects $1 billion in adjusted EBITDA at a flat 4.1 million home sales market, scaling to $2.5 billion at 6 million home sales, with $1.8 billion of NOLs shielding roughly $470 million of future cash taxes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to listen for management framing a “$1B EBITDA / $750M unlevered FCF scenario (at flat 4.1M existing-home sales)” as a 2027 base or aspiration; it did not mention the $2.5 billion scenario or the NOL shield.

description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.84, below the preview’s $1.09 consensus estimate and below its $1.05–$1.20 base-case range. The preview’s guidance-bridge math also implied roughly $1.22 per quarter for Q2–Q4, making the reported quarter weaker than that pace.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $19 million ($0.84 per share) in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.09” consensus; base scenario: “Adj. EPS $1.05–1.20”; the guidance bridge implies “~$1.22/quarter” across Q2–Q4.

description: Instead of the preview’s base case of normalized Portfolio Management marks, negative fair-value adjustments helped drive a $29 million GAAP net loss. The $84 million of negative adjustments included a $24 million non-cash charge on convertible notes tied to the roughly $11 share-price increase.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP net loss of $29 million,” driven by “$84 million in negative fair value adjustments,” including “a $24 million non-cash charge on convertible notes tied to an ~$11 per share stock price increase.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “Portfolio Management marks normalize”; the preview also described negative marks as a bear-case risk.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A $42 million non-cash benefit from releasing the deferred-tax-asset valuation allowance boosted results, an item the preview did not anticipate. Management said the effective tax rate should be more normalized going forward, so the benefit is not a recurring earnings tailwind.
fact_evidence: “A $42 million non-cash tax benefit from releasing the deferred tax asset valuation allowance boosted results,” and management “guided to a more normalized effective tax rate going forward.”

description: Management disclosed that the acquired $5.2 billion HECM MSR portfolio, with roughly $70 million of book value, is expected to earn a mid-teens yield and contribute to the P&L in the second half. The preview expected essentially no Q2 contribution and said the amount of Q3-onward accretion had not yet been disclosed; the yield and timing provide new, favorable detail.
fact_evidence: The acquired portfolio has “a book value of roughly $70 million,” is “expected to earn a mid-teens yield” and is “flowing through the P&L in the second half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 should show essentially zero P&L contribution”; “The number that matters is management's quantification of Q3-onward accretion ... neither has been disclosed.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Retail showed pronounced productivity gains: funded loans rose 33%, submissions rose 19%, and funded loans per call-center loan officer increased nearly 30% sequentially despite stable sales capacity. The preview looked for pipeline conversion and durable funnel gains but did not anticipate these specific operating-leverage figures.
fact_evidence: “Retail channel showed strong operating leverage with funded loans up 33%, submissions up 19%, and funded loans per call center loan officer increasing nearly 30% sequentially on stable sales capacity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case needed the Q1 submission cohort to convert and durable funnel gains, but gave no expectation for these retail productivity results.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company generated substantial cash from originations and capital-markets activity—$58 million in Q2 and about $116 million in the first half—despite the preview’s focus on the all-cash Onity acquisition as a draw on liquidity. The preview did not forecast this source of cash generation.
fact_evidence: “The company generated $58 million in cash from originations and capital markets activities in Q2 and approximately $116 million in the first half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted the Onity deal was “all-cash” and said the outlay and the Blackstone repurchase “both draw on the same liquidity.”

description: Management disclosed that the HECM MSR asset value was $326 million with only $46 million of financing, or roughly 14% leverage, and said it intends to increase that financing to unlock flexibility. This low leverage and plan to expand it were not discussed in the preview’s capital outlook.
fact_evidence: “The HECM MSR adjusted net asset value totaled $326 million as of June 30 with only $46 million of financing (roughly 14% leverage), which management intends to increase to unlock financial flexibility.”

description: DaVita reiterated FY26 guidance at a $2.2 billion adjusted operating income midpoint and $14.65 adjusted EPS midpoint, rather than making the raise the preview said was largely expected. That fell short of the preview’s stated bar of roughly a $0.40-or-more EPS midpoint increase.
fact_evidence: “DaVita reconfirmed full-year 2026 guidance with a midpoint of $2.2 billion for adjusted operating income and $14.65 for adjusted EPS.”
expectation_evidence: “A raise is largely expected”; “only a midpoint raise of ~$0.40+ on adj. EPS clears the bar.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Treatment growth was stronger than the preview’s full-year range and Q2 volume watchpoint implied: treatments grew 56 basis points year over year, above the 25–50 basis-point full-year range, and management now expects growth near its top end. The preview looked for the second Fresenius transfer tranche to drive Q2 volume, whereas management attributed the growth primarily to sustained mortality improvement.
fact_evidence: “U.S. dialysis treatments grew 56 basis points versus Q2 2025,” and management expects full-year growth “near the top end of its 25-50 basis point range, driven primarily by sustained mortality improvement.”
expectation_evidence: “FY guide: +50–75 bps per normalized day (+25–50 bps total treatments)”; “the remaining half [of Fresenius clinic-closure patient transfers] expected in Q2.”

description: Patient-care costs were not tracking the preview’s expected full-year range: despite a roughly $3 sequential decline per treatment, year-to-date costs grew more than 3%, above the expected 1.25%–2.25% full-year growth range.
fact_evidence: “Patient care cost per treatment declined about $3 sequentially, though year-to-date PCCs grew more than 3% versus the first half of 2025, above the expected full-year growth range of 1.25%-2.25%.”
expectation_evidence: “Patient care cost per treatment” was flagged as a key metric; the preview said it had “held flat” in Q1 and warned that an upward inflection would threaten margins.

description: The quarter’s earnings were a modest beat against the preview’s estimate: adjusted operating income was $579 million versus its roughly $570–575 million estimate, and adjusted EPS of $4.02 was just above even the contested $4.01 high-end consensus. The beat was limited relative to the preview’s roughly $580 million base case.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted operating income was $579 million, adjusted EPS was $4.02,” with enterprise OI “up about 5% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS … $3.88” with a contested range of “$3.88–$4.01”; adjusted OI estimate “~$570–575M”; base scenario “~$580M.”

description: DaVita disclosed a larger ACA-related commercial-mix headwind for 2027 than the preview had quantified: the expected impact is $70 million, versus $40 million in 2026. The preview discussed the $40 million 2026 headwind but did not flag a larger 2027 amount.
fact_evidence: “The declining commercial mix from ACA enrollment is expected to create a $40 million headwind in 2026 and a larger $70 million headwind in 2027, largely from new patients entering at lower commercial mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Management sized the ACA headwind at ~$40M.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management reported adverse reimbursement-policy developments not raised in the preview: the proposed 2027 ESRD base-rate increase still trails industry cost trends, and CMS cut its phosphate-binder spending estimate by nearly $500 million. These developments add pressure to future reimbursement and binder-related revenue expectations.
fact_evidence: “The proposed 2027 ESRD payment rule again includes a base rate increase that tracks below industry cost trends, and CMS has cut its phosphate binder spend estimate by nearly $500 million.”

description: IKC produced a $40 million adjusted operating income upside versus expectations, but management attributed it to revenue timing, making the quarterly beat less indicative of ongoing performance than the headline suggests.
fact_evidence: “IKC delivered $40 million of adjusted operating income above expectations due to revenue timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described IKC’s “Q1 operating loss of $19M, on forecast” and said it was “optional[ity], not yet earnings.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: DaVita secured supply of FDA-approved expanded HD dialyzers compatible with its existing machines, an unanticipated development, but said any financial benefit from improved mortality would not begin until 2028 and would be insignificant near term.
fact_evidence: “DaVita secured supply of FDA-approved Nipro expanded HD dialyzers compatible with existing machines,” but the benefit is expected “to only begin in 2028 and remain insignificant near-term.”

description: Management newly indicated that both IKC and International are expected to contribute roughly $20 million each to full-year enterprise OI growth, identifying two sources of growth the preview had not quantified.
fact_evidence: “Both IKC and International are each expected to contribute roughly $20 million to full-year enterprise OI growth.”

description: Revenue was $386.6 million, above the preview’s $377.4 million consensus and its $380 million base estimate; average daily sales grew 9.3%, faster than the roughly 7% expectation and above the preview’s 8% upside marker.
fact_evidence: Q2 revenue grew 7.7% to $386.6 million, or 9.3% on an average daily sales basis; similar momentum continued into Q3.
expectation_evidence: Consensus net sales were $377.4M; the preview’s base estimate was $380.0M. It expected average daily sales growth of ~7% and said above 8% would be notably strong.

description: Canada accelerated to 33.7% local-currency growth, well above the preview’s recent comparison of 24.4%, while extending its run of double-digit growth for a fourth quarter.
fact_evidence: Canada revenue surged 33.7% in local currency, its fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Canada had grown 24.4% local currency in Q1 and that a fourth consecutive double-digit quarter would confirm the strategy; deceleration to single digits was its downside concern.

description: The quarter’s gross margin was 34.7%, modestly below the preview’s roughly 35.0% consensus and 35.1% base estimate. The margin decline reflected elevated transportation and fuel costs plus unfavorable product and channel mix, though it remained above the preview’s 34.5% downside threshold.
fact_evidence: Non-GAAP gross margin was 34.7%, down from 37.1%; management attributed the decline to elevated transportation/fuel costs and unfavorable product and channel mix.
expectation_evidence: The preview put gross margin at ~35% consensus and 35.1% in its base case, and said below 34.5% would be a key downside signal.

description: Management’s outlook held gross margin around 34.7%–34.8% for the rest of 2026, below the preview’s mid-35s expectation for the base case and its May-call framing.
fact_evidence: Management guided that gross margins for the balance of 2026 should remain roughly in line with the recent 34.7%–34.8% range.
expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as GM in the mid-35s and said the expected margin was around 35.0%.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Volume and mix, rather than pricing alone, supplied most of the growth, and volume improved for a third consecutive quarter. That is a stronger demand/volume signal than the preview’s concern that the prior quarter’s volume acceleration could prove one-off as pricing moderated.
fact_evidence: Pricing contributed about 4 points of growth while volume and mix drove the rest, marking the third consecutive quarter of volume improvement.
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether Q1’s ADS acceleration was a one-off and flagged that price appreciation was expected to moderate as the company lapped prior pricing actions.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company generated $41.3 million of operating cash flow, a reversal from the $4.7 million in Q1 that the preview highlighted as a working-capital concern; cash also ended above the prior-quarter $61.7 million level.
fact_evidence: The company generated $41.3 million of operating cash flow and ended the quarter with $86.7 million in cash.
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged Q1 operating cash flow of only $4.7M and said to watch for a working-capital reversal and cash versus the $61.7M exit balance.

description: Share repurchases rose to about $4.7 million, up from the $0.6 million Q1 pace the preview called conspicuously light, while the company also maintained its $0.28 quarterly dividend.
fact_evidence: The company repurchased about 160,000 shares for $4.7 million while declaring a $0.28 quarterly dividend.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted only ~22,000 shares ($0.6M) repurchased in Q1 and said to watch buyback pace; it expected no further dividend raise.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company disclosed approximately $26 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, including $21 million benefiting cost of sales, $4 million reducing inventory, and $1 million of interest income; it excluded the refunds from non-GAAP results and expects future refunds to be immaterial. The preview discussed future Section 301 duties, not a refund of this size.
fact_evidence: Approximately $26 million in IEEPA tariff refunds was recorded ($21 million benefiting cost of sales, $4 million inventory reduction, $1 million interest income), excluded from non-GAAP results; future refunds are expected to be immaterial.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported that the GPO business is on pace for roughly $100 million in annualized sales and that e-procurement connections exceeded 1,300 customers, with more than 50 added in the first half—commercial-channel momentum the preview did not address.
fact_evidence: The GPO business is on pace to reach roughly $100 million in annualized sales this year, and e-procurement connections surpassed 1,300 customers with over 50 new connections added in the first half.

description: Management said it is now building an M&A pipeline to accelerate its go-to-market strategy, an incremental strategic and capital-allocation development not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: Management is now building an M&A pipeline to accelerate its go-to-market strategy.

description: Q1 revenue came in above both the company’s range and the preview’s higher Street estimate: total revenue was $190.2 million, and service revenue was $185.3 million. The service-revenue result also exceeded the $175–$180 million company guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 total revenue was $190.2 million ... and service revenue was a record $185.3 million ... both exceeding guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $180M–$185M | ~$182.3M ... vs. ~$186.0M”; “Service revenue | $175M–$180M.”

description: Gross margin was materially below the Q1 outlook, at 61.6% versus guidance of 63.5%–64.5%. The new full-year gross-margin range of 60.5%–61.5% also signals that the weaker margin mix extends beyond the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 61.6% due to mix shift toward lower-margin usage-based offerings, and full-year gross margin guidance was set at 60.5% to 61.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin | 63.5%–64.5%.”

description: The company raised FY2027 service-revenue guidance by $18 million and lifted total-revenue guidance, but did not raise its roughly $70 million operating-income outlook or its EPS range. The higher sales outlook therefore did not translate into a higher earnings outlook.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year service revenue guidance by $18 million to $725-$745 million and total revenue to $745-$765 million, while holding operating income at roughly $70 million and EPS at $0.33-$0.38.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY2027 guidance ... Revenue $727M–$747M; non-GAAP EPS $0.33–$0.38”; the preview flagged “FY2027 full-year guidance reaffirmation/revision.”

description: Operating performance exceeded the company’s Q1 outlook: operating income was above the high end of guidance and the 9.9% margin topped the preview’s 8.5%–9.5% range. EPS of $0.09 was at the high end of company guidance but above the preview’s approximately $0.07 Street estimate; lower operating expenses, mostly in sales and marketing, helped drive the result.
fact_evidence: “Operating income reached $18.9 million (9.9% margin) above the high end of guidance, aided by operating expenses falling more than $8 million YoY, mostly in sales and marketing”; “fully diluted EPS of $0.09, at the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin | 8.5%–9.5%”; “Non-GAAP EPS (diluted) | $0.08–$0.09” and Street consensus “~$0.07.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash flow was substantially stronger than the company’s forecast, reaching $17 million against guidance of $10–$12 million.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow of $17 million significantly beat guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash flow from operations | $10M–$12M.”

description: Management guided to platform-usage growth slowing to 30%–35% in Q2 from 63% in Q1, citing a tougher comparison. The preview highlighted usage growth and its pace as a key issue, but did not anticipate this degree of near-term deceleration.
fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance calls for platform usage growth to slow to 30-35% YoY (from 63%) against a tougher comparison.”
expectation_evidence: “Platform usage revenue ... Grew >70% YoY in Q4 FY2026 and now ~23% of service revenue — pace of this shift affects both growth rate and gross margin.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call provided concrete evidence of rapid AI and product-adoption traction: AI-solution adoption grew 121%, AI Studio reached more than 200 organizations and 2,900 agents within 3.5 months, and half of those organizations were converting to paying customers. Customers using three or more products also rose 18% to about 38% of recurring revenue, more specific monetization and cross-sell evidence than the preview had quantified.
fact_evidence: “AI solution adoption grew 121% YoY, AI Studio surpassed 200 organizations and 2,900 agents within 3.5 months of launch (half converting to paying customers), while customers using 3+ products rose 18% YoY to about 38% of recurring revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said that “any early commentary on attach/monetization could move the stock,” but gave no adoption or conversion figures.

description: The term loan is due to become a current liability next quarter, and although management expressed confidence in refinancing, it gave no specifics. The preview discussed ongoing debt reduction but did not flag this near-term refinancing issue.
fact_evidence: “The term loan (maturing August 2027) will reclassify to current liabilities next quarter, and management expressed confidence in refinancing but offered no specifics.”

description: Trailing-12-month cash interest paid was down 25% to $16.6 million, a favorable financing-cost improvement that the preview had not quantified.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month cash interest paid down 25% to $16.6 million.”

description: Freshworks reported $55.9 million of non-GAAP operating income at a 24% margin, well above the preview’s roughly $42 million and 17.7–18.3% margin expectation.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income reached $55.9 million (24% margin)”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op income … ~$42M (17.7–18.3% mgn)”

description: Freshworks reached positive GAAP net income ahead of schedule, although the preview did not flag the timing of GAAP profitability as an expectation to watch.
fact_evidence: “Positive GAAP net income of $3.2 million ($0.01 GAAP EPS) ahead of schedule, having originally targeted GAAP profitability by end of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Originally targeted GAAP profitability by end of 2026.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.17, above both the $0.13 consensus and the preview’s $0.15–0.16 base-case range.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.17.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS … Consensus $0.13”; “Non-GAAP EPS … $0.15–0.16”

description: The company had deployed over $200 million on buybacks year-to-date and reduced shares outstanding by 7%, a much faster pace than the preview’s concern that buybacks were proceeding slowly after just $45.4 million had been used in Q1.
fact_evidence: “Deployed over $200 million on stock buybacks year-to-date, reducing shares outstanding by 7%.”
expectation_evidence: “$45.4M of $400M used in Q1”; “Slow pace at $12 with $780M cash invites ‘why not?’ questions.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Freddy AI Copilot attach on new deals above $30,000 exceeded 70%, above the preview’s already-high threshold of over 65%; the call also disclosed more than 7,000 paying AI customers and paid Copilot adoption by 22% of eligible EX customers.
fact_evidence: “Freddy AI Copilot attach rate on new deals above $30,000 exceeded 70%, with over 7,000 customers paying for an AI SKU and 22% of eligible EX customers now paying for Copilot.”
expectation_evidence: “>65% attach in >$30K deals.”

description: Stock-based compensation fell to 16% of revenue from 19% in Q1, an improvement the preview did not specifically anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Cut stock-based comp to 16% of revenue (down from 19% in Q1).”

description: Q2 revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million, slightly below the $68.5 million low end of guidance, rather than landing within the expected range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million ... slightly below the low end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue before reimbursements | Company Guidance ... $68.5M – $70.0M.”

description: Global S&BT declined sequentially to $35.6 million, contrary to the preview’s estimate of $37.5 million and expectation for sequential growth.
fact_evidence: “S&BT ($35.6M, down 2%)” compared with the prior quarter’s $36.4 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Global S&BT at “$37.5M” and listed its “Guided direction” as “Up seq.”

description: Oracle Solutions fell to $15.3 million, rather than rising sequentially toward the preview’s $16.2 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Oracle ($15.3M, down 1%)” and was expected to “rebound sequentially” in Q3.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Oracle Solutions at “$16.2M” and listed its “Guided direction” as “Up seq.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $68–70 million is somewhat below the preview’s base-case range of $69–71 million, even though the EPS guide supports the anticipated inflection.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue before reimbursements of $68-70 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q3 base scenario was “Rev $69–71M”; its bull scenario was “Rev ≥$71M.”

description: The Q3 gross-margin target of approximately 46–47% adds a stronger margin step-up than the preview discussed, which focused on Q2 reaching 44–45%.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance target[s] a further step-up to approximately 46-47%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 adjusted gross margin of “44% – 45%” and highlighted whether that level would be achieved.

description: SAP Solutions grew 9% sequentially to $17.4 million, substantially above the preview’s $15.5 million estimate and opposite its forecast of a sequential decline.
fact_evidence: “The SAP Solutions segment grew 9% sequentially to $17.4 million on higher software sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated SAP Solutions at “$15.5M” and listed its “Guided direction” as “Down seq.”

description: IBM deferred joint go-to-market activities, a setback to a collaboration the preview identified as part of the company’s partner and AI-platform narrative.
fact_evidence: “IBM, which launched a global go-to-market collaboration in March, has deferred joint go-to-market activities.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “the IBM go-to-market collaboration” among the initiatives that were “narrative, not numbers.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management put a number on AI-enabled delivery productivity: it estimates it is capturing about 20% of the potential today and expects to reach closer to 50% by year-end, a new operational disclosure not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Management estimates it is capturing roughly 20% of the productivity and margin potential from its AI-enabled delivery model and expects to reach closer to 50% by year-end.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company disclosed an approximately $1 million Q3 AI transition charge, primarily severance, adding a near-term cost from AI-driven headcount reductions that the preview’s base case did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “The company will incur an approximately $1 million AI transition charge in Q3, primarily for severance from headcount reductions tied to AI-driven productivity improvements.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described an “In-line quarter”; its bear case, by contrast, flagged “another AI transition charge.”

description: The company reported $4 million of Q2 buybacks and reduced net debt by $6.1 million, providing concrete capital-return and balance-sheet action rather than only the buyback activity the preview was watching for.
fact_evidence: “Net cash from operations was $15.2 million in Q2, enabling a $6.1 million net debt reduction, $4 million in stock buybacks (377,000 shares at an average $10.58), and a maintained $0.12 quarterly dividend.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Buyback activity at these levels” would be “a genuine confidence signal,” and noted the $22 million remaining authorization.

description: The company amended its credit facility to raise borrowing capacity to $125 million against $81 million of debt outstanding, a financing change the preview did not discuss.
fact_evidence: “The company amended its credit facility to increase borrowing capacity to $125 million against $81 million of total debt outstanding.”

description: Management said Q4 results should exceed prior-year levels despite significantly fewer high-margin VAR sales, extending the outlook beyond the preview’s focus on a Q3 inflection.
fact_evidence: “[The company] expects Q4 results to exceed prior-year levels despite significantly fewer high-margin VAR sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview centered on whether “Q3 is the quarter where adjusted EPS is supposed to exceed prior-year on flat revenue.”

description: Kodak’s Q2 revenue was $311 million, well above the preview’s $276 million estimate. The $35 million beat was substantially stronger than the preview’s modeled 5% year-over-year growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 18% year-over-year to $311 million from $263 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q2 2026E (my base) $276M”; “YoY +5%.”

description: Operational EBITDA reached $36 million versus the preview’s $23 million estimate. That was a much larger result than the preview’s expected continuation of the recovery.
fact_evidence: “Operational EBITDA jumped 300% to $36 million from $9 million in Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Operational EBITDA … Q2 2026E (my base) $23M”; “a $23M base is a continuation, not a heroic assumption.”

description: Advanced Materials and Chemicals grew 40%, far faster than the preview’s 9% growth estimate and its concern that growth might remain in low single digits. The reported result decisively exceeded the preview’s modeled pace.
fact_evidence: “The Advanced Materials and Chemicals segment grew revenue 40% to $105 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Advanced Materials & Chemicals … Q2 2026E (my base) $82M”; “YoY +9%.” The preview also flagged a second low-single-digit quarter as a key risk.

description: Gross profit and margin both exceeded the preview’s estimates: gross profit was $82 million rather than $63 million, and margin was 26% rather than 23%. This happened despite reported higher aluminum and silver costs, rather than the preview’s concern that raw-material costs could constrain margins.
fact_evidence: “Q2 gross profit increased 61% to $82 million, lifting gross margin to 26% from 19% a year earlier despite higher aluminum and silver commodity costs.”
