expectation_evidence: “Q2 carries a normal seasonal decline”; the preview also noted physical occupancy had “fell 290bps sequentially to 76.4% in Q1.”

description: Management said Q3 will be the toughest year-over-year comparison, with same-store NOI growth likely below Q2 levels, but projected close to flat year-over-year growth in Q4. The preview discussed the expected fading FX tailwind but did not set out this quarter-by-quarter path.
fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 2026 to be the toughest year-over-year comparison with same-store NOI growth likely below Q2 levels, while Q4 is projected to reach close to flat year-over-year same-store NOI growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FX tailwind was expected to diminish in the second half, but gave no Q3 or Q4 same-store NOI outlook.

description: The preview looked for a concrete portfolio-review deliverable; instead, Lineage described plans to divest more than $1 billion of assets and said a comprehensive review update is expected by year-end, without reporting a completed transaction. The asset-sale plan is a concrete step, but the timing of a fuller update leaves the anticipated transaction detail outstanding.
fact_evidence: “Reported leverage is approximately 6.0x versus a targeted 5.0x-5.5x range, and management plans to divest over $1 billion of assets, with a comprehensive strategic review update expected by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “portfolio review deliverable” such as an “asset sale, JV, or portfolio transaction” and said silence for a second consecutive quarter could read as inability to transact.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Lineage reported a development and ramping pipeline of 20 facilities, with $1.1 billion invested, more than $134 million of expected incremental stabilized NOI, and 71% pre-leasing—operating detail not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company has 20 facilities under construction or ramping with $1.1 billion invested, expected to deliver over $134 million of incremental stabilized NOI, and pre-leasing stands at 71%.”

description: Q2 comparable sales growth was 4.2%, well above the preview’s 1.8% consensus growth estimate. Sales of $1.8 billion also exceeded company expectations.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 4.2% on a comparable basis to $1.8 billion” and “exceeding company expectations.”

description: Primo raised its full-year comparable sales growth range to 2%–4%, rather than simply holding the prior 1%–3% range the preview said was likely safe. This was the second consecutive quarterly increase.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 comparable net sales growth guidance for a second consecutive quarter to 2%-4%, up from the prior 1%-3% range.”
expectation_evidence: “Sales guide (+1–3%) is likely safe.”

description: Direct delivery sales turned slightly positive at 0.4%, a quarter earlier than the preview’s expected breakeven. However, the improvement came from price/mix rather than volume, and the customer base remained smaller, tempering the recovery signal.
fact_evidence: “Direct delivery net sales returned to growth at 0.4%, a 340 basis point sequential improvement and one quarter ahead of expectations, though driven by price/mix rather than volume as the customer base remained smaller.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided Q2 to breakeven, H2 to modest growth.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Despite strong comparable sales growth, companywide volume contributed negative 0.1%; the 4.3% price/mix contribution accounted for essentially all the growth. That leaves the reported growth less volume-led than the preview’s recovery discussion around direct-delivery customers implied.
fact_evidence: “Total comparable growth was almost entirely price/mix-driven, with a 4.3% price/mix contribution offset by a negative 0.1% volume contribution.”
expectation_evidence: “Direct Delivery reaching breakeven and net customer adds turning positive” was listed as a catalyst, and the preview described the recovery narrative as depending on direct delivery.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management reported tighter freight conditions and higher spot transportation rates as a margin pressure, rather than the freight moderation or mitigation the preview identified as a needed support for the EBITDA bridge.
fact_evidence: The company “faces margin pressure from a tighter freight market and higher spot transportation rates.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the EBITDA bridge needed “freight/commodity mitigation” and described “freight moderating” in its bull scenario.

description: The preview expected Insulet to reaffirm FY26 guidance, or possibly narrow it to the low end. Instead, management cut the full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17–19%, citing weaker-than-expected Type 2 retention and utilization.
fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17-19%,” with worse-than-anticipated Type 2 retention and utilization accounting for roughly two-thirds of the reduction.
expectation_evidence: “Currently 21–23% cc total company / 22–24% Omnipod … Reaffirm = neutral-to-positive. Narrowing to the low end = the recall cost them volume.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview highlighted Type 2 as a key growth story and expected it to remain around 40% of new starts, but did not anticipate the retention and utilization problem. Management reported that Type 2 patients were over 40% of U.S. starts, yet their retention and utilization were weaker than Type 1, especially in the first 90 days.
fact_evidence: “Type 2 patients represented over 40% of U.S. new customer starts,” but the company saw “lower retention and modestly lower utilization versus Type 1,” concentrated in “the critical first 90 days of onboarding.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch … whether Type 2 stayed ~40% of new starts (~5% penetrated — the primary long-duration growth story),” and whether management disclosed “attrition/churn.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $1.36, below the preview’s $1.42 consensus midpoint and even its $1.38 low estimate, as well as its $1.45–$1.52 base-case range. This was a miss despite EPS growing about 42% year over year.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew approximately 42% year-over-year to $1.36.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.42 mid (range $1.38–$1.47)” and base case “Adj. EPS $1.45–1.52.”

description: Management introduced a preliminary FY27 U.S. Omnipod growth range of 9–14%, with a 12% midpoint and no benefit assumed from remediation actions. The preview anticipated competitive entrants as a risk but did not provide an expectation for this growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “2027 U.S. Omnipod growth [was] framed in a wide 9-14% range (12% midpoint) that assumes no benefit from remediation actions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged a “2027 competitive patch-pump wave” and listed upcoming competitors, but gave no FY27 U.S. Omnipod growth expectation.

description: The company said total-company constant-currency revenue growth would exit 2026 in the mid-teens, signaling a sharper late-year deceleration than the preview’s FY26 growth outlook alone conveyed.
fact_evidence: Management “preliminarily expects total company constant currency revenue growth to exit 2026 in the mid-teens.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was “21–23% cc total company” and expected a reaffirmation or possible nudge, but did not forecast the exit growth rate.

description: Adjusted gross margin rose sharply rather than showing the margin pressure emphasized in the preview: it expanded 320 basis points to 72.9%, helped by productivity, pricing, and volume.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points year-over-year to 72.9%, driven by manufacturing productivity gains, positive pricing, and higher volumes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 adjusted gross margin was “71.0%, down 90bp Y/Y,” and highlighted recall costs and raw-material and freight costs as headwinds to watch.

description: Insulet raised its FY26 adjusted EPS growth outlook to at least 30%, above its prior company target of more than 25% cited in the preview.
fact_evidence: The company “now expects adjusted EPS growth of at least 30% for 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the current FY26 target as “>25% adj. EPS growth.”

description: International Omnipod guidance was raised to 30–32% constant-currency growth for the year, with management pointing to strong first-half momentum. The preview expected international strength, but did not anticipate this full-year guidance increase.
fact_evidence: Management “raised international Omnipod full-year growth guidance to 30-32% constant currency,” citing strong first-half momentum, including Omnipod 5 becoming Australia’s “#1 pump for new users” and a Spain launch.
expectation_evidence: The preview expected international strength in its base case, citing “Spain + Libre 3 Plus,” and listed the Spain launch as a catalyst; it did not state a full-year international growth outlook.

description: Revenue was essentially in line with sell-side consensus but slightly exceeded the company’s Q2 constant-currency guidance range: constant-currency growth was 22.7% versus the guided 20–22%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company revenue reached $802 million, growing 23.5% reported and 22.7% constant currency, exceeding company expectations.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed total-company Q2 guidance of “+20–22%” constant currency and consensus revenue of “~$803M.”

description: Recursion cut its FY2026 cash operating expense guidance to $375 million, below the preview’s standing guide of less than $390 million. It said this represents nearly a 40% reduction from comparable 2024 pro forma expenses while maintaining all outcome targets.
fact_evidence: “lowered its 2026 full-year cash operating expense guidance to $375 million,” representing “a nearly 40% reduction from comparable 2024 pro forma expenses while maintaining all outcome targets.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash operating expenses < $390M for FY2026”; the bull scenario allowed for the guide to be “lowered.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The quarter-end cash balance was about $557 million, below the preview’s estimated range of $575–595 million. The reported operating runway through early 2028 was in line with the preview, but the cash balance itself came in light.
fact_evidence: “ended the quarter with approximately $557 million in cash and equivalents,” providing “an operating runway through early 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash & equivalents: ~$575–595M (est.)”; the standing guidance was “Operating runway into early 2028.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Recursion reported more than $260 million in upfront and milestone payments from Roche-Genentech, versus the preview’s cited $213 million. It also disclosed potential for over $300 million in additional milestones for each future small molecule program.
fact_evidence: “The Roche-Genentech collaboration has yielded more than $260 million in upfront and milestone payments, with potential for over $300 million in additional milestones for each future small molecule program.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$213M from Roche/Genentech” and noted a “$30M milestone in 2025.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: REC-7735 advanced beyond the preview’s expected 2H26 go/no-go decision: it received FDA IND clearance, and Recursion said its Phase I trial will start later this year. The preview had not anticipated IND clearance or a trial start on that timetable.
fact_evidence: “REC-7735 received FDA IND clearance”; “The Phase I ZINNIA trial will initiate later this year with first data expected in the first half of 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “REC-7735 and REC-102 go/no-go calls were guided for 2H26.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Recursion disclosed that its engine advances candidates using about 330 compounds over roughly 1.5 years, compared with industry benchmarks of about 2,500 compounds over 4 years. The preview discussed the platform narrative but did not anticipate these specific speed and capital-efficiency comparisons.
fact_evidence: “Recursion's engine advances candidates using roughly 330 compounds over about 1.5 years, compared with industry benchmarks of roughly 2,500 compounds over 4 years, representing major speed and capital efficiency gains.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “how the Recursion OS platform is monetized versus advanced internally,” without giving efficiency benchmarks.

description: Recursion announced two senior hires—a Chief AI Officer from Microsoft Research and a new head of drug design—which the preview had not anticipated. The preview expected attention on the new CEO’s narrative and possible portfolio or infrastructure decisions, but did not flag these appointments.
fact_evidence: “The company strengthened leadership by hiring Dr. Hoifung Poon (from Microsoft Research) as Chief AI Officer and Dr. Donovan Chin to head drug design.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “portfolio prioritization, headcount/infrastructure decisions, or any pivot in how the Recursion OS platform is monetized versus advanced internally.”

description: The preview treated Q3 guidance and July trends as the quarter’s main new information, but Shake Shack said it will stop issuing quarterly guidance and move to annual-only guidance. That removes the expected near-term quarterly outlook.
fact_evidence: “Shake Shack is discontinuing quarterly guidance in favor of annual-only guidance going forward.”
expectation_evidence: “The entire event risk sits in the Q3 guide” and “Q3-to-date / July comps” were identified as key items to watch.

description: The preview focused on whether restaurant margins could stabilize, but management said the prior 2025–2027 margin-expansion target is under review and identified that target—not unit growth—as the key uncertainty. This is a more explicit challenge to the longer-term margin outlook than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The prior three-year (2025-2027) targets of low-teens unit growth and 50+ basis points of annual restaurant margin expansion are under review, with the restaurant margin goal being the key uncertainty rather than unit growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a specific 2027 recovery bridge” and described the margin trajectory as a key debate, but did not indicate that the targets were under review.

description: Restaurant-level margin reached 23.0%, above the preview’s 22.5% estimate and at the top of the company’s 22.0%–23.0% range. The beat came despite record-high beef costs, though the preview had already identified beef inflation as the main pressure.
fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level profit margin declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 23.0% of Shack sales,” with record-high beef costs “up mid-teens,” partially offset by “60 basis points of labor efficiency.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated restaurant-level margin at “~22.5%” against guidance of “22.0%–23.0%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Same-Shack sales were 3.5%, above the preview’s 2.5%–3.0% range, and traffic was positive rather than the negative-traffic outcome the preview warned about. However, the estimated World Cup benefit reduces underlying comps to roughly the mid-2% range, close to expectations.
fact_evidence: “Same-Shack sales grew 3.5% (2.0% traffic, 1.5% price mix),” but excluding an estimated “~90 basis point World Cup benefit,” comps were “closer to mid-2%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected same-Shack sales of “~+2.5–3.0%” and flagged the possibility that the comp could come “with negative traffic.”

description: Management put full-year adjusted EBITDA and net income at the low end of the existing ranges. The preview viewed reaffirmation as a mild upside surprise because it feared another cut, but the low-end positioning and cost explanation are more cautious than a strong reaffirmation.
fact_evidence: Management guided full-year adjusted EBITDA and net income to the low end of the “$225-$235 million range” due to “persistent beef inflation and higher fuel and distribution costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the market was watching whether Shake Shack would “reiterate $225–235M or cut again,” and that “a reiteration is the mild upside surprise.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview highlighted H2 pricing as a question, but management quantified near-term pricing roll-offs: 2% in August and another 1.4% in December. With beef still elevated into July, further price increases remain possible, suggesting continued cost pressure and potential reliance on pricing.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 2% of pricing rolls off in August and an additional 1.4% rolls off in December, while beef costs remained elevated into July, leaving open the possibility of further price increases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Beef cost guidance + H2 menu pricing” as a key issue and said to “watch for a stated H2 pricing action.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The app channel grew much faster than the preview’s discussion of the value platform suggested, with management describing it as a highly incremental, high-frequency channel. The preview did not provide an app-growth or app-mix expectation.
fact_evidence: “Comparable app channel sales grew nearly 30% year-over-year and the app now represents just over 10% of channel mix,” described as “the highest-frequency and most incremental channel.”

description: Other operating expenses rose as a share of sales, partly because of higher delivery commissions. The preview did not forecast this pressure separately from restaurant-level margin.
fact_evidence: “Other operating expenses rose 80 basis points partly due to higher delivery commissions.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Shake Shack reported that new units are generating over 30% cash-on-cash returns, a unit-economics detail not addressed in the preview. The preview did expect roughly 16 openings and continued 60–65 unit guidance, so the surprise is the return disclosure rather than the opening pace.
fact_evidence: The company opened “16 new company-operated Shacks (a Q2 record),” reached 33 year-to-date, reaffirmed 60–65 openings for 2026, and said new units generate “over 30% cash-on-cash returns.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~16” Q2 company-operated openings and cited full-year guidance of “60–65.”

description: Revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus estimate, though it remained inside the company’s pre-announced range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue rose 17.2% year-over-year to $417.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$416M” and cited company guidance of “$415–420M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Gross bookings reached more than $58 billion, above both the $57.2 billion Street estimate and the $57.75 billion high end of company guidance. The reported 22% growth rate was at the top of the preview’s expected 20–22% range, but the dollar result exceeded the bar.
fact_evidence: “Gross bookings grew 22% year-over-year to more than $58 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross Bookings: $57.2B (Street)” and company guidance of “$56.25–57.75B”; the preview described implied growth of “~+20–22%.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS growth was 35%, above the preview’s expected 29–32% growth. Using the preview’s $0.63 prior-year EPS, that growth implies roughly $0.85 per share, above the $0.83 consensus estimate and the $0.82 high end of guidance.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS grew 35% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “+29–32%” growth and listed consensus EPS of “$0.83” with guidance of “$0.78–$0.82.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Uber disclosed a nearly 500-basis-point year-over-year decline in Mobility revenue take rate, with about 400 basis points attributed to an optical UK business-model change. The preview had flagged persistence of accounting-related take-rate pressure as a key question but gave no expectation for a decline of this size; the 7.6% Mobility operating-income margin was described as strong.
fact_evidence: “Mobility revenue take rate declined nearly 500 basis points year-over-year, with about 400 basis points attributable to an optical UK business model change, while mobility operating income margin remained strong at 7.6%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked “how much of that [business-model] headwind persists in Q2” and highlighted “Take rate and the revenue/bookings divergence.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Uber gave concrete AV rollout milestones—live in 7 cities, targeting 15 by year-end, and planning more markets in 2027—plus a commitment to deliver 120,000 vehicles over the next few years. However, AV trips are still less than 0.5% of roughly 300 million weekly trips, so the disclosed rollout has not yet translated into meaningful platform volume.
fact_evidence: “Uber is live with AV partners in 7 cities and on track to reach 15 cities by year-end”; AV trips “represent less than 0.5% of Uber's total volume of roughly 300 million trips per week”; the company has a “commitment to deliver 120,000 vehicles over the next few years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side wanted “deployment numbers, not commentary,” specifically “live vehicle counts, city-level utilization, and unit economics per AV trip.”

description: Uber said its Delivery Hero agreement could expand reach to nearly 100 markets and roughly double the number of markets offering both mobility and delivery. That is a broader footprint opportunity than the preview’s description of Delivery Hero as operating in 50 markets.
fact_evidence: The agreement is “expected to expand reach to nearly 100 markets and roughly double the number of markets offering both mobility and delivery.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Delivery Hero as “50 markets” and focused on accretion, dilution, synergies, and the antitrust path.

description: Uber spent about $4 billion toward Delivery Hero stock purchases in Q2. The preview described the $14.8 billion transaction as all-stock and emphasized its dilution and accretion implications, but did not anticipate this additional stock-purchase deployment.
fact_evidence: “Uber deployed about $4 billion toward Delivery Hero stock purchases in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the deal “$14.8B all-stock” and asked for “share count impact, synergy targets, and how they intend to run capital returns through the pendency.”

description: Share repurchases were not simply continuing at the prior pace: Uber said it bought back $3.5 billion year-to-date but plans to rebuild repurchases within months toward its 50%-of-free-cash-flow target. That is a more qualified near-term buyback picture than the preview’s request for reaffirmation of buyback capacity.
fact_evidence: “Uber ... has bought back $3.5 billion of stock year-to-date, with plans to rebuild share repurchases within months toward its 50%-of-free-cash-flow target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “whether buybacks continue” as a key question and said the bull case required “reaffirmed buyback capacity despite the all-stock DH deal.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: US Mobility trips and bookings accelerated, with management attributing growth partly to suburban markets where fewer than 10% of eligible consumers have used Uber, versus more than 50% in dense markets. The preview was watching for intact US demand but did not identify this large suburban usage gap as a specific growth runway.
fact_evidence: “US mobility trips and gross bookings accelerated in Q2” and in suburban markets “under 10% of eligible consumers have used Uber versus over 50% in dense markets.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case called for “US demand intact”; it did not give an expectation for suburban adoption or usage.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Uber disclosed that only 20% of consumers use both rides and Eats, while cross-platform users are growing 1.5 times faster than single-product users. The preview discussed membership and advertising as platform-margin drivers but did not flag this cross-product adoption gap or growth differential.
fact_evidence: “Only 20% of consumers use both rides and eats, and cross-platform users are growing 1.5x faster than single-product users.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Trailing 12-month free cash flow surpassed $10 billion for the first time in Uber’s history. The preview offered a quarterly FCF estimate of roughly $2.4–2.7 billion but did not anticipate or set an expectation for this record annual run-rate milestone.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow surpassed $10 billion for the first time in company history.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed quarterly free cash flow of “~$2.4–2.7B” as its own estimate, with “no clean consensus.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: VCP traction fell short of the preview’s bar: VYX had 25 signed customers versus the expected 28–32, and $286 million of remaining contract value versus the expected more than $350 million. RCV was also below the $293 million reported in Q1, despite growing 65% year over year.
fact_evidence: “VCP contracts reached 25 signed customers representing $286 million of remaining contract value, up 65% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for ~28–32 cumulative contracts and RCV >$350M.”

description: Retail outperformed the preview’s already-positive momentum expectations: revenue grew 4% excluding the hardware impact, while adjusted EBITDA rose 20% and margin reached 26.6%. The preview’s bull case required Retail margin of at least 18%, well below the reported level.
fact_evidence: “Retail revenue grew 4% excluding the hardware impact and retail adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $97 million, with margin up 880 bps to 26.6% (350 bps excluding hardware).”
expectation_evidence: “Retail momentum and payments attach”; the bull case required “Retail EBITDA margin holds ≥18%.”

description: Restaurants’ EBITDA decline worsened rather than moderating: adjusted EBITDA fell 15%, compared with an 8% decline in Q1. Revenue remained down 6% excluding hardware, with delayed refreshes, SMB weakness, and the Brazil divestiture cited as pressures.
fact_evidence: “Restaurant revenue declined 6% excluding hardware (a $10 million drop) driven by delayed hardware refreshes, SMB weakness, and the Brazil divestiture, with adjusted EBITDA down 15% to $58 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for on-time launch confirmation and whether Restaurants EBITDA decline moderates.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Recurring revenue was a larger share of sales than the preview’s post-transition expectation: it reached 83% of total revenue, above the preview’s expectation of more than 75%. Recurring revenue also grew 3%, including 6% growth in software.
fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue reached 83% of total revenue in Q2”; recurring revenue was “up 3% (software +6%, services +1%).”
expectation_evidence: “Recurring revenue … should be >75% of revenue post-ODM.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The quarter included an unanticipated cost and demand headwind: memory-chip inflation is expected to cost $20–$30 million, and passing it through in prices is contributing to customer caution and delayed hardware and project purchases.
fact_evidence: “Memory chip cost inflation represents a $20-$30 million headwind being passed through via price, contributing to customer caution and delayed hardware and project purchases.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS beat the preview’s consensus estimate, coming in at $0.17 versus $0.15. The call said EPS was flat year over year because of a higher tax rate.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was flat at $0.17 due to a higher tax rate.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: $0.15.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was within the preview’s expected dollar range, but the margin result was stronger than the preview’s expectation of modest Q2 margins: margin expanded 460 basis points, or 80 basis points excluding the hardware transition.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 5% to $98 million with margin expanding 460 basis points to 18.7% (80 bps excluding the hardware transition).”
expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly guided Q2/Q3 margins to be ‘modest’”; Q2 adjusted EBITDA was estimated at “~$95–100M.”

description: VYX disclosed share repurchases that the preview did not anticipate: it bought back approximately $11 million of shares during the quarter.
fact_evidence: “The company generated $56 million adjusted free cash flow (before restructuring), ended the quarter at 2x net leverage, invested $41 million in CapEx, and repurchased approximately $11 million of shares.”

description: Q2 revenue was $277.8M, above the preview’s $268–271M company guide and ~$269.7M consensus. That is a clear beat of both the guide and the consensus bar.
fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 26.6% to $277.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Company guide … $268–271M”; “Consensus ~$269.7M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 bookings reached $295.9M, above the preview’s $280–285M guide and $282.5M midpoint, exceeding even the preview’s cited ~$285M buy-side whisper.
fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings grew 33% year-over-year to $295.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total Bookings … $280–285M”; “Total Bookings vs. $282.5M midpoint”; “Buy-side whisper is effectively the guide high end, ~$285M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.4%, well above the preview’s roughly 32% estimate and the 32% key-metric threshold, and it exceeded the 35% margin target set at IPO. The reported ~900 bps of year-over-year expansion was also much greater than the preview’s ~400–500 bps base case.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin hit 36.4%, exceeding the 35% target set at IPO five years ago, with roughly 900 basis points of margin expansion year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA / margin … ~$85–88M / ~32%”; “Base … margin ~32%, +400–500bps Y/Y”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ≥ 32%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected over 80% eGate coverage by the end of Q2, but the company reported coverage of only over 70%. The rollout’s reported progress therefore fell short of the specific target investors were told to watch.
fact_evidence: “eGates now cover over 70% of the network.”
expectation_evidence: “Management targeted >80% of the network by end of Q2”; “eGate coverage hits ~80%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Active CLEAR+ members reached 8.3M, below the preview’s ~8.4M estimate and its 8.35–8.42M base-case range. The increase from Q1’s 8.2M was about 100,000, short of the preview’s 150,000-net-add threshold.
fact_evidence: “Active CLEAR+ members grew 15.2% to 8.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Active CLEAR+ members … ~8.4M”; “Active CLEAR+ 8.35–8.42M”; “Active CLEAR+ ≥ 8.4M with net adds ≥150k.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company raised standard membership pricing by $10 effective July 1 and said early retention remained healthy with no observed impact. The preview treated a pricing-action update as a potential bull catalyst and otherwise anticipated a measured approach to increases.
fact_evidence: “The company raised standard membership pricing by $10 (from $209 to $219) effective July 1st, with early retention rates remaining healthy and no observed impact on retention.”
expectation_evidence: “A … pricing-action update” was listed as a bull catalyst; the base case anticipated a “measured approach to price increases.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CLEAR1 net new customer signings and pipeline each increased over 50% sequentially, providing concrete evidence of continued momentum beyond the preview’s Q1 reference point. The preview emphasized CLEAR1 as a key debate but said hard dollar or ARR disclosure would be the stronger catalyst; the call’s figures were sequential rather than dollar or ARR disclosures.
fact_evidence: “CLEAR1 net new customer signings increased over 50% sequentially from Q1 to Q2, and the pipeline also grew over 50% quarter-over-quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “CLEAR1 growth rate and disclosure quality” was a key metric; “Any hard dollar disclosure, ARR figure, or named multiyear logos is a bull catalyst.”

description: The company repurchased about $22M of shares in Q3 to date, a substantial shift from the preview’s cited $1.2M Q1 buyback. The preview specifically flagged a return to repurchases as a potentially meaningful capital-allocation signal.
fact_evidence: “Repurchased ~$22 million of shares in Q3 to date at an average price of $52.73.”
expectation_evidence: “Buyback was only $1.2M in Q1”; “a shift back toward repurchase … would read as management calling the stock cheap.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: A $315M accrued Amex partnership liability will be paid in Q3, resulting in negative Q3 free cash flow. The preview discussed the full-year FCF outlook but did not flag this large payment or a negative quarterly cash-flow period.
fact_evidence: “A $315 million accrued partnership liability with the Amex credit card partner will be paid out in Q3, resulting in negative Q3 free cash flow (already reflected in guidance).”

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $284M–$287M puts the midpoint at $285.5M, modestly above the preview’s $280M–$285M base-case range and above its $283M checklist threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $284M-$287M.”
expectation_evidence: “Base … Q3 guide $280–285M”; “Q3'26 revenue guide ≥ $283M.”

description: Revenue was about $248 million, based on the reported 11% year-over-year decline, below the preview’s $255.5 million consensus and implying a steeper decline than the expected 8.2%. Management attributed the weakness partly to a 34% drop in network revenue and a shift away from larger jobs after a mid-March oil and gas price spike.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 11% year-over-year,” driven by “a 34% drop in network revenue” and “a demand shift away from larger jobs following a mid-March oil and gas price spike.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $255.50M” with implied year-over-year change of “‑8.2%.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Angi recorded a $235 million non-cash goodwill and trade name impairment on its U.S. reporting unit, an unanticipated charge tied to a sustained decline in market capitalization. It does not affect cash, liquidity, or covenants, but is a substantial reported one-off charge.
fact_evidence: “$235 million non-cash goodwill and trade name impairment charge entirely on its U.S. reporting unit,” triggered by “a sustained decline in market capitalization,” with “no impact on cash, liquidity, or covenants.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: U.S. service requests fell 6% and leads fell 13% year over year, reversing the growth in proprietary requests and leads reported for Q1. Revenue per lead did rise 1%, as Angi moved away from heavily discounted legacy ad products.
fact_evidence: “U.S. service requests fell 6% and leads fell 13% year-over-year,” while “revenue per lead rose 1%” due to shifting away from discounted legacy ad products.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 “Proprietary Service Requests +17%, Proprietary Leads +13%” and said pro count and churn were the “core bear thesis,” with stabilization important.

description: Management said July EBITDA margin was already several hundred basis points above Q2, an encouraging improvement in the near-term profitability trajectory that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “July EBITDA margin was already several hundred basis points above Q2.”

description: Angi shifted about $6 million of inefficient TV advertising spend to higher-ROI channels in Q2 and expects to remove a comparable amount in Q3. The preview had not anticipated this specific marketing reallocation and planned further reduction.
fact_evidence: “Reallocated about $6 million of inefficient TV spend in Q2 to higher-ROI channels” and “expects to remove a comparable amount in Q3.”

description: The large Pro segment is growing more than 20% year over year despite fewer than 10 sellers deployed year to date, with 30 planned by year-end. This is a positive growth and sales-expansion proof point not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of pro churn and revenue weakness.
fact_evidence: “The large Pro segment is growing more than 20% year-over-year with fewer than 10 sellers deployed year-to-date,” with plans “to reach 30 sellers by year-end.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described a sizable opportunity from increasing Angi’s penetration among large Pros: roughly $2.5 billion in revenue at small-to-midsized penetration levels and a longer-term $5 billion opportunity before Pro software and services. The preview did not flag these market-size estimates.
fact_evidence: Matching small-to-midsized penetration in large Pro could bring revenue to “roughly $2.5 billion,” with “a longer-term $5 billion revenue opportunity before entering Pro software and services.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Pro sales effectiveness and per-Pro capacity showed stronger figures than the preview had discussed: win rates were up about 20% year over year, and average capacity per Pro grew about 13%.
fact_evidence: “Pro win rates have risen roughly 20% year-over-year,” from “about 1 in 9 leads won two years ago to roughly 1 in 6 currently,” and “average capacity per Pro grew about 13% year-over-year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Overall Pro capacity improved sharply from being down 13% in Q1 to roughly flat year over year in July. Management identified this as a key gate for returning to growth in 2027, a more specific improvement signal than the preview provided.
fact_evidence: “Pro capacity trends improved from down 13% in Q1 to down 2% in June and roughly flat in July year-over-year,” and are “a key gating factor for returning to growth in 2027.”

description: Angi said ChatGPT ads were already generating roughly $3 million in revenue run rate at a profit, an AI monetization result not anticipated by the preview.
fact_evidence: “Generating roughly $3 million revenue run rate on ChatGPT ads at a profit.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The first Pro AI agent, AI Front Desk, was live with dozens of Pros and about 80% retention, going beyond the preview’s expectation that the first agent would be testing within several weeks.
fact_evidence: “Its first Pro AI agent (AI Front Desk) is live with dozens of Pros and about 80% retention.”
expectation_evidence: On the Q1 call management targeted first agent testing “within several weeks.”

description: Management reaffirmed approximately $50 million in annual adjusted EBITDA minus CapEx as a target, whereas the preview characterized that figure as a directional floor rather than a commitment. The reaffirmation provides somewhat firmer support for the stated level.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed its target of approximately $50 million in annual adjusted EBITDA minus CapEx.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said approximately “$50M/yr of Adjusted EBITDA less capex” was framed as a “directional floor, not a commitment.”

description: The preview’s base case was about $69 million of adjusted EBITDA, with a guidance-implied range of roughly $65–75 million. ADV reported $76 million, a smaller year-over-year decline than the preview’s roughly 20% midpoint expectation, though below its stated $78 million threshold for a clear beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 12% to $76 million” (down 9% excluding divestitures).
expectation_evidence: “My Base” adjusted EBITDA was “$69M (−20%)”; the preview also identified “~$65–75M guidance-implied band” and said “Above $78M = genuine beat.”

description: The preview expected the first half to account for only the low 40% range of full-year adjusted EBITDA, implying a more heavily backloaded year. Management instead said the second half would be about 53% of the total, implying roughly 47% in the first half.
fact_evidence: “Second-half adjusted EBITDA will represent approximately 53% of the full-year total, with Q4 expected to exceed Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited management’s prior expectation that “the first half [would] represent in the low 40% range of full year adjusted EBITDA.”

description: Net revenue was above the preview’s $742 million base estimate and grew faster than its expected 0.8% year-over-year increase. The preview’s $887 million consensus was on a different, GAAP revenue basis, so it is not directly comparable to the reported net-revenue figure.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenues rose 3% year-over-year to $757 million (up 4% excluding divestitures).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “Revenue (Net) … $742M (+0.8%).”

description: Experiential revenue growth was within the preview’s expected range, but adjusted EBITDA grew much faster than revenue. That contrasts with the preview’s base-case concern that growth in the segment would be margin-dilutive.
fact_evidence: “Experiential Services was the standout segment, with revenues up 19% to $296 million and adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $34 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Experiential growth of “15–20% but margin-dilutive”; it said to watch whether “EBITDA growth keeps pace with revenue.”

description: Retailer Services grew revenue but suffered a steep adjusted EBITDA decline, rather than showing the steadier performance suggested by its recent results and role as a higher-margin segment. Management attributed the decline partly to temporary higher execution costs on a new project.
fact_evidence: “Retailer Services revenue grew 3% to $237 million but adjusted EBITDA fell approximately 25% to $20 million” due partly to “higher execution costs on a new project management deemed temporary.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Retailer as “the steady one” that carried “higher margins,” and cited Q1 Retailer revenue growth of 4.2% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 14.4%.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage was materially higher than the preview’s estimate, despite its expectation that another quarter of debt paydown would support deleveraging. Management said cash would primarily go toward debt reduction, but reported leverage of about 4.5x trailing EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $102 million in cash and net debt of approximately 4.5x trailing EBITDA,” with free cash flow directed primarily toward debt reduction.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net leverage … ~4.0–4.2x” and said “Another quarter of paydown de-risks the equity stub materially.”

description: The release quantified divestitures as a meaningful drag on both Q2 and full-year results, a headwind not addressed in the preview’s estimates. The Q2 impact also explains part of the difference between reported and excluding-divestiture performance.
fact_evidence: “Divestitures created a Q2 headwind of roughly $5 million to revenues and $3 million to adjusted EBITDA, with full-year 2026 headwinds expected at approximately $20 million to revenues and over $10 million to adjusted EBITDA.”

description: Q2 revenue was $34 million, about 17% above the preview’s roughly $29.1 million consensus and above even its $32–34 million bull-case range’s lower end. This was a substantial beat against the expected quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $34 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $29.08M (Zacks); $29.30M (alt. compiler)”

description: Gross margin reached 27%, exceeding the preview’s roughly 24% estimate and its 25% bull-case threshold. The reported margin therefore came in well above the expected recovery from Q1’s 20%.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 27% in Q2, up from 20% in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~24% (not formally polled)”; the bull case expected “≥25%.”

description: Amprius raised its full-year revenue floor to $140 million, up from $130 million. That exceeded the preview’s bull-case threshold of $135 million rather than merely reaffirming the existing guide.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to at least $140 million revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guide: revenue ≥$130M”; the bull case anticipated a raise “to ≥$135M.”

description: Full-year gross-margin guidance rose to at least 28%, above the preview’s cited 25% FY target. The increase goes beyond the anticipated Q2 margin recovery and signals a higher full-year margin floor.
fact_evidence: “[Raised] full-year 2026 guidance … to … at least 28% gross margin.”
expectation_evidence: “Management reaffirmed a 25% FY target.”

description: The company’s full-year net-loss ceiling moved from less than $8 million in the preview to $10 million or less. That is a looser loss target, despite the preview’s focus on how H1 losses already appeared to exceed the old full-year limit.
fact_evidence: “Amprius reiterated … a net loss of $10 million or less.”
expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guide: … net loss <$8.0M (≤$0.06/sh).”

description: Q2 GAAP net loss was $5.1 million, or $0.04 per share, versus the preview’s roughly $4.3 million expected loss and $0.03 per-share consensus. The company cited a one-time noncash $1.9 million warrant fair-value adjustment; adjusted net loss was $3.2 million.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed to $5.1 million (negative $0.04 per share) in Q2, including a onetime noncash $1.9 million warrant fair-value adjustment; adjusted net loss was $3.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) | ($0.03)”; the preview estimated “Q2 net loss is ~$4.3M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended Q2 at $74.5 million, up $12.2 million in the quarter, well above the preview’s $62.4 million starting balance and its flat-to-up expectation. The reported increase was supported by warrant and option exercises, rather than being presented as an operating-cash or AR-collection improvement.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $74.5 million cash and no debt, up $12.2 million in the quarter, funded by $12.3 million from warrant exercises and $4.5 million from option exercises with no ATM program.”
expectation_evidence: “$62.4M at Q1-end”; “Cash flat-to-up on AR collection is the tell.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Amprius disclosed a three-year Stark Future contract expected to generate at least $100 million through 2029, with shipments beginning early next year. The preview discussed possible partner announcements but did not anticipate a contract of this scale or identify this customer.
fact_evidence: “Amprius signed a 3-year contract with Barcelona-based Stark Future expected to generate at least $100 million in revenue through 2029, with shipments starting early next year.”
expectation_evidence: “New order / partner announcements” were a catalyst to watch; the preview said additional US partner announcements were “expected.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company reported a new $24 million order from a European drone manufacturer for SA124 SiCore cylindrical cells, to be delivered over roughly 2.5 quarters. The preview watched for order conversion but did not specify or forecast this order.
fact_evidence: “The company won a new $24 million order from a European drone manufacturer for SA124 SiCore cylindrical cells, expected to be delivered over roughly 2.5 quarters.”
expectation_evidence: “The question is conversion: how much flows to Amprius cells and when.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Amprius said its cells are used by half of the 19 drone manufacturers invited to a Department of War demonstration, with a possible 60,000-drone order to follow for top performers. The preview discussed defense-customer awards and cell demand generally, but did not flag this specific demonstration or potential procurement.
fact_evidence: “Amprius cells are used by half of the 19 drone manufacturers invited to the Department of War's Fort Carson demonstration, after which the DoW plans to order 60,000 drones from top performers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted defense customers had received “~$500M in new orders” and asked “how much flows to Amprius cells and when.”

description: The preview expected announcements about additional US manufacturing partners, but the reported update identified Nanotech as the US partner and described a target of full US NDAA compliance in 2027 rather than announcing another partner. That leaves the anticipated near-term partner announcement unreported.
fact_evidence: “Over 2 GWh of annual capacity across four China partners, three South Korea partners, and U.S. partner Nanotech, targeting full U.S. NDAA compliance in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Management said pouch-cell announcements with additional US partners were ‘expected.’”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview framed the key mix debate as US defense versus China LEV, while the reported results said EMEA generated 68% of revenue. This makes EMEA the dominant stated regional contributor, a geographic mix detail the preview had not anticipated.
fact_evidence: “SiCore accounting for 98% of revenue and EMEA driving 68% of revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Mix: US defense vs. China LEV.”

description: Q3 adjusted EPS growth was stronger than the preview’s 9.3% consensus growth expectation: Cencora reported 12% growth, implying roughly $4.48 per share versus the $4.37 consensus estimate. The preview’s higher $4.43 whisper proxy was also below that implied result.
fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EPS grew 12%, supported by $1 billion of opportunistic share repurchases executed at an average price of $268 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $4.37” versus “$4.00” a year earlier; “Most Accurate” (whisper proxy) was “$4.43.”

description: Adjusted operating income grew 17% to $1.2 billion, well ahead of the preview’s low Q3 bar: its summed segment estimates implied only about 3.9% growth. The preview expected much of the year’s acceleration to be back-loaded into Q4.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income grew 17% to $1.2 billion, with double-digit growth across both reportable segments and the 'other' category.”
expectation_evidence: “Summed segment OI of ~$1,099M is only +3.9% YoY” and “The Street is loading essentially the entire back-half acceleration into Q4.”

description: U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income substantially exceeded the preview’s $940.9 million consensus and its expected 4.3% growth, reaching $966 million with 16% growth. The preview said $960 million or more would de-risk the Q4 ramp, and Cencora also reported double-digit organic growth excluding One Oncology and the lost customer.
fact_evidence: “U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income grew 16% to $966 million, delivering double-digit organic growth even when excluding One Oncology and the lost oncology customer, a sharp acceleration from 7% last quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “USHS segment op income $940.9M” and “+4.3%”; the preview added, “Anything ≥$960M de-risks the Q4 hockey stick materially.”

description: International Healthcare Solutions operating income grew far faster than the preview’s 1.4% expectation, rising 21% as reported and 23% in constant currency. The reported strength was partly helped by favorable timing of manufacturer price adjustments, making the beat less purely operational.
fact_evidence: “International Healthcare Solutions operating income rose 21% as-reported (23% constant currency) to $166 million, aided by favorable manufacturer price adjustment timing in a developing market country.”
expectation_evidence: “IHS segment op income $158.5M” and “+1.4%.”

description: Cencora raised both ends of its FY26 adjusted EPS range by $0.05, rather than merely narrowing to the upper end of the existing range as the preview’s base case anticipated. The increase was positive but smaller than the preview’s bull-case operational raise.
fact_evidence: “Cencora raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.75-$17.95, up from the prior $17.70-$17.90 range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “FY26 narrowed to upper half ($17.80–$17.90)” and the bull case as “FY26 raised to ≥$17.90–$18.05 on operations.”

description: Management disclosed a quantified FY27 earnings headwind if the MWI/Covetrus merger closes midyear: roughly $150 million of operating income, or about $0.35 per share. The preview flagged the deal and regulatory uncertainty but did not anticipate a quantified impact on FY27.
fact_evidence: “A mid-fiscal-year MWI/Covetrus merger close would create a ~$150 million operating income headwind, netting to roughly a $0.35 EPS headwind, as a modeling consideration for fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged an “MWI Animal Health / Covetrus” regulatory update and said any “divestitures, timeline slippage, or deal risk” was live Q&A; it also cited FY27 EPS consensus of “$19.81.”

description: Management lowered International revenue growth expectations to approximately 8% (7% in constant currency) because of a stronger dollar. The preview discussed International operating income and reported a segment revenue consensus, but did not anticipate this reduction in the revenue outlook.
fact_evidence: “Lowered International revenue growth expectations to approximately 8% (7% constant currency) due to a stronger dollar.”

description: U.S. revenue was guided to the lower half of the existing 4%-6% growth range, a softer outlook than the preview’s broad company-level range alone suggested. The preview did not give a specific U.S. forward-growth expectation.
fact_evidence: “Management guided U.S. revenue to the lower half of the 4%-6% growth range.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue growth 4–6%.”

description: Gross profit margin expanded 61 basis points, with management attributing the increase largely to One Oncology. The preview was watching for the acquisition’s accretion ramp after noting a smaller-than-expected contribution in Q2, but it did not forecast this margin expansion.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanding 61 basis points to 4.16%, largely driven by the One Oncology acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said One Oncology contributed “smaller than expected” operating income in Q2 and called Q3 “the first clean quarter,” with a quantified contribution a key item to watch.

description: CDW reported Q2 net sales of $6.6 billion, up 10%, well above the preview’s $6.21–6.26 billion consensus range and expected 3.8%–4.7% growth. The sales beat was much larger than anticipated, although gross profit came in around the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales of $6.6 billion (up 10%)” and gross profit of “$1.3 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Consensus | $6.21–6.26B | +3.8% to +4.7%”; gross profit estimate “~$1.29–1.31B.”

description: Q2 gross margin fell to 20.1%, down 70 basis points year over year, substantially below the preview’s estimated 20.6%–20.9% and its expectation of flat to down 20 basis points. CDW attributed the decline to large enterprise hardware infrastructure deals and a lower relative services contribution.
fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin declined 70 basis points year-over-year to 20.1%,” driven by “mix shift toward large enterprise hardware infrastructure deals and lower relative services contribution.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | *~20.6–20.9%* | flat to -20bps”; the preview also said “Below ~20.5% is a problem.”

description: CDW raised its full-year outlook beyond the preview’s expected framing: it now expects high-end high-single-digit non-GAAP EPS growth rather than the high end of mid-single digits, and mid-single-digit gross profit growth rather than low-to-mid single digits. The 200–300 basis-point outperformance expectation for the U.S. IT market was reiterated, not raised.
fact_evidence: Management “raised full-year guidance,” expecting “mid-single-digit gross profit growth, high-end high-single-digit non-GAAP EPS growth, and US IT market growth in the mid-single digits with 200-300 bps of CDW outperformance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross profit growth of “low-to-mid single digits,” non-GAAP EPS growth at the “high end of mid-single digits,” and “200–300bps” outperformance.

description: Despite the sales and EPS strength, CDW expects full-year gross margin to be modestly below 2025, with second-half margin below the comparable 2025 period. That is weaker than the preview’s expectation that full-year margin would be approximately in line with 2025.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 gross margin is expected to be modestly below 2025,” with “second-half gross margins projected below second-half 2025 levels due to product and end-market mix.”
expectation_evidence: “FY guide is ‘approximately in line with 2025.’”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Adjusted free cash flow conversion was sharply lower in the first half than the preview’s recent-quarter comparison suggested: it was 42% of non-GAAP net income versus 85% in Q1, and management said it was well below its 80%–90% target. A roughly $400 million inventory increase drove the shortfall, which management expects to normalize by year-end.
fact_evidence: “First-half adjusted free cash flow was $278 million (42% of non-GAAP net income), well below the 80-90% target,” driven by “a roughly $400 million inventory increase” that management expects “to normalize by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 adjusted FCF $251M at 85% conversion”; the preview also flagged adjusted FCF and buyback as a key item to watch.

description: Government sales rose about 14%, stronger than the preview’s concern that federal weakness could continue to weigh on the segment. The preview highlighted federal declines and described state and local growth as masking them; the reported overall government growth was considerably stronger.
fact_evidence: “Government net sales rose approximately 14%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 Government was “+4.6% with state/local double-digit masking federal decline” and flagged federal/government commentary as a key debate.

description: International growth accelerated to approximately 23%, ahead of the preview’s expectation that the U.K. and Canada would sustain the +17.9% pace seen in Q1; Canada also had a record quarter.
fact_evidence: “International grew approximately 23% (a record quarter in Canada).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull-case requirements included “UK/Canada sustaining the +17.9% pace seen in Q1.”

description: CDW’s non-GAAP EPS grew 11.9% and operating income grew 7%, both faster than gross profit growth of 6.3%. That is a more favorable operating-leverage picture than the preview’s cited Q1 negative jaws and its call for evidence of SG&A leverage.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS growth of 11.9% and operating income growth of 7% both exceeded gross profit growth of 6.3%,” signaling “an inflection toward improved operating leverage.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 SG&A +7.0% vs. GP +6.0% — negative jaws” and said investors wanted “an SG&A leverage datapoint.”

description: CFO Al Miralles announced that he plans to retire in 2027, a management succession development not anticipated in the preview. The call said the transition would be orderly and that a successor search is underway.
fact_evidence: “CFO Al Miralles announced plans to retire in 2027 after completion of an orderly transition, with a search for his successor currently underway.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 exceeded both the $2.80 consensus and management’s prior $2.79–$2.83 guidance range, though the beat was much smaller than the sales surprise.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 (up 11.9%).”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $2.80”; management’s Q2 guide was “high single-digit YoY growth → $2.79–2.83.”

description: BioCryst raised 2026 total-revenue guidance to $690–$715 million, above both its previous $635–$660 million range and the preview’s $669.4 million Street estimate. The increase was substantially larger than the preview’s scenario for a possible guide raise.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $690-$715 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue (Street): $669.4M”; “A raise is the cleanest bull catalyst”; bull scenario: “guide raised to ≥$640–655M.”

description: Q2 non-GAAP operating profit was far above the preview’s estimate, at $113.2 million versus roughly $58–$62 million. This is a large quarterly beat, though the call facts also report a sizable license payment that boosted revenue.
fact_evidence: “The company posted a non-GAAP operating profit of $113.2 million for the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating profit: ~$58–62M (my est.).”

description: Q2 total revenue was boosted by a $55.7 million navenibart European license upfront payment, making revenue materially higher than the preview’s $166–$169 million anchor expectation. The preview mentioned a possible unmodeled Neopharmed payment as an explanation for an aggregator outlier, but did not use it as its base expectation.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 45% year-over-year on a comparable basis, boosted by $55.7 million recognized from the navenibart European license upfront payment with Neopharmed Gentili.”
expectation_evidence: “Anchor on $166–169M total”; the preview also described the $183.3M aggregator figure as possibly “including a Neopharmed milestone nobody else is modeling.”

description: ORLADEYO revenue of $158.2 million came in slightly below the $161 million consensus estimate, although it was within the preview’s $158–$164 million base-case range and comparable growth was close to the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “ORLADEYO revenue reached $158.2 million in Q2 2026, growing 10% year-over-year on a comparable basis.”
expectation_evidence: “ORLADEYO net revenue: $161M”; base scenario: “$158–164M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Pediatric pellets had already generated 47 prescriptions through July 31, exceeding the total number the company had expected for all of 2026. The preview treated pediatric revenue conservatively and focused on confirming availability, not on prescriptions running ahead of the full-year expectation so early.
fact_evidence: “ORLADEYO pediatric pellets received 47 prescriptions through July 31, already exceeding the total expected for all of 2026, with several prescriptions coming from physicians new to prescribing ORLADEYO.”
expectation_evidence: “Pediatric ORLADEYO pellets … available early August 2026”; “peds was conservatively modeled.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: BioCryst reported positive cash flow even excluding the license upfront payment, alongside cash of just over $350 million. That is a stronger cash-generation update than the preview’s balance-sheet snapshot alone implied, though no specific cash-flow forecast was provided.
fact_evidence: The company “ended with just over $350 million in cash, generating positive cash flow even excluding the license upfront payment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “cash $259M ($331M pro forma with the $70M Neopharmed upfront)” and highlighted the balance sheet as “the underappreciated item.”

description: Management said excess cash flow could support business development, debt reduction, and/or buybacks. This broadened the capital-allocation possibilities discussed, but management did not announce a specific transaction or commitment.
fact_evidence: Management “signaled flexibility to pursue business development, debt reduction, and/or buybacks with excess cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said capital-structure commentary was a key watch item and that “any commentary on refinancing or buying back the royalty obligation is a genuine re-rating lever”; its base case assumed “no BD.”

description: The preview warned that warrant and derivative marks might produce a large non-cash gain and a misleading EPS beat. Instead, Eos reported a $276 million net loss, driven primarily by non-cash fair-value adjustments to warrants and derivatives.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss of $276 million” and “the net loss [was] driven primarily by non-cash fair value adjustments to warrants and derivatives.”
expectation_evidence: “With the stock down sharply through Q2, warrant liabilities likely marked down again — a large non-cash gain.”

description: The call cited adjusted gross margin of negative 52% and product adjusted gross margin of negative 40%, substantially less negative than the preview’s expected gross margin of negative 69% to negative 73%. fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was negative 52% and product adjusted gross margin improved to negative 40%.”
