dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and marketable securities were $19.2 million, below the preview’s expectation of liquidity at roughly $20 million or more after the offering. The difference is modest, but the reported balance came in below that post-offering expectation.
fact_evidence: “Combined cash and marketable securities” were “$19.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Pro forma for ~$9.0M net proceeds, liquidity should be ~$20M+.”

description: SG&A increased to $1.5 million from $1.2 million, largely because of one-time, noncash stock-option expenses. The preview raised the possibility of first-quarter cleanups but did not anticipate this specific expense.
fact_evidence: “SG&A rose to $1.5 million from $1.2 million a year ago, driven largely by one-time noncash stock option expenses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted the first reported quarter for the new CFO could bring “possible reserve/estimate cleanups.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Navy exercised a six-month option in June for ACV lightweighting work, extending that program. The preview did not mention this option exercise.
fact_evidence: “The Navy exercised a 6-month ACV lightweighting option in June.”

description: A backlog of SBIR/STTR proposals dating back to August 2024 is still awaiting government funding decisions, indicating that this potential work remains unresolved. The preview did not flag these pending decisions.
fact_evidence: “A backlog of SBIR/STTR proposals dating back to August 2024 still awaits government funding decisions.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Army-funded tungsten warhead development is scheduled to run through fall 2027, providing a longer-dated program runway not mentioned in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Army-funded tungsten warhead development runs through fall 2027.”

description: Corebridge reported operating EPS of $1.12, above the $1.08 consensus, despite a weak contribution from Variable Investment Income. Run-rate operating EPS was $1.35 after adjusting for below-target VII, indicating stronger underlying earnings than the headline comparison suggested.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted pretax operating income was $664 million with EPS of $1.12, while run rate operating EPS reached $1.35, up 16% year-over-year after adjusting for below-target Variable Investment Income.”
expectation_evidence: “Operating EPS: Q2 2026 consensus $1.08.”

description: Variable Investment Income remained weak and management expects it to stay below target for the rest of the year, rather than rebound. That leaves Corebridge diverging from peers that were guiding to second-half improvement.
fact_evidence: “Variable Investment Income underperformed due to weak private equity marks and is expected to remain below target for the remainder of the year, diverging from peers guiding to second-half improvement.”
expectation_evidence: “Variable investment income was weak in Q1 ($22M vs. $88M a year ago) — watch for a rebound, as it swings operating EPS quarter to quarter.”

description: The merger’s combined-company targets are more specific and accelerated than the preview’s stated synergy and accretion goals: management now targets $5 billion of earnings, $4 billion of cash generation, and over 15% ROE by 2027. The preview described more than $500 million of synergies and over 10% EPS accretion by the end of 2028.
fact_evidence: “The combined Corebridge-Equitable company targets $5 billion of earnings, $4 billion of cash generation, and over 15% ROE by 2027, supported by $500 million in cost synergies.”
expectation_evidence: “The companies target more than $500 million of run-rate expense synergies and >10% EPS accretion by end-2028.”

description: Buybacks are set to slow sharply after Q2: management expects only approximately $350 million of repurchases in the second half, despite more than $1.4 billion of holdco liquidity above 12-month needs. That implies about $1.9 billion of buybacks for 2026, a slower pace than the preview’s question about whether the large buyback pace would continue ahead of the merger.
fact_evidence: “Management guided to only approximately $350 million in share repurchases for the second half despite holding over $1.4 billion in holdco liquidity exceeding 12-month needs, implying roughly $1.9 billion of total 2026 buybacks.”
expectation_evidence: “Merger execution: any update on regulatory approvals (‘on track’ as of the Q1 call), integration planning, synergy phasing, and whether the buyback pace continues ahead of the close.”

description: Institutional Markets reversed the weak flow trend highlighted in the preview, with APTOI up 36% year over year and reserves expanding 17%. The quarter also included $1.8 billion of GIC issuances, and management described the low GIC share of the general account as room to grow.
fact_evidence: “Institutional Markets APTOI grew 36% year-over-year on 17% reserve expansion, with $1.8 billion of GIC issuances in the quarter”; GICs are “just 5% of the general account versus 10-15% for peers.”
expectation_evidence: “Institutional Markets premiums/deposits fell 45%. Watch flows and spread income in the retirement businesses.”

description: Life Insurance’s run-rate APTOI came in above the top of guidance on favorable mortality, outperforming the weak segment trend suggested by the prior quarter. Reported APTOI still fell year over year, but the run-rate result was better than management’s stated range.
fact_evidence: “Life Insurance delivered run rate APTOI of $122 million above the top end of guidance on favorable mortality, though reported APTOI declined 11% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 adjusted pre-tax operating income fell YoY in Individual Retirement (−9%), Group Retirement (−28%), and Life (−11%).”

description: Regulatory progress was more concrete than the preview’s description of approvals as the main remaining merger condition: federal antitrust and FINRA approvals are complete, all state and international filings have been submitted, and the deal remains on track for a year-end close.
fact_evidence: “The merger regulatory process is advancing with federal antitrust and FINRA approvals complete and all state/international filings submitted, keeping the transaction on track to close by year-end 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “With both shareholder bases having approved the Equitable merger on July 30 … regulatory approvals [are] the principal remaining condition.”

description: FRP cut full-year NOI guidance to about $36.2 million from its original $37.1 million plan. Delayed industrial lease-up and D.C. multifamily headwinds drove the reduction, partly offset by stronger mining performance.
fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year NOI guidance to approximately $36.2 million from an original plan of $37.1 million,” driven by “$800,000 in delayed industrial lease-up and $1 million of D.C. multifamily headwinds,” partly offset by “$850,000 of stronger mining performance.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Industrial tenant interest had not converted into signed leases as the preview hoped to see: only about 20,700 square feet were signed, despite 97,500 square feet in active negotiations. Management said stronger tenant activity had not yet translated into signed leases.
fact_evidence: “Only about 20,700 square feet have been signed with 97,500 square feet in active negotiation,” and “stronger tenant activity has not yet translated into signed leases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for signed leases converting to occupancy” after management reported “53,000 sq ft signed or under LOI.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: A Maryland same-store industrial portfolio suffered a sharp occupancy decline, from 92% in Q1 2025 to 70.6%, due to lost government tenants and a tenant bankruptcy. That specific deterioration adds to the industrial leasing weakness flagged in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The Maryland same-store industrial portfolio (Hollander and Cranberry) fell to 70.6% occupancy from 92% in Q1 2025 due to lost government tenants and a tenant bankruptcy.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described industrial occupancy as weak and said to “watch for signed leases converting to occupancy.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: D.C. multifamily weakness included substantial rent nonpayment, lengthy eviction timelines, and new tenants paying lower rents than departing tenants. The preview flagged underperforming D.C. assets and a goal of stabilizing occupancy, but did not anticipate these specific collection and trade-out headwinds.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 8% of tenants are not paying rent,” evictions take “12 to 18 months due to district policies,” and “new-tenant trade-out rates are running 10% below prior tenants.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted D.C. assets were underperforming and management’s “2026 priority is stabilizing DC occupancy.”

description: Management signaled that most future discretionary growth capital will go to industrial real estate, a strategic allocation shift not identified in the preview. Multifamily and mining remain part of the business, but are not the stated focus for most new discretionary growth capital.
fact_evidence: “Most future discretionary growth capital will target industrial real estate,” signaling a pivot toward that segment “while maintaining multifamily and mining.”

description: Despite shareholders pressing for repurchases and citing a roughly $40 NAV against a share price near $21.50, management reiterated that it prioritizes development over dividends or meaningful buybacks. The preview did not flag this capital-allocation debate.
fact_evidence: “Multiple shareholders, including the fourth-largest holder, pressed hard for buybacks citing a NAV near $40 versus a ~$21.50 share price,” but management “reiterated it prioritizes new development capital over dividends or meaningful buybacks.”

description: The preview treated 15% AMS/DRS organic growth as the floor for the 14th consecutive quarter. BCO reported 14%, falling short of that threshold and breaking the expected streak.
fact_evidence: “AMS/DRS grew 14% organically” and delivered its “14th consecutive quarter of mid-teens or better organic growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “would be the 14th” quarter at ≥15% and called a print below 15% the largest de-rating risk.

description: Revenue growth was slightly below the preview’s implied consensus pace: total revenue grew 7%, versus consensus-implied year-over-year growth of 7.7%. The FX tailwind was also 3%, below the roughly 6% tailwind cited for Q1.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 organic revenue growth was 4% with total revenue up 7% (including a 3% FX tailwind).”
expectation_evidence: The preview put revenue consensus at “$1.40B” and implied year-over-year growth at “+7.7%”; it also said to watch whether the FX tailwind persisted at Q1’s “~6%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Several large AMS/DRS installations moved out of Q2 into the second half because of customer timing, leaving organic growth at about 2% in North America, Latin America, and Europe. The preview did not flag these project delays, so some expected Q2 activity was deferred rather than realized in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Several large AMS/DRS installations slipped from Q2 into the second half due to customer-driven timing,” contributing to growth decelerating to “about 2% in North America, Latin America and Europe.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a 14th quarter of at least 15% AMS/DRS organic growth and discussed regional operating profit, but did not anticipate Q2 installation delays.

description: EBITDA and margins came in above the preview’s expectations: adjusted EBITDA was $257 million versus about $255 million expected, and the 18.5% margin exceeded the roughly 18.2% expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 EBITDA margins reached a record 18.5%, up 70 basis points year-over-year,” and adjusted EBITDA was “up 11% to $257 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Adj. EBITDA ~$255M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~18.2%.”

description: EPS of $2.13 beat the $2.05 consensus, but fell just short of the preview’s stated $2.15 realistic ‘beat’ threshold. The result was therefore better than consensus but a little below the preview’s higher bar.
fact_evidence: “EPS grew 18% to $2.13.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus EPS of “$2.05” and said “$2.15–2.25 is the realistic ‘beat,’ not $2.06.”

description: BCO raised full-year profit guidance, whereas the preview’s base case expected the FY26 framework to remain unchanged. The 30–50 basis-point margin-expansion framework was reaffirmed rather than narrowed.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year profit guidance, with Q2 EBITDA above the midpoint of prior guidance,” while reaffirming mid-single-digit organic growth and 30–50 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the FY framework to be “reaffirmed”; it identified a raised margin-expansion band toward 50 bps as a bull-case outcome.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Trailing 12-month free cash flow was $468 million, below the preview’s cited $502 million run rate and its roughly 50% conversion figure. Conversion was still 46%, above the 40–45% full-year target range.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $468 million with 46% EBITDA conversion, above the full-year target range of 40–45%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said TTM FCF had crossed “$500M” at “$502M, ~50% conversion.”

description: The Atleos closing timeline moved forward to early Q1 2027 from the preview’s expectation of end-Q1 2027, with substantial regulatory progress also reported.
fact_evidence: “The NCR Atleos acquisition closing timeline was moved forward to early Q1 2027,” with U.S. antitrust early termination granted and “80%+ of money transmitter jurisdictions cleared.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the deal as not closing until “end-Q1 2027” and identified international regulatory approval as the remaining gate.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: BCO reported a notable set of new customer wins that the preview had not identified: a 5,000-location U.S. retail DRS agreement, a European bank consortium outsourcing deal, and an Indonesia Mandiri Bank AMS deal covering more than a third of its ATM estate.
fact_evidence: The new wins included “a 5,000-location U.S. retail DRS enterprise agreement (nearly doubling wallet share),” a European bank consortium deal, and Mandiri Bank servicing “over 1/3 of its 13,000+ ATM estate.”

description: The call reported North America EBITDA margins at 19.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, approaching an intermediate 20% target—a margin milestone the preview did not discuss.
fact_evidence: “North America EBITDA margins hit 19.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, approaching the 20% intermediate target.”

description: Limbach’s adjusted EBITDA was $13.9 million, well below the preview’s estimated $19–20 million, while adjusted diluted EPS of $0.64 and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.39 were also below the preview’s respective consensus estimates of $0.93–$0.98 and about $0.73.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 22.3% to $13.9 million” and “adjusted diluted EPS declined to $0.64”; net income was $4.7 million, or “$0.39 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.93–0.98”; “GAAP diluted EPS ~$0.73”; “Adjusted EBITDA ~$19–20M (derived).”

description: Gross margin came in at 21.5%, below the preview’s roughly 25% consensus estimate and its 24% base estimate. The preview highlighted margin recovery as the key test, but GCR margin fell to 14.5% and ODR margin to 24%.
fact_evidence: “Total gross margin compressed sharply to 21.5%”; GCR segment margin was “14.5%” and ODR margin was “24%.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~25% (derived)” and “I model…24.0%”; the preview said “Anything below ~24% makes the FY guide arithmetically unreachable.”

description: The full-year outlook was reset in opposite directions: revenue guidance rose to $760–790 million, above the preview’s expected trimmed range, but adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to $78–84 million, below both the prior guide and the preview’s likely range.
fact_evidence: Management reset 2026 guidance, “raising revenue to $760-790 million but lowering adjusted EBITDA to $78-84 million” because of “near-term margin and execution headwinds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated a trimmed guide of “~$700–730M / $82–88M”; it also identified guidance as the “highest-variance item.”

description: Revenue was $173.5 million, below the preview’s $177–179 million consensus range, despite 21.9% reported growth. The preview had already warned that revenue consensus might be too high, but the actual result still fell short of that stated market expectation.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 21.9% to $173.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $177–179M.”

description: ODR organic revenue declined 3.4%, rather than inflecting to positive growth as the preview said it needed to do; the reported revenue increase came entirely from Pioneer Power.
fact_evidence: “The entire increase was driven by a $30.9 million contribution from the Pioneer Power acquisition, as ODR organic revenue actually declined 3.4%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “ODR organic growth…must inflect positive tonight” and modeled “ODR organic ~+3%.”

description: Limbach completed a $30 million CYMCOR acquisition, adding an immediate cash-and-revolver-funded transaction where the preview had warned that further M&A activity could be a negative. The company sees potential data-center and cross-selling benefits, but expects no CYMCOR contribution in current guidance.
fact_evidence: “The company acquired CYMCOR for $30 million (funded by cash and revolver borrowings)” and expects it to generate “$12 million of program management revenue and $4 million of adjusted EBITDA in 2027,” with “no contribution included in current guidance.” CYMCOR oversees budgets exceeding “$8 billion”; management cited roughly “$3 million” of services revenue pulling through “approximately $60 million” of bookings.
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “more M&A talk tonight would read as a negative” given rising leverage and unproven integration.

description: Adjusted EPS was $1.90, far above the preview’s $1.60 “real bar” and the $1.55 published consensus. The result also exceeded the preview’s implied $1.58–$1.64 range based on management’s prior Q2 growth framing.
fact_evidence: Materion delivered record adjusted EPS of $1.90 in Q2 2026, up 39% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: “Treat $1.60 as the real bar”; the preview also says management’s Q1 framing implied “$1.58–$1.64” for Q2.

description: Materion raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.80–$7.20, well above the preview’s existing $6.00–$6.50 range and even its bull-case guidance scenario of $6.35–$6.65.
fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.80–$7.20, up from $6.00–$6.50.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed current guidance of “$6.00–$6.50” and a bull-case outcome of “guidance narrowed/raised to $6.35–$6.65.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow was much stronger than the preview’s base-case expectation of modestly positive cash flow, and exceeded even its bull-case threshold of $40 million. This was a strong reversal from the preview’s emphasis on weak Q1 cash flow and the risk of another negative quarter.
fact_evidence: The company generated $59 million in free cash flow, approximately 150% conversion.
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “FCF modestly positive,” while the bull case specified “FCF positive $40M+”; the preview also warned about “Two consecutive negative-FCF quarters.”

description: The company raised its full-year top-line outlook to mid-teens sales growth, adding a second consecutive quarterly increase. The preview focused on a possible EPS guidance raise but did not anticipate this top-line outlook increase.
fact_evidence: The company raised its full-year top-line outlook to mid-teens sales growth, marking the second consecutive quarterly guidance increase.

description: Record value-added sales of $308.2 million topped the preview’s roughly $300.8 million implied consensus and cleared its stated $305 million threshold for a strong underlying quarter.
fact_evidence: Record value-added sales reached $308.2 million, up 15% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: The preview gave implied VA sales of “~$300.8M” and said “a $305M+ VA sales print is” what matters.

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 23.3%, above the preview’s implied estimate of about 21.3%. The beat was partly helped by roughly $2–3 million in one-time positive items, which qualifies the strength of the underlying result.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 23.3% ($71.8 million), with 250 basis points of year-over-year expansion, “though aided by roughly $2-3 million in one-time positive items.”
expectation_evidence: The preview implied adjusted EBITDA of “~$64M / ~21.3% of VA.”

description: Electronic Materials’ adjusted EBITDA margin reached 32%, substantially exceeding the preview’s 27% segment consensus and its expectation of at least 28.5% for continued expansion. Management cautioned that Q2 was likely the richest mix of the year.
fact_evidence: Electronic Materials achieved a record 32% adjusted EBITDA margin, up nearly 900 basis points year-over-year; management flagged Q2 as likely the richest mix of the year.
expectation_evidence: The segment consensus listed a “27%” margin; the preview expected “28.5%+” for a fifth consecutive quarter of margin expansion.

description: Precision Optics’ margin was 21.4%, above the preview’s 16% consensus estimate. However, its 26% sales growth was slightly below the preview’s 30% sales-growth expectation.
fact_evidence: Precision Optics surpassed 20% EBITDA margin at 21.4%, while adjusted EBITDA rose 206% year-over-year on 26% sales growth.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment consensus forecast Precision Optics sales growth of “+30%” and a “16%” margin.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog growth accelerated beyond the preview’s already strong expected pace: it was up roughly 30% year-over-year and 20% since the start of the year, versus expectations of about 20% year-over-year and 15% year-to-date.
fact_evidence: Record backlog grew roughly 30% year-over-year and 20% since the start of the year, with first-half incoming orders up nearly 30%.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 backlog was “+20% YoY and +15% YTD” and asked whether backlog would “hold the +20% YoY pace.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The defense RFQ pipeline expanded substantially beyond the preview’s $300 million reference point, with more than $500 million in open RFQs. The preview had highlighted conversion from the existing pipeline as something to watch, but did not anticipate this increase in its size.
fact_evidence: Defense had over $500 million in open RFQs, up from approximately $300 million last quarter.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$300M in open RFQs” and said to watch how much of that pipeline converted.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Space orders doubled year-over-year and now account for roughly a quarter of aerospace and defense sales, a specific strength not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of defense orders and overall A&D order rates.
fact_evidence: Space orders doubled year-over-year and now represent roughly 25% of aerospace and defense sales.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted A&D order rates running “+50% YoY” and focused on defense orders and RFQs, but did not state an expectation for space orders or their sales mix.

description: The $65 million beryllium capacity investment will push CapEx above the preview’s stated $75 million forecast, but incoming customer funds will offset the added spending. The funding offset makes the higher reported CapEx less of a cash-flow burden than the preview’s spending figures alone suggested.
fact_evidence: A $65 million customer-funded beryllium capacity investment will flow through CapEx above the disclosed $75 million forecast but be offset by incoming funds.
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “$75M capex plus $25M mine development” and said to watch for an update on “the $65M US defense investment.”

description: KHC increased the planned incremental investment by another $100 million, almost entirely for marketing, on top of the preview’s $600 million plan. That is more spending than investors were told to expect, though management framed it as an investment from a position of strength.
fact_evidence: Management announced “an additional $100 million in incremental spending—almost entirely marketing—on top of the prior $600 million,” framing it as “spending from a position of strength.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$600M reinvestment” in the U.S. business and focused on whether that spend was “buying volume and share.”

description: Only about one-third of the original $600 million investment had been spent, leaving most of the outlay for the second half. The preview emphasized whether the spending was already translating into volume and share, so the back-loaded timing makes that proof point later than investors might have hoped.
fact_evidence: Only “roughly $200 million” of the planned $600 million had been spent; the remaining roughly $500 million was weighted to the second half, broadly evenly between Q3 and Q4.
expectation_evidence: The preview said that “1H tracking to the upper half” would be a bull unlock and that the key question was whether the $600 million was “buying volume and share.”

description: Management said the 2026 investment year would not be followed by a wraparound of investment spending in 2027, presenting 2026 as the margin trough setup for 2027 growth. The preview called 2026 a trough year but did not specify whether elevated spending would continue into 2027.
fact_evidence: Management reiterated that “2026 is the base investment year with no wraparound of investment spend into 2027,” positioning it as the “margin trough setup for 2027 growth.”

description: Management disclosed 2027 inflation of 4% to 5%, a future cost pressure not flagged in the preview. It said the pressure was manageable and that productivity would offset as much as possible while margins were maintained and strengthened, tempering the adverse cost signal.
fact_evidence: Management expects “2027 inflation in the 4% to 5% range” but said it is manageable and intends to offset as much as possible through productivity while “maintaining and strengthening margins.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: U.S. consumption improved from a roughly 2.5% decline in Q2 to about a 1% decline in July, and management expects sequential improvement in Q3 and Q4. That is a more constructive demand trend than the preview’s roughly 4.3% expected company volume/mix decline suggested, although consumption and KHC’s volume/mix are not identical measures.
fact_evidence: “U.S. consumption declined about 2.5% in Q2 but improved to roughly -1% in July,” with management guiding to sequential improvement in Q3 and Q4.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed expected volume/mix of “~-4.3%” and identified volume as “the whole thesis.”

description: Heinz and U.S. condiments showed notable growth: Heinz was up 3% worldwide year-to-date, and U.S. condiments were up 3% year-to-date versus flat in the prior year. The preview highlighted Taste Elevation and emerging markets as areas to watch, but did not anticipate these specific growth figures.
fact_evidence: “Heinz grew 3% worldwide year-to-date” with a 12% increase in emerging markets in the quarter, and “U.S. condiments grew 3% year-to-date versus flat last year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Taste Elevation (Heinz, Philadelphia, sauces)” and described emerging markets as the growth narrative, but gave no expectation for these Heinz or condiment figures.

description: KHC paid down $1.9 billion of debt during the quarter and another $1 billion after quarter-end, while raising its cash-conversion expectation. The preview focused on roughly 100% FCF conversion and dividend cover, so the higher conversion expectation is favorable; free-cash-flow guidance in dollars, however, was essentially unchanged.
fact_evidence: The company “paid down $1.9 billion of debt in the quarter plus another $1 billion after quarter close, raised its cash conversion expectation, and kept free cash flow guidance essentially unchanged in dollar terms.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited an FY “FCF conversion guide ~100%” and flagged “FCF and dividend cover” as a key watch item.

description: At the midpoint, the second-half organic-sales outlook looks weaker than the first half on the surface, but management said underlying performance improves by roughly 70–80 basis points after adjusting for the Q1 snowstorm benefit and Q2 shipment phasing. The preview did not lay out this specific second-half profile, so the apparent slowdown and the more favorable normalized comparison are both new context.
fact_evidence: “At the midpoint, second-half organic sales appear weaker than the first half,” but normalizing for the “~0.7 pp Q1 snowstorm benefit” and “~0.8 pp Q2 shipment phasing into Q3” shows underlying performance improving by roughly 70–80 bps.

description: Continuing-operations revenue was just under $2.0 billion, far below the preview’s $2.68 billion consensus, which included an $804 million Food Ingredients estimate. The scope difference makes this a large reported-revenue gap, not evidence by itself of an underlying sales collapse; on the continuing-operations basis, revenue was up roughly 6%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 continuing operations revenue was just under $2 billion, up roughly 6%.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $2.68B”; the segment table includes “Food Ingredients: $804M.”

description: Adjusted operating EBITDA was $408 million, well below the preview’s roughly $538 million segment-sum bogey, which also included Food Ingredients. The comparison is therefore heavily affected by the changed reporting perimeter, although the continuing-operations figure itself rose 6%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted operating EBITDA rose 6% to $408 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Implied adj. op. EBITDA (sum of segment consensus): ~$538M”; the segment table includes Food Ingredients.

description: The full-year dollar guidance reset sharply lower than the preview’s expected ranges: sales to $7.4–$7.6 billion from an expected $10.5–$10.8 billion, and EBITDA to $1.53–$1.6 billion from $2.05–$2.15 billion. The scale of the gap is large, but it reflects a different business perimeter following the Food Ingredients divestiture rather than a like-for-like reduction in the outlook.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to sales of $7.4-$7.6 billion ... and EBITDA of $1.53-$1.6 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $10.5–10.8B sales and $2.05–2.15B adjusted operating EBITDA.”

description: Despite the lower nominal guidance, IFF raised its sales-growth outlook: the range became 2%–4%, with the low end up from 1%, rather than the preview’s expectation that the prior range would be reaffirmed at its low end. That is a positive change in the outlook on the continuing-operations basis.
fact_evidence: “Sales of $7.4-$7.6 billion (2%-4% growth, up from 1%-4%).”
expectation_evidence: “Comparable CN sales growth would land at the low end of the 1–4% range”; the base case expected guidance to be “reaffirmed at low end of sales range.”

description: The preview asked for a capital-allocation framework but did not anticipate a $2.5 billion repurchase authorization with roughly $500 million planned before the transaction closes and the remaining $2 billion afterward. The size and staged timing make this a substantial return-of-capital commitment.
fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a $2.5 billion share repurchase program”; “about $500 million expected in H2 2026” and “the remaining $2 billion following close by end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy side wants a framework: buyback size vs. further deleveraging vs. bolt-on M&A.”

description: IFF also committed more than $1 billion of divestiture proceeds to debt reduction and set a net-leverage target of 2.0x–2.5x by the end of 2027. The preview highlighted the need for a proceeds framework but did not specify an expected debt-repayment amount or target.

description: The full-year U.S. royalty-rate expansion outlook of 7–9 basis points is stronger than the preview’s expected mid-single-digit-basis-point growth. Q2’s 11-basis-point increase also indicates stronger current rate expansion than that outlook.
fact_evidence: Guidance for “U.S. royalty rate expansion to 7-9 basis points”; “U.S. average royalty rate increased 11 basis points on favorable brand mix shift.”
expectation_evidence: “U.S. effective royalty rate hit 5.22% in Q1 (+11bp); guide is mid-single-digit-bp growth.”

description: Global net rooms growth guidance rose to approximately 1.5% from about 1%, a stronger outlook than the preview’s roughly 1% full-year expectation.
fact_evidence: Guidance for “global net rooms growth to approximately 1.5% (up from ~1%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Global net rooms ~+1%” in the FY2026 guidance in force.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The U.S. conversion pipeline was up 24% year over year and 6% sequentially, with most expected 2026 openings and signed agreements converting to openings this year. That provides a more encouraging U.S. conversion and near-term opening picture than the preview’s concern about a shrinking global pipeline, although the preview had noted strong Q1 agreement growth.
fact_evidence: “The U.S. conversion pipeline is up 24% year-over-year and 6% sequentially,” with conversions expected to represent “~90% of 2026 U.S. openings” and about 75% of year-to-date signed agreements expected to open this year.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “Global pipeline” was “>77,700 rooms at Mar-26 vs. 93,000+ at Jun-25” and called the absolute contraction “a legitimate bear talking point”; it also noted Q1 franchise agreements awarded were up 65% in the U.S.

description: The call disclosed that Q3 EBITDA comparisons will lose roughly $9.5 million of prior-year liquidated damages. That creates a near-term comparison headwind not discussed in the preview, although management linked it to improved franchisee retention.
fact_evidence: “Q3 EBITDA comparisons face a headwind from roughly $9.5 million of prior-year liquidated damages that are not expected to recur, reflecting improved franchisee retention.”

description: Management gave a first-asset-disposition timetable for the hotel-ownership exit: the first sale is expected in the first half of 2027, with about $450 million of owned hotels among $650 million of related balance-sheet assets. The preview anticipated lower capital spending but did not specify a disposition timetable or the assets involved.
fact_evidence: “Capital outlays for hotel development declined 80% year-over-year in the first half as the company exits hotel ownership, with the first asset disposition expected in the first half of 2027 (~$450 million of owned hotels among $650 million in related balance sheet assets).”

description: Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.02 exceeded the preview’s cited consensus of $1.96–1.97, although it was essentially in line with the preview’s own $2.03 estimate. This is a modest beat against consensus, not against the preview’s central estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 5% to $2.02.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus was “$1.96–1.97”; the preview’s estimate was “Adj. EPS $2.03.”

description: Q2 revenue was $6.5 million, above the preview’s $5.5 million base case and its $6.0 million “real test,” though slightly below the preview’s suspect $6.71 million consensus. The result also reversed the preview’s expectation of a seasonal trough and a likely revenue miss.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenues rose 17% to $6.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | My Base | $5.5M”; “The real test is >$6.0M”; published consensus “$6.71M,” which the preview cautioned was “a weak anchor.”

description: APC revenue grew 11% year over year, rather than declining from the prior-year quarter as the preview’s $2.2 million estimate implied. The preview expected thin backlog and “no new deliveries,” making the reported growth a positive surprise.
fact_evidence: “APC up 11%” year over year.
expectation_evidence: “APC revenue | $2.2M”; “vs. $2.5M Q2’25; thin backlog, no new deliveries.”

description: FuelChem grew 21% year over year, well ahead of the preview’s roughly $3.3 million estimate versus $3.1 million a year earlier. That was stronger than the modest growth implied by the model despite the expected seasonal trough.
fact_evidence: “FuelChem up 21%” year over year.
expectation_evidence: “FUEL CHEM revenue | $3.3M”; “vs. $3.1M Q2’25”; the preview described Q2 as “FUEL CHEM’s seasonal trough.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: APC backlog reached $14.3 million, far above the preview’s $6.9 million March-quarter starting point and the roughly $7 million level it identified as a bullish threshold. The preview highlighted backlog as the most important disclosure, so the increase was a substantial positive surprise.
fact_evidence: “APC backlog reached $14.3 million at June 30, 2026—the largest quarter-end backlog since 2018”; “about $10.5 million expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.”
expectation_evidence: “APC entered the quarter with only $6.9M backlog”; the preview said a backlog “with a ‘7’ or higher handle at 6/30” would be a bull signal.

description: Margins came in materially below the preview’s 44% gross-margin estimate, with APC margin falling rather than improving. Management attributed APC’s sharp decline to project mix and execution costs, while the preview had anticipated improving APC mix.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin declined to 41% from 46%”; “APC margin dropping sharply to 36% from 44% due to project mix and execution costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | 44.0%”; “APC mix improving, FUEL CHEM softening.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview expected $3–5 million of data-center business to close by the end of Q2 or early Q3, but the update described only one inquiry that may convert before the end of Q3, with potentially material revenue in 2027. That leaves a prospective opportunity rather than a reported award and pushes the possible timing later than the preview’s stated window.
fact_evidence: “One data center inquiry may convert to a commercial award before the end of Q3 2026 via a capacity reservation agreement, potentially generating material revenue in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “$3–5M expected to close ‘by end of Q2 or early Q3’”; the preview asked whether a data-center SCR award had converted.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The data-center opportunity was described at a much larger scale than the preview’s $75–100 million total pipeline: the reported figure was approximately $75–100 million per project, with projects potentially involving 30–40 units. This is a major increase in the stated potential size, although it remains pipeline rather than awarded revenue.
fact_evidence: “The data center sales pipeline approximates $75–$100 million per project,” with units priced at “$1–$4 million” and projects ranging “up to 30–40 units.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$75–100M pipeline” and “8–10 projects at $1–3M per unit.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The FuelChem demonstration had not converted and was paused; it was now expected to restart only in mid-Q4. That is later and less advanced than the preview’s near-term conversion watch, though the potential annualized revenue if it converts remained in the same range.
fact_evidence: “A paused FuelChem demonstration is expected to restart in mid-Q4 2026” and, if converted, “could add $2.5–$3 million in annualized revenue in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a demonstration “that started November 2025” and flagged conversion as a near-term item; it said conversion adds “$2.5–3.0M annualized” and noted management had said “later in the year.”

description: The CEO’s retirement, effective just days after the release, and the appointment of a successor were not anticipated in the preview. The successor’s M&A and operating experience could support the company’s acquisition strategy, but the transition itself adds uncertainty.
fact_evidence: “CEO Vincent Arnone will retire effective August 10, 2026, after 27 years, succeeded by Ramesh Nagahali,” who brings “M&A and operational experience relevant to potential acquisition strategy.”

description: Continuing-operations revenue was $334 million, below the preview’s $369–376 million consensus range and its $360–375 million base estimate. The preview anticipated provisional-pricing pressure, but the reported result was also affected by Greens Creek concentrate produced in Q2 but not sold until early August, shifting revenue into Q3.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue from continuing operations fell to $334 million from the record $411 million in Q1, driven by lower metal prices and a timing gap where Greens Creek silver concentrate was produced but not sold until early August, shifting that revenue into Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $368.8M – $375.5M”; “Revenue $360–375M” in the preview’s base estimate.

description: Hecla cut Keno Hill’s full-year silver outlook to 2.2–2.6 million ounces and said meaningfully higher production is not expected until roughly the end of 2029. The preview expected full-year production guidance to be reaffirmed and described the ramp as gated by permit amendments not expected until mid-2029.
fact_evidence: “Keno Hill's full-year silver guidance was cut to 2.2-2.6 million ounces as the company deliberately runs the mine at a lower rate, with a ramp-up to meaningfully higher production not expected until roughly the end of 2029 pending permits and infrastructure investment.”
expectation_evidence: “Production guidance 15.1–16.5 Moz Ag / 51–55 koz Au reaffirmed”; “the 440 tpd ramp remains gated on permit amendments not expected until mid-2029. Watch for any pull-forward.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview expected the quarter’s free cash flow to be $90–130 million and to decline from Q1’s record $144 million. Instead, Q2 free cash flow was $136 million, slightly above that estimate range and nearly matching the Q1 record.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of $136 million nearly matched last quarter's record $144 million with all three mines contributing.”
expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow $90–130M” and “Down from Q1's record $144M.”

description: Greens Creek guidance improved: full-year silver production guidance was raised to 8.0–8.3 million ounces and cash-cost guidance improved to negative $12.15 to negative $12.00 per ounce. The preview expected production guidance to be reaffirmed and identified better-than-guidance costs as a possible positive.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year Greens Creek guidance to 8.0-8.3 million ounces of silver with cash costs improving to negative $12.15 to negative $12.00 per ounce.”
expectation_evidence: “Production guidance 15.1–16.5 Moz Ag / 51–55 koz Au reaffirmed”; “A cost guidance cut is plausible and would be a genuine positive.”

description: Lucky Friday lowered its full-year cash-cost guidance to $9.00–$9.75 per ounce, while the preview had highlighted possible cost-guidance reductions generally rather than this specific mine-level improvement.
fact_evidence: “[Management] lowered Lucky Friday cash cost guidance to $9.00-$9.75 per ounce.”
expectation_evidence: “Cost guidance revision — a cut to AISC guidance partially offsets the price shock and is the most likely positive surprise.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Greens Creek and Lucky Friday each set new site-level quarterly free-cash-flow records, and Lucky Friday also produced a record 1.5 million ounces of silver. The preview expected total silver production to be roughly in line, but did not anticipate these mine-level records.
fact_evidence: “Greens Creek and Lucky Friday each set new site-level quarterly free cash flow records of $130 million and $88 million, respectively, and Lucky Friday posted a record 1.5 million ounces of silver on higher mill rates.”
expectation_evidence: “Silver production 3.8–4.1 Moz” and “~3.9 Moz” consensus.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management described a potential Greens Creek pyrite-concentrate circuit that could add about 1.0–1.2 million ounces of silver and 10,000–15,000 ounces of gold annually for relatively low capital investment. The preview did not flag this potential production project.
fact_evidence: “The proposed Greens Creek pyrite concentrate circuit could add roughly 1.0-1.2 million ounces of silver and 10,000-15,000 ounces of gold annually at low capital intensity of $40-60 million and incremental operating costs of $10-15 million per year, with first production targeted for Q4 2027 to H1 2028.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management highlighted a large but still unproven tailings-reprocessing opportunity at Greens Creek: more than 600,000 ounces of gold in the tailings and Phase 3 metallurgical testing beginning this month. The preview did not mention this opportunity, and the call facts do not establish that the gold can be recovered economically.
fact_evidence: “The Greens Creek tailings reprocessing project contains over 600,000 ounces of gold with an in-situ value estimated near $6.1 billion at June 30 prices, with Phase 3 metallurgical test work commencing this month to determine viability.”

description: Management said fuel is only about 3% of consolidated costs, limiting the effect of oil-price spikes. The preview raised cost inflation at Lucky Friday and Keno Hill as a risk but did not identify this degree of fuel-cost insulation.
fact_evidence: “Fuel represents only about 3% of the consolidated cost structure due to high-grade underground mining and hydro-based power, insulating margins from oil price spikes relative to peers.”
expectation_evidence: “Cost inflation at Lucky Friday/Keno Hill” was listed as a bear-case driver.

description: Revenue was $25.7 million, about 9% above the preview’s $23.56 million consensus. The preview’s bull case was also close at $25.5 million, but the reported result substantially exceeded its base-case expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $25.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | ~$23.56M”; the preview’s base scenario was $23.0M.

description: The quarter produced $2 million of net income and $0.47 per diluted share, far above the preview’s near-break-even base EPS estimate and the dispersed consensus range. The preview cautioned that EPS estimates were unreliable, so the size of the beat should be treated cautiously.
fact_evidence: “Q1 net income turned positive at $2 million (47 cents per diluted share).”
expectation_evidence: Published consensus EPS ranged from “$(0.01) to $0.07”; the preview’s base scenario estimated “~$0.00” EPS.

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.5 million, well above the preview’s $0.6 million base-case estimate. The preview expected the positive-EBITDA streak to continue, but the reported quarterly amount was much stronger than its modeled outcome.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.5 million from $200,000 year-over-year,” the seventh consecutive positive quarter.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario projected “Adj. EBITDA ~$0.6M”; it also said a seventh straight positive quarter was part of the base case.

description: Gross margin reached 34.6%, well above the preview’s expectation of roughly 30%. About 130 basis points came from a one-time tariff-related net benefit, but margin still exceeded the expected level after accounting for that benefit.
fact_evidence: “Overall gross margin expanded to 34.6% from 30.1%, though roughly 130 basis points came from a one-time net benefit of tariff changes and refunds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~30% (guided)” and said a 30–31% result was fully guided.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog fell to approximately $24 million from $30.1 million at the end of Q4, a larger sequential drop than the preview’s base-case range of $28–32 million. The preview had warned that a decline toward the mid-$20 millions would undermine confidence in the full-year outlook.
fact_evidence: “Backlog exiting Q1 stood at approximately $24 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said backlog holding “≥$30M” was the bull case, while its base scenario anticipated “backlog ~$28–32M”; it warned that a decline “toward the mid-$20Ms” would undermine the guide.

description: Management said it does not expect the intra-year revenue ramp seen in prior years because Q1 benefited from a roughly $15 million exterior-lighting project recognized largely across Q4 and Q1. That makes the strong Q1 result more project-timing-dependent than a steady quarterly run rate, while the preview had derived consensus from an even annual cadence and described Q1 as structurally the weakest quarter.
fact_evidence: “Management does not expect the intra-year revenue ramp seen in prior years, as Q1 was bolstered by a ~$15 million exterior lighting project largely recognized across Q4 and Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had indicated FY27 should “play out relatively evenly over the year” and derived an even-quarter range of “$23.75–24.25M”; it also said “Q1 is structurally the weakest quarter.”

description: LED revenue was $17.7 million, above the preview’s already-strong bull-case threshold of more than $15 million and well above the roughly $12 million FY26 first-three-quarter run rate cited in the preview. LED margin also improved substantially year over year.
fact_evidence: “LED lighting segment revenue grew to $17.7 million from $12.9 million with margin improving to 37.8% from 31.8%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 LED needed to be “meaningfully above the ~$12M FY26 run-rate” and set “LED >$15M” as a bull-case marker.

description: EV charging revenue rose to $4 million, beating the preview’s bull-case marker of at least $3.5 million and reversing the sharply declining trend the preview highlighted. The increase was partly offset by weaker segment profitability.
fact_evidence: “EV charging revenue rose to $4 million from $2.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q4 revenue of $2.3 million, down 61% year over year, and used “Voltrek stabilizes ≥$3.5M” as a bull-case assumption.

description: EV charging gross margin fell to 26.9% from 33.8%, a significant deterioration alongside the revenue rebound. The preview focused on whether segment revenue would stabilize and did not anticipate this margin decline.
fact_evidence: “EV charging ... gross margin fell to 26.9% from 33.8% amid sector-wide market uncertainty.”

description: The hyperscale data-center opportunity appears to contribute later than the preview had suggested: management now expects most revenue in fiscal 2028, rather than the preview’s expectation of revenue landing in late fiscal 2027. The update also describes potentially multi-million-dollar opportunities per building, which adds scale to the longer-term opportunity.
fact_evidence: “The newly entered hyperscale data center lighting business is expected to generate most of its revenue in fiscal 2028, with each building potentially representing seven-figure (multi-million dollar) opportunities.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said data-center revenue “lands in late FY27” and expected “~zero Q1 revenue contribution.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said a potential interior Home Depot project was progressing, providing a specific additional project lead that the preview did not mention. It remains unbooked, so it is not yet backlog or secured revenue.
fact_evidence: “A potential interior Home Depot project remains unbooked but progressing.”

description: OSS raised its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 25%–30% from 20%–25%, rather than reaffirming the old range. The higher range moves beyond the preview’s most likely case, though its lower end is still 25%.
fact_evidence: “Increased full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 25%-30%, up from prior guidance of 20%-25%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a reaffirmation was the base case and that a raise was the cleanest bull catalyst; its bull case called for “above 25% growth / to $42M+.”

description: Q2 continuing-operations revenue was $9.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $8.8 million estimate and its $8.5–9.0 million beat/miss range. That is a modest beat, rather than merely the roughly 50%–60% growth expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue from continuing operations grew 62.3% year-over-year to $9.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue | ~$8.8M (derived, not published consensus)”; the caveat says to treat the threshold as “a range ($8.5–9.0M).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings remained exceptionally strong: $15.1 million and about 1.7x book-to-bill were above the preview’s base-case range of roughly 1.0–1.2x and well above the level it said should be achievable from the defense award. The ratio was just below Q1’s 1.8x, but did not show the expected possible deceleration.
fact_evidence: “Record bookings of $15.1 million in Q2 and over $30 million year-to-date, yielding a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 1.7.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “book-to-bill ~1.0–1.2x”; it said above 1.0x should be achievable, while Q1 was “~$15M bookings / 1.8x.”

description: A previously unmentioned $6.25 million legal settlement charge drove a $7.3 million GAAP loss, but excluding that charge the loss was only $0.01 per share—better than the preview’s expected $0.02–$0.03 loss. The unexpected charge and the better underlying result make this a mixed surprise.
fact_evidence: “A $6.25 million legal settlement charge drove a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $7.3 million ($0.29/share),” while excluding it “the non-GAAP net loss narrowed to just $0.2 million ($0.01/share).”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 EPS estimates of “~$(0.02) to $(0.03)” and modeled a net loss of about “$(0.03)”; it did not mention a legal settlement charge.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: OSS reported support for 14 multi-year programs with combined estimated revenue potential above $42 million, a more concrete and substantial program base than the preview had specified. The preview focused on conversions of named programs and possible new adds but gave no comparable count or combined value.
fact_evidence: “OSS is now supporting 14 multi-year programs with estimated combined revenue potential exceeding $42 million,” up from one such program three years ago.
expectation_evidence: The preview watched for “program-level conversions” and “any new prime-customer program adds,” but did not give an expectation for 14 programs or $42 million of potential.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call included a $2.2 million robotics production booking, whereas the preview explicitly treated the announced robotics order as a Q3 booking rather than a Q2 one. If included in Q2 bookings as stated, the order arrived earlier than the preview expected.
fact_evidence: “New bookings included … a $2.2 million robotics production order with $10-15 million five-year potential.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the July 21 “$2.2M autonomous construction/mining order” as “a Q3 booking, not Q2.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: OSS also reported a renewable-energy data-center order that could scale toward a $10 million opportunity, a specific new order and opportunity not identified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “New bookings included … a renewable energy data center order scaling toward a $10 million opportunity.”

description: Hagerty raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $270–280 million, well above the preview’s expected range of roughly $245–255 million in the base case and even above its $255–265 million bull case. The increase is substantially larger than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 ... adjusted EBITDA guidance to $270-280 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated guidance “raised modestly to ~$245–255M”; its bull case anticipated “$255–265M.”

description: Hagerty now expects FY2026 GAAP net income of $18–30 million, rather than the preview’s expected full-year GAAP net loss of $41–51 million. That is a substantial reversal in the expected bottom-line outlook.
fact_evidence: “Set GAAP net income guidance of $18-30 million.”
expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance was a “GAAP net loss $(51)M–$(41)M incl. ~$190M pre-tax transitional costs.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: First-half written premium growth was 19%, above the preview’s roughly 17% Q2 estimate and the then-current 15–16% full-year growth guide. Hagerty also raised its full-year written premium growth outlook, though only to 16–17%.
fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 written premium grew 19%”; full-year guidance was raised “to 16-17% (up from prior 15-16%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated written premium at “$415M (+17%)” for Q2 and identified the standing FY guide as “+15–16%.”

description: Q2 revenue appears materially above the preview’s estimate: first-half revenue of $667 million less the already reported Q1 revenue of $311.8 million implies about $355 million for Q2, versus the preview’s $320 million estimate. The preview cautioned that revenue was mechanically affected by the fronting transition, so the beat is less informative about underlying performance.
fact_evidence: “Reported GAAP revenue fell 6% to $667 million” in the first half; Q1 revenue was reported as $311.8 million in the preview, implying approximately $355 million in Q2.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue at “$320M (range $305–335M)” and cited consensus of “$315.4M – $316.2M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New business accelerated sharply, with quarterly counts rising from roughly 100,000 to 160,000, largely through State Farm conversions, and first-half member additions reaching a record 279,000. That runs against the preview’s concern that the record pace could decelerate as the prior-year comparison became harder.
fact_evidence: “Added a record 279,000 new members in the first half” and quarterly new business count jumped “from roughly 100,000 to 160,000 largely due to State Farm conversions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the +102% comp gets harder from here” and urged investors to watch “the run-rate of new business.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Hagerty Re’s first-half loss ratio was 41%, below the preview’s roughly 42% seasonal expectation. The reported 88% combined ratio also indicates somewhat better underwriting results than the preview’s cited Q2 2025 combined ratio of 89.6%.
fact_evidence: “Hagerty Re's first-half combined ratio was 88% (90% in Q2) with a loss ratio of 41%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a Q2 loss ratio of “41–42%” in its base case and described “~42% seasonal normal”; it cited Q2 2025 combined ratio of 89.6%.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Retention was 88%, below the preview’s 88.5% threshold, and declined both year over year and sequentially. The shortfall is modest, but it is a negative quality signal alongside rapid new-member growth.
fact_evidence: “Retention held at an industry-leading 88%, though it declined 50 basis points year-over-year and 30 basis points sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview set “retention ≥ 88.5%” as a key metric and called “Sub-88%” a yellow flag.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA appears slightly below the preview’s $78 million base estimate: the reported first-half $160 million less the preview’s already reported Q1 $85.2 million implies about $75 million for Q2. This modest quarterly shortfall contrasts with the much stronger full-year guidance raise.
fact_evidence: “First-half adjusted EBITDA grew 32% to $160 million”; the preview reported Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $85.2 million, implying approximately $75 million for Q2.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 adjusted EBITDA at “$78M” (range “$65–88M”).

description: Marketplace results were stronger than the preview’s concern that high auction sales might fail to translate into revenue: Q2 marketplace revenue rose 48%, and first-half marketplace sales increased 17%. Broad Arrow’s growth and sell-through rate were also strong, although private sales declined against a prior-year large collection sale.
fact_evidence: “Marketplace total sales grew 17% to $65 million with Q2 marketplace revenue up 48% to $40 million,” led by “Broad Arrow's 74% first-half sales increase and a 91% sell-through rate”; private sales declined against a prior-year large collection sale.
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged Q1’s “record $135.4M aggregate auction sales (+80%)” alongside marketplace revenue down 12%, and said “Strong headline auction totals with weak marketplace revenue is the pattern to watch for.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 oil and total production both exceeded company guidance, and Talos raised its full-year stand-alone production ranges despite excluding the pending Gulf of America acquisition and including the shelf divestment. The preview expected 2026 guidance to be reiterated rather than revised before the acquisition closed.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 oil production averaged approximately 69,000 barrels per day and total production nearly 94,000 BOE per day, both exceeding guidance”; Talos “raised full-year 2026 stand-alone production guidance to 64,000-68,000 barrels of oil per day and 87,000-91,000 BOE per day.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 guidance of oil “63–67 MBbl/d” and total “88–92 MBoe/d,” and said, “Management said it will update 2026 guidance after closing, so expect guidance to be reiterated rather than re-cut on Aug 4/5.”

description: BP declined to exercise its preferential right, preserving the Na Kika interests in the Gulf of America acquisition and allowing Talos to operate Coulomb. The preview identified an exercise of the right—and losing the Na Kika interests—as a material risk.
fact_evidence: “BP declined to exercise its preferential right, allowing Talos to operate the Coulomb field and become a partner in the Na Kika platform.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If exercised, Talos gets Coulomb only — roughly halving the deal’s scope,” and called the outcome “the single highest-information item of the event.”

description: The Gulf of America acquisition is now expected to close in Q3 2026, earlier than the preview’s expectation of closing by year-end 2026.
fact_evidence: The acquisition “is expected to close in Q3 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the acquisition was “Expected to close by year-end 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The acquisition’s stated production contribution is approximately 18,000 BOE per day, above the preview’s approximately 16,000 BOE per day estimate. The call also described accretive oil cut, operating expense, and EBITDA margins.
fact_evidence: The acquisition adds assets “producing approximately 18,000 BOE per day and roughly 20% oil production growth, with accretive oil cut, operating expense, and EBITDA margins.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the acquisition as adding “~16 MBoe/d (Q1’26, ~77% oil).”

description: Talos reported record adjusted free cash flow and adjusted EBITDA, for which the preview said it had no consensus estimates. The results therefore add a strong reported financial outcome without a preview benchmark to quantify a beat against.
fact_evidence: “The company generated record adjusted free cash flow of approximately $232 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $402 million in Q2 2026.”

description: The gas-weighted shelf divestment removed approximately $54 million of future abandonment obligations and improved the portfolio’s oil weighting; the preview did not flag this transaction or these benefits.
fact_evidence: “The noncore gas-weighted shelf divestment eliminated approximately $54 million of future abandonment obligations and improved portfolio oil weighting.”

description: Talos refinanced its 9% notes due 2029 with 8% notes due 2034, lowering the coupon and extending maturities—an unanticipated financing action in the preview, which discussed acquisition funding but not this refinancing.
fact_evidence: “The company issued $800 million of 8% senior notes due 2034 to redeem $625 million of 9% notes due 2029, lowering the coupon and extending maturities.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Before the acquisition close, cash and leverage were stronger than the preview’s Q1 balance-sheet figures: cash was about $578 million and leverage was 0.5x, versus $386.4 million and 0.8x cited in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Leverage declined to 0.5x with cash of approximately $578 million and total liquidity of approximately $1.2 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 balance-sheet figures of “$386.4M cash” and “0.8x net debt/LTM EBITDA.”

description: Talos made no share repurchases in Q2 because of an acquisition-related blackout, whereas the preview highlighted Q1 buybacks and identified the pace of buybacks during the acquisition as an open question. The call also reported that cumulative returns since Q2 2025 had reduced the share count by about 7%.
fact_evidence: “Talos returned approximately $135 million to shareholders since Q2 2025, reducing share count by about 7%, but repurchased no shares in Q2 2026 due to an acquisition-related blackout.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 buybacks of “2.7M shares / $38.2M (34% of FCF)” and said, “With $450–500M of cash going out the door for Shell, the buyback pace is a live question.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Talos disclosed a roughly 4-million-acre Honduras position and a first-ever 3D seismic program beginning in the second half of 2026, a new exploration program not discussed in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The Honduras position spans roughly 4 million acres (equivalent to 700 Gulf of America blocks) with a first-ever 3D seismic program starting in the second half of 2026.”

description: Voya reported adjusted operating EPS of $1.51, well below the preview’s $1.88–$1.99 range. The preview had already estimated a $0.50–$0.60-per-share alternative-investment drag, but the reported combined drag was about $0.90 per share and included severance costs that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted operating earnings of $1.51 per diluted share ($140 million), which included an approximate $0.90 per share drag from below-expectation alternative investment performance and severance costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$1.90 as the number to beat and $2.00 as the whisper”; the preview’s bridge estimated an “Alt investment income shortfall” of “-$0.50 to -$0.60” and implied Q2 EPS of “~$1.90–2.00.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Voya released $8 million of stop-loss reserves, whereas the preview’s base case anticipated no new release. The release is positive evidence on claims, though smaller than the prior quarter’s $25 million release noted in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company released $8 million of stop-loss reserves while holding reserves at the high end of its best estimate range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “stop loss on track, no new release”; it identified a second reserve release as part of the bull scenario.

description: Quarterly excess-capital generation was about $150 million, below the roughly $200 million per quarter the preview expected. This is a shortfall in generation even though year-to-date generation was $350 million.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $150 million of excess capital in Q2 ($350 million year-to-date).”
expectation_evidence: “~$200M/quarter generation.”

description: Voya bought back about $200 million of shares in Q2, exceeding the $150 million Q2 buyback the preview said had been committed. It also plans at least $100 million more in Q3, for which the preview gave no specific expectation.
fact_evidence: “Voya returned approximately $200 million to shareholders in Q2 ($300 million in buybacks year-to-date…) and plans at least $100 million of additional buybacks in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “$150M committed for Q2.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash conversion came in above 100%, better than the preview’s expectation of roughly 90% or more.
fact_evidence: “Cash conversion above 100%.”
expectation_evidence: “~90%+ cash conversion.”

description: Management said Q2 severance costs should be fully offset by expense savings by year-end, with a six-month payback, and expressed confidence in meaningfully higher second-half earnings. The preview did not anticipate this cost-savings timing or earnings outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management expects the Q2 severance costs to be fully offset by expense savings by year-end (a six-month payback), supporting confidence in meaningfully higher second-half earnings.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: A legacy sub-advised relationship wind-down will pressure Investment Management flows in the second half, an issue not flagged in the preview. Management said the 2026 revenue impact would be immaterial, limiting the near-term significance.
fact_evidence: “A legacy sub-advised relationship wind-down will pressure H2 flows with immaterial 2026 revenue impact.”

description: Government Services 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was updated to $55–65 million, below the preview’s $70–80 million expectation. Management also said delayed AW189 deliveries and prolonged transition costs would reduce 2026 adjusted operating income by about $8 million, rather than the transition-cost roll-off the preview was watching for.
fact_evidence: “Government Services 2026 guidance was updated to $475 million-$495 million in revenue and $55 million-$65 million in adjusted operating income”; delayed Leonardo AW189 deliveries “adversely impacted 2026 Government Services adjusted operating income by approximately $8 million through elevated KPI penalties and prolonged transition costs.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 segment guide is $70–80M”; the preview said to watch whether “UKSAR2G transition costs ... are rolling off.”

description: Offshore Energy Services adjusted operating income guidance was raised to $235–245 million, above the preview’s $225–235 million range, on stronger rates and activity and contracts lasting longer than expected.
fact_evidence: “The Offshore Energy Services segment's 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was raised to $235 million-$245 million on stronger rates, activity, and longer-than-expected contracts.”
expectation_evidence: “OES needs ~$58–62M/quarter of adj. op income ... to hit the $225–235M guide.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was implied at about $79.8 million—$59.3 million in Q1 plus the reported $20.5 million sequential increase—slightly above the preview’s $73–78 million estimate. The increase was supported by lower repairs and maintenance costs, contrary to the preview’s concern about a second consecutive quarter of R&M inflation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased $20.5 million sequentially, driven by higher utilization, fuel revenues, and lower repairs and maintenance costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$73–78M”; the preview warned that “a second consecutive quarter of R&M inflation breaks the guidance bridge.”

description: A jet-fuel price spike reduced Government Services profitability by $1.5 million through the UKSAR2G deferred price adjustment mechanism. The preview did not flag this cost, although the company said a contract amendment had tightened the mechanism and the issue should not recur.
fact_evidence: “A jet fuel price spike hurt Government Services profitability by $1.5 million due to a UKSAR2G deferred price adjustment mechanism, which has since been tightened via contractual amendment and should not recur.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash flow turned positive at $41.4 million in Q2 after an $8.3 million use in Q1, a stronger indication of working-capital normalization than the preview had quantified.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow swung to $41.4 million positive in Q2 from an $8.3 million use in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the CFO “guided to working-capital normalization,” while noting Q1 operating cash flow was “−$8.3M.”

description: The preview expected management to reaffirm 15–20% Belmont Core growth, but the call reaffirmed growth of about 15%, the bottom of that range. With first-half growth at only 3%, reaching the reaffirmed target requires very strong growth in the second half.
fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed full-year Belmont Core gross written premium growth of ~15% over 2025, despite only 3% growth in the first half, implying very strong double-digit growth is required in the second half.
expectation_evidence: Management guided on the Q1 call to 15–20% full-year growth in Belmont core gross premium. The preview said the bull case required management “reaffirming 15–20% Belmont core growth.”

description: The expense ratio was materially worse than the preview’s on-track threshold: it was 40.9%, versus an expectation that Q2 would be below 39%. Management also put the return to roughly 36% in the latter half of 2028, later and more precisely than the preview’s description of optimization over the next seven quarters.
fact_evidence: The expense ratio is elevated at 40.9%, running roughly 4.5 points above long-term targets due to Catalyx/Kaleidoscope technology investments, with management targeting a return to ~36% by the latter half of 2028.
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is seasonally better (38.8% in Q2 2025). Sub-39% is on-track; 40%+ again says the program isn't converting.” The preview also said optimization was a “major tactical objective over the next seven quarters.”

description: Valiant Re assumed reinsurance grew sharply, a segment development the preview did not flag: Q2 premiums rose 79%, and the treaty count expanded with three additions. This is a notable source of growth beyond the preview’s focus on Belmont Core and Wholesale Commercial.
fact_evidence: Valiant Re assumed reinsurance premiums surged 79% in Q2 to $21.5 million (43% for the half), with in-force treaties expanding to 22 after adding 3 new treaties in the quarter.

description: Specialty products premiums fell sharply because products were terminated, a decline not anticipated in the preview. The ongoing programs were nearly stable, so the reported drop was concentrated in discontinued products rather than broad weakness across the remaining programs.
fact_evidence: Specialty products premiums fell 36% in Q2 to $7.8 million due to terminated products, though the 11 ongoing programs were only down 1%.

description: Penn-America returned to growth at 2% after two quarterly declines, but management’s accompanying warning of intensifying E&S competition and moderating rate momentum tempers that improvement. The preview discussed softening market conditions, but did not anticipate this specific segment’s return to growth or the call’s rate commentary.
fact_evidence: Penn-America returned to growth (+2% in Q2) after two consecutive quarterly declines, but management flagged intensifying E&S competition with flat first-half rate change and moderating rate momentum.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The investment portfolio’s book yield was somewhat better than the preview’s roughly 4.3% estimate, and management gave a 4.9% year-end 2026 target. The reported 1.08-year duration, however, remained close to the short-duration positioning the preview described.
fact_evidence: The fixed income book yield rose to 4.42% with a short 1.08-year duration, with $177 million of maturities reinvested at 5.45%, and management targets a 4.9% book yield by year-end 2026.
expectation_evidence: The preview described the portfolio as having a “roughly 1-year duration, 4.3% book yield” and said management had signaled possible extension within 12–24 months.

description: Discretionary capital was $302 million, above the preview’s $290 million figure, but management said fully deploying it would take 2 to 2.5 years. The preview already expected no buybacks, so that part of the capital stance was not a surprise.
fact_evidence: Discretionary capital stood at $302 million, with management expecting a 2 to 2.5-year ramp to fully deploy it and no share buybacks currently planned.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$290M of discretionary capital” and said “No buybacks planned for 2026.”

description: FY2026 sales guidance jumped to $1.02–1.06 billion from $890–970 million. Much of the increase is sulfur-cost pass-through—now expected to be $220 million rather than $155 million—so the higher sales outlook does not translate proportionally into EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 sales guidance was raised to $1.02-1.06 billion (from $890-970 million), driven partly by higher sulfur pass-through now expected at $220 million versus $155 million prior.”
