expectation_evidence: “FY26 consensus revenue of $966.7M is within $3M of the top of the $890–970M range”; the prior company guidance assumed “~$155M of sulfur cost pass-through.”

description: Q2 sales were $250 million, about $12 million above the $237.54 million consensus estimate, but most of the year-over-year increase came from sulfur pass-through with no material EBITDA impact. The revenue beat was therefore less substantial economically than the headline suggests.
fact_evidence: “Q2 sales were $250 million, up $74 million year-over-year, though approximately $55 million of that increase was sulfur cost pass-through with no material EBITDA impact.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus: $237.54M.”

description: The updated EBITDA outlook included a modest improvement in the legacy business, rather than only adding Calabrian to the prior forecast: the legacy-business low end rose from $180 million to $185 million. The overall $195–207 million range is close to the preview’s expected additive range, so the upside is mainly this organic floor increase.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $195-207 million, with legacy business guidance low end lifted to $185 million and Calabrian expected to contribute $10-12 million in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a clean additive update would be “roughly $190–205M” and described its base case as “~$185–197M organic plus ~$11M Calabrian → ~$196–208M; no organic raise.”

description: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance rose to $0.58–0.72 from the prior $0.50–0.65 range, putting the consensus estimate of $0.66 inside the updated range rather than above its top end.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS is guided to $0.58-0.72.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$0.50–0.65” and noted that “FY26 consensus EPS of $0.66 sits above the top of the company's $0.50–0.65 guide.”

description: Adjusted free-cash-flow guidance increased at the low end to $45 million from $40 million, despite capex guidance also moving up. This reverses the preview’s concern that cash flow was the likeliest place for a quiet disappointment.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to $45-55 million … with capex now $85-95 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave prior adjusted FCF guidance of “$40–55M” and said, “This is the most likely place for a quiet disappointment.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Virgin sulfuric acid volume grew at a double-digit rate, a stronger reported volume signal than the preview’s expectation that mining-driven demand would hold and its call to watch for volume evidence.
fact_evidence: “Virgin sulfuric acid volume grew double digits year-over-year, aided by the Waggaman plant acquired in May 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “mining-driven virgin acid demand” as a tailwind and said to watch whether “mining virgin acid demand” was holding.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management warned of a possible temporary destocking-related demand impact, adding a specific near-term risk to the sulfur outlook. The preview had flagged industrial softness and expected sulfur easing in Q4, but did not identify destocking as a risk.
fact_evidence: “Management expects sulfur prices to plateau or moderate modestly with a risk of temporary destocking-related demand impact.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “potential softness in some industrial applications” and said management “expects easing in Q4.”

description: The preview expected modest or moderate full-year operating profit, but management now expects a moderate operating loss for 2026. That is a clear deterioration from the recovery outlook investors were told to expect.
fact_evidence: Management expects a “moderate operating loss for full-year 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management was expected to reiterate “modest/moderate full-year 2026 operating profit guidance” and described a guidance cut to the “modest full-year operating profit” outlook as a bear-case risk.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings rose 17% sequentially and more than doubled from Q2 2025, reaching their highest quarterly level in three years. The preview expected momentum to confirm an H2 inflection, but did not anticipate growth of this scale.
fact_evidence: Bookings reached $680 million, “up 17% sequentially and more than double Q2 2025,” and were the “highest quarterly level in 3 years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “bookings/backlog momentum confirming the H2 inflection” as a key watch item; Q1 bookings had increased 7% sequentially.

description: Despite the preview’s expectation that Q2 would be the low point for operating profit, the operating loss improved by about $10 million from Q1. This was a better quarter-to-quarter operating result than the trough framing implied.
fact_evidence: The consolidated operating loss improved to $18 million, “roughly $10 million better than Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 2026 is expected to be the low point for operating profit and net income.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash flow turned positive rather than continuing the cash burn highlighted in the preview. Operating cash flow improved by about $50 million from Q1, when it was negative.
fact_evidence: Operating cash flow “turned positive at $17 million,” an improvement of “approximately $50 million from Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “cash burn and leverage” as a Q2 watch item and described continued cash burn as a bear-case concern.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The $35 million tariff refund did not provide straightforward relief: it was largely offset by unfavorable capitalized material costs and higher gross tariff expense. The preview was looking for tariff mitigation, so the offsetting costs limit the benefit investors might have expected from refunds.
fact_evidence: The quarter included “$35 million in tariff refunds,” largely offset by “unfavorable capitalized material costs and $10 million in higher gross tariff expenses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “progress on [tariff] mitigation” as a key watch item and noted “~$40M of tariff refund applications and $15–20M expected from suppliers.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Bookings have not yet translated into shipments as quickly as the preview’s H2 recovery framing might suggest: production is temporarily lagging, with trucks being reshored to North America and customer deliveries rescheduled. This adds a specific near-term execution constraint to the expected backlog-led recovery.
fact_evidence: Management said production growth is “temporarily lagging bookings” because trucks planned for Europe are being reshored to North America after the April Section 232 tariff change and customer delivery rescheduling.
expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated a “meaningful second-half recovery driven by rebuilding backlog, tariff mitigation, and restructuring savings” and highlighted bookings/backlog momentum as confirmation of the H2 inflection.

description: Management added a longer-range recovery marker not covered in the preview: it expects trailing 12-month EBITDA to exceed pre-COVID levels in the second half of 2027 and targets 7% operating profit over the cycle. The targets are positive, though they are distant and depend partly on footprint savings.
fact_evidence: Management expects trailing 12-month EBITDA to exceed pre-COVID levels in the second half of 2027, cites $15–$20 million in annualized benefits from manufacturing footprint optimization, and targets “7% operating profit over the cycle.”

description: DK reported adjusted EBITDA of about $639 million and adjusted EPS of $5.48, far above the preview’s implied $400–425 million EBITDA bar and the most current $2.39–$2.67 EPS estimates. Even excluding the 50% RVO adjustment, EBITDA was about $490 million and EPS about $3.64, still a substantial beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of approximately $344 million ($5.48 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $639 million, though excluding the 50% RVO adjustment, adjusted EBITDA was ~$490 million and adjusted EPS ~$3.64.”
expectation_evidence: “$2.39” and “$2.67” Q2 adjusted EPS estimates; “adjusted EBITDA of roughly $400–425M.”

description: DKL produced about $144 million of EBITDA, slightly above the preview’s $130–140 million read-through, and set a company quarterly record. The upside versus the expected range was modest.
fact_evidence: “The Logistics segment (DKL) posted its best quarterly results in company history at approximately $144 million in adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “Read-through is a Q2 logistics contribution around $130–140M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management was strongly optimistic about pending 2025 SRE petitions and cited a $468.4 million 2025 RVO obligation at roughly $1 per gallon RIN pricing. The preview expected no sizing of the August exemption and treated further relief as uncertain; the call offered more concrete context, though it did not give a dollar value for the exemption itself.
fact_evidence: “Krotz Springs was recently awarded a small refinery exemption after a prior denial,” and management expressed “strong optimism about pending 2025 SRE petitions,” citing “the total 2025 RVO obligation at $468.4 million at roughly $1 per gallon RIN pricing.”
expectation_evidence: “SRE deferred to Q3 with no sizing”; the preview also said the market wanted “a dollar figure and a share count” for the exemption.

description: Management introduced a mid-cycle free-cash-flow outlook of $650–700 million, equivalent to a roughly 15–20% yield at current prices. The preview discussed the balance sheet and buybacks but gave no comparable FCF forecast.
fact_evidence: “Management projects mid-cycle free cash flow of $650 million to $700 million including DKL distributions, representing a roughly 15% to 20% free cash flow yield at current prices.”

description: DK did repurchase shares, but Q2 buybacks were about $20 million—some activity after almost none in Q1, but not evidence of the large-scale step-up the preview identified as a possible catalyst. The reported 10% cumulative repurchase since early 2025 adds context but does not make the quarter’s buyback amount large.
fact_evidence: “Returned capital during the quarter via ~$16 million in dividends and ~$20 million in buybacks,” and “repurchased approximately 10% of the company since the beginning of 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the absence of a buyback step-up would be conspicuous” and listed “evidence of meaningful Q2/July repurchase” as a catalyst.

description: The company reduced its term loan by $70 million and stand-alone net debt by $72 million in the quarter, an additional balance-sheet improvement not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Refinanced its term loan, reducing it from $920 million to $850 million,” while “stand-alone Delek net debt (excluding DKL) declined by $72 million in the quarter.”

description: Q3 guidance included no planned turnarounds for the rest of the year and throughput of 296,000–316,000 barrels per day. The preview flagged Q3 guidance as important but did not anticipate a no-turnaround schedule or provide a Q3 throughput range.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for total system throughput of 296,000 to 316,000 barrels per day with no planned turnarounds for the rest of the year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Q3 guidance — throughput, turnaround calendar” as a key item to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said the sharp easing in crude backwardation—from $6–7+ in Q2 to about $1.50 in Q3—should improve refining margin capture roughly one-for-one. This was a favorable Q3 margin-capture signal not specified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Crude backwardation eased sharply from $6-$7+ in Q2 to a roughly flat curve (~$1.50) in Q3,” and management said it “should translate roughly one-to-one into improved refining margin capture.”

description: Kadant reported adjusted EPS of $3.42, far above the $2.94 consensus and $0.44 above the high end of its prior guidance. The call attributed the beat to lower operating expenses and stronger acquisition performance.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS reached a record $3.42, up 26% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance by $0.44 due to lower operating expenses and stronger acquisition performance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Consensus | $2.94”; company guidance was “$2.88–$2.98.”

description: Revenue of $313 million exceeded the $299.17 million consensus by about 4.6%. The reported 23% total growth included 8% organic growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 23% to a record $313 million, with organic revenue up 8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $299.17 million.”

description: The full-year revenue range rose to $1.19B–$1.21B, and the adjusted EPS floor increased from $12.33 to $12.43 while the ceiling stayed at $12.68. This modest improvement contrasts with the preview’s focus on whether the prior EPS guidance cut would persist.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.19B-$1.21B and narrowed adjusted EPS guidance to $12.43-$12.68, up from $12.33-$12.68.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 full-year guidance” was “Revenue: $1.178B–$1.203B” and “Adjusted EPS: $12.33–$12.68”; the preview said to watch “for any update to the $12.33–$12.68 FY adjusted-EPS range.”

description: Despite the strong Q2 beat and higher full-year guidance, Q3 guidance was $297M–$307M in revenue and $2.90–$3.00 in adjusted EPS, with management cautious about capital-project timing. The preview highlighted guidance sensitivity and bookings momentum but did not anticipate this specific near-term outlook.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $297M-$307M and adjusted EPS of $2.90-$3.00, implying no upside from the Q2 beat as management remains cautious on capital project timing.”
expectation_evidence: “Forward commentary — especially any update to the $12.33–$12.68 FY adjusted-EPS range — is likely to matter more for the share-price reaction than the Q2 beat/miss itself.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 21.8% from 20.5%, even as gross margin fell and the aftermarket mix declined. The preview expected aftermarket mix to support margin resilience, but did not anticipate this degree of EBITDA margin expansion.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $68.1 million, up 30%, with margin expanding to 21.8% from 20.5% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Continuation of this mix supports margin resilience.”

description: Organic capital revenue surged 23%, reaching the company’s second-best Q2 capital-equipment revenue in its history despite a prolonged capital-investment downturn. That strength was not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of demand and bookings.
fact_evidence: “Organic capital revenue surged 23%, representing the second-best Q2 capital equipment revenue in company history despite a prolonged capital investment downturn.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 bookings and backlog as “a positive underlying demand signal to reconcile against cautious guidance,” but did not flag a capital-revenue surge.

description: Gross margin declined 210 basis points to 43.8% as aftermarket parts fell to 68% of revenue from 71%. This runs counter to the preview’s expectation that continued aftermarket mix would support margin resilience.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 210 basis points to 43.8% as higher-margin aftermarket parts fell to 68% of revenue from 71%, reflecting a higher capital mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Aftermarket parts revenue has been a recurring highlight”; “continuation of this mix supports margin resilience.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings rose 16%, but the preview had pointed to Q1’s record bookings and backlog as a positive demand signal; Q2 bookings were lower than that Q1 record, and large capital-project orders were delayed. The reported total was supported by acquisitions and aftermarket parts rather than broad capital-project momentum.
fact_evidence: “Bookings increased 16% to $312 million, driven by recent acquisitions and strong aftermarket parts demand, even as large capital project orders were delayed.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 2026 bookings were a record $320.8M (+25.2%, +10% organic) with backlog of $326M” and were described as “a positive underlying demand signal to reconcile against cautious guidance.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net debt rose $129 million sequentially after acquisition borrowing, and leverage increased to 1.72 from 1.27. The preview discussed acquisition-related EPS dilution but did not flag this increase in borrowing or leverage.
fact_evidence: “Net debt rose $129 million sequentially to $373 million after borrowing $181.8 million for acquisitions, lifting the leverage ratio to 1.72 from 1.27.”

description: Capital expenditures more than doubled to $10.9 million, partly because Kadant purchased a facility it had previously leased. This facility purchase and higher capex were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures more than doubled to $10.9 million partly due to purchasing a previously leased facility.”

description: IPAR held full-year guidance at about $1.48 billion in sales and $4.85 EPS, rather than raising it toward the preview’s higher consensus estimates of $1.50 billion and $4.88. The preview said a reaffirmation would be a mild negative because the Street was leaning toward a raise.
fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was maintained at approximately $1.48 billion in sales and $4.85 diluted EPS.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 consensus: $1.50B / $4.88”; “consensus already assumes a modest raise”; “a simple reaffirm is a mild negative.”

description: The company now expects full-year gross margin to improve about 150 basis points, rather than stay flat as management had previously targeted and the preview expected. Tariff refunds are expected to contribute 110 basis points, with mix and cost efficiencies providing the rest.
fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin is expected to improve roughly 150 basis points, with 110 basis points from tariff refunds and the balance from mix and cost efficiencies.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had a “flat full-year GM target” and listed “anything above that” as a genuine positive surprise.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: IPAR recognized $6.9 million of IEEPA tariff refunds in Q2, with the remaining refunds expected to benefit Q3 and Q4. The preview identified the roughly $17 million refund as a major uncertainty and described its base case as the refund remaining excluded, so the reported recognition and timing are favorable relative to that case.
fact_evidence: “The company received $17.6 million in IEEPA tariff refunds ($6.9 million recognized in Q2) that will benefit Q3 and Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the refunds were “explicitly excluded from guidance” and that the base case assumed “refund still excluded”; it also called whether any refund would be recognized or deferred the largest EPS swing factor.

description: IPAR authorized a share repurchase program for both Interparfums, Inc. and Interparfums SA shares, backed by a new credit line of up to $250 million. The preview did not anticipate this capital-allocation announcement; the buyback is favorable, while the credit-line funding makes the development mixed.
fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a share repurchase program (for both Interparfums, Inc. and Interparfums SA shares) backed by a new line of credit of up to $250 million.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half operating cash flow rose to $46 million from $5 million, alongside a 12% inventory reduction. The preview did not flag cash generation or this working-capital improvement as an earnings debate, making the stronger cash flow an unanticipated positive.
fact_evidence: “H1 operating cash flow surged to $46 million (49% of net income) from $5 million (5%) prior year, aided by a 12% inventory reduction to $376 million and the tariff refunds.”

description: Asia Pacific grew 14% and South America 15%, while the Middle East and Africa fell 24% due to the war. The preview focused on the Middle East headwind and U.S./European performance, but did not anticipate these strong results in other regions.
fact_evidence: “The Middle East and Africa region fell 24% due to the ongoing war, while Asia Pacific rose 14% and South America grew 15%, demonstrating geographic diversification benefits.”

description: Lacoste’s reported decline was 16%, somewhat less severe than the preview’s Q2 expectation of a 19% decline. The improvement was limited, and the preview had already noted a 16% first-half decline.
fact_evidence: “Lacoste declined 16% against a 44% prior-year comparison.”

description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.82, well above the preview’s $0.65 consensus estimate and its $0.63–$0.66 base-case range. The preview also cautioned that like-for-like adjusted growth was likely materially below the headline growth math, whereas the call reported adjusted EPS up 52%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS rose 52% to $0.82”; results were supported by “roughly $16 million of new revenue from new rates plus greater-than-anticipated Texas HB 4384 benefits.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS $0.65”; base case: “EPS $0.63–$0.66.” The preview said “true like-for-like YoY growth is likely materially below 22.6%.”

description: Management moved the full-year outlook from an affirmed range to the upper half, narrowing adjusted EPS guidance to $4.89–$4.95 and adjusted net income to $310–$314 million. The new EPS range retains the old high end but raises the low end from $4.83.
fact_evidence: “Management now expects full-year results in the upper half of guidance, narrowing to adjusted net income of $310-314 million and adjusted EPS of $4.89-4.95.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance was “affirmed, not raised” and listed adjusted net income of “$305.9–314.0M” and adjusted EPS of “$4.83–$4.95.”

description: Texas HB 4384 contributed more than anticipated, with management now expecting about $0.42 per share for the full year and roughly $0.28–$0.29 already realized in the first half. The preview discussed Texas GRIP as a July/Q3 benefit but did not anticipate this separate HB 4384 contribution.
fact_evidence: “Texas House Bill 4384 is now expected to contribute approximately $0.42 to full-year adjusted EPS, with about $0.28-0.29 already realized in the first half”; Q2 included “greater-than-anticipated Texas HB 4384 benefits.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Texas GRIP’s “~$36.9–37M revenue increase” would be effective with July bills, “Q3, not Q2”; it did not mention HB 4384.

description: O&M growth eased to 6.6% in Q2 from above 8% in Q1, better than the preview’s concern about a second consecutive high-single-digit increase. Management also expects back-half sequential growth to fall meaningfully below its 3–4% long-term rate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 O&M expenses rose 6.6% year-over-year (down from 8%+ in Q1)”; management expects sequential growth to fall “meaningfully below the 3-4% long-term rate in the back half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “a second consecutive high-single-digit O&M print” the most likely source of a miss and asked about the path back to the “3–4% CAGR target.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The large-load pipeline had advanced beyond the preview’s one identified signed agreement: management reported three high-volume projects under contract, representing about $15 million of annual revenue and $175 million of capital, alongside five late-stage and 17 early-stage opportunities.
fact_evidence: “Three high-volume large-load projects under contract represent roughly $15 million of incremental annual revenue and $175 million of associated capital”; there are “5 late-stage large-load prospects plus 17 additional early-stage opportunities.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “six late-stage large-load projects” and “one signed Oklahoma data-center agreement.”

description: Kansas capacity-release revenue was already $2.8 million year-to-date, with another $1.2 million opportunity remaining this injection season. That is stronger and earlier progress than the preview’s description of a benefit of only “a couple million dollars” that was back-half weighted.
fact_evidence: “The company has realized $2.8 million in Kansas capacity release revenues year-to-date (shared 50-50 with customers), with an incremental $1.2 million opportunity remaining this injection season.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had sized the Kansas capacity-release benefit at “a couple million dollars,” “explicitly back-half weighted.”

description: Adjusted continuing-operations EPS was $0.45, below the $0.47 consensus and the preview’s $0.50–$0.54 base-case range. That is a modest headline shortfall despite growth from the clean prior-year comparison.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS from continuing operations rose to $0.45”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS (cont. ops) | Q2 2026 consensus | $0.47”; preview base case: “EPS $0.50–0.54.”

description: The California deferred-margin benefit was recognized in Q2 as expected, but the reported $9.7 million net-income benefit was below the preview’s estimated full-H1 catch-up of about $0.21 per share. The preview’s estimate was stated on a pre-tax basis, so the comparison is approximate rather than exact.
fact_evidence: “The California rate case decision…provided approximately $40 million of incremental annual revenue, with a $9.7 million net income benefit recognized in Q2 from deferred margin.”
expectation_evidence: “A full H1 true-up = ~$20M pre-tax ≈ $0.21/sh recognized in Q2.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The Great Basin project’s capital estimate rose by $600 million to approximately $2.3 billion after the company switched to a 48-inch pipeline—an unflagged cost increase, though the expanded project is expected to generate $270–$300 million of incremental annual margin once complete.
fact_evidence: “The Great Basin 2028 Expansion Project capital estimate increased to approximately $2.3 billion (a $600 million rise) after switching to a 48-inch pipeline, expected to generate $270-$300 million of incremental annual margin upon completion.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for capex quantification and whether design capacity is upsized above 1.0 Bcf/d.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Nevada intervenors converged on a 9.3% ROE and recommended an average revenue increase just under $40 million, well below the company’s approximately $74 million request. The preview identified the case and its timing but did not anticipate this materially lower intervenor recommendation.
fact_evidence: “In Nevada's general rate case, intervenor parties converged on a 9.3% ROE and recommended an average revenue increase just under $40 million versus the company's ~$74 million request, targeting an October 2026 effective date.”

description: The utility’s trailing ROE was 8.1%, below the preview’s cited 8.5% level; adjusted ROE was 8.0%, matching the preview. The reported overall return therefore showed less improvement than the earlier trailing figure suggested.
fact_evidence: “The utility delivered a 12-month trailing ROE of 8.1% (8% adjusted), still below its weighted average authorized return of 9.89%.”
expectation_evidence: “Utility ROE trajectory | 8.5% trailing / 8.0% adjusted at 3/31/26.”

description: Management now expects 2026 EPS to land in the top half of the $2.95–$3.15 range, improving on the preview’s base case of an unchanged outlook. The range itself was not narrowed.
fact_evidence: Management raised its expectation to deliver 2026 EPS in the top half of its $2.95 to $3.15 guidance range, citing strong year-to-date performance and improved second-half visibility.
expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “guidance reaffirmed unchanged at $2.95–$3.15”; the preview also called a move to the upper half “the single most bullish outcome available.”

description: Q2 EPS was $0.01, above the preview’s near-zero adjusted estimate and the consensus range for a GAAP loss. This was a positive headline surprise despite weaker-than-modeled contributions from SiEnergy and Water.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total EPS was $0.01, flat year-over-year but above expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS” consensus: “$(0.05) – $(0.082)” (midpoint about “$(0.06)”); “Adjusted EPS” estimate: “~$0.00.”

description: Northwest Natural Gas EPS was $0.09, well above the preview’s $0.01 estimate, even though the preview expected higher costs to weigh on the segment.
fact_evidence: “Northwest Natural Gas EPS declining to $0.09 from $0.12.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated NWN Gas Utility EPS at “$0.01” and said “depreciation, O&M and interest keep climbing.”

description: SiEnergy EPS was $0.05, below the preview’s $0.07 estimate, despite customer growth and backlog broadly meeting the preview’s operating expectations.
fact_evidence: “SiEnergy rising to $0.05 from $0.03.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated SiEnergy EPS at “$0.07” and cited “16% organic meter growth” and a “250k+ meter backlog.”

description: Water EPS was $0.05, below the preview’s $0.07 estimate; management also said first-half Water results were modestly below plan. The segment earnings result was weaker than expected even though customer growth was stronger than the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Water falling to $0.05 from $0.07”; Water customer growth was 3.4%, “though first-half results were modestly below plan.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Water EPS at “$0.07” and “2.2% organic growth.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Water customer growth was 3.4% over the 12 months ended June, above the preview’s 2.2% organic-growth estimate.
fact_evidence: “Water customer growth was 3.4% for the 12 months ended June 30, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Water estimate cited “2.2% organic growth.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: MX3 was described as fully contracted with 25-year agreements, a more de-risked project status than the preview’s focus on EPC and permit progress. The expected end-2027 Notice to Proceed and conditional growth-target increase remained on the preview’s timeline.
fact_evidence: “The $300 million FERC-regulated MX3 storage expansion is fully contracted with 25-year agreements at a 12.5% ROE and 50% equity structure”; Notice to Proceed is “expected end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “MX3 (4–5 Bcf, ~$300M) EPC/permit progress” and whether NTP stayed “by late 2027”; it described the 5%–7% growth target as conditional on NTP.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end liquidity was about $628 million, above the preview’s stated $590 million, a modestly better funding position than expected.
fact_evidence: The company reported “liquidity of about $628 million at quarter end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$590M liquidity.”

description: The company completed an inaugural $75 million Water bond issuance after receiving an A- investment-grade rating, a financing development the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “The company completed its inaugural $75 million Water bond issuance after receiving an A- investment-grade rating.”

description: Mosaic lowered Q3 phosphate volume guidance to 1.1–1.4 million tonnes; the range puts a sub-1.3 million-tonne quarter within reach, beyond the preview’s general expectation of H2 volume cuts and into its downside scenario. This leaves a more pronounced near-term volume risk than the preview’s base case implied.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance lowered to a range of 1.1 to 1.4 million tonnes, signaling potential volume downside.”
expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “H2 volumes cut but offset by a higher DAP price guide”; “Bear” scenario: “Q3 phosphate guided <1.3 Mt.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described a much deeper fertilizer application downturn than the preview quantified: North American application is forecast down about 20% after last year’s roughly 15% decline, with a similar 30% decline in Brazil. The resulting large nutrient shortfall is a near-term demand concern, though management expects it eventually to support yields and pent-up fertilizer demand.
fact_evidence: “North American phosphate application is forecast down ~20% this year on top of last year's ~15% decline, cumulatively over 30% below normal, with a similar ~30% decline expected in Brazil”; cumulative under-application is estimated at 1.4 million tonnes of DAP-equivalent nutrient in the U.S. and up to 1.3 million tonnes in Brazil, which management expects to “eventually pressure crop yields and drive pent-up fertilizer demand.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview anticipated weak free cash flow, but the call quantified a substantial full-year funding gap: year-to-date operating cash flow of about $270 million versus roughly $1.5 billion in capex and dividends leaves Mosaic about $500 million short for the year. Debt is expected to remain stable in Q3 before declining in Q4, rather than falling sooner.
fact_evidence: “With year-to-date operating cash flow of ~$270 million against ~$1.5 billion in CapEx and dividends, the company expects to be roughly $500 million short for the year, keeping debt stable in Q3 before declining in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “Dividend is ~$280M/yr against a quarter that may generate little FCF — 16 consecutive years of payments makes a cut unlikely but the coverage commentary matters.”

description: Despite sequential margin pressure, phosphate stripping margins are expected to remain well above historical averages. That is more resilient than the preview’s discussion of margins below $300 per tonne and negative in some geographies suggested.
fact_evidence: “The company expects phosphate stripping margins to decline sequentially in Q3 due to higher sulfur/ammonia costs and reduced fixed cost absorption, but still remain well above historical averages.”
expectation_evidence: “Stripping margins compressed below $300/t vs. >$600 peaks, negative in some geographies.”

description: Q3 sulfur costs are set to rise sharply from Q2, despite the preview’s note of a July sulfur price decline. However, Mosaic says its new contract and Gulf Coast refiner relationships keep costs well below unsustainably high spot prices, partially cushioning the supply shock the preview emphasized.
fact_evidence: “Q3 sulfur costs are guided to $700-$710 per tonne (up from $522 in Q2) after settling a new contract at $705, though this remains well below unsustainably high spot prices due to Gulf Coast refiner relationships.”
expectation_evidence: “First relief signal: sulfur −7.03% month-over-month as of July 13”; “Mosaic is structurally short sulfur”; “Until the sulfur lane reopens, higher DAP prices do not translate into higher phosphate earnings.”

description: Mosaic cut full-year capex again, to $1.2 billion from the preview’s stated $1.25 billion level. The additional reduction supports expected sequential free-cash-flow improvement in the second half.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced full-year CapEx guidance to $1.2 billion (from $1.25 billion and an original $1.5 billion), supporting expectations of sequentially improving free cash flow in Q3 and Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “Is $1.25B capex holding or getting cut again?”

description: Fertilizantes’ Q2 EBITDA was $60 million, but management expects it to decline in Q3 as curtailed Brazilian commodity production limits sales. That conflicts with the preview’s base case that Brazil would peak in Q3.
fact_evidence: “Fertilizantes Q2 EBITDA of $60 million is expected to decline in Q3 as curtailed Brazilian commodity production limits sales.”
expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Fertilizantes ~$50–80M (shoulder quarter; Brazil peaks in Q3).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Potash netbacks face pressure from higher export freight rates and a Canpotex-weighted channel mix, a headwind not reflected in the preview’s picture of potash as the earnings floor amid a firm market backdrop.
fact_evidence: “Potash netbacks face pressure from higher export freight rates and a Canpotex-weighted channel mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Potash — the entire earnings floor”; “Market backdrop is genuinely firm”; “Reaffirmation of 9.0 Mt FY production matters as much as the price.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management still expects a $400 million working-capital release, but says it will be weighted toward Q4 collections from Brazil while customer prepayments there have fallen to near zero. The release could support cash generation, but its timing and dependence on collections add execution risk not discussed in the preview.
fact_evidence: “A $400 million working capital release (range $300-$500 million) is still expected, weighted roughly one-third in Q3 and two-thirds in Q4 as Brazil collections arrive, though customer prepayments in Brazil fell to near zero.”

description: SG&A was already down 20% year over year, with further second-half declines expected and management characterizing the savings as permanent. The preview identified a cost program but did not describe savings of this size as already realized or permanent.
fact_evidence: “SG&A costs were cut 20% year-over-year and are expected to decline further in the second half, with management characterizing these savings as permanent.”
expectation_evidence: “Cost program: >$150M annual ($100M value capture + $50M overhead).”

description: Prudential reported adjusted operating EPS of $4.08, well above the preview’s $3.35–$3.42 consensus band and even its $3.45–$3.50 effective-whisper estimate. Instead of the expected year-over-year decline, EPS was up 14%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 after-tax adjusted operating income was $1.4 billion, or $4.08 per share, up 14% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS: $3.42”; alternate consensus “$3.35”; effective whisper “closer to $3.45–3.50”; consensus YoY “–4.4%.”

description: The Japan suspension hit was materially lighter than the preview’s estimated $140–$160 million for the first full suspended quarter: Prudential reported $105 million, also below Q1’s $130 million. This was a favorable difference even though management retained the full-year range.
fact_evidence: “The Prudential of Japan sales suspension impact was $105 million in the quarter (below expectations, down from $130 million in Q1).”
expectation_evidence: “My estimate: $140–160M pretax”; the preview also noted Q1’s “$130M” impact.

description: Prudential announced a much broader footprint reduction than the preview’s general expectation of further portfolio pruning: it plans to exit 6–7 emerging markets and cut its retirement and insurance footprint roughly in half. The exits are expected to free substantial capital, but also mean a significant pullback from those markets.
fact_evidence: “Plans to cut its retirement and insurance footprint by roughly half, exiting 6-7 emerging markets (primarily via sales rather than shutdowns) to free up well north of $3 billion of capital over roughly a 5-year period.”
expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated “further portfolio pruning” and noted prior exits, but did not forecast this scale of retrenchment.

description: The strategy update set a larger PGIM ambition than the preview’s stated 25–30% long-term margin target: PGIM is to reach about 25% of PFI adjusted operating income versus roughly 12% currently, with margins targeted above 30%.
fact_evidence: “PGIM growing to about 25% of PFI's adjusted operating income, more than double its current ~12% contribution, and aims to expand PGIM margins above its 30% multiyear target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “25–30% long-term margin” and described PGIM as the “re-rating engine”; it did not give a target for PGIM’s share of PFI income.

description: Prudential raised its structural-efficiency ambition far beyond the small PGIM savings figure in the preview: the company now targets about $750 million of pretax run-rate benefits by year-end 2028, versus an original $150 million target for 2027. It also plans a further 150-basis-point expense-ratio improvement over three years.
fact_evidence: “Raised its structural efficiency target to approximately $750 million in pretax run-rate benefits by year-end 2028 (full benefit in 2029), up from the original $150 million target for 2027”; it also “expects to improve its adjusted operating expense ratio by an additional 150 basis points over the next 3 years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned PGIM’s “~$100M run-rate savings” but did not anticipate this company-wide target increase or the additional expense-ratio goal.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: PGIM’s private-capital deployment accelerated more than the preview’s expectation of continued deployment: it rose nearly 60% sequentially to almost $21 billion, including about $7 billion in asset-backed finance.
fact_evidence: “PGIM private capital deployment grew nearly 60% sequentially to nearly $21 billion (including ~$7 billion of asset-backed finance).”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 private-asset deployment of “$13B” and expected confirmation of PGIM’s margin trajectory, but did not forecast a further acceleration of this size.

description: Group Insurance produced record earnings of $155 million, a much stronger outcome than the preview’s concern about whether the weak Q1 disability experience would stabilize. The preview highlighted Q1 AOI of only $38 million and warned that another weak print would be concerning.
fact_evidence: “Group Insurance delivered record earnings of $155 million (up 24%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview called stabilization the key question after “Q1 AOI collapsed to $38M from $89M” and said two consecutive weak prints would reframe the issue as structural.

description: Individual Life earnings did not show the mean-reversion weakness the preview warned could follow Q1’s favorable mortality: earnings were $176 million and more than doubled year over year. That is a favorable result against the preview’s concern that reversion could reduce the U.S. contribution.
fact_evidence: “Individual Life earnings of $176 million more than doubled year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1’s “$139M vs $52M” as driven by favorable mortality and warned that “a reversion here quietly eats $50–80M of the U.S. beat.”

description: The preview treated the full FY2026 guidance range of $925M–$1.0B as still live in its base case. USANA instead lowered its full-year outlook, citing weaker expected HIYA second-half sales and reduced near-term Rise Wellness sales.
fact_evidence: “USANA lowered its full-year fiscal 2026 outlook,” citing “a more expensive direct-to-consumer digital marketing environment hurting HIYA's second-half sales and reduced near-term Rise Wellness sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Base = a verbatim reaffirmation of the full wide range with no phasing detail”; the preview identified whether the FY26 guide was “still live” as the central question.

description: The preview expected Rise Wellness to ramp, forecasting about $17M for Q2 and a $65M–$80M full-year range, with retailer rollouts underway. A packaging issue instead reduced its top-line guidance by roughly $30M–$40M and is expected to pressure margins by about $4M–$5M.
fact_evidence: “The Rise Wellness packaging issue lowered its top-line guidance range by roughly $30 million to $40 million and created about $4 million to $5 million of margin pressure.”
expectation_evidence: “Rise Wellness ~$17M” in Q2 and “$65–80M” for FY2026; the preview also said “nine new Rise retailers rolling out in Q2/Q3.”

description: The preview flagged HIYA's Meta-related acquisition-cost problem but looked for CAC to normalize and subscribers to stabilize or rise. The call instead described continuing Meta algorithm challenges and a strategic pivot toward TikTok, retail, and international markets.
fact_evidence: “HIYA has faced rising customer acquisition costs due to Meta algorithm challenges, prompting a strategic shift toward TikTok, retail expansion, and international markets.”
expectation_evidence: “Need subs flat-to-up sequentially plus commentary that CAC has normalized — otherwise the H2 Hiya reacceleration story loses credibility.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview anticipated HIYA weakness and risk to its outlook, but did not anticipate a large impairment. USANA reported a preliminary $29M non-cash goodwill charge tied to HIYA after weaker performance and lower near-term forecasts.
fact_evidence: “USANA recorded an estimated preliminary non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $29 million tied to the HIYA reporting unit, reflecting weaker-than-expected performance and reduced near-term forecasts.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview did not flag an unusual tax burden. USANA recorded $9M of tax expense despite a $19M pre-tax loss and said the elevated tax rate should persist through the year, well above the second-quarter catch-up level.
fact_evidence: “The company reported $9 million in income tax expense on a pre-tax loss of $19 million,” due to “a structural misalignment between where revenue is generated and where costs are incurred.” Management expects “an elevated tax rate to persist through the full year.”

description: The preview's segment build anticipated a modest decline in Core Nutritional, but the call highlighted a much sharper 20% drop in North Asia, mainly tied to prolonged softness in Korea after a leadership transition.
fact_evidence: “North Asia direct revenue declined 20%, driven mainly by prolonged softness in Korea following a leadership transition at the start of the year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview's segment build forecast Core Nutritional at about $194M, down 2.6%, without forecasting a 20% North Asia decline.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: USANA ended with more cash and no debt, compared with the preview's $163M cash and $14M debt. It also generated $20M of free cash flow, which the preview had not projected.
fact_evidence: “USANA ended the quarter with $169 million in cash, zero debt, and generated $20 million of free cash flow aided by improved working capital management.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$163M cash, $14M debt” and noted “zero repurchased in Q1.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected Rise Wellness growth and retailer rollouts, but the call gave a stronger scale update: it had already surpassed its full prior-year sales year-to-date and expects to be in more than 4,000 retail doors by year-end.
fact_evidence: “Rise Wellness has already exceeded its full prior-year sales year-to-date and expects to be selling in over 4,000 retail doors by year-end despite being less than a year old as a national brand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview forecast Rise Wellness at “~$17M” in Q2 and described a Costco/Walmart ramp and “nine new Rise retailers rolling out in Q2/Q3.”

description: WTRG said it had finalized rate cases and surcharges representing $56.6 million in annualized revenue year to date, well above the $15.1 million already completed as of Q1 cited in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date the company finalized rate cases and surcharges representing $56.6 million in annualized revenue, with ~78% from water and wastewater.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “$15.1M annualized already completed in 2026” as of Q1.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Management disclosed that full-year effective tax rates are expected to be below 5%, along with a one-time benefit later this year. The preview noted that prior-year favorable tax items would not repeat, so this is a more favorable tax outlook than it led investors to expect.
fact_evidence: Management expects “low single-digit (under 5%) effective tax rates for the full year plus a one-time benefit later this year disclosed in the S-4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 as having “no repeat of prior-year favorable tax items” and did not identify a later 2026 one-time benefit.

description: WTRG identified a broader municipal acquisition pipeline of about 400,000 customers, an opportunity not mentioned in the preview, which focused on Greenville and the pending DELCORA deal.
fact_evidence: The company cited “a broader municipal pipeline of ~400,000 customers.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The company maintained its Q1 2027 merger-close expectation, but added that Pennsylvania’s ALJ recommendation could shift the date and that Illinois’ statutory timeline runs through November 2026. The preview flagged both states as pending but did not describe these specific timing risks.
fact_evidence: “The merger with American Water is expected to close in Q1 2027”; “Illinois is the last state with a statutory merger timeline, finishing by November 2026,” and Pennsylvania’s ALJ “has up to 90 days to issue a recommendation that could shift the close date.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the close was targeted “by end of Q1 2027” and identified Pennsylvania and Illinois as still pending approvals.

description: Diluted EPS was $1.39, well below the preview’s $1.83 estimate, even though earnings from operations rose to $17 million from $3.9 million. The preview’s reported-EPS estimate was therefore materially too high despite expecting a large refund benefit.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS surged to $1.39 from $0.24”; “earnings from operations to $17 million from $3.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Reported diluted EPS” Q2’26E: “~$1.83.”

description: Reported gross margin reached 70.4%, far above the preview’s 44.0% estimate, as $15.3 million of tariff refunds was recorded as a reduction to cost of sales. The reported margin is not representative of the ongoing business: management said wholesale margin would be materially lower excluding the refund.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin jumped to 70.4%” from 43.3%, “largely inflated by $15.3 million in one-time IEPA tariff refunds recognized as a reduction to cost of sales”; “Excluding the $14.3 million tariff refund, wholesale gross margin would be materially lower.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin” Q2’26E: “44.0%.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The post-July tariff rate was higher than the 10% rate the preview described as scheduled to sunset: an incremental 12.5% tariff on imports from China and Vietnam took effect July 24. That adds near-term second-half margin uncertainty rather than resolving the sourcing-cost question.
fact_evidence: “The administration raised the incremental tariff on imports from China and Vietnam to 12.5% effective July 24, 2026, creating near-term gross margin uncertainty for the second half.”
expectation_evidence: “Section 122’s 10% across-the-board rate was scheduled to sunset ~July 24, 2026,” with Section 301 actions “widely expected as the replacement.”

description: Wholesale selling and administrative expenses were a much heavier burden relative to sales than the preview’s modest increase in consolidated SG&A suggested. The 37% wholesale expense ratio, up from 29%, pressured underlying operating margins.
fact_evidence: “Wholesale selling and administrative expenses climbed to 37% of net sales from 29% a year ago, driven by higher employee costs, pressuring underlying operating margins.”

description: Sales modestly exceeded the preview model, rising 7% to $62.2 million versus its $61.5 million estimate and projected 5.7% growth. Wholesale sales also came in above the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 7% year-over-year to $62.2 million”; “Wholesale net sales grew 7% to $48.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales” Q2’26E: “$61.5M” and “+5.7%”; segment estimate: “N.A. Wholesale $48.3M (+6%).”

description: Several wholesale brands performed better than the preview’s recent-trend discussion implied: Florsheim accelerated, Stacey Adams returned to growth, and Bogs grew despite being described as seasonally immaterial in Q2. Nunn-Busch, however, declined rather than holding flat, making the brand picture mixed.
fact_evidence: “Florsheim (+12%), Stacey Adams (+4%), and Bogs (+10%), while Nunn-Busch declined 3%.”

expectation_evidence: The preview cited “15–90 day NPL held at 8.0%” and said to watch whether it rose above 8.5%.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Adjusted free cash flow was positive at $214 million, avoiding the consecutive negative quarters the preview warned could raise funding concerns after Q1’s negative $56 million. This was achieved despite $441 million of capex and $2.1 billion invested in growing the credit book.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow was $214 million despite capital expenditure of $441 million and $2.1 billion invested into growing the credit book.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said adjusted FCF was “–$56M in Q1'26” and warned that “Two consecutive negative quarters would raise the question of whether the credit build eventually requires external capital.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Brazil credit-card issuance accelerated to 2.6 million cards from 1.6 million a year earlier, while card NIMAL was -2.5%. That indicates a larger and still loss-making card-growth push even as total portfolio NIMAL improved; the preview had flagged immature card cohorts as a drag but did not anticipate this issuance pace or card-level figure.
fact_evidence: “Credit card issuance in Brazil accelerated to 2.6 million cards this quarter versus 1.6 million a year ago, with card NIMAL at -2.5% (versus near breakeven a year ago) and each cohort reaching NIMAL breakeven in 12-18 months.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said NIMAL had fallen partly because of “credit-card mix (immature cohorts)” and asked whether overall NIMAL would stabilize near 17–18%.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The advertising business grew 73% year over year, with use of an AI ad-orchestrator tool up 66%. The preview did not set an advertising growth expectation, so this was an unanticipated positive operating datapoint rather than a beat against a stated forecast.
fact_evidence: “The advertising business grew 73% year-on-year, aided by AI tools including an ad orchestrator whose usage grew 66%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call highlighted unusually strong economics from customers using both Marketplace and Mercado Pago: these ecosystemic users grew 37% and generate materially more commerce, payments volume, and assets under management. The preview discussed engagement metrics but did not anticipate these cross-product economics or their scale.
fact_evidence: “Ecosystemic users (using both Marketplace and Mercado Pago) generate 70% more GMV, 90% more TPV and double the assets under management, growing 37% year-on-year, and are multiples more profitable.”

description: The call disclosed roughly $80 million more year-over-year AI investment, but also cited operating leverage in development and customer service: product development fell from 8.4% to 7.2% of revenue and the service-rep count declined from 10,000 to 7,000 despite threefold business growth. This adds quantified AI spending while showing efficiencies that the preview did not quantify.
fact_evidence: “AI investment rose roughly $80 million year-on-year, while product development scaled from 8.4% to 7.2% of revenues and customer service reps fell from 10,000 to 7,000 despite 3x business growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “AI” among the investment-cycle areas and said the key question was whether management had “stopped adding new investment buckets,” but gave no AI-spend or productivity figures.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: OraSure withdrew the InteliQuick CT/NG FDA submission and no longer expects clearance or a U.S. launch in 2026, rather than reaching the anticipated midyear clearance and H2 launch ramp. Management plans to resubmit after addressing FDA feedback.
fact_evidence: “Withdrew its FDA submission” and “no longer expects FDA clearance or U.S. launch in 2026,” planning to resubmit after incorporating FDA feedback.
expectation_evidence: Management had guided to “midyear clearance” with revenue ramping in H2; the preview said the key question was whether CT/NG was “under active review” or whether the launch would slide into 2027.

description: Q2 revenue was $30.6 million, above the preview’s preferred $29.0–$29.3 million consensus anchor and above the company’s $30 million guidance ceiling. The result was stronger than the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $30.6 million,” exceeding the company’s guidance range.
expectation_evidence: The preview said to treat “$29.0–29.3M as the number the tape will trade against” and listed company guidance of $27–30M.

description: Diagnostics revenue reached $19.4 million, well above the preview’s $17.3 million base-case estimate, and grew 14.7% sequentially. That segment was a major source of the revenue beat.
fact_evidence: “Diagnostics revenue reached $19.4 million, growing 14.7% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case modeled “Diagnostics ~$17.3M.”

description: Gross margins were higher than the preview’s roughly 42–43% Q2 expectation: GAAP margin reached 43.5% and non-GAAP margin 44.2%. Management attributed the improvement to lower scrap and operational efficiencies.
fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin expanded 120 basis points sequentially to 43.5%,” while “non-GAAP gross margin rose to 44.2% from 43.4%,” driven by “lower scrap and operational efficiencies.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross margin of “~42–43%” and cited Q1 margins of 42.3% GAAP and 43.4% non-GAAP.

description: Sample Management Solutions revenue was $9.9 million, above the preview’s $9.4 million base-case estimate, and rose 9% sequentially despite the preview’s concern about subdued academic and government demand.
fact_evidence: “Sample Management Solutions revenue was $9.9 million, up 9% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case modeled “SMS ~$9.4M” and described academic and government demand as “subdued.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The cash picture was better than the preview’s downside warning: cash ended at $161 million, above the roughly $155 million level it identified as a sign of accelerating burn, and operating cash flow was negative $9.9 million. Management also reaffirmed its breakeven operating cash flow target entering 2027, as the preview expected.
fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$161 million in cash and cash equivalents”; operating cash flow was “negative $9.9 million,” and management reaffirmed breakeven operating cash flow entering 2027.
expectation_evidence: The preview said cash “below ~$155M” would indicate accelerating burn and put the breakeven target under pressure; it also noted Q1 operating cash flow of –$14M.

description: The CT/NG delay was not expected to add to cash usage because reduced milestone payments on the contingent consideration would more than offset the added resubmission costs. The preview discussed the regulatory risk and cash-burn concern but not this offset.
fact_evidence: The delay “is not expected to increase cash usage,” as reduced milestone payments on the approximately $20 million contingent consideration will “more than offset incremental resubmission costs.”

description: OraSure sharply reduced Q2 repurchases, buying back only $2 million of shares, and said it had paused repurchases to preserve balance-sheet flexibility for launches. The preview flagged repurchase pace as a signal but did not specify an expected reduction.
fact_evidence: OraSure “paused share repurchases in Q2,” buying back “647,000 shares for $2 million,” to prioritize balance-sheet flexibility for product launches.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1’s $5 million buyback and said “buyback pace signals management’s own read.”

description: Sickle SCAN revenue was growing twice as fast in 2026 as in 2025, an encouraging product trend not anticipated in the preview’s description of the base business as flat-to-down.
fact_evidence: “Sickle SCAN revenue is growing twice as fast in 2026 as in 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the “base business” as “flat-to-down.”

description: Q2 revenue was $3.13 billion, beating the $3.00 billion consensus by $130 million and growing 13% year over year, versus the preview’s expected 8.6% growth. Strong LMR demand and accelerated quick-turn conversion drove the upside.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to a record level, beating consensus by $130 million, driven by strong LMR demand and accelerated quick-turn conversion.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus … $3.00B … Implied Y/Y +8.6%.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS reached $4.41, well above the $3.86 consensus and the preview’s $3.90+ buy-side whisper. The $0.25 IEPA tariff-refund benefit contributed, but EPS was still about $4.16 excluding it.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $4.41, up 24% from $3.57 a year ago, including a $0.25 benefit from IEPA tariff refunds.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus … $3.86”; “the buy-side whisper is effectively $3.90+.”

description: Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, far above the preview’s roughly flat year-over-year base case and its 29.5% bull-case threshold. Even excluding the $60 million IEPA refund benefit, margin expanded 140 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, or 140 basis points excluding the $60 million IEPA refund benefit.”
expectation_evidence: “Base … margin roughly flat y/y”; “Bull … non-GAAP op margin ≥29.5%.”

description: The company raised FY26 revenue guidance to approximately $12.975 billion and EPS guidance to $17.62–$17.72. This exceeded the preview’s expected revenue raise to at least $12.85 billion and its bar of at least $17.00 at the low end of EPS guidance.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $175 million to approximately $12.975 billion and lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to $17.62-$17.72 from $16.87-$16.99.”
expectation_evidence: “The bar … is a raise to ≥$17.00 at the low end plus revenue ≥$12.85B.”

description: Memory costs are now expected to reach $150 million this year, above the preview’s expectation of more than $100 million. Most of the impact is expected in the second half, adding more cost pressure than the preview’s already elevated estimate implied.
fact_evidence: “Memory costs are now expected to reach $150 million this year, up from $50 million last year and up $100 million from prior guidance, with most of the impact hitting the second half.”
expectation_evidence: “Memory/DRAM spend more than doubles to >$100M in 2026.”

description: Instead of the roughly $60 million tariff headwind the preview expected, tariffs are now expected to be net neutral for the full year because IEPA refunds offset the planned headwinds. The refund also contributed $0.25 to Q2 EPS.
fact_evidence: “Tariffs are now expected to be net neutral for the full year as $60 million in IEPA refunds offset previously planned tariff headwinds.”
expectation_evidence: “Tariffs are a ~$60M headwind weighted to H1.”

description: Silvus is now expected to generate roughly $850 million in FY26 revenue, $100 million above the $750 million target already in the preview. The preview anticipated a possible further raise, but the reported target was higher than that stated baseline.
fact_evidence: “Silvus generated about $230 million in Q2 (up from $210 million in Q1) and is now expected to deliver roughly $850 million in full-year revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Silvus revenue target raised to $750M for 2026”; “Watch for another Silvus raise.”

description: The call introduced a year-end 2026 APX Next subscriber target of 300,000, with nearly $100 million in ARR at roughly $300 per subscriber. The preview did not flag an APX subscriber or ARR outlook, so there was no stated benchmark to compare with this new target.
fact_evidence: “APX Next software subscribers are expected to reach 300,000 by year-end 2026 (up from ~200,000 in 2025), representing nearly $100 million in ARR at roughly $300 per subscriber.”

description: Envista raised its 2026 outlook to 3.5%-4.5% core growth, 11%-14% adjusted EBITDA growth, and $1.50-$1.55 adjusted EPS. That was a stronger move than the preview’s base case of reaffirming the prior EPS range, and the new EPS range is also above the preview’s bull-case range.
fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3.5%-4.5% core growth, 11%-14% adjusted EBITDA growth, and adjusted EPS of $1.50-$1.55.
expectation_evidence: “A raise is the bull trigger; a reaffirm is the base case”; the preview’s bull case was “Raise to $1.42–$1.48.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.41, well above the preview’s $0.34 consensus estimate. The 21% gap was materially larger than the preview’s expected year-over-year growth of 31% implied by consensus.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 58% to $0.41.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.34.”

description: Core sales grew 5%, above the preview’s implied 1%-3% range and the 4% threshold it highlighted. This was a stronger underlying-growth read than the preview’s base case of 3.5%-4.5%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 core sales grew 5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed core sales growth of “~1–3% (implied)” and highlighted “Core growth ≥ 4%” as a catalyst.

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 14.7%, above the preview’s roughly 13.5% implied estimate and its 13.8%-14.2% base case. The 230-basis-point expansion also exceeded the preview’s expected margin expansion.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 230 basis points to 14.7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA margin ~13.5% (implied)” and gave a base case of “~13.8–14.2%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow recovered to $105 million, above the preview’s $90 million-plus bull-case marker and the $76.4 million generated in Q2 2025. The result was stronger than the preview’s concern that Q2 needed a very large catch-up after Q1’s negative cash flow.
fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $105 million (158% conversion), up $29 million year-over-year”; full-year conversion is expected “near 100%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Envista “needs a very large H1 catch-up” and cited “FCF > $90M” in its bull case.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The cash-flow recovery included a $13 million IEEPA tariff recovery that the preview had not anticipated. That makes part of the strong Q2 cash result a one-off benefit rather than recurring operating cash generation.
fact_evidence: Q2 free cash flow was “aided by a $13 million IEEPA tariff recovery.”

description: China commentary was more constructive than the preview’s concern that double-digit declines and destocking would persist: management projected a return to moderate growth and said implant price compression would be only 10%-15%. The offset is substantial expected ortho price compression of roughly 45%.
fact_evidence: “China VBP is now expected in the second half, with roughly 45% price compression on ortho (VBP 1) but only 10%-15% on implants (VBP 2), and China is projected to return to moderate growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said China implants had seen “strong double-digit declines,” warned that “channel destocking likely persisted through Q2,” and flagged the risk of “extended VBP 2.0 destocking through Q2.”

description: Envista repurchased about 2.4 million shares in Q2, up from the 1.6 million shares cited for Q1, while the preview had raised the possibility that weak cash flow could constrain buybacks. The stronger cash result and continued repurchases indicate a faster pace than that risk scenario implied.
fact_evidence: “Envista repurchased approximately 2.4 million shares in Q2 at an average price of $24.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 repurchases of “1.6M shares for ~$43M” and said a soft FCF print “constrains the buyback narrative.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The implant F Series launch was running ahead of plan, with about 25% of sales coming from competitive conversions—an additional favorable product-launch update not specifically anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The implant F Series launch is running ahead of plan with about 25% of sales from competitive conversion.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The full-year non-GAAP tax-rate outlook was lowered by about two percentage points, providing an additional EPS tailwind that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year non-GAAP tax rate guidance to approximately 26%, about 2 points below initial guidance, aiding EPS growth.”
expectation_evidence: The call states the new rate is “about 2 points below initial guidance.”

description: Revenue of $731 million was above the preview’s published consensus range of $716-$720 million, but essentially matched its estimated buy-side whisper range of $728-$735 million. Thus it beat the published bar without surprising relative to the preview’s higher expectation.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue of $731 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview treated “$716–720M as published consensus” and “$728–735M as the realistic buy-side whisper.”

description: SiTime guided to Q3 combined revenue of $285–$295 million, well above the preview’s $250–$265 million base case and above its $280 million bull-case threshold. The midpoint is $290 million, versus the preview’s roughly $255 million street-math benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for combined revenue of $285-$295 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Combined base case: $250–265M”; the bull case was “$280M+.”

description: The Q3 outlook for core SiTime, excluding TPD, was $200–$210 million, or about 30% sequential growth. That is stronger than the preview’s estimate of $172–$188 million for the organic business, suggesting the combined-guide upside is not just from the acquisition.
fact_evidence: “Core SiTime (ex-TPD) expected to grow ~30% sequentially to $200-$210 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Organic SiTime at $150M in Q2 growing high-teens sequentially … → $172–188M.”

description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $2.34, above both the preview’s $1.93 consensus and its $2.10–$2.20 buy-side whisper range. The result also exceeded the preview’s $2.30 bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income reached $65.7 million, or $2.34 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus” EPS was “$1.93”; “The buy-side whisper” was “$2.10–2.20”; the bull case was “$2.30+.”

description: Q2 revenue of $157.4 million beat the preview’s $145.09 million consensus and slightly exceeded its $152–$156 million buy-side whisper range. It came just below the preview’s $158 million bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $157.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$145.09M”; the whisper was “$152–156M”; the bull case was “$158M+.”

description: Q2 gross margin reached 67.1%, 2.1 percentage points above the preview’s roughly 65% expectation. The preview had framed margin progress as important to the deal thesis, although its specific 66–68% range was for the Q3 guide, not Q2.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 67.1%, up 8.9 points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin consensus was “~65%”; company guidance was “~65.0% ±1.0 pt.”

description: TPD is expected to contribute about $85 million in Q3, above the preview’s estimated $68–$80 million for the initial quarter. Management also said it is tracking well above the original $300 million annualized run-rate target, rather than merely reiterating that target.
fact_evidence: “TPD … is expected to contribute ~$85 million in Q3 alone, tracking well above its original $300 million annualized run-rate target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated TPD at “$68–80M” in the first stub quarter and said reiterating “≥$300M” was the floor.

description: Despite the zero-coupon notes, management warned that Q3 interest income will fall to about $4 million after the proceeds were deployed. The preview expected no cash interest drag from the converts and did not anticipate this reduction in interest income.
fact_evidence: “Management funded the acquisition with a $1.35 billion zero-coupon convertible notes offering due 2031, but warned Q3 interest income will drop to ~$4 million after proceeds were deployed.”
expectation_evidence: “Because the converts carry a 0% coupon, there is no cash interest drag.”

description: Management offered a specific, upbeat 2027 optical-growth outlook: 1.6T optical-module revenue is expected to grow 100%, with 800G also growing. The preview discussed datacenter and optical demand as key drivers but did not anticipate this growth outlook or quantify it.
fact_evidence: “In 2027, the company expects its 1.6T optical module revenue to grow 100% (with 800G also growing).”

description: Management said it sees no signs of a 2027 slowdown and reaffirmed a multiyear growth rate of about 30% or slightly higher, while citing a potential $2.5 billion expansion of CED’s addressable market by 2030 from timing integration into chiplets and modules. The preview did not identify these specific longer-term growth and market-expansion claims.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed a multiyear growth rate of ~30% or slightly higher, sees no signs of slowdown in 2027, and projects timing integration into chiplets and modules could expand its CED SAM by $2.5 billion by 2030.”

description: Q2 revenue was just $0.1 million, below the preview’s roughly $0.5–2 million base case and the $1.0 million Zacks estimate. The preview also described revenue as a proxy for TVA-related pre-FEED progress, so the reported figure did not show that activity in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “NuScale reported Q2 2026 revenue of just $0.1 million,” down from $8.1 million a year earlier, because Fluor’s RoPower FEED Phase 2 work ended in late 2025 and there was no comparable current activity.
expectation_evidence: “consensus expects roughly the same in Q2” after Q1 revenue of $0.6M; the consensus table lists Q2 revenue of “$1.0M,” and the base scenario expects “~$0.5–2M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash, cash equivalents and investments reached about $1.9 billion—far above the preview’s expected Q2 level of roughly $830–850 million. The preview had expected a sequential decline absent a binding PPA, while the call reported a $900 million increase since March 31.
fact_evidence: “NuScale closed Q2 2026 with approximately $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, an increase of $900 million since March 31, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Absent a PPA, Q2 cash should land near $830–850M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The potential TVA deployment discussed on the call extended up to 8 GW, above the preview’s description of the existing TVA–ENTRA1 agreement as covering up to 6 GW. This points to a potentially larger program, although the PPA was still under discussion rather than signed.
fact_evidence: ENTRA1 was in “active discussions with the Tennessee Valley Authority toward a definitive PPA for a potential 6-to-8 gigawatt deployment.”
expectation_evidence: “The Sept 2025 TVA–ENTRA1 agreement covers up to 6 GW (72 modules).”

description: NuScale described a broader and more advanced supplier base than the preview’s reference to 37 key suppliers aligned to 2026 milestones: it said it had more than 60 specialized suppliers, agreements with over half, and components already in production. That suggests more supply-chain readiness than the preview had highlighted.
fact_evidence: NuScale had “assembled a network of more than 60 specialized suppliers” and signed master supplier agreements with “more than half”; many components, including Doosan heavy forgings, had been in production over the past two years.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s secondary watch list referred to “37 key suppliers aligned to 2026 milestones” and asked about long-lead component production status.

fact_evidence: “Approximately 60% of the prior CFPP project’s Combined Construction and Operating License Application (COLA) can be carried over to a new U.S. project, potentially saving significant time and regulatory cost.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones

fact_evidence: “Construction from first safety-related concrete pour to mechanical completion is expected to take a little less than 40 months, excluding upfront NRC licensing time.”
