fact_evidence: “NuScale’s OEM/module scope [is expected] to represent roughly 30%+ of total project cost, with the remainder going to EPC and other contractors.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call emphasized NuScale’s existing NRC design certification and use of conventional low-enriched uranium, avoiding the commercial-scale HALEU supply risk facing some competitors. These readiness advantages were not identified in the preview’s stated watch items.
fact_evidence: NuScale “remains the only SMR company to have received NRC design certification” and “uses conventional low-enriched uranium, avoiding the commercial-scale HALEU supply risk faced by several competing designs.”

description: Enact raised its 2026 capital-return target to $550–600 million from $500 million, above the preview’s expectation that the roughly $500 million target would be reaffirmed. The increase was attributed to strong first-half performance and excess capital.
fact_evidence: “Enact raised its 2026 capital return guidance to $550-600 million, up from prior guidance of $500 million, citing strong first-half business performance and excess capital.”
expectation_evidence: “Capital return **~$500M** for 2026”; the base case expected capital-return guides to be “reaffirmed.”

description: Full-year operating-expense guidance fell to $205–210 million from $215–220 million, better than the preview’s expectation that the existing range would be reaffirmed.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 operating expenses (excluding reorganization costs) are now forecast at $205-210 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Operating expenses **$215–220M**, excluding reorganization costs”; the preview said to watch for qualification of the guide and described reaffirmation in its base case.

description: Adjusted EPS of $1.26 topped the preview’s $1.19–$1.21 consensus band, though it was within the preview’s $1.24–$1.28 functional buy-side bar and at the top of its base-case range. The result was a modest consensus beat rather than an obvious beat over the higher bar.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted operating income was $177 million, with diluted EPS of $1.26.”
expectation_evidence: “Working band for this note: EPS $1.19–$1.21”; the preview also said “the functional buy-side bar is closer to **$1.24–$1.28**” and gave a base-case range of “$1.20–$1.26.”

description: Enact expected its base premium rate to remain relatively flat versus 2025, a steadier outlook than the preview’s emphasis on gradual premium-rate declines across the market and the risk of pricing pressure.
fact_evidence: “Base premium rate expected to remain relatively flat versus 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Gross premium rates have continued to drift lower gradually” at peer MGIC and flagged “any gross premium rate commentary” as a key issue to watch.

description: Management said second-half delinquencies could rise partly because newer, lower-HPA purchase vintages have higher LTVs and DTIs. The preview anticipated seasonal increases and portfolio aging, but this added a specific risk factor beyond the expected seasonal framing.
fact_evidence: “Management expects delinquency rates to rise in the second half of 2026 due to seasonality and newer, lower-HPA purchase vintages carrying higher LTVs and DTIs.”

fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $61.9 million,” up 45% year-over-year and 40% sequentially.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $52.5M”; the preview also said the “functional bar is likely $53–55M.”

fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $230 million to $260 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the company guide as “$225–260M” and said the base case was “Guide reaffirmed unchanged at $225–260M.”

fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss was $9.6 million, a 33% year-over-year improvement.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called narrowing “toward ~$20M” the bull marker and put base-case burn at “~$24–27M.”

fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 58% (flat YoY but up 8 points sequentially)” and “GAAP gross margin rose to 45% (up 6 points YoY).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Holding the 50% line non-GAAP is the bar,” flagged “a third consecutive compression quarter,” and set the bull case at non-GAAP gross margin “back above 50%.”

description: Management set a future gross-margin target above 70%, a higher stated destination than the preview’s discussion of scaling toward software margins and its near-term focus on holding the 50% line. The call did not provide a timeline for reaching that target.
fact_evidence: Management is “targeting over 70% gross margin in the future.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the thesis as “scale into software margins” and focused on “Holding the 50% line non-GAAP”; it did not state a target above 70%.

description: Loss per share was better than consensus on both bases: adjusted loss was $0.02 versus the expected $0.03, and GAAP loss was $0.10 versus the expected $0.13. This ran counter to the preview’s warning that the GAAP result could show a meaningful step-down.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $42.8 million ($0.10 per share) while non-GAAP net loss was $9 million ($0.02 per share).”
expectation_evidence: Consensus was “EPS — adjusted | −$0.03” and “EPS — GAAP | −$0.13”; the preview said “a −$0.13 GAAP Q2 implies a meaningful GAAP-only step-down.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company disclosed a sizable customer commitment signed in under 90 days from demo to contract, delivered as a channel deal serving customers across 20 countries. The preview asked for evidence of contracted large deals but did not anticipate this specific win.
fact_evidence: “The company signed an 8-figure customer commitment in under 90 days from initial demo to contract,” a “channel deal serving customers across 20 countries.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said evidence of “named enterprise wins” or “confirmation that H2 large deals are contracted rather than pipelined” would support the bull case; it did not identify this commitment.

description: Management gave a positive closing expectation for LivePerson, saying the deal is expected to close before year-end. The preview highlighted the August 20 shareholder vote as a real execution risk and said hedging on the vote would be concerning.
fact_evidence: LivePerson “secured all key regulatory clearances and is expected to close before year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the August 20 vote “a real execution risk” and listed “any hedging on the Aug 20 meeting” as a catalyst to watch; it already noted that all regulatory gates appeared cleared.

description: The call added specific LivePerson deal benefits not laid out in the preview: the acquisition would add 25 Fortune 100 brands and eliminate LivePerson’s debt. These are additional strategic and financial details, rather than a change to the previewed $350–400M 2027 framework.
fact_evidence: The acquisition is “adding 25 of the Fortune 100 brands and eliminating LivePerson's debt.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: OASYS was described as driving record win rates across demos, RFPs, and pilots, while restaurant renewal rates reached 100% for key accounts. The preview identified restaurants as a newer growth leg but did not anticipate these results.
fact_evidence: “OASYS, launched in May 2026, is driving record win rates across demos, RFPs, and pilots, with restaurant renewal rates hitting 100% for key accounts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “Restaurants/QSR and healthcare” as “the newer legs” and did not specify expected OASYS win rates or renewal rates.

description: SMB smart-answering revenue more than doubled year-over-year, a specific operating result the preview did not forecast.
fact_evidence: “SMB ‘smart answering’ revenue more than doubling year-over-year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: VEL’s held-for-investment NPL rate fell to 9.6%, below the preview’s expected 10.0%–10.4% range, and charge-offs were only $700,000, below the five-quarter trailing average. Resolutions continued to clear above par, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation for favorable resolution economics.
fact_evidence: “Non-performing loans fell to 9.6% of held-for-investment loans,” down from 10.3% a year ago; the company resolved $90.5 million of NPLs with net gains of 102.7% and total recoveries of 107.7%, while charge-offs were only $700,000, below the 5-quarter trailing average.
expectation_evidence: “NPLs flat ~10.0–10.4%” in the base scenario; the preview also said to watch for NPLs below 9.8% in the bull case and expected resolutions to keep clearing above 100%.

description: Portfolio NIM reached 3.66%, above the 3.5% standing target and above the preview’s base-case range of 3.50%–3.56%. It also exceeded the preview’s 3.60% bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Portfolio NIM was 3.66%, above the 3.5% target and up 10 basis points from Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “NIM stabilizing ~3.5% for FY26”; the base case was “3.50–3.56%” and the bull case was “≥3.60%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Loan production was $672.6 million, below the preview’s $700–$780 million base case and below its $680 million threshold for a weak quarter. Production did rise sequentially from Q1, but the dollar total fell year over year despite the preview’s expectation of a seasonal step-up.
fact_evidence: “Total loan production was $672.6 million,” down from $725 million a year ago; it increased 5.2% from Q1’s $639 million, while unit production rose 3.3%.
expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “$700–780M”; the preview said “anything below ~$680M” would put the second-half growth narrative in question and described Q2 as “the seasonal step-up quarter.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The portfolio reached $7.0 billion, but its 2.2% sequential growth was below the preview’s roughly 5% q/q expectation and its projected $7.15–$7.2 billion level. The 19% year-over-year increase was also below the preview’s roughly 25% growth context.
fact_evidence: “The total loan portfolio grew to $7.0 billion in UPB, a 19% year-over-year increase and 2.2% sequential increase from Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “~+5% q/q would put the book at ~$7.15–7.2B” and projected “~$7.15B” in its base scenario.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported that July was the best month ever for submissions, an encouraging new indicator for second-half production that the preview had not identified in its expectations.
fact_evidence: Management said “July was the best month ever for submissions.”

description: CMRC cut its FY2026 revenue outlook by $18 million at the midpoint and its non-GAAP operating-income outlook by $12.5 million, with both new ranges below the prior ranges’ low ends. The preview’s base case expected the full range to be reaffirmed; even its bear case described a cut to the lower half, not guidance below the previous low end.
fact_evidence: “The company cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $18 million at the midpoint (to $336.5-344.5 million) and non-GAAP operating income by $12.5 million (to $28-34 million), driven roughly evenly by a deliberate partner ecosystem decision and more cautious new account booking assumptions.”
expectation_evidence: “Base (~50%)” expected “FY range reaffirmed unchanged”; the bear case described “FY guide cut to lower half ($347.5–355M).”

description: Q2 non-GAAP operating income was $8.1 million, well above the $4–5 million guide and the preview’s $5–6 million base case. That was a much stronger profit result than expected despite revenue landing within guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $84.5 million (within guidance), with non-GAAP operating income of $8.1 million beating the high end of the $4-5 million guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income” guide: “$4M – $5M”; base scenario: “$5M–$6M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company reported that BigCommerce Payments GMV is running more than 30% ahead of its internal plans, with adoption reaching additional merchant groups. The preview worried the first full quarter might yield only underwhelming qualitative commentary, although it did not provide an external forecast for Payments volume.
fact_evidence: “BigCommerce Payments GMV is running more than 30% ahead of internal plans since its U.S. launch, with adoption expanding to select performance plan merchants and larger accounts, plus a UK launch planned later this year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “qualitative hand-waving = it's early and underwhelming,” while noting that “quantified attach = confidence.”

description: Non-GAAP gross margin fell 170 basis points sequentially, a steeper decline than the preview’s roughly 100-basis-point base-case assumption. Management attributed the pressure primarily to higher hosting costs from AI crawler and agent traffic that it chose to keep open.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined sequentially from 77.4% in Q1 to 75.7% in Q2, driven primarily by higher hosting costs from increased AI crawler and agent traffic that management deliberately chose to keep open.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “GM down ~100bps”; the preview said a “Q2 gross margin compresses another 200bps+” would be a downside case.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management identified longer sales cycles specifically in B2C replatforming, as merchants deliberate over AI and agentic discovery strategies. The preview discussed AI-related monetization as a potential opportunity but did not anticipate this decision-making delay; management said B2B, Feedonomics, and product intelligence had not materially weakened.
fact_evidence: “Softness is concentrated specifically in B2C replatforming, where longer sales cycles reflect merchants deliberating over AI/agentic discovery strategies, while B2B, Feedonomics, and product intelligence showed no material weakening.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: NRR improved to 95.8%, modestly above the preview’s estimated 95.5% and its base-case range, though it did not reach the 96% milestone the preview highlighted as evidence of stronger cross-sell.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention improved sequentially for the third consecutive quarter to 95.8%, up from 95.4% in Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated NRR at “~95.5%” and gave a base case of “95.3–95.7%”; it called “a print through 96%” the first real evidence the cross-sell motion works.

description: Albemarle reported Q2 sales of $1.7 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $858 million, above preview estimates of $1.59 billion and about $734 million. The quarter beat expectations on both measures, with the larger gap in EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 31% year-over-year to $1.7 billion,” and “adjusted EBITDA more than doubled (up 155%) to $858 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 Cons. | $1.59B”; “Adj. EBITDA (segment sum) | ~ $734M.”

description: The company cut its full-year energy storage volume outlook to 225,000–235,000 tons LCE, or flat to down 4% year-over-year, rather than maintaining the preview’s expectation of flat volume. The June Greenbushes CGP3 fire was the stated cause, partly offset by stronger Wodgina production.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 energy storage volumes were cut to 225,000-235,000 tons LCE (flat to down 4% year-over-year) due to the June 9 CGP3 fire at Greenbushes, partially offset by stronger Wodgina production.”
expectation_evidence: “FY guidance is flat volume”; the preview also called a volume raise “the cleanest bull signal.”

description: Albemarle raised its full-year specialties outlook, lifting sales to $1.4–$1.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $275–$325 million. This was an upside revision from the prior guidance range, with bromine price gains from Middle East supply disruptions driving the increase.
fact_evidence: “Albemarle raised its full-year specialties outlook to net sales of $1.4-1.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $275-325 million, driven by bromine price gains from Middle East supply disruptions.”
expectation_evidence: “FY raised at Q1 to $1.3–1.5B sales / $225–275M EBITDA”; the preview also said a further raise was part of its bull scenario.

description: Management guided to sequential declines in Q3 sales, EBITDA, and margins in both segments, despite the preview’s expectation that energy storage volumes would be seasonally stronger in Q2 and Q3. The outlook cites lower energy storage volumes, potentially lower pricing, and higher-cost spodumene inventory flowing through.
fact_evidence: “Management guided that Q3 sales, EBITDA and margins will decline sequentially in both segments,” citing “lower energy storage volumes, potentially lower pricing, and higher-cost spodumene inventory.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 was 53kt with CFO Neal Sheorey guiding Q2/Q3 seasonally stronger and Q4 weaker on 2025 year-end destocking.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Q2 energy storage realized pricing was about $20/kg LCE, below the preview’s roughly $21/kg estimate. The reported price was also about 15% below market pricing because of spodumene dilution and a three-month pricing lag.
fact_evidence: “Q2 realized price of ~$20/kg LCE was about 15% below market pricing due to spodumene dilution and a 3-month pricing lag.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~57kt LCE at ~$21/kg realized” and said Q2 realized price “should step up materially from Q1's ~$17/kg.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Current lithium market conditions were tighter than the preview’s demand-and-supply discussion suggested: demand was running above forecast and inventories were near record lows, despite the preview highlighting falling spot prices and supply restarts.
fact_evidence: “Global lithium demand grew 45% year-over-year through May, running above forecast, while inventories fell to near-record lows—carbonate under 3 weeks and hydroxide under a month.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the demand backdrop as “tracking 37%” and noted spot was “−15% in a month” after several supply restarts.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Albemarle raised its stationary-storage demand forecast for 2026 by 11% and lifted the low end of its 2030 total lithium demand outlook by 100,000 tons. The preview discussed demand growth generally but did not anticipate these upward forecast revisions.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 stationary storage forecast 11% to 900-1,100 GWh and lifted the low end of its 2030 total lithium demand outlook by 100,000 tons.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “15–40% demand-growth backdrop (tracking 37%)” but gave no expected upward revision to the stationary-storage or 2030 demand forecasts.

description: Management projected high-single-digit energy storage volume growth in 2027 and reaffirmed a 240,000–260,000-ton LCE target as CGP3 ramps to full run rate by Q1 2027. This provided a constructive growth outlook rather than the possible downside framing for 2027 raised in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Management expects high-single-digit energy storage volume growth in 2027 as CGP3 ramps to full run rate by Q1 2027, targeting 240,000-260,000 tons LCE consistent with its 15% CAGR trajectory.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether management would “re-introduce downside framing for 2027.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $1.92, well above the preview’s roughly $1.70 consensus estimate and even above its bull-case range of $1.85–$1.95’s lower bound by a small margin. The beat was about 12% versus the consensus midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EPS was $1.92, up from $1.68 in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$200M / $1.70 as the number to beat”; the bull scenario put adjusted EPS at “$1.85–1.95.”

description: Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $825–855 million, rather than being reaffirmed or raised from the prior $865–895 million range; it is also below the preview’s $869.9 million consensus. The preview had flagged guidance as the most important line and described narrowing toward the low end as a risk, but the reported range was cut below it.
fact_evidence: “[A] downward revision to full-year total revenue guidance of $825-855 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $869.9M (cons.) vs guide $865–895M”; the preview said a raise was the bull trigger and “narrow to the low end” would be a warning.

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to $445–470 million, below the prior $475–500 million range the preview expected management to reaffirm or improve. The new range implies essentially flat EBITDA despite projected revenue growth, rather than the EBITDA-accretive outcome the preview associated with the acquisition.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $445-470 million implies essentially flat performance versus 2025, despite 8% projected revenue growth at the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance as “$475–500M” and said the base case was to “Reaffirm $865–895M / $475–500M.” It also said management called the acquisition “immediately EBITDA-accretive.”

description: The Nuscenta franchise fell to $35.2 million, substantially below the preview’s $45 million estimate, with a 24% year-over-year decline rather than the expected 3% decline. The reported explanation was lower net pricing on authorized generics.
fact_evidence: “Nuscenta franchise revenue fell 24% year-over-year to $35.2 million due to lower net pricing on authorized generics.”
expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “Nucynta … Q2’26E … $45M (–3%).”

description: Jornay PM revenue reached $46.1 million, above the preview’s $44 million estimate, with 41% year-over-year growth versus the estimate’s 35%. Prescription growth was 13.1%, while prescribers reached a new high above 30,000.
fact_evidence: “Journet PM generated $46.1 million in net revenue, up 41% year-over-year, with prescriptions growing 13.1% and prescribers reaching an all-time high of over 30,000 HCPs (up 17.6%).”
expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “Jornay PM … Q2’26E … $44M (+35%).”

description: Belbuca revenue was $57.7 million, beating the preview’s $52 million estimate and growing 10% year over year rather than being flat. The company also reported new formulary access covering an additional 9 million lives, a development the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Belbuca revenue grew 10% year-over-year to $57.7 million and recently secured formulary access for an additional 9 million lives effective in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “Belbuca … Q2’26E … $52M (flat).”

description: Astaris contributed $12.9 million in its initial partial-quarter sales, versus the preview’s $10 million stub estimate. The company also raised its Astaris revenue guidance to $65–75 million, above the preview’s cited $60–70 million expectation.
fact_evidence: “Astaris … contributed $12.9 million in initial revenue from about a month and a half of sales”; “The company raised its full-year Astaris revenue guidance to $65-75 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “AZSTARYS (stub) … $10M” and said management targeted “$60–70M for the remainder of 2026.”

description: The company reported a $15.1 million GAAP net loss, largely because of $24.1 million in acquisition-related expenses. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not give an expectation for GAAP earnings or these expenses, so the gap versus expectations is not quantified.
fact_evidence: “The company posted a GAAP net loss of $15.1 million (loss of $0.46 per share) versus net income of $12 million a year earlier, largely due to $24.1 million in Astaris acquisition-related expenses.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $113.8 million, above the preview’s buy-side estimate range of roughly $105–112 million, though the top end was exceeded by only a small amount.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 8% to $113.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA at “~$105–112M (buy-side).”

description: The preview cited FY27 Street EPS of $13.48, implying roughly 7% growth, while management set low-single-digit revenue growth and only modest EPS leverage as the starting assumption. That points to a weaker FY27 earnings-growth outlook than investors were expecting.
fact_evidence: Management characterized FY27 as low single-digit revenue growth with only modest EPS leverage as a starting assumption, versus Street expectations of around 7% EPS growth.
expectation_evidence: FY27 Street EPS: $13.48.

description: The preview’s H2 bridge implied roughly $5.20 billion of Q4 revenue and described the Q4 ramp as demanding. Management instead expects Q4 revenue growth to slow to about 2.5% from Q3’s 4.4%, although it attributed the deceleration almost entirely to the tougher Alaris comparison rather than underlying weakness.
fact_evidence: Q4 revenue growth is expected to decelerate to roughly 2.5% from 4.4% in Q3, driven almost entirely by the tougher Alaris capital comparison rather than underlying weakness.
expectation_evidence: H2 FY26 implied revenue: ~$10.1B; Q4 implied residual: ~$5.20B. The preview called the Q4 ramp a “demanding bar.”

description: Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS both exceeded the preview’s consensus: revenue was about $110 million above the $4.89 billion estimate, and EPS was 9 cents above $3.14. The beats were meaningful but modest relative to the estimates.
fact_evidence: Q3 FY26 revenue was $5 billion, up 4.4% FX-neutral. Adjusted EPS was $3.23 and ahead of expectations.
expectation_evidence: Q3 FY26 consensus: revenue $4.89B; adjusted diluted EPS $3.14.

description: BD lifted the FY26 EPS guidance midpoint to $12.67 from $12.62, and moved revenue guidance to the high end of its low-single-digit FX-neutral range. The preview’s base case anticipated an upward narrowing of the EPS range, so the midpoint increase was favorable, though the range was not narrowed.
fact_evidence: BD raised the midpoint of full-year guidance to a range of $12.62 to $12.72. It also raised full-year revenue guidance to the high end of its low single-digit FX-neutral range.
expectation_evidence: Base scenario: FY26 range “narrowed upward”; the preview also flagged narrowing to $12.60–$12.72 as a sign the ramp was on track.

description: The preview highlighted BioPharma Systems as the only negative segment in Q2 and flagged vaccine demand as a drag. The reported facts instead emphasized broad portfolio growth: four platforms grew double digits and more than 90% of the portfolio grew at a high-single-digit rate, though they did not provide a specific BioPharma Systems result.
fact_evidence: Four growth platforms delivered double-digit growth (biologic drug delivery, advanced patient monitoring, PureWick, advanced tissue regeneration), with over 90% of the portfolio growing high single digits.
expectation_evidence: BioPharma Systems revenue and organic growth were flagged as a key watch: Q2 was “−1.8% FXN” and “vaccine demand is the drag.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Despite the preview noting $2.1 billion of debt retirement, BD ended the quarter with net leverage still above its long-term target, limiting balance-sheet flexibility. The preview did not specify an expected leverage level, so the remaining constraint is new information rather than a direct miss against a stated target for this quarter.
fact_evidence: Net leverage ended at approximately 2.9x, still above the long-term target of 2.5x, constraining balance sheet flexibility.

description: Net revenue was $331 million, down 13%, a smaller decline than the preview’s estimated 15.6%–20.3% drop and above its $320.7 million consensus estimate. The preview expected the refranchising and partnership exit to weigh on the headline, but the reported decline was less severe.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue fell 13% to $331 million due to the planned re-franchising of the Western US and Japan, though organic revenue was essentially flat excluding those deals.”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $320.7M” and “~$303M (−20.3% YoY)”; the preview also characterized consensus as “−16% to −20% YoY.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $28.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $30–32 million estimate, and the 8.7% margin was below its 9.8% base case. EBITDA still grew 43% and accelerated from Q1’s 38% growth, but the reported dollars and margin fell short of the preview’s expectation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 43% year-over-year to $28.8 million,” and “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 340 basis points to 8.7%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … my est. ~$30–32M” and “My working base case: … adjusted EBITDA $31M (9.8% margin).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: U.S. average weekly sales per door reached about $697, up 33% year over year. That was a much stronger increase than the preview’s expected continuation of the +16.7% trajectory, although it remained just below the preview’s bull-case threshold of more than $700.
fact_evidence: “US average weekly sales per door rose 33% year-over-year to approximately $697.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1: $685, +16.7% YoY” and the base case called for sales per door “up low-double-digits”; the bull case specified “Sales/door >$700.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half capex was down 70% year over year and free cash flow improved by more than $100 million versus the prior-year first half. That is a stronger cash-generation update than the preview’s more general expectation that positive free cash flow would be sustained.
fact_evidence: “First-half capex dropped 70% year-over-year to $16.1 million, and free cash flow improved by more than $100 million versus the first half of last year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Sustaining positive FCF is the proof point” and noted the $50–60 million capex guide was “roughly a 50% cut versus 2025.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Management newly highlighted that the prior-year Q3 comparison included a $9.3 million cyber-insurance gain. That creates a specific comparison headwind for assessing the expected second-half acceleration that the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: The company maintained guidance “while noting Q3 2025 included a $9.3 million cyber insurance gain that inflated the prior-year comparison.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the “H2 acceleration promise” and said “H2 comps go clean once McDonald's fully laps,” without mentioning the Q3 cyber-insurance gain.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported digital sales growth and loyalty engagement that the preview did not discuss: digital sales grew 8% and represented about 22% of U.S. retail sales, while the loyalty base approached 18 million members. These are favorable channel and engagement datapoints, but the preview provided no benchmark for how much growth to expect.
fact_evidence: “Digital channel sales grew 8% year-over-year and now represent about 22% of total US retail sales,” with “a loyalty program of nearly 18 million members who visit ~30% more frequently.”

description: EPAM cut its FY2026 revenue growth outlook to 3.2%–4.2% reported and 2%–3% organic constant currency, below the previous 4.0%–6.5% reported and 2.5%–5.0% organic range. This was a second cut, with the organic-growth floor now below the preview’s stated 2.5% floor.
fact_evidence: Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 3.2%-4.2% reported (2%-3% organic constant currency), citing North American weakness they described as largely idiosyncratic to EPAM rather than macro-driven.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance: revenue growth +4.0% to +6.5% (organic cc +2.5% to +5.0%); the preview called the organic cc floor of +2.5% the most important framing.

description: The Q3 revenue outlook was well below the preview’s implied $1.44–$1.46 billion range, and management expected revenue to be flattish from Q3 to Q4 rather than accelerating in the second half. The $1.410–$1.425 billion range implies only 1.7% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
fact_evidence: Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $1.410-$1.425 billion implies only 1.7% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, with revenue expected to be flattish from Q3 to Q4.
expectation_evidence: Consensus math implies Q3 around $1.44–$1.46B. The preview said the FY26 range mathematically requires H2 acceleration.

description: Large AI-led client deals that were expected to support second-half acceleration were still unsigned, and meaningful revenue contribution was pushed out to the first half of 2027. That is a later timeline than the preview’s H2 2026 assumption.
fact_evidence: A pipeline of large AI-led deals (Agentic managed services, application maintenance) with existing clients remains unsigned, with meaningful revenue contribution now pushed to first half of 2027 rather than second half 2026.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the ~10 large multi-year vendor-consolidation deals in the pipeline underpinned an assumed H2 acceleration, while noting conversion timing was uncertain.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash generation did not rebound as the preview hoped: Q2 operating cash flow was slightly negative after Q1’s negative quarter, and management reduced its full-year free-cash-flow conversion outlook to around 70%, below the typical 80%–90% range.
fact_evidence: Q2 operating cash flow turned negative at -$2 million (versus +$53 million a year ago) with DSO rising to 82 days, prompting a cut in full-year free cash flow conversion guidance to around 70% versus the typical 80%-90%.
expectation_evidence: The preview called for a clean Q2 OCF rebound after Q1’s –$36.4M and said a second negative quarter would be a serious problem; it also highlighted the FY cash-conversion story.

description: EPAM’s Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $3.38 exceeded the $3.14 consensus and the prior guidance range’s $3.18 high end. The gap was substantially larger than the preview’s expected modest beat or $3.20–$3.25 whisper range.
fact_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS grew 22% year-over-year to $3.38.
expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance was $3.10–$3.18, with Street consensus at $3.14; the preview estimated a buy-side whisper of $3.20–$3.25.

description: Pure AI-native revenue exceeded the preview’s $145–$155 million expected range and the $140 million caution threshold. It was also the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth, and management remained on track for the $600 million 2026 target.
fact_evidence: Pure AI native revenues exceeded $160 million (over 11% of business), marking the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth and keeping the company on track for its $600 million 2026 target.
expectation_evidence: Straight-line-to-target requires roughly $145–$155M in Q2; below $140M would challenge the growth narrative.

description: The Americas, EPAM’s largest region, slowed from 2.5% growth in Q1 to just 0.5% in Q2 instead of showing the inflection the preview said mattered most. Management attributed the broader North American weakness to company-specific factors.
fact_evidence: Americas, representing 57% of revenue, grew only 0.5% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Americas growth of +2.5% in Q1 and said an inflection there mattered more than the EMEA number.

description: Software & Hi-Tech swung from 10.9% growth in Q1 to a 1.3% decline in Q2. The preview’s latest reported baseline for this vertical was still strong growth.
fact_evidence: Software and Hi-Tech declined 1.3% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: Q1 vertical growth: Software & Hi-Tech +10.9%.

description: Business Information & Media’s decline deepened from 0.7% in Q1 to 2.1% in Q2, indicating further deterioration in a vertical that was already slightly down.
fact_evidence: Business Information & Media fell 2.1%.
expectation_evidence: Q1 vertical growth: Business Information & Media –0.7%.

description: Despite the weaker revenue outlook, management raised profitability guidance to the high end of the 15%–16% adjusted operating-margin range. expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP operating margin guidance was 15%–16%; Q1 was 14.3% and the preview said the Q2 guide needs about 100bps of sequential expansion. The preview said trimming the FY margin band would be a negative signal.

description: Q2 revenue came in at the top of the company’s outlook range and slightly above the $1.407 billion consensus, although the beat was small.
fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $1.415 billion, up 4.5% year-over-year reported and 3.4% organic constant currency, coming in at the high end of the outlook range.
expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was $1.407B; company guidance was $1.400B–$1.415B.

description: HAE raised FY27 guidance from 4%-7% reported and 3%-6% organic revenue growth to 5%-8% reported and 4%-7% organic growth. The new ranges are one percentage point higher at both ends.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY27 guidance to 5%-8% reported revenue growth and 4%-7% organic growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue growth: 4–7% reported; 3–6% organic.”

description: Q1 revenue was $339 million, above the preview’s $327.9 million consensus and $332 million estimate. Revenue grew 6%, versus consensus-implied growth of 2%.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% (both reported and organic) to $339 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $327.9M”; the preview’s own estimate was “$332M (+3.3%).”

description: Plasma organic growth reached 8%, well above the preview’s roughly 3%-5% estimates and above its stated +6% threshold for the most bullish Plasma datapoint.
fact_evidence: “Plasma revenue grew 8% organic.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Plasma at “$136M (+4.7%)” and said “Plasma above +6% organic is the single most bullish datapoint available.”

description: Adjusted EPS of $1.14 exceeded the preview’s $1.07-$1.09 consensus range, despite the preview’s bearish estimate-revision trend.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 4% to $1.14.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.07 – $1.09.”

description: Gross margin was 60.4%, about 100 basis points above the preview’s roughly 59.4% consensus. Management said margin expanded when excluding the prior-year software-license benefit, clarifying that the reported year-over-year decline did not reflect underlying contraction.
fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin was 60.4%, down 40 basis points year-over-year, but expanded excluding a ~200 basis point prior-year benefit from upfront software license revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin: ~59.4% (street).”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Persona PLUS was converting faster and delivering greater yield improvement than the preview quantified: rollout was ahead of schedule, at 30-40 centers per week, with yields more than 5% above earlier Persona offerings and potential to convert the U.S. market this year.
fact_evidence: “Persona PLUS is delivering yield improvements exceeding 5% over prior Persona offerings, rolling out ahead of schedule at 30-40 centers per week with potential to convert the entire U.S. market this year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Persona PLUS conversions” as a Plasma swing factor but did not forecast this rollout pace or yield improvement.

description: Adjusted operating margin of 23.4% was below the preview’s 24%-25% estimate, even though management reaffirmed its full-year margin-expansion target.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin was 23.4%, down 70 basis points year-over-year, with the company reaffirming 50-100 basis points of operating margin expansion for FY27.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin: ~24–25% (my est.).”

description: Although Interventional Technologies returned to growth, sensor-guided technologies still faced ensoETM and OEM weakness. The preview had said the OEM and esophageal-cooling headwinds were now lapped, so their continued drag was a negative qualification to the inflection.
fact_evidence: “Interventional Technologies returned to growth at 3% organic ... though sensor-guided technologies were dragged down by ensoETM softness and OEM weakness.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the decline was attributed to “OEM sourcing changes and esophageal cooling headwinds now lapped.”

description: Management said M&A was off the table for now, emphasizing organic growth and deleveraging. The preview noted deleveraging was co-prioritized with buybacks but did not flag an explicit pause in M&A.
fact_evidence: “The company paid down $100 million of revolver debt ... with M&A stated as off the table for now in favor of organic growth and deleveraging.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The Roivant webcast reported a $950 million upfront payment from the Moderna settlement, with roughly $770 million going to Genevant and the remainder to Arbutus. Roivant also said cash was just under $4 billion before receipt of the $772 million; the preview did not anticipate this Roivant-level inflow, and that cash figure is not comparable to its Immunovant cash estimate.
fact_evidence: “received a $950 million upfront payment from the Moderna settlement,” with “roughly $770 million going to Genevant”; “cash stood just under $4 billion before receipt of the $772 million.”

description: A favorable appellate ruling in the '498 case could produce a further $1.3 billion, and Roivant said it filed three new international lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech in July. The preview did not flag these litigation developments or potential proceeds.
fact_evidence: “A favorable appellate ruling in the ongoing '498 Federal Circuit case could yield an additional $1.3 billion,” and “three new international lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech were filed in July.”

description: Roivant repurchased about $200 million of stock during the quarter, with a slightly higher amount including March. The preview mentioned watching Roivant’s capital-allocation commentary but did not anticipate a buyback; the reported average price in the high $20s was also well above the roughly $10 average in the earlier $1.5 billion round.
fact_evidence: “repurchased about $200 million of stock in the quarter (slightly more including March), buying back at an average price in the high $20s versus around $10 per share in the earlier $1.5 billion round.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Roivant call framing” and “any hint at a strategic transaction, partnership, or further monetization of the Immunovant stake”; it did not mention a Roivant buyback.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Roivant expected a dermatomyositis launch by the end of September after priority review, but characterized the ramp as “slow and steady,” noting limited prior off-label JAK use and a concentrated referral-center base. The preview did not discuss this Roivant product or its launch outlook.
fact_evidence: “expects to launch brepiprazole (brepocitinib) in dermatomyositis by the end of September 2026,” while management guided to a “‘slow and steady’ dermatomyositis launch”; “only low-to-mid single-digit percentages of patients have prior off-label JAK experience” and about “200 myositis referral centers treat roughly half of U.S. patients.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Roivant reported a greater-than-20-point Phase II cutaneous sarcoidosis benefit versus roughly no change on placebo—well beyond its 5-point clinical-meaningfulness goal—and said it had started the Phase III study ahead of schedule. The preview did not flag this program or signal.
fact_evidence: “greater than 20-point benefit on the CSAMI scale versus roughly nothing on placebo,” “well above the 5-point clinical meaningfulness goal,” and the Phase III study was initiated “ahead of schedule.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Roivant said PH-ILD top-line data are expected in the second half of 2026, while cautioning that the study is not powered for six-minute walk distance and that management is hoping for a clear PVR signal. This program and endpoint caveat were not covered in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Top-line PH-ILD data … is expected in the second half of 2026,” with the company “hoping for a clear PVR signal but not powered for six-minute walk distance.”

description: Q2 revenue was $653 million, far above the preview’s operative expectation of about $496 million and also above published consensus of about $597.7 million. The result therefore beat even the higher consensus figure, while sharply exceeding management’s previously implied flat-sequential revenue shape.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $653 million, up 31% versus Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$500M as the operative revenue bar”; published consensus revenue was “~$597.7M.” The preview also said management guided Q2 revenue “in line with Q1” at “~$496M.”

description: Management raised the FY2026 revenue range to $2.6–$2.7 billion rather than trimming it toward the low end as the preview’s base case anticipated. The new midpoint is $150 million above the prior midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.6-$2.7 billion (from $2.4-$2.6 billion).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said the “FY revenue guide [is] trimmed toward $2.4–2.5B low end”; it listed the existing range as “$2.4–2.6B.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $28 million, above management’s implied roughly $22 million expectation and above the low end of the preview’s $25–$30 million derived consensus range. Some of the beat came from recognizing development work earlier than expected, which also reduces the near-term EBITDA step-up.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $653 million… with adjusted EBITDA of $28 million… both above management's expectations”; the outperformance “stemmed from recognizing prior-year development originally expected in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview put management-implied Q2 adjusted EBITDA at “~$22M” and derived consensus at “~$25–30M.”

description: The expected Q2-to-Q3 EBITDA increase is now only about $4–$7 million because some development was recognized in Q2. That is a smaller step-up than the preview’s stated expectation for $10–$15 million of sequential improvement in Q3 and Q4.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA outperformance stemmed from recognizing prior-year development originally expected in Q3, so the Q2-to-Q3 increase was cut to ~$4-$7 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said sequential EBITDA improvement of “$10–15M” was “coming in Q3 and Q4.”

description: The FY2026 adjusted EBITDA range was narrowed and its midpoint raised to $127.5 million, rather than simply being held at $110–$140 million as the preview’s base case expected. The midpoint increase is modest compared with the revenue-guidance revision.
fact_evidence: “Narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $120-$135 million (from $110-$140 million), raising the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the “EBITDA guide $110–140M held”; its catalyst checklist said the guide might be “held vs. cut.”

description: Management made a new 2027 commitment for at least $150 million of adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint, with revenue growth above 25%, based on contracts already under agreement. The preview focused on whether near-term launches would support FY2026 guidance and did not set out this 2027 outlook.
fact_evidence: “The company committed to a 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint at or above $150 million and expects revenue growth of more than 25% in 2027, based on contracts already under agreement.”

description: Q2 MER rose to 95%, about 200 basis points worse than Q1 and above the preview’s roughly 93% expectation. This is a weaker near-term medical-cost result even though the full-year MER expectation remained around 93%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 medical expense ratio was 95%, up ~200 basis points from Q1's 93%, driven by the May 1 Highmark Performance Suite launch.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed management-implied Q2 MER at “~93%” and said the FY guide was “~93%.”

description: The call quantified a Medicaid expansion membership decline that the preview had not anticipated: an industry-wide drop of about 20%, translating into a 4–5% membership headwind for Evolent and likely flat-to-down Tech & Services revenue in 2027. This adds a specific future headwind to the outlook.
fact_evidence: “The company expects a ~20% decline in Medicaid expansion members industry-wide, translating to a roughly 4-5% Medicaid membership headwind for Evolent, with Tech & Services revenue likely flat to down in 2027.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed an oncology Performance Suite partnership expected to generate about $300 million in annualized revenue, with a launch expected by December 2026. The preview discussed other expected launches but did not identify this partnership or its revenue contribution.
fact_evidence: “A new oncology Performance Suite partnership with an existing imaging client covering ~1.5 million lives across 11 states is expected to launch by December 2026 and generate ~$300 million in annualized revenue.”

description: The preview highlighted a need for a quantified ACA exchange disenrollment figure, but the reported facts provide a quantified Medicaid expansion headwind instead and no ACA exchange disenrollment number. The specific uncertainty the preview called out therefore remains unaddressed in the information provided.
fact_evidence: The call facts quantify “a ~20% decline in Medicaid expansion members industry-wide” and a “4-5% Medicaid membership headwind for Evolent”; no ACA exchange disenrollment figure is reported in the provided facts.
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “ACA exchange disenrollment — quantified” as a key metric and said “A hard number, even a bad one, removes uncertainty.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company reported net debt of $808.3 million, below the preview’s rough estimate of about $843 million of net debt based on $985 million of debt and $142 million of cash. However, unrestricted cash was $115.7 million and the ABL revolver was paid down only to its $62.5 million minimum, so the liquidity picture is not uniformly better.
fact_evidence: “Evolent ended Q2 with $115.7 million in unrestricted cash and $808.3 million in net debt, paid down the ABL revolver by $10 million to its $62.5 million minimum.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “$985M total debt against $142M cash.”

description: KLIC’s Q4 revenue guide was $375 million, well above the preview’s implied bar of about $328 million and even above its bull-case threshold of $355 million.
fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue to $375 million, a 13.5% sequential increase.”
expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 FY2026 guide bar: ~$328M revenue (+6% q/q)” and the bull case called for “≥$355M.”

description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $1.42 substantially exceeded the preview’s implied $1.13 bar and its bull-case threshold of $1.30.
fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026… non-GAAP EPS [is guided] to $1.42,” up from Q3’s $1.20.
expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 FY2026 guide bar:… ~$1.13 non-GAAP EPS” and the bull case called for “≥$1.30.”

description: Q3 revenue was approximately $330 million, above the $310 million consensus and just above the top of the company’s $310 million ± $20 million guidance range. The preview treated the quarter as largely de-risked, but this was still a modest beat against its live consensus bar.
fact_evidence: Revenue “increased 36.2% sequentially” and “exceed[ed] guidance”; Q2 revenue was $242.6 million, implying Q3 revenue of about $330 million.
expectation_evidence: Q3 revenue consensus was “$310M”; company guidance was “$310M ± $20M.”

description: Q3 EPS beat the preview’s estimates: non-GAAP EPS was $1.20 versus $1.00 expected, and GAAP EPS was $1.07 versus about $0.87 expected.
fact_evidence: Q3 EPS was “$1.07 GAAP and $1.20 non-GAAP.”
expectation_evidence: Q3 consensus was “$1.00” non-GAAP diluted EPS and “~$0.87” GAAP diluted EPS.

description: Advanced Solutions revenue exceeded its prior-quarter record by 20%, whereas the preview highlighted a recent sequential decline in APS and flagged another decline as a possible negative signal.
fact_evidence: “Advanced Solutions segment revenue exceeded last quarter's record by 20%.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 base… APS down sequentially on lower refurbished-system sales”; “a second consecutive decline there would be a quiet negative signal.”

description: KLIC gave a concrete, substantial FY2027 TCB revenue outlook: $150 million to $200 million, implying 50–100% growth over its FY2026 target. The preview asked for FY2027 TCB framing but did not anticipate a quantified range.
fact_evidence: “Management projects thermal compression bonding (TCB) revenue of $150 million to $200 million in FY2027, implying 50-100% growth over the FY2026 target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any FY2027 TCB framing.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Demand and visibility appeared stronger than the preview’s durability concerns implied: utilization was above 95% in China and around 90% in memory and general semiconductor, with purchase orders extending unusually far into fiscal Q2 2027.
fact_evidence: “Utilization rates reached over 95% in China and around 90% across memory and general semiconductor end markets, with inbound POs extending unusually far into fiscal Q2 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called memory and China the “most cyclical, least visible piece of the beat” and flagged whether China was “pulling in or digesting.”

description: General semiconductor revenue rose 52.6% sequentially, a particularly sharp acceleration relative to the preview’s Q2 baseline of 19.4% sequential growth and its general expectation of strength through the business.
fact_evidence: “General semiconductor revenue surged 52.6% sequentially to $227.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q2 General Semiconductor revenue of “$148.9M (+19.4% q/q)” and quoted management expecting “strength throughout the business.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: KLIC disclosed that it had quadrupled traditional wire-bonding capacity over two quarters and said it had previously supported quarterly revenue run rates of $400 million. The preview discussed Advanced Solutions capacity, but did not anticipate this scale of traditional wire-bonding capacity expansion or the historical run-rate detail.
fact_evidence: “The company increased its traditional wire bonding capacity 4x over the past two quarters and indicated it has previously supported $400 million quarterly run rates.”
expectation_evidence: The preview focused on spending to build capacity for “~$400M of annual Advanced Solutions revenue by 1H FY2027.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described data center demand as an important source of NAND wire-bonding demand, saying data centers represent about 40% of the NAND market and rely on wire bonding at least as much as smartphones and PCs. The preview discussed NAND and AI-related memory demand but did not forecast this specific market framing.
fact_evidence: “Data center now represents approximately 40% of the NAND market and relies on wire bonding at least as much as smartphones and PCs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “NAND capacity” and “new vertical-wire solutions targeting LPDDR for on-prem AI,” but gave no expectation for data center’s share of NAND or its relative wire-bonding reliance.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: KLIC set a first-half FY2027 delivery window for a hybrid-bonding tool to a customer, a concrete milestone beyond the preview’s discussion of hybrid-bonding R&D and qualification activity.
fact_evidence: “The company plans to deliver a hybrid bonding tool to a customer in the first half of fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted increased R&D in “hybrid bonding” and called for a “concrete HBM datapoint,” but did not specify a hybrid-bonding tool delivery date.

description: KDP reported Q2 EPS of $0.57, above the preview’s $0.55 consensus, and 16.3% growth exceeded management’s high-single-digit growth framing. That was a clear earnings beat, though not as large as the preview’s bull-case threshold of $0.58.
fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS grew 16.3% to $0.57, exceeding company expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $0.55”; management “guided to high-single-digit EPS growth in Q2.”

description: Legacy KDP sales grew 7.3%, above the company’s 4–6% full-year range, and management now expects full-year growth at the high end of that range. This points to stronger legacy-business growth than the preview’s guidance baseline.
fact_evidence: “Excluding JDE Peet's, legacy KDP net sales grew 7.3%”; management “now expects growth at the high end of the 4-6% range.”
expectation_evidence: “Legacy KDP 4–6% cc sales.”

description: Consolidated net sales growth of 74.6% was ahead of the preview’s 72.3% consensus growth estimate, despite the preview warning that the first fully consolidated JDE Peet’s quarter made the headline difficult to model.
fact_evidence: “Total net sales up 74.6%, largely driven by the JDE Peet's acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales … +72.3%” versus the prior-year quarter.

description: U.S. Refreshment Beverages grew 10%, ahead of the preview’s 7% consensus, with 6.5 points from volume/mix. It remained below Q1’s 11.9% growth, but volume/mix was stronger than the preview’s minimum 5-point threshold.
fact_evidence: “U.S. Refreshment Beverages … delivered 10% net sales growth (6.5 points volume/mix, 3.5 points pricing).”
expectation_evidence: Consensus implied “+7.0%”; the preview said investors wanted volume/mix to “stay ≥5 pts.”

description: U.S. Coffee operating income fell 24.7% amid green coffee inflation and tariffs, while pod shipments also declined sharply. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation that coffee margin pressure would meaningfully ease in Q2 after peaking in Q1.
fact_evidence: “U.S. Coffee operating income fell 24.7% due to green coffee inflation and tariffs, with pod shipments down 11.6% as reported (8.3% excluding the Peet's reporting shift).”
expectation_evidence: Management had said Q1 was “peak year-over-year margin pressure for coffee,” with “meaningful” easing in Q2; the preview called Q2 the first test of that promise.

description: Management said JDE Peet’s Q2 profit contribution likely marks the high watermark for quarterly earnings contribution in 2026 because of timing benefits and the Peet’s K-Cup reporting shift. The preview highlighted uncertainty around modeling the new structure but did not flag this near-term peak risk.
fact_evidence: “Management warned this Q2 profit likely represents the high watermark for quarterly earnings contribution in 2026 due to timing benefits and the Peet's K-Cup reporting shift.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The energy portfolio has already reached more than 9% market share and about $1.5 billion in net sales, with a double-digit share goal achieved at 15 major customers. The preview did not identify this business as a catalyst or discuss its scale.
fact_evidence: “The energy portfolio crossed 9% market share … now a ~$1.5 billion net sales business … tracking toward a double-digit share goal already achieved in 15 major customers.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: KDP disclosed an incremental 2% non-cash EPS headwind from purchase-price-allocation depreciation, offset by a one-time cash benefit from tariff refunds, leaving the net EPS impact neutral. Neither offsetting item was in the preview.
fact_evidence: “An incremental 2% non-cash depreciation EPS headwind from the JDE Peet's purchase price allocation, offset by a one-time cash benefit from tariff refunds, netting to neutral EPS impact.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Pro forma leverage improved to 4.4x, slightly better than expected and below the preview’s cited mid-year level of about 4.5x. This is a modestly better starting point for the planned deleveraging.
fact_evidence: “Pro forma management leverage improved to 4.4x at quarter end (slightly better than expected).”
expectation_evidence: “Net leverage ~4.5x at mid-year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Brewer shipments returned to growth at 2.1%, a positive counterpoint to the decline in coffee pods that the preview did not specifically anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Brewer shipments returned to growth at +2.1%.”

description: Kemper reported a $464.8 million GAAP net loss, or $7.90 per share, after a $460 million non-cash goodwill impairment in specialty auto. The preview discussed the stock’s decline and possible new-CEO reserve actions, but did not anticipate a goodwill write-down of this size.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $464.8 million, or $7.90 per share, driven primarily by a $460 million non-cash goodwill impairment in its specialty auto segment.”

description: Adjusted operating EPS was $0.45, above the preview’s $0.32–$0.33 consensus range by about 36%–41%. The preview’s base case was $0.28–$0.38, so the result also exceeded its central expectation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted consolidated net operating income was $26.3 million, or $0.45 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS: $0.32 – $0.33”; the base scenario projected “$0.28 – $0.38.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Kemper recorded a $16.6 million after-tax allowance for credit losses on surplus notes issued to Kemper Reciprocal Exchange, an unanticipated charge that weighs on reported results. The company also said roughly $15 million of notes remain to be evaluated.
fact_evidence: “The company recorded a $16.6 million after-tax ($21 million pre-tax) allowance for credit losses on surplus notes issued to Kemper Reciprocal Exchange, with roughly $15 million of surplus notes remaining to be evaluated going forward.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: California personal-auto policies fell 10% sequentially and California’s share of the personal-auto portfolio declined 2.5 percentage points. The preview expected Kemper to shrink California, but the pace of this decline makes the portfolio contraction sharper than its general expectation of controlled shrinkage.
fact_evidence: “California's share of the personal auto portfolio declined 2.5 percentage points during the quarter, driven by a 10% sequential decline in policies in force.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the book as “deliberately shrinking in California” and asked whether “the California shrink [is] controlled or uncontrolled.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Commercial auto had $17.7 million of adverse prior-year reserve development, continuing a pattern the call described as roughly five consecutive quarters. The preview’s base case assumed a clean quarter with no new charges, although it had flagged adverse development as a risk.
fact_evidence: “Reported results were hurt by $17.7 million of prior year reserve development, marking roughly the fifth consecutive quarter of adverse development.”
expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “a clean quarter, no new charges”; the preview also noted Q1 had “only $3.2M” of development and identified adverse prior-year development as a bear-case risk.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said commercial auto would take meaningfully more rate and tighten underwriting, accepting slower near-term growth because of reserve exposure concentrated in bodily injury and litigious California. That is a more cautious growth stance than the preview’s expectation of continued double-digit PIF growth.
fact_evidence: “Commercial auto holds about $1 billion in reserves, 90% tied to bodily injury coverage and 45% concentrated in litigious California, prompting management to take meaningfully more rate and tighten underwriting at the expense of near-term growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected commercial auto to hold “~92%” combined ratio “with continued double-digit PIF growth,” and cited Q1 PIF growth of about 10% year over year.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Holding-company liquidity was reported at $766 million, far above the preview’s cited Q1 level of $80 million. This materially eases the capital and dividend-coverage concern emphasized in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $766 million of holding company liquidity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$80M of holding company liquidity” at Q1 and highlighted capital adequacy and dividend coverage as a key concern.

description: Kemper identified more than $80 million of cumulative annualized restructuring savings, up $20 million from the prior quarter. That is ahead of the preview’s expectation of more than $60 million in run-rate savings.
fact_evidence: “Identified more than $80 million of cumulative annualized run-rate restructuring savings (up $20 million from last quarter).”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “>$60M” in restructuring run-rate savings, with “$50M actioned.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Intellia reported a major Phase III HAELO efficacy result, with lonvo-z significantly improving the primary and all key secondary endpoints and reducing mean monthly attacks by 87% versus placebo. The preview did not anticipate a new Phase III readout in this release.
fact_evidence: HAELO “achieved statistical significance on the primary and all key secondary endpoints,” with an “87% reduction in mean monthly attacks versus placebo”; 62% of patients were entirely attack-free and therapy-free.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call disclosed a previously unflagged nex-z liver-safety risk associated with HLA-C*05:01: carriers had significantly higher rates of Grade 3+ transaminase elevations. The reported rarity and transience of Grade 4 elevations and new monitoring measures partly temper, but do not remove, this concern.
fact_evidence: An analysis of over 600 samples found C*05:01 carriers (12% of samples) had “significantly higher rates of Grade 3+ transaminase elevations,” with all five highest elevations in carriers. Grade 4 elevations occurred in less than 1% of MAGNITUDE patients, were transient and mostly resolved without intervention; management implemented HLA typing and monitoring measures.
expectation_evidence: The preview's bogey was “zero new hepatic SAEs under the new mitigation protocol” and it warned that “any new Grade 3/4 transaminase event resets the platform-risk debate.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Intellia gave additional strong nex-z target-engagement data that the preview had not identified as an expected update: a 90% mean TTR reduction, reached within a month and maintained across patients since 2021 dosing.
fact_evidence: Nex-z “demonstrated a 90% mean TTR reduction,” with serum TTR below 20 micrograms per milliliter, achieved within one month and maintained consistently across all patients since 2021 dosing.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Lonvo-z's reported treatment-arm safety was especially favorable: all treatment-emergent adverse events were Grade 1 or 2, with no serious adverse events reported by the cutoff. The preview did not set out a lonvo-z safety expectation for this release.
fact_evidence: “All treatment-emergent adverse events” were Grade 1 or Grade 2, with “no serious adverse events in the treatment arm as of the data cutoff.”

description: Management offered a firmer 2027 performance framework than the preview had specified: it expects a meaningful step-up and targets a steady-state operating margin of about 23%. It also did not dispute analyst 2027 EPS estimates of roughly $11.25–$11.50.
fact_evidence: “Management expects a meaningful step-up in financial performance in 2027, targeting a steady-state operating margin of approximately 23%, and did not dispute analyst EPS estimates of roughly $11.25-$11.50 for 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any long-range framework” from the new CEO, but did not provide a 2027 margin target or EPS expectation.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Teleflex cited Freesolve, a resorbable scaffold, as a future growth driver and disclosed a BIOMAG-II randomized-data readout expected in late 2027. The preview did not mention this product or readout.
fact_evidence: “The Freesolve resorbable scaffold (BIOMAG-II randomized data readout expected late 2027) [is a] key future growth driver.”

description: Q2 revenue was $16.7 million, far above the $9.20 million consensus and also well above the preview’s inferred $10.5 million “real bar.”
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $16.7 million,” up 107% sequentially.
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$9.20M”; the preview also described “a ~$10.5M whisper” inferred from the Q1 growth trend.

description: Management’s internal Q4 revenue target of $25 million implies a much stronger second half than the preview’s roughly flat H2 expectation, although the targets are explicitly not formal guidance.
fact_evidence: Management gave an “internal (non-guidance) revenue target” of “$25 million in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus implied “~$18.3M for H2” and “a flat H2 at ~$9.1M/quarter.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview did not anticipate a specific near-term order wave from the Drone Dominance Gauntlet Program; management said more than 60,000 drones are expected to be ordered in the second half, mostly in Q4.
fact_evidence: “More than 60,000 drones are expected to be ordered under the Drone Dominance Gauntlet Program Phase 2 in the second half of 2026, mostly in Q4.”

description: The Q3 internal target calls for a sequential revenue decline, contrary to the preview’s expectation—based on management’s prior framing—that revenue would continue growing sequentially through 2026.
fact_evidence: Management targeted “$12-14 million in Q3,” with “a sequential decline due to infrastructure buildout.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had described “consistent growth… full speed growth,” with “no anticipated 2026 slowdown,” and that the company was “guiding to sequential growth every quarter.”

description: Management cited an aspirational 2027 revenue target of $250 million, far above the preview’s $52.25 million FY2027 consensus, but also said current capacity supports only about $20 million per quarter—making the target ambitious rather than an assured run rate.
fact_evidence: Management cited “$250 million as the aspirational 2027 revenue target”; “current 70,000 sq ft capacity supports only about $20 million per quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY2027E revenue $52.25M” and called for a capacity datapoint, including motor output targeted at 100,000 per month later in 2026.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Q2 was affected by supply-chain disruption from outgrowing an electronics vendor, turning a risk the preview raised as a possible downside scenario into an actual operating problem.
fact_evidence: Management cited “outgrowing an electronics vendor causing supply chain disruptions.”
expectation_evidence: The bear scenario said “Supply-chain/lead-time slippage pushes shipments to Q3,” and the preview flagged supply-chain and lead-time slippage as a risk.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management also disclosed an intermittent quality problem on a motor SKU that required production-process remedies; the preview did not identify this specific issue.
fact_evidence: Management cited “an intermittent quality issue on a motor SKU requiring production process remedies.”

description: The company raised $60 million through ATM block transactions despite the preview’s view that its large cash balance meant there was no financing risk; this adds liquidity but also entails share issuance.
fact_evidence: “The company raised $60 million at $30 per share via ATM block transactions,” and ended the quarter with “$229 million cash, no debt.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “$222.9M cash and $312.7M working capital at 3/31 means no financing risk.”

description: Revenue was $435 million, well above the preview’s $386 million consensus and its own roughly $395 million base case. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s expected 2–3% upside to consensus.
fact_evidence: “Revenue reached a record $435 million (up 24% year-over-year).”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of $386M”; “My base case revenue is ~$395M, ~2.5% above the Street.”

description: Adjusted EPS of $2.21 substantially exceeded the preview’s $1.79–$1.81 consensus range and even its $1.98 bull case. The preview had cautioned that a reported $2.24 projection was spurious, making the actual result a clear beat against the usable consensus anchor.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS hit a record $2.21.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (diluted, w/ tax benefit) | $1.79–$1.81”; the bull scenario estimated “~$1.98.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Long-term net flows swung to a $4.2 billion inflow, far stronger than the preview’s base case of roughly $0.2 billion of outflows to breakeven. Management also said flows accelerated further into Q3.
fact_evidence: “Record net long-term inflows of $4.2 billion represented a nearly $5 billion positive swing from the same quarter last year,” and “flows accelerated further into Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “LT net outflows narrow to roughly -$0.2B to breakeven” in the base case; the preview said a first positive net-flow quarter would be “a genuine narrative unlock.”

description: The adjusted EBITDA margin reached 55.8%, well above the preview’s 53%+ bogey and its 54.5% bull-case assumption. This was a stronger margin result than the preview’s already-optimistic seasonality-driven outlook.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55.8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 should get comp relief; 53%+ is the bogey”; the bull scenario assumed “54.5% EBITDA.”

description: Victory raised long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 49% to 50%, citing structural efficiency gains after Pioneer. The preview watched for a synergy increase but did not cite this higher long-term margin target.
fact_evidence: “Management raised long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 49% to 50%, reflecting structural efficiency gains post-Pioneer.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided cash comp to low-to-mid 20% of revenue”; the preview flagged “any raise to the synergy number,” but did not state an expected long-term margin-guide change.

description: The realized average fee rate was 47.9 basis points, above the preview’s expected 46–47 basis-point normalized range and its concern that mix could pull the rate down to 46 basis points. Management nevertheless guided to a normalized 46–47 basis-point range going forward.
fact_evidence: “Revenue reached a record $435 million … at an average fee rate of 47.9 basis points, though management guided to a normalized 46-47 bps range going forward.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided the investment management realized fee rate to 46–47 bps long-term”; the preview said mix shift could “drag it to 46 bps.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Pioneer’s integration was completed in five quarters and the full $110 million of net run-rate synergies was realized. fact_evidence: “The Pioneer integration was completed in five quarters, with the full $110 million in net run rate expense synergies fully realized.”
expectation_evidence: “$104M of the $110M target already realized; integration ‘substantially complete.’”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: International AUM through the Amundi partnership was $62.6 billion, above the preview’s cited $55 billion scale, and management said the partnership was trending above its initial financial expectations. The preview already noted that the partnership had been net-flow positive since the Pioneer close.
fact_evidence: “International AUM reached $62.6 billion across 61 countries via the Amundi partnership, which management said is trending above initial financial expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “The Amundi distribution partnership, now $55B AUM across 60 countries and net-flow positive since close.”

description: A Term Loan B repricing cut annual interest expense by about $2.5 million, a modest financing benefit not discussed in the preview.
fact_evidence: “A Term Loan B repricing that cut annual interest expense by ~$2.5 million.”

description: The preview expected linear advertising to decline about 21%, with the NBA lapse accounting for roughly a 20% drag. WBD reported a decline of nearly 30%, and management said international ad markets weakened further in Q2 versus Q1 amid consumer caution.
fact_evidence: “Linear advertising revenue declined nearly 30%, driven largely by the loss of the NBA, with international ad markets weakening further in Q2 versus Q1 amid consumer caution.”
expectation_evidence: “total ad revenue forecast down ~21%”; “The NBA rights lapse is now a ~20% drag on advertising.”

description: The preview anticipated that the related-party distribution deal would make streaming distribution growth harder to read in Q2, with the full benefit landing in Q3.
