fact_evidence: “Excluding a previously disclosed related-party deal, streaming distribution revenue growth would have been in the low teens, with management guiding to teens-level growth for the remainder of the year.”
expectation_evidence: “laps related-party distribution deal (full benefit lands Q3)”

description: The preview expected a weak Studios quarter because of the tough comparison and slate miss, but management said the film business underperformed expectations this year. The call facts do not give a result or quantify how far it fell short of the preview’s $300–400 million Studios EBITDA estimate.
fact_evidence: “The studio segment underperformed expectations in the film business this year against a tough Q2 2025 comp.”
expectation_evidence: “Studios” Q2’26E EBITDA “$300–400M”; “Brutal comp; slate miss.”

description: Management said the studio segment had fallen short of its over-$3 billion adjusted EBITDA goal even in a strong 2025, a negative qualification to the long-term target that the preview did not report. Management nevertheless maintained the goal.
fact_evidence: “Management maintained its long-term goal of over $3 billion in adjusted EBITDA for the studio segment, acknowledging it fell short of that target even in a strong 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “The $3B annual Studios EBITDA target reaffirmed on the Q1 call is now the pressure point.”

description: Management offered a more upbeat streaming retention outlook, expecting 2026 to be its best year ever for retention and lowest for churn, supported by expanding bundles including Disney in the U.S. The preview focused on subscriber growth and the year-end target but did not flag this retention outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to be its best year ever for streaming retention and lowest churn, driven by expanding distributor and programmer bundles such as the Disney partnership in the U.S.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management described a substantial planned increase in film production—from 14 films this year to 19 in 2027—and named a richer slate of tentpole IP. The preview focused on the current-year slate miss and did not anticipate this production ramp or slate detail.
fact_evidence: “Film production is ramping from 14 films this year to 19 films in 2027, with a richer slate of tentpole IP including Lord of the Rings, Batman, Superman, and Minecraft II.”

description: Management highlighted the scale and durability of library and licensing revenue: roughly $5 billion annually with healthy demand even for decade-old shows. fact_evidence: “The library and content licensing business generates roughly $5 billion in high-margin revenue annually, with healthy demand even for decade-old shows.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2’25 delivered … large content licensing deals.”

description: The preview set a bar of at least 8% growth for digital advertising, with programmatic growth above 20%; Q2 growth came in at 11% and programmatic accelerated to 27%. Management also expects Q3 digital advertising growth to exceed Q2's 11%.
fact_evidence: “Digital Advertising revenue grew 11% year-over-year in Q2, accelerating from 6.8% in Q1, with programmatic (now ~70% of digital ad revenue) up 27%; management expects Q3 digital advertising growth to be even stronger than 11%.”
expectation_evidence: “Bar: ≥8% Y/Y”; Q1 programmatic was “+21%” and management said Q2 growth would be “higher than Q1's,” with programmatic “over 20%.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview did not flag a material FCC license impairment; the company recorded $26.6 million of non-cash charges in Q2, contributing to a $41.8 million net loss. The reported adjusted EPS was positive, but the impairment created a much larger GAAP loss than the preview's adjusted-EPS framing addressed.
fact_evidence: “Non-cash FCC license impairment charges of $26.6 million in Q2 ($35.2 million year-to-date), driving a Q2 net loss of $41.8 million ($2.36 per diluted share).”

description: The preview did not identify a media-partnership revenue ramp of this scale. Management now expects revenue to more than double from about $6 million in 2025 to over $12 million in 2026, with a four-year target of $50 million in revenue and a 20% profit margin.
fact_evidence: “The media partnership business expects revenue to more than double from ~$6 million in 2025 to over $12 million in 2026, targeting $50 million in revenue at a 20% profit margin ($10 million profit) within four years.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Townsquare reported its first technology licensing deal, a new recurring-revenue opportunity that the preview did not discuss. SummitMedia is adopting the in-house Blueprint CRM, which management says also deepens partner integration.
fact_evidence: “Townsquare completed its first technology licensing deal, with SummitMedia adopting its in-house 'Blueprint' CRM, creating a new recurring revenue stream and deeper partner integration.”

description: The preview said Interactive's margin staying above 33% mattered less than the revenue trajectory; instead, the margin reached a record 37.6%, up from about 33% a year earlier. That was a stronger margin outcome than the preview's stated benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Townsquare Interactive segment profit margin rose to a record 37.6% (up from ~33% in Q2 2025).”
expectation_evidence: “Margin holding above 33% matters less than the trajectory.”

description: The preview expected adjusted EPS of $0.19, while adjusted EPS was $0.21. This was a modest beat of the limited analyst consensus.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.21 versus $0.22 a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (adjusted) — $0.19.”

description: The preview's base case expected broadcast revenue to decline about 6% excluding political, whereas the reported ex-political decline was 7.2%. Although that was an improvement on 2025's roughly 8% declines, it was weaker than the preview's near-term expectation.
fact_evidence: “Broadcast revenue declined 5.5% (7.2% ex-political), an improvement from the consistent 8% ex-political declines throughout 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “broadcast ~–6% ex-political.”

description: The preview looked for Townsquare Interactive's margin recovery into the mid-to-high 20s from Q1's seasonal level; Q2 segment margins were 30%, above that range. Management expects margins to moderate to the high 20s for the rest of the year, broadly matching the preview's forward expectation.
fact_evidence: “Segment margins of 30% expected to moderate to high-20s for the remainder of the year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether segment margin “recovered to the promised mid-to-high 20s from Q1's seasonal ~19%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones

fact_evidence: “The sales force remains 40% below peak and won't be rebuilt to target levels until 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Sales headcount is still ~40% below peak” and said to listen for hiring pace, but gave no timeline for rebuilding to target.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items

fact_evidence: “The company does not expect to be a material cash taxpayer until roughly end of 2028 given ~$121 million of federal NOLs.”

description: Q2 revenue was $235.5M, below the preview’s $237.9M consensus and at the low end of company guidance. The company attributed the late-quarter softness to the final two weeks of June, which had been unexpectedly weak.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $235.5 million,” landing “at the low end after unexpected softness in the final two weeks of June.”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $237.9M” consensus; the preview also said revenue consensus sat “at the very top of company guidance.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA of $32.9M was well above the preview’s roughly $28–29M expectation, but the reported result included an $11.8M tariff-refund benefit. That benefit more than explains the headline gap, while roughly $6M of incremental pre-launch investment partly offset it.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $32.9 million (14% margin),” including “an $11.8 million tariff refund benefit that offset roughly $6 million of incremental pre-launch investments.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$28–29M (implied)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin: ~12.0%.”

fact_evidence: “Trailing-12-month active customer growth was only 4.1%” and management “flag[ged] soft traffic,” while “pointing to a Q4 rebound in active customer growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything with a 4-handle or below on growth confirms the market's core bear case”; the preview also said to watch for “2.72–2.76M” active customers.

description: The company disclosed that it will reinvest all $14.4M of tariff refunds recognized this year rather than allow the proceeds to flow through to the bottom line. The preview discussed tariff-related margin relief but did not anticipate this specific use of the refund proceeds.
fact_evidence: “The company is recognizing a total $14.4 million tariff refund this year and plans to reinvest all proceeds back into the business rather than let it flow to the bottom line.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Warby Parker said about half of its existing customers are still unaware it offers eye exams, a potential awareness barrier not raised in the preview. fact_evidence: “Eye exams grew over 30% year-over-year to ~7% of revenue,” with “long-term potential of 15-20%,” though “roughly 50% of existing customers are still unaware Warby Parker offers exams.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “eye exams +30% Y/Y” and insurance penetration as an “ARPC engine,” but did not mention customer awareness.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Insurance-related reach and usage included a new milestone: covered lives rose to more than 35 million, and out-of-network claim-submission penetration surpassed in-network penetration. The preview noted the chain-wide out-of-network tool, but not that its penetration had overtaken in-network.
fact_evidence: “In-network insurance lives grew to over 35 million (up from 32M last quarter) with penetration reaching ~8%, while out-of-network claim submission penetration has now surpassed in-network, both driving higher average order values.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “an out-of-network submission tool rolled out chain-wide in March” and described insured customers as carrying “higher AOV and frequency.”

description: Axcelis raised its FY2026 outlook from approximately flat revenue to mid-single-digit year-over-year growth, a stronger outlook than the preview’s flat-revenue framing and roughly flat consensus.

expectation_evidence: Management has explicitly guided FY26 “approximately flat vs. 2025”; FY26 revenue consensus was $843.9M (+0.6%).

fact_evidence: Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $230 million and EPS of approximately $1.11.
expectation_evidence: Q3 revenue “needs to be ≥$215M”; “$220M+ validates it outright.” The preview’s implied H2 EPS was “~$1.10/qtr.”

expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$203.4M – $205.0M” and non-GAAP EPS was “$0.89 – $0.894.”

expectation_evidence: Q2 guided to “~43%”; the preview said “Delivering 43%+ is table stakes.”

fact_evidence: Bookings were $131 million with a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 1x, and total backlog exited the quarter at $452 million.
expectation_evidence: “Q2 bookings realistically need to be $180M+ (book-to-bill ≥0.9).” The preview also flagged a second sub-0.7 quarter and backlog eroding toward ~$400M as a concern.

fact_evidence: China revenue rose to 46% of total (up from 40% prior quarter).
expectation_evidence: The preview listed China at “40% of Q1 revenue” and flagged the elevated mix as an export-control overhang to watch.

fact_evidence: Silicon carbide bookings in the first half exceeded the average levels of the past two years, with two new China customers added and orders secured for high-energy channeling superjunction applications.
expectation_evidence: The preview said H2 depended on SiC “converting” and called for “concrete” evidence; its bull case required power/SiC bookings to inflect.

description: Q2 revenue was $33.3 million, above the preview’s $29.8–$30.7 million consensus range and its inferred $27–$28 million whisper. The beat was substantial even against the published high-end estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew 50% year-over-year and 60% sequentially to $33.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $29.8M – $30.7M”; the preview also says “the practical whisper is closer to $27–28M.”

description: Space-based intelligence and AI services revenue reached $24.5 million, well above the preview’s $19–20 million sequential on-track range. The preview had identified this as the key metric, so the size of the step-up was a notable upside surprise.
fact_evidence: “Record space-based intelligence and AI services revenue of $24.5 million (up 50% from Q1).”
expectation_evidence: “$19–20M is on-track”; Q1 was “$16.5M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $4.7 million rather than merely around breakeven or slightly positive, as the preview expected. That is a meaningful profitability upside against the preview’s implied Q2 threshold.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $4.7 million (a 14.2% margin), a $7.5 million improvement over the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~breakeven to slightly positive implied by FY guide”; the preview says “Q2 essentially has to reach breakeven-or-better.”

fact_evidence: “The company secured up to $200 million in year-to-date bookings.”
expectation_evidence: “Bookings support the story — ~$160M of YTD contract awards.”

fact_evidence: “Won an 8-figure NRO contract to accelerate AROS development toward a targeted 2028 launch.”

fact_evidence: “International space-based intelligence subscription revenue grew 150% year-over-year, and multi-year international contracts now comprise over 80% of total funded backlog.”

fact_evidence: “Gen 3-related products and services are driving 90% of the company's growth, delivering 35-centimeter imagery at roughly one-fifth the cost of legacy platforms.”

fact_evidence: “The company raised $150 million through ATM offerings, boosting cash to $244.1 million … and total liquidity above $325 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “meaningful ATM issuance” and asked investors to watch “ATM usage to date, share count, and whether $50–60M capex is funded without further dilution.”

fact_evidence: “Record net revenue of $385 million in Q2 2026,” “above the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus net revenue of “$365.7M” and guidance of “$350–370M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

fact_evidence: “Comparable written sales surged 12.5% in Q2,” lifting year-to-date comparable written sales “to positive 2.8%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called written comps “the single most important number” and said they needed to be “at least flat-to-positive.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comparable delivered sales increased 4%, compared with Q2 guidance of -5% to flat. Deliveries were therefore materially better than the preview’s already cautious range.
fact_evidence: “Comparable delivered sales rose 4%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 comparable delivered guidance as “−5% to flat.”

fact_evidence: “Total refunds requested were $37.8 million and have since been fully received in cash”; the company recognized “a one-time $23.8 million benefit in cost of goods sold.”

expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$40–49M” and consensus of “~$44–46M.”

description: Management raised full-year net income and adjusted EBITDA guidance, rather than simply reaffirming the outlook assumed in the preview’s base case. Adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to $160–171 million from the preview’s cited $150–161 million range.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year net income guidance to $71–80 million and adjusted EBITDA to $160–171 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “FY reaffirmed unchanged”; it said a raised FY guide was required for its bull case. It cited FY adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$150–161M.”

description: The company disclosed about $10 million of higher shipping costs tied to Middle East disruption, an additional headwind beyond the tariff and fuel pressures discussed in the preview.
fact_evidence: The company faces “roughly $10 million in higher shipping costs tied to Middle East disruption.”

description: SG&A rose 16.1%, lifting its share of revenue by 230 basis points to 30.6%. The preview flagged possible eCommerce investment changes but did not anticipate this scale of reported expense growth and increased burden.
fact_evidence: “SG&A rose 16.1% to $118 million, increasing the SG&A load by 230 basis points to 30.6%,” including “roughly $3 million in strategic technology investments and $7.9 million higher selling expenses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “eCommerce investment gets re-based,” but gave no expected SG&A increase.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Client deposits ended the quarter up 11.8% year over year, a strong forward-demand signal that corroborated the written-sales rebound highlighted in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Client deposits ended the quarter up 11.8% year-over-year at approximately $264 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified client deposits as “the cleanest corroboration of a written-demand recovery” and cited $233.1 million in Q2 2025.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: A June delivery-fee increase is expected to generate $5–6 million in annual run-rate benefit, with virtually no customer pushback. The preview did not anticipate this pricing action or its expected contribution.
fact_evidence: A June delivery fee increase, “the first in 3–4 years,” is expected to add “$5–6 million in annual run-rate benefit with virtually no customer pushback,” beginning to flow through in Q3.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $5.8 million, far above the preview’s $0.5–2.0 million guidance range. That was a much stronger profit result than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $5.8 million (a 5% margin), far outperforming guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” Q2 FY26 guidance: “$0.5–2.0M.”

description: The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $13–15 million, well above the roughly $9–11 million implied by the prior outlook. The preview had highlighted the risk of a softened outlook, not an increase of this size.
fact_evidence: “Driving a raise in full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $13-$15 million.”
expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted EBITDA was described as “Profitable, slightly lower than 2025” and estimated at “~$9–11M”; the preview also said H2 EBITDA implied “~$12.4–14.4M.”

description: Q2 net sales of $115.1 million exceeded the expected $110–112 million range implied by guidance and the $111.4 million current consensus. The result was also above the high end of company guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales grew approximately 5.7% year-over-year to $115.1 million, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview translated guidance into “~$110–112M” and cited consensus of “$111.4M” (while noting a stale estimate of $115.7M).

description: Gross margin reached 57.9%, above the preview’s implied 55–57% range, and improved about 360 basis points sequentially—more than the preview’s 150-basis-point threshold for confirming recovery from Q1. The year-over-year decline was limited to about 40 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 57.9%, down about 40 basis points year-over-year but up roughly 360 basis points sequentially from Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview put gross margin at “~55–57% (implied)” and said to watch for “sequential GM improvement ≥150bps.”

description: Adjusted operating expenses showed leverage across all three categories, with total adjusted OpEx improving 250 basis points as a share of sales. Marketing leverage was 130 basis points, more than the 90 basis points cited in the preview as the Q1 comparison point.
fact_evidence: “Year-over-year operating expense leverage across all three adjusted categories,” with “marketing down 130 bps to 22.8% of sales and total adjusted OpEx improving 250 bps to 53%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “23.6% of sales in Q1 with 90bps of leverage” and asked for a bridge to H2 EBITDA.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AOV rose about 8% to roughly $2,238, accelerating from the 3.3% growth reported in Q1. The preview expected AOV durability but did not anticipate this degree of sequentially stronger year-over-year growth.
fact_evidence: “Average order value rose about 8% year-over-year to roughly $2,238.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 AOV was “$2,131 (+3.3%)” and noted that AOV growth had been driven by “price increases and customer mix.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Although total orders fell about 2%, orders excluding sub-$500 purchases rose 5%, and two-year stacked order growth was 16%. That indicates better underlying order momentum than the aggregate decline alone suggests, despite the preview’s concern that higher AOV could come with weakening unit demand.
fact_evidence: “Total orders declined about 2% year-over-year, but excluding sub-$500 orders (a few percent of sales), orders rose 5%, and two-year stacked order growth was 16%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned: “A quarter where AOV is up but orders are flat-to-down means price increases are now destroying units.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at about $75 million, roughly $16 million higher sequentially, rather than the preview’s expectation that the balance would likely be below the prior $58.6 million level after H1 working-capital use.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with about $75 million in cash and no debt, a sequential increase of roughly $16 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “H1 is a working-capital use of cash, so the Q2 balance is likely below $58.6M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings from showroom walk-ins without appointments grew 47% year-over-year, an operating-channel result the preview did not flag. This suggests stronger walk-in showroom demand than investors had been led to expect from the preview.
fact_evidence: “Showroom bookings from walk-in customers without appointments grew 47% year-over-year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The new Beverly Hills flagship generated over 40% higher bookings and about 10% higher AOVs than prior locations, a specific store-performance result not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The new Beverly Hills flagship delivered over 40% higher bookings and about 10% higher AOVs versus prior locations.”

description: Q2 revenue was $29.1 million, about 9% above the preview’s $26.6 million consensus (and above its $28.5 million bull-case threshold).
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $29.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue was “$26.6M”; the bull scenario called for “$28.5M+.”

description: Management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $104–108 million, exceeding the prior “at least $100M” guide and topping the preview’s $103.2 million consensus at the midpoint. The preview’s bull case anticipated a raise to $103–106 million, so the reported range was also somewhat higher than that scenario.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $104-108 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 revenue consensus of “$103.2M” versus guide of “at least $100M”; its bull case expected “FY guide raised to $103–106M.”

description: Gross margin substantially outperformed the preview’s roughly 85% Q2 expectation, reaching 90%; management also raised FY26 gross-margin guidance above the preview’s stated range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 90% versus 86% a year ago, with full-year guidance raised to 86-89%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 gross margin of “~85% (guide 84–87%)” and noted FY26 guidance of “84–87%” as the operative range.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $7.6 million, well above the preview’s base-case expectation of approximately breakeven, and the company continued to expect positive adjusted EBITDA for FY26.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA” was “$7.6 million in Q2 2026”; the company “expects positive adjusted EBITDA for the full year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “adj. EBITDA ~breakeven,” while its bear case was “adj. EBITDA clearly negative”; it also flagged the FY26 positive-EBITDA commitment as a key test.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: HEPZATO kit volume grew 30%, but revenue grew only 21% because 340B pricing reduced effective ASP from about $185,000 to $170,000–$173,000 per kit. The preview flagged volume versus price as something to watch but did not anticipate this specific pricing drag.
fact_evidence: “HEPZATO revenue grew 21% year-over-year but represented 30% volume growth,” with the gap “entire[ly] attributable to 340B pricing” that cut effective ASP from “~$185K to ~$170-173K per kit.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management disclosed that breast-cancer trial enrollment, like colorectal-cancer enrollment, is running below expectations because of training challenges. The preview already identified slow colorectal enrollment, but did not flag a similar enrollment problem in the breast trial.
fact_evidence: Management acknowledged “enrollment in both colorectal and breast cancer trials is running below expectations due to training challenges.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described colorectal enrollment as “slower than anticipated,” but said the breast-cancer Phase 2 had its “first patient dosed July 2026” and referenced “>20 sites.”

description: The company reported that it had already repurchased about $9 million of stock under its $25 million buyback program, a capital-allocation action the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $95.9 million in cash and investments, generated $5.7 million in operating cash flow, and has repurchased ~$9 million of stock under a $25 million buyback program.”

description: Excelerate raised and narrowed its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $490–515 million, rather than simply reaffirming $480–510 million. Both ends of the range moved higher, although the new range still overlaps the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Raised and narrowed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $490 million to $515 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 Adj. EBITDA (company guide): $480–510M”; the base case expected the guide to be “reaffirmed $480–510M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The FSRU Express received a firm seven-year Colombia charter with a projected 35% increase in its annual EBITDA contribution beginning in early 2027. The preview looked for redeployment economics but did not anticipate these specific commercial terms or quantified uplift.
fact_evidence: “The FSRU Express was recontracted to Colombia under a seven-year charter… expected to boost the vessel's annual EBITDA contribution by roughly 35% starting in early 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Express redeployment at ‘improved economics’” and said firm commercial terms could shift the conversation past Iraq.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Excelerate gave a more specific Iraq startup target—early Q2 2027—and reported a five-year take-or-pay contract with minimum offtake of 250 million standard cubic feet per day. That is more concrete than the preview’s general 2027 expectation, though the preview’s requested construction restart date was not provided.
fact_evidence: “Iraq LNG terminal operations are now expected to commence early in Q2 2027 under a five-year take-or-pay contract with a minimum contracted offtake of 250 million standard cubic feet per day.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the terminal had slipped “to 2027” and that investors “need a restart date, not a startup date”; it also cited a “60-month contract clock starting at operational startup.”

description: The selected FSRU conversion vessel pushed expected conversion capex above the previously communicated roughly $200 million, even though management said returns should remain in line with prior guidance. This is an unanticipated increase in the project’s capital requirement.
fact_evidence: “FSRU conversion capex is now expected to exceed the previously communicated ~$200 million due to the higher-capability vessel, though returns are expected to remain in line with prior guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the FSRU conversion” as part of the 2027–2028 bridge but gave no expectation of higher conversion capex.

description: Excelerate named and agreed to buy a specific LNG carrier for about $79 million as its FSRU conversion candidate, advancing the conversion beyond the preview’s general discussion of the project. Deployment is expected in early 2028.
fact_evidence: “The company agreed to purchase the LNG carrier Methane Patricia Camilla for approximately $79 million as its FSRU conversion candidate, with commercial deployment expected in early 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “the FSRU conversion” as a 2027–2028 bridge item but did not identify a vessel or purchase.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end net debt and leverage were higher than the preview’s figures: $898 million and 1.9x trailing leverage versus $714 million and 1.5x. The company nevertheless said leverage remained below its target range and reported substantial cash and revolver availability.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $342 million in cash, full $500 million revolver availability, net debt of $898 million, and trailing net leverage of 1.9 times, below its target range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Net debt was $714M at 1.5x trailing” and asked whether the dividend plus capex plan implied leverage drifting above 2x.

description: Revenue was $235.6 million, $4.1 million below the $239.7 million consensus, and fell 1.5% sequentially instead of the preview’s expected slight sequential increase. This was worse than the preview’s base range and crossed its ≤$236 million bear-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue declined 1.5% ($3.6 million) sequentially to $235.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus service revenue was “$239.7M”; the preview said Q2 was “the quarter where consolidated revenue should stop declining” and its base range was “$237.5–240M.”

description: The 2027 notes were not refinanced in the quarter; Cogent now plans to refinance them in Q3 with secured debt and indicated a cost near the 8.8%–8.9% yield on existing secured notes. That is less favorable than the preview’s upside case of a completed refinancing at 8% or less, although its base case allowed for a refinancing still in progress.
fact_evidence: “Cogent is refinancing its $750 million 2027 unsecured notes (now current) with secured debt in Q3 2026” and management indicated “a higher cost of capital near the 8.8%-8.9% yield on existing secured notes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether refinancing “has been executed, and at what coupon?” Its bull case assumed “2027 notes refinanced at ≤8%”; its base case said “refi in progress.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management acknowledged that Cogent is not generating positive free cash flow without T-Mobile subsidy payments, which end in under two years. The preview highlighted the payments and their eventual run-off, but did not state that the business would remain free-cash-flow negative without them.
fact_evidence: “Management acknowledged the business is not generating positive free cash flow excluding T-Mobile subsidy payments, which end in under two years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$25.0M/quarter T-Mobile IP transit payments” were “the entire gap” between unadjusted and adjusted EBITDA and that the payments “run off in late 2027.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $71.1 million, below the preview’s $72–74 million base range and the roughly $73 million implied estimate. Margin reached 30.2%, within the preview’s base-case range but well below the roughly 32% needed to stay on pace for more than 200 basis points of 2026 expansion; severance and integration wind-down costs weighed on the result.
fact_evidence: “EBITDA as adjusted rose only $0.9 million sequentially to $71.1 million, with margin up 90 basis points to 30.2%, dampened by severance and integration wind-down costs including a 6% (113-employee) workforce reduction.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$72–74M / 30.0–30.9%”; it said Q2 needed “roughly 32% (~$76–77M)” to average more than 200 basis points of margin expansion in 2026.

description: Wavelength revenue was $14.8 million, below the preview’s $15.0–15.5 million base case, though it landed at the preview’s stated $14.8 million threshold rather than below it. Connection growth, by contrast, was within the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: “Wavelength revenue grew 63.8% year-over-year and 9.2% sequentially to $14.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$15.0–15.5M”; it said “Below $14.8M” would confirm the bear thesis.

description: The Sprint Wireline revenue base had fallen further than the preview’s estimate, to $34 million per quarter versus roughly $39 million expected. Cogent Classic was slightly ahead of its expected run-rate at $200 million versus about $198 million, but had not offset the deeper Sprint decline.
fact_evidence: “The acquired Sprint Wireline revenue base has declined 71% since deal closing, from $118 million to $34 million per quarter, while Cogent Classic revenue grew 29% from $155 million to $200 million per quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said legacy Sprint was “down to ~$39M/quarter from $118M at close” and Cogent Classic’s run-rate was “$198M.”

description: Cogent repurchased $138.8 million of the principal on its 2032 secured notes below par, reducing the balance and realizing a gain. The preview expected deleveraging from the data-center sale proceeds but did not flag this specific debt repurchase.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $138.8 million par value of its 2032 secured notes at an average price of $90.348, realizing a cumulative $13.4 million gain, reducing the principal balance to $461.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the data-center sale proceeds would “accelerate deleveraging,” but did not mention repurchasing the 2032 notes.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage improved to 6.23x, below the preview’s 6.5x bull-case threshold after the data-center proceeds and T-Mobile payments. This was a better reported leverage outcome than the preview’s cited Q1 net-leverage figure suggested.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage as adjusted improved to 6.23x EBITDA from 6.79x last quarter and 6.61x in Q2 2025, aided by data center sale proceeds and T-Mobile payments.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 exit net leverage of “7.41x” and included “leverage <6.5x post-proceeds” in its bull case.

description: Capital spending fell substantially from Q1, and management guided to further sequential declines, easing the preview’s concern that another capex overshoot could create a liquidity problem.
fact_evidence: “CapEx fell 16.7% sequentially and 31.4% year-over-year to $38.5 million, with capital lease principal payments down 27.7% to $9.7 million, and management guiding to further sequential declines.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “another overshoot against ~$14.8M of operating cash flow is a liquidity problem” and identified capex discipline as a key issue.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The data-center sale produced a $130.7 million GAAP gain, a positive one-off result whose size and direction were not specified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company sold 10 former Sprint data centers in June for $225 million cash … generating a GAAP gain of $130.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the sale closed during Q2 and that “any book gain/loss land[s] in this print,” but did not forecast the gain’s amount or direction.

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $107 million, below the preview’s $118–$126 million estimate range, and fell year over year because of restatement costs. Excluding those costs, EBITDA rose 3.4%, so the reported shortfall was concentrated in the expected-but-costly accounting work.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell $7.9 million to $107 million due to restatement costs (though excluding those costs EBITDA rose 3.4%).”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$118–$126M (~23–24% margin) — author estimate”; the preview also cited “$15M+ in Q2” of restatement costs as guided.

description: Management kept the full-year guidance ranges, but indicated results would land near their low ends. The preview viewed a modest lift to the low end as the bullish outcome after Q1 and noted that an unchanged range could imply second-half risk.
fact_evidence: “Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance … but signaled results will land near the low end of the range.”
expectation_evidence: “Given Q1 came in ahead, a reiteration is the base case and a modest raise to the low end is the bull tell”; “Buy-side wants the low end lifted toward $440M+ after a Q1 beat.”

description: Restatement costs are tracking to the top end of the $35–$45 million annual range, and about $3 million shifted from Q2 into Q3. The annual total remains within the preview’s range, but the shift pushes some cost into Q3 despite the preview’s expectation of $15 million or more in Q2 and a lower run rate in the second half.
fact_evidence: “Restatement costs are now expected at the top end of the initial $35M–$45M range, with $20.9M incurred year-to-date and roughly $3M shifting from Q2 into Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “Restatement costs (P&L drag): $15M+ in Q2 (guided); $35–45M FY”; the preview said “2H has to drop toward ~$5–8M/quarter.”

description: Take 5’s same-store sales growth was close to the preview’s mid-3% expectation, but its EBITDA margin declined about 70 basis points as inflation and store operating expenses rose. The preview flagged unit-margin risk from promotions, but did not anticipate this specific cost-driven margin decline.
fact_evidence: “Take 5 delivered its 24th consecutive quarter of same-store sales growth … but its EBITDA margin declined about 70 basis points due to inflation and store operating expenses.”
expectation_evidence: “Take 5 SSS: ~+3.5% (management-guided ‘mid 3% range’)”; the preview also warned that promotional flexibility “hurts unit margin.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The customer groups that had been softening were described as stabilized, while remaining cohorts showed resilience in average check, premium mix, and attachment rates. That is better than the preview’s concern about continued softening and its description of stabilization as a bullish outcome to watch for.
fact_evidence: “Lower-income and newer customers continue to moderate but have stabilized, while remaining cohorts show resilience with rising average check, premium mix in the low 90s, and attachment rates in the high 50s.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “softening traffic and higher churn among newer and sub-$50K-income households” and said stabilization of the sub-$50K cohort would be a bull signal.

description: Management cited rising base-oil input costs tied to the Middle East conflict, made modest price increases at the end of Q2, and expects further pricing in the second half. The preview discussed inflation and price/mix generally but did not anticipate this specific input-cost shock and pricing response.
fact_evidence: “Rising base oil input costs from Middle East conflict prompted modest price increases at the end of Q2, with the company managing to gross margin dollars in the short term and expecting further pricing in the back half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to inflation as a factor in customer softness and discussed Take 5’s “price/mix,” but did not mention rising base-oil costs or planned price increases.

description: The board disclosed that it unanimously rejected activist ADW’s acquisition proposal, calling it highly conditional and significantly undervaluing the company. The preview did not anticipate an acquisition proposal or a board decision on one.
fact_evidence: “The board unanimously rejected activist ADW's acquisition proposal, calling it highly conditional and stating it significantly undervalued the company.”

description: Cognex gave a full-year outlook for the first time alongside Q2 and raised 2026 guidance to $1.13–$1.15 billion of revenue and $1.64–$1.68 of adjusted EPS. Management said visibility into the second half had improved, making this a substantial step-up from the prior target of exiting the year at a 25% EBITDA run rate, although it cautioned that visibility remains only 3–4 months.
fact_evidence: “raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.13-$1.15 billion (~15% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EPS of $1.64-$1.68 (~63% growth), well ahead of its prior target of a 25% EBITDA run rate exit”; “issued full-year guidance alongside Q2 results for the first time,” citing improved second-half visibility while noting “only 3-4 months of visibility.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q3 FY2026 revenue guidance — the single most important number” and framed the event around the Q3 guide; it did not anticipate a first-time full-year guide alongside Q2.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 32.2%, far above the preview’s roughly 29.5% implied consensus and above the company’s 28–31% guidance band. That was a much stronger margin result than the preview’s base case of 29.5–30.5%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 32.2%,” expanding 1,150 basis points year over year and “exceeding the guidance midpoint by more than 250 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. EBITDA margin ~29.5% (implied)” and forecast a base scenario of “29.5–30.5%,” against company guidance of 28–31%.

description: Adjusted EPS of $0.45 beat the preview’s $0.42 consensus estimate, though it was within the preview’s inferred $0.45–$0.46 whisper range. The result was also stronger year over year than the preview’s implied 68% growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 80% year-over-year to $0.45,” driven by roughly 100% revenue flow-through.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. diluted EPS $0.42” consensus and inferred a “whisper at ~$0.45–$0.46”; it also showed “+68%” implied year-over-year growth.

description: The full-year growth outlook improved across nearly all end markets: logistics was forecast at high-single-digit growth, while packaging, electronics, and semiconductor were forecast at double-digit growth. The preview expected logistics to normalize to mid-to-high single digits and described electronics and semiconductor as high-single-to-double-digit opportunities, so the broader upgrades—especially packaging—were better than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Full-year outlooks were raised across nearly all end markets: logistics to high single-digit, packaging to double-digit, electronics to double-digit, and semiconductor to double-digit growth, with automotive maintained at flat to low single-digit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said logistics was expected to “normalize to mid-to-high single digits” and described semiconductor and electronics outlooks as “high-single-to-double-digit.”

description: The Q3 memory-cost headwind was larger than the preview’s 50-basis-point estimate: management now expected roughly 75 basis points of gross-margin pressure in Q3, with some spillover into Q4. Management characterized it as a timing issue and expected pricing to fully offset it by 2027.
fact_evidence: “Rising memory prices are expected to create roughly 75 basis points of gross margin headwind in Q3 (with some spillover into Q4),” which management viewed as “a timing issue” it expects to “fully offset through pricing by 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “a 50bps gross-margin headwind in Q3 from memory-chip costs.”

description: China revenue grew 42% year over year in constant currency, a strong result in light of the preview’s concern that growth in China ex-automotive could decelerate. The comparison is not exact because the preview’s 36% figure was for China ex-auto in Q1, while the reported 42% was for China overall in Q2.
fact_evidence: “China was the fastest-growing region with revenue up 42% year-over-year in constant currency.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Greater China ex-automotive (+36% in Q1)” and said “a deceleration there would validate the bear concern.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management disclosed data center supply-chain revenue as a rapidly growing, early-stage platform, with growth above 30% year over year. Its current scale is still limited, at a low-single-digit percentage of total revenue, but the comparison to logistics a decade ago introduced a growth opportunity the preview had not identified.
fact_evidence: “Data center supply chain revenue represents a low single-digit percentage of total revenue but is growing more than 30% year-over-year,” and was described as “an early-stage growth platform similar to logistics a decade ago.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Cognex reported adding roughly 9,000 customers in 2025 and another 4,500 year to date in 2026. The preview discussed product opportunities and monetization but did not flag customer additions as a metric to watch, so this was new evidence of customer acquisition momentum rather than a beat against a stated target.
fact_evidence: “Cognex added ~9,000 new customers in 2025 and ~4,500 year-to-date in 2026.”

description: FA reported Q2 revenue of $449 million, up 15% year over year, versus the preview’s $415 million consensus and 6.3% implied growth. Even excluding the temporary customer initiatives, management estimated growth of 11%–12%, still well above the preview’s expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 15% year-over-year to $449 million”; excluding one-time customer initiative benefits, “Q2 total revenue growth was still 11% to 12%.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $415.0M” and “Implied Y/Y | +6.3%.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.35, substantially above the preview’s $0.29 consensus. The 30% year-over-year increase was also far stronger than the preview’s implied 5.6% growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 30% year-over-year to $0.35.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.29” and “Implied Y/Y | +5.6%.”

description: The preview expected base revenue to be flat to down 2%, but it grew 6.7%. The quality of that upside was qualified: roughly half came from episodic customer initiatives expected to normalize by Q4, leaving underlying base growth at about 3.3%.
fact_evidence: “Base revenue grew an exceptionally strong 6.7%, with roughly half attributed to episodic customer-driven volume initiatives expected to normalize by Q4,” implying “underlying base growth of about 3.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Management's FY26 assumption is 0% to -2%” for base revenue; base revenue “turned flat in Q1.”

expectation_evidence: “This is the first clean read on the decay curve without the marketing crutch. Sequential growth = bull case intact; a >15% sequential drop = the whole SuperPlay valuation narrative wobbles.”

description: Management disclosed that Super Play titles, including Disney Solitaire, are expected to decline sequentially in the second half, with Super Play marketing investment being cut roughly 70% versus the first half and the largest step-down in Q3. The preview focused on the immediate post-spend Disney trajectory and did not anticipate this explicit second-half revenue decline and steep investment reduction.
fact_evidence: “Super Play titles, including Disney Solitaire, will see revenue decline sequentially in the second half due to deliberately front-loaded user acquisition spend tied to the earnout structure”; “Overall Super Play marketing investment is being cut by roughly 70% in the second half versus the first half, with the largest step-down concentrated in Q3.”

description: Bingo Blitz weakened more than the preview’s already-negative outlook: revenue fell 9.5% year over year versus the preview’s cited 5.4% decline, and it also fell sequentially. Management attributed the weakness to players acquired in the last 12 months after shifting away from incentive-driven acquisition channels.
fact_evidence: “Bingo Blitz revenue fell to $145.1 million, down 5.6% sequentially and 9.5% year-over-year, with declines concentrated in players acquired in the last 12 months after a shift away from incentive-driven acquisition channels.”
expectation_evidence: “Bingo Blitz $153.7M (−5.4% YoY).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Audience metrics deteriorated more than the preview anticipated: DAU fell 9.1% year over year versus the preview’s expected 4.4% decline. Daily paying users also declined, though the preview did not give a specific expectation for that metric.
fact_evidence: “Average daily active users down 9.1% year-over-year to 8 million and daily paying users down 2.9% to 367,000.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ARPDAU rose substantially faster than the preview expected, increasing 16.1% year over year versus the preview’s cited 8.0% increase. This more than offset the expected level of monetization growth even as the audience contracted.
fact_evidence: “ARPDAU rose 16.1% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Shrinking-audience-squeezed-harder … 8.6M DAU (−4.4% YoY) monetized harder at $0.94 ARPDAU (+8.0%).”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management newly cited softening consumer sentiment and inflation pressure on discretionary spending, including a steeper-than-typical demand step-down from May to June. The preview discussed softer DTC traffic as a risk but did not flag this broader demand deterioration or the unusually sharp monthly step-down.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged softening consumer sentiment and inflation pressure on discretionary spending, observing a steeper-than-typical demand step-down from May to June.”

description: Q1 revenue was $265.7 million, well above the $249.7 million consensus estimate. The roughly $16 million beat was stronger than the preview’s expectation that the quarter’s headline print would be close to flat year over year.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue rose 6.5% to $265.7 million” and beat internal sales expectations.
expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 Consensus” revenue: “$249.7M”; the preview said the quarter’s print was “close to irrelevant” and consensus implied “~flat” year-over-year revenue.

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.98, above the preview’s $0.88–$0.89 consensus range. That also reversed the expected year-over-year decline, despite higher acquisition-financing interest expense.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased approximately 3% year-over-year to $0.98,” partly offset by higher interest expense from acquisition financing.
expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 Consensus” adjusted diluted EPS: “$0.88 (some feeds $0.89)” and implied “–7.5%” year-over-year.

description: Organic revenue growth was 3.2% excluding FX and Breathe Right, stronger than the preview’s base-case expectation of a decline and above its flat-to-modestly-negative hurdle. However, about 2 points came from retailer order timing, which management expects to reverse into a modest organic decline in Q2.
fact_evidence: “Organic growth of 3.2% excluding FX and the Breathe Right acquisition”; retailer order timing “added about 2 points of growth in Q1 and is expected to reverse in Q2,” prompting guidance for “a modest organic revenue decline” in Q2.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Organic –2% to –4%”; it said Q1 needed to be “at least flat-to-modestly-negative” to support the full-year outlook.

description: Q1 adjusted gross margin was 55%, above the preview’s approximate 52%–54% range and with less year-over-year compression than its expected 250–350 basis points. Management still reported a 120-basis-point decline, citing transportation costs and mix.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 55% in Q1 (down 120 basis points year-over-year on higher transportation costs and mix).”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 gross margin at “~52–54%” and expected “–250 to –350 bps” year-over-year.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarterly adjusted free cash flow reached a record $83.7 million, contrary to the preview’s expectation that it would likely be down because of interest and deal costs. Management attributed much of the result to favorable working-capital timing, so the record may not represent a recurring run rate.
fact_evidence: “Quarterly record adjusted free cash flow of $83.7 million, largely driven by favorable working capital timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said free cash flow was “Likely down on interest + deal costs.”

description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $4.55–$4.65 was below the preview’s pro forma bridge of roughly $4.60–$4.75, especially at the top end. The guidance was raised, but its range leaves less earnings upside than the preview modeled.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2027… adjusted EPS [guidance was raised] to $4.55-$4.65.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s pro forma FY27 bridge estimated “~$4.60–4.75”; its base scenario expected “$4.60–4.72.”

description: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance rose to at least $270 million, above the May guidance of at least $250 million. This was a favorable increase against the prior outlook, even though the preview had warned that near-term cash flow could be pressured.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to at least $270 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave May FY27 guidance as “FCF ≥$250M.”

description: The preview expected Q2 revenue of about $505.5–506.3 million. Adding continuing-operations revenue of $442 million and TheFork's $61 million of discontinued-operations revenue gives $503 million, a small miss against that expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 continuing operations revenue was $442 million”; “TheFork (now discontinued operations) contributed $61 million revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $505.5–506.3M.”

description: The preview put adjusted EBITDA at about $80–82 million. The reported $76 million from continuing operations plus $11 million from TheFork totals $87 million, above that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 continuing operations revenue was $442 million with adjusted EBITDA of $76 million, while TheFork (now discontinued operations) contributed $61 million revenue and $11 million adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$80–82M (implied).”

description: The preview expected Hotels & Other revenue to decline 21–24%, implying roughly $156–162 million. It came in at $163 million, slightly better than the top of that range, while its 28% adjusted EBITDA margin remained strong.
fact_evidence: “The Hotels & Other segment revenue declined 21% to $163 million, though it remained highly profitable at 28% adjusted EBITDA margin, down only about 100 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “Hotels & Other — still the profit engine — is guided to shrink 21–24%.”

description: For Q3, Experiences bookings are guided to grow 5–7%, but revenue is guided from down 2% to up 1%. That leaves a bookings-to-revenue gap wider than the roughly 3-point spread the preview treated as the expected case, even allowing for about 1 point of currency headwind.
fact_evidence: “Q3 Experiences guidance projects 5% to 7% bookings growth but revenue of -2% to +1% (including ~1 point of currency headwind).”
expectation_evidence: “Guidance implies bookings growing ~3pts faster than revenue, blamed on higher cancellations. If that gap holds at ~3pts, it's a macro story. If it widens, it's a structural take-rate story.”

description: The preview framed FY26 as approximately flat in revenue and expected investors to look for that framing to be reaffirmed. The new Q3 outlook instead calls for continuing-operations revenue to fall 7–10% and describes the second-half outlook as more prudent, a more cautious trajectory than the preview's flat-year framing.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for continuing operations revenue declines of 7% to 10% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 17% to 20%, reflecting a more prudent second-half outlook.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: ‘approximately flat revenue, approximately flat adj. EBITDA margin.’”

description: Experiences adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 11%, down 290 basis points, as channel mix shifted toward free channels. The preview highlighted the question of whether cost reductions could offset mix decay; the segment's margin contraction shows that mix pressure was substantial.
fact_evidence: “Experiences segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $31 million (11% of revenue), down 290 basis points, due to a free/paid channel mix shift across Viator and Tripadvisor points of sale.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch whether cost-out is offsetting mix decay or merely masking it.”

description: The preview described $700 million as inbound cash from TheFork; the company now expects approximately $680 million in net proceeds. The deal remains expected to close before year-end, but expected net cash is below the headline transaction value.
fact_evidence: “Tripadvisor agreed to sell TheFork to American Express for $700 million, expecting approximately $680 million in net proceeds”; closing is “anticipated before year-end.”
expectation_evidence: “TheFork ($700M cash to American Express)” and “$700M of inbound cash.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: VAC’s Q2 contract sales were far above the preview’s roughly $470 million estimate and +4% to +8% company guide: sales rose 22% to $545 million. The result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case marker of $481 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 contract sales rose 22% year-over-year to $545 million,” exceeding the high end of guidance.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Consolidated contract sales ~$470M” and cited company guidance of “+4% to +8% ($463–481M).” Its bull case was “$481M+ (+8%+).”

description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised substantially, rather than merely reaffirmed or narrowed toward the upper half as the preview hoped. The new $805–830 million range is $50 million above the prior range and implies a stronger H2 than the preview’s already demanding ramp.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by $50 million to $805-830 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$755–780M” and said the buy side wanted it “narrowed to the upper half or raised”; its base case was “reaffirmed,” while its bull case was “narrowed to the upper half or raised.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Q2 VPG result greatly exceeded the preview’s expectation of a mid-to-high-single-digit increase and its view that VPG might decelerate from April while remaining positive. VPG instead rose 23% and exceeded the high end of guidance.
fact_evidence: Contract sales were driven by “industry-leading VPGs of $4,477 (up 23%), exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed VPG as “Up mid-to-high single digits” and said its base case was that “VPG decelerates from April’s +12.7% but stays positive.”

description: Management described unusually strong monthly momentum: May and June were the company’s two highest sales months on record, and July growth stayed near 29%. That was much stronger than the preview’s concern that momentum might roll over after April, particularly given HGV’s late-quarter weakness.
fact_evidence: “May and June were the two highest sales months in company history,” and “July trends continued at roughly 29% growth, consistent with May/June.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide leaned on momentum with only April in hand, asked whether “June held,” and highlighted HGV’s report that sales execution “fell short in the back half of the quarter.” Its base case expected VPG to “decelerate from April’s +12.7%.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA beat both the preview’s guide-midpoint estimate and the top of the company’s prior range. The $215 million result was $20 million above the midpoint of guidance.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 6% to $215 million, coming in $20 million above the midpoint of Q2 guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA at “~$194M (guide midpoint)” and cited company guidance of “$187–202M.”

description: Full-year contract sales growth guidance was lifted to 18%–20%, with management indicating 25%–29% growth in the second half. The preview focused on the existing Q2 guide and H2 EBITDA ramp, but did not anticipate this substantially higher full-year sales outlook.
fact_evidence: Management “lifted contract sales growth guidance to 18-20%, implying 25-29% growth in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 contract sales guidance of “+4% to +8%” and discussed the H2 EBITDA ramp, but gave no comparable full-year contract-sales growth outlook.

description: The full-year adjusted free cash flow range rose to $410–460 million, a $35 million increase at the midpoint. The preview’s existing reference point was $375–425 million, although it did expect H1 cash flow above roughly $200 million to keep the story intact.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date adjusted free cash flow reached $201 million versus just $22 million in the prior-year period,” and full-year guidance was raised to “$410-460 million (a $35 million midpoint increase).”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited the “$375–425M FY guide” and said “H1 FCF tracking above ~$200M keeps the story intact”; its bull case anticipated a guide raised “above $425M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Owner sales and owner VPG were exceptionally strong, with owner contract sales growing faster than the already-surprising companywide result. The preview did not set an owner-sales or owner-VPG expectation.
fact_evidence: “Owner contract sales surged 41% year-over-year, fueled by a 33% lift in owner VPG.”

description: VAC provided a much larger quantified scale-up for its Inner Circle events than the preview had available: the platform is expected to grow from about 50 events in 2026 to 1,000 in 2027, with VPGs well above average. The preview had asked for quantified proof points from the initiative but did not anticipate this scale or performance detail.
fact_evidence: “The Inner Circle event platform is scaling aggressively from about 50 events in 2026 to a targeted 1,000 events in 2027,” with events “generating VPGs well above average.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “quantified early reads” on the modernization initiatives, including Inner Circle, and said investors needed “package sales, tour flow generated, conversion,” not adjectives.

description: Management signaled openness to opportunistic share repurchases once leverage falls into the upper 3s. The preview highlighted capital returns and buyback pace as a watch point, but did not have this specific conditional buyback signal.
fact_evidence: Net corporate debt was $3.1 billion and leverage fell to “~4x from 4.2x”; management signaled “openness to opportunistic share repurchases as leverage drops into the upper 3s.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Buyback pace … leverage trajectory” as a key item to watch, but did not describe a specific repurchase trigger or management commitment.

description: Adjusted core EPS was $1.19, well above the preview’s central estimate of about $0.90 (and above the cited alternative estimate of $1.11). That is a positive reversal from the preview’s expected 22% year-over-year decline.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted core EPS increased 3% to $1.19.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS — adjusted core: ~$0.90 (some feeds $1.11)” and “Implied Δ: –22% YoY.”

description: Reported diluted EPS was only $0.09, far below the preview’s derived estimate of $0.50–$0.65. The call attributed the gap to $23 million of charges and operating costs tied to legacy fraudulent problem loans.
fact_evidence: “Reported diluted EPS was only $0.09 due to $23 million of charges and operating costs tied to legacy fraudulent problem loans.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS — GAAP diluted: not cleanly published; my est. $0.50–0.65.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Transaction volume reached $14.4 billion, below the preview’s $15.5–$16.5 billion estimate and representing just 3% year-over-year growth rather than the preview’s implied 11–18%. Financing volume grew, but that did not prevent the overall shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 transaction volume rose 3% year-over-year to $14.4 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Transaction volume … my est. $15.5–16.5B” and “Implied Δ: +11–18% YoY.”

description: Management said the core business would land toward the lower end of original guidance if current market conditions persist, rather than offering the confident, on-track outlook the preview expected in its base case. The outcome could be higher if conditions improve, so this was a conditional caution rather than a stated guidance cut.
fact_evidence: “The core business would land toward the lower end of original guidance if current market conditions persist, or middle-to-upper range if conditions improve.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as the guide being “on track” and the bull case as “FY guide reaffirmed with confidence.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The legacy Fannie Mae review is expected to produce another $12–$16 million of credit-related charges in Q3, despite management saying no further loan repurchases are anticipated from either GSE. The additional charges are a negative departure from the preview’s no-new-charges bull-case catalyst, while the expected end of repurchases is a favorable part of the update.
fact_evidence: “An additional $12 million to $16 million in credit-related charges in Q3 2026 to finalize Fannie Mae's review, with no further loan repurchases anticipated from either GSE.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “repurchase exposure ≤$165M with zero new charges” as a catalyst and said any new disclosure could reset the trust discount.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending volume fell 10% in the quarter even though the preview emphasized expanded GSE lending capacity as a source of volume runway. The year-to-date share gain to nearly 15% is a counterpoint, but the quarterly volume decline was weaker than that constructive capacity backdrop suggested.
fact_evidence: “Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending volumes fell 10% in the quarter against a strong prior-year comparison, though year-to-date GSE market share climbed 350 basis points to nearly 15%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the 2026 caps provided a “volume runway” and highlighted that “the volume runway exists if WD can take it.”

description: Viatris beat the Q2 revenue consensus by about 3%, while adjusted EPS of $0.69 was about 11% above consensus; adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion also topped the preview’s $1.00–$1.05 billion estimate. The profitability beat was especially strong relative to those expectations.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues of $3.8 billion … adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion, and adjusted EPS of $0.69, all exceeding expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … $3.68B”; “Adjusted EPS … $0.62”; “Adjusted EBITDA ~$1.00–1.05B (my est., not published consensus).”

description: Greater China growth came in much stronger than the preview’s expected slowdown: sales grew 16% year over year versus the preview’s 7.3% estimate, with e-commerce up 36%.
fact_evidence: “Greater China net sales grew 16% year-over-year with e-commerce sales up 36%.”
expectation_evidence: The segment table put Greater China at “$631.7M” and “+7.3%” year over year, and said “Street models a big slowdown.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview expected management to reiterate no policy change this year, but the call flagged a hospital-channel procurement policy change that is expected to moderate Greater China growth in the second half. This adds a newly identified headwind to the strong current-quarter performance.
fact_evidence: Management “expects growth to moderate in the second half due to a hospital-channel procurement policy change.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to listen for “reiteration of Le Goff’s ‘no policy change this year’ (VBP) call.”

description: The Nashik facility fire and May FDA inspection are expected to cost $100–$150 million of second-half revenue, a supply disruption not identified in the preview. The impact is limited to low-margin generics, with no single affected product above $20 million.
fact_evidence: “Supply disruptions from the Nashik facility fire and May 2026 FDA inspection are expected to reduce second-half revenues by $100 million to $150 million, primarily affecting low-margin generics with no single impacted product exceeding $20 million.”

description: Adjusted gross margin reached 57.5%, improving by nearly a percentage point, against the preview’s 56.0% Q1 reference point. The preview flagged margin quality as a key watch item but did not forecast this improvement.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin improved nearly 1 percentage point to 57.5%, driven by strong Greater China performance and favorable North American generics product mix.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adjusted gross margin vs. 56.0% (Q1)” as a metric to watch.

description: Management gave a new, favorable outlook for fast-acting meloxicam: FDA approval is expected by year-end and peak sales could reach $500 million. The preview discussed new-product revenue and Gwyn Lo, but did not flag this product’s approval timing or sales potential.
fact_evidence: “Fast-acting meloxicam is expected to gain FDA approval by year-end and is projected to reach up to $500 million in peak sales,” with opioid-sparing labeling negotiations beginning in October–November.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management said selatogrel could still be commercially acceptable with a 10%–15% benefit, even though the Phase III study is powered to detect a 20% risk reduction. This is new framing that may lower the efficacy bar for commercial viability, while also highlighting that the study could deliver a smaller benefit than its design targets.
fact_evidence: “The selatogrel Phase III SOS study is powered for a 20% risk reduction but management believes a 10-15% benefit would be commercially acceptable,” with a readout expected in the first half of 2027.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Both cenerimod Phase III SLE studies enrolled more than 70% interferon-1 high patients, exceeding the target, an encouraging trial-enrollment update not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Both Phase III cenerimod SLE studies enrolled over 70% interferon-1 high patients (exceeding target), with top-line results expected in early 2027.”

description: Viatris disclosed that it divested its Tirva eye-care rights, a portfolio change not discussed in the preview; the facts provided do not indicate the financial terms or rationale.
fact_evidence: “The company divested its Tirva eye-care rights.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The FDA approved Viatris’s Winland contraceptive patch, a product approval not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “[The company] received FDA approval for the Winland contraceptive patch.”

description: CARS’ adjusted EBITDA margin reached 29.4%, above both the 28.0–29.0% company range and the preview’s roughly 28.5% consensus expectation. Adjusted EBITDA was $53 million, also above the preview’s roughly $51.5 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded nearly 100 basis points to 29.4%, outperforming the high end of guidance for the second consecutive quarter, with adjusted EBITDA of $53 million up 4% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~28.5% (implied)” and “Company Guide (set May 7) 28.0–29.0%”; “Adj. EBITDA ~$51.5M (implied).”

description: The Q3 margin range of 28.5–29.5% is below the roughly 30–31% H2 pace the preview said was needed to achieve the reaffirmed full-year 29–30% margin guidance. The full-year guide was held, but the near-term range leaves the back-half ramp unresolved.
fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of flat to 2% revenue growth and 29% to 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, with Q3 revenue guided flat to up 2% and Q3 margin of 28.5% to 29.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “To hit the FY 29–30% guide, H2 margins need to run ~30–31%” and “The back-half ramp is the single biggest credibility question on this print.”

description: OEM and national revenue fell 18%, substantially steeper than the preview’s base expectation of an 8–12% decline and worse than the prior-quarter decline. That is a sharper Q2 drop than the preview’s expected trough scenario suggested, even though total revenue remained in guidance.
fact_evidence: “3% dealer revenue growth offsetting an 18% decline in OEM and national revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified OEM & National revenue as “−12% Y/Y” in Q1, said management called Q2 “the trough,” and gave a base case of “OEM/National −8–12%.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.51 exceeded the preview’s $0.49 consensus estimate. The beat was positive but relatively small.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased to $0.51 from $0.41.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.49.”

description: Marketplace revenue grew more than 7%, and marketplace subscribers reached their highest level since 2023. That is stronger evidence of marketplace growth than the preview’s concern that another sequential dealer-count decline could undermine the subscription-growth thesis.
fact_evidence: “Marketplace revenue grew over 7% year-over-year, the fastest growth rate in the company's public history outside of 2021's pandemic recovery, with marketplace subscribers hitting their highest level since 2023.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a second sequential decline turns ‘intentional pruning’ into ‘churn,’ and the bull case on marketplace subscription growth breaks,” with dealer count expected around 19,390 sequentially in its base case.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: ARPD reached $2,500, a record for marketplace-only ARPD, slightly above the preview’s base-case estimate of about $2,480 and providing evidence that package bundling is raising monetization.
fact_evidence: “Q2 ARPD was $2,500, up 3% year-over-year and 1% sequentially, setting a new record for marketplace-only ARPD driven by Premium Plus.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “ARPD ~$2,480”; it also said “ARPD > $2,500 would be the first hard evidence the bundle is monetizing.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Website units declined, and management described a product-innovation turnaround that will take 2–3 quarters, with renewed website growth not expected until 2027. The preview focused on declining traffic but did not flag this product-led recovery timeline.
fact_evidence: “Website (DI) units declined year-over-year, with management signaling a 2-3 quarter product-innovation turnaround plan and expecting renewed website growth in 2027.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Despite lower traffic and unique visitors, lead conversion rose by double digits and performance-marketing cost per lead improved. That is a more favorable efficiency result than the preview’s emphasis on persistent traffic declines as a structural concern.
fact_evidence: “Website traffic and unique visitors declined year-over-year due to an intentional shift away from low-converting traffic, while Q2 lead conversion rose double digits and performance marketing cost per lead improved.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted traffic declines as “the structural bear thesis” and called for watching “Persistent double-digit UV decline.”

description: Allstate reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $8.99, far above the preview’s tradeable expectation of roughly $5.75–$5.85. The gap was about 54%–56%, substantially larger than the preview’s base-case EPS of about $6.40.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted net income was $2.3 billion or $8.99 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat $5.75–5.85 as the tradeable bar”; the preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS ~ $6.40.”

description: Property-Liability profitability was substantially better than the preview’s base case: the reported combined ratio was 86.6% versus a modeled base of about 92.0%. The underlying loss ratio improved 1.1 points, while a 1-point higher expense ratio partly offset that improvement.
fact_evidence: “The Property-Liability combined ratio improved 4.5 points to 86.6%,” with “1.1 points of underlying loss ratio improvement,” partly offset by “a 1-point higher expense ratio.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario forecast a “Reported P-L CR ~92.0” and an underlying CR of “~81.0”; the preview said “At or below ~80 is a clean beat; 82+ confirms the margin-rollover thesis.”
