description: Nine reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million, below the $10–15 million guidance range and well below the preview’s $12.5 million base estimate. Management attributed the shortfall to coiled tubing margin compression.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million fell below original guidance, driven by coiled tubing margin compression.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” guidance of “$10.0–15.0M” and a “$12.5M” base estimate; the preview also said “EBITDA below $10M cannot be” excused.

description: Coiled tubing costs rose about 12% quarter-over-quarter, and price increases did not fully offset the inflation. That left margins compressed, contrary to the preview’s upside case that price increases would stick.
fact_evidence: “Coiled tubing costs including consumables, labor, and repairs rose about 12% quarter-over-quarter, and price increases failed to fully offset the inflation, causing margin compression.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case required that “first price increases stick,” and its pricing checklist asked whether “anything actually” stuck.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Two large-diameter coiled tubing units—about 17% of that fleet—were taken out of service for maintenance, with one not expected back until near year-end. The preview identified coiled tubing rate erosion as a risk but did not anticipate this equipment outage.
fact_evidence: “Two large-diameter coiled tubing units (about 17% of the large-diameter fleet) went out of service on maintenance issues,” and the second is “not expected to return until near year-end.”

description: The Q3 outlook was weaker than the preview’s base case: revenue guidance of $133–143 million is centered below Q2 revenue, and adjusted EBITDA is expected to be flat to modestly down rather than flat to modestly up.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $133 million to $143 million, with adjusted EBITDA expected to be flat to modestly down versus Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 guide flat to modestly up.”

description: Completion tools substantially outperformed the preview’s estimate: revenue reached $37.1 million, up 44% quarter-over-quarter, versus an estimated $29.0 million and 12% growth. The reported drivers were a 45% increase in stages, strong international sales, and domestic share gains.
fact_evidence: “Completion tools revenue surged 44% quarter-over-quarter to $37.1 million on a 45% increase in stages, boosted by strong international sales and domestic market share gains.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated completion tools revenue of “~$29.0M” and “+12%.”

description: Wireline missed the expected weather-driven rebound: revenue was $23 million, down 4% quarter-over-quarter, versus the preview’s $27.5 million estimate and 15% expected growth.
fact_evidence: “Wireline revenue declined 4% to $23 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated wireline at “~$27.5M” and “+15%,” calling it the “largest weather snapback.”

description: Coiled tubing revenue fell 2% to $26.4 million instead of the expected 2% increase. Days worked rose 16%, but the day rate fell 15%, indicating a sharper rate decline than the preview’s modest-growth estimate implied.
fact_evidence: “Coiled tubing days worked rise 16% but day rate fall 15% (revenue down 2% to $26.4 million).”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated coiled tubing revenue of “~$27.5M” and “+2%,” while noting Q1 day rates were down 18%.

description: Cementing grew more slowly than forecast: revenue rose 3% to $55.3 million, rather than reaching the preview’s $56.5 million estimate and 6% growth.
fact_evidence: “Cementing revenue grew 3% to $55.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated cementing revenue of “~$56.5M” and “+6%.”

description: The company now expects full-year CapEx toward the middle-to-lower end of its $20–30 million range and said this supports cash flow neutrality in the second half. That is more reassuring than the preview’s concern that back-half-weighted spending could pressure H2 cash flow.
fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance of $20 million to $30 million was reaffirmed but now expected in the middle-to-lower end, supporting cash flow neutrality in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “back-half weighted spend could pressure H2 FCF.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.29, above the preview’s $0.26–$0.27 consensus estimates and $0.28 base estimate, though it reached the preview’s stated buy-side whisper range. The result was a modest beat against the base estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 12% to $0.29.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.26” and “$0.27” consensus; “My estimates (base) … Adj. EPS $0.28”; “buy-side whisper is realistically … $0.28–0.29 adj. EPS.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA of $59.4 million came in below the preview’s estimated $60–$62 million range and $62 million base estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA up 6% to $59.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$60–62M”; “My estimates (base) … Adj. EBITDA $62M.”

description: Management maintained full-year guidance, but said revenue should land at the high end while gross profit and adjusted EBITDA should land at the low end because of margin pressure. That was weaker than the preview’s expectation of at least a midpoint nudge or, in its base case, reaffirmation with language that results were tracking to the upper half.
fact_evidence: “The company maintained full-year guidance but expects revenue at the higher end ($1.01-$1.04 billion range) while gross profit ($405-425M) and adjusted EBITDA ($230-245M) will land at the lower end due to margin pressure.”
expectation_evidence: “The market is positioned for at least a midpoint nudge”; the base scenario expected “FY26 guide reaffirmed with ‘tracking to upper half’ language.”

description: Payables revenue growth was 21.6%, below the preview’s view that growth above roughly 25% would be a clean beat. It was not the mid-teens slowdown the preview identified as a concern, but it fell short of the expected stronger growth.
fact_evidence: “Payables revenue grew 21.6% to $30.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything above ~25% is a clean beat; a step down to mid-teens reframes Q1 as a pull-forward.”

description: Payables’ faster growth came with a sharp deterioration in profitability: adjusted gross profit fell and margin contracted 760 basis points as lower-margin buyer-funded revenue became dominant and was booked gross. The preview expected Payables growth to be a strong contributor and said management had flagged no one-time items, but did not anticipate this margin effect.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross profit fell 10.4% and margins dropped 760 basis points to 21.4% as buyer-funded revenue (up 26.3%) now dominates and is booked on a gross basis at lower margins.”
expectation_evidence: “+35.6% to $32.4M in Q1 with adj. EBITDA +55%, driven by enterprise customers using it as a working-capital substitute for revolvers. Management flagged no one-time items.”

description: Treasury Solutions revenue grew 14.9%, in line with the preview’s mid-teens expectation, but its margin fell about 590 basis points. The preview described Treasury as the profit engine with roughly 89.8% Q1 adjusted gross margin and anticipated that the rate headwind was mainly a comparison issue, not this degree of mix-driven compression.
fact_evidence: “Treasury Solutions revenue grew 14.9% to $60.5 million, but gross margins compressed roughly 590 basis points to 88.5% due to mix shift from Passport (up 125%) and Priority Tech Ventures (up nearly 400%), which run at only 30-40% margins.”
expectation_evidence: “It grew 17.5% in Q1 despite 75bp of Y/Y Fed cuts compressing float income”; “the rate headwind is now purely a comp issue that rolls off in Q4”; “If balances hold ~$1.9B and growth stays mid-teens.”

description: Merchant Solutions grew faster than its recent pace and its adjusted gross profit and margin improved, countering the preview’s concern that organic growth might stall. Revenue growth was 7.7% overall and 4.5% organically, versus Q1 growth of 6.7% and 3.9% organic.
fact_evidence: “Merchant Solutions revenue rose 7.7% to $175.8 million (4.5% organic), with adjusted gross profit up 12.4% to $39.8 million and margins improving over 100 basis points to 22.7%, aided by acquisitions.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 revenue +6.7% (only +3.9% organic)”; the preview flagged “Merchant Solutions card volume (the deceleration risk)” and said volume below about 2% would confirm the organic engine was stalling.

description: Recently enacted Mastercard and Visa interchange increases added cost of goods sold, creating an additional margin headwind alongside the lower-margin gross-basis Payables mix. The preview did not flag these price increases.
fact_evidence: “Recently enacted Mastercard and Visa interchange price increases raised cost of goods sold, creating a margin ‘double whammy’ alongside the gross-revenue accounting on growing buyer-funded payables.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net leverage improved to 3.8x from 4.0x in Q1, reaching the preview’s highlighted threshold for a potential deleveraging catalyst. The preview also flagged buyback activity as a possible catalyst, but the provided call facts do not report any buyback.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved to 3.8x at quarter-end from 4.0x in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “A print at ≤3.8x plus visible buyback under the $40M authorization is the de-rating catalyst.”

description: Management declined to comment on the ongoing special committee evaluation of a take-private proposal, leaving the matter unresolved. The preview did not mention the proposal or identify it as an overhang.
fact_evidence: “Management declined to comment on the ongoing special committee evaluation of a take-private proposal, which analysts noted is a key overhang preventing share movement despite solid fundamentals.”

description: REPX raised full-year oil production guidance by 2% to a midpoint of 23,000 barrels per day, above the preview’s 22,000–23,000 range. The roughly 30% year-over-year growth was already expected, but the higher midpoint was not.
fact_evidence: “Full year oil production guidance was raised 2% to 23,000 barrels per day at the midpoint.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The Targa pipeline, which the preview expected to begin commercial operations in Q3, is now expected in early Q4. The delay also means drilling and completion activity is shifting from Texas to New Mexico, with DUCs carrying into next year.
fact_evidence: “The Targa high-pressure gathering pipeline is expected in service early Q4 2026,” and a “1.2 drilled-to-turned-in-line ratio” is “carrying DUCs into next year.”
expectation_evidence: “Targa high-pressure trunk line timing (New Mexico) — guided to Q3 commercial operations with 20+ drilled-but-uncompleted wells waiting on it.”

description: Full-year CapEx guidance rose to $236 million, above the preview’s $200–220 million range and 12% above the prior guidance. About two-thirds of the new total is for infrastructure, making this a substantial increase over the expected spending level.
fact_evidence: “Full year CapEx guidance was raised 12% (or $26 million) to $236 million, with roughly one-third tied to upstream activity and two-thirds to infrastructure.”
expectation_evidence: “capex $200–220M ($210M mid).” The preview also said “a second FY capex raise … would be poorly received.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was $6 million, below the preview’s base-case estimate of $10–20 million. Operating cash flow rose, but cash CapEx jumped sharply to $73 million and absorbed most of it.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow rose 35% quarter-over-quarter to $64 million, but cash CapEx jumped 153% to $73 million, cutting Q2 free cash flow to just $6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FCF ~$10–20M”; it also said Q2 FCF “could compress toward breakeven.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Instead of reducing debt as the preview said management prioritized, REPX drew on its credit facility and principal debt increased by $26 million to $273 million. Leverage stayed around 1.0x, but the debt balance moved in the opposite direction from the expected paydown.
fact_evidence: “Principal debt increased 11% (or $26 million) to $273 million as the company drew on its credit facility, keeping leverage around 1.0x.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the majority of excess FCF post-dividend goes to debt reduction from $247M” and flagged the “debt trajectory from $247M / 1.0x.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: April and May midstream constraints forced temporary well shut-ins that reduced Q2 oil production by about 2,000 barrels per day. The preview focused on the Q2 production range and the future Targa line, but did not anticipate this specific production interruption.
fact_evidence: “Midstream constraints during April and May forced temporary well shut-ins that reduced Q2 oil production by approximately 2,000 barrels per day.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Silverback production is now about twice the buy-side case projection even though no new wells have been drilled, and per-well workover costs have fallen about 59%. This substantially exceeds the projection cited on the call and indicates better production and workover economics than that case assumed.
fact_evidence: “The Silverback acquisition's production is now approximately double the buy-side case projection with no new wells drilled, and per-well workover costs fell about 59%.”
expectation_evidence: The call described the comparison as “double the buy-side case projection.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: A relatively small, intentional workover spend produced a notable increment of oil from low-decline wells: about $2.3 million added roughly 700 barrels per day. The preview did not flag this production contribution or its cost.
fact_evidence: “Roughly $2.3 million of intentional workover spend added about 700 barrels of oil per day of incremental production from low-decline wells.”

description: Tennant’s adjusted diluted EPS was $0.83, well below the preview’s $1.33–$1.34 consensus, and adjusted EBITDA was $35.3 million versus the preview’s estimated $47–49 million. The shortfall was much larger than the preview’s expected modest year-over-year declines.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $35.3 million (10.9% of sales) … and adjusted diluted EPS dropped to $0.83,” with roughly half the shortfall from gross margin and half from higher operating expenses.
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS Consensus: $1.33–$1.34”; “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$47–49M (derived).”

description: Instead of reaffirming the existing full-year guidance as the preview’s base case anticipated, Tennant raised its sales range but cut profitability guidance: adjusted EPS fell to $3.80–$4.45 from $4.70–$5.30, and adjusted EBITDA to $155–$170 million from $175–$190 million. The sales increase alongside the profit cuts signals stronger demand but materially weaker expected profitability.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year net sales guidance to $1.27–1.31 billion but cut adjusted EBITDA guidance to $155–170 million and adjusted EPS to $3.80–4.45 (down from prior $4.70–5.30).”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year guidance treatment. Reaffirm, narrow, raise, or cut”; the base case expected “FY guide reaffirmed unchanged,” and the preview called a guidance raise “unlikely.”

description: Gross margin reached 39.5%, below the preview’s 40% expectation, and the recovery outlook is slower than the preview’s anticipated low-40s second half: management expects Q3 to remain flat near 39.5% before reaching roughly 41% in Q4.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 39.5%, down 260 basis points year-over-year but up 140 basis points sequentially,” with Q3 expected “to stay flat near 39.5% before improving to roughly 41% in Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ≥40%”; the preview also expected “low 40s” for the second half and said to look for “visible sequential gain through the quarter.”

description: Net sales were $324 million, missing the preview’s $329.55 million consensus and its $328–$332 million base-case range. North American parts shortages constrained shipments despite stronger orders.
fact_evidence: “Net sales grew only 1.7% to $324 million as North American parts shortages constrained shipments.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales Q2 FY26 Consensus: $329.55M”; the base case expected “~$328–332M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Orders and backlog built more strongly than the preview’s expected backlog-conversion story: orders rose 6.6% year over year and backlog reached $127 million, rather than drawing down the $109 million Q1 backlog. This indicates demand was stronger than shipments showed, but also that fulfillment constraints persisted.
fact_evidence: “Orders reached $339 million, up 6.6% year-over-year,” and “Backlog climbed to $127 million, up $18 million from Q1 and $50 million since year-end,” while parts shortages constrained shipments.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “must show that backlog converting to shipped revenue” and called for the “$109M backlog” to be “drawn down.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The North American ERP recovery timeline slipped further: normal operations are now expected in the first half of 2027 rather than the original second half of 2026. That postpones the operational recovery the preview framed as central to Q2’s backlog conversion and margin improvement.
fact_evidence: “The ERP optimization timeline slipped one to two quarters, with a return to normal North American operations now expected in the first half of 2027 versus the original second half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 the “ERP recovery quarter” and said “Q2 must show that backlog converting to shipped revenue.”

description: Robotics growth remained strong but was far below the preview’s expectation that growth would stay near Q1’s 85% rate: Q2 robotics revenue grew 37% year over year. The full-year outlook and 2028 target still point to substantial growth, but the near-term pace was slower than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Robotics revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $31 million in Q2,” with full-year guidance of $130–145 million and a target of $250 million by 2028.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “sustaining anything near +85% growth supports the premium multiple” and flagged sustaining “anything near +85%” as the trajectory to watch.

description: Regional performance was weaker than the preview’s recent trends suggested: EMEA shifted from +1.0% organic growth in Q1 to a 2.8% decline, with negative pricing, while APAC fell 10.6% versus Q1’s 2.0% decline. North America was essentially flat rather than clearly inflecting positive, although Latin America grew 21%.
fact_evidence: “EMEA organic sales declined 2.8% with negative net pricing from increased discounting,” “APAC fell 10.6%,” and “North America was essentially flat (-0.2%) and Latin America grew 21%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 organic growth of “EMEA +1.0%, APAC -2.0%” and said the Americas was the region that “must inflect.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The expected cash-flow inflection was not evident in the first-half result: operating cash flow remained a $26.2 million use, compared with $22.1 million generated in the prior-year first half. The preview specifically looked for Q2 cash flow to swing decisively positive from Q1’s outflow.
fact_evidence: “First-half operating cash flow was a use of $26.2 million versus $22.1 million generated a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 OCF needs to swing decisively positive” from Q1’s “- $31.2M”; the catalyst checklist called for an “Operating cash flow inflection.”

description: The preview put Q1 revenue consensus at $592.9 million, but the reported tobacco and ingredients revenues add up to about $524 million, roughly 12% below that estimate. Tobacco revenue fell 13% and ingredients revenue fell 3%.
fact_evidence: Tobacco revenue was down 13% to $437 million; ingredients revenue was down 3% to $87 million.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $592.9M” for Q1 FY2027 consensus.

description: The preview expected adjusted EPS of $0.25, but the company reported a $5 million net loss and just $2.3 million of consolidated operating income. This was a much weaker profitability result than the preview’s base case implied.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated operating income fell to $2.3 million from $33.8 million year-over-year, and the company posted a net loss of $5 million versus net income of $8.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (adjusted) | $0.25” for Q1 FY2027 consensus.

description: Tobacco operating income was far below the preview’s expected $28–36 million base-case range, collapsing to $3.5 million. The preview anticipated a difficult comparison and customer delays, but not a result this far below its modeled range.
fact_evidence: “Tobacco segment operating income collapsed to $3.5 million in Q1 FY2027 from $35.7 million a year earlier,” with customers delaying purchases amid oversupply.
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “tobacco op income $28–36M.”

description: Ingredients slipped into an operating loss rather than delivering the roughly breakeven result in the preview’s base case. The loss was relatively small, but it continued the segment’s weak performance.
fact_evidence: Ingredients reported a “$700,000 operating loss” versus $1.7 million of operating income a year earlier, with revenue down 3%.
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Ingredients ~breakeven”; the preview also identified the $1.7 million prior-year operating income as the Q1 comparison.

description: Foreign currency movements created a specific additional headwind to tobacco operating income that the preview did not identify in its operating outlook.
fact_evidence: “Foreign currency movements caused a $4.4 million negative operating income variance in the tobacco segment versus the prior-year quarter.”

description: APA maintained its Egypt BOE outlook despite revising gross oil and gas guidance, avoiding the further adjusted-production cut the preview identified as a key risk. It also said about half of Egypt gas production now benefits from revised pricing, with minimal free-cash-flow impact.
fact_evidence: “In Egypt, APA revised guidance to gross oil production of about 118,000 bpd and gross gas of 535 million cubic feet per day, maintaining the original BOE outlook with minimal free cash flow impact, and now has about half of gas production benefiting from revised pricing.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for a second cut” in Egypt adjusted guidance; the base case expected Egypt to “drift[] to ~67–69 MBoe/d,” while the bear case anticipated a cut “again to ~64–66 MBoe/d.”

description: APA raised its full-year free-cash-flow outlook to about $2.3 billion at current strip pricing, modestly above the roughly $2.2 billion level the preview said investors wanted reaffirmed. The company attributed roughly $950 million pretax to its gas trading portfolio.
fact_evidence: “At current strip pricing, APA expects approximately $2.3 billion of total free cash flow in 2026, including roughly $950 million pretax from its gas trading portfolio.”
expectation_evidence: “Any FCF guide below the standing ~$2.2B is the bear trigger”; the catalyst checklist said investors wanted “reaffirmation” of FY26 FCF at that level.

description: APA increased its year-end annualized cost-savings target to about $500 million, exceeding the preview’s expected $450 million target. The company also reported total reductions including interest savings of roughly $675 million versus 2024.
fact_evidence: “Raised its year-end annualized run-rate cost savings target to approximately $500 million, up from the prior $450 million goal, with total cost reductions including interest savings reaching roughly $675 million versus 2024.”
expectation_evidence: The preview stated the target was “$450M cumulative run-rate by YE26.”

description: APA raised full-year Permian oil production guidance by 3,000 barrels per day while planning to operate with only four rigs for the rest of the year and keeping its capital budget unchanged. The preview’s base case expected guidance to be reaffirmed, while higher Permian volumes were described as an upside scenario.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year Permian oil production guidance to 123,000 barrels per day (up from 120,000) while cutting the rig count to 4 for the rest of the year and holding the $1.3 billion capital budget unchanged.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “FY guidance reaffirmed, not raised”; its bull case required “an explicit H2 volume restoration in the Permian.”

description: APA repaid more debt in the first half than the preview cited and now expects to reach its $3 billion net-debt target in 2027, ahead of the original three-to-four-year timeline. That is faster progress than the preview’s central discussion of the debt target and paydown cadence suggested.
fact_evidence: “The company repaid $752 million of bond debt in the first half of 2026 (including $673 million in Q2) and now expects to reach its $3 billion net debt target in 2027, ahead of the original 3-4 year timeline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “YTD debt repayment $634M” and described the $3 billion net-debt target as an outstanding goal to monitor.

description: APA disclosed plans for higher exploration spending in 2027, including two Alaska wells and a Uruguay well, rather than providing only the general exploration-related swing narrative flagged in the preview. ENI will partly fund the Uruguay well, which offsets some of that spending exposure.
fact_evidence: “Exploration spend rises in 2027 (~$100-120 million for two Alaska wells) with a Uruguay well planned for late 2027 partly funded by new partner ENI.”

description: MMI reported Q2 revenue of $203 million, about 4.5% above the preview’s $194.3 million consensus. The beat was stronger than the preview’s base case of $192–198 million.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 18% year-over-year to $203 million in Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $194.3M”; base scenario: “$192–198M.”

description: MMI earned $0.10 per share, beating the preview’s $0.03 consensus by $0.07 and delivering positive GAAP earnings in a quarter when the preview described crossing zero as the key test.
fact_evidence: “Net income swung to $4 million ($0.10 per share) from a net loss of $11 million ($0.28 per share) a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) +$0.03”; “Consensus wants MMI's first positive Q2 EPS of the cycle.”

description: Private client brokerage reached $106 million, exceeding the preview’s roughly $95 million whisper despite the preview’s concern about weakness in MMI’s core single-asset market.
fact_evidence: “Private client brokerage grew 14% to $106 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Private-client brokerage revenue vs. ~$95M whisper”; the preview also described multifamily individual asset sales as “–7% Y/Y” and said the market had “decelerated in Q2.”

description: Middle-market brokerage returned to growth, rising 13% to $22 million, rather than remaining weak after its Q1 decline. The preview had identified a return to growth as a bull-case condition, not its expected baseline.
fact_evidence: “Middle market grew 13% to $22 million,” with “broad-based recovery across price segments for the first time since the market disruption began.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a bull case required “middle market ($10–20M) returns to growth after Q1's –5.9%”; its bear case said “middle market stays negative.”

description: Transactions above $20 million grew 43% to $33 million, a sharp acceleration after an extended period of institutional softness; the preview had not forecast this scale of growth.
fact_evidence: “The larger transaction segment (deals above $20 million) grew 43% to $33 million, the strongest growth since Q4 2024 after an extended period of institutional softness.”

description: Brokerage growth came in at 18%, above the preview’s implied 12–15% growth range. The stronger brokerage result helped drive the overall revenue beat.
fact_evidence: “Brokerage up 18%.”
expectation_evidence: “Brokerage commissions: ~$158–162M (est.)” versus $141.4 million a year earlier, implying “+12–15%.”

description: Financing revenue rose only 15%, below the preview’s estimated $31–34 million and implied 18–29% growth range. Loan count rose 17%, but dollar volume grew just 5%, showing weaker dollar-volume growth than the headline loan-count increase.
fact_evidence: “Financing revenue rose 15% to $30 million on a 17% increase in transaction count to 480 loans, though dollar volume grew only 5% to $4 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Financing fees ~$31–34M (est.)” and implied “+18–29%”; the preview also said “sustaining even +25% signals” the buildout was compounding.

description: SG&A stayed virtually flat in dollars instead of rising modestly as the preview expected, falling to 35% of revenue and producing stronger operating leverage than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “SG&A held virtually flat in dollars but fell to 35% of revenue from 42% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: Q1 guardrails called for “SG&A up modestly in absolute dollars.”

description: Management said cost of services is expected to increase sequentially in Q3 as commissions to senior producers rise. The preview focused on the Q2 cost range and did not flag this additional Q3 cost pressure.
fact_evidence: “Cost of services rose 50 basis points to 62.4% of revenue, reflecting higher commissions paid to more senior producers, and is expected to increase sequentially in Q3.”

description: The preview estimated Q2 GAAP EPS of $0.10–$0.15, while the call reported net income of $12.6 million, or $0.08 per share. That is below the preview’s GAAP estimate, though the preview cautioned that derivative marks could make GAAP EPS noisy.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $12.6 million ($0.08 per share)”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS +$0.10 to +$0.15 (derivative reversal)”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was $31 million, well above the preview’s estimate of roughly $15–20 million. The result was also a 50% sequential increase, rather than the modest cash generation the preview modeled.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose 50% sequentially to $31 million in Q2”
expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow: ~$15–20M”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The balance sheet improved beyond the preview’s roughly $220 million net-debt trajectory: cash exceeded $150 million, net debt fell to $200 million, and leverage was 1.2x. Management also said the ratio could fall below 1x by year-end, better than the preview’s expectation of leverage at or below 1.5x.
fact_evidence: “Cash on hand grew to over $150 million while net debt fell to $200 million, lowering the trailing 12-month net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio to 1.2x, with management targeting potentially under 1x by year-end 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “$55M+ keeps net debt/EBITDA at/below 1.5x” and “validates the ~$220M net debt trajectory.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 production reached 34,700 boe/d, modestly above the preview’s roughly 34,300 boe/d guide-midpoint expectation, and was up year over year despite no new drilling or acquisitions.
fact_evidence: “Q2 production reached 34,700 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 3% year-over-year despite no new drilling or acquisitions”
expectation_evidence: “Production ~34.3 MBoe/d (guide midpoint)”

description: The Q3 production outlook was for more than 35,000 boe/d, but the preview said the buy side wanted roughly 36,000 boe/d back after the turnaround. The stated floor is therefore below the preview’s desired recovery level, although it does exceed 35,000.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance exceeding 35,000 boe/d.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy side wants ~36 MBoe/d back in Q3”

expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $211.4M.”

description: F&G contributed only $65 million to Q2 adjusted net earnings, well below the preview’s $85–95 million base case. Its share of FNF’s first-half adjusted net earnings was also 23%, below the preview’s roughly 32% expectation.
fact_evidence: “F&G's adjusted net earnings contribution to the segment declined to $65 million from $89 million in Q2 2025”; F&G contributed “23% of the first-half total,” down from 32% a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “F&G ~$85–95M” and described F&G as “now ~32% of consolidated adjusted earnings.”

description: Commercial title activity appears to have run ahead of the preview’s expected Q2 range. The reported first-half total of $778 million, less the preview’s stated Q1 result of $338 million, implies about $440 million for Q2, above the $380–400 million Q2 expectation.
fact_evidence: “Direct commercial revenue reached $778 million in the first six months, up 24% over $626 million in the first half of 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Look for FNF commercial revenue of $380–400M vs. $333M last year”; the preview also reported Q1 direct commercial revenue of $338M.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: F&G’s AUM grew more slowly than the preview anticipated: $74.7 billion and 8% year-over-year growth, versus an expectation of about $75 billion and 11% growth.
fact_evidence: “F&G's assets under management before reinsurance grew 8% year-over-year to $74.7 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “AUM ~$75B before flow reinsurance (+11%).”

description: F&G announced a formal process to explore strategic alternatives for Peak Altitude, an event the preview did not identify as a likely catalyst. Management’s preference for a 51% partner and use of proceeds to grow the core business rather than pursue M&A makes the potential outcome and shareholder benefit uncertain.
fact_evidence: “F&G has launched a formal process to explore strategic alternatives for its Peak Altitude distribution unit” after nearly $700 million invested and with $80 million of 2025 EBITDA; management favors a “51% partner structure” and says proceeds would likely go toward growing the core business over M&A.
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Capital return and F&G stake strategy” as a catalyst and said “Any further F&G distribution or accelerated buyback” was the most plausible narrative-shift catalyst.

description: Matador exceeded the high end of its Q2 production guidance, then raised its full-year oil-growth outlook to 4%–7% while reducing capital expenditures by 1%. The preview’s base case expected FY volumes to be held, with a further guidance increase only in its bull scenario.
fact_evidence: “Matador exceeded the high end of its production guidance and raised full-year year-over-year oil growth guidance to a range of 4% to 7% while simultaneously reducing capital expenditures by 1%.”
expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “FY26 volumes held”; “Bull” scenario: “FY26 guide raised again.”

description: Despite generating $303 million of Q2 free cash flow, Matador now expects about $900 million for the full year, below the preview’s expected reaffirmation of roughly $1.0 billion.
fact_evidence: “Matador generated near-record adjusted free cash flow of $303 million in Q2 2026 and expects to generate approximately $900 million in free cash flow for the full year.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 Adjusted FCF — guided $1.1–1.2B in May, cut to ~$1.0B on July 23. Does it hold at current strip?” The base case expected “~$1.0B AFCF reaffirmed.”

description: Matador has already used $200 million of Q2 cash flow to reduce acquisition-related RBL borrowing from $1.25 billion to below $1 billion, and expects the debt to be largely repaid by year-end. That is a faster paydown path than the preview’s 12–18-month leverage target after the acquisition closes.
fact_evidence: “The company used $200 million of the quarter's cash flow to pay down acquisition-related bank debt, reducing the RBL borrowing from $1.25 billion to under $1 billion, and expects it largely repaid by year-end.” Management also “targets monthly debt repayment of roughly $100 million at current prices” and considers “$70/barrel oil” sufficient to remain profitable.
expectation_evidence: “Management targets ~1.0x leverage within 12–18 months of close — any slippage in that framing is the bear trigger.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The quarter included a significant marketing gain that management said was non-recurring, an earnings-quality caveat not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the quarter’s price and gas-realization drivers.
fact_evidence: “The quarter included a significant marketing gain that management characterized as non-recurring.”
expectation_evidence: The preview focused on realized gas pricing as “the single largest swing factor” and described the base case as “realized gas ~$0.30/Mcf”; it did not flag a one-time marketing gain.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Matador disclosed projected returns above 80% on newly acquired assets, compared with above 50% on existing assets, citing high-quality rock, 15%–20% higher oil EURs, and 12.5% federal royalties. The preview discussed acquisition acreage but did not anticipate this return differential.
fact_evidence: “Newly acquired assets are projected to deliver rates of return above 80%, compared to over 50% on existing assets, driven by high-quality rock, 15%-20% higher oil EURs, and low 1/8 (12.5%) federal royalty rates.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the Paloma acquisition’s acreage, production, reserves, and locations, but gave no projected return comparison.

description: Matador expects well costs on the new federal acreage to fall to about $600 per foot through batch development and longer laterals, an operational cost outlook not included in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Well costs on the new federal acreage are expected to fall to approximately $600 per foot, aided by batch development across 9 or more benches and longer laterals.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The BLM lease sale extended inventory life to more than 15 years, with drilling potentially starting by late 2026 or early 2027 across nine zones. The preview discussed Woodford optionality and the Rae’s Creek well but did not anticipate this inventory-life extension or drilling timetable.
fact_evidence: “The BLM federal lease sale extended inventory life to over 15 years, with management drilling potentially beginning as early as end of 2026 or early 2027 across acreage featuring 9 different zones.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Woodford / Ridge Runner optionality” and asked investors to watch for a follow-up well program or 2027 capital allocation, but did not give this inventory-life or timing outlook.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Drilling efficiency on three-mile laterals improved from roughly 20 days to about 10 days, a substantial operational improvement not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Drilling efficiency on 3-mile laterals improved from roughly 20 days to about 10 days.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Matador reported a 5% increase in oil and natural gas reserves during the quarter, from 667 million to 703 million BOE; the preview did not discuss a quarterly reserve change.
fact_evidence: “Oil and natural gas reserves grew 5% during the quarter, rising from 667 million to 703 million barrels of oil equivalent.”

description: Q2 sales were $172 million, above the preview's $162.8 million consensus by about 5.6%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total sales rose 17% year-over-year to a record $172 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 Consensus | $162.80M”

description: Loar raised its 2026 sales, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS guidance, with the new sales range above the preview's bull-case range and the EPS range above the prior guide and Street estimate. The higher outlook is a stronger raise than the preview's base-case scenario anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its calendar 2026 guidance to net sales of $665M-$675M, adjusted EBITDA of $265M-$270M (~40% margin), and adjusted EPS of $1.32-$1.36, up from $1.26-$1.30 prior.”
expectation_evidence: “Bull” scenario: “FY guide to ~$658–668M / EPS $1.32–1.36”; “Base” scenario: “FY guide nudged to ~$650–660M.” The preview listed Street sales at “$653.67M” and adjusted EPS at “$1.30.”

description: Management said it expects to “meet or beat” the high end of the newly raised annual guidance. That suggests a more confident, potentially conservative outlook than the preview's focus on whether Loar would raise enough to clear a Street already near the prior guide's top end.
fact_evidence: Management framed guidance as a figure they expect to “meet or beat” at the high end, with first-half sales and adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 38% and 47%, respectively.
expectation_evidence: “A merely in-line quarter with a reaffirmed guide is a de-facto disappointment”; “The buy-side is underwriting another raise.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview flagged Harper's initial margin dilution as a risk, but management reported that all three recent acquisitions—Beadlight, LMB, and Harper—are performing ahead of expectations.
fact_evidence: “All three recent acquisitions (Beadlight, LMB, Harper) are performing ahead of expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Harper Engineering … was called ‘significantly dilutive’ to margins initially”; the preview also said to watch whether “Harper integration is pulling margin toward the ~40% FY target.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company said about $200 million of its organic pipeline had converted into secured initial orders, an update beyond the preview's expectation of simply seeing the pipeline grow. The orders are purchase-order based rather than long-term agreements, which qualifies the strength of the conversion.
fact_evidence: “The organic new business pipeline totals approximately $750 million of revenue potential over five years (up ~$50M from May), with ~$200 million now converted to secured initial orders”; the orders are “on a purchase-order basis (not long-term agreements).”
expectation_evidence: “Another sequential increase is the cheapest credibility signal management can deliver.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Year-to-date free cash flow was about 1.9 times reported net income while capital expenditure remained around 3% of sales. The preview discussed leverage and possible M&A but did not set an expectation for cash conversion or capex.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) reached approximately 1.9x reported net income, with capex held at ~3% of sales (~$20M).”

description: Cheniere raised 2026 EBITDA guidance to $7.9–$8.4 billion and DCF guidance to $5.3–$5.8 billion, above the preview’s expected ranges; the new low end is higher than the previous high end for both metrics. The preview expected incremental upside to come mostly from optimization, but management attributed most of the quantified increase to higher production and locking in open volumes, with $100–$150 million from optimization.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $7.9-$8.4 billion consolidated adjusted EBITDA and $5.3-$5.8 billion DCF, with the new low end exceeding the previous high end for both metrics.” The increase included “roughly $300 million from a 0.5 million-tonne production increase, $200 million from locking in open volumes and higher Henry Hub, and $100-$150 million from optimization activities.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave FY26 guidance of “$7.25–7.75B” EBITDA and “$4.75–5.25B” DCF; its bull scenario expected “$7.6–8.0B” EBITDA and “$5.0–5.4B” DCF. It also said “the incremental lever is mostly optimization/trading, not spot exposure.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Cheniere signed a $4.7 billion turnkey EPC contract for Sabine Pass Phase 1 and has financing underway, a concrete project-development step not anticipated in the preview. The expected early-2027 FID timing itself remained consistent with the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company signed a ~$4.7 billion lump-sum turnkey EPC contract with Bechtel for Sabine Pass Phase 1,” adding “over 6 million tonnes per annum (~10% platform growth),” with “FID expected early 2027 and financing already underway.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “LNTP guided for late 2026, FID early 2027” for the next growth leg; it did not anticipate a signed EPC contract or financing already underway.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The mid-scale Corpus Christi Trains 8 and 9 were further along than expected: they were over 48% complete versus 37% at Q1 in the preview, while still ahead of schedule.
fact_evidence: “Mid-scale Trains 8 and 9 are over 48% complete and ahead of schedule.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the trains were “37% complete at Q1” and “tracking ahead of schedule.”

description: Management said the $8-plus-billion EBITDA level can be sustained even when marketing margins normalize to $2.50–$3, rather than depending on today’s unusually high margins. The preview did not anticipate this specific normalized-margin run-rate claim.
fact_evidence: Management expects the “$8+ billion EBITDA level to be sustainable run-rate even at normalized $2.50-$3 marketing margins (versus current $10-$13), rather than a one-off tied to elevated LNG prices.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Cheniere designated most IPM volumes for normal-purchase/normal-sale accounting, which management said would remove mark-to-market derivative swings from those volumes and reduce the number of negative-net-income quarters in the historical comparison. The preview warned that derivatives distorted GAAP results but did not anticipate this accounting change.
fact_evidence: “The company designated normal-purchase/normal-sale accounting for ~75% of IPM volumes starting mid-June,” which “will eliminate mark-to-market derivative swings and would have cut negative net income quarters since 2021 from six to two.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described GAAP EPS as “dominated by non-cash mark-to-market on IPM gas supply derivatives” and said “Do not trade the EPS line”; it did not mention a change in accounting treatment.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The Strait of Hormuz disruption and resulting shift in LNG flows were not anticipated in the preview: Qatar and UAE exports fell, U.S. exports to Asia reached a record, and Europe faced a large storage deficit. Those conditions are supportive of demand for Cheniere’s exports, though the disruption itself makes the market backdrop mixed.
fact_evidence: The disruption “cut Qatar/UAE exports by ~18 million tonnes in the quarter, drove U.S. exports to Asia to a record ~11 million tonnes, and left Europe with an ~11 Bcm storage deficit that management expects will struggle to reach even 70% fullness before winter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed softened TTF and JKM prices and an Asia premium, but did not anticipate a Hormuz-related supply disruption or its reported export and storage effects.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Chord generated $414 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2, which the call said exceeded expectations. The preview anticipated a strong quarter but did not give a consensus FCF estimate.
fact_evidence: “Generated adjusted free cash flow of $414 million in Q2 2026, exceeding expectations.”
expectation_evidence: The call states that Q2 adjusted free cash flow exceeded expectations.

description: Chord returned $220 million, or 54% of adjusted FCF, in Q2—a firmer payout than the preview's concern that management might taper repurchases and prioritize the balance sheet. The preview expected at least a 50% return under the stated framework, so the result was above that floor, though the call did not break out the repurchase amount.
fact_evidence: “Returned 54% ($220 million) to shareholders via base dividends and share repurchases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a sub-$75M buyback quarter would confirm that deleveraging now outranks returns,” and described the framework as “≥50% of adj. FCF returned at leverage <1.0x.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported oil-volume result was at the high end of company guidance, but fell short of the preview's 166–168 MBopd functional whisper; Chord also held full-year guidance at 161,000 bpd rather than delivering the second raise the preview identified as a catalyst.
fact_evidence: “Oil production came in at the high end of guidance” and full-year oil volume guidance “was maintained at 161,000 barrels per day.”
expectation_evidence: The preview put the functional whisper at “~166–168 MBopd” and said to watch for “a second FY oil guidance raise.”

description: Chord raised full-year LOE guidance to $10.30/BOE, near the top of the preview's stated $9.55–$10.35/BOE range, reflecting higher workover, non-operated, and production-enhancement costs.
fact_evidence: “Full-year LOE expense guidance was raised to $10.30 per BOE,” reflecting “higher workover costs, and increased non-operated LOE.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 LOE guidance as “$9.55–10.35/Boe.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Although Bakken crude traded at a premium to WTI in Q2, Chord expects that premium to fade and now guides differentials to just below WTI. That is less favorable than the preview's expectation that the differential would tighten toward flat or a premium.
fact_evidence: “Bakken crude traded at premiums to WTI during Q2 2026,” but the company “now guides differentials to just below WTI as the premium is expected to fade over the year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the differential historically “tightens ... toward flat or a premium” and identified “≤ −$1.00/bbl” as a potential beat driver.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The hedge update showed 38% of second-half 2026 oil volumes hedged, the same coverage level the preview cited before the release, rather than reporting a higher 2H percentage after the preview flagged possible additions. Coverage for 2027 did rise from the preview's 14% figure to about 18%.
fact_evidence: “Hedged approximately 38% of its second-half 2026 oil volumes and about 18% of 2027 volumes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “~38% of oil ... hedged for balance of 2026” and “~14% oil for 2027,” and asked whether management had layered on hedges in April/May.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Chord reported successful execution of the basin's first trimulfrac and said it could make up 20%–50% of next year's development program, offering a potential completion-cost reduction that the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Successfully executed the basin's first trimulfrac, which could represent 20% to 50% of next year's development program to reduce completion costs.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected fuel-supply economics of about +2 cpg overall, with core contribution around 2.5 cpg and a possible inventory drag. Murphy instead said the controllables portion alone earned over 7 cpg, a substantially stronger result for that component than the preview’s core estimate suggested.
fact_evidence: “The controllables portion of the fuel supply business earned over $0.07 per gallon this quarter,” reflecting “the advantage of Murphy's supply assets during the current supply-constrained environment.”
expectation_evidence: “Fuel supply segment cpg (and inventory revaluation split)”: “+2 cpg (core ~2.5, mark ~-0.5 to -3).”

description: The preview looked for elevated fuel margins and cited further margin expansion as a possible Q3 tailwind, but management’s back-half all-in fuel-margin guide was about 35 cpg and described as intentionally conservative. That is cautious guidance relative to the high-30s margins reported for early August, though management sees upside if prices fall for an extended period.
fact_evidence: Management guided to “an all-in fuel margin of approximately $0.35 per gallon for the back half of the year,” characterized as “intentionally conservative with upside if prices fall for an extended period.” The first five days of August had margins “in the high 30s cents per gallon.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said July/August QTD margins in the “high-30s/40s cpg” would support the bull case and noted that lower expected Q3 gasoline prices “historically supports further margin expansion.”

description: Merchandise contribution is now expected toward the low end of guidance, below the preview’s roughly $230 million estimate. Management cited consumer budget pressure and the lingering effect of Q1 storm closures, rather than the preview’s modeled merchandise growth.
fact_evidence: “Merchandise contribution is expected to land toward the low end of the guidance range due to consumer budget pressures and Q1 weather impacts that closed up to half the network during winter storms.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated merchandise contribution of “~$230M” and described the base case as “merch ~$230M.”

description: New-store deliveries are expected near 45 units, the bottom of the 45–55-unit range, rather than tracking more broadly toward the preview’s on-track view. Management said the upper end depended on tuck-in acquisitions that are not in the current pipeline.
fact_evidence: “New store (NTI) deliveries will come in closer to 45 units at the lower end of guidance,” because “the high end assumed tuck-in acquisitions that are not currently in the pipeline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “45–55 NTIs + up to 30 raze-and-rebuilds guided for FY26” and described the unit-growth outlook as “On track.”

description: Capital spending is trending to the high end of the guided range, with spending pulled forward and additional life-cycle and land-bank investment. The preview gave the $475–525 million range and expected the plan to be on track, but did not anticipate these specific spending drivers or the high-end trajectory.
fact_evidence: “CapEx is trending to the high end of the range” due to “pulling forward 2027 store construction, proactive life-cycle investments, and land bank investment”; new stores take about three years to reach full profitability ramp.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “capex $475–525M” and characterized the unit-growth outlook as “On track.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described fuel-supply tightness from the geopolitical conflict as persisting well into next year, rather than quickly normalizing. The preview discussed the ceasefire and resumption-of-traffic news behind the price decline but did not anticipate this prolonged-tightness outlook; the implications are mixed because tight conditions also benefit Murphy’s supply assets.
fact_evidence: Management believes “fuel supply tightness from the geopolitical conflict will not normalize until well into next year” and “does not expect a quick resolution.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the Brent decline as driven by “ceasefire/resumption-of-traffic news” and framed the quarter around the resulting price waterfall.

description: Revenue was just over $51 million, well below the preview’s $58.7–$59.0 million consensus range—roughly a 13% shortfall, despite 48% year-over-year growth.
fact_evidence: “Revenue rose 48% year-over-year to just over $51 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $58.7 – $59.0M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $34 million, below the preview’s roughly $40 million estimate. The 49% year-over-year increase still fell about 15% short of that expectation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 49% to $34 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$40M (my est., no published consensus).”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.57, below the preview’s $0.68–$0.78 estimate range. Separately, GAAP EPS of $0.72 was slightly below the stated $0.75 consensus, though the preview cautioned that the consensus accounting basis was unclear.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income reached $21 million ($0.57 per share)” and “Net income was approximately $27 million ($0.72 per share).”
expectation_evidence: “My estimates: … Adj. EPS $0.68–0.78”; the preview also lists “EPS | $0.75” and says it is unclear whether that figure is GAAP or adjusted.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Realized gas price fell to $1.36 per Mcf, far below the preview’s $2.30–$2.55 estimate. The preview anticipated soft gas pricing, but the reported price was substantially weaker than that expectation.
fact_evidence: “Realized natural gas prices fell sharply to $1.36 per Mcf from $3.13 in the prior quarter due to widening regional differentials.”
expectation_evidence: “Gas … Q2E Realized $2.30–2.55/Mcf”; the preview attributed its estimate to “HH ~$2.94 less Mid-Con discount.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Production of 19.7 Mboe per day came in just above the preview’s estimated 18.5–19.5 Mboe per day range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 production grew 11% year-over-year to 19.7 Mboe per day.”
expectation_evidence: “Production | ~18.5–19.5 MBoe/d (my est.).”

description: SandRidge paid another $0.20 special dividend alongside its regular dividend, following the prior quarter’s special, rather than the preview’s base-case expectation of maintaining only the $0.13 regular dividend. It also declared the regular $0.13 dividend for August.
fact_evidence: “SandRidge paid $10.6 million in dividends during the quarter, including a 13-cent regular dividend and a 20-cent special dividend, and declared another 13-cent dividend for August 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “base dividend $0.13 maintained, no special,” and said “A second consecutive special says the cash engine is intact.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: A step-out well below the Cherokee Shale delivered a strong result and pointed to possible stacked-pay development, an opportunity the preview did not identify as an upcoming catalyst.
fact_evidence: “A step-out well testing a sub-member below the Cherokee Shale delivered a 90-day average rate of approximately 11,000 Mcfe per day and over 1 Bcf cumulative production after 100 days, opening potential stacked-pay development.”

description: The 2026 plan now calls for completing nine operated Cherokee wells, one more than the eight completions the preview expected, while retaining the expected 10-well drilling program.
fact_evidence: “The 2026 capital program is budgeted at $76 million to $97 million to drill 10 operated Cherokee wells (completing nine).”
expectation_evidence: “The 2026 program is one rig, 10 operated Cherokee wells drilled, 8 completed, 2 rolling into 2027.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management said the $76–$97 million 2026 capital program is fully funded by operating cash flow, a reassuring funding statement against the preview’s warning that Q1 free cash flow was negative and the company was not self-funding quarter after quarter at low prices.
fact_evidence: “The 2026 capital program is budgeted at $76 million to $97 million … fully funded by operating cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 free cash flow was −$1.1M — this is not a self-funding quarter-in, quarter-out story at low prices.”

description: DXP reported Q2 sales of $576.5 million, 6.2% above the $543 million consensus in the preview. The result was also in line with the preview’s estimate that holding April’s sales pace through the quarter would produce about $576 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total sales grew 15.6% year-over-year to $576.5 million, with organic sales up 11.1% and acquisitions contributing $49.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $543.0M”; the preview also said, “holding April's pace all quarter implies ~ $576M revenue (+15.5%).”

description: Diluted EPS was $1.76, about 11% above the preview’s $1.59 consensus and above its base-case range of $1.60–$1.70. The result was close to, but just below, the preview’s bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS rose to $1.76 from $1.43 in Q2 2025, with net income increasing to $28.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS $1.59”; the base scenario expected “$1.60–1.70.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $70.4 million versus the preview’s estimated $62 million, and the 12.2% margin exceeded its roughly 11.4% consensus estimate. That is a stronger profitability result than the preview’s base case of an 11.4%–11.7% margin.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $70.4 million with margins expanding to a record 12.2%, up from 11.5% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$62M (est.)”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~11.4%.” The base scenario expected “EBITDA margin 11.4–11.7%.”

description: IPS sales grew 52.6%, with organic growth of 13.3%, rather than the project-timing downside highlighted in the preview. Acquisitions supplied $47 million of IPS sales, so the surge was partly acquired, but organic growth was still strong.
fact_evidence: “The Innovative Pumping Solutions segment surged 52.6% year-over-year to $142.7 million, though $47 million came from acquisitions with organic IPS growth of 13.3%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “IPS project timing slips right” in its bear scenario and said a “backlog decline here reframes the whole 2H setup even on a Q2 beat.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Water and wastewater had a larger role in IPS than the preview quantified: it was approaching 70% of segment sales and was identified as supporting the record EBITDA margin. The preview expected the 15th consecutive quarter of DXP Water sequential growth, but did not anticipate this pronounced mix contribution to margins.
fact_evidence: “Water and wastewater is now approaching 70% of IPS segment sales, driving the higher-margin mix that supported the record EBITDA margin.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a 15th consecutive quarter of sequential water growth would “sustain[] the secular story that supports the multiple.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half free cash flow reached $56 million, a substantial improvement from the preview’s discussion of Q1 cash generation and its concern that M&A had consumed most YTD capital deployment. The preview provided no first-half FCF estimate, so the size of the result was not explicitly forecast.
fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 free cash flow reached $56 million, a sharp reversal from negative $8.6 million in the prior year period, with trailing four-quarter free cash flow of $118.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 FCF of “$26.3M” and said “FCF conversion … and working capital … matter because M&A consumed 95% of YTD capital deployment.”

description: DXP completed four acquisitions in the first half, more than the preview’s stated expectation of one to two acquisitions before the end of Q2. The higher pace supports growth but also means more acquisition spending and integration activity than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “DXP completed four acquisitions in the first half for $135.6 million total consideration.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “1 to 2 acquisitions before the second quarter ends.”

description: DXP also completed the Mico Limited deal to establish a Canadian DXP Water presence, a geographic beachhead not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the expected Mequipco transaction. The deal was funded with cash and stock.
fact_evidence: “Plus the Mico Limited deal (funded with cash and stock) to establish a DXP Water beachhead in Canada.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified Mequipco as “signed August 1” and described it as “a Q3 event”; it did not mention Mico Limited or a Canadian beachhead.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: DXP’s credit profile was stronger than the preview’s leverage concern suggested: secured leverage was 2.31x versus the 2.6x Q1 figure, and S&P upgraded the issuer rating from B to B+. The preview had flagged leverage and balance-sheet capacity as items to watch but did not anticipate the rating upgrade.
fact_evidence: “S&P Global upgraded DXP's issuer credit rating to B+ from B,” and the company reported “$374.5 million in total liquidity with a secured leverage ratio of 2.31x and $842.5 million in total debt.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch secured leverage vs. the 2.6x base and the ≤3.5x net target” and raised the question of whether stock consideration signaled “the balance sheet is tightening.”

description: Non-GAAP operating loss was $4.6 million, worse than the preview’s expected $2.0–$3.0 million company-guidance range and roughly $2.5 million consensus loss. Management attributed $1.7 million of pressure to unexpected French employer payroll taxes tied to RSU vesting as the stock price rose.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating loss was $4.6 million” and was “pressured by $1.7 million in unexpected French employer payroll taxes tied to RSU vesting amid a rising stock price.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. loss” company guide “$(2.0)–$(3.0)M”; consensus “~$(2.5)M.”

description: Management described the first non-GAAP operating profit as possible “as early as Q4,” which is less firm on timing than the preview’s expectation of profitability “by Q4 2026.” The profitability path remains in view, but the phrasing leaves more room for it to occur later.
fact_evidence: “Management expects to report its first non-GAAP operating profit as early as Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Management has guided to non-GAAP profitability by Q4 2026”; the preview also said “Any language softening the Q4 breakeven commitment is a de-rating event.”

description: Royalties remained strong over the trailing year, but they dipped slightly sequentially because of a customer’s supply-chain issues. The preview highlighted continued royalty growth and expansion in large royalty reporters, but did not anticipate a sequential dip.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month royalties hit a record $8.6 million, growing 65% year-over-year, though royalties showed a slight sequential dip due to a customer's supply chain issues.”
expectation_evidence: “TTM $7.9M, +67% Y/Y”; the preview said to “watch both the quarterly royalty dollar figure and whether the >$1M reporter count expands again.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: RPO reached a new high of $135 million, up from the $118.3 million Q1 baseline cited in the preview; just over half is expected to convert to revenue within 12 months. The preview gave no Q2 RPO expectation, so the record level was not specifically anticipated there.
fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation (RPO) reached an all-time high of $135 million, with just over half expected to be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months.”

description: The company ended the quarter with $123 million in cash after completing an ATM that raised about $72 million net, a substantial change from the preview’s cited $41.9 million of cash and investments. The added liquidity is positive, though it came from issuing shares.
fact_evidence: “The company completed its ATM program raising ~$72 million in net proceeds at an average price over $35, ending the quarter with $123 million in cash and no debt.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash + investments ~$41.9M, no debt.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management reported that no customer accounted for more than 10% of first-half revenue and that enterprise computing averaged 29% of ACV plus royalties over the past four quarters. This provided new evidence of customer and business-line diversification, although the preview supplied no numerical expectation for either measure.
fact_evidence: “No single customer exceed[ed] 10% of revenue in the first half of 2026, while enterprise computing averaged 29% of ACV plus royalties over the past four quarters.”

description: Q2 revenue was $125.8 million, about 4.8% above the preview’s $120 million consensus estimate and above the preview’s $123–126 million bull-case range at the top end. Constant-currency growth was 9%, stronger than the 6.2% growth implied by consensus.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $125.8 million, up 9% year-over-year on a constant currency basis.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 Consensus” revenue: “$119.99M”; implied Y/Y: “+6.2% reported.”

description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was reiterated at $92–99 million, below the preview’s stated $100–107 million guide. That is a lower outlook despite the Q2 adjusted EBITDA result exceeding the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: “Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance” of adjusted EBITDA “$92-$99 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA” guide: “$100–107M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $26.4 million, just above the preview’s estimated $24–26 million range. The beat was modest rather than a substantial overshoot.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 7% from $24.8 million to $26.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus: “~$24–26M (est.).”

description: Despite the adjusted EBITDA beat, adjusted EBITDA margin fell about 90 basis points to 21%, with management attributing the decline to higher R&D investment after the Endospan acquisition. This contrasts with the preview’s expectation of margin expansion implied by the annual guide.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin declined roughly 90 basis points to 21% due to increased R&D investments following the Endospan acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY guide “implies 100bps expansion” and set an adjusted EBITDA bogey of “≥$25M, GM ≥65%.”

description: Stent graft growth accelerated to 12%, exceeding the preview’s minimum 10% bogey, even against a tougher comparison. This is a positive update on a metric the preview identified as important to the second-half growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “Stent graft revenue accelerated to 12% growth (from 10% in Q1) against a tougher comp.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bogey was “≥+10% cc (matching Q1).”

description: ONIX grew 18%, ahead of the preview’s expectation of at least 15% growth. The reported growth was attributed to global market-share gains among patients under 65.
fact_evidence: “ONIX grew 18% on global market share gains in patients under 65.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s ON-X bogey was “≥+15% cc.”

description: Tissue processing grew about 1% rather than producing the negative print the preview said was expected on the hard comparison. However, management said roughly $2 million of tissue releases shifted from Q3 into Q2, making the result partly a timing benefit rather than evidence of stronger underlying demand.
fact_evidence: “Tissue processing revenue was approximately $26 million (up 1%), aided by roughly $2 million of upside from tissue releases that shifted from Q3 into Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said preservation services faced “difficult comps in Q2 and Q3” and that “A negative print here is expected.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was negative $12 million, with $1.5 million of Endospan diligence costs and a $10.2 million contractually required transaction bonus booked as a post-acquisition expense. The preview flagged financing and integration costs but did not identify this bonus payment or forecast a cash outflow of this kind.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $12 million in Q2,” impacted by “$1.5 million of Endospan diligence costs” and a “$10.2 million contractually required transaction bonus payment booked as a post-acquisition expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “no cost surprise” while flagging Endospan “integration cost, interest expense, contingent consideration.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The acquisition financing left net leverage at 3.1x, excluding a $25 million AMDS milestone paid in July. The preview noted the borrowing but did not quantify this leverage level or the additional milestone payment, adding a financing burden beyond the details it highlighted.
fact_evidence: The Endospan/Nexus acquisition closed for “a $135 million purchase price funded by $150 million of borrowings, raising net leverage to 3.1x (excluding a $25 million AMDS milestone paid in July).”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted a “$150M term loan draw” and flagged “Endospan financing drag,” including expected interest expense and any integration or contingent-consideration charges.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: BARK’s underlying subscriber economics improved despite the expected sharp drop in DTC orders: retention rose more than 170 basis points year over year, average order value increased 45 cents per unit, and BarkBox lifetime value approached its highest level as a public company.
fact_evidence: “Subscriber retention rate improved by over 170 basis points year-over-year,” “average order value grew 45 cents per unit,” and subscriber lifetime value was “near its highest level as a public company.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the tell is in subscriber and DTC commentary” and called for “new-subscriber acquisition and retention commentary,” while anticipating DTC declines of about 28%.

description: Commerce revenue fell 11% to $12.1 million, rather than coming in around the preview’s implied $14 million and roughly flat year over year. Management expects meaningful increases heading into the holidays, but the reported decline deepens the weakness in a segment the preview said needed to scale.
fact_evidence: “Commerce revenue fell 11% year-over-year to $12.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q1 Commerce at “~$14M (implied)” and “~flat” year over year, and said “a second consecutive down quarter here breaks the diversification story.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Reported gross margin reached 72.7%, but the figure was lifted by a one-time $7.4 million tariff recovery; normalized margin was 63.4%, slightly below the 63.8% a year earlier. The recovery’s effect was flagged as a possibility, but its scale produced much higher reported margin than the preview’s roughly 62% historical margin reference would suggest.
fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin was 72.7%, inflated by a one-time $7.4 million IEPA tariff recovery from FY26; normalized gross margin was 63.4% versus 63.8% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited 62.3% consolidated gross margin for Q1 FY26 and said, “Watch how much landed in Q1, and where — a COGS credit would flatter gross margin and adjusted EBITDA.”

description: Bark Air reached $3.2 million of revenue, above the preview’s roughly $3 million estimate, and more than 90% of Q2 seats were already sold, offering a favorable demand indicator beyond the expected growth in the business.
fact_evidence: “Bark Air revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $3.2 million, with over 90% of Q2 seats already sold.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q1 BARK Air revenue at “~$3M” and growth of “~+30%.”

description: BARK made share repurchases under its $40 million program, confirming that the authorization was being used, while cash declined from $19.3 million at fiscal year-end to $16.1 million. The preview had identified both buyback execution and ending cash as unresolved questions.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter debt-free with $16.1 million in cash, down from $19.3 million at fiscal year-end due to working capital build and share repurchases under its $40 million buyback program.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Any Q1 repurchases, and the ending cash balance ex-refund, tell you whether the buyback is real or ornamental,” and described the authorization as “funded by ongoing free cash flow” as “a stretch.”

description: Marketing spend was cut 37% year over year, a much larger reduction than the preview’s question about whether marketing would be redeployed suggested. The lower spend supports cost control but leaves less visible support for acquiring subscribers as DTC orders fall.
fact_evidence: “Marketing spend was cut 37% ($5.6 million) year-over-year to $9.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “whether marketing spend is being re-deployed” as something to watch alongside the DTC subscriber trajectory.

description: AerSale reported $70.9 million of revenue, $10.3 million below the preview’s $81.2 million consensus. There were no flight equipment sales, versus the preview’s base case of a couple of engine transactions; the preview had flagged a zero-sale quarter as a downside scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $70.9 million” and was driven primarily by “the absence of flight equipment sales versus $33.4 million (eight engines) in the prior-year period.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$81.2M”; “Base requires: a couple of engine transactions”; “Zero units means revenue lands near $65–70M and EPS goes negative.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.09 rather than the preview’s expected $0.11 profit, a 20-cent shortfall. The preview warned that consensus depended on high-margin whole-asset sales, but its base case still assumed some engine transactions.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted loss per share of $0.09.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS ~$0.11”; the preview said clearing $0.11 required “a meaningful slug of high-margin whole-asset sales.”
