description: Adjusted EBITDA was only $2.2 million, far below even the preview’s bear-case range of $5–8 million. The result reflected both the missing high-margin equipment sales and lower gross margin.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA collapsed to $2.2 million (3.1% of revenue) from $18.3 million (17% of revenue) a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario projected “Adj. EBITDA $5–8M”; its base case projected “$9–12M.”

description: Gross margin fell to 22.9%, below the preview’s 28–30% base-case range and its 30% marker for the startup drag to have eased. The call attributed the decline to lost high-margin equipment sales as well as startup costs at Goodyear and Millington.
fact_evidence: “Overall gross margin fell to 22.9% from 32.9% due to lost high-margin equipment sales and startup costs at Goodyear and Millington.”
expectation_evidence: The base case called for “GM 28–30%”; the preview said Q2 was when startup drag “should visibly abate” and flagged “Gross margin ≥30%” as the marker to watch.

description: Even excluding flight equipment sales, revenue declined 4.2% year over year: lower USM sales outweighed growth in leasing and MRO. That was weaker than the preview’s recurring-revenue thesis and expectation that TechOps would grind higher.
fact_evidence: “Excluding flight equipment sales, overall revenue declined 4.2% year-over-year as lower USM sales offset growth in leasing and MRO.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called sustained growth in Asset Management Solutions ex-flight-equipment “the recurring-revenue thesis” and said the base case required “TechOps [to] grind higher.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Liquidity was tighter than the preview’s already-cautious balance-sheet framing: available liquidity was $34 million, including just $2.2 million of cash, and revolver availability was $31.8 million. The preview identified availability below roughly $35 million with cash near zero as the point when liquidity could become the main issue.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date cash used in operating activities was $33.5 million,” leaving “available liquidity of just $34 million ($2.2 million cash plus $31.8 million revolver availability).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Below ~$35M with cash near zero” the conversation shifts from growth to the balance sheet; it cited Q1 “$2.1M cash” and “$41.8M total availability.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Goodyear was operating at under 20% of available capacity, despite the preview’s expectation that the MRO network was filling and that startup drag should begin to abate. The landing gear shop was much busier at about 80% of single-shift capacity, a contrast that points to uneven utilization across the operation.
fact_evidence: “Goodyear is operating at under 20% of available capacity with 84 stored ex-Spirit Airlines aircraft awaiting maintenance work, while the landing gear shop runs at about 80% single-shift capacity with plans to add a second shift.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the MRO network is filling” and that Q2 was when the “startup drag should visibly abate.”

description: Feedstock acquisitions dropped to $5.6 million from $27.1 million a year earlier. The preview anticipated disciplined purchasing but also highlighted the risk of continued feedstock deployment; the sharp pullback limits that buying, while reflecting a hyper-competitive market.
fact_evidence: “Feedstock acquisitions dropped sharply to $5.6 million in Q2 from $27.1 million a year ago due to pricing discipline in a hyper-competitive acquisition market.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the “disciplined-acquisition posture” but also warned of liquidity risk “if Q2 is another no-asset-sale quarter with continued feedstock purchases.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management disclosed a specific $35 million 737 sale to the U.S. Marshal Service expected to close in late Q3 or early Q4, plus 17 engines in repair expected to exit over the coming months. This offers concrete future monetization and repair activity, though neither the aircraft sale nor the engine exits add to Q2 results.
fact_evidence: “Management secured a $35 million 737 aircraft sale to the U.S. Marshal Service plus several engine sales expected to close in late Q3 or early Q4, and has 17 engines in work expected to exit repair over the coming months.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management might point to “Q4-weighted asset monetization” and warned that pipeline strength could be offered “rather than closed transactions.”

description: The preview expected no likely update on the unresolved CSL arbitration, but CSL Seqirus instead terminated the collaboration. Arcturus regained global rights to CoStave and its broader infectious-disease portfolio, received a one-time $12 million payment, and was released from roughly $16 million in liabilities.
fact_evidence: “The CSL Seqirus collaboration was terminated, returning global rights to the CoStave COVID vaccine and the broader infectious disease portfolio (seasonal flu, pandemic flu, RSV, EBV) plus a one-time $12 million cash payment and release from roughly $16 million in liabilities.”
expectation_evidence: “CSL Seqirus arbitration (EU KOSTAIVE milestone) … No update likely.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected ARCT-032 enrollment to be on track and wanted a specific data window, with data guided for H1 2027. Management instead centered guidance on a Q4 2026 go/no-go decision for Phase 3; that gives a dated decision point but does not provide the expected data window.
fact_evidence: “The pivotal go/no-go decision to advance the CF candidate ARCT-032 into Phase 3 is expected in Q4 2026”; management “reframed CF guidance to focus on the Q4 2026 Phase 3 decision rather than a data disclosure or enrollment completion.”
expectation_evidence: “ARCT-032 12-week Ph2 enrollment + data guidance … Enrollment ‘on track’; data guided H1 2027”; investors wanted “a specific data window.”

description: Arcturus reported lower Q2 R&D spending than the preview’s $21–24 million estimate: $17.5 million. That is a notable reduction against the expected quarterly spend, though the facts do not explain the cause.
fact_evidence: “R&D expenses declined to $17.5 million (Q2) … from $29.6 million” a year earlier.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected the ARCT-810 end-of-Phase-2 meeting to be scheduled or reaffirmed for H2 2026. Instead, management said full Phase 2 data and the regulatory path, including a plan for the meeting, would be disclosed in Q3; the update gives a nearer data disclosure but does not report a scheduled meeting date.
fact_evidence: “Enrollment and study-drug dosing were completed for … ARCT-810, with full Phase 2 data (including FDA-requested supplementary Type C data) and the regulatory path forward, including an end-of-Phase 2 meeting plan, to be disclosed in Q3 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “ARCT-810 End-of-Phase-2 meeting … Guided to H2 2026”; the preview also said a “scheduled date” would de-risk the pivotal design.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview did not anticipate the CF study’s expansion into Israel and Turkey. Management said those locations have a larger share of patients with eligible null mutations than the US group described in the call, which is intended to boost recruitment.
fact_evidence: “The CF Phase 2 study was expanded to Israel and Turkey, where 30%-40% of CF patients carry null mutations eligible for enrollment versus up to 10% ineligible-for-modulator patients in the US, boosting recruitment.”
expectation_evidence: “Up to 20 Class I CF patients, US + ex-US”; the preview expected enrollment to be “on track.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call gave more reassuring ARCT-032 dosing and safety detail than the preview provided: more than 50 participants had been dosed, including at the highest stated dose, without steroid pretreatment or clinic-based administration. The preview had focused on enrollment and the timing of data rather than these treatment details.
fact_evidence: “ARCT-032 has now been dosed in over 50 participants at up to 15 mg daily for 28 days without steroid pretreatment and with at-home self-administration,” and management said “no serious safety issues have required disclosure in the ongoing 12-week study.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “12-week Ph2 enrollment + data guidance” and expected enrollment to be “on track.”

description: Arcturus reported Q2 G&A expense of $11 million, above the preview’s $9–10 million estimate. The difference is modest compared with the larger-than-expected reduction in R&D.
fact_evidence: “G&A remained roughly flat at $11 million (Q2) … .”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview did not flag a change in the Japanese CoStave profit split. With CSL out, Arcturus’s profit share will be split two ways with Meiji instead of three ways, improving its share of the Japanese economics.
fact_evidence: “In Japan, the loss of CSL means the CoStave profit share will now be split two ways with Meiji instead of three ways.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the KOSTAIVE royalty stream and CSL arbitration, but did not anticipate a change to the Japanese profit split.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview did not mention progress on the pandemic-flu program ARCT-2304. The call reported that Phase 1 was complete, results were accepted by Nature Communications, and EMA scientific advice was planned for Q4 2026.
fact_evidence: “The pandemic flu program ARCT-2304 completed Phase 1 with results accepted by Nature Communications and EMA scientific advice planned for Q4 2026.”

description: The Q3 outlook calls for loan volume to fall to $1.375–$1.525 billion and revenue to $49–$52 million, rather than the preview’s base case of roughly flat volume and $56–$62 million revenue. Revenue guidance is also at or below the preview’s bear-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies a sequential decline, with loan volume of $1.375-$1.525 billion” and “net revenues of $49-$52 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “volume roughly flat QoQ” and “Q3 Revenue Guide” of “$56–62M”; its bear case was “$50–55M.”

description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $15–$18 million is worse than the preview’s base-case loss of $10–$13 million and reaches below the preview’s bear-case threshold of a loss worse than $15 million.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies … an adjusted EBITDA loss of $15-$18 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “$(10)–(13)M”; its bear case was “Worse than $(15)M.” It also cited a “~$(10)M ‘on track’ whisper.”

description: Management said it will miss the previously guided September adjusted EBITDA break-even goal and did not provide a replacement target month. The preview’s base case anticipated a dated push to 1H27, so leaving the timing unanchored is less specific than that expectation.
fact_evidence: The company “will fall short of its previously guided goal of reaching adjusted EBITDA break-even by September,” and management “declined to re-anchor to a specific target month.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “Breakeven formally pushed to 1H27”; it also listed “withdraw” as a possible outcome and called breakeven language the “highest-variance sentence on the call.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q2 refinance volume rose sharply despite the preview’s concern that refinance demand was contracting in a high-rate environment. The growth is a positive contrast to that market setup, although management still described the business as rate-sensitive.
fact_evidence: “Refinance volume surged 239% year-over-year to $549 million,” though it “remains highly rate-sensitive amid an elevated rate environment management expects to persist over the medium term.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said refinance applications were “down 9% YoY” and noted that BETR’s growth was “disproportionately refi-levered into a market where refi demand is now contracting.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Ending cash was about $102 million, plus $10 million restricted, versus the liquidity cushion implied by the preview’s Q1 cash balance and subsequent equity raise. The reported balance makes the liquidity position tighter than that context suggested, even as warehouse capacity remained substantial.
fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “~$102 million in cash plus $10 million restricted cash.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 ended with ~$136M cash/equivalents/restricted, plus a $69M April equity raise” and highlighted “Q2 ending cash” as a key item to watch.

description: Management disclosed that signed HELOC partnerships, including Credit Karma, have not launched and are excluded from Q3 guidance, with meaningful contributions expected only from Q4. That means they will not support the near-term outlook, while also identifying a later-period growth contribution not discussed in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Signed HELOC partnerships—including Credit Karma—have not yet launched and are excluded from Q3 guidance, with meaningful contributions expected to begin in Q4 2026.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview expected cash to fall to roughly $95–105 million after the Q1 decline and April JV contribution. Instead, cash and short-term investments rose to $138 million, with less than $5 million left to contribute to the Maas JV.
fact_evidence: “Cash and short-term investments grew to $138 million at quarter-end (up from $126 million in March), with less than $5 million remaining to be contributed to the Maas Energy Works dairy JV.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 could exit near ~$95–105M”; “Anything under ~$100M with no financing plan articulated reopens the dilution conversation.”

description: The preview expected the dairy RNG ramp to improve through the year, but the upstream business was already approaching EBITDA breakeven in Q2 as South Fork and East Valley ramped. That is a more concrete profitability milestone than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The RNG upstream business approached breakeven EBITDA in Q2 as South Fork (Texas) and East Valley (Idaho) ramped.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch South Fork (TX) and East Valley (Idaho, ~3.5M gal/yr, commissioned Q1) throughput”; management “explicitly promised improvement through the year.”

description: The preview described the company as still waiting for updated GREET guidance and said a quantified 45Z benefit could be upside. The call put a number and timing on it—up to $5 million of incremental EBITDA with guidance expected in Q4—but also said a delay into 2027 or minimal benefit could put EBITDA below the stated range.
fact_evidence: “Finalized 45Z GREET model guidance—now expected in Q4—could add up to $5 million of incremental adjusted EBITDA, but a delay into 2027 or minimal benefit would push EBITDA below the $70-$75 million range.”
expectation_evidence: “Quantified 45Z capture would be a clean upside surprise; continued ‘we’re waiting’ is neutral-to-negative.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected the dairy RNG ramp to support volumes, but most of the reported total fuel-volume growth came from conventional natural gas rather than RNG. That makes the growth mix less driven by the RNG ramp than the preview's focus suggested.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 fuel volumes rose 7% year-over-year to 81.8 million gallons, with about two-thirds of the growth coming from conventional natural gas rather than RNG.”
expectation_evidence: “Upstream dairy RNG production ramp”; “management explicitly promised improvement through the year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call disclosed that X15N truck adoption remains slow, with a large prebuy of legacy diesel trucks contributing to the weakness. The preview did not flag this demand or adoption issue.
fact_evidence: “X15N truck adoption remains slow, hurt by a large prebuy of legacy diesel trucks amid uncertainty over final 2027 EPA emission standards.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company announced a $27 million contract for its largest hydrogen fueling station, using a cost-plus structure that avoids commodity and capital risk. The preview did not anticipate this contract.
fact_evidence: “The company secured a $27 million contract with Orange County Transportation Authority for its largest hydrogen fueling station, using a low-capital cost-plus model that avoids commodity and capital risk.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company described a new off-pipeline power-generation opportunity using existing tube trailers and underutilized compression capacity across 600 stations, with little to no new investment. This opportunity was not raised in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Clean Energy is pursuing an off-pipeline power-generation market (data centers, fulfillment centers, EV charging) using existing tube trailers and underutilized compression capacity at 600 stations, requiring little to no new investment.”

description: Blink cut its FY2026 revenue outlook from $105–115 million to $83–90 million, a substantial reduction from the guide the preview expected to be tested. The new range is roughly 21%–22% below the prior range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance” was cut “to $83-90 million from the prior $105-115 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Standing guidance ... FY26 revenue $105–115M”; the preview called whether the guide was “held, narrowed, or cut” the “single largest binary.”

description: Q2 revenue was $21.7 million, well below the preview’s roughly $24.6 million consensus estimate. That is an approximately 12% miss, despite sequential growth.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue fell to $21.7 million from $28.7 million year-over-year, though it rose 4.3% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | ~$24.6M (range $24.25M–$24.6M).”

description: Service revenue was $11.5 million, missing the preview’s roughly $14.5 million estimate and falling sequentially from Q1’s $13.3 million. This reversed the sequential uptrend the preview said was needed to support the recurring-revenue story.
fact_evidence: “Service revenue grew 6.2% to $11.5 million”; Q1 service revenue was listed in the preview as $13.3 million.
expectation_evidence: “Service revenue (est.) ~$14.5M”; “service revenue needs to clear ~$14.7M to re-establish a sequential uptrend.”

description: Product revenue came in at $7.4 million, below the preview’s estimated $8–9 million. The shortfall was smaller than the service-revenue miss but added to the overall revenue disappointment.
fact_evidence: “Product revenues dropped to $7.4 million from $14.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Product revenue (est.) ~$8–9M.”

description: Blink said the revenue-guidance reduction reflected its focus on revenue quality and the Envoy divestiture, rather than weak demand. That is more reassuring than the preview’s framing that a cut would indicate the turnaround was stalling.
fact_evidence: Blink cut guidance, “citing revenue-quality focus and the Envoy divestiture rather than weak demand.”
expectation_evidence: “A cut converts BLNK from ‘turnaround executing’ to ‘turnaround stalling.’”

description: Q2 GAAP gross margin reached 38.9%, well above the preview’s roughly 33% base case and its 35% bull-case threshold. The reported margin improvement was stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin expanded to 38.9% from 16.8% year-over-year”; adjusted gross margin was 47.9%.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “GM ~33%,” and its bull case specified “GAAP GM ≥35%.”

description: Blink raised its FY2026 GAAP gross-margin outlook to approximately 38% from 35%, rather than merely maintaining the prior target. That is a meaningful upward revision to the full-year margin expectation.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 GAAP gross margin outlook was raised to approximately 38% from 35% previously.”
expectation_evidence: “Standing guidance ... FY26 GAAP gross margin ~35%.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $2.2 million, substantially better than the preview’s expected loss of roughly $4–5 million. It also came close to the preview’s bull-case threshold of a loss no worse than $2 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $2.2 million ... a 72% improvement and a multiyear low.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.) ~−$4M to −$5M”; the bull case listed “adj. EBITDA ≥ −$2M.”

description: Management gave a concrete target to exit 2026 at approximately adjusted-EBITDA breakeven and said it expects positive adjusted EBITDA for full-year 2027. The preview had noted that management had previously declined to provide a 2026 breakeven target.
fact_evidence: “Management targets exiting 2026 at approximately breakeven adjusted EBITDA and a positive full-year adjusted EBITDA in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “has explicitly declined to provide a 2026 adjusted-EBITDA breakeven target.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The disclosed 2026 DC build plan was 25 sites and 118 stalls, below the preview’s cited target of 27 sites and 136 stalls. The difference is modest but leaves the stated buildout smaller than the plan investors had been told to track.
fact_evidence: “Blink plans to build 25 DC fast charging sites (118 stalls) by end of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “27 sites / 136 stalls targeted” and said those were the Q1 targets.

description: Q3 sales guidance of about $13.5 million was below the preview’s $15 million-plus threshold for keeping the trucking ramp on track, and even below its $14–16 million base-case range. Management attributed the softer outlook to timing factors for EBITDA, but the sales guide itself is materially short of the preview’s expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for net sales of approximately $13.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs to guide to $15M+ with a line of sight to $17.5M”; the base case expected “Q3 guided $14–16M.”

description: Reported gross margin of 33.0% was well above the preview’s 22–25% expectation, but the margin included a $1.1 million tariff-refund benefit. Excluding that benefit, the margin would be about 24.7%, near the upper end of the expected range, so the headline outperformance was largely due to the refund.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 470 basis points to 33.0%, though this included a $1.1 million benefit from tariff refund payments recognized in cost of sales.”
expectation_evidence: “At $13.2M of revenue the fixed-cost absorption argument should deliver 22–25%.”

description: The company reported only $13.2 million of Q2 sales, $0.6 million below the $13.8 million consensus estimate, although it met its own $13.2 million guidance. The preview treated company guidance as the more reliable benchmark, making this a modest consensus shortfall rather than a miss against management’s guide.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $13.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Company Guide (5/14/26) ~$13.2M | Consensus $13.8M”; the preview also says “the company’s own guidance is the more reliable benchmark.”

description: Lenders deferred senior leverage and fixed-charge coverage covenant compliance until September 2027, extending relief beyond the preview’s stated covenant-waiver period through December 2026. That is a more favorable financing runway than the preview described.
fact_evidence: “Lenders ... deferred senior leverage and fixed charge coverage covenant compliance until September 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said covenants were “waived through 12/31/26.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Stevens Transport plan now involves a possible conversion of the customer’s full 2,500-truck fleet, with Werner and other carriers also advancing through the pipeline. The preview highlighted a Stevens order across about 500 trucks, so the broader fleet opportunity and additional carrier pipeline were incremental commercial upside, though not confirmed fleet-wide orders.
fact_evidence: “Stevens Transport shipments have begun as the first phase of a plan to convert its full fleet of 2,500 trucks, with Werner Enterprises and additional carriers advancing through the pipeline.”
expectation_evidence: “Stevens Transport is a $3M+ order across ~500 trucks with deliveries starting Q2.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was a $1.6 million loss, $0.3 million better than the company’s guided $1.9 million loss and slightly better than the $2.7 million sequential improvement implied by guidance. This was a modestly better Q2 result despite continued losses.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.6 million, a $0.6 million year-over-year improvement and a $3.0 million sequential improvement from Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Company Guide (5/14/26) ~$(1.9)M”; the preview says this “implies $2.7M sequential improvement.”

description: Q2 revenue was nearly $1 billion, up 20% year over year, versus preview estimates of $929–939 million and 12.6%–14% growth. That was a clear top-line beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached nearly $1 billion, representing 20% year-over-year growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $929M ...; $939M”; the preview also described implied growth of “+13% to +14%.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.20 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.92–$0.95 consensus range and the author’s $0.98 estimate, rather than landing near the expected level.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.20.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $0.92 ...; $0.93–$0.95”; the preview’s “My estimates (base case)” were “non-GAAP EPS $0.98.”

description: VOXZOGO grew 14% against the preview’s forecast of about 5%, while patient growth and retention also held up despite the new competitor. Management said more than 20% more children were treated globally and approximately 90% of U.S. patients stayed on therapy.
fact_evidence: “VOXZOGO grew 14% year-over-year in Q2 with more than 20% growth in children treated globally, and approximately 90% of U.S. patients remained on therapy despite a U.S. competitor launch in February.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled VOXZOGO at “$232M (+5%)” and flagged the first competitor as “the entire bear case,” asking investors to watch treated-patient growth and any erosion.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management quantified competitor switching at fewer than 100 patients over roughly six months, describing the impact as small relative to projected VOXZOGO revenue. The preview highlighted competitor entry as a major risk but had no quantified switching estimate.
fact_evidence: “Competitor switching at approximately 10% of VOXZOGO patients, equating to fewer than 100 patient switches over roughly six months—a small impact on nearly $4 billion in projected revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called VOXZOGO’s first competitor “the entire bear case” and said “Competitor entry has been priced in as a fear, not yet as a number.”

description: BioMarin raised full-year revenue, VOXZOGO revenue, and non-GAAP EPS guidance, whereas the preview treated reaffirmation as the base case and said a raise would be a bull-case outcome.
fact_evidence: “BioMarin raised full-year 2026 guidance for total revenues, VOXZOGO revenue and non-GAAP diluted EPS.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed FY26 guidance “reaffirmed at both revenue and EPS”; it said “FY26 revenue guide raised or narrowed to the top half” would characterize the bull scenario.

description: The disclosed $220 million annual synergy run rate by 2028 was above the preview’s bull-case threshold of at least $150 million. Management also specified that more than 70% would come from G&A, quantifying a substantial cost reduction.
fact_evidence: “Cost synergies of approximately $220 million annual run rate are expected by 2028, representing a ~50% reduction from Amicus’ 2025 non-GAAP operating expenses of $432 million, weighted over 70% toward G&A.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said synergy detail was due on the call and described “a named synergy number (≥$150M)” as part of its bull scenario.

description: Management put the combined peak-revenue potential at $2.6 billion, with Galafold at $1.4 billion and POMBILITI/OPFOLDA at $1.2 billion. The preview expected both assets could exceed Amicus’ prior roughly $1 billion-each framing, but did not anticipate these specific, higher figures.
fact_evidence: “The Amicus acquisition adds combined peak revenue potential of $2.6 billion, with Galafold targeted at $1.4 billion ... and POMBILITI/OPFOLDA at $1.2 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had hinted “both assets can exceed Amicus’ prior $1B-each peak framing.”

description: The Amicus products showed sharply different growth rates: POMBILITI/OPFOLDA grew more than 65% pro forma while Galafold grew about 10%. The preview described Amicus revenue growth broadly as high-teens to low-20s, so the POMBILITI/OPFOLDA pace was much faster than that framing, while Galafold was slower.
fact_evidence: “On a pro forma basis Q2 Galafold grew ~10% and POMBILITI/OPFOLDA grew over 65% year-over-year, while total metabolic conditions revenue was $695 million, up 25%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Amicus’ FY25 revenue as “growing high-teens/low-20s.”

description: The deal was expected to be close to breakeven in 2026 and substantially accretive starting in 2027, with deleveraging pulled forward by about a year. The preview focused on debt and integration but did not provide an expected accretion or deleveraging timetable.
fact_evidence: “The Amicus deal is expected to be close to breakeven (modestly dilutive) in 2026 but substantially accretive to non-GAAP EPS beginning in 2027, with half or slightly more of synergies realized next year and deleveraging pulled forward by about one year.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: BioMarin submitted the VOXZOGO hypochondroplasia sNDA in 79 days from database lock, adding a roughly 14,000-patient global opportunity and targeting a 2027 launch. The preview anticipated a second-half 2026 submission but did not give this rapid filing timeline or market-size detail.
fact_evidence: “BioMarin submitted its sNDA for VOXZOGO in hypochondroplasia in just 79 days from database lock, targeting a ~14,000-patient global addressable market with anticipated launch in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said hypochondroplasia Phase 3 results supported a “2H’26 submission planned.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: BioMarin disclosed BMN 820, an oral CCR2 inhibitor for FSGS, with an estimated 30,000 U.S. addressable patients and Phase III data expected in 2028. The preview did not mention this asset or program.
fact_evidence: “New pipeline asset BMN 820 (oral CCR2 inhibitor for FSGS) targets an estimated 30,000 U.S. addressable patients with Phase III data expected in 2028.”

description: Avalaya brought in $3.6 million in its first full commercial quarter, about 67% above the preview’s $2.15 million consensus estimate. The preview viewed the quarter’s revenue as a low-signal launch print, but the reported amount still materially exceeded that bar.
fact_evidence: “Avalaya (Ablea) generated $3.6 million in net product revenue in its first full commercial quarter for Hunter syndrome.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus | $2.15M”; the preview also described its estimate as “$2.0–2.5M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management pushed DNL593 data from the preview’s expected year-end 2026 timing to the first half of 2027, a delay of at least several months. The stated reason was to allow longer observation of biomarkers.
fact_evidence: “DNL593 for FTD-granulin data was delayed from end of 2025 to first half of 2027 to allow longer observation of biomarkers like neurofilament light chain.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said DNL593 was guided “by end of 2026” and that the timing “must survive verbatim.”

description: Q3 product-revenue guidance of $10–12 million implies a fast sequential ramp, but is below the roughly $16 million per quarter H2 pace implied by the preview’s FY2026 revenue consensus. If Q3 lands within guidance, reaching that annual consensus would require a substantially higher Q4 quarter.
fact_evidence: “Management guided to Q3 net product revenue of $10-12 million, implying roughly 3x sequential growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 revenue consensus of $33.97 million, less roughly $2.2 million expected in Q2, “leaves ~$31.8M for H2 — roughly $16M per quarter.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Pro forma cash exceeded $1.15 billion, well above the preview’s estimate of $920–940 million exiting Q2. The comparison includes $195 million received in July from the voucher sale, so it is a pro forma figure rather than cash at June 30.
fact_evidence: “Pro forma cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities exceeded $1.15 billion, including $195 million received in July from the sale of a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + securities (6/30) … ~$920–940M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Denali reported concrete early access and engagement figures: policies covered more than half of lives, 14 state Medicaid programs listed coverage, and the company had engaged over 100 families. That is a positive launch signal against the preview’s uncertainty about payer access and patient metrics, though coverage was below the preview’s greater-than-70% bull-case marker.
fact_evidence: “Commercial policies covering more than 50% of lives have been established, with 14 state Medicaid programs publicly listing Ablea as covered in the first quarter of launch”; Denali “engaged more than 100 families, representing over one-quarter of eligible US patients.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Payer coverage” and asked for “quantified launch metrics”; its bull case required “payer policy coverage above ~70% of covered lives.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The DNL593 program also received FDA orphan drug designation, a favorable regulatory development the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: DNL593 “recently received FDA orphan drug designation.”

description: Operating expenses were below the preview’s modeled level: Q2 R&D of $97 million and SG&A of $36.3 million total about $133 million, versus the preview’s roughly $141 million estimate. SG&A was also below the preview’s $40 million estimate and its $37 million marker for especially disciplined launch spending.
fact_evidence: “Q2 R&D expenses were $97 million … while SG&A rose to $36.3 million … keeping overall OpEx roughly flat year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “R&D expense … ~$101M” and “G&A expense … ~$40M”; it said “below ~$37M suggests disciplined, targeted deployment.”

description: MYQORZO product revenue was far above the preview’s implied $14–16M, reaching $25.3M; total revenue of $28.6M also exceeded the $17.6M consensus estimate. The strong product launch, rather than a recurring collaboration payment, drove the headline beat.
fact_evidence: MYQORZO generated $25.3 million in net product revenue ($23 million U.S., $2.3 million Europe); total Q2 revenue was $28.6 million.
expectation_evidence: “Consensus total revenue” of $17.6M; consensus “backs into roughly $14–16M of product sales.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Acacia produced a better clinical result than the preview’s unresolved efficacy-and-safety debate implied: it met both primary endpoints and had no new safety signals. The preview had highlighted the LVEF signal and awaited the fuller data readout.
fact_evidence: “The Phase III Acacia HCM trial in nonobstructive HCM met both dual primary endpoints (KCCQ Clinical Summary Score and peak VO2) with no new safety signals.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for FDA feedback on “whether the agency has engaged on the LVEF signal” and said the later readout would show the “full efficacy-safety tradeoff,” including the 10% LVEF <50% rate.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The planned nHCM sNDA moved substantially earlier than the timing embedded in sell-side models: management plans to submit in Q4 2026 rather than the modeled H2 2027 filing window.
fact_evidence: The Acacia results support “a planned sNDA submission to the FDA in Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said sell-side models “embed an H2 2027 filing” and clarified that this was a modeling assumption, not company guidance.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: More than 80% of Q2 dispensed prescriptions were paid for, ahead of the preview’s expectation that paid conversion would hold above 70%.
fact_evidence: “Over 80% of Q2 dispensed prescriptions” were paid for.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed conversion “holds ~70%” and its checklist said investors wanted “>70% paid maintained.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported 1,500 dispensed patients fell short of the preview’s 1,600–1,800 cumulative-patient in-line scenario, even as product revenue and paid conversion were stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: MYQORZO “was dispensed to 1,500 patients by the end of Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario anticipated “in-line adds (~1,600–1,800 cumulative patients).”

description: The company raised its expense guidance instead of reaffirming the existing range, increasing the midpoint by $25M. Management attributed the increase to commercial readiness for a potential 2027 nHCM launch.
fact_evidence: FY2026 combined GAAP R&D and SG&A guidance rose to $860–890 million from $830–870 million, driven by commercial readiness investments for a potential 2027 nHCM launch.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Reaffirmation is expected”; it also noted a raise could reflect launch investment but would pressure runway.

description: The quarterly loss per share was narrower than expected: the company reported a $1.50 loss per share versus the preview’s $1.63 loss estimate.
fact_evidence: Net loss was $198.8 million, or $1.50 per share.
expectation_evidence: Q2 EPS estimate: “$(1.63).”

description: A public offering lifted cash and investments to about $1.7B, a significant financing outcome beyond the preview’s starting cash balance and discussion of a possible opportunistic raise. It improves liquidity, though the financing was an equity offering.
fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with approximately $1.7 billion in cash and investments, up from $1.1 billion, largely from a May public offering generating roughly $760 million in net proceeds.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited cash and investments of “~$1.1B” and said “an opportunistic equity raise is a live risk.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management quantified a large potential treatment runway for obstructive HCM: it estimates only about one-fifth of eligible patients are treated today and that class penetration could eventually reach 60–70%. The preview did not provide these market-size or penetration estimates.
fact_evidence: Management estimates 110,000–120,000 eligible oHCM patients, with about 20,000–25,000 treated (roughly 20% penetration), and projects peak class penetration of 60–70%.

description: CTSO was expected to report revenue of about $9.3M–$9.39M and a year-over-year decline; it reported approximately $9.6M, flat year over year and up 9% sequentially. The result was modestly above the preview’s revenue estimates.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $9.6 million, flat year-over-year but up 9% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $9.39M | My Estimate $9.3M”; the preview also modeled “Revenue YoY | –2% | –3%.”

description: Gross margin was expected to be about 69.5%; it came in at 73%, a sizeable beat. The company attributed the improvement to manufacturing optimization and cost management.
fact_evidence: “Gross margins improved to 73%, up from 71% in the prior-year quarter and 69% in Q1 2026, driven by manufacturing optimization and cost management.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | … My Estimate 69.5%.”

description: The preview’s base case expected management to soften the H2 2026 operating-cash-flow break-even target to ‘exiting 2026.’ Instead, the company said it remained on track for break-even in the second half, with operating cash burn reduced to about $200,000 excluding restructuring costs.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash burn was reduced to approximately $200,000 excluding restructuring costs, keeping the company on track to reach operating cash flow break-even in the second half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “breakeven softened to ‘exiting 2026’” and warned to watch for a reframe from “H2 2026” to “exiting 2026” or “in 2027.”

description: Distributor and strategic partner revenue had been flat in Q1, and the preview treated a recovery as uncertain. It grew 16% year over year and 18% sequentially in Q2, a stronger channel result than the preview’s setup suggested.
fact_evidence: “Distributor and strategic partner revenue grew 16% year-over-year and 18% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 distributors as “flat” and identified the revenue mix, including distributors, as a key metric to watch.

description: The preview’s base case expected Germany to stabilize, but Germany remained weak. That leaves the key sales-territory recovery unresolved despite the overall revenue beat.
fact_evidence: “Direct sales outside Germany rose 9%, offsetting continued weakness in Germany and the Middle East.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “Germany stabilizes but flat,” and called Germany’s return to growth the “single most important operating datapoint.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected feedback on the DOAC pre-submission filed around June and cited a late-2026/early-2027 De Novo timeline. Instead, the company described two FDA pre-submission meetings still scheduled for later this month and said it would file a new De Novo after gathering more mechanistic and real-world evidence, leaving the submission path less settled than expected.
fact_evidence: “The company plans to file a new de novo application for DrugSorb-ATR after gathering additional mechanistic and real-world evidence data, with two separate FDA pre-submission meetings scheduled later this month.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “FDA feedback on the DOAC … pre-submission filed ~June 2026” and described the De Novo timeline as “late 2026/early 2027.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The upcoming DOAC pre-submission meeting covers a parallel indication and management framed the Eliquis/Xarelto market at about $20B. The preview discussed the DOAC pathway but described the combined opportunity as $500M–$1B, so the reported market framing is substantially larger, though it is not the same as an estimate of CTSO’s obtainable revenue.
fact_evidence: “Two separate FDA pre-submission meetings [are] scheduled later this month, including one for a parallel DOAC-removal indication targeting the ~$20 billion Eliquis/Xarelto market.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the DOAC indication and said the “Combined TAM [was] framed by management at $500M–$1B.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The STAR-T CABG per-protocol analysis showed a statistically significant reduction in severe bleeding, an encouraging result not anticipated in the preview. However, the primary MITT endpoint was not statistically significant, tempering the positive signal.
fact_evidence: “In the CABG per-protocol analysis of the STAR-T pivotal trial, DrugSorb-ATR achieved a statistically significant 58% risk reduction in severe bleeding or >1L blood loss (win ratio 1.59) with a number needed to treat of six, though the primary MITT endpoint was not statistically significant.”

description: The company plans to add three to five sales representatives through early 2027, mainly to restore German territory coverage. The preview discussed sales-team restructuring and Germany’s weakness, but did not anticipate this specific hiring plan; it could rebuild coverage while adding expense for a cash-constrained company.
fact_evidence: “Headcount has been reduced by roughly 23% since September 2025, and the company plans to selectively add three to five sales reps through early 2027, mainly to restore German territory coverage weakened by restructuring.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified Germany’s sales-team restructuring as a key issue but did not state that the company planned to rehire sales representatives.

description: Operating loss was $2.6M, slightly worse than the preview’s $2.4M estimate, even though it improved substantially year over year.
fact_evidence: “Operating loss narrowed 27% to $2.6 million … versus the prior-year period.”
expectation_evidence: “Operating loss | … My Estimate $(2.4)M.”

description: Full House's adjusted EBITDA grew 19.5%, well below the preview's implied expectation of roughly 35–45% growth. The gap is meaningful even though the preview cautioned that its EBITDA estimate was a back-solve rather than published consensus.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenues grew 5.6% while adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ... ~$15–16M implied”; the preview's back-solve described expected growth of “+35–45%.”

description: Revenue growth was slightly below the preview's 6.1% consensus-implied growth rate. The reported 5.6% increase points to a small shortfall, rather than the roughly 6.1% increase expected.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenues grew 5.6%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview forecast Q2 revenue of “$78.4M” versus Q2 2025 actual revenue of “$73.9M,” implying “+6.1%.”

description: American Place grew faster than the preview's estimate: revenue reached $34.8 million, above the preview's $32.5–33.5 million range. It also reported its best quarter ever and a May monthly gaming revenue record, rather than the deceleration the preview was watching for.
fact_evidence: “American Place revenues increased 13.4% to $34.8 million”; it had “its best quarter ever” and “set a monthly gaming revenue record of $12.7 million in May 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated American Place revenue at “$32.5–33.5M” and flagged growth below roughly 5% as concerning, against a “+7.1% (Q1 26)” comparison.

description: Rising Star's results were hit by an unanticipated power outage: it moved from a $500,000 profit a year earlier to a $100,000 loss, with no insurance recovery expected. The preview did not flag this event.
fact_evidence: “Rising Star lost $100,000 in the quarter due to a 42-hour power outage from a downed power line, versus a $500,000 profit a year earlier, with no business interruption insurance recovery expected.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management disclosed that Chamonix's win per position per day is only about half the Blackhawk average, indicating a substantial gap in current productivity. It also described sizeable potential if Chamonix reaches or exceeds that benchmark, an operational opportunity not quantified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Chamonix's win per position per day is only about $175, roughly half the Blackhawk average of $330,” with management targeting “roughly $30 million of annual EBITDA at the Blackhawk average and up to $40 million at a 15% premium.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The city approved keeping the temporary Waukegan structure as an event center for five years after the permanent casino opens. The preview discussed the temporary casino's operating extension, but did not anticipate this additional use of the structure.
fact_evidence: “Gained city approval to retain the temporary structure as an event center for five years after the permanent casino opens.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were about $10 million, well above the preview’s $7.0–7.5 million estimate. Management also said it is targeting positive adjusted EBITDA using existing cash without a dilutive raise, rather than the preview’s base case of continued opportunistic ATM use.
fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and marketable securities declined to approximately $10 million as of June 30, 2026”; management is “targeting positive adjusted EBITDA by Q3 2027 using existing cash without a dilutive capital raise.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash & equiv. (6/30) … My estimate: $7.0–7.5M”; base case included “continued opportunistic ATM use.”

description: Management raised full-year revenue guidance to greater than 30% growth, whereas the preview expected roughly 30% growth to be reaffirmed. That is an upside change, although the call’s facts do not quantify how far above 30% the new outlook is.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to greater than 30% growth over 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance of ~30% growth”; “FY ~30% reaffirmed” was the base case, and “a raise is the bull trigger.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.8 million, but that was worse than the preview’s expected $1.3–1.6 million loss for the base case. The loss did improve sequentially and year over year, but it did not reach the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 26% year-over-year and 25% sequentially to $1.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA ($1.3M)–($1.6M)”; the preview also expected a clean quarter under the new cost base.

description: Revenue was flat sequentially at $9.5 million, below the preview author’s $10.0 million estimate and expected 4% sequential growth. It was essentially in line with published consensus, so the shortfall is against the preview’s higher estimate rather than consensus.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $9.5 million, up approximately 28% year-over-year but flat sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “My estimate” was “$10.0M” and “+4% QoQ”; the preview also said revenue of at least $10.0M was a catalyst.

description: Prescription gammaCore growth was weaker than the recent momentum highlighted in the preview: revenue grew about 11% year over year and fell roughly 4% sequentially, compared with the preview’s cited Q1 gammaCore growth of 26%. The call did not provide total VA prescription revenue, so the preview’s $8.2 million VA base case cannot be directly tested.
fact_evidence: “Prescription gammaCore revenue grew about 11% year-over-year but declined roughly 4% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “VA prescription revenue ($7.9M in Q1, +48% YoY; gammaCore +26%). … Base case ~$8.2M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company disclosed that its top 15 VA accounts generated 54% of Q2 VA revenue, adding a concentration risk not quantified in the preview’s discussion of VA facility utilization.
fact_evidence: “The top 15 VA accounts produced 54% of Q2 VA revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified VA prescription revenue and facility utilization as key metrics to watch, but gave no expectation for account concentration.

fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 50.7% in Q2, expanding roughly 150 basis points year-over-year and marking the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~51–52% (my est.)” and “Gross margin ≥51% ... confirms the pricing thesis.”

expectation_evidence: “Base … FY guide nudged to $125–129M or reiterated at high end”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide raised to ≥$126M.”

expectation_evidence: “Look for ~$74–77M of GP at ~22% margin.”

fact_evidence: “A final tranche of ~13.5 million Class B shares converts to Class A in late September, leaving an estimated 35-37 million Class A shares held by insiders, subject to trading restrictions until after Q3 earnings in November.”

description: The preview expected Canada CFR credit sales to appear in Q3, but did not quantify the scale or describe the pathway’s retroactive reach. fact_evidence: “Management expects the carbon business to deliver over $30 million per year in run-rate revenue, excluding banked CFR credit sales.”

fact_evidence: “The company may recover up to $8 million of additional prior tariff costs not included in guidance.”

description: Balance-sheet indicators improved rather than deteriorating: debt fell by $20.5 million sequentially and inventory days declined from about 150 to 136, while leverage stayed around 3.7x.

expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus net sales of “$353.1M” and a base case of “$353–358M.”

expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance language — ‘reaffirm $2.15–$2.55’ is the base case.”

description: The planned securitization is sized at $300–$400 million, below the preview’s expected $400–$500 million Q4 collateral pool at most of the range. The call facts do not confirm that the planned deal has the same timing or scope as the preview’s expected Q4 ALP securitization.
fact_evidence: “The company plans a securitization out of the bank sized between $300 million and $400 million.”

expectation_evidence: “Credit quality — the swing factor nobody models well.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Assets grew 50% year over year while expenses rose only 3.6%, indicating substantially faster growth in assets than in expenses. The preview did not quantify or flag this degree of operating leverage.
fact_evidence: “Assets grew 50% year-over-year while expenses rose only 3.6%, demonstrating operating leverage.”

description: LOCO raised full-year system-wide comp guidance to 3.5%-4.5% from 2%-4%, a larger improvement than the preview’s discussion of the existing range and possible downside risk. The higher range is a positive update to the sales outlook.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year system-wide comp sales guidance to 3.5%-4.5%.”
expectation_evidence: “System-wide comps | +2% to +4% (raised from +2–3%).”

fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level margin improved to 19.5% from 19.1% a year earlier, staying within the 18-20% long-term target despite 4.1% commodity inflation driven largely by produce.”
expectation_evidence: “Food & paper inflation | +1.5% – 2.5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Early Q3 comps were running at 5.8%, even though management expects the full quarter to land at 3.5%-4.5% after an outsized July benefit from World Cup advertising and tougher comparisons. fact_evidence: “Q3-to-date (through July 29) system-wide comparable sales accelerated to 5.8%, but management guided full Q3 comps to 3.5%-4.5%, citing outsized July benefit from World Cup advertising and tougher upcoming comparisons.”
expectation_evidence: “That implies either genuine deceleration in May/June or standard conservatism.”

description: GAAP net income reached $12.8 million, or $0.43 per share, largely because of a $6.3 million legal settlement; adjusted EPS was $0.30, a much more modest result. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not anticipate this one-off boost to the GAAP headline.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net income jumped to $12.8 million ($0.43/share) from $7.1 million ($0.24/share), largely boosted by a $6.3 million legal settlement, while adjusted EPS was more modest at $0.30 versus $0.28.”

description: Labor expense fell 90 basis points to 29.9% of restaurant sales, with wage inflation below 1% in the quarter—better than the preview’s 1.5%-2.5% wage-inflation outlook. Lower health insurance and workers’ compensation costs also helped.
fact_evidence: “Labor expense improved 90 basis points to 29.9% of restaurant sales, aided by wage inflation under 1% in the quarter and lower health insurance and workers' comp costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Wage inflation | +1.5% – 2.5%.”

description: The company lowered 2026 capital spending guidance to $33-$37 million from $37-$40 million because of remodel timing. This reduces expected spending, though the stated reason is timing rather than a reduction in planned investment.
fact_evidence: “The company cut 2026 capital spending guidance to $33-$37 million due to remodel timing.”

description: LOCO paid down $21 million on its revolver, leaving $30 million in debt, and extended its $150 million credit facility to 2031. The longer facility and paydown improve the debt picture, while the new spread is roughly 50 basis points higher; the preview had no specific expectation for these financing changes.
fact_evidence: “Paid down $21 million on its revolver leaving $30 million in debt, and extended its $150 million credit facility to 2031 at a spread roughly 50 basis points higher.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The large auto-insurance carrier relationship stabilized rather than continuing to worsen in Q2, which is better than the preview’s expectation that the shortfall would hit Q2 harder. It still remained below levels seen earlier in the year, so the issue was not resolved.
fact_evidence: “The company's largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized but remains below levels seen earlier in the year.”
expectation_evidence: “Management said monetization from one large auto carrier ‘started running below expectations’ in Q1 and would hit Q2 harder.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance implies 17% year-over-year growth, a stronger growth outlook than the preview’s basic expectation that guidance should at least imply growth. The guide is boosted by student-loan regulatory tailwinds and the February college-finance acquisition.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $244–$260 million implies 17% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, boosted by student loan regulatory tailwinds and the February college finance acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: “A Q3'26 guide that doesn't imply growth off that base signals the search erosion is outrunning banking/loans growth.”

description: SMB revenue declined 11%, a milder drop than the preview’s estimate of about 15% decline. Business-loan originations partly offset continued organic-search declines.
fact_evidence: “SMB revenue fell 11% year-over-year to $22 million, dragged down by organic search declines in non-loan products but partially offset by growth in business loan originations.”
expectation_evidence: “Guidance midpoint implies … SMB ~$21M (−15%).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow doubled to a record $141 million, but the result was helped by tax refunds and the absence of federal corporate tax payments. Management also said federal corporate taxes are not expected in 2026, with normalized taxes anticipated in Q2 or Q3 2027.
fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow grew 100% year-over-year to a record $141 million, aided by $9 million in tax refunds and no federal corporate tax payments”; the company “does not expect to be a federal corporate taxpayer in 2026” and anticipates normalized taxes in “Q2 or Q3 of 2027.”

description: Management disclosed a much larger customer-acquisition investment for longer-payback customers: roughly five times the 2025 level for paybacks beyond the current year, creating a $15–$20 million 2026 operating-income headwind. The preview anticipated multi-quarter investment but did not quantify this headwind.
fact_evidence: “Management is increasing customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year roughly fivefold versus 2025, representing a $15–$20 million NGOI headwind for full-year 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Base = repetition of ‘multi-quarter initiative’ with no new numbers”; the preview also said an explicit spend-peak quarter was a key marker to watch.

description: Full-year NGOI guidance was narrowed to $90–$105 million rather than reaffirmed unchanged at $85–$110 million. The midpoint is unchanged, but the higher floor and lower ceiling give a tighter range; profitability is also expected to be more concentrated in Q3 than in prior years.
fact_evidence: “Full-year NGOI guidance was narrowed to $90–$105 million while maintaining the prior midpoint, with profitability expected to be more concentrated in Q3 than in prior years.”
expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects reaffirmation”; the preview’s base case was “FY $85–110M reaffirmed unchanged.”

description: Consumer revenue was slightly above the preview’s segment estimate: $175 million and 8% growth versus an estimate of about $173 million and 7% growth. Personal loans and deposit accounts drove growth, while credit cards continued to decline from organic-search headwinds.
fact_evidence: “Consumer revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $175 million, driven by personal loans (up $12 million) and deposit accounts, though partially offset by continued declines in consumer credit cards from organic search headwinds.”
expectation_evidence: “Guidance midpoint implies Consumer ~$173M (+7%).”

description: Q2 revenue was about $753 million, well above the preview’s $695–715 million credible whisper range, and growth was about 38% reported or 40% excluding true-ups versus the preview’s expected 28–31% growth. This was a substantially larger beat than the preview’s already-high revenue hurdle.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was approximately $753 million, up ~38% year-over-year (~40% ex true-ups)”
expectation_evidence: “I put the credible buy-side whisper at $695–715M”; the base scenario expected “$700–715M (+28–31% Y/Y).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

fact_evidence: “Clinical MRD (Signatera) units of 283,000 growing ~56% year-over-year and rising 34,000 units sequentially, its largest sequential increase to date.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for 268–275k”; “above 278k re-rates the story”; management had guided to “quarterly growth along the lines of the trailing 12-month average” (~“+20k”).

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Signatera ASP reached roughly $1,275 in Q2, rather than merely being on track to reach that level by year-end. The preview’s stated target was therefore reached earlier than expected.
fact_evidence: “Signatera ASP rose ~$25 sequentially to roughly $1,275.”
expectation_evidence: “~$1,250 in Q1”; “target $1,275 by year-end”; “Signatera 268k+ units and ASP on track to $1,275.”

description: The preview expected gross margin recovery to 66% or better, but reported gross margin was about 65%. That was below the preview’s 66%+ watch level and the 65.5–66.5% base-case range, although it remained within company guidance.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin held strong at ~65%.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for 66%+”; the base scenario expected “65.5–66.5%.”

description: The call’s Q3 Signatera outlook was for sequential growth above the prior roughly 25,000-unit record, more than the preview’s approximately 20,000-unit trailing-average reference. Management did caution that Q3 would not match Q2’s exceptional 34,000-unit increase.
fact_evidence: “Q3 Signatera growth will not repeat the record 34,000 units—partly inflated by weather-suppressed Q1—but expects to exceed the prior sequential record of roughly 25,000 units.”
expectation_evidence: Management had guided to “quarterly growth along the lines of the trailing 12-month average” (~“+20k”).

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position

expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “a repeat outsized true-up alongside rising DSOs” as the quality-of-earnings risk.

The preview flagged the seven pending histologies but did not provide this quantified ASP contribution or timing.
fact_evidence: “The 7 additional Signatera tumor-type indications submitted to MolDX could add an estimated $150–$200 to ASP, with rolling approvals expected over the next 12–18 months and impact weighted toward 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for … any update on the seven additional histologies in MolDX/CMS review.”

fact_evidence: “Signatera achieved multiple regulatory milestones, becoming the first MRD test with FDA companion-diagnostic approval (muscle-invasive bladder cancer).”

description: Women’s health delivered high-single-digit year-over-year growth despite the preview’s emphasis on Q2 as the seasonally slowest quarter. Management attributed performance to market-share gains and the enhanced Panorama test.
fact_evidence: “Women's health delivered high single-digit year-over-year growth despite seasonal softness, aided by market share gains and the enhanced Panorama test.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 as “management's explicitly stated seasonally slowest women's health quarter.”

fact_evidence: “The enhanced Panorama test … cut the no-call rate from ~2% to 0.5%.”

description: Q2 total revenue of $56.5 million beat the $54.06 million consensus, and net product revenue of $53.6 million exceeded the preview’s implied $51–52 million range and the company’s $50–52 million guide. description: Earnings substantially exceeded expectations: Puma reported $8.2 million of GAAP net income and $0.16 per diluted share, versus consensus EPS of $0.04 and company guidance for $2–4 million of net income.

fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to mark the first-ever back-to-back years of positive year-over-year U.S. NERLYNX demand growth in the drug's launch history.”

description: PLSE expected to have about $68–72 million in cash at quarter-end, and the preview said no financing in the base case. expectation_evidence: “Cash & equiv. 6/30/26: $68–72M”; the base scenario anticipated “no financing announced,” while the preview called a raise a key downside risk.

expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “GAAP net loss ~($20.2M)” and “Non-GAAP net loss ~(17.5).” It also gave “~($21–24M) implied” GAAP consensus.

fact_evidence: “A per-site enrollment cap of 15% is being managed as several early high-volume sites have already reached their cap, with the active study site base expanded to 12 (of up to 30 allowed) and continuing to grow.”

fact_evidence: “The surgical clamp EU feasibility study treated over 70 patients across six sites with 94% pulmonary vein isolation success at three months and average ablation time of 4.41 seconds per patient, remaining on schedule for CE Mark filing before end of 2026.”

expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$0.53M” consensus; the preview’s own estimate was “$0.45M” and its stated range was “$0.4–0.6M.”

expectation_evidence: The Q2 estimate was “Cash & equivalents ... ~$0.80M – $0.90M.”

fact_evidence: Management outlined four plans, with “Plan A”—Gauzy emerging from bankruptcy and resuming full production—“viewed as the most likely outcome, possibly as soon as next month.” A “recent $7 million financing” and court approval had “started funds flowing to rehire workers and restart German production”; automotive programs remained intact and volumes could “ramp back up by the end of the year.”

fact_evidence: “A French court directed the sale of Gauzy’s entire Vision Systems division to Clayens for about EUR 9 million despite a signed EUR 125 million offer for just part of it,” with a “final appeal scheduled for mid-September that could bring substantial capital to Gauzy.”

expectation_evidence: “I model revenue above consensus”; the base case forecast “$215–217M.”
