description: The full-year tax-rate outlook was higher than the preview expected: the new 23–24% range is 0.5 percentage points above the prior 22.5–23.5% range at both ends. Q2 did receive a one-time benefit from resolving a state tax matter.
fact_evidence: “The Q2 effective tax rate was 20.3%, benefiting 5.8% from resolution of a state income tax matter, with full-year rate expected at 23%-24%.”

description: Incremental legal fees tied to CTU litigation weighed on operating income, an expense headwind the preview did not identify. Management said CTU operating income would have grown year over year without those costs.
fact_evidence: “Rising legal fees at CTU tied to previously disclosed litigation weighed on operating income,” and “CTU operating income would have grown year-over-year excluding these incremental costs.”

description: The company raised the low end of its full-year adjusted operating income and adjusted EPS ranges while leaving the high ends unchanged. That was an incremental positive versus the preview’s prior ranges, though it did not reach the preview’s bull-case threshold of adjusted EPS guidance at or above $3.15.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was set at $258-263 million” and “adjusted EPS guidance of $3.10-$3.16.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior guidance of “adj. operating income $254–$263M” and “adj. EPS $3.05–$3.16”; its bull case called for FY adjusted EPS “raised to ≥$3.15.”

description: USAHS’s adjusted operating income nearly doubled in Q2, substantially stronger than the preview’s expectation of double-digit annual growth. Its revenue growth was close to the double-digit trajectory the preview expected.
fact_evidence: “The University of St. Augustine posted the strongest growth, with enrollment up 6% to ~4,200 students, revenue up 10.2% to $40.5 million, and adjusted operating income nearly doubling to $10.7 million from $5.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “double-digit adj. operating income growth for the year” and expected USAHS to “hold[] double-digit trajectory.”

description: Operating adjusted EBITDA was $66 million, well above the preview’s modeled range of $35–45 million. The company called it its best core operating quarter in nearly three years.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million with operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million,” described as “the best core operating quarter in nearly 3 years.”
expectation_evidence: “Operating Adj. EBITDA” Q2 estimate: “$35–45M”; the preview also said “>$40M = the deleveraging story has an engine.”

description: Revenue came in far below the preview’s roughly $295 million model, with trading gains of just $12.9 million versus modeled investment gains of about $75 million. The call attributed the year-over-year decline in trading gains primarily to a lower fair value on the Babcock & Wilcox investment, rather than the roughly flat BW mark the preview assumed.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenues rose $14 million year-over-year to $239 million, but trading gains fell $14.8 million to $12.9 million primarily due to lower fair value on the Babcock & Wilcox investment.”
expectation_evidence: The model estimated “Total revenues” at “~$295M” and “Investment gains” at “~$75M,” based on “SpaceX carry, flat BW.”

description: Net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million, below the preview’s $50–70 million model. This was a substantially weaker bottom-line result than anticipated despite the strong operating adjusted EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net income to common” Q2 estimate: “~$50–70M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management said it could cover both remaining-2026 note maturities with investment securities and cash, addressing the preview’s central concern about whether the September maturity was funded. The stated maturities total just over $300 million, versus $723 million in investment securities plus more than $150 million in cash.
fact_evidence: “Two senior note maturities in the remainder of 2026 totaling just over $300 million ($142 million due September 30 and $164 million due December 31), which management says it can cover with $723 million in investment securities plus over $150 million in cash.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called whether the September maturity was “fully covered” the “single most important sentence on the call,” and noted “$337M against $175.8M of cash at Q1-end.”

description: The preview expected about $70.4 million net from the SpaceX carried-interest position, but the call quantified a $26.4 million first-half increase in carried-interest value from a fund owning SpaceX. The call facts do not establish a like-for-like Q2 amount, but they do not confirm the expected full-sized recognition.
fact_evidence: “First-half gains [were] driven by a $26.4 million increase in carried interest value from a fund owning SpaceX.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had guided to “~$84.2M gross / $70.4M net” from SpaceX carried interest and framed Q2 recognition as a key issue.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The debt picture was mixed against the preview’s estimates: total debt was slightly above the modeled range, while net debt was below its modeled range. Thus gross debt reduction fell a little short of the model, but net leverage was better than expected.
fact_evidence: “Total debt was reduced by $497 million from December 2024 to $1.277 billion at June 30, 2026, with net debt declining $87 million in the quarter to $285 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Total debt” at “~$1.15–1.25B” and “Net debt” at “$300–380M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call cited several signs of Capital Markets activity building: $21 billion of aggregate deal value, five senior producers added, dormant institutional accounts reactivated, and ATM fees more than doubling sequentially. The preview expected Capital Markets momentum to improve, but these concrete activity indicators were not quantified in its outlook.
fact_evidence: “The firm participated in transactions representing $21 billion in aggregate deal value in Q2, added 5 senior producers, reactivated dormant institutional accounts, and saw ATM fees more than double sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 as BRS’s “best capital-raising quarter in five years (~$10B raised)” and said Riley expected deal share to “go up meaningfully.”

description: ResMed reported Q4 revenue of $1.5 billion, above the preview’s $1.46 billion consensus and its $1.48–$1.50 billion bull scenario. The gap was modest, but the result landed above the base case.
fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue grew 9% (8% constant currency) to $1.5 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $1.46B” consensus; the bull scenario was “$1.48–1.50B.”

description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $2.95 beat the $2.90 consensus, but only reached the bottom of the preview’s $2.95–$3.00 buy-side whisper range. That makes the surprise positive versus consensus but not versus the more demanding expectation.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS up 16% to $2.95.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.90” consensus; “Buy-side whisper is realistically $2.95–$3.00.”

description: Q4 gross margin was 62.3%, below the preview’s 62.8%–63.0% base-case range and down about 50 basis points sequentially. ResMed attributed the sequential decline to electronic-component and freight inflation and a 20-basis-point FX headwind.
fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin expanded 90 basis points year-over-year to 62.3%, though it declined ~50 basis points sequentially due to inflation in electronic components/freight and a 20bp FX headwind.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario called for “GM 62.8–63.0%”; the preview identified Q3 gross margin as 62.8%.

description: ResMed issued its first-ever forward revenue and EPS guidance, whereas the preview said the company did not guide revenue or EPS. The FY2027 core revenue range of 5%–7% constant-currency growth is below the preview’s long-term high-single-digit growth framework; core EPS growth is stronger at 12%–14% excluding deal-related dilution.
fact_evidence: “For the first time in company history, ResMed issued forward guidance: FY2027 core constant currency revenue growth of 5%-7% and non-GAAP EPS of $12 to $12.25 (7%-10% reported growth).” It added: “Excluding ~$0.30 dilution from the MatrixCare divestiture and ~$0.20 dilution from the Noctrix acquisition, FY2027 core EPS growth is guided to 12%-14%.”
expectation_evidence: “Company does not guide revenue or EPS”; the long-term algorithm was “high-single-digit revenue growth through 2030 with earnings growing faster than revenue.”

description: The Astral field safety notice creates an unanticipated FY2027 sales suspension and a measurable financial drag: about $75 million of revenue and $0.15 of EPS, with a $42 million provision booked in Q4.
fact_evidence: “The Astral field safety notice creates a ~$75 million (130bp) FY2027 revenue headwind and ~$0.15 EPS drag, as ResMed suspends all new Astral sales for the year; a $42 million provision was booked in Q4.”

description: ResMed disclosed a MatrixCare divestiture that will remove about $220 million in revenue and $58 million in non-GAAP operating profit, and will dilute FY2027 EPS by about $0.30. The preview discussed portfolio-review questions but did not anticipate a sale; TSAs are expected to largely offset stranded costs in year one.
fact_evidence: “The MatrixCare divestiture, expected to close around September 1, removes ~$220 million in revenue and $58 million in non-GAAP operating profit, with TSAs expected to largely offset stranded costs in year one.” The FY2027 guide excludes “~$0.30 dilution from the MatrixCare divestiture.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said that mid-single-digit Residential Care Software growth could “revive[] portfolio-review questions,” but did not forecast a divestiture.

description: ResMed announced a much larger FY2027 shareholder-return program than the preview specified: over $1.85 billion in total, including $1.5 billion of buybacks and a 10% dividend increase. The preview noted a planned Q4 buyback and the existing dividend, but not a comparable FY2027 commitment.
fact_evidence: “ResMed plans to return over $1.85 billion to shareholders in FY2027 (up over 75% YoY), including $1.5 billion in buybacks (with a $450 million accelerated repurchase funded by MatrixCare proceeds) and a 10% dividend increase to $0.66/share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$175M buyback planned for Q4” and a “$0.60 dividend,” and flagged capital allocation as a topic for the incoming CFO.

description: Life-support device revenue fell sharply in both reported regions—45% in the Americas and 38% in Rest of World. The preview focused on expected growth in total devices and did not flag declines of this scale in life-support products.
fact_evidence: “Q4 Americas life support device revenue fell 45% and Rest-of-World fell 38%.”

description: SIGA’s Q2 revenue was about $41 million, well above the preview’s modeled ~$23 million. The main driver was $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered in Q2 versus roughly $5 million modeled for the quarter; that delivery also completed the final product order under the 19C contract earlier than the preview’s end-of-Q3 deadline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 product-related revenues were $38 million,” including “$24 million of IV TPOXX” and $13 million of oral TPOXX; R&D revenue was approximately $3 million. The Q2 IV delivery “fulfilled the final product order under SIGA's 19C contract.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 total revenue at “~$23M” (range $18–30M) and IV TPOXX at “~$5M”; it said $26M of IV deliveries was due by the end of Q3.

description: Quarterly profitability materially exceeded the modeled level: net income was about $12 million and diluted EPS was $0.17, compared with modeled net income of ~$5 million and EPS of ~$0.07. Pre-tax operating income was also about $14 million versus the preview’s ~$6 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was approximately $12 million, or $0.17 fully diluted EPS”; pre-tax operating income was “approximately $14 million for the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Operating income ~$6M,” “Net income ~$5M,” and diluted “EPS ~$0.07.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended June above the preview’s expected range: SIGA reported approximately $118 million, versus the preview’s estimate of $95–105 million.
fact_evidence: SIGA ended June 30, 2026 with “approximately $118 million in cash and no debt.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash (6/30/26) ~$95–105M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management described a concrete goal of pursuing a new international customer contract with an order and hopes to deliver against it by March next year. The preview identified international orders as a possible upside, but did not point to this specific target or timing.
fact_evidence: Management is “targeting a new international customer contract with an order, and hopes to deliver against that order by March of next year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any first order” or “any new international procurement” as items to watch, and listed a new international order as a bull-case possibility.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $17 million, above the preview’s $11–13 million guided range and roughly $5 million above its ~$12 million consensus estimate. This was a substantially stronger result than expected.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $17 million,” well above the guided range of “$11-13 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$12M” consensus; company guide “$11–13M.”

description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39–46 million from $35–45 million, rather than merely maintaining the prior range as the preview’s base case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Raising adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39-46 million from $35-45 million.”
expectation_evidence: Base case: “FY reaffirmed at $280–295M and EBITDA $35–45M.” The preview also called maintaining $35–45M the key test.

description: Q2 revenue was about $72.1 million, below the $73.54 million consensus and at the bottom of the company’s $72–77 million range. The miss was modest, but weaker than the preview’s base-case $73–75 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue came in at approximately $72.1 million,” at the “lower end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus: “$73.54M”; base case: “$73–75M.”

description: Despite the stronger Q2 and higher full-year EBITDA outlook, management said second-half adjusted EBITDA would be under $17 million versus about $25 million in the first half, citing lower gross margins, increased R&D and commercial spending, and normalizing expenses. That signals a sharper near-term slowdown than the preview’s cost-discipline framing suggested.
fact_evidence: “Second-half adjusted EBITDA is expected to decline to under $17 million versus $25 million in the first half,” due to gross margins of about 68%, $4 million more R&D/commercial spend, and normalizing operating expenses.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “Cost cuts … continue offsetting volume decline,” and its central question was whether the “$35–45M FY EBITDA guide survives.”

description: The FY26 revenue range was reduced again: its top end fell from $295 million to $290 million, while the low end stayed at $280 million. The preview’s base case expected the prior range to be reaffirmed.
fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year revenue guidance to $280-290 million (cutting the top end).”
expectation_evidence: Q1 baseline FY26 revenue guidance: “$280–295M.” Base case: “FY reaffirmed at $280–295M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company reported only 770 systems placed, below the preview’s base-case expectation of 800–900 and continuing the equipment weakness the preview highlighted. This was a weaker placement result than expected, though not as low as the preview’s bear-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Only 770 systems placed versus 957 in the prior year,” reflecting continued capital equipment weakness.
expectation_evidence: Base case: “placements 800–900”; bull case: “placements >900.”

description: The company moved beyond the reverse-split risk discussed in the preview and said it would seek shareholder approval at a September 22 special meeting. This makes the potential listing-related action more concrete than the preview’s discussion of a possible future split.
fact_evidence: “The company received a NASDAQ notice for trading below the $1 minimum bid price and will seek shareholder approval for a reverse stock split at a September 22 special meeting.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a reverse split might be required and warned that “any mention of a reverse split” would pull forward dilution fears; it described the deadline and possible second 180-day period.

description: Consumables revenue declined 3.5%, a milder decline than the preview’s base-case estimate of 4–6%. The reported decline was still the second consecutive one, and the call did not provide the ex-China figure the preview identified as the key test.
fact_evidence: “Consumables revenue declined 3.5% to $53.9 million on lower utilization,” marking the “second consecutive quarterly decline.”
expectation_evidence: Base case: “consumables −4–6%”; the preview ranked “Consumables revenue ex-China” as the highest-importance metric.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management outlined a US device-rental program and a product pipeline spanning a Q4 booster, a non-HydroFacial device planned for 2027, and a next-generation HydroFacial platform targeted for 2028. These were additional growth initiatives not anticipated in the preview, though most are not near-term revenue catalysts.
fact_evidence: “New growth initiatives include a US device rental program launched in August, a next-generation HydroFacial platform targeting a 2028 launch, a new clinically validated booster in Q4, and a new non-HydroFacial device planned for 2027.”

description: The preview treated Q2 revenue of about $122.5 million as essentially set at the pre-announced high end; the reported $123.8 million was about $1.3 million above that level and grew 10.8% year over year, faster than the preview's 9.3%–9.6% estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $123.8 million, up 10.8% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “High end → ~$122.5M”; revenue growth expected at “+9.3% to +9.6%.”

description: Q2 profitability substantially exceeded the preview's expected high-end operating income: the reported 12.9% non-GAAP operating margin implies roughly $16 million of operating income on the reported revenue, versus the preview's estimate of about $10.3 million. The preview had characterized the quarter as de-risked, but this was a notable additional margin beat.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 12.9%, up 370 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income” consensus “~$10.3M”; pre-announced “High end → ~$10.3M.”

description: The company raised its full-year profitability outlook well beyond the prior ranges: non-GAAP operating income guidance is now $68.3–$70.3 million versus $54.9–$60.4 million, and EPS is $1.11–$1.15 versus $0.88–$0.97. The preview identified the full-year outlook as the central uncertainty but expected, at most, a maintained or narrowed outlook in its base case.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance, with non-GAAP operating income of $68.3–$70.3 million … and non-GAAP EPS of $1.11–$1.15.”
expectation_evidence: Prior FY2026 guidance: non-GAAP operating income “$54.9–$60.4M,” non-GAAP EPS “$0.88–$0.97”; base case: “Maintained, narrowed to high half.”

description: Management raised the Q4 exit-margin target to about 17%, above the preview's stated target of about 15% and the preview's bull-case threshold of 17%–18%+. This indicates more of the cost savings is expected to flow through to margins than the prior target implied.
fact_evidence: “The company guided to exit Q4 2026 with a non-GAAP operating margin near 17%.”
expectation_evidence: Management targeted exiting Q4'26 at “~15% non-GAAP operating margin”; the preview said buy-side wanted “≥17%.”

description: The announced workforce reduction was already known, but management now says it will reduce the non-GAAP cost structure by at least $50 million annually, above the preview's estimated $30–$40 million of gross annualized savings. Full realization is not expected until 2027, which tempers the benefit near term.
fact_evidence: “A roughly 20% headcount reduction expected to cut its non-GAAP cost structure by at least $50 million on an annualized run-rate basis, though full realization won't occur until 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$30–40M gross annualized savings.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance is a little softer than the preview's implied H2 run rate: the $123.3–$124.1 million range has a midpoint of $123.7 million, below the preview's implied roughly $124–$126 million per quarter. Management also expects CRPO to moderate and the sub-$30,000 customer cohort to turn slightly negative before stabilizing in 2027.
fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $123.3–$124.1 million implies deceleration, with management expecting CRPO to moderate and the sub-30K cohort to turn slightly negative before stabilizing in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The FY guide implied H2 revenue of “$248.5–$251.5M, or ~$124–$126M per quarter”; the preview said “≥$124M = intact.”

description: Management identified the lapping of the Newswhip acquisition starting in Q3 as an additional headwind. The preview discussed possible SMB weakness and decelerating growth, but did not flag this specific acquisition comparison as a source of pressure.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged continuing headwinds including lapping the Newswhip acquisition starting Q3 2026.”

description: The company said it plans to begin executing its $50 million buyback this quarter. The preview highlighted buyback pace as a key signal and warned that zero usage would be a negative tell, so a stated near-term start is a positive update, although no execution amount was given.
fact_evidence: “Planning to begin executing its $50 million buyback this quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “~10% of market cap” and that “zero usage is a tell”; it described aggressive execution as a bull-case signal.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call disclosed stronger contract-duration and booking indicators that the preview had not quantified: multi-year contracts are now nearly half of the mix, compared with about one-third two years ago, and Q2 ACV rose 14.8% year over year. These provide new evidence of contract strength beyond the preview's focus on larger customers.
fact_evidence: “Multi-year contracts now represent nearly half of the contract mix, up from about one-third two years ago, and Q2 ACV increased 14.8% year-over-year.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was $8.3 million, up about 60% year over year, with trailing-12-month free cash flow around $54 million. The preview did not provide a free-cash-flow expectation, so this is new favorable information rather than a quantified beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP free cash flow was $8.3 million, up approximately 60% year-over-year, bringing trailing-12-month free cash flow to roughly $54 million.”

description: Q2 revenue was $11.4 million, above the preview’s $10.0–10.5 million consensus range and its $9.3 million estimate. It also grew 1.7% year over year, rather than declining 6%–11% as consensus implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $11.4 million, up only 1.7% year-over-year from $11.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$10.0–10.5M” and “YoY implied | −6% to −11%”; the preview’s own estimate was “$9.3M.”

description: Management reiterated the $54–57 million full-year revenue range instead of cutting it or narrowing it toward the low end, as the preview’s base case anticipated. That leaves the previously stated growth target intact despite the preview’s concerns about the H2 ramp.
fact_evidence: “The company reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $54 million to $57 million.”
expectation_evidence: “A cut or a ‘narrow to the low end’ is my base case”; the base scenario anticipated the guide being “trimmed to ~$48–52M or narrowed to low end.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: CMS granted a new G-code extending TriNav reimbursement to the office-based lab setting, adding a site of care and potentially widening access. The preview did not identify this reimbursement expansion as an expected catalyst.
fact_evidence: “In July, CMS granted a new G-code extending TriNav reimbursement into the office-based lab (OBL) setting, expanding site-of-care access.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at $46.3 million, below the preview’s expected $48–50 million. The gap was $1.7–3.7 million versus that estimate.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $46.3 million in cash, which management believes fully funds its strategic growth plan.”

description: Sales and marketing expense reached $11.4 million—equal to quarterly revenue—and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to about $7.1 million. The preview flagged sales-force ramp costs and productivity as issues, but did not anticipate this reported spending level or the wider EBITDA loss.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to approximately $7.1 million from $5.3 million in Q2 2025, driven by sales force expansion costs”; “Sales and marketing expenses surged to $11.4 million from $7.2 million a year earlier, equaling the entire quarter's revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted a “6–9 month ramp on new hires” and flagged “Sales-force productivity” as a key metric to watch, without giving an expense or EBITDA forecast.

description: Gross margin was 86.8%, slightly above the preview’s expected 85–86% range. The reported improvement was attributed to lower TriNav unit costs and manufacturing improvements.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 86.8% from 83.9% year-over-year due to lower TriNav unit costs and manufacturing improvements.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~85–86%.”

description: Q2 revenue was $56.4 million, below the preview’s $60.5 million consensus and its $58–62 million base case; the preview expected year-over-year growth, but revenue was essentially flat. This is weaker than expected even though it landed just above the preview’s bear-case range.
fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $56.4 million, essentially flat year-over-year versus $56.8 million, as retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of the quarter.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $60.5M”; “YoY +6.6%”; base scenario: “$58–62M (in line).”

description: Gross margin was reported at 38.8%, far above the preview’s 29–32% estimate, but $4.3 million of tariff refunds lifted the headline figure. Excluding those refunds, margin was approximately 31.2%—within the preview’s expected range rather than a comparable jump in underlying performance.
fact_evidence: Gross margin rose 660 basis points to 38.8% from 32.2%, but excluding $4.3 million of tariff refunds the underlying margin was approximately 31.2%.
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~29–32% (est.)”; the preview said the bull case required “a snapback toward 32%+.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Retail partners continued to keep channel inventory below historical norms, rather than showing the rebound the preview said would test management’s explanation for Q1 weakness. That leaves the expected channel restock unconfirmed.
fact_evidence: Retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of the quarter.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 would test management’s expectation that channel inventories would “rebound,” and identified “channel restock lands” as a bull-case driver.

description: Operating expenses rose sharply to 44% of revenue, and the net loss widened despite improved gross margins. That runs counter to the operating-expense leverage the preview said was needed to support the full-year EBITDA target, although adjusted EBITDA did turn positive.
fact_evidence: Operating expenses jumped to $24.9 million (44% of revenue) from $18.6 million (33% of revenue), reflecting increased marketing spend; net loss widened to $7.3 million from $2.9 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview said meeting the EBITDA guide “demands simultaneous volume, gross margin, and opex leverage”; its Q2 adjusted EBITDA estimate was “~$0M.”

description: The company repurchased roughly $25 million of stock in one quarter, a substantial use of the authorization despite the balance-sheet concerns the preview highlighted. The preview explicitly identified an aggressive repurchase as a possible signal of confidence, so the scale of the buyback is favorable versus a pause.
fact_evidence: The company repurchased roughly $25 million of stock (nearly 2 million shares at an average $12.53) in Q2, leaving about $31 million remaining under its buyback authorization.
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch buyback pace against “$56M remaining authorization” and that “aggressive repurchase signals confidence; a pause signals liquidity discipline.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: New tariff actions raised the effective rate on China and Vietnam imports, an unflagged cost risk, though management expects to largely offset the impact without materially affecting profitability.
fact_evidence: New tariff actions raised the effective rate on China and Vietnam imports to approximately 12.5% from 10%, but management expects to largely mitigate the impact without materially affecting profitability.

description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $1.3 million, above the preview’s roughly breakeven estimate, even as revenue missed and marketing costs rose.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA improved to positive $1.3 million from negative $3.0 million in the prior year period, reflecting stronger gross margins.
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$0M (est.).”

description: Q2 revenue was $73.2 million, about 6% below the preview’s $78.13 million consensus, and the year-over-year decline was 25% rather than the expected 20%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell 25% year-over-year to $73.2 million,” with continued demand weakness in both end markets.
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $78.13M”; implied year-over-year decline: “-20.0%.”

description: A one-time $5.1 million tariff recovery lifted adjusted EPS to $0.34, far above the $0.03 consensus, but EPS was only about $0.04 excluding the recovery. The recovery is excluded from full-year guidance, so the headline beat did not represent a comparable improvement in underlying earnings.
fact_evidence: “A non-recurring $5.1 million tariff recovery boosted adjusted EPS to $0.34 per diluted share”; excluding it, adjusted non-GAAP profit was “~$0.04 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. non-GAAP diluted EPS | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $0.03.”

description: Gross margin excluding the tariff recovery was about 27%, below the preview’s key 28% threshold and down from 29.9% a year earlier. Higher component costs and unfavorable currency were additional pressures.
fact_evidence: Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was “35.4% as reported but only ~27% excluding the tariff recovery, down from 29.9% a year ago,” pressured by “~240 bps of higher component costs and ~150 bps of unfavorable currency.”

description: Airbnb raised its full-year revenue outlook to at least mid-teens growth from low-to-mid-teens growth, improving on the preview’s expected reaffirmation of the prior framework.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance, now expecting revenue growth of at least mid-teens (up from low-to-mid teens).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 framework was “low-to-mid-teens” revenue growth and described its base case as “FY reaffirmed.”

description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA margin floor rose to at least 35.5%, above the preview’s expectation that Airbnb would reaffirm a 35% floor.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5% (up from 35%).”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA margin ≥35% — reaffirm or hedge”; the base case expected “FY reaffirmed.”

description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to decline slightly year over year because of investment timing, a softer near-term margin outlook than the preview’s base case of an intact margin story.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be down slightly year-over-year due to investment timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described the “margin story” as “intact,” while warning that reinvestment could eat into margin in its bear case.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.3 billion, above the preview’s derived estimate of about $1.25 billion, even though the reported 35% margin matched the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.3 billion at a 35% margin.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$1.25B / ~35%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: First-time bookers grew 11%, the highest rate in four years, with acceleration across several core markets. The preview discussed new World Cup guests but did not anticipate this broader strength in first-time booking growth.
fact_evidence: “First-time bookers grew 11%, the highest growth rate in four years, with acceleration in core markets including the U.S., France, U.K. and Australia.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “1 in 6 tournament guests are new to Airbnb” but gave no expectation for overall first-time booker growth.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Hotel nights are growing about three times faster than home nights, and roughly 35% of first-time hotel guests later book a home. The preview flagged hotels as a small-scale area to watch but did not anticipate these growth and conversion figures.
fact_evidence: “Hotel nights are growing approximately 3x faster than the homes business despite still being a single-digit percentage of nights booked, and roughly 35% of first-time hotel guests return to book a home.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “hotel nights <1% of total” and advised investors to “watch for first hard numbers” on hotels.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Airbnb said its single service fee, which pressures pricing downward to improve competitiveness, already covers about half of active listings and is expected to reach most remaining hosts by year-end. The preview did not flag this broad rollout or its pricing implications.
fact_evidence: “The single service fee, which pressures pricing downward for competitiveness, now covers about half of active listings and is expected to roll out to the majority of remaining hosts by year-end.”

description: AI reduced customer-support cost per booking by about 16% year over year, with nearly 45% of AI-assistant issues resolved without a human agent. The preview did not anticipate these quantified efficiency gains.
fact_evidence: “AI adoption cut customer support cost per booking by about 16% year-over-year, with nearly 45% of AI-assistant issues resolved without a human agent.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was $1.3 billion and trailing-twelve-month free cash flow reached $4.8 billion, above the preview’s $4.5 billion TTM figure. The reported TTM margin was 37%, versus the preview’s 36%.
fact_evidence: “Airbnb generated $1.3 billion of free cash flow in Q2 (TTM $4.8 billion, 37% margin).”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$4.5B TTM FCF (36% margin).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Q2 net income included a $77 million tax benefit, an unanticipated one-off that boosted the reported $816 million result.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $816 million, boosted by a $77 million tax benefit.”

description: Adjusted EPS of $0.91 substantially exceeded the preview’s adjusted estimate range of $0.62–$0.66. GAAP EPS was also $0.67, above the preview’s cited $0.37 GAAP bogey, and rose year over year rather than declining.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose to $0.91 from $0.85 year-over-year”; “GAAP net income slipped to $30.3 million from $31 million but improved to $0.67 per share from $0.64.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$0.62–0.66 as the adjusted Street bogey and ~$0.37 as the GAAP bogey”; the preview also cites a $0.51 EPS estimate.

description: AMPH reported Q2 revenue of $183.9 million, above the preview’s estimates of $179.92 million and $182.06 million, though within its stated base-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 5% year-over-year to $183.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue estimates of “$179.92M” and “$182.06M,” and a base case of “$177–183M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: BAQSIMI sales still declined despite substantial prescription growth: higher rebates and 340B discounts more than offset the increase in prescriptions. That leaves the expected price-and-rebate recovery unresolved, despite the preview’s focus on the May price increase and 340B work.
fact_evidence: “BAQSIMI net sales fell 3% to $45.5 million despite ~17% prescription growth,” as lower prices from higher rebates and 340B discounts cut sales by “~$8.1 million” versus a “$6.9 million unit volume gain.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said BAQSIMI’s 2026 guidance was “flat to low-single-digit growth” and called for watching whether “the May 1 price increase and the third-party 340B duplicate-discount work show up.”

description: The new ipratropium product generated $8.4 million in its first quarter, below the preview’s threshold for a genuine upside surprise of roughly $10–12 million or more. It was nevertheless approaching its targeted market-share range.
fact_evidence: “The newly launched ipratropium bromide (generic Atrovent) contributed $8.4 million in sales in its first quarter and is approaching its 50%-80% targeted market share goal.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a disclosed number above ~$10–12M is a genuine upside surprise” and described vagueness about its contribution as potentially underwhelming.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call disclosed an FDA warning letter at IMS, a business representing about one-third of corporate sales, and several quarters of added remediation expense. The preview did not flag this development; continued manufacturing and shipping without a required shutdown limits the immediate disruption.
fact_evidence: “IMS, which represents about one-third of corporate sales, received an FDA warning letter tied to a December 2025 inspection but continues manufacturing and shipping without a required shutdown”; remediation is expected to add “$2 million to $3 million per quarter for several quarters,” with capex redirected from the Amphastar facility.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: BAQSIMI’s third contract year crossed the $175 million sales threshold, triggering a $100 million payment to Eli Lilly in Q3 2026—an obligation the preview did not discuss.
fact_evidence: “BAQSIMI generated $178.3 million in net sales in its third contract year, exceeding the $175 million threshold and triggering a $100 million milestone payment to Eli Lilly due in Q3 2026.”

description: AMPH repurchased about $45 million of shares, accelerating from the $29.5 million bought back in Q1 and exceeding the preview’s expectation of continued aggressive repurchases.
fact_evidence: “The company accelerated buybacks, repurchasing roughly $45 million of shares in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Buyback pace” as a key metric, cited “$29.5M in Q1,” and called for “continued aggressive repurchase.”

description: AMN reported Q2 revenue of $673 million, well above the preview’s $626 million consensus and the company’s $620–635 million guidance. The $25 million of labor-disruption revenue, versus $10 million assumed in guidance, contributed to the beat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $673 million,” “6% above the high end of guidance”; “Labor disruption revenue came in at $25 million versus the $10 million assumed in guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus **$626M**”; company guide “$620–635M”; Q2 guidance “embeds only ~$10M.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.77, far above the preview’s $0.22 consensus. This was a much larger earnings beat than the revenue beat alone would suggest, though non-recurring items also lifted EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS jumped to $0.77 from $0.30 a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS … Q2'26 Consensus **$0.22**.”

description: Reported adjusted EBITDA margin reached 10.9%, far above the preview’s 6.7–7.2% guidance range, but about $27 million of non-recurring true-ups and reserve reversals added 370 basis points. Excluding that boost, the margin was roughly 7.2%, near the expected range, so the headline EBITDA strength is not expected to repeat in Q3.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $73 million (10.9% of revenue)”; “roughly $27 million in non-recurring items … added 370 basis points to EBITDA margin and are not expected to repeat in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … 6.7–7.2% margin.”

description: Nurse and Allied revenue grew 11% to $422 million, rather than being flat to down 2% as implied by the preview’s segment guide. Travel nurse and allied volumes both grew, with AMN describing their growth rates as the strongest in four years.
fact_evidence: “The Nurse and Allied segment grew revenue 11% to $422 million (12% above consensus), with travel nurse volume up 6% and allied volume up 7%, the highest growth rates in four years.”
expectation_evidence: Nurse & Allied was guided “Flat to −2%,” with implied revenue of “$374–382M.” The preview said the market wanted “volume growth ≥5% YoY.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Travel nurse orders strengthened substantially after turning positive in May: by early August they were up about 40% year over year and 20% above August 2024. That supports projected double-digit Q3 volume growth and is stronger forward momentum than the preview’s focus on whether growth could return consistently.
fact_evidence: “Travel nurse orders turned positive in May and by early August were up about 40% year-over-year and 20% higher than August 2024, supporting projected double-digit Q3 volume growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 travel nurse volume was “on the cusp of getting back to positive year-over-year growth on a consistent basis” and identified Q2 volume growth as a key debate.

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $640–655 million is above the preview’s base-case range of $620–650 million, despite only $7–8 million of strike revenue being included. The higher-than-expected guide therefore does not rely on the larger strike contribution anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of $640-655 million”; “only $7-8 million of strike revenue is embedded in the Q3 outlook.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “Q3 guided $620–650M with BWH strike revenue offsetting core softness” and its bull case looked for “~$650M+ with $30M+ disruption revenue.”

description: The Q3 outlook includes only $7–8 million of strike revenue, below the preview’s estimate that the known BWH event alone could contribute $20–35 million. The preview’s figure was an analyst estimate, not company guidance, but the reported embedded amount is notably lower.
fact_evidence: “Only $7-8 million of strike revenue is embedded in the Q3 outlook.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated BWH alone could be “$20–35M of Q3 revenue” and described a base case with BWH strike revenue offsetting core softness.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Physician and Leadership revenue declined 6%, within the preview’s expected range, but search activity was much stronger: physician search bookings rose 40% and leadership search volume rose 60%. The preview did not anticipate this strength in search.
fact_evidence: “Physician and Leadership Solutions revenue fell 6% to $165 million, though search revenue grew 27% year-over-year with physician search bookings up 40% and leadership search volume up 60%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview guided to Physician & Leadership revenue of “−6% to −8%” and discussed locums as a structural headwind, with no expectation stated for search growth.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at $362 million, substantially above the preview’s $175 million expectation, partly because of $117 million in strike-related client deposits. The balance-sheet figure is therefore higher than expected, but the deposits help explain the difference.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $362 million in cash (well above the $175 million expected due to $117 million in strike-related client deposits).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 working capital should unwind sharply” and expected a “big negative FCF quarter”; it also referenced about $175 million in client deposits retained from Q1.

description: Technology and Workforce revenue was in line with its expected decline, but management said language-services pricing pressure is expected to continue through 2026. That extends the pricing headwind beyond the preview’s discussion of Q1 pricing and a possible segment inflection.
fact_evidence: “Technology and Workforce Solutions revenue declined 15% to $87 million with language services pricing down 8% year-over-year while volume was flat, and management expects continued pricing headwinds through 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Technology & Workforce to decline “−14% to −16%” and said language services in Q1 showed “200bps sequential margin improvement on a new offshore/customer-device service model.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Kaiser contract is now in a competitive RFP process ahead of its year-end 2026 expiration. The preview flagged Kaiser concentration and renewal commentary as a tail risk, but did not indicate that a competitive process was underway.
fact_evidence: “The Kaiser contract expires at the end of 2026 and is now in a competitive RFP process.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Client concentration — Kaiser is roughly 22% of revenue; any contract/renewal commentary is a tail risk in both directions.”

description: AMN lowered its expectations for international nurse growth in 2027 toward single digits because of embassy appointment backlogs and travel bans. The preview did not flag this outlook reduction.
fact_evidence: “International nurse growth expectations for 2027 were lowered toward single digits due to embassy appointment backlogs and travel bans.”

description: CarGurus raised its full-year profitability outlook: instead of the previewed 1.5–2.5 points of adjusted EBITDA margin compression, it now expects only about 0.5–1.5 points of compression, citing AI-driven efficiency gains.
fact_evidence: Management now expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA margins to compress only ~50 to 150 basis points versus 2025, citing AI-driven efficiency gains.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 guide: adj. EBITDA margin down 1.5–2.5pts vs. 2025 (explicit “investment year”).

description: International revenue grew 28%, below the preview’s 30% threshold for avoiding a negative surprise and well below the 39% growth cited for Q1.
fact_evidence: International revenue growing 28% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: “Sub-30% growth would be a negative surprise.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described dealer spending as softer than the preview’s stable-to-modestly-supportive market backdrop suggested, citing dealer margin pressure, fewer days on lot, and FTC pricing rules. It tempered that concern by calling the factors temporary and noting some improvement over the first half.
fact_evidence: Management attributes softer dealer spending to temporary factors—dealer margin pressure, fewer days on lot, and FTC all-in pricing rules—rather than structural issues, noting some improvement over the first half.
expectation_evidence: “Net: a stable-to-modestly-supportive dealer ad-spend environment.”

description: Q2 buybacks were only $29 million, a sharp reduction from the $175 million repurchased in Q1 and a realization of the preview’s concern that a much slower pace could remove an EPS tailwind. Year-to-date repurchases nevertheless reached $204 million of the $250 million program.
fact_evidence: The company repurchased $29 million in shares in Q2 (bringing year-to-date buybacks to $204 million of the $250 million 2026 program).
expectation_evidence: “A sharply reduced Q2 repurchase pace removes an EPS crutch and signals balance-sheet caution.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position

fact_evidence: The company converted 103% of adjusted EBITDA into $88 million of free cash flow, ending the quarter with $122 million in cash, up $50 million sequentially.
expectation_evidence: “$175M of buyback against $63.2M of FCF drew cash down to $72M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

expectation_evidence: “The question the buy side will press: how much of this is free/bundled trial versus incremental ARPU already inside QARSD?”

expectation_evidence: “Any quantification of incremental ARPU from Shopper Signals / PriceVantage / Dealership Mode would be a narrative unlock; continued adoption-only stats will read as deflection.”

description: Total operating revenue and other income was $744.3 million, above the preview’s $716.35 million consensus and its $690–720 million base case. That is a positive departure from the preview’s modal expectation of an optical revenue miss.
fact_evidence: “Total operating revenue and other income increased 89% year-over-year to $744.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $716.35M”; the base case forecast was “$690–720M” and the bottom line said the modal outcome was “a revenue ‘miss’.”

description: Diluted EPS of $2.50 edged above the preview’s working consensus range of $2.41–$2.49, though it was within the preview’s broader base-case range of $2.35–$2.60. The beat versus the cited consensus band was narrow.
fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to common shareholders was $47.4 million … or $2.50 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat $2.41–$2.49 as the working consensus band.”

description: ROE reached 28.1%, above the preview’s recent mid-20s reference point and the company’s 20% long-term target. That was stronger than simply sustaining the mid-20s level the preview identified as a potential positive signal.
fact_evidence: “Return on average equity reached 28.1%, materially exceeding the company's long-term target of 20%.”
expectation_evidence: “ROE … 26.8%” in Q1; “Sustained mid-20s materially re-rates the multiple.”

description: Interest expense was essentially flat sequentially at about $123 million, even though the preview cited management’s expectation for quarterly interest expense to increase through 2026. The company also reported tighter spreads on term ABS and its first AAA bond ratings, favorable funding developments the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Interest expense more than doubled to $123 million from $54 million”; it reflected Mercury debt and growth financing, but “the company issued term ABS at tighter spreads and achieved its first AAA bond ratings.”
expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly guided to ‘increased quarterly interest expense throughout 2026.’”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

fact_evidence: “Total managed receivables grew approximately 126% year-over-year to $6.9 billion, up 2.5% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “receivables ~$7.0B.”

fact_evidence: “Management expects ROE to revert toward 20% as the company delevers.”
expectation_evidence: “Sustained mid-20s materially re-rates the multiple”; the base case anticipated “no change to the 20% ROE framing.”

description: Direct mail originations were behind plan and solicitation volumes above 50% year over year were raising acquisition costs. fact_evidence: “Direct mail solicitation volumes are up over 50% year-over-year, raising customer acquisition costs and leaving direct mail originations behind plan, though digital originations are running ahead of plan.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said mail response rates were “somewhat lower due to increased mail solicitation” and flagged “acquisition cost per account.”

description: The quarter still benefited from a $5.5 million favorable Mercury contingent-consideration adjustment. fact_evidence: “A $5.5 million favorable adjustment to Mercury-related contingent consideration boosted the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 included “~$13M of favorable contingent-consideration release” and that consensus required “underlying sequential improvement”; it also noted concern if a beat came from “another favorable mark.”

description: Management introduced the possibility of capital actions if ROE remains in the high 20s. The preview discussed the ROE target and returns but did not flag potential capital actions.
fact_evidence: “Capital actions [are] possible if it stays in the high 20s.”

description: Century’s Q3 adjusted EBITDA guide of $325–345 million was well above the preview’s $270–300 million base-case expectation. The guide is especially strong given management’s stated summer energy and hedge-settlement headwinds.
fact_evidence: Management guided Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA to a range of $325 million to $345 million, with headwinds including $10-15 million in summer energy costs and $20-25 million from realized hedge settlements.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Q3 guided EBITDA of $270–300M; it said consensus math needed at least $300M.

description: Century’s Q2 net sales were $752 million, well below the preview’s $818.7 million consensus estimate, even though realized LME and regional premiums were higher and shipments increased sequentially.
fact_evidence: Q2 net sales rose $103 million sequentially to $752 million, driven by higher realized LME and regional premiums, plus a 6% shipment increase to ~131,000 tonnes.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2'26 consensus revenue of $818.7M.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Century shipped about 131,000 tonnes in Q2, below the preview’s expected recovery toward 135,000–145,000 tonnes. Shipments did rise 6% sequentially, but the quarter fell short of the anticipated range.
fact_evidence: Shipments increased 6% to ~131,000 tonnes.
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 shipments should recover from 122,865t toward ~135–145kt.

description: Century’s adjusted EPS of $2.46 exceeded the preview’s $2.35 consensus estimate, despite the revenue shortfall.
fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted net income was $257 million ($2.46/share).
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2'26 consensus adjusted EPS of $2.35.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Century’s realized LME price was $3,250 per tonne, $75 above the $3,175-per-tonne assumption in its Q2 guide. The preview considered that assumption conservative-to-fair, so the realized price was a modest favorable variance.
fact_evidence: Realized LME was up $350 to $3,250/tonne.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2'26 guided realized LME at $3,175/t and said the assumption looked “conservative-to-fair.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Century reduced net debt to $98 million, substantially below the preview’s cited $220 million level, and reported that cash exceeded total debt by the end of July. The preview had noted that capital returns might become possible after credits and recoveries cleared, but did not anticipate this degree of debt reduction.
fact_evidence: Net debt reduced to $98 million with $66 million in debt repayments, and cash on hand exceeded total debt as of end of July after receiving a $94 million 45X tax credit and ~$20 million in insurance recoveries.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited net debt of $220M and said returns were possible once project spend, insurance recoveries and 45X credits cleared.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: A new executive order lets Century import up to 300,000 metric tons annually from 2027 at a 25% tariff rather than 50%, creating a potential earnings and cash-flow benefit that the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: A new July 20 executive order will let Century import up to 300,000 metric tons annually at a reduced 25% tariff (versus 50%) starting in 2027, a potentially material EBITDA and cash flow benefit to help fund the Oklahoma project.

description: Century’s retained 6.8% Hawesville stake gained a potential monetization catalyst after partner TeraWulf signed Anthropic to a 20-year lease expected to generate about $19 billion in total lease revenue. The preview did not anticipate this data-center development.
fact_evidence: Century's retained 6.8% stake in the Hawesville data center gained value as partner TeraWulf signed Anthropic to a 20-year lease expected to generate ~$19 billion in total lease revenue, with monetization possible beginning one year after 2027 energization.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described a persistent global aluminum deficit of about 1 million tonnes and inventory days approaching all-time lows, supporting elevated prices. That outlook contrasts with the preview’s emphasis on falling LME prices and a potential H2 price reset.
fact_evidence: Management expects a persistent global aluminum deficit of ~1 million tonnes in 2026 continuing into 2027, with global inventory days of consumption approaching all-time lows, supporting elevated prices.
expectation_evidence: The preview described LME aluminum’s slide from ~$3,790–3,855/t to ~$3,170/t in late July and said the market had pre-traded the H2 price reset.

description: Century expects the new Jamalco turbine to enable fully self-generated energy from August and save roughly $20 per tonne, an operational cost benefit the preview did not specify. Lower-quality bauxite remains a modest offsetting headwind for a couple more quarters.
fact_evidence: The new TG4 power turbine at Jamalco enables full self-generated energy starting August, delivering roughly $20/tonne in cost savings, though lower-quality bauxite remains a modest headwind for a couple more quarters.

description: Q2 revenue was $1.4 million, far below the preview’s $11.33 million consensus estimate. fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue fell to $1.4 million from $18.7 million in Q2 2025, primarily due to the conclusion of the BMS and Astellas collaborations”; the July Regeneron payment is “to be recognized over several years as work progresses.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026E | $11.33M”; the preview says consensus “clearly assumes ratable” recognition of the Regeneron payment.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position

fact_evidence: “CytomX ended Q2 2026 with $330.3 million in cash”; it “received an additional $37 million payment from Regeneron in July,” bringing pro forma cash to “approximately $367 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 should be up sequentially: ~$18M burn offset by the $37M Regeneron cash receipt → ~$365M expected.”

description: R&D spending came in below the preview’s estimate: $17.6 million versus an estimated $20–22 million. Total operating expenses were $25.2 million, below the preview build’s implied total of roughly $30.5–32.5 million using its R&D and G&A estimates.
fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose to $25.2 million” and “R&D [was] up $4.3 million to $17.6 million, driven by Varseta-M manufacturing.”
expectation_evidence: “My build … R&D ~$20–22M … G&A ~$10.5M”; the preview also said a “jump to $24M+ signals commitment.”

description: Q2 revenue was $49 million, below the preview’s estimated $50–51 million buy-side bar, even though it exceeded the published $48.21 million consensus. The preview had specifically warned that a $48–49 million print would miss the market’s positioning.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue reached $49 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat the buy-side whisper as ~$50–51M, not $48.2M”; “A print of $48–49M … would be a miss versus how the stock is positioned.”

description: Cryoport reaffirmed its $192–196 million FY26 revenue range instead of raising it as the preview expected after a Q2 beat. Management cited geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, and the preview characterized a reaffirmation as signaling caution about the second half.
fact_evidence: “Cryoport affirmed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $192 to $196 million, citing geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty as reason for conservatism despite ~$97 million first-half revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “A repeat implies $194–198M. Simply reaffirming $192–196M after another mid-single-digit beat would signal H2 caution”; “FY26 guidance raised to ≥$194M at the low end.”

description: Commercial cell and gene therapy revenue reached $9.4 million, below the preview’s expected threshold of more than $10 million, and growth was 9% versus 26% in Q1. The services portion grew 26%, but that did not prevent the total commercial CGT line from falling short of the preview’s bar.
