dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The memory supply outlook extended beyond the preview’s stated coverage: NETGEAR secured supply through the first half of 2027, whereas the preview said its pre-buy covered virtually all 2026 production and identified 2027 as the real exposure.
fact_evidence: “The company secured memory supply through the first half of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said NETGEAR had “secured DDR4 supply for virtually all 2026 production” and that “2027 [was] the real risk.”

description: Enterprise results masked a pronounced regional weakness: APAC enterprise revenue fell 16% year over year, prompting a go-to-market restructuring and new regional leadership, while the Americas and EMEA grew.
fact_evidence: “APAC enterprise revenue declined 16% year-over-year, contrasting with 15% growth in the Americas and 9% in EMEA, prompting a go-to-market restructuring and new regional leadership.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Recurring revenue improved more than the preview’s stated ARR reference, but subscriber count fell short of the preview’s build expectation: ARR reached $41.6 million and grew 15%, while subscribers were 558,000 versus the preview’s approximately 575,000-plus watchpoint and 559,000 at Q1 end.
fact_evidence: “Total annual recurring revenue grew 15% year-over-year to $41.6 million, with the company exiting Q2 with 558,000 recurring subscribers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$39.7M ARR, +12% YoY, 559K paid subscribers at Q1 end” and flagged “ARR crossing ~$41M and subscribers above ~575K.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Q2 enterprise price action appears more limited than the preview’s expectation of broad increases: the company implemented a small increase and was still evaluating additional actions for the second half, rather than reporting broad 5–6% increases as established across the portfolio.
fact_evidence: “The company…implemented a small enterprise price increase in Q2, with additional pricing actions being evaluated for the second half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “pushed 5–6% price increases broadly across the enterprise portfolio” and called Q2 the first clean read on whether they stuck.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Sweetgreen’s Q2 comparable sales fell 6.2%, about 2.2 percentage points worse than the roughly 4% decline implied by consensus. Revenue was also slightly below the $194.4 million consensus estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $192.7 million” and “comparable restaurant sales declined 6.2%.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $194.4M”; same-store sales were “~–4% implied by revenue.”

description: Restaurant-level margin was 13.1%, well below the preview’s estimated 16–17% range and below the level the preview said would make the existing full-year margin guide unreachable. The preview anticipated a possible guide cut, but the reported Q2 margin was substantially weaker than expected.
fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level profit margin fell to 13.1% from 18.9% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Restaurant-level margin: ~16–17% (buy-side)” and “anything below ~15.5% makes the FY margin guide unreachable and forces a cut.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was a $0.2 million loss rather than the preview’s estimated $5–8 million profit, a much weaker result than the buy-side expectation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $0.2 million versus a $6.4 million profit in the prior year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$5–8M (buy-side).”

description: The full-year comparable-sales outlook was reset to an 8%–7% decline, materially worse than the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly a 6%–4% decline after a likely guide cut. The cut itself was anticipated; its depth was worse than that expected range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered to comparable sales decline of 8% to 7%.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected the “FY comp guide trimmed to ~–6%/–4%”; the preview also said to “Assume a meaningful probability the FY comp … ranges get cut or re-based tonight.”

description: The revised full-year margin outlook fell to 10.5%–11%, a steep reset from the prior 14.2%–14.7% guide. The preview warned that a cut was needed if Q2 margin came in below about 15.5%, but did not anticipate a revised range this low.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered to … restaurant-level margin of 10.5% to 11%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the reiterated FY margin guide as “14.2%–14.7%” and said “anything below ~15.5% makes the FY margin guide unreachable and forces a cut.”

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to a $23–27 million loss, far worse than the preview’s base case of a cut to the low end of the old positive $1–6 million range. The preview identified negative full-year EBITDA as a tail risk, but not as its base case.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered to … adjusted EBITDA loss of $27 million to $23 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the prior FY guide as “$1M–$6M” and its base case expected “EBITDA to the low end”; it described a cut “to negative FY EBITDA” as a tail risk.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The outbreak’s sales impact was severe: it reduced July comparable sales by about 600 basis points, and guidance assumes another 600–700 basis points of comp impact in Q3. The preview flagged the outbreak as a key uncertainty and sought quantification, but the reported scale points to a sustained, substantial hit.
fact_evidence: The outbreak “cut July comparable sales by about 600 basis points”; guidance assumes “continued 600-700 bps comp impact in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 commentary and “cyclospora quantification” were key, and asked whether management would size the July/August traffic hit and whether it had recovered. It did not specify an expected impact of this size.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Transactions improved sharply late in the quarter, reaching roughly flat in June from down 11.2% in Q1, with positive comps and transactions in the first 10 days of July before the outbreak. That late-period momentum was stronger than the preview’s implied Q2 traffic decline of about 2%, although the outbreak then reversed it.
fact_evidence: “Comparable transactions improved sequentially from down 11.2% in Q1 to roughly flat in June,” with “positive comps and transactions in the first 10 days of July before the cyclospora outbreak disrupted momentum.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “–4% comp built on –2% traffic is a turnaround” and described monthly positive June comps as a bull-case signal.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Wraps had a measurable transaction and repeat-visit contribution, but their lower entry price created meaningful check and mix drag. The preview flagged both incrementality and mix-down risk; the concrete 500-basis-point transaction improvement and repeat-purchase rate provide a stronger quantified contribution than it had projected.
fact_evidence: “Wraps achieved roughly 20% incidence and drove about 500 basis points of transaction improvement,” and “more than half of wrap buyers” returned within 30 days, but “their lower entry price created meaningful check/mix drag.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “wraps performance” for “incrementality … and effect on average check,” noting that wraps’ lower price posed “a mix-down risk.”

description: Serve cut 2026 revenue guidance from about $26 million to $9–10 million, far below the preview’s expectation built around the $26 million outlook. Management attributed the reduction mainly to removing an assumed second-half ramp in Uber delivery volume.
fact_evidence: Serve “slashed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $26 million to a range of $9-10 million,” primarily because it removed an assumed second-half ramp in Uber delivery volume.
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue ~$26M”; consensus was “$26.01M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Serve said it does not currently expect to renew its Uber agreement when it expires in early 2027 unless the operating model improves meaningfully. That is a sharper break from the prior growth pattern than the preview anticipated: Uber delivery volume had grown for 17 consecutive quarters before reversing in Q2.
fact_evidence: Serve “does not currently expect to renew its Uber agreement when it expires in early 2027 unless the operating model meaningfully improves”; Uber delivery volume had grown “for 17 consecutive quarters before reversing in Q2.”

description: Q2 revenue was $3.2 million, below both the $3.49 million consensus and the preview’s $3.8–4.1 million whisper range. The reported 9% sequential increase versus Q1’s reported figure did not meet the preview’s higher expectation for sequential growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $3.2 million, up 9% sequentially from Q1 and over 400% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 consensus was “$3.49M”; the preview said, “Assume a whisper of ~$3.8–4.1M, i.e. 10–18% real sequential growth.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and marketable securities ended Q2 above $240 million, well above the preview’s estimated $150–165 million. That leaves Serve with substantially more funding for its strategic pivot than the preview expected.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with more than $240 million in cash and marketable securities, providing runway to fund its strategic pivot.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$150–165M expected at 6/30/26.”

description: Gross margin improved from Q1’s negative 302% to negative 271%, but remained well short of the preview’s cited marker of moving toward negative 200% or better. The gross loss was still approximately $8.8 million.
fact_evidence: “Gross loss of approximately $8.8 million and gross margin of negative 271%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Any narrowing toward (200)% or better is the strongest possible evidence that scale is converting to leverage.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: DoorDash delivery volume grew rapidly, providing a potential alternative as Uber weakened: it rose nearly 50% sequentially and then another 50% from June to July. The preview did not identify this specific platform as a growing offset.
fact_evidence: “DoorDash delivery volume grew nearly 50% sequentially last quarter and grew another 50% between June and July, positioning it as a growing alternative to Uber.”

description: Serve lowered its non-GAAP operating expense outlook to about $140–150 million rather than holding the prior $160–170 million guidance, and also reduced planned 2026 capital expenditures to $15–17 million from about $25 million. The lower spending supports cash preservation, though it also comes alongside the much weaker revenue outlook.
fact_evidence: Serve “reduced planned 2026 capital expenditures from about $25 million to $15-17 million and cut non-GAAP operating expense guidance from $160-170 million to approximately $140-150 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 non-GAAP opex guidance of “$160–170M” and its base case expected the “opex guide held.”

description: The loss-per-share results differed depending on the measure: GAAP loss of $0.80 per share was worse than the preview’s $0.69 loss consensus, while the non-GAAP loss of $0.59 was better than the preview’s scenario range of $0.65–0.72. The two measures therefore gave contrasting signals.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $64 million (-$0.80 per share) and non-GAAP net loss was $47.1 million (-$0.59 per share).”
expectation_evidence: The preview showed Q2 EPS consensus of “$(0.69)” and a base-case non-GAAP EPS range of “$(0.65)–$(0.72).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Serve disclosed that advertising made up nearly half of robotic food delivery revenue and that recurring revenue exceeded half of total revenue. The preview did not anticipate this advertising contribution; the software revenue figure itself was broadly consistent with the prior-quarter level.
fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue exceeded 50% of total revenue, with advertising accounting for nearly 50% of robotic food delivery revenues and software revenue again reaching nearly $1 million.”

description: Management set an August 17 announcement covering a new delivery marketplace partner, the Beacon countertop integration device, new market launches, and autonomy advances. The preview sought named H2 catalysts but had not anticipated this announced package or date.
fact_evidence: Serve “plans an August 17 summer announcement covering a new delivery marketplace partner, its Beacon countertop integration device, new market launches, and autonomy advances.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to look for a “specific H2 bridge” with “named platforms/cities/hospitals.”

description: Revenue was $612 million, about 4.5% above the $585.4 million consensus and $585 million company frame, exceeding even the preview’s $598–608 million bull-case range. Leasing and services revenue grew 6%, while delivery and installation revenue surged more than 25%.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $612 million… beating the company's own guidance of approximately $585 million, driven by 6% leasing and services revenue growth”; “Delivery and installation revenue surged over 25% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue ($585.4M) sits exactly on the number management framed… (~$585M)”; bull case revenue was “$598–608M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA beat the $223 million outlook by $5 million, but the margin was 37.2%—below the preview’s roughly 38.1% expectation and its 38.2% “good” threshold. The margin decline was about 500 basis points year over year, worse than the preview’s expected 420-basis-point decline.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $228 million (beating the $223 million outlook), but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 37.2%, a roughly 500 basis point year-over-year decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA margin ~38.1%” and said “≥38.2%” would look good; it expected “−420 bps” year over year.

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.28, above the $0.246 consensus and the preview’s $0.24–0.26 base case, rather than declining about 9% year over year as consensus implied. Reported diluted EPS was flat at $0.26 year over year.
fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS was flat year-over-year at $0.26 (adjusted EPS $0.28).”
expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted EPS was “$0.246” versus $0.27 a year earlier, a “−9%” estimate; the base case was “$0.24–0.26.”

description: Management raised 2026 revenue guidance by $50 million to about $2.3 billion and lifted adjusted EBITDA guidance to about $920 million, rather than merely reiterating the prior $2.25 billion and $915 million outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $50 million to approximately $2.3 billion… and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $920 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance as “Revenue ~$2.25B” and “Adj. EBITDA ~$915M” and said the base case was that the guide would be reiterated.

description: Net CapEx guidance rose to about $375 million, $50 million above the preview’s $325 million estimate. Adjusted free cash flow was consequently just $55 million, well below the preview’s $120–135 million expectation, as the company directed more capital to fleet.
fact_evidence: “Net CapEx guidance was raised to approximately $375 million”; “Q2 adjusted free cash flow [fell] to $55 million as the company reinvests over half its capital generation into demand-driven fleet.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net capex ~$325M” and estimated “Adj. FCF ~$120–135M”; its bull-case commentary expected “net capex held at $325M.”

description: Management gave a more specific path for margin recovery, calling for 200–300 basis points of sequential expansion in Q3 and another 300–500 basis points in Q4, with flat-to-positive year-over-year EBITDA margin comparisons possible by Q4. This addressed the preview’s concern about the required second-half margin ramp with quantified quarterly targets.
fact_evidence: “Management guided to sequential margin expansion of 200-300 basis points in Q3… and 300-500 basis points in Q4, potentially reaching flat-to-positive year-over-year EBITDA margin comparisons by Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “a credible H2 margin bridge” and said management needed to attribute the ramp “specifically… with quantification”; it identified the implied “~43.1% margin” in H2 as the key risk.

description: Q2 revenue was $292.9 million, above the preview’s roughly $272 million working consensus and its roughly $280 million whisper. The result cleared both expectations by a substantial amount.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $292.9 million, up 36% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Working consensus used here: Rev ~$272M”; “A reasonable whisper was ~$280M revenue.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Shipments were $281.5 million, below revenue, despite the preview’s emphasis that shipments should continue to outpace revenue. Shipment growth also slowed to 36% from 54% in Q1, weakening the forward-demand signal the preview highlighted.
fact_evidence: “Shipments of $281.5 million, also up 36%.”
expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly guided shipments to keep outpacing revenue”; “Any print where shipments come in below revenue breaks that commitment.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: First-half purchase orders rose 105% year-over-year, with more emphasis on newer products across all categories. The preview focused on shipments as a bookings proxy and on possible shipment deceleration, but did not anticipate this reported order growth.
fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 orders (POs) increased 105% year-over-year, with a heavier emphasis on newer products across all categories.”

description: Single-wafer cleaning, Tahoe and semi-critical cleaning revenue fell 14.2%, a much steeper decline than the 5.5% decline cited for Q1. The preview flagged stabilization versus a steepening decline as a key debate, and the reported result showed the decline had steepened.
fact_evidence: “Single-wafer cleaning, Tahoe and semi-critical cleaning revenue fell 14.2% to $133.0 million”; the decline was “reflecting minimal contribution from newer SPM products.”
expectation_evidence: “SWC is the legacy franchise and it shrank 5.5% YoY in Q1”; “If SWC declines are steepening rather than stabilizing, the growth story becomes a single-product (ECP) story with concentration risk.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management flagged tightening component supply and lead times that could extend from four to six months, creating a potential constraint on second-half shipments. The preview highlighted shipment trends but did not anticipate this specific supply risk; the company said key suppliers had not raised prices so far.
fact_evidence: “Tightening component supply and longer lead times (extending from 4 months to potentially 6 months) as a potential constraint on second-half shipments, though without price increases from key suppliers so far.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ACM reported orders for its panel-level horizontal plating tool, including a production order from an advanced-packaging customer in Mainland China and an evaluation system for a new customer in Asia. The preview identified international customer wins as a proof point to watch but did not anticipate these specific tool orders.
fact_evidence: “The company received orders for its panel-level horizontal plating tool from advanced packaging customers, including a production order in Mainland China and an evaluation system for a new customer in Asia.”
expectation_evidence: “Tools installed outside mainland China, Oregon on-schedule commentary, and named international customers are the metrics that would break” the China-domestic-substitution framing.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Customer concentration improved sharply: only one customer accounted for more than 10% of first-half revenue, versus three such customers accounting for 49.9% a year earlier. The preview did not set an expectation for this change.
fact_evidence: “Only one 10%+ customer at 12.7% of first-half revenue versus three 10%+ customers representing 49.9% in first-half 2025.”

description: Q2 revenue was $715 million, about $37 million below the $751.6 million consensus, and fell 3% year over year instead of growing about 8%. The call also said it was well below the company’s own expectations.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $715 million, up just 3% year-over-year ... well below the company's historical ~34% CAGR and its own expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $751.6M” consensus; “Implied Y/Y +8.3%.”

description: Q3 guidance was dramatically below the preview’s derived $800–810 million estimate: the company guided to at least $650 million, implying about a 12% year-over-year decline. Management also said it is allowing time for its substantially overhauled leadership team to ramp up.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of at least $650 million, implying roughly a 12% year-over-year decline”; guidance assumptions “allow time for these new leaders to ramp up.”
expectation_evidence: “Derived Q3 setup ... Q3'26 consensus ≈ $800–810M”; the preview called for attention to whether guidance was below “~$790M.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $241 million versus roughly $260 million expected, and the 34% margin was also below the preview’s roughly 34.6% estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $241 million (34% margin).”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$260M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~34.6%.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.34, below the preview’s $0.40–$0.41 non-GAAP EPS estimate. GAAP net income was $64 million, while adjusted net income was $158 million.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $158 million ($0.34 per diluted share)” and “GAAP net income was only $64 million ($0.14 per diluted share).”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $0.41 (Zacks); $0.40 per StockStory.”

description: Management attributed the weakness not only to macro pressure on large customers but also to its own execution shortfalls. The preview emphasized macro and agency-spend risks, but did not anticipate management acknowledging execution problems.
fact_evidence: “Management attributed underperformance to both macro headwinds affecting a handful of large customers and its own execution shortfalls,” while characterizing the issues as “cyclical rather than systemic.”
expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated “macro caveats” and identified “agency spend still impaired” as a bear-case driver.

description: Despite the weak overall quarter and concerns about CTV competition, the company reported more than 50% year-over-year CTV growth in both EMEA and APAC, with those regions each growing nearly 30% year to date and China above 100%.
fact_evidence: “EMEA and APAC each growing nearly 30% year-to-date, China growing over 100% year-to-date, and CTV growing over 50% year-over-year in both EMEA and APAC.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “CTV / biddable CTV and Amazon share” as a key watch item and said to watch for “any quantified CTV growth rate” amid intensified competition.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Revenue associated with joint business plans grew six times faster than overall revenue, offering a bright spot for agency relationships even as total growth slowed sharply.
fact_evidence: “217 joint business plans (JBPs) as of Q2, up 38% year-over-year, with revenue under JBPs growing at 6x the overall revenue growth rate.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called JBP growth “the cleanest tell on agency trust” and highlighted Publicis-related agency concerns.

description: SUI Group reported $1.2 million of Q2 revenue, well above the preview’s $0.55–$0.65 million model. The increase was aided by new staking and digital-lending interest income.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose to $1.2 million in Q2 2026 from $948,000 a year earlier, aided by new SUI staking and digital lending interest income.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: ~$0.55–0.65M.”

description: The reported net loss of $18.9 million, or $0.23 per diluted share, was materially smaller than the preview’s modeled $26–$30 million loss and $0.34–$0.39 loss per share.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $18.9 million ($0.23 per diluted share).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The quarter included a large, unexpected loss tied to the Bluefin loan and another loss on returned SUI tokens from Galaxy Digital. The preview modeled Bluefin lending income and allowed only $0–$3 million for other investment marks, rather than these specific losses.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $16.6 million of non-cash losses on digital assets and receivables, driven largely by a $14 million loss tied to the additional Bluefin loan and a $2.4 million loss on returned SUI tokens from Galaxy Digital.”
expectation_evidence: “Digital lending interest: ~$0.15–0.25M”; “Other investment marks: −$0M to −$3M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and cash equivalents were only $3.1 million at quarter-end, far below the preview’s roughly $11 million modeled cash-and-stablecoin balance. Management nevertheless said the company has over two years of operating runway excluding treasury assets.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents fell to $3.1 million as of June 30, 2026 from $21.9 million at year-end 2025, though management claims over two years of operating runway excluding treasury assets.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash + stablecoins” were modeled at “~$11–12M” at 6/30; the base case expected “cash ~$11M.”

description: The company made $6 million of new investments in AI and agentic-finance companies, a capital-allocation move not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of buybacks versus the equity line. That is notable alongside the much lower-than-modeled cash balance.
fact_evidence: “New agentic-finance investments of $3 million in AI firm N of 1 (via a SAFE) and $3 million in Recursive Superintelligence.”
expectation_evidence: “Buyback vs. equity line” was flagged as a key issue; the preview described the choice as resuming buybacks or drawing the equity line.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The reported mNAV of about 0.72x was below the preview’s estimate of roughly 0.78x, indicating a larger discount to treasury value than the preview had modeled.
fact_evidence: “SUI Group's stock traded at an mNAV of approximately 0.72x as of August 3, 2026, signaling a discount to the underlying treasury value.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The legacy specialty-finance book was down to about $2.2 million at fair value, with $900,000 of first-half repayments and no significant new originations expected near-term. That is a more concrete run-off picture than the preview’s focus on credit risk, delinquencies, and recent provisions.
fact_evidence: “The legacy specialty finance portfolio has shrunk to approximately $2.2 million of non-bank loans at fair value, with about $900,000 in repayments received in the first half and no significant new originations expected near-term.”
expectation_evidence: “Chairman Polinsky flagged ‘increased credit risk and uncertainty regarding borrower delinquencies.’ Q1 carried a $1.15M provision plus $1.37M receivable impairment.”

description: Q2 revenue was $973 million, about 1.3% below the $985.7 million consensus estimate. The shortfall was modest, while adjusted EBITDA of $69 million was close to the roughly $68 million consensus and within the expected guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $973 million”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus: “$985.7M.”

description: Astrana raised the low end of its full-year adjusted EBITDA range by only $5 million, to $255 million, rather than the preview’s reasonable-ask range starting around $260 million. It did raise the floor, but less than the preview said the market wanted.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $255M-$280M.”
expectation_evidence: “The market wants the low end taken up” and “a narrow-up to ~$260–280M is the reasonable ask.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80 exceeded the preview’s derived expectation of about $0.75, though the preview cautioned that adjusted and GAAP EPS estimates could be confused.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS hit a record $0.80.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS — adjusted diluted”: “~$0.75” consensus (derived).

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Medical costs were slightly better than the 5.2% full-year assumption overall, but commercial outpatient specialties were trending slightly above expectations. This is more mixed than a uniformly favorable trend reading.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date medical cost trend is running slightly better than the 5.2% full-year assumption, with Medicare favorable and Medicaid in line, but commercial trending slightly above expectations in outpatient specialties.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 was “slightly better than 5.2%” and that “holds ~5% against a peer group running 7%” would support the bull case; it flagged elevated utilization or trend at the high end of the assumption as a bear signal.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A CMS billing-anomaly adjustment for ACO REACH 2025 caused a one-time $15 million revenue reduction that the preview had not anticipated. A corresponding expense reduction largely offset it, leaving EBITDA impact immaterial.
fact_evidence: “A one-time $15 million revenue reduction tied to CMS billing anomaly adjustments for ACO REACH 2025 was largely offset by a corresponding expense reduction, resulting in an immaterial EBITDA impact.”

description: G&A improved about 210 basis points year over year, with management expecting it to reach roughly 6% of revenue by year-end. The preview discussed Prospect synergies but did not flag this degree of G&A improvement or the exit-rate target.
fact_evidence: “G&A improved approximately 210 basis points year-over-year, with the company expecting to exit 2026 at roughly 6% of revenue.”

description: Management said it is putting mid-to-high single-digit millions—about three-quarters of its outperformance—back into payer contracts, provider partnerships, and expansion markets. The preview speculated that a buyback might be possible, but did not anticipate this specific reinvestment plan.
fact_evidence: “The company is reinvesting mid-to-high single-digit millions (about three-quarters of its outperformance) into new payer contracts, provider partnerships, and expansion markets in Texas and Hawaii.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management would “evaluate dynamically” on risk-adjusted returns and that an authorization was a possibility: “Any repurchase announcement lands as a confidence signal.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Astrana disclosed plans to convert tens of thousands of California Medi-Cal members from professional to full-risk arrangements over the next 12 months, a specific and substantial conversion initiative not identified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Converting tens of thousands of California Medi-Cal members from professional to full-risk arrangements over the next 12 months.”

description: Management reaffirmed medium-term mid-to-high teens organic EBITDA growth, including for 2027, despite Medicaid work-requirement changes beginning January 1, 2027. The preview discussed Medicaid and the 2027 setup but did not anticipate this explicit growth reaffirmation alongside the policy change.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed medium-term mid-to-high teens organic EBITDA growth, including for 2027, despite Medicaid work-requirement changes starting January 1, 2027.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings were $16.2 million, well below the preview’s $19.0 million guidance midpoint and even below the $17.1 million low end. The resulting bookings growth of 25% year over year was also far below the preview’s implied 47% growth.
fact_evidence: “Bookings grew 25% year-over-year to $16.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross bookings” guidance was “$19.0M ±10% ($17.1–20.9M),” with “Implied YoY” growth of “+47%.”

description: The Q3 revenue midpoint of $17 million is below the preview’s roughly $19 million expectation, and even the top of the guidance range is below $19 million. description: Q2 sales of $395.7 million exceeded both the $391.3 million consensus and the $395 million high end of company guidance, though the beat over the guidance ceiling was small.

expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus net sales of “$391.3M” and company guidance of “$385–395M.”

description: Q2 repurchases were $8.8 million, below the $12 million repurchased in Q1 rather than accelerating. The company still bought back about $21 million year to date, while generating strong operating cash flow.

expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “buyback acceleration” as something to watch and noted that Q1 repurchases were “$12M.”

description: Oklo raised 2026 operating cash-use guidance to $120–150 million from $80–100 million, a substantial increase over the preview’s baseline range. The company attributed the higher spending to accelerated first-of-a-kind project work at Aurora-INL.
fact_evidence: “Oklo raised its 2026 operating cash use guidance to $120–150 million (from $80–100 million), driven by accelerated first-of-a-kind project spending at Aurora-INL.”
expectation_evidence: “2026 operating cash use **$80–100M**”; the preview also said to watch “Cash burn, capex guidance, and dilution.”

description: Oklo disclosed $400–500 million of 2026 PP&E capex and raised that guidance by $50 million at both ends, to fund accelerated Aurora-INL spending. The preview anticipated that a capex bracket could be provided, but did not anticipate this higher revised range.
fact_evidence: “PP&E capex guidance to $400–500 million (from $350–450 million), driven by accelerated first-of-a-kind project spending at Aurora-INL.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said an “explicit FY2026 capex bracket” would be worth watching and modeled “~$40–60M capex” for Q2.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash and marketable securities reached $3 billion, well above the preview’s estimated $2.44–2.48 billion. But the higher balance came alongside $1.9 billion raised through 2026 ATM programs, making the liquidity upside come with substantial share issuance rather than simply lower-than-expected spending.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $3 billion in cash and marketable securities, including $1.9 billion raised via ATM programs in 2026.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Oklo said Aurora-INL remains on track for a planned 2028 startup, whereas the preview’s reference schedule was late 2027/early 2028 and flagged a move into 2028 as a downside risk. The call also reported DOE safety-analysis approval, an unexpected project milestone that partially offsets the less favorable timing wording.
fact_evidence: “Aurora-INL received DOE approval of its Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis and remains on track for a planned 2028 startup.”
expectation_evidence: “Aurora-INL schedule reaffirmation (late 2027 / early 2028 operations)” and “Any softening of language … or a slip into 2028” was identified as a downside risk.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Oklo was selected for advanced negotiations over surplus plutonium that could be blended into HALEU-equivalent bridge fuel. The preview highlighted fuel supply as a key constraint, but this specific potential source was not anticipated; timing remains outside the company’s control.
fact_evidence: “DOE selected Oklo for advanced negotiations on surplus plutonium … that could be blended at 10–13% plutonium content to create HALEU-equivalent bridge fuel, though timing remains outside Oklo's control.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Fuel supply” and said a “fuel contract or facility authorization” could be an underrated catalyst.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: A Centrus letter of intent contemplated enough domestic HALEU for initial cores and reloads for up to five Aurora powerhouses over multiple years. This is a concrete potential supply source, although it is an LOI and deliveries are not expected to begin until 2029.
fact_evidence: “The Centrus letter of intent contemplates domestic HALEU supply sufficient for initial core and reload needs of up to 5 Aurora powerhouses for multiple years, with deliveries expected to begin in 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified HALEU sourcing as a key issue and said a fuel contract or facility authorization could be a catalyst.

description: Oklo acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers to bring more engineering and manufacturing capability in-house. The preview did not flag either acquisition; ARMEC was already contributing to Aurora-INL procurement, while CEI adds sodium and alkali-metal systems experience.
fact_evidence: “During the quarter Oklo acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers (CEI) to strengthen in-house engineering and manufacturing,” with ARMEC contributing to Aurora-INL procurement and CEI adding “~30 years of sodium/alkali metal systems experience.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Oklo signed an MOU with Kiewit for EPC planning for the Ohio campus and is advancing PJM interconnection applications, an incremental development step not specified in the preview. The call did not report a binding, priced power contract or provide full project-cost guidance.
fact_evidence: “Oklo signed an MOU with Kiewit to support EPC planning for the initial phase of its planned 1.2-gigawatt Ohio clean energy campus and is advancing multiple PJM interconnection applications, though full project cost guidance has not yet been provided.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a “binding, priced PPA with a delivery date” was what would move the market and called for watching grid interconnection progress.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: National's leverage ratio improved to 21:1, better than the preview's Q1 level of 23:1 and below the sub-22:1 threshold it identified as a positive surprise.
fact_evidence: National's leverage ratio (gross par to statutory capital) improved to 21-to-1 from 24-to-1 at year-end 2025, with insured gross par declining ~$1.5 billion to about $20.8 billion.
expectation_evidence: National insured portfolio runoff & leverage: $21.5B gross par and leverage 23:1 from 24:1; “Sub-22:1 leverage would be a positive surprise.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: National's statutory capital reached $968 million, above the preview's expected range of $940–960 million and its Q1 level of $950 million.
fact_evidence: National's statutory capital rose $31 million to $968 million versus year-end 2025.
expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “National stat cap $940–960M”; Q1 level: “$950M stat cap (+$13M q/q).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: National's PREPA exposure fell by $35 million from the preview's $425 million baseline after claims were paid on bonds maturing July 1; the call also said only $20 million payments are due in each of 2027 and 2028.
fact_evidence: National's PREPA exposure fell by $35 million to $390 million of gross par value following insurance claims paid on bonds that matured July 1, 2026, with only $20 million payments due in each of 2027 and 2028.
expectation_evidence: PREPA Q1 level: “$425M gross par, unchanged”; the preview also said “~$35M of PREPA-related debt service remained payable across the rest of 2026.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: MBIA Insurance Corp. reported $27 million of statutory net income after the preview described its capital as flat and flagged Zohar as a legacy exposure, but did not anticipate a large reserve benefit from reassessing Zohar recoveries.
fact_evidence: MBIA Insurance Corp. posted statutory net income of $27 million in Q2 2026 (up from $4 million a year earlier), driven by a large loss reserve benefit tied to Zohar CDO recovery reassessments.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management put the rejected PREPA offer at roughly $0.30–$0.40 per dollar while recent market indications were about $0.75, highlighting a larger gap between the offer and bondholder value indications than the preview had quantified.
fact_evidence: Management estimated the rejected settlement offer valued bonds at roughly $0.30 to $0.40 on the dollar, versus recent market indications of about $0.75.

description: Adjusted EPS was one cent worse than the preview's $0.13 loss-per-share consensus, though it fell within the preview's broader base-case range.

expectation_evidence: Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) consensus: “–$0.13”; base scenario: “–$0.13 to –$0.18.”

description: ARKO reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $72 million, below the preview’s guidance-implied $80–85 million bogey. Management said the decline was largely driven by $3.3 million of higher same-store credit card fees as fuel prices rose.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA declined to $72 million from $76.9 million”; the decline was “largely driven by $3.3 million of higher same-store credit card fees tied to elevated fuel prices.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA bogey math” put Q2 at “roughly $80–85M”; the base case also expected “$80–85M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

expectation_evidence: “What good looks like” was “≥ +1.0%”; the preview said the market wanted “a second positive quarter with an acceleration.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Same-store retail fuel gallons fell 5.7%, weaker than the preview’s expectation that the decline improve to better than 3%.
fact_evidence: “Same-store retail fuel gallons fell 5.7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “SS gallons better than −3%” would be a key signal.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Retail fuel margin reached 48.7 cents per gallon, above the preview’s 46-cent threshold, and management raised the full-year outlook to 45.5–47.5 cents from the 41.5–43.5-cent range cited in the preview.
fact_evidence: Same-store fuel cents-per-gallon margin “rose 6.5% to $0.487,” and management “raised its full-year retail fuel margin outlook to $0.455–$0.475 per gallon.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s key-metric threshold was “≥46¢”; it cited a FY guide of “41.5–43.5¢.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: ARKO reported a 5% quarterly increase in loyalty enrollment and said enrolled members spend more than twice as much as non-enrolled members; the preview did not identify loyalty as a metric to watch.
fact_evidence: “Loyalty enrollment grew by over 100,000 members (5%) in the quarter,” and enrolled members spend “more than 2x” that of non-enrolled members.

description: ARKO disclosed that it repurchased $38 million of its senior notes for $35 million in cash, an unanticipated capital-allocation action that reduced long-term debt. The preview had instead highlighted a possible step-up in equity buybacks.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $38 million of its 5.18% senior notes for $35 million cash”; long-term debt was $675 million, down $29 million from Q1.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s capital-returns watch item listed “Buyback step-up.”

description: Wendy’s withdrew its full-year 2026 outlook instead of reaffirming or narrowing it, and said continued traffic headwinds mean it does not expect year-over-year system-wide sales growth in either Q3 or Q4. That is a more severe reset than the preview’s base case of narrowing the outlook and its stated possibility of a cut.
fact_evidence: Management withdrew its full-year 2026 financial outlook, citing a comprehensive turnaround assessment, and expects continued traffic headwinds preventing year-over-year system-wide sales growth in Q3 or Q4.
expectation_evidence: “A cut or a narrowing to the low end is a live possibility”; the base case expected the FY guide to be “narrowed to the low end.”

description: Wendy’s cut its quarterly dividend in half, from the preview’s cited $0.14 per share to $0.07, to fund turnaround investments. The preview flagged dividend-cut risk, but the actual reduction was a concrete and substantial cut rather than just softer dividend language.
fact_evidence: “The company cut its quarterly dividend to $0.07 per share” to “create flexibility for turnaround investments.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the dividend as “$0.14/qtr” and said “the market is partly pricing a cut.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Traffic remained sharply weak: U.S. traffic fell 12.5%, with negative double-digit declines in each period, while new products and promotions lifted average check but did not bring in the expected traffic. The preview’s base case expected comps to be roughly flat versus April, and its bull case expected the launches to drive traffic.
fact_evidence: U.S. same-restaurant sales were driven by a “12.5% traffic decrease,” with “negative double-digit traffic in each period”; launches “boosted average check but failed to drive expected traffic.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected U.S. SRS to be “−6% to −7%, roughly flat vs. April”; the bull case said “Biggie Deals + Pretzel Bacon Pub / Minions LTOs drive traffic.”

description: U.S. company-operated restaurant margin reached 13.8%, well above the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 11.5%–12%. That strength came despite commodity inflation running around 9%, above the preview’s cited 8% level, and labor inflation remaining around 4%.
fact_evidence: “U.S. company-operated restaurant margin was 13.8%,” pressured by “roughly 9% commodity cost increases” and “about 4% labor rate inflation.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “margin ~11.5–12%”; the preview cited “8% commodity and 4% labor inflation.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: First-half free cash flow reached $120.3 million, up $10.8 million year over year. Against the preview’s full-year guide of $190–205 million and its expectation that cash flow would be back-half weighted, this leaves substantially less of the annual target to generate in the second half than the preview implied.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose $10.8 million to $120.3 million for the first half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 free cash flow guidance of “$190–205M” and described it as “Back-half weighted.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.18, two cents above the preview’s $0.16 consensus estimate. The beat was positive but modest in absolute terms.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.18 for the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus EPS of “$0.16.”

description: Post said preliminary FY2027 adjusted EBITDA should be roughly flat against a comparable base of about $1.48 billion. The preview framed the market as looking for a path back to growth in FY2027, so flat guidance points to a weaker recovery trajectory than investors were hoping to hear.
fact_evidence: “Preliminary FY2027 guidance is for EBITDA roughly flat” versus a “comparable adjusted EBITDA base of approximately $1.48 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus is not asking POST to grow this quarter; it is asking management to defend the FY guide and articulate a path back to growth in FY27.”

description: Although Post bought back 4% of its shares in Q3 and reduced the year-to-date share count by about 17%, management said it is shifting from aggressive buybacks toward debt reduction. The preview treated Q3 repurchases as a key signal of conviction and highlighted the new authorization, but did not anticipate a move away from buybacks.
fact_evidence: “Post repurchased 4% of outstanding shares in Q3,” bringing the year-to-date reduction to “approximately 17%”; management is “shifting capital allocation from aggressive share buybacks toward debt reduction,” despite “no bond maturity for four years.”
expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace in Q3 is a direct read on management's own conviction. An aggressive number is the strongest available signal”; the preview also cited the new $600 million authorization.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Post attributed roughly 60% of the year-over-year pet business decline to value brands, mostly 9Lives, which is facing promotions from two rivals pricing below it. The preview focused on whether 9Lives distribution losses had stopped compounding, so the reported competitive pressure suggests the pet weakness remained a live issue rather than a clear stabilization.
fact_evidence: “Roughly 60% of the year-over-year pet business decline is attributable to value brands, mostly 9Lives,” which “faces competitive promotions with two rivals pricing below its brand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether “9Lives distribution losses from prior price increases have stopped compounding” and whether pet food’s decline was “decelerating from −14.1%.”

The preview emphasized pet volume and the Nutrish and 9Lives outlook, but did not flag this additional cost-savings opportunity.
fact_evidence: “The pet business has reached approximately 30% market share,” with “substantial untapped cost-savings opportunities in pet beyond footprint, including portfolio simplification and formula harmonization.”

description: Post said FY2027 cereal volume is expected to decline about 2.5%, but that its underperformance gap versus the category is narrowing as assortment adjustments take effect. The continuing decline is not a return to growth, though the narrowing gap is more encouraging than the preview’s concern about a further cereal step-down.
fact_evidence: “Cereal volume is expected to decline about 2.5% in FY2027,” while Post is “narrowing its underperformance gap to category” as assortment adjustments take effect.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited tracked-channel data showing a “further ‘step-down’ in PCB” and warned that cereal could join pet food “in accelerating decline”; it also sought an FY2027 path back to growth.

description: Post plans to close two peanut butter plants following the AW integration, using the cost-optimization approach previously applied to three cereal plants. This is a newly disclosed opportunity for efficiency improvement that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “Post is closing two peanut butter plants following the AW integration,” applying “the same cost-optimization playbook used to close three cereal plants.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Post described refrigerated retail pressure from fuel and freight costs and egg prices falling below its grain-based procurement costs, in addition to timing and HPAI comparisons. The preview anticipated HPAI-related normalization and modeled a weaker refrigerated retail quarter, but did not flag this unfavorable procurement-cost mismatch.
fact_evidence: “Q3 refrigerated retail was pressured” by “higher fuel/freight costs and unfavorable egg market dynamics where market prices plummeted below the company's grain-based procurement costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Refrigerated Retail at about $40 million of EBITDA and cited the Crystal Farms divestiture as a likely source of lower sales; it also highlighted lapping peak HPAI-related economics elsewhere.

description: Management expects FY2027 pricing actions mostly later in the year, concentrated in PCB/pet, with inflation toward the high end of prior expectations and pricing lagging inflation because of retailer negotiations. The later-year timing was consistent with the preview, but the higher inflation pressure and lagged pricing imply a less favorable near-term recovery in those costs.
fact_evidence: “Most FY2027 pricing actions” are expected “later in the year,” concentrated in “the PCB/pet segment where inflation is running toward the higher end of prior expectations,” with “pricing lagging inflation due to retailer negotiation timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected fuel-surcharge inflation to be absorbed in FY2026 “with pricing deferred to FY2027.”

description: RGCO cut FY2026 EPS guidance to $1.29–$1.32, below the preview’s expected $1.31–$1.37 range and its expectation that guidance would be reaffirmed or narrowed toward the upper end. Management attributed the revision to unusual May weather and associated gas delivery.
fact_evidence: “Management narrowed its full-year fiscal 2026 EPS forecast to a range of $1.29 to $1.32, citing unusual May weather patterns and associated gas delivery.”
expectation_evidence: “Management either reaffirms $1.31–$1.37, narrows to the upper half, or trims”; the ranked checklist said “Narrow to $1.35–$1.37.”

fact_evidence: “The Roanoke Gas rate case settled at $3.85 million in incremental annual revenues, below the $4.3 million originally sought.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected a final order “at/near $4.3M.”

expectation_evidence: The preview’s rate-case watch item said “no material refund reserve.”

The company did establish a regulatory asset and expects recovery in a future proceeding, partly offsetting the longer outage concern.

expectation_evidence: The preview said the facility was “unavailable for winter 2026-27” and identified reliability and capital risk; it expected SCC regulatory-asset treatment to be confirmed.

expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q3 diluted EPS consensus of “$0.06” and net income of “~$0.6M implied.”

expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $0.42”; the preview also cites a “Most Accurate Estimate (~$0.39).”

expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est.): ~$125–127M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin (my est.): ~21.3–21.5%” and “+40–60 bps.”

description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to $485–495 million, above the preview’s anticipated buy-side range of $465–485 million. The new midpoint is about $20 million above the prior guide midpoint, as the preview expected a raise but not one reaching $495 million.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … adjusted EBITDA of $485-$495 million (about $20 million higher at midpoint).”
expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects a raise to roughly … $465–485M EBITDA.”

fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 10% year-over-year to $606 million, with core revenue (excluding Pivot) up 8% to $589.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $591.7M–$592.5M” and “Implied YoY | +7.5%.”

description: Daily patient visits topped 56,000, exceeding the roughly 55,500–55,800 implied by the preview and its expected 1–1.5% growth. The reported 2.6% increase was a better organic-volume result than the preview’s base expectation, though short of its 56,500-plus clean-beat marker.
fact_evidence: “Total patient visits rose 2.6% to over 56,000 per day.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of ~$592M backs into roughly 55,500–55,800 visits/day (+1% to +1.5% YoY)” and “56,500+ is a clean beat.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said “employer services visits go negative YoY” was a key risk and listed “Employer services visits vs. flat”; it also noted Q1 ex-Nova visits grew “just +0.7%.”

expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “RPV ~$151 (+3.5%)” and said “RPV growth below 3%” would signal a risk.

fact_evidence: “The Onsite Health Clinics segment grew revenue 72.1% to $38.8 million (27.9% excluding Pivot).”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Onsite health organic growth ≥20%” and cited Q1 organic growth of “+20.9% ex-Pivot.”
