description: Net leverage was already just under 3x in Q2, reaching the preview’s year-end target well ahead of schedule. The reduction also triggered a 25-basis-point Term Loan B spread step-down.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to just under 3x from 3.4x in Q1, reaching the year-end target well ahead of schedule and triggering a 25 basis point Term Loan B spread step-down to 175 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed net leverage “comfortably below 3.0x at year-end (3.4x at Q1).”

description: The company raised its full-year free-cash-flow guidance midpoint by $5 million, to $230 million from $225 million. The preview gave the existing range but did not specifically anticipate a free-cash-flow raise.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … free cash flow of $220-$240 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow $215M–$235M.”

description: The preview did not anticipate a CEO succession announcement. The company disclosed a planned transition in which Keith Newton becomes Executive Chairman and current President and CFO Matt DiCanio becomes CEO on November 1, 2026.
fact_evidence: “CEO Keith Newton will transition to Executive Chairman effective November 1, 2026, with current President and CFO Matt DiCanio becoming President and CEO as part of a multi-year succession plan.”

description: Spectrum Brands’ Q3 sales growth was stronger than the preview’s roughly 4.7% expectation: sales rose 7.7% year over year, or 6.6% organically excluding favorable FX.
fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 7.7% year-over-year (6.6% organic excluding $7.5 million favorable FX) with all three business units delivering growth in Q3 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Consensus $732.4M | +4.7%”; the preview’s segment model estimated total growth of about 4.8%.

description: Home & Garden substantially outperformed the preview’s estimate: sales rose 19% to $225 million, versus the preview’s model of about 9% growth to $206 million. The quarter also exceeded the preview’s seasonal framing, reaching demand levels above the pandemic-era peak.
fact_evidence: “Home & Garden delivered a record quarter with net sales of $225 million, up 19%, surpassing even COVID-19 pandemic-era demand levels.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Home & Garden sales of “~$206M (+9%)” and described Q3 as the seasonal peak.

description: Global Pet Care organic growth fell short of the preview’s expected momentum: organic sales rose 2.9%, rather than the roughly 7% growth modeled or the mid-to-high-single-digit growth the preview said was needed. Its margin, however, expanded more than the preview modeled.
fact_evidence: “Global Pet Care organic net sales rose 2.9% with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 250 basis points to 19.7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Global Pet Care sales growth of “~7%” and said organic growth “needs to hold mid-to-high single digits”; it estimated an 18.6% margin.

description: Home & Personal Care delivered better operating results than the preview modeled: all three business units grew, while HPC adjusted EBITDA excluding refunds rose to $14.4 million from $7 million in the year-ago quarter, above the preview’s $9 million estimate. Management also disclosed an impairment charge tied to the Oaktree partnership that the preview had not anticipated.
fact_evidence: “All three business units delivering growth”; “Home & Personal Care adjusted EBITDA (ex-refunds) rose $7.4 million to $14.4 million with margin expanding 270 basis points to 5.4%, as the Oaktree partnership drove an impairment charge.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled HPC sales of “~$253M (−1%)” and adjusted EBITDA of “~$9M”; it flagged post-Oaktree economics but did not mention an impairment charge.

description: Underlying adjusted EPS was far below the preview’s $1.49 consensus estimate: excluding the tariff refund, EPS was $0.89 and down year over year. The $2.79 reported figure therefore did not reflect the underlying result investors were expecting.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS reached $2.79 including a $1.90 per share tariff refund benefit, but was only $0.89 excluding refunds, down year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Consensus $1.49 | +20.2%” year over year.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A large tariff refund provided unmodeled upside to reported results: it added $60.6 million to adjusted EBITDA and $1.90 per share to adjusted EPS. The preview had noted that any refund recognition would be unmodeled upside and that refunds were excluded from guidance.
fact_evidence: “A one-time $60.6 million tariff refund lifted reported adjusted EBITDA to $158.3 million”; adjusted EPS included “a $1.90 per share tariff refund benefit.”
expectation_evidence: “Any refund recognition is unmodeled upside”; company guidance excluded tariff refunds.

description: Even excluding tariff refunds, adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s implied estimate: $97.7 million was above its roughly $90–93 million range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA excluding tariff refunds was $97.7 million, up 27.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA (no formal consensus) | ~$90–93M implied.”

description: Management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to mid-single-digit growth, while the preview’s base case expected the framework to be reaffirmed. The preview had identified a raise as possible, so the direction was anticipated but the result was better than its base expectation.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to mid-single-digit growth (excluding tariff refunds).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “FY26 framework reaffirmed, not raised”; it also described a raise to mid-single-digit growth as a possible outcome.

description: Management’s Q4 outlook was more cautious than the preview’s favorable seasonal setup suggested: it warned of tough comparisons in Global Pet Care and elevated retailer inventories and unfavorable late-season weather in Home & Garden.
fact_evidence: “Management warned Q4 will face headwinds as Global Pet Care laps tough prior-year comparisons and Home & Garden contends with elevated retailer inventories and unfavorable late-season weather.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Home & Garden’s retailer inventories as “clean” and flagged a possible constructive line on sell-through into July/August as a bull signal.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The balance sheet was stronger than the preview’s snapshot: cash was $258.9 million and net leverage was about 1x, below the preview’s 1.66x estimate, with no revolver borrowings.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $258.9 million in cash, zero drawn on its revolver, and a net leverage ratio of about 1x, well below its 2-2.5x target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Net leverage 1.66x” and approximately “$0.1B cash.”

description: Share repurchases accelerated from the prior quarter’s sharply reduced pace, contrary to the preview’s concern that continued restraint could be a narrative risk: the company bought back about 200,000 shares for $15.8 million, versus 100,000 shares for $6.8 million in Q2.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 200,000 shares for $15.8 million during the quarter, with over $300 million of Board authorization remaining.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted buybacks had “slowed sharply to 100k shares / $6.8M in Q2” and flagged “continued restraint” as a risk.

description: Q2 sales were $421 million, about 7% below the $452 million consensus and below the preview’s $445–458 million base case; year-over-year growth was about 3%, rather than the roughly 10% consensus growth implied by the estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales reached $421 million, up approximately 3% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $452M”; the preview’s base case was “$445–458M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $32 million, well short of the roughly $50 million implied consensus and the preview’s $47–53 million base case. It also fell $24 million year-over-year despite the preview’s expectation of roughly flat EBITDA dollars.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell $24 million year-over-year to $32 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (implied) ~ $50M”; the preview called for “roughly flat YoY EBITDA dollars” and gave a base case of “$47–53M.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.19 versus $0.56 consensus. The call attributed much of the decline to a higher effective tax rate resulting from prior-year 45Q credits, an added drag on the quarterly result.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped $1.05 to $0.19, largely due to a higher effective tax rate from prior-year 45Q credits.”

description: Despite the weak total results, the sequential price-versus-raw-material bridge improved sharply: net pricing over raw materials moved from a $10 million headwind in Q1 to a $39 million tailwind in Q2. That exceeded the preview’s expectation of cost recovery without margin expansion, although the company described the year-over-year Q2 position as neutral.
fact_evidence: “Net pricing over raw materials swung from a $10 million headwind in Q1 to a $39 million tailwind in Q2 on a sequential basis”; the company “fully offset a $72 million year-over-year raw material cost headwind” and achieved “neutral net price-over-raws in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: Management had said amsul price increases were “largely offsetting sulfur input costs rather than driving margin expansion”; the base case expected seasonal Plant Nutrients strength to “offset record sulfur roughly dollar-for-dollar.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Volume was down 15% even as higher pricing lifted sales, with softer spring ammonium sulfate demand and lower plant nutrient sales contributing. The preview framed Q2 as Plant Nutrients’ seasonal peak and expected seasonal strength to help offset sulfur costs.
fact_evidence: Sales were “driven by 18% favorable pricing that offset a 15% decline in volume”; volume was “a $17 million unfavorable impact primarily from lower plant nutrient sales, as spring ammonium sulfate demand softened.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 “Plant Nutrients’ seasonal peak” and said the base case required “seasonal Plant Nutrients strength” to offset sulfur costs.

description: The company expects full-year 2026 ammonia sales volume to rise 30% to a new record, with first-half sales already up to 49,000 short tons from 33,000. The preview flagged the ammonia-allocation decision but did not anticipate this scale of volume growth.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 ammonia sales volume is expected to rise 30% versus 2025 (a prior record), with first-half sales of 49,000 short tons up from 33,000 a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management was “moderating ammonium sulfate production to push merchant ammonia sales” and asked investors to quantify the mix shift; it gave no volume target.

description: The expected Q3 Plant Nutrients sequential earnings headwind is now forecast to exceed the historical $10–15 million range, due to weak fall-fill pricing and channel inventory liquidation. This is worse than the preview’s already-cautious Q3 seasonal-step-down framing.
fact_evidence: “The Q3 plant nutrient sequential earnings headwind is expected to exceed the historical $10 million to $15 million range due to weak fall fill pricing and channel inventory liquidation.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a “post-planting seasonal step-down in amsul” and identified Q3 framing as a key risk, but did not anticipate a headwind above the historical range.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management cited an expected sulfur-price decline of about $200 entering 2027, which would be a future cost tailwind. The preview highlighted record Q3 sulfur and near-term pressure, but did not mention this prospective reversal.
fact_evidence: “Third-party experts forecast an approximately $200 decline in sulfur prices entering 2027, expected to be a tailwind amid tighter domestic ammonium sulfate supply”; each $100 per long ton change represents roughly $35 million in annual cost impact.
expectation_evidence: The preview focused on Q3 Tampa sulfur at a “record $705/lt” and said “the sulfur problem gets worse before it gets better.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The 10%–15% full-year effective tax-rate guide is below the 23% tax assumption used in the preview’s implied EBITDA calculation, a favorable tax outlook despite the higher tax burden that hurt Q2 EPS.
fact_evidence: The company “guides to a 10%-15% full-year effective tax rate before additional claims.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s implied EBITDA calculation used “23% tax.”

description: Scripps reported a Q2 loss of $12.68 per share, far worse than the preview’s expected loss of $0.43. The result included a $1.1 billion noncash impairment of goodwill and intangibles in Scripps Networks, which the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a Q2 loss of $12.68 per share, including a $1.1 billion noncash goodwill and intangible impairment charge for the Scripps Networks business.”

description: Full-year political advertising guidance of $225 million–$250 million came in well below the preview’s directional expectation of about $340 million and its discussion of a $300 million-plus political year. The preview framed that higher level as central to the investment case.
fact_evidence: “The company expects full-year 2026 political advertising revenue of $225 million-$250 million, well above the $198 million recorded in the 2022 midterm cycle.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year political ambition of at least ~$340M (treat as directional, not hard guidance)” and “a full-year political number in the $300M+ range is the entire equity thesis.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end net leverage reached 4.9x, rather than remaining near the preview’s 3.9x level and below the 4.0x threshold it highlighted. Cash was only $13 million, although the company had no revolver drawn and no near-term maturities.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage rose to 4.9x at quarter-end from 4.4x in Q1, with just $13 million in cash, no revolver drawn, and no near-term debt maturities after extending the credit line to July 2029.”
expectation_evidence: “3.9x at Mar 31” and “Below 3.9x = deleveraging on track. Above 4.0x = the equity stub compresses fast.”

description: Scripps Networks revenue was $172 million, below the preview’s roughly $183 million–$185 million expectation, and segment profit was only $26 million versus the preview’s $31 million estimate. Profit fell to less than half its year-ago level as Nielsen measurement changes and soft direct response advertising weighed on the segment.
fact_evidence: “Scripps Networks Q2 revenue dropped 13% to $172 million and segment profit collapsed to $26 million from $57 million a year ago, driven by Nielsen measurement changes and soft direct response advertising.”
expectation_evidence: “Scripps Networks revenue ~$185M (guide: ‘down ~10%’)” and “Networks segment profit $31M.”

description: Local Media revenue was $317 million, well below the preview’s roughly $338 million–$340 million expectation and down 1% year over year instead of the company’s prior guide for low-single-digit growth. Core advertising fell 4.8%, also weaker than the preview’s low-single-digit decline estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 Local Media revenue was $317 million (down 1% YoY) with core advertising down 4.8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Local Media revenue ~$340M (guide: ‘up low single digits’)” and “Local Media revenue $338M”; the model assumed “core ad down LSD.”

description: The full-year net distribution revenue outlook was reduced to mid- to high-single-digit growth, below the low-double-digit growth the preview said had been raised at Q1 and was important to preserve. Lower network affiliation costs support net revenue despite the expected decline in gross distribution revenue.
fact_evidence: “Full-year gross distribution revenue is now expected down low single digits, but net distribution revenue is guided up mid- to high single digits, aided by lower network affiliation costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch also whether the FY26 net distribution revenue guide of ‘low double-digit growth’ (raised at Q1) survives.”

description: Management raised the year-end transformation savings run-rate target to $100 million, 33% above prior guidance and above the preview’s roughly $75 million run-rate expectation. The longer-term incremental EBITDA target was maintained.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its year-end transformation run-rate savings target to $100 million, up 33% from prior guidance, while maintaining the $125 million-$150 million incremental EBITDA target by 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “~$75M run-rate into 2027”

description: The company disclosed that workforce reductions have reached about 12% of total positions, including 268 employees notified this week. The preview anticipated substantial transformation costs but did not specify cuts on this scale; the announced $40 million–$50 million cash restructuring cost matches the preview’s expected cost-to-achieve range.
fact_evidence: “The workforce reduction totals 432 eliminated positions plus 126 open positions (about 12% of the total) year-to-date, including 268 employees notified this week, with $40 million-$50 million in cash restructuring costs expected.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management gave added visibility on distribution renewals: 70% of pay-TV subscribers renewed this year, with only 5% resetting in 2027 and about 20% in 2028. The preview noted that major renewals had closed, but did not anticipate these specific renewal and reset figures.
fact_evidence: “The company renewed 70% of its pay-TV subscribers this year, with only 5% resetting in 2027 and about 20% in 2028, providing multiyear distribution visibility.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: DTI generated $4.1 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2, above the preview’s roughly $1–3 million base-case expectation. Q2 capex was also lower than expected at about $4.2 million, versus the preview’s estimate of roughly $6.5 million in its base case.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $4.1 million”; “Q2 capital expenditures fell to approximately $4.2 million from $7.7 million in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “adj. FCF +$1–3M” and “capex steps down to ~$6.5M.” The preview also assumed approximately “+$2M” Q2 adjusted FCF if revenue was at consensus.

description: Despite the low Q2 capex, management said the usual second-half capex taper will not happen because of ClearPath stabilizer investment for Norway, and that full-year free cash flow is likely to land toward the low end of guidance. The preview had flagged a possible lower-end FCF outcome if investments accelerated, but did not anticipate this specific investment or the absence of the usual taper.
fact_evidence: “Elevated CapEx tied to ClearPath stabilizer investment for the Norwegian market means the usual second-half CapEx taper won't occur, likely pushing full-year free cash flow toward the lower end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 capex “must fall toward ~$5M/quarter for the FCF guide to hold at all,” while also noting management had warned FCF could “land at the lower end” if targeted investments accelerated.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net debt rose to $51.7 million from $48.9 million at the end of Q1, exceeding the preview’s stated $50 million bear-case threshold even though Q2 free cash flow was positive. Management attributed the increase primarily to the Norway investment.
fact_evidence: “Net debt rose modestly to $51.7 million as of June 30, 2026, primarily due to the Norway investment, with cash of only $2.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “net debt >$50M” as a bear-case outcome and described leverage as “the tail risk, not the base case.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Tool rental gross margin stayed above 70%, as expected, but management added that pricing compression appears to have stabilized after several quarters of decline. The preview anticipated continued pricing pressure and treated a break below 70% as the downside risk; stabilization is a more favorable update than it forecast.
fact_evidence: “Tool rental gross margin remained above 70% even amid pricing compression, which management believes has now stabilized after several quarters of decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said DTI had flagged “continued pricing pressure on US land” and identified rental gross margin holding “>70%” as a key metric to watch.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: DTI reported that the global rig count fell nearly 4% sequentially, including an almost 7% decline in the Middle East, yet still delivered Q2 results that stepped up from Q1 and the year-ago quarter. The preview emphasized improving U.S. and Canadian activity rather than a global rig-count decline of this size.
fact_evidence: “Results were achieved despite a global rig count decline of nearly 4% sequentially, with the Middle East rig count falling almost 7% and accounting for roughly half of the global decline”; revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted free cash flow were a “step up from both Q1 2026 and the year-ago quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted a “meaningfully positive y/y activity backdrop,” including U.S. rig counts up 48 year over year and Canada up 42 year over year.

description: The completion of former sponsor HHEP’s share distribution left about 90% of DTI’s shares in public hands, improving independence and trading liquidity—an ownership change the preview did not flag.
fact_evidence: “Following the completion of former sponsor HHEP's share distribution, approximately 90% of outstanding shares are now in public float, improving DTI's independence and trading liquidity.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.02 per share better than the preview’s $0.04 loss estimate, while GAAP EPS was a $0.05 loss, one cent worse than that estimate. The earnings comparison is mixed because the preview did not specify whether its EPS estimate was GAAP or adjusted.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a Q2 net loss of approximately $1.8 million ($0.05 per share) and an adjusted net loss of $575,000 ($0.02 per share).”

description: Geospace reported Q3 revenue of $15.8 million versus the preview’s $23.5 million estimate, and a $0.75 diluted loss per share versus the estimated $0.48 loss. Revenue was about one-third below the model and the per-share loss was substantially worse.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $15.8 million” and the company reported “a net loss of $9.7 million ($0.75 per diluted share).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “Revenue $23.5M” and “Diluted EPS $(0.48).”

description: Energy Solutions revenue was $5.9 million, less than half the preview’s $12.0 million estimate. Rather than the expected PRM-led sequential ramp, the segment declined 28% year over year amid weak ocean-bottom nodal demand and the prior-year sale of the streamer recovery device line.
fact_evidence: “Energy Solutions Q3 revenue declined 28% to $5.9 million,” hurt by “weak ocean bottom nodal product demand” and “the prior-year sale of the streamer recovery device product line.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Energy Solutions revenue of “$12.0M” and expected “PRM ramps on schedule.”

description: Intelligent Industrial revenue was $5.2 million, below the preview’s $6.3 million estimate, and fell 14% year over year instead of coming in roughly flat or slightly higher.
fact_evidence: “Intelligent Industrial revenue slipped 14% to $5.2 million in Q3” on lower industrial sensor demand and reduced contract manufacturing services.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Intelligent Industrial revenue at “$6.3M” and “flat” sequentially; its year-over-year estimate was “+3%.”

description: Smart Water improved from Q2 but its $4.6 million of revenue was below the preview’s $5.2 million estimate, with Hydroconn demand still sharply lower. It did, however, narrowly clear the preview’s roughly $4.5 million warning threshold for deeper destocking.
fact_evidence: “Smart Water segment posted the steepest deterioration, with Q3 revenue plunging 56% to $4.6 million from $10.5 million due to reduced Hydroconn connector demand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Smart Water at “$5.2M” and said “anything below ~$4.5M means destocking is deeper or longer than framed.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Customer-requested scope changes pushed the PRM contract schedule back by one quarter, contrary to the preview’s base case of an on-schedule ramp. Management said the contract’s total value was unchanged and there was no financial impact, tempering the timing setback.
fact_evidence: “Customer-requested scope changes delayed the PRM contract”; management said “there is no financial impact and the total contract value remains unchanged,” describing it as “effectively representing a one-quarter delay.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “PRM ramps on schedule”; it identified a one-quarter PRM timing slip as a bear-case risk.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Quantum/SADAR-PRM contract’s revenue is expected to extend into FY2028, later than the preview’s description of the award as running through the end of FY2027. The contract award itself was anticipated, but the reported recognition schedule reaches beyond that preview timeframe.
fact_evidence: The $10.8 million contract has delivery expected “by end of December 2027” and revenue recognized “over time across FY2027 and FY2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the July 30 award as “running through end of FY2027.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Mercer reported going-concern status, reclassified its Canadian and German revolvers as current liabilities, and said it will likely breach the German facility’s leverage ratio in Q4 2026. That is materially worse than the preview’s base case of “no covenant news” and its stated expectation that the company would comply by Q4.
fact_evidence: “The company disclosed going-concern status, reclassifying its Canadian and German revolving credit facilities to current liabilities and warning it will likely breach its German facility's leverage ratio in Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Management expects compliance by Q4 2026”; the base case anticipated “no covenant news,” while the bear case flagged “going-concern language changes.”

description: Operating EBITDA was -$21 million, far below the preview’s derived $20–30 million expectation. Both pulp and solid wood lost money, and the German mills were below cash break-even, with management estimating $35–40 million of improvement needed to reach break-even including capital needs.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 operating EBITDA turned negative at -$21 million”; pulp was “-$13 million” and solid wood “-$8 million.” The German mills were “operating below cash break-even,” requiring “$35-40 million total improvement to reach break-even including capital needs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Operating EBITDA ~ $20–30M” and said the base case was “$18–30M”; it expected solid wood “near breakeven” on the mass timber ramp.

description: Mercer’s net loss was $76 million, or $1.13 per share, versus the preview’s approximately $0.58-per-share loss consensus. A $29 million non-cash inventory impairment driven by high German fiber costs contributed to the worse result.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $76 million ($1.13 per share) ... including a $29 million non-cash inventory impairment ($0.43 per share) driven by high German fiber costs.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) Consensus: ~-$0.58 (range -$0.56 to -$0.62).” The preview’s EBITDA test also described a clean quarter as having “no repeat impairment.”

description: German fiber costs rose rather than stabilizing, and management expects German pulp fiber to remain elevated in Q3. The increase was concentrated in Germany: Canadian fiber costs declined.
fact_evidence: “German pulp and sawmill fiber costs rose roughly 7% quarter-over-quarter to historically high levels,” while Canadian fiber costs “declined about 4%”; management expects German pulp fiber to “remain elevated in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided for fiber to “stabilize in Q2 on better German availability and US chip supply to Celgar,” and called stabilization the key fiber-cost watch item.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Mercer’s liquidity fell to about $192 million, below the preview’s $195–215 million base-case range. The decline was $37 million despite the preview identifying the quarter-end liquidity figure as the most important number.
fact_evidence: “Aggregate liquidity fell $37 million to about $192 million ($79 million cash plus $113 million undrawn revolvers) due to weak operating results.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated liquidity “drifts to ~$195–215M”; it flagged “above $210M” as relief and “below $180M” as the bear case.

description: Mercer disclosed that it had engaged advisors and was negotiating with holders of its 2028 and 2029 notes and other stakeholders to restructure its capital structure. The preview discussed refinancing the Canadian revolver as a potential positive, but did not anticipate negotiations to restructure the broader capital structure.
fact_evidence: “Management has engaged advisors and is negotiating with holders of its 2028 and 2029 senior notes and other stakeholders to restructure its capital structure and enhance liquidity.”

description: The Torgau restructuring includes eliminating 100 positions in July and another 250 by Q2 2027, with about $3 million of severance costs in each of 2026 and 2027. The company targets a turnaround exceeding $20 million, making this a substantial new cost-cutting plan with both execution costs and prospective savings.
fact_evidence: “The Torgau restructuring includes cutting from four shifts to three, eliminating 100 positions in July with 250 more by Q2 2027, targeting a turnaround exceeding $20 million with severance costs of about $3 million in each of 2026 and 2027.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Mass timber’s reported backlog was $151 million, below the preview’s cited $171 million, while roughly 70% of the backlog was hyperscaler data-center work versus the preview’s estimate of roughly 60%. The report gave revenue growth of over 25% quarter over quarter, alongside production growth of about 40%.
fact_evidence: “The mass timber business grew Q2 revenue over 25% and production about 40% quarter-over-quarter, with a $151 million backlog roughly 70% comprising hyperscaler data center projects.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$171M” mass timber backlog and said “~60%” of the work was hyperscaler data-center work; it flagged backlog direction as something to watch.

description: The preview estimated Q2 adjusted EBITDA at about $30–33 million and worried margins might not reach the roughly 5.5% needed to support consensus EPS. Manitowoc reported $49 million of adjusted EBITDA, with margin above 8%, a substantially stronger result than expected.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $49 million with margin expanding 330 basis points to over 8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA *~$30–33M (est.)*”; the preview also said “Consensus EPS of $0.11 needs roughly 5.5% EBITDA margin.”

description: The preview expected the full-year EBITDA guide to be reaffirmed or narrowed, with its base case pointing to $125–140 million. Instead, the company raised the range to $150–170 million, taking the new low end up to the old high end and lifting the midpoint by $22.5 million.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to… adjusted EBITDA of $150-$170 million”; “The adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint was raised $22.5 million (from $137.5 million to $160 million).”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 company guidance… adj. EBITDA $125–150M”; the base scenario expected EBITDA guidance to be narrowed “to $125–140M.”

description: Q2 sales were well above the $564 million consensus estimate. The $595 million result was a roughly 5.5% beat, rather than the preview’s expected in-line range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 10% year-over-year to $595 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 Consensus | $564.0M.”

description: The preview expected full-year sales guidance to be reaffirmed or potentially narrowed, while noting Street revenue consensus was below the existing guide’s floor. The company instead raised its sales range by $50 million at both ends, to $2.3–2.4 billion.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to net sales of $2.3-$2.4 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 company guidance… Net sales $2.25–2.35B”; the preview said guidance might be “reaffirmed, narrow, or cut” and identified $2.22 billion as Street consensus.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview framed tariffs primarily as a worsening second-half cost headwind and noted refund claims and a possible Customs-related charge risk. Instead, refunds were already a material Q2 benefit, with additional benefit expected in Q3 and a positive full-year net EBITDA contribution.
fact_evidence: “Tariff refunds contributed a $12 million operating income benefit in Q2 (from $26 million cash received),” with a “full-year net EBITDA benefit… estimated at $16 million” and “another ~$4 million benefit expected in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “tariffs hit us for more in the second half than the first half,” cited “~$25M of IEEPA refund claims filed,” and flagged the Customs disclosure as a “tail risk that could surface as a charge.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview’s base case expected exit backlog around $930–970 million. Backlog instead reached $1.05 billion; that exceeded the base case, although it crossed a level the preview had identified in its bull scenario.
fact_evidence: Orders lifted backlog to “$1.05 billion (up $321 million from a year ago), with roughly $750 million expected to ship this year.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “backlog roughly flat at $930–970M”; the bull scenario specified “backlog >$1.0B.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview reported net leverage at 3.1 times after Q1 and identified deleveraging as an important issue. By Q2, leverage had fallen below the company’s three-times target to approximately 2.6 times.
fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to approximately 2.6 times, dropping below the company's three-times target on stronger first-half performance.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 FCF $19.2M… liquidity $316M, net leverage 3.1x”; the preview described deleveraging progress as important to supporting equity value.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview characterized the July Japanese crawler-crane duty order as a modest wildcard, citing a 2.79% weighted-average margin and expecting sentiment or long-run share effects rather than a significant near-term earnings effect. The reported 12–20% import tariffs were a stronger competitive measure than that framing suggested.
fact_evidence: “The U.S. Department of Commerce and ITC confirmed Japanese crawler crane dumping and imposed import tariffs ranging from 12% to 20%, improving Manitowoc's competitive positioning.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the order “headline-positive and strategically real, but the weighted-average margin is only 2.79%… — this is sentiment and long-run share, not a 2026 earnings driver.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: July orders above $200 million in a seasonally slow month provided an additional demand signal that the preview had not anticipated. It supports momentum after the strong Q2 order intake.
fact_evidence: “July orders exceeded $200 million despite being a seasonally slow month.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management’s comments gave a mixed picture of end-market demand not specifically anticipated in the preview: oil, gas, and mining had not yet contributed meaningfully despite higher commodity prices, while data-center and semiconductor investment demand was expected to continue into 2027.
fact_evidence: “Management noted oil, gas, and mining sectors have yet to contribute meaningfully despite higher commodity prices, while data center and semiconductor investment demand is expected to continue into 2027.”

description: Q3 revenue was $999.4 million, about 4.6% above the preview’s $950 million working estimate and well above the $948.8–$955.5 million consensus range. Revenue growth of 28.2% also exceeded the preview’s expected 21.6–22.6%.
fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue reached $999.4 million, up 28.2% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “I'd treat $950M as the true bar”; consensus revenue was “$948.8–955.5M” and implied “+21.6–22.6% y/y.”

description: Despite the revenue beat, adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.3%, below the preview’s 17.0% expectation and even below its 16.5% downside threshold. Adjusted EBITDA dollars were near expectations, so the shortfall was chiefly in margin rather than the absolute EBITDA result.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $163 million (up 24%) with a 16.3% margin”; gross profit margin was “roughly flat at 16.8% versus 16.9% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q3 estimate was “$161.5M (17.0% margin)” and it said “Sub-16.5% makes the FY guide arithmetically strained.”

description: The company raised its full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, whereas the preview’s base case anticipated a revenue nudge but no EBITDA increase. The new adjusted EBITDA range tops the preview’s $565 million threshold, though its midpoint is $564 million.
fact_evidence: “The company raised fiscal 2026 guidance to revenue of $3.64–$3.68 billion, net income of $165–$168 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $559–$569 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said its base case was “FY revenue nudged up for Ellsworth, EBITDA range narrowed not raised,” and that “The buy-side wants EBITDA raised to $565M+.”

description: Organic growth was 8.9%, above the preview’s 7–8% full-year target and its 7–8% Q3 revenue-build assumption. This suggests the quarter’s growth was not solely an acquisition-driven beat.
fact_evidence: Revenue growth comprised “8.9% organic growth and 19.3% acquisitive growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s revenue build assumed “7–8% organic,” and identified “Organic growth (7–8% FY target)” as a key metric to watch.

description: Acquisitive growth contributed 19.3 percentage points to Q3 revenue growth, more than the preview’s roughly even split of the expected $225–235 million of second-half acquisition revenue implied for Q3. The stronger-than-modeled acquired contribution makes the revenue beat more acquisition-heavy than anticipated.
fact_evidence: Revenue growth comprised “8.9% organic growth and 19.3% acquisitive growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$225–235M of acquisitive revenue across the full second half” and assumed “~$113–118M in Q3.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog reached $3.36 billion, above the preview’s $3.20–$3.30 billion estimate and its stated concern about a sequential decline below roughly $3.10 billion. That was a stronger forward-work signal than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Record project backlog hit $3.36 billion at June 30, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Backlog (6/30/26) $3.20–3.30B” and warned that “A sequential decline below ~$3.10B would confirm the deceleration narrative.”

description: Management pointed to about $140 million of carryover revenue from Ellsworth and prior acquisitions into fiscal 2027, supporting expected strong organic growth. The preview focused on Ellsworth’s limited contribution to Q4 FY26, not this FY27 carryover and growth outlook.
fact_evidence: “The completed Ellsworth Construction acquisition and prior deals contribute approximately $140 million of carryover revenue into fiscal 2027, supporting expected strong organic growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Ellsworth “closed July 13 — that's fiscal Q4, not Q3” and would contribute “only ~2.5 months to Q4.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Liquid asphalt price inflation added $8–$10 million to Q3 revenue, an identifiable pricing contribution the preview did not flag. It is a modest part of the revenue beat and may not represent underlying volume growth.
fact_evidence: “Liquid AC price inflation added $8–$10 million to Q3 revenue.”

description: The company expanded its revolving credit facility by $200 million and added $300 million of Term Loan B while lowering interest-rate margins. The preview discussed leverage and Ellsworth-related debt, but did not anticipate this financing package or the lower pricing.
fact_evidence: “The company expanded its revolving credit facility from $500 million to $700 million and added $300 million in incremental Term Loan B while lowering interest rate margins.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Free cash flow and leverage” as a key issue and noted that “Ellsworth added debt.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management said it expected no disruption to federal funding in FY26 or FY27 and cited a proposed bill that would raise IIJA-level highway funding by about 7.2%, with roughly 45% of IIJA funding still undeployed. This was a more reassuring public-funding outlook than the preview’s concern about project-start timing and public lettings.
fact_evidence: “Management expects no disruption to federal funding in fiscal 2026 or 2027,” and said the House's Build America 250 Act “would raise IIJA-level highway funding by about 7.2%” while “~45% of IIJA funding remains undeployed.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “timing of project starts” and “public lettings normalizing” as potential warning signs in management commentary.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management highlighted substantial data-center construction activity in CPI’s footprint and large Texas and Oklahoma project pipelines, a demand opportunity not identified in the preview. The figures indicate a pipeline rather than secured awards, so the near-term impact is uncertain.
fact_evidence: “An estimated 70–75% of new US data center construction is occurring in CPI's 8 states,” with Texas and Oklahoma platforms showing project pipelines exceeding “$100 million and $130 million respectively.”

description: Vistra kept its 2027 adjusted EBITDA opportunity range at $7.4B-$7.8B, as the preview’s base case expected, but management said it was trending toward the lower end because ERCOT forward curves were meaningfully lower and only partly offset by PJM prices, hedging and the nuclear PTC.
fact_evidence: “Maintained the 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint opportunity range of $7.4B-$7.8B but acknowledged trending toward the lower end due to meaningfully lower ERCOT forward curves only partly offset by higher PJM prices, hedging, and the nuclear PTC.”
expectation_evidence: “Base: ... FY26 and 2027 reaffirmed unchanged”; the preview also identified the 2027 range as the key re-rating question and said silence could confirm concerns about the outlook.

description: The unchanged 2026 guidance came with stronger language than a plain reaffirmation: management expressed confidence in delivering at or above the midpoint, rather than simply leaving the range unchanged.
fact_evidence: “Vistra reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $6.8B-$7.6B adjusted EBITDA and $3.925B-$4.725B adjusted free cash flow, expressing confidence in delivering at or above the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a third consecutive plain reaffirmation at the midpoint” would be a tacit admission that hedges capped upside, while narrowing to the upper half would be the “cleanest bullish tell.”

description: Vistra quantified potential additional 2027 EBITDA from the still-pending Cogentrix acquisition and Meta nuclear PPAs: together they could add roughly $700 million to the midpoint opportunity, though both remain excluded from current guidance.
fact_evidence: “The pending Cogentrix acquisition and Meta nuclear PPAs, both excluded from current guidance, could add roughly $700 million to the 2027 midpoint opportunity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side investors wanted “a quantified 2027 EBITDA contribution” from Cogentrix and noted that the 2027 range excludes Cogentrix and Meta; it did not give a combined contribution estimate.

description: Vistra announced a new commitment of up to $1 billion to Helix Digital Infrastructure and a preferred-power-partner role, a specific platform investment and commercial relationship not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Vistra committed up to $1 billion to the new Helix Digital Infrastructure platform (with KKR, NVIDIA, and the Kuwait Investment Authority), with amounts above $500 million contingent on milestones, and will serve as preferred power partner.”
expectation_evidence: The preview watched for “any new hyperscaler PPA” and mentioned the growth pipeline, but did not anticipate the Helix platform, investment commitment or preferred-partner arrangement.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management outlined more than $10 billion of available cash across 2026-2027, but said $2B-$2.5B would still be unallocated through year-end 2027 after planned equity-holder returns and growth investments.
fact_evidence: “Vistra expects more than $10 billion of available cash across 2026-2027, allocating ~$3B to equity holders, $4.5B-$5B to growth investments, and leaving $2B-$2.5B of additional cash still to be allocated through year-end 2027.”

description: Vistra said cumulative shareholder returns since November 2021 had already exceeded its $6 billion target, with about $1.2 billion of authorization remaining and a commitment to exhaust it by end-2027; the preview had indicated about $1.5 billion remained.
fact_evidence: “Since November 2021, Vistra has retired approximately 171 million shares at an average cost of about $38, returning over $6.5 billion to shareholders, ahead of its $6 billion target, with roughly $1.2 billion of authorization remaining to be exhausted by end of 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “$1.5B authorization remaining, ≥$1B/yr committed, ~$600M returned Dec-2025 through May-2026.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management put a much smaller number on realistic ERCOT data-center load than the volume of requests in the queue: 12-15 GW by 2030 versus requests exceeding 400 GW. That sharp distinction was not quantified in the preview, which discussed AI-power demand and an ERCOT record peak but not the likely realized load or queue scale.
fact_evidence: “Management estimates realistic ERCOT data center load of 12-15 GW by 2030 versus queue requests exceeding 400 GW, supporting a queue cleanup under Governor Abbott's directive.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the debate as “payback period on AI capex, not physical demand” and said the market “currently pays for none” of the contracted-revenue potential, without providing a realistic-load estimate or queue comparison.

description: Q2 revenue was $839 million, well above the preview’s $793 million consensus and the stated $800 million high end of guidance; the call said it exceeded the high end of adjusted guidance by about $9 million. This was a substantial upside print against the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $839 million, up 9% year-over-year and exceeding the high end of adjusted guidance by about $9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 total revenue consensus of “$793M” and company guidance of “$780–800M.”

description: Q3 political revenue guidance of $165–185 million was far above the preview’s $70–85 million buy-side expectation. The preview expected a Q3 political number with a “7-handle”; guidance instead started with a 1.
fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 political revenue to a range of $165 million to $185 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Buy-side wants a Q3 political number with a 7-handle in front of it ($70M+)” and described the buy-side whisper as “$70–85M.”

description: Q2 political revenue reached $83 million, above both the $60–70 million company guidance range and the preview’s roughly $65 million estimate. It also approached the $90 million reported for the 2022 presidential-year quarter, rather than merely delivering the expected political uplift.
fact_evidence: “Q2 political revenue of $83 million far surpassed the $60-70 million guidance range” and “beat the $47 million from the 2024 presidential-year quarter and approached the $90 million from 2022.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 political consensus of “~$65M” and company guidance of “$60–70M.”

description: Net retransmission revenue was $150 million, above the preview’s roughly $142 million estimate and the $141–143 million guidance range, despite a distributor blackout that lasted until May 1. The preview had identified retransmission as a key structural test, so the upside despite the blackout was better than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net retransmission revenue of $150 million topped guidance despite including a blackout with a major distributor that ended May 1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed net retransmission consensus of “~$142M” and guidance of “$141–143M,” and flagged “Net retransmission + full-year reaffirmation” as a key metric to watch.

description: Management said refinancing activity could cut interest expense by more than $30 million from the current 2026 estimate of $440 million, with the benefit flowing dollar-for-dollar to free cash flow because of the 163(j) limitation. The preview expected refinancing commentary but did not anticipate a quantified reduction of this size.
fact_evidence: “Refinancing activity could reduce interest expense by over $30 million from the current full-year 2026 estimate of $440 million, benefiting free cash flow dollar-for-dollar due to a 163(j) deductibility limitation.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “expect an updated year-end leverage target and refinancing commentary.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Acquisitions delivered 0.18x of deleveraging, short of the roughly 0.25x initially anticipated. Although total net leverage fell to 5.73x from 5.94x, the acquisition contribution to deleveraging was less than expected.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated total net leverage stood at 5.73x as of June 30, 2026, down from 5.94x in Q1, with acquisitions delivering 0.18x of deleveraging versus the ~0.25x initially anticipated.”
expectation_evidence: The call said acquisitions were expected to deliver “~0.25x” of deleveraging.

description: Full-year CapEx guidance was lowered to $120–130 million from $140 million, an additional reduction beyond the preview’s stated $140 million plan. That is a favorable change to the expected spending and cash-flow outlook.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance was lowered to $120-130 million from $140 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Capex $140M (back-end weighted).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The full-year tax estimate was reduced to $80–100 million, below the preview’s $90–110 million estimate. The ranges overlap, but both ends of the updated range are $10 million lower.
fact_evidence: “The full-year tax estimate was reduced to $80-100 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY tax guidance cut $25M to $90–110M.”

description: The Board authorized up to $250 million of additional open-market debt repurchases. The preview anticipated continued repurchases but did not identify an authorization of this size.
fact_evidence: The company “received Board authorization to buy back up to $250 million of debt in the open market.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “continuation of the July open-market note repurchases” the cleanest bridge to deleveraging, but gave no expectation for a new authorization.

description: The company redeemed $50 million of Series A preferred equity, an additional capital-structure action not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company redeemed $50 million of Series A preferred equity.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: TDS Telecom delivered 66,000 fiber service addresses in Q2 and 106,000 in the first half, above the preview’s roughly 53,000-per-quarter guide pace. TDS then raised its full-year address target by 50,000, while also raising CapEx guidance to fund the faster build.
fact_evidence: “Delivered approximately 66,000 marketable fiber service addresses in Q2 and about 106,000 in the first half”; “raised its 2026 fiber service address guidance by 50,000 to a range of 250,000-300,000, and increased CapEx guidance to $625 million-$675 million.”
expectation_evidence: “The FY bridge needs ~53–70k per quarter”; original guidance was “200,000 – 250,000” new marketable fiber addresses and “$550 – $600M” Telecom CapEx.

description: TDS Telecom lowered its 2026 revenue guidance to $1.0–$1.025 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $310–$330 million, rather than maintaining the prior ranges. Management attributed the pressure to copper and cable legacy revenue declines falling to the bottom line.
fact_evidence: “Lowered its 2026 total telecom revenue guidance to $1.0 billion-$1.025 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA to $310 million-$330 million, citing copper and cable legacy revenue pressures falling to the bottom line.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Telecom guidance of “$1,015 – $1,055M” revenue and “$310 – $350M” adjusted EBITDA, and said a formal revenue-guide cut was “the clearest bear trigger.”

description: Residential revenue still fell by $6 million even as fiber revenue grew, rather than fiber and residential growth roughly offsetting legacy erosion as the preview expected. Cable revenue declined about 10%, though fiber revenue increased 13% and helped cushion the decline.
fact_evidence: “Fiber revenue grew 13% (+$11 million) to help offset a roughly 10% decline in cable revenue and total residential revenue falling $6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimate logic expected “Fiber/residential growth roughly offsetting copper + coax erosion.”

description: Array raised its 2026 guidance: the low end of revenue guidance moved up to $205 million, and adjusted OIBDA guidance increased to $60–$75 million. This was stronger than the preview’s existing revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges.
fact_evidence: “Array raised its 2026 guidance, increasing adjusted OIBDA to $60 million-$75 million and adjusted EBITDA to $220 million-$235 million, and lifted the low end of revenue guidance to $205 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Array revenue guidance of “$200 – $215M” and adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$50 – $65M.”

description: Array completed a $168 million T-Mobile spectrum sale during Q2, while the preview described the residual T-Mobile spectrum piece as potentially still pending. Together with the Verizon transaction, agreements now cover roughly 70% of Array’s spectrum holdings, with C-band retained and no near-term build-out requirement.
fact_evidence: “Reached agreements to monetize roughly 70% of its spectrum holdings, closing a $168 million sale to T-Mobile and a $1 billion transaction with Verizon during Q2, while retaining its highly valued C-band with no near-term build-out requirements.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If the residual T-Mobile spectrum piece is still pending, this creates a live question,” and listed “any update on residual spectrum monetization” as something to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Array’s tenancy ratio improved sequentially to 0.96 excluding DISH, a constructive result against the preview’s focus on T-Mobile decommissioning churn and colocation as key indicators.
fact_evidence: “Its tower tenancy ratio improved sequentially from 0.94 to 0.96 excluding DISH.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “churn vs. colocation” and said “Net site rental growth, new colocation applications, and tenancy ratio are the tells.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed that DISH had stopped making payments and filed for bankruptcy, a counterparty risk not identified in the preview. The facts provided do not quantify the resulting revenue or cash impact.
fact_evidence: DISH “stopped payments in December and has filed for bankruptcy.”

description: TDS made no share repurchases in Q2, leaving $520 million under its authorization because of restrictions connected to the pending Array minority-interest offer. The preview highlighted buyback pace as a key capital-allocation signal but did not anticipate a quarter with no repurchases.
fact_evidence: “TDS made no share repurchases in Q2 due to restrictions tied to its pending offer to acquire Array's minority interest, leaving $520 million remaining under its buyback authorization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “buyback pace” and noted that “buyback commentary carries outsized signal value.”

description: TDS agreed to acquire Granite State Communications, adding 11,000 fully fiber service addresses for $25 million, an unanticipated tuck-in transaction that expands the fiber footprint.
fact_evidence: “Agreed to acquire Granite State Communications, adding 11,000 fully fiber service addresses for $25 million with an expected Q3 close.”

description: Q2 sales were $528 million, $17.5 million above the preview’s $510.5 million consensus estimate, a beat of about 3.4%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales hit a record $528 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $510.5M”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.82, $0.03 above the preview’s $0.79 consensus. The preview’s base case was roughly $0.78–$0.80.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose to $0.82.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.79”; “Base … Adj. EPS … ~$0.78–$0.80.”

description: The full-year adjusted EPS range moved up at the low end to $2.85 from the prior $2.75, narrowing the range to the upper half the preview said investors wanted. The top end stayed at $3.00.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS is guided to $2.85 to $3.00.”
expectation_evidence: “Current FY26 … adj. EPS $2.75–$3.00”; “The buy-side wants the range narrowed to the upper half ($2.85–$3.00).”

description: Full-year revenue guidance was raised: its midpoint is about $2.003 billion, versus $1.980 billion in the preview’s prior guidance range, and the low end rose by $30 million.
fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance is $1.975 billion to $2.03 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Current FY26: sales $1,945–2,015M”; the preview’s base case expected “FY guidance reaffirmed unchanged.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $109 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of about $105–106 million, alongside the sales beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $109 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived) | ~$105M”; “$0.79 adj. EPS ⇒ … ~$105–106M adjusted EBITDA.”

description: The company lowered the top of its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook by 25 basis points, citing moderating pricing and FX benefits and Middle East-related cost pressures.
fact_evidence: “Narrowed full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 19.75%-20.25%, lowering the top end by 25 basis points due to moderating pricing/FX benefits and Middle East-related cost pressures.”
expectation_evidence: “Current FY26 … adj. EBITDA margin 19.5–20.5%.”

description: Industrial Solutions EBITDA margin fell sequentially to 18.9% because of one-time Koch transition inefficiencies, below the preview’s focus on integration progress and a run-rate of at least $40 million without highlighting such margin disruption.
fact_evidence: “Industrial Solutions EBITDA margin dipped sequentially to 18.9% on one-time transition inefficiencies.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for: run-rate ≥$40M, integration confirmed on schedule”; “Full integration was guided to complete early Q3 2026.”

description: The planned 2026 share-repurchase range is lower than the preview’s cited $20–40 million plan: the new range is $14–20 million. Management instead said surplus cash would go toward gross-debt repayment.
fact_evidence: “Share repurchases for 2026 are guided at $14M-$20M”; “management now intends to allocate surplus cash toward paying down gross debt.”
expectation_evidence: “Buyback plan is $20–40M for 2026”; the preview also said “Deleveraging pace matters more than repurchase here.”

description: The full-year Power Solutions outlook includes 1.5% pricing and about a 2% FX tailwind, both above the preview’s assumptions of roughly 1% total pricing and 1% FX.
fact_evidence: “Power Solutions expected to see … ~1.5% pricing, and ~2% FX tailwind.”
expectation_evidence: “FY assumes ~1% total pricing (base + tariffs …) [and] ~1% FX tailwind.”

description: PPL reported ongoing EPS of $0.33, below the preview’s $0.35 estimate by $0.02. That is a modest miss against the expected quarter.
fact_evidence: “PPL reported Q2 2026 ongoing earnings of $0.33 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Ongoing EPS | Q2 2026E | $0.35”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Pennsylvania’s data-center pipeline and its conversion to more committed stages were ahead of the preview’s base-case range: signed agreements reached about 32 GW, with over 11 GW under ESAs and over 6.5 GW under construction. The preview expected 28–30 GW overall and cited about 10 GW under ESAs and 5 GW under construction.
fact_evidence: “Signed data center agreements in Pennsylvania rose for the tenth consecutive quarter to about 32 gigawatts, with over 11 gigawatts now under ESAs carrying financial commitments and over 6.5 gigawatts under construction.”
expectation_evidence: “Base = … pipeline 28–30 GW”; the preview also cited “~10 GW under signed ESAs and ~5 GW under construction.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Kentucky’s probability-weighted expected new load rose to 3.7 GW from the preview’s 3.5 GW estimate, and management said this is likely to trigger a $3.5–4 billion CPCN filing by year-end. This modestly strengthens the expected Kentucky growth pipeline.
fact_evidence: “Kentucky’s development pipeline expanded to 13.7 gigawatts with probability-weighted expected new load now at 3.7 gigawatts by 2032 … likely triggering a new CPCN filing of $3.5-4 billion by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: “KY economic-development pipeline 12.9 GW through 2032, probability-weighted ~3.5 GW”; a new CPCN filing was described as possible “as early as later in 2026.”

description: PPL disclosed $10–12 billion of potential incremental investment through 2032 from Kentucky generation and Invitium, beyond the $23 billion plan through 2029. The preview discussed possible incremental transmission capex, but did not anticipate this additional long-dated investment scale or these sources.
fact_evidence: “$10-12 billion of potential incremental capital from Kentucky generation and Invitium through 2032.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “at least another $500M” of incremental transmission beyond the $23B/2029 plan.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Pennsylvania rate increase took effect as expected, but the settlement also includes a two-year stay-out provision through July 1, 2028, providing additional rate-case certainty not highlighted in the preview.
fact_evidence: “PPL’s Pennsylvania rate case settlement took effect July 1 with a $275 million increase … including a 2-year stay-out provision through July 1, 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “PA distribution rate increase (+$275M annualized) only took effect July 1, 2026”; it did not mention a stay-out provision.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: PPL disclosed large-load contract protections requiring 10- to 15-year terms, minimum 80% capacity-payment guarantees, upfront collateral, and termination fees. These terms provide more explicit customer-commitment protections than the preview discussed.
fact_evidence: “Large-load tariffs require 10-year (PA) to 15-year (KY) contracts with minimum 80% capacity payment guarantees, upfront collateral, and termination fees.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Pennsylvania large-load customers will also contribute $11 million annually to low-income assistance starting in 2027, a customer-related cost or obligation not raised in the preview.
fact_evidence: “PA large-load customers will contribute $11 million annually to low-income assistance starting 2027.”

description: SharpLink’s SG&A rose to $9.1 million from $2.4 million a year earlier, an increase the preview did not call out. The company attributed it to a full quarter of ETH-treasury operating costs, including personnel, custody, insurance, and public-company expenses.
fact_evidence: “SG&A expenses jumped to $9.1 million from $2.4 million,” reflecting “a full quarter of ETH treasury operations including personnel, custody, insurance, and public company costs.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash on hand nearly doubled to $56.2 million from $28.5 million at year-end 2025, a stronger cash position than the preview discussed. The preview noted the June offering but did not give an expected cash balance.
fact_evidence: “Cash on hand nearly doubled to $56.2 million as of June 30, 2026 from $28.5 million at year-end 2025.”

description: Q2 revenue was $26.1 million, far above the preview’s $17.5 million estimate—about 49% higher. The preview expected growth, but not a quarter this large.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $26.1 million,” up 19% sequentially.
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 est.” for total revenue: “$17.5M.”

description: Management raised FY2026 revenue-growth guidance to greater than 90%, from greater than 60%, rather than merely reaffirming the prior target. It also expects adjusted EBITDA margins above 10%, a stronger target than the preview’s expectation of positive full-year adjusted EBITDA.
fact_evidence: Management “raised full-year 2026 guidance for a second time in five months,” now expecting “revenue growth greater than 90% (up from prior >60%)” and “adjusted EBITDA margins in excess of 10%,” roughly a year ahead of the original 2026 plan.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY >60% reaffirmed, not raised”; its key bar was “>60% FY revenue growth and FY-positive Adj. EBITDA reaffirmed.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $2.6 million, well above the preview’s $1.0 million estimate and its $0.5–$1.5 million range. The company also recorded a second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA, compared with the preview’s expectation of a first positive quarter in Q2.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “$2.6 million (10% margin)” versus a $3.5 million loss a year earlier, “marking a second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted EBITDA $1.0M (range $0.5–1.5M)” and described Q2 as “positive swing.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The aviation fleet expanded to 38 assets, but only 23 were generating lease revenue—below the preview’s target of about 25 on lease. The larger fleet leaves 11 recently acquired assets awaiting lease placement, so deployment was less complete than expected even as the asset base grew.
fact_evidence: The fleet grew “to 38 assets from 27 quarter-over-quarter,” with “23 assets generating lease revenue (up from 21), leaving 11 recently acquired assets pending lease placement.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “25 of 27 assets” would be on lease and said “four of six new engines” were expected to be leased in Q2.

description: Sand improved more than the preview’s still-loss-making base case: volumes were about 229,000 tons versus an estimated recovery to about 210,000, and average price was $21.36 versus an assumed roughly $20. Gross margin turned positive and the adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sharply rather than remaining a substantial drag.
fact_evidence: Sand volumes rose to “~229,000 tons from ~156,000 tons,” average price improved to “$21.36 from $19.49,” gross margin “turned positive,” and the adjusted EBITDA loss “narrowed by roughly 71% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled sand volume recovering “toward ~210k tons, at ~$20/ton” and said its base case had “sand still loss-making.”
