description: RadNet reported Q2 revenue of $622.7 million, $12.7 million above the preview’s $610 million consensus estimate and also above its $620 million bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company revenue rose 25% year-over-year to a record $622.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $610.0M”; the bull case called for “≥$620M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Same-center advanced imaging growth came in above the preview’s roughly 8% base case and 9% bull-case marker, with a favorable shift in procedure mix toward advanced imaging.
fact_evidence: “Same-center advanced imaging volumes grew 9.6% (MRI +10%, CT +8.6%, PET-CT +8.8%), driving a 238 basis point favorable mix shift toward advanced imaging, which reached 29.9% of total procedure volume.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Same-center advanced imaging ≥8%” was a key metric, with “same-center ~8%” in the base case and “≥9%” in the bull case.

description: RadNet raised imaging-center EBITDA guidance by $5 million at both ends and raised free-cash-flow guidance by $3 million at both ends, rather than holding those ranges flat as the preview’s base case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 imaging center guidance, lifting … adjusted EBITDA to $345–$358 million, and free cash flow to $115–$125 million.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated a “Modest imaging revenue raise, EBITDA/FCF trimmed to reaffirmed.” The prior ranges were $340–$353 million for adjusted EBITDA and $112–$122 million for free cash flow.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management’s initial estimate for the proposed 2027 Medicare rates was nearly neutral for RadNet, as RVU increases offset most of the conversion-factor cut; the preview flagged the proposal but did not forecast this offset.
fact_evidence: “Management's initial analysis of proposed 2027 Medicare rates indicates a net-neutral impact (less than $1 million negative) on roughly $2.4 billion in revenue, as RVU increases offset the 1.68% conversion factor cut.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any read on the CY2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule proposal” as something to watch, but gave no expected impact.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management disclosed a proposed 2027 site-neutrality provision that could sharply reduce hospital reimbursement for certain non-contrast studies and said it could accelerate health-system partnership discussions; this policy detail was not in the preview.
fact_evidence: “A proposed 2027 site-neutrality provision would cut hospital reimbursement 30%–50% on certain non-contrast studies, which management expects to accelerate health system partnership discussions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed reimbursement commentary, including Medicare rates, but did not mention this site-neutrality provision.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management gave a specific, aggressive deployment trajectory for AI-powered draft reporting, including productivity gains and adoption across a large share of RadNet volumes; the preview noted the breast-ultrasound clearance but did not anticipate this rollout guidance.
fact_evidence: “With expanding draft reporting delivering 20%–30% productivity gains, management expects about 15% of RadNet volumes through AI-powered draft reporting by year-end 2026, rising to over 50% by mid-2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted the July 30 FDA clearance for DeepHealth Breast Ultrasound and flagged its monetization path, but gave no draft-reporting adoption or productivity targets.

description: Q2 sales were $117 million, well below the preview’s $134 million estimate, with international sales down 18% rather than showing the anticipated catch-up after Q1’s decline. The international weakness was the main driver of the roughly 10% year-over-year sales drop.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales fell approximately 10% year-over-year to $117 million from $129 million, driven primarily by an 18% decline in international sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales … My estimate: $134M”; international: “If the ‘timing’ explanation was correct, Q2 should show catch-up.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $6.6 million, far below the preview’s $11.5–12.5 million estimate; it fell 40% year over year instead of coming in around or above the prior-year $11 million. First-half adjusted EBITDA was also $17 million, short of the preview’s roughly $22 million expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA dropped 40% to $6.6 million from $11 million a year earlier”; “First-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose more than 20% to $17 million from $14 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My estimate: $11.5–12.5M (vs. $11M LY)”; “H1 FY26 adj. EBITDA will land near $22M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and net debt moved the wrong way for a quarter the preview expected to be a source of cash: cash fell to $43.9 million and net debt increased to $224.7 million. The preview had flagged a cash balance materially below about $60 million as a concern.
fact_evidence: “Net debt increased sequentially to $224.7 million from $194.7 million, while cash fell to $43.9 million from $70.9 million at the end of Q1 due to peak seasonal working capital needs.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is a US-crop collection quarter and should be a source of cash”; “A Q2 cash balance materially below ~$60M … would raise real covenant-headroom questions.”

description: U.S. crop sales fell 9%, rather than continuing the growth the preview’s base case expected, although management attributed much of the decline to cotton portfolio sales shifting into Q3. U.S. specialty growth of 11% partly offset the crop decline.
fact_evidence: “U.S. specialty business grew 11% in the quarter and 10% in the first half, offsetting a 9% decline in U.S. crop sales driven largely by cotton portfolio sales shifting into Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “US Crop was +17% to $67.0M in Q1”; the base scenario expected “US Crop growth moderates from +17%.”

description: Management disclosed a longer-term growth roadmap that the preview did not anticipate: more than $600 million of annualized run-rate revenue by the second half of 2028, alongside a goal of 50 product launches generating $100 million in annualized revenue by 2030. R&D and regulatory spending was already up 12% to support that pipeline, making the announcement promising but also involving higher investment.
fact_evidence: “The company set a longer-term target of exceeding $600 million in annualized run-rate revenue by the second half of 2028, roughly 20% above 2025 levels, with double-digit EBITDA margins”; “R&D and regulatory spending rose 12% year-over-year to support a goal of 50 new product launches over five years generating $100 million in annualized revenue by 2030.”

description: Sonida’s same-store community NOI grew 16.9% and its NOI margin reached 32.6%, 10 basis points above the preview’s 31.5–32.5% range; growth also accelerated from 14% in Q1. Labor costs fell 130 basis points to a portfolio-low 40.4% of revenue, stronger than the preview’s expectation of a stable cost profile.
fact_evidence: “Same-store community NOI grew 16.9% year-over-year with NOI margin expanding 250 bps to 32.6%, accelerating from 14% NOI growth in Q1”; “labor costs fell 130 bps to a portfolio-low 40.4% of revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected same-store NOI margin of “31.5–32.5%” and said “outsized rate increases plus a stable cost profile” would drive margin gains.

description: The six communities transitioned to Sonida in early May posted NOI improvement exceeding 60% and 850 basis points of margin expansion. The preview looked for early margin lift on these communities but did not anticipate an improvement of this scale.
fact_evidence: “Six communities transitioned to Sonida management in early May delivered year-over-year NOI improvement exceeding 60% and 850 bps of NOI margin expansion versus Q2 2025.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch completion count and any early margin lift on the first six” as proof of concept, without forecasting the size of the lift.

description: The preview expected the $170 million bridge loan to be refinanced with property-level mortgage debt. Instead, Sonida completed a $380 million five-year Ally Bank term loan that refinanced the bridge loan and prior debt, with 97% of maturities pushed to 2029 or later.
fact_evidence: “A post-quarter $380 million five-year term loan with Ally Bank refinanced the $170 million bridge loan and prior debt, pushing 97% of total debt maturities to 2029 or later.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to refinancing the bridge “with property-level mortgage debt” by the end of Q2 or early Q3.

description: The 2025 acquisition cohort’s NOI margin recovered from negative 1% in Q4 2025 to 15% this quarter, while occupancy remained just 70.4%. The preview highlighted acquired-portfolio operating performance as a key debate but did not forecast this sharp margin recovery or the remaining occupancy gap.
fact_evidence: “The 2025 acquisition cohort saw NOI margin swing from -1% in Q4 2025 to 15% this quarter, with occupancy still at 70.4% (up 1,400 bps in occupancy since Q4).”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “first clean look” at the acquired communities’ operations and highlighted the gap between total SHOP occupancy and same-store occupancy, but gave no expectation for this cohort’s margin or occupancy.

description: Sonida had approximately $88 million of assets under contract with projected mid-teens unlevered IRRs and expected accretion to normalized FFO and NAV per share once stabilized. The preview did not flag a specific acquisition pipeline transaction.
fact_evidence: “The company is under contract to acquire approximately $88 million of assets expected to generate mid-teens unlevered IRR and be accretive to normalized FFO and NAV per share on a stabilized basis.”

description: Sonida issued approximately 672,000 ATM shares in July to fund near-term acquisitions. The preview identified equity funding as a potential bear-case signal, but did not expect a specific share issuance in the reported facts.
fact_evidence: “The company issued approximately 672,000 shares via its ATM program in July at an average price of $41.05 for net proceeds of $27.3 million to fund near-term acquisitions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “a first-time reference to equity as a funding source” as a bear-case signal.

description: Management did not provide full-year 2027 normalized FFO guidance now; it said guidance would begin after CHP and pipeline integrations are complete. The preview viewed a guidance framework initiated this quarter as a possible positive surprise, so the timing is later and more conditional than that upside scenario.
fact_evidence: “Management expects to begin issuing full-year normalized FFO guidance for 2027, deferring guidance until CHP and pipeline integrations are complete.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said that “initiating” a guidance framework would be a “genuine narrative shift” and a possible underpriced positive surprise.

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $50 million versus the preview’s approximately $47 million estimate. The reported figure is stated on a total-portfolio basis, whereas the preview labeled its estimate at-share, which limits the comparability of the apparent beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $50 million on a total portfolio basis for Q2 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA (at-share)” at “~$47M.”

description: Revenue was $8.2 million, above the preview’s expectation of results near the $7.5–$7.8 million guided range. That is a clear upside beat against the company’s guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $8.2 million” and was “above the guided range of $7.5 to $7.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue will almost certainly land in or near the $7.5–7.8M guided range.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Consumables growth and flow-cell sales were stronger than the preview’s already-positive operating expectations: consumables grew 30% rather than roughly 20%, and flow-cell sales exceeded the 9,000-unit watch level. The result reflects faster utilization growth than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Consumable revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $4.3 million”; “Flow cells sold hit a record 9,219 units, up 27% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for >9,000 flow cells and continued 20%-ish consumables growth”; the catalyst checklist also specifies “Consumables growth ≥18% and flow cells ≥9,000.”

description: Adjusted gross margin reached 53%, well above the preview’s roughly 49% base-case expectation. That is a substantial improvement on the anticipated margin level.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached a record 53% in Q2 2026,” compared with 52% a year ago.
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “GM ~49%.”

description: The company raised the low end of full-year revenue guidance to $31 million from $30 million, rather than narrowing toward the preview’s base-case range of about $30–$31 million. The $33 million top end was retained rather than cut.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance had its low end raised to $31-$33 million (9%-16% growth).”
expectation_evidence: The preview called narrowing to “~$30–31M” the base case and said the $33 million high end was “not credible on current trajectory.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Demand is exceeding manufacturing capacity, leaving a flow-cell backlog expected to take until mid-to-late Q4 to clear. The preview anticipated strong flow-cell demand but did not anticipate that production limits would constrain fulfillment.
fact_evidence: “Demand continues to outpace manufacturing capacity, creating a backlog expected to clear by mid-to-late Q4 2026”; the full-year top end was held back due to capacity constraints.
expectation_evidence: The preview looked for “>9,000 flow cells” and described utilization as compounding, but did not flag manufacturing capacity or a backlog.

description: Despite the Q2 revenue beat, Q3 guidance implies only flat-to-modest sequential growth, with management citing large orders that could slip between quarters. The preview did not provide a Q3 expectation, but this is a cautious near-term outlook alongside the stronger Q2 result.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $8.2-$8.6 million” implies “roughly flat-to-modest sequential growth,” reflecting “conservatism around large orders at risk of slipping quarters.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash and securities were slightly above the preview’s $8–$10 million estimate, and the company said runway extends into at least Q1 2027. This is somewhat better than the cash estimate, though it does not remove the financing concern: the company still signaled potential future financing needs.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with only $10.4 million in cash and securities, with runway extending into at least Q1 2027, signaling potential future financing needs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$8–10M exiting Q2” and described management’s prior runway claim as “into 2027,” while warning of “well under two quarters of runway.”

description: CRC’s operating update pointed to only about 1% gross entry-to-exit production growth, rather than the preview’s roughly 175,000 BOE/day exit target. The full-year average guide is approximately 153,000 BOE/day, but the reported growth outlook signals a much flatter production trajectory than the preview had highlighted.
fact_evidence: Full-year guidance is approximately 153,000 BOE/day and roughly 1% gross entry-to-exit production growth.
expectation_evidence: “~175 MBoe/d exit target.”

description: CRC cut the expected H2 California rig count to five while keeping production nearly flat, reducing 2026 D&C and workover capital by $10 million. That is a sharper move toward lower spending than the preview’s 7-rig peak plan and its expectation that the H2 program might be defended.
fact_evidence: “Improved drilling efficiency cut time-to-market by ~25%, allowing California operations to run 5 rigs in H2 2026 instead of 6 while keeping production nearly flat, reducing 2026 D&C and workover capital by $10 million.”
expectation_evidence: “The May raise added $100M and 3 rigs (2 California, 1 Uinta) to reach a 7-rig peak”; “Whether CRC defends or trims this program at $85 Brent”; base case: “H2 rig program defended on efficiency gains.”

description: CRC also lowered its normalized California maintenance requirement to six rigs—one fewer than previously projected—and cut the associated D&C and workover capital estimate by about 5%, with a $450–475 million go-forward range. This adds a lasting capital-efficiency improvement beyond the near-term H2 rig reduction.
fact_evidence: “Normalized California maintenance now requires 6 rigs (one fewer than previously projected) and ~5% lower D&C and workover capital, with go-forward maintenance capital range of $450-475 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY capex $520–560M”; the preview also noted the earlier plan had “<$400M of D&C/workover capital” as a contrast to the expanded rig program.

description: Berry integration savings were further along and larger than the preview’s estimates: CRC said it had exceeded the 2026 target six months early, with about $103 million of annualized savings, and raised cumulative synergies and structural cost reductions through 2028 to as much as $470 million.
fact_evidence: “Berry integration synergies were delivered at over 100% of the 2026 target six months ahead of schedule,” representing “~$103 million of annualized savings”; cumulative synergies and structural cost reductions were raised “to up to $470 million through 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “Berry synergies at $90–100M annually, >80% of original target captured, ~$460M cumulative through 2028.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: A temporary pipeline-operator dispute and takeaway constraints created unexpected operating headwinds. CRC said the takeaway constraints reduced Q2 EBITDAX and operating cash flow by about $25 million each, while the marketing dispute pressured differentials; CRC limited the differential impact to roughly $2/barrel and expects Q3 realizations of about 93% of Brent before recovering to its 94% full-year outlook.
fact_evidence: “Temporary takeaway constraints reduced EBITDAX and operating cash flow by approximately $25 million each”; marketing disputes pressured differentials, but CRC “limited its impact to roughly $2/barrel,” guided Q3 realizations to “~93% of Brent” as the year’s low point, and maintained full-year realizations of “~94%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch 2027 exposure” and “Realized oil price with hedges,” but did not flag a pipeline dispute or takeaway constraint.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CRC reported substantially better-than-expected well results: about 80% of wells drilled year to date beat the type curve, with average initial production more than 10% above expectations. The company also put new California production costs at roughly $2,000–7,000 per flowing barrel, far below the $28,000–30,000 paid in the Era and Berry acquisitions.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 80% of wells drilled year-to-date outperformed the type curve with average initial production more than 10% above expectations,” and California drilling delivers new production at “roughly $2,000-7,000 per flowing barrel versus $28,000-30,000 paid in the Era and Berry acquisitions.”

description: CRC announced an all-cash purchase of Crimson’s approximately 2,000-mile California crude pipeline network at about 4.4 times estimated 2027 EBITDA, which it described as below prevailing midstream multiples. The preview did not anticipate this acquisition.
fact_evidence: “The company announced an all-cash acquisition of Crimson's ~2,000-mile California crude pipeline network at approximately 4.4x estimated 2027 EBITDA, below prevailing midstream valuation multiples,” with tentative PUC approval received.

description: CRC completed no share repurchases in the quarter, despite the preview identifying accelerated buybacks as a potential signal of conviction and noting that the prior quarter’s $10 million repurchase was small. The preview did not make a buyback an unconditional base-case expectation, so the gap is limited.
fact_evidence: “Executed no share repurchases this quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 FCF was −$32M … with only $10M of repurchases”; “the cheapest bullish surprise available to management … [is] an accelerated buyback”; “Buyback pace — $10M in Q1 was negligible.”

description: Management described the Uinta as a non-core asset unlikely to receive long-term capital, a firmer capital-allocation stance than the preview’s description of the asset as still under evaluation with development and monetization both live options.
fact_evidence: CRC “viewed the Uinta as a non-core asset unlikely to receive long-term capital.”
expectation_evidence: “Uinta remains ‘evaluation stage’ — 4 wells by year-end, with full development or monetization both live.”

description: CRC said its Elk Hills CCS project had begun capturing about 270 tonnes per day and had recorded first revenue. The preview noted that injection had already occurred but identified first revenue recognition as something still to watch.
fact_evidence: “CRC commenced CO2 injection and achieved first revenue at California's first CCS project at Elk Hills, capturing ~270 tonnes/day (targeting ~100,000 tons/year).”
expectation_evidence: “First CO₂ injection at CTV I / Elk Hills achieved (May–June 2026)”; “Watch: 45Q monetization mechanics, first revenue recognition.”

description: CRC refinanced its remaining 2029 notes with debt due in 2035, extending weighted-average maturities and lowering annual interest expense. The preview did not flag a refinancing as an expected event.
fact_evidence: “Refinanced its remaining 2029 senior notes with notes due 2035, extending weighted average debt maturity from 5.5 to 8 years and cutting annual expense by $5.5 million.”

description: Q2 revenue was $28.1 million, about 3% above the $27.29 million consensus, and growth accelerated to 33%. That was a modest beat against consensus, though it was within the preview’s $27.8–28.2 million buy-side whisper range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $28.1 million, up 33% year-over-year, accelerating from 29% growth in Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $27.29M”; “Revenue vs. $27.29M consensus / ~$27.8–28.2M buy-side whisper.”

description: Gross margin reached 92%, above the preview’s high-80s expectation. Even excluding the $1.6 million tariff refund, the 89% margin was at or slightly above the expected range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin hit a record 92%, or 89% excluding a $1.6 million tariff refund.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~87–88% (guided ‘high-80s’)”; “guided high-80s all year.”

description: The company raised its 2026 revenue range to $114–117 million, but the increase was smaller than the preview’s more bullish buy-side bar of roughly $115–118 million and its expectation for a roughly $3 million raise. The new range matched the preview’s base case, so the shortfall is against the higher bar rather than its central scenario.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $114-$117 million … from prior guidance of $112-$116 million.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy-side bar is a raise to roughly $115–118M”; “anything less than a ~$3M raise reads as H2 caution.” The preview’s base case was “guide to $114–117M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The delirium commercial launch was brought forward to Q4 2026, rather than remaining as late as early 2027 under prior guidance. The preview focused on launch detail and potential 2027 economics but did not flag this timing pull-forward.
fact_evidence: “Delirium will launch commercially in Q4 2026, pulled forward from prior guidance of Q4 2026/early 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “pulled forward from prior guidance of Q4 2026/early 2027.”

description: The GAAP loss per share was $0.51, four cents worse than the $0.47 loss consensus. This was at the lossier end of the preview’s base-case range, while adjusted EBITDA was better than its stated threshold.
fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $19.3 million ($0.51 per share) from $13.6 million ($0.38 per share) a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP net loss/sh) | ($0.47).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said account growth relied less on VA accounts than in prior quarters, suggesting sales-force maturation beyond simply meeting the expected account-add count. The preview anticipated strong adds but did not identify this change in account mix.
fact_evidence: “The company added 32 active accounts to reach 712 total, with growth relying less on VA accounts than in prior quarters, indicating organic sales force maturation.”
expectation_evidence: “Net new accounts ≥30”; the preview described whether Q1’s adds reflected “a step-function in sales-force productivity.”

description: The refinancing adds access to up to $60 million of committed capital, lowers interest expense beginning in Q4, and extends repayment into 2031. The preview raised cash-burn and financing concerns but did not anticipate this facility refinancing.
fact_evidence: “The company held $129.3 million in cash and marketable securities and refinanced its credit facility to access up to $60 million committed capital, reducing interest expense starting Q4 and extending repayment into 2031.”
expectation_evidence: “Any wobble on that commitment reopens the financing question”; the preview cited “cash and marketable securities $141.2M, net cash ~$119M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management highlighted that less than 4% of the core seizure market is penetrated and that top accounts use the product at roughly three times the rate of similarly sized average accounts. This offered a specific adoption and utilization runway that the preview had not quantified.
fact_evidence: “The company cited less than 4% penetration in its core seizure market, with top accounts using the product at roughly three times the rate of average accounts of similar size.”

description: Total revenue was $243.7 million, well above the preview’s $218.7–$222.2 million consensus range and its $232 million estimate. That is roughly a 10% beat versus the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total revenues were $243.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $218.7M – $222.2M (commonly cited $220.9M)” and “My Est.: $232M.”

description: Attruby revenue reached $222.4 million, above the preview’s $214 million estimate, and increased $41.8 million sequentially. The preview expected about a $35 million sequential addition, with consensus implying only about $25 million.
fact_evidence: “Attruby net product revenue reached $222.4 million in Q2” and marked “another quarter with a sequential increase of at least $35 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Implied Attruby US net … ~$205M (+13% q/q)” and “My Est.: $214M (+18% q/q)”; the preview also said “Holding [the sequential dollar add] flat gets you to ~$214M” and consensus implied “~+$25M q/q.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The market commentary was stronger than the preview’s category-deceleration concern: the ATTR market grew 19% in the quarter and 51% year over year, while Attruby was the fastest-growing brand and gained an estimated 2–3 percentage points of first-line share.
fact_evidence: “Attruby was the fastest-growing brand in the ATTR space at 23%, with overall market growth of 19% in the quarter (up 51% year-over-year) and first-line share gains estimated at 2-3 percentage points.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the “bear read” that “the whole category is decelerating” and said “BBIO’s category commentary is the arbiter.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash was only $72.2 million, far below the preview’s expected $780–$850 million. The July 1 preferred investment raised cash to about $1.7 billion, but that was also below the preview’s roughly $1.8 billion pro forma expectation.
fact_evidence: The preferred investment “closed … on July 1, lifting cash to approximately $1.7 billion, up from just $72.2 million at quarter end.”
expectation_evidence: “Expect reported Q2 cash of roughly $780–850M with ~$1.8B pro forma.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New kidney-protection data turned a previously perceived acoramidis drawback into a potential advantage: among patients with acute eGFR dips at or above the median, outcomes favored acoramidis with a hazard ratio of 0.42.
fact_evidence: “In patients with acute eGFR dips at or above the median, acoramidis favored survival/CV-hospitalization outcomes with a hazard ratio of 0.42 (p=0.006), reframing a previously perceived drawback as a differentiator.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New real-world evidence reported substantially better outcomes for Attruby than tafamidis, including fewer diuretic intensifications, heart-failure hospitalizations, and deaths, with differences appearing early.
fact_evidence: “New real-world evidence associated Attruby with a 34% reduction in diuretic intensification, heart failure hospitalization and mortality versus tafamidis, with separation observed as early as 30 days.”

description: Management gave a substantial portfolio revenue outlook not specified in the preview, projecting more than $10 billion in risk-adjusted revenue and saying acoramidis should reach worldwide blockbuster status in 2026.
fact_evidence: “Management projected the portfolio supports over $10 billion in risk-adjusted revenue ($8 billion post-Phase III), [and] guided to acoramidis reaching worldwide blockbuster status in 2026.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management described chronic hypoparathyroidism as a potential additional blockbuster opportunity for encaleret, adding commercial upside beyond the preview’s focus on the ADH1 regulatory timeline.
fact_evidence: Management framed encaleret’s chronic hypoparathyroidism opportunity as “a potential additional blockbuster,” citing “~200,000 patients in U.S. and EU.”

description: Management supplied a path to breakeven by late 2027, after several quarters of stable operating results. The preview highlighted rising launch spending and asked whether management would outline operating leverage, but did not give a breakeven timeline.
fact_evidence: Management “expects stable operating results for several quarters before trending toward breakeven by late 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “whether management frames any path to operating leverage” and described a base case of “EPS miss on launch spend.”

description: Revenue was well above both the $44.64 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $44 million base estimate. The $48.4 million result also represented 25% growth on a continuing-business basis, above the preview’s roughly 19% implied growth.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $48.4 million” and was “up 25% year-over-year on an aggregate continuing business basis.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$44.64M”; the preview’s base estimate was “~$44.0M” and said it implied “~+19% YoY on continuing operations.”

description: Commerce Media Solutions revenue exceeded the preview’s estimate, reaching $30.5 million rather than the modeled $28.5 million. Its 90% growth was also above the preview’s modeled 75–85% range.
fact_evidence: “Commerce Media Solutions revenue grew 90% year-over-year to $30.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled CMS at “$28.5M” and “~+77% YoY,” with its key-metrics section giving a “~+75–85% YoY” model.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CMS exited the quarter above the preview’s $120 million run-rate bogey, with an annual revenue run rate exceeding $125 million. That was stronger than the preview’s base-case $115–120 million range.
fact_evidence: “Commerce Media Solutions exited Q2 with an annual revenue run rate of over $125 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected a “run rate $115–120M”; its ranked metric said “>$120M = thesis intact.”

description: Owned and operated revenue held up substantially better than the preview modeled: $16.3 million versus an estimate of $12.5 million. Its 24% decline was also much less severe than the historical decline rates highlighted in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Owned and operated revenue declined 24% year-over-year to $16.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimate build modeled Owned & Operated at “$12.5M”; its key-metrics section cited recent declines of “-49% (Q2'25) → -50% (Q1'26).”

description: SDC fell 3.6% organically to $24.5 million, worse than the preview’s base case of flat-to-slightly-up performance. Past-due backlog also rose about $1 million from its year-end low, indicating the Q4 backlog reduction did not provide a durable fix.
fact_evidence: “SDC…posted a 3.6% organic decline to $24.5 million due to delivery reliability issues”; “SDC past-due backlog rose about $1 million from its year-end low.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “SDC flat-to-slightly-up on tough comp”; the preview said to “watch backlog commentary specifically.”

description: Adjusted operating income was $15.4 million at a 25.6% margin, above the preview’s implied roughly $14.6 million and 24% margin. That exceeded the preview’s threshold for evidence that margin gains were durable, although management cautioned against annualizing the seasonally light quarter.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income excluding unusual items grew 19.5% to $15.4 million (25.6% of revenue vs. 21.7% prior year), nearly 390 basis points of margin expansion,” with management warning “against annualizing this seasonally light quarter.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus implied AOI “roughly $14.6M, or ~24.0% margin”; the preview said “anything at or above 25% suggests the FY26 expansion is durable.”

description: Clinical Genomics was essentially flat rather than showing the stabilization the preview expected; China was still down 7%. Non-China growth of 0.6% limited the overall decline but did not deliver the anticipated clearer improvement.
fact_evidence: “Clinical Genomics was essentially flat at -0.1% ($10.3 million), with China down 7% but non-China up 0.6%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “CG China stabilization” was a key metric and that the drag “should mathematically fade”; it noted CG was “+5.8% organic in 4Q26.”

description: The preview anticipated GAAP/non-GAAP divergence largely because of acquisition-related amortization, but the reported GAAP net-income decline was driven by a $2.7 million swing in non-operating expense from unrealized FX losses on an intercompany loan. This left GAAP net income down sharply despite stronger operating income.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net income fell 40.3% to $2.8 million ($0.49 per diluted share) driven by a $2.7 million non-operating expense swing from unrealized FX losses on an intercompany loan, not operations.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cautioned that “similar GAAP/non-GAAP divergence” could persist “given acquisition-related intangible amortization”; it did not identify an FX-driven expense swing.

description: Management gave a specific net-leverage target of 1.5x–1.75x by fiscal year-end and explicitly deprioritized acquisitions, providing a clearer and more debt-focused capital-allocation signal than the preview’s base case of qualitative strategy framing.
fact_evidence: “The company repaid $8.7 million of debt, lowering net leverage to 1.85x… with a target of 1.5x-1.75x by fiscal year-end and an explicit de-prioritization of acquisitions.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “qualitative strategy framing only”; the preview said the first call was a “natural venue to define a target” and signal whether capital would go to debt, buybacks, or M&A.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash flow increased substantially, reaching $14.7 million, a positive cash-generation result the preview did not specifically anticipate for the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow rose $12.8 million to $14.7 million.”

description: The company installed a new general manager for BPD, an operational leadership change not specifically identified in the preview’s possible strategic announcements.
fact_evidence: “A new general manager was installed for BPD.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Mesa said it had accelerated the next-generation Gyrolab platform launch to fiscal 2028, its first new platform since 2018. The preview did not flag this product-timing announcement, and no revenue contribution was provided.
fact_evidence: “The next-generation Gyrolab platform launch was accelerated to fiscal 2028 (its first new platform since 2018), though no revenue was attached to it.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was only just over $5 million, versus the preview’s $11–13 million base case and its roughly $12.5 million estimate. The 9.3% margin was also far below the expected 19–21%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA exceeded $5 million” and the “adjusted EBITDA margin [was] 9.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA / margin” estimated at “~$12.5M / ~20%”; base case “$11–13M (19–21%).”

description: Revenue reached $58 million, below both the $61.8 million consensus and the preview’s approximately $61 million build, despite recurring fees coming in near the expected level.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue reached $58 million.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$61.8M”; the preview’s revenue build estimated “~$61.0M.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: AlTi recorded a nearly $19 million unrealized loss on its external Asian Credit and Special Situations fund stake after the manager unexpectedly decided to unwind the fund. The call also said net loss from continuing operations widened to $31 million, versus the preview’s positive $0.06 EPS consensus, with $20 million of other expense affecting the result.
fact_evidence: “An unrealized investment loss of nearly $19 million” followed the manager’s decision to unwind the fund; “net loss from continuing operations widened to $31 million versus $26 million a year earlier, impacted by $20 million of other expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “EPS $0.06” consensus, while noting EPS was a “low-signal metric for ALTI.”

description: The fund unwind also creates a forward revenue headwind not anticipated in the preview: the fund had contributed recurring management fees and incentive distributions that will now diminish.
fact_evidence: The fund had contributed “about 75 basis points of recurring management fees and about 650 basis points of the incentive portion of distributions year-to-date, which will now diminish.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Client flows were much stronger than the preview’s base case: wealth management had about $700 million of net inflows, and the company said overall AUM growth was driven partly by net positive client inflows.
fact_evidence: “Wealth management generated gross client inflows of nearly $800 million and net flows of about $700 million”; AUM growth was driven by “net positive client inflows.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected flows “~flat to −$0.3B”; the preview described positive net flows as part of the bull case.

description: The expected cost improvement appears pushed further out: the preview looked for expense normalization in the second half of 2026, while management said the benefits of zero-based budgeting and vendor rationalization would accelerate into 2027.
fact_evidence: Management expects cost-reduction benefits “to accelerate into 2027,” with further reductions targeted in both compensation and non-compensation expenses.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to “normalization in 2H26” and flagged that if normalized opex was not below about $56 million, “the cost story slips a quarter.”

description: AAON reported Q2 net sales of $627 million, far above the preview’s $501–515 million consensus range. The result exceeded the top of that range by about 22%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales hit a record $627 million,” up 101% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus band: “~$501–515M.”

description: AAON raised its 2026 sales-growth outlook to 55%–60%, above the prior 40%–45% guide and the preview’s base-case expectation that the guide would be reaffirmed. The scale of the increase was a substantial upgrade.
fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 sales growth guidance to 55%-60%.”
expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “40–45%”; the preview’s base case expected the “FY guide [to be] reaffirmed.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.69, above the preview’s $0.51–$0.52 diluted-EPS consensus range. The reported figure is adjusted, while the preview labels its consensus diluted EPS without specifying an adjusted basis.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 213.6% to $0.69.”
expectation_evidence: Diluted EPS consensus band: “~$0.51–0.52.”

description: Q2 gross margin fell to 24.3%, well below the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 26%–27%. Memphis ramp costs, outsourcing, and price-cost timing weighed on the result.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 24.3% from 26.6%,” pressured by “Memphis ramp-up costs, increased outsourcing, and inflationary price/cost timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “GM ~26–27%,” and its bull case expected “GM holds ≥27%.”

description: AAON cut its full-year gross-margin guide by about 200 basis points, from 27%–28% to 25%–26%. The reduction was driven largely by lower-margin Memphis volume mix, against a preview base case that expected the guide to be reaffirmed.
fact_evidence: “Cut gross margin guidance by roughly 200 basis points to 25%-26%, driven largely by lower-margin Memphis volume mix.”
expectation_evidence: Prior gross-margin guidance was “27–28%”; the preview’s base case expected the “FY guide [to be] reaffirmed.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview flagged the sequential backlog decline and sub-1 book-to-bill as a risk and asked whether it reflected order softening. Management said BASX bookings were below recent elevated levels because of lumpy large-project timing, not cancellations or a change in market opportunity, offering reassurance on the cause even though bookings softened.
fact_evidence: “BASX bookings fell below recent elevated levels,” which management attributed to “lumpiness in large-project timing rather than any specific order cancellation or a change in market opportunity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called backlog “SOFT,” noted it was “down from $2.13B at Q1,” and asked whether the decline was “a timing artifact” or “genuine order softening.”

description: Q2 revenue was $19.3 million, about 3.5% below the roughly $20.0 million consensus and the company’s own Q2 expectation. The shortfall was worse than the preview’s base-case range of $19.8–20.3 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $19.3 million” and was “below company expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus / Guide | $20.01M”; “The company's own words on the May 12 call were ‘approximately $20.0 million’”; base case: “Q2 Revenue | $19.8–20.3M.”

description: OviTex PRS deteriorated much more sharply than the preview’s discussion of US mix and pricing suggested: revenue fell to $5.5 million from $7.3 million, with units down 23%. A failed dedicated-rep pilot and losses concentrated among fewer than 10 sites and several surgeons on leave were unexpected explanations for the weakness.
fact_evidence: “OviTex PRS revenue fell to $5.5 million from $7.3 million,” with a “23% unit volume decline”; the decline was attributed to “a failed dedicated-rep pilot” and customer concentration, including surgeons out on leave.
expectation_evidence: The preview focused on US demand shifting toward “smaller, cheaper units” and said the concern was “a pricing problem,” while its base case called for an “in-line quarter.”

description: Gross margin came in well above the preview’s 66–67% expectation, at 72%. The improvement was helped by a tariff refund and lower inventory charges, so some of the upside came from favorable items rather than only underlying operations.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 72% from 70%, aided by a refund of previously paid tariffs and lower excess/obsolete inventory charges.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~66–67% (no formal guide)” and the preview asked whether inventory charges would “keep gross margin below 67%.”

description: OviTex global revenue growth was 6.6%, better than the preview’s low-single-digit revenue-growth scenario, even though unit growth was 12%. The shift toward smaller, lower-priced robotic hernia units still meant revenue lagged volume.
fact_evidence: “Global OviTex unit volume grew 12% year-over-year to 5,776 units, outpacing its 6.6% dollar revenue growth due to a shift toward smaller, lower-priced robotic hernia units.”
expectation_evidence: “If Q2 repeats ‘units up double digits, revenue up low single digits’...”

description: Interest expense was higher than the preview’s estimated quarterly loan cost, contributing to a wider net loss. The preview estimated roughly $1.8 million per quarter in facility interest, while the reported amount was $2.1 million.
fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $11.3 million from $9.9 million,” largely due to interest expense of “$2.1 million” versus “$1.2 million previously.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated the facility would cost “~$1.8M/quarter.”

description: Liquifix grew 39%, an additional product-line bright spot that the preview did not identify while focusing on the revenue and US hernia risks. The preview provided no specific growth expectation for Liquifix.
fact_evidence: “Liquifix revenue grew 39%, remaining [a] bright spot[] against domestic weakness.”

description: Q2 revenue was $5 million, far above the preview’s roughly $1.9 million estimate, which assumed Hawthorne Airport operations would be the main revenue source. The reported figure was more than twice the estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew to $5 million, a 213% increase over the prior quarter, driven by growth in operations at Hawthorne Airport in LA.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $1.95M”; the preview’s estimate was “$1.9M” and noted “Hawthorne Airport FBO ops only.”

description: Management said the acquisitions would not structurally increase Archer’s cash burn and targeted relatively flat burn after closing. That is better than the preview’s concern that the burn curve could steepen ahead of deal synergies.
fact_evidence: “The acquisitions will not structurally increase overall cash burn, targeting relatively flat cash burn post-close through synergies across Midnight, Halo/Thunder, and ZEE platforms.”
expectation_evidence: “Standalone Q3 guide of >-$200M signals the burn curve steepening ahead of any Boeing-deal synergies.”

description: Archer held Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance at $170 million to $200 million rather than moving toward the higher losses the preview considered possible. The preview’s base case was $190 million to $215 million, with a loss above $200 million flagged as a risk.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance held in the same range” as the $170 million to $200 million Q2 range.
expectation_evidence: “Q3 guide -$190M to -$215M” in the base case; “Standalone Q3 guide of >-$200M signals the burn curve steepening.”

description: The adjusted EBITDA loss was $177 million, modestly better than the preview’s $186 million estimate, although still within the company’s expected guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was $177 million, at the lower (better) end of the $170 million to $200 million guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA: -$186M” and cited company guidance of “-$170M to -$200M.”

description: Archer added a near-term profitability outlook for its AI businesses: ZEE and SkyGrid could generate revenue and become profitable as early as next year, with a potential significant ramp in the second half of 2027 and beyond. The preview discussed the acquisitions but did not anticipate this timing or profitability target.
fact_evidence: “Archer targets its AI solutions (ZEE and SkyGrid) to be revenue-generating and profitable as early as next year, with potential for a significant ramp in the back half of 2027 and beyond.”

description: The call described Boeing’s consideration as locked-up Archer stock and said the warrants have exercise prices far above Archer’s current share price. That provides more detail and appears less immediately dilutive than the preview’s unresolved concern about the deal’s dilution and warrant math.
fact_evidence: “Boeing took all stock with a lockup and committed future equity investments, plus warrants with exercise prices far in excess of Archer's current share price.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the deal was being priced as “strategically positive but dilutive and un-quantified” and flagged the “four-year warrant strip” and post-Boeing share count.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Archer reported that Midnight is already in the FAA’s fourth and final type-certification phase and cited more than 150 piloted test flights, including intercity flights over 50 miles. The preview knew Phase 3 had closed and focused on TIA event counts and upcoming transition testing, but had not anticipated these reported flight-volume details or the stated final-phase status.
fact_evidence: “Archer reports being the only industry OEM in the fourth and final phase of the FAA type certification process for Midnight, having flown over 150 piloted test flights, up to 5 times a day, including intercity flights over 50 miles.”
expectation_evidence: “Archer closed FAA Phase 3 in April 2026”; the preview focused on “~10 discrete TIA events” and whether piloted transition testing remained slated for 2H26.

description: APEI’s adjusted EBITDA was $20.7 million, well above the $18 million top of its Q2 guidance and above the preview’s $17.5–18.5 million base-case range. The 275-basis-point margin expansion to 12% made this a stronger operating result than the preview’s expected moderation implied.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 36.8% to $20.7 million with margin expanding 275 basis points to 12%, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $16.5–18.0M” and the base scenario anticipated “$17.5–18.5M”; the preview also said the marketing step-up “moderates” Military+ margin toward long-range targets.

description: Diluted EPS of $0.52 exceeded both the $0.36 consensus and the preview’s estimated $0.42–0.48 functional whisper. Net income of $9.8 million also came in above the company’s $6.5–7.5 million guidance range, making the earnings result stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: “Net income available to common stockholders was $9.8 million or $0.52 per diluted share, reversing a prior-year loss of $0.02 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS” guidance was “$0.34–0.39” and consensus was “$0.36”; the preview described the “functional whisper” as “$0.42–0.48.” Net income guidance was “$6.5–7.5M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Military Plus registrations were about 98,300, at the bottom of the expected range and below the preview’s 99,000–100,000 base-case level. The reported 2% growth and deployment pressure were anticipated, but the count landed at the low end of the outlook.
fact_evidence: “Military Plus revenue grew 4.7% to $85.5 million on 2% net course registration growth to ~98,300,” with active-duty registrations “pressured by Middle East deployments.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “registrations ~99–100K”; the stated guidance range was “98,300–100,300.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The combination removed the 2021 Department of Education growth restriction on Rasmussen’s total enrollment, an enrollment-growth opportunity the preview did not identify. The preview anticipated the combination and approvals, but not this specific consequence.
fact_evidence: The combination “united all units under a single HLC accreditation and lift[ed] the 2021 Department of Education growth restriction on Rasmussen's total enrollment.”

description: APEI introduced Q3 guidance of $164.5–167 million in revenue and $14–17 million in adjusted EBITDA, with about $6 million of revenue and $4 million of EBITDA shifted into Q4. The preview had no Q3 forecast; management attributed the softer quarterly profile to the September 7 Military Plus start date and nonrecurring marketing optimization costs.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance (revenue $164.5-167 million, adjusted EBITDA $14-17 million) reflects a ~$6 million revenue and ~$4 million EBITDA timing shift into Q4 due to a September 7 Military Plus start date plus nonrecurring marketing optimization costs.”

description: The company lowered its full-year capex outlook to $25–28 million from $28–32 million. The preview listed the prior capex range but did not anticipate a reduction.
fact_evidence: APEI raised full-year guidance while “lowering capex to $25-28 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Capex $28–32M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: APEI discussed a potential tuition-assistance increase under a pending NDAA provision, which could let it raise active-duty tuition while preserving its zero out-of-pocket commitment. This potential pricing opportunity was not raised in the preview and remains contingent on the provision.
fact_evidence: “A pending NDAA provision could raise military tuition assistance 40% (from $250 to $350 per credit hour), potentially allowing APEI to reprice active-duty tuition while maintaining its 23-year zero out-of-pocket commitment.”

description: Q2 revenue was $319.7 million, far above the preview’s $196.97 million consensus estimate. The preview expected a beat to be likely, but the reported figure was much higher than that already-low forecast.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue surged 130% year-over-year to $319.7 million, exceeding both company and consensus expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $196.97M” and “A revenue beat is the higher-probability outcome.”

description: B&W raised the 2026 adjusted EBITDA range to $80–$105 million rather than keeping the preview’s $80–$100 million range. The increase was partly due to Base Electron revenue being recognized ahead of schedule, indicating faster-than-expected progress on that project.
fact_evidence: “B&W raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA target range to $80 million to $105 million, driven partly by ahead-of-schedule Base Electron revenue recognition.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 core adj. EBITDA guidance | $80M–$100M” and “guidance reaffirmed at $80–$100M.”

description: Skilled-labor shortages increased direct costs on a construction project during Q2, requiring incentives, rehires, and delayed retirements to address staffing. The preview did not flag this project-cost pressure.
fact_evidence: “Skilled labor shortages raised direct costs on a specific construction project during Q2, prompting incentives, rehires, and delayed retirements.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: B&W secured reservation rights for an additional 1 gigawatt of Siemens Energy steam turbines, with first deliveries expected in 12 to 14 months. This additional capacity was not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “B&W secured reservation rights from Siemens Energy for an additional 1 gigawatt (20 50-megawatt steam turbines) with first deliveries in 12 to 14 months.”

description: The preview said management had promised a comprehensive update on the restaurant strategic-alternatives process, but the call facts report restaurant closures and operating results without a sale, deal, or comprehensive process update. That leaves the central restaurant-monetization question unanswered.
fact_evidence: The call facts describe the restaurant group’s revenue decline, reduced traffic, and O’Charley’s store closures, but report no comprehensive update or transaction on the strategic-alternatives process.
expectation_evidence: Management had promised a “comprehensive update this quarter”; the preview said “Silence = credibility hit.”

description: Cannae repurchased no stock in Q2, despite the preview’s expectation of continued repurchases, and it allocated about $45 million to investments during the quarter. The preview specifically raised the possibility that buybacks would slow as capital went to new sports assets.
fact_evidence: “Repurchased no stock in Q2 due to recently announced transactions”; Cannae allocated “approximately $45 million to investments in Q2” and $54 million year-to-date through July.
expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated “~1–2M shares bought back” in its base case and flagged buybacks slowing as cash was redirected to “Exeter/new sports assets” as a bear-case signal.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The restaurant group recorded $45 million of non-cash impairments, a much heavier charge than the preview’s base-case expectation of a modest impairment. The charges accompanied reduced traffic and O’Charley’s store closures.
fact_evidence: The restaurant group “incurred $45 million of non-cash impairment charges (versus $1 million a year earlier) due to reduced traffic and O’Charley’s store closures.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “another modest impairment”; further closures and impairments appeared in the bear case.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The SpaceX IPO produced an $83.4 million mark-to-market gain, an unanticipated boost to Q2 reported results. Management also warned that future earnings could vary with these marks, so the gain is not a stable operating improvement.
fact_evidence: The IPO “triggered mark-to-market accounting, producing an $83.4 million gain in Q2 based on the June 30th trading price,” with management warning of “future earnings variability from these marks.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Cannae disclosed an additional $45 million federal tax refund expected in 2026, a cash source not identified in the preview. It adds to the liquidity outlook, although the preview had already flagged the Watkins and Brasada proceeds.
fact_evidence: Cannae had “$124 million” of liquidity after the Watkins and Brasada transactions, “with an additional $45 million federal tax refund expected in 2026.”

description: Black Knight Football’s adjusted EBITDA excluding player trading was $34 million, versus $8 million a year earlier, while total EBITDA reached $80 million. The preview emphasized that player-trading profits were lumpy and highlighted recurring EBITDA quality as a key question, making the reported ex-trading result a favorable operating datapoint.
fact_evidence: Black Knight Football revenue rose 45% to $89 million and EBITDA was $80 million versus $8 million; “adjusted EBITDA excluding player trading was $34 million versus $8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that $113 million of LTM EBITDA came from player-trading profit, described it as “lumpy and non-recurring,” and said to watch “BKFC economics ex-player-trading.”

description: Q2 revenue was $102 million, above the $99.65 million consensus estimate. The beat was modest, and revenue still declined from the prior year.
fact_evidence: Restaurant-group revenue was “$102 million from $110 million.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue estimate: “$99.65M.”

description: BODI reported $49.6 million of Q2 revenue, above the $48.5 million guidance midpoint but below the preview’s $51 million functional bar. That makes the result a modest shortfall against the preview’s high-end expectation, despite being within company guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $49.6 million, above the guidance midpoint”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. the $51M guide ceiling — not vs. the $52.9M ‘consensus.’” The preview also says “landing inside the range is a de facto disappointment.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Digital subscriptions ended at 760,000, below the preview’s roughly 780,000 reference point, with a 6.2% sequential decline. That is worse than the preview’s desired flattening of better than about 5%, though it remains within the preview’s stated 760,000–785,000 base-case range.
fact_evidence: “Digital subscriptions fell 6.2% sequentially and 19.1% year-over-year to 760,000.”
expectation_evidence: “Digital subs vs. ~780K” and “Sequential decline better than ~-5% = the erosion is flattening”; the base scenario gave “Subs 760–785K (-4% to -6% q/q).”

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $44 million to $48 million came in below the preview’s $46 million to $51 million base-case range and its bull-case stabilization level near $48 million to $50 million. The lower end signals a steeper step-down than that base expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $44 million to $48 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario put Q3 guidance at “$46–51M”; it said “anything implying stabilization near $48–50M is the bull’s evidence” and “another step down says the digital base is still leaking.”

description: Q3 nutrition and other gross margin guidance extends down to 42%, below the preview’s 43% floor for acceptable nutrition margin. Management attributed the expected further decline to lower-priced products and promotions.
fact_evidence: “Nutrition and other gross margin dropped about 470 basis points year-over-year to 46.7%, and Q3 guidance calls for a further decline to a 42%-45% range due to lower-priced product mix and promotions.”
expectation_evidence: “If nutrition margin lands below the 43% floor, the retail pivot’s unit economics come into question.”

description: Q2 profitability exceeded the guidance ceiling: net income was positive rather than merely at breakeven, and adjusted EBITDA was $6.7 million versus a $6 million high end. The preview expected a fourth consecutive profitable quarter, but the results were better than the provided guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Net income of $1.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $6.7 million … both exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 guidance of “Net income: -$3M to breakeven” and “Adj. EBITDA: $3–6M.”

description: GoPro said the strategic-alternatives process is in its later stages and that it has received inquiries from defense, consumer, and financial-sector parties. The preview expected no process update, so this is a meaningful departure from the expected silence, although no transaction or bidder commitment was reported.
fact_evidence: “inquiries spanning defense, consumer and financial sectors,” and management stated they are “in the later stages of the process.”
expectation_evidence: “Management said it does not intend to provide ongoing updates”; the base case expected “no process update.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The subscriber attach rate reached a record 69%, up from 54% a year earlier, while retention held at 67%. This is a stronger subscription-engagement signal than the preview’s focus on whether the subscriber base would stabilize or continue to erode.
fact_evidence: “subscriber attach rate hit a record 69% in Q2, up sharply from 54% in the same period last year, while retention held steady at 67%.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the sub base stabilizes near 2.2M or keeps eroding.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: GoPro is offering a limited-time $100 discount on the new Mission cameras. That was not part of the preview’s scenario in which the Mission line could support higher ASPs and mix, and the promotion may indicate a need to stimulate awareness or sell-through; no sales impact was provided.
fact_evidence: “offering $100 off Mission 1, Mission 1 PRO and Mission 1 PRO Grip Edition for a limited time,” to “drive awareness and sell-through.”
expectation_evidence: The bull scenario assumed “MISSION 1 8K/4K cinema cameras carry higher ASPs”; the preview did not mention a discount campaign.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: GoPro set a September launch for a third Mission camera, the Mission 1 PRO ILS, with support for more than 300 Micro Four Thirds lenses. The preview discussed the Mission 1 line but did not anticipate this additional camera or its launch timing.
fact_evidence: “The Mission 1 PRO ILS … is set to launch in September 2026” and supports “more than 300 Micro Four Thirds interchangeable lenses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s product discussion referred to “MISSION 1 / pro line” but did not mention the PRO ILS or a September launch.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: GoPro expanded distribution of its new cameras through major retailers, a constructive channel development against the preview’s concern about softness in the sales channel. Management nevertheless said retail representation remains incomplete worldwide, and no sell-through results were disclosed.
fact_evidence: “expanded distribution … through Best Buy, Walmart, B&H and Adorama globally” but “still lacks full retail representation worldwide.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “further softness in the sales channel” and listed “Hardware/channel signals” as a key watch item.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The AGV co-developed motorcycle helmet remains on track and has achieved ECE 22.06 safety-standard compliance, an unanticipated product-development milestone. The preview did not discuss the helmet program.
fact_evidence: “The tech-enabled motorcycle helmet co-developed with Italian brand AGV remains on track and recently achieved ECE 22.06 safety standard compliance.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: GoPro announced a MAX2 360-camera firmware upgrade adding 10-bit GP-Log and 200 Mbps recording, and said it won a third technology and engineering Emmy Award. These product and recognition updates were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The MAX2 360 camera received a June firmware update adding 10-bit color with GP-Log and 200 Mbps recording bit rate, and won GoPro its third technology and engineering Emmy Award.”

description: DH narrowed its FY2026 revenue outlook to $220–222 million, lowering the midpoint from the previous $223 million and the top end from $226 million. The preview’s base case expected the $220–226 million guide to be reiterated, so the tighter, lower range was a negative surprise.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was tightened to $220-$222 million (an 8-9% decline).”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide (reiterated at Q1): revenue $220–226M”; “Base (55%): ... Guide reiterated.”

description: Professional services revenue came in weaker because analytics engagement bookings were lighter, and management said the weakness is expected to pressure the second-half top line. The preview did not anticipate this specific bookings shortfall and was focused on whether the full-year guide would hold.
fact_evidence: “Professional services revenue underperformed due to lighter analytics engagement bookings, a weakness expected to also pressure the second-half top line.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 landed at the high end of guide and they held FY — a repeat is the base case.”

description: Q2 revenue was $55.2 million, below the preview’s roughly $55.5 million consensus and well below its base-case expectation of $56.0–56.5 million, although it remained within company guidance. That makes the result a modest shortfall rather than a guidance miss.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $55.2 million, down 9% year-over-year, but landed within the guided range on the top line.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~ $55.5M”; “Base (55%): Revenue $56.0–56.5M (high end / small beat).”

description: DH raised the midpoint of its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook by $1 million, to $58 million, and expects margins to rise roughly 100 basis points. The preview expected the existing $55–59 million range to be reiterated, so this was a favorable guidance change.
fact_evidence: “The adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint was raised $1 million to $57-$59 million with margins up roughly 100 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide (reiterated at Q1): ... adj. EBITDA $55–59M (25–26%).”; “Base (55%): ... Guide reiterated.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The biopharma business had its strongest new-business quarter in three years outside of Q4 and won back four customers that had left before 2025. That was a stronger response than the preview could count on while it awaited evidence that life-sciences bookings would recover after the claims-data disruption.
fact_evidence: “The biopharma segment posted its strongest new business quarter in three years outside of Q4, including four win-back customers that had left before 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the first clean quarter to test whether life sciences bookings actually respond”; the bear case required that “life sciences fails to recover post-claims fix.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was modestly above the high end of quarterly guidance, and adjusted EPS of $0.05 exceeded the preview’s $0.03 consensus. The preview already allowed for $0.04–0.05 EPS in its base case, so the EPS outperformance was limited relative to that scenario.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $14.6 million (26% margin), modestly above the high end of guidance, and adjusted EPS was $0.05.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ... Co. guidance $13.5–14.5M”; “Adj. EPS ... Consensus $0.03”; “Base (55%): ... Adj. EPS $0.04–0.05.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The trailing 12-month EBITDA-to-cash conversion rate fell about five percentage points year over year. The preview highlighted DH’s cash generation and cited nearly $50 million of trailing free cash flow, but did not anticipate or flag weaker conversion.
fact_evidence: “The company generated $50 million of unlevered free cash flow on a trailing 12-month basis, with a 75% EBITDA-to-cash conversion rate, down about 5 points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “DH is a cash-generative SaaS asset (TTM unlevered FCF $49.9M...).”

description: The preview called a buyback authorization a notable potential capital-allocation catalyst, but the supplied call facts report no buyback announcement. That leaves the preview’s specifically flagged capital-return question unanswered.
fact_evidence: The supplied call facts report no buyback authorization or other capital-return announcement.
expectation_evidence: “Buyback authorization — at ~1.5x EV/EBITDA with net-zero leverage, the absence of one is a signal”; “Silence on capital return would be conspicuous.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Monovate’s European card issuance is still constrained after a Bank of Lithuania inspection, and management said restoring it is gating both Monovate growth and Exodus Pay adoption. Exodus is pursuing TixiPay to restore issuing licenses, but the deal awaits Bank of Latvia approval and the company is targeting a new issuing arrangement in Q4 2026—an unanticipated obstacle to the payments ramp.
fact_evidence: “Monovate's card issuance in Europe remains constrained following a Bank of Lithuania inspection,” and restoring it is “gating both Monovate growth and Exodus Pay adoption.” Exodus is acquiring TixiPay, pending Bank of Latvia approval, and is “targeting a new issuing arrangement in Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 the “first quarter that tests the payments pivot with actual revenue” and said the market-implied setup required payments to “contribute meaningfully out of the gate”; it did not flag an issuing-license constraint.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The reported loss was burdened by unusually large one-time costs: the company reported an $18.6 million net loss and a $21.5 million EBITDA loss, versus a $6.7 million adjusted EBITDA loss. The preview warned of an ugly Q2 cost line, but did not anticipate approximately $17 million of transaction-related incentives and $5.8 million of professional-services costs.
fact_evidence: “Net loss of $18.6 million,” “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $6.7 million,” and “EBITDA loss was $21.5 million.” One-time Q2 costs included “approximately $17 million in transaction-related incentives and $5.8 million in professional services.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated GAAP EPS of about “$(0.50)” and warned to “Expect an ugly Q2 cost line,” but its identified restructuring charge was expected in Q3.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The legacy business held up better on swap volume than the preview’s base case implied: reported quarterly swap volume was $1.13 billion and roughly flat quarter-over-quarter, versus the preview’s $0.97 billion base-case processed-volume estimate and its concern that another 25% quarterly decline was possible.
fact_evidence: “Legacy Exodus metrics held roughly flat quarter-over-quarter,” with “$1.13 billion in quarterly swap volume.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected “Processed volume” of “$0.97B” and said “another −25% q/q” would indicate structural decline.

description: Monovate’s reported revenue was $5 million, below the preview’s roughly $6 million base case for its two months in the quarter, though above the preview’s $4.5 million level that would fail to validate the pivot.
fact_evidence: Q2 revenue included “$5M from Monovate.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Payments (2 mos, May–Jun)” at “$6.0M” and said “below $4.5M does not” validate the pivot.

description: The planned $10–13 million in annualized operating-expense savings is now expected to be at full run rate by Q4 2026, earlier than the preview’s framing that savings were on track for 2027.
fact_evidence: After reducing the team by approximately 25%, Exodus expects “$10-13 million in annualized operating expense savings with the full run rate in place by Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case description said management would point “to 2027 for the $10–13M annualized savings.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Monovate disclosed strong transaction-volume growth despite a large concentrated client moving processing in-house: normalized Q2 volume was up 60% quarter-over-quarter, and first-half volume excluding that client was up over 50% year-over-year. The preview did not anticipate this volume disclosure or the client’s departure.
fact_evidence: Monovate processed “$1.8 billion in gross transaction volume year-to-date (roughly $900 million in Q2), representing a 60% quarter-over-quarter increase on a normalized basis.” Excluding “one large concentrated client that moved card processing in-house,” transaction volumes grew “over 50% in the first half of 2026 versus the prior year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Monthly active users were 1.4 million, below the preview’s 1.5 million figure for MAU, even though the call described legacy metrics as roughly flat quarter-over-quarter.
fact_evidence: Exodus reported “1.4 million monthly active users.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “MAU held at 1.5M.”

description: Revenue was about $1.7 million, nearly twice the preview’s $0.90 million estimate, rather than growing only about 2% year over year. The company attributed the increase to barter advertising, Truth+ Patriot Package subscriptions, and Truth.Fi ETF management fees.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $1.7 million, up 92% sequentially and 89% year-over-year,” driven by barter advertising, Truth+ Patriot Package subscriptions, and Truth.Fi ETF management fees.
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” Q2 FY2026E: “~$0.90M” and “+2% y/y.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company reported only $215 million of cash and $209 million of short-term investments, far below the preview’s roughly $0.9–1.0 billion cash expectation. Its $1.9 billion in gross financial assets included substantial bitcoin-related assets, so it did not represent comparable cash available for the nearly $1 billion of convertible notes coming due.
fact_evidence: TMTG ended Q2 with “$1.9 billion in gross financial assets,” including “$215 million cash,” “$209 million short-term investments,” and “$1.2 billion in bitcoin and bitcoin-related assets,” with approximately “$893 million net of debt.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Cash ~$0.9–1.0B” in its base case and described company cash as “~$1.01B.”

description: The net loss was $238 million, about $58 million—or roughly one-third—worse than the preview’s modeled $180 million loss. The loss was down sequentially but remained much larger than expected for the quarter.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a net loss of $238 million for the quarter, down 41% sequentially but more than 10x higher year-over-year, largely from non-cash mark-to-market losses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimate table put “Net loss (GAAP)” at “~$(180)M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Truth API had more than 10 customer agreements, above the preview’s report of at least five firms signed. The disclosed monthly prices were in the expected $60,000–$100,000 range, but recognized revenue remained modest and no contracted ARR figure was given.
