description: RPO grew sequentially and was more than 1.7 times full-year revenue guidance, with an estimated gross margin well above the company’s current reported margin. The preview did not call out RPO as a specific expected result, so this adds an unanticipated backlog and future-economics data point.
fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation grew 4.5% sequentially to $312.6 million, exceeds 1.7x full-year revenue guidance, and carries an estimated ~66% gross margin versus current 51% reported gross margin.”

description: The preview expected FY2027 adjusted EPS of $5.86, with the tax rate normalizing to roughly 23–25%. H&R Block guided to $6.04–$6.24 while projecting an effective tax rate of approximately 23%, putting even the low end above consensus despite the expected tax normalization.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for” adjusted diluted EPS of “$6.04-$6.24” and an effective tax rate “rising to approximately 23%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS (initial guide vs.) $5.86”; the preview also described a normalized rate of “~23–25%.”

description: The preview put FY2027 revenue at $4.05 billion and considered a guide around $4.03–$4.08 billion in-frame. H&R Block guided to $4.11–$4.16 billion, above that expectation.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $4.11-$4.16 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue (initial guide vs.) $4.05B”; the scenario analysis described a base range of “$4.00–4.06B.”

description: The preview expected a new or upsized buyback authorization, with at least $1.5 billion cited in its bull case. Instead, H&R Block said about $600 million remains on the existing authorization and plans approximately $400 million of buybacks for FY2027.
fact_evidence: “Plans about $400 million in buybacks for fiscal 2027 with roughly $600 million remaining on authorization.”
expectation_evidence: “A new/upsized authorization plus a high-single/low-double-digit dividend raise is expected”; the bull case specified “buyback re-upped to ≥$1.5B.”

description: FY2026 revenue and adjusted EPS both exceeded the preview’s expectations and the company’s prior-year guidance ranges. Revenue was about 1% above the preview’s $3.91 billion estimate, while adjusted EPS was about 3% above its $5.16 estimate.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 revenue of $3.95 billion” and “adjusted EPS up 13.9% to $5.31.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $3.91B”; “FY26 adj. EPS $5.16”; the preview listed FY26 guide ranges of “$3.910–3.920B” revenue and “$5.10–5.20” adjusted EPS.

description: FY2026 EBITDA growth was stronger than the preview’s operating-growth framework implied: EBITDA grew faster than revenue, at about 1.7 times the revenue growth rate, versus the preview’s roughly 1.5-times framework.
fact_evidence: “EBITDA up 8.3% to $1.06 billion” as revenue “was up 4.9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management reaffirmed “EBITDA at ~1.5x” revenue growth.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: H&R Block reported unusually large gains in conversion and retention that the preview did not identify as expected outcomes: conversion had its largest single-year improvement in company history, and retention also rose.
fact_evidence: “Conversion improved 200 basis points this season (the largest single-year gain in company history) and retention rose 190 basis points.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The client mix has shifted substantially toward the $50,000–$200,000 household AGI range, a strategic change toward more complex, higher-lifetime-value clients that the preview did not discuss.
fact_evidence: “The percentage of clients in the target household AGI range of $50,000-$200,000 has risen from 38% to 50%,” reflecting a mix shift toward “more complex, higher-lifetime-value clients.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management now expects industry growth below the historical roughly 1% norm, attributing the moderation to slowing job growth. The preview focused on the company’s growth algorithm and competitive dynamics but did not flag this industry slowdown.
fact_evidence: “Management expects moderated industry growth below the historical ~1% norm due to slowing job growth.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The call disclosed an $8.3 million severance charge in Q1 FY2027 tied to changes in office leadership and support functions. The preview did not anticipate this near-term restructuring cost, although the charge is excluded from guidance.
fact_evidence: “The transition to a year-round office leadership model plus streamlining of support functions triggered an $8.3 million severance charge in Q1 fiscal 2027 that is excluded from guidance.”

description: Peraso reported gross margin of 63.7%, well above the preview’s expected 50–55% range and guidance into the 50s. Management attributed the improvement to favorable millimeter-wave mix and sales of previously written-down inventory.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 63.7% in Q2 2026,” boosted by “favorable millimeter wave product mix and sales of previously written-down inventory.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~50–55%”; Q1 guidance was “into the 50s” as product mix rises.

description: Management provided no quarterly guidance, rather than a Q3 revenue outlook investors could assess; it cited irregular FWA order patterns and limited visibility. The preview already warned that Q3 guidance was likely to disappoint, but did not anticipate that management would withhold guidance altogether.
fact_evidence: “Management declined to provide quarterly guidance, citing limited near-term visibility due to irregular fixed wireless access order patterns” and elevated memory prices.
expectation_evidence: “Q3 guidance” was a key metric to watch; the preview said the sell-side “explicitly warns that Q3 guidance is likely to disappoint” and called for listening for a specific Q3 revenue number.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended at $3.3 million, above the preview’s expected $1.5–2.5 million range, but the increase was supported by substantial ATM equity sales. That improves near-term liquidity while also indicating dilution.
fact_evidence: “Cash rose to approximately $3.3 million” from $2.7 million, “aided by $2.4 million in net proceeds from at-the-market equity sales.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “cash ~$1.5–2.5M pre-CEF”; the preview also said to watch for ATM usage during Q2.

description: The call disclosed that Peraso had already generated seven-figure revenue from its Israeli defense IFF partner and expected increasing volume as the application shifts to drone use. The preview discussed the defense opportunity and possible future orders, but did not anticipate revenue already being generated from this partner.
fact_evidence: “Peraso has generated seven-figure revenue from its Israeli defense IFF (identification friend or foe) partner” and expects “increasing volume over the coming quarters” as it transitions to drone-based use.
expectation_evidence: The preview described the Intact drone-identification win, August field trials, and volume targeted for Q3/Q4’26; it said to watch for “a named, quantified purchase order.”

description: Management flagged elevated DDR4/DDR5 memory prices as likely to persist into Q4, a forward cost and visibility headwind not raised in the preview. This contributed to the decision not to provide quarterly guidance.
fact_evidence: Management cited “elevated third-party memory (DDR4/DDR5) prices expected to persist into Q4.”

description: Total Q2 revenue was $5.5 million, far above both the $2.21 million consensus and the preview’s $2.4–2.7 million model. The beat came from license revenue, not from stronger-than-expected US product sales.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $5.5 million,” including “$3.8 million in ex-US license revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus: “$2.21M”; preview model: “$2.4–2.7M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Product volume came in below the preview’s growth expectations: about 27,000 monthly packs were sold, up only 9% from Q1, versus an estimate of 32,000–34,000 paid scripts and a roughly 30,000-script hurdle. This is a weak Q2 result against the expected lift from expanded territories, TV advertising, and direct dispensing.
fact_evidence: “Over $1.7 million in product revenue (~27,000 monthly packs sold, up 9% from Q1).”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “32,000–34,000” paid scripts, “(+28–36%),” and said “Anything below ~30,000 scripts (+20%) says the commercial investment isn't converting.”

description: License revenue was dramatically higher than expected, accounting for most of the revenue beat. The quarter included both a first regulatory milestone from the TEA/Health Canada submission and a first sublicense milestone connected to Everest’s sale of Greater China rights to Cork Cell, whereas the preview modeled only $0.2–0.5 million and did not assume material revenue from the Everest transaction.
fact_evidence: “$3.8 million in ex-US license revenue,” including “the first regulatory milestone from the TEA/Health Canada submission” and “the first sublicense milestone tied to Everest Medicine's asset sale of Greater China rights to Cork Cell.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “License revenue” of “$0.2–0.5M” and said the Everest/Corxel China upfront “may not accrue to LENZ this period.”

description: The net loss was substantially smaller than the preview expected, and the reported loss per share was better than both consensus and the preview’s own estimate. LENZ reported a $1.02 loss per share against consensus of $1.21 and the preview’s estimated range of $1.44–$1.56 loss per share.
fact_evidence: “Net loss was $31.9 million ($1.02 per share).”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed GAAP EPS consensus of “−$1.21” and its own estimate of “−$1.44 to −$1.56.”

description: Adjusted SG&A fell rather than rising with the Q2 TV campaign and expanded commercial footprint. It was down 14% sequentially, a notably lower spending trend than the preview’s $48–52 million SG&A estimate, though the reported $34.9 million figure excludes stock-based compensation and is therefore not directly comparable to an unqualified SG&A estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A (excluding stock-based comp) fell 14% quarter-over-quarter to $34.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “SG&A” of “$48–52M,” noting that national TV was “the swing factor” and expected a step-up in spending.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call provided encouraging repeat-purchase evidence that had not previously been disclosed: more than 60% of e-pharmacy buyers purchased multiple packs, and the mature Q4 cohort had bought slightly more than five packs on average before a full year. That is positive evidence on persistence despite the weaker Q2 volume.
fact_evidence: “More than 60% of e-pharmacy patients who purchased VIZ since launch have bought more than one monthly pack”; the mature Q4 2025 cohort “has purchased slightly more than five monthly packs on average (before reaching a full year).”
expectation_evidence: The preview said LENZ “has not disclosed patient refill rates or daily-dose consumption per patient” and identified refill/persistence disclosure as a key metric to watch.

description: Despite high physician awareness and a broad prescriber base, management said retail uptake remained poor and prescribing was not consistently recurring, prompting a pivot toward consumer-driven demand. That is a concern about the existing ECP and retail channel even as the company pursues telehealth and advertising.
fact_evidence: “Retail uptake tracked through Symphony or IQVIA has been described as poor and limited”; despite “more than 75% prescribing multiple times,” high awareness “has not translated into consistent recurring prescribing, prompting a pivot toward consumer-driven demand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the July telehealth launch as an option that “bypasses the ECP bottleneck entirely” and highlighted the commercial trajectory and refill/persistence as key debates.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Early July momentum was stronger than the preview’s qualitative watch item suggested: prescriptions rose more than 45% month over month, with management attributing the increase to telehealth and national TV advertising lifting all channels. This is a promising post-quarter signal, though it does not undo the weaker Q2 product-volume result.
fact_evidence: “July prescriptions grew over 45% month-over-month versus June,” driven by the telehealth option and national TV campaign, which “lifted all sales channels.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called telehealth a “Q3 item, commentary only” and said early conversion anecdotes would shape Q3 expectations, without anticipating a specific growth rate.

description: Management did not announce the explicit quarterly spending ceiling or breakeven quarter the preview identified as the most important capital-allocation signal. Instead, it said it would use Q3 data to reallocate commercial investment toward the best-performing initiatives, leaving the size of future spending and a cash-flow timeline unspecified.
fact_evidence: Management plans “to use Q3 data to reallocate commercial investment toward the highest-performing initiatives.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted a “peak-spend statement” and described an SG&A cap as the “print's real catalyst”; it also said a named breakeven quarter would be especially powerful.

description: Energy Vault raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $270–310 million, above the prior $225–300 million range and above the preview’s bull-case threshold of guidance above $300 million. The increase to the lower end of the range is especially notable against the preview’s base case of reaffirmed guidance.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $270–310 million from the prior $225–300 million range.”
expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … FY26 guide reaffirmed at $225–300M”; “Bull (25%): FY26 guide raised above $300M.”

description: Q2 revenue of $17.4 million exceeded the preview’s approximately $14.2 million consensus estimate, though the preview cautioned that Q2 revenue estimates were unreliable and not the main focus.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $17.4 million.”

description: The Q2 GAAP loss per share was $0.17, worse than the preview’s consensus estimate of a $0.13 loss. The narrower year-over-year net loss does not change the miss against that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net loss narrowed to $29.7 million (loss of $0.17 per share).”
expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 EPS: –$0.13”; the preview also cited an alternative estimate of “–$0.14.”

description: FY2026 GAAP gross-margin guidance improved at the low end, moving from 15–25% to 20–25%. That is better than the preview’s concern that a low-end margin outcome could undermine the profitability narrative.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 GAAP gross margin guidance was narrowed to 20–25% from 15–25%.”
expectation_evidence: “The FY guide is 15–25% GAAP”; “Any print at the low end while revenue disappoints breaks the ‘scale into profitability’ narrative.”

description: Q2 margins were strong: GAAP gross margin was 31% and adjusted gross margin was 38.6%, with adjusted margin up about 900 basis points year over year. This was a favorable result against the preview’s focus on margin pressure after adjusted gross margin had fallen to 27.9% in Q1.
fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP gross margin at 31% (up 140 bps) and adjusted gross margin at 38.6% (up ~900 bps year-over-year).”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin: 27.9%, down from 57.1%”; “Any print at the low end while revenue disappoints…”

description: The company raised the lower end of its year-end cash guidance to $160 million from $150 million, and reported $148 million of cash and equivalents including restricted cash at June 30. This is ahead of the preview’s base-case cash expectation, although the reported cash increase was partly supported by an AR facility draw.
fact_evidence: “Year-end 2026 cash guidance was raised to $160–200 million from $150–200 million”; “Total cash and equivalents including restricted cash were $148 million on June 30th, up ~$31 million sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … cash mid-$90Ms–$110M”; the preview also flagged “Cash and liquidity vs. the $150–200M year-end target.”

description: Management projected nearly $3 billion of backlog by year-end, an additional forward target beyond the preview’s discussion of the current backlog and its $2.5 billion-plus level as a clean beat. The actual backlog reported at about $2 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s current-backlog expectations.
fact_evidence: “Management projects backlog approaching nearly $3 billion by year-end.”

description: Management outlined a path to roughly 5 gigawatts online by 2030, above the 4-gigawatt installed-by-2030 target cited in the preview, and added a target of approximately $2 billion in annualized EBITDA. This raises the stated scale ambition, though it remains a long-term target.
fact_evidence: “Outlined a path to roughly 5 gigawatts online generating approximately $2 billion in annualized EBITDA by 2030.”
expectation_evidence: “Asset Vault platform expansion (4 GW installed by 2030 target).”

description: Q2 revenue was $19.7 million, below the preview’s $23.5 million estimate and even below its $21–26 million base-case range. The preview expected a content-gap quarter, but the reported decline was worse than its central expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $19.7 million,” driven by drops in ASA and ASE sales, partly offset by Bellwright.
expectation_evidence: “My estimate: $23.5M (range $21–26M)” and the base case projected “$22–25M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings were $21.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $25 million estimate and just under its $22–29 million range. That is a weaker demand read than the preview’s central expectation, even though bookings remained above revenue.
fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings fell to $21.8 million from $27.1 million,” reflecting lower ASE and ASA sales, partly offset by Bellwright.
expectation_evidence: “Bookings: $25M (range $22–29M)” and the base case projected “$24–27M.”

description: The preview expected Fantastic Tames to be the only material new paid content contribution inside Q2, but some Fantastic Tames content was deferred for recognition into Q3 and Q4. This meant less of that content’s revenue was recognized in the quarter than the preview’s framing implied.
fact_evidence: “Current deferred revenue rose to $28.5 million as phased DLC content releases for the Fantastic Tames pack and Dragontopia defer recognition into Q3 and Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “Fantastic Tames Season 1 (May 2026) contribution. The only material new paid content inside the quarter.”

description: The reported $3 million net loss was materially worse than the preview’s roughly break-even estimate and its stated -$0.50 to +$0.30 EPS range. The year-over-year narrowing in the loss was largely due to the absence of a prior-year tax provision, rather than stronger underlying results.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss narrowed sharply to $3 million from $16.6 million a year earlier,” primarily because the prior-year quarter included a $14 million income tax provision.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “EPS (post-split): -$0.05 (range -$0.50 to +$0.30).”

description: A reduced ARK licensing fee structure generated roughly $1.5 million of quarterly savings and boosted gross profit, an offset to the revenue decline that the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: The reduced fee structure effective April 2026 “saved roughly $500,000 monthly (about $1.5 million per quarter), boosting gross profit even as revenue fell.”

description: Management said R&D and G&A should stay consistent quarter-over-quarter and that R&D spending is nearing its peak, a more reassuring expense trajectory than the preview’s expectation that operating costs were more likely to rise.
fact_evidence: Management indicated “R&D and G&A expenses should remain consistent quarter-over-quarter” as investment in three in-development AAA titles nears completion, with R&D spend “approaching its peak.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Opex was $9.6M in Q1 and is more likely to rise than fall,” and estimated Q2 operating expenses at about $10.0 million.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bellwright’s console launch reached the top five paid games on Xbox, adding a specific sign of console traction that the preview did not forecast, though it had described Bellwright as potentially durable.
fact_evidence: Bellwright’s PlayStation and Xbox launch “reached the top five paid games list on Xbox,” building on over 1 million lifetime units sold and 46.4 million playtime hours.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Bellwright durable” as a possible bull-case driver but did not forecast a console launch ranking.

description: Q2 revenue was $7.7 million, about 10% below the $8.52 million consensus and below the preview’s $8.0–8.7 million base case. The quarter had no robotic system deliveries, making the result weaker than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue totaled $7.7 million,” declining year-over-year “due to the absence of any robotic system delivery.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $8.52M”; the preview’s base case was “$8.0–8.7M.”

description: Despite the revenue miss, recurring revenue appears to have been a strong positive: with no system deliveries, the $7.7 million total was above the preview’s >$6.0 million recurring-revenue bogey. Robotic catheter revenue also exceeded $1 million after the MAGIC launch, indicating a sharper near-term ramp than the preview’s threshold implied.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue totaled $7.7 million” with “absence of any robotic system delivery”; robotic catheter revenue “surpassed $1 million,” growing “roughly 270-300% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Bogey: >$6.0M and up sequentially.”

description: The H2 outlook fell short of the preview’s expected revenue shape: guidance implies about $10 million in Q3 and $11 million in Q4, or roughly $35 million for 2026 including Q1 and Q2—not the prior >$40 million target. Q3 is no longer guided above $10 million, and Q4 is well below the preview’s roughly $14.2 million consensus estimate.
fact_evidence: Management guided recurring revenue to “approximately $7 million in Q3 and $8 million in Q4 2026” and system revenue to “approximately $3 million in each of Q3 and Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: Management had previously guided to “>$40M with Q3 and Q4 each above $10M”; the preview’s consensus shape was “Q3 ~$11.0M” and “Q4 ~$14.2M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview highlighted a 500-catheters-per-month exit-2026 target and said the absence of a quantified production rate would be a negative tell. The call facts report strong catheter growth but no monthly production run-rate, and say sales remain supply-constrained with only about a dozen U.S. sites approved to purchase MAGIC in Q2.
fact_evidence: Catheter sales “remain supply-constrained with a customer backlog”; “only about a dozen U.S. sites received hospital approval to purchase MAGIC in Q2.” No monthly production run-rate is reported in the call facts.
expectation_evidence: Management targeted “500/month exiting 2026”; “If they don't quantify it at all, treat that as a negative tell.”

description: Management disclosed an internal cash-flow-profitability target for the first half of 2027, a more constructive milestone than the preview’s emphasis on Robocath being dilutive to the P&L for roughly three years. The company expects incremental recurring revenue to carry through to operating profit under its lean cost structure.
fact_evidence: “Internally modeling cash flow profitability in the first half of 2027,” with “the majority of incremental recurring revenue flowing to operating profit under its existing lean cost structure.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Robocath “is not breakeven until year three” and would be “dilutive to the P&L for ~3 years.”

description: The preview cited a $3 million Synchrony revenue target for 2026; management now expects Synchrony to contribute over $1 million in system revenue per quarter at an ASP near $200,000. That run-rate would be materially higher than the stated 2026 target if sustained, though the timing is not specified.
fact_evidence: Management “expects synchrony to contribute over $1 million in system revenue per quarter at an ASP near $200,000.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided to $3M in 2026 revenue.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company reported its first U.S. GenesisX purchase from an academic medical center, with installation expected this fall. The preview was looking for GenesisX proof points and order-book conversion, but had not identified a U.S. academic-center purchase as an existing expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company announced its first U.S. GenesisX purchase from an academic medical center (install expected this fall).”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for named ‘pioneering accounts’ demonstrating GenesisX compatibility” and evidence of GenesisX orders converting to installations.

description: Q2 revenue was $3.1 million, about 13% below the $3.55 million consensus and below the preview’s $3.2–3.6 million base-case range. The year-over-year decline was roughly 24%, materially steeper than the preview’s expected 12% decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million,” down roughly 24% from $4.1 million in Q2 2025.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus: $3.55M”; implied year-over-year “−12%.” The base scenario expected “$3.2–3.6M.”

description: Despite the revenue shortfall, Seer reaffirmed its $16–18 million full-year revenue guidance rather than narrowing it to the low end, as the preview’s base case anticipated. That keeps in place a demanding second-half recovery after a roughly 30% first-half decline.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $16-18 million,” implying “second-half growth north of 20% after a roughly 30% first-half decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected guidance to be “narrowed to ‘low end of $16–18M’”; it also described the 2H bridge as “very stretched.”

description: Gross margin came in at 49%, above the preview’s estimated 40–46% range and its 38–44% base case. It also rebounded sharply from Q1, although it remained below the year-ago margin.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 49%,” down from 52% in Q2 2025 but “up 1,300 basis points sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “40–46%” and gave a base-case range of “38–44%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The quarter-end cash balance was above the preview’s estimate, with a smaller-than-expected decline from the prior-quarter balance. Cash still declined and the company continued to burn cash, but the reported balance was modestly better than anticipated.
fact_evidence: Seer ended the quarter with “approximately $209.5 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments”; six-month free cash flow was “approximately negative $25.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 cash at “$204–207M,” from $219.5 million at March 31, and cited a burn estimate of “~$14.6M/qtr.”

description: Seer bought back about 1.4 million shares during Q2 while the two proposals were outstanding. The preview specifically identified whether the company repurchased shares during this period as an open question; the purchases also continued the reduction in shares outstanding.
fact_evidence: Seer repurchased “about 1.4 million Class A shares at an average of $1.68 in Q2,” bringing cumulative buybacks to 13.4 million shares and reducing net shares outstanding by “~15%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked: “Whether the company bought stock in Q2 — while two bids were outstanding — is a live governance question.”

description: The net loss was narrower year over year, but at $16.9 million it exceeded the preview’s approximately $15 million estimate. Lower operating expenses helped limit the loss, but did not bring it down to that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $16.9 million from $19.4 million,” while operating expenses were $18.3 million versus $22.6 million a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimated Q2 net loss was “~$15M.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Seer reported substantially more validation evidence for the Proteograph platform, including head-to-head studies showing broader coverage than Olink and SomaLogic. The preview discussed competitive and moat concerns but did not anticipate this specific body of platform evidence.
fact_evidence: Validating publications “surpassed 95,” an “approximately 80% increase over the prior 12 months,” including head-to-head studies showing broader proteome coverage than Olink and SomaLogic.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The PRECISE SG100K team had completed running 10,000 samples and planned to present preliminary data in September. The preview identified the cohort as a potential program but did not report that this sample milestone had been completed or that data were due so soon.
fact_evidence: The PRECISE SG100K team “completed running 10,000 samples from the 100,000-sample cohort in May” and will present preliminary data at HUPO in September.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “PRECISE SG100K (10,000 participants, expanding toward 100,000)” as a population-scale biobank program.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Seer disclosed that shipments were coming from both prior STAC customers and the SIP program, with some SIP placements converting into owned instruments. This provides evidence of instrument-placement channels and conversion, though the preview had no specific expected shipment mix.
fact_evidence: In the first half, “one-third of instrument shipments came from prior STAC customers and one-third from the SIP program,” with some SIP placements converting into owned instruments.
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “instrument placements and consumables pull-through” as a metric to watch, including “evidence the reorder cycle is actually converting.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview focused on the pending FCC PNT notice but did not flag that the lower 900 MHz band could be left out of the final direct-to-device NPRM. The final NPRM excluded the band even though the draft had proposed allowing unlicensed space-to-first transmissions there, a negative change in the regulatory picture for NextNav’s spectrum proposal.
fact_evidence: “NextNav's lower 900 MHz band was ultimately not included in the FCC's final direct-to-device NPRM despite the draft proposing to permit unlicensed space-to-first transmissions in the band.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview said the final derivative and warrant mark would likely swing in NextNav’s favor and could produce a GAAP beat. Instead, the company reported a $33.8 million net loss, including a roughly $32 million noncash loss on the fair-value change in derivative and warrant liabilities.
fact_evidence: “Net loss of approximately $33.8 million for Q2 2026, driven by a ~$32 million noncash loss on the change in fair value of derivative and warrants liability, partially offset by a ~$21 million gain on debt extinguishment.”
expectation_evidence: “The derivative mark likely swings in NextNav's favor, meaning a headline GAAP ‘beat’ that means nothing.” The preview also gave a base EPS range of “-$0.10 to -$0.16.”

description: NextNav reported 15.2 million shares issued to convert all debt, slightly above the preview’s estimate of about 14.9 million conversion shares. The difference is small, and the conversion itself—and becoming debt-free—was expected.
fact_evidence: “The company became debt-free by converting all its debt to 15.2 million shares, with all debt holders electing shares over cash.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated that converting the notes would issue “~14.9M shares” and expected “zero convertible debt.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: NextNav reported approximately 20-nanosecond timing accuracy across outdoor, indoor, and GPS-denied settings, a concrete performance result not anticipated in the preview. Management said it exceeds critical-infrastructure requirements.
fact_evidence: “Demonstrated approximately 20 nanoseconds of timing accuracy over its operational 5G PNT network across outdoor, indoor and GPS-denied environments,” which management says “exceeds critical infrastructure requirements.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: NextNav disclosed a new Tier 1 partner arrangement to put its Z-access software and reference data on devices for 911 vertical-location services. The preview discussed commercial opportunities but did not anticipate this device-based partnership.
fact_evidence: “A new partnership brings NextNav's Z-access software and reference data onto a Tier 1 partner's devices for 911 vertical location services,” advancing its device-based strategy and “creating incremental revenue opportunities.”

description: Revenue was $260 million, above the preview’s $245–250 million company range and $245.98 million consensus. That is a clear quarterly beat, rather than the in-range result expected in the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $260 million, up 27% year-over-year.”

expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.) | ~$42–44M / ~17%”; “≥17.5% consolidated is a clean pass”; bull case: “≥18%.”

description: Adjusted EPS was approximately $0.70 versus the preview’s $0.53 consensus, a substantially larger beat than the preview’s base-case range of $0.55–0.58. The preview cautioned that share-count restatement made the consensus uncertain, but the reported figure still exceeds the stated estimate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of approximately $0.70.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.53”; base case: “$0.55–0.58.”

description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.02–1.04 billion, above the preview’s prior $970 million–$1.0 billion range and even above its bull-case range of approximately $1.00–1.02 billion. The new range also takes the company above $1 billion for the first time.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year guidance to $1.02-$1.04 billion, crossing the $1 billion threshold for the first time.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 Revenue … Company Guidance: $970M – $1.0B”; bull case: “Raised to ~$1.00–1.02B.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings reached $306 million, extending the sequence of quarterly increases and exceeding the preview’s $250–270 million range for holding visibility and its >$270 million bull-case marker. Rather than normalizing from Q1’s record, bookings set another all-time high.
fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings reached an all-time high of $306 million,” following $210M, $257M, and $290M over the prior three quarters.
expectation_evidence: “A number in the $250–270M range … keeps the visibility story intact”; bull case: “> $270M.”

description: Aerospace operating margin was 21.4%, materially above the preview’s 18%+ bull-case marker for the segment. The segment also reported record sales and backlog, adding strength beyond the preview’s focus on margin improvement.
fact_evidence: “Aerospace segment sales grew 22.6% to a record $237.3 million with adjusted operating margin of 21.4% (up 510 bps), while backlog hit a record $657.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Aerospace operating margin prints 18%+” in the bull-case operational description.

description: The call added a sizable, previously unflagged program contribution: MV-75 FLRAA generated a $27.4 million booking and is expected to provide about $35 million of 2026 revenue, with management describing it as potentially the company’s largest military program.
fact_evidence: “The MV-75 FLRAA program generated a $27.4 million booking in Q2, is expected to contribute roughly $35 million in revenue in 2026, and is described as potentially the largest military program in company history.”

description: The $44.7 million Army radio production order itself was already expected, but management now anticipates similar annual orders for the next four to five years. That adds a longer stream of expected demand than the preview’s stated $40–50 million annual run-rate framing.
fact_evidence: “A $45 million (specifically $44.7M) production order for the U.S. Army 4549/T radio test program, expected to support deliveries over 18 months with similar annual orders anticipated for the next 4-5 years.”

description: Astronics recognized a $2 million IEEPA tariff refund in Q2, adding about 70 basis points of margin, whereas the preview said no refunds had yet been recognized. The preview noted tariff-refund upside generally, but not a refund already benefiting this quarter.
fact_evidence: “Results benefited from a $2 million IEEPA tariff refund (about 70 bps of margin).”
expectation_evidence: “Tariffs were a ~$2M Y/Y headwind with no refund benefit yet recognized.”

fact_evidence: “Management expects an ongoing tariff run rate of $3-$4 million per quarter before mitigation.”
expectation_evidence: “Tariffs were a ~$2M Y/Y headwind” in Q1.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Long-term debt fell to $310.3 million and available liquidity rose to $253.2 million, compared with the preview’s Q1 snapshot of $334.9 million of total debt and $231.8 million of liquidity. expectation_evidence: “Total debt / liquidity | $334.9M / $231.8M.”

description: After quarter-end cash of $10.8 million came in slightly above the preview’s $9.5–10 million estimate, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments had fallen to about $5.6 million by July 31. The company also issued a going-concern warning, making the post-quarter liquidity deterioration worse than the preview’s roughly $4 million monthly burn assumption suggested.
fact_evidence: “~$5.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of July 31, 2026, down from $10.8 million unrestricted cash at quarter end,” and “issued a going-concern warning.”
expectation_evidence: “Straight-lining puts June 30 liquidity at ~$9.5–10M”; the preview also described cash depletion at roughly “$4.0M/month.”

expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | ~$0.1M (Stocktwits) / $404K (ChartMill).”

description: ESS had repaid $37 million of the original $40 million Yorkville promissory note, a substantial debt reduction not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of financing options. The deleveraging is favorable, though it comes amid sharply reduced cash.

description: Q2 revenue was approximately $64,000, far below the preview’s $300,000 estimate and even below its $150,000–$700,000 range. The preview expected a small, lumpy quarter, but not revenue this low.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $64,000.”

fact_evidence: “Pixelworks repurchased $3.2 million of common stock during Q2, its single largest cash use, with $1.8 million remaining on the buyback authorization.”
expectation_evidence: “Base: … token or no buyback”; “Shares repurchased in Q2 … vs. an expectation of something.”

description: Management said Q3 revenue should increase sequentially based on business already booked, giving a more constructive near-term revenue signal than the preview’s expectation of a small, lumpy business with no formal guidance. Management still cautioned that revenue will remain lumpy until the business scales.
fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 2026 revenue to increase sequentially based on currently booked licensing and motion grading business, though revenue will remain lumpy until scale is achieved.”
expectation_evidence: “Formal guidance: None — company does not guide”; the base case anticipated “revenue lumpy and small.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash was $53 million, below the preview’s estimated $55.0–$56.5 million. The preview also expected a buyback, and the reported $3.2 million of repurchases was the largest cash use, so the shortfall came alongside meaningful capital return.
fact_evidence: “Pixelworks ended Q2 2026 with $53 million in cash and cash equivalents and zero debt”; it “repurchased $3.2 million of common stock during Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Quarter-end cash … My Estimate: $55.0–56.5M.”

description: Gross margin reached 60.9%, slightly above the preview’s estimated 55–60% range.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin improved to 60.9% in Q2 2026 from 56.7% in the prior quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My Estimate: ~55–60%.”

fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $5.1 million”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $5.84M (range ~$5.4–5.9M)” and “Base … Revenue | $5.5–7.0M”

fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin improved to 22.6% in Q2 2026 from 18.1% in Q1”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … my est. 15–19%” and “Sustained ≥18% supports the ‘this is a real business’ narrative”

fact_evidence: “Drone demand from its top five large customers already exceeds 1.5 million cells annually against roughly 700,000-800,000 deliverable capacity, with order visibility into 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “NDAA drone cells convert from samples to purchase orders” and “A hard dollar number for Q2 drone revenue is the swing factor”

fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net loss was $13.1 million ($0.04/share) in Q2, wider than Q1's $11.1 million loss, hurt by lower revenue and a bad debt provision on a legacy EV service contract.”

fact_evidence: “The company was certified by Solark as a battery partner, reducing residential ESS competition from roughly 20 players to about three (alongside Enphase and Tesla), aided by new restrictions on foreign-produced inverters.”

fact_evidence: “R&D expense in the second half of 2026 is expected to double first-half levels and increase again in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “10 ongoing studies across YUTREPIA and L606, including new indications” and Re-Spire’s ramp, but did not state an expectation for this degree of R&D spending growth.

fact_evidence: “Progressively higher YUTREPIA doses at weeks 8, 16, and 24 produced 6-minute walk improvements of 21.5, 31.5, and 41 meters respectively without worsening cough scores.”

expectation_evidence: The preview called the '782 patent litigation “the dominant variable in the equity” and urged questions about the case timeline, but did not mention an imminent 327 ruling.

expectation_evidence: “Product (Symvess) … est. ~$1.0M”; “My Estimate … ~$0.7M (~40 units).”

fact_evidence: “Net loss was $36.8 million in Q2 2026”; the “six-month net loss of $54.4 million compared to net income of $1.5 million a year prior, driven largely by non-cash remeasurement of the contingent earn-out liability.”
expectation_evidence: “Net loss … ~$(23)M.”

expectation_evidence: “R&D … ~$16.5M”; the preview also expected R&D to step down “toward ~$16M.”

fact_evidence: “At least 20 major U.S. healthcare systems are in the process of adopting Symbest in the second half of 2026,” and “a new national account strategy targets access to roughly 1,000 additional hospitals.”

fact_evidence: “The FDA accepted the IND for the CTEV coronary bypass program, with a 10-patient Phase 2a study expected to open this quarter.”

description: SG&A was slightly above the preview’s estimate: $8.0 million versus about $7.0 million, while management characterized it as roughly flat year over year.

fact_evidence: “50% of pemvidutide patients with baseline FIB-4 above 1.3 dropped below 1.3 after just 24 weeks, versus only 17% on placebo.”

expectation_evidence: Q2 FY2026 consensus EPS: “$(0.01)”; bull scenario EPS: “$0.01 – $0.02.”

fact_evidence: “Helly Hansen delivered positive operating profit of roughly $2 million in Q2, its seasonally smallest quarter,” possibly “the first time ever the brand achieved this.”

description: The Lee divestiture comes with about $0.55 per share of stranded or unmitigated costs in addition to $0.90 of lost operating earnings, and Kontoor expects it to take 12–18 months to offset them. description: Kontoor is putting about $25 million of incremental brand-building spending into the updated outlook, an estimated $0.36 per-share drag, rather than allowing all of the gross-margin improvement to flow through to earnings. The preview did not anticipate this investment.
fact_evidence: “The updated outlook incorporates approximately $25 million of incremental brand-building investment (a ~$0.36 EPS drag)” to support growth “for 2027 and beyond.”

description: Wrangler's female business grew 20% in the first half, with Q2 trends accelerating. The preview identified the business as a growth priority and noted it was about 10% of revenue, but gave no expectation of growth at this pace.
fact_evidence: “Wrangler's female business, currently ~10% of total revenue … grew 20% in the first half with accelerating Q2 trends.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called out “the women's business (~10% of Wrangler revenue, a stated growth priority)” but gave no growth-rate expectation.

description: Helly Hansen's China JV revenue grew nearly 70% in Q2, and the brand plans to debut at Dick's House of Sport in 18 doors in October. The preview noted the JV's contribution to prior-quarter pro forma growth and discussed fall/winter orders, but did not anticipate this JV growth rate or the specific retail rollout.
fact_evidence: “Helly Hansen's China JV revenue (excluded from consolidated results) grew nearly 70% in Q2” and “the brand debuts at Dick's House of Sport in 18 doors in October.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 growth was “>20% pro forma with the China JV” and flagged the fall/winter order book, but gave no Q2 JV growth-rate or Dick's rollout expectation.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended Q1 at approximately $116 million, above the preview’s $85–90 million base-case range for the quarter-end balance. The call attributed part of the balance to $20 million from stock-option exercises, an additional cash source not included in the preview’s cash-bridge discussion.
fact_evidence: “Anterix ended the quarter with approximately $116 million in cash and no debt,” bolstered by “$16 million in customer payments and $20 million from stock option exercises.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “cash ~$85–90M”; the preview also framed the FY27 cash bridge around “roughly $30–45M of net cash burn in FY27 absent new signings.”

description: Management forecast at least single-digit-million-dollar broadband license gains in the following quarter, suggesting gains could arrive sooner than the preview’s description of FY27 revenue recognition as heavily back-end loaded into the CPS Energy Q4 delivery. This is a forecast of gains, not a change to the expected Q1 revenue annuity.
fact_evidence: “Management expects at least single-digit-million dollar broadband license gains in the following quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “the entire FY27 revenue ramp to $20.8M consensus is back-end loaded into a single delivery event” and identified “$13M of revenue recognition in Q4 FY2027” on CPS Energy delivery.

description: The call did not provide a newly signed agreement or contracted-proceeds figure, leaving the preview’s central question about whether utility discussions had converted into deals unanswered. Management instead described active opportunities and accelerating conversations, so the facts do not establish that no agreements were signed.
fact_evidence: The call cited “nearly a dozen active utility opportunities” and accelerating conversations, but no newly signed agreement or added contracted-proceeds amount is reported in the call facts.
expectation_evidence: The preview called new agreements and “dollars of contracted proceeds added” the “entire print,” and said the bar was “roughly $25M+” while “zero new agreements would be a genuine problem.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management described nearly a dozen active utility opportunities spanning 7-, 8-, and 9-digit deal sizes, with conversations accelerating over the past two months. That is more specific and more clearly accelerating pipeline commentary than the preview’s base case of constructive pipeline discussion without pricing disclosure, though it is not evidence of signed deals.
fact_evidence: “Nearly a dozen active utility opportunities” span “7-digit, 8-digit, and 9-digit deal sizes,” and “conversations [have been] accelerating over the past two months.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “pipeline commentary constructive but no pricing disclosure,” and cautioned that “the pipeline is strong” was “the price of admission, not a catalyst.”

description: Management did not commit to renewing the expiring buyback authorization, but the CFO said she would not be surprised if it were renewed and kept buybacks in the capital-allocation toolkit. That is a more constructive signal than a quiet lapse, while leaving the actual decision unresolved.
fact_evidence: The “$226 million buyback authorization expires in late September,” and the CFO “would not be surprised if the program is renewed” while keeping buybacks “in the capital allocation toolkit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had to address “renewal, lapse, or use” of the authorization and described renewal as part of its bull scenario.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said 40% of counties had been cleared in the full 10 MHz broadband configuration and expressed confidence it could monetize the entire country. This adds a concrete nationwide-clearing progress measure to the preview’s concern about the pace of 6-to-10 MHz conversion.
fact_evidence: “The company has cleared 40% of counties in the full 10 MHz broadband configuration” and expressed “confidence it can monetize 100% of the country.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any hedging … on 6→10 MHz conversion pace” as a bear-case concern and noted that conversion was “in progress across the 219 exchanged / 155 delivered county base.”

description: The preview estimated Q2 EBITDA of about $1.25 million, but Stran reported $551,000. That was a substantial shortfall despite the quarter remaining profitable.

expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 estimate: … EBITDA ~$1.25M”; the base scenario also estimated “EBITDA ~$1.25M.”

expectation_evidence: The base scenario estimated “SLS $8.8M”; the preview said “Anything ≥$9.5M is a genuine upside surprise.”

expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 estimate: revenue $32.7M (+0.4% YoY)”; the base scenario likewise forecast “$32.7M (+0.4%).”

description: Core Stran grew, but more slowly than the preview’s base estimate: revenue was $23.3 million versus an estimate of about $23.9 million, and growth was 6.9% rather than the forecast 9.6%.
fact_evidence: The Stran segment’s Q2 revenue increased 6.9% to $23.3 million.
expectation_evidence: The base scenario forecast “Core Stran $23.9M (+9.6% YoY).”

expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$18.0M”; the preview also says the “realistic buy-side bar” was “$16.8–17.5M.”

fact_evidence: “Net loss was $1.6 million, or negative $0.05 per share,” versus “$1.1 million, or negative $0.04 per share” a year earlier; “Operating loss widened to $1.6 million from $1.1 million,” primarily due to “higher stock-based compensation within G&A.”

description: PodcastOne reported portfolio additions through acquisitions of named shows and original launches. The preview discussed possible network M&A, but did not anticipate these specific content additions.

expectation_evidence: The preview described “a strong pipeline” of potential network acquisitions and listed M&A as a catalyst, but did not identify these content acquisitions or launches.

description: Q2 revenue was $11.9 million, about 9.8% above the $10.84 million consensus estimate, despite the expected year-over-year decline from the completion of large contracts.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $11.9 million,” down approximately 31% year-over-year.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $10.84M” consensus.

expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated that “H2 recovery [would be] reiterated but not quantified”; the Q1 commitment was for H2 results to “significantly improve.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said “Sub-6% organic at PFG” would “break the share-gain narrative” and listed base-case cases of 6–7%.

expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case called for FY27 EBITDA of “$2.05–2.15B”; its bull case specified FY27 EBITDA “≥$2.15B and sales ≥$71B.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said “Quantified Cheney synergy/cost relief in Q4 and FY27” was needed and that it “needs a number, not adjectives.”

fact_evidence: “LiveOne reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue of $19.3-19.4 million”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue **$21.23M**” and “**~$20.7M**” total in the base case.

expectation_evidence: “**Adj. EBITDA consolidated** … **~$1.2M**” in the base case; the preview also said it expected the first clean positive consolidated quarter.

description: PodcastOne’s $16.1 million of quarterly revenue was below the preview’s roughly $17 million base case and the cited $18.03 million Street estimate, despite being a record. This was a notable contributor to the weaker-than-expected consolidated revenue.
fact_evidence: “PodcastOne delivered record quarterly revenue of $16.1 million”
expectation_evidence: “PodcastOne” base case “**~$17.0M**”; the preview also cited “Street has PODC at **~$18.03M** for Q1.”

That qualifies the apparent EBITDA beat against the preview’s expectation of a genuinely positive consolidated quarter.
fact_evidence: “Slacker's Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $4.7 million was heavily boosted by non-recurring stock-for-service deals and elimination of ~$1.5 million in past liabilities, with management indicating margins will revert to normal levels absent further such deals.”

description: LiveOne disclosed that Amazon represented over $20 million and Paramount more than $27 million in revenues, giving concrete scale to existing partnerships. expectation_evidence: “B2B pipeline converting to dollars” and “A named, dollar-sized contract is the bull catalyst”; the preview said existing opportunities had “not yet been quantified in revenue.”

expectation_evidence: The preview described the B2B opportunities as not yet quantified and said “A named, dollar-sized contract is the bull catalyst.”

fact_evidence: “a podcast-only distribution partnership with Netflix and its 700 million members.”

expectation_evidence: “An actual signed deal would be a genuine narrative unlock”; the preview also warned that another quarter of “imminent” without a deal would be a discount.

fact_evidence: “Management set an aspirational target of over $250 million in revenue within three years, with a nearer-term goal of surpassing $100 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY2027 revenue guidance of “**$85–95M+**” and did not state a longer-term revenue target.

description: The preview said the commercial debate centered on whether bem-rusosvir could compete with generic Epclusa and called for specific payer or pricing evidence. fact_evidence: Management projected peak annual U.S. net revenue potential in excess of $700 million and a total U.S. market potentially expandable up to $2.5 billion annually. Market research found 76% of high-volume DAA prescribers would be extremely likely to prescribe bem-rusosvir, while only 6% of surveyed physicians reported no unmet need in current therapies.
expectation_evidence: “The question is net price against a generic incumbent”; “A credible, specific answer on payer conversations ... is what would begin closing the EV gap.”

expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + marketable securities (6/30): $208–215M” and identified runway “through 2027” as an expected outcome.

fact_evidence: “An NDA submission [is] anticipated in Q2 2027 pending positive results” from C-FORWARD.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “never given an NDA date” and asked whether Atea would file “on C-BEYOND alone, or wait for C-FORWARD”; it called a “2026 filing on C-BEYOND” the most bullish possibility.

expectation_evidence: The preview said Phase 1 initiation was guided for mid-2026 and “proof-of-concept was guided for around year-end.”

expectation_evidence: “Net loss … My estimate: −$2.2M to −$2.4M”

fact_evidence: “R&D expense decreased $0.5 million to $0.9 million in Q2 2026, primarily due to the closeout of the original CARDiAMP heart failure trial.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said “the two niche products haven't landed yet” and noted “No pre-announcement, no in-licensing deal.”

description: Emrosi’s dermatology prescriber count rose to more than 4,500 from 3,700 at the end of Q1. The preview highlighted the prior increase to 3,700 but did not set an expectation for another increase of this size.
fact_evidence: “Unique Emrosi dermatology prescribers grew to over 4,500 ... up from 3,700 at the end of Q1.”

description: QUELIMMUNE revenue was $615,000, about 12% above the preview’s $550,000 point estimate, and year-over-year growth accelerated to 82% versus the modeled roughly 63%. The result remained within the preview’s $420,000–$720,000 range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 QUELIMMUNE net revenue reached $615,000, an 82% year-over-year increase and an acceleration from the 69% growth rate in Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 FY26 QUELIMMUNE net revenue at “$0.55M (range $0.42–$0.72M)” and year-over-year growth at “~+63%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The adult AKI trial was slightly below the preview’s 225-patient progress marker, and management now gives completion timing as around year-end 2026 or in Q1 2027 rather than simply around year-end. Enrollment of 8–12 patients per month is also below management’s new 15–20-per-month target, though more sites are expected to come online.
fact_evidence: “The neutralize AKI adult pivotal trial has enrolled 223 of a targeted 339 patients, with enrollment expected to complete around year-end 2026 or in Q1 2027”; current enrollment is “roughly 8-12 patients per month,” with management targeting “15-20 per month.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “A Q2 number below ~225 puts the YE2026 completion target — and the 2027 PMA — at risk,” and described enrollment completion as “~YE2026.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash at quarter-end was approximately $7 million, above the preview’s expected $6.0–$6.6 million range. The company still reported ongoing cash burn, so the surprise is the higher balance rather than an improvement in the funding outlook.
fact_evidence: “Cash fell to approximately $7 million at June 30, 2026 from $12 million at December 31, 2025, reflecting an ongoing quarterly cash burn.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Cash (period end)” at “$6.0–6.6M.”

description: Operating expenses reached $4.4 million, slightly above the preview’s implied combined R&D and G&A estimate of $3.8–$4.3 million. The increase was driven by trial R&D and higher G&A, although the reported net loss remained within the preview’s forecast range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 operating expenses more than doubled to $4.4 million from $2.1 million a year earlier, driven by increased clinical trial R&D and higher G&A costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated R&D of “$2.2–2.5M” and G&A of “$1.6–1.8M.”

description: Q4 revenue was $2.05 billion, about 3% above the preview’s $1.98–$1.99 billion consensus, and reached the top of company guidance. This was a clear beat, though it was below the preview’s bull scenario of $2.05–$2.10 billion.
fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue was a record $2.05 billion”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~ $1.98–1.99B”; Q4 guidance was “$1.91B – $2.05B.”

description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 exceeded the preview’s working consensus of $1.62 and its stated effective buy-side bar of $1.72, although it was only slightly above that higher bar.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $1.74”
expectation_evidence: “Model against $1.62 as the working number and $1.72 (guide high) as the effective buy-side bar.”

description: The data center and communications segment appears to have delivered about $1.62 billion of Q4 revenue—79% of the $2.05 billion total—versus the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion estimate. The data center business also grew 56% year over year and 24% sequentially, stronger than the preview’s expected roughly 10% sequential increase for the segment.
fact_evidence: “The data center and communications segment, 79% of Q4 revenue, grew 59% year-over-year”; “the data center business alone [was] up 56% year-over-year and 24% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Datacenter & Comms revenue: ~$1.50B”; “Another ~10% sequential step puts it at ~$1.50B.”

description: The Q1 FY27 revenue outlook was stronger than the preview’s roughly $2.15 billion reference point: the range is $2.2–$2.4 billion, with a $2.3 billion midpoint. The range clears the preview’s $2.25 billion bull-case threshold at its midpoint, though not at its low end.
fact_evidence: “Management guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $2.2–$2.4 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue guide vs. ~$2.15B”; “>$2.25B validates the street’s $9.66B FY27.”

description: Management added a target to reach its first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of FY27, a stronger stated exit-rate ambition than the preview’s discussion of FY27 growth exceeding FY26 and its $9.66 billion full-year model.
fact_evidence: “Expects to reach its first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Sell-side FY2027 modeling sits at $9.66B revenue (+36.9%)”; management had said FY27 growth would “exceed” FY26’s roughly 21%.

description: Management expects data center revenue growth to exceed 80% year over year in the current quarter, a particularly strong near-term growth rate not specified in the preview’s Q1 expectations.
fact_evidence: “Management expects data center revenue growth to exceed 80% year-over-year in the current quarter.”

description: Q4 capex reached $556 million, well above the preview’s $350–$400 million quarterly step-up framework. The stated roughly 18-month payback on data center investments helps explain the spending, but the outlay is still substantially larger than the preview contemplated.
fact_evidence: “Q4 capital expenditures surged to $556 million (from $131 million a year ago) with a roughly 18-month payback on data center investments.”
expectation_evidence: “A capex step to $350–400M/qtr is demand confirmation but pressures FCF.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview anticipated leverage of 0.5x, while management reported 0.7x, modestly above that expected level despite substantial debt payments.
fact_evidence: “Debt leverage was cut to 0.7x from 2.0x a year earlier via $513 million in debt payments.”
expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet supports either: ~$3B cash post-NVIDIA, leverage down to 0.5x from 2.1x a year ago.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management outlined additional product ramps, including ultra-high-power CW lasers beginning in the December quarter and ThermaDit thermal management in the second half of calendar 2027; these specific revenue streams were not in the preview’s roadmap discussion.
fact_evidence: “New revenue streams are set to ramp, including ... ultra high-power CW lasers beginning in the December quarter ... and thermal management (ThermaDit) in the second half of calendar 2027.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was only about $243,000, well below the preview’s roughly $600,000 floor for keeping the FY26 target math credible and the $500,000–$900,000 base-case range. First-half adjusted EBITDA was a loss of about $224,000, making the preview’s expectation of year-over-year improvement in Q2 and its FY26 ambition materially harder to achieve.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to about $243,000 in Q2 2026 from roughly $628,000 a year earlier, and first-half adjusted EBITDA was a loss of about $224,000.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything below ~$0.6M in Q2 puts the ‘surpass $2.9M’ ambition mathematically under strain”; the base case expected “$0.5–0.9M” of adjusted EBITDA.

description: GAAP results were worse than the preview’s EPS estimate: DLPN reported a $0.13 loss per share versus an expected $0.07 loss. Net loss also widened year over year to $1.6 million from $1.4 million, rather than showing the improvement implied by consensus.
fact_evidence: “Loss per share was $0.13 in Q2 2026 on ~12.8 million weighted average shares, up from ~11.2 million shares a year earlier”; “net loss of $1.6 million versus $1.4 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS | $(0.07)” versus Q2’25 actual “$(0.12)” and described as “improving.”

description: The quarter included roughly $720,000–$800,000 in retention bonuses and litigation-related legal fees that the preview had not anticipated. Management said both costs are expected to roll off in Q3, so the reported burden is unusually high but temporary.
fact_evidence: “Approximately $360,000-$400,000 of one-time retention bonuses and another ~$360,000-$400,000 of litigation-related legal fees, both expected to roll off in Q3.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash was $7.7 million at June 30, above the $6.3 million reported at March 31 and therefore a build over the quarter, despite being below the $8.8 million year-end balance. That is better than the preview’s cash-draw concern and matches its stated positive signal for cash generation.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents declined to $7.7 million as of June 30, 2026, from $8.8 million at year-end 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash at 6/30/26 vs. $6.3M at 3/31/26 — direction of travel matters more than the level: a build supports the FCF claim, a draw revives the raise risk.”

description: Management identified an additional roughly $1 million of annual savings when the New York and Los Angeles leases roll off late next year, a source of future free-cash-flow improvement that the preview did not flag. The preview had already noted the expected $2.2 million annual debt-service savings, so that portion is not new.
fact_evidence: “Management expects meaningfully improved free cash flow from bank debt maturing in about two years (freeing ~$2.2 million annually in principal and interest) and NY/LA leases rolling off in late next year (saving ~$1 million annually).”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “payoff saves $2.2M/yr in principal and interest,” but did not mention savings from the NY/LA leases.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Management highlighted approximately $127 million in NOLs, saying they would let nearly all future cost savings flow directly to the bottom line. The preview did not discuss this potential tax benefit.
fact_evidence: “The company holds approximately $127 million in NOLs, allowing nearly all future cost savings to flow directly to the bottom line.”

description: The CEO said he expects to own more than 5% of DLPN within a week or two under his 10b5-1 buying plan, a stronger ownership signal than the preview’s description of small, immaterial regular purchases.
fact_evidence: “CEO Bill O'Dowd expects to own over 5% of DLPN common stock within the next week or two under his 10b5-1 buying plan, signaling insider alignment.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described recent purchases as “small, regular open-market blocks” and said “the dollar amounts are immaterial.”

description: Beyond the expected first DealMaker venture deal before year-end, management said it had identified two candidates and aspired to complete three to four capital-light equity-plus-fee ventures annually within a few years. That adds pipeline detail and a longer-term scale ambition not stated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company expects its first Dealmaker venture deal in market before year-end, with two candidates identified and an aspiration to complete 3-4 capital-light equity-plus-fee ventures annually within a few years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management “targeted a first deal announcement by YE2026” and described an “~six-figure annual marketing fee per deal.”

description: GO reported adjusted EBITDA of $65.7 million and adjusted EPS of $0.20, well above the preview’s roughly $56 million and $0.12 consensus estimates and above company outlook. The earnings beat was substantially larger than the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $65.7 million” and “adjusted EPS was $0.20, both above outlook.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$56M” and “Diluted adj. EPS $0.12”; company outlook was “$55–58M” EBITDA and “$0.11–$0.13” EPS.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comparable sales fell just 0.3%, far better than the preview’s roughly 1.5% decline expectation and the company’s 1.5%–2.0% decline outlook. The decline also improved 70 basis points sequentially.
fact_evidence: “Comparable store sales down 30 basis points, a 70bp sequential improvement from Q1 and beating the outlook for a 1.5%-2% decline.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 comps were expected at “~−1.5%” with company guidance of “−1.5% to −2.0%”; the preview’s functional bar was “comps no worse than −1.5%.”

description: GO raised the low end of its full-year outlook, including comps from −2.0% to −0.5%, and lifted the low end of EBITDA guidance from $220 million to $225 million. This was stronger than the preview’s central concern that the existing FY26 range might only be reaffirmed or trimmed.
fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full-year guidance to comps of -0.5% to 0.0%, net sales of $4.7-$4.72 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $225-$235 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.51-$0.55.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY guidance of “−2.0% to 0.0%” comps and “$220–235M” adjusted EBITDA, and flagged whether it would be “reaffirmed vs. trimmed.”

description: Revenue reached $1.19 billion, about $23 million above the preview’s $1.167 billion consensus, and grew 1% rather than declining year over year as expected. This was a clear top-line beat alongside the stronger comps.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 1% to $1.19 billion.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 net sales consensus was “$1,167M”; the preview listed Q2 FY25 sales of “$1,180M” and expected “−1.1%” year-over-year.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The opportunistic assortment gained momentum faster than the preview’s turnaround test required: its comps accelerated about 500 basis points from Q1’s start, and total company comps turned positive in May and June. The preview identified rebuilding opportunistic units per transaction as a key condition for recovery.
fact_evidence: “Opportunistic comp sales accelerated about 500bp from the start of Q1 and op mix expanded over 300bp, lifting total company comps into positive territory in May and June.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required “units-per-transaction to stop deteriorating” through “the opportunistic branded closeout assortment genuinely rebuilding.”

description: Gross margin was 30.2%, above the preview’s 29.8%–30.0% outlook range, and its year-over-year decline was only 30 basis points rather than the roughly 70-basis-point contraction expected. Promotions and closure markdowns still weighed on the year-over-year result.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin of 30.2% exceeded the 29.8%-30.0% outlook but declined 30bp year-over-year due to promotions and store-closure markdowns.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “29.8%–30.0%” and expected gross margin down “~−70bp YoY.”

description: The preview expected the closed-store savings to be visible in Q2, but the call said most of the $12 million annualized EBITDA benefit from the 36 closures is expected in 2027. The closures remain on track, but the timing of most of the benefit is later than the preview suggested.
fact_evidence: “The closure of 36 underperforming stores completed in April remains on track to eliminate a $12 million annualized adjusted EBITDA drag, with most benefit expected in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the closures were completed by April, cited the “~$12M annualized EBITDA benefit,” and said “Q2 is the first quarter where it should be visible in SG&A and four-wall margin.”

description: A multi-state cyclospora outbreak is expected to reduce Q3 company comps by about 100 basis points, an unanticipated headwind for the quarter the preview identified as the most important guidance issue. The company said its products were not involved in any recalls.
fact_evidence: “A multi-state cyclospora outbreak is expected to create a roughly 100bp headwind to total company comps in Q3, though products were not involved in any recalls.”

description: Yartemlia net sales reached $28.5 million in its first full quarter, far above the preview’s $15.5 million base case and even its $18–21 million bull range. Sequential net sales growth of 188% also substantially exceeded the preview’s roughly $12–13 million “no-acceleration” benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026, its first full quarter on the market,” generated “$28.5 million in net sales”; “net sales grew 188%” quarter over quarter.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s “My base case” was “$15.5M”; its bull scenario was “$18–21M,” and it called roughly “$12–13M” the “no-acceleration” number.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The launch reached 73 ordering accounts by June 30, well above the preview’s 50-plus account level that it said would feel good. P&T approval had also reached roughly 55–60% across tracked top-center cohorts, supporting strong breadth of adoption.
fact_evidence: “73 unique accounts had ordered Yartemlia (up 143.5% since March 31),” with P&T committee approval at “roughly 55-60% across tracked top transplant center cohorts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “I’d want 50+ to feel good,” compared with 30 unique ordering accounts at Q1 exit.

description: The company reported $1.8 million of adjusted net income, or $0.02 per share, rather than the adjusted loss the preview expected. The reported $13.2 million GAAP profit was partly a $12.1 million non-cash derivative gain, but the adjusted result was still positive.
fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net income was $13.2 million ($0.18/share), but non-GAAP adjusted net income was only $1.8 million ($0.02/share) after excluding a $12.1 million non-cash mark-to-market derivative gain.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s adjusted EPS “My base case” was “–$0.20”; it also said a second large non-cash gain and headline GAAP profit were likely, while cautioning not to read that as an operating beat.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Company-wide operations generated positive cash flow in Q2, much earlier than the preview’s expected timeline for company-wide breakeven. The mid-2027 target itself is broadly consistent with the preview’s expected Q3 2027 timing.
fact_evidence: “Company-wide operations generated $4.1 million of positive cash flow in Q2,” supporting guidance to reach company-wide cash flow positivity “by mid-2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management targeted “company-wide positive cash flow within 18 months (~Q3 2027)” and expected $115–125 million of cash at June 30.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and investments ended Q2 at $132 million, above the preview’s expected $115–125 million range. This is a positive cash-position surprise separate from the quarter’s positive operating cash flow.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $132 million in cash and investments.”
expectation_evidence: “I’d expect ~$115–125M cash at June 30.”

description: Omeros disclosed a substantial July repurchase of its 9.5% 2029 convertible notes, reducing principal outstanding by 43% and eliminating future interest expense. The preview discussed the notes and earlier capital actions but did not anticipate this transaction.
fact_evidence: “In July, Omeros repurchased $30.5 million of its 9.5% 2029 convertible notes for $60.2 million,” cutting outstanding principal “43% to $40.3 million,” eliminating “$8.6 million in future interest,” and reducing conversion shares from 11.4 million to 6.5 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview described the 2029 notes as having “$70.8M principal” and discussed retiring the 2026 converts and buying back shares, but did not forecast a 2029-note repurchase.
