Faster adult growth is favorable to the adult launch, but the much smaller pediatric share makes the current mix less favorable to pediatric-market expectations.
fact_evidence: “Adult utilization grew at more than twice the rate of pediatric utilization, with adults now representing approximately 95% of Yartemlia sales,” approaching the historical “85%/15% adult-pediatric split.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted Omeros “already sees a higher-than-expected pediatric mix vs. the historical 85/15 adult-pediatric split.”

description: The preview’s base case anticipated advanced discussions with multiple parties and a term sheet expected before the October 30 deadline. Instead, Spruce reported no committed refinancing arrangements at quarter end and only preliminary lender discussions for SP1, leaving the debt maturities unresolved.
fact_evidence: “No committed refinancing arrangements were in place at quarter end”; “only preliminary lender discussions underway for SP1.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “advanced discussions with multiple parties, term sheet expected before Oct 30.”

description: Revenue was $30.3 million, below the preview’s $31.5 million estimate, and fell 9% year over year rather than the preview’s modeled 5% decline. The call attributed the weakness partly to lower SP5 SREC production and a slower-than-expected Spruce Pro revenue ramp.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 9% year-over-year to $30.3 million”; drivers included “lower SP5 SREC production” and “a slower-than-expected Spruce Pro revenue ramp.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue of “$31.5M” and a “-5%” year-over-year change.

description: Operating EBITDA reached $26.5 million, exceeding the preview’s $24.0 million estimate and the $23–25 million base-case range. This was stronger than the preview’s expected solid but broadly in-line operating quarter.
fact_evidence: “Operating EBITDA rose to $26.5 million from $24.6 million a year earlier”; core operating expenses fell 21% to $13.8 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Operating EBITDA $24.0M” and gave a base-case range of “$23–25M.”

description: Spruce reported net income of $3.3 million, or $0.14 per diluted share, instead of the preview’s expected $3.5 million net loss and $0.19 loss per share. The call said favorable non-cash interest-rate-swap valuation changes partly aided the reversal, consistent with the preview’s warning that EPS could be affected by swap marks.
fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to stockholders of $3.3 million ($0.14 per diluted share)”; results were “partly aided by favorable non-cash interest rate swap valuation changes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss attrib. to stockholders -$3.5M” and “EPS -$0.19.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Unrestricted cash ended the quarter at $44.7 million, below the preview’s expected $46–50 million range. It remained above the preview’s roughly $42 million level identified as a particularly concerning cash threshold.
fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$81.5 million in total cash (including $44.7 million unrestricted).”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Unrestricted cash $46–50M” and said cash below “~$42M” would compress the runway meaningfully.

description: SKYX reported Q2 revenue of $25.3 million, about 5% above the published $24.07 million consensus, though slightly below the preview’s ~$25.4 million whisper estimate. That makes the result a modest beat against published consensus, not a clear beat against the broader expected range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% sequentially to a record $25.3 million, up 10% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $24.07M (Investing.com)” and “Treat $24–25.4M as the real goalpost band.”

description: Gross margin fell to 29%, below the preview’s roughly 30% expectation, as sales mix held back gross profit growth despite revenue growth. Management expects higher-margin products and B2B supply to help in the back half, but the current-quarter margin result was weaker than expected.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 29% in Q2 2026 from 30% in Q1, with only 4% year-over-year gross profit growth to $7.3 million, lagging revenue growth as sales mix weighed on margins.” Management said higher-margin products are expected to improve margins in the back half.
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~30% (no formal consensus)” and “Gross margin vs. the 30% line.”

description: The announced B2B pipeline has not yet produced meaningful revenue: project shipments are only beginning this quarter and are expected to continue into later periods. The preview sought evidence of B2B conversion, including shipped-unit figures, so the lack of quantified current contribution leaves that conversion less established than a bullish outcome would have implied.
fact_evidence: “B2B project shipments are only beginning this quarter and will continue into Q4, Q1, and 2027, meaning meaningful revenue from the announced pipeline remains largely ahead.”
expectation_evidence: “B2B conversion — does the pipeline show up as revenue?” and “A specific number is bullish; another qualitative list is not.”

description: Gen 3 appears less certain and potentially later than the preview’s expectation that production would be landing around mid-to-third quarter. Production samples are testing well, but mass production still depends on regulatory approvals and management gave only a hoped-for next-quarter launch, without a firm timeline.
fact_evidence: “The Gen 3 monitoring product has working production samples testing well but remains dependent on FCC and other regulatory code approvals before mass production, with no firm timeline beyond a hoped-for next-quarter launch.”
expectation_evidence: “Guided to ‘mid-to-third quarter 2026’ production — meaning it should be landing now.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: KOMZIFTI recorded 115 new patient starts, above the preview’s 95–110 base-case range and its 100+ threshold for meaningful demand. That suggests a stronger quarter of new-patient demand than the preview’s base case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 115 new patient starts”; new patient starts grew “about 35% quarter-over-quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “New patient starts” base case of “95–110”; the preview said “100+ starts into a soft class quarter” would be genuine share capture.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix

This is a favorable resolution of the preview’s debate about Kura’s share relative to Syndax’s broader market-share claim.
fact_evidence: KOMZIFTI was “capturing a majority share of new patient starts” in the relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML menin inhibitor market.
expectation_evidence: “Kura claimed ~40% share of R/R NPM1 new starts in Q1” and “Tonight’s new-start number adjudicates it.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Prescription growth outpaced new-start growth, and management said the results were not driven by inventory or one-time stocking. That is stronger evidence of ongoing use than a quarter whose sales were boosted by channel fill, and addresses a central concern in the preview.
fact_evidence: “New patient starts grew about 35% quarter-over-quarter while total prescriptions grew about 60%,” with “no meaningful inventory or one-time stocking effects.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether Q1 was “a stocking-and-switching pop or a real launch curve” and called a “rising scripts-per-start ratio” the “single most bullish quiet datapoint.”

description: KOMZIFTI had preferred status requiring step-through before other menin inhibitors for approximately 16 million covered lives, while more than 95% of covered lives had no label restrictions. The preview did not flag this access position, so it adds a favorable commercial detail beyond the launch metrics it highlighted.
fact_evidence: “Over 95% of covered lives” had “no label restrictions,” and “approximately 16 million lives carry preferred status requiring patients to step through KOMZIFTI before other menin inhibitors.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Komet-007 data showed high response and survival figures, including 94% overall survival at 12 months and median overall survival not reached after 17.6 months. The preview did not identify this data as an expected catalyst or provide an efficacy benchmark for it.
fact_evidence: In 99 patients, “96% ORR” was reported in relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML, with “94% overall survival at 12 months” and “median OS not reached at 17.6 months follow-up,” versus historical 12-month OS of “45%-80%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Darlifarnib showed a 44% response rate in cabozantinib-exposed RCC, compared with the 17%–22% historical range cited on the call, and reported 33%–50% ORR with 13-month median PFS in cabo-naive RCC. The preview mentioned pending KCRS RCC data but did not set expectations for these efficacy results.
fact_evidence: Darlifarnib demonstrated a “44% objective response rate and 94% disease control rate in cabozantinib-exposed RCC (versus 17%-22% historical),” and “33%-50% ORR with 13-month median PFS in cabo-naive RCC.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any darlifarnib (KO-2806) development decision after the July 24 KCRS RCC data,” without giving an expected efficacy result.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: About 40% of new patient starts involved physician-initiated combinations with venetoclax/azacitidine or FLT3 inhibitors, despite promotion being limited to the approved monotherapy indication. The preview mentioned combination use as a possible bull-case signal but did not anticipate this level of physician-initiated use.
fact_evidence: “Physician-initiated combination use with venetoclax/azacitidine and FLT3 inhibitors represented approximately 40% of new patient starts,” while the drug is “only promoted for its approved monotherapy indication.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario listed “combination use >40%.”

description: The reported net loss was substantially below the preview author’s $77 million estimate, with both R&D and SG&A also below that preview’s estimates. This was a better expense result than expected, even though the loss still widened from a year earlier.
fact_evidence: Net loss was “$68.3 million,” versus $77 million in the preview estimate; SG&A was “$31.8 million” versus the preview’s $33 million estimate, and R&D was “$61.9 million” versus its $67 million estimate.
expectation_evidence: Preview estimate: “Net loss” $77M, “R&D” $67M, and “SG&A” $33M.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management cited data suggesting that up to half of AML patients may be responsive to menin inhibition based on MEIS1 expression. The preview discussed category expansion but did not flag this biomarker-based estimate.
fact_evidence: Management cited “data suggesting up to 50% of AML patients may be responsive to menin inhibition via MEIS1 expression.”

description: Revenue was $278 million, about $9 million above the preview’s $268.6 million consensus estimate and above its $270 million base case, although it still declined year over year because of restaurant closures. The result was near the top of the preview’s $274–278 million bull scenario.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue fell $6.1 million to $278 million, primarily due to restaurant closures partially offset by higher comp sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q2 FY26 Consensus $268.6M”; “My Base Est. $270M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was well below the preview’s roughly $21–22 million expectation, at $18.9 million. The preview anticipated higher marketing spend, but the reported $4 million increase in marketing behind Big Yum was associated with a larger EBITDA shortfall than its base case implied.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined $3.5 million year-over-year to $18.9 million, driven mainly by a $4 million increase in marketing spend behind the Big Yum value platform.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$21–22M (implied)”; “My Base Est. $22.5M.”

description: Management kept the $70–73 million full-year EBITDA guidance rather than updating or rebasing it after the refranchising deals, as the preview expected it might. The guidance explicitly excludes the transactions’ impact, so it does not provide the pro-forma EBITDA bridge the preview identified as the central issue.
fact_evidence: “The company maintained full-year 2026 guidance … adjusted EBITDA of $70–73 million … excluding any impact from the re-franchising transactions.”
expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly said it ‘expects to update guidance following the close of these transactions’”; the preview’s base case expected guidance to be “re-based to $58–65M.”

description: Restaurant-level margin rose to 14.7%, beating the preview’s 14.3% base case and its expectation of a flat-to-down result despite labor efficiencies beginning to lap and marketing spending rising. That was a better margin outcome than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level operating margin rose 20 basis points year-over-year to 14.7%, the highest second-quarter margin in four years.”
expectation_evidence: “Restaurant-level op. margin … My Base Est. 14.3%”; “Flat-to-down 30bps is the honest base case.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comps grew 1.3%, above the preview’s +0.8% base estimate and the roughly +1% threshold it said was needed to support the full-year comparable-sales guide. The preview’s scenario range included stronger results, but this exceeded its base case.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 same-store sales grew 1.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Comps … My Base Est. +0.8%”; “Q2 needs roughly +1% or better.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Traffic was down slightly rather than turning positive, but its 20-basis-point decline was better than the preview’s -0.5% base estimate and it outperformed the industry. This was an improvement over expectations, though it did not deliver the positive-traffic proof point the preview highlighted.
fact_evidence: “Traffic effectively flat (down 20 basis points) but outperforming the industry by 40 basis points, marking the best traffic performance since Q1 2023.”
expectation_evidence: “Traffic … My Base Est. −0.5%”; the preview said to “watch for the first positive traffic quarter in years.”

description: Management expected Q4 to outperform Q3 even though the preview highlighted tougher Big Yum comparisons in the back half. The forecast that commodity inflation would ease from about 5% to roughly 3% also provided a favorable cost outlook not quantified in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Management expects Q4 to outperform Q3 as tougher Big Yum comparisons hit the back half, with commodity inflation moderating from about 5% in the first half to roughly 3% in the second half as beef and poultry costs ease.”
expectation_evidence: “The risk is … Big Yummm comparisons hit back half”; the preview said full-year comps would require “~1.5% averaged across 2H.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The 3.3% price increase was materially higher than the preview’s estimate that pricing was running at about 1%. However, Big Yum mix and discounts reduced average-check growth to 1.5%, so the stronger pricing did not translate into equally strong check growth.
fact_evidence: “Average check rose 1.5%, consisting of a 3.3% price increase offset by a 1.8% decline in mix and discounts from Big Yum value offerings.”
expectation_evidence: “Pricing is now only ~+1%”; the preview also noted that “high value mix is good for traffic and bad for check.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CVV booked only about $1.2 million of orders and ended the quarter with $3.9 million of backlog, below the preview’s $1.5–2.5 million order and $4.0–5.5 million backlog ranges. The backlog also slipped below the preview’s $4 million downside threshold.
fact_evidence: “Orders during Q2 2026 totaled only about $1.2 million and backlog fell to $3.9 million as of June 30, 2026, reflecting persistent demand weakness.”
expectation_evidence: “Orders $1.5–2.5M”; “Backlog (period end) $4.0–5.5M”; and “<$1.5M of spares-only orders with backlog under $4M = thesis break.”

description: Gross margin reached 16.8%, above the preview’s 10–14% estimate despite continuing-operations revenue of about $2 million. The preview had highlighted weak fixed-cost absorption as a risk; the reported margin improvement instead came from a higher share of higher-margin nonsystem revenue.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 16.8% from 14.1% year-over-year, driven by a higher proportion of higher-margin nonsystem (consumables and spare parts) revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … Q2 2026E 10–14%”; the preview said to watch whether margin could return “toward the high teens even on ~$2M revenue.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The SDC divestiture gain was larger than the preview’s estimate: the call reported an approximately $13.5 million gain, versus the preview’s estimate in the mid-to-high single-digit millions. The preview expected headline net income to be positive, but not a gain of this size.
fact_evidence: “Total gain on divestiture of approximately $13.5 million” and “net income from discontinued operations of $13.9 million for the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “The pre-tax book gain plausibly lands in the mid-to-high single-digit millions”; headline GAAP net income was expected to be “positive.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: A customer responsible for a $0.8 million system order filed for Chapter 11 after quarter-end, putting that order and backlog at risk. The preview anticipated weak demand but did not flag a bankruptcy risk to a newly booked order.
fact_evidence: “The customer behind the $0.8 million system order received in Q2 filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy after quarter-end, putting that order and backlog at potential risk.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: CVV ended the quarter with $23.5 million in cash, above the preview’s $21.5–22.5 million estimate. The difference is modest, but it leaves the reported cash balance higher than modeled.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with approximately $23.5 million in cash and cash equivalents.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash & investments … Q2 2026E ~$21.5–22.5M.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management described the PVT/silicon-carbide market as saturated and reported no commercial engagement, a more adverse update than the preview’s description of a customer in a waiting pattern amid Chinese wafer oversupply.
fact_evidence: “Management sees the PVT/silicon carbide boule market as saturated by Chinese, onsemi, Wolfspeed, and Coherent suppliers with no commercial engagement to report.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “PVT200 customer still ‘in a waiting pattern’ on U.S. SiC wafer weakness / Chinese wafer oversupply.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Aerospace CMC tools were still being installed and commissioned, with follow-on orders only a future possibility. That provides less near-term commercial progress than the preview’s identification of aerospace and defense as a near-term hope.
fact_evidence: “Aerospace CMC tools remain in installation and commissioning phases before any potential follow-on orders.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “aerospace & defense” among the near-term hopes.

description: Crown Crafts reported $0.19 per share of net income instead of the preview’s modeled $0.08 per-share loss. The result was boosted by a much larger-than-expected tariff refund: $3.7 million reduced cost of products sold, and about $4.7 million of the requested refunds had been received, versus only $175,000 reported received in the preview.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net income of $2.1 million ($0.19 per share), reversing a prior-year loss of $1.1 million ($0.10 per share), though results benefited from tariff-related adjustments”; “Tariff refunds reduced cost of products sold by $3.7 million during the quarter, with about $4.7 million of a requested $5.6-5.7 million already received, mostly in July.”
expectation_evidence: The model estimated “Net income (loss) … ($0.8M)” and “Diluted EPS … ($0.08).” The preview also said the company had “applied for $5.5M in tariff refunds and received only $175K to date.”

description: Net sales were $16.8 million, up 8% year over year, well ahead of the preview’s $15.7 million estimate and +1.3% growth model. This was a sharper sales improvement than expected despite still-soft consumer demand.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 net sales grew 8% year-over-year to $16.8 million, driven primarily by improved inventory levels amid still-soft consumer demand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net sales … $15.7M” and “Y/Y +1.3%”; it described stabilization on an easy comparison as the base case.

description: Adjusted gross margin reached 25.6%, 160 basis points above the preview’s 24.0% estimate. The preview treated a margin above 26% as the stronger upside case, so the reported result materially exceeded its base expectation while stopping short of that threshold.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 290 basis points year-over-year to 25.6%, reflecting strategic pricing and a favorable shift toward higher-margin products.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin of “24.0%” and said “Above 26% and the leverage story is real.”

description: The Board cut the quarterly dividend rather than maintaining the preview’s expected $0.08 payment. The resulting yield is approximately 4%, down from the preview’s stated approximately 10.7%, as the company redirected cash toward debt reduction and growth initiatives.
fact_evidence: “The Board cut the quarterly dividend to free up cash flow for debt reduction and growth initiatives, now offering an approximately 4% dividend yield.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “dividend maintained at $0.08”; it also highlighted the dividend declaration as a key issue and noted the existing approximately 10.7% yield.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Groovy Girls relaunch performed better than the preview’s cautious first-year framing: Canadian demand was strong enough that U.S.-bound inventory is being redirected to Canada. The preview characterized the opportunity as low-seven-figures at best in year one and emphasized that sell-through and reorders were the key unknowns.
fact_evidence: “The relaunched Groovy Girls fashion doll line exceeded expectations, with such strong Canadian demand that U.S.-bound inventory is being diverted to Canada.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “a low-seven-figures-at-best annual opportunity in year one” and said “The real datapoint is sell-through and reorder commentary, not the sell-in dollars.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Debt fell to $9.6 million by quarter-end from more than $14 million at the start of the fiscal year, with $5.5 million of operating cash flow supporting the reduction. The preview cited $14.1 million of debt at FY2026 year-end and flagged debt and inventory as items to watch, but did not anticipate this much additional reduction in Q1.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced debt from over $14 million at the start of the fiscal year to $9.6 million at quarter-end, supported by $5.5 million in operating cash flow.”

description: Normalized marketing and administrative expense improved to 28% of sales, better than the preview’s estimate of roughly flat dollar expense against its sales forecast, which implied a higher share of sales. The improvement was reported despite more than $500,000 of tariff-related incentive accruals.
fact_evidence: “Normalized marketing and administrative expense improved to 28% of net sales versus 30.5% a year earlier, despite the quarter including over $500,000 of tariff-related incentive accruals.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated marketing and administrative expense of “$4.65M” versus “$4.7M” a year earlier and described the base case as “opex flat.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Allogene had already activated more than 80 Alpha-3 sites in July and now expects about 100 by year-end, above the preview’s expectation of expanding to 80+ globally. The call also identified Canada, Australia, and South Korea among the countries with sites.
fact_evidence: “Reached its year-end goal of activating over 80 Alpha-3 clinical sites in July” and “now expects approximately 100 active sites by year-end,” with sites in Canada, Australia, and South Korea.
expectation_evidence: “60+ North American sites expanding to 80+ globally.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call disclosed a 31% confirmed response rate for the optimized ALLO-316 regimen in CD70-high renal cancer, with all five confirmed responders still progression-free at follow-up. The preview flagged ALLO-316’s strategic disposition but did not anticipate this clinical update.
fact_evidence: “The optimized regimen produced a 31% confirmed overall response rate in CD70-high renal cell carcinoma,” and none of the five confirmed responders had progressed at follow-up of 8 to over 18 months after one dose.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Alpha-3 showed rapid MRD clearance in a majority of patients, and treatment was largely delivered as outpatient care, including at community practices without prior CAR-T experience. The preview focused on enrollment, regulatory pathway, and site expansion rather than these efficacy and delivery details.
fact_evidence: The interim futility analysis showed “rapid MRD clearance in a majority of patients with no treatment-related hospitalizations,” with most patients treated and followed entirely outpatient, including in community practices with no prior CAR-T experience.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management disclosed that statistical significance at Alpha-3’s interim EFS analysis will require overwhelming efficacy because of the alpha allocation between interim and primary analyses. The preview highlighted the interim readout as a catalyst but did not flag this higher statistical bar.
fact_evidence: “Achieving statistical significance at the interim EFS analysis will require overwhelming efficacy due to how alpha was allocated between the interim and primary analyses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the interim EFS analysis as “mid-2027” and identified enrollment progress as “the single most valuable disclosure,” without noting this statistical hurdle.

description: The call gave a 220-patient randomization target but no current screened, enrolled, or randomized patient count. That leaves the enrollment-funnel quantification the preview called its highest-priority disclosure unresolved.
fact_evidence: Alpha-3 “targets 220 patients randomized into two arms,” but the call facts provided no current patient enrollment or screening count.
expectation_evidence: “Any quantification — patients screened, MRD+ rate, patients randomized — is the single most valuable disclosure.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The ALLO-329 update is stated in the call facts as Q4 2025, while the preview expected Q4 2026. Taken literally, that would be substantially earlier, although the stated 2025 date is inconsistent with the August 2026 release date.
fact_evidence: “The ALLO-329 RESOLUTION autoimmune trial will report a clinical and translational data update in Q4 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Next update guided to Q4 2026” and “ALLO-329 stays Q4.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management argued that ongoing first-line CAR-T and bispecific studies should have minimal effect on post-frontline MRD positivity, and that in-vivo CAR-T is likely confined to replacing autologous CAR-T in relapsed/refractory disease. This was a reassuring defense of Alpha-3’s niche that the preview had not anticipated.
fact_evidence: Management expects first-line CAR-T and bispecific studies to have “minimal impact on post-frontline MRD positivity rates” and views in-vivo CAR-T as likely limited to relapsed/refractory settings, leaving Alpha-3’s community-based niche “well protected.”

description: Usio raised FY2026 revenue growth guidance to 14%–16%, above the preview’s expected 10%–12% reiteration and even the preview’s bull-case 12%–14% range. The higher range is a substantial positive change to the outlook.
fact_evidence: “Usio raised full-year fiscal 2026 revenue growth guidance to 14%-16%, up substantially from prior guidance of 10%-12%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance raised to 12–14%” in the bull case; the base case expected “guide reiterated at 10–12%.”

description: Gross margin was 24%, above the preview’s buy-side estimate of roughly 22%–23%, while also landing within management’s previously stated 23%–25% near-term target. That is a better margin recovery than the preview’s base case expected.
fact_evidence: Management said gross margins were “24% this quarter” and targeted “23%-25% near term.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~22–23% (buy-side)” and the base case expected “22.0–23.0%.”

description: PayFac growth was much faster than the preview’s expectation that PayFac was growing “20%+”: revenue surged 43%, with merchant count up 34% in the first six months. Total card revenue growth of 28% was broadly in line, but the PayFac engine was notably stronger.
fact_evidence: “PayFac business where revenue surged 43% and merchant count grew 34% in the first six months”; “Card revenue rose 28%.”
expectation_evidence: “PayFac now 78% of card revenue growing 20%+.”

description: Output Solutions grew 22% year over year, above the preview’s modeled 16%–18% growth despite the expected seasonal unwind after Q1. Pieces mailed rose 43%, and the new printer is roughly four times faster and more cost-effective, adding an operational improvement not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Output Solutions revenue increased 22% (accelerating from 19% in Q1), with pieces mailed up 43% and a new high-speed printer that is roughly 4x faster and more cost-effective.”
expectation_evidence: The segment build modeled Output Solutions at “+16–18% (Q1 tax seasonality unwinds).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: School-voucher programs expanded beyond the preview’s two-state, up-to-$1 billion framing to five or six states and estimated volumes around $1.5 billion. However, initial disbursements are mostly using lower-margin ACH rather than delivering the stronger card-issuing mix the preview was watching for, making the development mixed.
fact_evidence: “School voucher programs expanded from 2 to 5-6 states with estimated total volumes around $1.5 billion, though initial disbursements are flowing mostly through lower-margin ACH.”
expectation_evidence: Management had flagged “up to $1B in school-choice voucher distributions across two states” flowing through “card issuing + ACH”; the preview wanted “dollars and timing” on that volume.

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.1 million, above the preview’s $0.7–$0.9 million estimate, and first-half adjusted EBITDA was described as the best in years. This was a stronger profitability result than the preview’s base case.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.1 million in Q2, more than double the year-ago quarter, with first-half adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 million representing the best first half in years.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$0.7–0.9M (no formal consensus)” and base case “$0.85–1.0M.”

description: The second consecutive positive GAAP quarter was anticipated as a key milestone, but reported EPS of $0.01 was above the preview’s consensus range of -$0.01 to $0.00 and its base-case expectation of $0.00.
fact_evidence: “The company delivered its second consecutive quarter of positive GAAP net income, reporting $280,000 or $0.01 per share in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS: -$0.01 to $0.00”; the base case expected “$0.00.”

description: Management described a larger potential float-income opportunity from the Usio Ion platform than the preview had quantified: it could lift daily float balances from $80–$100 million currently to over $200–$300 million and help push gross margins above 25%. This is a prospective catalyst rather than a reported result.
fact_evidence: “The Usio Ion platform [is] positioned as the key catalyst to push margins above 25% via 100%-margin float income”; balances could grow “from the current $80-$100 million to potentially over $200-$300 million daily.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management should “size the rate headwind” from interest income and noted that higher-margin Real-Time Payments were part of the margin thesis, but did not describe this Ion float-balance potential.

description: Usio disclosed a first-half share repurchase, a capital-allocation action not discussed in the preview. The purchase was relatively small in scale.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 281,000 shares for $371,000 in the first half.”

description: Q2 sales were $211 million, above the preview’s $199.3–$200.3 million consensus range and its $203 million working estimate. The year-over-year decline was 4%, narrower than the roughly 8%–10% decline implied by those estimates.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales totaled $211 million, a 4% decline year-over-year, though this beat expectations and reflected a narrowing rate of decline.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $199.3M – $200.3M”; “My working numbers: revenue $203M (-7.9%).”

description: Gross margin reached 62.4%, far above the preview’s 57.8% working estimate and its expected 57%–59% range. The reported increase was attributed to full-price selling, supply-chain initiatives, and lower tariffs versus last year.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 490 basis points to 62.4%, driven by the shift to a full-price selling model, supply chain initiatives, and lower tariffs versus last year.”
expectation_evidence: “My working numbers: … gross margin 57.8%”; “A Q2 print of 57–59% without one-offs confirms the de-promotion thesis.”

description: Management raised the full-year adjusted operating margin range by one percentage point at both ends, from 3%–5% to 4%–6%, rather than reiterating the existing guide.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin of 4% to 6% (up from 3% to 5%).”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. op. margin guide | 3% – 5%”; “Reiteration of -4/-6% sales and 3–5% adjusted operating margin is the neutral outcome.”

description: The full-year sales decline outlook improved by one percentage point at both ends, to 3%–5% from 4%–6%. The preview described a guidance raise as the upside case, while its neutral outcome was a reiteration.
fact_evidence: “Net sales to decline 3% to 5% (improved from 4% to 6%).”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 net sales guide | -4% to -6%”; “A raise … is the bull trigger.”

description: Q2 adjusted operating income was roughly $9 million, above the preview’s $6–8 million working estimate. That is a better result than the already-anticipated improvement from last year’s $4 million comparison.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted operating income doubled year-over-year to roughly $9 million.”
expectation_evidence: “My working numbers: … adjusted operating income $6–8M (~3.3%).”

description: The company now expects positive free cash flow for full-year 2026, better than the preview’s approximately breakeven expectation.
fact_evidence: “The company now expects to generate positive free cash flow for full-year 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF guide | ~breakeven.”

description: Fossil-brand traditional watches grew 12% globally in wholesale, including 16% growth in US wholesale. That exceeded the preview’s expectation that wholesale hold mid-single-digit growth and that core traditional watches sustain high-single-digit growth.
fact_evidence: “Fossil brand traditional watch business grew 12% globally in the wholesale channel, with US wholesale traditional watch growth of 16%.”
expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires wholesale to hold mid-single-digit growth”; “core traditional watches up high-single-digits.”

description: The expected year-end store count was about 185, but the company now expects approximately 178 locations after 17 net Q2 exits and two more planned closures. The 11 South Africa locations transitioned to a distributor, so the change reflects both closures and a shift in distribution.
fact_evidence: “Fossil closed 17 net stores in Q2 (6 closures plus 11 transitioned to a South Africa distributor), plans two more closures, and expects to end the year with approximately 178 locations.”
expectation_evidence: “7 closed in Q1, ~15 planned for 2026, ending at 185 doors.”

description: Sales were $458.5 million, $31.6 million below the $490.1 million consensus, and comparable sales fell 6.2% rather than the preview’s implied 0% to +1%. Leslie’s also said online comps were positive, but physical-store traffic had not improved—so the expected Q2 customer momentum did not carry through to overall Q3 comps.
fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 total sales declined 8.4% year-over-year to $458.5 million, with comparable sales down 6.2% driven primarily by lower customer traffic and transactions”; the company also reported positive Leslies.com comps but said physical store traffic gains remained its central challenge.
expectation_evidence: “Net sales $490.1M”; “Comparable sales ~0% to +1% (implied)”; and “Comparable sales — did Q2’s +6.6% hold?”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $55.7 million, well below the preview’s implied $78–82 million range and below the roughly $75 million level the preview said was needed to avoid mechanically breaking the full-year plan.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 31.7% to $55.7 million from $81.6 million a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$78–82M (implied)” and “If Q3 adj. EBITDA prints below ~$75M, Q4 has to do >$57M vs. $45.2M LY to save even the low end of the guide.”

description: Gross margin contracted to 36.5%, below the preview’s estimated 38.5–39.5% range and its stated 37.5% downside warning level. The reported pressures included fewer higher-margin specialty-chemical sales, unfavorable mix, and higher distribution and manufacturing costs.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin contracted 310 basis points to 36.5% from 39.6%, hurt by fewer sales of higher-margin specialty chemicals, unfavorable mix, and higher distribution and manufacturing costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~38.5–39.5%” and “below 37.5% suggests the Price Drop is eating structural margin.”

description: Leslie’s withdrew its fiscal 2026 sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance and provided no replacement outlook, rather than reaffirming or merely trimming the range. The preview had identified withdrawal as a bear-case possibility, but its base case anticipated a trim to the low half of guidance.
fact_evidence: “Leslie’s withdrew its full-year fiscal 2026 sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance and declined to provide an updated outlook, citing weak peak-season traffic and macro uncertainty.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance: reaffirmed / trimmed / withdrawn”; the base case said “guide trimmed to low half,” while the bear case said “FY guide withdrawn.”

description: Net income rose by $26.1 million to $47.8 million, but a previously unflagged $17.5 million credit-card interchange-fee settlement recorded in SG&A helped produce the improvement, making the reported increase partly one-off rather than a straightforward operating gain.
fact_evidence: “Net income improved $26.1 million to $47.8 million, but the gain was aided by a one-time $17.5 million credit card interchange fee settlement recorded in SG&A.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory was down 15% year over year, while Leslie’s said it maintained strong in-stock levels. The preview warned that further destocking could risk in-stock performance, so the reported availability held up despite lower inventory.
fact_evidence: “Inventory declined 15% year-over-year to $233.4 million, reflecting optimization efforts and the closure of 80 underperforming stores while maintaining strong in-stock levels.”
expectation_evidence: “Further destocking flatters cash but risks in-stock and margin.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: HYPE ended the quarter at $65, above the preview’s $55–62 estimate, lifting treasury value and NAV beyond their forecast ranges. The company reported $133 million of HYPE holdings and $134 million of NAV, versus estimates of $112–125 million and $110–120 million, respectively.
fact_evidence: “The company's hype treasury reached $133 million (2.04 million tokens at a $65.0 quarter-end price)” and “net asset value nearly doubled to $134 million from $70 million in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “HYPE price, period end: ~$55–62”; “Gross HYPE holdings: ~$112–125M”; “NAV: ~$110–120M.”

description: Net income was $31.0 million, below the preview’s $35–47 million estimate, despite being a record. The reported facts do not explain the shortfall relative to that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 net income hit a record $31.0 million versus $8.8 million in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “GAAP net income: ~$35–47M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $53.7 million, above the preview’s estimated $40–50 million range. The reported treasury gains were also above the preview’s modeled range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA jumped to $53.7 million from $19.5 million, driven largely by $54.8 million in treasury gains.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$40–50M”; “Unrealized gain on digital assets: +$38–50M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Rather than only the anticipated Skew deployment of 500,000 HYPE, management reported new Q3 partnerships with SKU and Entropy using 1 million HYPE. The deals also include rights to 5% of SKU’s equity and 5% of its tokens, while the preview had noted that roughly 300,000 HYPE still lacked a disclosed home.
fact_evidence: “Within weeks of the USDH headwind, the company redeployed 1 million hype into new Q3 house partnerships with SKU (HIP4) and Entropy (HIP3), securing improved economics plus a right to 5% of SKU's equity and 5% of its tokens.”
expectation_evidence: “The replacement — the Skew Technologies HAUS agreement for 500K HYPE — was not signed until July 15” and “300K HYPE still without a disclosed home.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company disclosed its first institutional credit transaction on Avia, lending USDC against staked HYPE at 8% APY. The preview discussed yield deployments and capital allocation but did not anticipate this credit product or deal.
fact_evidence: “The company completed its first institutional credit deal on the Avia platform, lending $1 million USDC against natively staked hype at 8% APY, with collateral custodied at Anchorage Digital.”

description: Management said operating expenses excluding stock-based compensation fell to $2.3 million and expects a further 10–20% reduction after the legacy biotech segment runs off. The preview anticipated declining expenses and a wind-down, but not that additional quantified reduction.
fact_evidence: “Operating expenses excluding stock-based comp fell 21% quarter-over-quarter to $2.3 million” and management guided “to a further 10–20% reduction after fully running off the legacy biotech segment.”
expectation_evidence: “Opex: ~$2.8–3.1M”; the preview also described a “declining trend” and a “near-complete wind-down by end of Q2 2026.”

description: Shares outstanding were approximately 15.5 million, above the preview’s 15.16 million reference point. The facts do not establish when or why the share count increased, so they do not show whether this reflects a new issuance.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 15.5 million shares outstanding as of August 10.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Shares out: 15.16M” and said “There has been no capital raise since the May 8 offering close.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Staking and yield-enhancement dollars rose sharply, but HYPE earned from staking was flat versus Q1 and third-party validator commissions contributed only about 500 tokens. That leaves the validator-commission component of the preview’s described multi-layer yield strategy small in the reported quarter.
fact_evidence: “Staking yield rose 69% to $527,000 and yield enhancement grew 58% to $334,000,” while the company earned “about 11,000 hype tokens in Q2—flat versus Q1—with only ~500 tokens coming from third-party validator commissions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “triple-dip yield (native staking + validator commissions + DeFi deployment/HAUS agreements)” and estimated “staking ~10K/qtr.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $39,000, essentially breakeven, versus the preview’s estimated operating loss of roughly $0.7 million. Management also said the cost run rate had fallen below $22 million annually, implying quarterly breakeven revenue of about $5.25–$5.5 million, and July was near cash-flow neutral.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached essentially breakeven at positive $39,000”; the company reduced its “total COGS and operating expense run rate below $22 million annually” and established a breakeven revenue point of “approximately $5.25M-$5.5M per quarter”; July preliminary numbers showed “near cash flow neutrality.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated an “Operating loss” of “~($0.7M)” and said normalized operating expense of “~$3.5M/quarter is the bogey.” It also inferred “~$3M of cash consumption in the quarter.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The accounting explanation was more reassuring than the preview’s concern about a potentially recurring fair-value liability charge: most of the $873,000 interest expense was noncash and described as nonrecurring, and the convertible notes had converted to preferred stock, leaving the company with no debt. The reported $0.17-per-share loss was worse than the preview’s stale $0.05 consensus, but less severe than its base-case EPS range of $0.20–$0.35 loss.
fact_evidence: The $1.6 million net loss was “driven almost entirely by $873,000 of interest expense from convertible debenture accounting,” of which “~$863,000 was noncash and nonrecurring”; the company “now carries no debt after convertible notes converted to Series B preferred stock on July 8.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that liability classification could mean “permanent quarterly EPS volatility tied to the stock price” and gave a base-case GAAP EPS range of “($0.20)–($0.35).” It also noted the “–$0.05 EPS figure almost certainly does not contemplate the derivative/valuation charge.”

description: Management quantified the pending transformational acquisition’s potential scale, saying it is expected to nearly double annual revenue run rate; the preview discussed the roughly $23 million deal but did not provide an expected revenue contribution of that size.
fact_evidence: The pending transformational acquisition “is expected to nearly double annual revenue run rate.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the pending “$23M deal” and its unresolved financing gap, but did not estimate that it could nearly double the company’s annual revenue run rate.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The IAR embedded-security asset acquisition introduced a set of monetization opportunities not covered in the preview: software, support, licensing, and per-token revenue using the existing LumenX platform, with potential demand tied to regulation.
fact_evidence: The IAR asset acquisition adds “four new revenue streams (software platform, support contracts, licensing fees, and per-token charges)” leveraging LumenX and positioning the company for “regulatory-driven demand such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog ended below the preview’s base-case range even though bookings landed within that range. Management attributed the decline to faster order-to-ship performance, rather than the preview’s concern that it could signal weak demand or backlog conversion.
fact_evidence: Q2 bookings were $4.9 million, while backlog fell to $2.1 million from $2.6 million “due to faster order-to-ship performance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected bookings of “$4.5–5.5M” and backlog of “$2.5–3.0M,” and said backlog below “~$2.3M” could indicate the revenue surge was backlog conversion rather than demand recovery.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company reported six new customer logos in the first half across automotive, robotics, and global communications, and said robotics revenue could become significant in the second half of next year; the preview did not flag these wins or the robotics outlook.
fact_evidence: The company signed “6 new customer logos in the first half (3 automotive, 2 robotics, 1 global communications),” with robotics revenue expected to become significant in the second half of next year.

description: Jack in the Box reported Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $61.2 million, above the preview’s $53–57 million estimate. The preview expected a much lower quarterly result based on the full-year guidance run-rate.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $61.2 million from $57.1 million on lower G&A.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $53–57M”

description: Operating EPS was $0.96, beating the preview’s $0.89–$0.90 consensus estimate. The preview’s base case anticipated roughly $0.88–$0.95.
fact_evidence: “Operating EPS was $0.96.”
expectation_evidence: “Operating EPS (non-GAAP) | $0.89–$0.90”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Q3 same-store sales decline was 1.1%, just below the preview’s expected range of roughly flat to down 1%. That narrowly misses the preview’s stated threshold for maintaining the sequential-improvement narrative.
fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 same-store sales declined 1.1% overall.”
expectation_evidence: “System same-store sales: ‑1% to +1%”; the preview also said “Anything worse than ~‑1% breaks the sequential-improvement narrative.”

description: Management said Q4-to-date comps had turned positive in the low single digits and now expects full-year comps to be flat to slightly up. That is a better outlook than the preview’s account of the prior low-single-digit-decline guidance, though management said the Philly Cheesesteak launch was pulled forward.
fact_evidence: “Q4-to-date same-store sales have turned positive in the low single-digit range, and management expects full-year comps to be flat to slightly up after pulling forward the Philly Cheesesteak platform launch.”
expectation_evidence: “May: SSS ‘low single-digit decline’”; the preview also described the marker as “approaching flat” and said to watch for a “specific positive Q4-to-date comp number.”

description: Franchise-level margin was $60.3 million, below the preview’s $62–64 million estimate, and its 37.4% margin rate was below the preview’s 38–39% estimate. The reported drivers included lower same-store sales, fewer restaurants, and higher bad debt.
fact_evidence: “Franchise-level margin dropped to $60.3 million (37.4% of franchise revenues) from $66.2 million (39.3%), hurt by ~$1.7M lower same-store sales, ~$1.5M fewer restaurants, and ~$1M higher bad debt.”
expectation_evidence: “Franchise-level margin | $62–64M (38–39%).”

description: The FY2026 adjusted EBITDA range was narrowed from $225–235 million to $225–230 million. The floor was unchanged, but the top end was lowered rather than the range being reaffirmed intact as the preview’s base case expected.
fact_evidence: “Management updated FY2026 guidance to … $225-230 million adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide ($225–235M)”; the base case anticipated the guide would be “reaffirmed at $225–235M.”

description: The FY2026 restaurant-level margin outlook was updated to about 16.5%, below the preview’s roughly 17% full-year guidance reference. This is also below the preview’s estimated Q3 margin range only in the full-year context, not the reported Q3 result.
fact_evidence: “Management updated FY2026 guidance to ~ … 16.5% restaurant-level margin.”
expectation_evidence: “May: … RLM ~17%”; the preview also said the FY guide was “~17%.”

description: The company lowered its FY2026 SG&A outlook to $112–115 million, below the prior $115–125 million range cited in the preview. That implies a better cost outlook than expected.
fact_evidence: “Management updated FY2026 guidance to … $112-115 million SG&A.”

description: Management disclosed that Chicago reduced consolidated restaurant-level margin: excluding Chicago, the margin would have been 18.5% rather than the reported 17.6%. The preview did not flag this market-specific drag.
fact_evidence: “Excluding the Chicago market, restaurant-level margin would have been 18.5% versus 17.6% reported, making Chicago a key drag on consolidated profitability.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The Hot Ones promotion underperformed because its products were too polarizing and spicy and checks were lower; management responded by changing the builds and value panels and ending the promotion early. The preview did not anticipate this promotion-specific weakness.
fact_evidence: “The Hot Ones promotion underperformed due to polarizing, overly spicy products and lower checks,” and the team “add[ed] less-spicy builds, swap[ped] value panels for higher-priced core items, and end[ed] the window early.”

description: Management said elevated restaurant closures are expected to continue into 2027 and 2028 as franchisee profitability remains under pressure. The preview expected closures to accelerate in FY2026, but did not anticipate the elevated pace extending for those additional years.
fact_evidence: “The company closed 40 restaurants year-to-date and expects 10-20 more in Q4, with elevated closures now anticipated to extend into 2027 and 2028 as franchisee profitability remains under pressure.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 plan is 50–100”; the preview described the need for closures to “accelerate in H2.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net debt-to-EBITDA was 6.3x, slightly above the preview’s approximately 6.2x pro forma expectation. The company nevertheless reported substantial debt reduction since Jack on Track began.
fact_evidence: “The company completed a summer refinancing, fully paying down the August 2026 debt tranche and cutting debt by $244 million since Jack on Track began, lowering net debt/EBITDA to 6.3x from 6.9x.”
expectation_evidence: “Net debt/adj. EBITDA … ~6.2x pro forma for the $99M August-tranche prepayment.”

description: Harmonic’s Q2 broadband revenue was $133.5 million, above the $125 million top of guidance and the preview’s $120.9 million consensus. That was a substantial upside to an expected range the preview described as nearly pre-announced.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 broadband revenue grew 54% year-over-year to $133.5 million, exceeding the high end of guidance ($115-125 million).”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $120.9M | $115M – $125M”; “the quarter itself is nearly pre-announced by guidance.”

description: The company raised its FY2026 broadband revenue range to $505–525 million from $475–495 million, rather than reaffirming the range as the preview’s base case anticipated. The new midpoint is 6.2% higher than the prior midpoint.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 broadband revenue guidance [was raised] to $505-525 million, up from the prior $475-495 million range, representing a 6.2% increase at the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “FY *reaffirmed* $475–495M” was the preview’s base case; it also framed a raise as a key catalyst.

description: FY2026 EPS guidance rose to $0.67–0.75 from $0.57–0.67, a roughly 14.5% increase at the midpoint. The preview’s guidance table showed the lower prior range and its base case expected the FY range to be reaffirmed.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 EPS guidance was raised to $0.67-0.75, up approximately 14.5% from the prior midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $0.57 – $0.67”; “FY *reaffirmed* $475–495M” was the preview’s base-case expectation.

description: Q2 EPS of $0.21 topped the company’s $0.19 guidance ceiling and the preview’s $0.168 consensus. This was a clearer beat than the preview’s expected in-line-to-modest-beat scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS of $0.21 beating the $0.15-0.19 guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $0.168 | $0.15 – $0.19”; the preview’s base scenario was “In-line-to-modest beat.”

description: The margin outlook was better than the preview’s implied roughly 48.8% second-half gross margin and its concern that a four-handle would confirm the bear case. Harmonic guided to 51–52% for Q3 and the full year, citing mix and supply-chain mitigation despite continued memory costs.
fact_evidence: “Gross margins are guided at 51-52% for Q3 and full-year”; “full-year margin guidance was improved due to customer mix and supply chain mitigation.”
expectation_evidence: “2H26 implied … Gross margin … ~48.8%”; “A 2H GM guide with a 4-handle confirms the bear math.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog and deferred revenue reached $587.6 million, only modestly above the preview’s $582.1 million reference and below its $600 million bull-case marker. However, 73% is expected to convert within 12 months, above the preview’s stated 60% conversion figure.
fact_evidence: “Backlog and deferred revenue reached a record $587.6 million, up 71% year-over-year, with 73% expected to convert to revenue within 12 months.”
expectation_evidence: “Backlog + deferred revenue was $582.1M, +87% YoY, with 60% converting inside 12 months”; the bull scenario cited “backlog >$600M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Bookings indicators were stronger than the preview’s expectation of overall book-to-bill around 1.0: rest-of-market represented about 60% of bookings and book-to-bill was well over 1.5. This adds stronger demand evidence than the preview’s already-positive expectation that rest-of-market book-to-bill was meaningfully above 1.0.
fact_evidence: “Rest-of-market comprising approximately 60% of bookings and a book-to-bill well over 1.5.”
expectation_evidence: “overall B2B of 1.0 (rest-of-market meaningfully >1.0).”

description: Q2 rest-of-market revenue was 37% of total revenue, below the preview’s 42% Q1 share and its stated 42% level to watch. Its 44% Q2 growth also trailed the prior Q1 growth rate of 78%, although first-half growth remained strong at about 60%.
fact_evidence: “Rest-of-market revenue grew 44% year-over-year to nearly $50 million (37% of total revenue), with first-half rest-of-market revenue surpassing $100 million, about 60% higher than the prior year.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1: … rest-of-market +78% YoY at 42% of revenue”; the preview’s catalyst checklist said “Rest-of-market holding ≥42% of revenue.”

description: The $200 million buyback program saw no Q2 repurchases, despite the preview highlighting buyback pace and describing aggressive repurchases as the cleanest support. The program had repurchased $122 million cumulatively, but the quarter’s pause was not what that framing suggested.
fact_evidence: “The $200 million buyback program [had] $122 million repurchased but no shares bought in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation of the $145M. Buyback pace (Q1: 4.2M shares / $43M)”; “Aggressive repurchase at ~$12 is the cleanest support.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Q2 free cash flow was negative $7 million because memory inventory arrived early, an unexpected cash-flow drag despite the preview’s focus on cash proceeds and buyback use. The call characterized the driver as inventory timing rather than a demand shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was negative $7 million due to early memory inventory delivery.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 net cash “an open item” and focused on proceeds, buybacks, and working-capital adjustments; it did not anticipate negative free cash flow from early memory inventory delivery.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Harmonic reported meaningful early traction for its intelligence platform, which the preview did not discuss: Beacon was live at about 20 customers, broader offerings were running with about 10 operators, and the company reported more than 30% fewer subscriber service calls.
fact_evidence: “Beacon live at approximately 20 customers and broader offerings running with about 10 operators, showing over 30% reductions in subscriber service calls.”

description: The preview described the video business sale as a $145 million transaction, while the call cited $137.9 million at closing. The reported closing amount was $7.1 million below that preview figure.
fact_evidence: “Harmonic completed the sale of its video business to Mediakind … for $137.9 million at closing.”
expectation_evidence: “Video sold to MediaKind for $145M.”

description: Q2 revenue was $11.0 million, slightly below the $11.2 million consensus estimate, and the year-over-year decline was therefore somewhat steeper than the preview implied. The sequential increase to $11.0 million did meet the preview’s expectation of an inflection.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $11 million, up sequentially from $10.6 million in Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $11.20M” and “Consensus $11.20M would still be −4.3% YoY.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $16.0–$16.5 million is above the preview’s roughly $15 million quarterly combined-company run-rate benchmark. Management attributed much of the sequential jump to having a full quarter of Arcania.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $16 million to $16.5 million,” with the jump “largely reflecting a full quarter of Arcania operations.”
expectation_evidence: “The combined target is a ~$15M quarterly run rate ($60M annualized)” and “Q3 combined guide reiterated or raised toward $15M+.”

description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.3–$2.5 million is above the preview’s roughly $2 million-or-more standalone framing; at the guided revenue level, it also implies margins above the preview’s 10%+ combined-company benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects … adjusted EBITDA of $2.3 million to $2.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Prior standalone Q3 framing was ‘~$2M or more’ adj. EBITDA” and the combined target included “10%+ adj. EBITDA margins.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash fell again, to $8.2 million from $9.0 million, rather than building as the preview said it would if Q2 adjusted EBITDA landed in guidance. The call attributed the decline to transaction and realignment costs, but the cash result still failed that expected cross-check.
fact_evidence: “Cash declined to $8.2 million at the end of Q2 from $9 million in Q1, primarily due to transaction expenses and organizational realignment costs.”
expectation_evidence: “If Q2 adj. EBITDA is genuinely +$1.7M, cash should build even after Archenia deal costs.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management gave a concrete example of AI verified outcomes more than doubling one customer’s annualized analytics contribution, providing realized evidence of the cross-sell opportunity the preview was looking for rather than only a broad opportunity claim.
fact_evidence: A home services client with “~$500,000 in annualized analytics revenue adopted AI verified outcomes, more than doubling its contribution to over $1 million annually.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said bundles can “double revenue per customer” and called for an “updated penetration count” as a forward indicator of organic growth.

description: The call repeated the earlier top-customer presentation and paid-pilot figures but did not report a newer penetration count or evidence that adoption had advanced across the group. That left the preview’s key request for an updated cross-sell progress measure unanswered.
fact_evidence: Management said it had “previously presented new products to nearly one-third of the top 100 customers, with about half of those already purchasing on a recurring or paid pilot basis.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for an updated penetration count” and “If that ratio hasn't advanced, the growth story is a slide, not a pipeline.”

description: The preview estimated $0.7–1.0 million of Q3 revenue from STS, but the call said STS contributed only about $200,000 to Nano after the May 22 closing. STS’s $3.9 million of revenue in the first six months of calendar 2026 was business revenue, not Nano’s post-close contribution.
fact_evidence: “The acquired STS fuel transportation business generated approximately $3.9 million in unaudited revenue in the first six months of calendar 2026, contributing only $200,000 to Nano after the May 22 closing.”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 captures ~40 days → ~$0.8M”; my model estimates revenue of “$0.7–1.0M (STS stub).”

description: Nano used its ATM to raise about $26 million during the quarter, contrary to the preview’s expectation that it would not use the facility. The preview had specifically flagged no ATM issuance as preferable at the share price then prevailing.
fact_evidence: “The company raised approximately $26 million in net proceeds through its ATM facility during the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “‘We did not use the ATM in the quarter and have no near-term need to’ is worth more than the EPS line.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end liquidity was about $580 million, above the preview’s estimate of roughly $545–555 million. It also increased about $11 million from the prior quarter rather than declining as the preview’s cash walk projected.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q3 2026 with approximately $580 million in liquidity,” up “roughly $11 million from the prior quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + ST investments” at “~$545–555M” and expected it to walk down from $568.7 million.

description: Nano reported progress toward a framework agreement with a global infrastructure developer for a multi-gigawatt AI data center pipeline, with possible preferred-provider status and milestone-based investments of tens of millions up to $100 million. The preview said a binding commitment would be the meaningful commercial conversion; this remains a prospective framework, not a reported signed order or investment.
fact_evidence: “Nano is advancing toward an initial framework agreement with a global infrastructure developer” that “could name Nano the preferred nuclear provider” and include “milestone-based investments of tens of millions up to $100 million.”
expectation_evidence: “What re-rates the stock is a binding order, deposit, or Phase II/site-specific defense award”; the base case anticipated pipeline discussion “with no conversions.”

description: The reported Q3 net loss was $10.1 million, near the preview’s own $10.0–10.5 million estimate but materially narrower than the roughly $15 million loss implied by the consensus EPS estimate. The call facts do not provide reported EPS, so the comparison is on net loss.
fact_evidence: “Q3 net loss widened to $10.1 million from $7.6 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 net loss at “~$10.0–10.5M” and described consensus as “~$15M implied.”

description: The STS acquisition required about $7 million in initial payment, with additional payments tied to retention, rather than the preview’s stated deal terms of up to $13 million in cash and stock. The call did not state the ultimate total consideration, so the difference is in the upfront payment structure, not necessarily the total cost.
fact_evidence: “The STS acquisition required only about $7 million in initial payment plus future retention-based payments,” with management describing a focus on “small, capability-adding deals rather than large outlays.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said STS “Closed May 22, 2026 for up to $13M cash/stock.”

description: Headcount nearly tripled year over year to 85 employees and contractors, with further significant technical and fuel-cycle hiring expected. The preview modeled higher expenses but did not flag this scale of staffing growth.
fact_evidence: “Headcount grew nearly threefold to 85 employees and contractors as of Q3 end versus 31 one year prior,” with “continued significant expansion of technical and fuel-cycle staff” expected.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management described a fuel-flexibility feature not raised in the preview: Kronos can use commercially available LEU Plus fuel now and switch to HALU later without redesign or retooling. That is presented as a way to reach market earlier than HALU-dependent competitors.
fact_evidence: “Kronos is designed to run on commercially available LEU Plus fuel today and can switch to HALU in the future without any reactor redesign or plant retooling, giving Nano an earlier-to-market advantage over HALU-dependent competitors.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The NRC environmental assessment target was stated as Q1 2027, earlier and more specific than the preview’s Spring 2027 target. The safety evaluation remains in 2027 and construction is still targeted for H2 2027.
fact_evidence: The NRC “expects to complete its environmental assessment in Q1 2027 and safety evaluation in Q3 2027,” keeping construction start “in H2 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed environmental assessment in “Spring 2027,” safety evaluation in “early fall 2027,” and construction in “2H 2027.”

description: Tapestry guided FY27 adjusted EPS to $7.80–$7.90, above the preview’s $7.45–$7.50 consensus range and slightly above its $7.65–$7.80 Amplify-implied range.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for… EPS of $7.80-7.90 (low double-digit growth).”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27 adj. EPS is ~$7.45–7.50”; Amplify implies “~$7.65–$7.80.”

description: Kate Spade’s FY27 outlook was materially weaker than the preview’s expected return to roughly flat-to-up revenue and positive operating income: Tapestry instead expects a high-single-digit decline and a modest operating loss.
fact_evidence: “The FY27 guide embeds… a high single-digit decline at Kate Spade, which is expected to post a modest operating loss.”
expectation_evidence: “The Street needs FY27 KS guided to roughly flat-to-up with positive operating income”; the catalyst checklist asks whether it will return to growth “and positive operating income.”

description: Coach’s Q4 growth was stronger than the preview’s low-teens expectation, at 14% constant currency.
fact_evidence: “Q4 constant currency sales rose 11%, with Coach up 14%.”
expectation_evidence: “Coach revenue… low-teens %”; the preview says the Street models low-teens Coach growth.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Coach’s Q4 handbag growth came from mid-teens AUR increases while unit volumes were roughly flat, rather than both AUR and units growing as the preview said would support the quality of the beat.
fact_evidence: “Coach Q4 handbag AUR increased mid-teens with unit volumes roughly flat by design due to fewer promotion days.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 had “units +20% and AUR up low-double-digit” and that if Q4 growth became “AUR-only… the quality of the beat deteriorates.”

description: Q4 EPS of $1.32 exceeded both the preview’s $1.25 consensus and the roughly $1.22 implied by the FY26 guide, even with a tax headwind.
fact_evidence: “Q4 EPS grew 28% to $1.32, beating guidance despite a $0.05 tax headwind.”
expectation_evidence: Q4 adjusted EPS consensus was “$1.25”; the preview calculated “implied Q4… ~$1.22 EPS.”

description: FY26 revenue was modestly above the preview’s approximately $7.95 billion guide, and Tapestry said it achieved its three-year Investor Day commitments two years early.
fact_evidence: “Tapestry achieved fiscal 2026 revenue of $8 billion, growing 17% on a pro forma constant currency basis, hitting its Investor Day 3-year commitments two years ahead of plan.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY26 revenue ~$7.95B (guide)” and approximately 16% pro forma constant-currency growth.

description: FY26 EPS finished above the preview’s $6.97 consensus and approximately $6.95 guide, reaching $7.05.
fact_evidence: “EPS grew 38% to $7.05.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS: $6.97” consensus and “guide ~$6.95.”

description: FY26 operating-margin expansion was somewhat greater than the preview’s guided increase: 340 basis points versus approximately 300 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Full-year operating margin expanded 340 basis points to over 23%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 operating margin at “~23% (guide, +300bps).”

description: Q2 sales were $93.5 million, about $3.3 million above the preview’s roughly $90.2 million consensus estimate and flat with Q1 rather than the sequential decline the preview highlighted as a risk. The result also landed in the preview’s $93–95 million bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales reached a record $93.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “consensus sits at ~$90.2M”; the preview also said, “If Q2 lands at $90–91M, that is −3% q/q,” and its bull case forecast “$93–95M.”

description: China sales reached $52.3 million, well above the preview’s $45 million bogey, and grew 10% sequentially. The preview anticipated normalized inventory and demand-driven sequential growth, but the reported revenue was considerably stronger than that threshold.
fact_evidence: “China net sales grew over 100% year-over-year and 10% sequentially to $52.3 million, with no evidence of inventory build at distributors or hospitals, indicating demand-driven growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s China bogey was “China ≥$45M with inventory at/below 6 mo.”

description: Diluted EPS was $0.16, below the preview’s $0.22 consensus and its $0.20–$0.25 base-case range. STAAR returned to profitability, but the reported per-share result fell short of the earnings level the preview considered achievable.
