dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Title-related mortgage loan originations rose 14% year over year, an unanticipated positive operating datapoint alongside the preview's focus on retail and auto weakness.
fact_evidence: “Title-related mortgage loan originations rose 14% year-over-year.”

description: The preview’s house estimate was $8.3 million in revenue, and it highlighted $8.5 million as the run-rate test. TPCS reported $9.1 million, exceeding both the estimate and the nine-million-dollar threshold.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue rose 23% year-over-year to $9.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The house estimate was “$8.3M”; the preview also said “Revenue ≥ $8.5M” validates the run-rate step and noted the CEO’s goal to get into “nine-plus.”

description: The preview expected a 17.5% consolidated gross margin and $1.45 million of gross profit. Reported gross profit was about $1.4 million on $9.1 million of revenue, implying a margin of roughly 15.4%—below the margin expectation despite the revenue beat.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross profit up 36% to $1.4 million” on revenue of “$9.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The house estimate listed “Gross profit” of “$1.45M” and “Gross margin” of “17.5%.”

description: The preview expected Ranor to carry the quarter at about a 35% margin. Its reported $1.6 million of gross profit on $5.5 million of revenue implies a margin of about 29%, below that expectation, even though management cited favorable project mix.
fact_evidence: “Ranor segment revenue grew 27% to $5.5 million and generated $1.6 million in gross profit, driven by favorable project mix.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Ranor carries the quarter at ~35% margin.”

description: The preview made Stadco crossing into positive gross profit the key test and said gross profit above roughly $0.3 million would validate the turnaround. The call reported a 65% increase in Stadco gross profit, but also said the segment was still not profitable, so it did not establish the expected turnaround into profitability.
fact_evidence: “Stadco revenue increased 22% to $4.1 million with gross profit up 65% (a $300,000 increase), though the segment remains not yet profitable.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “Stadco gross profit sign” “the whole ballgame,” said “a Stadco gross profit above ~$0.3M” would validate the turnaround, and described FY27 as the year Stadco should cross into positive gross margin.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview highlighted liquidity pressure and possible financing needs. Instead of merely preserving debt, TPCS cut total debt by $2 million, but cash also fell from $431,000 to $279,000, leaving liquidity tighter; the combined balance-sheet outcome was therefore mixed.
fact_evidence: “Total debt was cut from $7 million to $5 million,” while “Cash balance declined to $279,000” from $431,000; the call also cited “$2 million in financing activity paydowns.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Liquidity and the balance sheet,” citing “$431K cash against $6.9M of debt,” and said management wanted to invest while paying down debt; it raised the possibility of “a facility, a raise, or customer-funded equipment.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview cited about $25 million of unfunded orders to watch. The reported amount was approximately $22 million, below that reference point, although funded backlog remained within the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: “Funded backlog stands at $52 million … plus approximately $22 million in unfunded purchase orders.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “the ~$25M unfunded” and said to watch whether any of it converted to funded backlog.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call gave a more specific account of Stadco’s turnaround actions than the preview anticipated: less than half of its business was still under legacy loss-making contracts, with price-adjustment requests and new estimate-to-complete gates in use. This offers concrete evidence of remediation, though it does not by itself establish profitability.
fact_evidence: “Less than 50% of Stadco's business is now operating under legacy loss-making contracts,” with management using “price adjustment requests and new estimate-to-complete gating processes to improve margins.”

description: SRTS reported Q2 revenue of $2.3 million on 11 units, far below the preview’s $4.6–5.0 million revenue range and its estimate of roughly 16–18 units. Management said eight units were held out of Q2 because a third-party bank had not completed financing approval by June 30; those units have since been approved and sold and are expected to be recognized in Q3.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue dropped approximately 68% to $2.3 million”; the company sold “11 units”; financing approval timing “prevented recognition of 8 units in Q2,” which “will be recognized in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $4.60M” and an alternate “$5.03M”; the model showed “~16–18 needed” units.

description: The reported loss was much larger than the preview’s expected per-share loss, largely because SRTS recorded a $5.7 million valuation allowance against net deferred tax assets. The preview had flagged a valuation allowance as a risk to the tax benefit supporting reported EPS, but the actual loss was substantially beyond the consensus range.
fact_evidence: “Net loss of $8.7 million ($0.53 per share)”; the loss was “driven largely by a $5.7 million valuation allowance against net deferred tax assets.”
expectation_evidence: EPS consensus was “−$0.115” and an alternate “−$0.13”; the preview also warned, “If Sensus books a valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets, that cushion disappears and headline EPS gets structurally worse.”

description: Despite the weak Q2 unit count, management guided to more than 20 units in each of Q3 and Q4. That is a stronger near-term unit outlook than the preview’s roughly 16–18-unit Q2 model and its general expectation of sequential improvement, and the delayed eight units are expected to contribute to Q3.
fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed expectations of sequential unit growth,” guiding to “20-plus units in each of Q3 and Q4”; the eight delayed units are expected to be recognized in Q3.
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~16–18” Q2 units and said management had “committed publicly to sequential improvement every quarter.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said the overall revenue mix is running roughly 50/50 between outright purchases and recurring-revenue models, and it is expanding higher-margin CensusLink subscriptions to nearly all new customers and existing installed systems. The preview described recurring revenue as building but small and highlighted attach-rate disclosure as an open question, so the stated breadth of the subscription rollout is more encouraging than that setup implied.
fact_evidence: Management indicated the “overall revenue mix is running roughly 50/50 between outright purchases and recurring-revenue models” and is expanding CensusLink subscriptions to “nearly all new customers and existing installed systems.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario described “recurring revenue building but small”; it flagged “Sensus Link attach rate” and said “Any quantified ARR/attach data” would be notable.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management cited a proposed 26% increase in Level 1 radiation hospital reimbursement as support for SRT economics. The preview emphasized the January 2026 CPT-code increase but did not mention this additional proposed reimbursement increase.
fact_evidence: “A proposed 26% increase in Level 1 radiation hospital reimbursement supports SRT economics.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described dedicated CPT codes taking effect January 1, 2026, with “roughly a 300% increase in the per-fraction delivery code,” but did not mention the proposed 26% increase.

description: SoundThinking cut its 2026 revenue outlook by roughly $10 million, from $109–111 million to $99–100 million. The cut was larger than the preview’s bear-case range of about $104–107 million.
fact_evidence: “cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $109-111 million to $99-100 million, a roughly $10 million reduction”; about 70% was attributed to timing/pushouts into 2027 and 30% to slower sales growth.
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue (guide) | $109.0–$111.0M”; the bear case described “FY cut to ~$104–107M.”

description: The company lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 8–9%, far below the preview’s expected 16–18% range. This is a substantial reset to expected profitability, not just a weaker-than-expected quarter.
fact_evidence: “full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was reduced to 8-9%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EBITDA margin (guide) | 16–18% — reaffirmed.”

description: Q2 revenue was $23.9 million, well below the $25.76 million consensus and the preview’s $25.5–26.2 million base-case range. It also fell 7.7% year over year, rather than tracking roughly flat to slightly down as expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $23.9 million from $25.9 million a year earlier”; it missed the company’s “$25.9 million half-year pacing target by about $2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | $25.76M (~flat to -0.5% YoY)”; base case revenue was “$25.5–26.2M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was just $1.2 million in Q2, below the preview’s base-case expectation of $2–3 million. The sequential improvement from Q1’s roughly negative $100,000 was a positive detail, but it did not make the quarter meet the expected range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $1.2 million from $3.4 million in Q2 2025, though it improved sequentially from roughly negative $100,000 in Q1 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “adj. EBITDA $2–3M.”

description: GAAP loss per share was $0.37, materially worse than the preview’s consensus estimates of a $0.177–$0.20 loss. The net loss also widened year over year, unlike the preview’s prior-year EPS comparison of a $0.24–$0.25 loss.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $4.8 million ($0.37 per diluted share) versus a $3.1 million loss ($0.24 per share) in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS (GAAP) | -$0.177”; the alternative estimate was “-$0.20.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said ShotSpotter performance was weakening in both bookings and go-lives, and acknowledged internal sales execution problems. The preview anticipated budget pressure and ARPA funding wind-down as attrition risks, but did not flag weak bookings and sales execution as additional problems.
fact_evidence: Management flagged “deteriorating ShotSpotter performance driven by both weak bookings and go-lives,” citing “elongating sales cycles, ARPA funding wind-down, and admitted internal sales execution underperformance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance assumed “higher attrition than historical, tied to budget pressure and the end of ARPA funds.”

description: The Puerto Rico ShotSpotter recapture was removed entirely from 2026 guidance, rather than being a signed deal that supported the planned second-half ramp. This was one of the specific contracts the preview said the H2 plan depended on.
fact_evidence: “The Puerto Rico ShotSpotter contract recapture (originally ~$1.5 million) was removed entirely from 2026 guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Puerto Rico was “positively engaged” but timing uncertain, and that “Signed = FY guide is live; slipped to 2027 = guide is arithmetically broken.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: SoundThinking did win the Texas statewide Crime Tracer deal, worth about $2.5 million in annual recurring revenue. The preview treated signing the state deal as an unresolved H2 catalyst, so the award is a positive result against the base-case expectation that deals could remain in pipeline.
fact_evidence: “Won a fourth statewide Crime Tracer deal in Texas worth approximately $2.5 million in annual recurring revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Puerto Rico and the “~$2.5M CrimeTracer state contract” were “explicitly embedded in the H2 ramp”; its base case had H2 deals “still described as pipeline.”

description: SafePointe deployment delays reduced expected revenue by about $2 million, despite nearly 90 new lanes being booked in Q2. The preview expected a substantial SafePointe drag, but also described revenue scaling from $3.6 million toward $6.5 million or more, rather than this specific deployment-related reduction.
fact_evidence: “SafePointe deployment delays reduced expected revenue by about $2 million despite nearly 90 new lanes booked in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said SafePointe had a “>$8M annualized drag in 2026” and that “Revenue should scale $3.6M → $6.5M+.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company recognized $900,000 of restructuring costs in Q2. The preview anticipated about $4 million of annualized workforce savings and raised the question of how much was in the run-rate, but did not flag this quarter’s restructuring charge.
fact_evidence: “$900,000 in restructuring costs recognized in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “$4M annualized workforce savings ($2.5M in-year)” and asked whether the savings were “fully in the Q2 run-rate.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash fell from $14.2 million at Q1-end to $6.4 million at Q2-end, while the company still had $4 million drawn on its credit facility. The preview flagged liquidity as a concern if the quarter brought cash burn and a guidance cut, but did not anticipate this specific cash balance.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only $6.4 million in cash, $4 million drawn on its credit facility.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Ended Q1 with $14.2M cash, $4M drawn” and said “a cash-burn quarter plus a guide cut would put the balance sheet into the conversation.”

description: The company’s ARR outlook was only for growth from $95.4 million to over $100 million entering 2027, below the preview’s approximately $110 million exit-2026 target. The call’s wording leaves the amount less precise, but does not affirm the previously expected target.
fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed ARR growth “from $95.4 million to over $100 million entering 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed an “Exit-2026 ARR target | ~$110M (from $95.4M entering 2026).”

description: The Chicago ShotSpotter RFP decision could slip to February 2027, and the 2026 outlook assumes no revenue from a renewed Chicago contract. The preview did not discuss this contract or its timing; the ballot referendum and pro-detection mayoral candidates provide a possible offsetting path to a comeback.
fact_evidence: “The Chicago ShotSpotter RFP decision could extend to February 2027, and guidance assumes no revenue contribution from any renewed Chicago contract, though a November ballot referendum and pro-detection mayoral candidates support a potential comeback.”

description: Q2 revenue was $1.1 million, about 27% below the preview's $1.502 million consensus, and fell 14% year over year rather than rising 15.9%.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue declined 14% year-over-year to $1.1 million from $1.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $1.502M | ... Implied Δ +15.9% YoY / +8.0% QoQ.”

description: Engineering services and OEM product sales were reported together at $0.2 million, well below the preview's $0.40–0.45 million engineering-services estimate and its $400,000 threshold for evidence of monetization. The combined sales also declined 8%, contrary to the preview's focus on quarter-after-quarter growth in OEM and waveguide revenue.
fact_evidence: “Engineering services and OEM product sales dropped 8% to $0.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Engineering services ... est. ~$0.40–0.45M”; “>$600K is the first genuine evidence the pivot is monetizing. <$400K means the defense wins are still press releases, not revenue”; management had promised OEM + waveguide revenue would “climb quarter after quarter throughout the year” in 2026.

description: The gross loss was $0.6 million, worse than the preview's expected $0.2–0.4 million loss and the $0.378 million loss in Q1. That missed the preview's anticipated continued narrowing, although the loss did improve year over year.
fact_evidence: “The Q2 2026 gross loss improved 15% to $0.6 million from a $0.8 million gross loss in the prior-year quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross profit ... n/a (est. $(0.2)–(0.4)M)”; “Gross loss narrowed ... to $(378)K in Q1”; “A near-breakeven or positive gross line is the single most bullish datapoint available in this print.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash burn rose to $6.6 million, above the preview's expected $5–6 million quarterly range and higher than the $5.6 million Q1 burn it cited.
fact_evidence: “Net cash used in operating activities rose to $6.6 million from $4.8 million a year earlier, an increase of $1.8 million in cash burn.”
expectation_evidence: “check it against a $5–6M quarterly burn”; the preview cited “Q1 operating burn of $5.6M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The $17.3 million cash balance was below the preview's base-case estimate of roughly $22–26 million and its suggestion that cash could print above $25 million after inferred ATM proceeds.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with $17.3 million in cash, approximately $18 million in net working capital, and no debt outstanding.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “cash ~$22–26M after ATM”; the preview also said cash “could therefore print up at ~$25M+” if inferred ATM issuance occurred.

description: Product sales were $0.9 million, below the preview's estimated $1.0–1.1 million and its expectation that sales holding around $1.0 million or more would be acceptable.
fact_evidence: “Product sales fell to $0.9 million from $1.0 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Product sales | n/a (est. ~$1.0–1.1M)”; “Product sales holding ~$1.0M+ is fine.”

description: Net loss attributable to common shareholders was $7.7 million, below the preview's roughly $8.9 million loss estimate. The per-share loss was $0.09, which the preview had already considered a likely mechanical outcome because of the higher share count.
fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common shareholders was flat at $7.7 million, though loss per share improved to $0.09 from $0.10 due to a larger share count.”
expectation_evidence: “Net loss | ~$(8.9)M at $(0.11)”; the preview also said a mechanical EPS beat “at $(0.09) to $(0.10) is the likelier outcome.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Vuzix disclosed new inbound interest in planar waveguides for optical interconnect in AI data centers, an opportunity the preview did not flag. The report describes interest, not orders or revenue, so the commercial significance is not yet established.
fact_evidence: “Vuzix disclosed new inbound interest in its planar waveguides for optical interconnect in AI data centers.”

description: The preview expected initial Q2 EVT-based Amazon Ultralite Pro shipments, but the reported facts do not confirm that shipments occurred or give a production timeline. The reported expansion to next-generation Ultralight Pro glasses for AI-driven data-center maintenance is favorable, but does not resolve the expected shipment milestone.
fact_evidence: “Its Amazon relationship expanded to next-generation Ultralight Pro smart glasses for AI-driven data center maintenance.” The reported facts provide no confirmation of EVT shipments or a production window.
expectation_evidence: “Management said Q2 would see initial EVT-based OEM shipments for AI/data-center support use cases”; the preview said a production window or unit commitment mattered.

description: Q2 revenue was $38 million, about $4–5 million below the preview’s $42–43 million expectation, despite being modestly above the prior-year quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose modestly to $38 million from $37.3 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue: “~$42–43M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $635,000, below the preview’s modeled $800,000–$1.0 million range, even though it more than tripled year over year.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $635,000 from $183,000.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$0.8–1.0M (no formal consensus).”

description: DHS awarded a six-month, $113 million-ceiling CWMS 2.5 bridge during the protest, providing a concrete continuity arrangement where the preview said no bridge had been publicly disclosed.
fact_evidence: “DHS awarded a six-month CWMS 2.5 bridge contract with a $113 million ceiling on August 6 to ensure business continuity and no ordering gaps during the protest period.”
expectation_evidence: “Nothing has been publicly disclosed about a stop-work order or a bridge extension”; the call “must confirm” whether “there [is] a bridge/extension in place.”

description: Management added a substantial longer-term CWMS 3.0 earnings opportunity: it expects about $150 million of additional annual managed-services/solutions work at an 8%–10% net profit margin, strengthening earnings once scaled by the end of 2028. The preview knew of the $3.1 billion award but did not quantify this incremental work or its expected margin.
fact_evidence: “The ~$150 million in additional annual CWMS 3.0 opportunity [is] concentrated in managed services/solutions work carrying an 8%-10% net profit margin,” with earnings strengthening “once fully scaled by end of 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the known “$3.1B DHS CWMS 3.0” award but did not state an incremental annual revenue or profit-margin expectation.

description: WidePoint disclosed several new near-term cost pressures: one-time CWMS 3.0 incentive payments, accelerated SEC filer compliance costs, and post-quantum cryptography capital investments. The preview did not flag these headwinds.
fact_evidence: Management “flagged upcoming one-time CWMS 3.0 incentive payments, accelerated SEC filer compliance costs, and post-quantum cryptography capital investments as near-term expense headwinds.”

description: The Chief Revenue Officer announced he will retire at year-end, an unanticipated leadership change after a decade with the company.
fact_evidence: “Chief Revenue Officer Jason Holloway announced his retirement at the end of the year after 10 years.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The carrier SaaS contract may have expansion beyond the expected federal deployment: management said state/local and Fortune 500 customers could potentially double the device count.
fact_evidence: The contract covers “2-2.5 million federal devices,” with “potential expansion into state/local and Fortune 500 clients possibly doubling device count.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the expected “~2.0–2.5M managed devices” and focused on the initial carrier deployment.

description: Xos reported only $4.7 million of Q2 revenue and delivered 30 units, far below the preview’s $14.30 million revenue consensus and estimated 90–130 deliveries. Management said multiple orders were deferred into future quarters.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell sharply to $4.7 million on 30 units delivered”; “multiple orders were deferred into future quarters.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $14.30M”; “Units delivered | n/a (est. 90–130).”

description: Q2 GAAP gross margin was 12.1%, well below the preview’s estimated 25–33% range and its roughly 30% validation threshold. The first-half margin was still a company-record 31%, but the Q2 result showed a sharp sequential deterioration.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross margin deteriorated sequentially to 12.1% GAAP (7.2% non-GAAP) from 38.9% GAAP (38.2% non-GAAP) in Q1”; “First-half 2026 GAAP gross margin reached a company-record 31%.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | n/a (est. 25–33%)”; “Anything above ~30% validates the ‘structural and durable’ cost-reduction claim; anything in the teens says Q1 was a mix accident.”

description: Xos cut its full-year revenue and unit-delivery outlook: revenue is now $35–43 million versus prior guidance of $40–50 million, and deliveries are 250–350 versus 350–500. The non-GAAP operating-loss range changed less substantially, widening from $11.9–13.3 million to $11.4–13.7 million.
fact_evidence: “Management cut full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $35-43 million, unit deliveries of 250-350 units, and non-GAAP operating loss of $11.4-13.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Standing guide: $40–50M revenue, 350–500 units, $11.9–13.3M non-GAAP operating loss.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended Q2 at $13.2 million, above the preview’s $9–12 million base-case range and above its $12 million bull-case marker. That was a better quarter-end liquidity outcome than the preview’s central expectation, though the facts do not state whether the going-concern language changed.
fact_evidence: “The company closed Q2 with $13.2 million in cash, up about 35% from $9.8 million at Q1-end.”

description: Xos used $2.2 million of its ATM in addition to the registered direct offering, raising total net proceeds of $7.6 million. The preview had flagged possible ATM use and dilution, but did not expect or quantify an ATM draw in its central setup.
fact_evidence: “Raising $7.6 million net via a $2.2 million ATM offering and $5.4 million registered direct offering.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch also the remaining ATM capacity — $5.4M authorized as of the Q1 filing. If the ATM was drawn during Q2 ... dilution is worse than the share count implies.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Xos produced a record 29 energy-storage hubs in Q2, but some remained in the factory awaiting pickup and therefore were not counted as deliveries. The production record is positive, while the pickup timing limits how much it explains the weak reported quarter.
fact_evidence: “Produced a record 29 hubs in Q2, though not all counted as deliveries since some remain in the factory awaiting pickup.”
expectation_evidence: “What matters: does management quantify a Hub backlog or pipeline in dollars for the first time?”

description: The preview highlighted a quantified Hub backlog or data-center pipeline as a key potential catalyst, but the facts provided report no dollar backlog or pipeline figure. The call instead gives deployment and production measures, leaving that key commercial visibility question unanswered.
fact_evidence: The call facts report “over 250 MWh of energy storage deployed” and “a record 29 hubs in Q2,” but give no quantified Hub backlog or pipeline.
expectation_evidence: “What matters: does management quantify a Hub backlog or pipeline in dollars for the first time?”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The launched PowerHub flagship is described as a 3.1 MWh unit delivering 1.5 MW of continuous AC power, compared with the preview’s description of a 2.5 MWh Power Hub. The larger stated flagship capacity is a product-specification upgrade, although the preview had already anticipated the launch.
fact_evidence: “Xos launched its PowerHub battery energy storage line in June, featuring a flagship 3.1 MWh unit delivering 1.5 MW of continuous AC power.”
expectation_evidence: “The 2.5MWh Power Hub launched June 2 (1.2–4.0 MWh range).”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Full system-level UL certification remains incomplete: one standard is expected within weeks, while others may slip into 2027. The preview did not flag certification timing as an issue; management said it is not currently gating customer deliveries.
fact_evidence: “Full UL system-level certification is incomplete, with one standard expected within weeks and others potentially slipping into 2027, though management says this is not gating customer deliveries.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Xos reported that Bluebird has ordered more than 100 powertrains since the partnership began in Q2 2025, and identified Bluebird’s acquisition of a Detroit Chassis facility with roughly 20,000 units of annual capacity as a potential future growth opportunity. The preview focused on Bluebird concentration and looked for a second named OEM, rather than highlighting this added customer-side capacity opportunity.
fact_evidence: “Bluebird has ordered over 100 powertrains since the partnership launched in Q2 2025”; its Detroit Chassis facility has “capacity ~20,000 units/year” and “represents a potential future EV powertrain growth opportunity for Xos.”
expectation_evidence: “63 of Q1's 95 units were Bluebird school-bus powertrains”; “Watch for a second named OEM.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Xos said Q2 hub cells and packs are sourced domestically from its Illinois facility to meet U.S. content requirements for defense and other customers. This sourcing detail and its relevance to defense requirements were not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Q2 hub cells and packs are sourced domestically from Goshen's Illinois facility to meet U.S. content requirements for defense and other customers.”

description: Innventure reported only $1.0 million of Q2 revenue, far below the preview’s $3.42 million consensus and roughly $3 million implied Accelsius contribution. Accelsius generated just $0.9 million, and consolidated revenue fell from $1.4 million in Q1.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenue was $1 million,” with “Accelsius contributing 96% ($0.9 million).”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 consensus” revenue was “$3.42M”; the preview said the implied path was “roughly Q2 ~$3M.”

description: Management went beyond the preview’s possible target reframe: it suspended all Accelsius revenue targets and pushed expected breakeven beyond 2026. The preview described a softer “entering 2027” target as a likely risk, but not the withdrawal of all targets.
fact_evidence: “Management suspended all Accelsius revenue targets” and “no longer expects it to exit this year near cash flow breakeven at a ~$100 million annualized run rate, extending breakeven beyond 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether the December target was “reaffirmed, softened, or reframed,” and identified “run rate entering 2027” as a likely reframe.

description: Innventure abandoned its goal of consolidated positive cash flow by 2028, an additional setback beyond the delayed Accelsius target. The preview did not anticipate the company withdrawing this longer-term consolidated goal.
fact_evidence: “Innventure abandoned its prior goal of consolidated positive cash flow by 2028 due to Accelsius's delayed path to profitability.”

description: The DarkNX purchase order was removed from the 2026 forecast after the customer lost its development site, with transfer to another location uncertain. The preview had flagged the DarkNX campus as something to monitor but did not anticipate the order dropping out of the forecast.
fact_evidence: “The DarkNX purchase order was removed from the 2026 forecast after the customer lost its development site due to power envelope constraints,” and a transfer to an alternate location is on “an uncertain timeline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “progress on the DarkNX 300MW Ontario campus” among the items to watch.

description: Management signaled that further dilutive capital raises may be needed in the second half, adding financing pressure. However, the roughly $13 million already raised at an average $6.21 was at a much higher price than the preview’s anticipated sub-$4 SEPA draws, making that completed issuance less dilutive than expected.
fact_evidence: “Accelsius raised approximately $13 million through its standby equity purchase agreement at an average price of $6.21,” and Dave “signaled potential additional dilutive capital raises in the second half of the year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to expect “continued SEPA draws at sub-$4” in its base case and warned that raising capital at the current $3.69 price would be more dilutive.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: A third-party benchmark showed materially better NeuCool cold-plate performance than the preview had any evidence to expect: cooler GPUs with substantially less coolant flow and a higher viable facility-water temperature. This is positive technical validation, though the preview had emphasized that Accelsius had not disclosed unit economics or demonstrated the ramp in revenue.
fact_evidence: The benchmark showed GPUs running “9–14°C cooler” using “roughly one-third of the coolant flow,” extending viable facility water temperatures from “~45°C to 54°C and beyond.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Accelsius is now focusing on large hyperscalers, whose two-to-three-year adoption cycles leave no visibility into 2027 revenue. That shifts the commercial focus toward slower-cycle customers and adds a longer-term visibility concern beyond the preview’s focus on near-term shipments and backlog conversion.
fact_evidence: “Accelsius is now targeting large hyperscalers rather than small early adopters,” but “hyperscaler adoption cycles run two to three years, making 2027 revenue visibility unavailable.”
expectation_evidence: The preview focused on whether “any HyperStart-program hyperscaler has converted to a purchase order” and whether Q2 backlog was converting to shipments.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The two-phase market forecast was raised to $9 billion by 2030, a favorable market-size update that the preview had not anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The two-phase market forecast raised to $9 billion by 2030.”

description: Revenue was $12.3 million, below the preview’s $13.29–$13.70 million consensus range and even below its $12.5 million bear-case threshold. The preview’s revenue expectation was therefore meaningfully missed.
fact_evidence: “Revenue declined about 14% to $12.3 million in Q2 2026 from $14.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $13.29M (MarketBeat) / $13.70M (Investing.com)” and the bear case was “Revenue | <$12.5M.”

description: Industrial Assets produced only about $600,000 of operating income, well below the preview’s $1.2 million Q1 run-rate reference despite the preview describing Q2 as seasonally the strongest quarter. Smaller deals and the absence of larger auctions weighed on results; consolidated adjusted EBITDA also fell to $1.2 million from $2.8 million a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “The Industrial Assets Division's operating income fell to roughly $600,000 in Q2 2026 from $1.3 million a year earlier, hurt by an absence of larger auctions and prevalence of smaller-scale deals”; “adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.2 million from $2.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 run-rate was Industrial $1.2M + Financial Assets $1.0M − DebtX $(0.6)M” and “Q2 is seasonally the strongest quarter.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Ending ARR was $11.6 million, far below the preview’s roughly $15.8 million estimate and below the $15.9 million year-ago level. The preview expected a modest sequential recovery; instead, a June contract reduction helped drive another substantial decline.
fact_evidence: “Ending ARR fell to $11.6 million” from $15.9 million a year ago, including “a $2.6 million contract reduction in June 2026,” partially offset by $1.5 million of net ARR growth.
expectation_evidence: “My estimates (base): … ARR $15.8M”; the preview also identified “Ending ARR vs. $15.9M” as the key metric and described a base case of “$15.6–16.1M.”

description: Management withdrew its original goal of significant ARR growth by year-end 2026, rather than reaffirming it or providing the quantified ARR target the preview said investors were looking for. The preview expected the goal might be repeated without detail, not withdrawn.
fact_evidence: “Management withdrew its original target for significant ARR growth by year-end 2026,” citing the contract reduction, no committed upsell, and limited time remaining.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “repeatedly promised ‘significant ARR growth’ in 2026” and described the base case as “‘significant ARR growth’ repeated without quantification.”

description: Subscription revenue was $3.7 million, $0.6 million below the preview’s $4.3 million estimate. The reported decline was larger than expected and was attributed to the expired contract.
fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue dropping $900,000 to $3.7 million” due to the expired October 2025 contract.
expectation_evidence: “My estimates (base): Revenue $7.2M (subscription $4.3M, service $2.9M).”

description: Service revenue came in at $3.6 million, $0.7 million above the preview’s $2.9 million estimate, offsetting some of the subscription shortfall.
fact_evidence: Service revenue “increased $300,000 to $3.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: “My estimates (base): Revenue $7.2M (subscription $4.3M, service $2.9M).”

description: Total revenue of $7.4 million modestly exceeded the preview’s $7.09–$7.32 million consensus range and $7.2 million base estimate, despite the subscription miss.
fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue” was $7.4 million.
expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$7.09M … / $7.32M”; the preview’s base estimate was “Revenue $7.2M.”

description: GAAP loss per share widened to $0.54, substantially worse than the preview’s roughly $0.33 loss estimate. The call attributed much of the loss to stock-based compensation and severance for the former CEO.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss per diluted share widened to $0.54” from $0.38, largely due to “$5.4 million of stock-based compensation and $700,000 of severance for the former CEO.”
expectation_evidence: Consensus EPS was “–$0.33”; the preview’s GAAP EPS estimate was “–$0.31.”

description: On the non-GAAP basis, loss per share was $0.08, better than the preview’s $0.10–$0.15 expected loss and its $0.12 base estimate.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net loss per share improved to $0.08 from $0.11.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “non-GAAP EPS –$0.12” and said the comparable was closer to “–$0.10 to –$0.15.”

description: Secure gift card revenue is now not expected to add anything for the rest of 2026, including the holiday season, and meaningful ARR growth has shifted to late Q4 2026 or early Q1 2027. The preview already knew one large rollout had moved to January 2027, but was watching for retailer conversions before the holidays; the lack of any committed 2026 revenue is a further setback.
fact_evidence: “Meaningful gift card ARR growth has been deferred a few quarters to late Q4 2026/early Q1 2027”; there is “no incremental gift card revenue committed for the balance of 2026 including the holiday season.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the pipeline would “convert to signed orders before holiday season” and called a “second slip” the highest-probability bear catalyst.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Secure gift card demand showed more concrete traction than the preview had established: the pipeline grew more than 30-fold, two more retailers committed to deployments, and the previously postponed retailer will run a smaller pilot in September. That adds near-term activity even though broad revenue contribution remains delayed.
fact_evidence: The pipeline grew “over 30x” to “more than 31 large and midsized retailers”; “two additional retailers have committed” to deploy, and the postponed retailer will start a smaller pilot in September.
expectation_evidence: The preview described a pipeline of “15 North American retailers / 8 of top 20 by sales” and asked whether it would convert to signed orders before the holiday season.

description: The company is planning a capital raise and expects to use over 90% of proceeds to build go-to-market teams and programs. The preview already noted the $17.5 million ATM, but did not anticipate this specific allocation of proceeds toward rebuilding commercial capacity.
fact_evidence: With “only $8.8 million in cash and short-term investments and no debt,” the company is “planning a capital raise with over 90% of proceeds earmarked for building out go-to-market teams and programs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Digimarc had put “a $17.5M ATM in place” and expected approximately “$8.5M at 6/30 ex-ATM.”

description: The new CEO has moved quickly to add commercial leadership, hiring a VP of Retail Solutions in addition to the CRO already noted in the preview, with the full senior team expected by the end of Q3. This is more concrete organizational action than the preview’s expectation that the CEO might still be assessing the business.
fact_evidence: The CEO was “only 30 days into the role” and had “already hired a Chief Revenue Officer and a VP of Retail Solutions,” with the full senior leadership team expected by the end of Q3 2026.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the realistic outcome was “‘I’m 5 weeks in, plan at a later date’” and asked whether rebuilding the sales organization would push costs back up; it noted the CRO had already been hired.

description: Digimarc is narrowing its direct commercial focus to retail and CPG and shifting several other verticals to a partner-led approach. The preview did not flag this change in go-to-market scope.
fact_evidence: The company is “narrowing its commercial focus to retail and CPG” while shifting pharma, life sciences, media, technology, and government “to a partner-led approach.”

description: The preview expected management to reaffirm FY2026 revenue guidance of at least $50 million; instead, management declined to reaffirm it, citing timing shifts in an international 5G deployment. It said no backlog orders had been canceled, but the guidance stance was materially weaker than expected.
fact_evidence: “Management declined to reaffirm its prior full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $50 million, citing timing shifts in an international 5G deployment, while insisting no backlog orders have been canceled.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue guidance of ‘at least $50 million’” and “Watch for the exact construction. ‘Reaffirm at least $50 million’ is one outcome.”

description: Q2 gross margin was 27.9%, well below the preview's 42% estimate and 40–44% base-case range. It also fell sharply from Q1's roughly 48% as product mix shifted, despite the large year-over-year improvement.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross margin expanded to 27.9% from 7.8% in Q2 2025 … but sequentially margin fell from roughly 48% in Q1 to 28% due to product mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026E … Gross margin … 42%” and the base scenario expected “GM … 40–44%.”

description: The loss was much larger than the preview's operating model implied: it estimated about $4.4 million of quarterly opex and a $0.37 million net loss, while the company reported roughly $3.09 million of net loss. SG&A nearly doubled and R&D more than doubled, including substantial 5G development spending.
fact_evidence: “The company posted a Q2 operating loss of approximately $3.2 million and a net loss of approximately $3.09 million, driven by deliberate investments ahead of revenue”; “SG&A expenses nearly doubled to about $4.08 million … while R&D more than doubled to $1.37 million (of which $1.08 million was 5G development).”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Opex (implied) … ~$4.4M” and “Net income … –$0.37M.”

description: The preview's own Q2 revenue estimate was $9.0 million, with a base-case range of $8.5–10 million; actual revenue was $8.1 million, slightly below that build. It was nevertheless essentially in line with the $8.0 million consensus estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $8.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026E (base) … Revenue … $9.0M” and the base scenario expected “Revenue … $8.5–10M”; consensus was “$8.00M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Orders from the customer associated with the original $40 million LOI have already exceeded that LOI's amount, a stronger cumulative conversion update than the preview's specific expectation of more than $6 million in July follow-on orders.
fact_evidence: “The company received $6 million in follow-on purchase orders in July 2026 alone, and stated its original $40 million LOI has already been exceeded in orders from the same customer.”
expectation_evidence: “July added >$6M in follow-on orders (~$4M under the North American MNO LOI, ~$2M other).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview expected roughly $36–38 million of pro forma cash after the Series A proceeds; the reported June 30 cash and marketable securities plus the July net proceeds total about $33 million. The gross rights proceeds were close to the preview's expected subscription amount, but net proceeds and the resulting pro forma total were lower.
fact_evidence: “The July 2026 exercise of Series A rights generated approximately $21.92 million gross and $20.12 million net proceeds, adding to the roughly $13 million cash/marketable securities … at June 30.”
expectation_evidence: “Series A rights closed at ~$21.9M in subscriptions” and “Pro forma cash should be ~$36–38M.”

description: Q2 net sales were $2.4 million, below the preview’s roughly $3.0–$3.1 million expectation. The shortfall reflected a $0.7 million Simpliderm decline tied to a contract-manufacturer disruption, partly offset by a $0.4 million cardiovascular gain as Elutia returned to direct sales.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales of $2.4 million”; a “$0.7 million decline in Simpliderm (from a contract manufacturer production disruption)” was “partially offset” by a “$0.4 million cardiovascular gain from returning to direct sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue (as-reported basis) ~ $3.0M”; the base-case model expected “Revenue $3.1M (SimpliDerm $2.1M + Cardio $1.0M).”

description: Elutia secured a new $15 million Avenue Capital credit facility, with $10 million already received, and said its current and projected cash sources total about $54 million, supporting a runway through at least 2028. That is materially stronger funding visibility than the preview’s tight-runway assessment and expectation of no new capital in the base case, although some proceeds depend on future milestones or transactions.
fact_evidence: The company secured “up to $26 million in new capital without an equity offering,” including a “$15 million Avenue Capital credit facility ($10 million already received).” It reported “about $54 million” in current and projected cash sources, providing “runway through at least 2028”; another “$5 million” from Avenue is available upon NXT 41X clearance.
expectation_evidence: The preview described total liquidity of “~$44.5M” as covering “roughly five to six quarters” and “tight, not comfortable,” and its base case assumed “no new capital raised.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Despite the improved financing outlook, quarter-end cash was below the preview’s expected range: $19.9 million versus an estimated $22–24 million. This is a negative cash-balance variance even though the newly disclosed financing and sale proceeds improve the forward runway picture.
fact_evidence: “Elutia ended the quarter with $19.9 million in cash.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Cash 6/30 ~$22–24M”; its catalyst checklist used “~$23M” as the reference point.

description: Adjusted gross margin reached 70.7%, up 8 percentage points year over year, a favorable result not anticipated in the preview’s margin estimate. GAAP gross margin of 59.6%, by contrast, was within the preview’s expected range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 8 percentage points to 70.7% from 62.7%, while GAAP gross margin rose to 59.6% from 52.9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case model estimated “GAAP GM ~58–60%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported unusually strong stated interest in NXT 41X from a blinded survey of 50 board-certified plastic surgeons, including willingness to champion it at hospitals and use it for high-risk patients. The preview did not flag this survey evidence, which adds favorable product-adoption commentary beyond the expected regulatory timeline.
fact_evidence: In a survey of 50 surgeons, “96% expressed interest in adopting NXT 41X,” “92% said they would champion it at their hospital’s value analysis committee,” and “100% would use it for high-risk patients.”

description: Elutia said its in-house facility could support at least $300 million of revenue capacity when NXT 41X launches, with further expansion requiring only more personnel and shifts, and targeted gross margins above 80% at scale. The preview did not include these manufacturing-capacity or scaled-margin claims.
fact_evidence: The company expects “at least $300 million of revenue capacity at NXT 41X launch” from its Gaithersburg GMP facility, says further expansion requires “only added personnel and shifts,” and “targets gross margins above 80% at scale.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview estimated Q2 cash at $6–8 million and flagged a balance below $5 million as a major concern; CXAI reported $11.7 million at June 30. The reported cash balance was well above the preview’s estimate.
fact_evidence: “The company held $11.7 million in cash as of June 30, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Est. Q2 exit cash $6–8M — verify”; “Anything below ~$5M forces another raise.”

description: The preview emphasized that investors needed organic revenue disclosed separately, but the reported facts give only total Q2 revenue and no organic-versus-EngineRoom breakdown. That leaves the preview’s central question about the health of CXAI’s standalone business unanswered.
fact_evidence: The reported Q2 revenue is given as “about $1.7 million”; no organic revenue figure is provided in the reported facts.
expectation_evidence: “Organic (ex-EngineRoom) revenue” was ranked the top metric to watch; “a company confident in its core will break it out.”

description: The preview said a reverse-split ratio and effective date were a critical near-term catalyst, with silence on the ratio described as bearish. No ratio or effective date is reported in the call facts.
fact_evidence: The reported call facts contain no reverse-split ratio or effective-date announcement.
expectation_evidence: “Silence on the ratio today is a meaningfully bearish signal”; “the split must be effective on or about Aug 24, 2026.”

description: CXAI set breakeven for the second half of 2027. The preview called for a dated target and cited H1 2027 as the breakeven timing in its bull scenario, so the target is specific but later than that optimistic benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Management targets breakeven in the second half of 2027 followed by profitable growth.”
expectation_evidence: The bull scenario called for a “credible EBITDA-breakeven date (H1'27)”; the preview also said the path-to-profitability discussion needed “a quarter, not a direction.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CXAI reported ARR of $11.5 million, up from $3.6 million quarter over quarter and 156% year over year from $4.5 million. The preview focused on reported revenue and acquisition run-rate rather than this substantially higher recurring-revenue figure.
fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue jumped from $3.6 million to $11.5 million quarter-over-quarter, a 156% year-over-year increase from $4.5 million.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: A new three-year multimillion-dollar financial-services contract came through a competitive RFP, alongside renewals from two Fortune 500 customers; management said new enterprise wins are expected to add roughly one-third to revenue. The preview expected Q1 enterprise bookings to begin converting but did not anticipate these specific wins or the stated uplift.
fact_evidence: “The company signed a new 3-year multimillion-dollar financial services deal via competitive RFP and secured renewals from two Fortune 500 customers, with new enterprise wins expected to add roughly one-third revenue uplift.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1’s “$5M TCV across three 3-year enterprise deals should begin converting.”

description: Operating expenses rose only 5.6% while revenue grew 79% sequentially, a favorable divergence that the preview did not forecast. Cash EBITDA remained negative, but improved modestly from Q1.
fact_evidence: “Cash EBITDA improved modestly to negative $2.68 million in Q2 from negative $3 million in Q1, while operating expenses rose only 5.6% against 79% revenue growth.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CXAI reported NRR of 99.3%, up from the preview’s Q1 reference of 98%. The improvement is positive, though relatively small.
fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention improving to 99.3%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “NRR 98%” as the Q1 FY26 reference and called its trend a key quality signal.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call reported Sky 2.0 entering production deployment, the Events module reaching general availability in September, and BEAT expected to launch in Q4. The preview did not flag these product milestones; their financial impact was not quantified in the reported facts.
fact_evidence: “Sky 2.0 moved into production deployment, a new Events module reaches general availability in September, and the personal productivity product BEAT is expected to launch in Q4.”

description: Caliber’s platform adjusted EBITDA reached about $0.3 million of profit, better than the preview’s expectation of breakeven or near breakeven and the base case of a small loss.
fact_evidence: “Platform adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $0.3 million,” improving about $0.4 million from a $0.1 million loss a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: “The buy-side's real bar” was “breakeven or better”; the base scenario expected “-$0.1 to -$0.3M.”

description: Platform revenue fell to $3.7 million, missing the preview’s $4 million-or-more bar. The shortfall came as development and construction fees were pushed to later periods, rather than arriving in Q2 as the preview’s Steamboat financing thesis anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Platform revenue declined approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million from $4.1 million,” driven by “the timing of project financings shifting to later periods.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side bar was “platform revenue ≥ $4M” and identified the Steamboat financing, which “closed in April 2026,” as the “single most likely source of an upside surprise.”

description: Caliber sold far more LINK during the quarter than the preview’s prior-quarter sale suggested, ending Q2 with fewer than half the Q1-end tokens. The sale generated $2.5 million for redeployment into real estate, but the scale of the reduction was not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company sold approximately 278,357 LINK tokens for $2.5 million in proceeds during the quarter” and held “229,204 LINK tokens valued at $1.7 million at quarter-end,” redeploying capital into its real estate platform.
expectation_evidence: The preview reported “507,560 LINK tokens” at Q1-end and noted that “~55,000 tokens were sold in Q1 for $0.5M”; it flagged the June 30 mark as a swing factor but did not anticipate a comparable Q2 sale.

description: Platform expenses rose despite lower platform revenue, with additional bad-debt reserves on uncollectible development and construction fees contributing to the increase. The preview did not flag this cost or collection pressure.
fact_evidence: “Platform expenses rose approximately 11% to $5.9 million from $5.3 million,” primarily due to “increased bad debt charges from additional reserves on uncollectible development and construction fees.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The call disclosed a sizable near-term maturity burden among unsecured notes: $21 million of roughly $26 million principal comes due within 12 months. Refinancing and conversions provide some relief, but the preview had not identified this specific maturity schedule.
fact_evidence: Caliber had “148 unsecured notes totaling ~$26 million principal, of which $21 million matures within 12 months,” and had refinanced $6.4 million into a 36-month program and converted about $5.3 million into equity through August 13.

description: Caliber reported additional hotel-platform activity not anticipated in the preview: a pipeline of eight CHT acquisition assets, six hotels moved to an owner-centric model, and purchase of a Hyatt Studios site near the planned TSMC investment. The pipeline includes only one asset under an executed letter of intent, so much of the reported pipeline is not yet a completed acquisition.
fact_evidence: The company “grew its CHT hotel acquisition pipeline to eight assets with one under executed letter of intent,” “transitioned six hotels to a new owner-centric management model,” and “purchased a 2.5-acre Hyatt Studios site near TSMC's $265 billion Phoenix semiconductor investment.”

description: HIT reaffirmed its $45–50 million FY2026 revenue guidance rather than trimming it, as the preview expected investors to fear. The company cited contracted and pipeline revenue metrics in support of the range.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $45 million to $50 million, supported by contracted and pipeline revenue metrics.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy-side expects a cut”; the preview’s base case said “FY guide trimmed to ~$40–45M or steered ‘toward the low end,’” and its bear case expected a cut or withdrawal.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The amount of contracted revenue expected in the second half was only $14 million, well below the preview’s >$25 million benchmark for contracted revenue remaining in 2026. The reported pipeline was $66.3 million, but $64.4 million was not yet contracted and carried only a 15%–40% expected conversion rate.
fact_evidence: “Contracted revenue totaled $32.3 million for the first half of 2026, with $17.3 million already recognized, $14 million expected in the second half, and $1 million in 2027.” The pipeline was “$66.3 million as of July 31,” with “the remaining $64.4 million” carrying a “15%-40% expected conversion rate.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “> $25M” in contracted revenue remaining in 2026 and said this was “the single cleanest” measure of whether new business was landing.

description: Q2 revenue was $8.1 million, below the preview’s $9.3 million estimate and its $9.0–10.5 million base-case range; revenue also fell 13.5% year over year rather than being roughly flat. It did beat the preview’s low-confidence $7.55 million consensus, but the preview had already described a beat versus that figure as likely.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP revenue fell 13.5% year-over-year to $8.1 million from $9.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 revenue estimate is $9.3M, roughly flat YoY”; the base scenario forecast “$9.0–10.5M” and said “a headline revenue beat versus $7.55M is the high-probability outcome.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash was $6.5 million, well below the preview’s expectation of more than $9 million. The sharp rise in AR days to 55 from 20 also disclosed a collection-timing strain associated with the carrier transition that the preview had not quantified.
fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents declined to $6.5 million from $8.1 million a year ago, while AR days rose sharply to 55 days in the first half from 20 days in the prior-year period due to the carrier transition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s cash metric said “Loss narrowing; cash >$9M” and flagged $10.3 million of Q1 cash.

description: Management said the switch to an A-rated stop-loss carrier, expected within 30 days, could lift projections by 20%–30% by opening access to large brokerages that require A-rated carriers. The preview did not anticipate this potential source of a substantial increase in projections.
fact_evidence: “The company is switching to an A-rated stop-loss carrier, expected within 30 days,” which management believes “could lift projections by 20% to 30%” by unlocking business from large “alpha” brokerages.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The distribution network reached 933 partners, short of the preview’s >950 “good looks” threshold. The reported 19.9% year-over-year growth was also consistent with the preview’s concern that partner growth was decelerating.
fact_evidence: “The distribution partner network grew 19.9% year-over-year to 933 brokers, TPAs and agencies from 778.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “>950” partners would be good and noted growth was “Decelerating from +87% YoY (Q2'25) and +34% (Q4'25).”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: HIT said its HitRix large-group stop-loss marketplace would launch within 2–3 weeks. The preview did not flag this near-term launch as a catalyst.
fact_evidence: “The company plans to launch its HitRix large-group stop-loss marketplace within 2-3 weeks.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported an anticipated pipeline of roughly 30 monthly submissions from municipalities and government agencies for the rate-stabilization program, a specific prospective source of activity not identified in the preview.
fact_evidence: The company “secured its first employer group under its 3-year rate stabilization program, with an anticipated pipeline of roughly 30 submissions per month from municipalities and government agencies.”

description: LIVE reported diluted EPS of -$0.34, well below the preview’s modeled -$0.03, and swung to a $1.1 million net loss. The loss was materially deeper than the near-breakeven result the model anticipated.
fact_evidence: The company swung to a net loss of approximately $1.1 million (loss per share of $0.34) versus net income of $5.4 million and diluted EPS of $1.24 in the prior year period.
expectation_evidence: Diluted EPS: Q3 FY2026 est. ~$(0.03).

description: Retail-Flooring revenue fell to $21.4 million, below the preview’s $23.4 million estimate, and its year-over-year decline was steeper than the model’s expected decline. The segment’s deterioration was worse than the already-weak trajectory the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: Retail-Flooring segment revenue fell 29.4% to $21.4 million due to continued weakness in new home construction and home refurbishment markets.
expectation_evidence: Retail-Flooring Q3 FY2026 estimated revenue: $23.4M; Q3 FY2025 revenue: $30.4M.

description: Operating income was $5.3 million, above the preview’s $3.8 million model estimate, despite declining 34% year over year. The reported result was substantially better than the forecasted year-over-year decline of 53%.
fact_evidence: Operating income decreased 34% to $5.3 million from $8 million, hurt by lower gross profit and higher operating expenses.
expectation_evidence: Operating income: Q3 FY2026 est. ~$3.8M, YoY –53%.

description: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $9.3 million, above the preview’s $7.8 million estimate. Its 29.5% year-over-year decline was also less severe than the model’s expected 41% decline.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA dropped 29.5% (about $3.9 million) to $9.3 million, down from $13.2 million a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA: Q3 FY2026 est. ~$7.8M, YoY –41%.

description: Steel Manufacturing revenue reached $36.3 million, above the preview’s $33.0 million estimate, while operating income surged 68.9% against a model that estimated $1.4 million of operating income. The segment performed considerably better than the preview’s expectation that Steel would stabilize around that level.
fact_evidence: Steel Manufacturing segment revenue rose 7.3% to $36.3 million, with operating income surging 68.9% and adjusted EBITDA up 16.3%.
expectation_evidence: Steel Mfg Q3 FY2026 estimated revenue / operating income: $33.0M / $1.4M. The base case said, “Steel returns to ~$1.5M operating income.”

description: Gross margin improved to 34.1% rather than declining to the preview’s estimated 33.5%. Gross profit still fell, but the margin result was better than the expected 50-basis-point year-over-year contraction.
fact_evidence: Gross margin improved slightly by 10 basis points to 34.1%, while gross profit declined 3.1% to $37.1 million.
expectation_evidence: Gross margin: Q3 FY2026 est. ~33.5%, YoY –50 bps.

description: Q2 sales of $41.3 million exceeded the preview’s $34–37 million estimate and its $38 million bull-case threshold. The preview cautioned that published consensus was stale, but the result also came in well above its own bottom-up forecast.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales surged 244% year-over-year to $41.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “My estimate: $34–37M”; the bull scenario projected “$38M+.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $3.0 million, above the preview’s $0.5–1.5 million base estimate and above its bull-case threshold of $2.5 million. It reached the low end of the quarterly pace the preview said was needed to support the full-year guide.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA jumped to $3.0 million in Q2 2026 from just $0.1 million a year earlier,” reflecting acquired-business contributions and early synergy realization.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “$0.5–1.5M” in its base case and said “EBITDA ≥$2.5M” in the bull case; it also said the full-year guide required “~$3.0–4.4M per quarter” across Q2–Q4.

description: Management reaffirmed the entire $138–148 million sales and $8–12 million adjusted EBITDA ranges rather than narrowing EBITDA toward the low end. The CFO also said she would be personally disappointed if revenue finished below the guidance midpoint, a more confident stance than the preview’s expectation of a low-end outcome.
fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $138 million to $148 million in net sales and $8 million to $12 million in adjusted EBITDA”; the CFO said she “would be personally disappointed if full-year revenue lands below the midpoint of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected revenue guidance to be “Reaffirm at low end” and projected to “Narrow toward $8M” for adjusted EBITDA.

description: The preview expected low-to-mid-30s gross margins in the second half, with commodity relief and tariff refunds as potential support. Management instead described low-30s as the appropriate go-forward range, indicating that a meaningful margin recovery should not be assumed even though Q2’s 30.3% was within the preview’s estimated range.
fact_evidence: “Management flagged low-30s% as the appropriate go-forward gross margin range,” reflecting the confirmed lower profitability of Terrasoul.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “low-to-mid 30s in H2 on commodity relief and tariff refunds,” and estimated Q2 gross margin at “30–33%.”

description: GAAP net loss was substantially worse than the preview’s EPS range, despite the strong adjusted EBITDA result. The reported loss included sizeable business-combination and integration costs and intangible amortization.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $1.8 million (-$0.25 per share) from $0.4 million (-$0.03) a year ago,” driven by “$3.5 million of business combination/integration costs and $1.1 million of intangible amortization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave a GAAP EPS estimate of “-$0.05 to +$0.02” and cited consensus of “-$0.033.”

description: The Walmart launch was in more than 1,000 stores, but essentially all of its revenue contribution is expected in Q3 and Q4. That pushes the sales impact later than the preview’s expectation that the new distribution would start showing up in the current results.
fact_evidence: “The company launched 5 coffee and creamer SKUs into more than 1,000 Walmart stores nationwide, with essentially all revenue impact expected in Q3 and Q4 rather than Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Walmart distribution “should start showing up” and included the new Walmart/Target distribution in its discussion of the expected second-half step-up.

description: Management reported early synergy realization from the acquisitions, a positive development against the preview’s expectation that operational integration and production shifts would occur later.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA growth reflected “early synergy realization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said production shifting to Terrasoul’s facility was expected “later in 2026 or beyond,” and that “any pull-forward is a genuine positive.”

description: Revenue was $191.3 million, about 3.2% below the $197.7 million consensus and down 14% year over year, a steeper decline than the preview’s expected 11.1% decline. The result also missed the preview’s expected slight sequential increase.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $191.3 million, down 14% year-over-year on a pro forma basis.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 consensus $197.70M … Implied Δ −11.1% YoY, +0.3% QoQ.”

description: Normalized EBITDA reached $21.9 million, well above the preview’s $17–19 million base case and the $15.6 million level it said the quarter needed to exceed. It also rose 8.4% year over year, rather than merely improving sequentially as management had committed.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 normalized EBITDA reached $21.9 million, up 8.4% year-over-year and 40.6% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Normalized EBITDA (must be > $15.6M)” and the base case was “$17–19M”; management had committed to EBITDA “increasing in Q2.”

description: Adjusted gross margin reached a record 24.9%, above the preview’s 23.3–24.0% base-case range and its 24.5% bull-case threshold. The fourth consecutive quarterly expansion itself was expected, but the margin level exceeded those expectations.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded for the fourth consecutive quarter to a record 24.9%, up 290 basis points year-over-year and 140 basis points sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “23.3–24.0%” and its bull case was “24.5%+”; it also asked whether gross margin would achieve a “4th straight expansion.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: New ACV bookings rose to $36 million, beating the preview’s $32 million bull-case marker and reversing the prior quarter’s 3.7% year-over-year decline. Total contract value also increased to $121.3 million from Q1’s $108.1 million.
fact_evidence: “New ACV bookings reached $36 million, up 57% year-over-year and 32.1% sequentially, while total contract value closed at $121.3 million, up 51.6% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch new ACV “vs. the ~$27–30M trailing average,” noted Q1 new ACV was “$27.3M (−3.7%),” and set “new ACV >$32M” as a bull-case marker.

description: Technology revenue grew 9.8% year over year and its adjusted gross margin expanded to 64.2%, sharply better than the preview’s concern that the segment’s 26.4% Q1 revenue decline might continue. This also materially strengthens the segment’s performance relative to the preview’s discussion of it as a possible divestiture candidate.
fact_evidence: “The technology segment grew revenue 9.8% year-over-year to $24.5 million with adjusted gross margin expanding 690 basis points to 64.2%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Technology had “Q1: $18.7M, −26.4%, 52.4% GM” and warned that “a −26% decline there undercuts” the separate-asset thesis.

description: Applied Workflow Automation revenue fell 16.7%, a steeper decline than its 12.6% Q1 decline and beyond the preview’s 14% decline marker for its bear case. That indicates greater weakness in the segment the preview identified as the main source of revenue declines.
fact_evidence: “The applied workflow automation segment revenue fell 16.7% to $166.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited AWA’s “Q1: $178.4M, −12.6%” and defined the bear case as an “AWA decline steepens past −14%.”

description: Management raised its annualized operational-efficiency target to $65–75 million from $55–60 million and projected about $35 million of benefit during 2026. The higher target was an improvement beyond the cost-savings program the preview described.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its targeted annualized operational efficiency range to $65-75 million (up from $55-60 million), with an expected in-year 2026 benefit of approximately $35 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$55–60M annualized target” and said roughly half was implemented but “not yet visible in the P&L.”

description: The strategic-alternatives process advanced to hiring a financial advisor. The preview wanted evidence that the process was active, including bankers being named, but reported no news since the May announcement.
fact_evidence: Management “has engaged a financial advisor for its previously announced strategic alternatives process.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted “evidence of a live process — bankers named, a signed LOI, or a disposal of the Technology segment,” and noted “No timeline given, no news since.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported sales pipeline was $2.5 billion, up 17.2% year over year. The preview focused on bookings but did not discuss or set an expectation for pipeline size.
fact_evidence: “The total sales pipeline stood at $2.5 billion as of June 30th, a 17.2% increase year-over-year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management highlighted revenue per employee rising to about $89,000 from $82,000 last quarter, with a projection near $100,000 by year-end. The preview anticipated cost savings beginning to show in the P&L but did not forecast this productivity measure.
fact_evidence: “Revenue per employee grew to approximately $89,000 from $82,000 last quarter and is projected to approach $100,000 by year-end.”

description: AirJoule raised full-year 2026 cash-spend guidance to $27–28 million from $25 million, above the preview’s expectation that spending would track the roughly $25 million guide. Management said the added spending is for accelerated JV commercialization and deployments, tempering the negative cash-spend surprise.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 cash spend guidance was raised slightly to $27-28 million (from $25 million), with the incremental spend directed toward accelerated JV commercialization and deployments.”
expectation_evidence: “burn in line with $25M FY guide”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: AirJoule disclosed a Core DH dehumidifier product aimed at an estimated 1.2 million installed conventional desiccant-wheel systems, with a targeted 2027 product timeline. The preview focused on the Core AWG launch and did not anticipate this additional product opportunity.
fact_evidence: “The Core DH dehumidifier product targets an estimated 1.2 million installed base of conventional desiccant wheel systems, focusing on facilities operating at 30%-50% relative humidity, with a targeted 2027 product timeline.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The first full-scale Prime system is already commissioned and running 24/7, and is tracking toward its target of up to 2,000 liters per day. The preview looked for confirmation of the European deployment timing but did not anticipate this operating-performance update.
fact_evidence: “The first full-scale Prime system, commissioned in Newark in May and running 24/7, is tracking toward its target of up to 2,000 liters per day.”
expectation_evidence: “AirJoule Prime European deployment ... — timing confirmation.”

description: AirJoule said it is preparing for contract manufacturing targeted for 2027 and exploring partners to reduce its internal CapEx needs. The preview highlighted cash and commercialization milestones but did not anticipate this manufacturing approach.
fact_evidence: “The company is advancing contract manufacturing preparations targeting 2027 ... and is exploring partners to reduce internal CapEx needs.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview estimated about $9.5 million of cash at June 30 and treated less than 12 months of runway as the base case. Acurx reported $10.7 million and said it funds the PATHFINDER trial and operations for at least one year.
fact_evidence: Acurx ended Q2 2026 with $10.7 million in cash, up from $7.6 million at year-end 2025, which management says funds the Pathfinder trial and operations for at least one year.
expectation_evidence: “My estimate: ... cash at 6/30 **≈ $9.5M**”; the preview also said Q1 had stated cash “would **not** fund 12 months.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview expected PATHFINDER’s first enrollment by August 2026, but management now anticipates enrollment in Q4. The study is fully funded, which is reassuring, but it does not offset the delay against the stated timing expectation.
fact_evidence: The 20-patient open-label PATHFINDER trial is fully funded, with enrollment anticipated to begin in Q4 2026.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “first enrollment **by August 2026**” and listed “rCDI pilot first-patient-in” as a key metric to confirm.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview noted the FDA’s general single-Phase-III pathway guidance, but the call added that the FDA is open to reviewing the totality of evidence at a pre-NDA meeting after ASPIRE and PATHFINDER, particularly if efficacy is robust. That is a more specific and encouraging indication of regulatory receptiveness than the preview described.
