expectation_evidence: The preview described the Texas project as “not yet booked as firm equipment orders” and flagged “timing of the Texas 36-burner equipment phase.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The California 32-burner project has advanced to the test-furnace stage, a constructive development even though the preview highlighted conversion to the equipment order as a key question and no firm equipment order was reported.
fact_evidence: “The 32-burner California flat-flame project is progressing to test-furnace stage.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “conversion of the California 32-burner engineering phase (~$0.5M) into the ~$3.2M equipment order” as a key item, while its base case anticipated “no backlog number given.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: One three-burner order uses a licensing arrangement: the customer builds from ClearSign’s drawings, lowering reported revenue per unit while keeping profit-margin dollars unchanged. The preview did not anticipate this revenue-recognition nuance.
fact_evidence: “One of the 3-burner orders was structured as a licensing/royalty deal” that reduces revenue per unit “but preserv[es] the same profit-margin dollars.”

description: Management described a path to a $6–7 million run rate from midstream and flare products alone, and said double-digit-million annual revenue is feasible as process-burner installations activate. The preview focused on lumpy 2H revenue and the October startup, but did not set out this scale of revenue potential.
fact_evidence: Management sees “a path to a $6-7 million run rate from midstream and flare product lines alone” and views “double-digit-million annual revenue as feasible as process burner installations activate.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the key question was “whether 2H26 is being framed as another Q4-weighted year” and described the base case as “spare parts + M-series + flare revenue only.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Operating cash use rose to about $1.2 million from roughly $511,000 a year earlier, with management attributing the increase to customer cash-collection timing. The preview emphasized burn and runway but did not anticipate this year-over-year increase.
fact_evidence: “Net cash used in operations jumped to about $1.2 million in Q2 2026 from roughly $511,000 a year ago,” driven by “customer cash collection timing.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash and burn” and said “Runway matters more than EPS here,” but gave no expectation for Q2 operating cash use.

description: The year-over-year loss improvement came almost entirely from lower G&A legal fees associated with a dissolved Board special committee, rather than clearly indicating recurring operating-cost discipline. That makes the improvement less indicative of ongoing savings than the preview’s cost-control framing suggested.
fact_evidence: Net loss narrowed by $373,000, “primarily due to a $368,000 drop in G&A expenses tied to reduced legal fees from a dissolved Board special committee.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said a lower operating loss would “mark real cost control” and highlighted “Opex discipline.”

description: The preview's Q1 whisper was roughly $150–165 million of total revenue, but management guided to $140–160 million of device revenue alone. Q4 device revenue was $106 million, so the device outlook signals a strong sequential increase, although the call facts do not give total Q1 revenue for a direct comparison.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 guidance calls for device revenue of $140 million to $160 million.” Q4 device revenue was “~$106 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Whisper sits around $150–165M”; the key question was whether the company guides to “the first sequential growth quarter in over two years.”

description: The preview wanted an EBITDA or cash-flow breakeven date or at least a FY2027 framework, but management provided no timeline. Instead, it said gross-margin breakeven requires roughly an $800 million annual revenue run rate, with the exact level depending on mix.
fact_evidence: “Management estimates a roughly $800 million annual revenue run rate is needed to reach breakeven gross margin,” while the “exact point depends on product mix.”
expectation_evidence: “The buy-side expects a date or at least an FY2027 framework”; “Silence here is a bear signal.”

description: The Q1 operating-expense outlook of $62–66 million is above the preview's roughly $61 million flat-cost expectation. That leaves less room for operating-cost reductions than the preview's base case assumed.
fact_evidence: Q1 FY2027 guidance newly disclosed “operating expenses of $62 million to $66 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave operating expenses of “~$61M” and said the base case assumed “Cost discipline holds.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Management highlighted a refinancing opportunity in roughly $630 million of first-lien debt carrying about 16% interest, a specific high-cost debt burden and potential cash-burn lever not featured in the preview's account of manageable debt service. Any benefit is prospective, not a completed refinancing.
fact_evidence: “First lien debt of roughly $630 million carries ~16% interest,” representing “a major refinancing opportunity that could meaningfully reduce the company's $54 million quarterly operating cash burn.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described debt service as “fixed and manageable” and cited cash interest of “~$145M/yr” after emergence.

description: Gross capital expenditures fell to $5 million from $38 million in the prior quarter, a sharp reduction the preview had not forecast for Q4. The preview did flag FY2027 capex plans, but gave no Q4 gross-capex expectation.
fact_evidence: “Gross capital expenditures fell sharply to $5 million in Q4 from $38 million in the prior quarter.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: A $41 million inventory reduction boosted operating cash flow, providing a substantial working-capital benefit that the preview did not anticipate. The call facts do not state the resulting total operating cash flow.
fact_evidence: “Inventory reduction contributed a $41 million benefit to operating cash flow.”

description: Holders converted $46 million of convertible notes to equity during the quarter, reducing debt and annual interest expense but also bringing forward some equity dilution that the preview had identified as a risk to watch.
fact_evidence: “Holders of $46 million of convertible notes voluntarily converted debt to equity during Q4, saving approximately $1 million in annual interest expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any signal on ~44M shares of potential convert dilution.”

description: The preview looked for FY27 core revenue growth of about 13–14%, with 13%+ described as preserving the durable-growth narrative. BILL guided to 11–14%, a midpoint of 12.5%, and cited a three-point growth headwind from spend-and-expense dynamics and bank channels.
fact_evidence: “FY27 core revenue guidance of $1.669B-$1.719B implies 11%-14% growth,” including “3 points of year-over-year growth headwind (2 points from spend & expense dynamics and 1 point from bank channels).”
expectation_evidence: “A first FY27 guide of 13%+ preserves the durable-growth narrative”; the modeled buy-side bar was “~13–14% core.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected roughly 3,800 or more Q4 net adds and flagged fewer than 3,500 as a sign of post-restructuring disruption. BILL added only about 1,800; management attributed the shortfall to restructuring and deliberate focus on its ideal customer profile.
fact_evidence: “The company added only ~1,800 net new customers in Q4,” below recent trends due to “organizational restructuring and deliberate ideal-customer-profile focus.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Net adds ≥~3,800” and said net adds “<3,500” would signal RIF disruption.

description: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin reached 23%, well above the roughly 19.5% implied by the preview’s expected operating income and revenue. The margin also expanded substantially year over year.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 23%, expanding 860 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 non-GAAP operating income at “~$84M” on consensus revenue of “$430.5M,” implying a margin of about 19.5%.

description: The preview put Q4 core revenue consensus at about $397 million. BILL reported $400.5 million, a modest beat and slightly above the preview’s expected 15% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q4 core revenue grew 16% year-over-year to $400.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: Core subscription and transaction revenue consensus was “~$397M (implied),” with “+15%” implied year-over-year growth.

description: The preview anticipated a Rule-of-40 framework and a GAAP margin roadmap, but BILL provided a specific FY27 profitability outlook: it expects to exceed the Rule of 40 exiting the year and generate well over $125 million of GAAP profits for the full year.
fact_evidence: “The company expects to exceed the Rule of 40 (net revenue growth plus operating margin) exiting FY27 and to generate well over $125 million of GAAP profits for the full year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Rule of 40 and GAAP margin expansion were deferred to this call, and flagged a “no-show” on the framework or GAAP roadmap as a risk.

description: The preview highlighted the $1 billion authorization and said Q4 execution would matter to the FY27 EPS bridge, but BILL disclosed about $300 million of Q4 repurchases and roughly 15 million shares retired since Q3—nearly 14% of shares outstanding.
fact_evidence: “BILL repurchased ~$300 million of stock at an average price of $35.31 in Q4, retiring ~15 million shares (nearly 14% of shares outstanding) since Q3,” with $400 million remaining on the authorization.
expectation_evidence: The preview called out “buyback pace against the $1.0B/24-month authorization” and said Q4 execution would “directly drive[] the FY27 EPS bridge.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview cited joint AP/AR and spend-and-expense customers growing about 39%; BILL reported 35% growth, indicating slower expansion in that cross-sell cohort. The disclosed 111% net revenue retention for existing multiproduct customers provides a positive counterpoint.
fact_evidence: “Joint AP and spend-and-expense customers grew 35% year-over-year,” and “existing multiproduct customers showed net revenue retention of 111%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the cross-sell cohort as “20,000+ joint AP/AR + S&E customers growing ~39%.”

description: The preview did not anticipate a specific timing for the growth low point. Management said Q2 FY27 should be the trough of the year’s growth trajectory, implying a later improvement after that point.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 is expected to mark the trough of the year's growth trajectory.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: BILL announced that it will report revenue net of rewards expense beginning in Q1 FY27, moving rewards from sales and marketing expense to a reduction of subscription and transaction fees. The preview did not flag this change; it affects reported revenue presentation but not operating or net income.
fact_evidence: “Beginning Q1 FY27, BILL will report revenue net of rewards expense,” reclassifying rewards to “a reduction of subscription and transaction fees,” with “no impact on operating or net income.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview discussed BILL’s AI-native reorganization but did not anticipate the disclosed adoption and credit-performance metrics. More than 175,000 businesses use its AI agents, while AI-driven invoice financing grew about 30% in both volume and revenue and its expected loss rate improved by more than 50%.
fact_evidence: “Over 175,000 businesses are now using BILL's AI agents”; AI-driven invoice financing saw “both volume and revenue grow ~30% year-over-year in FY26 while the expected loss rate improved by more than 50%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to an “AI-native” reorganization but did not provide expectations for agent adoption or AI invoice-financing growth or loss rates.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview did not identify a further improvement in S&E fraud and credit losses as a watch item. BILL reported that these losses improved nearly six basis points sequentially as a percentage of TPV.
fact_evidence: “S&E fraud/credit losses improved nearly 6 basis points sequentially as a percentage of TPV.”

description: AAP reported a slight comparable-sales decline rather than the roughly 2% growth expected, and sales of $2.0 billion came in below the $2.03–$2.04 billion consensus range. Management attributed the shortfall to a larger-than-expected low-single-digit DIY decline as household budgets tightened late in the quarter.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales were $2 billion with a slight comparable sales decline,” with “a larger-than-expected low single-digit DIY decline driven by tighter household budgets in the last 4 weeks.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales $2.03–2.04B”; “Comparable store sales ~+2%.”

description: Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.03 substantially exceeded the $0.80–$0.81 consensus, even topping the preview’s $0.95–$1.05 bull-case range at its upper end. This was a much stronger reported quarter than the central expectation despite the weak comps.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose to $1.03 from $0.69 a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus of “$0.80–0.81”; the bull scenario estimated “$0.95–1.05.”

description: AAP raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS range to $2.60–$3.30 from $2.40–$3.10, rather than reaffirming guidance. The $0.20 increase to the floor was positive, although it remained below the preview’s suggested roughly $2.70 floor, and management said about $100 million of interest income helped the outlook.
fact_evidence: “Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $2.60-$3.30, aided by roughly $100 million of interest income.”
expectation_evidence: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was “$2.40–3.10”; the preview said “lifting the floor toward ~$2.70” was the “single most likely upside catalyst.”

description: The reported 5.6% adjusted operating margin was well above the preview’s roughly 4.5% bar, but excluding tariff refunds it was 4.3%, just below that bar. The apparent margin beat therefore depended materially on refunds rather than entirely reflecting underlying performance.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin was 5.6%, but excluding IEEPA tariff refunds it was 4.3%, representing nearly 130 basis points of underlying expansion.” Adjusted gross margin expanded about 240 basis points, including 130 basis points from refunds and roughly 110 basis points from merchandising initiatives.
expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Adjusted operating margin vs. ~4.5%” as the key metric and said the company had implied margins “toward the high end of guidance” in Q2/Q3.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Same-SKU inflation reached about 4% in Q2, above the roughly 3% level discussed in the preview and beyond the prior 2%–3% plan. Full-year inflation is now expected at about 3%, roughly 100 basis points above original plans.
fact_evidence: “Same-SKU inflation stepped up to approximately 4% in Q2 from 3% last quarter” and full-year inflation is “now expected at about 3%, roughly 100 basis points above original plans.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said same-SKU inflation was “running at ~3% vs. the 2–3% plan” and management had said tariffs had changed nothing about that plan.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: AAP generated positive year-to-date free cash flow of $120 million, a sharp reversal from the prior-year outflow and a stronger early cash inflection than the preview’s concern that front-half FCF had been negative suggested.
fact_evidence: “The company generated $120 million of year-to-date free cash flow,” versus “a $201 million outflow last year,” marking positive free cash flow for the first time in two years.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “FCF has been negative in the front half of the year (−$75M in Q1)” and that “the H2 conversion story needs to start here.”

description: Management said national-account headwinds should be about half as large in the second half as in the first, indicating a better expected Pro comparison than the preview had specifically described. Main Street Pro was already outperforming total Pro, while total Pro growth remained low-single-digit.
fact_evidence: “Main Street Pro comps exceeded total Pro comps by more than 200 basis points,” and “national account headwinds are expected to be about half as large in the second half as in the first half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged Pro versus DIY and noted that national-account softness was tolerable if Main Street held, but did not anticipate a halving of national-account headwinds in the second half.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AAP reported markedly improved customer and fulfillment measures that the preview had not identified as expected outcomes: NPS rose nearly 80 points year over year, attachment rates approached 30%, and Pro deliveries were consistently under 40 minutes.
fact_evidence: “NPS rising nearly 80 points from the high-60s a year ago,” in-store attachment rates “climbing to nearly 30% from the mid-to-high 20s,” and Pro order delivery “consistently under 40 minutes.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: AAP accelerated its market-hub rollout: it now plans 15–20 openings this year and is targeting 50 by year-end, compared with the preview’s expectation of 10–15 additional hubs in 2026.
fact_evidence: “Market hub openings were accelerated to 15-20 this year (targeting 50 by year-end) toward a 60-location goal by mid-2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “10–15 more planned in 2026” and “60 targeted by 2027.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: AAP reported improved leverage and a debt repurchase alongside a $3.1 billion cash balance, developments not covered in the preview’s setup. Net debt leverage fell to 2.1x from 2.4x last quarter.
fact_evidence: “Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 2.4x last quarter,” the company repurchased “approximately $30 million of 2028 senior notes,” and ended with “$3.1 billion cash.”

description: ONFO reported only $1.5 million of Q2 revenue, about 11% below the $1.682 million consensus in the preview; the year-over-year decline was 52%, worse than the preview’s implied 47% decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell 52% year-over-year to $1.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $1.682M”; the preview also gives an “Implied YoY” decline of “-47%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash ended the quarter at just $251,000, below the preview’s $0.6–1.0 million base estimate and even below its bear-case threshold of $350,000. The preview had flagged the cash balance as a central solvency issue.
fact_evidence: “Cash fell to just $251,000 at June 30, 2026,” down from $842,000 at Q1-end, and the company made going-concern disclosures in the 10-Q.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash at 6/30” at “$0.6–1.0M” in its base case and “<$0.35M” in its bear case.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: June 30 stockholders’ equity was a $3.11 million deficit, far worse than the preview’s $1.0–2.0 million base estimate and below its bear-case estimate of less than $500,000 or negative. Management says later note conversions made equity positive, but the reported quarter-end figure was nowhere near the $2.5 million Nasdaq threshold.
fact_evidence: “Stockholders' equity was a deficit of approximately $3.11 million at June 30, below Nasdaq's $2.5 million requirement,” although “note conversions have since pushed equity positive.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Stockholders' equity” of “$1.0–2.0M”; its bear case was “<$0.5M or negative,” and it identified $2.5 million as the Nasdaq threshold.

description: The senior secured notes were fully extinguished after quarter-end, a more complete resolution than the preview’s expectation of watching for further conversions. However, settling the notes and related penalties required issuing about 2.3 million shares in total, including shares for the $8.2 million in floor penalties and $412,000 in liquidated damages, making the resolution highly dilutive.
fact_evidence: The holder converted “$5.5 million principal into ~721,000 shares” and settled “~$8.2 million in floor penalties plus $412,000 in liquidated damages via ~1.58 million additional shares”; the notes were “fully extinguished after quarter end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “conversions after 6/30” and described a “convertible-note death spiral,” but did not anticipate that the notes would be fully extinguished through these conversions and share settlements.

description: Gross margin remained around 49%, rather than recovering toward the preview’s 53% base estimate or management’s previously guided mid-60% range. The mix also deteriorated as higher-margin B2C fell to less than 19% of revenue from about 35% a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin held roughly flat at about 49% versus the previously guided mid-60% range,” as B2C product revenue fell “to under 19% of total revenue from about 35% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “Gross margin” of “53%” and said the CFO had guided GM “toward the mid-60% range over 2026.”

description: B2B revenue fell 41% and the segment swung from operating income to a loss, with management attributing the disruption to AI-related sales weakness at its largest agency, Eastern Standard. The preview anticipated deliberate agency consolidation and revenue shrinkage, but did not flag this specific sales disruption or segment loss.
fact_evidence: “B2B revenue declined 41% to $1.22 million and swung to an operating loss of ~$103,000 (versus $70,000 income prior year), driven by AI-related sales disruption at largest agency Eastern Standard.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said revenue decline was partly deliberate, including “B2B agency consolidation −30% opex,” but did not anticipate AI-related sales disruption at Eastern Standard.

description: The company made more financing progress on acquisitions than the preview’s description of the deals as unfunded and pending capitalization: it signed a letter of intent for a roughly $4 million adjusted-EBITDA acquisition with 100% seller financing and reduced another deal’s upfront cash requirement from $3.5 million to $1.3 million. These remain transactions targeted for a future close, not completed acquisitions.
fact_evidence: ONFO signed “a letter of intent for a 100% seller-financed acquisition with roughly $4 million in trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA, targeting an October 1 close,” and renegotiated another deal so its upfront cash requirement “was cut from $3.5 million to $1.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the LOIs as “unfunded” and said they had been retained “to pursue as its capitalization improves”; its base case expected LOIs to remain “pending capitalization.”

description: The reported net loss widened to $4.6 million, driven largely by a $2.95 million noncash derivative-liability fair-value loss. The preview noted that a large noncash derivative gain was a live possibility, so the reported loss was a worse outcome than that potential upside, although it also cautioned that the direction was ambiguous.
fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $4.6 million from $534,000 a year earlier, driven largely by a $2.95 million noncash loss on the change in fair value of derivative liabilities tied to the senior secured notes.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “a large non-cash ‘gain’ on the derivative is a live possibility,” while also noting that “Direction is genuinely ambiguous.”

description: Nordson reported Q3 sales of $818 million, well above the preview’s $779 million consensus and even the preview’s $800–810 million bull case. Adjusted EPS of $3.25 also beat the $3.09 consensus and the roughly $3.16 whisper, exceeding the high end of company guidance by $0.10.
fact_evidence: “Record Q3 FY2026 sales of $818 million”; “Adjusted EPS reached a record $3.25” and was “$0.10 above the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $779M”; “Adjusted EPS: $3.09”; the preview’s “informal buy-side bar” was “~$3.16”; its bull case forecast revenue of “$800–810M” and EPS of “$3.25–3.35.”

description: The full-year guidance raise was stronger than the preview’s bull-case range: Nordson’s new sales range reaches $3.075 billion and its EPS range reaches $12.00, above the preview’s bull-case ceilings of approximately $3.03 billion and $11.90. This also decisively exceeds the existing full-year guidance cited in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year guidance to sales of $3.035-$3.075 billion and adjusted EPS of $11.80-$12.00.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case anticipated “FY26 raised to ~$3.00–3.03B / $11.70–11.90”; the existing guidance was listed as “$2,930–3,010M / $11.30–11.80.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog grew 35% year over year, far above the preview’s reported starting point of 18% and its bull-case threshold of 20% or more. The preview treated backlog as central to the H2 and FY27 outlook, and the reported growth provides stronger visibility than it anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Backlog grew 35% year-over-year,” broadly across segments, “providing visibility into fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 backlog was “+18% YoY” and described “backlog +20%+” as part of the bull case.

description: ATS sales reached $220 million, about 15% above the $190.9 million consensus, and its EBITDA margin expanded to 30%. That margin was well above the roughly 27% level the preview said needed to be sustained, while the preview’s bull case had called for ATS sales above $200 million and margin of at least 28%.
fact_evidence: “Advanced Technology Solutions delivered an all-time record $220 million in sales, up 28% (31% organic), with EBITDA margin expanding to a record 30% from 24% a year prior.”
expectation_evidence: ATS consensus was “$190.9M”; the preview said “Sustaining ~27%+ validates” the margin story and set its bull case at “ATS >$200M with margin ≥28%.”

description: Medical and Fluid Solutions substantially outgrew the preview’s modest growth expectation and achieved record profitability despite the divested-business drag. The preview had highlighted regulatory-related margin costs as a risk, whereas the reported segment posted a record 38% margin.
fact_evidence: “Medical and Fluid Solutions posted record sales of $231 million with 11% organic growth and record EBITDA of $88 million at a 38% margin, despite a 6% headwind from the divested contract manufacturing business.”
expectation_evidence: MFS consensus was “$224.4M” and “+2.3%”; the preview called MFS “the soft spot” and flagged “regulatory-driven product change costs as a near-term margin headwind.”

description: IPS organic growth was 3%, better than the preview’s inference that consensus implied organic growth would be flat to slightly negative. The segment’s margin was flat, however, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would defend rather than expand margins.
fact_evidence: “Industrial Precision Solutions grew just 3% organically with EBITDA margin flat at 35%,” as management prioritized growth over margin expansion amid inflationary pressures.
expectation_evidence: The preview said IPS consensus “implicitly assumes IPS organic growth of roughly flat to slightly negative,” and that management’s strategy was “defending margins rather than expanding them.”

description: Management added a caution to the strong ATS outlook: it expects growth to normalize toward mid-single digits in FY2027 from a peak, and said North American chip-infrastructure investment has not yet produced Nordson orders. The preview emphasized early-stage semiconductor momentum and the FY27 setup, so the normalization comment is a more restrained near-term outlook, though the unconverted investment remains potential upside.
fact_evidence: “Management expects ATS growth to normalize toward mid-single digits off a peak in fiscal 2027”; “North American chip infrastructure investment has not yet generated Nordson orders, representing future upside.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described an “early-innings semiconductor packaging cycle in ATS,” said backlog was driving “the FY27 setup,” and identified the “early-stage momentum in panel-level packaging” as a signal to watch.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Nordson reported lower leverage and a material year-over-year decline in net interest expense, aided by a new commercial paper program. The preview did not set an expectation for these financing results.
fact_evidence: “Net debt declined to approximately $1.6 billion with leverage reduced to 1.7x, and net interest expense fell over $5 million year-over-year aided by a new commercial paper program.”

description: Walmart raised its full-year outlook despite the preview’s base case that guidance would be reaffirmed or narrowed. Sales guidance moved to 4%-5% from 3.5%-4.5%, operating income to 7%-8.5% from 6%-8%, and EPS to $2.80-$2.87 from $2.75-$2.85.
fact_evidence: “Full-year sales guidance was raised to 4%-5% (from 3.5%-4.5%), operating income guidance to 7%-8.5% (from 6%-8%), and EPS to $2.80-$2.87 (from $2.75-$2.85).” Guidance now absorbs “more than $2 billion of incremental fuel-related costs” and a roughly 20 basis point Vibe acquisition headwind.
expectation_evidence: “FY27 guidance action — raise, reaffirm, or trim”; “no raise is now the base case”; the base scenario expected guidance to be “reaffirmed/narrowed, not raised.”

description: Adjusted EPS growth exceeded the preview’s expected 7.4%-8.8% by a wide margin: the call reported growth of more than 19%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased over 19%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS” consensus was “+7.4% to +8.8%” year over year, with estimates of $0.73-$0.74.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Reported adjusted operating income growth was far above the 7%-10% guide, but the gap came from a large tariff-refund benefit rather than a comparable improvement in underlying performance. Excluding the refunds, growth was only at the top end of the original guide.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income rose 17.4%”; Q2 operating income included a “~750 basis point benefit from approximately $2.9 billion in tariff refunds,” which management is “reinvesting into price”; “excluding this, underlying OI growth was at the top end of the 7%-10% guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The company’s Q2 adjusted operating income guide was “+7% to +10% cc.”

description: Management issued a notably soft Q3 outlook, with operating income growth of only 2%-4% and EPS of $0.62-$0.64, and asked investors to assess Q2 and Q3 together. The preview did not flag this quarterly slowdown, although Walmart said the two quarters together would average about 10% operating income growth per quarter.
fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 operating income growth of just 2%-4% and EPS of $0.62-$0.64,” and urged investors to “view Q2 and Q3 together” because price reinvestment is concentrated in Q2.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Walmart U.S. reported comps of 2.6%, below the preview’s roughly 3.5% expectation. Management attributed 125 basis points of drag to maximum fair price drug regulation and put underlying core comps closer to 3.5%, making the shortfall largely a reported-versus-underlying gap.
fact_evidence: “Walmart U.S. comp sales rose only 2.6%, hurt by a 125 basis point drag from maximum fair price drug regulation,” while management framed “underlying core comps closer to 3.5%.” In-store comps declined low single digits due to health and wellness.
expectation_evidence: “Walmart U.S. comp ex-fuel” was expected at “~3.5% (BofA)”; the catalyst checklist cited “~3.5–4.0%.”

description: U.S. e-commerce reached double-digit incremental margins in the first half, a concrete profitability milestone beyond the preview’s general focus on e-commerce profitability. E-commerce sales growth itself was broadly in line with the preview’s low-20s expectation.
fact_evidence: “Global e-commerce net sales grew 23%,” with Walmart U.S. up 24%, Sam’s Club U.S. up 26%, and International up 19%; “U.S. e-commerce reached double-digit incremental margins in the first half.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “eComm low-20s%”; the preview also listed “eCommerce profitability” as a secondary item to watch.

description: Walmart disclosed a roughly 20 basis point operating-income headwind from the Vibe acquisition, which the preview did not identify among the expected margin pressures.
fact_evidence: Guidance now absorbs “roughly 20 basis points of OI headwind from the Vibe acquisition.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Walmart U.S. sharply expanded its rollback program, with management linking the promotions to transaction and unit growth and food-share gains but warning that they temporarily depress sales through deflation before the sales benefit arrives. The preview discussed consumer trade-down and pricing, but did not anticipate this specific scale of rollback activity or its timing effect.
fact_evidence: “Walmart U.S. deployed over 11,000 rollbacks (up from ~7,200 in Q1),” driving transaction and unit growth and strong food-category share gains; management warned of “a temporary deflationary effect with a lagged sales benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “low-income cohort behavior and trade-down” and a possible comp slowdown from “lapping last year’s tariff-driven price increases.”

description: U.S. marketplace sales grew 52%, a strong result for a high-margin business the preview identified as part of the margin story but for which it gave no growth-rate expectation.
fact_evidence: “U.S. marketplace up 52%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “the high-margin flywheel: advertising, membership, marketplace” and said the operating-income bridge had to come from “advertising, membership, marketplace/fulfillment mix,” but gave no marketplace growth forecast.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Walmart highlighted broad store-fulfillment and automation scale while also raising capital spending to about 4% of net sales. The preview discussed e-commerce profitability but did not set expectations for these operating milestones or the higher CapEx level.
fact_evidence: “Stores now fulfill 80% of e-commerce orders”; automation serves “3,100 U.S. stores” and processes “over 50% of e-commerce fulfillment volume”; “CapEx was raised to ~4% of net sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “eCommerce profitability” among secondary items to watch but gave no CapEx or automation expectation.

description: Unifi reported $144.2 million of Q4 sales, about $3.1 million above the preview’s $141.1 million consensus estimate. The 4% year-over-year increase also exceeded the preview’s implied 1.9% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 consolidated net sales rose 4% year-over-year to $144.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q4 FY26 Consensus | ~$141.1M”; consensus implied “+1.9% YoY.”

description: Gross margin reached roughly 10%, above the preview’s 7–8.5% base range and even above its 8.5% bull-case threshold. Gross profit swung to $14.3 million from a loss a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit swung to $14.3 million (roughly 10% margin) from a gross loss of $1.1 million (-0.8% margin) a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “GM 7–8.5%”; its bull case called for “GM ≥9%.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $8.2 million, above the preview’s implied $6–7 million estimate. That is a meaningful but not enormous beat against the preview’s range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved by $12.3 million year-over-year to $8.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$6–7M (implied, not published).”

description: The real-estate sale was already known, but the call gave more favorable transaction economics than the preview could establish: management said NOLs should keep tax leakage minimal and that the sale could leave Unifi essentially bank debt-free, without reducing production capacity.
fact_evidence: The $60 million sale is “expected to close by year-end with minimal tax leakage due to NOL carry-forwards, without reducing production capacity”; management said it “could make the company essentially bank debt-free by the end of the calendar year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said net proceeds and cash-tax leakage were unknown, specifically asking “does the NOL position shelter the gain?” It expected the deal to be reaffirmed but said net-of-tax proceeds might be left vague.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Full-year free cash flow reached $21.5 million and improved by more than $50 million from fiscal 2025. The preview focused on a possible Q4 working-capital build and did not anticipate or quantify this full-year cash-flow result.
fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow reached $21.5 million, an improvement of over $50 million versus fiscal 2025.”

description: Unifi pushed its goal of REPREVE reaching 50% of fiber sales out to 2030. The preview highlighted the current mix decline and the importance of recovering above 30%, but did not flag a delay to the 50% target.
fact_evidence: “REPREVE's target of 50% of fiber sales has been pushed out to 2030.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “A move back above 30% supports the premium-mix argument; continued erosion undercuts pricing power.”

description: Q4 revenue was $114.4 million, well above the preview’s $100–104 million working consensus and even the $106–112 million bull range; full-year sales of $381.3 million also exceeded the preview’s $370.9 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $114.4 million, up 18.3% year-over-year (15.9% organic), with full-year sales of $381.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Working consensus used here” was “~$100–104M” for Q4 revenue; the bull scenario called for “$106–112M.” The preview cited a “$370.9M FY26 revenue estimate.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow reached $17.2 million, far above the preview’s roughly $7 million base case and above even its bull case of more than $10 million. Net leverage also fell to 0.5x, substantially below the preview’s stated 1.1x.
fact_evidence: “Q4 free cash flow was $17.2 million and net leverage improved to 0.5x … with net debt of $13.8 million and trailing EBITDA of $29.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “FCF ~$7M”; the bull scenario anticipated “FCF >$10M.” The preview stated “Net leverage 1.1x.”

description: Q4 gross margin was 26.3%, well below the preview’s roughly 29% base case and below the 28% level it identified as a sign that tariffs and mix were biting. The decline included a prior-year favorable adjustment that the preview did not identify.
fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin contracted approximately 600 basis points to 26.3% due to product mix, tariff dilution (60 bps impact), and a prior-year $3 million favorable one-time adjustment.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “GM ~29%”; the preview said “sub-28% implies tariffs plus mix are biting.” It also compared against “31.0% prior-year Q4.”

description: Reported EPS of $0.64 exceeded the preview’s $0.23–$0.50 range, but about $0.17 per share came from a tax benefit. That benefit differed from the preview’s expectation that TWIN would have normalized tax expense after the earlier valuation-allowance reversal.
fact_evidence: “Q4 net income was $9.4 million ($0.64 per diluted share), boosted by roughly $0.17 per share from an income tax benefit tied to reversal of the domestic valuation allowance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave a Q4 EPS range of “~$0.23–0.50” and said the Q2 reversal meant “TWIN now books a normalized tax expense (~30% implied in Q3).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Defense was 17% of backlog, above the preview’s roughly 15% expectation, and its backlog grew 53% in the quarter—stronger than the preview’s stated 20% growth figure. The pipeline figure, however, was below the preview’s expected range and is listed separately.
fact_evidence: “Defense now comprises 17% of total backlog, with the defense portion of backlog growing 53% in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said defense was “~15% of total, +20% YoY.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The defense project pipeline was reported at $30–50 million, below the preview’s $50–75 million identified pipeline range.
fact_evidence: “A defense project pipeline of $30-50 million as of June 30th.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the defense pipeline as “$50–75M identified pipeline.”

description: Land-based transmission sales grew 26% year over year, accelerating from the 22.2% growth noted in the preview despite its warning about North American customer caution.
fact_evidence: “Land-based transmission sales grew 26% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Land-Based Transmissions “(+22.2% in Q3 but management flagged North American customer caution).”

description: Management gave a specific FY2027 CapEx outlook of more than $20 million, with spending tied to the Finland facility, the ARFF product-line move, and machine tools. The preview noted there was no numeric company guidance, so this was new forward-looking detail, though it is investment spending rather than revenue guidance.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 CapEx is guided to north of $20 million to fund the new Finland facility, the ARFF product line move to Lufkin, Texas, and new machine tools, supporting 2030 targets of $500 million revenue and 30% gross margins.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “TWIN does not give numeric guidance,” and described any move toward formal guidance or an explicit FY2030 milestone as “a genuine narrative event.”

description: The preview put Q4 sales consensus at $802.0 million, implying a 1.3% year-over-year decline, but sales rose 17%. Full-year sales growth was also 6%, well above the preview’s 1.1% estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q4 net sales rose 17% year-over-year while full-year sales grew 6%.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $802.0M … | Implied Y/Y −1.3%”; “FY26 total revenue | $3.07B (+1.1%).”

description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS was $1.46, far above the preview’s $1.14 consensus and the roughly 12% growth implied by that estimate; reported EPS growth was 43%.
fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP EPS grew 43% year-over-year to a record $1.46 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $1.14”; the preview says this implied “+11.8%” year-over-year growth.

description: FY27 organic guidance is stronger than the preview’s in-line case: 6%–10% revenue growth and $158–165 million of adjusted EBITDA, excluding MicroAge, exceed its $3.15–3.25 billion revenue and $150–158 million EBITDA ranges. The EBITDA range also reaches above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $158 million.
fact_evidence: “FY27 organic guidance calls for revenue growth of 6% to 10% and adjusted EBITDA of $158-165 million (4.6-4.65% margin), excluding any MicroAge contribution.”
expectation_evidence: “In-line ≈ $3.15–3.25B revenue / $150–160M EBITDA”; the base scenario says “$3.15–3.25B revenue / $150–158M EBITDA.”

description: Specialty Technology Solutions sharply outperformed the preview’s expected Q4 decline: segment sales rose 18% and adjusted EBITDA rose 28%, rather than decelerating against the tough comparison.
fact_evidence: “The Specialty Technology Solutions segment grew Q4 net sales 18% year-over-year with adjusted EBITDA up 28% to $36.7 million, led by broad-based North America hardware growth including physical security.”
expectation_evidence: “SCSC is guided to decline ~1–4% in Q4 against a tough +8.9% comp.”

description: The company moved beyond the preview’s general expectation that it would keep exploring acquisitions and signed a definitive agreement for MicroAge. The deal is intended to expand the company into cloud, cybersecurity, data center, and AI, though it is not included in FY27 organic guidance.
fact_evidence: “The company signed a definitive agreement to acquire MicroAge, expected to close by the end of Q1 FY27, to expand its TAM into cloud, cybersecurity, data center, and AI.”
expectation_evidence: Management “continues to explore acquisition opportunities” to expand recurring revenue.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The reported $114 million of full-year free cash flow exceeded the preview’s $90 million floor, but it was below the preview’s cited $118.6 million for the first nine months. That implies a Q4 cash-flow drawdown rather than the full-year figure simply extending the already-surpassed nine-month total.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 free cash flow reached $114 million, representing 124% cash conversion of non-GAAP net income.”
expectation_evidence: “9M FCF was $118.6M against a full-year guide of ‘≥$90M’ — the guide is already beaten and is effectively a floor”; the preview also flagged a possible “large Q4 working-capital build.”

description: The newly added Juniper networking line will contribute more slowly than might be expected from its addition: supplier constraints are expected to limit the ramp through the first half of FY27, with fuller contribution only in the second half.
fact_evidence: “The newly added Juniper (HPE) networking line will ramp slowly through the first half of FY27 due to supplier supply-chain constraints, with fuller contribution expected in the second half.”

description: JBSS reported Q4 diluted EPS of $0.71, far below the preview’s $1.17–$1.30 published-consensus range and its estimated $1.40–$1.45 buy-side whisper. Full-year EPS was also $5.26, below the preview’s implied estimate of about $5.85.
fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net income fell to $8.4 million ($0.71 per diluted share) from $13.5 million ($1.15 per diluted share) a year earlier”; “diluted EPS rising 4.6% to $5.26 from $5.03 in fiscal 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS **$1.30** (range $1.17–$1.30)”; “The buy-side bar is almost certainly **$1.40–$1.45**”; “FY26 EPS (implied) ~$5.85.”

description: Q4 gross margin was 15.7%, well below the preview’s estimated 18.3% and even below the 17.5% level the preview said would break the margin-expansion narrative. The quarter’s compression reflected recall costs as well as higher claims, freight, and manufacturing inefficiencies.
fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin contracted to 15.7% from 18.1%, hurt by $2.7 million in recall-related costs from third-party dry milk powder, higher customer claims, freight, and manufacturing inefficiencies.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~18.3% (my est. of embedded)”; “Anything ≥19% with volume growth is a clean beat; sub-17.5% breaks the FY26 margin-expansion narrative.”

description: Q4 sales of $280.4 million exceeded the $274.9 million consensus estimate, a roughly 2% beat.
fact_evidence: “Q4 sales growth to $280.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales **$274.9M**.”

description: Full-year sales reached $1.2 billion, above the preview’s $1.17 billion estimate. This was a modest upside to the annual revenue expectation despite the much weaker-than-expected Q4 EPS.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 net sales reached a record $1.2 billion, up 6.2%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $1.17B.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The company returned to volume growth in Q4, with volume up 1.4% after five consecutive quarters of declines. The preview’s base case assumed roughly flat volume, so the positive result was a modest upside on a key watch item.
fact_evidence: “Q4 marked a return to volume growth (up 1.4%) after five consecutive quarters of decline.”
expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … volume roughly flat”; “Positive Y/Y pounds in Q4 validates it.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Despite the preview’s concerns about continuing consumer and private-brand weakness, JBSS’s private-label snack/trail shipments rose 3% and Fisher snack/trail rose 15%. The broader snack nut and trail mix category was still declining, making the company’s shipment growth a notable contrast to the expected weakness.
fact_evidence: “The snack nut and trail mix category declined 7% in volume and 3% in dollars in Q4, but the company's private label snack/trail shipments outperformed, rising 3%, and Fisher snack/trail rose 15%.”
expectation_evidence: “Consumer channel / private brand. Down 4.5% in Q3 (private brand −5.3%).”; “Fisher snack nut/trail mix −8%”; “private-label bars −17%.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A $2.7 million recall-related charge from third-party dry milk powder was a specific unexpected cost in the quarter, adding to the margin shortfall beyond the cost pressures the preview discussed.
fact_evidence: “$2.7 million in recall-related costs from third-party dry milk powder.”

description: Management said pricing offsets for higher input, freight, fuel, and packaging-resin costs are not expected until Q2 FY2027. That timing leaves the cost pressure weighing on profitability for longer than the preview’s general discussion of inflation and pricing implied.
fact_evidence: “Higher input, freight, fuel, and packaging resin costs reduced Q4 profitability by roughly a couple million dollars, with pricing offsets not expected to materialize until Q2 fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 is when the pecan carry-out gets marked”; the preview flagged that “pecan/tree-nut cost inflation runs ahead of pricing” as a risk, but gave no specific timing for pricing offsets.

description: Raw nut and dried fruit inventory cost per pound rose 12.1% year over year, a further increase from the 10.5% year-over-year level cited at Q3. The preview specifically flagged inventory cost per pound as a key margin indicator, so the continued increase was negative for the cost outlook.
fact_evidence: “The weighted average cost per pound of raw nut and dried fruit inventory rose 12.1% year-over-year, driven by higher pecan and almond acquisition costs partially offset by lower walnut costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Inventory cost per pound was **+10.5% Y/Y** at quarter-end”; “Inventory cost/lb and new-crop pecan commentary” were on the catalyst checklist.

description: Management quantified more than $300 million of potential growth from the new high-speed bar lines at Elgin over three to five years. The preview anticipated discussion of startup economics and possible protein-bar distribution wins, but did not flag an opportunity of this stated size.
fact_evidence: “The company estimates over $300 million in potential new growth from its new high-speed bar lines at Elgin, which management expects to be realized over a 3-to-5-year timeline.”
expectation_evidence: “Elgin bar line — startup economics”; “Watch for … any first commentary on protein-bar distribution wins.”

description: CEO Jeffrey Sanfilippo will step down in October to become Executive Chairman, with his brother and current COO Jasper Sanfilippo succeeding him as CEO. The preview did not anticipate a leadership transition.
fact_evidence: “CEO Jeffrey Sanfilippo will step down in October to become Executive Chairman, with his brother and current COO Jasper Sanfilippo succeeding him as CEO.”

description: Hovnanian was expected to earn at least breakeven adjusted pre-tax income, with the preview’s base case at $5–9 million, but instead reported a $2 million loss. The miss was attributed largely to weak JV income and delayed new JV deliveries.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted pre-tax income was a $2 million loss—the first time in 23 quarters that pre-tax income missed the guidance range, driven largely by weak JV income and delayed new joint venture deliveries.”
expectation_evidence: Q3 guidance was “breakeven – $10M”; the preview’s base case expected “$5–9M.”

description: The preview expected a significant but unquantified Q4 step-up, with its bull case calling for revenue above $800 million and gross margin of at least 15.5%. Hovnanian guided to $800–900 million of revenue and 15%–16.5% gross margin, with an especially strong 15.8% midpoint, alongside $15–30 million of adjusted pre-tax income and $50–65 million of adjusted EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 guidance projects revenues of $800-$900 million, adjusted pre-tax income of $15-$30 million, adjusted EBITDA of $50-$65 million, and JV income of $10-$20 million”; gross margin guidance is “15%-16.5% range (15.8% midpoint).”
expectation_evidence: Management had promised “a significant step-up in fourth quarter performance”; the preview’s bull case anticipated “> $800M revenue” and “≥15.5% GM.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected Hovnanian to maintain double-digit absorption, based on Q2’s 11.3 contracts per community. Instead, quarterly contracts fell 4% year over year to 1,359, with management citing geopolitical volatility, high mortgage rates, and cautious buyers.
fact_evidence: “Quarterly contracts declined by 57 homes to 1,359 (a 4% drop) year-over-year,” with softness attributed to “geopolitical volatility, high mortgage rates, and cautious buyer behavior.”
expectation_evidence: “HOV holding double-digit absorption is a genuine differentiator”; the base case anticipated “absorption ~10–11.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

expectation_evidence: Management's expected “flat-to-slightly-higher” FY27 orders.

fact_evidence: “Net income of $1,379 million or $5.10 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted): $4.67 – $4.85”; “Net income (implied): ~$1.26–1.31B.”

description: Deere raised the FY2026 net income outlook's lower bound from $4.5 billion to $4.75 billion, while keeping the $5 billion upper bound. This is an upward revision, though slightly short of the preview's bullish scenario of a $4.8–$5.0 billion range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 net income guidance was raised to $4.75 billion to $5 billion.”
expectation_evidence: Standing guidance was “$4.5 – $5.0B”; the preview said narrowing to “$4.8–5.0B” would be bullish.

description: Q3 total net sales and revenues were $12.608 billion, modestly above the preview's comparable total-revenue estimate of roughly $12.4–$12.5 billion.

expectation_evidence: “Total net sales & revenues ~$12.4–12.5B.”

expectation_evidence: Small Ag & Turf consensus sales growth was “+12.0%” with an “Implied Margin” of “14.6%”; standing full-year margin guidance was “13.5–15%.”

fact_evidence: “Construction & Forestry Q3 sales jumped 18% to $3,618 million with 8 points of positive price realization (partly lapping prior-year incentives), and customer backlogs now extend well into fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: C&F consensus sales growth was “+16.9%”; the preview noted the order book was “+60% since November” and “>80% of production slots filled.”

expectation_evidence: “Net sales … $222.8M” versus “$155.1M a year ago,” or “+43.6%.”

description: Organic growth substantially exceeded the preview’s modeled 2–3%: the company reported 8% organic Q4 growth. Display Solutions organic growth was especially strong at 18%, well above the preview’s mid-to-high-single-digit expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q4 sales grew 51% (8% organic).” Display Solutions had “18% organic growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Organic +2–3%”; for Display Solutions it expected “mid-to-high single-digit growth.”

description: Full-year sales and adjusted EPS both finished above the preview’s estimates: sales reached $689 million versus roughly $678 million expected, and adjusted EPS was $1.25 versus an estimated $1.20–$1.22.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 net sales reached a record $689 million” and “adjusted EPS growing to $1.25.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated FY26 sales of “~$678M” and adjusted EPS of “~$1.20–1.22.”

fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin of 10.9% came in below expectations.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA margin ~11.5%” and described the base case as “~11.5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Lighting at “$69–70M” versus $72.7M, describing it as a “Guided mid-single-digit decline,” and flagged whether quote-to-order conversion improved as a key issue.

expectation_evidence: The preview said a Display Solutions margin “≥12%” would be the bull-case proof point and called for watching whether consolidated margin “holds the 12% set in Q3 including Royston.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix

expectation_evidence: The preview said Royston was underwritten at “~14% adjusted EBITDA margins” and identified margins of “≥13%” as an accretion proof point.

expectation_evidence: The preview said “the buy-side wants a new multi-year frame,” and described a reaffirmation of the existing target as “a disappointment.”

fact_evidence: “CFO Jim Galeese announced he will retire by end of October 2027 after nearly a decade of service, with a formal successor search already underway.”
