expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FCF margin: ~24.5% (seasonal low)” and described Q2 as “the seasonal trough.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS exceeded the preview’s $0.29 estimate, reaching a record $0.31. The preview expected 26.1% year-over-year growth, versus the reported 34% growth.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was a record $0.31, up 34% YoY on a split-adjusted basis.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS (post-split)” consensus was “$0.29,” with “+26.1%” year-over-year growth.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Ending ARR modestly exceeded the preview’s $5.79 billion expectation and grew faster than the preview’s approximately 24% estimate. CrowdStrike also reported a fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating ending ARR growth.
fact_evidence: “Ending ARR reached $5.84 billion (up more than 25% YoY), marking the fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating ending ARR growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed ending ARR consensus of “$5.79B” and “+24%” year-over-year growth.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Falcon Flex strength exceeded the preview’s already high prior-quarter benchmarks: ARR growth accelerated from 99% to 101%, and CrowdStrike added more than 935 Flex accounts, exceeding the prior three quarters combined. The reported 53% uplift for customers who reflexed at least twice was close to the preview’s 51% historical figure.
fact_evidence: “Falcon Flex ARR surpassed $2.29 billion, accelerating to 101% YoY growth”; “more than 935 new Flex accounts added—exceeding the prior three quarters combined.” Customers who reflexed at least twice had ending ARR “53% higher than their initial Flex baseline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Flex accounts had reached “$1.9B ending ARR, +99% y/y,” with “300+ accounts added in Q1,” and cited a “51% uplift” for customers who had reflexed multiple times.

description: The preview specifically wanted an AIDR ARR amount, but the reported call fact gave only a sequential comparison: AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1, without stating its dollar value. That leaves the requested dollar disclosure unmet even as the growth description was strong.
fact_evidence: “AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1”; no AIDR dollar amount is provided in the supplied call facts.
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Investors need a disclosed dollar figure, not another percentage off an undisclosed base.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Okta’s current RPO growth accelerated by roughly 200 basis points, stronger than the preview’s roughly 12–13% buy-side bar for another quarter of acceleration. Management attributed the strength mainly to large enterprises, rather than AI.
fact_evidence: “Current RPO growth accelerated by roughly 200 basis points,” which management attributed “primarily to large enterprise strength rather than AI.”
expectation_evidence: “Buy-side bar is realistically $2.53B+ (~12–13% growth) — a second straight quarter of cRPO acceleration is the entire re-rating thesis.”

description: Okta raised its FY27 revenue-growth outlook to 10–11%, above the prior 9–10% range and the preview’s expectation that a meaningful raise would be to at least $3.23–3.24 billion. The call facts provide a growth range, not an updated dollar range, so the size of the increase against that dollar threshold cannot be confirmed.
fact_evidence: “Okta guided FY27 total revenue growth to 10–11%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance to be updated: revenue $3.185–3.205B (+9–10%).” The preview also said the bar was “a raise to ≥$3.23–3.24B.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: New products rose to approximately 30% of bookings, above the 25% Q1 level highlighted in the preview. The preview flagged new-product mix as an important measure but did not give a specific Q2 forecast.
fact_evidence: “New products represented approximately 30% of bookings in Q2,” with Okta Identity Governance the leading contributor.
expectation_evidence: “New products ≈25% of Q1 bookings”; the preview also identified “New-product mix” as a key item to watch.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call provided concrete evidence of paid AI-agent deals—including several worth over $1 million—where the preview said quantified agent contribution was the key proof investors wanted and qualitative-only commentary was the likeliest disappointment. However, management said the business remains too small to register in Okta’s roughly $3 billion revenue base.
fact_evidence: “Okta closed dozens of Okta for AI agents deals including several worth over $1 million,” but management said this “remains too small to show up in the ~$3 billion revenue base.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any quantified contribution — agent-identity bookings, ACV, pipeline, or customer counts” and called “Qualitative-only commentary” the likeliest disappointment vector.

description: FY27 free-cash-flow margin guidance of 28–29% was above the preview’s prior 27–28% range, while the non-GAAP operating-margin guide of 26% was at the top of its prior 25–26% range.
fact_evidence: “Okta guided FY27 … non-GAAP operating margin of 26% and free cash flow margin of 28–29%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance to be updated … non-GAAP op. income … (25–26%) … FCF … (27–28%).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported strong growth in Okta’s largest customer tier—more than 20% year over year in customers above $1 million ACV, to over 600—without a comparable forecast for that tier in the preview. This adds evidence of large-enterprise strength beyond the preview’s discussion of $100,000-plus customers.
fact_evidence: “Customers with over $1 million in ACV grew more than 20% year-over-year, bringing the total to over 600 such customers.”

description: Okta completed the Premiso acquisition, adding a platform with 400 native risk detections versus Okta’s existing 90. The preview did not flag this acquisition or the added detection capability.
fact_evidence: “Okta completed its acquisition of Premiso,” which offers “400 native risk detections versus Okta’s existing 90,” to strengthen AI security and agentic runtime controls.

description: Okta used cash to settle the remaining $350 million of convertible notes and repurchased $125 million of shares, with $555 million still available under its buyback authorization. The preview noted an active buyback and cash balance but did not anticipate the debt settlement or give a repurchase amount.
fact_evidence: “Settled the remaining $350 million of convertible notes in cash in June, leaving no convertible debt,” ended with “about $2.3 billion in cash and investments,” and repurchased “1.5 million shares for $125 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “cash $2.589B; buyback active.”

description: Q2 revenue was $96B, above the preview’s $94–95B buy-side whisper and well above its roughly $92B consensus; growth also accelerated for a fourth consecutive quarter rather than merely matching the implied growth rate.
fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 total revenue reached a record $96 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, with growth accelerating for the fourth consecutive quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus $91.9–92.3B”; “Buy-Side / Whisper $94–95B.”

description: The Q3 revenue guide of $108B exceeds the preview’s ~$104B consensus and its $105B bull-line threshold, reaching the top of the preview’s bull scenario rather than its base case.
fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $108 billion (plus or minus 2%).”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY27 rev guide” consensus “$103.8–104.1B”; “$105B as the bull line”; bull scenario “≥$106–108B.”

description: The margin outlook is materially weaker than the preview’s expectation of about 75% with no dilution from the Rubin ramp: management now expects 74% in Q3, a 71–72% trough in Q4, and only 72–73% in FY2028.
fact_evidence: “Gross margins are being reset lower due to extreme memory pricing, with Q3 expected at 74%, bottoming at 71-72% in Q4, then settling at 72-73% in fiscal 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin” company guidance “74.9% GAAP / 75.0% non-GAAP ±50bp”; consensus “~75%”; buy-side “≥75%, no dilution from Rubin ramp.”

description: Data Center revenue reached $89B, above the preview’s roughly $85.7B consensus and its $85–87B base-case range. AC I&E grew faster sequentially than hyperscale, supporting the expected broadening of demand.
fact_evidence: “Q2 data center revenue rose 18% sequentially to $89 billion, with hyperscale at $49 billion (up 13% QoQ) and AC I&E at $40 billion (up 25% QoQ and 138% YoY).”
expectation_evidence: “Data Center rev” consensus “~$85.7B”; base case “Data Center $85–87B”; the preview identified “continued ACIE broadening” as an important proof point.

description: Management put a specific FY2028 growth outlook at about 70%, while saying unconstrained demand would imply roughly 100% growth. The preview did not give a FY2028 growth estimate, so the gap is against the demand ceiling stated on the call, not a published consensus forecast.
fact_evidence: “Management guided fiscal 2028 revenue growth of approximately 70%, describing it as supply-constrained since unconstrained demand points to roughly 100% (doubling) growth.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call quantified a major AWS deployment commitment that the preview had not specified: AWS is to deploy an additional 2 million GPUs over several quarters, providing concrete multi-quarter demand visibility.
fact_evidence: “AWS is deploying an additional 2 million GPUs from this quarter through Q2 fiscal 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “inference mix and backlog/supply commentary” and said “any quantified visibility (multi-quarter booked demand) supports the durability case,” but gave no deployment figure.

description: Management disclosed a substantial AI-lab financing and investment effort not anticipated in the preview: nearly $50B invested in Frontier AI labs and partnerships to raise over $500B in third-party financing. This adds a new, large funding channel to the demand outlook.
fact_evidence: “NVIDIA's revenue opportunity per gigawatt has expanded from ~$18 billion with Hopper to $25 billion with Blackwell to $40 billion with Vera Rubin, and is expected to rise further.”

description: The call newly indicated that AI labs using NVIDIA’s balance sheet are expected to account for roughly one-quarter of next year’s business. That is a substantial, previously unquantified source of demand, though it also ties some of the outlook to NVIDIA-backed financing.
fact_evidence: “The company expects demand from AI labs that leverage NVIDIA's balance sheet to contribute roughly one-quarter of next year's business.”

description: Ooma raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $332–333.5 million, above the preview’s cited prior range of $326–328.5 million and beyond its base-case expectation of a nudge to roughly $328–330 million. The new adjusted EBITDA and EPS ranges also exceed the prior ranges, with EPS reaching $1.35–$1.38.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2027 guidance projects revenue of $332-333.5 million”; “Full-year fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $47.5-48.3 million with non-GAAP EPS of $1.35-$1.38.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY2027 guidance (raised at Q1): revenue $326.0M–$328.5M; non-GAAP EPS $1.29–$1.34; adj. EBITDA $45.0M–$46.5M.” The preview’s base case expected guidance “nudged to high end (~$328–330M / $1.32–1.35).”

description: Q2 revenue of $83.2 million exceeded the preview’s $82.3 million high end of company guidance. The beat was also well above the roughly $80.2 million consensus figure.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $83.2 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY27 Company Guidance … $81.6M – $82.3M | Street Consensus … ~$80.2M.” The preview called the “real bar” the “high end of guidance (~$82.3M).”

description: Q2 profitability came in above the preview’s already-strong expectations: non-GAAP EPS was $0.35 versus a $0.34 guidance high end, while adjusted EBITDA was $12.4 million versus an implied range topping out around $12.0 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA hit a record $12.4 million (15% of revenue), up 74% year-over-year, while non-GAAP net income grew 58% to $10.2 million ($0.35 diluted EPS).”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $0.33 – $0.34”; “Adj. EBITDA (implied) | ~$11.5M – $12.0M.”

description: Ooma raised its residential outlook from an expected decline to expected growth, improving the segment outlook beyond the preview’s flat-to-1% decline plan. The preview had identified a second consecutive quarter of residential user growth as a possible narrative upgrade, but did not anticipate this stronger revenue outlook.
fact_evidence: “Residential revenue outlook was raised from a 1-2% decline to flat-to-1% growth.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 plan assumes residential subscription flat to -1%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Ooma reported a record $30.2 million of trailing-12-month free cash flow and $17.6 million of buybacks over four quarters, neither of which the preview anticipated; the preview focused instead on debt reduction and capacity for possible acquisitions.
fact_evidence: “The company generated record trailing-12-month free cash flow of $30.2 million, spent $17.6 million on buybacks over four quarters.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “continued quarterly paydowns to rebuild capacity for further tuck-in North American UCaaS deals” and said another acquisition was “a live possibility.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call disclosed 8% blended ARPU growth and a core-user count of 1.427 million, with business users now 49% of the total. The preview specifically said it did not expect ARPU or core-user metrics to be disclosed.
fact_evidence: “Blended ARPU rose 8% year-over-year to $16.95, and business users now represent 49% of the 1,427,000 total core users.”
expectation_evidence: “Ooma does not disclose net dollar subscription retention or ARPU in its releases, and stopped emphasizing a ‘core users’ count — do not expect those metrics.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Business-user additions were held down by IWG churn and a one-time count correction: reported growth was 4,000 users, versus 11,000 without those factors. The preview focused on organic business subscription growth but did not flag these specific headwinds.
fact_evidence: “Business user growth was dampened by 4,000 users of IWG churn and a one-time count correction, without which business users would have grown 11,000 instead of the reported 4,000.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “organic business subscription growth (ex-FluentStream/Phone.com)” and cited a 9% Q1 organic rate, without mentioning IWG churn or a count correction.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: MyPhone was already expected to be available through Walmart.com, with in-store shelf placement expected in the fall, but the call reported sales through Costco, Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Target. The wider set of named retail channels was not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: Residential additions were “driven largely by the newly launched MyPhone product now sold at Costco, Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said MyPhone was “on walmart.com with in-store shelf placement expected this fall.”

description: Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $3.91, well above the $3.67 consensus and the $3.69 top of guidance. The preview’s own base case was $3.78, so the earnings beat was larger than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $3.91” and exceeded guidance.
expectation_evidence: “Consensus $3.67”; guidance “$3.63–$3.69”; the preview’s base-case model was “non-GAAP EPS $3.78.”

description: Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $15.04–$15.10, a larger uplift than the preview’s expected modest increase to $14.80–$14.90. The new range is also well above the prior $14.72–$14.80 guidance.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance by $0.31 at the midpoint to $15.04-$15.10.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY26 EPS to be “nudged to $14.80–14.90”; existing guidance was “$14.72–14.80.”

description: Free cash flow guidance rose by $600 million to about $2.6 billion, substantially above the preview’s $2.0 billion figure. Cash-from-operations guidance also increased and planned CapEx fell, contributing to the larger FCF outlook.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was raised $600 million to approximately $2.6 billion,” cash from operations guidance was raised $500 million to about $2.8 billion, and CapEx was reduced to approximately $225 million.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance was “OCF ~$2,300M, FCF ~$2,000M, capex ~$300M.”

description: Q3 revenue exceeded both the $2.44 billion consensus and the top of guidance, rather than landing merely within the range. The beat was modest in percentage terms.
fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue reached $2.477 billion,” beating the high end of guidance.
expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$2.44B”; guidance was “$2,410–2,460M.”

description: Design IP revenue was $474 million, below the $487.4 million consensus, and growth of about 11% was below the preview’s expected 14%. The segment did return to growth, but its revenue recovery was weaker than expected.
fact_evidence: “The Design IP segment returned to growth with revenue of $474 million, up approximately 11% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: Design IP consensus was “$487.4M” and “+14%”; the preview said the Street needed “a second clean sequential quarter.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog edged down to $10.9 billion from the $11 billion reported at Q2, rather than rising. The decline was attributed to the processor IP solutions divestiture, which makes the signal less concerning than an unexplained decline but still falls short of the preview’s desired backlog progress.
fact_evidence: “Backlog remained strong at $10.9 billion but declined modestly quarter-over-quarter due to the divestiture of the processor IP solutions business.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$11B at Q2” and said “flat-to-down Synopsys backlog” would be a concern.

description: The reported non-GAAP operating margin of 41.6% exceeded the roughly 40% margin implied by the preview’s Q3 guidance discussion.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin of 41.6%,” exceeding guidance.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Guidance implies ~40% non-GAAP operating margin this quarter.”

description: Management now expects EDA to accelerate to double-digit organic growth in Q4 and for full-year 2026. The preview did not identify that acceleration outlook, making it a constructive growth-durability signal beyond the reported 8.5% Q3 growth.
fact_evidence: “EDA revenue grew 8.5% year-over-year” and management expects it “to accelerate to double-digit organic growth in Q4 and for full-year 2026.”

description: Synopsys reported record hardware-assisted verification revenue, with 12 new and 66 repeat customer wins. That was stronger evidence of hardware demand than the preview’s description of hardware/emulation timing as normalizing between Q3 and Q4.
fact_evidence: “Record hardware-assisted verification revenue,” with “12 new and 66 repeat HAV customer wins in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “hardware/emulation timing was framed as normalizing between Q3 and Q4.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview cited a PCIe 7.0 win rate above 90%; management reported wins in over 95% of opportunities, alongside 25 LPDDR6 design wins year-to-date and a die-to-die business on pace to double. These were stronger and broader IP traction signals than the preview had specified.
fact_evidence: “Over 95% of PCIe 7 opportunities won, 25 LPDDR6 design wins year-to-date, and a die-to-die business on pace to double year-over-year with over 100 cumulative design wins.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “PCIe 7.0 (>90% win rate), UCIe, HBM4 and custom AI silicon.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The first joint Synopsys-ANSYS multiphysics Fusion solution launched with customer-validated design-closure improvements of up to 10x, an unanticipated product milestone. However, management said it will not contribute revenue until 2027, so monetization is not near term.
fact_evidence: “The first joint Synopsys-ANSYS multiphysics Fusion solution launched in Q3” with results of “up to 10x faster design closure,” but “revenue contribution is not expected to begin until 2027.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: GAAP EPS included a gain from the processor IP divestiture, an additional positive one-off item not quantified in the preview. The preview anticipated the sale’s closure but discussed it as a revenue headwind, not as a gain affecting reported GAAP EPS.
fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS was $2.84 including a gain from the processor IP divestiture.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “close of the Processor IP Solutions sale” and an “~$40M FY26 revenue headwind,” but did not mention a gain.

description: Q2 revenue was $928 million, above the preview’s $904–905 million consensus and $902–905 million company guide. The roughly 2.5% beat was stronger than the preview’s stated base-case range of $915–922 million.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue reached $928 million,” exceeding the company’s guidance.
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $904.1M (Zacks) / $905.3M (street composite) | $902–905M”; the base case was “$915–922M.”

description: Non-GAAP operating income reached $416 million, well above the preview’s roughly $393 million consensus and $392–395 million guide. That also implies an operating margin around 44.8%, versus the preview’s expected roughly 43.6% and year-over-year compression.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $416 million,” exceeding the company’s guidance.
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income | ~$393M | $392–395M”; “Non-GAAP op margin | ~43.6%”; the preview described Q2 margin as down about 110 bps year over year.

description: Commercial subscription growth was about 13%, above the preview’s 11.3% estimate and contrary to its concern that this was the weaker side of the business. Growth was also double-digit excluding Crossix, with strength across CRM, content, data, and Crossix.
fact_evidence: “The commercial subscription segment grew approximately 13% year-over-year, with double-digit growth even excluding Crossix,” driven by broad-based strength.
expectation_evidence: “Commercial Solutions subscription growth (est. +11.3%). The weak side of the house”; the preview said a sub-11% print would undercut the CRM-win narrative.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: CRM momentum appears ahead of the preview’s expectation that Veeva would win a majority of four remaining top-20 migration decisions: management reported 12 of the top 20 committed, with only two more expected to be decided by year-end. The call also identified Regeneron as a Vault CRM selection; Biogen’s selection had already been announced before the release.
fact_evidence: “Best CRM quarter ever,” including “Biogen and Regeneron selecting Vault CRM”; “12 of the top 20 biopharma companies committed to Vault CRM, with only 2 remaining that are expected to be decided by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: Management had expected “to win the majority of the four remaining top-20 CRM migration decisions by fiscal year-end”; the preview also noted Biogen was already announced.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: More than 180 CRM customers are now live, substantially above the preview’s cited installed-base reference of more than 125 exiting FY26. The preview flagged the live-customer count as a metric to watch but did not anticipate a figure this high.
fact_evidence: “Veeva has over 180 CRM customers live.”
expectation_evidence: “Total live customers (was >125 exiting FY26).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AI use has moved beyond general monetization discussion to a large-scale customer deployment: one top-20 customer activated AI across its entire sales force, while management said Salesforce had no customers live. The preview focused on Falcon economics and monetization rather than this adoption proof point.
fact_evidence: “One top 20 customer activated AI across its entire sales force this quarter, contrasting with Salesforce having no customers live.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Veeva AI monetization detail” and described quantified Falcon bookings or revenue framing as the potential upside surprise.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Falcon has five early adopters and first go-lives are expected this year, but management said product readiness—not customer interest—is the constraint. That tempers the opportunity: the preview highlighted monetization proof and an upcoming early-adopter release, but did not flag Veeva’s own product readiness as the bottleneck.
fact_evidence: “Veeva Falcon … has 5 early adopters including one top 20 pharma, with first go-lives expected this year,” and management identified “being the rate-limiter on product readiness as the key constraint despite very high customer interest.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Falcon early adopters were expected ahead of a November release and described bookings, pipeline, or FY28 revenue framing as the key potential upside.

description: Management expects Falcon gross margins to be roughly similar to software margins, a more favorable cost outlook than the preview’s concern that AI investment was weighing on margins without yet producing AI revenue.
fact_evidence: “Management expects Falcon gross margins to be roughly similar to software margins,” because much of the work is pushed into deterministic software and AI model prices are expected to decline.
expectation_evidence: The preview said AI investment was “showing up in the P&L” and framed the bear case as “AI capex without AI revenue.”

description: Management described a longer-dated route to recapturing CRM customers that chose Salesforce: it expects some wins primarily in 2027–2028, before the backstop expires at the end of 2029. That provides a competitive opportunity but places the expected recovery mainly beyond the near term.
fact_evidence: Management is targeting “maintained CRM market leadership of over 70% share” and expects to win back some customers who selected Salesforce, “primarily in 2027-2028 before the Veeva CRM backstop expires end of 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the Vault CRM scoreboard and asked when revenue from new wins would turn on, noting that near-term contribution was likely immaterial; it did not provide a win-back timeline.

description: Management disclosed a horizontal CRM startup, Aspen, with a simplified $50-per-user monthly price plus usage overages. The planned financial exposure is minimal and no revenue is included in plans, while management is confident the market exists but uncertain about execution—an unanticipated new initiative with both limited near-term downside and execution risk.
fact_evidence: “The Aspen horizontal CRM startup carries minimal financial investment with no revenue factored into plans,” uses “$50 per user per month plus usage overages,” and management expressed “100% confidence the market exists but uncertainty on execution.”

description: HP reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $0.83, well above the $0.66 consensus bar and even the preview’s roughly $0.70 whisper. The $0.11 tariff-refund benefit helped, but EPS was still above the high end of company guidance without it.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $0.83, up 11%, and included $0.11 from tariff refunds, though EPS still exceeded the top of guidance even excluding that benefit.”
expectation_evidence: “Zacks consensus (as of the Aug 2026 preview) is $0.66”; “Treat $0.66 as the published bar and ~$0.70 as the whisper.”

description: Q3 revenue of $15.7 billion substantially exceeded the preview’s $14.60 billion consensus estimate and was also above the preview’s bull-case range of $14.9–$15.2 billion.
fact_evidence: “HP delivered record Q3 revenue of $15.7 billion, up 13% year-over-year (11% in constant currency).”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $14.60B (Zacks)”; bull scenario: “Revenue $14.9–15.2B (+7–9%).”

description: HP raised FY26 EPS guidance to $3.19–$3.29 from $2.90–$3.10, a much stronger upward revision than the preview’s base case of no raise or a narrow-up. The new range includes an estimated $0.19 tariff-refund benefit.
fact_evidence: “HP raised full-year EPS guidance to $3.19–$3.29 (from $2.90–$3.10) … including $0.19 of estimated tariff refund benefit for the year.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS guide vs. $2.90–$3.10”; base case: “FY26 guide narrowed to ~$2.95–$3.10 (no cut, no raise)”; a floor increase was described as “a genuine surprise.”

description: The Q4 EPS outlook of $0.69–$0.79 was higher than the preview’s base-case expectation of about $0.65 and the roughly $0.67 implied by the prior full-year guide. The range includes $0.08 of tariff-refund benefit.
fact_evidence: “Q4 EPS guidance is $0.69–$0.79, including $0.08 of tariff refund benefit.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 EPS framed at ~$0.65”; the preview also said the old full-year guide implied Q4 EPS of “~$0.67.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Personal Systems units fell about 16%, a sharper decline than the 7% drop cited for Q2, even as price and premium mix lifted segment revenue. That is a concerning indication of the unit elasticity the preview flagged as a key debate around PC price increases.
fact_evidence: “Personal Systems revenue hit a record $11.8 billion, up 18%, with commercial up 22% and consumer up 10%, despite units declining ~16%, driven by pricing, premium mix, and services.”
expectation_evidence: “Units fell 7% in Q2 … even as revenue rose 13% — all growth was price/mix”; “the question is whether 15–20% price increases start destroying demand.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Tariff refunds provided an unanticipated one-off boost to reported results: they contributed $0.11 to Q3 EPS and were the main reason Print operating margin rose year over year. The preview discussed trade-related costs but did not flag refunds as a benefit.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $0.83 … and included $0.11 from tariff refunds”; Print margin was “~1 point higher year-over-year mainly due to tariff refunds.”

description: HP also raised FY26 free-cash-flow guidance to $3.0–$3.2 billion from $2.8–$3.0 billion, above the preview’s expected reaffirmation and back-half weighting.
fact_evidence: “HP raised … free cash flow guidance to $3.0–$3.2 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF guide $2.8–$3.0B”; base case: “FCF reaffirmed but back-half weighted.”

description: The preview expected adjusted EBITDA of roughly negative $15–19 million; FCEL reported negative $36.7 million, a substantially larger loss than the expected range.
fact_evidence: “negative $36.7 million Adjusted EBITDA this quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “adj. EBITDA $(15)–(19)M” in the base scenario; the preview also cited Q2 adjusted EBITDA of “$(17.1)M.”

description: Revenue was expected to be about $38.8–41.3 million, with a roughly 16% year-over-year decline. Instead, revenue fell 29% to $33 million, below even the preview’s bear-case threshold of $34 million.
fact_evidence: “Total Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue fell 29% year-over-year to $33 million from $46.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $38.82M (-16.3% YoY)” and “Revenue (alt.) $41.31M”; the bear case was “<$34M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported $3.6 billion total committed-and-awarded capacity backlog was far above the preview’s expected roughly $1.05–1.15 billion. But $2.4 billion is awarded capacity that is not guaranteed to convert to revenue; the committed portion is $1.3 billion, only modestly above the preview’s $1.3 billion bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Total committed and awarded capacity backlog reached $3.6 billion,” including “$1.3 billion of committed backlog” and “a new $2.4 billion awarded capacity backlog that is not guaranteed to convert to revenue.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Backlog roughly flat at $1.05–1.15B”; the bull case required “Total backlog >$1.3B.”

description: The preview did not anticipate the scale of the Fit Energy-related gross loss: FCEL recorded a $24.5 million gross loss, including $17 million in charges because current costs exceeded contractual pricing for Phase 0. This was a worse gross result than the prior-year quarter’s $5.1 million loss cited in the call facts.
fact_evidence: “gross loss of $24.5 million (versus $5.1 million a year ago), primarily due to $17 million in charges” tied to Phase 0 of Fit Energy, “reflecting current costs exceeding contractual pricing.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview expected the deposit-backed 30 MW Fit Energy tranche to convert into product backlog and described the remaining capacity as phased against milestones. The call clarified that only Phase 0’s 30 MW is committed; the other 350 MW is at the customer’s sole election and creates no payment obligation unless elected.
fact_evidence: “only the 30-megawatt Phase 0 is committed, with Phases 1-3 (350 MW) at the customer's sole election and carrying no payment obligation until elected.”
expectation_evidence: “The Fit Energy 30 MW deposit-backed tranche should convert into product backlog this quarter”; the “remainder [was] phased against milestones.”

description: FCEL’s reported loss per share was worse than the preview’s consensus range, despite the year-over-year improvement in net loss. The preview had warned that share-count changes could make EPS comparisons noisy, but the reported $0.64 loss still exceeded the expected loss of roughly $0.39–$0.50 per share.
fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $45.3 million, or $0.64 per share,” compared with $92.5 million and $3.78 per share a year ago; weighted average shares were 70.4 million.
expectation_evidence: “EPS $(0.41)” with alternatives of “$(0.39) / $(0.50).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: After warning that the pipeline was a soft metric and looking for signed conversion evidence, the preview did not anticipate a specific 75 MW data-center capacity reservation. The agreement is a positive proof point, though definitive agreements and project timing remain pending.
fact_evidence: “Subsequent to quarter end, the company closed a 75-megawatt capacity reservation agreement with a major co-location data center operator for a Texas project, with definitive agreements and timing still pending.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “signed LOIs, deposits received, contracts executed,” and listed a “named new data-center contract” as a bull-case condition.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The pipeline was expected to be around 4–5 GW, with about 89% data-center-weighted proposals. FCEL reported roughly 10 GW of active proposals in fiscal 2026, with approximately 97% of Q3 pipeline tied to data centers—far more pipeline growth and concentration than anticipated, though pipeline is not the same as booked business.
fact_evidence: “Data center applications now account for approximately 97% of the third quarter pipeline,” which “has grown to roughly 10 gigawatts of active proposals in fiscal 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “4 GW” pipeline and expected “pipeline 4–5 GW”; it described the pipeline as “~89% data-center-weighted proposals.”

description: The preview expected the $225 million July offering to bolster liquidity and said silence on further issuance would be bullish. The reported cash balance reached $737.3 million, but the call also attributed roughly $298 million in net equity proceeds to the offering and open-market sales, indicating additional equity sales beyond the offering alone.
fact_evidence: “record $737.3 million in total cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash,” up from $440.9 million, “boosted by roughly $298 million in net equity proceeds from a July underwritten offering and open market sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$225M upsized equity offering” and said “Silence is bullish” on further issuance; it warned that “any further equity issuance signal post the $21 July offering” mattered.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview wanted evidence that production was visibly ramping but did not anticipate a disclosed annualized rate of only 37 MW for the quarter. FCEL aims to reach 100 MW by October 2026, with the 500 MW goal still dated June 2028, leaving a substantial near-term scale-up ahead.
fact_evidence: “The company operated at only a 37-megawatt annualized production rate this quarter and aims to reach 100 megawatts by October 2026,” with a goal of “500 megawatts by June 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “module production visibly ramping at Torrington” and cited the 500 MW capacity plan, but gave no quarterly production-rate estimate.

description: Management introduced a target for positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY2027, a concrete profitability milestone not specified in the preview. The target is qualified by backlog conversion, delivery schedules, and cost reductions, especially notable alongside the quarter’s negative $36.7 million adjusted EBITDA.
fact_evidence: “Management set a new target of achieving positive Adjusted EBITDA in Q4 fiscal 2027,” contingent on “backlog conversion, customer delivery schedules, and cost reductions.”

description: The preview anticipated reported EPS of $0.55–$0.65, partly from a gain on a May vessel sale, and consensus implied about $19.7 million of net income. The reported EPS was $0.46 and net income was $17.3 million, below those expectations.
fact_evidence: “Net income was $17.3 million” and “EPS of $0.46 for the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “Reported EPS could print $0.55–0.65” and “Net income | ~$19.7M implied.”

description: Revenue came in below both the $44.9 million consensus and the preview’s $43.5–$44.5 million estimate. The preview had anticipated a smaller fleet and Hormuz-related idle time, but actual revenue was still lower than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenues were $42.9 million,” driven by “fewer operational vessels and increased spot-market idle time.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 Consensus” revenue of “$44.9M”; “Our estimate: revenue $43.5–44.5M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Liquidity rose well beyond the preview’s estimate of about $155 million by early June: it was $168.3 million at quarter-end and later exceeded $250 million after the Echo Wizard insurance proceeds were collected. The preview treated the settlement as a Q3 event to monitor, rather than anticipating that more than $77 million would already have been collected after quarter-end.
fact_evidence: “Liquidity grew 70% in six months from $99 million to $168.3 million by June 30, and has since climbed to over $250 million after collecting more than $77 million from the Echo Wizard insurance settlement.”
expectation_evidence: “Cash was $131.2M at Q1-end and $155M by the June 5 call”; the settlement was “announced July 7, i.e. a Q3 event.”

description: Voyage expenses were materially above the preview’s roughly $5 million estimate, as higher bunker costs and Persian Gulf insurance premiums raised the bill to $7.2 million.
fact_evidence: “Voyage expenses rose to $7.2 million due to higher bunker costs and Persian Gulf insurance premiums.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimate build included “voyage expense ~$5M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Near-term 2026 charter coverage improved more than the preview’s Q1-exit figure, but the forward-year coverage did not improve and total secured revenue through 2029 was lower than the preview’s backlog figure. This left the expected defensive improvement concentrated in the remaining 2026 days rather than extending into 2027.
fact_evidence: “60% of remaining 2026 fleet days are secured”; “~$30 million secured for 2027 and total future secured revenues of about $90 million through 2029,” while “one-year forward coverage of 45% is below historical norms.”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 exit: 55% of remaining 2026 days and 45% of forward-year days fixed, ~$100M contracted into 2029.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The disruption was more severe than the preview’s cited 3% decline in global LPG exports: exports fell 8% in the first half, with sharp drops in Chinese imports and Indian demand. At the same time, rerouting increased ton-miles and drove VLGC rates to all-time highs, an offsetting rate benefit beyond the preview’s concern about idle and repositioning days.
fact_evidence: “The Persian Gulf conflict and Hormuz closure cut global LPG exports 8% in H1 2026 and slashed Chinese imports 29% and Indian demand 20%, but rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope boosted ton-miles and drove VLGC rates to all-time highs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “a 3% drop in global LPG exports” and highlighted “idle/repositioning days” as a Q2 revenue and utilization item.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview treated the Eaton relationship as an early-stage narrative with no quantified contribution; on the call, ChargePoint said early-access Express Solo units had begun shipping through the collaboration. This is a modest product milestone, though no revenue or broader commercial impact was reported.
fact_evidence: Richard Wilmer noted Express Solo and its collaboration with Eaton, and said early access units began shipping.
expectation_evidence: “Any quantification of Eaton / Mercedes-Benz ... / PDX contribution” was listed as a catalyst; the preview also described Eaton as “early innings.”

description: The preview expected gross margin around 28.5%-29.5% in its base case and called 29% or higher a positive result. Daktronics reported 30.5%, a stronger margin outcome than that expected range.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanded 80 basis points to 30.5%,” aided by operating leverage and favorable mix.
expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario gross margin was “28.5–29.5%”; the preview also said “Anything ≥29% is a clear positive.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview did not expect a tariff refund to land in the quarter and treated a refund disclosure as only a possibility. Daktronics said about $3 million in cash-basis tariff refunds helped gross margin, though rising input costs largely offset them.
fact_evidence: “About $3 million in cash-basis tariff refunds” aided gross margin and were “largely offset by rising input costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Do not assume it lands this quarter” and “a disclosed receivable or a sizing comment on the call is a real possibility.”

description: The preview’s EPS-based calculation implied roughly $23–24 million of operating income and about a 10.0% operating margin. Daktronics reported $24.9 million of operating income, above that implied range, while remaining within its 10%-12% target.
fact_evidence: “Operating income increased 7.2% to $24.9 million” and the company remained within its “10%-12% operating margin target range.”
expectation_evidence: “$0.40 EPS backs into roughly $23–24M of operating income, or ~10.0% operating margin.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected backlog to hold at or above $350 million, with a decline alongside weaker orders identified as a warning sign. Backlog instead entered Q2 at $311 million, and bookings and backlog both declined year over year; management attributed the movement to order timing and said substantial deals could convert in Q2.
fact_evidence: “Bookings and backlog declined year-over-year, with backlog entering Q2 at $311 million,” down from $356 million entering Q1; management said several substantial deals are expected to convert to purchase orders in Q2.
expectation_evidence: The preview said a backlog “holding ≥$350M” was favorable and that “a decline plus a backlog draw is the bear trigger.”

description: The preview did not flag a possible exit from Daktronics’ highly customized international transportation business. Management is considering an exit and has started a collective redundancy consultation affecting employees at its Ennistymon facility.
fact_evidence: The company is “considering exiting its highly customized international transportation business,” with a collective redundancy consultation process affecting Ennistymon employees.

description: The preview did not anticipate disclosure of SEC and NBA requests for information related to the Kawhi Leonard and Clippers investigation. Daktronics said it is cooperating, leaving an unresolved legal overhang.
fact_evidence: “Cooperating with SEC and NBA requests for information regarding the investigation of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers,” described as an unresolved legal overhang.

description: The preview gave a prior CapEx range of $14-$16 million but did not anticipate a higher investment plan. Management now plans annual CapEx of around $20 million to fund manufacturing automation.
fact_evidence: Management plans to “raise annual CapEx to around $20 million (from $14-16 million) to fund manufacturing automation.”

description: G-III guided Q3 sales to about $870 million and non-GAAP EPS to $1.34–$1.45, and said the quarter reflects the fiscal year's largest year-over-year PVH revenue reduction. The preview highlighted holiday and order-book commentary as important but did not provide a Q3 estimate, so the scale of this outlook was not quantified in advance.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of about $870 million (down from $989 million) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.34-$1.45 versus $1.90 last year, reflecting the largest year-over-year PVH revenue reduction of the fiscal year.”

description: Q2 sales were $555 million, below the preview's roughly $570 million guidance and consensus and its $578 million base estimate. The reported 10% year-over-year decline was also steeper than the preview's implied 7% decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell 10% year-over-year to $555 million, coming in slightly below plan due to European macro softness and the winding-down of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger licenses.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 guidance and consensus of “~$570M,” its base estimate of “$578M,” and an implied year-over-year decline of “−7%.”

description: Although G-III said Marc Jacobs would be slightly dilutive for the rest of FY2027 and accretive thereafter, it excluded the acquisition from current guidance and did not provide a quantified EPS dilution or a comparable FY2027 bridge. The preview's base scenario anticipated a Marc Jacobs range with the second-half drag acknowledged.
fact_evidence: “The Marc Jacobs acquisition is expected to be dilutive for the first 12 months (slight dilution in the remainder of fiscal 2027) and accretive thereafter, and is excluded from current guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview's base scenario anticipated “MJ guidance given as a range with acknowledged 2H drag”; it also called for the stub dilution and pro-forma impact to be quantified.

description: Q2 EPS of $0.26 narrowly beat the preview's $0.25 consensus and the $0.25 top of guidance, but fell short of the preview's $0.28 base estimate and its stated $0.28–$0.32 whisper range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS was $0.26, exceeding guidance of $0.15 to $0.25.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave “$0.25” consensus, a base estimate of “$0.28,” and said the whisper was “likely $0.28–0.32.”

description: G-III raised FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.20–$2.30 from the preview's then-current $2.15–$2.25 range, while leaving the approximately $2.71 billion sales outlook unchanged. This was a modestly stronger earnings outlook than expected.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.20-$2.30 (from prior levels) while reiterating net sales guidance of approximately $2.71 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance as it stands (excludes Marc Jacobs entirely): net sales ~$2.71B” and “non-GAAP EPS $2.15–2.25.”

description: Donna Karan sales grew more than 45%, above the preview's roughly 40% Q1 growth benchmark. This was stronger brand momentum than the preview's reference point.
fact_evidence: “Donna Karan sales up more than 45%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Donna Karan +~40%” as its Q1 anchor.

description: DKNY.com grew in the mid-20% range, slower than the roughly 40% growth cited in the preview for the prior quarter. Growth remained strong, but the reported pace had decelerated.
fact_evidence: “dkny.com growing in the mid-20% range year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “dkny.com +40%” as a Q1 anchor and warned that “Any deceleration in Donna Karan or a DKNY comp turning negative breaks the thesis.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The company received about $134 million in tariff refunds, a sizable cash source that supported liquidity. The preview identified the remaining receivable and cash timing as an open question but did not anticipate this reported refund amount.
fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $529 million in cash and roughly $1 billion in available liquidity, aided by approximately $134 million in tariff refunds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “the remaining balance of the $140M IEEPA receivable ($102.7M recognized in Q1) and its cash timing.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory was down 13% year-over-year, a cleaner position than the preview's Q1 reference of an 8% decline and supportive of the preview's clean-inventory thesis into holiday.
fact_evidence: “Inventory down 13% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 inventory “$417.9M (−8% Y/Y)” and said “Clean inventory into holiday supports the full-price selling narrative.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $1.42 versus the preview’s $1.14 estimate, but about $0.35 per share came from one-time tariff refunds. Excluding that refund contribution, EPS was roughly $1.07—below the estimate despite the large reported beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 43% to $1.42” and “roughly $0.35 of EPS came from one-time EPA/IEEPA tariff refunds.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $1.14.”

description: Net sales were $741 million, below the preview’s roughly $757 million consensus, even though sales rose year over year on new-store openings.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 9.1% to $741 million driven by new store openings.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales $757.9M” (with another cited estimate of $756.4M).

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comparable sales fell 1.8%, missing the preview’s +0.3% consensus, though the decline was less severe than the preview’s roughly –1% buy-side whisper. Transactions were flat and a lower basket drove the decline.
fact_evidence: “Comparable store sales declined 1.8% amid flat transactions and a lower basket.”
expectation_evidence: “Comparable store sales: +0.3%”; the preview also cited a buy-side whisper of “~–1%.”

description: Reported gross margin reached 43.5%, far above the preview’s 40.2–40.6% estimate, but tariff refunds supplied more than the entire reported year-over-year expansion. Excluding refunds and price investment, margin was about 40.3–40.4%, only modestly above the preview’s range.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 360 basis points to 43.5%, but 380bp of the benefit came from tariff refunds”; excluding refunds and price investment, gross margin “would have been ~40.3-40.4%.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~40.2–40.6% (my est.).”

description: The new full-year adjusted EPS range of $4.57–$4.65 is above the preview’s cited prior guidance of $4.45–$4.55 and above its base case of holding that range, even as the sales and comp outlook was reduced.
fact_evidence: Full-year adjusted EPS is now projected at “$4.57-$4.65.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance as of Q1 … adj. EPS $4.45–4.55”; the preview’s base case said “adj. EPS $4.45–4.55 held.”

description: Management put roughly $28 million of net tariff refunds into the full-year outlook, with a stated roughly 100bp gross-margin benefit partly offset by about 50bp of price investments. The preview said refunds had previously been excluded from guidance and identified their inclusion as an open question.
fact_evidence: “The company expects roughly $28 million in net tariff refunds … for the full year, benefiting gross margin ~100bp offset by ~50bp of price investments, with margins guided to 41.3%.”
expectation_evidence: Management had “explicitly excluded” refunds from prior guidance; the preview asked, “Tariff refunds — in or out of guidance?”

description: The company raised its full-year buyback plan to $175 million from the preview’s approximately $125 million target, after repurchasing $137 million year to date.
fact_evidence: “Repurchased $84 million of stock in Q2 and $137 million year-to-date” and “raised its full-year buyback plan to $175 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Buyback ~$125M”; the preview said an accelerated repurchase would be a possible signal to watch.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The call reported 50 new stores opened in Q2 versus the preview’s consensus of 15, a much faster pace than expected. The provided facts also say 42 stores opened in the first half, so the reported Q2 and first-half figures do not reconcile.
fact_evidence: “Ollie's opened 50 new stores in Q2 (42 in the first half) toward a 75-store full-year target.”
expectation_evidence: “New stores opened: 15”; the preview also said the 75-store full-year target was reaffirmed.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management quantified about $15 million of full-year price investments, including roughly $10 million in the back half, and said it was willing to spend more to protect price leadership. The preview anticipated price reinvestment in general but did not quantify this commitment or the willingness to increase it further.
fact_evidence: “The company plans approximately $15 million in full-year price investments (~$10 million in the back half) and signaled willingness to spend more to protect its price leadership position.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management’s bias was to “widen price gaps” and reinvest margin, but gave no investment amount.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Weather-sensitive categories were said to have directly reduced comps by more than 100bp, with softness concentrated in the Midwest and Texas and longer drives amplifying fuel-price pressure. The preview discussed weather as a possible explanation but did not anticipate this quantified drag or these regional details.
fact_evidence: “Weather-sensitive categories like lawn/garden and room air created over 100 basis points of direct comp drag,” with softness in “the Midwest and Texas where longer drive times amplified fuel-price headwinds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the regional split and said a repeat of weather-related weakness could mean “the weather excuse holds.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said acquired Big Lots stores were comping better than the typical negative mid-to-high-single-digit second-year pattern, a more favorable performance signal than the preview discussed.
fact_evidence: “Acquired Big Lots stores are comping better than the typical negative mid-to-high single-digit second-year pattern.”

description: Petco had guided to Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $110–112 million and the preview expected no further tariff refunds. Adjusted EBITDA was $122 million including a $6.8 million net tariff refund; even excluding it, normalized EBITDA of $115 million beat the company’s outlook, though it was within the preview’s $114–116 million whisper range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $122 million (8.2% of sales), including a $6.8 million net tariff refund, while normalized adjusted EBITDA of $115 million exceeded both prior year and the company's outlook.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: $110–112M guide”; “The functional buy-side bar is therefore ~$114–116M”; “management explicitly said Q2 carries the anticipated tariff headwind and assumed no further refunds.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Petco Perks relaunch led to far more point redemptions than projected, creating an unexpected sales drag of mid-single-digit millions, mainly in services.
fact_evidence: “The Petco Perks membership relaunch triggered point redemptions that far exceeded projections, negatively impacting Q2 sales by an estimated mid-single-digit millions, primarily in the services business.”

description: SG&A increased only $1 million despite lapping a roughly $9 million actuarial benefit, implying underlying expenses fell about $8 million. The preview highlighted whether the turnaround could deliver SG&A leverage or further cost take-out, but did not anticipate this degree of underlying expense reduction.
fact_evidence: “SG&A was $543 million (36.5% of sales), up only $1 million despite lapping a ~$9 million actuarial benefit, implying underlying expenses fell about $8 million.”
expectation_evidence: “The distinguishing question on the call: does H2 EBITDA growth come from comp-driven SG&A leverage … or from another round of cost take-out and store closures?”

description: Petco voluntarily prepaid another $75 million of debt on September 1, bringing paydown over nine months to $170 million—more concrete and substantial deleveraging than the preview had specified as an open possibility.
fact_evidence: “The company voluntarily prepaid an additional $75 million in debt on September 1st, bringing total pay down over the last nine months to $170 million as it targets a 2x leverage ratio.”
expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet — further debt paydown below $1.48B, FCF, or any refinancing/maturity commentary.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview described a 2027 veterinary expansion decision as still ahead; management instead said new hospital openings are planned to begin in 2027, alongside double-digit growth in visits, doctor days, and vet diet sales.
fact_evidence: “Vet business delivered double-digit growth in total pet visits, double-digit expansion in doctor days, and double-digit vet diet sales growth for both dogs and cats, with new hospital openings planned to begin in 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “the 25 underutilized hospitals being optimized ahead of a 2027 expansion decision”; “any commitment to 2027 hospital expansion”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The total customer base returned to slight growth in Q2, an encouraging customer trend not specifically anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “The total customer base inflected to slight growth in Q2.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: A seven-store new-format test launched in May is already showing sizable lifts in new and reactivated customers, larger baskets, improved margins, and NPS up hundreds of basis points; the preview did not flag this test or these results.
fact_evidence: “A 7-store new-format market test launched in May is showing sizable lifts in new and reactivated customers, larger baskets, improved margins, and NPS up hundreds of basis points, with a broader remodel rollout targeted for 2027.”

description: REX reported diluted EPS of $1.06, far above both the preview’s $0.42 consensus and its own $0.43–$0.50 estimate. The result was more than double the preview’s modeled range.
fact_evidence: “Record second quarter net income of $1.06 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS (to REX) … $0.42”; the preview’s estimate build put EPS at “~$0.43–0.50.”

description: Gross profit reached $53.3 million, well above the preview’s $22–$27 million estimate. The call also said gross profit grew about 144% year over year even excluding 45Z credits, indicating strength beyond the credits themselves.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit surged to $53.3 million from $14.3 million a year earlier,” and grew “approximately 144% year-over-year even excluding 45Z tax credits.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Gross profit … ~$22–27M (14–16%).”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: REX recognized $18.4 million of 45Z income in the quarter, substantially above the preview’s roughly $7.0–$7.3 million estimate based on a $0.10-per-gallon accrual. The preview specifically identified a higher accrual or true-up as something to watch, but the reported amount was much larger than its modeled run rate.
fact_evidence: “The company recognized approximately $18.4 million in Section 45 production tax credit income during the quarter,” flowing directly through gross profit.
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “45Z credit … ~$7.0–7.3M” and said REX was “conservatively booking $0.10/gal.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The EPA issued draft Class 6 injection well permits for three One Earth carbon-capture wells, a meaningful regulatory step beyond the preview’s baseline of ongoing review and a pending state application. The permits remain drafts in public comment, rather than final approvals.
fact_evidence: “On August 17, the U.S. EPA issued draft Class 6 injection well permits for three wells associated with the One Earth carbon capture project,” now in public comment.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “EPA review ongoing” and described a filing, completed technical review, or “a dated permit expectation” as the valuable disclosure to watch; its base case was “permits still pending.”

description: SG&A was $15.6 million, materially above the preview’s $9.5–$10.5 million estimate, primarily because of higher incentive compensation and restricted stock issued during the quarter. This was a meaningful cost headwind even as earnings substantially exceeded expectations.
fact_evidence: “SG&A expenses rose to $15.6 million from $6.2 million a year earlier,” primarily due to “higher incentive compensation and restricted stock issued during the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “SG&A … ~$9.5–10.5M.”

description: Management said third-quarter results should be profitable and better than the same period last year, supported by record ethanol export demand. The preview did not identify this forward-looking earnings outlook.
fact_evidence: “Management guided that third quarter results are expected to be profitable and better than the same period last year, supported by record ethanol export demand.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The expansion remains on schedule for end-2026 completion, but REX’s target of reaching production near 200 million gallons is early-to-mid next year. That points to full-volume production after the preview’s expectation of full operation in late FY2026, even though the construction completion date remains on track.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

fact_evidence: “Fiscal August comps accelerated to 14.6%, extending the streak to 13 consecutive months of comparable sales growth despite tougher year-over-year comparisons.”
expectation_evidence: Preview: the Q3 trend would be signaled by “mid-single-digit-or-better comps”; its base case assumed “May’s run-rate simply holds,” with +3–5% Q3 comps.

description: The Q3 outlook is substantially stronger than the preview’s framework: sales guidance of $150–155 million and comps up 10–14% are well above its $138–144 million sales and +3–6% comp bogeys. fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $150-155 million (comps up 10-14%).”

expectation_evidence: Preview’s Q3 framework was “EPS around breakeven to +$0.05” versus $(0.05) last year.

expectation_evidence: Preview cited “TTM net loss of $3.25M” and said confirming positive cash generation mattered.

fact_evidence: “Improved performance triggered $1.5 million in bonus accruals in Q2, an expense absent from the model for four years that will continue to pressure SG&A leverage.”
expectation_evidence: Preview modeled Q2 SG&A at “$48M – $49M” and discussed expected leverage, but did not anticipate a bonus accrual; it noted “100–150bps of likely occupancy leverage.”

description: HPE reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.11, well above the preview’s $0.97–$1.00 whisper range and above the high end of its $0.88–$0.93 guidance. It was also the first quarter in which HPE exceeded $1 of EPS.

fact_evidence: “HPE raised FY26 EPS guidance to $3.75–$3.85 and free cash flow to at least $3.75 billion.”

expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Gross profit ~$107M (1.85%).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview highlighted Google’s dual-sourcing of ASICs as a concern and called for updates on TPU share. Broadcom instead announced a long-term Google agreement expected to deliver multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually, with the next-generation TPU already in production.
fact_evidence: “A long-term agreement with Google will deliver multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually over several years, with next-gen TPU v8i now in production ahead of the prior Ironwood generation.”
expectation_evidence: “Tan conceded last quarter that Google is dual-sourcing ASICs. Watch for … any color on Google TPU share.”

description: The preview described OpenAI’s roughly $18B, 1.3GW first phase as reportedly stalled and noted deployment was still guided to 1GW+ in 2027. The call projected OpenAI as Broadcom’s second-largest XPU customer, with over 5GW of deployment in 2028; that projection does not itself resolve the preview’s question about the first phase or its 2027 timing.
fact_evidence: “OpenAI is projected to become Broadcom's second-largest XPU customer, with over 5 gigawatts of deployment in 2028.”
expectation_evidence: “The ~$18B, 1.3GW first phase reportedly stalled”; “Volume XPU deployment is still guided to 1GW+ in 2027.”

description: The preview did not cite a specific Anthropic deployment scale or forecast it becoming Broadcom’s largest XPU customer. Management said it is on track to become the largest in 2027, with deployments rising from 1GW in 2026 to 5GW in 2027 and an additional 10GW in 2028.
fact_evidence: “Anthropic is on track to become Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027, deploying 5 gigawatts of TPU v8i in 2027 and an incremental 10 gigawatts in 2028, after 1 gigawatt of Ironwood in 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Anthropic among the “current six” named XPU customers but gave no customer-ranking or deployment forecast for it.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview did not flag a Broadcom accelerator performance or cost comparison with Nvidia’s product. The call reported that OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator outperforms Grace Blackwell Ultra at roughly half the cost of a GPU.
fact_evidence: “Its Jalapeno accelerator reportedly outperforms Grace Blackwell Ultra at roughly half the cost of a GPU.”

description: The preview expected Q3 gross margin around 74%. Broadcom reported 75%, about one percentage point above that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin … in Q3” was 75%.
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin … ~74%.”

description: The preview centered on gross margin around 74% and described below 73% as a bear-case outcome. Broadcom guided Q4 gross margin to about 73%, indicating further decline rather than holding near 74%.
fact_evidence: “[Gross margin] is guided to fall to about 73% in Q4 due to rising XPU and memory mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP GM ~74%”; the preview’s bear scenario included “GM guided <73%.”

description: The preview expected operating margin around 67%. Management said Q4 operating margin would be about 66%, a modest step below that level, despite describing operating leverage as resilient.
fact_evidence: “Operating margin remains resilient at ~66% from operating leverage.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin ~67%”; the preview said bulls needed management to re-anchor on “operating margin (67%).”

description: The preview did not include a long-term EPS target. Management said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 in EPS in FY2028, adding a specific long-range earnings milestone.
fact_evidence: “Broadcom stated it is on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview estimated net new ARR of roughly $33–37 million and set $35 million as the bar; Netskope reported $54 million. That is a large dollar beat, although the reported 9% growth rate is less compelling than the preview’s hoped-for reacceleration.
fact_evidence: “Net new ARR of $54 million growing only 9%.”
expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR (not guided): ~$33–37M (my est.)”; “Bar: ≥$35M, and ideally flat-to-up YoY.”

description: Operating margin was much better than the preview’s expected Q2 range: negative 9% versus guidance of negative 14% to negative 15%. The improvement was driven largely by an approximately 8-point reduction in R&D as a percentage of revenue.
fact_evidence: “Operating margin improved 11 percentage points year-over-year to negative 9%, significantly ahead of guidance, driven largely by an ~8-point improvement in R&D as a percent of revenue.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin: (14)% to (15)%.”

description: Revenue of $220.5 million cleared both company guidance and the preview’s assumed buy-side bar of roughly $216–217 million, rather than merely delivering the expected beat.
fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 29% to $220.5 million, beating guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $213–215M”; “Assume buy-side bar ≈ $216–217M.”

description: Netskope raised its FY2027 revenue outlook to $888–892 million, above the preview’s base-case raise to $885–888 million and around the preview’s $890 million confidence threshold. The company said the increase exceeded the Q2 beat.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $888-892 million (~26% growth), lifting it by more than the Q2 beat.”
expectation_evidence: “A raise to $890M+ with explicit 2H net new ARR commentary is the bull trigger”; base case: “Raised to $885–888M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Free cash flow improved substantially from Q1 but remained weaker than the preview’s preferred Q2 range of roughly negative $20 million to breakeven. Full-year FCF margin is now guided to about 2%, the bottom of the preview’s prior 2%–4% range; Q3 positive FCF and faster-than-expected annual-billing transition partly offset the shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $29.8 million in Q2, with full-year free cash flow margin guided to ~2% and Q3 FCF of $10-20 million, aided by a faster-than-expected transition to annual billings that grew contracted future billings 75%.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FCF materially worse than roughly ‑$20M to breakeven” was the downside threshold; FY guidance was “+2% to +4%”; management had called Q1 the “low-water mark” and expected positive quarterly FCF in the back half.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Expansion and product adoption were stronger than the preview’s already-high baseline: NRR rose to 114% from 113%, 4+ product adoption reached 59% from the 57% Q1 baseline, and 41% of customers used 5+ products.
fact_evidence: “Net retention rate rose to 114% and gross retention hit an all-time high, with 59% of customers now using 4+ products (up from 51%) and 41% using 5+ products (up from 35%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “NRR (113%)” and “57% of customers on 4+ products” as metrics to watch.

description: The AI security pipeline showed meaningful progress, with about one-third of it in or entering POC, but the disclosed 6–12-month enterprise sales cycle pushes expected AI revenue contribution toward the second half and Q4 rather than showing near-term conversion.
fact_evidence: “Roughly one-third of its AI security pipeline is in or entering the POC phase, with most deals following a 6-to-12-month enterprise sales cycle that pushes AI revenue contribution toward the second half and Q4.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called AI suite conversion a key watch item: “pipeline → closed ARR contribution, named logos, attach rates,” while noting that prior commentary concerned “pipeline, not bookings.”

description: The company disclosed an approximately 5% workforce reduction alongside a shift of spending toward AI infrastructure and tokens. The preview did not anticipate this restructuring and investment reallocation.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced approximately 5% of its workforce while reallocating spend toward AI infrastructure and tokens as part of driving ‘AI nativeness’ across the business.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management presented AI security as a new revenue pillar and sized it as a roughly $170 billion greenfield opportunity within a $336 billion total addressable market—an expansive market framing not raised in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Netskope frames its opportunity as a $170 billion greenfield AI security market within a $336 billion total addressable market, positioning AI security as a new revenue pillar beyond SASE/SSE.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was $32.9 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $30–32 million; the reported 25% margin also exceeded its 23.7% base estimate. This was a modest operating-performance upside relative to the preview.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $32.9 million with a 25% margin.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$30–32M”; base estimate: “$31M (23.7% margin).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Phreesia reported a 2.4% Payment Solutions revenue rate, above the 2.3% rate the preview highlighted as the level to watch. That points to a slightly better rate than expected to hold as AccessOne mixed in.
fact_evidence: “Total managed payments were $1.626 billion in the quarter, with a Payment Solutions revenue rate of 2.4%.”
expectation_evidence: “Payment Solutions rate (2.3%) … Watch whether the rate holds as AccessOne mixes in.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: A Provider Connect study produced follow-on business during FY27, earlier than the preview’s framing of Provider Connect primarily as an FY28–FY30 opportunity. The preview did describe FY27 dollars as possible upside, so the commercial conversion is an upside signal rather than a wholly unanticipated revenue contribution.
fact_evidence: “A 4-month GLP-1 category study using Provider Connect showed a 4% incremental lift in new-to-brand prescriptions versus a matched control group and more than 1,000 new patient starts, and converted follow-on business.”
expectation_evidence: “Management has framed ProviderConnect as an FY28–FY30 runway, so any FY27 dollars are upside.”

description: The preview highlighted a possible buyback authorization as a notable capital-allocation surprise, while the reported capital-allocation action was to reduce debt principal by more than $23 million. The provided facts do not report a buyback, so the disclosed action leaned toward deleveraging rather than the potential repurchase catalyst.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced debt principal by over $23 million during the quarter while maintaining a healthy cash balance of $74.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Management named ‘share repurchases, as appropriate’ as a priority”; “A buyback authorization at ~$12 … would be a meaningful sentiment reset.”

description: Snowflake reported $1.49 billion of product revenue, above the preview’s $1.46–$1.48 billion whisper range and the $1.47 billion bull-case threshold. The beat was modest, but growth accelerated to 37%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 product revenue reached $1.49 billion, growing 37% year-over-year, marking the third consecutive quarter of acceleration.”
expectation_evidence: “Product revenue … Est. Buy-Side Whisper $1.46–1.48B”; the bull case expected “≥$1.47B.”

description: Snowflake raised FY’27 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, well above the preview’s anticipated $5.95 billion-or-higher bar. This was a substantially larger raise than the preview’s base-case range of $5.88–$5.94 billion.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year FY'27 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% growth), an increase of over 500 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 product guide ≥$5.95B” was the catalyst threshold; the base scenario expected “$5.88–5.94B.”

description: The company lowered FY’27 non-GAAP product gross margin guidance to 74%, below the preview’s 75% catalyst threshold and the level at which it warned AI-related margin dilution would become a concern. Management attributed the reduction to the growing mix of lower-contribution-margin AI workloads.
fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP product gross margin guidance was lowered to 74% due to a higher revenue mix from fast-growing AI workloads that carry lower contribution margins today.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP product gross margin ≥75%” was a catalyst; the preview said “Sub-74.5% turns the AI story into a margin-dilution story.”

description: Snowflake raised FY’27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5%, above the preview’s 13–14% whisper range. Q2 margin was also 15%, expanding by more than 400 basis points year over year.
