fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance was raised from 13.5% to 14.5%, with Q3 guided at 15.5%”; Q2 margin “expanded over 400 basis points year-over-year to 15%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Non-GAAP op margin … Est. Buy-Side Whisper 13–14%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Net new customer additions exceeded the preview’s expected range: Snowflake added 692 customers, versus the preview’s sell-side expectation of 440–490 and its comparison point of 616 additions in Q1. Total customers reached 14,554, above the preview’s 14,450-plus whisper.
fact_evidence: “692 net new customers added (a 32% year-over-year increase) bringing total customers to 14,554.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~14,350–14,400 (+440–490 net)” by consensus and “14,450+” in its whisper; it also noted “+616 in Q1.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: CoCo adoption was stronger than the preview’s already-raised expectation: it reached 9,100 accounts, versus the preview’s Q1 reference of 7,100 and expectation for accounts “well above” that level.
fact_evidence: “CoCo surpassed 9,100 accounts, adding over 2,000 net new accounts in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “CoCo accounts vs. 7,100 last quarter” and described the bull case as having accounts “well above 7,100.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The revenue acceleration was not solely dependent on AI products: management attributed roughly half to AI and the other half to core platform strength, migrations, and other products. That counters the preview’s concern that the prior-quarter AI surge might have been a pull-forward.
fact_evidence: “Roughly half of the revenue acceleration” came from AI products, “with the other half from core platform strength, migrations, and other products.”
expectation_evidence: The preview raised the possibility that “Q1's Cortex Code surge” was “a pull-forward” and said the bear case would involve Q1 acceleration reflecting “front-loaded AI experimentation.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: RPO growth slowed to 30% from 38% in Q1, a weaker headline trend than the prior-quarter figure the preview highlighted. However, the portion expected to convert within 12 months implies about 42% year-over-year growth, making the signal mixed rather than uniformly weak.
fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligations grew 30% year-over-year to $9 billion, with approximately 54% expected to be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months (about 42% year-over-year growth).”
expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “RPO growth (+38% in Q1)” as a key metric to watch and noted that RPO “is lumpy on large renewals.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call disclosed CoWork at 5,800 accounts, up nearly 11% quarter over quarter. The preview discussed AI adoption and CoCo but did not anticipate or provide an expectation for CoWork adoption.
fact_evidence: “CoWork expanded to 5,800 accounts, up nearly 11% quarter-over-quarter.”

description: Genesco reported an adjusted loss of $0.83 per share, substantially smaller than the preview’s $1.34 expected loss, even though revenue and comparable sales were roughly in line.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted loss per share improved to $0.83” and “bottom-line results came in well ahead of expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS Consensus $(1.34).”

description: Genesco cut its full-year comparable-sales outlook from growth of 1%–2% to flat, and now expects total sales to fall about 2% rather than its prior outlook of down 1% to flat; it cited greater pressure at schuh in the promotional UK market.
fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was cut to flat comparable sales (from up 1%-2%) and total sales down approximately 2%, reflecting greater sales pressure at schuh in the increasingly promotional UK market.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance … comps +1–2%; total sales –1% to flat.”

description: While the $2.00–$2.40 full-year adjusted EPS range was not raised, Genesco now expects to finish at its high end, above the midpoint expectation described on the call and more constructive than simply reiterating the range.
fact_evidence: “The company now expects full-year adjusted EPS at the high end of its $2 to $2.40 range, up from the prior midpoint expectation.”
expectation_evidence: “Reiteration of $2.00–$2.40 is the minimum acceptable outcome”; the preview’s base case was that the FY guide would be reiterated.

description: Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 basis points, well ahead of the company’s 50–70-basis-point Q2 guide; schuh’s 300-basis-point improvement and a 10-point rise in full-price mix were key drivers.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 basis points to 47.2%, driven largely by schuh's 300 basis point margin improvement as full-price mix rose 10 percentage points.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … +50–70 bps.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Journeys’ comp accelerated from 2% for Q2 to mid-single digits in August, providing a stronger late-quarter signal than the preview’s concern that back-to-school demand had shifted later and needed confirmation in Q3.
fact_evidence: “Journeys posted its eighth consecutive quarter of positive comps (up 2%) and accelerated to a mid-single-digit comp in August.”
expectation_evidence: “2026 BTS intent has skewed later (September 29% of intent vs. August 26%), pushing revenue into Q3”; the preview called for explicit September/Q3 color to establish whether demand had shifted or failed to materialize.

description: NetApp reported Q1 revenue of $2.03 billion, well above the $1.836 billion consensus and the $1.90 billion high end of guidance. Even excluding the roughly $65 million from the extra week flagged in the preview, revenue was about $1.965 billion.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% year-over-year to a record $2.03 billion (26% growth excluding the extra week that added ~$65 million), exceeding the high end of all guidance ranges.”

description: Q1 non-GAAP EPS reached $2.58, far above the $2.12 consensus and even the preview’s bullish scenario of $2.30–$2.40. The preview’s base case was $2.18–$2.26.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.58, up 66% year-over-year—more than double the revenue growth rate.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus (as of 9/1/26): $2.12”; the bull scenario forecast EPS of “$2.30–2.40.”

description: Q1 operating margin reached 31.9%, substantially above the approximately 28.9% consensus expectation. That was a 6.1-point year-over-year expansion, versus the preview’s expected 3.1-point expansion.
fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 6.1 points to 31.9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 operating-margin consensus at “~28.9%” and implied year-over-year growth of “+310bp.”

description: NetApp raised its FY27 revenue midpoint to $8.1 billion, well above the prior $7.45 billion midpoint and the preview’s roughly $7.5 billion consensus. It also lifted the EPS midpoint to $9.88 from $8.85, above the preview’s roughly $8.90 consensus.
fact_evidence: “Management materially raised full-year FY27 guidance, increasing the revenue midpoint by $650 million to $8.1 billion (17% growth) and lifting the EPS midpoint to $9.88 (22% growth).”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 company guidance of “$7.325–7.575B” revenue and “$8.70–9.00” EPS, with consensus of “~$7.5B” revenue and “~$8.90” EPS.

description: The Q2 revenue midpoint of $2.1 billion is far above the $1.84 billion consensus, despite the preview’s base scenario of $1.87–$1.95 billion. The reported 23% year-over-year growth represents deceleration from Q1, but the dollar guide is much stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies decelerating growth of 23% year-over-year at the $2.1 billion revenue midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue: $1,840M”; the preview’s base scenario forecast “Q2 rev $1.87–1.95B.”

description: Q2 EPS guidance of $2.59 is well above the $2.16 consensus and the preview’s base-case range of $2.18–$2.26.
fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies … EPS midpoint of $2.59.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 EPS: $2.16”; the preview’s base scenario forecast “Q2 … EPS ~$2.18–2.26.”

description: The Q2 gross-margin guide of 67%–68% is below the preview’s key threshold of 69% and well below the level it said would confirm the product-margin trough. Product gross margin had also fallen 150 basis points sequentially to 54.6% as component costs rose.
fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies … gross margin of 67%-68%”; “Product gross margin declined 150 basis points sequentially to 54.6% due to higher component costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Above 69.5% = trough confirmed”; “Below 69.0% = the FY27 $8.70–9.00 bridge is in question.”

description: Despite the weak near-term gross-margin guide, management said product gross margin for the rest of FY27 should be slightly better than its prior low-50% outlook, as pricing actions are being captured faster. That is better than the preview’s concern that component-cost increases might outrun pricing.
fact_evidence: “Management now expects [product gross margin] to run slightly better than the prior low-50% outlook for the rest of the year as pricing actions are captured faster.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned: “If the Q2 GM guide is below ~69%, the trough call breaks,” and noted that price increases would have their “full effect over 2–3 quarters.”

description: All-flash array revenue grew 47%, a sharp acceleration from the 18% growth reported in Q4, and product revenue rose 51%, lifting its share of total revenue to 49% from 42%. The preview flagged the AFA run rate but did not anticipate this degree of acceleration.
fact_evidence: “All-flash array revenue grew 47% year-over-year to $1.31 billion, and product revenue jumped 51% to $987 million, rising to 49% of total revenue versus 42% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q4 AFA revenue of “$1,216M (+18% y/y)” and FY26 AFA growth of “+11%.”

description: Public cloud revenue grew 28% year over year, or 19% excluding the extra week, accelerating from the preview’s cited Q4 growth of 11% (18% excluding Spot). The preview highlighted public cloud as a metric to watch but did not set a Q1 growth estimate.
fact_evidence: “Public cloud revenue grew 28% year-over-year to $206 million (19% excluding the extra week).”
expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q4 public cloud revenue of “$182M (+11%; +18% ex-Spot)” and identified public cloud as a key metric to watch.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: NetApp reported about 350 AI and data-lake modernization wins, down from roughly 500 in the prior quarter and below the preview’s 500–600 base-case expectation. Increasing deal sizes temper the weaker count, but management still declined to quantify AI’s revenue contribution.
fact_evidence: “The company won approximately 350 AI and data lake modernization deals with increasing deal sizes, down from about 500 in the prior quarter, though management declined to quantify AI's revenue contribution.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “AI wins ~500–600” and identified conversion into production deployment as a key debate.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory nearly doubled sequentially and inventory turns fell to 6. The preview discussed sharply rising component costs and demand, but did not anticipate this degree of inventory build or the resulting drop in turns.
fact_evidence: “Inventory nearly doubled sequentially as the company secured supply against rising component costs and strong demand, with inventory turns falling to 6.”

description: Ciena’s Q3 adjusted operating margin reached 22.5%, 250 basis points above its 19–20% guidance and above the preview’s 21% whisper estimate. That was a much stronger margin result than investors were led to expect.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin more than doubled year-on-year to a record 22.5%, exceeding guidance by 250 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin | 19–20% | ~19.6%”; the preview also says Morgan Stanley modeled “21% operating margin.”

description: Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.11 substantially exceeded both the $1.73 consensus and the preview’s roughly $1.95 whisper estimate. The preview described its $1.72–1.76 guidance-based build as having “no beat embedded.”
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS hitting a record $2.11.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS ... consensus $1.73”; “Treat ... ~$1.95 EPS as the real whisper.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Backlog rose by $800 million to $8.5 billion, beating the preview’s greater-than-$8.3 billion bogey and its requirement for sequential growth above Q2’s $600 million. The call also added that backlog is on track to exceed $10 billion by fiscal-year-end.
fact_evidence: “Backlog increased $800 million in Q3 to $8.5 billion, and Ciena expects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion in backlog.”
expectation_evidence: “Morgan Stanley's stated bogey is sequential growth greater than Q2's $600M, i.e., backlog >$8.3B.”

description: Ciena’s preliminary FY27 outlook was far more specific and strong than the preview expected: it projected at least 30% revenue growth to $8.3–$8.4 billion and a record 25–27% operating margin, despite calling the revenue outlook a supply-constrained floor.
fact_evidence: “Preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook projecting revenue growth of at least 30% to $8.3–$8.4 billion (a supply-constrained floor) ... and record operating margin of 25–27%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 framing (no formal guide expected until December)”; “Any quantified FY27 growth framing is the single biggest potential narrative unlock.”

description: Q4 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion was above the preview’s implied Q4 estimate of about $1.677 billion, and the FY26 revenue midpoint rose to $6.42 billion versus the preview’s $6.3 billion guidance. Full-year adjusted operating margin was also lifted to 20–21%, above the preview’s Q3 margin guidance range of 19–20%.
fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 revenue is guided to $1.75 billion (+/- $50 million), raising the full-year midpoint to $6.42 billion and lifting full-year adjusted operating margin to 20–21%.”
expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 is ~$1,677M”; “FY26 guidance is $6.3B ± $100M”; Q3 adjusted operating margin guidance was “19–20%.”

description: Gross margin was 46.4%, above the preview’s roughly 45.0% consensus and 45.5% whisper, although a one-time tariff refund contributed 70 basis points. The underlying result therefore beat expectations by less than the headline gap suggests.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 46.4% (including a one-time 70 bps tariff-refund benefit).”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin ... Consensus ~45.0%”; Morgan Stanley modeled “45.5% GM.”

description: Direct cloud provider revenue grew more than 80% year-on-year, exceeding the preview’s expected growth of about 70%.
fact_evidence: “Direct cloud provider revenue grew over 80% year-on-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview describes direct cloud revenue as “(+70% Y/Y).”

description: Data-center-related growth exceeded the preview’s stated target: “in and around the data center” revenue quadrupled year-to-date versus a committed 3x target. Interconnects also more than doubled, for which the preview gave no specific bogey.
fact_evidence: “Interconnects more than doubled, and ‘in and around the data center’ revenue quadrupled year-to-date, well ahead of the committed 3x growth target.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says management had guided “pluggables ... to more than double vs. 2025” and flags data-center growth drivers, but does not give an expectation of quadrupling; the call says the 3x target was exceeded.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said negotiated price increases ranging from high single digits to high-teens or low-20s percentages will selectively apply to existing backlog. The preview did not anticipate repricing already-booked orders, a potential lift to future revenue economics.
fact_evidence: “Ciena secured negotiated price increases ranging from high single digits to high-teens/low-20s percent that will selectively apply to existing backlog.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Ciena secured long-term supply agreements for key optical components through 2029, providing a specific supply-security development beyond the preview’s open question about capacity investments and constrained components.
fact_evidence: “New long-term supply agreements securing key optical components through 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asks whether “capacity investments are landing in FY27” and whether management will discuss pump-laser and DSP-modem constraints; it gives no expectation of agreements extending through 2029.

description: RLS Hyper-Rail was described as on track for customer standardization by the end of 2026 and expected to generate several hundred million dollars in 2027 at above-company-average margins. That is more specific about the timing, scale, and economics than the preview’s expectation of deployments beginning in FY27 and hundreds of millions over multiple years.
fact_evidence: “RLS Hyper-Rail is on track for customer standardization by end of 2026 and is expected to ramp to several hundred million dollars of revenue in 2027 at margins accretive to the corporate average.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says Hyper-Rail had “hundreds of millions over multiple years” and that “deployments begin FY27.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management said the supply-demand imbalance is likely to persist into at least 2028, extending the constraint horizon beyond the preview’s focus on constraints into FY27. That tempers the otherwise strong outlook by indicating supply is not expected to normalize soon.
fact_evidence: “Management believes supply-demand imbalance persists into at least 2028.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flags “continued constraint into FY27” as a possibility and asks whether capacity investments are landing in FY27; it does not extend the outlook to 2028.

description: Ciena said it expects to raise combined optical systems and plug market share by about four points to roughly 30% in Q4. The preview discussed market-share-related growth drivers but did not set an expectation for this gain.
fact_evidence: “Expects to raise combined optical systems and plug market share by about 4 points to roughly 30% in Q4.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call disclosed that hyperscalers represent about half of Ciena’s business, highlighting greater exposure to that customer group than the preview’s cited customer-concentration figure alone conveyed. This underscores concentration risk, even as cloud demand is strong.
fact_evidence: “Hyperscalers now represent about 50% of Ciena's business, and two customers each contributed more than 10% of revenue in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview says “Two customers at 34% of revenue” in Q2 and identifies customer concentration and diversification as a key issue; it does not state that hyperscalers represent about half of the business.

description: Gross margin was expected to be about 47.5%, but reached 52%, a much larger improvement than the preview anticipated. The call attributed most of the increase to the IEPA tariff refund.
fact_evidence: Gross margin expanded approximately 320 basis points to 52%, primarily driven by the IEPA tariff refund.
expectation_evidence: My Base Est.: Gross margin ~47.5% (−150bp).

description: Adjusted EBITDA was expected to be about $12.5 million, but came in at $11 million, the bottom of the $11–14 million guide. The call said tariff-refund benefits were offset by the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse-management-system disruptions.
fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA fell $4 million year-over-year to $11 million, as tariff refund benefits were offset by the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse management system disruptions.
expectation_evidence: My Base Est.: Adj. EBITDA $12.5M; Q2 guide $11.0–14.0M.

description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA range was lowered to $62–70 million, below the prior $68–78 million guide; the preview specifically identified a cut below $68 million as a bearish trigger.
fact_evidence: Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $62–$70 million.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 guide: Adj. EBITDA $68–78M. The preview also said an outright EBITDA cut below $68M was the bear trigger.

description: The new full-year adjusted EPS range of $0.44–0.72 is higher than the prior $0.32–0.65 range, improving both the low and high ends even as the EBITDA guide was cut.
fact_evidence: Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $0.44–$0.72.
expectation_evidence: FY2026 guide: Adj. EPS $0.32–0.65.

description: The reported $9 million U.S. e-commerce growth obscured weaker underlying performance: the preview expected underlying low-single-digit growth, while management said year-to-date growth was essentially flat and that Q2 growth was inflated by catching up on Q1 backlog.
fact_evidence: U.S. e-commerce sales grew 9% year-over-year, but management disclosed this was inflated by Q1 backlog catch-up, with underlying year-to-date U.S. e-commerce growth essentially flat.
expectation_evidence: Management said the DC systems rollout delayed Q1 shipments and that underlying demand supported low-single-digit growth; those delayed orders should be a Q2 revenue tailwind.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory remained substantially above the preview's desired trajectory: it was up 13% year-over-year rather than closing toward flat. The explanation that last year's position was intentionally lean and tariff headwinds continued gives context, but does not remove the gap from the preview's expectation.
fact_evidence: Inventory rose 13% year-over-year to $342 million, attributed largely to an intentionally lean prior-year position amid tariff uncertainty and continued tariff headwinds.
expectation_evidence: Inventory ... needs to close toward flat. Still +10%+ means H2 margin is pre-committed to markdowns.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected the Q1 shipment delays to create a Q2 recapture tailwind, but school-uniform shipments were delayed and backlog rose during Q2. Management did say throughput is now normal or higher and expects no Q3/Q4 guidance impact beyond Outfitters catch-up, which partially limits the concern.
fact_evidence: Warehouse management system issues delayed school uniform shipments and raised backlog, but management stated operations are now running at normal or higher throughput with no expected impact on Q3/Q4 guidance beyond Outfitters catch-up.
expectation_evidence: Those delayed orders should be a Q2 revenue tailwind. The preview also identified Q1 shipment recapture as a key metric to watch.

description: Adjusted net income and EPS were below the preview's point estimates: $2.7 million and $0.09 per share versus estimates of $3.5 million and $0.11. Both results were still within the preview's stated ranges.
fact_evidence: The company reported Q2 adjusted net income of $2.7 million, or $0.09 per share.
expectation_evidence: My Base Est.: Adj. net income $3.5M; Adj. diluted EPS $0.11. Preview ranges: $2.0–5.0M and $0.06–0.16.

description: Third-party marketplace revenue fell roughly 20%, an outcome the preview did not flag, although management said it was intentional: like-for-like gross margin improved by more than 500 basis points as the company prioritized profitability.
fact_evidence: Third-party marketplace revenue declined roughly 20% as the company prioritized profitability, yet like-for-like gross margin improved over 500 basis points year-over-year.

description: The company repurchased about 900,000 shares for roughly $11 million in the quarter, a capital-allocation action not discussed in the preview; $89 million remained under the authorization.
fact_evidence: The company repurchased approximately 900,000 shares for about $11 million in Q2, leaving $89 million remaining on its $100 million buyback authorization through March 2029.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: ABL borrowings were $60 million, above the preview's roughly $30 million post-repayment reference point. The company had repaid the term loan with WHP proceeds and reduced interest expense, but the higher ABL balance is a less favorable borrowing position than the preview suggested.
fact_evidence: ABL borrowings increased to $60 million from $35 million a year ago, though the $300 million WHP Global proceeds were used to fully repay the term loan, reducing interest expense.
expectation_evidence: Net debt near zero post-repayment (~$30M ABL vs. $23.1M cash at Q1).

description: Q4 sales reached $436.9 million, 2.1% above the $427.9 million consensus, while organic growth was 8.4%—above the preview’s 7–8% base-case range. That put revenue above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $435 million.
fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 total sales grew 10% (8.4% organic, 1.1% acquisitions, 0.5% FX).”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue | $427.9M”; base case “$425–435M” and “Organic ~7–8%”; bull case “>$435M.”

description: Americas and Asia organic growth reached 11.6%, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of 10%, and segment profit rose 43.9% with margins expanding 530 basis points. This was stronger than the preview’s recent-growth reference of 8.2%.
fact_evidence: “The Americas and Asia region posted 11.6% organic growth with segment profit up 43.9% to $74.3 million, expanding margins 530 bps to 25.1% (23.7% excluding the tariff benefit), led by wire ID growth of nearly 20%.”
expectation_evidence: “Organic growth in Americas & Asia. Ran +8.2% in Q3”; bull case: “Americas organic >10%.”

description: Gross margin was 52.9%, above the preview’s roughly 51.8% run-rate expectation and above its bull-case threshold of 52%. The improvement was partly helped by a roughly $4 million tariff refund, though margin still rose 110 basis points after adjusting for one-time items.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 52.9% from 50.4%, though this included a ~$4 million tariff refund; adjusting for one-time items, gross margin rose 110 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin. 51.8% in Q3”; base case “GM ~52%”; bull case “GM >52%.”

description: FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance has a $6.50 midpoint, slightly below the $6.55 consensus, although it meets the preview’s stated $6.50 buy-side hurdle. The $6.25–$6.75 range also extends below the preview’s expected $6.40–$6.60 base-case range; the expected roughly $0.80 IPS accretion was included.
fact_evidence: “FY2027 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of $6.25 to $6.75 (18.1%–27.6% growth), including ~$0.80 of IPS accretion weighted toward the second half.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue / adj. EPS | $2.84B / $6.55”; “Buy-side needed ≥$6.50 to validate the ~$0.80 stated accretion”; base case FY27 guide “$6.40–6.60 (in line).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Printer unit sales surged 25% in Q4, supporting nearly 10% organic growth in high-margin specialty adhesive consumables. The preview discussed engineered-product mix but did not anticipate this specific volume surge or consumables growth.
fact_evidence: “Printer unit sales surged 25% in Q4 and 10% for the full year, driving high-margin specialty adhesive consumable sales that together represent over 40% of Brady's organic sales and grew nearly 10% organically.”

description: Management identified rising input costs—especially memory-chip pricing that shifts quarter to quarter—as a margin headwind, prompting price increases, product redesigns, and longer-term supplier contracts. The preview focused on product mix and integration risks, not this specific cost pressure.
fact_evidence: “Rising input costs, especially memory chips whose pricing is shifting quarter to quarter, pose a margin headwind, prompting IPS to implement price increases, redesign products for alternative memory, and secure long-term supplier contracts.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The acquisition was described as giving Brady the #2 position in AIDC across an approximately $14 billion addressable market. The preview anticipated the acquisition’s roughly 70% scale relative to the existing business, but did not flag this market position or addressable-market framing.
fact_evidence: “The PSS/IPS acquisition from Honeywell closed a month ago, increasing Brady's annualized top-line revenue by over 70% and giving it the #2 market position in the AIDC sector across a ~$14 billion addressable market.”
expectation_evidence: “The $1.4B Honeywell PSS acquisition … is 70% the size of the existing revenue base.”

description: Management set a target to reduce net leverage below 2x within two years while continuing dividends and buybacks. The preview flagged deleveraging as a key issue but did not provide or anticipate this specific timeline and leverage target.
fact_evidence: “Management targeting net leverage below 2x within two years while maintaining dividends (41st consecutive annual increase) and buybacks ($44 million authorization remaining).”
expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet / deleveraging path. Brady ran net cash into the deal. Q4 cash generation sets the starting point for absorbing $1.4B.”

description: The full-year adjusted EPS outlook of $1.65–$1.80 came in below the preview’s $1.90 consensus and mostly below its roughly $1.80 effective-bar estimate. Management also expects a sharp Q1 decline, with EPS turning positive only in Q4, signaling a particularly back-end-loaded recovery.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was set at $1.65 to $1.80, with a sharp Q1 decline expected and EPS turning positive only by Q4.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS: $1.90 | Street; TD Cowen $1.87, BofA $1.77”; the preview also says the effective bar is “closer to $1.80.”

description: The full-year organic sales outlook of approximately down 3% is weaker than the preview’s expectation of FY26 organic sales down 2% to 1% and its implied Q4 organic sales roughly flat to slightly positive. The preview had identified that expected inflection as the most checkable claim in the print.
fact_evidence: “Campbell's guided to fiscal 2026 organic net sales down approximately 3% at the midpoint.”
expectation_evidence: “FY guide of −2% to −1% with management pointing to the lower end implies Q4 organic roughly flat to slightly positive”; the preview also describes the FY26 guide as “−2% to −1%.”

description: Campbell’s reduced its dividend, contrary to the preview’s base expectation that it would be held flat and its emphasis on an unambiguous affirmation. The preview identified dividend language as a central issue, but anticipated no cut signal.
fact_evidence: “Management confirmed the dividend was reduced as a necessary decision.”
expectation_evidence: “Dividend held flat, no cut signal”; the preview also calls for a “Dividend maintained with unambiguous language.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company disclosed price increases averaging 4%–5% across about 60% of its portfolio, with assumed elasticity of 1.5x and expected volume pressure. The preview anticipated planned pricing but described pricing as a last resort and framed the base case as “surgical,” so the breadth and expected volume trade-off are more pronounced than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The company took price increases averaging 4% to 5% on about 60% of its portfolio, assuming elasticity of 1.5x, which will pressure volumes but benefit the bottom line starting in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “On the Q3 call pricing was a ‘last resort’ behind RGM and trade optimization”; the base-case commentary expected “surgical pricing.”

description: Snacks are now expected to decline high single digits in Q1, with margin recovery delayed until the second half. That is weaker near-term performance than the preview’s base case of Snacks still down about 4%–5% with margin holding around 10%–11% and its question about whether the Q4-exit margin would hold and build.
fact_evidence: “Snacks are expected to decline high single digits in Q1, hurt by lapping prior holiday shipments ahead of consumption and new trade investment, with margin recovery not occurring until the second half.”
expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “Snacks still −4/−5% but margin holds ~10–11%”; the preview asks, “Does the ~10% Q4-exit margin hold and build?”

description: Campbell’s announced a new $500 million savings program for fiscal 2027–2030, including $350 million of incremental savings, rather than merely continuing the existing program the preview expected to be reaffirmed. The incremental savings target is a favorable addition to the expected cost offsets.
fact_evidence: “Campbell's announced a new $500 million cost savings program running from fiscal 2027 to 2030, including $150 million rolled over from the prior peak program and $350 million of incremental savings from headcount cuts, procurement, and supply chain optimization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case commentary expected “reiteration of the $375M savings program on track.”

description: Logistics inflation is expected to run around double digits before easing, an additional near-term cost pressure beyond the preview’s stated expectation of 5%–6% total inflation. The preview anticipated inflation to be front-loaded but did not flag this specific logistics magnitude.
fact_evidence: “Management projects cost inflation of plus 5% to 6% throughout the year, with logistics inflation running around double digits before easing later in the year.”
expectation_evidence: “Management framed 5–6% total inflation … with pressure front-loaded into 1H.”

description: Management expects full-year gross margin to decline 50–100 basis points, with a significant Q1 drop and improvement only later in the year. The preview focused on whether productivity and pricing could offset inflation and expected a credible bridge, but did not provide a specific gross-margin decline forecast.
fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin is expected to be down 50 to 100 basis points, declining significantly in Q1 before improving sequentially and turning positive in the second half.”
expectation_evidence: “How much is covered by productivity + the pulled-forward $100M SG&A program versus list pricing?”; the base case anticipated “inflation guide confirms 5–6% with credible offsets.”

description: Interest expense is projected to be roughly $25 million higher year over year, adding a specific financing headwind that the preview did not quantify. The preview discussed leverage and a possible hybrid instrument, but not this increase in interest expense.
fact_evidence: “Interest expense is projected to be roughly $25 million higher year-over-year, driven by the La Regina acquisition debt and refinancing of a $500 million bond maturing in March, with a hybrid issuance under consideration.”

description: VS&Co reported adjusted EPS of $0.95, well above the preview’s $0.75–0.77 consensus range and even the preview’s $0.90+ bull-case threshold.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS nearly tripled to $0.95 from $0.33, beating guidance of $0.65-0.75.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS ~ $0.75–0.77”; the bull case specified “$0.90+.”

description: Adjusted operating income reached $124 million, beating both the preview’s roughly $100 million implied consensus and the top of company guidance by $24 million.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income surged 125% to $124 million, exceeding the high end of guidance ($90-100M) by $24 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income ~$100M (implied)”; company guidance was “$90–100M.”

description: Adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points, exceeding the prior quarter’s 240-basis-point expansion and the preview’s bull-case threshold of 200 basis points, with most of the increase coming from stronger merchandise margin and less promotion.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points to 38.8%, with roughly two-thirds driven by higher merchandise margin from increased regular-price selling and reduced promotions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “the 240bp Q1 expansion repeat[s]” and described “GM +200bp+” as part of the bull case.

description: The company raised its full-year sales, adjusted operating income, and adjusted EPS ranges rather than merely maintaining or nudging up its previous guidance. The increase was real but remained below the preview’s bull-case levels of about $7.20 billion in sales and $4.75+ EPS.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance was raised to net sales of $7.10-7.18 billion … adjusted operating income of $560-590 million, and adjusted EPS of $4.45-4.70.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “FY nudged to high end of existing range, not raised”; it also said a raise was a catalyst and described the bull case as “~$7.20B / EPS $4.75+.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: VS&Co received more than $140 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, which were excluded from non-GAAP results but substantially strengthened cash and left the company with no ABL borrowings. The preview highlighted tariff exposure but did not anticipate these refunds.
fact_evidence: “The company received IEEPA tariff refunds of over $140 million (over 95% of IEEPA tariffs paid), which were excluded from non-GAAP results, boosting the cash balance to $522 million … with no ABL borrowings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the “tariff step-up” and tariff assumptions, but did not mention refunds.

description: Q3 guidance includes $10–20 million of operating income, meaning the company expects to be profitable in a historically loss-making quarter despite the preview’s concern that Q3 would be the first fully tariff-loaded quarter. The preview did not provide an operating-income estimate for Q3.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $1.57-1.60 billion (7-9% growth), with operating income of $10-20 million versus roughly break-even last year, signaling the company's return to profitability in a historically loss-making quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 “the first fully-loaded quarter” for tariffs and said its guidance was “the single highest-leverage item on the call,” but gave no Q3 operating-income forecast.

description: Sales of $1.611 billion were near the top of company guidance but came in slightly below the preview’s $1.617–1.62 billion consensus range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales increased 10% year-over-year to $1.611 billion, near the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales ~ $1.617–1.62B”; the preview noted consensus was “at or above the top of management's own guidance range.”

description: Management plans to raise marketing spend from just over 7% of sales toward the high single digits over the next couple of years, an incremental investment plan the preview did not specifically anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Management plans to raise marketing spend from just over 7% of sales toward high single digits over the next couple years, funding investments like the Angels Among Us docu-series and Fashion Show.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: DLTH reported adjusted EPS of $0.50 versus the preview’s $0.01 consensus, but $0.44 per share came from a $16.3 million tariff refund; excluding that contribution, EPS was about $0.06, a much narrower beat. The preview noted roughly $12 million of potential refunds and no benefit in guidance, so receiving and recognizing $16.3 million in Q2 was a larger-than-anticipated upside item.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50, which included $16.3 million in tariff refunds contributing $0.44 per share.”
expectation_evidence: “Management confirmed it paid ~$12M in IEEPA tariffs and has applied for refunds with zero benefit in guidance”; “~$12M is ~9% of market cap in cash, entirely off-model. Any timing/recognition commentary is asymmetric upside.” Consensus adjusted EPS was “$0.01.”

description: DLTH raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance by $10 million at both ends, to $38–42 million, far beyond the preview’s expected $28–32 million hold and even above its bull-case range of $30–34 million.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $38-42 million from the prior $28-32 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the expected guide was “$28–32M” and that a hold was the base case; its bull case assumed “FY EBITDA raised to $30–34M.”

description: Gross margin expanded much more than the preview expected: roughly 59.6% excluding tariff refunds, versus a preview estimate around 57% and expected year-over-year expansion of about 200–300 basis points. The preview’s upper range for the absolute margin was 57.5%, still well below the reported level.
fact_evidence: “Excluding tariff refunds, underlying gross margin still expanded 490-520 basis points to roughly 59.6%, driven by nearly 6% higher average unit retails and direct factory sourcing savings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Gross margin ~57%” and expected YoY expansion to “roughly halve to +200–300bps”; its base case was “~57.0–57.5%.”

description: Q2 sales were modestly ahead of consensus and near the top of the preview’s guidance-implied range: $121.4 million versus $119.9 million consensus and an implied Q2 range topping out at $121.7 million. The 7.8% decline was also less severe than the preview’s 9.0% consensus decline.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales declined 7.8% to $121.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus net sales of “$119.9M” and an implied Q2 range of “$112.4M–$121.7M,” with consensus implying “-9.0%” year over year.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: DLTH ended the quarter with no ABL debt and generated $13 million of free cash flow, a $41 million year-over-year improvement, versus the preview’s expectation of $6 million drawn on the ABL and $6.1 million of cash. That is a stronger liquidity and debt position than the preview described.
fact_evidence: “Ended the quarter with zero debt on its ABL facility (versus $32.5 million a year ago) and generated $13 million in free cash flow, a $41 million year-over-year improvement.”
expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet: $6.1M cash, $6M drawn on a $100M ABL.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory was lower in dollars than the preview expected, but the year-over-year reduction and current-product mix were weaker than its estimates: actual inventory was down 15.5% with 85.4% current products, versus the preview’s expected 24.8% decline and 90.2% current mix. The sharp reduction in clearance inventory is a favorable counterpoint.
fact_evidence: “Total inventory fell 15.5% (down $22.9 million) to $125.2 million”; “Clearance inventory was cut 43.1% in dollars and 46.6% in units, improving the inventory mix to 85.4% current products.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Inventory -24.8% to $132.4M with 90.2% current / 9.8% clearance.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The channel and customer picture was less uniformly encouraging than the preview’s expectation of positive retail comps and improving DTC: stores were flat for the first half while DTC declined 7.6%, and management said the customer base had contracted as promotions were reset. Retention and NPS improved, with NPS up 11%, providing a positive counterpoint.
fact_evidence: “Retail stores outperformed direct, delivering flat first-half sales versus a 7.6% DTC decline, though the customer base has contracted as promotions were reset even as retention and NPS (up 11%) improved.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said retail “comped +3.3%” in Q1, described DTC’s Q1 decline as “-8.7%,” and said “Any sequential improvement in DTC decline is the leading indicator for the H2 guide.”

description: The call disclosed steep declines in women’s product sales and the AKHG brand, which the preview did not quantify or flag as a segment-level risk. Management attributed them to SKU rationalization and exits from lower-margin categories, including swimwear, so the sales weakness came alongside deliberate assortment cleanup.
fact_evidence: “Women's product sales fell 15% and AKHG brand sales dropped 26% due to SKU rationalization and exiting low-margin categories like swimwear.”

description: Q3 revenue guidance came in well above the preview’s roughly $114M bar: the $119.5M midpoint is also above the preview’s base-case range of $112M–$116M. Management attributed the expected sequential growth to physical-AI demand from IoT.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance is $115M-$124M ($119.5M midpoint), representing ~10.5% sequential growth led by physical AI demand from IoT.”
expectation_evidence: “Bar is ~$114M”; base scenario Q3 guide midpoint “$112–116M.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Ambarella raised its five-year SAM growth forecast from about 18% to about 20% annually, and said IoT will make up about 70% of the terminal-year market, primarily due to the new edge-infrastructure business. The preview did not flag this larger market outlook or mix shift.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its 5-year serviceable market (SAM) forecast to grow from $8.5 billion in FY2027 to $22.9 billion in FY2032, a ~20% CAGR, up from the prior ~18% CAGR estimate”; “IoT markets now representing about 70% of the terminal year, driven primarily by the new edge infrastructure business.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The call disclosed two seven-year indirect-channel partnerships, each expected to generate about $0.5B in revenue. That adds substantial prospective business not flagged in the preview, though management said meaningful revenue is still 2–3 years away.
fact_evidence: “Ambarella signed two 7-year indirect channel partnerships (Capgemini and Macnica), each expected to generate approximately $0.5 billion in revenue, though meaningful revenue is 2-3 years away.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Ambarella introduced a standalone AI-accelerator line and previewed the X7 SoC, an unanticipated product disclosure in the preview. The product is still in simulation, so the announcement is an early-stage opportunity rather than near-term revenue evidence.
fact_evidence: “The company introduced a new standalone AI accelerator product line, previewing the X7 SoC (currently in simulation), which requires only 4MB of memory and a 4-5 watt power envelope to run large language models as an AI coprocessor.”

description: Gross margin was below the preview’s roughly 59.8% expectation, although it remained within the company’s 59.0%–60.5% guidance range. Management said it plans to pass rising supply-chain costs to customers to defend its long-term margin target.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 59.3%, below the guidance midpoint, and management plans to pass rising supply chain costs to customers to maintain its long-term 59%-62% gross margin target.”
expectation_evidence: Preview consensus for non-GAAP gross margin was “~59.8%”; company guidance was 59.0%–60.5%.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Memory-cost and scarcity risks had been flagged as a potential second-half demand problem, but management reported that they had already caused a small revenue impact in Q2 and Q3 and were creating uncertainty about Q4 order volumes.
fact_evidence: “Rising memory prices and scarcity are creating Q4 uncertainty, as customers may reduce order volumes; management noted a small revenue impact was already seen in Q2 and Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had warned of “much higher DRAM and NAND pricing plus potential shortage in H2” and described customer demand reduction as a risk.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory days rose from 145 to 157 rather than stabilizing or declining, moving close to the preview’s 160-day warning threshold. This occurred even though Q2 revenue was not at the low end of expectations.
fact_evidence: “Inventory days rose from 145 to 157 days.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said 145 days “needs to stabilize” and that days coming down or holding would support the supply-preparation explanation; it warned about 160+ days if revenue landed low.

description: The call disclosed the cancellation of an automotive-autonomy customer’s development project, an unanticipated customer/project setback. The cancellation reduced GAAP R&D expense by $9M, but management said it did not affect the non-GAAP outlook.
fact_evidence: “A $9 million reduction in GAAP R&D expense was recognized from the cancellation of an automotive autonomy customer's development project, with no impact on non-GAAP outlook.”

description: The board authorized a new $50M share-repurchase program, which was not anticipated in the preview. No shares were repurchased during Q2.
fact_evidence: “The board authorized a new $50 million share repurchase program valid through June 30, 2027, though no shares were repurchased during Q2.”

description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.18, one cent above the preview’s $0.17 consensus estimate.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.18.”
expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS consensus: “$0.17.”

description: The preview expected Learning revenue of $99–104 million, down 10%–14%; Wiley reported $93 million, down 20%, with both Academic and Professional down 20%. Learning's adjusted EBITDA margin also fell to 15.1% from 27.4%, a sharp deterioration beyond the revenue weakness the preview highlighted.
fact_evidence: “Learning revenue fell 20% to $93 million, with both academic and professional down 20%, and segment adjusted EBITDA margin collapsed to 15.1% from 27.4% on revenue declines and mix.”
expectation_evidence: “Learning ~$99–104M (−10% to −14%) — Academic ~$54M, Professional ~$45M”; the preview also flagged another double-digit Professional decline as a bear-case concern.

description: The preview expected a roughly $25 million year-over-year revenue headwind from prior-year AI licensing projects. Management reported a $29 million headwind, $4 million greater than that estimate, though it said the comparison did not change full-year expectations.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue faced a known $29 million headwind from AI licensing revenue that landed in the prior-year quarter, which management said does not change full-year expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “~$25M unfavorable year-over-year revenue comparison in Q1 from prior-year AI licensing projects.”

description: Emerald contributed $13 million of revenue, slightly below the preview's approximately $14 million expectation for its two-month contribution. Its $5 million of adjusted EBITDA implies a margin of about 38%, essentially matching the preview's expected 37%–38% operating margin.
fact_evidence: “Emerald contributed $13 million of revenue and $5 million of adjusted EBITDA in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: “~$14M from two months of Emerald”; the preview asked whether Emerald would land at “~$14M for two months at the promised 37–38% operating margin.”

description: Wiley reported a GAAP loss of $0.23 per share, versus earnings of $0.22 a year earlier, due to restructuring and Emerald acquisition and integration costs. The preview forecast positive adjusted EPS, but did not give a GAAP EPS estimate, so the GAAP loss was not directly covered by its estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q1 GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.23 versus earnings of $0.22 a year ago, driven by restructuring charges and Emerald acquisition and integration costs.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS ~$0.46” consensus; the preview's own adjusted EPS estimate was “~$0.28–0.38.”

description: Research revenue and Publishing growth were broadly in line with the preview, but Research adjusted EBITDA grew 9% and its margin expanded 130 basis points to 29.6%. The preview did not anticipate that degree of margin improvement.
fact_evidence: “Research adjusted EBITDA grew 9% with margin expanding 130 basis points to 29.6%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected Research revenue of “~$294–298M (+4–6%)” and Publishing organic growth, but gave no Research adjusted EBITDA or margin-growth estimate.

description: Matrix provided no FY2027 revenue guidance, despite the preview treating an initial guide as likely and describing $950 million–$1.0 billion as the in-line range. Management said it would wait until a permanent CFO is onboarded.
fact_evidence: The company “will not provide guidance until a permanent CFO is onboarded”; A.J. Smith is serving as Interim CFO.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the release would “most likely” include the initial FY2027 revenue guide, and that “$950M–$1.0B is in line.”

description: Q4 gross margin was 8.0%, well short of the preview’s 9.5%+ watch level and below its 8.5% concern threshold. The margin did improve sharply year over year, but not to the level the preview looked for as evidence of overhead recovery.
fact_evidence: Q4 gross margin was “8.0%” versus 3.8% a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for 9.5%+ consolidated gross margin” and flagged “Below 8.5%” as putting the operating-leverage story in question.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Awards of $169 million and 0.7x book-to-bill fell short of the preview’s roughly $200 million base case and the approximately $220 million needed to hold backlog near $1 billion. Ending backlog was $953 million, below the preview’s roughly $981 million base-case estimate, though just above its $950 million warning level.
fact_evidence: “Q4 project awards totaled $169 million for a weak 0.7x book-to-bill,” and backlog ended at “$953 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Matrix needed “~$220M+ of awards (0.9x)” to hold backlog near $1.0 billion; its base case was “~$200M” of awards and “~$981M” exit backlog.

description: Process and Industrial Facilities remained weak rather than showing the Q4 inflection the preview was watching for: revenue was $33.6 million, down from $47.3 million a year earlier, and its margin was only 2.9%. The call facts do not establish whether the anticipated mining project started, but the segment results themselves did not show a recovery.
fact_evidence: Process and Industrial Facilities revenue “dropped to $33.6 million from $47.3 million,” while its Q4 margin was “2.9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the newly awarded Western US mining project “the stated inflection” and said confirmation it started on schedule was “the cleanest test” of the rebuild.

description: Q4 revenue was slightly below the $247 million consensus estimate, although it remained inside the guidance-implied range and the preview’s expected $241 million–$251 million band. This was a small consensus miss, not a miss of the company’s revenue guidance.
fact_evidence: Q4 revenue was “$244.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Revenue $247.0M” consensus and said a revenue print in the “$241–251M band” would meet guidance.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company incurred $3.4 million of restructuring costs in Q4, an unanticipated charge that weighed on the quarter; management said future restructuring should be insignificant.
fact_evidence: “$3.4 million of restructuring costs hit Q4,” with future restructuring “expected to be insignificant.”

description: The company said it was actively evaluating a stock buyback, introducing a potential shareholder return that the preview did not identify as a possibility. It remains under evaluation, not a committed repurchase.
fact_evidence: Matrix had “$283.9 million in total liquidity” and was “actively evaluating a stock buyback.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Matrix was selected for FEED work on America First Refining’s Brownsville storage tank farm, a specific project opportunity not identified in the preview. The larger award is still contingent on a final investment decision and may not enter backlog until late Q3 or early Q4 FY2027.
fact_evidence: Matrix was “selected for the FEED” on the tank farm, with a larger award “potentially converting to backlog in late Q3 or early Q4 fiscal 2027 pending FID.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Year-end total liquidity was lower than the Q3 figure, despite the preview flagging roughly $20 million of expected legacy-dispute cash inflows and Q4 seasonality as reasons to check for cash generation. The call facts do not say whether the dispute proceeds arrived or explain the movement.
fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$283.9 million in total liquidity” and “$223 million unrestricted cash,” versus Q3 total liquidity of $297.2 million in the preview.
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “~$20M of cash inflow from resolving two legacy disputes” and asked investors to check Q4 cash flow because “Q4 is seasonally the cash quarter.”

description: Q3 net sales were $1.23 billion, above the preview’s $1.19–$1.20 billion consensus and even the $1.20–$1.22 billion buy-side range. Growth of 8.4% also exceeded the preview’s implied consensus growth of 5.8%.
fact_evidence: “Q3 net sales grew 8.4% to $1.23 billion (6.2% organically).”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | ~$1.19–1.20B”; buy-side revenue expectations “likely sit at the high end, ~$1.20–1.22B.”

description: Toro raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance rather than merely narrowing or holding it: the midpoint rose by over $0.07 to $4.63. The preview identified a raise as needed but considered a narrow-and-hold the likeliest outcome.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60-$4.65 (midpoint $4.63) from the prior $4.50-$4.62, lifting the midpoint by over $0.07.”
expectation_evidence: “A narrow-and-hold at $4.50–$4.62 is the single most likely source of a negative reaction”; the base case was guidance “narrowed to ~$4.54–$4.62 (midpoint held/nudged).”

description: Full-year sales growth guidance was raised to 6.3%–6.6%, substantially above the prior 4%–6.5% range. The preview’s base case anticipated narrowing with the midpoint held or nudged, while its bull case anticipated a raise.
fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales growth guidance was raised and narrowed to 6.3%-6.6% from the prior 4%-6.5% range.”
expectation_evidence: The standing guidance was “+4.0% to +6.5%”; the base case expected it to be “narrowed to reflect year-to-date performance,” while the bull case anticipated “raising the low end of the sales range.”

description: Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.33 beat the $1.30 consensus, although it landed within the preview’s stated $1.32–$1.34 buy-side whisper range.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $1.33.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $1.30 (range $1.29–$1.32)”; the buy-side EPS whisper was “~$1.32–1.34.”

description: Residential sales growth of 8.6% surpassed the preview’s expected +2%–+6% range. However, its 5.9% margin remained below the preview’s high-single-digit margin expectation despite improving 400 basis points year over year.
fact_evidence: “The residential segment grew net sales 8.6% and improved adjusted operating margin by 400 basis points year-over-year to 5.9%.”
expectation_evidence: Residential sales were estimated at “+2–6%”; the preview called for “a high-single-digit margin” and cited a “swing from 1.9% to ~8% margin.”

description: Professional sales growth of 8.8% was well above the preview’s projected 5%–6% growth. But the segment’s 20.9% margin declined 40 basis points and fell short of the preview’s 21.3% year-ago benchmark and its clean-beat threshold of 21%.
fact_evidence: “The professional segment grew net sales 8.8% (6.1% organic) but adjusted operating margin declined 40 basis points to 20.9% due to product mix, higher manufacturing costs, and Tornado acquisition dilution.”
expectation_evidence: Professional sales were estimated at “+5–6%”; the preview highlighted the “21.3% Q3 FY2025 comp” and said “Anything ≥21% is a clean beat.”

description: The AMP program had already reached its $125 million run-rate savings target, ahead of the preview’s expectation that it was on track to reach that target by year end. The additional comment that unrealized in-year benefits should carry into fiscal 2027 points to continued margin expansion.
fact_evidence: “The AMP productivity program has already reached its $125 million run-rate savings target, with unrealized in-year benefits expected to carry into fiscal 2027 for continued margin expansion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “$95M of the $125M run-rate savings target delivered; on track to hit $125M by year end.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The refund outlook was lower than the preview’s roughly $20 million full-year expectation: guidance for anticipated IEEPA refunds was reduced from $12 million to $7 million. The company also removed $5 million reclassified outside Phase 2 from Q4 residential margin, complicating the expected tariff and margin bridge.
fact_evidence: “Anticipated IEEPA tariff refunds in guidance were reduced to $7 million from $12 million, with $5 million reclassified outside Phase 2 and removed from Q4 residential margin.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$20M expected refunds” and said management needed to “quantify how much of the Q3 hit was absorbed and confirm Q4 mitigation is landing.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Year-to-date free-cash-flow conversion reached 128%, above the preview’s 1H rate of 124.5% and its ≥120% conversion benchmark. The company used $358 million for share repurchases, an allocation not specifically anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow reached $425 million at a 128% conversion rate, funding $358 million of share repurchases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “1H FCF $265.5M at 124.5% conversion” and said to watch for reaffirmation of “≥120%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory and working capital improved materially, driven by lower finished-goods balances. The preview discussed field inventory being below target but did not anticipate these reported company inventory and working-capital reductions.
fact_evidence: “Inventory improved $153 million year-over-year and working capital improved $217 million, driven by lower finished goods balances.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The Q3 tax rate was 22.4%, above the preview’s approximately 21.7% full-year assumption, and was a larger EPS headwind than that assumption implied. The release attributed a $0.08 EPS offset to the higher tax rate.
fact_evidence: “Q3 EPS benefited from $0.12 in operational performance, $0.05 from buybacks, and $0.06 from tariff refunds, partially offset by an $0.08 higher tax rate (22.4%).”
expectation_evidence: Standing guidance included a “tax rate ~21.7% (+300bps, ~$0.04 EPS headwind).”

description: Lululemon cut FY2026 EPS guidance to $9.48–$9.73, far below the preview’s roughly $10.94 consensus and even below the low end of its bear-case range. Revenue guidance also fell to $10.35–$10.5 billion, versus the preview’s $11.0–$11.15 billion company guide.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was lowered to $10.35-$10.5 billion (down 5-7%), with full-year EPS cut to $9.48-$9.73 versus $13.26 in 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS” consensus “~$10.94”; the preview’s base case expected “EPS trimmed modestly to ~$10.40–10.75,” while its bear case was “~$9.50–10.00.”

description: China Mainland growth fell well short of the preview’s mid-to-high-teens expectation: revenue grew just 4% reported and declined 2% in constant currency, with comps down 8%. Management attributed the shortfall mainly to negative social-media sentiment and a weaker Tmall 618 event.
fact_evidence: “China Mainland revenue grew only 4% reported (down 2% constant currency) with comps down 8%, the primary source of the quarterly shortfall driven by negative social/media sentiment and a weaker Tmall 618 event.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed China Mainland at “mid-to-high teens” growth and described it as “the last growth engine.”

description: Q2 revenue was about $2.4 billion, below the preview’s $2.46 billion consensus, and declined 4% rather than the expected 2%–3%. Comparable sales were down 10%, contributing to the full-year guidance cut.
fact_evidence: “Q2 total net revenue declined 4% (5% in constant currency) to $2.4 billion with comparable sales down 10%, driving a full-year guidance cut.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 revenue consensus of “$2.46B” and expected growth of “–3% to –2%.”

description: The Q3 outlook points to a sharp further deterioration: revenue is forecast down 10%–11%, operating margin around 6.5%, and EPS $0.93–$0.98. The preview did not provide Q3 estimates, but its base case anticipated only a modest FY EPS trim, not this degree of near-term weakness.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $2.29-$2.32 billion (down 10-11%), operating margin of ~6.5% versus 17% a year ago, and EPS of $0.93-$0.98 versus $2.59 last year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “EPS trimmed modestly to ~$10.40–10.75”; it gave no specific Q3 revenue, operating-margin, or EPS estimate.

description: Management expects North America to deteriorate from Q2’s 12% comparable-sales decline to a mid-teens decline in Q3. The preview warned that a mid-teens US decline would break the thesis, but its base case expected US comps around down 11%.
fact_evidence: “North America revenue fell 8% with comparable sales down 12%, and management guides Q3 North America to worsen to a mid-teens decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “US comps ~–11%”; it said “Mid-teens = thesis break.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A $134.5 million pretax IEEPA tariff refund materially lifted Q2 results, adding 560 basis points to margin and $0.86 to EPS. This was an unexpected one-off tailwind; reported operating margin was still 18.8%, below 20.7% a year earlier.
fact_evidence: “Q2 operating margin was 18.8% versus 20.7% a year ago, but included a $134.5 million pretax IEEPA tariff refund that added 560 basis points and contributed $0.86 to EPS.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY tariff assumptions included “no recovery assumed on tariffs paid.”

description: Q3 SG&A is expected to deleverage by 800 basis points year over year, with about 450 basis points of deleverage for the full year. That is a substantial expense burden amid lower sales, even as management increases marketing and cuts discretionary costs.
fact_evidence: “Q3 SG&A is expected to deleverage 800 basis points year-over-year due to lower sales, increased marketing, and expense timing, with full-year SG&A deleverage of ~450 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described 2H marketing spend as “bolder,” but did not flag this degree of SG&A deleverage.

description: Demand weakened sharply in specific product categories: leggings sales fell about 20% as guests shifted toward away-from-body silhouettes, and accessories declined 13% amid bag softness. The preview noted that recent launches had fallen short, but did not anticipate these category declines or this shift in customer preference.
fact_evidence: “Leggings sales dropped approximately 20% in Q2 as guests shift toward away-from-body silhouettes, while accessories declined 13% amid softness in bags.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had admitted recent launches “ran ‘short of expectations.’”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Lululemon reduced planned net new store openings to about 35, below the preview’s stated low-end plan of 40–45, and also cut pop-up stores from 65 to about 40. This indicates a deeper pullback in physical expansion than the preview anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The company cut planned net new store openings to approximately 35 (from ~40), is reducing pop-up stores from 65 to ~40.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY net new stores were guided to “the low end of 40–45.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was reported at $23.3 million, well above the $12–16 million Q2 guidance, because an $11.1 million tariff refund benefit was recognized. Excluding the refund, EBITDA was $12.1 million, within guidance; the refund also lifted the headline full-year outlook to $76–86 million while the underlying $65–75 million outlook stayed unchanged.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $23.3 million (10% margin), but excluding an $11.1 million tariff refund benefit, it was $12.1 million (5.2% margin), within guidance.” The full-year outlook was raised to $76–$86 million “to reflect the tariff refund,” with the underlying outlook unchanged at $65–$75 million.
expectation_evidence: “Guidance excludes Phase 1 ($9–11M) and Phase 2 ($1.5–2.5M).” The preview also described “$9–11M refund collected” as part of its bull scenario.

description: Q2 net sales of $231.7 million came in below the preview’s practical $236 million bar and just below the company’s $232 million guidance floor. That is a modest shortfall, even against the preview’s below-consensus adjusted bar.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell to $231.7 million … with comparable sales declining 6.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Treat $236M (guide midpoint) as the real bar.” Company Q2 guidance was “$232–240M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comparable sales declined 6.3%, worse than the preview’s base-case expectation of a 3%–5% decline, although not as weak as its bear-case threshold. The later July improvement does not change that Q2 comparison.
fact_evidence: “Comparable sales declining 6.3%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case called for “Comps -3% to -5%”; its bear case was “Comps -7%+.”

description: Gross margin excluding the tariff refund was 33.9%, down 170 basis points year over year because of targeted promotions. That was below the preview’s roughly 35.5% base-case expectation, despite the reported gross margin rising to 38.7% with the refund benefit.
fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin rose to 38.7% from 35.6%, but excluding the tariff refund, gross margin declined 170 basis points to 33.9% due to targeted promotions.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “GM ~35.5%”; its bull case called for “GM ≥36%.”

description: Management said comparable sales had turned positive in July and expected comparable-sales growth in the back half, a stronger stated trend than the preview’s expectation of roughly flat back-half sales. All 11 marketing channels were improving sequentially.
fact_evidence: “Comparable sales inflected positively in July with all 11 marketing channels improving sequentially, and management expects a return to comparable sales growth in the back half.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said sales were expected to “inflect from -9% to roughly flat” in the back half, with implied H2 sales of “$458–478M (-2.8% to +1.5%).”

description: The store-optimization program was essentially complete at 177 total closures, with management expecting about $40 million of expense savings in fiscal 2026. The preview noted prior closures but did not flag completion or quantify these savings.
fact_evidence: “The store optimization program is essentially complete with 177 total closures … and is expected to deliver ~$40 million in expense savings in fiscal 2026.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Digital monetization and app engagement were stronger than anything the preview had identified: paid revenue grew double digits on lower spend, and the app reached nearly 40% of digital revenue with roughly seven times the conversion rate of desktop/mobile web.
fact_evidence: “Paid revenue grew double digits on lower spend, now representing 12% of digital revenue (up from 9%), while the mobile app hit an all-time high of nearly 40% of digital revenue and converts at roughly 7x desktop/mobile web rates.”

description: Q2 revenue was $216.4 million, above the $214.15 million consensus and the $215 million top of guidance. That also reversed the preview’s expected growth deceleration: reported growth was 10%, versus 8.8% implied by consensus.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue was $216.4 million, up 10% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1 and exceeding the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus” revenue was “$214.15M”; the guide was “$213–215M” and implied “+8.8%” year-over-year.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AI Studio and AI teammates contributed about 25% of net new ARR, or about 22% excluding one large deal—well above the 15% full-year target and above the preview’s >20% bull-case threshold. The preview expected an AI update, but this level of contribution was stronger than its 17–19% base case.
fact_evidence: “AI Studio and AI teammates drove approximately 25% of net new ARR (about 22% excluding one large deal), up from 17% last quarter and above the 15% full-year target set in March.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 was “17% vs. a 15% full-year target,” identified “>20%” as the bull trigger, and put the base case at “AI 17–19% of net-new ARR.”

description: The full-year revenue range’s ceiling stayed at $863.5 million, short of the preview’s hoped-for raise to at least $865 million, despite the Q2 beat. The low end did rise by $3 million, so this was not a wholly unchanged range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 revenue guidance is $858.5 million to $863.5 million (9% growth at midpoint).”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 needs to move to ≥$865M to be read as a raise”; the preview also said a range “merely” reaffirmed would read as a de facto cut.

description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 10%, about 110 basis points above the preview’s roughly 8.9% consensus, while EPS was $0.10 versus $0.0875 consensus. Both profitability measures outperformed expectations despite the anticipated StackAI margin drag.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 10%, expanding roughly 300 basis points year-over-year, with net income of $23.8 million or $0.10 per diluted share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 non-GAAP operating margin consensus at “~8.9%” and EPS consensus at “$0.0875”; it also expected a “~1pt operating margin drag in Q2” from StackAI.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Overall dollar-based NRR improved to 97%, but remained one point below the preview’s 98% in-quarter expectation. Core-customer and $100,000-plus-customer NRR both reached 98%, with the latter improving from 96%.
fact_evidence: “Overall dollar-based net retention rate improved to 97% from 96%, with core customer NRR and $100,000+ customer NRR both reaching 98% (the latter up from 96%).”
expectation_evidence: The preview called “in-quarter NRR 98%” the cleanest proof of improvement and said “NRR 96% / 97%” was the prior-quarter trailing/in-quarter figure.

description: The company disclosed a new second-half revenue timing headwind from consumption-based AI revenue recognition and AWM packaging, plus additional gross-margin pressure. The preview discussed PLG and StackAI pressures but did not flag these specific timing and margin effects.
fact_evidence: “The transition to consumption-based AI revenue recognition and AWM packaging creates a $1.2 million second-half revenue timing headwind, split between Q3 and Q4, plus about 150 bps of second-half gross margin pressure.”

description: Gross margin declined about 120 basis points sequentially to 87% as AI infrastructure costs rose, Stack AI was added, and the mix shifted toward AI products. The preview focused on StackAI’s operating-margin drag, not this reported gross-margin decline.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined about 120 basis points sequentially to 87%, driven by higher AI infrastructure costs (80 bps), the Stack AI addition (30 bps), and mix shift toward AI products.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described StackAI as carrying a “~1pt operating margin drag in Q2 and 2H.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Enterprise AI adoption was evidenced by a record AI expansion agreement: a Fortune 500 media company signed a three-year multimillion-dollar deal with nearly half of contract value from AI products. More than one-quarter of customers spending over $100,000 had purchased AI Studio or an AI teammate; the preview had not specified these adoption milestones.
fact_evidence: “Over 25% of customers spending $100,000+ have now purchased AI Studio or an AI teammate,” and the company “signed its largest AI expansion deal ever,” a “3-year multimillion-dollar agreement with a Fortune 500 media company,” with AI products at “nearly half of total contract value.”

description: U.S. revenue returned to double-digit growth for the first time in more than two years. The preview did not identify this U.S. growth milestone as an expectation or a key debate.
fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue grew 10% year-over-year, returning to double-digit growth for the first time in over two years.”

description: The technology vertical posted a second consecutive quarter of growth, continuing its recovery after the prior quarter’s turn positive. The preview noted the initial turn but said tech outperformance was excluded from the FY outlook, leaving continued growth as potential upside.
fact_evidence: “The technology vertical posted a second consecutive quarter of growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the tech vertical had “turn[ed] positive after eight quarters” in Q1, while the FY outlook “excludes tech-vertical outperformance.”

description: The preview did not mention an Investor Day or Analyst Day, but eGain announced that both would be held in Chicago on October 13 alongside eGain Solve. This is an unexpected event announcement, though the facts provided do not indicate its financial or operational implications.
fact_evidence: The call announced an Investor Day and Analyst Day to be held in conjunction with eGain Solve on October 13 in Chicago.
