description: Revenue of $54.6 million exceeded the preview’s $53.1 million anchor and its $54.0 million alternate consensus figure. The beat was modest, and it was closer to the preview’s roughly $54 million buy-side bar.
fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue grew 55% year-over-year to $54.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $53.1M (Zacks) / $54.0M (S&P agg.)”; the preview also says, “Assume the buy-side bar is $0.06 and ~$54M.”

description: Diluted EPS was $0.06, above the preview’s published $0.05 consensus, though it matched the preview’s higher $0.06 whisper estimate. Adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million also topped the preview’s $5.3 million estimate.
fact_evidence: “Net income more than doubled, rising 100.9% to $2.6 million ($0.06 per diluted share)”; “Adjusted EBITDA increased 68.9% to $5.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $0.05”; “Adj. EBITDA | ~$5.2M”; the preview also says, “the buy-side bar is $0.06.”

description: Gross margin was 24.0%, just below the preview’s 24.3% estimate, and did not show the stronger recovery the preview identified as a possible validation of easing startup costs. Management instead said it shifted about $0.5 million into trade spend and spent over $1 million more on trade year over year, pressuring near-term gross margin.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved sequentially to 24.0% from 23.6% in Q1 but declined from 24.9% year-over-year”; management “intentionally shifted about $0.5 million (roughly a full point of margin) from marketing into trade spend and spent over $1 million more in trade than the prior year due to high returns.”
expectation_evidence: “My estimates: Revenue $53.5M, gross margin 24.3%”; the preview says Q2 is “the first quarter where those startup costs should begin unwinding” and describes 24.0–24.9% as “acceptable, on-track.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Mama’s announced a first-ever Kroger launch for next month, an expansion the preview did not flag. The initial placement is limited to over 100 stores—about 10% of Kroger’s roughly 1,300 banner locations—with four items.
fact_evidence: “The company will launch in Kroger for the first time next month, starting with over 100 stores in the Louisville division with four items … representing about 10% of Kroger's ~1,300 banner locations.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Costco confirmed a second-half multi-vendor mailer across all eight regions that management forecasts will be larger than last year. The preview focused on a Costco everyday placement to watch, rather than anticipating this broader mailer.
fact_evidence: “Costco confirmed a second-half multi-vendor mailer across all eight regions forecasted to be larger than last year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview lists “the Costco San Diego branded beef meatball everyday placement” among the items to watch.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Walmart distribution grew beyond the preview’s cited 2,000-plus-store footprint, reaching over 2,300 stores with nine items. This is a positive expansion beyond the distribution level the preview described, although the preview had specifically called for sell-through and repeat-rate detail.
fact_evidence: “Walmart distribution expanded to over 2,300 stores (up from ~2,000) with nine items.”
expectation_evidence: The preview describes “7 Walmart chicken SKUs in 2,000+ stores” and says to watch for “actual velocity/repeat-rate commentary versus another list of door counts.”

description: The company said its larger cash balance enables larger, more transformative M&A, but the reported update remained a broad statement of capacity rather than the targets, size, or timing the preview said investors wanted.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $138.6 million in cash … against only $4.8 million total debt, enabling larger and more transformative M&A.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said investors “need a timeline” and wanted “targets, size, timing, and whether the $94M is one deal or several.”

description: Oxford cut FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $1.60–$2.00 from $2.30–$2.70, a much steeper reduction than the preview’s bear case of $2.30–$2.50. The new range is also below fiscal 2025 adjusted EPS of $2.11.
fact_evidence: “Slashed full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.60-$2.00,” down from $2.11 in fiscal 2025.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY2026 adjusted EPS guide was $2.30–$2.70 and identified a trim to $2.30–$2.50 as the bear case.

description: Lilly Pulitzer weakened more than the preview’s expected sequential improvement from Q1, and management does not expect a positive trend change until spring 2027. The preview had described assortment fixes as a possible contributor to the current-year recovery.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said the reported growth rate understates underlying momentum: it estimated growth would be several percentage points higher if the perpetual-versus-subscription mix had remained at last year’s level.
fact_evidence: Management indicated “the accelerating shift toward subscriptions is masking underlying momentum, estimating growth would be several percentage points higher if the perpetual/subscription mix had stayed constant with last year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q3-to-date same-store sales are tracking above 3%, ahead of the preview’s 3.0% bogey and Evercore’s 2.5% consensus estimate. That points to a somewhat stronger near-term comp than expected.
fact_evidence: “Q3 currently tracking above 3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Bogey: ≥3.0%”; Evercore: “Q3 +3.0% vs. cons. +2.5%.”

description: The Q2 revenue result was above the preview’s functional consensus midpoint: total revenues were $208 million versus an expected approximately $202 million. The result was still within the disclosed $189 million–$214 million range.
fact_evidence: “Total revenues rose 10% to $208 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~ $202M” with a disclosed range of “$189M – $214M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was above the preview’s approximately $111 million midpoint, but the reported 7% growth understates the result excluding an advertising timing difference. The call also cited $8 million of lower costs from exiting the area director model, addressing the preview’s concern about cost pressure.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 7% to $114 million”; growth “would have been 18%” absent the advertising timing difference, aided by “$8 million in lower costs from exiting the area director model.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~ $111M” with a disclosed range of “$107M – $117M”; the preview also flagged “incremental public-company G&A” as a risk to the EBITDA outlook.

description: The initial full-year guide calls for adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20%, with management saying a G&A step-down will drive growth above its algorithm. That is more encouraging than the preview’s concern that public-company costs could pressure EBITDA, although the preview had no published EBITDA consensus.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for … adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20% … with a step-down in G&A driving above-algorithm EBITDA growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch incremental public-company G&A and how much of it is already in the Q2 base”; the preview also warned that a clean EBITDA result could “quietly become a 2027 estimate cut.”

description: The full-year unit-growth floor is at least 8%, slightly below the preview’s approximately 8.5% reaffirmation bogey. The wording is a floor rather than a specific forecast, so the shortfall from that bogey is limited.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for … net unit growth of at least 8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Bogey: reaffirm ~8.5% unit growth for FY26”; “Unit growth reaffirmation at ~8.5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management said Q2 same-store sales growth was predominantly transaction-driven, addressing the preview’s concern that the comp might rely on price rather than traffic. That makes the reported comp composition better than the preview’s downside scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 same-store sales grew 2.3% … driven predominantly by transactions.”
expectation_evidence: “A +2.3% comp carried by price with negative traffic is a materially worse print than the same comp on flat traffic.”

description: Revenue came in above the preview’s $2.97–3.00 billion total-revenue estimate: SUNB reported $3.1 billion, with rental revenue of $2.9 billion also above the preview’s roughly $2.70–2.73 billion estimate.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 total revenue grew 11.2% to $3.1 billion” and “rental revenue grew 12.5% to $2.9 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $2.97–3.00bn”; “Rental revenue | ~$2.70–2.73bn (est.).”

description: Adjusted EPS substantially exceeded the preview’s $1.04–$1.08 consensus range, reaching $1.18. The preview’s bull-case EPS was $1.15.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 20.4% to a first-quarter record of $1.18.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $1.04–1.08”; the bull scenario projected “$1.15.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA and especially its margin fell short of the preview’s expectations: EBITDA was about $1.3 billion versus an estimated $1.33–1.36 billion, and the 42.2% margin was well below the expected 44.5–45.5%.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 8.7% to $1.3 billion but margin declined to 42.2% from 43.2% a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$1.33–1.36bn”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~44.5–45.5%”; the preview set a bar of “roughly −100bps YoY (≈44.8%).”

description: Rather than reaffirming FY2027 guidance unchanged as the preview expected, SUNB raised its revenue-growth ranges and EBITDA guidance above the prior ranges.
fact_evidence: “Management raised FY2027 guidance to total revenue growth of 6%-9%, rental revenue growth of 7%-10%, and adjusted EBITDA of $4.92 billion-$5.12 billion.”
expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “+4.5% to +7.5%” total revenue growth, “+5% to +8%” rental revenue growth, and “$4.85–5.05bn” adjusted EBITDA; the preview said “the base case is a reaffirm.”

description: SUNB also raised its capital-spending ranges, indicating more investment than the preview’s already-established FY2027 capex ranges.
fact_evidence: “Gross capital expenditure guidance was raised to $2.75 billion-$3.15 billion and net rental capex to $2.4 billion-$2.8 billion, driven by mega project, specialty and energy demand.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed gross rental capex of “$2.45–2.85bn” and net rental capex of “$2.05–2.45bn.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Specialty rental growth was much stronger than the preview’s roughly 12% watchpoint and its 15%+ bull-case marker; specialty dollar utilization also rose more than the preview’s cited 200-basis-point prior-quarter increase.
fact_evidence: “North American Specialty rental revenue surged 25.3% with dollar utilization up 300 basis points to 77%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said specialty deceleration “below ~12%” would be a concern and described “specialty +15%+” in its bull scenario; it cited specialty utilization rising “200bps to 75%.”

description: General Tool growth was a clear upside to the preview’s threshold for a genuine surprise: revenue grew 7.4%, above the level the preview identified as meaningful upside for the segment.
fact_evidence: “General Tool rental revenue grew 7.4% with dollar utilization flat at 47%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “General tool above +4% would be the genuine upside surprise.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview did not identify the FIFA World Cup as a growth driver, but management attributed a sizable portion of quarterly rental growth to it.
fact_evidence: “The FIFA World Cup contributed roughly 250 basis points … to rental revenue growth in the quarter.”

description: Signet’s adjusted operating income reached $107 million, well above the preview’s roughly $88 million consensus estimate, while adjusted EPS growth was 36% versus the preview’s expected 6.8%. The 140-basis-point operating-income rate expansion also contrasts with the preview’s focus on gold-cost pressure.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income rose 25% to $107 million with 140 basis points of rate expansion”; “adjusted EPS growth of 36%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income … ~$88M (implied)”; “Adj. diluted EPS … $1.72 (+6.8% YoY).”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Signet secured an early seven-year Bread Financial renewal with substantial benefits that the preview did not anticipate: more than $1 billion in incremental noncomp revenue and operating income over the agreement’s life, including a $200–250 million operating benefit over 36 months and about $80 million of Q3 cash.
fact_evidence: “Signed an early 7-year renewal with credit partner Bread Financial through December 2035,” expected to generate “over $1 billion in incremental noncomp revenue and operating income”; the deal is expected to provide “$200-250 million” over 36 months and “roughly $80 million in cash” in Q3.

description: Shareholder returns were set to accelerate beyond the buyback pace the preview identified as a key watch item: Signet increased its authorization by nearly $400 million, announced a $125 million ASR, and said buybacks plus dividends would return 12% of its recent market cap in the first nine months.
fact_evidence: “Nearly $400 million increase to its share repurchase authorization and a $125 million ASR,” with “$575 million remaining”; combined with dividends, returns will total “12% of its recent market cap” in the first nine months.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$355M authorization remaining” and listed “Buyback/ASR pace” as a catalyst to watch.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The sales mix was notably uneven: comps were strong at price points above $2,000 and in timepieces, while fashion comps declined, particularly at Banter and in lower-priced metal pieces. This gives a concrete version of the preview’s concern that AUR and mix could carry results while lower-priced demand remained weak.
fact_evidence: “High single-digit comp growth occurred at price points over $2,000 and timepieces grew nearly double digits, while fashion posted a 1% comp decline driven by weakness at Banter and lower-priced metal pieces.”
expectation_evidence: The preview warned of “AUR carries the comp while units go negative” and highlighted the need to watch “Bridal: units vs. AUR.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Tariff refunds were quantified, but they are only a partial offset to the tariff burden: $30 million is expected this year, including $15 million in Q2, while indirect refunds are pushed to fiscal 2028. The preview anticipated that refunds could provide a near-term earnings source but had said their timing was too early to quantify.
fact_evidence: “Tariff refunds of $30 million are expected this year (including $15 million in Q2), but represent less than half of the net headwind from incremental tariffs, with indirect refunds expected to benefit fiscal 2028 instead.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said refund timing was “too early to quantify” and that “Quantified refunds would be a clean, low-quality-but-real EPS source.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Signet ended with cash up nearly $250 million year over year to about $525 million while inventory was down 1% despite gold-cost inflation. The preview did not flag this combination of stronger cash and lower inventory as an expected result.
fact_evidence: “Inventory ended down 1% to $2 billion despite gold cost inflation, and cash rose nearly $250 million year-over-year to about $525 million.”

description: Adjusted EPS was +$0.05 rather than the preview’s -$0.04 estimate, while adjusted EBITDA reached $7.7 million—above even the preview’s $4–6 million bull-case range. Both measures were substantially stronger than expected.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.7 million (6.9% of sales) from $4.7 million a year ago, while adjusted EPS improved to $0.05 from $0.01.”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (adjusted) -$0.04”; the scenario analysis put “adj. EBITDA $1–3M” in the base case and “adj. EBITDA $4–6M” in the bull case.

description: Gross margin rose to 47.9%, far above the preview’s roughly 44% base-case expectation, but a one-time $4.6 million tariff refund drove the result. Excluding the refund, merchandise margin would have been about 70 basis points worse year over year, so the headline strength did not reflect stronger underlying merchandise margin.
fact_evidence: “A one-time $4.6 million IEPA tariff refund benefited merchandise margin and drove gross margin up 270 basis points to 47.9%, but excluding the refund merchandise margin would have been roughly 70 basis points worse than last year.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “GM ~44% on tariffs,” and the preview flagged “Gross margin vs. the 100bps tariff headwind.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and investments were $20.1 million, above the preview’s expected $13–16 million range and the $16.2 million Q1 balance. The company also reported no debt, consistent with the expectation of no revolver draw.
fact_evidence: “The company reported a fortress balance sheet with $20.1 million of cash and investments, no debt, and $61.7 million of excess availability.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “cash ~$13–16M” and “no revolver draw”; the preview identified cash and liquidity as the key metric, starting from “$16.2M cash.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Although the quarter’s -3.5% comparable-sales decline was within the preview’s expected range, monthly comps improved from -5.7% in May to -1.9% in July. That was a stronger sequential trajectory than the preview’s base case of modest improvement suggested.
fact_evidence: “Monthly comps improved sequentially from -5.7% in May to -2.8% in June and -1.9% in July, signaling an improving sales trajectory.”
expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “Modest sequential improvement” and comps of “-3% to -5%”; the preview asked whether the Q1 “-3.8% comp stabilize[d] into the easier Q2 base.”

description: Management gave new detail on a multi-year store rationalization plan: about three stores are expected to close this year, with a few dozen 2027 lease renewals under review. The company expects occupancy costs and sales per square foot to improve beginning in 2027; the preview did not forecast this plan.
fact_evidence: “Management is executing a multi-year store rationalization plan closing about 3 stores this year and evaluating a few dozen lease renewals in 2027, expected to reduce occupancy costs and improve sales per square foot beginning in 2027.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview characterized GLP-1-related sizing changes as a secular threat to DXL’s addressable market. The call confirmed that some customers are pausing purchases while losing weight, but added that a majority say they intend to return once their size stabilizes, tempering that concern.
fact_evidence: “GLP-1 medication adoption among a meaningful portion of customers is driving weight-loss-related purchase pauses, though a majority of these customers say they intend to return to DXL once they reach a stable size.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described GLP-1 medications as “shifting customer sizing” and called this “a secular TAM question, not a cyclical one.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported measurable early traction across growth initiatives that the preview did not quantify: brand awareness rose from 40% to 49% in seven months, ThermaChill demand was up 56% year to date, and FitMap had scanned more than 150,000 customers, with higher average order values and lower return rates.
fact_evidence: “Early results from growth initiatives include brand awareness in the core 35-64 demographic (household income above $100,000) rising from 40% to 49% in seven months, ThermaChill private-brand demand up 56% year-to-date, and over 150,000 customers scanned via FitMap showing higher AOV and lower return rates.”

description: ODD guided Q3 revenue to decline only about 5% year over year, much better than the preview’s base-case decline of 15%–22% and its better-than-15% recovery threshold. Management said the worst of the acquisition-driven pressure is behind it.
fact_evidence: “The company guided Q3 net revenue to decline only ~5% year-over-year,” attributing the improvement to “the worst of the acquisition-driven pressure being behind them.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case called for “‑15% to ‑22%”; it said narrowing to “better than ‑15%” would validate recovery.

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $13 million, above the preview’s $8–$10 million guidance range. The beat was sizeable relative to the expected range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $13 million beat the $8-$10 million guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$8M–$10M” and consensus of “~$9–10M.”

description: Q2 revenue reached $181 million, slightly above the preview’s $176.5–$178.2 million consensus range and at the favorable end of company guidance. The beat was modest, since the preview already expected revenue in the upper part of guidance.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue declined 25% year-over-year to $181 million, landing at the favorable end of guidance for a 25%-30% decline.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave consensus of “$176.5M–$178.2M” and noted that consensus sat in “the upper third of the guided range.”

description: The full-year revenue outlook implies about $656 million, above the preview’s approximate $630 million revenue anchor. That points to a better full-year revenue outcome than the preview’s illustrative estimate, even though revenue is still expected to decline year over year.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 net revenue is expected to decline approximately 19%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described a business that “should still do ~$630M of revenue this year.”

description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook is now quantified at $30–$32 million rather than left at a general commitment to be positive. That gives investors a concrete target, though the preview did not provide a numerical estimate to compare against.
fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA [is] guided to $30-$32 million and Q3 to $18-$20 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 adjusted EBITDA was expected to be “positive” but “unquantified,” and called quantifying it a sign of restored confidence.

description: First-order net revenue was still down about 40% year over year. That is an improvement from Q1’s 50% decline, but it remains in the preview’s downside range rather than approaching the stronger recovery scenario.
fact_evidence: “Q2 first-order net revenue fell approximately 40%” year over year, driven by IL MAKIAGE.
expectation_evidence: The preview called first orders “the forward indicator” after Q1’s “‑50%,” and its bull scenario required first orders to improve to “better than ‑25%”; its bear scenario cited “still ‑40%+.”

description: Gross margin fell to 68.7%, below the preview’s roughly 70% expectation for stabilization. Management attributed much of the decline to an approximately 8% AOV drop and characterized it as non-structural and recoverable, which partly softens the miss.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin compressed approximately 360 basis points year-over-year to 68.7%, driven largely by an ~8% AOV decline,” which management called “non-structural and recoverable.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~70%” and said stabilization “at ~70%” would show remediation held.

description: Repeat-order net revenue declined about 20%, worse than the 15% decline cited for Q1. The preview had highlighted repeat orders and warned that lost first-order cohorts could weigh on future repeat activity, so the direction was a concern it had flagged, but the further deterioration was unfavorable.
fact_evidence: “Q2 ... repeat-order net revenue fell approximately 20% year-over-year,” driven by IL MAKIAGE.
expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 repeat orders at “‑15%” and warned that “Lost H1 first orders mechanically depress the 2027 repeat cohort.”

description: SpoiledChild is expected to grow at least 35% and approach $350 million of 2026 revenue, a much more specific and substantial growth outlook than the preview’s expectation that it would simply continue growing.
fact_evidence: “SpoiledChild is on track to grow at least 35% and approach $350 million of net revenue in 2026,” reaching that milestone more than a year faster than IL MAKIAGE did.
expectation_evidence: The preview said SpoiledChild “continues to grow” with “milder CPA impact,” without giving a growth rate or revenue target.

description: METHODIQ is now expected to deliver higher first-year revenue than SpoiledChild, beyond the preview’s stated expectation that it was tracking to a $25 million FY2026 target. The call did not provide a specific updated dollar target.
fact_evidence: “METHODIQ, launched less than a year ago, is expected to deliver higher first-year revenue than SpoiledChild.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said METHODIQ was “tracking to its $25M FY2026 target.”

description: The company outlined a planned move into longevity and metabolic health, including prescription injectable and peptide therapies in 2027, alongside a planned fourth brand launch. Those initiatives were not part of the preview’s diversification expectations.
fact_evidence: Management plans to expand METHODIQ into “longevity/metabolic health including prescription injectable and peptide therapies in 2027, alongside a planned Brand 4 launch.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s diversification discussion focused on METHODIQ’s “$25M FY2026” target and SpoiledChild’s continued growth.

description: ODDITY repurchased $50 million face value of its 2030 exchangeable notes for $35 million. The preview highlighted cash and undrawn facilities but did not anticipate this discounted debt repurchase.
fact_evidence: The company “repurchased $50 million face value of its 2030 exchangeable notes for $35 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Debt | $0 (plus $350M undrawn facility)” and did not mention a planned note repurchase.

description: Gross margin was expected around 34.5%, with 34%+ viewed as confirmation that Q2's improvement could hold. OCC reported 37.4%, well above that level, citing manufacturing operating leverage.
fact_evidence: “Q3 gross profit jumped 43.9% to $9.1 million, with gross margin expanding to 37.4% from 31.7% a year earlier due to manufacturing operating leverage.”
expectation_evidence: “My model (base case): revenue $24.5M, GM 34.5%”; “Sustained 34%+ on higher volume is the bull confirmation.”

description: OCC's diluted EPS of $0.21 slightly exceeded the preview's $0.20 estimate and its $0.18–0.19 model range.
fact_evidence: “Q3 net income surged to $1.9 million ($0.21 per diluted share).”
expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 est. EPS (basic/diluted): $0.20”; “EPS ~$0.18–0.19.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview said OCC was evaluating workforce expansion and equipment additions; the call reported that it is expanding capacity and hiring across facilities, including Roanoke and Dallas. The expansion is not quantified, but it is more concrete than the preview's evaluation-stage description.
fact_evidence: “The company…is expanding capacity and hiring across facilities (notably Roanoke and Dallas).”
expectation_evidence: “Management is ‘evaluating workforce expansion and equipment additions’”; “Any capex commitment, a quantified capacity ceiling, or concrete revenue attributable to Lightera would be new information.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview flagged a possible equity raise as a financing overhang given low cash and working-capital needs. Management instead said working capital had strengthened and that the revolver and operating cash were sufficient to fund growth, without indicating a need for an equity raise.
fact_evidence: “Working capital strengthened to $19.2 million from $13.9 million at fiscal year-end 2025, with management asserting the credit revolver and operating cash are sufficient to fund growth without indicating a need for an equity raise.”
expectation_evidence: “Any equity raise into strength…is a real overhang”; the preview also noted cash of “$146K” and that growth was “working-capital hungry.”

description: OCC reported that it had begun recording initial Lightera product sales. The preview identified concrete Lightera revenue as new information, although the call did not quantify the contribution.
fact_evidence: “The company has begun recording initial sales of Lightera products under its strategic collaboration.”
expectation_evidence: “Any…concrete revenue attributable to Lightera would be new information”; “first quantified revenue contribution would be genuinely new.”

description: Sales were slightly below the $24.5 million estimate: OCC reported $24.3 million, or 22% year-over-year growth, versus the preview's implied 23% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 22% year-over-year to $24.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $24.5M”; “Implied Y/Y: +23%.”

description: SG&A came in above the preview's $6.5 million model, and at 28.7% of sales it missed the preview's operating-leverage marker of below about 28%.
fact_evidence: “Q3 SG&A rose to $7 million from $5.7 million but held essentially flat at 28.7% of sales versus 28.8% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “My model (base case)…SG&A $6.5M”; “the operating leverage story requires SG&A to stay below ~28% of sales.”

description: SailPoint raised its FY27 ARR target by $11 million to $1.38 billion, rather than holding the prior $1.369 billion target as the preview’s base case anticipated. The increase is positive, though it is below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.385 billion.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance was raised by $11 million to $1.38 billion ARR (up 23%).”
expectation_evidence: “Base: ... FY ARR held at $1.369B”; “Bull ... FY27 ARR raised to ≥$1.385B.”

description: Adjusted operating margin was 20.3%, well above the preview’s 18.4% quarterly guide and its expectation of roughly 200 basis points of year-over-year compression. This was a clear reversal of the anticipated margin pressure.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin was 20.3%.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income ... (18.4% margin)”; “Guide implies ~200bps of Y/Y compression.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Total ARR reached $1.231 billion, $11 million above the guidance midpoint and above the preview’s base-case range of $1.220–$1.228 billion. It was slightly short of the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.235 billion.
fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 total ARR reached $1.231 billion ... exceeding the guidance midpoint by $11 million.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Net new SaaS ARR was $66 million, up 34%, compared with $35 million in Q1, when reported growth was only 5%. That is a strong sequential improvement against the preview’s focus on whether SaaS additions would reaccelerate, although the call facts do not specify constant-currency growth.
fact_evidence: “Net new SaaS ARR of $66 million (up 34%).”
expectation_evidence: “Q1 was $35M, +5% reported but +30%+ cc”; “The bear case is cc growth decelerating below ~25%; the bull case needs reacceleration.”

description: Revenue was $309 million, slightly below the $310.4 million consensus estimate, though still inside the $308–312 million company guide. The call attributed an approximately $5 million in-period revenue headwind to the higher SaaS mix and the timing difference between SaaS and term revenue.
fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $309 million”; “The higher SaaS mix created an approximately $5 million revenue timing headwind.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue ... $308–312M”; “Consensus ... $310.4M.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: SaaS accounted for 97% of net new ARR, above the 90–95% range the company had guided. The greater SaaS share supports the ARR mix, while also contributing to the reported revenue timing headwind.
fact_evidence: “Net new SaaS ARR ... accounting for 97% of total net new ARR—above the guided 90-95% range.”
expectation_evidence: “Guided 90-95% range.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AI-driven ARR had already exceeded $70 million by quarter-end, putting SailPoint well ahead of pace for its $100 million fiscal year-end target. The preview discussed AI monetization as an upside lever but did not give this FY27 target or report this level of progress toward it.
fact_evidence: “Total AI-driven ARR already surpassed $70 million by end of Q2, putting the company well ahead of pace to hit its $100 million fiscal year-end target.”
expectation_evidence: “$100 million fiscal year-end target.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Existing customers adopting AI-driven solutions increased annual spend by more than 60%, exceeding the 25–50% uplift range discussed at Analyst Day. The reported expansion was materially above that prior benchmark.
fact_evidence: “Existing customers adopting AI-driven solutions increased their annual spend by over 60%.”
expectation_evidence: “25-50% uplift range discussed at Analyst Day.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AI-driven solutions represented more than 30% of Q2 net new ARR, and the AI-driven pipeline had more than doubled to over $200 million since Investor Day less than three months earlier. These figures provide stronger quantified adoption and pipeline evidence than the preview had specified.
fact_evidence: “AI-driven solutions accounted for more than 30% of net new ARR in Q2, and the AI-driven pipeline has more than doubled to over $200 million since Investor Day less than three months ago.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported that Entro-based POCs are shortening sales cycles to 30–45 days compared with traditional agentic suite purchases. The preview noted Entro and agentic conversion as issues to watch but did not anticipate this specific faster POC path.
fact_evidence: “Entro-based POCs are shortening sales cycles to 30-45 days versus traditional agentic suite purchases.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Organic vs. inorganic ARR” and “Agentic Fabric / non-human identity monetization” as key metrics to watch, but gave no POC-cycle expectation.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: More than two-thirds of migrations included an AI-driven solution, and those migrations carried a 2–3x ARR uplift. The preview discussed migration pace and Modernization Flex use, but did not anticipate this degree of AI attachment or the reported uplift.
fact_evidence: “Over two-thirds of migrations ... included an AI-driven solution with 2-3x ARR uplift.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “On-prem migration pace” and noted Modernization Flex was used in “~1/3 of migrations”; it did not state an expectation for AI attachment or ARR uplift.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: RPO growth accelerated to 30% at $1.9 billion, while current RPO grew 27% to $931 million, with the call pointing to larger deal sizes. The preview did not discuss RPO or set an expectation for this forward-demand measure.
fact_evidence: “RPO accelerated to 30% growth ($1.9 billion) and current RPO grew 27% to $931 million on larger deal sizes.”

description: Korn Ferry reported $756 million of fee revenue, above the preview’s $736.8 million consensus and the $745 million high end of prior guidance; adjusted EPS of $1.43 also exceeded the $1.36 consensus. Both headline results came in stronger than the preview’s modest-growth baseline.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 fee revenue grew 7% year-over-year to $756 million” and “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 9% year-over-year to $1.43.”
expectation_evidence: “Fee revenue | Consensus $736.8M | Company Guidance $725M – $745M” and “Diluted EPS | Consensus $1.36.”

description: The Q2 fee-revenue guide of $860–$878 million is at the upper end of, and extends above, the preview’s $845–$870 million framework for a credible guide including about two months of AMS. The two-month AMS contribution itself was expected.

description: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.15 exceeded the preview’s $1.11–$1.12 consensus range. The preview noted Cooper’s history of repeated EPS beats, so the result was better than the estimate but not an entirely unexpected pattern.

fact_evidence: The Board approved a “$1 billion increase to share repurchase authorization,” bringing capacity to about $1.5 billion; Cooper repurchased $339 million in Q3 and $445 million year to date.
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “size of buyback executed in Q3 and any new authorization” as a key watch item and noted only $13 million had been repurchased in Q2.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: A favorable HMRC examination resolution produced a large discrete tax benefit and extended non-GAAP tax benefits for at least another decade, an unanticipated positive development.
fact_evidence: The company recognized a discrete tax benefit of “~$307 million” following favorable resolution of an HMRC examination, providing non-GAAP tax benefits for “at least 10 additional years.”

fact_evidence: The scheduled GILTI increase is expected to move the non-GAAP effective tax rate from roughly 15.5% this year to roughly 17.5% in fiscal 2027.

fact_evidence: Q3 non-GAAP EPS included “~$0.03 from tariff refunds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said whether the excluded “~$15M in refunds materializes” mattered.

expectation_evidence: “FY27 guide reaffirmed at $388–406M” was the base case; the preview also called guidance action “the binary.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $33.4 million, well above the preview’s $26–28 million estimate, and the margin reached 34% versus an expected 27–28%. fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations rose 7% to $33.4 million, with margin expanding to 34% from 31% a year earlier, aided by a 12% cut in selling and marketing expenses.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$26–28M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~27–28%.” The base case described “cost discipline” holding “the ~28% margin.”

fact_evidence: “Dollar retention rate improved to 95% from 94% year-over-year, though the LTM DRR slipped to 98% from 99%.”
expectation_evidence: “A second consecutive quarter ≥100% validates the go-to-market redesign; a relapse into the low 90s guts the H2 ramp story.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position

fact_evidence: “The Global Knowledge disposal is estimated to consume about $15 million of fiscal 2027 cash ($12 million already incurred through July 31), plus ~$4 million of Q3 advisory costs.”
expectation_evidence: The bear scenario cited “GK separation costs run above the $8–10M guided.”

description: The preview identified refinancing progress on the 2028 term loan as a key debate and said silence or a repeat of general priority language would be negative. fact_evidence: “Addressing upcoming debt maturities [was] identified as management's top financial priority following the Global Knowledge divestiture.”
expectation_evidence: “Anything concrete — advisors engaged, lender conversations, a term sheet, an amend-and-extend — is a bigger stock event”; “Silence or a repeat of ‘we're evaluating all alternatives with discipline and urgency’ is a negative.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call provided specific early AI-product adoption indicators that the preview had not flagged: Casey conversation-simulator learners and using organizations grew year over year, and AI Coach was being piloted by seven organizations. These are positive early signs, though the facts do not quantify bookings from that adoption.
fact_evidence: “Casey conversation-simulator learners [were] up 23% year-over-year and using organizations up 9%, plus AI Coach now piloted by seven organizations out of 30-plus early-access customers.”

description: The preview expected Q3 adjusted EBITDA to reach roughly breakeven, but Gloo guided to a $3.5 million loss. Management now targets adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026, one quarter later than the preview’s key expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $55 million and adjusted EBITDA of -$3.5 million”; management committed to “reaching adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the implied Q3/Q4 revenue was “roughly Q3 ~$52M and Q4 ~$57M,” and called “Q3 breakeven” the “make-or-break item”; it also said that if Q3 breakeven were “pushed to Q4,” the profitability narrative would break.

description: Gloo raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $200 million, rather than merely reaffirming the preview’s expected $195 million. The increase is inclusive of Cedarstone, though the call did not provide a clean organic-growth figure.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $5 million to $200 million, inclusive of the Cedarstone acquisition.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 revenue guidance of “$195.0M” and said the base case was that FY guidance would be “reaffirmed.”

description: Q2 revenue exceeded the $44 million guide and consensus by $2.6 million, a roughly 6% beat. The preview had cautioned that anything below a 3–5% beat could signal decelerating momentum.
fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue grew 188% year-over-year to $46.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue guidance and consensus at “$44.0M” and said “Anything less than a ~3–5% beat reads as decelerating momentum.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Quarter-end cash was below the preview’s estimated range and below its $40 million risk threshold. The July offering brought in more net proceeds than the preview’s rough estimate, but did not prevent the ending cash balance from coming in lower than expected.
fact_evidence: Gloo “raised $23.7 million net in a follow-on offering” and “ended the quarter with $39.3 million in cash.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$42–46M” cash at July 31 and said “Below ~$40M” would reopen dilution risk; it estimated “~$21M net” from the July offering.

description: Q3 revenue guidance of $55 million is above the preview’s approximate $52 million expectation, suggesting a stronger near-term revenue run rate than the preview’s H2 build implied.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $55 million,” driven by peak advertising and fundraising season for Masterworks and Westfall Gold.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s H2 math implied “roughly Q3 ~$52M.”

description: The call did not provide the clean organic-growth disclosure the preview identified as the highest-value disclosure; instead, it said platform growth was driven substantially by acquisitions. That leaves the preview’s concern about how much growth is acquired unresolved.
fact_evidence: Platform solutions revenue rose 209% and platform revenue rose 170%, “both driven substantially by acquisitions like Masterworks, Westfall Gold, and EMD”; the call facts provide no organic-growth percentage.
expectation_evidence: The preview called a “clean organic figure” the “single highest-value disclosure” and said “Silence on it is a negative.”

description: Cost of revenue improved substantially year over year, an unexpectedly favorable margin development given the preview’s concern that a greater services mix could weigh on revenue quality.
fact_evidence: “Cost of revenue improved 10.8 percentage points to 64.0% of total revenue from 74.8% a year earlier,” aided by scale and favorable acquisition mix.
expectation_evidence: The preview warned that Cedarstone’s outsourced accounting and fractional CFO work was “services, not software,” and that a mix “drifting toward solutions justifies a lower multiple.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was slightly better than expected, at a loss of $8.3 million versus the preview’s $8.5 million loss estimate. The improvement is small compared with the more consequential shortfall against the preview’s Q3 breakeven expectation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved $3.2 million sequentially to -$8.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance and consensus at “–$8.5M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Gloo reported a first customer above $10 million in annual contract value and more than 30 customers above $1 million, providing a customer-scale milestone the preview did not forecast.
fact_evidence: “The company now has more than 30 customers with over $1 million in annual contract value and reached its first customer exceeding $10 million in annual contract value.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The call disclosed a $4.4 million restructuring charge tied mainly to severance, which the preview did not flag. Management also said it plans to invest in additional salespeople, so integration-related cuts are not the only operating-cost move.
fact_evidence: “The company took a $4.4 million restructuring charge in Q2, primarily for severance related to integrating business lines, while planning to invest in additional salespeople.”

description: Gloo said its $13.2 million senior secured loan was extended to April 2028, a financing-term update not anticipated in the preview and potentially easing near-term refinancing pressure.
fact_evidence: The company “extended its $13.2 million senior secured loan to April 2028.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said future acquisitions are targeted to use a 20–25% cash structure, an unanticipated detail that could limit cash use in future deals. The call also quantified Cedarstone’s customer contribution at more than 250 new mid-market customers.
fact_evidence: “The Cedarstone acquisition added over 250 new mid-market customers with strong Masterworks cross-selling potential,” and management targeted a “20-25% cash structure for future deals.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described Cedarstone as an acquisition of outsourced accounting and fractional CFO services and raised concern about “Cedarstone cash consideration still to come,” but did not specify its customer contribution or a target cash structure for future deals.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The cash management fee rate was 55 bps, below the preview’s expected 56–57 bps range and at the preview’s stated bear-case threshold. That puts more pressure on the cash revenue model than the base case anticipated.
fact_evidence: “The annualized cash management fee rate fell 6 basis points year-over-year to 55 basis points,” driven by the APY-to-APR conversion at lower Fed funds rates and higher client incentive costs.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected a “fee rate 0.56–0.57%”; it said a rate “below ~0.55%” would be a bear-case trigger.

description: Cash management revenue was $61.8 million, below the preview’s estimated $62–64 million. This was a modest shortfall even though total revenue landed near the preview’s overall estimate.
fact_evidence: “Cash management revenue declined 10% to $61.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated cash revenue at “~$62–64M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Cash management assets fell 4% year-over-year, a steeper decline than the roughly 2% decline the preview cited. Quarter-end cash assets were still around the preview’s expected $44–45 billion range, but the year-over-year contraction was worse.
fact_evidence: “Cash management assets fell 4% year-over-year to $44.9 billion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said cash management assets were “down ~2% YoY” and projected “cash assets flat ~$44–45B.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management attributed cash outflows in part to the 2023 and 2024 client cohorts lagging in investment adoption after joining during peak rates. fact_evidence: “The 2023 and 2024 client cohorts, which joined during peak rates, have lagged in investment adoption and driven cash outflows.”
expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether cash attrition was “a rate-cycle artifact or genuine share loss to higher-yielding competitors,” without identifying these cohorts as a driver.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs

fact_evidence: “Targeted incentives improved July and August cash net deposits to the best level since March.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said cash net deposits needed “to turn positive, or at least shrink the outflow from -$235M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The call reported 1.1 million funded clients, far below the preview’s last disclosed figure of 1.49 million for June, even as the call described funded clients as up 14% year-over-year. The provided materials do not reconcile the difference, so the implication for client growth is unclear.
fact_evidence: “Funded clients rose 14% year-over-year to 1.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s metrics table listed “Jun 30 … Funded clients 1.49M.”

description: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.10, slightly above the preview’s bottom-up expectation of roughly $0.06–$0.09 for GAAP EPS. It was still below the preview’s $0.13–$0.14 public estimates, which the preview warned could reflect adjusted rather than GAAP conventions.

expectation_evidence: The preview said “GAAP EPS lands ~$0.06–$0.09” if SBC stayed near $17 million per quarter.

description: Investment advisory revenue reached $28.8 million, modestly above the preview’s estimate of about $28 million. The advisory business therefore performed a little better than the preview’s build implied.
fact_evidence: “Investment advisory revenue grew 31% to $28.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated advisory revenue at “≈ $28M.”

expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS | ZAR 5.50–6.00”; the preview’s implied Q4 adj. EPS range was “1.26” to “1.76.”

expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Merchant revenue growth turns positive” and described the base case as “Merchant flat.”

expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “FY27 guided ex-Bank Zero at ZAR 1.5–1.6bn EBITDA” and said a clean ex-Bank Zero guide was most likely.

expectation_evidence: The preview reported leverage at “2.1x at Q3 vs a 2.0x target.”

description: Management warned that one-off and restructuring costs in Merchant will pressure Q1 FY27 results, an additional near-term headwind not identified in the preview.
fact_evidence: Management “flagged one-off and restructuring costs that will pressure Q1 FY27 results.”

expectation_evidence: “Sell-side consensus sits at $220.5M”; the preview’s bull case forecast revenue of “$230–235M.”

expectation_evidence: “Gross Booking Volume … Consensus $2.86B (+37%).”

expectation_evidence: “TTM FCF +$2M (vs. −$52.4M prior year)” and “$681M cash and short-term investments.”

fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year FY27 … non-GAAP operating income guidance to $82-86 million (9% margin), marking the second raise this year.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP op income $76–80M (~9% margin)” and “Watch whether op income is raised alongside revenue.”

fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for … non-GAAP operating income of $35.5-36.5 million (14% margin).”
expectation_evidence: “The Q2 margin guide implies a ~460bp sequential non-GAAP operating margin compression” and “H2 must carry $38–42M: either margins step up hard or the op-income guide gets raised too.”

fact_evidence: “New signed GBV for the sales-led growth (SLG) enterprise business reached $4 billion over the trailing 12 months, up 60% versus Q2 last year, serving as a leading indicator of future revenue.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Navan said it now serves 50 S&P 500 companies, up from 45 last quarter, exceeding the preview’s cited count of 45. The preview had highlighted enterprise-logo growth, so the additional five companies were a favorable update.
fact_evidence: “The company now serves 50 companies in the S&P 500, up from 45 last quarter, with rising win rates and ASPs.”
expectation_evidence: “45 at Q1, up from 28 a year prior.”

description: Product-led growth revenue more than doubled year over year, a strong result for a business line the preview did not quantify or identify as a specific Q2 expectation.
fact_evidence: “Product-led growth revenue more than doubled year-over-year.”

description: Subscription revenue grew 39% to $21 million, another strong revenue stream update that the preview had not specifically anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue was $21 million (up 39%).”

description: Navan reported that its AI agent resolved about 60% of customer interactions and that its own models accounted for half of usage, up from 30% in Q1. This puts specific operating results behind the preview’s discussion of possible AI-driven support savings.
fact_evidence: “AI agent Ava resolved approximately 60% of customer interactions in Q2, driving structural gross margin gains, with Navan-owned AI models rising to 50% of usage from 30% in Q1.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s commentary tells included “AI-driven support cost savings.”

fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin exceeded 75% for the first time in company history (up 200 bps year-over-year).”

fact_evidence: “Payment volumes reached $1.3 billion (up 34%).”
expectation_evidence: “+35%+ is a genuine positive surprise; another sub-30% quarter says Navan is a travel company with a card attached.”

expectation_evidence: “Street sits at ~$1.52B (roughly flat).” A guide to “another year of decline” was identified as “the bear trigger.”

fact_evidence: The company guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA of $10 to $15 million, which “absorbs roughly $12 million of additional variable compensation expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “flat-to-up revenue with a $25M+ EBITDA floor” as the bull trigger, while its base scenario expected FY2027 guidance to be framed qualitatively, “no hard EBITDA number.”

expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch FY26 FCF, revolver capacity, and any covenant language” and listed “first mention of covenant headroom or refinancing” as a bear signal.

fact_evidence: Q4 Gourmet Foods and Gift Baskets revenue declined 15.4%. The Easter timing shift reduced that segment’s revenue by roughly 2.5 to 3.5 percentage points and overall Q4 revenue by about 1.5%, with no full-year impact.
expectation_evidence: The preview’s secondary watch list described “Gourmet Foods holding flat (Q3 $106.9M, ~flat).”

description: BloomNet returned to growth, contrary to the preview’s concern that the historically stable segment was now declining. Its Q4 increase also reversed the decline reported for Q3.
fact_evidence: BloomNet revenue increased 1.9% in Q4.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “BloomNet trend (Q3 −5.9% — the historically stable, high-margin franchise segment is now declining).”

description: Net debt rose well above the preview’s Q3 estimate, and the company ended the year with only $11 million of cash. The preview anticipated a cash-consumptive quarter, but the reported net debt was roughly $34–$37 million above its cited Q3 level.
fact_evidence: Net debt rose to $128 million from $114 million a year earlier, with cash of $11 million, $139 million in term debt, and no revolver borrowings.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q3 exit net debt of “~$91M (management cited $94.3M)” and said, “Q4 is a cash-consumptive quarter.”

description: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA came in slightly above the top of the breakeven ±$2 million guide, and the Q4 loss was smaller than the preview’s derived estimate. This was a modest positive versus the guide, rather than the serious guide miss the preview warned about.
fact_evidence: Full-year adjusted EBITDA was $2.9 million; Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss was $31 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY2026 guidance of “breakeven ±$2M” and derived Q4 adjusted EBITDA of approximately “−$32M to −$34M.”

description: Designer Brands raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $0.47–$0.52 from $0.28–$0.38, a much larger increase than the preview’s base case of reaffirming the range with high-end language.
fact_evidence: “Raised full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $0.47-$0.52,” from prior guidance of “$0.28-$0.38.”
expectation_evidence: The base case expected “FY guide reaffirmed with ‘high end’ language intact”; UBS was also described as expecting a reaffirmation.

description: Adjusted gross margin reached 47.9%, far above the preview’s 44.8% estimate. The gain was partly boosted by a tariff refund claim—280 basis points of the 430-basis-point expansion—while underlying improvement was 150 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 430 basis points to 47.9%,” including “280 basis points” from a “$20.2 million tariff refund claim,” with “150 basis points of underlying improvement.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin of “44.8%,” or “+110 bps,” and said tariff impacts and refund claims were expected to be largely offset by new tariffs.

description: Q2 sales were below the preview’s $742 million base-case estimate, with sales down about 1% rather than up 0.3%.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell approximately 1% year-over-year to $730.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bottom-up estimate was “$742M (+0.3% Y/Y),” with an implied range of “$735–750M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Retail comps were weaker than the preview’s expectation that retail would be flat to slightly up: comparable sales fell 2.4%, and retail segment sales declined 2%. Sandals explained roughly 200 basis points of the retail decline, leaving sales approximately flat excluding sandals.
fact_evidence: Comparable store sales were “down 2.4%,” retail segment sales “declined 2%,” and seasonal sandals accounted for “roughly 200 basis points” of the retail decline; excluding sandals, retail sales were “approximately flat.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided Q2 retail to “flat to slightly up” and identified the retail comp as the key inflection test.

description: The company also raised its sales outlook, narrowing the downside and moving the range’s low end to flat growth. This was a smaller improvement than the EPS guidance increase.
fact_evidence: Full-year sales guidance was lifted “to flat-to-up 1% from prior negative 1% to positive 1%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed the existing FY2026 net sales guide as “−1% to +1%” and expected a reaffirmation in its base case.

description: Brand Portfolio sales grew 18%, above the preview’s 12–15% Q2 build, despite being slightly below the prior quarter’s 19.4% growth.
fact_evidence: “Brand Portfolio sales grew 18%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 build assumed “Brand Portfolio +12–15%.”

description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.34 edged above the preview’s $0.32 bottom-up estimate, though it was nearly flat with the prior-year $0.33 and the tariff benefits were offset by higher taxes and interest expense.
fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted net income was “$19.2 million ($0.34 per diluted share), only modestly above last year's $16.4 million ($0.33), as tariff benefits were offset by higher taxes and interest expense.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s bottom-up Q2 estimate was “$0.32” adjusted EPS.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Debt fell further than the preview’s balance-sheet snapshot implied: it was $423.1 million, below the preview’s cited $475.3 million level, and liquidity was somewhat higher than the cited $189 million.
fact_evidence: Total debt was reduced “to $423.1 million from $516.3 million a year ago,” and the company ended the quarter with “roughly $198 million in total liquidity.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited debt of “$475.3M” and liquidity of “$189M.”

description: Q4 diluted EPS was $0.02, half the preview’s current $0.04 estimate. The preview cautioned that its published full-year EPS figure was unreliable, so the more current quarterly estimate is the relevant comparison.
fact_evidence: “Q4 net income fell to $666,000 ($0.02) from $2.4 million ($0.09)”
expectation_evidence: “TipRanks' next-quarter estimate of $0.04 (range $0.03–$0.04) is the more current mark and is what I use.”

description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA was $5.8 million, below the preview’s expected $6.0–$6.2 million. The preview also set a $1.6 million Q4 floor, but the provided call facts do not state Q4 adjusted EBITDA, so that quarterly comparison cannot be confirmed here.
fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA increased to $5.8 million from $5.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adjusted EBITDA should land ~$6.0–6.2M vs. $5.3M in FY2025 (+13–17%).”

description: Gross margin improved more than the preview anticipated: fiscal 2026 reached 51.9%, up 260 basis points, and Q4 reached a record 53%, versus an expected roughly 100-basis-point full-year improvement and about 52% for Q4.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 gross margin improved 260 basis points to 51.9%, with Q4 hitting a record 53%.”
expectation_evidence: “The story this table tells: ... gross margin +450bp in FY25, another ~100bp in FY26”; Q4 gross margin estimate: “~52%.”

description: Transaction revenue showed better stabilization than the preview’s roughly 8% Q4 decline estimate: its year-over-year decline narrowed to 6.7% from 11% in Q3. Management also expects only a low-single-digit decline in FY2027, rather than the further steep decline the preview warned could make revenue negative.
fact_evidence: “Transaction revenue's year-over-year decline improved to 6.7% in Q4 from 11% in Q3, and management expects only a low-single-digit decline in fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: Q4 transaction revenue estimate was “~$6.7M” versus “$7.3M” a year earlier; the preview said “another double-digit decline means FY2027 revenue goes negative outright.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: AI/MCP sales showed commercial traction beyond the preview’s pipeline question: Q4 AI-related bookings were about $800,000, MCP deals were almost entirely upsells, and adding MCP/agentic AI access roughly doubled contract value on average. The preview had asked for closed AI business rather than another pipeline figure but gave no booking target.
fact_evidence: “AI-related bookings reached about $800,000 in Q4, representing 125% sequential growth”; “Adding MCP/agentic AI access roughly doubled contract value on average, MCP deals were almost entirely upsells to existing customers, and about three-quarters of MCP usage now comes from paid plans.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 is the first full quarter — look for closed ARR, not pipeline. Repeating the pipeline number without conversion is a tell”; the Q3 pipeline was “exceeding $1 million in opportunities.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: B2C ARR declined by about $380,000 over the year to roughly $6.3 million, rather than remaining flat around $6.4 million as the preview described it in the recent quarters. The hoped-for B2C stabilization or sequential turn was not evident in the reported full-year figure.
fact_evidence: “About $6.3 million in B2C ARR, which declined by roughly $380,000 for the year.”
expectation_evidence: “B2C ARR has been flat at $6.4M for two quarters after declines — first sequential increase would confirm the turn.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Platform deployment additions rebounded to 29 in Q4, compared with 15 in Q3, and average sales price rose 4.7%. That was better than the recent collapse in deployment additions that the preview had highlighted, though it had not set a Q4 deployment estimate.
fact_evidence: “The company added 105 net new platform deployments during the year (29 in Q4) to reach 1,276 total, while average sales price increased 4.7%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said net new deployments “collapsed from 47 in Q2 to 15 in Q3” and noted that Q4 was “the first quarter those fixes could show up.”

description: Management gave a positive FY2027 profitability and cash-flow outlook, saying both should grow, although it offered no top-line guidance. The directional commitment was more than the preview’s base case of silence, but it was not a numeric target or full growth algorithm.
fact_evidence: “Management guided to further EBITDA and cash flow growth in fiscal 2027 despite offering no top-line guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Silence is the base case; anything concrete is a genuine catalyst either way”; the preview looked for “even a directional ‘return to double-digit ARR growth’ or an EBITDA target.”

description: Fiscal 2026 revenue of $48.3 million was slightly above the preview’s $48.17 million full-year estimate, though the difference was very small.
fact_evidence: “Total fiscal 2026 revenue declined slightly to $48.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “The only published full-year figure is FY2026 revenue $48.17M / EPS $0.13.”

description: Cash ended the year at nearly $13 million, above the preview’s $12.1 million figure, and management said it was evaluating buybacks and other capital options. However, it did not announce a buyback authorization, so the concrete action flagged as a potential catalyst was not delivered.
fact_evidence: “The company holds nearly $13 million in cash with no debt after funding four quarters of Scite earn-out payments”; management said the stock was trading “far below fair value” and it was “evaluating buybacks and other capital options.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called a “buyback authorization” the “highest-ROI capital allocation available” and listed it as a catalyst; it also cited cash of “$12.1M, no debt.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Lovesac recognized about $20 million of tariff refunds through cost of merchandise sold, far more than the roughly $3.4 million already received and embedded in the preview’s gross-margin guide. That lifted reported gross margin to 68.4% and contributed $0.86 per share to EPS of $0.51, versus the preview’s expected EPS loss of roughly $0.36–$0.39.
fact_evidence: The company received approximately $21 million in IEPA tariff refunds, with $20 million recognized through cost of merchandise sold, contributing an $0.86 per diluted share benefit to reported Q2 EPS of $0.51. Gross margin rose to 68.4%, while gross margin excluding the refunds was approximately 56%.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “~$3.4–3.6M of IEEPA refunds are embedded in the guide” and cited expected Q2 EPS of “$(0.36) to $(0.39).”

description: Lovesac cut its FY27 outlook rather than reiterating the prior $700–740 million sales and $35–46 million Adjusted EBITDA ranges. The new sales range is $690–710 million and Adjusted EBITDA is $31.5–35.5 million, with net income now guided to $0.5–18.5 million.
fact_evidence: The company cut its full-year outlook to net sales of $690–710 million, net income of $0.5–18.5 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $31.5–35.5 million.
expectation_evidence: The preview called reiteration of “$700–740M / $35–46M EBITDA” the base case and warned that “any Q2 wobble compresses an already back-loaded year.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Omnichannel comparable sales fell 1.9%, a weaker result than the preview’s roughly flat whisper and worse than the prior quarter’s 1.0% decline. Headline revenue was near consensus, but comps showed weaker underlying demand than expected.
fact_evidence: Omnichannel comparable sales declined 1.9%.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the “whisper is roughly flat” for omnichannel comparable sales and noted Q1 FY27 comps of “−1.0%.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Major product launches are now expected to contribute meaningfully in Q4 rather than Q3, and Q3 is guided to a $9–12 million net loss. That pushes more of the planned second-half recovery into the final quarter than the preview’s late-summer launch timing suggested.
fact_evidence: Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $140–150 million and a net loss of $9–12 million, reflecting product launches shifted toward Q4; four major launches are planned for the second half, with meaningful revenue impact concentrated in Q4.
expectation_evidence: The preview said domestic Sactionals manufacturing was “Guided to start ‘late summer’ — inside this quarter” and described product and marketing efforts as starting to culminate toward year-end. It also said a quantified Q3 range would be constructive.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The under-$6,000 Sactionals segment remained pressured and had not returned to growth despite promotional and pricing changes. The preview specifically looked for opening-price campaigns to stabilize the low end, so that improvement did not materialize.
fact_evidence: Sactionals configurations over $6,000 grew double digits, while the under-$6,000 segment remained pressured and had not yet returned to growth despite promotional and pricing adjustments.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required opening-price campaigns to “stabilize the low end” and flagged whether high-end transaction strength would broaden.

description: Lovesac repurchased more stock in Q2 than the preview’s concern about a passive quarter implied: first-half repurchases reached $7.2 million, up from the $2.4 million deployed in Q1 alone. The remaining authorization fell to $46.9 million.
fact_evidence: The company repurchased approximately $7.2 million of stock in the first half, with $46.9 million remaining under authorization.
expectation_evidence: The preview noted “only $2.4M deployed in Q1” and said a passive quarter could read as a lack of conviction; it cited $51.7 million remaining after Q1.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comparable sales rose 2.7% (2.8% on a go-forward basis), above the preview’s implied +1.5% to +2% range. The preview’s bull case began at +2.5%, so the result was stronger than the central expectation and reached the bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Q2 comparable sales growth of 2.7% (2.8% on a go-forward basis).”
expectation_evidence: “Comparable sales (O+L+M): ~+1.5% to +2% implied by revenue consensus”; bull case: “+2.5% to +3.5%.”

description: Net sales of $4.9 billion topped the preview’s $4.77–$4.82 billion consensus range and even exceeded its base-case range. This was a modest but clear upside to the expected sales result.
fact_evidence: “Net sales up 1.1% to $4.9 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $4.82B” from Zacks and “$4.77–4.78B” from LSEG/Investing.com; base case “$4.80–4.85B.”

description: Adjusted EPS was $0.63, well above the preview’s $0.35–$0.37 consensus, but the reported result included a roughly $0.23 tariff-refund benefit. Excluding that benefit, EPS was about $0.40, still above the company’s guidance high end and up 14% year over year, but within the preview’s $0.39–$0.43 buy-side bogey.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.63 versus $0.35 a year ago, but included a roughly $0.23 net tariff refund benefit; excluding this, adjusted EPS rose 14% year-over-year and beat the high end of guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Street $0.35–$0.37 EPS”; the buy-side bogey was “~$0.39–$0.43.”

description: Reported gross margin reached 41.5%, well above the preview’s roughly 39.6%–39.7% bogey. But the underlying expansion was only about 10 basis points, so the large headline margin beat did not represent a similarly large improvement in underlying margin quality.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 41.5% of net sales versus 39.7% last year, but underlying gross margin (excluding tariff and fuel impacts) expanded only about 10 basis points.”
expectation_evidence: “Bogey is ~39.6–39.7%”; the preview also said to “strip [a tariff-refund] benefit out before crediting the beat” and highlighted “GM ≥39.6%, ex-tariff-refund.”

description: Macy’s raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $2.15–$2.35 and comparable-sales guidance to +1.0% to +1.5%. The EPS range’s high end was above the preview’s expected $2.15–$2.30 area, but second-half sales assumptions were unchanged, falling short of the preview’s call for an explicit second-half improvement.
fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised to adjusted diluted EPS of $2.15 to $2.35 and comparable sales of up 1.0% to 1.5%, with second-half sales assumptions unchanged from prior outlook.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY EPS of “$2.15–$2.30” in its base case and said “anything that doesn’t also raise 2H will read as a downgrade of the back half.”

description: The Q3 comp outlook of down 0.5% to up 0.5% was weaker than the preview’s warning threshold: it said a guide below roughly +1% would signal caution. The stated 3.2% prior-year comp makes the comparison tougher, but the guidance still landed below the preview’s expected level.
fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance implies a comp sales range of down 0.5% to up 0.5% … against a tougher prior-year comp of 3.2%.”
expectation_evidence: “Management has guided conservatively and beaten for five straight quarters, so a Q3 comp guide below ~+1% signals real caution.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The Macy’s nameplate grew comps only 1.1%, below the preview’s aspiration for the nameplate to turn “solidly positive” and well below the companywide comp result. Reimagined stores still outperformed the nameplate at 1.9%, but that spread did not widen from the Q1 spread implied by the preview’s figures.
fact_evidence: “The Macy’s nameplate grew comps 1.1%, with reimagined stores outperforming at 1.9%; these ~200 reimagined locations now represent nearly 60% of go-forward stores and 75% of go-forward store sales.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Macy’s nameplate comp turning solidly positive” and asked whether the Reimagine-200 spread was “widening.” Its Q1 figures were Macy’s +1.6% and Reimagine 200 +2.4%.

description: Bloomingdale’s reached its highest second-quarter sales volume in its 154-year history, a milestone the preview did not anticipate. Its 11.3% comp growth itself was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the business would remain double-digit.
fact_evidence: “Bloomingdale’s posted 11.3% comparable sales growth … achieving the highest second-quarter sales volume in its 154-year history.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Bloomingdale’s was “going for an eighth straight positive quarter” and expected it to “stay[] double-digit.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company received the full $116 million in tariff refunds, including $18 million after quarter-end, whereas the preview framed refunds as a possible one-time item and otherwise cited tariff and fuel costs as a drag. Macy’s said it would put most of the refund back into the business rather than send it to the bottom line.
fact_evidence: “The company received all $116 million of expected tariff refunds ($98 million in Q2 plus $18 million after quarter-end) and is flowing only ~$20 million (~$0.05 EPS) to the bottom line while reinvesting the rest.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Tariff + fuel drag: $0.10–$0.20 FY, $0.03–$0.04 in Q2” and listed “IEEPA tariff refunds” among the one-timers to watch.

description: First-half free cash flow was a $262 million inflow, and shareholder returns included $100 million of buybacks in the quarter—twice the $50 million buyback amount cited for Q1. This was stronger cash generation and a faster buyback pace than the preview’s stated Q1 baseline, although the preview had flagged capital returns as an item to watch.
fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was an inflow of $262 million in the first half versus an outflow of $88 million last year, and the company returned $201 million to shareholders (dividends plus $100 million buybacks) with ~$1 billion remaining on its buyback authorization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “buyback pace” and cited “$50M in Q1, $1.07B remaining.”

description: Vince reported adjusted EBITDA of $18 million, far above the preview’s roughly $7 million guidance-implied figure, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.02 versus the preview’s $0.11–$0.27 consensus range. A $10.4 million tariff refund was included in the results, while the preview said any quantified refund would be upside not in the estimates.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $18 million” and adjusted diluted EPS was “$1.02,” including “a $10.4 million tariff refund benefit.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave guidance-implied adjusted EBITDA of “~$7.0M” and said, “A quantified refund would be pure upside not in any model”; adjusted EPS consensus was “$0.11 to $0.27.”

description: Even with reported gross margin at 60.9%, the margin excluding the tariff refund fell 290 basis points, a much weaker underlying result than the preview’s expected tariff-related pressure suggested. The preview identified gross margin as a key debate and described roughly 50 basis points of adjusted operating-margin compression as expected.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose to 60.9% from 50.4%, but excluding the tariff refund benefit, gross margin actually declined 290 basis points due to higher product and freight input costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance implied “~50 bps of adjusted margin compression, driven by tariffs,” and described that as “expected, not a miss.”

description: Vince raised FY2026 guidance to 8%–10% net sales growth and a 9%–9.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, above the preview’s stale pre-raise guide of 7%–8% sales growth and 5.5%–6.0% adjusted EBITDA margin. The preview treated the forward guide as the main catalyst and its base case contemplated a reiterated guide.
