fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2026 Vince guidance to net sales growth of 8% to 10%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 9% to 9.5%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance of “+7–8%” sales growth and “5.5–6.0%” adjusted EBITDA margin, and said its base case was “FY guide reiterated ex-OVO.”

description: The OVO operating business came with a disclosed scale and growth target that the preview said had not yet been quantified: nearly $50 million of calendar 2025 net sales and a target of more than $100 million by FY2030, with low double-digit adjusted EBITDA margins. This provides concrete economics where the preview had only noted that the run-rate was undisclosed.
fact_evidence: OVO was “generating nearly $50 million in calendar 2025 net sales” and has a target of “$100 million-plus revenue by fiscal 2030 with low double-digit adjusted EBITDA margins.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called OVO deal economics “still undisclosed,” said its revenue and EBITDA run-rate were unknown, and noted that “any hard number here” would provide new information.

description: Wholesale sales grew 10.4% year over year, accelerating from the 5.9% growth cited for Q1 in the preview, rather than merely relying on continued DTC strength. That is evidence of the wholesale reacceleration the preview identified as an important condition for the bullish case.
fact_evidence: “Wholesale [was] up 10.4% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case needed “wholesale reacceleration” and identified fall/holiday wholesale order-book commentary as a leading indicator; it cited Q1 wholesale growth of “+5.9%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The balance sheet improved despite the preview’s concern that Vince would need to fund OVO and holiday inventory from a thin cash position: long-term debt was reduced to $12.3 million, and inventory was below its year-ago level. The preview had highlighted borrowings of $29.1 million and warned about funding strain.
fact_evidence: “Long-term debt [was] reduced to $12.3 million and net inventory [was] down to $73.4 million from $76.7 million a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 borrowings of “$29.1M” and warned Vince had to fund OVO and holiday inventory “off a thin cash position.”

description: CULP reported $54 million of sales, above the preview’s $53.2 million consensus and $52.8 million base estimate. That is a modest beat, especially given the quarter had one fewer selling week than the year-ago quarter.
fact_evidence: “Net sales rose to $54 million from $50.7 million year-over-year despite one fewer selling week.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$53.20M” and a base estimate of “$52.8M.”

description: Bedding sales reached $31.8 million, above the preview’s $30.8 million estimate. More notably, bedding gross margin rose to 13.6%, above the preview’s expectation that it would recover toward low double digits; management said the margin gain did not include allocated tariff recoveries.
fact_evidence: “Bedding segment sales grew 13.2% to $31.8 million with gross margin expanding to 13.6% from 10.5%, a gain management said was not aided by any allocated tariff recoveries.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated bedding sales of “$30.8M” and said bedding margin needed to “move toward low double digits.”

description: Gross profit excluding tariff recoveries was $8.4 million, or 15.6% of sales, versus the preview’s estimate of $7.4 million and 14.0%. The underlying margin and profit were therefore stronger than expected even without counting the one-time recovery.
fact_evidence: “Excluding tariff recoveries, gross profit was $8.4 million (15.6% of sales), up roughly 17% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross profit of “$7.4M (14.0%).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net debt was $3.1 million, below the preview’s roughly $5 million estimate, and management said it is targeting net cash by fiscal year-end. The company also used the full tariff recovery to pay off all higher-rate U.S. debt, a stronger balance-sheet outcome than the preview’s estimate implied.
fact_evidence: “The company reduced net debt approximately 70% to $3.1 million” and “used the full tariff recovery to pay off all higher-rate U.S. debt”; management is “targeting a net cash position by fiscal year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Net debt @ 8/2/26 ~$5M (from $10.8M).”

description: The call disclosed a CFO transition not flagged in the preview: Ken Bolling will retire effective September 14, with COO Mary Beth Hunsberger succeeding him and Bolling consulting through December. The disclosure is new, but the provided facts do not establish whether the change is good or bad for shareholders.
fact_evidence: “CFO Ken Bolling will retire and be succeeded by COO Mary Beth Hunsberger effective September 14, 2026, with Bolling staying on in a consulting capacity through December.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Management also highlighted substantial assets not discussed in the preview: approximately $95 million of U.S. federal NOL carryforwards associated with about $20 million of future tax benefits, and a Stokesdale hub estimated to be worth $40 million versus a $12 million book value. These are potentially valuable resources, though no monetization plan was reported.
fact_evidence: “The company holds approximately $95 million in U.S. federal net operating loss carryforwards (~$20 million in future tax benefits) and owns its Stokesdale, NC hub with an estimated $40 million market value versus $12 million book value.”

description: The preview called the first combined-company FY27 guide the decisive event and cited $604.6 million of revenue consensus. Instead, the reported guidance is for the six-month July–December transition period; the supplied call facts give no FY27 revenue or earnings guide.
fact_evidence: “The company is transitioning to a December fiscal year-end and guided the 6-month transition period (July-December 2026) to net sales of $287-291 million, adjusted EBITDA of $29-32 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.66-0.76.”
expectation_evidence: “First guide for the combined company. FY27 guidance, not the Q4 print, is the real event”; FY27 revenue consensus was “$604.60M.”

description: Legacy Q4 sales were above the preview’s guidance-implied standalone estimate: $96.6 million versus about $93 million. The reported 21.5% growth also exceeded the preview’s implied 17.0% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q4 legacy net sales grew 21.5% to $96.6 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Revenue | Q4 standalone (guidance-implied) | $93.0M (+17.0% YoY).”

description: Legacy Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin substantially exceeded the preview’s guidance-implied 15.9%: the reported margin was 19.3%, a 3.4 percentage-point gap.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 730 basis points to 19.3%, driven by premium X-Series mix and lower discounts.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated a “15.9% margin” for Q4 standalone.

description: Full-year company sales beat the published consensus estimate, reaching $348.9 million against $338.25 million. The preview cautioned that reported results would include the acquisition and would not be comparable to standalone guidance.
fact_evidence: “Total company fiscal 2026 net sales reached $348.9 million (up 22.8% YoY).”

description: Legacy full-year adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s cited $40 million standalone FY26 guidance, reaching $43.8 million. Legacy sales also finished slightly above the cited $312 million sales guidance.
fact_evidence: “Legacy fiscal 2026 net sales were $315.6 million … and legacy adjusted EBITDA rose 79.6% to $43.8 million, exceeding prior increased guidance.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the May 7 standalone FY26 guide was “$312M sales / $40M adj. EBITDA.”

description: The acquired segment brought in more six-week revenue than the preview’s roughly $31 million stub estimate, but its $1.8 million of adjusted EBITDA was below the preview’s estimated $3–5 million contribution. Management cautioned that the short period does not show the segment’s true earnings power.
fact_evidence: “The newly acquired Recreation and Sport Fishing segment added $33.3 million in revenue but only $1.8 million of adjusted EBITDA during its 6-week window, which management said does not reflect its true earnings power.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “+ MPX stub (47 days)” of “~$31M” revenue and “~$3–5M” adjusted EBITDA.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Both businesses’ dealer inventories were down substantially rather than showing a channel refill: legacy inventory fell about 30%, and Chaparral/Robalo inventory fell about 20%. Legacy turns were also better than pre-pandemic levels, easing the inventory and margin concern flagged in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Legacy field inventory ended the year down approximately 30% YoY with turns better than pre-pandemic levels, while Chaparral and Robalo inventory was down about 20%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Dealer inventory and retail registrations” as a key metric, asked whether there would be “any shift toward channel refill,” and identified an “inventory step-up hit to gross margin” as a bear risk.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Retail results were better than the weak industry and recent unit-volume backdrop implied: MasterCraft retail rose low-single digits and Robalo grew high-single digits while the broader powerboat industry declined mid- to high-single digits.
fact_evidence: “MasterCraft retail rose low-single digits and Robalo grew high-single digits, both outperforming a broader powerboat industry that declined mid- to high-single digits.”
expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “MCFT's own unit volumes are falling” and described the marine retail market as a risk to the outlook.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The post-acquisition balance sheet was stronger than the preview’s downside scenario allowed for: the company ended the year with cash, no debt, and full revolver availability, while also generating $22.3 million of free cash flow.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the year with $43.9 million in cash, no debt, full availability on its $75 million revolver, and generated $22.3 million in free cash flow after $8.1 million capex.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called the post-deal net cash/debt position a key disclosure and included “modest net debt” in its bear case; it also said the combined company’s cash generation profile was “unproven.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management put a concrete decline on near-term demand and responded by pausing Chaparral Surf Series production and moderating Chaparral/Robalo volumes. The preview warned of weak marine demand, but did not specify a 5%–10% decline or these production actions.
fact_evidence: “Management expects retail demand to decline approximately 5% to 10% over the next six months and has paused Chaparral Surf Series production while moderating Chaparral/Robalo volumes to align with retail.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “MCFT's own unit volumes are falling” and identified a challenged marine retail environment as a risk, but gave no quantified next-six-month decline or production pause.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The reported $10.1 million non-cash Crest brand impairment was a specific additional charge not identified in the preview’s discussion of purchase accounting. It contributed to the Q4 GAAP loss, alongside acquisition-related purchase accounting and transaction costs.
fact_evidence: “Q4 GAAP net loss of $7.0 million (-$0.35 per share) versus $5.5 million income ($0.33) a year prior, driven by a $10.1 million non-cash Crest brand impairment plus acquisition-related purchase accounting and transaction costs.”
expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated poor GAAP results from purchase accounting, but discussed inventory step-up, amortization of acquired intangibles, and goodwill—not a Crest brand impairment.

description: The preview expected a first quantified synergy target and timeline, but the supplied call facts report no quantified target or timeline. That leaves the deal’s synergy opportunity unquantified in the reported information.
fact_evidence: The supplied call facts contain no quantified synergy target or timeline.
expectation_evidence: The preview said “First hard number lands here” and that “continued qualitative language is a disappointment.”

description: SHOE reported Q2 net sales of $284.3 million, about 5% below the $299.19 million consensus in the preview and below the company’s own expectations. This was a materially weaker sales result than the preview’s roughly $298–300 million base case.
fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 net sales declined 7.2% to $284.3 million”; sales “falling short of the company's own expectations.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $299.19M”; base scenario “~$298–300M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Comparable sales fell 7.1%, far worse than the preview’s estimated decline of 2% to 3%. The comp result missed even the preview’s bear-case estimate of roughly down 6%.
fact_evidence: “Comparable store sales down 7.1%.”
expectation_evidence: “Comparable sales | ~−2% to −3% (my est.)”; bear scenario: “Comp ~−6%.”

description: Q2 gross margin contracted 690 basis points, worse than the preview’s already cautious expectation of a decline exceeding 500 basis points and worse than its bear-case estimate of about 650 basis points. Management attributed part of the merchandise-margin decline to the expired prior-year pricing benefit and the rest to promotions and inventory liquidation.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin fell 690 basis points to 31.9%”; roughly 390 basis points of the merchandise-margin decline came from “lapping a temporary prior-year pre-tariff pricing benefit” and about 240 basis points from “promotions and inventory liquidation.”
expectation_evidence: Q2 compression was forecast as “potentially exceeding 500 basis points”; bear scenario: “~32.3% (−650 bps).”

description: The company cut full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $0.75–$0.90 instead of reaffirming the prior $1.40–$1.60 range. The new range is roughly 40%–53% below the midpoint of the old range, a much steeper reset than the preview’s bear-case cut to about $1.10–$1.30.
fact_evidence: “Lowered full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to … adjusted EPS of $0.75-0.90.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1…) … Adjusted EPS $1.40–$1.60”; bear scenario anticipated a cut “to ~$1.10–$1.30.”

description: Full-year net sales guidance was also reduced to $1.1–$1.111 billion, below the prior $1.125–$1.147 billion range. The preview’s central expectation was that the existing full-year guidance would be reaffirmed, not cut.
fact_evidence: “Lowered full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.1-1.111 billion (down 2-3%).”
expectation_evidence: Prior guidance: “Net sales $1.125–$1.147B (−1% to +1%)”; the preview described reaffirmation of the FY26 guide as the central case.

description: The new full-year gross-margin outlook of 32.5%–32.7% is well below the preview’s approximately 34% expectation. The company now expects 390–410 basis points of compression rather than the previously guided 260 basis points.
fact_evidence: Full-year guidance includes “gross margin of 32.5-32.7% (390-410 bps of compression).”
expectation_evidence: Prior guidance: “Gross margin ~34% (−260 bps vs. FY25).”

description: The preview looked for the back-to-school reset to create a stronger second-half recovery, with its base case repeating management’s “down first half, up second half” framing. Instead, management expects roughly flat Q3 comps, says growth is deferred to Q4, and guides second-half comps to only down 1% to up 1% while assuming no improvement in promotions.
fact_evidence: “Management expects roughly flat comps in Q3 with growth deferred to Q4”; it “does not assume any improvement in the promotional environment for the second half” and guides second-half comps to “down 1% to up 1%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said BTS and fall were “the primary earnings opportunity”; its base case expected management to repeat “down first half, up second half.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Within the weak quarter, online comparable sales rose 18.8% while comparable store sales fell 9.5%. The preview did not anticipate this sharp divergence between the e-commerce and store channels.
fact_evidence: “Comparable online sales up 18.8% in Q2, even as comparable store sales fell 9.5%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management identified store traffic—not conversion—as the main problem: conversion had reached multi-year highs, and the response was to intensify advertising rather than rely on deeper discounting. That differs from the preview’s emphasis on promotional liquidation as a key part of the quarter’s margin and inventory story.
fact_evidence: “Store traffic was identified as the core problem while conversion improved to multi-year highs in both banners, prompting a shift toward intensified advertising rather than deeper discounting.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “first-half promotional liquidation runs to hit the inventory target” and highlighted promotional intensity as a key driver to watch.

description: The inventory-reduction objective was narrowed to the low end of the preview’s $50–$65 million year-end target, with management citing weaker sales. The quarter-end inventory itself was down year over year, but the intended reduction is now less ambitious than the top of the prior range.
fact_evidence: “Inventory ended down 5.0% to $426.6 million,” with a target of “approximately $50 million reduction by year-end” and the company “now aiming for the low end of that range due to weaker sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Inventory down $50–65M by year-end.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $671,000, well above the preview’s roughly $300,000 base-case model, even as the company expanded its commercial organization. This was a substantially stronger quarter than the modeled baseline.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA surged to approximately $671,000” and marked “the fifth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Adj. EBITDA at “~$0.3M” in the base case.

description: Oncology services margin reached 51%, above the preview’s approximately 48% model and its 48% threshold for confirming the in-housing benefit. Gross margin also expanded to 50%, while oncology revenue costs fell despite higher revenue.
fact_evidence: “Oncology services margin improving to 51% from 43%”; gross margin “expanded to 50% from 43%.” Cost of oncology revenue “fell roughly $500,000 to $7.5 million despite higher revenue,” primarily from bringing radiolabeling in-house.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the oncology services margin model was “~48%” and that “holding ≥48% would confirm the in-housing benefit is structural rather than a Q4 one-off.”

description: Data licensing brought in $893,000—more than the entire prior fiscal year’s licensing revenue—an unexpectedly strong contribution for the quarter, though management cautioned that it will remain lumpy.
fact_evidence: “Data licensing revenue reached $893,000 in the quarter—more than all of fiscal 2026 combined,” but management cautioned “it will remain lumpy.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 had shifted to “smaller licensing agreements” and described licensing as “violently lumpy”; it noted that any large one-time deal could inflate revenue.

description: Revenue of $15.2 million narrowly exceeded the $15.05 million consensus estimate. The beat was small, though revenue also rose about 10% sequentially from Q4, slightly more than the preview’s stated 9% sequential ask.
fact_evidence: Q1 revenue was “$15.2 million,” up from $14 million a year earlier.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus revenue of “$15.05M” and said consensus asked for “+9% sequential.”

description: Sales and marketing expense was $3 million, modestly above the preview’s $2.8 million Q4-run-rate assumption. Management attributed the increase to a deliberate expansion of the commercial organization, indicating somewhat higher spending than that model implied.
fact_evidence: “Sales and marketing expense rose to $3 million from $1.8 million a year earlier due to a deliberate expansion of the commercial organization.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said its estimates were “built off reported FY26 quarterly actuals and Q4 opex run-rate,” including “$2.8M S&M,” and described FY27 priorities as including “financial discipline” and “selective investment.”

description: Revenue of $87.1 million exceeded the preview’s $80 million base estimate, although it also came in well above the stale $62.6 million consensus cited there. The result was stronger than the preview’s already-strong quarter forecast.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached an all-time high of $87.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 base est.” revenue: “$80M”; consensus revenue: “$62.6M.”

description: Net income and EPS fell short of the preview’s own base estimates, despite beating the cited consensus EPS. Net income was $34.8 million and EPS $0.75 versus the preview’s estimates of about $43.5 million and $0.95.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $34.8 million (EPS $0.75).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “Net income … ~$43.5M” and “EPS (basic) … ~$0.95”; it also cited consensus EPS of “$0.58.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Tanker revenue realization was stronger than the preview’s rate assumptions: tanker TCE was near $71,500 per day, above the preview’s peer benchmarks around $51,900–$53,000 and its $45,000/day marker for strong MR realization.
fact_evidence: “Q2 daily fleet revenue exceeded $50,000” and “tanker TCE near $71,500/day.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited MR peer spot rates of “$51,900/day” and “$53,000/day,” and said “If MR spot prints above ~$45,000/day, IMPP captured the market.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Operational utilization was far below the preview’s watch threshold: it came in at 73.5%, versus the preview’s concern about utilization slipping below roughly 85%. Six drydockings caused off-hire, with seven more scheduled by year-end.
fact_evidence: “Operational utilization fell to 73.5% due to 6 drydockings,” with “7 more drydockings scheduled by year-end.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for utilization slipping below ~85%” and its bull case assumed “utilization >90%.”

description: Drydocking costs were substantially above the preview’s estimate, reaching $7.5 million versus its $1.5 million forecast. This was a much larger cost drag than the model allowed for.
fact_evidence: “Drydocking costs hit $7.5 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Drydocking … $1.5M.”

description: Voyage costs rose much more than the preview’s model allowed for: the preview budgeted $15 million of voyage expenses, while the call reported a $14.4 million increase, attributed to more spot days and higher Brent prices.
fact_evidence: “Voyage costs rose $14.4 million (58% more spot days plus Brent averaging $97 vs $67).”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Voyage expenses … $15.0M” and identified voyage-expense inflation as a possible bear-case factor.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Suezmax market rates ended Q2 well above the preview’s cited peer benchmark, exceeding $145,000 per day versus the preview’s $121,800/day Teekay reference, and at times surpassed $200,000 per day.
fact_evidence: “Suezmax daily rates surged to over $145,000 by end of Q2 2026” and “at times exceeded $200,000/day.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$121,800/day (Teekay, 60% of days through mid-May)” as the Q2 Suezmax benchmark.

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The company disclosed a profitable August sale of the Suez Enchanted that the preview had not anticipated. The sale generated a profit exceeding $32 million, though it occurred after Q2.
fact_evidence: “The company sold the 2007-built tanker Suez Enchanted in August for a profit exceeding $32 million.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Cash and time deposits were higher than the preview’s cited liquidity level, rising to $245.2 million at quarter-end and roughly $260 million afterward, while the company remained debt-free.
fact_evidence: “Cash and time deposits rose to $245.2 million as of June 30 and have since increased to roughly $260 million,” with the company “fully debt-free.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$212.6M liquidity and zero debt” and said “Fully self-funded is the base case.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: Some of the company’s dry bulk vessels remained stranded in the Strait of Hormuz since late May, a company-specific disruption not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the dry bulk fleet.
fact_evidence: “Some dry bulk vessels remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz since late May.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described the dry bulk market as “~flat” and said IMPP’s “drybulk half … was flat.”

description: FEIM reported $23.5 million of Q1 revenue, far above the preview’s $17.85 million consensus and above the preview’s $19.5–21.0 million bull-case range. The preview said record quarters were expected in later quarters, making an all-time record in Q1 an additional upside surprise.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue hit an all-time record of $23.5 million, up 70% year-over-year and 52% sequentially.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $17.85M”; “The record-revenue language is a fiscal-year statement, not a Q1 commitment”; bull scenario: “Revenue $19.5–21.0M.”

description: Reported gross margin reached 45.8%, exceeding the preview’s 40% recovery benchmark and its 42% bull-case threshold. That is a stronger recovery than the preview’s base case of 37–41%.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 9 percentage points to 45.8%.”
expectation_evidence: “Watch for ≥40% reported”; base scenario: “reported GM 37–41%”; bull scenario: “reported GM ≥42%.”

description: Quarterly EPS was $0.41 versus the preview’s $0.15 consensus, a substantial beat even though the preview cautioned that EPS was a less reliable measure than revenue, margin, and backlog. Operating income and margin also showed strong profitability, rather than an earnings result dependent only on a possible tax benefit.
fact_evidence: “Net income surged to approximately $4.2 million ($0.41 per share)”; “operating margin reached 22% (operating income of $5.2 million versus $364,000 a year ago).”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $0.15”; the preview said to “Anchor on revenue, gross margin, and backlog instead” because EPS could include part of the anticipated tax benefit.

description: Management reaffirmed the FY2029 targets as expected, but went further by suggesting the $150 million revenue goal could be reached sooner and be substantially larger. That upside ambition was not part of the preview’s stated expectation.
fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed its fiscal 2029 targets of $150 million+ in annual revenue, 50% minimum gross margin, and 30% minimum operating margin, while suggesting the revenue target could be reached sooner and be substantially larger.”
expectation_evidence: “FY29 targets ($150M / 50% GM / 30% OM) — reaffirmed, refined, or quietly softened.”

description: Management described unusually strong near-term conversion visibility: about 65% of funded backlog is expected to become revenue within 12 months, with unfunded backlog visibility multiple times the funded amount. The preview focused on whether awards would convert and warned about timing slippage, but did not anticipate this degree of stated conversion visibility.
fact_evidence: “Approximately 65% of the $129 million funded backlog is expected to convert to revenue within the next 12 months, with additional unfunded backlog visibility described as multiple times the funded portion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required awards to have “entered production, not just booking,” while the bear case could involve “slower” backlog conversion and programs spanning “one to three years.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: For a secured communications production contract already involving more than 1,000 systems, customers are asking for monthly production to rise by over 50% and have promised follow-on orders. This is an additional demand and production-acceleration signal beyond the preview’s general concern about getting new programs into production.
fact_evidence: “A secured communications production contract for over 1,000 systems is seeing customer requests to increase monthly production by more than 50% alongside promised follow-on orders.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required a “high-rate production” transition to show up in units shipped; it did not mention these production increase requests or follow-on orders.

description: TEN reported Q2 EPS of $4.40, far above the $2.48 consensus and also above the preview’s $3.60 base case. The result was close to the preview’s $4.50 bull case, but substantially stronger than the central expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q2 net income jumped to $139.3 million from $26.8 million (EPS of $4.40 vs $0.67).”
expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) $2.48”; the scenario analysis gave “Base ... EPS ~$3.60” and “Bull ... EPS ~ $4.50.”

description: Profit-sharing contributed $30.5 million in Q2 and $71 million in H1, and management expects a significant further increase in H2. The preview highlighted profit-sharing as a potential earnings driver and sought a Q2 figure, but gave no expectation for this level or for a further H2 increase.
fact_evidence: “Profit-sharing arrangements contributed $71 million in H1 2026 versus $10 million a year earlier ... with Q2 alone contributing $30.5 million, and management expects a significant further increase in the second half.”

description: Management signaled that a dividend increase would be announced after the November strategy meeting, contrary to the preview’s expectation of no change to the capital-return cadence. The $1.60 paid in calendar 2026 also exceeded the preview’s stated $1.50 aggregate.
fact_evidence: “The company paid dividends totaling $1.60 per share in calendar 2026 ($0.60 plus $1.00) ... with management signaling a dividend increase to be announced after the November strategy meeting.”
expectation_evidence: “2026 aggregate is $1.50”; “expect no new declaration” and “no change to capital return cadence.”

description: Management is considering redeeming the $120 million Series E preferred shares, which could add $0.30–$0.40 per share to the bottom line. The preview did not flag this potential earnings benefit.
fact_evidence: “Management is considering redeeming the $120 million Series E perpetual preferred at a 9.25% coupon, which could add $0.30-$0.40 per share to the bottom line.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: TEN’s 26-vessel newbuilding program was reported to have appreciated at least 30%, to an estimated $3.8–$3.9 billion value versus roughly $3.1 billion in cost. The preview discussed the program mainly as a funding and capex concern, without anticipating this reported increase in its value.
fact_evidence: “The 26-vessel, roughly $3.1 billion newbuilding program has already appreciated at least 30% (estimated ~$3.8-3.9 billion in value).”
expectation_evidence: “Watch capex schedule vs. cash generation — this is the bear's argument for why free cash doesn't reach shareholders.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The reported TCE rate of $43,503 per day was below the preview’s $46,000–$52,000 watch range and its $47,500 base-case estimate, though it was above the roughly $39,700 consensus-implied figure. That makes the rate result weaker than the preview’s central operating assumptions but better than the implied consensus bar.
fact_evidence: “The fleet's time charter equivalent rate rose 41% to $43,503 per day from $30,754.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to look for “$46,000–$52,000” and modeled a base case of “TCE/day ~$47,500”; it also cited “implied ~$39,700.”

description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $170.4 million, below the preview’s $192 million base case, although above its $168 million bear case. This was a weaker operating-profit result than the preview’s central scenario despite the much higher reported EPS.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased ... 81% to $170.4 million in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 scenario table estimated “Base ... Adj. EBITDA ~$192M” and “Bear ... Adj. EBITDA ~$168M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: TEN reported net debt to capitalization of about 44.5% and cash of $466 million, ahead of the preview’s monitored 48.4% leverage threshold and its cited Q1 cash balance of $321.4 million. The balance sheet was therefore stronger than the preview’s stated hurdle and starting-point figures suggested.
fact_evidence: “The pro forma 81-vessel fleet has a fair market value of approximately $4.9 billion against $2 billion of debt, with net debt to capitalization around 44.5% and cash of $466 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to look for “Net debt/cap below 48.4%” and cited Q1 “cash $321.4M.”

description: The preview expected Copart to give a non-answer about its reported CCC bid, but the call announced an agreed acquisition of ACV Auctions instead. Copart said the all-cash tender offer would be funded from cash on hand, with no financing conditions, and is expected to close by year-end.
fact_evidence: Copart announced that it had agreed to acquire ACV Auctions. The transaction is an all-cash tender offer funded from cash on hand with no financing conditions, and the company expects to close by the end of the calendar year.
expectation_evidence: “Expect the question; expect a non-answer” on CCC Intelligent Solutions; a premium CCC deal “likely runs $5–6B+, exceeding the $4.2B cash pile and putting debt on a historically debt-free company.”

description: The preview framed M&A discipline as a key issue, with the bull case expecting Adair to be walk-away-ready on CCC. Instead, Adair said the ACV deal does not preclude future acquisitions, signaling continued openness to further deals.
fact_evidence: Adair stated that the ACV deal does not preclude future acquisitions.
expectation_evidence: The preview said the call would test “how Adair frames M&A discipline” and described the bull case as CCC being “framed as disciplined/walk-away-ready.”

description: Q4 revenue was $21.2 million, about 3% above the preview’s $20.6 million estimate; full-year revenue of $71.7 million also slightly exceeded the $71.16 million estimate. The beat was modest, though, rather than the $22 million-plus revenue bull-case outcome.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue set a company record at $21.2 million”; full-year fiscal 2026 revenue was “$71.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 Consensus” revenue: “~$20.6M”; full-year revenue consensus: “$71.16M.”

description: Q4 gross margin reached 39.4%, above the preview’s roughly 37% expectation and even the 38% bull-case threshold. Management attributed the improvement to higher-margin mix and resolved yield and throughput problems, rather than price increases or one-time items.
fact_evidence: Gross margin “reached 39.4% in Q4,” driven by “higher-margin product mix and resolved yield/throughput problems rather than price increases or one-time items.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 gross margin at “~37%,” said “Anything ≥37% validates the ramp,” and set “GM ≥38%” in its bull case.

description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $2.1 million, above the preview’s $1.4–$1.8 million estimate, and its 10% revenue margin reached the top of the preview’s bull-case range. This marked a fourth consecutive profitable quarter.
fact_evidence: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was “$2.1 million (10% of revenue),” the “fourth straight profitable quarter.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 adjusted EBITDA at “~$1.4–1.8M” and described expansion “toward 8–10%” as the proof point.

description: LightPath disclosed that it had already raised $50 million in a June primary offering, leaving it with $93.2 million in cash and effectively no debt. The preview flagged the possibility of another raise, but did not anticipate that a substantial offering had already occurred; it strengthens funding capacity while also representing equity issuance.
fact_evidence: LightPath ended fiscal 2026 with “$93.2 million in cash and effectively no debt after a June primary offering raised $50 million,” to fund capacity expansion, working capital, and potential acquisitions.
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$55.2M cash at March 31” and said to watch for “any language pointing toward another raise.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Management said the Army delayed the NGSRI interceptor program by a few months. The preview emphasized the need for confirmation that the Lockheed Martin work was on schedule, so the delay is a negative development, although management characterized it as low-risk.
fact_evidence: “The NGSRI interceptor program was delayed a few months by the Army but management views it as low-risk.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said investors wanted “confirmation the LM seeker-head work is funded and on schedule.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported that camera systems are designed into or being evaluated on seven missile/seeker platforms, including three with Lockheed Martin. The preview sought reassurance on the Lockheed Martin opportunity but did not anticipate this broader platform count.
fact_evidence: “Its camera systems are now designed into or evaluated on seven missile/seeker platforms (three with Lockheed Martin).”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Detector lead times have lengthened from six months to more than ten, prompting LightPath to build inventory ahead of demand. This creates a supply and working-capital burden that the preview did not specifically flag.
fact_evidence: “Detector lead times have stretched from six to over ten months, prompting inventory buildup ahead of demand.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Net new ARR fell about 36–37% year over year. The preview expected the freemium strategy and deferred Creative Cloud pricing actions to weigh on individual-subscriber ARR, but did not indicate a decline of this size.
fact_evidence: “Net new ARR declined approximately 36-37% year-over-year,” attributed to “the intentional freemium funnel strategy prioritizing user acquisition over near-term monetization and deferred Creative Cloud pricing actions.”
expectation_evidence: Management had chosen to “accelerate freemium MAU growth and defer previously planned Creative Cloud ‘line optimizations’”; the strategy “lowers our second-half ARR growth expectations from individual subscribers.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: RPO growth slowed to 8%, its first single-digit growth since early fiscal 2023, with cRPO growth at 9%. The preview highlighted RPO and cRPO as the key forward-demand read, but did not set a specific Q3 growth expectation.
fact_evidence: “RPO growth decelerated to 8% (its first single-digit growth since early fiscal 2023) and cRPO grew 9%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview called RPO/cRPO “the cleanest forward-demand read for the enterprise” and “the hardest number to dress up,” without specifying a Q3 growth bar.

description: Q3 revenue and non-GAAP EPS both beat the preview’s consensus and Adobe’s guidance: revenue was $6.76 billion versus consensus of $6.69–$6.70 billion and guidance topping out at $6.72 billion; non-GAAP EPS was $6.13 versus consensus of $6.08–$6.09 and guidance topping out at $6.10.
fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.76 billion” and “non-GAAP EPS of $6.13.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus revenue of “$6.69–6.70B” and non-GAAP EPS of “$6.08–6.09,” with Q3 guidance of “$6.67B – $6.72B” revenue and “$6.05 – $6.10” non-GAAP EPS.

description: Both subscription segments came in just above the top of their previewed ranges: BP&C revenue was $1.91 billion versus a $1.89 billion high end, and C&MP was $4.65 billion versus a $4.64 billion high end. Their reported growth rates were otherwise close to the preview’s expected growth.
fact_evidence: BP&C subscription revenue was “$1.91 billion (up 15% CC)” and C&MP subscription revenue was “$4.65 billion (up 12% CC).”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave BP&C subscription revenue guidance of “$1.87B – $1.89B” and C&MP of “$4.61B – $4.64B,” with growth expectations of approximately 15% and 12%, respectively.

description: Adobe raised its full-year revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance, with the revenue midpoint rising by about $50 million and the EPS range moving up from $24.35–$24.45 to $24.45–$24.50. The increase was modest and did not reach the preview’s bull-case thresholds.
fact_evidence: Adobe raised FY2026 revenue guidance to “$26.576-$26.626 billion” and non-GAAP EPS to “$24.45-$24.50,” a “roughly $50 million midpoint raise.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited the existing FY26 guide as “$26.5–2.6B” revenue and “$24.35–24.45” non-GAAP EPS; its bull case called for revenue raised to “≥$26.7B and EPS ≥$24.60.”

description: Oracle reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.92, well above the preview consensus of $1.74. The roughly 10% beat was substantially larger than the preview’s expectation of a modest, largely de-risked quarter.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS rose 30% to $1.92.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $1.74”; the preview also said “the quarter itself is largely de-risked.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Oracle delivered 850 megawatts of AI capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs since Q4 end—nearly three times the entire Q4 delivery—while utilization remained near 98%. The preview framed OCI as a capacity-delivery risk, but this scale of delivery showed capacity coming online rapidly without utilization falling.
fact_evidence: “Oracle delivered 850 megawatts of AI capacity with over 300,000 GPUs since Q4 end—nearly 3x the entire Q4 delivery and 73% of all capacity delivered last fiscal year—while GPU utilization remained at 97.9%.”
expectation_evidence: “This is a capacity-delivery question, not a demand question”; the preview said a shortfall would mean “data centers landed late” and cited Q4 GPU utilization of 97.5%.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Oracle’s operating cash flow and free cash flow were better than the preview’s expected Q1 cash burn: free cash flow was negative $5 billion rather than the forecast negative $8–12 billion, despite $28 billion of CapEx. The record $23 billion of operating cash flow helped narrow the shortfall.
fact_evidence: “Q1 CapEx was $28 billion, producing negative free cash flow of $5 billion, though cash flow from operations hit a record $23 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “Expect Q1 FCF around negative $8–12B.”

description: Oracle raised its full-year EPS outlook to $8.10 from the previously reaffirmed $8.05. The revenue target remained around $90 billion, so the change was a modest upward revision rather than a broad reset of the annual plan.
fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance to at least $90 billion in total revenue (up 34%) and $8.10 in non-GAAP EPS.”
expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY27 … $90B revenue (+34%) and $8.05 non-GAAP EPS … both reaffirmed in June.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Oracle said it closed more than $30 billion in additional AI contracts without requiring additional capital from the company. That was favorable against the preview’s focus on who would fund the backlog and its concern about financing and capital needs.
fact_evidence: “The company closed more than $30 billion in additional AI contracts in Q1 without requiring additional capital from Oracle, using financing models like prepayments and bring-your-own-hardware arrangements.”
expectation_evidence: “The stock is not trading on the P&L. It is trading on RPO direction, capex, and who is funding the backlog”; the preview also identified new financing as a bear trigger.

description: Revenue was slightly above consensus, with 30% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s implied 28%. The beat was positive but relatively small compared with the EPS beat.
fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue reached a record $19.3 billion, up 30% year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus | $19.13B”; the preview gave implied growth of “+28%.”

description: Non-GAAP operating margin was 42%, below the preview’s 43–44% consensus estimate, although it held roughly flat despite gross-margin pressure from the data-center ramp. This missed the stated margin estimate but was more resilient than a step-down would imply.
fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income [was] up 31% to $8.2 billion and operating margin holding roughly flat at 42% despite declining gross margins from data center ramp-up.”
expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin | ~43–44% | guided to ‘step down’ on DC ramp.”

description: Q1 revenue grew sequentially for the first time in a Q1, breaking Oracle’s historical pattern of a lighter quarter after a record Q4. The preview did not quantify a sequential-growth expectation, but this result ran counter to the seasonal pattern described on the call.
fact_evidence: “[Revenue] grew sequentially for the first time in a Q1, breaking the historical pattern of a lighter Q1 following a record Q4.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: GPUs reaching renewal in Q1, most of them at least four years old, were renewed or resold at a 20% premium to prior contracts. The preview did not anticipate evidence that older hardware could retain or increase its contract value.
fact_evidence: “GPUs that came up for renewal in Q1, the majority being 4 years or older, were renewed or resold at a 20% premium to prior contracts.”

description: IBEX’s FY2027 revenue guide of $700–715 million came in above the preview’s modeled base range of $680–695 million, and its $90–94 million adjusted EBITDA guide was slightly above the modeled $88–92 million range. The guidance still implies slower revenue growth than FY2026, but it was stronger than the preview’s central expectation.
fact_evidence: “FY2027 guidance projects revenue of $700-715 million (9-11% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $90-94 million (9-14% growth).”
expectation_evidence: “Base: ... FY27 guided $680–695M / $88–92M”; the preview also modeled an initial guide of “$680–700M” revenue and “$88–93M” adj. EBITDA.

description: Q4 revenue of $164.3 million exceeded the preview’s $158–160 million consensus range and even the $162.2 million high end of the guide-implied range. Its 12% growth also topped the preview’s expected Q4 growth of roughly 8–10%.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue grew 12% to a record $164.3 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$158–160M”; guidance implied “Q4 revenue $158.2–162.2M (+7.6% to +10.3%).”

description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was slightly below the preview’s ~$20.8 million estimate, and the 12.3% margin was below its roughly 13.0% expectation. The reported pressures were new-client training, nearshore-to-offshore transfers, and higher fuel prices; the preview had specifically sought an explanation other than AI-related pricing concessions.
fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA slipped to $20.2 million (12.3% margin) from $20.5 million (13.9%) a year earlier, pressured by new client training costs, nearshore-to-offshore work transfers, and higher fuel prices.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$20.8M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~13.0%”; the preview said management needed to attribute any shortfall to “investment ... rather than price.”

description: The Sierra partnership update went beyond general enthusiasm, providing deployment activity across five verticals and quantified proof-of-concept resolution rates and CSAT scores, including a named BJ’s Wholesale example. However, the update did not provide the revenue or pipeline figures the preview wanted to establish monetization.
fact_evidence: “The Sierra AI partnership drove double-digit client AI agent deployments across five verticals, with proof-of-concept resolution rates of 20%+ (Philippine Airlines) to 40%+ (BJ's Wholesale) and CSAT scores above 4.7 out of 5.0.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management needed “named logos beyond Philippine Airlines, AI/digital revenue disclosure, or a quantified pipeline,” and warned that “Qualitative enthusiasm ... will be read as an absence of evidence.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Customer expansion showed additional strength: IBEX added nine trophy logos in Q4, while revenue from its top 10 clients grew 22%, above the 19% top-10 growth noted in the preview for Q3. The preview had flagged client retention and large-client expansion as important measures.
fact_evidence: “The company added nine new trophy logos in Q4 (17 for the full year), with revenue from its top five, top 10, and top 25 clients growing 24%, 22%, and 15% respectively.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “top-10 concentration 54% with largest client at only 9%” and said the top-10 cohort had grown “+19% in Q3.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Net cash rose to $30.9 million, well above the approximately $14 million the preview cited, with record full-year free cash flow of $31.2 million. FY2026 capex of $27.8 million, by contrast, was within the preview’s expected $25–30 million range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow reached a record $31.2 million and net cash improved to $30.9 million (from $13.7 million a year earlier), while capex rose to $27.8 million (4.3% of revenue) from $18.4 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “net cash ~$14.0M” and said FY2026 capex “was raised to $25–30M.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: Q4’s 10% tax rate reflected discrete benefits, while management indicated a normalized 20–22% rate going forward. The lower rate benefited the reported quarter, but the normalization implies a future tax headwind that the preview had not flagged.
fact_evidence: “Q4's tax rate fell to 10% from 19% due to discrete benefits, but management guided to a normalized 20-22% tax rate going forward, implying a future earnings headwind.”

description: FY2026 revenue finished modestly above the preview’s approximately $640 million guide-midpoint expectation and above the company’s $638–642 million guidance range. The gap was small compared with the larger Q4 beat.
fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 revenue rose 15.4% to $644.1 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “FY2026 full year (implied at guide midpoint): revenue ~$640M (+14.6%)” and cited company guidance of “$638–642M.”

description: Q2 revenue was $155.2 million, slightly above the top of the $154.0–$155.0 million pre-announced range and above the $154.43 million consensus. The beat was narrow, but it exceeded the range investors had been told to expect.
fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew 24.1% year-over-year to $155.2 million” and came in “above the high end of IPO estimates.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue” was pre-announced at “$154.0M – $155.0M”; consensus was “$154.43M.”

description: Profitability also came in above the pre-announced upper bounds: adjusted EBITDA was $25.4 million versus a $25.30 million high end, and net income was $12.4 million versus a $12.00 million high end. Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 16.4%, modestly above the preview’s roughly 16.2% calculation.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 54% to $25.4 million with margin expanding to 16.4%,” while “net income nearly doubled to $12.4 million from $6.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview gave adjusted EBITDA of “$24.92M – $25.30M,” net income of “$11.73M – $12.00M,” and calculated adjusted EBITDA margin of “~16.2%.”

description: The FY2026 revenue guide is a little above consensus: even its $602 million low end exceeds the $601.33 million estimate. The range implies H2 revenue modestly above the preview’s $334.5 million estimate, though it still points to a sharp slowdown from H1 growth.
fact_evidence: Full-year 2026 guidance calls for “net revenue of $602-606 million (18.6%-19.5% growth).”
expectation_evidence: FY2026 revenue consensus was “$601.33M”; the preview calculated implied H2 revenue of “$334.5M” and H2 growth of “+13.0%.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The company disclosed a meaningful decline in DTC revenue per customer despite growing its active-customer base. Newly acquired customers were lower-spending, which diluted DTC net revenue per customer by 1.4%.
fact_evidence: “LTM active customers grew ~23% to 1.2 million, but DTC net revenue per customer declined 1.4% to $417 due to the dilutive mix of lower-spending newly acquired customers.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified Active Customer adds as an open KPI and listed “strong Active Customer adds” as a bullish signal; it did not flag falling revenue per customer.

description: International growth was notably strong, including rapid customer growth in France, a market the preview had identified as an area where the company might disclose more but did not forecast. International revenue reached about one-fifth of the total.
fact_evidence: “International revenue grew 36.8% to $31.2 million (about 20% of total),” and new customer growth in France accelerated to “over 180% year-over-year in the first half of 2026.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “international contribution” among the metrics that were open for disclosure, without giving an expectation for its growth.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Wholesale revenue grew far faster than total revenue, driven by existing partners’ higher order volumes. That adds a channel-mix shift not quantified in the preview and partly offset the quarter’s gross-margin expansion.
fact_evidence: “Wholesale and other net revenue jumped 48.7% to $19.9 million,” driven mainly by “higher order volumes from existing partners”; faster wholesale growth partially offset gross-margin expansion.
expectation_evidence: The preview listed channel mix as an open KPI, but gave no wholesale growth expectation.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: Reformation laid out a rapid store-expansion plan: from 70 stores at quarter-end, it expects to reach 79–80 by year-end and aims to double the fleet over five years. The preview flagged store cadence as an open question but had no specific expansion target.
fact_evidence: The company had “70 stores at quarter-end (17 opened over the prior 12 months)” and plans to reach “79-80 stores by year-end,” targeting “a doubling of the fleet over the next five years.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “store-opening cadence and new-store productivity” as open questions, without a store-count target.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management provided concrete evidence that store openings can lift local demand, citing a sharp acceleration in Chicago customer growth and faster DTC revenue growth after openings. The preview had identified new-store productivity as unknown but did not anticipate this quantified market-halo example.
fact_evidence: In Chicago, new-customer growth accelerated “from 28% to 50% year-over-year” and DTC revenue growth rose “nearly 1.5x after openings.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “new-store productivity” as an open question and noted that the company might disclose it, but gave no expected halo effect.

description: The company disclosed that it borrowed ahead of its IPO to fund a large dividend, then used most of the IPO proceeds to repay debt. The dividend represents a shareholder cash distribution, while the repayment reduced leverage, making the newly disclosed financing history a mixed development.
fact_evidence: Ahead of the IPO, Reformation raised “$92 million in term loans to fund ~$90 million ($1.63/share) in dividends,” then used “~$110 million of $132.2 million net IPO proceeds to repay debt,” cutting net leverage to “~0.9x.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the IPO proceeds split was unconfirmed and noted Q1 cash of about $41.2 million, but did not describe the dividend-funded borrowing or subsequent debt repayment.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Identical sales excluding fuel grew only 0.2%, well below the preview’s +1.0%–1.3% expectation, and Kroger cut its full-year range to +0.2%–0.8%. The preview expected a narrower +1.0%–1.5% range, so both the quarter and the revised outlook were weaker than anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Identical sales without fuel grew just 0.2%”; Kroger “lowered its full-year identical sales without fuel guidance to 0.2%-0.8%, down sharply from its initial 1%-2% range.”
expectation_evidence: “ID sales ex-fuel | ~+1.0–1.3% (buy-side)”; the preview also said the sell-side expected management to “narrow[] FY26 ID sales to +1.0–1.5%.”

description: Despite the sales shortfall, Kroger held its full-year adjusted FIFO operating-profit and adjusted EPS ranges unchanged. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation of an EPS trim to $5.00–$5.20.
fact_evidence: “The company maintained full-year guidance for adjusted FIFO operating profit of $5.0-$5.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $5.10-$5.30 despite the lower sales outlook.”
expectation_evidence: “The sell-side consensus expectation is that management narrows FY26 ID sales to +1.0–1.5% and trims adjusted EPS to $5.00–$5.20.”

description: Adjusted EPS of $1.09 exceeded the preview’s $1.05–$1.06 consensus range, a roughly 3%–4% beat.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $1.09, representing 5% growth versus last year.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.05–$1.06.”

description: FIFO gross margin excluding fuel rose 13 basis points, better than the preview’s flat-to-down-20-basis-point expectation. The preview identified this as the most important metric and said flat-to-positive would be the best outcome.
fact_evidence: “FIFO gross margin rate excluding fuel rose 13 basis points year-over-year.”
expectation_evidence: “FIFO gross margin rate | Flat to –20 bps”; the preview called “Flat-to-positive” the “single best bull outcome.”

description: OG&A rate rose 33 basis points, worse than the preview’s expected 10–20-basis-point increase. Wage investments and healthcare costs added pressure, with sales deleverage also contributing.
fact_evidence: “OG&A rate increased 33 basis points due to wage investments, higher healthcare costs and sales deleverage.”
expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “OG&A +10–20 bps”; the preview flagged further OG&A deleverage as a key risk.

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The Cyclospora outbreak hit late in the quarter and is expected to keep weighing on Q3 sales. The preview discussed sales and pharmacy pressures but did not anticipate this specific outbreak or its carryover into the next quarter.
fact_evidence: “The Cyclospora outbreak hit late in the quarter after most competitors had closed their quarters, and lingering impacts are expected to weigh on Q3 sales.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Adjusted e-commerce sales grew 20%, above the preview’s expected 17%–19%, and Kroger reported a second consecutive quarter of profitable e-commerce growth.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted e-commerce sales grew 20%” and delivered “a second consecutive quarter of profitable e-commerce growth.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted eCommerce growth | ~+17–19%.”

description: Retail media grew 24%, its best growth since 2021. The preview highlighted digital economics as a key profit offset but gave no current-quarter retail-media growth expectation.
fact_evidence: “Retail media grew 24% (best since 2021).”

description: Kroger said the Inflation Reduction Act pharmacy headwind is projected to rise to approximately 150 basis points in Q4 as new high-cost drugs, including GLP-1s, enter the formulary in January, while stating there is no profit impact. The preview mentioned pharmacy reimbursement headwinds generally but did not flag this specific timing or scale.
fact_evidence: “The Inflation Reduction Act pharmacy headwind is projected to accelerate to approximately 150 basis points in Q4 as new high-cost drugs including GLP-1s enter the formulary in January, with no profit impact.”
expectation_evidence: The preview listed “pharmacy reimbursement headwinds” as a secondary issue to watch.

description: Q2 revenue was $15.8M, down 13% year over year, rather than the preview’s $20.9M base estimate or $21.53M consensus, both of which implied growth. Cash rewards rose 77% and were deducted from revenue, while Q2 total transaction value was flat.
fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue fell 13% year-over-year to $15.8 million”; “Cash rewards…rose 77% year-over-year to $5.1 million…masking underlying growth as total transaction value held flat at $20.9 million.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA remained loss-making at $1.6M, versus the preview’s expectation of a $0.9M profit. Even on a constant-FX basis, the company reported a $0.9M EBITDA loss, not a positive quarter.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed…to $1.6 million in Q2”; “constant-FX EBITDA loss narrowed 64% to $0.9 million in the quarter.”
expectation_evidence: “My base…Adj. EBITDA +$0.9M”; the preview said a positive quarter “should” print and described a second positive quarter as the expectation.

description: Hong Kong revenue was flat at $7.8M rather than the preview’s $10.0M estimate and expected 28% growth. That falls well short of the preview’s view of Hong Kong as the growth engine.
fact_evidence: “Hong Kong revenue held flat at $7.8 million” in Q2.
expectation_evidence: “Hong Kong…Q2'26E $10.0M…YoY +28%”; “Deceleration below ~+20% kills the base case.”

description: Singapore revenue fell 20% to $6.2M instead of reaching the preview’s $8.7M estimate and 12% growth forecast. The preview also identified a possible reacceleration as a bull-case driver, but the quarter instead declined.
fact_evidence: “Singapore revenue fell 20% to $6.2 million on cash-reward deployment.”
expectation_evidence: “Singapore…Q2'26E $8.7M…YoY +12%”; bull case: “SG re-accelerates toward Q4'25's +56%.”

description: Despite flat Hong Kong revenue, its segment profit rose to $0.5M from $0.1M a year earlier, an improvement not forecast in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Hong Kong…segment profit rising to $0.5 million from $0.1 million a year earlier.”

description: Singapore delivered a first-half segment profit of $0.2M, turning around from a $0.5M loss a year earlier. The preview focused on Singapore revenue growth and possible reacceleration, not a first-half segment-profit turnaround.
fact_evidence: “Singapore…delivered a first-half segment profit of $0.2 million, a turnaround from a $0.5 million loss a year earlier.”

description: Rent the Runway reported Q2 revenue of $97.7 million, above both the preview’s $91–95 million guidance range and its $94.5 million estimate. The beat was larger than the preview’s base case and even exceeded its $96–98 million bull-case range.
fact_evidence: “Record Q2 revenue of $97.7 million… exceeding the guidance range communicated in June.”
expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 guidance: $91–95M”; “My estimate: $94.5M.”

description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 12.9%, far above the preview’s expected 5–8% guidance range and 6.5% estimate. The result substantially outperformed expectations for a modest improvement over last year’s 4.4% margin.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $12.6 million (12.9% of revenue) in Q2, a sharp improvement from $3.6 million (4.4%) a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: 5–8% of revenue”; “My estimate: $6.1M (6.5%).”

description: Gross margin rose to 36.1%, sharply reversing the margin pressure the preview expected. The preview modeled 27.5% and warned that revenue-share costs could keep margins near 27% or below.
fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanded roughly 609 basis points to 36.1%, driven by lower fulfillment costs (down 370 bps) and reduced rental product depreciation and revenue share costs (down 240 bps).”
expectation_evidence: “Gross margin… My estimate: 27.5%”; “Watch whether the mix effect is stabilizing (27%+) or still deteriorating (sub-26%).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Ending active subscribers fell to 140,826, down 3.8% year over year, rather than reaching the preview’s 158,000 estimate or even its roughly 152,000 bear-case threshold. The decline was attributed to higher pauses and less promotional acquisition.
fact_evidence: “Ending active subscribers fell 3.8% year-over-year to 140,826, hurt by higher pause activity and reduced promotional acquisition compared to 2025.”
expectation_evidence: “Ending active subscribers… My estimate: 158,000 (+7.9%).”; “Anything below ~152K ending actives (+4% YoY) confirms the bear case.”

description: The company guided to a negative Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin of 3% to 6%, a sharp reversal from Q2’s 12.9% margin and weaker than the preview’s expected positive 4–7% FY2026 margin range. Management cited seasonal pauses and higher revenue-share inventory costs.
fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA is guided to negative 3% to negative 6% of revenue due to seasonal pause activity and higher revenue-share inventory costs.”
expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance… adjusted EBITDA margin 4–7%.”

description: Rent the Runway raised its FY2026 rental product investment guidance to $53–55 million, above the preview’s expected $45–50 million. The higher planned spend contrasts with the preview’s expectation that investment would remain reduced amid cash-flow concerns.
fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year rental product investment guidance to $53–55 million (up from $45–50 million) to ensure fuller stocking for second-half events and launches, though still below fiscal 2025’s $75 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Rental product acquired $45–50M (vs. $74.9M in FY2025).”; “rental product acquired is guided down ~$25M YoY.”

description: The company announced a $15 million backstopped rights offering and a new $10 million term loan. The preview discussed financing as a possible risk if cash burn continued, but did not anticipate this specific capital raise; it adds liquidity while bringing additional financing and potential dilution considerations.
fact_evidence: “Management announced a $15 million backstopped rights offering plus a new $10 million term loan from the same investor group that led the 2025 refinancing to bolster liquidity.”

description: Paige Thomas was named permanent CEO effective September 14, resolving the leadership uncertainty highlighted in the preview. The preview identified a permanent appointment as a live catalyst but had no disclosed search timeline.
fact_evidence: “The company appointed Paige Thomas, formerly Chief Commercial Officer and ex-CEO of Saks OFF 5TH, as permanent CEO effective September 14, with interim CEO Teri Bariquit becoming Nonexecutive Chair.”
expectation_evidence: “Permanent CEO search / strategic direction”; “No search timeline has been disclosed.”

description: Rent the Runway paused Marketplace, on-site advertising and monetization, and new B2B dry-cleaning partnerships, rather than advancing the diversification initiatives the preview highlighted as areas to watch. Management is instead concentrating resources on core rental and resale execution.
fact_evidence: “Rent the Runway paused several initiatives including Marketplace, on-site advertising/monetization, and new B2B dry cleaning partnerships to refocus resources on core rental and resale execution.”
expectation_evidence: “Also watch… the new diversification lines (RTR Marketplace, B2B dry-cleaning pilot, advertising).”

description: Q1 revenue was $31 million, above the preview’s $30.3 million bogey as well as the $29.6 million consensus estimate. The beat was positive but not as large as the preview’s $31.5 million bull case.
fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 60% year-over-year to $31 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. $29.6M … My bogey: $30.3M”; the bull case listed “$31.5M.”

description: Kestra raised its long-term gross-margin target from 70% to the mid-70% range, with 70% now expected for FY2029. The preview discussed the 70% margin bridge but did not anticipate a higher target.
fact_evidence: “Management raised its long-term gross margin target to the mid-70% range within the next 2-3 years, up from the prior 70% goal, expecting to deliver 70% for full-year fiscal 2029.”
expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “the 70%-GM long-term bridge” and cited the prior “~700bps of gross margin expansion” guidance.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: A significant national payer expanded coverage to non-ischemic patients on guideline-directed medical therapy, a newly reported access development not anticipated in the preview. The preview noted that this group represents over 60% of the typical WCD population.
fact_evidence: “A significant national payer expanded coverage to non-ischemic patients on guideline-directed medical therapy for the first time,” and “over 60% of the typical WCD population is non-ischemic.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Kestra estimated its WCD market share at about 15%, above the preview’s estimate of about 12%. That suggests a larger share position than the preview assumed.
fact_evidence: “Kestra estimates about 15% U.S. market share.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described KMTS as “at ~12% share.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Reported total liquidity was roughly $320 million, below the preview’s estimate of about $357 million. The call cited $245 million in cash and investments and the $200 million term loan.
fact_evidence: “The company holds $245 million in cash and investments as of July 31 and roughly $320 million in total liquidity, bolstered by a new $200 million nondilutive term loan announced in July.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 closed with “$262.2M cash & investments plus a newly-secured $200M term loan (~$357M total liquidity).”

description: The preview expected no announced refinancing solution as the base case and identified a Personal Care sale as the likely asset-sale upside.
