fact_evidence: “SG&A rose to 54% of net revenues from 51.2%, driven mainly by higher variable compensation, pressuring the operating margin despite the top-line gains.”
expectation_evidence: The preview modeled SG&A at “36.5 (50.3%)” of revenue.

description: Net income from continuing operations was $3.3 million, or $0.11 per diluted share, versus the preview’s roughly breakeven non-GAAP EPS expectation. The earnings basis is not directly comparable to the preview’s non-GAAP estimate, but the reported per-share result was materially positive against that expectation.
fact_evidence: “Net income from continuing operations improved by $3.8 million to $3.3 million ($0.11 per diluted share), versus a loss of $0.5 million (negative $0.02 per share) a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base model forecast non-GAAP EPS of “~$0.00” and said the buy-side whisper was “a roughly breakeven non-GAAP quarter”; it also cautioned that published EPS consensus had an “Ambiguous basis.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Inventory ended at $69.3 million, below the preview’s expected $72–78 million range. The decline was partly aided by a $5.3 million Project Restoration inventory reserve, so the reported reduction was not solely a result of inventory sell-through or purchasing.
fact_evidence: “Inventory ended the quarter down 28.4% year-over-year to $69.3 million, aided by a $5.3 million Project Restoration inventory reserve.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated inventory at “~72–78” and described an inventory number above “~$80M” as a warning sign.

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: Liquidity was stronger than the preview’s expected $12–18 million of cash: the company ended with $34.2 million, no debt, and generated $23 million of operating cash flow. The preview had expected zero ABL borrowing, but not this level of cash.
fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $34.2 million in cash (double the prior year's $15.2 million) and no debt, generating $23 million of operating cash flow.”
expectation_evidence: The preview projected “~12–18” in cash and “0” ABL drawn.

description: Management disclosed that it discontinued its third-party sales-rep agency and is rebuilding an in-house wholesale sales team. The preview anticipated wholesale growth and watched for partner expansion, but did not flag this change to the sales-team structure.
fact_evidence: “The company discontinued its third-party sales rep agency to rebuild an in-house wholesale sales team.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Management reported positive Google Search growth for “Vera Bradley” for the first time in over a decade, an encouraging brand-interest signal not anticipated in the preview.
fact_evidence: The company “reported positive Google Search growth for 'Vera Bradley' for the first time in over a decade.”

description: The preview centered on a FY2027 revenue outlook around $6.5–7.5 million, but management gave no official FY2027 revenue guidance. It cited only $2.3 million of booked government-contract revenue, another $2 million under discussion, and commercial NRE agreements still being negotiated, leaving the expected revenue outlook unconfirmed.
fact_evidence: “Management declined to provide official fiscal 2027 revenue guidance,” citing “only $2.3 million in currently booked government contract revenue with a potential additional $2 million under discussion”; the commercial NRE agreements “could add revenue in fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “Consensus is $6.74M”; the base scenario expected “$6.5–7.5M,” and the preview said FY2027 guidance was “the entire event.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview expected roughly $36 million of cash at the FY2026 exit, but the company ended Q4 with $56 million. The stronger balance sheet came partly from $20.1 million of ATM proceeds and the sale of 830,484 shares, meaning the cash improvement also involved more dilution than the preview had anticipated.
fact_evidence: The company closed Q4 with “$56 million in cash and no debt, up from $15.7 million at June 30, 2025,” aided by “$20.1 million in net ATM proceeds from selling 830,484 shares.”
expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$37.8M cash at March 31” and a base case of “cash ~$36M”; it flagged the live ATM and said to watch whether the company used it.

description: FY2026 losses were worse than the preview’s rough estimate implied: the preview’s $5.1 million nine-month net loss plus its estimated $2.9 million Q4 loss pointed to about $8 million for the year, versus the reported $9.2 million. The reported headcount increase to more than double its year-earlier level helps explain the greater expense burden, despite the preview already expecting spending to rise.
fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $9.2 million” from $3 million; adjusted EBITDA was “negative $5.2 million” versus positive $186,000, with the loss driven primarily by “increased headcount and operating expenses.” Headcount rose from 14 to over 30, with recruiting to continue.
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 net loss at “~-$2.9M” and reported nine-month FY2026 net loss of “$5.1M”; it also said management intended to increase spending.

description: The company disclosed a sizable FY2027 equipment outlay that the preview had not quantified: $10–12 million for two MOCVD reactors. Management described most of it as a one-time cost while maintaining a capital-light model, but it is still a substantial planned investment.
fact_evidence: Aeluma expects “capital expenditures of approximately $10 to $12 million in fiscal 2027,” largely a one-time cost for “two AIXTRON G10 MOCVD reactors,” while “maintaining a capital-light model.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any capex commitment attached” to manufacturing scale-up, but gave no expected amount.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Beyond the preview’s general focus on a possible commercial customer milestone, management disclosed negotiations for multimillion-dollar NRE agreements with marquee customers, almost entirely in AI DataCom. These remain negotiations rather than signed agreements or production orders, so they offer a potential revenue path without yet resolving the revenue-visibility concern.
fact_evidence: Aeluma is “negotiating several multimillion-dollar commercial NRE agreements with marquee customers,” “almost entirely focused on the AI DataCom market,” that “could add revenue in fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview identified a “first customer qualification” and a “first production purchase order” as potential milestones, and described AI-datacom photodiodes as the near-term commercial wedge.

description: Q4 revenue was $26.7 million, about 25% above the preview’s $21.3–$21.8 million consensus range. The preview’s bull case included $24–$27 million, but the result still substantially exceeded the stated consensus expectation.
fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached $26.7 million,” up 33% year-over-year and 43% sequentially.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $21.3M – $21.8M”; the preview also described $24–27M as its bull-case range.

description: The preview looked for cash flow to turn positive in H2 calendar 2026, but management said upcoming investment payments for the second Malaysian factory may delay reaching cash-flow-positive status. The call did not give a revised date, so the extent of any delay is unclear.
fact_evidence: “Upcoming capacity investment payments may delay reaching cash-flow-positive status.”
expectation_evidence: “‘Cash flow positive in H2 calendar 2026’ — reaffirm or walk back.”

description: Management raised the possibility of a significant IKE Tech joint-venture liquidity event during FY2027, beyond regulatory authorization. The preview discussed IKE Tech mainly as an age-gating/FDA-pathway option and did not anticipate a potential liquidity event on that timeline.
fact_evidence: “A potential significant liquidity event involving its IKE Tech joint venture during fiscal 2027, separate from any regulatory authorization.”
expectation_evidence: “IKE Tech age-gating / FDA pathway … Option value, not near-term revenue.”

description: Full-year operating expenses excluding credit losses fell 37% to $24.2 million, showing a substantially leaner cost structure. The preview focused on the operating-cost composition but did not flag a reduction of this size as an expectation.
fact_evidence: “Operating expenses excluding credit loss dropped 37% year-over-year to $24.2 million for the full year.”
expectation_evidence: “Composition of the ~$15.2M implied operating cost line.”

description: Although the preview expected the legacy receivables cleanup to remain unfinished and anticipated a large Q4 provision, management gave a new FY2027 timeframe for substantial resolution of the legacy write-offs. That provides a clearer endpoint than the preview had indicated.
fact_evidence: “Credit losses remained elevated at $9.2 million in Q4 and $20.7 million for the full year, with management expecting legacy receivable write-offs to be substantially resolved during fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: “A fourth consecutive large Q4 provision … means the AR cleanup is not finished.”

description: Q4 revenue was expected around $425.6–429.9 million, near the high end of guidance, but came in at a record $462 million—roughly 7–9% above those estimates.
fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue rose 94% year-over-year to a record $462 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 revenue… Consensus $425.6M (Zacks) / $429.9M (TradingView).”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected Q4 bookings of about $700 million, with $650–800 million as the base case; actual bookings were a record $1.5 billion, more than double the cited expectation, at a 3.3x book-to-bill ratio.
fact_evidence: “Q4 bookings hit a record $1.5 billion, up 375% year-over-year and 73% sequentially, producing a record book-to-bill ratio of 3.3x.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 bookings vs. ~$700M / book-to-bill vs. 1.5x”; the base case expected “bookings $650–800M.”

description: The preview’s FY2027 revenue consensus was $2.09 billion, while FPS guided to $2.4–2.6 billion, with a $2.5 billion midpoint—about 20% above consensus. More than 90% of the guidance is already covered by backlog, adding visibility the preview did not anticipate.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $2.4-$2.6 billion (76% growth at midpoint)… with over 90% of revenue guidance already covered by backlog.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue… Consensus $2.09B (+50%).”

description: The preview expected FY2027 adjusted EPS of $1.17 and warned that normalization could put margins below consensus. FPS instead guided to $1.26–1.40 per share; the midpoint is about 14% above consensus, while midpoint adjusted EBITDA and revenue imply an approximately 24% EBITDA margin, within the preview’s cited 24–25% consensus range.
fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for… adjusted EBITDA of $575-$625 million (86% growth), and adjusted EPS of $1.26-$1.40 (95% growth).”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS… Consensus $1.17 (+73%)”; the preview said consensus embedded an adjusted EBITDA margin of “roughly 24–25%” and its base case contemplated a “23–24%” guide.

description: The preview anticipated FY2026 revenue of $1.39 billion at the high end of guidance; reported revenue was $1.42 billion, above both that estimate and the stated guidance range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 revenue grew 89% to $1.42 billion.”
expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue… Company Guidance… $1,350–1,390M”; consensus was “$1.39B.”

description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was about $5 million above the preview’s implied $108 million estimate, although the 24.4% margin was slightly below the roughly 25% expectation. The margin still expanded 200 basis points sequentially, as anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA jumped 163% to $113 million with margins expanding 200 basis points sequentially to 24.4%.”
expectation_evidence: “Q4 adj. EBITDA… ~$108M (implied)”; the preview also expected a Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin of “≈25% (+200bps QoQ).”

description: The preview had no verified Powertrain Solutions revenue breakout and said to treat a circulating estimate of about $100 million as unverified. FPS reported $147 million in Q4 revenue for the segment, which had grown to 25% of full-year revenue and roughly 40% of backlog.
fact_evidence: “Powertrain Solutions revenue grew 187% year-over-year to $147 million in Q4, rising from 13% to 25% of full-year revenue and now comprising roughly 40% of backlog.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the segment breakout was not disclosed in the prior filing and, regarding circulating estimates, “Treat as unverified.”

description: The preview anticipated FY2027 capex of 1–1.5% of revenue, but FPS said capex would be roughly 3% of sales—about twice the upper end of that expected range.
fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures are expected to fall from 8% to roughly 3% of sales.”
expectation_evidence: “Management guided FY27 capex to 1–1.5% of revenue.”

description: The preview described FY2027 as a likely first year of material free cash flow and expected capex of only about $25–30 million, but the call added a concrete operating-cash-flow target of more than $300 million for FY2027. The preview had not specified an operating-cash-flow estimate.
fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow rose 2.5x to $109 million in fiscal 2026 and is guided to exceed $300 million in fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY27 should be the first year of material FCF” but gave no operating-cash-flow estimate.

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The preview discussed the existing expansion as supporting up to $5 billion of annual revenue, but did not anticipate the additional Tijuana facility. The new 385,000-square-foot site is expected to raise Powertrain Solutions capacity by more than 50% and total capacity to about $5.8 billion when it opens.
fact_evidence: “A new 385,000 square foot Powertrain Solutions facility in Tijuana will increase that segment's capacity by more than 50% and lift total revenue capacity to approximately $5.8 billion when it comes online in Q4 fiscal 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the existing “$205M expansion” was “meaningfully complete” and that capacity supported “up to $5B of annual revenue”; it did not mention the new Tijuana facility.

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: The preview broadly characterized FPS as an AI infrastructure supplier but did not anticipate a direct order from a Frontier AI lab or a new hyperscaler MSA. The lab’s first campus is expected to exceed 1 gigawatt, with a broader opportunity measured in multiple gigawatts.
fact_evidence: “The company received its first direct order from a Frontier AI lab and signed an MSA with a hyperscaler, with the Frontier lab's first campus expected to exceed 1 gigawatt and broader opportunity measured in multiple gigawatts.”

description: The preview did not provide a data-center revenue or customer-growth estimate. FPS reported 161% data-center revenue growth, roughly four times estimated market growth, driven mainly by a 121% increase in average revenue per customer rather than by customer additions.
fact_evidence: “Data center revenue grew 161% year-over-year (roughly 4x estimated market growth), driven mainly by a 121% increase in average revenue per customer rather than customer additions.”

description: The preview did not quantify FY2026 adjusted EBITDA expectations, but the call reported that the full-year result exceeded the high end of guidance raised in May.
fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026… adjusted EBITDA increased 91% to $323 million, exceeding the high end of guidance raised in May.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The preview expected backlog to remain above roughly $2.0 billion and identified a sequential decline as a potential bear trigger. Instead, year-end backlog reached a record $3 billion, up 256% year-over-year and more than twice FY2026 revenue.
fact_evidence: “Backlog reached a record $3 billion at year-end, up 256% year-over-year and now representing more than 2x fiscal 2026 revenue, versus roughly 1x a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “Backlog needs to hold above ~$2.0B; a sequential backlog decline would be the bear trigger.”

description: The preview put Q3 EPS consensus at $1.28–$1.30 and derived roughly $1.45–$1.50 from company guidance. Lennar reported $1.19 GAAP, or $1.23 excluding one-time items, below both benchmarks.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 EPS came in at $1.19 GAAP ($1.23 excluding one-time items)”
expectation_evidence: “EPS: $1.28 – $1.30”; “Guidance math → ~$1.45–1.50 in EPS.”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: The preview expected mortgage rates around 6.77% and flagged a 40–50bp rise as an affordability headwind. Rates were reported at approximately 7%, and management said nearly half of visitors could not immediately qualify, indicating more acute affordability pressure than the preview quantified.
fact_evidence: “The 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to approximately 7% from 6.4%-6.5% at the prior call”; “nearly 50% of visitors cannot immediately qualify.”
expectation_evidence: “30-year mortgage rates have since risen to ~6.77%”; “Rates up ~40–50bps since the June guide are a real incentive headwind.”

description: Gross margin improved sequentially and came in above the preview’s 15.3–15.5% implied-consensus range, but at 15.8% it still missed the roughly 16% company guide. The result was better than the preview’s implied Street expectation but short of the stated guide.
fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved sequentially to 15.8% (from 15.6%) but missed the roughly 16% guidance.”
expectation_evidence: “Homebuilding GM: ~16.0% (guide)”; “Backing into consensus implies roughly 15.3–15.5% gross margin.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Q3 new orders were 20,879, just below the 21,000–22,000 guided range and down from 23,000 a year earlier. The preview identified orders and sales pace as a key debate, with roughly 21,000 homes as the expectation.
fact_evidence: “New orders of 20,879 fell just below the guided range of 21,000-22,000 and declined from 23,000 a year earlier.”
expectation_evidence: “New orders & August/September sales pace”; “Q3 FY26 consensus” deliveries/order context of “~21,000.”

description: For Q4, Lennar guided to 19,500–20,500 new orders, below its Q3 result of 20,879. The preview highlighted rising rates and order pace as risks, but did not anticipate a specific Q4 order range.
fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for 19,500-20,500 new orders.”
expectation_evidence: “New orders & August/September sales pace”; “Rates up ~40–50bps since the June guide are a real incentive headwind.”

description: SG&A was 9.2%, above the preview’s expected 8.8–9.0% range. Lower divisional headcount and higher deliveries per corporate associate did not prevent the reported cost ratio from exceeding that range.
fact_evidence: “SG&A rose to 9.2%, above the 8.8%-9% expected range.”

dimension_name: Customer relationships, pricing, and business mix
description: Management said the entire gross-margin gap came from land costs, up about 6% per homesite, and that Lennar is deliberately giving up margin to maintain volume while monetizing legacy high-cost land. This clarifies that the margin shortfall reflects an intentional volume-versus-margin choice, rather than the recovery continuing as the preview’s central bull case hoped.
fact_evidence: “Management attributes the entire margin gap to land cost, which is up about 6% per home site, as it deliberately sacrifices margin to maintain volume and monetize legacy high-cost land.”
expectation_evidence: “The strategic question is whether management defends volume (incentives up, margin down) or margin (starts down, volume down). In Q2 they chose margin”; “Everything in the bull case depends on [gross-margin recovery] continuing.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Construction costs and cycle time improved beyond the preview’s already strong reference points: cost per square foot was about $80 versus $81, and cycle time was 116 days versus 121 days. These results indicate better operating efficiency than the preview baseline.
fact_evidence: “Construction cost per square foot fell to roughly $80, down 6% year-over-year and 14% since Q4 2023, while cycle time hit a record-low 116 days versus 126 a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “$81/sq ft construction cost (−7% YoY),” and “record 121-day cycle time.”

description: The company reported a Q4 multifamily loss of about $25 million, whereas the preview’s guidance bridge used a positive multifamily contribution of about $15 million. That is a meaningful negative change in the segment contribution assumed in the preview.
fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for ... a multifamily loss of ~$25 million.”
expectation_evidence: “Add ... Multifamily ~$15M” in the preview’s guidance math.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Lennar reported divisional headcount down about 12% year over year and deliveries per corporate associate up 12%. The preview emphasized operating efficiency but did not anticipate these specific workforce-productivity gains.
fact_evidence: “Divisional headcount is down ~12% year-over-year and deliveries per corporate associate are up 12%.”

description: The company repurchased 3 million shares for $256 million, below the preview’s cited Q2 pace of 5 million shares for $447 million, even as it paid dividends and redeemed $400 million of senior notes. Ending cash was $1.2 billion and debt-to-capital was 16.6%, versus the preview’s Q2 reference of $1.8 billion and 15.8%.
fact_evidence: “Repurchasing 3 million shares for $256 million, paying $119 million in dividends, and redeeming $400 million of senior notes, ending with $1.2 billion cash and 16.6% debt-to-capital.”
expectation_evidence: “Continued repurchases at this multiple”; Q2 reference: “Buyback 5M shares / $447M” and “Cash / debt-to-cap $1.8B / 15.8%.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview said trackers showed about 2.17 million SOL and treated holdings above 2.3 million as a bull-case outcome. Upexi reported 2.34 million tokens at June 30, confirming a larger treasury than the trackers suggested.
fact_evidence: “As of June 30, 2026, the company held approximately 2.34 million Solana tokens.”
expectation_evidence: “Trackers show holdings essentially flat at ~2.17M”; the bull scenario cited “Token count >2.3M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The preview estimated stockholders’ equity could be around negative $90 million at June 30. Reported equity was negative $53.8 million, substantially less negative than that estimate.
fact_evidence: “Total stockholders' equity swung to negative $53.8 million at June 30, 2026.”
expectation_evidence: “Stockholders' equity was −$51.9M at 3/31/26 and is likely near −$90M at 6/30/26.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview expected a June debt-for-equity swap that would add shares or warrants. Instead, Upexi reported retiring nearly $20 million of debt for about $10 million and recording a $10.3 million extinguishment gain.
fact_evidence: “The company extinguished roughly $20 million in debt in June (retiring nearly $20 million principal for about $10 million) and recorded a $10.3 million gain on debt extinguishment.”
expectation_evidence: “The June debt-for-equity swap being framed as accretive — it was priced at $1.60 ... but it added ~12.2M shares/warrants against $19.5M of debt.”

description: The preview looked for confirmation that cash expenses and interest were already below staking revenue from July 1. Management instead said it expects staking revenue to cover ongoing cash expenses going forward, without the supplied facts confirming that break-even had already been reached.
fact_evidence: Management “expects staking revenue to fully cover ongoing cash expenses going forward.”
expectation_evidence: Management had committed that “by July 1, 2026, ongoing cash expenses for operations and interest will be less than the treasury's staking revenue”; a clean confirmation was described as “the most valuable thing management can say.”

description: The preview anticipated a buyback could be a meaningful source of accretion and flagged that no new dilutive raise was signaled in its bear case. Upexi bought back $2.8 million of shares but then issued $2.5 million of ATM shares, largely offsetting the repurchase in dollar terms.
fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 2.9 million shares at an average of $0.96 (totaling $2.8 million) under its $50 million buyback program, but subsequently issued 2.5 million ATM shares for $2.5 million in gross proceeds.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q4 repurchases at sub-$1 prices “are highly accretive to SOL/share” and asked why they “were not larger”; its bear scenario included a “new dilutive raise signaled.”

description: Despite the preview’s expectation of sharply reduced operating costs from outsourcing and a much smaller workforce, full-year G&A more than doubled and stock-based compensation increased sharply. These expense increases were not anticipated in the preview’s description of modest operating costs.
fact_evidence: “Stock-based compensation ballooned to $21.9 million from $2.4 million the prior year, while G&A expenses rose to $26.4 million from $11.9 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview expected “modest opex” in its Q4 loss estimate and highlighted that “Headcount is down to 10, warehouse leases expired, brands fulfillment outsourced.”

description: Q1 sales were $923 million, about $20 million below the $943.3 million consensus and below the company’s $928 million guide low. The call attributed the shortfall to softer-than-anticipated North America Contract and Global Retail revenue.
fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales fell 3.4% year-over-year to $923 million, driven by softer-than-anticipated revenue in North America Contract and Global Retail.”
expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $943.3M”; “Company Guide (6/24/26) | $928–968M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Consolidated orders rose, but at $914 million they fell short of the preview’s more than $950 million inflection threshold and remained below shipments. The preview’s base case anticipated this level of growth, but its key bullish test—orders exceeding shipments to stop backlog erosion—was not met.
fact_evidence: “Consolidated orders rose 3.2% (3.5% organic) to $914 million, though backlog declined 3.1% to $669 million.”
expectation_evidence: “>$950M = inflection confirmed”; “Orders must exceed ~$948M of shipments to stop backlog erosion.” The base case also forecast “$910–930M, +3–5% org.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: North America Contract orders were still down 1.7%, while the preview highlighted a +5% HNI workplace-orders comparison and warned that a negative MLKN result against it would be concerning. The decline was much smaller than the prior-year comparison, but it did not deliver the positive order inflection the preview was watching for.
fact_evidence: “North America Contract sales dropped 5.3% to $506 million and orders fell 1.7% to $484 million, partly due to $55-60 million of orders pulled forward into Q4 FY25 from tariff-driven buying.”
expectation_evidence: “HNI reported workplace orders +5%”; “if MLKN is negative against that, it’s a share-loss story, not a cycle story.”

description: Adjusted EPS was a clear beat even after removing the tariff-refund benefit: the $0.42 underlying result exceeded both the $0.35 consensus and the top of the $0.33–$0.39 guidance range. The reported $0.53 included an $0.11 benefit from IEPA tariff refunds.
fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.53, but excluding a $0.11 net benefit from IEPA tariff refunds, adjusted EPS of $0.42 still beat the company’s guidance range.”
expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $0.35”; “Company Guide (6/24/26) | $0.33–0.39.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: International Contract orders jumped 17.3%, substantially stronger than the preview’s expectation of possible stabilization. The increase was helped by a South Korea project win, so the reported surge included a specific project contribution.
fact_evidence: “International Contract orders surged 17.3% year-over-year to $181 million (boosted by a South Korea project win).”
expectation_evidence: “International Contract … Lowest-expectations segment — stabilization is free upside.”

description: International Contract’s adjusted operating margin fell to 4.6%, down 390 basis points, rather than showing the stabilization the preview identified as potential upside. The decline was sharper than the preview’s cited FY26 margin deterioration of 250 basis points.
fact_evidence: “Segment adjusted operating margin fell 390 basis points to 4.6% on lower sales and showroom investments.”
expectation_evidence: “International Contract … $167.5M, 8.5% margin”; “FY26 … margin –250bps”; “stabilization is free upside.”

description: Global Retail’s adjusted margin reached 7.0%, well above the preview’s roughly 2.5% level that would “read well.” However, 410 basis points of the 580-basis-point year-over-year margin increase came from tariff refunds, so the underlying improvement was much smaller than the headline increase.
fact_evidence: “Global Retail … adjusted operating margin up 580 basis points to 7.0%, though 410 basis points came from tariff refunds.”
expectation_evidence: “Global Retail operating margin … anything above ~2.5% reads well.”

description: Management cut FY27 sales guidance to $3.88–$4.03 billion, below the preview’s expected reaffirmed range of $3.93–$4.13 billion. The adjusted EPS range was maintained, so the reduction was to the sales outlook rather than the EPS range.
fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year FY27 sales guidance to $3.88-$4.03 billion (3% growth at midpoint) while maintaining adjusted EPS guidance of $1.85-$2.15.”
expectation_evidence: “FY27 guide reaffirm | $3.93–4.13B / $1.85–2.15”; “Any narrowing to the low half … is the bear trigger.”

description: Management said new U.S.-Canada tariff actions are expected to reduce full-year EPS by about $0.07, a specific additional headwind not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of tariff costs and planned pricing. The company is responding with inventory pre-buys and dual sourcing.
fact_evidence: “New U.S.-Canada tariff actions are expected to create an approximate $0.07 per share unfavorable full-year impact, prompting inventory pre-buys and dual-sourcing mitigation efforts.”
expectation_evidence: “Realization on the planned ~4.5% price increase vs. net tariff cost.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Order momentum strengthened after quarter-end: the first three weeks of September were up 9% year over year across all three segments. That provides a more positive forward order signal than the Q1 orders result alone suggested.
fact_evidence: “Order momentum accelerated post-quarter, with the first three weeks of September up 9% year-over-year across all three segments.”
expectation_evidence: “The entire FY27 EPS bridge depends on an order inflection that has to start showing up this quarter.”

description: Q4 net revenue was $16.1 million, well above the preview’s approximately $12.3 million consensus and $11.8–12.4 million base case. That is a substantial top-line beat.
fact_evidence: “Total Q4 net revenue was $16.1 million (up 6% YoY).”
expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | Q4 FY2026E | ~$12.3M”; the base case was “Revenue roughly in line” at “$11.8–12.4M.”

description: EXXUA generated $3.9 million in Q4, above even the preview’s bull-case range of $3.0–3.5 million and well above its base expectation of roughly $2.3–2.7 million. Revenue also rose 63% sequentially, despite the preview’s warning that channel stocking could fade.
fact_evidence: “EXXUA generated $3.9 million in net revenue in Q4 FY2026, up 63% from $2.4 million in Q3.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “EXXUA ~$2.3–2.7M”; its bull case expected “EXXUA $3.0–3.5M.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: June 30 cash was $26.3 million, above the preview’s estimated $21–24 million range, while the company was deleveraging rather than showing the anticipated cash decline. The revolver was later fully repaid, and full-year interest expense fell to $1.9 million from $3.7 million.
fact_evidence: “Cash was relatively stable at $26.3 million at June 30 while the company deleveraged its balance sheet, reducing the revolver to $6.1 million (later fully repaid) and cutting full-year interest expense to $1.9 million from $3.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 burn of “$3.5–4.5M, putting cash at roughly $21–24M,” and highlighted cash “vs. ~$22M.”

description: The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4, rather than delivering the operating deterioration and cash burn the preview associated with the Q3 cost run-rate. Full-year adjusted EBITDA was still negative, so the improvement was quarterly rather than a full-year profit.
fact_evidence: “The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million in Q4 (versus negative $2.8 million in Q3), while full-year FY2026 adjusted EBITDA remained negative $3.7 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q4 burn “should run $3.5–4.5M” and expected an EPS miss on launch spend; it also noted Q3 adjusted EBITDA of “-$2.8M.”

description: ADHD revenue was $10.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $8.7–9 million expectation and its concern that a drop toward $7.5 million would signal faster erosion. The portfolio still declined from $13.1 million a year earlier, but the decline was less severe than the preview’s base case implied.
fact_evidence: “The ADHD portfolio [was] at $10.4 million (down from $13.1 million YoY).”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected ADHD at “~$8.7M” and said a print “holding ~$9M” would indicate a floor.

description: Pediatrics revenue was $1.8 million, twice the preview’s $0.9 million base-case estimate.
fact_evidence: “Pediatrics at $1.8 million.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Pediatric ~$0.9M.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: EXXUA’s prescriber base reached nearly 1,200 physicians, well above the preview’s roughly 750-prescriber validation threshold. However, many had prescribed to only one or two patients, so the breadth exceeded expectations while repeat or deeper adoption remained a caveat.
fact_evidence: “Nearly 1,200 unique physicians have prescribed EXXUA to nearly 2,500 unique patients, though many prescribers have only tried it with one or two patients so far.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required “prescribers above ~750” and called prescriber breadth the key tell for durable demand.

description: Management provided a more concrete FY2027 profitability framework than the preview expected: cash-based operating expenses of $45–49 million, a Q4 gross-margin target of 66–67%, and positive adjusted EBITDA in the six months ending June 30, 2027. The preview had warned that a lack of any FY2027 revenue or EBITDA framework would be a negative, although the call facts do not give total-company FY2027 revenue guidance.
fact_evidence: “For FY2027, management guided to $45-49 million in cash-based operating expenses (including up to $6 million more S&M deferred from FY2026), targeting 66-67% gross margin by Q4 and positive adjusted EBITDA in the six months ending June 30, 2027.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Any FY2027 revenue or EBITDA framework on the call” was a key catalyst, and that “Silence here is a de facto negative.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: The sales force temporarily fell from 43 representatives to 32 before recovering to about 42, while prescriptions per representative more than doubled. That combination of performance-based cuts and sharply higher productivity was not anticipated in the preview, which instead focused on rising launch spending.
fact_evidence: “The sales force fell to a low of 32 reps in July (from 43 in March) due to intentional performance-based cuts, but has since rebounded to approximately 42”; prescriptions per rep “more than doubled from ~18/month in March to ~43/month in July.”

description: Revenue was $6.6 billion, below the preview’s $6.70–6.71 billion estimate, and sales growth of 5.6% was below the expected 7.4%. The $56.05 EPS beat the $54.20 estimate on the headline, but included a $4.43 tariff-refund benefit; excluding LIFO charges in both years, EPS growth was only 8.5%, versus the preview’s implied 11% growth.
fact_evidence: “Q4 total sales grew 5.6% to $6.6 billion and EPS rose 15.1% to $56.05,” including “a $4.43 benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds”; excluding LIFO charges in both years, “EPS grew 8.5%,” versus reported growth of 15.1%.
expectation_evidence: “Revenue $6.70–6.71B” and “EPS $54.08–$54.42 (working: $54.20)”; implied EPS growth was “+11.0%.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: DIY same-store sales declined 0.6%, rather than showing the growth suggested by the preview’s expectation that Q4 domestic comps would be similar to Q3. Traffic fell more than 5%, with weakness concentrated among financially challenged consumers who deferred purchases or traded down.
fact_evidence: “Domestic DIY same-store sales declined 0.6% in Q4 as traffic fell more than 5% while average ticket rose about 5%,” with weakness among financially challenged consumers showing “deferrals and trade-down.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided Q4 domestic comps to “a similar range” to Q3 and noted Q3 DIY comps of “+2.2%.”

description: SG&A deleveraged sharply in Q4, despite the preview noting that SG&A had leveraged in Q3 and identifying loss of leverage as a miss scenario. Management also expects FY27 SG&A per store to rise about 3%.
fact_evidence: “SG&A deleveraged 101 basis points in Q4” and was up 8.9% in total; FY27 SG&A per store is expected to grow “~3%.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 SG&A “was +7.6% but leveraged 25bp” and described losing leverage as the miss scenario.

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Commercial comps were 8.6% in Q4, below the double-digit growth the preview described as the structural story supporting the thesis, though still above its stated sub-8% problem threshold. FY27 guidance of high-single- to low-double-digit growth leaves the business near, but not clearly above, that double-digit expectation.
fact_evidence: “Domestic commercial same-store sales grew 8.6% in Q4”; FY27 guidance is “high-single/low-double-digit growth.”
expectation_evidence: The preview said “Double-digit commercial growth is the structural story” and that “Sub-8% would be a genuine problem.”

dimension_name: Development, operational execution, and regulatory milestones
description: The store-opening plan is less ambitious over the longer term than the preview’s path toward roughly 500 annual openings by 2028: management cut the FY28 target to about 430 and plans about 400 in FY27. FY26 openings of 374 did exceed the preview’s 365 expectation.
fact_evidence: The company opened “374 new stores in FY26 (versus 304 in FY25)” and plans “approximately 400 in FY27, while cutting the FY28 target from ~500 to ~430 stores by slowing Brazil expansion.”
expectation_evidence: The preview described “365 store openings in FY26 stepping toward 500/year by 2028.”

dimension_name: Accounting, reporting practices, taxes, and special items
description: The preview expected a Q4 LIFO charge of about $30 million, but the reported charge was $15 million, reducing the quarter’s LIFO-related EPS drag. This was a favorable difference from the stated expectation.
fact_evidence: Q4 included “a $0.69 drag from a $15 million LIFO charge.”
expectation_evidence: The preview’s trajectory table listed a Q4 LIFO charge of “~$30M / 45bp (guided).”

dimension_name: Market environment, policy, opportunity size, and market valuation
description: A stronger peso provided a substantial Q4 tailwind and management expects another benefit in Q1, an exposure the preview did not flag. This supported reported sales and earnings beyond the operational growth described in the release.
fact_evidence: Peso strengthening of nearly 9% created a “$70 million sales, $21 million EBIT, and $0.87 EPS tailwind in Q4”; management expects a further “~$0.60 EPS benefit in Q1 FY27 at current spot rates.”

description: The FY27 gross-margin outlook is limited to flat to up 25 basis points excluding LIFO, despite the preview’s emphasis on gross-margin inflection as LIFO rolls off. The preview did not provide a specific FY27 margin estimate, so the difference is against the margin-inflection thesis rather than a precise consensus number.
fact_evidence: “FY27 gross margin (ex-LIFO) is guided flat to up 25 basis points,” with LIFO charges modeled at “$85-90 million” versus “$192 million recognized in FY26.”
expectation_evidence: The preview framed the debate as “whether gross margin inflects as LIFO rolls off” and called gross margin “the whole thesis.”

description: KB Home reported diluted EPS of $1.05, above the preview’s $0.88–$0.90 expectation. That is a meaningful upside gap, though the preview cited adjusted EPS while the call facts report diluted EPS.
fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 total revenues were $1.3 billion with diluted EPS of $1.05.”
expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.88 (Zacks) / $0.90 (Alphastreet).”

description: Q3 adjusted housing gross margin reached 16.8%, above both the preview’s roughly 16.3% consensus and the 16.0–16.6% company-guidance range. The result was also stronger sequentially than the preview’s cited Q2 margin of 15.2%.
fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted housing gross margin was 16.8% ... up sequentially from 15.7% in Q2.”
expectation_evidence: “Housing gross margin: ~16.3% (mid of guide)”; “16.0–16.6% ex-charges”; and “Q2 actual: 15.2%.”

description: The Q4 ASP outlook was cut to about $480,000 from roughly $500,000, and Q4 gross-margin guidance was reduced by about one percentage point, largely because of Southern California weakness. This reverses part of the expected Q4 step-up in ASP and margins.
fact_evidence: “Management lowered its Q4 ASP guidance to about $480,000 from roughly $500,000 and cut Q4 gross margin by about 1 percentage point, driven largely by Southern California weakness.”
expectation_evidence: “The implied Q4 ... midpoint (~$1.65B on ~3,300 homes) requires an ASP near $500K versus ~$470K in Q3.”

description: The full-year housing-revenue range was narrowed to $4.9–$5.1 billion, lowering its upper bound by $200 million from the preview’s stated $4.9–$5.3 billion range. The full-year gross-margin range of 16.0–16.2% is also below the preview’s cited 16.1–16.5% range.
fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was largely maintained: deliveries of 10,500-11,000 homes, housing revenues narrowed to $4.9-5.1 billion, and full-year gross margin of 16.0-16.2%.”
expectation_evidence: “FY guidance is 10,500–11,000 deliveries and $4.90–5.30B housing revenue”; the preview also refers to the “FY 16.1–16.5% guide.”

dimension_name: Recurring operating, demand, and activity KPIs
description: Unsold inventory was notably lower than the preview had quantified: total unsold homes were 26% of production and finished unsold homes just 9%, with about 1,100 homes sold but not yet started. These figures indicate less unsold inventory and more forward demand than the preview specifically anticipated.
fact_evidence: “Total unsold inventory fell to 26% of production from 41% a year ago, with finished unsold homes at just 9% versus 16%, and roughly 1,100 homes sold but not yet started.”

dimension_name: Cash flow, working capital, and financial position
description: The reported debt-to-capital ratio was 35.7%, higher than the 34.1% level the preview cited, adding to the balance-sheet constraint it had flagged around buybacks.
fact_evidence: “Debt-to-capital [rose] to 35.7% from 33.2% a year ago.”
expectation_evidence: “Debt-to-capital rose to 34.1% from 30.3%.”
